issues.title: [BUG] Streamable HTTP MCP: tools/call stays "still running" forever when the server dies mid-call — the client reconnects the GET stream but never fails the pending POST

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

labels.name: platform:linux
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on Linux

issues.body:
## TL;DR

**When a Streamable HTTP MCP server dies while a `tools/call` is in flight, Claude Code never fails that call. It logs `Tool '<name>' still running (Ns elapsed)` indefinitely, even though it has already noticed the peer go away and reconnected the GET stream.**

The server answers the `tools/call` POST with a `text/event-stream` response, and that stream ends before the result frame arrives (reset, clean close, or the whole server process dying). The pending request is never rejected. It is only failed when the client later closes its own transport for some other reason; in the repro below that was process teardown at 119 s, and in the original 240 s runs at 238 s. When that happens the client raises its existing "connection closed before the tool call was answered" error and applies its retry rule. `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` is the only bound, and unset it did not fire within 240 s.

Reproduced on **2.1.307** and **2.1.304**, using unmodified release binaries, Linux x64.

## Prior reports

These were all closed by bots and locked, and none was triaged:

- #44006, "MCP tool calls hang indefinitely with no way to cancel": closed as stale (`has repro`, `area:mcp`).
- #55992, "Streamable HTTP MCP: in-flight tool call Promise orphaned forever on connection drop": auto-closed as a duplicate of #44006.
- #60061, "2.1.143 silently hangs MCP tool calls after SSE drop": closed as stale (`has repro`, `area:mcp`).

This report adds a dependency-free local repro (one Python stdlib file, loopback only), results on two current versions, and one new observation: the client reconnects the GET stream within about a second of the server dying, so it does detect the dead peer, but it leaves the POST pending anyway.

## Repro

`repro_mcp.py`: on the first `tools/call` per tool, it opens an SSE response and then simulates the server dying, resetting that stream and every open GET stream. Later calls answer normally.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# repro_mcp.py PORT - Streamable-HTTP MCP server. The first tools/call per tool opens an
# SSE response, then the "server dies": that stream and every open GET stream are reset.
import json, socket, struct, sys, time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

TOOLS = [
    {"name": "poke", "description": "Changes state.", "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}},
    {"name": "peek", "description": "Reads state.", "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
     "annotations": {"readOnlyHint": True}},
]
faulted, gets = set(), []


def say(*a):
    print(time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), *a, flush=True)


def rst(conn):
    try:
        conn.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))
        conn.close()
    except OSError:
        pass


class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"

    def log_message(self, format, *args):
        pass

    def sse(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
        self.send_header("Mcp-Session-Id", "s1")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b": open\n\n")
        self.wfile.flush()

    def do_GET(self):
        say("GET stream opened")
        self.sse()
        gets.append(self.connection)
        while self.connection in gets:
            time.sleep(0.2)
        self.close_connection = True

    def reply(self, code, obj=None):
        body = b"" if obj is None else json.dumps(obj).encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        if obj is not None:
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Mcp-Session-Id", "s1")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_POST(self):
        msg = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)) or b"{}")
        mid, method, params = msg.get("id"), msg.get("method"), msg.get("params") or {}
        say("POST", method, params.get("name", ""))
        if mid is None:
            return self.reply(202)
        result = {}
        if method == "initialize":
            result = {"protocolVersion": params.get("protocolVersion", "2025-06-18"),
                      "capabilities": {"tools": {}}, "serverInfo": {"name": "repro", "version": "0"}}
        elif method == "tools/list":
            result = {"tools": TOOLS}
        elif method == "tools/call":
            if params["name"] not in faulted:
                faulted.add(params["name"])
                self.sse()
                time.sleep(0.5)
                say("  -> server dies: resetting the response stream and", len(gets), "GET stream(s)")
                for c in list(gets):
                    gets.remove(c)
                    rst(c)
                self.close_connection = True
                return rst(self.connection)
            result = {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": params["name"] + " ok"}]}
        self.reply(200, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": mid, "result": result})


ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])), H).serve_forever()
```

```sh
python3 repro_mcp.py 8765 &
echo '{"mcpServers":{"repro":{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp"}}}' > mcp.json
timeout 120 claude -p "Call the tool mcp__repro__poke once with no arguments. If it errors, do not call it again; reply with the error text." \
  --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config mcp.json --allowedTools mcp__repro__poke --debug-file debug.log
grep -E 'Calling MCP tool|still running|connection closed|session expired|Retrying' debug.log
```

### Observed (2.1.307)

Server:

```
19:59:42 POST server/discover
19:59:42 POST initialize
19:59:42 POST notifications/initialized
19:59:42 GET stream opened
19:59:42 POST tools/list
19:59:45 POST tools/call poke
19:59:46   -> server dies: resetting the response stream and 1 GET stream(s)
19:59:47 GET stream opened
```

Client (`debug.log`):

```
2026-10-22T00:59:45.940Z [DEBUG] MCP server "repro": Calling MCP tool: poke
2026-10-22T01:00:15.941Z [DEBUG] MCP server "repro": Tool 'poke' still running (30s elapsed)
2026-10-22T01:00:45.940Z [DEBUG] MCP server "repro": Tool 'poke' still running (59s elapsed)
2026-10-22T01:01:15.937Z [DEBUG] MCP server "repro": Tool 'poke' still running (89s elapsed)
2026-10-22T01:01:41.784Z [DEBUG] MCP server "repro": HTTP connection closed after 119s (cleanly)
2026-10-22T01:01:41.786Z [DEBUG] MCP server "repro": MCP session expired during tool call (connection closed), clearing connection cache for re-initialization
```

The client reopened the GET stream one second after the server died (`19:59:47`), but the POST stayed pending for the whole run. The `01:01:41` close is `timeout 120` killing the process, not anything the server did. In the longer runs below (240 s cap, server named `fake`), teardown came early enough for the tool result to reach the model, and it was:

```
MCP server "fake" connection closed before the tool call was answered. The tool may have run: check whether it did before running it again.
```

## Matrix

A larger version of the same server was run with one `claude -p` turn per case, and the model made exactly one `tool_use` in each SSE case, so any second arrival at the server is a client retry. Each SSE case hung until teardown (about 238 s under a 240 s cap):

| fault | 2.1.304 | 2.1.307 |
|---|---|---|
| SSE response ends cleanly (FIN), no result | hangs; at teardown re-sends every tool (2 arrivals) | hangs; at teardown re-sends only `readOnlyHint` / `idempotentHint` tools |
| SSE response reset (RST) | same | same |
| server dies: response stream and GET stream reset | same; GET reconnects at once, POST stays pending | same |
| plain JSON response, socket reset | 1 arrival; `ECONNRESET` returned to the model at once | same |
| HTTP 503 | 1 arrival; error returned at once | same |
| server dies, with `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT=20000` | not run | aborted at 30 s: `sent no response or progress for 30s; aborting` |

2.1.307's change ("only read-only or idempotent tools are now retried", related to #98466) is visible in the first row and works as described. It only acts once the transport has closed, though, which is the step this report is about.

## Expected

When the HTTP response stream that carries a pending request's result ends, by EOF or by error, before that request's JSON-RPC response has arrived, reject the pending request promptly. It could use the same `connection closed before the tool call was answered` error the client already raises at transport close, so the existing retry rule applies unchanged. If the server sent SSE event ids, one `Last-Event-ID` resumption attempt (per the Streamable HTTP spec) could come first.

A lower default idle timeout is not a substitute. A timeout cannot tell a dead stream from a slow but healthy tool, so any value either cuts off legitimate long silent calls or leaves this hang in place.

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.307 and 2.1.304 (native, linux-x64)
- Python 3, standard library only, for the repro server
- Model for the repro turns: `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` (the model is irrelevant to the hang)

issues.title: [BUG] macOS: Files & Folders gains a version-named entry on every update; denied entries cannot be removed (follow-up to #79053, #76615)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: platform:macos
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on macOS

issues.body:
Environment: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Claude Code 2.1.307 (native installer, arm64)

What's wrong
- `claude daemon run` is started by launchd and runs `~/.local/share/claude/versions/<ver>`
  directly. TCC keys grants to that versioned path, so every update adds a new entry
  named "2.1.xxx" under Privacy & Security → Files and Folders.
- A stable `~/.local/share/claude/ClaudeCode.app` (com.anthropic.claude-code) exists and is
  hard-linked to the same binary, but the daemon and background sessions do not run through it.
- Old entries stay after the updater deletes old binaries.
- On macOS 27 the per-user TCC.db sits in a ProtectedSystem container. It cannot be read or
  edited even with Full Disk Access.
- `tccutil reset All com.anthropic.claude-code` does not remove these path-keyed entries.
- The "—" button removes entries that only contain allowed records. An entry that contains a
  denied record (e.g. App Data → Google Chrome.app) cannot be removed, and its toggle cannot be
  changed. So every version with a denial leaves a permanent entry.

Expected: one stable "Claude Code" entry whose grants survive updates.
Suggested fix: launch the daemon and workers through ClaudeCode.app, as proposed in #79053.

#79053 and #76615 reported the same root cause and were closed by the stale bot without a fix.

issues.title: Artifact publish through a symlinked path wedges unattended sessions on an unanswerable consent dialog

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: platform:macos
labels.description: Issue specifically occurs on macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

Publishing an artifact from a path that contains a symlinked component wedges the session on a consent dialog that only the human can answer. In a multi-session setup the user has no way to tell which session is asking or why, and there is no setting that avoids it.

## Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.305, macOS (Darwin 25.5)
- ~10 concurrent sessions, most in auto mode, many unattended

## Repro

1. In a worktree, have a gitignored `scratch/` symlink pointing into another repo (or use `/tmp`, which on macOS is a symlink to `/private/tmp`).
2. Ask the agent to publish an artifact whose `file_path` goes through that symlink.
3. The publish-source check flags it as redirected and shows:

   > The publish source does not verifiably match its spelling - approval must see that, which only the full consent dialog shows

4. The session blocks until the user finds and answers the dialog.

## Impact

1. **Silent, indefinite block.** The session waits on a modal. Nothing outside that session tells the user which session is asking, so with 10 sessions running, finding it is guesswork.
2. **No pre-approval path.** No allow rule or setting covers this check. The only workaround is for agents to call `realpath` before publishing, which agents don't know to do.
3. **The workaround gets blocked too.** Telling sessions to use the real path, relayed from one session to another, was denied by the auto-mode classifier as "Auto-Mode Bypass". That wedged a second session in a loop of denials.
4. **Undocumented.** The message text is not on the artifacts or errors docs pages.

## Asks

- Resolve symlinks before the check, or show the resolved path in a normal approval card instead of the full consent dialog.
- Name the requesting session in the dialog, and send a desktop or mobile notification when a session blocks on one.
- Document the message and its fix.
- Let an allow rule cover artifact publishes of files inside the session's working directories.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Real-time plan usage/quota indicator in Cowork (5-hour & weekly limits)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched [existing requests](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20label%3Aenhancement) and this feature hasn't been requested yet
- [x] This is a single feature request (not multiple features)

### Problem Statement

Cowork has no visible indicator of PLAN USAGE / QUOTA consumption. Users cannot
see how much of their 5-hour window or weekly limit they have consumed during a
session. The only way to check is to leave the session and open Settings > Usage
on claude.ai, which shows limited, non-real-time data.

Claude Code solves this: `/usage` shows current 5-hour and weekly consumption and
reset times. Cowork users get nothing equivalent and only find out they are near
the cap when a warning appears close to the limit.

IMPORTANT — this is NOT about the context window / compaction indicator. Existing
requests (#37568, #20041, #35374) all cover context-window usage and were closed.
This request is specifically about PLAN QUOTA (5-hour and weekly rate limits),
which is a different metric and remains unaddressed in Cowork.

### Proposed Solution

1. A persistent, always-visible indicator in the Cowork UI showing current 5-hour
   and weekly quota consumption as a percentage, plus reset time.
2. This is the same data `/usage` already exposes in the CLI — extend it to Cowork.
3. Optional: a warning threshold (e.g. 80%) so users can plan work before hitting
   the cap.

### Alternative Solutions

Currently users must leave the session and check Settings > Usage manually, or rely
on unofficial third-party tray apps that read internal endpoints — fragile and a
security concern. Neither is acceptable for a first-party workflow tool.


### Priority

Medium - Would be very helpful

### Feature Category

Interactive mode (TUI)

### Use Case Example

Example scenario:
1. I open a Cowork session to work through a multi-step task (research + document
   generation) that spans 30-60 minutes.
2. Partway through, my 5-hour quota runs out with no advance warning — the session
   stops mid-task and I lose momentum.
3. With a visible quota indicator, I would have seen I was near the cap and could
   have paused, split the work, or waited for the reset instead of being cut off.
4. This saves time because I can plan around the limit proactively instead of
   discovering it reactively, the same way `/usage` already lets CLI users do.

### Additional Context

- Claude Code already exposes this data via `/usage` (5-hour and weekly consumption
  + reset times). The request is to surface the same data in the Cowork UI.
- Related closed issues cover the CONTEXT WINDOW indicator, not plan quota:
  #37568, #20041, #35374. This request is a distinct metric and should not be
  treated as a duplicate of those.
- Third-party tray apps exist but read internal endpoints — fragile and a security
  concern for a first-party tool.

issues.title: [BUG] ScheduleWakeup in a headless run reports a scheduled wakeup, ends the turn, and the wakeup never fires (still present in 2.1.307)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: has repro
labels.description: Has detailed reproduction steps

issues.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this hasn't been reported yet (it was, as #74685, which the stale bot closed as not planned and asked for a new issue if still relevant; it still is)
- [x] This is a single bug report
- [x] I am using the latest version of Claude Code (2.1.307, Agent SDK 0.3.307)

### What's Wrong?

In a headless run (an Agent SDK `query()` with a string prompt, same as `claude -p`), `ScheduleWakeup` succeeds and its result tells the model:

```
Next wakeup scheduled for 21:45:00 (in 88s). If you owe the user a status update this tick, write it now as ordinary response text; then end the turn — the harness re-invokes you when the wakeup fires or a task-notification arrives.
```

The model does what it is told and ends the turn. The run then exits about a second later, and the wakeup never fires.

The cost is not just a lost wakeup. The tool result tells the model to stop working and wait, so whatever it planned to do after the wakeup is silently dropped, and the final answer reads as if the work is in progress. We run Claude through the Agent SDK as a Slack and GitHub bot, and this is how it ends turns promising follow-ups that never come.

#74685 reported the same thing on 2.1.233 and was labelled `reproduced`. #82633 (open) describes the same return value in an interactive session outside `/loop`.

### What Should Happen?

Either of these, as long as the result matches what will happen:

- When the session cannot be re-invoked (a closed-input run, `-p`, or a string-prompt SDK `query()`), refuse the call with a clear reason, or leave the tool out of the tool list.
- Keep the process alive until the wakeup fires and run the follow-up turn.

### Error Messages/Logs

```
[5.3s] init, claude_code_version=2.1.307
[7.0s] tool_use ScheduleWakeup {"delaySeconds":60,"reason":"repro","prompt":"Say WOKE UP.","noop":false}
[7.1s] tool_result: Next wakeup scheduled for 21:45:00 (in 88s). If you owe the user a status update this tick, write it now as ordinary response text; then end the turn — the harness re-invokes you when the wakeup fires or a task-notification arrives.
[7.8s] result success: scheduled
[8.8s] query() iterator finished; process exits. No wakeup turn was delivered.
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.307` in an empty directory with `"type": "module"`.
2. Save this as `repro.mjs` and run `node repro.mjs`:

```js
import { mkdtempSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { query } from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk";

const t0 = Date.now();
const s = () => ((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1) + "s";
for await (const msg of query({
  prompt: "Call ScheduleWakeup with delaySeconds 60, reason 'repro', prompt 'Say WOKE UP.'. Then end your turn with the single word: scheduled.",
  options: {
    cwd: mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "wakeup-repro-")),
    model: "sonnet",
    settingSources: [],
    allowedTools: ["ScheduleWakeup"],
  },
})) {
  if (msg.type === "system" && msg.subtype === "init") console.log(`[${s()}] init, claude_code_version=${msg.claude_code_version}`);
  if (msg.type === "assistant") for (const b of msg.message.content) if (b.type === "tool_use") console.log(`[${s()}] tool_use ${b.name} ${JSON.stringify(b.input)}`);
  if (msg.type === "user") for (const b of msg.message.content ?? []) if (b.type === "tool_result") console.log(`[${s()}] tool_result: ${typeof b.content === "string" ? b.content : JSON.stringify(b.content)}`);
  if (msg.type === "result") console.log(`[${s()}] result ${msg.subtype}: ${msg.result}`);
}
console.log(`[${s()}] query() iterator finished; process exits. No wakeup turn was delivered.`);
```

3. Wait past the scheduled time. Nothing else happens; the process is already gone.

The same happens on 2.1.299 / SDK 0.3.299. Our workaround is `disallowedTools: ["ScheduleWakeup", "CronCreate", "CronDelete", "CronList", "Monitor", "ListAgents", "SendMessage", "TaskStop"]` plus `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1`. That env var makes background agents run in the foreground, but it does not remove `ScheduleWakeup`.

### Claude Model

Sonnet (default)

### Is this a regression?

No, this never worked

### Claude Code Version

2.1.307 (via @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.307)

### Platform

Anthropic API

### Operating System

macOS

issues.title: Safety classifier blocks the final report of a long, authorized defensive security audit, and the agent keeps using tokens without warning

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## What happened
- I asked Claude Code to run a read-only security audit of my own company's AWS account, repositories, and CI, plus a survey of recent public security incidents, and to compile the results into one visual HTML report.
- Claude Code ran 6+ parallel subagents (Opus) for over an hour, which used a large number of tokens. The subagents finished and their reports were shown in the conversation.
- When Claude started writing the consolidated HTML report, a safety classifier stopped the output twice and told it not to produce that content again, even reworded.
- After that, Claude declined to export the same findings as Markdown or to put them into a prompt for another tool, so the main deliverable could not be produced at all.
- Claude did not warn me beforehand that the final report might be blocked, and it kept spending tokens on investigation (including waiting for the remaining subagents) after the block happened.

## Expected
- Either the authorized defensive report can be produced, or Claude tells me early that this kind of deliverable may be blocked, before it spends a large number of tokens.
- After a block, Claude should clearly explain the impact and stop or ask before continuing expensive work whose output can no longer be delivered.

## Related
- #103937
- #103758

## Environment
- Claude Code CLI, model: Opus 5.5 (1M context)
- Date: 2026-10-22

releases.name: v2.1.307
releases.body:
## What's changed

- Added `/claude-api api-version` to move Claude API code to API version `2026-10-21`
- Added the `claude_code.safety_event` OpenTelemetry event for each tool call a permission rule, auto mode, a safety check, a hook or the sandbox stopped, prompted or sent back
- Fixed requests failing with a model-not-found error when `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT` is set and the model is an alias with the `[1m]` suffix, such as `opus[1m]`
- Fixed the `prompt-caching-scope` beta header being sent behind custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateways and on Foundry, where it has no effect
- Fixed MCP servers showing "needs authentication" in `claude -p` on macOS while the login keychain was locked; they now say why, and the next run after an unlock connects without a new sign-in
- Fixed MCP servers being reported as timed out, and staying failed in headless runs, when a macOS or Linux computer went to sleep while they were connecting
- Fixed HTTP MCP tool calls being sent twice when the connection closed mid-call; only read-only or idempotent tools are now retried
- Fixed a turn sometimes starting without an SDK MCP server's latest tools when a background task was running
- Fixed some "Autocompact is thrashing" errors in turns that read many PDF pages, images or other large tool results
- Fixed `/autocompact` in cloud sessions going back to the default window after the session restarted
- Fixed a conversation cleared with `/clear` sometimes coming back when a cloud or self-hosted runner session restarted
- Fixed `CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS` being ignored in Claude apps gateway sessions
- Fixed telemetry from Claude Desktop sessions behind a Claude apps gateway being rejected when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is set
- Fixed `/permissions` > Recently denied not showing the denied shell command, and auto mode's local classifier ignoring an approval from there when it checks a retried command; approving a row now names the command, not its description
- Fixed `/help` and the `/` command menu showing long model-facing descriptions for bundled skills such as `/claude-api` instead of their short descriptions
- Fixed subagent transcripts recording placeholder token usage and an empty stop reason for streamed responses
- Fixed model switches through the Agent SDK's `setModel()`, and apps built on it, being refused when the API took more than 5 seconds to confirm the model; Claude Code now waits up to 15 seconds
- Fixed a background command stopped through a connected app (such as the desktop app archiving an idle session) being reported to Claude as stopped by the user; the notice now names its output file
- Fixed WebFetch in Cowork cloud sessions reporting a tool error when a site answered with a 4xx status or a robots.txt refusal; it is now a normal result, as in local sessions
- Fixed write tools on a directly configured GitHub MCP server showing a form that closed without creating anything in the desktop app's Code tab
- Fixed Artifact tool reads failing with a connection reset when the server had closed a reused connection
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions with `--use-anthropic-git-proxy` committing a `.claude/settings.local.json` left in the clone by an earlier session
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed archiving or requeueing a session, or stopping the runner, during its checkout hook leaving the hook's processes running and the runner's slot held
- Improved recovery from unparseable tool calls: Claude Code now retries the call up to twice before ending the turn with an error
- Improved fork subagents launched together: each is now told which launch is its own, so forks are much less likely to try to start each other's work
- Improved browser sign-in: the success page now appears as soon as sign-in completes, without waiting for your account profile to load
- Improved web search errors in cloud and self-hosted runner sessions: a search refused with a 403 that gives a reason now shows that reason instead of a generic "Authentication error"
- Improved the time to the first reply in cloud sessions when one of the desktop app's MCP servers can't connect
- Improved Remote Control connect time for sessions whose transcript contains large pasted images or PDF reads
- Changed the notice Claude gets when the WebSearch budget is used up to also tell it not to query search engines in a browser or through computer use
- Changed the `axScreenReader` setting and `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER` in a settings `env` block to apply only from user, managed or `--settings` settings (since 2.1.305)
- Self-hosted runner: Changed checkout hooks to be stopped after 30 minutes by default, failing the session's setup; if yours needs longer, raise `--checkout-hook-timeout-min` or set it to `0`
- Self-hosted runner: Changed the certificate file built for Anthropic-managed git to filter its trusted certificates as the CLI does; a `[runner:warn]` line gives the number left out
- [VSCode] Added a notice on the microphone button when voice dictation stops by itself (15 seconds without recognized speech, or the 2-minute limit), saying why and that the text so far is kept
- [VSCode] Fixed a long prompt expanded with Show more covering the whole chat panel: a pinned prompt is now capped at 40% of the panel and scrolls
- [VSCode] Fixed part of a list item or table cell with LaTeX math pasting as a new list or table in rich text editors
- [VSCode] Fixed dictation failing behind a TLS-inspecting proxy when `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is set only in `~/.claude/settings.json`; it now also follows `CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE`
- [VSCode] Changed the "still open somewhere else" notice to also cover a Claude process left over from an extension restart, which usually ends on its own within about 10 minutes
- [VSCode] Changed voice dictation to filter its trusted certificates as the CLI does
- [VSCode] Changed the extension's own requests to filter their trusted certificates as the CLI does, and to trust the `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` file named in the environment or in user settings
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the repository picker saying "No repositories match" while a search was still running; it now shows "Searching…" until the results arrive
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed the "Waiting for a runner" status on self-hosted environments being cut off; with on-demand runners it now counts up from your last message and shows failed attempts
- [Code Review] Added `@claude review stop` (also `off` and `pause`) to Code Review, ending an `@claude review always` subscription on a pull request without starting a new review

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

**26.1016.51333, build 21161** — ChatGPT desktop app with the Codex interface, bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`.

The version was read from the installed app's `Info.plist`. Desktop logs during the recording independently show build 21161, commit `28ffa59d1a9faff009b5e11511b65a65183038f1`. Bundled CLI package metadata reports `0.163.0-alpha.11`; the active executor version has not been independently established.

An earlier inspection the same day was on 26.1013.40934 / build 20770. The relevant code branches were checked again in build 21161; the two inspections should not be conflated.

### What subscription do you have?

**Pro**.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.4, OS build 25E246, Apple Silicon.

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm`

Recording date: October 22, 2026, approximately 10:19:57–10:20:51, Asia/Shanghai.

### What issue are you seeing?

Two existing conversations in the same project behave differently. Both show **Codex** and **GPT-6 Astra Max**, in the same app window. **Settings → General → Follow-up behavior → Queue** is selected.

| Recorded behavior | Conversation A, affected | Conversation B, comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Permissions control below the composer | Missing | Shows Full access |
| Sending a short follow-up during an active response | The message immediately appears in the transcript, without a pending queue card | The message remains in a pending card above the composer while the original response continues |
| Pending card actions | No card is shown | Steer and delete actions are visible |

The follow-up text is the same short greeting, `你好` (“hello”). A sends it twice during the active response. The recording includes pointer interactions with the Send button in both conversations; no modifier-key combination is displayed. It is not a low-level keyboard event trace.

This is a conversation-specific difference in visible behavior. I previously described A as steering the current run; the directly recorded fact is immediate transcript insertion instead of a pending queue card. The exact backend submission intent for A still needs to be traced.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Using the existing conversations shown in the recording:

1. Select Codex and set Follow-up behavior to Queue.
2. Open conversation A, which has no permissions control beneath its composer.
3. Start a response. While it is still working, type `你好` and click Send.
4. Observe that the follow-up immediately appears in the transcript. Repeating it produces another transcript message, with no pending queue card visible.
5. Switch to conversation B in the same project, still using Codex and GPT-6 Astra Max.
6. Start a response and submit the same greeting with the Send button while it is working.
7. Observe the pending card with Steer/delete actions while the original response continues.
8. Open General settings: Follow-up behavior remains Queue; Send shortcut is Enter.

I recorded a 54-second reproduction; the observations above were checked against the recording. A fresh-profile sequence for creating the affected conversation has not yet been isolated. The recording does not follow B through completion and eventual queue delivery.

### What is the expected behavior?

- A normal follow-up should wait for the current response to finish when Queue is selected.
- If a particular conversation intentionally cannot queue, disclose the effective behavior and reason before sending.
- Explain why the permissions control is unavailable for that conversation, and show its effective permissions when possible.
- Provide a supported way to restore predictable behavior without losing the conversation history.

### Additional information

#### Recording evidence

A redacted recording excerpt is prepared but **is not attached to this issue yet**. The table below summarizes the reviewed footage. It is a 24-second, silent excerpt made from the original recording, with three cuts, no speed change, and privacy masks. It is sampled at 10 fps and scaled to 1800 pixels wide; its pixels are derived from the recording, not regenerated UI.

| Original recording time | Excerpt time | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 00:06–00:19 | 00:00–00:13 | A: active response, absent permissions control, two greetings entering the transcript |
| 00:31–00:39 | 00:13–00:21 | B: Full access, a greeting retained in a pending card, Steer action |
| 00:47–00:50 | 00:21–00:24 | General settings: Queue selected, Enter send shortcut |

The original also shows that both conversations are in the same project and that the subscription is Pro. The excerpt masks the sidebar, account menu, conversation titles, and an earlier personalized greeting, so those details are documented from the original rather than independently visible in the excerpt.

#### Configuration and log corroboration

Read-only inspection verified:

```toml
[desktop]
followUpQueueMode = "queue"
```

The startup cache also contains `electron-initial-follow-up-queue-mode: "queue"`. The recording independently shows Queue selected. Persistence does not establish the final effective value used by each conversation.

At **2026-10-22 10:20:31.859 +08:00**, the desktop log records a successful `thread/queue/add` response (`errorCode=null`). This aligns with the comparison conversation's pending card in the recording. The association is based on timing; the live thread metadata could not be retrieved to independently complete that mapping. No backend submission trace establishing A's final intent was obtained.

#### Relevant code branches; root cause not established

In the installed build 21161:

- `app-initial-f3e281fb9a71.js` selects `send-only` when either `threadStartKind` or `threadSource` equals `aeon`; otherwise it reads the follow-up preference. The resolver preserves `send-only` over a queue override.
- `app-primary-9bb8fd8d770a.js` suppresses `PermissionsModeDropdown` when `isAeonActive || isAeonThread` is true. Execution mode, layout, and other conditions also affect visibility.

These are possible investigation points, **not proof that conversation A is an Aeon or executes those branches**. A navigation event during the recording reports `threadIsAeon=false`, but omits a thread identifier and cannot conclusively classify A. Exact excerpts and file hashes for the recording build are included below.

The app's `list_threads` tool still failed with `Codex app tool request failed`; earlier `read_thread` attempts also failed. These diagnostic failures limit access to live metadata; their relationship to the reported UI behavior is unknown.

Please compare effective `followUpQueueMode`, `queueModeOverride`, final submission intent, composer mode, follow-up target type, `threadStartKind`, `threadSource`, `isAeonActive`, `isAeonThread`, runtime session status, execution host, and the specific permissions-rendering condition for the two conversations.

No application settings, permissions, caches, or databases were modified by the investigation. No raw logs, account identifiers, or conversation identifiers are published in this issue.

<details>
<summary>Installed-client excerpts and SHA-256 hashes (build 21161)</summary>

`webview/assets/app-initial-f3e281fb9a71.js`

SHA-256: `a9906c234f7dfb2f59785b40f9b489d6ce509205c58ce9fd53bdfea68b1d8252`

```js
function px(e,t){return e===`aeon`||t===`aeon`}
getMessageQueueMode:async t=>{let n=e.getConversation(t.conversationId);return px(n?.threadStartKind,n?.threadSource)?`send-only`:s.readFollowUpQueueMode()}
async function s(e){let t=await r(e);return t===`send-only`?t:e.queueModeOverride??t}
```

`webview/assets/app-primary-9bb8fd8d770a.js`

SHA-256: `761037cdef242fcbf0525ceb5acd414b7c9714e30ea45402dbee7aba29cb8969`

The component takes `isAeonActive:S,isAeonThread:C`, normalizes them as `ae=S!==void 0&&S,U=C!==void 0&&C`, and derives `Se=ae||U`. The permissions-rendering condition begins:

```js
O&&!Se&&r!==`cloud`&&(!ge||Ie)?(0,wG.jsx)(Sg,
```

`Sg` imports `Gr` from app-initial, whose exported binding `cEd` dynamically loads `PermissionsModeDropdown`. These minified symbols are build-specific. This identifies a conditional branch, not the live values for either conversation.

</details>

#### Related reports

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/17445 — Queue preference ignored, including a follow-up with a persisted queue setting; open when checked earlier on October 22.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/17285 — queued messages sent before response completion; a similar symptom, not a confirmed shared cause.

The added evidence here is the within-project comparison, the missing permissions control, the recorded send behavior, and the verified saved preference. Please consolidate with an existing tracker if appropriate.

issues.title: Windows: codex mcp-server / app-server and their child MCP servers are never reaped (accumulate to hundreds over time)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
## Summary
On Windows, using Codex through its MCP-server path (`codex mcp-server`, which a host like Claude Code launches) leaks processes: every request spawns a new `codex app-server`, which in turn spawns the MCP servers from `~/.codex/config.toml` — and **none of them are reaped** when the request/session ends. Over a few days of normal use they accumulate into the hundreds and noticeably degrade the machine.

`codex exec` (one-shot) does **not** have this problem — it spawns the same children but cleans them up on normal exit. The leak is specific to the persistent mcp-server/app-server path on Windows.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- codex-cli: 0.139.0 (model gpt-5.5)
- Configured MCP servers in `~/.codex/config.toml`: playwright, comfyui, node_repl (any configured stdio MCP servers reproduce this)

## Observed behavior (controlled A/B, measured with `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`)
- **Fresh reboot baseline:** 1 `codex mcp-server`, 0 child MCP processes.
- **One request through the MCP server:** +1 `codex app-server`, and +1 of each configured MCP server (each as a `cmd → npx → node` chain). After the request completes, **none of these exit.**
- **After a few days / many sessions:** ~800+ lingering `node` / `cmd` / `codex` processes. Parent analysis: only ~3 were true orphans; ~835 still had live parents — piled up under 2 long-lived `codex app-server` instances (52–56h old), i.e. children accumulating under persistent app-servers rather than being cleaned up.

## Contrast: `codex exec` is clean
Running the equivalent work via `codex exec --ephemeral ... -` spawns the same MCP children during the run, but **all of them return to baseline on normal exit** (verified). So the runtime *can* tear them down — the persistent mcp-server/app-server path on Windows doesn't.

## Possibly related
`codex app-server daemon <...>` reports: `app-server daemon lifecycle is only supported on Unix platforms`. This suggests Windows app-server lifecycle management is less complete, which may be why child trees aren't reaped on Windows.

## Repro
1. On Windows, configure one or more stdio MCP servers in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
2. Drive Codex through `codex mcp-server` (e.g. via an MCP host) and issue several requests.
3. Watch `codex.exe`, `node.exe`, and the MCP server processes via Task Manager / `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` — they accumulate and never exit.

## Impact
Resource exhaustion (hundreds of processes / multiple GB) over long-lived sessions on Windows.

## Suggested direction
Reap each `app-server` and its child MCP process tree when the request/session ends (or on mcp-server shutdown), including a Windows tree-kill (e.g. `taskkill /pid <pid> /t /f`) since Windows does not cascade-terminate child processes on parent exit.

_(Searched existing issues for duplicates; didn't find an obvious match.)_

## Summary

After upgrading the Windows desktop app from 26.908.9136.0 to 26.1007.9446.0, the in-composer microphone/dictation button disappeared. Settings > Voice now says **"Dictation unavailable — Dictation is not available in your current configuration"** and offers no dictation shortcut setting. Dictation worked on this same PC and account before the upgrade; Settings > Voice still lists successful recordings from October 14, including one at 19:07 local time.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300, x64.
- Installed OpenAI.Codex package: 26.1007.9446.0; package status reports OK.
- Bundled codex-cli: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- ChatGPT sign-in in the desktop app.

## Reproduction and impact

1. Open an existing Codex chat in the updated desktop app.
2. The composer has no microphone/dictation button.
3. Open Settings > Voice. The Dictation section says it is unavailable in the current configuration; there is no dictation shortcut control.
4. Recent recordings on that same screen show that dictation worked before the upgrade.

This removes the user's regular input method across Codex chats. A Windows voice-typing shortcut is not a workable substitute on this PC.

## Checks already performed

- The current local `~/.codex/config.toml` does not set `in_app_dictation = false`.
- The bundled runtime's `codex features list` reports `in_app_dictation` as `stable true`.
- Windows microphone permission for the app is allowed, the microphone device is present, and Windows audio services are running.
- The earlier signed installer is retained, but no downgrade was performed after this finding; a downgrade has not been verified as a fix.

## Expected result

Keep in-app dictation available after updating for an account where it previously worked. If a capability or workspace setting legitimately disables it, show the specific reason and a recovery path instead of only "current configuration". Please investigate why the desktop UI reports dictation unavailable while the local runtime reports `in_app_dictation = true`.

Related but different: #46452 reports a missing global shortcut while in-app microphone dictation still works. Here the in-app microphone and the Voice settings controls are both missing.

No chat transcripts or audio recordings are attached publicly. Private diagnostic details can be supplied if requested.

26.901.51231

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

### Summary

Coordinate-based Computer Use mouse actions fail with:

Computer Use server error -10005: noWindowsAvailable

in Safari, Google Chrome, and Krita on macOS Tahoe 26.6.2.

However, the same coordinate click and drag operations succeed in TextEdit.

Accessibility-element based interactions can also work, so this does not appear to be a general Accessibility permission failure.

### Environment

- Codex Desktop: 26.901.51231
- Also reproduced on: 26.901.41123
- macOS: Tahoe 26.6.2
- Apple Silicon
- Single display
- No external display
- No clamshell mode
- No Stage Manager
- No intentionally configured multiple Spaces

Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions for Codex Computer Use are enabled.

### Reproduction

I tested coordinate operations only. Accessibility-element clicking was not used.

#### TextEdit

- Coordinate click: (150,150) -> succeeds
- Coordinate drag: (150,150) -> (210,150) -> succeeds
- No error

#### Safari

- Coordinate click: (500,350) -> fails
- Coordinate drag: (500,350) -> (560,350) -> fails

Both return:

Error: Computer Use server error -10005: noWindowsAvailable

#### Krita

- Coordinate click: (400,300) -> fails
- Coordinate drag: (400,300) -> (460,300) -> fails

Both return:

Error: Computer Use server error -10005: noWindowsAvailable

Google Chrome showed the same failure earlier as well.

### Troubleshooting already attempted

- Verified Screen Recording permission
- Verified Accessibility permission
- Disabled fullscreen
- Completely restarted Codex
- Tested multiple applications
- Updated Codex from 26.901.41123 to 26.901.51231

The behavior remained unchanged after the update.

### Expected behavior

Coordinate click and drag should work in Safari, Chrome, and Krita just as they do in TextEdit.

### Additional observation

Computer Use can see the affected applications and inspect/interact with UI elements, but coordinate-based mouse operations fail with noWindowsAvailable.

Because coordinate operations still work in TextEdit, this appears to be related to application/window targeting rather than the general mouse-input or Accessibility permission path.

Please let me know if any logs or diagnostics would help.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch Codex Desktop on macOS Tahoe 26.6.2.
2. Enable Computer Use with Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions.
3. Open TextEdit.
4. Perform a coordinate click at (150,150).
5. Perform a coordinate drag from (150,150) to (210,150).
6. Both operations succeed without error.
7. Open Safari.
8. Perform a coordinate click at (500,350).
9. Perform a coordinate drag from (500,350) to (560,350).
10. Both operations fail with:

Computer Use server error -10005: noWindowsAvailable

11. Open Krita.
12. Perform a coordinate click at (400,300).
13. Perform a coordinate drag from (400,300) to (460,300).
14. Both operations fail with the same error:

Computer Use server error -10005: noWindowsAvailable

Google Chrome also showed the same failure earlier.

Accessibility-element clicking was not used in these tests.

The issue reproduces on Codex Desktop 26.901.51231 and was also reproducible on 26.901.41123 before updating.

### What is the expected behavior?

Coordinate-based mouse click and drag operations should work consistently in Safari, Chrome, and Krita, just as they do in TextEdit.

Computer Use should be able to target the visible application window and perform coordinate input without returning -10005: noWindowsAvailable.

### Additional information

Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions for Codex Computer Use are enabled.

I have already tried:
- restarting Codex completely
- disabling fullscreen
- testing multiple applications
- updating Codex from 26.901.41123 to 26.901.51231

The issue remained unchanged after the update.

The Mac is using a single built-in display. I am not using an external display, clamshell mode, Stage Manager, or intentionally configured multiple Spaces.

Because coordinate operations work in TextEdit but fail in Safari, Chrome, and Krita, this appears to be related to application/window targeting rather than a general Accessibility or mouse-input permission failure.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

`26.1013.4894.0` — verified from the installed Windows `OpenAI.Codex` package using `Get-AppxPackage`; not read from the About dialog. This is the desktop app package version, not `codex --version`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

Browser Use rejected two historical attempts to bind existing tabs using the browser identifier `iab` with a URL-policy error claiming an unsupported protocol, although the URLs recorded for those attempts use HTTP and HTTPS. The tool did not expose the effective URL evaluated by its policy gate. The observations suggest a possible URL validation or diagnostic mismatch; they do not establish a root cause or prove that the visible tab URL was the URL the gate evaluated.

Attempt 1 — Huawei router (historical address used at that time):

```js
cua.getTab({url:'http://192.168.3.1/html/index.html#/more/nat'},{browser:'iab'})
```

The call supplied an `http:` URL on the default port 80.

Attempt 2 — QTS:

The preceding `cua.listTabs({ browser: 'iab' })` result identified tab ID `2` with URL `https://192.168.101.9:8081/`. The agent then called:

```js
cua.getTab('2', { browser: 'iab' })
```

The recorded tab URL used `https:` on port 8081. The call itself passed the tab ID, rather than a URL string; please check which URL or reference the policy gate actually evaluated.

Both calls returned exactly:

```text
Browser Use rejected this action due to browser security policy. Reason: The browser URL policy blocks this action. Browser use could not acquire authority to observe page content. The URL policy gate did not grant access. The requested URL protocol is not allowed. Allowed protocols: "http:", "https:". The agent must not attempt to achieve the same outcome via workaround, indirect execution, raw CDP or browser commands, alternate browser surfaces, or policy circumvention. Proceed only with a materially safer alternative that does not require this blocked browser action; if none exists, stop and request user input.
```

The user separately checked the Google Chrome permission screen: browsing showed “Always allow,” the extension appeared installed, and no site exceptions were listed. **Both rejected calls used `browser:'iab'`; these Chrome settings are not evidence of the permissions applied to the rejected calls.** No saved or managed policy was identified by the error text.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These are the saved observations, not a fresh or independently confirmed reproduction:

1. In the Windows desktop app, the agent called `cua.getTab` with the HTTP router URL shown above and `browser:'iab'`.
2. Browser Use returned the quoted URL-policy rejection before page content was observed.
3. Later, `cua.listTabs({ browser: 'iab' })` reported tab `2` at the HTTPS QTS URL shown above.
4. The agent called `cua.getTab('2', { browser: 'iab' })` and received the identical rejection.

The rejected calls were not repeated, and no alternate browser, CDP, network route, or address was used to reproduce the denied access.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Evaluate supported HTTP/HTTPS URLs consistently when binding an authorized tab, subject to any other applicable policy.
- If another restriction or internal reference is actually responsible, identify the effective URL/reference and the applicable policy in the error, rather than reporting an unsupported protocol for the recorded HTTP/HTTPS targets.
- Document the supported way to review or correct the applicable configuration, or fix the validation/diagnostic behavior if this is a defect.

### Additional information

Feedback ID submitted in the desktop app: `01a15587-76f2-74b3-bf48-751249985d6d`.

Possibly related, without asserting a common cause: #55471 reports a URL-protocol/frame-authority denial during a later Chrome interaction with an HTTPS page; #49230 reports a protocol denial involving an internal tab mention on Windows. This report concerns initial tab binding through `getTab` in `iab` and includes one direct HTTP URL call plus one tab-ID call with an observed HTTPS tab URL.

Please investigate the URL/reference effectively evaluated in each attempt, the specific policy that denied it, and the supported recovery procedure. Only this sanitized summary is published; no full logs, session files, credentials, cookies, or unrelated tab data are attached.

issues.title: Persistent incorrect “1” badge on ChatGPT/Codex macOS Dock icon

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
Title: Persistent incorrect “1” badge on ChatGPT/Codex macOS Dock icon

I am experiencing a persistent red badge displaying “1” on the ChatGPT/Codex application icon in the macOS Dock, even though the application shows no outstanding notifications, unread tasks, or items requiring attention.

This is operationally important to me because I rely on the Dock badge to indicate when ChatGPT/Codex has completed work or requires action. A badge that remains present without a corresponding alert makes that signal unreliable.

Observed behavior

The ChatGPT/Codex Dock icon continuously displays a red “1.” Inside the application:

- The notification panel says “Nothing needs attention.”
- I have opened and cleared every visible blue-dot indicator across my projects.
- I have reviewed the alerts panel.
- I cannot find an unread conversation, completed task, approval request, or other item corresponding to the badge.
- The application’s available task states do not show a hidden task requiring attention.

Troubleshooting completed

I have tried all of the following without resolving the badge:

1. Reviewed every project for blue-dot or unread indicators.
2. Opened and reviewed the application’s alerts panel.
3. Fully quit ChatGPT/Codex using Command-Q and reopened it.
4. Opened macOS System Settings → Notifications → ChatGPT.
5. Turned “Badge application icon” off, waited, and turned it back on.
6. Restarted the macOS Dock process.
7. Removed ChatGPT from the Dock.
8. Fully quit the application.
9. Reopened ChatGPT directly from the Applications folder.
10. Added the application back to the Dock.
11. Shut down the computer completely and turned it back on.

The red “1” returned or remained after all of these steps.

Diagnostic findings

The installed application is:

- Application path: `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`
- Bundle identifier: `com.openai.codex`

Only one main ChatGPT application instance and one Dock entry were identified, so this does not appear to be caused by duplicate installations or Dock shortcuts.

The available Codex task-state check found no task marked as needing attention. All inspected tasks were idle, completed, or not loaded, apart from the active troubleshooting conversation.

Recent macOS system logs for `com.openai.codex` reported zero delivered ChatGPT notifications. The logs showed the application adding and subsequently removing notification requests successfully. Nevertheless, the Dock badge remained present.

This suggests that the displayed “1” is not synchronized with:

- the application’s “Nothing needs attention” state;
- the visible project unread indicators;
- the list of active or completed tasks; or
- the notifications currently delivered through macOS Notification Center.

Expected behavior

The Dock badge should display the number of genuine unread or actionable ChatGPT/Codex items. When the application says “Nothing needs attention” and there are no delivered notifications, the Dock badge should clear automatically.

If the badge represents a different category of state, the application should identify the corresponding item and provide a way to open or clear it.

Actual behavior

The Dock continuously displays “1,” but neither ChatGPT/Codex nor macOS identifies any corresponding unread notification or actionable item. No available user-facing action clears the badge.

Impact

I use the Dock badge as an operational signal that something requires review or action. Because this false-positive badge cannot be cleared, I can no longer rely on it to distinguish new work from stale state. Ignoring the badge is not a workable solution because doing so could cause me to overlook a legitimate future notification.

Feedback already uploaded

Feedback ID:

`019fd1b5-aa8c-7b62-8f08-3361847114b7`

The feedback upload should contain the associated task details and diagnostic context. I am providing the ID here so maintainers can correlate this report with the uploaded information.

Requested resolution

Please investigate why the ChatGPT/Codex macOS application is maintaining or restoring a Dock badge count of “1” when both the in-app attention list and macOS delivered-notification count are zero.

I would also appreciate confirmation of:

1. What underlying state currently controls the Dock badge.
2. Whether there is an undocumented way to identify and clear that state.
3. Whether this is related to the ChatGPT application using the `com.openai.codex` bundle identifier.
4. Whether a fix or reliable non-destructive workaround is available.

[Screenshot of problem.docx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30760786/Screenshot.of.problem.docx)

issues.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex Desktop App

### What feature would you like to see?

### Summary

I would love to see **ChatGPT-style Intelligent UI integrated natively into regular Codex Desktop conversations**, allowing Codex to automatically generate interactive visual explanations when appropriate.

The goal is to bring the rich, context-aware visual response experience of ChatGPT to everyday Codex conversations.

### Problem / Motivation

The new Intelligent UI experience in ChatGPT makes technical explanations significantly easier to understand through interactive diagrams, charts, controls, and visual layouts.

Codex is particularly well suited to this capability because users frequently discuss code, algorithms, system architecture, embedded systems, and complex technical concepts.

Although Codex already has some visualization capabilities through Visualize and MCP Apps, I would like this experience to become a seamless, reliable part of ordinary assistant responses.

Ideally, users should not need to explicitly invoke a specialized tool, generate a standalone HTML file, or switch to a separate viewer just to understand a technical explanation visually.

### Proposed Solution

I would like Codex Desktop to support:

1. **Automatic visual responses:** Codex should intelligently decide when a diagram, chart, or interactive component would improve an explanation, without requiring explicit instructions.
2. **Native inline rendering:** Interactive visualizations should appear directly within the assistant's response, alongside explanatory text.
3. **Interactive components:** Support diagrams, animations, charts, sliders, buttons, and other useful controls when appropriate.
4. **Conversational continuity:** Codex should be able to understand user interactions with these components and use them as context for follow-up responses.
5. **Consistent availability:** The experience should work reliably in regular Codex Desktop conversations, rather than depending on manual visualization workflows.

Simple questions should continue to receive simple text answers. Visualization should be used when it genuinely improves clarity.



### Expected Outcome

**Codex should offer the same kind of intelligent, native, interactive visual explanations that ChatGPT now provides, directly within normal conversations.**

This request is about the overall conversational experience, not simply adding another diagram-generation tool.

Thank you for considering this feature!

### Additional information

### Environment

- Product: Codex Desktop App
- Platform: Windows 10
- Request type: Feature enhancement / UX improvement

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51817 — Request to make Intelligent UI available in Dot conversations.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36660 — Proposal for inline visualization rendering in the Codex TUI.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33164 — Existing Visualize skill behavior and invocation issues.

### Scope Clarification

I understand that Codex already has some visualization capabilities.

This request is specifically about making **ChatGPT-style Intelligent UI a first-class, automatically available experience in regular Codex Desktop assistant responses**.

The desired behavior is broader than manually invoking Visualize, rendering a Mermaid diagram, or opening an MCP App canvas.

Ideally, the experience should feel as natural and integrated as it does in ChatGPT.

- Changing reasoning effort does not resolve the problem.
- Starting a fresh conversation does not resolve the problem.
- The account still has substantial available usage quota.
- The issue occurs intermittently rather than as a permanent access failure, making Codex unreliable for regular development work.

issues.title: Codex App: read_thread cannot select metadata-only or fail-closed existing-transport reads

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: app-server

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From ‘About Codex’ dialog)?

Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.9446.0`; bundled `codex-app-tools` plugin manifest: `0.1.6`. These are package/manifest observations, not a claimed About-dialog reading or a verified remote app-server version.

### What subscription do you have?

Not disclosed in this public report; the exact subscription tier was not verified as relevant to this reproduction.

### What platform is your computer?

`Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64`

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop `codex_app/read_thread` tool has no published selector for metadata-only reads, separate bounded history selection, or a fail-closed read using only an already-ready connection to the exact requested host. `includeOutputs: false` suppresses output presentation; it does not suppress the history read.

A previously observed attempt to read an existing paginated remote conversation returned:

```text
paginated_threads is not supported yet
```

The remote version, the current cause of that response, and the current live transport state are not established here. The report does not assert data loss or that this error has only one cause.

The problem is that the public read tool offers no way to request the documented summary-only operation or to express a no-start/no-reconnect requirement when merely inspecting existing work. A read-only workflow cannot safely infer these transport guarantees from a tool name or from a frontend connected-client check.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Inspect the published `read_thread` input schema in the affected app build. It exposes `threadId`, `hostId`, `cursor`, `turnLimit` (1–10), `includeOutputs`, and `maxOutputCharsPerItem`, but no metadata-only or existing-ready-transport selector. Do not send unsupported extra arguments to a real host.
2. Inspect the locally installed public bridge and query handler, without importing or executing their whole modules. The bridge obtains its tool catalog through `tools/list` and forwards calls to the app through `tools/call`; it is not an independent stored-history implementation.
3. An offline test isolated the actual bridge `listTools` function, its tool-call callback, and the actual app `dp` read handler, with a fake catalog/client and a deliberately permissive schema dependency. This fixture was entirely synthetic:

```json
{
  "threadId": "synthetic-thread-not-a-real-request",
  "hostId": "synthetic-existing-host",
  "turnLimit": 1,
  "includeOutputs": false,
  "maxOutputCharsPerItem": 20,
  "includeTurns": false,
  "existingReadyOnly": true,
  "strictHost": true
}
```

The last three fields are proposed controls, NOT currently supported public tool arguments. The permissive schema stub tests the stronger counterfactual: even if a bridge accepted them, the current app handler still does not pass them into the downstream read function. It is not a test of real Zod input validation.

4. In that isolated execution, the bridge forwards the fixture unchanged, but the actual `dp` handler constructs downstream arguments without those three controls. The downstream `rp` implementation defaults to `includeTurns = true`. The negative assertion requiring a selectable safe route fails (native exit 3); the diagnostic assertion confirming the observed blocked chain passes (native exit 0). This is not a fixed implementation or an end-to-end live reproduction.
5. Separately, static inspection of the request-dispatch/readiness path shows conditional readiness/start/reconnect behavior. A frontend-only flag would therefore be insufficient without enforcement through the actual dispatch path, including races and queued/coalesced requests. No remote startup or reconnect was executed to test this.

Source identities for correlating this offline observation:

- `server.mjs`: SHA256 `064893183a9cc09953a1f69ed82dfb4299b4f7e1653a3507259deeb5abbb9617`, symbols `listTools` and the `CallToolRequestSchema` handler.
- `webview/assets/execution-3f23be00c542.js`: SHA256 `cfbfc9d7c7f1b790463524f8fe73a048629e2c9b428b3c2eb93a9e00a8461806`, symbols `Pp`, `dp`, `rp`, `ep`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Please expose a supported metadata-only mode separately from bounded turn/item history, consistent with the documented `thread/read` summary and `thread/turns/list` / `thread/items/list` operations.

For observation-only workflows, please provide a strict exact-host, already-ready-transport-only contract that fails closed if the selected connection is unavailable or changes. It should not fall back to another host, resume a thread, start/install/reconnect a server, or silently broaden a read. Enforce this at dispatch as well as schema/UI level.

If the selected server does not support the required history capability, return a specific capability error without attempting a broader operation. A supported official app build or documented provider extension mechanism is preferable to modifying a protected installed package.

### Additional information

- Related error reports: #44981 and #40796. They concern resume/version-selection failures; this report focuses on the missing selectable read-only app-tool contract and its bridge-to-handler boundary. It does not adopt their diagnoses as the cause here.
- Official API reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server (stored thread reads without resuming; paginated turns/items). This documents app-server operations, not a promise that the current desktop tool exposes them.
- The offline source test and interpretation received an independent review. Only isolated callbacks with dependency stubs were executed; no full application bundle, real pipe/client, or remote request was run by that test. The test does not prove the currently loaded provider, all alternative paths, OS sandboxing, or actual history recovery.
- No protected app files, permissions, trust settings, services, or remote runtime were changed. No vulnerability exploit or unauthorized startup is alleged.
- No session/thread/request identifiers, hostnames, project names, personal filesystem paths, raw transcripts, logs, screenshots, credentials, or operational data are included or attached.

issues.title: ChatGPT Long-Response Truncation — Client-Side Investigation Report

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

issues.body:
----------------------------------------------------------------------
0. SUMMARY
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Since 2026-10-16 21:44 (CST), this account has repeatedly experienced
SILENT MID-GENERATION STOPS on LONGER CHINESE RESPONSES:

- Output ends abruptly in the middle-to-late part of the response, while
  the UI presents it as a NORMALLY COMPLETED turn - no network error, no
  quota error, no notification of any kind.

- Regenerate / continue controls appear immediately after the truncated
  content.

- BLANK assistant responses were also observed in the same conversation.

- Reproduced on THREE DIFFERENT CLIENTS: macOS native app (ChatGPT
  Classic 1.2026.184), macOS browser (web), and iOS app.

- Reproduced after changing proxies, across two egress paths of entirely
  different character.

CONCLUSION: The local environment (client installation, proxy software,
proxy node, egress IP, OS network stack) has been eliminated variable by
variable through controlled tests. The fault lies on the ChatGPT product
side - either the server ended the stream early, or the client
mishandles an interrupted/empty stream.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
1. REPRODUCIBLE ENVIRONMENT AND METHOD
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  Client ............... ChatGPT Classic 1.2026.184
                         (build 1784145287, bundle com.openai.chat)
  OS ................... macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Mac17,2
  Model ................ conversation modelSlug = gpt-6
                         (macOS-side config: gpt-6-pro / gpt-6-thinking: max)
  Proxy ................ ClashX 1.72.0
                         HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS all pointed at 127.0.0.1:7890
                         mode = global
  Direct connectivity .. NOT AVAILABLE
                         curl --noproxy '*' https://chatgpt.com/
                         times out after 12.004 s
                         A "bypass the proxy and connect directly" test
                         path therefore does not exist on this network.
  Method ............... Read-only throughout:
                         - ClashX control API /connections
                           (upload/download byte sampling every 2 s)
                         - ClashX logs
                         - lsof / netstat socket ownership
                         - unified log
                         - crash reports
                         - Sentry session state
                         - egress IP probes


----------------------------------------------------------------------
2. CONFIRMED FACTS (WITH EVIDENCE)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 REPRODUCED ON THREE CLIENTS
    => a single client implementation is excluded

  - ChatGPT Classic ... Mac / ClashX -> Tokyo datacenter IP ...... Failed
  - Web (browser) ..... Mac / ClashX -> Tokyo datacenter IP ...... Failed
  - ChatGPT Classic ... Mac / ClashX -> Taichung residential IP .. Failed
  - Web (browser) ..... Mac / ClashX -> Taichung residential IP .. Failed
  - ChatGPT iOS ....... Phone / phone's own independent proxy .... Failed


2.2 REPRODUCED AFTER CHANGING EGRESS
    => a targeted block of the egress IP is excluded

  The egress changed SUBSTANTIVELY during the fault window (recorded
  automatically every 60 s via the control API):

  Before switch (22:25-22:35):
      Egress IP ..... 185.200.65.144
      Attribution ... Tokyo, AS3258 xTom (DATACENTER IP)

  After switch (from 22:36):
      Egress IP ..... 114.26.119.124
      Attribution ... Taichung, AS3462 HiNet (RESIDENTIAL IP)

  Country, ASN and IP type all changed; the fault persisted.


2.3 NO ANOMALIES AT THE TRANSPORT LAYER

  - ClashX proxy log: warning/error count = 0 since 22:05
    (no dial failures, no resets, no EOFs).

  - TCP connect and TLS are normal: https://chatgpt.com/ through the
    proxy x3 - TLS handshake 0.30-0.34 s, TTFB 0.41-0.44 s.

  - Long-lived connection capacity tested and normal (two independent
    tests, neither against an OpenAI endpoint):
      * SSE at a 5 KB/s rate limit: survived a full 180 s (618 events),
        not cut by the proxy.
      * SSE 20 s test on the same node: 659 events / 984 KB, survived
        in full.

  - A SINGLE CONNECTION THAT WENT SILENT LATER RESUMED RECEIVING DATA:
    one connection established at 21:44:40 had its download freeze at
    82 KB for >= 20 s, and then received a further ~+115 KB on the SAME
    socket. This shows that TCP path had NOT become half-open / silently
    dead - i.e. "the link broke" does not hold.

  - Mechanistically: for HTTPS, Clash is a CONNECT TUNNEL; it does not
    parse, and cannot selectively truncate, an HTTP/2 response body.


2.4 NO ERROR RECORDS ON THE CLIENT SIDE

  - UNIFIED LOG IS EMPTY:
    log show --last 90m --info --predicate 'process == "ChatGPT Classic"'
    returns HEADER ONLY, 0 entries.
    The app writes no system log, so no client-side streaming error
    record exists.

  - NO CRASHES:
    Sentry session.current = {"status":"ok","errors":0}
    CrashState.json has crashedLastLaunch = false
    No .ips crash/hang report within the fault window.

  - NO HOST-LEVEL RESOURCE OR TUNNEL INTERFERENCE:
    systemextensionsctl list = 0 system extensions
    utun interfaces exist but the DEFAULT ROUTE IS VIA en0
    (192.168.31.1) - no tunnel carries this traffic.


2.5 THE STOPPING POINT IS NOT A FIXED LENGTH

  Conversation snapshot increments (approximating the body of each turn)
  across interruptions were:

      +14,937 B   /   +13,331 B   /   +1,413 B

  NOT clustered around any fixed value, which does not support "cut off
  precisely at a fixed output-length threshold".


----------------------------------------------------------------------
3. EVIDENCE NOT OBTAINABLE CLIENT-SIDE (EXPLICIT STATEMENT)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

The following was NOT obtained in this investigation. ROOT CAUSE SHOULD
NOT BE INFERRED FROM CLIENT-VISIBLE SYMPTOMS ALONE:

  - Raw SSE / streaming response frames
      Why: TLS 1.3 encrypted; no keys on the host; no MITM decryption
      performed.

  - finish_reason / termination reason
      Why: same as above, AND the client writes no logs whatsoever.

  - Token usage
      Why: same; not exposed by the app.

  - Precise per-request duration and cumulative output
      Why: the proxy can only see TCP byte counters; under HTTP/2
      multiplexing a byte range cannot be attributed to one particular
      response.

  - Whether the server's STORED reply is complete
      Why: the local conversation store is an ENCRYPTED BINARY;
      decryption was not attempted.

  - Whether the proxy "dropped frames"
      Why: structurally undecidable - for encrypted traffic, the relay's
      byte counters and the end-to-end content cannot be compared.

THEREFORE: whether the upstream completed voluntarily, ran out of output
budget, errored, or the client lost rendered data CANNOT BE DISTINGUISHED
FROM THE CLIENT SIDE.


----------------------------------------------------------------------
4. EXISTING REPORTS OF THE SAME ISSUE (FOR CROSS-REFERENCING)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  openai/codex issue #47826
  "Codex Desktop for macOS truncates long ChatGPT responses/writing
   blocks mid-stream"
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47826
  Filed 2026-09-24, STILL OPEN, labels: bug / app / connectivity
  Overlap: verbatim - "Rendering silently stops partway... The normal
  response controls appear immediately below the incomplete content,
  making the truncated response look as though it completed normally";
  also records that the STOPPING POINT DIFFERS BETWEEN ATTEMPTS, and
  that the server generated substantially more content than the client
  displayed.

  openai/codex issue #51543
  "ChatGPT iOS Work Mode: interrupted responses remain blank or show
   only 'Working'"
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51543
  Filed 2026-10-07, STILL OPEN, labels: bug / iOS / connectivity
  Overlap: corresponds to the BLANK RESPONSES seen here; likewise no
  explicit error and an indeterminate state after interruption.

  OpenAI status page - recent incidents of the same family (all resolved)
  https://status.openai.com/
      10-05  Elevated errors in ChatGPT conversations
      10-05  Elevated Work Mode errors
      10-07  Workspace Agents Degraded - "users may not see the responses"
      10-08  "Some APAC users are seeing errors in ChatGPT Work,
              conversations, and GPTs"
      10-13  Degraded performance in GPT-6.1 Sol Codex and Work mode
      10-14  Degraded performance in Codex and ChatGPT Work
      10-15  Widespread feature degradation


----------------------------------------------------------------------
5. QUESTIONS WE WOULD LIKE OPENAI TO ANSWER
----------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. Within this time window, are there server-side records of this
     account's requests being ENDED EARLY BY THE SERVER? What was the
     termination reason?

  2. Are there limits tied to CUMULATIVE OUTPUT TOKENS or REQUEST
     EXECUTION TIME (per-request output budget, generation length cap,
     execution time cap)?

  3. Is the STORED reply on the server complete? If it is, does this
     indicate the client lost streaming data?

  4. Is presenting an "abnormal termination" as a "normal completion"
     (no error shown, regenerate control displayed immediately) a known
     defect? Is there a fixed version?

  5. Is this the same root cause as open issues #47826 / #51543?
