issues.body:
### Description

Custom OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible providers configured in the Copilot App fail every inference request with `Authorization error, you may need to run /login`. The session records status 403, but the failed inference request never reaches the configured provider. `/login` is misleading for a BYOK provider with a valid API key.

### Environment

- Copilot App / CLI binary: `1.0.79-5`
- OS: Windows 11, ARM64
- Custom provider: self-hosted HTTPS endpoint behind Cloudflare
- Tested: Anthropic `/v1/messages` and OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` with `completions` wire API

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a custom Anthropic provider with a valid base URL, API key, and model.
2. Select the model and send a prompt.
3. Observe the 403 `/login` error.
4. Repeat with an OpenAI provider using a `/v1` base URL and `completions` wire API.
5. Observe the same failure.

### Expected behavior

The app sends the request to the BYOK endpoint using the stored API key.

### Actual behavior

The app reports a 403 authorization error before the request reaches the provider origin.

### Diagnostics performed

- Direct authenticated `GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/messages`, and `POST /v1/chat/completions` requests succeed with HTTP 200.
- Both affected model IDs return successful responses when called directly.
- The app successfully calls `GET /v1/models` with the same configuration.
- Windows Credential Manager contains the credential for the active provider UUID; it was compared locally and exactly matches the configured key without logging its value.
- An explicit static `Authorization: Bearer ...` header does not help.
- Recreating the provider, restarting the app, and using a fresh session do not help.
- Origin logs show model discovery but no inference POST at the timestamp of the app-generated 403.
- Equivalent large, streaming, tool-bearing requests outside the app reach the provider successfully.

### Relevant logs

```
Using custom provider: type=anthropic, baseUrl=https://<provider-host>, wireApi=completions
Using custom provider: type=openai, baseUrl=https://<provider-host>/v1, wireApi=completions
```

```json
{"type":"session.error","data":{"errorType":"authorization","message":"Authorization error, you may need to run /login","statusCode":403}}
```

No credentials or private endpoint details are included.

issues.title: Interactive autopilot stops after 600s while a background subagent is still running (regression in 1.0.102)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since 1.0.102, interactive autopilot stops whenever a background subagent runs for more than 600 seconds. The subagent is still working normally when this happens. The CLI shows:

> Autopilot stopped after 600s waiting for background tasks. Set COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to change the limit.

A common pattern is for the main agent to start a background agent (for example, to implement part of a feature) and then end its turn to wait for the result. Any subagent that needs more than 10 minutes now ends the autopilot run, and I have to continue it manually.

This worked in 1.0.101 and 1.0.100. The 1.0.102 changelog doesn't mention any change to this behavior, so it looks unintended.

### Affected version

1.0.102

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start Copilot CLI interactively and turn on autopilot (`/autopilot` or shift+tab).
2. Give it a task where the main agent starts a background subagent (`task` with `mode: "background"`) that takes more than 10 minutes.
3. Let the main agent end its turn to wait for the subagent.
4. After 600 seconds, autopilot stops with the message above, even though the subagent is still running.

### Expected behavior

Interactive autopilot keeps waiting for in-flight background agents and continues when they finish, as it did in 1.0.101. If a cap is needed, a running subagent that is making progress shouldn't count as stuck, or the cap should be opt-in for interactive sessions.

### Additional context

- In 1.0.101, `COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` / `autopilot_background_timeout` appear to apply only to prompt mode (`-p`). In 1.0.102 the native runtime adds new autopilot continuation logic, and the stop message and `autopilot_background_timeout` warning first appear there.
- Workaround: `export COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600` (or higher) before launching.
- The limit can't be turned off. `COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0` gives a 0 ms wait, not an unlimited one. Negative or non-numeric values fall back to 600 s.
- Related but different: #4628 (prompt mode on 1.0.80, closed).

issues.title: ACP: the autopilot task_complete summary is sent only as a tool call, not as an agent message

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp --stdio`), when an autopilot turn ends with the `task_complete` tool, the final answer of the turn reaches the client only as a `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` with `kind: "other"`. No `agent_message_chunk` carries the summary. Then `session/prompt` returns `stopReason: "end_turn"`.

Per ACP, `agent_message_chunk` is the response of the agent, and `tool_call` reports the execution of a tool ([prompt turn](https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/prompt-turn)). So ACP clients show the answer as a collapsed tool call, and the user must expand it to read the result. JetBrains Air (IntelliJ IDEA) is affected.

The Copilot TUI renders the `task_complete` summary as the final markdown answer (changelog 1.0.6). The ACP server does not. `task_complete` is an internal control tool of autopilot, so a client has no generic way to know that this tool call is the answer.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.96 (`agentInfo.version` "1.0.96"), started as `copilot --acp --stdio`. The same binary ships in `@github/copilot-language-server` 1.554.0 (`@github/copilot-win32-x64`). Windows 11, x64.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot --acp --stdio` and send `initialize`, then `session/new`.
2. Switch the session to autopilot: `session/set_config_option` with `configId: "mode"` and value `https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/session-modes#autopilot`.
3. Send `session/prompt` with the text `Create a file hello.txt with the text "hello", then finish the task.`

The `session/update` notifications of that turn, in order:

```
config_option_update
config_option_update
session_info_update
usage_update
tool_call            "Creating ...\hello.txt"   pending
agent_message_chunk  "Info: ...\hello.txt"
tool_call_update     completed
usage_update
tool_call            "task_complete"            pending
tool_call_update     completed
```

The `task_complete` notifications:

```json
{"sessionUpdate":"tool_call","toolCallId":"toolu_014obvFRV78u2US8vcmwXq8p","title":"task_complete","kind":"other","status":"pending","rawInput":{"summary":"Created hello.txt containing \"hello\"."}}
{"sessionUpdate":"tool_call_update","toolCallId":"toolu_014obvFRV78u2US8vcmwXq8p","status":"completed","content":[{"type":"content","content":{"type":"text","text":"Created hello.txt containing \"hello\"."}}],"rawOutput":{"content":"Created hello.txt containing \"hello\".","detailedContent":"✓ Task completed: Created hello.txt containing \"hello\"."}}
```

Then `session/prompt` returns `{"stopReason":"end_turn", ...}`. The only `agent_message_chunk` of the turn is the `Info:` line of the file tool.

### Expected behavior

The ACP server sends the `task_complete` summary as an `agent_message_chunk`, as the TUI renders it. It can also keep the tool call, or not expose `task_complete` as a client-visible tool call at all.

### Additional context

The same class of output loss is reported for other channels: #2482 (`-p` output) and #1324 (subagent result).

issues.title: Startup reports disabled MCP servers as “blocked by policy” and repeats the warnings
issues.body:
### Description

Copilot CLI displays organization-policy warnings at startup even though every configured third-party MCP server is explicitly disabled through `disabledMcpServers` in the user settings. The same pair of warnings appears twice during startup.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI: **1.0.101**
- OS: **Windows**
- Shell: **PowerShell**
- MCP configuration includes user-configured and plugin-provided servers.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have third-party MCP servers configured.
2. Disable all of them through the CLI, persisting their names in `disabledMcpServers`.
3. Start a new interactive CLI session with an account for which the CLI reports that third-party MCP servers are disallowed by organization policy.
4. Observe the startup warnings.

### Actual behavior

Startup displays:

```text
Third-party MCP servers are disabled by your organization's Copilot policy. Only built-in servers are available.

9 MCP servers were blocked by policy: ...
```

Both messages appear twice in the observed startup. Every server named in the warning is already explicitly disabled in the user settings.

### Expected behavior

- Already-disabled servers should not be counted as servers blocked by policy at startup.
- An unchanged policy notice should not be repeated during startup refreshes.
- If a general policy notice is intentional, it should be clearly informational and distinguish organization restrictions from user-disabled servers.

### Investigation notes

Read-only inspection of the locally installed **1.0.101** bundle found:

- In `cli-main.js`, `reloadMcpServersExclusive()` passes the configured server map to the policy filter without disabled-server settings. Disable settings are handed to the native lifecycle afterward.
- The interactive initialization path emits the general policy warning based on policy allowance, without checking whether any third-party servers are enabled.
- The general and filtered-server warnings have no deduplication at these emission points, allowing repeated initialization/reload calls to emit them again.

These observations explain the reporting behavior; **they do not establish that disabled servers are launched**. The exact trigger for the second initialization/reload has not been identified.

### Related issues

- github/copilot-cli#2567 - incorrect startup "blocked by policy" reporting in a different configuration scenario.
- github/copilot-cli#4907 - repeated MCP lifecycle notifications.

issues.title: Windows: with --sandbox, shell commands can't list or stat directories when the working directory is on a non-system drive

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, when Copilot CLI's command sandbox is enabled and the working directory is on a drive other than the system drive (for example `D:\`), sandboxed shell commands cannot list, stat or change into directories on that drive. `Get-ChildItem`, `Test-Path`, `cmd /c dir` and git repository discovery fail with **Access is denied**, and the shell does not start in the working directory: `Get-Location` reports `C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0`.

Reading a file by its full path still works, and so does .NET `[IO.Directory]::GetFiles`. The same commands work when the working directory is on `C:\`, and everything works on `D:\` without `--sandbox`.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Enterprise 26H1, OS build 28000 (x64)
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.101-0 (installed with WinGet)
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 as the sandboxed shell
- Volumes that reproduce it:
  - `D:` NTFS, fixed disk;
  - `E:` ReFS Dev Drive (trusted);
  - a freshly created 2 GB NTFS VHDX mounted as `T:`.
- Works: `C:` (NTFS, system drive).
- No sandbox settings beyond `--sandbox`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a test folder on a non-system drive:

   ```powershell
   New-Item -ItemType Directory D:\sandbox-probe | Out-Null
   Set-Content D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt 'hello'
   cd D:\sandbox-probe
   ```

2. Run the CLI with the sandbox enabled and ask it to run this probe:

   ```powershell
   copilot --sandbox --allow-all --no-ask-user -s -p @'
   Run exactly this PowerShell, once, then print its raw output verbatim:
   $w = 'D:\sandbox-probe'
   "location=$((Get-Location).ProviderPath)"
   try { (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $w -ErrorAction Stop).Name } catch { "Get-ChildItem: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   try { Test-Path -LiteralPath $w -ErrorAction Stop } catch { "Test-Path: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   cmd /c "dir /b D:\sandbox-probe"
   try { [IO.File]::ReadAllText('D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt') } catch { "ReadAllText: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   try { [IO.Directory]::GetFiles($w) } catch { "GetFiles: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
   '@
   ```

3. Run the same command **without** `--sandbox` as a control.
4. Optionally, repeat steps 1–3 with a folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp` on `C:` (adjust `$w`).

(`Set-Location` is left out of the probe because in `-p` mode it triggers a CLI approval prompt, which is unrelated to the sandbox. In our runs through the Copilot SDK with the same sandbox, `Set-Location D:\sandbox-probe` also fails with Access is denied.)

## Expected

The sandboxed shell starts in the working directory and can list and stat it, as it does on `C:`. `copilot help sandbox` says sandboxed commands can access the allowed paths, and the working directory is allowed by default. The sandbox's PowerShell setup is meant to make the working directory's drive enumerable when it isn't the system drive.

## Actual

With `--sandbox`, working directory `D:\sandbox-probe`:

```text
location=C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0
Get-ChildItem: Access is denied
False
Test-Path: Access is denied
Access is denied.
hello

D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt
```

Without `--sandbox` (control), same folder:

```text
location=D:\sandbox-probe
existing.txt
True
existing.txt
hello

D:\sandbox-probe\existing.txt
```

With `--sandbox`, working directory on `C:`: every probe succeeds, and `location` is the working directory.

Summary across volumes (sandbox on):

| Working directory | Get-ChildItem | Test-Path | cmd dir | git status | Read by full path | .NET GetFiles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C: NTFS (system) | OK | True | OK | OK | OK | OK |
| D: NTFS | Access denied | Access denied | Access denied | "not a git repository" | OK | OK |
| E: ReFS Dev Drive | Access denied | Access denied | Access denied | "not a git repository" | OK | OK |
| T: new NTFS VHDX | Access denied | Access denied | Access denied | "not a git repository" | OK | OK |

## Diagnostics

- **Engagement:** the sandbox reports itself as engaged (`process_container` backend), and host support reports filesystem enumeration as supported.
- **Policy:** the effective sandbox policy includes an enumeration grant for both the system drive and the working directory's drive (for D:, the roots `C:\` and `D:\`), and the working directory is in the read-write paths.
- **Not drive-specific:** a freshly created NTFS VHDX fails the same way, so this isn't about one drive's history or permissions. Dev Drive filter policy isn't the cause either, since plain NTFS volumes fail too.
- **ACLs:** the volume roots have ordinary default ACLs. One difference: the `C:\` root carries an extra capability ACE (`S-1-15-3-65536-…`) that the other roots lack. Copying that ACE to `D:\` did not fix it (since reverted).
- **Filters:** `fltmc instances` shows `bindflt` attached to `C:` only, and `bfs` attached to `C:` and `D:`. Attaching `bindflt` to `D:` did not fix it (since reverted).
- **Process Monitor:** a trace of a failing run showed no ACCESS DENIED result on the test folder. The denial may happen at a layer Process Monitor doesn't observe, such as the sandbox's own brokering. Raw traces are available on request.
- **Partial enumeration:** .NET `Directory.GetFiles` succeeds where `Get-ChildItem` and `cmd dir` fail. So enumeration is not blocked outright; some directory-open or metadata queries are denied while others succeed.

## Workarounds tried

- Working directory on `C:`: works.
- Adding the `C:\` root's capability ACE to `D:\` and `E:\`: no change (reverted).
- Attaching `bindflt` to `D:`: no change (reverted).

## Impact

On machines where repos live on a data drive or a Dev Drive (which Windows recommends for development), turning on the sandbox makes the working directory unusable for ordinary shell commands and git, even though the CLI reports the sandbox as engaged. The failure looks like the agent "can't see the repo", not like a sandbox restriction, so it's hard to diagnose.

## Suspected component

The Windows `process_container` sandbox (MXC): the drive-root enumeration grant for a non-system working-directory drive appears not to take effect, or to cover only some directory operations. We have not confirmed the exact denied operation.

issues.title: Option for 1-hour prompt cache TTL for Claude models (5-minute cache expires during normal interactive use)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Claude prompt caching in Copilot CLI appears to use Anthropic's default **5-minute** cache TTL. In normal interactive use (read the answer, think, write the next prompt) gaps of more than 5 minutes are common, so the full conversation gets re-written to cache on almost every turn instead of being read from cache.

I measured this with `copilot -p` / `--resume` in fresh sessions (~35k-token context), sending a follow-up after different idle gaps, and reading `cache_read_tokens` / `cache_write_tokens` from the local session usage data. Two independent runs gave identical results:

| Idle gap | Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 | GPT-6.1-sol / GPT-6-sol / GPT-5.6-sol |
|---|---|---|
| 2 min | ~95% cache read | ~95% cache read |
| 11 min | **0% cache read** (~100% cache write) | ~95% cache read |
| ~85 min | 0% | 0% |

My broader session history (Claude 5.x, CLI) shows the same pattern: 98% cache read for gaps < 4 min vs ~1% for gaps of 6–60 min.

Anthropic supports a 1-hour TTL (`cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}`). VS Code Copilot Chat already has experimental settings for this (`github.copilot.chat.anthropic.promptCaching.extendedTtl` / `extendedTtlMessages`), though they currently miss Claude 5.x models (microsoft/vscode#340830, fix in microsoft/vscode#340831). Copilot CLI has no equivalent option.

### Proposed solution

Add an option in Copilot CLI (config setting and/or env var) to use the 1-hour cache TTL for Claude models, covering the Claude 5.x family. Consider making it the default for interactive sessions, since the higher write cost (2x vs 1.25x) is usually recovered after one or two follow-up turns with a pause longer than 5 minutes.

### Example prompts or workflows

Any interactive session with a large context where the user pauses longer than 5 minutes between prompts (reviewing diffs, testing changes, meetings).

### Additional context

- Related: #3808 (prompt caching for Claude), #4724 (auto-compact on idle aligned to cache TTL)
- Triggered by this discussion: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1xauf3s/anthropic_caching_is_this_a_bad_joke/
- Tested with Copilot CLI 1.0.102-1 on Windows.

issues.title: Session wedged: task subagent with unknown model id falls back to 128k default caps and fails the whole turn with 'Request exceeds the model's prompt budget'
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In a long-running interactive session, the session gets stuck. On every turn where the main agent delegates to a `task` subagent, the whole turn fails with a prompt-budget error. The main context is far below its own limit. The cause appears to be a `task` call with a `model` id that isn't in the catalog. The runtime doesn't reject it. Instead it quietly falls back to default capabilities (128k), and the request then goes over that limit.

**What we saw (from local process logs and session events):**

1. The main agent model is `claude-opus-5.5`, picked in the model picker, with `contextTier` long_context (1M context, `maxPromptTokens` 968000). The main context is about 177k tokens, well within budget. Auto-compaction is measured against the long-context limit (earlier compactions logged `tokenLimit` 922000), so compaction never triggers.
2. The main model's response contains a `task` tool call (usage record `toolCounts {"task":1}`, and `{"task":2}` on the retry). Both responses also had `finishReason: "content_filter"` / `contentFilterTriggered: true`. That may or may not be related, but it looks suspicious.
3. Right after that, the process log shows this warning twice per turn:
   ```
   [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::native_message_turn] turn model is in neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog, nor the session's excluded-model capture; falling back to default capabilities and the chat-completions wire {"model":"claude-opus-4.8","latest_model_list_fetch_succeeded":true,"picker_models":23,"unfiltered_models":39,"catalog_only_models":6}
   ```
   So the subagent was requested with a model id (`claude-opus-4.8`) that isn't in the catalog. The `task` tool's own `model` enum doesn't list it either, but tool-argument validation didn't reject it.
4. Then a session-level error ends the user's turn:
   ```
   session.error {"errorType":"query","message":"Execution failed: Request exceeds the model's prompt budget after reserving output (143299 tokens; limit 128000). Reduce context or compact before continuing."}
   ```
   No `subagent.started` event is emitted. When the user prompts again, it fails the same way (143360 / 128000).
5. **Result:** the session is stuck. Every turn where the model delegates fails. The error tells the user to compact, but the main context is nowhere near its own limit. `/compact` doesn't fix the real cause, so the advice is misleading.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI 1.0.100, macOS arm64

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start an interactive session on a long-context model (for example `claude-opus-5.5` with the long_context tier).
2. Build up a moderately large context (about 140k+ tokens), still well under the main model's limit.
3. Have the main agent call the `task` tool with a `model` value that isn't a valid catalog id (seen here: `claude-opus-4.8`).
4. The turn fails with `Request exceeds the model's prompt budget after reserving output (~143k tokens; limit 128000)`, and the warning above appears in the log. Every later turn that delegates fails the same way.

### Expected behavior

- An unknown `model` value on the `task` tool is rejected at argument validation and returned to the model as a tool error, so it can retry with a valid id. It should not be silently mapped to default 128k capabilities.
- If a subagent request goes over its model's budget, that shows up as a failure of that one `task` tool call, not as a fatal session/turn error.
- The error message says which request and model hit the limit (subagent vs. main), so users aren't told to compact the wrong context.
- It would also help to know why the subagent prompt reaches about 143k tokens. Does a subagent inherit or fork the parent context?

### Additional context

Workaround: start a new session, or make sure subagent model ids are valid catalog ids.

Possibly related: #5201 (prompt-budget rejection has `errorType: "query"` and no stable error code) and #5127 (the same "neither the picker nor the unfiltered catalog" fallback, in BYOK/SDK mode).

## Bug: Cannot enable voice mode — "Failed to fetch model catalog" / "Couldn''t load voice model catalog"

### Summary
Activating voice mode with `/voice` fails because the CLI cannot fetch the voice (STT) model catalog. Voice mode can''t be enabled at all, since the catalog must be reachable before any speech-to-text model can be downloaded.

### What I see
Two dialogs appear when trying to enable voice mode:

**1) Voice models picker:**
```
Voice models

No STT models available.
Your CLI may be out of date. Run /update to update, or download from:
https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/releases

Failed to fetch model catalog. Press r to retry.
```

**2) Blocking dialog:**
```
Couldn''t load voice model catalog
The voice model catalog couldn''t be fetched.

Voice mode can''t be enabled until the catalog is reachable. Check your network connection and retry.

> Retry
  Cancel
```

Pressing `r` / **Retry** does not resolve it — the catalog still fails to load and no STT models become available, so voice mode never enables.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run the Copilot CLI.
2. Invoke `/voice` to enable voice mode (dictation transcription via Foundry Local).
3. The CLI attempts to fetch the voice model catalog and fails with the errors above.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11 (arm64)
- Copilot CLI version: 1.0.57
- Network: corporate environment. The machine was connected to a corporate VPN (Azure VPN). The failure occurs in this restricted-network context, which strongly suggests the model-catalog / model-download endpoints are being blocked by the VPN/proxy/firewall.

### Expected behavior
- Voice mode should be able to fetch the model catalog and download STT models in corporate/proxy/VPN environments, OR
- The error should clearly identify the exact endpoint(s) it''s trying to reach (host/URL) and respect system/HTTP(S) proxy settings, so the URLs can be allow-listed.

### Impact
Voice mode is completely unusable in restricted-network/VPN environments because the catalog fetch is a hard prerequisite and there is no offline / manual model-install fallback surfaced in the UI.

### Suggested improvements
- Surface the exact catalog/model URLs in the error so they can be allow-listed.
- Honor `HTTPS_PROXY` / system proxy and custom CA settings for the catalog + model download.
- Provide an offline / manual model-install path when the catalog is unreachable.

issues.title: Cloud agent: "Registry only" MCP policy blocks all repo-configured MCP servers — proxy-bridged configs can't be fingerprinted ("unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration")

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

With the org MCP policy set to **Registry only**, the Copilot **cloud agent** silently drops every repo-configured MCP server, even when the server is present in the configured registry with a matching package identity. Only the platform defaults (`github-mcp-server`, `playwright`) reach the session.

The CLI log inside the session (`~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`) shows:

```
[DEBUG] Registry <org-registry>: servers will be verified against this registry
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-A" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-A" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
[ERROR] MCP server "mcp-server-B" filtered: Could not verify server "mcp-server-B" against registry <org-registry>: unable to compute fingerprint from local configuration
```

With the policy switched to **Allow all**, the same servers mount and their tools work.

## Root cause (from reading the shipped runtime)

In the cloud agent, the CLI never sees the repo's MCP config. cca-engine (`dist-cca-v3/index.js`) replaces every proxy-discovered server with a bridge config:

```js
// ~line 80361
discoveredServers[name] = toBridgedMcpServerConfig(name, void 0, mcpProxyUrl);
```

```js
// ~line 79716
function toBridgedMcpServerConfig(serverName, serverConfig, mcpProxyUrl, customAgentName, customAgentVersion) {
  const args = [BRIDGE_SCRIPT_PATH, `--proxy-url=${mcpProxyUrl}`, `--server-name=${serverName}`];
  if (serverConfig) {
    args.push(`--config=${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(serverConfig)).toString("base64")}`);
  }
  ...
  return { type: "local", command: process.execPath, args, ..., tools: ["*"] };
}
```

So for every third-party server the CLI receives `node <bridge-script> --proxy-url=… --server-name=…`. The CLI derives a stdio server's identity from its command (`npx`→npm, `uvx`→pypi, `dotnet`→nuget, `docker`, `mcpb`; see the explanation in mindovermachine-dev/product-cli#20). `node` maps to nothing, so no fingerprint can be computed and the server is filtered.

- At line 80361 `serverConfig` is `void 0`, so even the base64 `--config` arg is omitted. The original config is not available to the CLI at all.
- Built-in servers pass only because they are marked runtime-authored (`markRuntimeAuthoredServer`, gated by `copilot_swe_agent_mcp_builtin_provenance`) and are exempt from third-party policy.
- From code reading (not tested end-to-end): remote/HTTP configs are bridged the same way when `mcpProxyUrl` is set (`toSdkMcpServerConfig`, ~line 79741), so switching to an `http` server does not avoid this in the cloud agent.

**Net effect:** under "Registry only", no repo-configured (or custom-agent) MCP server can ever pass verification in the cloud agent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Org settings → Copilot → Policies: **MCP servers in Copilot** = Enabled; **MCP registry URL** = a spec-compliant registry; registry access = **Registry only**.
2. Registry entry named `mcp-server-A`:
```json
   {
     "name": "mcp-server-A",
     "version": "0.0.2",
     "packages": [{
       "registryType": "oci",
       "identifier": "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A",
       "version": "0.0.2",
       "transport": { "type": "stdio" }
     }]
   }
```
   Verified: `GET <org-registry>/v0.1/servers/mcp-server-A/versions/latest` returns 200 with `server.name == "mcp-server-A"`.
3. Repo → Settings → Copilot → coding agent → MCP configuration:
```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "mcp-server-A": {
         "type": "local",
         "command": "docker",
         "args": ["run", "-i", "--rm", "<registry-host>/<path>/mcp-server-A:0.0.2"],
         "tools": ["*"]
       }
     }
   }
```
4. Assign a task to the cloud agent.
5. Observe:
   - cca-engine logs `Discovered MCP server: mcp-server-A` and `MCP servers configured for session: …, mcp-server-A, …`.
   - No `MCP server 'mcp-server-A': pending` / `connected` lifecycle events appear.
   - The CLI log shows the `unable to compute fingerprint` error above.

## What we ruled out

- **Registry reachability/auth:** Cloud Run access logs show 200s for the CLI's requests during the session.
- **Name lookup:** before aliasing, the error was `Not found in registry`. After making the registry resolve the config key, the error moved to the fingerprint stage.
- **Local config shape:** `type: local` vs `stdio`, `-e VAR` vs `--env=VAR`, and minimal args all gave the identical error.
- **Package type:** `registryType` `oci` vs `docker` gave the identical error.
- **Policy fetch:** succeeds (`servers will be verified against this registry`). This is not the fail-closed family in #4378 / #2498 / #4346.

## Expected behavior

Repo-configured servers that match a registry entry should be verified against their **original** configuration. issues.title: ACP mode: MCP OAuth token is never persisted after successful sign-in — every new session re-opens the browser

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp`), the OAuth token for a remote HTTP MCP server is never written to disk or the OS keychain after a successful sign-in. Each new ACP session (for example, each new thread in an ACP client) starts unauthenticated, gets a 401, and opens the browser authorization page again.

Evidence from a successful sign-in (macOS, Atlassian remote MCP `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`):

```
14:32:47.301Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"atlassian-cloud"}
14:32:47.302Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (...) {"server":"atlassian-cloud"}
14:32:59.348Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {...}
```

- The tools work for the rest of that session. No log line shows a token being stored.
- `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` does not exist. #4695 says this is where tokens are cached (`<hash>.tokens.json`). `COPILOT_HOME` is unset and HOME is the default.
- A scan of files modified in the two minutes after sign-in found only browser profile files. Nothing changed under `~/.copilot`, `~/.config`, `~/Library/Application Support` (excluding the browser), or the project directory.
- The keychain has no MCP or OAuth item. Only the `copilot-cli` GitHub login entry exists.
- The next ACP session, started about 50 minutes later, got a 401 and opened the authorization page again:

```
15:22:30Z [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::mcp::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (...) {"server":"atlassian-cloud"}
15:22:30Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"atlassian-cloud"}
15:23:48Z ... timed out after 60s
```

So the token appears to be held only in memory for the lifetime of the ACP process.

### Affected version

1.0.98 (installed by an ACP client, macOS arm64)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Configure a remote OAuth MCP server, e.g. in the project's `.mcp.json`:
   `{"mcpServers":{"atlassian-cloud":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp"}}}`
2. Start `copilot --acp` from an ACP client and open a session. The browser opens; complete the sign-in. The MCP tools work.
3. Close the session or process, then start a new ACP session in the same project.
4. The browser authorization page opens again. `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` still does not exist.

### Expected behavior

- After a successful sign-in, the token (and refresh token) is persisted, either in `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` or in secure storage per #2783.
- Later ACP sessions reuse it silently, as the 1.0.90 release notes describe ("reuses a still-valid cached token").
- Ideally, when no valid token exists, the browser opens only when an MCP tool is actually used, not at session start.

### Additional context

- Related to #4994 (the auth page opens on every ACP session since 1.0.89). This issue covers the underlying cause: nothing is persisted, so there is never a cached token to reuse.
- Also related: #4695 (duplicate cache keys preventing reuse) and #2783 (secure credential storage).
- Older 1.0.8x logs show the server only marked as "needing auth", with no browser opened.

issues.title: Shell guard refuses `kill $VAR`, `kill $!` and `kill %1`, and blocks a whole command line when `kill $(...)` matches nothing

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The shell tool's process guard refuses `kill` in several ordinary forms, even when the command targets one specific process. It also rejects a whole compound command when one `kill` in it has nothing to stop.

Name-based kills (`pkill`, `killall`, `taskkill /IM`, `Stop-Process -Name`) are refused on purpose: those messages point to `kill <PID>` instead. Protecting the runtime's own process tree ("this is an ancestor process of your own runtime") makes sense too. This issue is only about `kill` with a PID that the guard could resolve but doesn't.

Observed on Copilot CLI 1.0.95-2, each command run as its own call in the same shell session:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `sleep 4127 > /dev/null 2>&1 &` then `kill $(pgrep -f "sleep 4127")` | runs and stops the process |
| `PID=$(pgrep -f "sleep 4127") && kill $PID` | refused |
| `SLEEP_PID=$(pgrep -f "sleep 5131"); echo "pid=$SLEEP_PID"` | prints `pid=96400` |
| `kill $SLEEP_PID; echo killed-var` | refused, and `sleep 5131` (PID 96400) keeps running |
| `sleep 5132 > /dev/null 2>&1 & kill $!; echo killed-bang` | refused |
| `sleep 5133 > /dev/null 2>&1 & kill %1; echo killed-job` | refused |
| `kill $(pgrep -f "no-such-process-xyz") ; echo after-kill` | refused, so `after-kill` never prints |
| `echo before; kill $(pgrep -f "no-such-process-xyz") 2>/dev/null; echo after` | refused, so neither `before` nor `after` prints |

Every refusal is:

```
Command not executed. The 'kill' command must specify at least one numeric PID. Usage: kill <PID> or kill -9 <PID>
```

The guard resolves `$(...)` substitutions, but it refuses shell variables, `$!` and job specs, even when they hold a live PID. A variable set by an earlier command in the same session is refused too.

When a substitution matches no process, the guard refuses the entire command line. In a shell, `kill` with no PID just fails, and here its error is discarded by `2>/dev/null`. That is the common "stop the server if it's running" cleanup idiom, so with nothing to stop, the other commands on the line are skipped as well.

### Impact

- **`$!` doesn't work.** It is the standard way to remember a background job's PID, so an agent that started a server or watcher can't stop it with the PID it saved. It has to rerun `pgrep` inside `$(...)`, or copy the number into a new command.
- **The message is misleading.** It reads as if the agent forgot to pass a PID, so models retry variations, often `pkill`, which is also refused. Processes they meant to stop keep running and hold their ports.
- **Cleanup lines fail as a whole.** Commands like `npm test; kill $(lsof -ti:3000) 2>/dev/null; rm -rf tmp` are refused entirely whenever the process has already exited.

### Expected behavior

- `kill $VAR`, `kill $!` and `kill %1` run when they resolve to PIDs outside the runtime's protected process tree.
- A `kill` whose substitution finds no process fails on its own, as it would in a shell, instead of blocking the rest of the command.

### Suggestion

Check protected PIDs when the command runs instead of on the command text. For example, define a `kill` function in the shell session that resolves each argument after expansion, refuses only the runtime's own processes and their ancestors, and passes everything else to the builtin. That keeps the protection, handles variables, `$!` and job specs, and leaves the other commands on the line alone.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.95-2, macOS arm64, built-in shell tool.
- Also seen in VS Code 1.142.0 agent-host Copilot sessions, which use the same runtime.

Related: #3334, where the same guard treats the word "kill" inside a heredoc as a kill command.

issues.title: Autopilot repeatedly retries write_agent for completed non-resumable agent with conflicting selectors

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When a background agent has completed as blocked and is non-resumable, the coordinator can repeatedly call `write_agent` instead of replacing it. In the observed failure, the model also supplied all three mutually exclusive selectors (`agent_id`, `agent_ids`, and `scope`) on every retry, so each call failed schema validation before the runtime could report the target agent's terminal lifecycle state.

The result was a long Autopilot loop displaying repeated `Write <agent-id>` calls with no recovery.

Observed sequence:

1. A background general-purpose agent was launched successfully.
2. The agent completed with a blocked result because it started from the wrong working directory. Its launch metadata reported `resumable: false`.
3. The coordinator attempted to steer/resume the completed agent repeatedly.
4. Every generated `write_agent` call contained all three selectors:

   ```json
   {
     "agent_id": "<agent-id>",
     "agent_ids": ["<agent-id>"],
     "scope": "children",
     "message": "Resume..."
   }
   ```

5. The tool returned:

   ```text
   Provide exactly one of "agent_id", "agent_ids", or "scope"
   ```

6. Autopilot retried the same malformed operation many times instead of inspecting lifecycle state and starting a replacement.

The old agent had no durable resumable session. Starting a fresh agent with the original objective, preserved worktree, and absolute project root recovered the work.

## Affected version

```text
1.0.100
```

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start a background agent with `mode: "background"`.
2. Have the agent finish with a blocked result and a terminal/non-resumable lifecycle state.
3. Ask the main agent to resume or steer that completed agent.
4. Observe the main model call `write_agent` repeatedly.
5. In the failing case, inspect the tool calls and observe that `agent_id`, `agent_ids`, and `scope` are all populated.
6. Observe every call fail with `Provide exactly one of "agent_id", "agent_ids", or "scope"`.
7. Observe Autopilot continue retrying the dead agent instead of launching a replacement.

## Expected behavior

The tool and orchestrator should defend against both failure modes:

1. The generated `write_agent` call should contain exactly one selector.
2. When the target is completed, failed, cancelled, missing, or non-resumable, the tool should return a structured actionable result, for example:

   ```text
   agent_not_resumable:
   Agent <id> is completed/blocked and cannot accept messages.
   Do not retry write_agent. Start a new task agent using the original objective and preserved context.
   ```

3. Autopilot should treat that response as terminal for the old agent ID and automatically start a fresh replacement with the original objective and durable context.
4. After an invalid-selector response, the coordinator should retry at most once with only `agent_id`, not loop indefinitely.

## Additional context

- OS: macOS, arm64
- Interface: interactive TUI, Autopilot
- Agent: background general-purpose agent
- Model: `gpt-6.1-sol`, accessed through a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway
- API subtype: OpenAI Responses (`/v1/responses`)
- The replacement-agent workaround was successful when explicitly given the original objective, absolute worktree/project root, approved plan, constraints, and known progress.

Related open issues:

- #5143 — follow-ups to idle agents can be delayed; its documented workaround is starting a fresh agent.
- #4101 — `write_agent` may block while waking an idle agent.
- #4911 — background subagent stream failures can end without a failure status.
- #2595 — completed agents can disappear and become unrecoverable.

Those issues cover adjacent delivery, status, and retention failures, but I could not find one covering the exact combination of malformed selector retries plus failure to replace a terminal/non-resumable agent.

Suggested lifecycle handling:

- Permit `write_agent` only for agents currently reported as `running` or `idle`.
- Reject terminal/non-resumable agents with a dedicated error code and replacement guidance.
- Persist enough final metadata/result for the coordinator to seed a replacement safely.

issues.title: Explicit-approval requests silently denied in resumed sessions: 'could not request permission from user' / orchestrator 'permission request denied: unusable session working directory'

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

In interactive sessions that have been **resumed**, any tool action requiring explicit approval is silently denied instead of prompting the user, even though allow-all ("yolo") elevation is active for the session. Two records appear for each denial:

1. Tool result: `Permission denied and could not request permission from user. Copilot needed the user's approval and no one could answer. This is not an OS or sandbox error.` (error code `denied`)
2. CLI log: `[rust:permissions_engine::orchestrator] permission request denied: unusable session working directory`

Auto-approval of judge-clean actions still works, so the failure masquerades as a targeted block on specific commands (e.g. `sudo pacman …`). `sudo` itself is not special: in one affected resumed session `/usr/bin/sudo -n true && echo sudo-ok` and `sudo -n git --version` were auto-approved and ran, while other escalated commands in the same time window were denied.

Denied actions all involve destructive/privileged operations or file effects **outside the session working directory**; read-only / in-cwd / trivially safe commands in the same turns auto-approve:

| Denied (exact events) | Auto-approved in the same session/turn |
|---|---|
| `mkdir -p ~/Workspace/pkgcache && sudo pacman -Sw --cachedir ~/Workspace/pkgcache …` | `/usr/bin/sudo -n true && echo sudo-ok` |
| `systemd-inhibit --what=idle --mode=block --who=… sleep 3 & INH=$!; loginctl show-session …` | `v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video0 --info …` |
| `rm -rf /tmp/… && mkdir -p /tmp/… && cd /tmp/… && git init …` | `sed -n '411,500p' crates/…/index.rs` |
| `cp -a /run/media/…/build/… /tmp/… && cd /tmp/…` | `echo ok && ls /tmp \| head -3` |
| `cd /tmp && GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=0 git clone -q … && cd …` | `grep -n … …` |

All observed denials occurred in **resumed** sessions (one session resumed several times across 4 days; another resumed after a pause). Fresh sessions approve the same class of actions.

Onset: **2026-10-16 on 1.0.99-2** (prerelease channel, auto-update). No occurrences under 1.0.99-0 despite the same usage pattern. Still reproduces on 1.0.100-1 and 1.0.101-0. 24 denial events across `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log` since 10-16.

## Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.101-0` (first seen on 1.0.99-2; also reproduced on 1.0.100-1)

## Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use an interactive session with `defaultPermissionMode: "allow-all"` active (session events show `allowAllPermissions: true`), do some ordinary work in a project subdirectory, then end the session.
2. `/resume` (or relaunch the CLI and resume) that session later.
3. In the resumed session, run a command with privileged components or file effects outside the session cwd, e.g. `mkdir -p ~/Workspace/pkgcache && sudo pacman -Sw --cachedir ~/Workspace/pkgcache <pkg>` or `systemd-inhibit --what=idle --mode=block --who=test sleep 3`.
4. Observe the denial above; the orchestrator warning `permission request denied: unusable session working directory` appears in the process log at the same timestamp.
5. Control: the same command in a **fresh** session succeeds; a simple `sudo -n true` in the same resumed session also succeeds.

## Expected behavior

Escalated actions in an interactive session should present an approval prompt the user can answer, or the allow-all elevation (which the session state still reports as active) should cover them. At minimum, the denial should say why the request could not be raised — `unusable session working directory` is currently visible only in the log file, and it is unclear what makes the working directory unusable.

## Additional context

- `~/.copilot/settings.json`: `"defaultPermissionMode": "allow-all"`, `"sandbox": {"enabled": false}`. No managed policy: logs report `[managedSettings] effective policy resolved: source=none, bypassDisabled=false`.
- OS: Linux x86_64 (CachyOS), shell fish (CLI processes run with /bin/bash), terminal Ghostty.
- `copilot help config` says of `defaultPermissionMode`: *"Any value is ignored on resumed sessions, outside interactive runs, and when `--allow-all`/`--yolo` already elevated the session."* The runtime also contains the string `the session-claim bypass requires force=true (omitting the flag is treated as a refusal to escalate)`. If resume intentionally drops the bypass, the session state is misleading: `session.permissions_changed` events still show `allowAllPermissionMode: "on"` and `/yolo on` appears effective.
- Possibly related recent changes (bundled changelog): 1.0.98 *"Resuming a session now respects abandoned pending-permission work and continues only active permission requests."*; 1.0.99-0 / 1.0.100 assisted-permission judge routing for bash commands; 1.0.96 timeline attribution of "unattended fallback" permission decisions.
- Ruled out:
  - **Command concurrency**: ~61% of 4,550 successful tool calls in the most-affected session overlapped another in-flight call; only 5 of 18 denials had an overlapping sibling.
  - **OS/sudo policy**: `sudo whoami` / `sudo -n whoami` run fine in fresh sessions (and simple sudo probes auto-approve even in affected sessions).
  - **Sandbox**: disabled in settings and in effect.
- Evidence is available in `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl` (tool.execution_start/_complete pairs with exact commands and error payloads) and `~/.copilot/logs/process-*.log`; happy to attach sanitized extracts on request.

Questions: what condition produces `unusable session working directory` for a session whose cwd exists and is writable? And can the approval path recover (surface the prompt) instead of falling through to the unattended deny?

issues.title: Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
# Context window rollover fails: "checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover"

### Describe the bug
Long-running agent sessions crash when the context window fills and the runtime attempts a rollover:

```
Execution failed: Failed to start a fresh context window: checkpoint.md is absent for this agent; write it before requesting rollover
```

The turn ends and the session (or sub-agent) is effectively dead; it recurs on subsequent turns in the same session.

### What we observed
- The agent **had** written a `checkpoint.md` to the session's `files/` folder (via a normal file write / patch) ~7 minutes before the first failure, yet the runtime still reported it as absent "for this agent".
- The native runtime contains related errors ("Replacing checkpoint.md requires expected_revision; read or stat it first, or use append", "Stale checkpoint writer…"), which suggests checkpoints must be written through a runtime-managed store/tool rather than a plain file write. In our sessions the model did not appear to have any tool exposed for that store, so it could never satisfy the precondition.
- Seen repeatedly across multiple sessions/sub-agents (custom agents and the main agent), mostly in long tool-heavy sessions (builds, test runs, large tool outputs).

### Expected behavior
Either the runtime writes/derives the checkpoint itself before rollover, or the agent is given (and prompted to use) the tool needed to create it. Failing that, it should fall back to normal compaction instead of terminating the turn.

### Environment
- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.100 (also seen on 1.0.98)
- Windows 11 x64, PowerShell
- Models: GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 sessions

### Workaround
Manual `/compact` before the context fills avoids it.

issues.title: Attaching a 3840x2160 PNG wedges the TUI and kills all terminal sessions
issues.body:
### Description

# Bug report: Large payloads into TUI input wedge opencode and kill all terminal sessions

## Summary

Two distinct repros, same failure mode: pushing a large blob (image attach or clipboard paste)
through the opencode TUI wedges the whole box — all terminal windows die, keyboard rescue
(SysRq) needed. Long-running background jobs survive (launched with setsid), but every
interactive session is lost.

## Environment

- OS: Linux (Arch-ish), kernel with xe Intel GPU driver
- Terminal: multiple terminals open (kitty/gnome-term), several tmux-style workflows
- opencode TUI session running alongside heavy GPU training job (31GB RAM box, ~19GB in use)

## Repro 1 — attaching a 4K image

1. Attach a 3840x2160 PNG (phone screenshot) to a TUI message
2. opencode logs: `using resized image ... from=3840x2160 to=2000x1125`
3. ~90 seconds later the system is wedged; all terminals dead; SysRq required

Log evidence (~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log):

```
timestamp=2026-10-21T02:44:16.392Z level=INFO run=a979b0c1 message="using resized image" from_mime=image/png to_mime=image/png from=3840x2160 to=2000x1125
timestamp=2026-10-21T02:52:53.520Z level=ERROR run=a979b0c1 message=process session.id=ses_ea5bca27cffer5Tr9dvNKbM42l messageID=msg_15c5f952e00117trwoJuZB0CKi error=Aborted stack=undefined
```

Kernel journal (same window):

```
Oct 21 12:45:47 ares kernel: sysrq: HELP : loglevel(0-9) reboot(b) crash(c) ...
```

## Repro 2 — pasting large text

1. Copy a large block of text to clipboard
2. Paste into the opencode TUI input
3. Same wedge: all terminals die, system unresponsive, recovery required

(Repro 2 has no log capture yet — box was wedged before a log pull was possible.)

## Suspected common cause

Both paths push a multi-MB payload through the TUI input handling (base64 image data /
multi-hundred-KB paste text). Memory spike or blocking encode in the resize/paste path
appears to take down the TUI and its terminal children. The `error=Aborted` suggests a
Go runtime abort (possibly OOM) in the session process.

## Frequency

Image crash: reproduced multiple times over several days (user reports "sometimes" —
correlates with 4K screenshots). Paste crash: reproduced at least once.

## Workarounds

- Large text: write to a file and reference the path (`@/tmp/notes.txt`) instead of pasting
- Screenshots: save to disk first, attach by path
- Long jobs: always launch with `setsid`/`nohup` — they survive the carnage

## Impact

High: total loss of all interactive terminal sessions on the machine; rescue requires
SysRq or hard reboot. Data in running sessions is lost.

issues.title: desktop: macOS app silently denied ~/Documents (missing NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription) -> empty model selector
issues.body:
## Summary

On macOS, the OpenCode desktop app cannot use a workspace located under `~/Documents` (also affects `~/Desktop` / `~/Downloads`). The app does not declare `NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription` in its `Info.plist`, so macOS silently denies access with `EPERM` instead of showing an "Allow" prompt. Every location-scoped API call then returns HTTP 500, leaving the model selector empty and preventing the workspace from loading.

## Environment

- opencode version: desktop app **2.0.32** (bundled CLI 2.0.32, Electron 44.4.5). Note: a separate Homebrew `opencode` on `PATH` reports v2.0.18.
- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), Darwin 25.6.0, arm64 (Apple Silicon)
- Terminal: N/A for this issue (desktop app). Reported from WezTerm.
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: release (`latest` auto-update channel)
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. On macOS, make sure the app has no Documents access: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access → disable/remove OpenCode. (Do not grant Files and Folders → Documents either.)
2. Launch the OpenCode desktop app on a workspace under `~/Documents`, e.g. `/Users/<user>/Documents/Default Project`.
3. Open the model selector.

## Expected Behavior

The workspace loads and the model selector lists the configured models (providers `opencode` and `opencode-go`). If the OS needs permission, macOS shows a prompt to allow access to the Documents folder.

## Actual Behavior

All requests scoped to that workspace return HTTP 500, e.g. `GET /api/model`, `GET /api/provider`, `GET /api/config`, `GET /api/location`, `GET /api/fs/list`, and the session endpoints:

```
PlatformError: Unknown: FileSystem.realPath (/Users/<user>/Documents/Default Project)
  [cause]: Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, lstat '/Users/<user>/Documents/Default Project'
```

The model selector is empty. No permission prompt was ever shown. The same endpoints return HTTP 200 with a full model list when the workspace is outside the protected folders (e.g. `/Users/<user>`).

## Additional Context

- From the app's process context, `ls ~/Documents` returns `Operation not permitted`.
- `/Applications/OpenCode.app/Contents/Info.plist` has **no** `NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription`. Per macOS TCC rules, a missing usage string means the system does not prompt and the access is denied silently, so the app never appears under "Files and Folders" for the user to allow.
- **Workaround that fixed it:** grant OpenCode **Full Disk Access** (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access), then fully quit (⌘Q) and relaunch the app. After that, the Documents workspaces load and the model selector populates.
- Alternatively, using a workspace outside `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, or `~/Downloads` works with no permission change.
- Reproducible 100% until Full Disk Access is granted.
- Suggestions: add `NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription` (and likely `NSDesktopFolderUsageDescription` / `NSDownloadsFolderUsageDescription`) to the app's `Info.plist` so macOS prompts normally; and show a clear error in the UI when the workspace can't be read instead of an empty model list.

issues.title: desktop: fast scroll up from bottom snaps back down, older history loads one chunk at a time
issues.body:
## Description

In a long desktop chat session sitting idle at the latest message (bottom), scrolling up quickly snaps the viewport back down toward the bottom, so it's impossible to scroll up in one gesture. Older history lazy-loads one chunk at a time: mid-scroll loading doesn't happen — you must stop, wait, then resume. Reproducible, not intermittent.

Code pointers (verified against `dev`, may drift): the scroll handler in `packages/app/src/session/timeline/virtualizer.tsx` (`handleListScroll`, ~L753-769) can re-pin for any input via the `atEnd && arrived` heuristic (~L760-764, `endEpsilon` 0.5px), but only unpins for pointer-held/touch scrolls (~L765) — wheel unpin comes only from the wheel handler (~L652-657). Measurement-compensation writes can satisfy `arrived` and cause a spurious re-pin mid-gesture, after which the pinned `scrollToEnd()` forcers (~L354-359, end-anchoring ~L279-284) yank the viewport down. Separately, history loading is scroll-event-driven only (~L768) with top-edge/single-flight gates (`interaction.ts` ~L217-251, 20-message pages), so fast scrolling outruns it. Related but distinct: #56130 (row drift during wheel-up).

## Plugins

None found in config

## OpenCode version

2.0.29 (install/channel: latest)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a long session in opencode v2 desktop (Windows build + WSL server), idle/completed, viewport at the bottom.
2. Scroll up fast (mouse wheel) in one continuous gesture.
3. Observe the viewport snaps back down; older history appears only after stopping and waiting, one chunk at a time.

## Screenshot and/or share link

None

## Operating System

Windows desktop app + WSL server; WSL: Linux 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x64

## Terminal

opencode v2 desktop app (not terminal); shell in WSL: /bin/bash

## Expected / Actual

Expected: fast upward scroll travels up through history, loading older chunks mid-scroll. Actual: viewport snaps back down; chunks load only after stopping and waiting.

issues.title: tui: queued card for a delivered image message lingers above the prompt input
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows (v2 TUI), a user message with an image attachment keeps being rendered as a queued card directly above the prompt input long after it has been delivered and answered. The card does not clear when the turn completes; clicking it has no visible effect; the client's inbox sync (`PATCH /api/session/<session>/inbox/<message>`) returns `409 Conflict`. The card only disappears after restarting the TUI. Observed on both 2.0.29 and 2.0.32. Server-side state is clean (`session_inbox` empty) — nothing is actually pending.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.29 (first observed); 2.0.32 (still reproduces)
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.19045 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: Windows Terminal (TUI launched from powershell.exe)
- Shell: PowerShell
- Install/channel: npm global install of `@opencode/cli`, channel: latest
- Active plugins: `oh-my-openagent@4.5.1`; local plugin files: `compaction-offload.js`, `edit-journal.js`, `memory-context.js`

## Reproduction

1. In the TUI, send a user message with an attached image (renders as `[Image 1] …` plus a file chip). It is delivered and answered normally.
2. After the turn completes and the session goes idle, the same message is still shown as a queued card directly above the prompt input.
3. Clicking the card produces no visible response; the client attempts `PATCH /api/session/<session>/inbox/<message>` and receives `409 Conflict`. The card never clears.
4. Restarting the TUI clears the card.
5. Steps 1–2 reproduce on 2.0.32 as well (after updating and restarting).

Only messages with image attachments have been observed to stick; plain text messages do not.

## Expected Behavior

Once a queued message is delivered (promoted into the session), its queued card should disappear from above the prompt input. If an inbox sync fails because the server-side row is already gone (`409`), the client should reconcile and clear its local pending state instead of leaving the card stuck.

## Actual Behavior

- The delivered image message remained displayed as a queued card above the prompt input indefinitely (12+ minutes in the first occurrence, across multiple later turns).
- Clicking the card had no visible effect.
- `PATCH /api/session/<session>/inbox/<message>` returned `409` twice with no visible effect in the client.
- Still reproduces on 2.0.32: after updating and restarting, another image message left the same card above the prompt input after its turn completed (still present 7 seconds after the session went idle; the user reports it stays until restart).

## Additional Context

Observed instances (Windows Terminal, Windows 10.0.19045):

Instance 1 (2.0.29):
- session `ses_eb1c00cd0ffehEx1RlY2u9ZPoe`, user message `msg_14e47ae22001Q8qN1T36b4JC3V` (with PNG image) — sent 2026-10-18T09:11:25.080Z, delivered and answered normally (09:11:44 idle).
- Card still shown ~12 minutes later; clicking it produced no visible effect.
- Log (UTC):

```
2026-10-18T09:23:34.453Z  PATCH /api/session/ses_eb1c00cd0ffehEx1RlY2u9ZPoe/inbox/msg_14e47ae22001Q8qN1T36b4JC3V -> 409
2026-10-18T09:23:35.013Z  PATCH /api/session/ses_eb1c00cd0ffehEx1RlY2u9ZPoe/inbox/msg_14e47ae22001Q8qN1T36b4JC3V -> 409
```

- No other 409s in the entire log for this session; `session_inbox` / `session_pending` tables empty; the message exists exactly once in `session_message`.

Instance 2 (2.0.32):
- Same session, user message `msg_14e6cc7000016MmaXKno5jQHVv` (with PNG image) — sent 2026-10-18T09:51:56.798Z, answered 09:51:57.810Z → 09:52:21.257Z, idle at 09:52:21.263Z.
- Card still shown above the prompt input at 09:52:28Z (7s after idle; verified via screenshot).
- No further `PATCH .../inbox/...` requests were logged for this occurrence (the card had not been clicked yet).

Code references (v2.0.29): `packages/core/src/session/inbox.ts` — `projectDelivered` deletes the inbox row when the message is promoted; later mutations (`cancel`, delivery change) raise `LifecycleConflict`, which surfaces as `409` on `PATCH .../inbox/:id`. It looks like the client can hold a local pending entry whose server row is already gone, and a `409` does not make it clear the entry.

Related issues: #55179 (editing queued messages with attachments), #56115 (inbox cancel API), #44926 (editing queued messages), #16856 (v1: QUEUED badge stuck).

Workaround: restart the TUI. No code fix known; updating 2.0.29 → 2.0.32 did not resolve it.

issues.title: v2.0.29: agent `model` (config `agents.<id>.model` and agent frontmatter) is ignored for new sessions
issues.body:
### Summary

In 2.0.29, the `model` configured per agent is not applied when a new session starts. `opencode run` (default `build` agent, or `--agent <id>`) always uses the default model (`gemini-4-argon-contributor`) even though the agent sets `model` in `opencode.jsonc` / agent frontmatter. The equivalent V1 config (1.19.0) started sessions with the configured model, and the migration guide lists agent `model` as supported, so this looks like a V1→V2 compatibility regression.

### Environment

- OpenCode 2.0.29 (curl installer, channel `latest`), Linux x86_64
- Migrated from V1 1.19.0 (same machine); config converted to the native V2 shape
- Credentials present: `opencode auth list` → `OpenCode Go  API key  stored`
- `opencode debug config` shows the config source is loaded and normalized (see below)

### Config

`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (as normalized by `opencode debug config`):

```json
"agents": {
  "build":  { "model": { "providerID": "opencode-go", "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "variant": "max" } },
  "plan":   { "model": { "providerID": "opencode-go", "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "variant": "max" } },
  "general":{ "model": { "providerID": "opencode-go", "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "variant": "max" } },
  "explore":{ "model": { "providerID": "opencode-go", "model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash", "variant": "max" } }
}
```

Global agent files `~/.config/opencode/agents/*.md` also set `model: opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max` in frontmatter.

### Steps to reproduce / observed

1. `opencode run --standalone "Reply with exactly: ok"`
   → header shows `build · gemini-4-argon-contributor` (expected `deepseek-v4.1-flash`)
2. `opencode run --standalone --agent plan "Reply with exactly: ok"`
   → `plan · gemini-4-argon-contributor` (expected `deepseek-v4.1-flash`)
3. `opencode run --standalone --agent adversarial-review "..."` (custom agent file, frontmatter `model`)
   → `adversarial-review · gemini-4-argon-contributor` (expected `deepseek-v4.1-flash`)
4. Same as 1 with `agents.build.model` set as `"opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash"` (no `#variant`)
   → still `gemini-4-argon-contributor`
5. `opencode run --standalone -m opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash "..."` → `deepseek-v4.1-flash` ✓
6. `opencode run --standalone -m "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max" "..."` → `deepseek-v4.1-flash` ✓

So the model and credentials are usable; only the agent-level `model` selection is dropped. It is not variant-specific (4).

### Expected

A new session for a primary agent or an agent launched with `--agent` should use the agent's configured `model`, as in 1.19.0 and as described in the V2 agents documentation (“Model” section): <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/agents>.

### Additional observation

`opencode debug agents` prints `[]` even though agents resolve correctly by name (`--agent adversarial-review` runs). Possibly the same agent-definition loading path.

### Version

2.0.29

### Related

- #49765 — v2: subagent spawn ignores `agents.*.model` and uses parent session model
- #50925 — agents: `mode:all` configured model ignored at subagent spawn — parent model inherited
- #42835 / #46311 — ACP: per-agent model configuration has no effect / ACP session creation ignores the default agent's assigned model

issues.title: Critical: Agent ran destructive InfluxDB command without user approval, causing data loss
issues.body:
### Description

Summary
The opencode agent executed DROP MEASUREMENT govee_temperature against a live InfluxDB database without user approval, permanently deleting all temperature data across all retention policies. This was a catastrophic error during a dashboard editing task.

What happened
User asked to edit a Home Assistant dashboard (Govee T&H) to add average temperature lines and change humidity retention from 15 to 366 days.
Agent successfully modified the custom card JS and dashboard config.
Agent discovered that InfluxDB continuous queries needed updating to support the changes.
Agent connected to InfluxDB at local-govee-influxdb:8086 and created new CQs — this was reasonable.
Critical error: Agent then ran DROP MEASUREMENT govee_temperature intending to re-backfill temperature data with mean values. This deleted ALL temperature data from ALL retention policies (raw_3h, hourly_366d, hourly_15d).
Impact
All historical temperature data for 11 rooms permanently destroyed
Data was migrated from HA Recorder to InfluxDB at a cost of ~$20 in AI fees
No backup exists of the InfluxDB data
Humidity data was unaffected
Root cause
The agent used a destructive database command (DROP MEASUREMENT) without:

Asking the user for approval
Verifying the scope of the deletion (it affects ALL retention policies, not just one)
Considering safer alternatives (e.g., writing a new measurement, or accepting None values for historical mean)
What should have happened
Agent should have asked user approval before any database mutation
Agent should have used a non-destructive approach (e.g., accept None mean for historical data, or write to a new measurement)
Agent should never have run DROP MEASUREMENT on a production database
Suggested improvements
Add explicit user confirmation before any destructive database operations (DROP, DELETE)
Treat InfluxDB and other database systems as read-only unless user explicitly approves writes
Add a safety check that warns when a command will affect more data than expected
Log all database mutations for audit purposes
Affected user

Opencode, InfluxDB

Ask Opencode to a question without giving any instruction to do anything. It just goes on to perform tasks that it has not been asked to perform, including destructive actions.

issues.title: Go: deepseek-v4.1-flash returns 429 Endpoint is unavailable while other Go models succeed
issues.body:
﻿## Description

Requests to `deepseek-v4.1-flash` on the OpenCode Go endpoint fail with

```
HTTP 429
{"error":{"type":"server_error","message":"Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable."}}
```

while other Go models return `200` on the **same API key, same endpoint, in the same minute**.

This lines up with the open incident on status.opencode.ai ("Upstream provider issues — Go: deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-v4.1-flash are seeing increased error rates", started Oct 20 23:44 UTC), but for this workspace the failures started earlier and are still happening now. `deepseek-v4-pro` returns `503` with the same body.

## Control matrix

`2026-10-21T02:47Z`, one Go key, endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, requests issued back-to-back, all carrying `x-opencode-session`:

| model | attempt | HTTP | `x-opencode-log-id` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 1 | **429** | `01a15c5b-2540-7917-84d2-80df4fc4fab0` |
| `deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 2 | **429** | `01a15c5b-27d8-71f9-ab7e-008307fdc82e` |
| `glm-5.3` | 1 | 200 | `01a15c5b-2a4a-7c41-a486-f149cedf4d96` |
| `glm-5.3` | 2 | 200 | `01a15c5b-2dec-7e56-a6cd-a4b19d1ff8eb` |
| `kimi-k2.7-code` | 1 | 200 | `01a15c5b-311f-76d2-bc97-a976470f03bd` |
| `kimi-k2.7-code` | 2 | 200 | `01a15c5b-3665-7ab7-8bb3-50b002cfdb88` |
| `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` | 1 | 200 | `01a15c5b-418e-7d6e-9544-ee4a6f870717` |
| `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` | 2 | 200 | `01a15c5b-4655-76f1-ae6f-58a14449dd7e` |

Minimal body used:

```json
{"model":"<model id>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}
```

Earlier in the same window `deepseek-v4.1-flash` alternated inconsistently (`429`, then `200`, then `200`) for identical requests, which is what makes it hard to work around at the client level.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Go key whose workspace has an active subscription and region set to **Global**.
2. `POST /zen/go/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "deepseek-v4.1-flash"` and a minimal body.
3. Observe `429` / `503` `Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.`
4. Repeat with `glm-5.3`, `kimi-k2.7-code` or `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` seconds later — all return `200`.

## Environment

- **Client:** Hermes Agent `v0.21.7+132.gf594424` (sends a stable `x-opencode-session` per conversation; includes PR #101864)
- **Endpoint:** `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`
- **Wire format:** `chat_completions`
- **Workspace region:** Global
- **OS:** server Ubuntu 22.04, client Windows 11
- **Terminal:** OrcaTerm
- **OpenCode version:** N/A (not an OpenCode client)

## Impact

Every agent turn fails on the primary model. Since 2026-10-20T17:24Z, six scheduled runs in this workspace failed at this step. Workaround is pinning a non-DeepSeek model, which loses the DeepSeek quota the plan is priced around.

## Questions

1. Is a healthy upstream endpoint currently configured for the `deepseek-v4.1-flash` `chat/completions` route? The error carries an `x-opencode-log-id` but no `x-opencode-endpoint-id`, which in #53120 was the signature of the gateway giving up before an endpoint served the request.
2. #53120 describes per-conversation sticky provider binding (`stickyId = sessionId ?? workspaceID ?? ip`) that is only written on success. If this workspace got bound to a dead endpoint, can that binding be reset server-side, or does it expire on its own?
3. Given the status page reports monitoring data as missing on and off, is there a better signal we can watch than the public status page?

Happy to provide the full request/response dumps or more log ids if useful.

issues.title: [BUG]: macOS desktop: Cmd+Q leaves a half-dead instance, and the next Dock click stalls the renderer
issues.body:
## Summary

On macOS, quitting the desktop app with Cmd+Q leaves a half-dead instance: the process neither terminates nor enters its background-service state, and the Dock icon keeps showing it as running. The next click on the Dock icon shows the window but the renderer stalls indefinitely. Killing the leftover instance makes the next launch clean.

Reported and reproduced by richardding on shipped 2.0.29; the `sample` and `ps` snapshot are attached there.

## Environment

- macOS 27 (Darwin 27.0.0), Apple Silicon
- OpenCode Desktop 2.0.29 (prod channel, `ai.opencode.desktop`)

## Reproduction (deterministic on the reporter's machine)

1. Run the desktop app normally.
2. Cmd+Q.
3. The Dock icon remains — the app is neither terminated nor in the "run in background" state.
4. A single click on the Dock icon → the window shows, the renderer stalls.
5. If you `pkill -f OpenCode` at step 3 instead, the Dock switches to "run in background" and the next Dock click launches the GUI cleanly.

## Evidence

From `sample <renderer-pid> 8` during a stalled launch:

- Renderer main thread: 6120/6120 hits (100% of the 8s window) in `v8::internal::OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor::WaitUntilCompilationJobsDoneForIsolate` → `mach_msg2_trap`.
- No V8 compilation thread is present anywhere in the 8s sample: the main thread waits on compilation jobs while no worker thread is observable running them.
- Full `sample` + `ps` snapshot: https://gist.github.com/richardding/94b037afe00441b1dd0972978e75cf7f

## Why this is separate from #54296

#54296 tracks a main-thread block (the window is shown before the main bundle and layers finish). This is the quit path plus a renderer stall after the Dock click; the `oc://` asset starvation seen in the same report is a third mechanism. The reporter's reading — the hanging quit is upstream of the stall — is consistent with `pkill` clearing it.

issues.title: desktop: custom provider save always throws "unavailable on this server"
issues.body:
## Summary

OpenCode Desktop exposes the "Custom OpenAI-compatible provider" form in Settings → Providers, but the save handler unconditionally throws `provider.custom.unavailable`, so the flow can never succeed on any server — including the app's own bundled local server.

## Environment

- opencode version: Desktop 2.0.14 (bundled `opencode-cli v2.0.14`, dpkg `opencode 2.0.14`)
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux 7.0.0-31-generic, x86_64
- Terminal: Unavailable: this is the Desktop (Electron) UI, no terminal involved
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: release `.deb` downloaded from the Desktop section of https://opencode.ai/v2/docs
- Active plugins: none found in config

## Reproduction

1. Install `opencode-desktop-linux-amd64.deb` (Desktop 2.0.14) and launch OpenCode Desktop.
2. Open Settings → Providers.
3. Select the custom provider entry ("Custom OpenAI-compatible provider").
4. Fill in valid-looking values, e.g. provider ID `local`, name `My Local Server`, baseURL `http://localhost:8080/v1`, model ID `my-model`.
5. Click Save/Connect.

## Expected Behavior

The provider is written to the user config (`providers.<id>`) and shows up in the model picker — the same result as adding the block to `opencode.json` manually.

## Actual Behavior

Save always fails with the toast: **"Custom providers are unavailable on this server"** (i18n key `provider.custom.unavailable`).

The shipped `app.asar` build shows the mutation is a stub with no server or protocol condition:

```js
mutationFn: async e => {
  throw Error(a.t(`provider.custom.unavailable`))
}
```

It throws for every server, so the dialog is reachable but unusable.

## Additional Context

- Not a server/config problem: adding the provider manually to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` loads it correctly on the very server the app spawns — `GET /api/provider` on the bundled server returns `{"id":"local","name":"My Local Server","activation":"enabled", ...}`. The failure is isolated to the dialog's save path.
- Frequency: 100% reproducible (unconditional code path).
- Current source appears to rework this: the same handler is gated with `if ((await serverSDK().protocol) !== "v1") throw ...` and the settings entry is wrapped in `<Show when={protocol() === "v1"}>`, so it looks like the shipped 2.0.14 build predates that change.
- Suggestion: either ship the save implementation in the build, or hide the entry point until it works — the UI currently offers an action that can never succeed.
