issues.title: Context clamp sends 1-token output limit when the chars/3.5 estimate overshoots a large first turn

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

On a large first turn, pi asked the model for 16 output tokens although the prompt fit in the window. The reasoning model spent them on thinking and returned no answer.

Measured with a self-hosted DeepSeek V4 (`contextWindow` 262,144) over `openai-responses`, pi 1.3.0:

- One user message of 943,383 characters. The server tokenizer counted 225,255 tokens for it (4.19 chars/token) and 227,760 for the whole request.
- pi estimated the message alone at 269,538 tokens (chars / 3.5), which is more than the window.
- No assistant usage exists yet, so the estimate is the whole count. `clampMaxTokensToContext` returns 1, the Responses adapter raises it to 16, and the response stops on `length` with no text. Real free space was about 34,000 tokens.

Later turns are fine because they use reported usage. It happens on a large first turn, or after a large paste or tool result.

Related: #10497 (the estimate is too low for dense text, which is why 3.5 was chosen) and #9409 (the 16-token `length` response is not detected as an overflow). One fixed chars-per-token value cannot be right in both directions.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a model whose tokenizer averages clearly more than 3.5 chars/token on your text, with a 262,144-token window.
2. In a new session, send one message whose real token count fits the window but whose `length / 3.5` does not.
3. The request carries `max_output_tokens: 16` (`max_tokens: 1` on `openai-completions`) and the reply is empty.

Unit level: `buildBaseOptions` for a 10,000-token window and a first user message of 35,000 characters returns `maxTokens: 1`.

### Expected behavior

The clamp should not send a limit that cannot produce an answer. If the context is really full, the provider's overflow error is a better signal, and pi already recovers from it.

I want to implement this. Proposed fix: give the clamped limit a floor equal to the existing 4096-token safety margin, `min(maxTokens, max(4096, available))`. The request then goes past the estimated window only when the estimate alone leaves less than 4096 tokens. With it, the request above gets 4,096 output tokens instead of 16. Branch with tests: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/main...jbelnick:pi:fix/clamp-output-floor

An alternative is an optional per-model chars-per-token value in the model definition. It fixes the estimate for one tokenizer, but it adds a model field and does not cover content variance (#10497 measured 3.19 chars/token on DeepSeek). Which would you accept?

### Version

1.3.0 (same code on main at 02726086)

---

issues.title: Configurable thinking level/model for compaction

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

labels.name: to-discuss
labels.description: This ticket requires further discussion outside of triage.

issues.body:
## Summary

Compaction (automatic and manual) can't be given its own thinking level — it unconditionally reuses the session's current thinking level. For users who run auto-compaction on reasoning models, this makes the thinking budget of summarization inseparable from normal turns.

## Current behavior (v0.83.0)

- Both compaction paths pass the live session level: `core/agent-session.js` — manual `/compact` (`~L1423`) and auto-compact (`~L1657`) call `compact(..., this.thinkingLevel, ...)`, where `this.thinkingLevel` is `agent.state.thinkingLevel` (`get thinkingLevel()`, `~L584`).
- The summarization request then maps it to the provider `reasoning` option: `core/compaction/compaction.js` `createSummarizationOptions` (`~L426`) — `if (model.reasoning && thinkingLevel && thinkingLevel !== "off") options.reasoning = thinkingLevel;`
- `CompactionSettings` has no thinking field: `core/settings-manager.js` `getCompactionSettings()` (`~L526`) only exposes `enabled`, `reserveTokens`, `keepRecentTokens`.

## Use cases

1. **Higher quality summaries without paying for high thinking on every turn** — run normal conversation at `low`/`off` but let compaction summarize at `high` (compaction is relatively rare, so the extra cost is small).
2. **Cheaper compaction on a heavy-thinking workflow** — conversation at `high`, but cap summarization at `minimal`/`off` to cut the cost of frequent auto-compacts.

## Proposed change

Add an optional `thinkingLevel` to `CompactionSettings`:

```ts
interface CompactionSettings {
  enabled?: boolean;
  reserveTokens?: number;
  keepRecentTokens?: number;
  /** Overrides the session thinking level for summarization. undefined = follow session (current behavior). */
  thinkingLevel?: ThinkingLevel;
}
```

- `undefined` → keep today's behavior (session level).
- Explicit `"off"` → always summarize without reasoning (allowed even on a reasoning model).
- Any other level → clamp to the model's supported levels, same as `setThinkingLevel` does.

Open questions for maintainers: should the manual `/compact` path also expose an interactive pick, and should this count toward the same `ThinkingLevel` value set or a tighter subset for cost safety?

issues.title: session_before_compact: customInstructions is write-only — mutating the event has no effect

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

`SessionBeforeCompactEvent.customInstructions` cannot be used to steer the compaction summary: mutating the field in a handler has no effect, and there is no other way to add custom instructions without fully replacing the compaction.

## Details (v1.3.0; same shape in 1.0.0)

**Automatic compaction** (`_runAutoCompaction` in `dist/core/agent-session.js`, ~line 2519):

- The event is emitted with `customInstructions: undefined`.
- Only `extensionResult?.cancel` and `extensionResult?.compaction` are consumed from the emit result.
- The default summarizer then runs via `_runDefaultCompaction(preparation, model, undefined, ...)` — a literal `undefined`, never the event object.

**Manual compaction** (`compact(customInstructions)`):

- The event is emitted with the parameter, but afterwards `_runDefaultCompaction(preparation, model, customInstructions, ...)` uses the original parameter variable, not the possibly-mutated event field.

So the field is write-only in both paths. Note that `SessionBeforeTreeResult` does support `customInstructions` as a handler result ("Override custom instructions for summarization") — the before-tree event already has the intended pattern; before-compact lacks it.

## Why it matters

An extension that wants the summarizer to follow house instructions (e.g. a structured summary with required sections) is forced to return a full `{ compaction }` built with the exported `compact()` helper. That requires rebuilding the summarization call (model, stream fn, retry policy) and silently loses native behaviors such as virtual-model routing in `_getSummarizationRequestAuth`.

## Suggested fix

Either:

1. Read the mutated event field back after `emit` and pass it to `_runDefaultCompaction` (auto path), and use the mutated event field in the manual path too; or
2. Accept `customInstructions` in `SessionBeforeCompactResult` and pass it through, mirroring `SessionBeforeTreeResult`.

Thanks for pi — it is the foundation our harness extensions are built on.

issues.title: Compaction summarizer inherits the session thinking level, so the summary can hit its output cap and fail entirely

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### Environment

- pi 1.3.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)
- Model routed through an OpenAI-compatible gateway (reasoning model, `reasoning: true`)
- Session thinking level: `max` (`defaultThinkingLevel: "max"`)
- `contextWindow`: 200,000, model `maxTokens`: 32,000
- Compaction settings: defaults (`reserveTokens` unset → 16,384), `keepRecentTokens`: 40,000

### Symptom

Auto-compaction fails on every attempt:

```
Auto-compaction failed: Summarization failed: generation hit the token cap and the summary is incomplete
```

The queued user message stays blocked (`Queued for after compaction`, `Kept 1 post-compaction item blocked`). Because the trigger threshold is still exceeded, the next turn tries again — burning 1–2 minutes and ~50k input tokens per attempt — until the session hits the hard context wall and becomes unusable.

### Root cause

In `packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/compaction.js`:

```js
// 1. The summary output budget is derived from reserveTokens
const maxTokens = Math.min(Math.floor(0.8 * reserveTokens), model.maxTokens);
// default: 0.8 * 16384 = 13,107

// 2. The summarization request inherits the *session's* thinking level
function createSummarizationOptions(model, maxTokens, ..., thinkingLevel, ...) {
  const options = { maxTokens, signal, apiKey, headers, env, sessionId };
  if (model.reasoning && thinkingLevel && thinkingLevel !== "off") {
    options.reasoning = thinkingLevel;   // <- "max" is forwarded as-is
  }
  ...
}

// 3. If the summary doesn't fit, the whole thing is discarded
if (response.stopReason === "length") {
  return `${label} failed: generation hit the token cap and the summary is incomplete`;
}
```

Providers count reasoning tokens inside `max_tokens` (this is how DeepSeek documents it, and DeepSeek enables thinking by default with effort `high`). So the 13,107-token budget is shared between chain-of-thought and the summary text itself.

This also contradicts the design note in #92:

> Reasoning disabled (thinking level "off") since we just need a summary, not extended reasoning

### Measured evidence (one session, 4 consecutive compactions)

| attempt | wall time | input | cacheRead | output | of which reasoning | summary length |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 22s | 44,526 | 6,656 | 1,806 | 864 | 3,053 chars |
| 2 | 33s | 39,566 | 3,328 | 3,620 | 1,773 | 6,269 chars |
| 3 | 106s | 58,759 | 0 | 11,742 | 6,040 | 15,732 chars |
| 4 | 62s | 3,286 | 64,768 | 11,778 | 4,815 | 18,595 chars |
| failed attempt | — | ~59k | — | >13,107 | — | — |

Attempt 3 already used 89.6% of the cap, 51% of which was reasoning. Summaries grow monotonically (3k → 6k → 15.7k → 18.6k chars) because `UPDATE_SUMMARIZATION_PROMPT` requires *"PRESERVE all existing information"*, so the next attempt needs ~13.5k and fails; a retry can pass at 89.9% only because that particular run thought less. It's a coin flip at the boundary, not a hard wall — which is why this reproduces intermittently and is easy to blame on the model.

Note the cap is also independent of `keepRecentTokens`: raising `keepRecentTokens` reduces what must be summarized but does not change the 13,107 budget, so it does not fix the failure.

### Proposal

1. **Do not inherit the session thinking level for summarization.** Either force `reasoning: "off"` on the summarization request, or expose `compaction.thinkingLevel` with a default of `"off"`.
2. **Degrade instead of discarding.** On `stopReason === "length"`, retry once with thinking disabled (and/or a reduced transcript) before reporting failure. Today a single over-cap attempt throws away the entire summary and leaves queued messages blocked; there is no cooldown either, so the same doomed request is re-issued on the next turn.
3. **Optional:** separate `compaction.summaryMaxTokens` from `reserveTokens`. As written, widening the summary budget necessarily moves the auto-compact trigger earlier — an unrelated trade-off users cannot opt out of.

### Workaround for others hitting this

- Manual: `/thinking off` → `/compact` → `/thinking max`
- A `session_before_compact` extension that generates the summary with `reasoning: "off"` and a larger `maxTokens` (the hook's intended use). Happy to share a working one if useful.

issues.title: Windows installer: standalone Node is shadowed by an older system Node after restart, pi crashes on startup
issues.body:
### What happened?

I installed pi with `powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex"` as copied from pi.dev, on Windows 11. I already had Node 22.12.0 installed system-wide in `C:\Program Files\nodejs`. The installer saw it was older than 22.19.0 and offered to install standalone Node, and I said yes. The install finished fine.

After I opened a new PowerShell window, `pi` crashed on its first request:

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
TypeError: zlib.createZstdDecompress is not a function
    at Object.onResponseStart (.../pi-coding-agent/dist/bundle/chunks/chunk-66G7ITPS.js:129:70337)
```

Cause: `Install-NodeStandalone` calls `Add-UserPathEntry ... -Prepend`, which puts `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pi-node\current` first in the **user** PATH. Windows builds PATH as machine entries followed by user entries, so `C:\Program Files\nodejs` still comes first. During the install it works, because the installer also prepends to `$env:PATH` for its own process. The managed launchers (`pi.cmd`, `pi.ps1`) then call plain `node`, so in a new shell pi runs on 22.12.0, which has no zstd support.

`pi` works when started on pi-node directly:
`& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\pi-node\current\node.exe" "$env:USERPROFILE\.pi\agent\bin\pi-launcher.js"`

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, install a Node older than 22.19 system-wide (MSI, adds `C:\Program Files\nodejs` to machine PATH).
2. Run the installer and answer Y to installing standalone Node.
3. Open a new terminal and run `pi`. `node -v` shows the old version.

### Expected behavior

pi runs on the Node the installer put in place. For example, when the installer installs pi-node, the launchers could call that `node.exe` by full path instead of using whatever `node` is first on PATH. Or the installer could check `node -v` against a fresh machine+user PATH at the end and warn when an older Node shadows pi-node.

Related: #7771 (same crash from an old Node; a startup version check would make this one obvious too).

### Version

1.3.0 (installer from pi.dev, 2026-10-20), Windows 11, system Node 22.12.0, pi-node 22.23.3

Note: this report was drafted with AI assistance (Claude) from my debugging session. I reviewed and edited it before posting, and the cause and workaround were verified on my machine.

issues.title: Cache warming stops immediately for sessions on a virtual model (`registerVirtualModel`)
issues.body:
**Version:** pi-coding-agent 1.0.3 (managed install), `cacheWarming: "idle"`.

**What happens.** In a session whose selected model is a virtual model (an extension router registered with
`pi.registerVirtualModel`), cache warming never refreshes. `/session` reports the warmer inactive with
"conversation context changed" right after each request.

**Cause.** `dist/core/sdk.js` builds the warm run with `cacheContextIsCurrent(requestModel)`:

```js
return (currentModel.provider === requestModel.provider &&
        currentModel.id === requestModel.id && ...);
```

`currentModel` is `agent.state.model` — the virtual model (e.g. `router/worker`) — while `requestModel` is the
physical model the router chose (e.g. `fuelix-anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`). They never match, so
`CacheWarmer.validateRun()` stops the run with "conversation context changed" before the
`cache_warming_decision` hook fires; extensions cannot override it. The comment above it says routed requests
"may not be repeated by the next request" — but a router usually repeats the same physical model for long
stretches, and that is exactly when warming pays.

**Expected.** For a virtual selection, treat the request as current while the router's latest route still
names the same physical model (for example compare against the previous route's model, or let the
`cache_warming_decision` hook see and override the "context changed" case).

**Impact (measured).** Orchestrator sessions on a router: 9% of Claude calls came 5–60 minutes after the
previous call and paid a full cache rewrite each (avg $1.52 per Opus call at ~280k tokens); those calls were
46% of the Opus spend. Warming (or the 1-hour cache) recovers most of it.

**Workaround in use.** Per-request `cacheRetention: "long"` (Anthropic 1-hour cache) for orchestrator sessions,
set by the provider wrapper.

_Evironment: pi-coding-agent 1.0.3, model router extension with `registerVirtualModel` (`router/orchestrator`, `router/worker`)._

issues.title: [Urgent] google-shared: Gemini 4 models without thinkingLevelMap still send thinkingBudget: 0 on off and MINIMAL on minimal

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**Urgent (P0 regression / incomplete fix for #10890):** Custom `gemini-4-argon` and `gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive` configurations (including the exact `models.json` repro in #10890) still fail with HTTP 400 on `main` whenever reasoning is omitted/`off` or set to `minimal`. Fix PR: #11005.

### What happened?

After #10890 (`1692bba63`), `usesGoogleThinkingLevel` matches `gemini-4-*`, but two paths in `packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts` still send invalid `thinkingConfig` payloads for Gemini 4 models when `thinkingLevelMap` is not populated (for example, custom `models.json` definitions like the repro in #10890, `gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive`, or direct `pi-ai` `Model` objects):

1. **Reasoning omitted / `"off"` sends `{ thinkingBudget: 0 }`:**
   `getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig(model)` calls `clampThinkingLevel(model, "off")`. When `model.thinkingLevelMap?.off` is not `null`, `clampThinkingLevel` returns `"off"`, hitting `if (fallback === "off") return { thinkingBudget: 0 }` even though `usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model)` is `true`. Vertex AI rejects this with HTTP 400 (`Thinking budget is not supported for this model. Use thinking level instead.`).
2. **`"minimal"` sends `thinkingLevel: "MINIMAL"`:**
   Per the [Gemini 4 Argon developer guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/guides/gemini-4-argon), both `thinking_budget` and `thinking_level="MINIMAL"` return HTTP 400 on Gemini 4 (valid levels are `LOW`, `MEDIUM`, `HIGH`, same as Gemini 3 Pro). Without `thinkingLevelMap.minimal: null`, `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, "minimal")` resolves to `"minimal"` (`"MINIMAL"`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Define `gemini-4-argon` in `models.json` without `thinkingLevelMap` (as in #10890) or call `streamSimple` on a `Model` with `thinkingLevelMap: {}`:
   - Omit `reasoning` (or pass `--thinking off`): `getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig` emits `thinkingConfig: { thinkingBudget: 0 }`.
   - Pass `reasoning: "minimal"` (or `--thinking minimal`): `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel` emits `thinkingConfig: { includeThoughts: true, thinkingLevel: "MINIMAL" }`.
2. Both requests fail on Vertex AI / Gemini API with HTTP 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

### Expected behavior

- `getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig(model)` clamps from `"minimal"` rather than `"off"` for `usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model)` models so it never falls back to `{ thinkingBudget: 0 }`.
- `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, "minimal")` falls back to `"low"` for Gemini 4+ and Gemini 3 Pro models when `thinkingLevelMap.minimal` is not explicitly mapped, sending `{ thinkingLevel: "LOW" }` when thinking is disabled or set to `minimal`.

Fix and regression tests submitted in #11005.

### Version

`main` (`5ab7fe74c`) / 1.2.0

issues.title: powershell tool falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 when pwsh 7 is the Microsoft Store build
issues.body:
### What happened?

With PowerShell 7 installed from the Microsoft Store (7.6.7, no MSI), the built-in `powershell` tool runs Windows PowerShell 5.1.

`getPowerShellConfig` in `utils/shell.js` finds pwsh with `where pwsh.exe` and checks the first hit with `fs.existsSync`. The Store build puts an app-execution alias on PATH (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a zero-length reparse point). On that alias `existsSync` is false and `statSync` throws EACCES, while `lstatSync`, `accessSync`, and spawning it all work. So the check rejects a working pwsh and silently falls back to `powershell.exe`.

Windows 11 Pro 26300, Node 26.8.1, managed install. The resolver is identical in 1.0.0 and 1.2.0.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Only the Store PowerShell 7 installed (`Get-AppxPackage Microsoft.PowerShell`), no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`.
2. `pi -ne -p -t +powershell,-bash "Use the powershell tool to run: $PSVersionTable.PSEdition"` → `Desktop`.
3. Resolver directly:
   ```
   node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/utils/shell.js').then(m=>console.log(m.getPowerShellConfig().shell))"
   ```
   → `C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`
4. `where pwsh.exe` → the WindowsApps alias. On that path: `fs.existsSync` → `false`, `fs.statSync` → EACCES, `fs.lstatSync` → 85-byte reparse point, `spawnSync` → prints `Core`.

### Expected behavior

pwsh 7 is used, as `docs/windows.md` says ("runs commands through pwsh.exe when available"). Microsoft is steering users to the Store/MSIX build and retiring the MSI, so more Windows users will hit this.

Fix is small: in the Windows branch of `findExecutableOnPath`, verify the `where` hit with `fs.lstatSync` or `fs.accessSync` instead of `existsSync`, or trust `where` the way the Unix branch trusts `which`. Workaround I use today: `$env:Path = "$PSHOME;$env:Path"` before starting pi, so the real package folder comes first (a user-PATH entry alone is not enough from pwsh, because the Store build prepends its alias folder to PATH at startup). Happy to send a PR if you want one.

Related: #8582 has the same symptom from a different cause (a `where` timeout under load); this one is deterministic on an idle machine.

### Version

1.2.0

issues.title: A codemode script fails before it runs when it declares a top-level variable named `tools`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Hello!
First thank you for creating Pi and numerous blog posts which truly resonate with me. I switched from Claude Code to Pi recently and it is like breath of fresh air.
I came across small issue and thought that you may be open for a PR to fix. My AI told me that I need to open issue first and got a lgtm before opening PR, that's why I am so detailed here. PR itself perhaps would be shorter 🙂 

So, here is what happened.
I configured a new mcp, called fluffyjaws, which is a knowledge base search assistant.
The problem is that when I ask him at the first time I see the following codemode block:
```
 codemode                                                                                                                                                             
 const tools = await searchTools('fluffyjaws');                                                                                                                       
 console.log(JSON.stringify(tools, null, 2));                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                      
 Script error:                                                                                                                                                        
 SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name                                                                                                                  
     at codemode.js:1:41                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                      
 No tool calls were made.                                                                                                                                             
 ```

On the next turn it recovers and everything works.

I talked with claude opus 5.5 model trying to understand if this is a bug or something which can be fixed upstream. And it turned out that the problem is in variable name `tools`. Here is what it told me:
> Models write `const tools = await searchTools(...)` on their own, so this happens without the user doing anything unusual. It costs a turn to recover. 
> The cause is that the script body is wrapped as `(async (tools, console) => { ... })` in `packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts:327`, so those two names are function parameters.

I am happy to submit a small PR with the fix. Let me know if you're willing to accept such contribution.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `pi -ne` with codemode enabled
2. Ask pi to run **_exactly_** this codemode script:                                                                                                                       
    ```js
      const tools = await searchTools("read");
      return tools.length;
    ```

### Expected behavior
That script runs and returns a number.

### Actual behavior 
codemode ends up with an error:
```
Script error:
   SyntaxError: invalid redefinition of parameter name
       at codemode.js:1:41
```

### Version

1.3.0


### Potential approach for fix

`tools` and `console` are already globals: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L451-L453 so the wrapper could be `(async () => { ... })`, without `tools` and `console` arguments:
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/bd3c9b823762b7383954aa49e13ee350471015fe/packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts#L327
A script's `const tools` would then hide the global for that script only. Line numbers and `"use strict"` would keep working.

issues.title: Add an API to report usage separately from a tool call

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add an API so that extensions can report usage (tokens, cost, etc) independently of a tool call.

### Why?

Some extensions may make model calls to implement features or behavior that are independent of an actual tool call, or that happen after a tool call returns a result to the model. In these cases the usage of those calls cannot be attached to a tool call.

Examples:

* A subagent extension that returns a tool result immediately but starts a child agent. The usage of the child agent cannot be reported in the tool call, since the tool call returns before the child finishes.
* An extension that captures "memories" and occasionally "compacts" them in the background. The memory tool calls should not block on the compaction, but the extension needs to make a model call of its own to do the compaction, so the usage happens separately from the tool call.

### How? (optional)

Pi already has `SessionManager.appendUsage(kind, provider, model, usage, note?)` and uses it for `cache_warm` usage. Extensions can't use it because they get `ReadonlySessionManager`, which does not have `appendUsage`. This can be solved by exposing `appendUsage` to extensions somehow.

issues.title: pi-durable: afterTool for calls that never ran, and a turn limit
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Two small, independent additions to pi-durable:

- `afterTool` also runs for calls that never executed (unknown tool, invalid arguments, blocked by `beforeTool`).
- `HarnessSettings.maxTurns` ends a run after N model turns (`turn_limit`).

### Why?

I run pi-durable in a browser worker for Galaxy's Olit. Each addition fills a gap I hit there, and none of it is Galaxy-specific:

- An extension that screens or annotates tool results misses the ones for calls that never ran, though the model reads those too.
- There is no way to bound how many model turns a single run takes.

### How? (optional)

One commit per addition, each with its own tests; `npm run check` and the durable suite pass, and the changelog is untouched. Existing `afterTool` handlers now also see the error results of calls that never ran; nothing else changes for existing hooks.

Diff: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/main...guerler:pi:pi.000

Happy to split it into separate PRs, or drop any part you'd rather not have in core.

issues.title: modelOverrides are silently ignored for classifier models

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

`modelOverrides` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json` are silently ignored for classifier models. No error, no warning.

`docs/models.md` says they change metadata for "an existing built-in or extension-provided model", and that only unknown IDs are ignored. This model is built-in and the ID matches.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Point Pi at a llama.cpp router serving a decision model (GGUF `architecture.output_modalities: ["decisions"]`), so Pi registers it as `type: "classifier"`, `api: "typesafe-system-one"`. ID here: `clef-flash`.
2. In `models.json`:

```json
{"providers":{"llama.cpp":{"modelOverrides":{"clef-flash":{
  "name":"Clef Flash Q8_0 (Spark)","contextWindow":8192}}}}}
```

3. Restart Pi, then in codemode:

```js
const m = await models.getModelOfType("classifier","llama.cpp","clef-flash");
return m.name; // "clef-flash", not "Clef Flash Q8_0 (Spark)"
```

The identical override on a chat model in the same file does apply, so the file, merge and reload are fine; only the model type differs. Loading `ModelRuntime` with a temp `models.json` reproduces it with no extensions involved.

### Cause

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts`, `composeModelProvider()`:

```ts
const override = config?.modelOverrides?.[model.id];
return override && isModelType(model, "chat") ? applyModelOverride(model, override) : model;
```

`rawModelHeaders()` has the same chat-only gate, so `modelOverrides[...].headers` is dropped as well. Present in 1.2.0, 1.3.0 and `main`. #5021 and #6367 covered dynamically registered/extension providers, a different path.

### Expected behavior

Either apply overrides to every model type (at least `name`, `input`, `contextWindow`, `cost`, `headers`), or say in the docs that `models.json` overrides are chat-only and warn instead of silently ignoring them.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: OpenCode Go Claude (anthropic-messages): 400 on replayed thinking block after tool list change; block_binding only sent for supportsMidConvoEffort
issues.body:
_Disclosure: this report was written by an AI agent (Claude Code) at the request of a downstream app's maintainer. The experiment below was run by the agent against the real OpenCode Go endpoint with synthetic input._

### What happened?

Same failure as #10324, but on `anthropic-messages` through the OpenCode Go gateway (`opencode-go` / `claude-haiku-5-5`). Replaying a signed thinking block after the tool list changed returns:

```
400 invalid_request_error: messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to "drop_block". ... The `tools` list differs from the one this block was created with.
```

`anthropic-messages` only sends `block_binding` + `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` when `compat.supportsMidConvoEffort` is true. The generated catalog entry for this model (1.2.0, `opencode-go.json`) is `compat: { forceAdaptiveThinking: true, supportsTemperature: false }`, so it takes the plain path.

### Steps to reproduce

Using `streamSimple` with the `opencode-go` provider, model `claude-haiku-5-5`, `reasoning: "high"`:

1. Send a prompt that makes the model think and call a tool (2 tools in `context.tools`).
2. Send the tool result back with the same history and a 3rd tool added.

Results on the same history:

| Step 2 | Result |
|---|---|
| same tools | 200 |
| one tool added | **400** (above) |
| one tool added + `thinking.block_binding = { prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block" }` + beta `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` in `betas` (via `onPayload`) | 200 |
| one tool added, thinking blocks stripped from history | 200 |

Context: I embed `pi-ai` / `pi-coding-agent` via the SDK in a desktop app whose on-demand tool loading changes the active tool set mid-run, so it hits this often. No pi extensions are involved; this is not the `pi` CLI.

### Expected behavior

The gateway path should not 400 on a changed prefix, as Bedrock no longer does after #10324. prs.title: Strip whole-line HTML comments from context files
prs.body:
## What

`loadContextFileFromDir` drops whole-line HTML comments from a context file before it reaches the model.

## Why

Claude Code skips whole-line HTML comments in `CLAUDE.md`, so maintainers keep notes for human reviewers in them. Pi reads the file verbatim, so those notes go to the model as prompt text.

A real file I use has a 44-line block of banned phrasings. Line 74 of that file says:

> `<!-- Claude Code doesn't load them, so the bad words never reach an agent. -->`

True for Claude Code. False for pi: a pi session reads all 33 banned phrasings. The block is also 4782 of the file's 8683 bytes, so 55% of the prompt is a note for a human.

I want to use that file as `AGENTS.md`. Without this change my only options are to delete the notes or keep a second copy that drifts.

## Behaviour

- A comment is removed only when it starts a line and ends on a line of its own.
- A comment that shares a line with rule text is kept, so no rule is lost.
- A `<!--` that never closes keeps the original file, because guessing where it ends would delete rule text.
- The blank lines a removed block leaves behind collapse to one.
- A file with no comment is returned unchanged.

On the real file above: 8682 bytes to 3900, 33 AVOID lines to 0. The 2 `<!--` that remain are inside backticks and are rule text, so they stay.

## Scope

Only context files. `resolvePromptInput` (line 174) and the `package.json` read (line 79) still use plain `stripBom`.

## Tests

8 cases in `test/resource-loader.test.ts`: whole-line, indented, multi-line block, unclosed comment, rule-then-comment on one line, blank-line collapse, no comment, and `CLAUDE.md`.

`resource-loader.test.ts`: 61 passed. `tsc --noEmit`: clean. Pre-commit checks: pass.

Full suite: 2715 passed, 4 failed. Those 4 (`package-command-paths`, `2791-fswatch-error-crash`, `6999-models-json-hot-reload`) fail the same way on `upstream/main` with this change stashed.

## Scope of the fix

`pi/pikcg.sh` in my own repo passes `-nc`, which turns off context files. A session started through that launcher loads no `AGENTS.md`, so this change does nothing for it. The change applies to a session started with a plain `pi` command.

prs.title: fix(codemode): allow scripts to declare tools and console bindings
prs.body:
## Problem

Codemode wraps the script as `(async (tools, console) => {code})`, so `tools` and `console` are parameters of the wrapper. A script that declares either name at the top level is rejected before it runs:

```js
const tools = await searchTools("issues");
// SyntaxError: Identifier 'tools' has already been declared
```

Models write this often, since `tools` is the natural name for the result of `searchTools()`. It fails the same way on every model. A script that declares its own `console` fails too.

## Fix

The prelude already puts `tools` and `console` on `globalThis`, and they are the same objects `run(fn)` passed as arguments. The parameters are redundant, so this PR removes them:

- `vm.ts`: the wrapper is now `(async () => {code\n})`.
- `prelude-source.ts`: `run` now calls `fn()` with no arguments.

A script's `const tools` now shadows the global inside the script, which is valid JavaScript.

prs.title: fix(ai): tolerate missing finish_reason on non-empty openai-completions streams
prs.body:
## Problem

The `openai-completions` streaming handler throws `Stream ended without finish_reason` whenever the SSE stream closes without any chunk carrying a truthy `choice.finish_reason`. This kills every session on gateways that violate the spec by omitting the terminal finish_reason chunk.

The observable SSE pattern from such a gateway:

```
data: {"id":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"hello"},"finish_reason":null}]}
data: {"id":"...","choices":[],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":10,"completion_tokens":5}}
```

The final content chunk has `finish_reason: null`; the next chunk has `choices: []` (a metadata/usage chunk). Then the stream closes — no `[DONE]` sentinel. The existing code skips `choices: []` chunks via `if (!choice) continue` without ever setting `hasFinishReason`. After the loop, `output.stopReason` is still `"pending"` and the handler throws.

## Fix

Track `receivedAnyChunk` — set `true` for any structurally valid chunk (after the `!chunk || typeof chunk !== "object"` guard, before the choices-based `continue`). At end-of-stream:

- **No finish_reason, no chunks received** → keep throwing (`"Stream ended without finish_reason"`). A genuinely empty stream is a real transport failure and must stay loud.
- **No finish_reason, but chunks were received** → emit `console.warn` and resolve with `stopReason: "stop"` (or `"toolUse"` if tool calls are present), matching the existing `!compat.supportsFinishReason` fallback semantics.

The diff is seven lines across one file. No behaviour change for spec-compliant streams.

## Test coverage

Two test files updated/added:

**`packages/ai/test/openai-completions-missing-finish-reason.test.ts`** (new) — uses an isolated OpenAI mock, does not import the model catalog:
1. **Content without finish_reason** — stream delivers content chunks with `finish_reason: null` then a `choices: []` usage chunk; resolves with `stopReason: "stop"` and emits exactly one warning.
2. **Zero-chunk stream** — empty stream still throws `"Stream ended without finish_reason"` (transport failure path unchanged).
3. **Normal stream** — content chunk followed by a `finish_reason: "stop"` chunk; resolves correctly with no change in behaviour.

**`packages/ai/test/openai-completions-tool-choice.test.ts`** (updated) — the existing test `"errors when a stream ends after only null finish_reason chunks"` asserted the old error contract for a content-bearing stream. It is renamed and its expectations updated to the new contract (`stopReason: "stop"` + one `console.warn`). The zero-chunk throw path is covered by the new test file above.

All tests pass. `./test.sh` and `npm run check` both exit 0 (pre-existing tsgo type errors in unrelated packages are unchanged).

## Note on test.sh and the fresh-clone environment

In a fresh clone without running `npm run generate-models`, several `packages/ai` test files that import the model catalog cannot load and are silently uncountable by vitest. This caused an earlier `./test.sh` run (before the conflicting test was identified) to report exit 0 while the tool-choice test file was actually broken at import — not because the assertion passed, but because no test in the file could execute at all. After running `npm run generate-models` to hydrate the model data, the tool-choice file loads, the conflicting test is confirmed to fail under my change, and the fix above makes it pass.

## Strictness preserved

The fix does not weaken the zero-chunk check. An empty stream — which signals a genuine transport or API failure — continues to throw. Only a stream that delivered actual data before closing without a finish_reason is treated leniently.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): recovery omits tool results with the truncated tool call
prs.body:
Fixes #11227.

Problem: recovery of a recoverable length stop hides the failed assistant message with a context edit. `_omitRecoveryAttempt()` only hid the tool results its caller passed. The end-of-run check passed the turn's results from `turn_end`; the pre-prompt check in `_prepareRun()` passed none.

Trace, for a resumed session ending in:

```
user
assistant(call_x, stopReason "length")
toolResult(call_x, "not executed")
```

1. The next prompt runs the pre-prompt check. `_findLastAssistantMessage()` skips the trailing tool result and returns the truncated assistant.
2. Recovery hides the assistant only.
3. The request contains `toolResult(call_x)` without its call. OpenAI rejects it, and the persisted edit breaks every later prompt.

Fix: `_omitRecoveryAttempt()` finds the matching tool results itself, in the projected context between the assistant and the next assistant message, so every caller hides the call and its results together. This matches the end-of-run path, compaction cut points, and `orderToolResults()` in durable. The `_lastAssistantToolResults` plumbing and the `toolResults` parameter of `_checkCompaction()` are removed.

Test: `test/suite/regressions/11227-recovery-omits-tool-results.test.ts` fails before the fix and passes after.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): grep tool ignores ripgrep config via --no-config
prs.body:
## Problem

The built-in `grep` tool spawns `rg` with the inherited process environment. If `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` points to a ripgrep config containing e.g. `--fixed-strings`, the tool's semantics silently change: `literal: false` searches become literal, and the agent gets incomplete results with no error and no indication anything is off.

## Fix

Pass `--no-config` to `rg` so the tool contract (`literal`, `glob`, `limit`, ...) is deterministic regardless of ambient user config. Verified with ripgrep 15.2.0 that `--no-config` fully neutralizes `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`.

## Audit of other built-in tools

- `find` (fd): fd has no config file or env-var mechanism — not affected.
- `bash` / `powershell`: intentionally inherit the full environment.
- `ls` / `read` / `edit` / `write`: pure Node fs, spawn nothing.
- `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / global git excludes still apply to grep and find, which is intended and documented.

Users who want customized grep behavior can wrap the tool with an extension or call `rg` through the `bash` tool.

## Test

Regression test in `packages/coding-agent/test/tools.test.ts` sets `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH` to a config with `--fixed-strings` and asserts both regex matches are returned with `literal: false`.

closes #11203

prs.body:
## Summary

Adds Scaleway Generative APIs as a built-in OpenAI-compatible provider. Closes #6165.

- **Auth:** `SCW_SECRET_KEY`, the env var Scaleway's docs and CLI already use, or `/login scaleway`
- **Endpoint:** serverless `https://api.scaleway.ai/v1`; dedicated deployments via a
  `baseUrl` override in `models.json`
- **Default model:** `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, with vision input, 256k context / 32k output,
  reasoning efforts `none` / `low` / `high` / `max` sent as native `reasoning_effort`

## Compat

Scaleway's documented OpenAI-compat gaps are encoded as generated compat flags:
`store` unsupported, no developer role, `strict` tool schemas ignored, usage in
streaming, and `max_completion_tokens` as the output cap.

The catalog is generated from models.dev in `processScalewayModels`. Scaleway is
exempted from the cross-provider DeepSeek-V4 rule: it accepts `reasoning_effort`
natively and does not require `reasoning_content` on replayed assistant messages
(verified against the live API).

## Testing

- `packages/ai/test/scaleway-models.test.ts`: no-network payload, thinking-level-map,
  and env-key tests
- Scaleway blocks in the live suites (`stream`, `abort`, `total-tokens`,
  `image-tool-result`, ...) gated on `SCW_SECRET_KEY`
- Verified live: `none`/`low`/`high`/`max` efforts accepted, `medium` rejected, and
  image tool results read correctly by the default model

## Note on `npm run check`

The branch carries stale model references (`mimo-v2.5-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-r1`,
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`) left over from the models.dev drift at the branch point;
`main` has since updated them, and merging takes `main`'s versions of those lines, so
the merge result is clean. Nothing in this PR contributes errors: the Scaleway
additions type-check and pass their tests against a fresh `npm run generate:models`
hydration.

Adds provider attribution headers to pi-durable, using the same header table as the coding agent.

prs.title: feat(ai,coding-agent): add Anthropic Claude support to Google Vertex AI provider
prs.body:
## Problem

In Google Cloud Vertex AI Model Garden, users can access Anthropic Claude models (such as Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku) using their Google Cloud credentials (ADC or API key). Previously, the `google-vertex` catalog generator explicitly excluded all non-Gemini models with `if (!modelId.startsWith("gemini-")) continue;`, and the provider only exposed the `google-vertex` Gemini API. As a result, users with GCP credentials authorized for Claude models could only view and invoke Gemini models.

## Solution

1. **Model Catalog Generation (`packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts`)**:
   - Updated `processGoogleModels` so `claude-*` models under `google-vertex` are included with `api: "anthropic-messages"`, `provider: "google-vertex"`, and base URL `https://{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`.
   - Claude models inherit proper tool-calling, vision modalities, reasoning options, and cost metadata.

2. **Vertex Anthropic Adapter (`packages/ai/src/api/vertex-anthropic.ts`, `packages/ai/src/api/vertex-anthropic.lazy.ts`)**:
   - Implemented a request adapter for Anthropic Messages on Vertex AI.
   - Obtains Google Cloud OAuth authorization headers from Application Default Credentials / service account files or Google Cloud API keys via `@google/genai` without adding new dependencies.
   - Rewrites messages requests to the Vertex AI publisher endpoint format:
     `https://${location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/${project}/locations/${location}/publishers/anthropic/models/${modelId}:${stream ? "streamRawPredict" : "rawPredict"}`
   - Formats the request body for Vertex AI (removes `model` from JSON body, sets `"anthropic_version": "vertex-2023-10-16"`).
   - Injects Google authorization headers (`Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `x-goog-api-key: <key>`) while stripping Anthropic-specific API key headers.
   - Connects to `anthropic-messages.ts` streaming machinery so tool use, extended thinking, streaming deltas, and usage calculations work identically.

3. **Tree-Shaking & Bundle Isolation**:
   - The Vertex adapter is exposed as a lazy API module (`vertex-anthropic.lazy.ts`).
   - `anthropic-messages.ts` remains decoupled from `@google/genai`, preserving browser bundle tree-shaking for `anthropicProvider()`.

4. **Provider Dispatch (`packages/ai/src/providers/google-vertex.ts`)**:
   - Configured `googleVertexProvider` with an API dispatch map for `"google-vertex"` (Gemini) and `"anthropic-messages"` (Vertex Claude).

## Verification

- `npm run check`: full check passed (biome formatting, linting, imports, runtime dependencies, shrinkwrap, install lock, TypeScript checks, and browser smoke check).
- `vitest --run packages/ai/test/vertex-anthropic.test.ts`: all 10 tests passed covering catalog verification, provider dispatch, request URL/header/body transformation, error handling, and streaming.
- Existing tests in `packages/ai/test/google-vertex-api-key-resolution.test.ts` and `packages/ai/test/providers.test.ts` pass.

prs.title: fix(ai): avoid thinkingBudget and MINIMAL on unmapped Gemini 4 models
prs.body:
**Urgent (P0 incomplete fix for #10890):** Unblocks Gemini 4 (`gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive`) requests before the next release so custom `models.json` definitions (including the exact repro in #10890) and `pi-ai` callers without `thinkingLevelMap` do not fail with HTTP 400 on `off` or `minimal`.

### Problem

After #10890 (`1692bba63`), `usesGoogleThinkingLevel` matches `gemini-4-*`, but two paths in `packages/ai/src/api/google-shared.ts` still emit invalid `thinkingConfig` payloads when `thinkingLevelMap` is not populated (such as custom `models.json` definitions like the repro in #10890, `gemini-4-argon-cyber-permissive`, or direct `pi-ai` `Model` objects):

1. When reasoning is omitted or `"off"`, `getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig(model)` calls `clampThinkingLevel(model, "off")`. Without `thinkingLevelMap.off: null`, `clampThinkingLevel` returns `"off"`, hitting `if (fallback === "off") return { thinkingBudget: 0 }` even though `usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model)` is `true`. Vertex AI rejects this with HTTP 400 (`Thinking budget is not supported for this model. Use thinking level instead.`).
2. Per the [Gemini 4 Argon developer guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/guides/gemini-4-argon), both `thinking_budget` and `thinking_level="MINIMAL"` return HTTP 400 (`LOW`, `MEDIUM`, and `HIGH` are the only valid levels, same as Gemini 3 Pro). Without `thinkingLevelMap.minimal: null`, `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, "minimal")` resolves to `"minimal"` (`"MINIMAL"`).

### Solution

- Clamp disabled thinking from `"minimal"` instead of `"off"` in `getDisabledGoogleThinkingConfig(model)` so `usesGoogleThinkingLevel(model)` models never fall back to `{ thinkingBudget: 0 }` when `thinkingLevelMap.off` is not `null`.
- Map unmapped `"minimal"` to `"low"` in `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel(model, level)` for Gemini 3 Pro (`/gemini-3(?:\.\d+)?-pro/`) and Gemini 4+ (`/gemini-(?:[4-9]|[1-9]\d)/`) models.
- Add regression tests in `packages/ai/test/google-thinking-level-map.test.ts` covering both omitted reasoning (`{ thinkingLevel: "LOW" }`) and `minimal` reasoning (`{ includeThoughts: true, thinkingLevel: "LOW" }`) on unmapped `gemini-4-argon`.

fixes #11003

prs.title: fix(ai): use OpenRouter-reported total cost
prs.body:
OpenRouter reports the actual amount billed for each request. This will often differ from Pi’s catalog estimate because OpenRouter routes requests to differently priced providers. OpenRouter's [Usage Accounting docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/administration/usage-accounting) explain how this works; we've referenced those docs and the type schemas for making this change.

This commit adds `applyOpenRouterReportedCost` such that for OpenRouter requests, we make `cost.total` be the reported cost. This means
- `cost.total` is the best available total cost
- `cost.input`, `cost.output`, `cost.cacheRead`, and `cost.cacheWrite` remain catalog-derived estimates.
- If the cost is missing or invalid, `cost.total` falls back to the sum of those estimates.
- For BYOK requests, the total includes both OpenRouter’s fee and the upstream inference cost.

We have confirmed for non-BYOK and BYOK (OpenAI and Anthropic) that the cost.total is now correct, where it would in a few cases have been incorrect.

But I'm not sure this is the best solution since now cost.total may intentionally differ from the sum of the component fields.

This fixes #9980, partially addresses #8940 although that also asks for some more metadata like which provider served the request.

releases.name: v1.4.0
releases.body:
### New Features

- **Image input for classifiers**: codemode `models.classify()` accepts `images` for TypeSafe's Jev and Cloudflare's Clef models on `typesafe`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and OpenRouter. See [Use classifier models](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/models.md#use-classifier-models) and [Codemode](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md#models).
- **Models Configuration reference**: every provider, model, model override, and compatibility field of `models.json`, generated from its schema. See [Models Configuration](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/models-configuration.md).
- **Summaries without a fixed output cap**: compaction and branch summaries use the model's output limit, so long reasoning no longer makes them fail. See [Compaction](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/compaction.md#compaction).
- **Codemode waits for a free worker**: parallel scripts and in-process subagents queue instead of failing, and `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` raises the limit. See [Codemode limits](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md#limits).
- **Rex terminal support**: OSC 8 hyperlinks, truecolor, and inline images.

### Added

- Added a Models Configuration reference generated from the `models.json` schema, listing all provider, model, model override, and compatibility fields ([#10790](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10790))
- Codemode `models.classify()` now accepts `images` for TypeSafe's Jev and Cloudflare's Clef models on `typesafe`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, and OpenRouter, and lists Clef Omni and Jev 1.14 on Workers AI.
- Provider-level `compat` in `models.json` now also applies to classifier models, with the System One fields `imageInput` and `sendImageOptInHeader` for proxies that serve another service's classifiers. Extension classifier models accept `compat` too.
- Added `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` to the `minimax` and `minimax-cn` providers, with thinking levels low through max ([#11121](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11121))
- Added support for the Rex terminal: OSC 8 hyperlinks, truecolor, and inline images ([#11131](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11131), [#11150](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11150) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll), [#11183](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11183) by [@nihaals](https://github.com/nihaals))

### Changed

- Provider attribution headers now come from pi-ai's client identity. Extensions' `before_provider_headers` handlers no longer see the OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, and OpenCode attribution headers; returning `null` for one still removes it. Cloudflare requests send pi's detailed `User-Agent` instead of `pi-coding-agent`, as do GitHub release checks for tool downloads, and OpenCode requests send `x-opencode-client` whenever attribution is enabled, not only with a session.
- `generateSummary()` and `generateSummaryWithUsage()` now ignore their `reserveTokens` parameter. Summary requests use the model's output limit instead.
- Changed the default GitHub Copilot model from `gpt-5.4`, which Copilot retired, to `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Changed the default NVIDIA model to `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b` ([#10910](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10910) by [@cv](https://github.com/cv))
- Changed the default Xiaomi model to `mimo-v2.6-pro` for the `xiaomi` and Xiaomi Token Plan providers, since `mimo-v2.5-pro` left the catalog.
- Grok 4.3 and Grok 4.5 on the `xai` provider now offer the `xhigh` thinking level.
- Sign in with ChatGPT: ChatGPT Business workspace usage-limit errors are not retried and tell the user to ask their workspace admin to increase the limit.

### Fixed

- Fixed compaction and branch summaries failing with "generation hit the token cap" when reasoning used most of the fixed summary output limit. Summaries now use the model's output limit, and `compaction.reserveTokens` only controls when compaction starts ([#9512](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9512), [#9075](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9075)).
- Fixed `models.schema.json` missing descriptions for provider and model fields, so editors showed no hints for them ([#10790](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10790))
- Fixed `pi update` failing with "Managed install marker is missing or invalid" when `managed-install.json` starts with a UTF-8 BOM, which Windows PowerShell 5.1 adds when it rewrites the file.
- Fixed HTML export showing literal asterisks for Markdown bold and italic next to CJK punctuation ([#3353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/3353), [#10154](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10154))
- Fixed the terminal staying in mouse-tracking, focus-reporting, Kitty keyboard, and alternate-screen modes when pi exits without its normal terminal teardown, which flooded the shell prompt with escape sequences ([#11170](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11170))
- Fixed concurrent extension `select`/`confirm`/`input`/`editor` dialogs and inline `custom()` components in interactive mode: a second dialog replaced the first and the first promise never settled; closing the visible dialog now shows the previous one again ([#11166](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11166), [#9909](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9909))
- Fixed pasting in the shell hanging after copying text in pi and suspending it with Ctrl+Z on Linux: the background `wl-copy`/`xclip`/`xsel` process that keeps serving the clipboard was suspended along with pi ([#11179](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11179))
- Fixed codemode scripts failing immediately when both codemode workers are busy, for example with parallel codemode calls or in-process subagents. Scripts now wait up to 60 seconds for a free worker, and `PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS` raises the limit of two workers ([#11184](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11184))
- Fixed extensions failing to load when importing `@earendil-works/pi-ai/models` (e.g. for `clampThinkingLevel`) by exposing the subpath through the extension loader aliases and virtual modules ([#11156](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11156))
- Fixed `mcp.json` files that start with a UTF-8 BOM failing to parse, which skipped all their MCP servers and made `pi mcp add`/`pi mcp remove` fail ([#11191](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11191))
- Fixed `/compact <instructions>` ignoring the instructions when summarizing the start of a turn that compaction splits. When the split turn was the only new content since the last compaction, the instructions were ignored entirely ([#11058](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11058))
- Fixed resumed sessions and `/tree` navigation leaving extension tools inactive when the branch recorded its tools before they were registered, such as tools from extensions installed after the session started. Extension tools the branch never added or removed are now active unless they are registered with `defaultActive: false` ([#11062](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11062), [#11075](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11075))
- Fixed sessions breaking after recovery from a response cut off at the output limit: the truncated tool call was omitted but its tool results were kept, so providers rejected every later request ([#11227](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11227), [#11233](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11233) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed the `grep` tool following `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`, where options such as `--fixed-strings` silently changed regex searches into literal ones. The tool now runs `rg --no-config` ([#11203](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11203), [#11230](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11230) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed Windows shell detection rejecting runnable Microsoft Store shell aliases ([#9504](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9504) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed Windows shell detection missing PowerShell outside `PATH` and the legacy WSL `bash.exe` launcher when Windows is not installed in `C:\Windows`. pi now checks `%ProgramFiles%\PowerShell\7`, `%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0`, and `%SystemRoot%` ([#9501](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/9501) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed GitHub Copilot sessions with large request bodies, such as many images, failing with HTTP 413 `failed to parse request` instead of compacting and retrying ([#11016](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11016) by [@petrroll](https://github.com/petrroll))
- Fixed the `openai-codex` provider offering `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, which always fail for ChatGPT accounts ([#11173](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11173) by [@lucasmeijer](https://github.com/lucasmeijer))
- Fixed whitespace-only tool output (for example a bare `\r\n` from bash) making OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Google requests fail with a 400 ([#8720](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8720))
- Fixed automatic retry not triggering for more gateway upstream failures, `stream disconnected before completion` errors relayed by Codex CLI proxies, and transient Google Vertex OAuth token refresh failures, and retrying errors because of digits inside request ids or byte counts ([#10920](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10920), [#11057](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11057), [#10996](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10996))
- Fixed OpenAI Responses models losing the prompt cache on every deferred tool load after a tool was removed ([#10940](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10940))
- Fixed Cloudflare Workers AI classifier pricing: Clef Flash costs $0.038 and Jev $0.042 per million input tokens instead of Jev being listed as free.
- Fixed an unclosed `$$` display-math block swallowing or corrupting every Markdown table after it ([#11159](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11159))
- Fixed Markdown bold and italic not rendering next to CJK punctuation ([#10730](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10730) by [@theBucky](https://github.com/theBucky))
- Fixed `@` file autocomplete returning no results for queries containing regex metacharacters such as `[` or `(` ([#10972](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10972))

issues.title: Managed Agent: list archived Sessions and search by title

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/session-management
labels.description: Session state and persistence

labels.name: roadmap/session-management
labels.description: Roadmap: Session management features

issues.body:
## What would you like to be added?

Session listing in Managed Agent should support an archived filter and a title search.

Today `GET /v1/agents/sessions` and the WebShell list route return only live Sessions, paged by an opaque cursor. Two fields that users expect are declared but not implemented:

- An archived filter (the field exists in the contract as planned, so archived Sessions can never be listed).
- A title search, which has no field at all.

The request is to implement the archived filter on both the public and WebShell surfaces, and to add a title search that works without loading every Session into the client.

## Why is this needed?

Managed Agent already supports archiving and renaming Sessions. Archiving without a way to list archived Sessions makes the operation one-way from the user's point of view: the Session disappears and cannot be found again through the API.

Search matters more as the Session count grows. A user with a few hundred Sessions can only page through them to find the one called "investigate checkout failure". The legacy daemon already offers `sessions/search`, so users moving to Managed lose this ability.

## Additional context

The contract file already reserves the archived field with a "planned" implementation status, which suggests the shape was decided and only the query work remains. The search field is new, so its shape is open: a case-insensitive substring match on the title is probably enough for a first version, with the exact matching rules stated in the contract rather than left to the storage engine.

Whatever is chosen must stay tenant-scoped and must page consistently with the existing cursor behavior, so a search result set cannot leak a Session from another tenant or shift while the client pages through it.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

## 希望增加什么？

Managed Agent 的会话列表应支持归档过滤与标题搜索。

目前 `GET /v1/agents/sessions` 与 WebShell 列表路由只返回活跃会话，使用不透明游标分页。用户期望的两个字段存在缺口：

- 归档过滤：契约中已有该字段但标记为 planned，因此归档会话永远列不出来。
- 标题搜索：完全没有对应字段。

希望做到：在公开接口与 WebShell 两个面上实现归档过滤，并新增标题搜索，且不需要客户端把所有会话拉到本地再筛。

## 为什么需要？

Managed Agent 已经支持归档与重命名会话。能归档却不能列出归档会话，从用户角度看这个操作就是单向的：会话消失了，通过接口再也找不回来。

会话数量增长后搜索更重要。有几百个会话的用户想找名叫「investigate checkout failure」的那个，只能一页页翻。旧守护进程提供 `sessions/search`，迁移到 Managed 的用户会失去这个能力。

## 补充信息

契约文件已为归档字段保留了位置并标记为 planned，说明形状已经确定，剩下的是查询工作。搜索字段是全新的，形状待定：首版用标题的大小写不敏感子串匹配大概足够，但匹配规则应写进契约，而不是留给存储引擎决定。

无论选择哪种方案，都必须保持租户隔离，并与现有游标分页行为一致，确保搜索结果不会泄露其他租户的会话，也不会在客户端翻页时发生漂移。

</details>

issues.title: Add a setting to make top-level subagents run in the foreground by default

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Issue needs to be triaged and labeled

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

A user/project-level setting that flips the default execution mode of top-level regular subagents from background to foreground, for example:

```json
{ "agents": { "defaultBackground": false } }
```

Current precedence is: the explicit `run_in_background` tool argument, then the agent definition frontmatter `background`, then the built-in default (top-level regular agents run in the background). That built-in default cannot be changed globally — `settings.json` only exposes concurrency caps such as `agents.maxParallelAgents` and `agents.maxParallelAgentsByModel`.

With such a setting, users who always want an inline result would no longer have to:

- add `background: false` to every agent definition (built-in agents cannot be edited at all), or
- rely on the model remembering to pass `run_in_background: false` on every call, for example through an AGENTS.md rule.

### Why is this needed?

A background agent result only arrives as a completion notification on a later turn. If the session ends right after the main turn — quitting the TUI, `/clear`, closing the session, Ctrl+C, loop detection, or a turn/time budget limit — running background agents are aborted and their results are lost. In short one-shot conversations, and especially in bot/channel-style sessions that publish one final reply and then close, the background default means work is silently discarded. A configurable foreground default would make "the reply I get is the complete reply" the predictable behavior, with background execution as an opt-in.

### Additional context

- The precedence chain lives in the Agent tool background classification (`backgroundRequested` in `packages/core/src/tools/agent/agent.ts`), documented in `docs/developers/tools/task.md` and `docs/users/features/sub-agents.md`.
- A global default should preserve the existing guards: nested launches stay foreground, headless forks stay background, and unnamed caller-owned `working_dir` launches stay foreground.
- Related but different: #12959 asks for a concurrency setting for background subagents, not a default-mode switch.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

### 希望增加什么？

希望有一个用户级/项目级配置，可以把顶层普通子 agent 的默认执行方式从后台改为前台，例如：

```json
{ "agents": { "defaultBackground": false } }
```

当前优先级是：调用时显式传入的 `run_in_background` → agent 定义 frontmatter 里的 `background` → 内置默认值（顶层普通子 agent 走后台）。这个内置默认值无法全局修改，`settings.json` 里只有 `agents.maxParallelAgents`、`agents.maxParallelAgentsByModel` 这类并发上限参数。

有了这个配置，总是想要同步结果的用户就不必：

- 给每个 agent 定义都加上 `background: false`（内置 agent 根本没法改），或者
- 依赖模型每次都记得传 `run_in_background: false`（例如在 AGENTS.md 里写规则约束）。

### 为什么需要？

后台子 agent 的结果只会在后续轮次以完成通知的形式回来。如果主轮次结束后会话就终止——退出 TUI、`/clear`、关闭 session、Ctrl+C、触发 loop 检测或轮次/时间预算上限——正在跑的后台 agent 会被 abort，结果直接丢失。在简短的一次性会话里，尤其是「发一条最终回复就结束」的机器人/渠道类会话中，默认后台意味着工作被静默丢弃。可配置的前台默认值能让「我拿到的回复就是完整回复」成为可预期的行为，后台执行则变成显式选择。

### 补充信息

- 优先级链在 Agent 工具的后台判定逻辑里（`packages/core/src/tools/agent/agent.ts` 的 `backgroundRequested`），文档见 `docs/developers/tools/task.md` 与 `docs/users/features/sub-agents.md`。
- 全局默认值应保留现有约束：嵌套调用仍为前台，headless fork 仍为后台，未命名的 caller-owned `working_dir` 调用仍为前台。
- 相关但不同的诉求：#12959 要的是后台子 agent 的并发配置，不是默认模式开关。

</details>
