prs.title: feat(memory): add scoped external import jobs for CLI and HTTP
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a Qwen-owned external memory import service for CLI and cloud integrations, starting with Codex. Clients submit relative Markdown paths and contents, inspect a deterministic preview, explicitly select sections and destination scope, then start durable background consolidation using the selected workspace's configured model. Results enter native memory search, fetch, recall and forget. Main checkouts and registered linked worktrees share the imported project layer while ordinary memory isolation remains unchanged.

The service exposes `memory_import_v1`, workspace-qualified HTTP preview/submit/status/source/cancel/retry endpoints, and offline `memory import codex --dry-run --json`. Unknown source scope stays unassigned. The server owns destination paths and validates active workspace trust; it never falls back to the primary runtime. Only selected source snapshots are retained. Journaled publication, idempotency, cancellation and retry protect existing, edited and forgotten memories.

Consolidation uses bounded batches per source project and confirmed scope, a compact same-scope metadata index with relevant evidence, and durable aggregate call/token reservations. Preview exposes usage estimates without reading native memories or invoking a model. Failure, cancellation and retry do not replenish the budget. Saved batch proposals preserve per-source recovery and edit/forget protection; imported repository identity lookups are cached and skipped entirely when no imported layer exists.

## Why it's needed

A cloud runtime cannot read a user's laptop filesystem. Direct per-bullet conversion also loses historical context and does not reconcile old knowledge with existing native memory. This replaces #14149 with shared backend capabilities and model-backed consolidation. No external product UI, independent collector, dependency installation requirement or unrelated CI repair is included.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Submit a synthetic Codex source set containing two projects and a referenced distilled Markdown resource. Preview should return grouped sections, references and assignment reasons without model calls or memory/task writes. An ambiguous section should stay unassigned.
- Select only one project and submit to a trusted non-primary workspace. Observe queued/running/completed results, then fetch its retained source and search the native result. The other project's text must never reach the model or retained snapshot; unknown/untrusted/draining destinations must not fall back to primary.
- Repeat the same request/key and then try another key with the same selected content. Native documents should not multiply. Edit or forget an imported document; another import must return conflict rather than restore it.
- Cancel during consolidation, retry a failed item, and restart after a forced process kill before/after publication. Recovery should wait out a dead worker's lease, preserve accurate counts/refs and publish each document only once.
- Verify the imported project result through a linked worktree, and verify an independent clone remains isolated. Ordinary per-worktree memory must retain its existing behavior.

- Verify a 12-section selected project is processed in two bounded calls, while excluded groups never reach the model. Preview should show group and aggregate usage estimates; retrying a budget-exhausted task must not reset the allowance. Interrupt between publications and verify saved proposals resume without another paid call or restoring edited/forgotten knowledge.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the installed baseline CLI rejected `memory import codex`, and the base daemon did not advertise the capability. After: synthetic shipped-CLI dry-runs (bare, leading debug and safe mode) returned versioned pure JSON with zero network attempts and zero filesystem changes. Confirmed CLI import and the real bundled daemon → real ACP child → loopback OpenAI-compatible model produced native searchable memory without unselected input. Bare/safe confirmed import rejected before source access or authentication.

Initial implementation tests passed: 559 CLI cases, 31 core cases, and the focused cold-workspace ACP bridge case. Full workspace build and typecheck passed; affected packages were rebuilt after final edits, with a final bundle and CLI typecheck. ESLint and formatting passed. Real SIGKILL probes left stale lock directories and recovered automatically after approximately 120 seconds, without manual lock deletion; both interruption points produced one document and correct original-batch counts. Two self-audit passes and a local medium review found no remaining issue; these are not formal approval.

Latest cost update after merging main: 55 focused CLI and 126 core tests passed, along with full build, bundle, typecheck, lint and format. Real bundled CLI/HTTP each processed 12 selected sources as [8, 4], with two requests and no extra request on repetition. Synthetic existing-context payload fell from 199,080 to 2,170 bytes. Interrupted-batch, budget-recovery and cross-group ordering probes passed. Production billing savings are not asserted.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Synthetic CLI, real daemon/ACP/model transport, native memory and process recovery |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Awaiting CI |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Awaiting CI |

### Environment (optional)

Isolated synthetic HOME, runtime, source and repository directories; deterministic loopback provider only. The full build used an 8 GiB Node heap. No actual user memory or production provider was accessed.

## Risk & Scope

- Budget limits: 32 logical invocations and 512,000 conservative reserved token units per task, with 8,192 output tokens per request. These are not guaranteed provider-billed-token or currency caps; oversized metadata/relevant evidence fails closed.
- Main risk or tradeoff: this is a cross-package feature with native memory reader and ACP integration; maintainer architectural review is requested. Model output is schema/native-format checked and cannot overwrite existing documents, but production-model semantic quality still requires evaluation.
- Not validated / out of scope: external product UI, standalone collectors, continuous sync, cross-instance sync and production deployment. SSH workspaces and legacy memory base/local path overrides are rejected in v1. Resource/context limits are documented; oversized context fails instead of silently truncating.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: additive capability and endpoints; ordinary writable memory roots remain unchanged. This does not migrate experimental state from #14149.

Design and API contracts are complete and synchronized in both languages: [Design (English)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import.md), [设计（中文）](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import.zh-CN.md), [API (English)](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import-api.md), [接口（中文）](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/external-memory-import/docs/design/external-memory-import-api.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Supersedes #14149 following the requested backend redesign.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

### 本 PR 的变更

提供由 Qwen 自身负责的外部记忆导入服务，供 CLI 和云端系统接入，首版支持 Codex。客户端提交相对 Markdown 路径和内容，查看确定性预览，明确选择章节和目标范围后，启动使用目标工作区模型的持久化后台整理任务。结果进入原生记忆搜索、全文、召回和遗忘流程。主检出与已注册 linked worktree 共享导入项目层，普通记忆的既有隔离语义保持不变。

提供 `memory_import_v1`、限定工作区的 HTTP 预览/提交/状态/来源/取消/重试接口，以及离线 `memory import codex --dry-run --json`。未知归属保持待分配。目标路径由服务端管理，检查活动工作区信任状态，不回退主运行时。只保留选中来源快照，通过提交日志、幂等、取消和重试保护已有、已编辑和已遗忘的记忆。

整理按来源项目和确认范围分成有界批次，发送紧凑的同范围元数据索引及相关证据，并持久化总调用/token预留预算。预览展示估算，不读取原生记忆、不调用模型；失败、取消、重试不会重置预算。整批提案持久化后支持逐来源恢复，继续保护编辑和遗忘。仓库身份采用有界缓存，没有导入层时跳过遍历。

### 为什么需要

云端运行时无法直接读取用户电脑的文件系统；逐条转换 Markdown 列表还会丢失历史上下文，无法协调历史知识和已有原生记忆。本 PR 以共享底层能力和模型整理替代 #14149。不包含外部产品界面、独立收集器、额外安装要求或无关 CI 修补。

### 评审测试计划

使用含两个项目和一个引用 Markdown 资源的合成来源，验证预览返回分组、引用和归属原因，不调用模型，不写记忆或任务；歧义章节保持待分配。只选择一个项目并提交到可信次工作区，观察任务状态、查看保留来源并搜索原生结果；未选内容不得进入模型或快照，未知、不可信和退出中的目标不得回退主工作区。

重复同一请求/幂等键，再用新键提交相同内容，文档数量不应增加。编辑或遗忘导入文档后再次导入应返回冲突，不恢复内容。验证取消、失败重试，以及发布前后强制结束进程后的重启恢复：等待旧锁租约后自动继续，计数和引用正确且只发布一次。验证 linked worktree 共享结果、独立 clone 隔离及普通记忆原有行为。

### 前后证据

基线已安装 CLI 不支持该命令，基线 daemon 无此能力标识。实现后，成品 CLI 的普通、前置 debug 和 safe 模式预览均输出版本化纯 JSON，零网络尝试和零文件变化。确认后的 CLI 导入，以及真实 daemon → 真实 ACP 子进程 → 本地 OpenAI 兼容模拟模型的链路，均生成可搜索原生记忆且不包含未选来源。bare/safe 模式确认导入在读取来源或认证前被拒绝。

本地通过 559 项 CLI、31 项 core 测试及冷启动工作区 ACP 专项测试。全工作区构建和类型检查通过；最后修改后重新构建受影响包，完成最终 bundle 和 CLI 类型检查。ESLint、格式检查通过。真实 SIGKILL 遗留锁目录，约 120 秒后自动恢复，无需手工删锁；两个中断点均只生成一个文档，原批次计数正确。两轮自审和本地 medium 审查无剩余问题，不等同正式批准。

最新成本更新同步主线后，55 项 CLI、126 项 core 定向测试及全构建、bundle、typecheck、lint/format 通过。真实 CLI/HTTP 均将 12 条选中来源分成 8＋4，只调用两次，重复提交不增加调用；预览展示每组和总用量估算。合成已有上下文从 199,080 降至 2,170 字节，中断恢复、预算不重置与交错项目顺序验证通过。这不是生产账单节省率。

### 平台与环境

macOS 已完成合成 CLI、真实 daemon/ACP/模型传输、原生记忆和进程恢复验证；Windows、Linux 等待 CI。使用隔离的合成 HOME、运行目录、来源和仓库，以及确定性本地模拟模型；全量构建使用 8 GiB Node 堆。未访问真实用户记忆或生产模型。

每任务上限为 32 次逻辑调用及 512,000 个保守预留 token 单位，每次输出最多 8,192 token；不保证供应商实际计费 token 或金额硬上限。元数据或相关证据超限时明确失败。

### 风险、范围与迁移

本功能跨包并接入原生记忆读取和 ACP，需要维护者架构评审。模型输出经过结构化和原生格式校验且不能覆盖现有文档，但生产模型语义质量仍需评估。不包含外部产品界面、独立收集器、持续同步、跨实例同步或生产部署。v1 拒绝 SSH 工作区及旧式记忆 base/local 路径覆盖；资源和上下文限制已说明，超限失败而不静默截断。

新增能力和接口，普通记忆写入根目录不变。不迁移 #14149 的实验状态。双语设计与接口文档内容完整同步，链接见上方。本 PR 按重新设计要求替代 #14149。

prs.title: fix(core): emit protocol-tag sanitization telemetry on the non-streaming route
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes the non-streaming request path emit the same `protocol_tag_sanitized` telemetry (and the matching `debugLogger.warn` line) that the streaming path already emits when the converter strips a trailing orphan `</think>`/`</thinking>` tag from a model answer.

The converter stamps `RequestContext.protocolTagSanitized` whenever the trailing-tag filter removes such a tag, and that stamp is not streaming-gated, so it also lands on the non-streaming route (`pipeline.execute()`). But the only reader of that field lived inside `processStreamWithLogging`, so on the non-streaming route the tag was stripped from the answer with no event and no log line — the answer silently lost text with nothing to observe it. This PR hoists the emission into a single pipeline-level helper that both routes call, and calls it in `execute()` after `convertOpenAIResponseToLlm`, then clears the field.

It also mirrors the streaming route's `toolCallCount` backfill in `convertOpenAIResponseToLlm`: the filter stamps the tag name before the tool calls are read, so a non-streaming response carrying `functionCall` parts used to report `toolCallCount: 0` in the event, contradicting the response's own tool calls.

## Why it's needed

This is an observability gap the trailing-tag filter introduced on the non-streaming route. `convertOpenAIResponseToLlm` is called from real non-streaming call sites (prompt-hook runners, `baseLlmClient`, the managed-agent hosted-hook model), so real user-facing answers can have a trailing tag stripped with the sanitization never surfacing in telemetry or logs. The existing streaming reader is the only thing that turns the stamp into a `ProtocolTagSanitizedEvent`; sharing it with `execute()` closes the gap with one emission site, as the issue proposes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Reproduce the missing emission on the non-streaming route with the real converter, then confirm the new unit tests and the two touched suites.

A minimal real-converter probe (non-streaming) shows the field is produced but never read:

```
$ npx tsx repro_nonstream.ts
[text-only] finish=stop returnedParts=[{"text":"Answer."}]
[text-only] protocolTagSanitized={"tagName":"thinking","toolCallCount":0}
[text+toolcalls] finish=stop returnedParts=[{"text":"Answer."},{"functionCall":...},{"functionCall":...}]
[text+toolcalls] protocolTagSanitized={"tagName":"thinking","toolCallCount":0}   <- count contradicts the two tool calls
```

The new `pipeline.test.ts` case drives `pipeline.execute()` with a mocked completion whose converter sets `protocolTagSanitized` and stamps `toolCallCount: 2` and asserts `logProtocolTagSanitized` is called once with `tagName: 'thinking'` and `tool_call_count: 2` (a stub and an assertion that are both 0 cannot tell a pass-through from a re-stamped count); the new `converter.test.ts` case asserts the count is backfilled from the response's `functionCall` parts, including when the completion carries no `finish_reason` at all. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Destructive check — tests kept, implementation reverted:

```
$ git checkout -- packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/pipeline.ts packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/converter.ts
$ npx vitest run pipeline.test.ts converter.test.ts
 FAIL  pipeline.test.ts > ContentGenerationPipeline > execute > logs protocol-tag sanitization on the non-streaming route
   AssertionError: expected "spy" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
 FAIL  converter.test.ts > OpenAIContentConverter > stream-local parser state > fills toolCallCount for a nonstreaming suffix alongside its tool calls
   AssertionError: expected { tagName: 'thinking', …(1) } to deeply equal { tagName: 'thinking', …(1) }
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  2 failed | 585 passed (587)
```

With the implementation restored:

```
$ npx vitest run pipeline.test.ts converter.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  587 passed (587)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   N/A  |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux (WSL2), Node v24, `pnpm`, unit tests only — `npx vitest run` inside `packages/core`. No TUI/browser surface is involved.

Three review-driven corrections are in the same branch (which is rebased onto `main` `4b136b52`): the `toolCallCount` backfill is keyed on the stamp rather than on a truthy `finish_reason` (an absent reason maps to `STOP`, so the strip and the stamp happened without one and the event reported 0 beside two `functionCall` parts), the route test now stamps and asserts a non-zero count, and the response-converter stub is restored after the case that installs it, with a sentinel pinning it.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `execute()` now reads and clears `context.protocolTagSanitized` after each non-streaming call, so a caller that inspects that field after `execute()` returns will find it cleared — the field is per-request pipeline state and the streaming route has always cleared it after reading, so this only aligns the two routes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full `npm run preflight` gate was not run end to end (it does a clean install, full build and every workspace's suite); the targeted gates that were run are `tsc --noEmit` (clean), `eslint` on the four touched files (clean), `prettier --check` (clean), the two touched suites (585 passed), and the whole `packages/core` suite.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No wire, API or config change.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #13660

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

让**非流式**请求路径也发出与流式路径相同的 `protocol_tag_sanitized` 遥测事件（以及同一条 `debugLogger.warn` 日志）。

当转换器把模型回答末尾的孤立 `</think>`/`</thinking>` 标签剥离时，会写入 `RequestContext.protocolTagSanitized`；该写入并不以流式为条件，因此在非流式路径（`pipeline.execute()`）上同样会发生。但该字段唯一的读取点位于 `processStreamWithLogging` 内部，于是非流式路径上标签被从回答中删掉后既没有事件、也没有日志——回答静默丢失文本，且没有任何可观测痕迹。本 PR 把这段发射逻辑提取为一个管线级方法，两条路径共用，并在 `execute()` 中于 `convertOpenAIResponseToLlm` 之后调用，随后清空该字段。

同时，在 `convertOpenAIResponseToLlm` 中补齐流式路径已有的 `toolCallCount` 回填：过滤器在读取工具调用之前就写上标签名，所以此前带 `functionCall` 的非流式响应会在事件里报 `toolCallCount: 0`，与响应自身的工具调用自相矛盾。

## 为什么需要

这是尾随标签过滤器在非流式路径上引入的可观测性缺口。`convertOpenAIResponseToLlm` 存在真实的非流式调用点（prompt hook runner、`baseLlmClient`、managed-agent 的 hosted-hook model），因此真实回答可能被剥离尾随标签却完全不上报。现有的流式读取点是唯一把该写入转成 `ProtocolTagSanitizedEvent` 的地方；让 `execute()` 复用它，即可用一个发射点补上缺口——与 issue 给出的方案一致。

## 审阅与验证

- 用真实转换器的非流式探针证明字段会产生但无人读取（见英文部分 Before 输出）。
- 新增的 `pipeline.test.ts` 用例驱动 `pipeline.execute()`，断言 `logProtocolTagSanitized` 被调用一次且 `tagName: 'thinking'`；新增的 `converter.test.ts` 用例断言计数由响应的 `functionCall` 部分回填。
- 破坏性验证：保留测试、回退实现后两个用例均 FAIL（2 failed | 583 passed），恢复实现后 PASS（585 passed）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：`execute()` 现在会读取并清空 `context.protocolTagSanitized`；流式路径一直如此，这里只是对齐两条路径。
- 未验证/超出范围：未完整运行 `npm run preflight`（它包含 clean install、全量构建与所有 workspace 的测试）；实际运行的门禁见英文部分。
- 破坏性变更：无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #13660

## AI 参与声明

实现与测试由 AI 编码助手起草；账号本人逐行读过整个 diff，并独立核对了复现、破坏性验证与仓库门禁；本人对内容负责。

</details>

## Highlights

The bundled CLI 0.23.0 includes two fixes requested in #11022:

- Managed memory availability now respects the `memory.enableManagedAutoMemory` setting (#6941). Hosts that disable managed auto memory no longer see remember/dream requests admitted or managed-memory instructions in the system prompt; local patches can be removed.
- Size-triggered microcompaction now clears old tool results toward a low watermark (#8464), so it no longer rewrites another part of the conversation prefix on every subsequent turn. Provider prompt-cache reuse is preserved across long tool-heavy sessions, reducing cached-input cost.

releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v1 -->

## Highlights

_See the complete change list below._

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Complete Change List

### Features

- feat(daemon): support session-targeted Skill and Extension refresh ([#14050](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14050)) by @callmeYe
- feat(runtime-broker): Session-create warm for Workspace-isolated bound Sessions ([#14599](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14599)) by @doudouOUC
- feat(managed-agent): ship a configuration template in the reference distribution ([#14631](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14631)) by @wenshao
- feat(serve): run private CSI file turns through Hosted Harness ([#14487](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14487)) by @doudouOUC
- feat(managed-agent): support local and SSH workspace file references ([#14639](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14639)) by @doudouOUC
- Adds a read-only --check preflight that prints PASS, WARN, FAIL, or SKIP for managed-agent deployment checks and exits nonzero on failure. ([#14632](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14632)) by @wenshao
- Lets a successor Hosted owner finish private CSI file turns that already have durable receipts, preserving tool responses and avoiding repeated file operations. ([#14523](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14523)) by @doudouOUC
- Managed Agent submissions now accept up to 8 MiB of attachment input, preserve large pending requests across refresh, and let users discard unrecoverable drafts. ([#14628](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14628)) by @doudouOUC
- Hosted Turn recovery now asks the Runtime Broker for execution evidence and treats unprovable outcomes as unknown instead of transient faults. ([#14669](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14669)) by @wenshao
- Adds systemd units and setup guidance for single-host managed-agent deployments so Runtime workers stay running when Broker restarts ([#14633](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14633)) by @wenshao
- Parks managed-agent turns with unknown Runtime outcomes for later rechecks instead of repeatedly retrying cancellation, keeping them active and avoiding false FAILED results ([#14681](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14681)) by @wenshao
- feat(artifacts): record files the agent creates or edits ([#14292](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14292)) by @zjgzx1988
- Adds a managed-agent credential bootstrap that generates required deployment tokens and writes protected configuration to simplify secure setup. ([#14634](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14634)) by @wenshao
- Completes private CSI cold recovery so settled file work can resume from saved results without repeating file effects or extra model requests. ([#14695](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14695)) by @doudouOUC
- Adds an optional Generated UI extension that renders model-generated HTML/CSS cards with bounded local JavaScript, letting users adjust inputs without another model turn. ([#14338](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14338)) by @qqqys
- feat(workflow): authorize daemon ancestor workflows ([#14646](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14646)) by @qqqys

releases.name: cua-driver-rs v0.26.0
releases.body:
Qwen CUA Driver prebuilt binaries
(vendored under `packages/cua-driver`).

- **macOS**: codesigned + notarized universal binary + `QwenCuaDriver.app`
- **Linux**: unsigned (x86_64 + arm64, glibc 2.31 floor)
- **Windows**: unsigned UIAccess worker + native SDK payload
  (x86_64 + arm64); deployments must sign and trust the worker
  on the target machine before UIAccess activation
- **Node.js**: the same workflow publishes `@qwen-code/cua-sdk`
  after a clean install against these release assets and publishes
  the same-version browser SDK and `@qwen-code/node-repl-mcp` package
  after its MCP protocol smoke tests

Enable relative coordinates: `CUA_DRIVER_RS_COORDINATE_SPACE=1`
(default `0` = off; optional `CUA_DRIVER_RS_COORDINATE_SCALE=1000`).

Enable textual MCP payload filtering for affected model API routes:
`MCP_MODEL_PAYLOAD_FILTER=1` (default off).

issues.title: bug: SSE retries are capped by the stream-open window, and the HTTP/1.1 fallback returns raw HTTP errors without retries or classification

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Summary

On a transient provider 429 the turn dies with:

```
SSE stream request failed: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests: Upstream model provider is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
```

even with `[retry] max_retries = 35`, and the turn then reports an unrelated budget:
`Retry stopped: empty-stop used 1/2 retries; turn failed`.

Three things combine:

1. the client retry loop is bounded by the stream-open timeout, so `max_retries` above ~8 can never run;
2. the HTTP/1.1 fallback returns a raw response, losing both retries and error classification;
3. provider plan/usage-limit 429s are classified as transient rate limits, so they consume the whole window before failing.

## Environment

- codewhale 0.10.2 (dev), built from `f9fd6a75ec39` (current `main`), Linux
- `[retry]`: `enabled = true`, `max_retries = 35`, `initial_delay = 2.0`, `max_delay = 30.0`, `exponential_base = 2.0`
- `[stream]`: `max_resumes = 10`, `max_transparent_retries = 10`, `max_stream_errors = 10`, `open_timeout_secs = 150`

## What happens

1. `handle_chat_completion_stream` → `open_chat_stream_response` → `open_sse_response`, which wraps the entire attempt in `tokio::time::timeout(open_timeout, attempt(policy))` (`crates/tui/src/client/stream_entry.rs:403`).
2. For the normal dual policy, `attempt` is `open_stream_json_with_retry` (`crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs:1366`) → `send_retry_loop` → `with_retry` with the configured `max_retries`. That loop does inspect the status and retries 429s correctly (`crates/tui/src/client.rs:4243-4266`).
3. With a 2 s initial delay, ×2 backoff and a 30 s cap the waits are 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30, 30…, cumulative 2, 6, 14, 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 s. About 7–8 attempts fit inside a 150 s window; the remaining 28 of the configured 35 never run. `[stream] open_timeout_secs` clamps to `5..=300`, so even at the maximum only 12–13 attempts can run.
4. When the window expires, `open_sse_response` treats it as a response-header stall and retries once over HTTP/1.1 (`stream_entry.rs:435`). That branch sends directly (`crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs:1345-1360`): one attempt, no retry loop, and the response status is never converted into an `LlmError`. The single attempt is deliberate (replay-billing guard), the missing classification is not.
5. The non-success response reaches `crates/tui/src/client/chat.rs:1408`, which bails with an untyped `SSE stream request failed: HTTP {status}: {body}`.

A raw HTTP status can only reach that bail through the single-shot HTTP/1.1 branch (or a client already pinned to HTTP/1): the retry loop converts every non-success status into `LlmError` before returning. So the visible failure is the one attempt guaranteed not to be retried, and it carries no classification — a 401/402/403 that would surface as an auth or quota error arrives as a raw HTTP string.

The `empty-stop` counter in the summary is a third, unrelated budget: `EMPTY_STOP_MAX_RETRIES = 2` (`crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:6393`), hard-coded and not configurable. It requires `stream_errors == 0` and a terminal stop reason, so it cannot describe a 429; the closing line names a budget that did not fail.

## Evidence from stored turns

`turn_outcomes` across sessions touched since 2026-10-12 (two files over 25 MB skipped):

- 7 × `SSE stream request failed: HTTP 429 … temporarily unavailable` (all on 2026-10-21)
- 10 × plan/usage-limit 429s (`You've reached your weekly/5-hour usage limit … limit resets at …`)
- 4 × `Chat Completions stream closed before [DONE] or finish_reason`
- 1 × HTTP 529, 1 × connection dropped mid-body, 1 × `Model stream ended with no answer or tool call`

## Why the plan limits matter

`has_explicit_quota_phrase` (`crates/tui/src/llm_client/mod.rs:933`) matches "insufficient credits", billing-quota wording and "monthly spending limit", but not "usage limit", "reached your … limit" or "limit resets at". A 429 saying `You've reached your weekly usage limit for your plan. Your limit resets at …` is therefore `LlmError::RateLimited` — retryable — so an exhausted plan burns the full retry window and then reports a raw HTTP 429 instead of failing fast as `QuotaExhausted`.

## Suggested fixes

1. Size the open window from `max_retries × max_delay` with an explicit cap, or make the retry deadline per attempt, so `max_retries` is either reachable or honestly bounded by the documented key.
2. Classify the HTTP/1.1 fallback response into `LlmError` so the caller's retry/resume policy applies. This does not require replaying more than the existing single attempt.
3. Extend the quota matcher to "usage limit", "reached your … limit" and "limit resets at", so a plan limit fails fast as `QuotaExhausted`.
4. Report the budget that actually ended the turn in the "Retry stopped" line, or mark it as a per-kind counter so it is not read as the cause.

## Related

- #6699 (closed) — turn failed with no retry when the SSE request never received response headers. This report is the residual in the HTTP/1.1 fallback branch that path introduced.
- #6700 (closed) — configurable stream retry budgets and transport timeouts.
- #103, #6310 — transparent stream retries and empty-stop retries.
- Not the same as #6954, which is about holder gates during resume.

issues.title: Sub-agent max_steps is model-guessed and can only narrow; add an owner-set floor or disable per-call override

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

### What problem does this solve?

`agent` children accept a per-call `max_steps`, and the value is chosen by the model. The model has no reliable way to know how many model turns a task needs: it depends on the number of files, tool latency, retries, context size, and how much re-reading the task requires. A guessed low value kills the child at `turn.at_max_steps()` with `child model-step work budget exhausted`, before it can write a useful report. The parent then usually reports only "the child ran out of budget", and the owner has to retry manually with a larger number.

The existing global key does not solve this:

- `[subagents] default_max_steps` is applied only when the `agent` start has **no explicit** `max_steps` (`crates/tui/src/config.rs:1792-1797`, getter at `crates/tui/src/config.rs:7511`).
- `resolve_max_steps` combines role, configured, and explicit values with `narrow_model_steps` (`crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:306-312`): every layer can only **lower** the budget. There is no lower bound.
- The docs state the same contract: per-call limits "can only narrow" (`docs/SUBAGENTS.md:634-640`).

So an owner can set `default_max_steps = 0` (unbounded), but the model can still pass `max_steps: 12` and lose the run. This is not the old 100k per-step context cap: #6504 was fixed by #6518, and current children compact instead of dying at a context boundary. This is the remaining, model-controlled step cap.

**Reproduction (behavioral, not a crash):**

1. Use `codewhale 0.10.2 (dev)`.
2. Set `[subagents] default_max_steps = 0` (unbounded) and `default_wall_time_secs = 86400`.
3. Ask an agent to start a review child with `max_steps: 12`.
4. The child consumes 12 model turns and ends with `budget_exhausted` / `child model-step work budget exhausted`, often without a final report.
5. In our runs, a larger allowance (15-18 turns) completed the same review; the 12-turn run did not.

The owner cannot make the model "know" the right number. A retry with a larger number is a guess too.

### What should Codewhale do?

Add an owner-controlled policy for child step budgets. Possible shapes, in order of preference:

**A. `[subagents] min_max_steps` (owner floor).**

```toml
[subagents]
min_max_steps = 40
```

- `0`/unset disables the floor.
- After role/configured/explicit values are resolved, clamp the result **up** to at least `min_max_steps`, then apply the hard `MAX_SUBAGENT_STEPS` ceiling.
- The model can request a larger value but cannot go below the floor.
- The effective value and the fact that it was raised should be visible in the child runtime budget context.
- The key should be honored from user and managed config; a project overlay should not be able to lower it.

**B. `[subagents] allow_model_max_steps = false`.**

- Keep `max_steps` parse-accepted for compatibility, but ignore the model-supplied value for `agent` starts.
- Only owner/Fleet configuration sets the child step budget.
- This is closer to "the model cannot influence the limit", but it removes a useful knob from the model entirely.

**C. Remove `max_steps` from the advertised `agent` schema.**

- Keep parsing it for saved transcripts and old clients, but do not advertise it and do not honor it from model-facing calls.
- Operator/Fleet config remains the only source.
- Highest compatibility risk; probably needs a deprecation window.

Whichever shape is chosen, the important properties are:

- the model cannot lower an owner-set floor;
- a low guess is impossible, not merely discouraged by prompt text;
- the hard ceiling (`MAX_SUBAGENT_STEPS = 2_000`, `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:279`) and wall-clock ceiling remain;
- the child sees the effective budget, including "requested X, effective Y (owner floor)";
- `budget_exhausted` must still hand back a partial report rather than silently ending.

### Where?

- [x] TUI (terminal interface)
- [x] CLI command (`codewhale exec`, ...)
- [x] Other / not sure — sub-agent runtime / `agent` tool

### Workarounds or other tools (optional)

Today the only workaround is prompt discipline: tell the parent "do not pass `max_steps`" and rely on the global default. That is not enforceable: a model can forget, or can pass a small number "to be safe". Raising `default_max_steps` does not help when an explicit lower value is present. A `tool_call_before` hook can rewrite `agent` input, but that is a local workaround, not a product guarantee, and it requires every user to build and protect a hook.

### Contributing

- [ ] I would like to open a pull request for this.

### Open questions

- Is a floor (`min_max_steps`) acceptable, or does it conflict with the current "all limits only narrow" safety model?
- Should the floor be managed-config-only, user-config, or both?
- What happens when `min_max_steps > MAX_SUBAGENT_STEPS` or `> wall_time` / role cap: clamp, warn, or fail configuration?
- Should the same floor apply to Fleet task specs and workflow children, or only the interactive `agent` tool?
- Should the model keep any ability to set `max_steps`, or should the field become operator-only?

### References

- `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:306-312` — `resolve_max_steps`; `narrow_model_steps` can only lower.
- `crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:279` — `MAX_SUBAGENT_STEPS = 2_000`.
- `crates/tui/src/config.rs:1792-1797` — `default_max_steps` is a default, not a floor.
- `crates/tui/src/config.rs:7511` — `subagent_default_max_steps` getter.
- `docs/SUBAGENTS.md:634-640` — per-call limits narrow; omission inherits.
- #6504 — old 100k per-step context cap, closed; fixed by #6518.
- #5566, #6198, #3885 — closed budget/default work; not this owner-floor problem.

issues.title: bug: a second session cannot be resumed in one workspace while any session is open (workspace-wide coordination flock)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
## Summary

With one Codewhale session open in a workspace, `codewhale resume` for a **different** session in the same directory is refused:

```
error: canonical history operation mounted-history:<key>; retained outcome must be recovered using this exact key
  caused by: another Codewhale process owns delegated coordination for <workspace>: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)
```

The refusal is clean — the target session's document and runtime store are untouched — but the workflow is blocked. Two sessions with history cannot be open in one folder at the same time; the practical ceiling is one resumed session per workspace.

## Environment

- `codewhale 0.10.2 (dev)`, built from `f9fd6a75ec39` (current `main`), Linux
- Workspace used in the reproduction: `/home/f2/Documents/Shared/Research`

## Steps to reproduce

1. `codewhale resume <session A>` — opens normally.
2. In a second terminal, same directory: `codewhale resume <session B>` — the error above.
3. Quit A, repeat step 2 — opens normally.

While A is open, `/proc/locks` contains a shared lock on the workspace coordination file:

```
FLOCK  ADVISORY  READ  <pid of A>  103:02:<inode>  0 EOF
```

for `<workspace>/.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.lock`.

This is not specific to two sessions: five long-lived sessions in the same workspace held `READ` locks on that file at once, and every `resume` was refused until all five had exited.

## Where it comes from

- Every session acquires the workspace coordination lock in **shared** mode for the lifetime of the process: `new_shared_subagent_manager_with_state_root_and_timeout` (`crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:11281`) calls `require_coordination_process_lock`; on failure that path only warns ("this session cannot append to the shared coordination ledger").
- `resume` and `fork` go through `new_shared_runtime_subagent_manager` (`crates/tui/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:11235`), which sets `coordination_exclusive = true` (`mod.rs:11261`) and treats failure as fatal.
- `flock` cannot take an exclusive lock while any shared holder exists, and it cannot upgrade an existing lock, so retrying does not help.
- The lock is workspace-scoped by design (`docs/architecture/delegated-coordination.md`, "Embedding state boundary"): the worker ledger, transcript artifacts and the coordination lock share `<workspace>/.codewhale/state`. The lock arbitrates **sub-agent write claims**; here it is also acting as the mutex for a **per-session** operation, mounting a different session's document.

The two sessions are not disagreeing about anything: they own different documents and different runtime stores. The refusal comes from a workspace-wide lock held by an unrelated session.

## Expected behaviour

Several independent sessions in one working directory, each with its own history. That is the normal way to use a CLI coding agent — Claude Code, opencode and Codex CLI all support it — and nothing in the two sessions' data overlaps.

## Suggested fix (either)

1. Let a mount take the shared lock, or hold the exclusive lock only for the mount itself and release it immediately, instead of for the process lifetime.
2. Expose `EngineConfig::subagent_state_root` (added for embedding hosts in #5252) as a config key or flag, so a session can use a session-owned coordination root. The architecture document already states the trade-off: different state roots are different coordination domains and do not arbitrate write claims across each other.

## Workaround (verified on 0.10.2)

`flock` is advisory and bound to the inode, so replacing the file lets the next mount proceed:

```bash
mv <workspace>/.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.lock \
   <workspace>/.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.lock.aside-$(date +%s)
codewhale resume <session B>
```

The open session keeps its lock on the old inode; the new mount locks a freshly created file. Caveat: until the older session exits, the two processes sit in different coordination domains and concurrent sub-agent ledger writes are not serialized (tmp+rename keeps the file intact, but the last writer wins), so do not run sub-agents in both at the same time. The workaround has to be repeated before each subsequent mount.

## Related

- #6954 — holder-gate refusals on resume. The maintainers' acceptance run there treats "a resume refused because another TUI holds the workspace lock" as correct behaviour; this issue is the workflow consequence of that rule rather than the same defect.
- #5036 (closed) — isolated-worktree Fleet builders contending on the same lock; a related but different case.
- #5252 — the `subagent_state_root` option for embedding hosts.

issues.title: A saved session document larger than 8 MiB can no longer be resumed or forked, and the refusal names no remedy — the journal is what pushes it over
issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed for: `"transport bound"`, `"exceeds full-history"`,
session document size limit, resume + size, journal + resume. Closest matches:

- **#6842** (open) — the session journal has no bound and grows without limit.
  That is the growth side of the same structure; this report is the *access*
  side: once the file crosses a hard 8 MiB transport bound, the session can no
  longer be opened at all.
- **#6688** (closed) — same class (an oversized input is refused before anything
  runs), different path (`exec` argv vs the session document).
- #6161, #6175, #6361 — unrelated changes that only matched the search terms.

# What happened?

```
$ codewhale resume 481c2659-…
error: selected saved history could not be captured; no mutation attempted
  caused by: session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained
```

The source is retained (good), but there is no way forward. `codewhale fork`
refuses the same way, and I could not find any CLI path that reduces a saved
document: `codewhale --help` lists no prune/compact command, and `codewhale thread`
offers only list/read/resume/fork/archive/set-name/clear-name. The message does
not name the size, the field that dominates it, or any remedy.

Measured on the affected session (the file is 13 982 336 bytes against an 8 MiB
bound, i.e. 8 388 608 bytes):

| part of the document | size (approx, as serialized in the file) |
|---|---|
| whole file | 13.98 MB |
| `journal.entries` (3870 entries) | 8.96 MB |
| `messages` (1361 messages) | 2.96 MB |
| `work_state` / `metadata` | 0.38 MB / 0.13 MB |

The conversation itself is well inside the bound. Only the 1361 journal entries
on the active leaf path are projected into messages
(`crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs:262`, `:329`); the remaining 2509 entries
are abandoned branches — yet the whole document has to fit.

# Steps to reproduce

The check is a plain file-size comparison, so any saved document over the bound
reproduces it deterministically; I did not build a synthetic one, my numbers are
from a real session (a long session with heavy sub-agent use, which is what grows
the journal — see #6842).

1. `stat -c%s ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>.json` — compare against 8 388 608.
2. `codewhale resume <id>` (and `codewhale fork <id>`) → the error above.

Code path, read from `main`:

- `prepare_mounted_session` reads the source with
  `load_session_snapshot_bounded(&id, MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES)`
  (`crates/tui/src/lib.rs:9943`). Every `codewhale resume` goes through this
  (`run_interactive_with_notice`).
- The read refuses before parsing when the *file* is larger than the limit:
  `crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs:3406`
  ("session exceeds full-history transport bound; source retained").
- `MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024`
  (`crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:79`; the entry-count sibling is at `:78`).
- The same constant bounds the serialized mutation request, which embeds the
  whole document as JSON: `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:221` —
  so raising only the read would not be enough; the transport itself is bounded.

Recovery that worked by hand (and is what a supported path would need to do):
keeping only the active leaf path in `journal.entries` took the file from
13.98 MB to 7.61 MB and the session resumed. It costs the abandoned branches'
structure (`/branch` history), which is why it should be an explicit,
maintainer-designed operation rather than a user's manual surgery. The same
operation is not the only lever — any bound change has to keep the request under
the same limit, because the document travels inside it.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
today (`MAX_CANONICAL_HISTORY_BYTES` is unchanged).

# Where did it happen?

- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Impact: the session is readable in files but unreachable from the product; the
only routes left are manual surgery on the JSON or discarding the session.

Options as I see them (maintainer's call):

- **A. Transport only what the operation needs.** The canonical handoff needs
  the messages, the journal witness (leaf + entry count) and the metadata; the
  journal body is copied only because the target document is the source document.
  A host-side rebuild of the target document would remove the journal from the
  payload entirely.
- **B. Make the bound count the projected history, not the file**, or expose it
  as a bounded, documented knob. `messages` here was 2.96 MB of a 13.98 MB file.
- **C. Keep the bound and make the failure actionable**: name the size and the
  dominant field, and provide a supported prune/compact command that drops
  journal entries outside the active path (with a dry run and a backup), so an
  oversized session is recoverable. Also worth a pointer to #6842.

Open questions: is 8 MiB a memory/allocation guard or an API payload guard? Should
a journal that is not projected into messages count against it at all? What is a
user expected to do today when a session crosses it — is discarding the session
the intended outcome?

Verification (for A/B/C, once the direction is chosen):

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/session_manager.rs
```

Out of scope:

- Bounding the journal itself (#6842).
- Changing the conversation, or auto-truncating history on resume.

issues.title: codewhale resume refuses any session whose saved history still holds a raw sub-agent handoff — the canonical acknowledgement compares the Engine-restored messages with the saved document
issues.body:
# Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate.

Searched open and closed in this repository: `"mailbox acknowledgement"` → 0,
`"selected saved history"` → 0, `"exceeds full-history"` → 0, `"retained outcome"`
→ 6 unrelated results (release and PR titles). Closest reports, each a different
mechanism: #6102 (closed — resume failed with ENOENT while resolving the runtime
store dir), #6225 (closed) and #6418 (closed) — older "cannot restore/resume"
reports. None of them mention this comparison.

# What happened?

`codewhale resume <id>` fails deterministically for a saved session, and no
retry or recovery route works:

```
$ codewhale resume f5ba9347-…
error: canonical history operation mounted-history:48204ec8-…; retained outcome must be recovered using this exact key
  caused by: canonical history mailbox acknowledgement changed
```

Expected: the session resumes. The suggested recovery ("retained outcome must be
recovered using this exact key") cannot succeed, because the recovery path runs
the same acknowledgement: `settle_prepared_history_operation` also calls
`synchronize_history_operation` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1032`;
the fresh path is `:1663`).

# Steps to reproduce

1. In a project, run `codewhale` and have the session spawn a sub-agent (the
   `agent` tool) so a `subagent_completion` handoff is appended to the live
   history. Let the turn end and quit.
2. Confirm the saved document still holds the RAW envelope: the message has
   exactly two text blocks, block 2 is exactly
   `<turn_meta>\nInput provenance: subagent_handoff (non-authoritative)\n</turn_meta>`
   and block 1 starts with `<codewhale:runtime_event kind="subagent_completion"
   visibility="internal">` (`crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:15`).
3. `codewhale resume <id>` → the error above.

Observed on a 351-message, 3.97 MB session with 5 such envelopes: every attempt
failed. After neutralising the recognition of those 5 messages in the saved data
(renaming the transport tag so the restore projection becomes a no-op), the same
command resumed normally and printed `Resumed session: …`.

# Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.1 (dev)`, built from a git checkout. Still present on `main`
(today): `synchronize_history_operation` is unchanged at
`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`.

# Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)
- CLI command (`codewhale resume`, `codewhale fork`)

# Operating system

Linux

# How did you get Codewhale?

Built from a git checkout

# Provider and model

custom openai-compatible route (does not matter — the failure is before any provider call)

# Terminal and shell

tmux + fish

# codewhale doctor (optional)

Not run for this report; the refusal happens in the resume preflight, before the
TUI starts, and leaves no log line in `~/.codewhale/logs/`.

# Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

Written from reading `main` (not a guess at the cause):

- `RuntimeThreadManager::synchronize_history_operation`
  (`crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs:11684`) sends `Op::SyncSession` and then
  requires `observed.messages == session.messages` (`:11708`-`:11713`), i.e. the
  Engine's post-restore messages must equal the saved document byte for byte.
- The Engine's restore first replaces every live sub-agent handoff with a
  restored checkpoint: `Engine::restore_session_history`
  (`crates/tui/src/core/engine.rs:2931`) calls
  `runtime_handoff::project_owned_messages_for_restore`
  (`:2959` → `crates/tui/src/runtime_handoff.rs:918`,
  rewrite decision in `rewrite_message_for_restore`, `:927`, recognition in
  `raw_runtime_handoff_text`, `:1042`).
- So the two sides are structurally different objects whenever the saved
  document still holds a raw envelope, and the equality can never hold. The
  document only becomes "projected" after a *successful* restore persists it,
  which is exactly the step this check forbids — the first canonical resume of a
  session that used sub-agents is the failing case.

Suggested fix directions (maintainer's call):

- **A. Make the acknowledgement projection-aware.** Compare against
  `project_owned_messages_for_restore(session.messages.clone())` (plus the
  compaction checkpoint step `compaction::restore_compaction_checkpoint`, to
  mirror `restore_session_history` exactly). The same codebase already does this
  for the sibling rollback check: `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/apply.rs:1406` projects
  `.messages` before demanding that the Engine acknowledged them.
- **B. Persist the projected form** so a saved document is always in the form a
  restore produces (bigger change; it would drop raw envelopes from saved
  sessions earlier than today).

Related, found while recovering this session: a refused canonical attempt still
publishes a holder thread plus an uncommitted turn operation in the Runtime
store. Once the document is repaired, the next attempt then stalls on the holder
checkpoint (`saved holder checkpoint differs from the saved history; refresh
history`, `crates/tui/src/runtime_api/thread_history.rs:1255`) and, with the
checkpoint refreshed, on `saved holder has a successor outside the selected
document` (`:1281`) — the holder fingerprints the pre-repair bytes. A refused
attempt could avoid publishing a holder, or the repair path could refresh it.

Done when:

- [ ] a saved session whose history still contains a raw `subagent_completion`
      (or `subagent_failed` / `waiting_for_subagents` / `agent_topology`)
      envelope resumes through the canonical path;
- [ ] `codewhale fork` works for the same session;
- [ ] the acknowledgement still refuses a genuinely changed history (an Engine
      that did not install the document), i.e. the check is not simply removed;
- [ ] a regression test in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs` (`mod mounted_history_tests`)
      saves a fixture session containing one raw handoff envelope and asserts the
      mounted resume succeeds.

Verification:

```sh
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib
scripts/dev-test.sh crates/tui/src/lib.rs mounted_history_tests::
```

Out of scope:

- The sub-agent handoff wire format and the restore rendering itself.
- The size bound on the saved document (separate report).

issues.title: Deferred-toolbox eviction is economically net-negative under provider prompt caching: full-prefix re-prefill + write premiums, permanent stale recovery notes, wire-byte-blind budget
issues.body:
### What happened? 发生了什么？

The bounded deferred-tool toolbox (`ToolActivationCache`, 8 names / 16 KiB, `crates/tui/src/core/session.rs:17-19` at HEAD `008d21d69`) is **cost-blind**, and under current provider prompt-cache pricing its eviction path is economically net-negative. Concretely:

**1. Eviction invalidates the entire downstream prefix — the one toolbox operation with no offsetting benefit.**
The prefix fingerprint is `SHA256(system) + SHA256(tools wire array)` with order load-bearing (`crates/tui/src/prefix_cache.rs`), and tools sit at the front of the rendered prompt on every provider. Any admission/eviction mutates the tools array, so system + tools + the **entire conversation history** re-prefills at miss price. `docs/CACHE.md` calls this "an expected, one-request miss" (lines 39-40) — wording written when cache writes were free:

| Provider/API | Cached-input read | Write premium | Tool-change invalidation |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat/Responses | 0.1x | 1.25x (GPT-5.6+) | prefix from that point (tools are first) |
| Anthropic Messages | 0.1x | 1.25x (5m) / 2x (1h) | **any tool change invalidates the entire cache** (tools are block 1) |
| DeepSeek | 1/30 – 1/50 | none | prefix-based |
| Moonshot Kimi k3 | 0.1x | 1x (5m) / 2x (1h) | prefix from that point |

Break-even for evicting one ~400-token schema from a session with H tokens of history: pay ≈ 0.9–2.25 × H once, save ≈ 0.9 × 400 per later request → needs ~75 further tool-free requests at H = 30K. Real conversations run 6–40 requests. Admission at least unlocks a needed capability; **eviction only pays when the session is about to end anyway**. LRU position alone is the eviction trigger today — no hysteresis, no cost term, and two alternating overflowing searches would re-prefill the full prefix every round.

**2. The eviction→recovery cycle multiplies the loss (relevant to the in-flight reporting work).**
Reporting evictions (as the Pinvou fork's open PR #101 does) is necessary for correctness — silent eviction caused a live incident where a model fabricated tool results for tools that had vanished from its `<functions>`. But the recovery contract ("re-search to re-activate") completes a cycle whose full cost stack, for one eviction of 4 browser tools (~460 tokens of schema) in a 30K-token history with 20 requests remaining (0.1x reads, 1.25x writes):

| # | Cost item | Tok-eq |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eviction invalidation (re-prefill + write premium) | ~34,500 |
| 2 | Eviction note in history (≈72–147 tokens/event; rides the result forever; 1 + 19×0.1x) | ~427 |
| 3 | Recovery re-search round trip | ~3,050 |
| 4 | Search-result payload becomes history | ~1,160 |
| 5 | Re-activation invalidation (tools array changes again — second re-prefill + write) | ~34,500 |
| | **Total vs never evicting** | **≈ 73,600 (~2.5× the entire history)** |

Two structural gaps in the reporting design: (a) **notes are never retracted** — ride-time netting (`render_toolbox_eviction_notes`) only trims the note at the moment it attaches to a result; once in history it is permanent, and the only "compaction" that removes it is generic conversation compaction; (b) **re-activation carries no supersession marker** — the re-admitting search result is byte-identical to a first-time hit (`tool_references` list only), so after recovery the model's history permanently contains "these tools are no longer callable" next to a tools array that has them again. (Compare: the direct-call hydration path does emit an explicit "was deferred and has now been loaded" receipt.)

**3. The headline saving is first-turn-only, and the budget does not measure wire bytes.**
The historical justification ("reduce catalog tokens 73%") measures a first-request, native-tools-only, `bytes/4`-estimated ratio — no provider, no tokenizer, no MCP, caching never modeled. Under caching, both an eager stable header and the deferred header are hit-priced after request 1; the durable steady-state saving is ~0.1x-scale. Separately, the 16 KiB toolbox budget is measured in engine-side serde bytes (`ToolActivationCache::serialized_bytes`), while the same tool serializes differently per wire family (Chat Completions wrapper ~69 B/tool, Anthropic ~40 B, Responses ~71 B) and per-provider sanitizers (Moonshot MFJS, root-level `oneOf/anyOf` flattening) change schemas further — so the budget is a proxy that matches no provider's actual token accounting.

**4. In practice the mechanism survives by accident.**
Across five real sessions on k3/DeepSeek (93–94% hit ratios with heavy `tool_search` churn vs 92.5% baseline without), activation happened at request 1 (short history) and the surface then stayed stable within turns. The measured re-prefill drivers were skill loading and engine restarts — not tool_search. The one live failure (mid-task silent eviction) is exactly the case with no offsetting saving.

### Expected 期望

Surface-change decisions — especially LRU eviction — should be cost-aware or at least cost-attributed, and the eviction-recovery loop should not leave permanent stale statements in history:

1. **Hysteresis / eviction economics**: a minimum activation lifetime, or an eviction cost term once current re-prefill size exceeds a few multiples of the evicted schema. Pure LRU position makes mid-task eviction the default worst case.
2. **Update `docs/CACHE.md`**'s "expected, one-request miss" for the write-premium era, and reconcile observed `cache_hit_tokens`/`cache_miss_tokens` against declared `change:<what>` re-pins — today telemetry and decisions never meet (`calculate_cache_savings` is `#[cfg(test)]`-only).
3. **Supersession semantics for recovery**: when a reported-evicted tool is re-activated, emit an explicit restored/re-admitted marker (hydration-receipt style) so the history's "no longer callable" note is not left as the last word; consider bounding note persistence (e.g. drop after the next successful activation of the named tools, or fold into compaction).
4. **Evaluate append-in-context injection** for dynamic tools (Moonshot's documented pattern: keep the top-level `tools` array stable, append dynamic declarations as a trailing system message inside `messages`) — zero prefix invalidation by construction, which sidesteps items 1 and 5 of the cost stack entirely.
5. **Measure the toolbox budget in wire-shaped bytes** (or tokenizer tokens) per active wire format rather than engine serde bytes.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Economic issue rather than a crash; the observable sequence:

1. Start a conversation that activates ≥8 deferred tools (e.g. a browser task: `tool_search` for browser tools, then a second search for page-management tools).
2. Observe the second search silently evicting earlier activations from the request tools array (no model-visible signal at HEAD `008d21d69` — `delta.evicted` is consumed by `remove_evicted_cache_activations` in `execute_tool_search_inner`, `tool_catalog.rs:1546-1551`).
3. Watch `/cache stats` + provider usage: the next request reports a miss covering the full history; on Anthropic routes the write premium applies; re-searching to recover triggers a second full miss + write.
4. Cross-check the arithmetic against `calculate_turn_cost_from_usage_with_prision`-billed totals for the session.

### Codewhale version 版本

`008d21d69` (workspace 0.10.2; latest tag v0.10.1) — verified at this HEAD on 2026-10-13; the mechanism is unchanged from v0.9.12 through HEAD. Observed live via the Pinvou downstream (fork pinned at v0.9.12 + maintenance), engine-level, platform-independent.

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

Engine — affects all surfaces (TUI / CLI / Desktop / Web) and all providers with prefix caching, which in 2026 is all of them.

### Before you start 前置确认

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。（recent 100 issues swept for tool/cache/deferred/eviction — no overlap）

issues.title: 0.10.2: Read-only roles have no second route when Web fetch fails — no network in bash, no curl fallback, no browser

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: Agent blocked; requires human decision or credentials

labels.name: subagents
labels.description: Sub-agent orchestration, lifecycle, and completion handling

labels.name: web-search
labels.description: Web search tool, search backends, result parsing, and browser/fetch search UX

issues.body:
## Why this matters

Every research and verification subagent runs read-only. A read-only role has no network in `bash`, no `curl` escape hatch, no persistent PTY, and — per #5904 — no browser habit. When `Web fetch` fails, such a role has no route left at all.

On the session that found this, the combination forced both research children onto the single weakest tool available and made a whole class of source unreachable. One child additionally misdiagnosed the restriction, reporting "bash denied for non-admitted programs" — the label was wrong, the restriction is real, and a role with no way to test it will guess.

## Current behavior

- `bash {"read_only": true, "command": "curl -sS --max-time 20 https://gitee.com/..."}` -> `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: gitee.com`, `http=000`.
- `bash {"read_only": true, "command": "date -u"}` -> works. So this is network isolation, not a program allowlist.
- `shell_fallback_available()` (`crates/tui/src/tools/web/fetch.rs:380`) is true only for `ShellPolicy::Full`; `network_authorized()` (`fetch.rs:384`) respects a `network_access: Some(false)` authority envelope that also removes the web tools from the registry.
- #5904 records the same gap directly: "Read-only Fleet roles (explore/scout) additionally cannot fall back to `curl` (blocked by the read-only shell grammar by design), so when the Web tool fails, agents without the browser habit just lose the source."

This is by design, and coherent in isolation. The problem is the composition: read-only + no network + fragile extractor leaves the research path as a single point of failure.

## Desired behavior — a decision is needed

Pick one and record it:

- **(a)** Allow read-only roles bounded outbound HTTP GET — no shell, no writes, no credentials in the request.
- **(b)** Make the Web tool strong enough that read-only roles never need a second route (see #7038).
- **(c)** Keep the restriction and state it in the role's own guidance, so a subagent reports "I could not fetch this" rather than inventing a cause or implying no network exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One of (a)/(b)/(c) is chosen and written down.
- [ ] An explore-role probe fetches one JS-shell URL and one raw file from a git host, or reports the restriction explicitly by name.
- [ ] No role reports a network restriction as a different fault (program allowlist, missing binary, blocked command).

## Related

#5904, #6531 / CW-6931, #7038 (the fetch-escalation half of the same chain), #3834.

issues.title: 0.10.2: Provider-native search returns unvalidated citations — a returned URL 404s and a fabricated PR reference reached a subagent's conclusion

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: web-search
labels.description: Web search tool, search backends, result parsing, and browser/fetch search UX

labels.name: reliability
labels.description: Reliability, flaky behavior, retries, fallbacks, and robustness

issues.body:
## Why this matters

A wrong-but-confident search result is worse than no result. It is indistinguishable from a verified one, it propagates into subagent conclusions, and it costs the most tokens to discover.

In the session that found this, a fabricated citation was reported by a child research agent as an established fact. Nothing in the response shape let the child tell synthesis from evidence.

## Current behavior

`Web action=search` on the current route is answered by the provider model, not by an index. Receipt from the session:

```
"source": "provider-native/deepseek/deepseek-flash"
"count": 3
capabilities: max_results=supported, recency=unsupported, domains=unsupported,
              locale=unsupported, published_date=unknown
receipt.honored: { max_results: true, recency: false, domains: false }
```

Four defects:

1. **Citations are never validated.** A URL returned as a search result was fetched immediately afterwards and came back `HTTP 404` with `<title>404 Not Found</title>`. It had been presented as a citable source.
2. **Synthesis is the same object as results.** `message` holds fluent prose; `results[].title` is frequently the bare domain (`"title":"www.theverge.com"`). The shape invites treating prose as evidence.
3. **A confident wrong answer never falls back.** `SearchBackendChain::from_context` (`crates/tui/src/tools/web/backend.rs:127`) plus `run_backend_chain` advance the chain only on `Err`, so the DuckDuckGo and configured-provider fallbacks are unreachable whenever the native backend returns prose.
4. **`max_results` is reported as honored while ignored.** `max_results: 8` was requested and 3 results returned with `honored.max_results: true`.

### Verified false citation

A child agent reported that winit PR **#3748** was "Add OpenHarmony support". Actual:

```
$ gh api repos/rust-windowing/winit/pulls/3748 --jq '.title'
Remove myself as codeowner            # merged 2024-06-22
$ gh api repos/rust-windowing/winit/pulls/4684 --jq '.title, .state'
feat: add OpenHarmony platform backend
open                                  # updated 2026-10-08
```

The real PR is #4684. The child passed search synthesis into its report unchanged.

A second instance: the search backend returned a Verge URL that resolved to `404` — see the receipt above.

## Desired behavior

1. Every returned URL is validated (HEAD, or a bounded GET) before it is citable; dead links are dropped or explicitly marked `dead`.
2. Provider synthesis gets its own field (e.g. `synthesis`) separate from `results`, and cannot be the sole content of a successful search.
3. `recency` and `domains` are either honored or the request is rejected. Never report `honored: true` for a capability that was ignored.
4. `max_results` is honored, or the receipt reports the shortfall.

## Repro or evidence

Source `28ada98a94`, 2026-10-21. The receipts above, the 404 fetch, and the two `gh api` calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A search result whose URL returns 404 cannot be presented as a citable result.
- [ ] `results` contains only validated entries; provider synthesis lives in its own field.
- [ ] `honored` reflects reality for every capability flag, including `max_results`.
- [ ] A fixture whose native backend returns a dead URL either falls through to the next backend or fails loudly.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that a bare-domain-only `title` is not emitted as a result title.

## Related

#6531 / CW-6931 (closed in v0.10.1; covered pre-emption and the missing recency/domain wiring, not citation validity), #7037 / CW-7480 (DeepSeek search parser test), #6508 (native answers cut at 4,000 chars), #5037.

issues.title: 0.10.2: Web fetch never escalates to the configured browser, and discards page metadata when a JS shell defeats extraction

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: web-search
labels.description: Web search tool, search backends, result parsing, and browser/fetch search UX

labels.name: tools
labels.description: Tool execution, tool schemas, tool UX, and built-in tool behavior

issues.body:
## Why this matters

Research and verification lose primary sources whenever a page is client-rendered. Chinese vendor documentation (Huawei / OpenHarmony), documentation portals and pricing pages are shaped exactly this way, so the loss is systematic rather than random.

The session that found this **already had a working browser connected** (Playwright MCP, `browser_navigate` resolved the same URL), and the fetch path neither used it nor named it.

## Current behavior

`Web action=fetch` on a 2xx whose body carries no readable node raises `js_required_error`, retries once past every cache, then fails terminally:

```
No readable page content was found at https://consumer.huawei.com/cn/support/content/zh-cn16091898/
after 2 attempts, the second past every cache (attempt 1: HTTP 200; attempt 2
(Cache-Control: no-cache): HTTP 200). The response parsed but held no readable body, which usually
means the page renders its content with JavaScript. Recovery: no Codewhale web tool runs JavaScript
(`web.run` shares this fetch and extractor), so opening the URL again returns the same shell.
```

Four separate defects in that one message:

1. **The recovery claim is false when a browser is registered.** `web.run` does share the extractor, but a browser MCP server connected to the same session renders the URL correctly. `js_shell_recovery` (`crates/tui/src/tools/web/fetch.rs:399`) has role-aware branches for `web_tool_available()` and `shell_fallback_available()`, but no branch for "this session owns a browser surface".
2. **The page's own metadata is discarded.** The same URL with `format: "raw"` returns 200 with a populated `<title>` and `meta[name=description]`. `html_title()` already exists (`crates/tui/src/tools/web/extract.rs:505`); nothing reads `meta`/`og:description` as a degraded result, so a page with a perfectly usable summary is reported as unreadable.
3. **The threshold is tuned for prose, not documents.** `meaningful_text()` (`crates/tui/src/tools/web/extract.rs:473`) requires >=32 non-whitespace characters and >=5 tokens, with `script`, `style` and `noscript` blocked at `extract.rs:437`. Any SPA shell falls under that regardless of how much real content its payload carries.
4. **The cache-busting retry works** and should be preserved — this issue is about what happens after it fails.

## Desired behavior

1. When extraction fails on a 2xx, return a degraded result instead of an error: title, `meta[name=description]`, `og:description`, canonical URL and best-effort text, marked `partial: true` so the model can judge the source.
2. When a browser surface is available to the session, the recovery text names that exact tool. Automatic escalation (fetch -> browser render -> extract) is the better end state; naming the tool is the minimum.
3. Never assert "no Codewhale web tool runs JavaScript" while a browser tool is registered.
4. Keep the existing cache-busting retry.

## Repro or evidence

Source `28ada98a94`, 2026-10-21.

1. `Web {"action":"fetch","url":"https://consumer.huawei.com/cn/support/content/zh-cn16091898/","format":"text"}` -> the error above, HTTP 200 on both attempts.
2. `Web {"action":"fetch","url":"<same>","format":"raw"}` -> HTTP 200, `<title> 华为鸿蒙电脑融合开发引擎（Linux子系统）相关问题 | 华为官网</title>` and a populated `meta[name=description]`.
3. `mcp_playwright_browser_navigate` on the same URL -> page title `华为鸿蒙电脑融合开发引擎（Linux子系统）相关问题 | 华为官网`. The browser is in-session and works.
4. `https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/doc/harmonyos-guides/ndk-development-overview` fails identically in text mode.
5. `https://docs.openharmony.cn/...` is itself an SPA (`<noscript>...doesn't work properly without JavaScript enabled`) and will never be readable by extraction alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A 2xx with no readable body returns title + description metadata with `partial: true`, not an error.
- [ ] With a browser surface registered, the failure text (or an automatic escalation) names it; the "no Codewhale web tool runs JavaScript" sentence cannot appear in that state.
- [ ] A fixture SPA shell carrying `<meta name="description">` yields the description.
- [ ] The cache-busting retry still fires (no regression in the `fetch.rs` attempt sequence).

issues.body:
## Symptom

Typing a message that mentions MCP shows the send-time plugin toast
**"This looks like convex work — install it from catalog …"**. It has nothing
to do with the question; the message was asking why MCP servers were not
connecting.

## Mechanism — reproduced deterministically

`crates/tui/src/plugins/matcher.rs` matches a draft against catalog-declared
`keywords`, `domains` and the plugin `name`, guarded by ASCII word boundaries
and a short generic-word stoplist. The Convex catalog entry
(`anthropic:convex`) declares 15 keywords including **`mcp`**:

```json
"keywords": ["convex","backend","database","realtime","reactive","websocket",
             "auth","storage","scheduler","cron","agent","rag","mobile",
             "typescript","mcp"]
```

Running the real matcher over the shipped catalog (295 candidates) against the
exact draft that triggered it:

```
ALL matching terms (longest first):
  'mcp'  ->  convex
```

It was the only candidate that matched any term. Toast text comes from
`crates/localization/locales/en.json:588-590`.

## Why this is a policy collision, not a typo

`GENERIC_TERM_STOPLIST` (`matcher.rs:83`) is deliberately short —
`accessibility, automation, browser, browsers, chrome, codebase, docs,
documentation, extension, extensions, screenshot, screenshots, web, website,
wiki` — with a comment recording the "#6290 rework" decision that *declared
keywords are the catalog author's call*. `mcp`, `agent`, `tool`, `model` and
`session` all match on purpose, and a test enforces it
(`declared_vocabulary_matches_and_only_mechanics_filter_terms`).

But `mcp`, `agent`, `tool`, `model` and `session` name the host's own features.
A draft that mentions them is not evidence the user wants a particular vendor's
plugin; it is evidence they are talking about Codewhale.

## Options

**Option 1 (recommended) — the host's own vocabulary joins the stoplist.**
Add the host concepts to `GENERIC_TERM_STOPLIST` and to the mirrored `STOPLIST`
in `codewhale-plugin-marketplace/scripts/check-marketplace.mjs`. The two lists
are required to change together; the script rejects a manifest keyword that is
on it, so a catalog author finds out at review time instead of the term
silently never matching. `code` and `data` are in the same family and probably
belong in the same decision.

Costs: the list itself; the two tests that currently assert `mcp`/`agent`/
`tool`/`model`/`session` match; and any catalog manifest declaring one of those
words has to drop it.

**Option 2 — fix the Convex manifest only.** Remove `mcp` (and arguably
`agent`) from that entry. Smaller, but the next catalog author re-creates the
defect and the marketplace script will not catch it.

Either way this changes a decision recorded in the code, so it wants an
explicit call rather than a drive-by edit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] "why did my mcp servers get stuck at connecting" produces no plugin
      toast.
- [ ] A draft naming a genuinely distinctive term (`convex`, `supabase`,
      `stripe`) still produces one.
- [ ] The marketplace check passes against the shipped catalog.
- [ ] Whichever list changes, the Core list and the marketplace `STOPLIST` agree.

issues.body:
## Symptom

The session-page footer can read `MCP · N connecting` and never settle, on a
config whose servers have all finished (or failed) their handshakes.

## What was tried

Isolated home, the same 7-server `mcp.json` (aws, github, linear, playwright,
stripe, chrome-devtools, moda), run on the installed RC (`0.10.2 cc4b96dc0544`)
and on current `main`, footer captured at 3/6/10/15/20/30/45/60 s. Both settled
within 6 s and held:

```
t=3s   MCP · connecting (2) · connection failed (1)
t=6s+  MCP · connection failed (2) · authorization required (3) · connected (2)
```

So the happy path is fine. **This report does not include a reproduction**, and
that is the first thing to fix: the mechanism below is the strongest candidate,
not a confirmed cause.

## Mechanism

Four facts in `main`, in order:

1. **The UI seeds a prediction, not a fact.** `tui/app/init.rs:1082` sets
   `mcp_initializing = !mcp_connecting.is_empty()`, where `mcp_connecting` is
   the *eager set* (`required` plus whatever `tools.always_load` covers) read
   from config **before any handshake happens**.
2. **The engine is supposed to replace it** with `Event::McpSessionBoot`,
   `finished: true`, which sets `app.mcp_initializing = false`
   (`tui/ui/event_loop.rs:7446`).
3. **Every emission is fire-and-forget.** All call sites in `core/engine.rs`
   (`7916, 8103, 8249, 8325, 8414, 8499, 8510, 8776`) are
   `let _ = self.tx_event.try_send(...)`, and `emit_mcp_session_boot` (`:8037`)
   returns early — emitting nothing — when
   `snapshot.servers.is_empty() && connecting.is_empty()`.
4. **Nothing reconciles.** `app.mcp_initializing` is a bare `bool`
   (`tui/app.rs:2283`) with no timestamp, no TTL and no periodic re-emit.

So the chip is "connecting" because one message never arrived, and nothing will
ever correct it. Any of these produces it:

- the `finished` event is dropped when the engine→UI channel is momentarily
  full (`try_send` failure is silent);
- the engine's snapshot is empty for its own reasons (config load differing
  from the UI's) while the UI's prediction was non-empty;
- the boot task is aborted at a session/workspace boundary
  (`drop_mcp_pool`) after the UI was told "booting" and before a settled event
  lands.

`tui/session_boot.rs:235` makes the same bet in the render layer:
`unnamed_connecting = configured_count` while `snapshot.is_none()`, so a
prediction alone can paint `N connecting`.

## Proposed fix

Make the chip **fail closed to settled, not open forever**:

1. **Stamp the seed.** Add `mcp_boot_started_at: Option<Instant>` to `App`, set
   beside `mcp_initializing = true`, cleared on any settled event. In
   `SessionBootSurface::from_parts`, treat `initializing` as false once the
   stamp is older than a bound comfortably above the slowest cold start. That
   bound must exceed `connect_timeout` (30 s default) plus a first-run
   `npx -y`/`uvx` package fetch; `engine.rs`'s `MCP_BOOT_UI_WAIT` already
   reasons about this, so reuse that reasoning rather than adding a second
   number.
2. **Stop discarding the settlement.** Either send the `finished` event with
   backpressure instead of `try_send`, or re-emit the snapshot once on the next
   supervisor tick if `mcp_boot_in_flight` has gone false while the UI still
   believes it is initializing. The 5 s supervisor tick already exists, so this
   needs no new timer.

When the deadline passes with no snapshot, say something true and actionable
(e.g. the servers the last snapshot knew about, or point at `/mcp`) rather than
leaving a prediction standing as fact.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Seed the chip, drop the `finished` event, advance past the bound: the
      chip settles and does not claim "connecting".
- [ ] A real cold start of a slow `npx`/`uvx` server still shows "connecting"
      while it genuinely is.
- [ ] The normal path is unchanged: settles within today's window.
- [ ] A test pins the dropped-event case so this cannot regress.

## Notes

Repro attempt and full code tracing are documented operator-locally; no
provider spend, no CI, macOS only. Windows/Linux and the desktop/web surfaces
were not exercised.
