issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A WhatsApp group's session acquires a spurious `conversations` row with kind="direct" but peer_id equal to the group's own JID, gets promoted to role="primary" in session_conversations, and every subsequent inbound message for that group then fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'`.

### Steps to reproduce

No confirmed deterministic manual repro. Observed correlation (not proven causal) across two independent occurrences on the same long-lived WhatsApp group session, both times while Control UI/dashboard `chat.history`/`chat.metadata` RPC calls against that session were failing with errorCode=UNAVAILABLE, errorMessage="session history is rebuilding; retry shortly" — i.e. dashboard access to the session's history while the WhatsApp channel is actively processing a message for that same session.

### Expected behavior

Inbound messages for a WhatsApp group should always resolve to the existing kind="group" conversation row for that peer_id. No kind="direct" row should ever be created with a peer_id that is a group JID, and session_windows.chat_type for a group session should remain "group".

### Actual behavior

conversations table ends up with two rows for the same peer_id (120363429459936309@g.us): one kind="group" (correct, original) and one kind="direct" (spurious). The spurious row is promoted to session_conversations.role="primary" for the session, demoting the correct group row to role="related". session_windows.chat_type for that session then reads "direct" instead of "group". Every subsequent inbound message for the group fails with:
Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'
Reproduced twice in one calendar day on the same session_id, both times yielding the identical spurious conversation_id hash (conv_183828435603d295e6cd182f3d908148) — consistent with the conversation-ref hash being deterministic over (channel, accountId, kind, peerId, parentConversationRef, threadId), so the same wrong inputs regenerate the same wrong row.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1 (first occurrence), 2026.8.2 (second occurrence, same day, after upgrading)

### Operating system

Windows 11 Pro

### Install method

npm global install (openclaw package). Gateway run as a Windows Scheduled Task service, loopback bind.

### Model

deepseek-v4-flash (custom-registered model entry, not in built-in catalog)

### Provider / routing chain

WhatsApp channel -> OpenClaw Gateway (local, loopback) -> agent "wa" -> DeepSeek API (openai-completions-compatible, api.deepseek.com). Fallback chain (gpt-5.4, claude-sonnet-5) not implicated; failure occurs at the conversation/session bookkeeping layer, before any model call.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Custom deepseek-v4-flash model entry with manually-declared contextWindow/contextTokens. session.dmScope="per-channel-peer". tools.sessions.visibility="self". tools.agentToAgent enabled. No custom hooks touch conversation identity resolution.

### Logs

```shell
"message":"message processed: channel=whatsapp chatId=+52XXXXXXXXXX messageId=3AD1AC718294DC014478 sessionId=be37c314-124e-4823-9466-cb86754e8ef3 sessionKey=agent:wa:whatsapp:group:120363429459936309@g.us outcome=error duration=178ms error=\"Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: index 'idx_agent_conversations_identity'\""

Preceding, repeatedly, at the time of both occurrences:
"message":"⇄ res ✗ chat.history 133ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=session history is rebuilding; retry shortly"

conversations table excerpt (sanitized):
{"conversation_id":"conv_2954465dff82db10951e6b76b19da7a5","channel":"whatsapp","account_id":"default","kind":"group","peer_id":"120363429459936309@g.us", ...}
{"conversation_id":"conv_183828435603d295e6cd182f3d908148","channel":"whatsapp","account_id":"default","kind":"direct","peer_id":"120363429459936309@g.us", ...}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Sanitized SQLite excerpts and a full trajectory export (openclaw sessions export-trajectory) are available on request.

### Impact and severity

Affected: a single WhatsApp group channel used for team/business communication (one agent, one account). Severity: blocks workflow entirely — total inbound-message outage for the affected group until a manual database repair (delete the spurious row, restore role="primary" on the correct group conversation, respecting the partial unique index on session_conversations.role='primary'). Frequency: intermittent, but recurred twice within roughly 9 hours on the same session_id. Consequence: missed incoming business messages until manually detected and fixed; no automated alerting surfaces this failure mode.

### Additional information

Jarvis is the display name/persona of the WhatsApp bot as seen by the group's human participants, not an OpenClaw-internal name — included for context since it appears in session labels/logs. Not confirmed as a regression: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO on last-known-good version, as this was not deliberately bisected. Suspected root cause (unconfirmed): the dashboard/session-resolution code path may create conversation rows without the WhatsApp admission context (group vs. direct) available, defaulting to kind="direct" keyed by whatever raw JID it has, instead of resolving the existing kind="group" conversation for that peer_id.

**Environment**
- OpenClaw: 2026.9.6 (upgraded from 2026.9.5)
- Host: Linux arm64, 16 vCPU cloud instance

- Main gateway process (`node ... gateway`) consistently shows 240–276% CPU
- Memory usage climbs to 6.7–8.5 GB
- Problem returns 1.5–3.5 hours after each restart
- `sessions.list` and `sessions.preview` operations repeatedly take 3+ seconds in the "materialize" phase

**Relevant log excerpts**
```
[sessions] slow session list operation=sessions.list
  handlerElapsedMs=3313–3317
  phaseDurationsMs={"setup":0,"materialize":3264–3282,...}
[sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite coordinator lock wait ... operation=cron.job-family-adoption
[sessions] slow session list operation=sessions.list ... materializedRowCount=100 dirtyRowCount=309
```

**Likely cause**
New 30-day usage reporting and session index materialization (added in 2026.9.6) appears to be getting stuck in a hot loop of repeated full materializations and SQLite lock contention.

Host CPU alerts firing; gateway becomes unresponsive for other work.

**Workaround**
Restarting the gateway temporarily lowers CPU, but the issue recurs.

**Request**
Please investigate the session materialization / usage reporting path in v2026.9.6.

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.6, Usage → **Started by** reports substantial identifiable scheduled usage as **Unattributed**, while **System** shows zero tokens. Existing cron sessions lack creator metadata, and the usage projection has no attribution for those sessions despite surviving metadata identifying their cron origin.

This is an observed attribution/legacy-data compatibility gap, not a claim that newly created cron sessions always lose attribution. The lifecycle stage responsible for missing metadata has not been established.

## Exact observed reconciliation

Date range: **2026-08-26 through 2026-09-24 inclusive**, Australia/Sydney. Read-only inspection of stored usage rollups reproduces every displayed session count, token total and rounded cost:

| Started by | Sessions | Tokens | Cost shown |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared owner | 9 | 31,091,998 | $49.80 |
| Unattributed | 80 | 21,958,218 | $37.48 |
| main (agent) | 2 | 2,561,343 | $2.01 |
| System | 2 | 0 | $0.00 |

The **21,958,218 unattributed tokens** break down as:

| Identified workload | Tokens |
|---|---:|
| Daily memory-maintenance cron | 7,202,105 |
| Weekly memory-review cron | 2,874,879 |
| Release-check cron | 3,118,272 |
| Two recovery cron jobs | 529,218 |
| One deleted dashboard session | 8,054,776 |
| Other sessions | 178,968 |

**62 cron instances account for 13,724,474 tokens and $14.94448776**—62.5% of the Unattributed bucket. Those are identifiable scheduled sessions, not unexplained model requests. Two newer sessions with explicit `createdActor.type = "system"` are recognized as System, but have zero cached tokens.

## Evidence and mechanism

- The existing daily/weekly memory and release-check session nodes have no `createdActor` or `createdVia` in their stored entries.
- `session_windows` / `session_transcript_archives` metadata still identifies cron-origin session keys, including historical instances.
- The deployed usage projection reads `session.storeEntry ?? session.creatorEntry`, then `entry?.createdActor`. If the actor is missing it immediately returns the unknown creator bucket: [projectUsageCreator in v2026.9.6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.6/src/gateway/server-methods/usage.ts#L118).
- Historical attribution depends on available current/family creator metadata. Identifiable historical usage can consequently remain unattributed.
- The deleted dashboard session contributes another 8,054,776 tokens / $22.295539. Its session key survives in archive metadata, but its creator was not recoverable from the records inspected. This is a related historical-attribution preservation concern, **not evidence that it should automatically be assigned to the owner**.

Inspection used cached `session-cost-usage-rollup-v3` records, session-node/window/archive metadata, and filename-based archive-cache mapping. No transcript message bodies were read, no cache rebuild was triggered, and no production state was changed. This reconciles the displayed cache snapshot; it does not certify completeness against provider billing.

## Observed reproduction path

1. On an upgraded installation with existing scheduled-session history, open Usage for a range containing cron runs.
2. Observe Started by → Unattributed despite identifiable cron activity; System may show zero.
3. Inspect the corresponding session entries: `createdActor` is absent, while persisted session metadata identifies their cron origin.
4. Sum their cached usage in the same date range and compare with the Unattributed bucket.

This was reproduced/reconciled on an existing installation. A fresh-install synthetic reproduction and a precise first-affected release have **not** been established.

## Expected behaviour / suggested investigation

- Preserve explicit session-creation attribution for scheduled work, including across reset, archival and deletion where usage history is retained.
- Establish whether this case requires a legacy-data migration/backfill, a current writer/lifecycle repair, or both.
- Where trustworthy persisted scheduler provenance exists, resolve scheduled work consistently with the explicit System attribution path. Do not blindly infer human ownership, or turn arbitrary user-controlled session-key text into trusted identity.
- Keep genuinely unknown historical creators unknown; ideally explain missing legacy attribution in the UI.

Useful regression coverage: creatorless legacy cron history; new cron creation/execution/reset; archival/deletion with retained usage; genuinely unknown history; and unchanged aggregate token/cost totals after attribution repair.

## Separate from usage ingestion failures

Related deployment also has usage-refresh worker heap-exhaustion report #156898. This issue is intentionally narrower: the usage above is **already present in stored rollups**, but its creator projection is unknown. A failed refresh is not required to explain that projection. We have not proven a shared cause or causal independence of their histories, and missing main-session usage is not part of this issue's reproduction claim.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a **bounded launch contract** for Swarm `agents.run` so a verification lane can be stricter than an ordinary collector without gaining new authority.

Implementation: #155442.

### Proposed API

`agents.run(..., { boundedLaunch })` may specify:

- `boundary: "isolated" | "summary-only" | "evidence-only" | "artifact-only"`;
- `requirements.sandbox: "require"`;
- required candidate/artifact fields;
- a `candidateBinding` containing candidate/source/recipe/policy digests.

The contract is monotone: it can only remove explicit handoff information or request stricter existing admission. It cannot grant tools, credentials, approval, publish, merge, or deploy authority.

### Architecture boundary

This is the freeze/seal measurement seam:

`explore -> select -> freeze/seal exact candidate -> bounded launch -> verify`

That vocabulary matches current OpenClaw concepts: frozen/sealed candidates, candidate bindings, and bounded launch contracts.

Adaptive population dynamics, novelty/disagreement/correlation feedback, phase classification, sampling temperature, and compute allocation remain caller/plugin policy (#158068), not core launch authority.

### Ownership

- `sessions_spawn` owns admission/execution.
- The existing sandbox path owns sandbox admission.
- The registry owns replay/idempotency.
- Existing tool/source policy remains authoritative.

### Evidence

#155442 proves boundary projection, authority-shaped-field rejection, fail-closed sandbox admission, exact candidate binding, replay invalidation across candidate/source/recipe/policy, legacy behavior, and real native-path execution.

### Product decision requested

Should OpenClaw expose this narrow generic bounded-launch primitive in core?

Maintainer edits are enabled.

issues.body:
# Bug: App "Update" 按钮失败 - plugin-target-unavailable

## 现象
用户在 OpenClaw Desktop App 点击"更新"按钮，失败并提示：
```
plugin-target-unavailable
Exit code: 1; packages or registry are available, use openclaw update --tag <older-version>, 
or disable the affected plugin and retry.
```

## 根因
当用户安装了自定义插件（通过 `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/` 安装），且这些插件的 `package.json` 包含 `overrides` 字段时，`control-ui` 触发路径在 validating 阶段会因 npm peerDependencies 冲突而失败。

受影响的自定义插件示例：
- `@openclaw/deepseek-provider` (path: `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-deepseek-provider-*/package.json`)
- `@openclaw/duckduckgo-plugin` (path: `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-duckduckgo-plugin-*/package.json`)

这些插件的 `package.json` 中有 ~30 个 `overrides` 条目，用于锁定依赖版本。当 App 触发更新时，validation 步骤尝试解析这些插件与新 core 版本的兼容性，npm overrides 导致解析失败。

## 对比
- **CLI 路径** (`openclaw update --yes`)：✅ 正常工作
- **App control-ui 路径**：❌ 失败，plugin-target-unavailable

## 复现步骤
1. 安装带有 npm overrides 的自定义插件
2. 在 App 中点击"更新"按钮
3. 失败，错误码 plugin-target-unavailable

## 临时解决方案
```bash
# 1. 禁用自定义插件
openclaw plugins disable deepseek duckduckgo
# 2. 执行更新
openclaw update --yes
# 3. 重新启用
openclaw plugins enable deepseek duckduckgo
```

## 建议修复方向
`control-ui` 触发路径的 validation 步骤应跳过或宽容处理自定义插件（非 stock 插件）的 peerDependencies 冲突，与 CLI 路径保持一致。或者在 validation 失败时给出更明确的错误信息，指示用户禁用特定插件后重试。

## 系统信息
- OpenClaw 版本: 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)
- Node 版本: v24.21.0
- 平台: macOS 15.8 (x64)
- 自定义插件数量: 3 (deepseek, duckduckgo, lean-offline)

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

An observed gateway preparation pause delayed the first model request by about two minutes and coincided with a 122.8-second heartbeat timer overrun and channel reconnection.

## Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Expected behavior

The same running gateway normally completes preparation in seconds. Later observed turns in the same conversation completed preparation in under four seconds; the observed two-minute heartbeat gap is abnormal relative to the recovered gateway.

## Actual behavior

One request reached the gateway, then the aggregate preparation interval labeled session-resource-loader took 124,108 ms. The model call started only after this interval. The gateway then reported a 122,811 ms heartbeat gap, and WhatsApp reconnected. The eventual reply was acknowledged about 167 seconds after arrival. Mac power logs did not show a corresponding sleep/wake transition.

## OpenClaw version

Observed release string: OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (2b26444). The deployment carries previously reviewed local changes. The new incident diagnostic patch has not been applied. These observations have not been reproduced on current upstream main.

## Operating system

macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon; gateway Node 24.21.0.

## Install method

Source checkout with a launchd-managed gateway and a versioned runtime build.

## Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw embedded agent through the configured OpenAI subscription route. The measured pause preceded the model call.

## Additional provider/model setup details

Durable SQLite-backed conversation. Exact private history is unavailable for public sharing. This report does not claim that database size or the aggregate preparation label identifies the underlying cause.

## Logs

```text
original request: received t=0
preparation: session-resource-loader=124108ms
heartbeat overrun: gapMs=122811
model request starts after preparation
WhatsApp reconnect: approximately t=139s
reply send acknowledged: approximately t=167s
```
Durations and ordering are extracted from production logs. Identifiers and message contents are omitted.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

A separate process loaded the exact runtime resource loader in 1.7 ms; settings preparation took 305 ms. A consistent database snapshot reproduced a 16.9-second event-loop block while opening the database, with CPU profiling showing about 16.6 seconds inside a full SQLite integrity check. No matching slow database-open record from the gateway process was found for the original incident, so this is a separate reproduced concern, not an established explanation for the 124-second pause.

## Impact and severity

One observed private direct-chat request was delayed about 167 seconds, with channel disruption during the pause. The gateway recovered. Frequency and exact triggering operation remain unknown.

## Additional information

Related but not equivalent: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144592 tracks asynchronous storage work, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153432 now addresses one synchronous interrupted-replay path. Neither has been demonstrated to explain this incident. A prepared diagnostic patch separates transcript-state, session-open, replay, bootstrap, settings, and resource-loader timings; it has not been submitted, built, or activated. No minimal deterministic reproduction is available yet.


## Proposed follow-up and acceptance criteria

1. Add timing around transcript-state lookup, session opening, replay preparation, bootstrap, settings, and resource loading, correlated with event-loop delay. Reconcile the inspected source with the exact loaded build before attribution.
2. Capture the delayed operation during a recurrence, or reproduce it with an isolated synthetic database/history fixture. Keep the separate integrity-check reproduction separate unless the live path is demonstrated.
3. Submit a focused change for the proven operation, preserving persistence, cancellation, and replay behavior. Compare affected behavior before and after with the smallest relevant regression tests.
4. Verify the built/activated revision, responsive gateway heartbeat/channel handling under the reproducer, and an acknowledged end-to-end reply. A successful health endpoint alone is not closure evidence.

This is an AI-assisted report of measured production symptoms. A deterministic upstream reproduction and permanent fix remain outstanding.

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156230

These reports describe distinct observed phases; a shared root cause has not been established.

## Summary

## Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

## Expected behavior

Later observed requests on this deployment completed preparation in under four seconds. A private request with a short exact-response prompt should not spend over a minute preparing before inference, and preparation diagnostics should let operators distinguish the delayed operation.

## Actual behavior

The hosted request spent 65,985 ms in system-prompt preparation and 66,168 ms in total preparation, then successfully answered in a 6,850 ms model interval. A separate queued local-provider request spent 150,845 ms in system-prompt preparation, followed by a roughly 50 ms model attempt. Resource-loader work in those runs took 55 and 224 ms, respectively. The hosted request also waited about 44 seconds in the session queue, so an 85-second CLI wait expired before the successful final result was available.

Observed release string: OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (2b26444). The deployment carries previously reviewed local changes. The new incident diagnostic patch has not been applied. These observations have not been reproduced on current upstream main.

macOS 27.0 (26A428), Apple Silicon; gateway Node 24.21.0.

## Install method

Source checkout with a launchd-managed gateway and a versioned runtime build.

## Model

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash for the successful hosted check; configured local deepseek-v4.1-flash for the other measured preparation span.

## Provider / routing chain

Hosted check: OpenClaw -> official DeepSeek endpoint. Other measured preparation: OpenClaw -> operator-managed local OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint. The reported intervals precede inference.

## Additional provider/model setup details

Both timings come from the same preserved durable conversation after compaction. The successful hosted check requested a short exact response with delivery disabled.

```text

bundle-tools completed @121ms
system-prompt:65985ms@66106ms
session-resource-loader:55ms
model interval: durationMs=6850
terminal result: successful, exact expected response

Current evidence does not isolate the slow operation or prove a continuous synchronous event-loop block.

## Impact and severity

Two observed preparation delays in one conversation; the hosted diagnostic succeeded but its overall queue-plus-preparation latency exceeded the CLI wait. The last observed later replies were faster. Recurrence conditions remain unknown.

## Additional information

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148349 corrected attribution of tool preparation, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153432 addresses a separate interrupted-replay boundary. Neither establishes a fix for these observed system-prompt spans. This report is separate from the original 124-second session-preparation/channel stall. ## Proposed follow-up and acceptance criteria

1. Instrument runtime-prompt lookup, docs/source resolution, memory-prompt plugins, optional project-memory lookup, and synchronous prompt assembly separately. | `sources/` | 46 | no `type` |
| `reports/` | 10 | no `type` (1 also: no frontmatter — `reports/lint.md`) |
| `concepts/` | 4 | no `type` — these are OKF-imported pages, see #156209 |
| `syntheses/` | 1 | no `type` |
| vault root | 4 | no frontmatter (`AGENTS.md`, `WIKI.md`, `Willkommen.md`, `inbox.md`) |

## Why this is worth fixing

**This is an enhancement, not a bug report** — the vault works fine as a wiki, and the OKF docs describe `wiki okf import` as an ingest path, not an export format. But the asymmetry is worth a look:

1. **The importer enforces OKF conformance on the way in, and nothing enforces it afterwards.** `wiki okf import` skips any concept without a non-empty `type` (`missing-type` warning). So a page must be OKF-conformant to get in, and then stops being conformant the moment it lands. Verified: re-importing an imported page fails with `missing-type` (filed as #156209).

2. **There is no way to get a vault back out as OKF.** `openclaw wiki okf` only has `import`. A user whose vault *is* their OKF corpus has no round-trip, and the corpus is non-conformant regardless.

3. **OKF §11 makes it cheap and safe.** Adding `type` is additive — §11 explicitly says consumers MUST NOT reject a bundle for unknown `type` values or unknown extra keys. Nothing to change for existing consumers.

4. **A vault page is a "Concept" in OKF's sense** (§2: "A single unit of knowledge within a bundle, represented as one markdown document"). A natural mapping already exists for each directory:
   - `sources/` → `type: source`
   - `reports/` → `type: report`
   - `syntheses/` → `type: synthesis`

## Concrete request

Populate a top-level `type` on generated pages, using the directory as the default:

```yaml
type: source        # sources/
type: report        # reports/
type: synthesis     # syntheses/
```

Our vault alone would go from 17 → ~77 conformant pages with that one change.

## Secondary, smaller points (same theme)

**a. `okf_version` has nowhere to live.** OKF §12 allows `okf_version: "0.2"` in a bundle-root `index.md` frontmatter block — and that is the *only* place frontmatter is permitted in an `index.md` (§8). But the vault-root `index.md` is plugin-generated and contains a managed block (`<!-- openclaw:wiki:index:start -->`), so a user can't safely add the key. Consider emitting it during generation.

**b. `status: active` on imported pages.** `wiki okf import` writes `status: active`, while OKF §5.4 defines the lifecycle vocabulary as `draft | stable | deprecated`. It is tolerated as an unknown value, but it does not map to a lifecycle state (absent `status` means `stable`). `stable` would be the conformant choice. Also noted in #156209.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), Linux x64
- Bundled `memory-wiki`, `vaultMode: bridge`, `renderMode: obsidian`
- Audit method: walked the vault, parsed each file's YAML frontmatter block, checked for a non-empty `type` per OKF §11 rules; `index.md`/`log.md` excluded as reserved (§3.1)

Happy to help test.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Declaring any `models.providers.openai` block in config (even `models`-only, with `models.mode: "merge"`) silently switches **every** `openai/*` model from the implicit Codex harness to the embedded `openclaw` harness on a ChatGPT OAuth setup. Adding `models.providers.openai.agentRuntime: { id: "codex" }` does not restore Codex and does not fail closed either: runs keep succeeding on the `openclaw` harness.

Side effects observed on the default model (`openai/gpt-6-astra`): effective context drops from 828,400 (`contextTokensSource: runtime`) to 272,000 (`resolved`), the system prompt grows from ~30.8k to ~80.2k chars, and `costUsd` starts being reported. Separately, a partial `models` array wipes displayed metadata (input/context shown as `-`) for the non-declared OpenAI models.

The motivation was raising `contextTokens` for two models; there is no other place to set it (`agents.defaults.models.*` only accepts `agentRuntime`, `alias`, `codeMode`, `params`, `pickerRuntimes`, `streaming`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.5, OpenAI via ChatGPT OAuth profile, no `models.providers.openai` in config, default model `openai/gpt-6-astra`.
2. Baseline turn:
   ```sh
   openclaw agent --agent <id> --session-key "agent:<id>:t-base" --model openai/gpt-6-astra --json -m "Reply only: ok"
   ```
   → `agentHarnessId: "codex"`, `contextTokens: 828400`, `contextTokensSource: "runtime"`.
3. Add model entries (here: the 8 bundled manifest entries for gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4-pro, gpt-5.4-nano, copied verbatim minus `status`/`replacedBy`, which the schema rejects):
   ```sh
   openclaw config set models.providers.openai.models '<json array>' --strict-json --merge
   ```
4. Repeat the turn → `agentHarnessId: "openclaw"`, `contextTokens: 272000`, `contextTokensSource: "resolved"`.
5. `openclaw config set models.providers.openai.agentRuntime '{"id":"codex"}' --strict-json --merge` and repeat → still `openclaw`, 272000.
6. Also tried declaring the provider with the Codex route shape (`baseUrl: "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex"`, `api: "openai-chatgpt-responses"`, `auth: "oauth"`) plus the same models → still `openclaw`.
7. `openclaw config unset models.providers.openai` → back to `codex`, 828400.

Variant: declaring only two entries in `models.providers.openai.models` makes `openclaw models list` show `-` for input/context on every other OpenAI model, including the default.

### Expected behavior

- With `models.mode: "merge"`, authored model entries should merge into the provider catalog without changing the route or harness selection of the provider or of other models.
- Explicit provider `agentRuntime.id: "codex"` should either select Codex or fail closed, as documented in `gateway/config-agents/runtime-and-cli-backends.md` ("makes Codex a fail-closed requirement").
- Ideally, a supported way to override `contextTokens` for a single model without authoring the whole provider.

### Actual behavior

Any authored `models.providers.openai` disables the implicit Codex harness for all OpenAI models; explicit `agentRuntime: codex` is silently ignored and runs continue on the embedded harness with a smaller effective context.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

### Operating system

macOS 27.0 (arm64)

### Install method

npm (global, bundled Node 24.19.0)

### Model

openai/gpt-6-astra (default), also observed on openai/gpt-5.6-sol, openai/gpt-6-sol, openai/gpt-6-luna

### Provider / routing chain

openai (ChatGPT OAuth profile) → implicit Codex harness (baseline) vs embedded openclaw harness (after override)

### Additional provider/model setup details

`models.mode: "merge"`. `agents.defaults.models` has `"openai/gpt-6-astra": {}` (no per-model runtime). Related but distinct: #156122 / #155989 (GPT-6 Sol/Luna discovery), #155937.

### Logs

Relevant `agentMeta` diff for the same prompt on `openai/gpt-6-astra`:

```
agentHarnessId       base=codex    override=openclaw
contextTokens        base=828400   override=272000
contextTokensSource  base=runtime  override=resolved
systemPrompt.chars   base=30819    override=80239
costUsd              base=None     override=0.226
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See logs above; reproducible on every run.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: OAuth/Codex users who author any `models.providers.openai` entry (for example to fix context metadata or register a model missing from the catalog).
- Severity: silently changes the harness and effective context of the default model for all agents.
- Frequency: always.
- Consequence: smaller effective context, different tool/prompt behavior, and no supported path to raise `contextTokens` on the Codex route.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)`
- Linux x64, Node `v24.19.0`
- Gateway: single process, local loopback, systemd user service, 14 agents / ~490 sessions
- Providers in play: one hosted OpenAI-compatible provider (`openai-completions` API), one local `ollama`, one managed local `llama-cpp` (embeddings-only)
- Relevant config: `gateway.reload` **unset** (runtime default = `hybrid`)

## Summary

A config hot reload that touches `plugins.entries.*` invalidates the plugin inventory. If an **auth-triggered** prepared-model-runtime publication is in flight at that moment (in our case because the provider was simultaneously returning HTTP 401 and rotating auth profiles), the publication resolves a **stale plugin generation** and fails with:

```
[agents/prepared-model-runtime] auth-triggered model runtime refresh failed:
PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.
```

`onOwnerFailure` only **logs a warning** — it does not re-materialize the owner against the new plugin generation. The affected owner therefore stays unpublished, and every consumer of the model catalog fails with:

```
Error: Model catalog is not ready. Retry after Gateway startup or refresh finishes.
```

until something else happens to republish it.

Observed duration: **~61 minutes** (first failure `08:23:31`, last catalog failure `09:24:20`), driven by a failure burst that lasted **under one second**.

## Impact

- Control UI Models page: *"部分模型无法刷新。请打开「模型」重试。"*
- `models.list` → `UNAVAILABLE: Error: Model catalog is not ready.`
- `chat.metadata` → `UNAVAILABLE`
- `sessions.list` slow — the `modelCatalog` phase alone measured 1.1–11 s, and `sessions.list` handlers up to 11 s
- On a multi-agent host this reads as "the whole model layer is down", while the Gateway itself is healthy and the provider is reachable (chat completions returned HTTP 200 throughout)

## Timeline (all timestamps `+08:00`)

```
08:16:11  hosted provider returns HTTP 401 for the configured key
          → [agent/embedded] failover decision=rotate_profile reason=auth

08:22:50  [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload
          (plugins.entries.<plugin>.config.<key>)
08:22:57  [reload] config hot reload applied
          (plugins.entries.<plugin>.config.<key>)     ← plugin inventory invalidated

08:23:31.357  [agents/prepared-model-runtime] auth-triggered model runtime refresh failed:
08:23:31.484  PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled;
08:23:31.931  use its current tools.
   (+2 more in the same second → 5 total, ALL inside 08:23:31)

08:23:31.448  [gateway] request handler failed: Error: Model catalog is not ready.
                       Retry after Gateway startup or refresh finishes.   ← first catalog failure

08:29:34  [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload
          (agents.entries.<id>.model.primary, auth.profiles.<provider>:setup-<uuid>)
08:29:37  [reload] config hot reload applied

08:33:29  [ws] res ✓ models.authRefresh 1869ms
08:33:47  [diagnostic] lane task error:
          "Explicit auth order for <provider> has no usable profiles."

08:34:19  [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload
          (agents.entries.<id>.model.primary)
08:35:50  [reload] config hot reload applied
08:35:50  [ws] res ✓ models.authRefresh 90079ms                     ← 90 s
08:35:17  [diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=warning reason=rss_threshold
          rss=2.18 GiB threshold=2.09 GiB
08:36:06  [ws] res ✓ models.authRefresh 1942ms

09:24:20  [ws] res ✗ models.list … "Model catalog is not ready."     ← last catalog failure
```

Totals in the `08:00–10:00` window:

- `auth-triggered model runtime refresh failed` → **5** (all at `08:23:31`)
- `Model catalog is not ready` → **24** (excluding `raw_params` self-echo), spanning
  `08:23:31.448` → `09:24:20.202`

Note the asymmetry: **5 log lines in one second** produced **~61 minutes** of catalog outage.

## Code pointers

Bundled `dist/prepared-model-runtime-*.mjs` (names from the installed 2026.9.5 tree):

- `drainPendingAuthMutations(commit)` →
  ```js
  authPublication.drain({
    owners,
    publish: async (entries, includeCredentialProviders) =>
      await publishPreparedModelRuntimeOwnerBatch({
        entries, owners, agentBuildCompletions,
        buildTimeoutMs: modelRuntimeBuildTimeoutMs,
        ...(includeCredentialProviders ? { includeCredentialProviders: true } : {}),
        reusePluginGenerations: true,
      }),
    publishOwners: (publishedOwners) => replyDispatchPublication.replace(publishedOwners),
    commit,
    onOwnerFailure: (error) => {
      const refreshError = toStringifiedError(error);
      notifyPreparedModelRuntimePublication({ phase: "failed", error: refreshError });
      log.warn(`auth-triggered model runtime refresh failed: ${String(refreshError)}`);
    },
  });
  ```
- `invalidateForAuthMutation(event)` → `invalidatePreparedModelRuntimeOwnersForAuthMutation(...)`
- `registerRuntimeAuthProfileStoreMutationListener(invalidateForAuthMutation)`
- `enqueuePreparedModelRuntimePublication(task)` — uses a `refreshTail` promise chain, i.e. the publication path **is already serialized**; this is not a missing-lock bug.
- `PreparedModelRuntimePublicationSupersededError` — superseded transactions are skipped, so the "a newer publication replaced me" case *is* handled. The "my plugin generation vanished" case is not.
- `DEFAULT_MODEL_RUNTIME_BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000` — a module constant, not configurable (`setModelRuntimeBuildTimeoutMsForTest` is gated behind `process.env.VITEST`).

`gateway.reload` exposes exactly one key on 2026.9.5 (`mode`: `off` | `hybrid`), so there is no supported knob to debounce, serialize, or suppress this interaction.

## Root-cause hypothesis

`publishPreparedModelRuntimeOwnerBatch(..., reusePluginGenerations: true)` reuses the plugin generation captured when the auth mutation was registered. A concurrent config hot reload that changes `plugins.entries.*` replaces that plugin instance. The publisher then resolves the *stale* generation and throws `PluginInstanceUnavailableError`. Because the failure path only logs (and emits a `phase: "failed"` notification with no recovery), the owner is left unpublished and is never retried against the *current* generation.

This needs both halves: (a) a plugin-entry config reload, and (b) a concurrent auth-triggered publication — which in our case was sustained by the provider's 401 loop rotating auth profiles.

## Suggested directions

1. **Self-heal instead of warn.** In `onOwnerFailure`, when the error is a stale-plugin-generation error (`PluginInstanceUnavailableError`), re-enqueue the publication against the *current* plugin generation rather than only logging.
2. **Coordinate the two paths.** Have the plugin reload / config-reload path explicitly invalidate *and* republish the prepared-model-runtime owners for the affected providers, instead of relying on `reusePluginGenerations` still being valid.
3. **Bound the degradation.** If an owner stays unpublished past a threshold, surface that state explicitly (health/diagnostics) rather than letting every `models.list` caller see the generic "not ready … retry" message for an hour.
4. **Consider serving the last-good catalog.** Let `models.list` return the last-good catalog with a `stale`/`degraded` flag instead of `UNAVAILABLE`, so the Control UI is not left with an empty model picker during a publication stall.

## Workarounds used on the host (FYI, not a fix)

- A manual plugin reload republishes plugin generations; we used it to clear stale plugin instances left behind by the failed publication.
- Batch config edits into a single write; avoid editing `plugins.entries.*`, agent model entries, or `auth.profiles.*` while a provider is failing auth.
- Monitoring: watch for `auth-triggered model runtime refresh failed` and for a rising rate of `Model catalog is not ready`.

## Not claimed

- We did **not** reproduce this deterministically; the analysis is from production logs plus the bundled 2026.9.5 code paths above.
- We did **not** test whether `gateway.reload.mode: "off"` avoids it (it would also disable hot config application generally — a heavy trade-off).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

During post-update convergence on 2026.9.5, `openclaw doctor --fix` retires `openai/gpt-5.4` and substitutes **`openai/gpt-5.6-terra`**, writing that id into `modelPolicy.allow` and into a live agent's **fallback chain**. That model is not resolvable on this install — `openclaw models list` reports it with no `Input`, no `Ctx`, and `Auth no`, while every other configured model shows full metadata and `Auth yes`.

The result is an agent whose fallback chain silently contains a model that cannot serve. It does not fail at write time, and it would not fail until the primary and first fallback are both unavailable — i.e. during an incident, which is the worst possible moment to discover it.

### Environment

- Upgraded `2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)` → `2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)`
- Install mode: npm global; linux arm64; node 26.7.0, npm 11.19.0
- Providers configured: openai, anthropic, vllm (xai served from the built-in catalog)

### What Doctor reported

```
◇  Doctor changes
│  Moved retired agents.defaults.models.openai/gpt-5.4 to
│  openai/gpt-5.6-terra.
│  Replaced retired agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow.0 "openai/gpt-5.4"
│  with "openai/gpt-5.6-terra".
│  Replaced retired agents.entries.<agent>.model.fallbacks.1
│  "openai/gpt-5.4" with "openai/gpt-5.6-terra".
```

### What the catalog says about the substitute

```
Model                               Input      Ctx         Local Auth  Tags
anthropic/claude-sonnet-5           text+image 1000k       no    yes   default,configured,alias:Claude
openai/gpt-5.5                      text+image 272k/1049k  no    yes   fallback#1,configured,alias:GPT
openai/gpt-5.4-mini                 text       524k        no    yes   configured,alias:gpt-mini
openai/gpt-5.6-terra                -          -           no    no    fallback#2,configured,alias:Codex
```

Empty `Input` and `Ctx` plus `Auth no` — on a machine where `OPENAI_API_KEY` is present and every other `openai/*` model authenticates — reads as "this id is not in the catalog", not "credentials are missing".

### A second consequence: an orphaned agent runtime

The retired entry carried a harness mapping, which Doctor moved verbatim:

```json
"openai/gpt-5.6-terra": { "alias": "Codex", "agentRuntime": { "id": "codex" } }
```

So the `codex` agent runtime is now attached to a model that cannot serve, and the harness has effectively no model. Migrating a retirement needs to consider that the retired entry may be the only thing binding a runtime.

### Expected behavior

Either substitute an id that is present in the catalog, or leave the retired reference in place and warn loudly. Writing an unresolvable id into `modelPolicy.allow` and a fallback chain converts a visible "this model is retired" warning into an invisible latent failure.

A cheap guard: after substitution, resolve the replacement against the catalog and refuse (or warn) if it does not resolve.

### Related: dotted config paths cannot address model ids

Cleaning this up by hand hits a second issue. Model ids contain dots, and the config path parser splits on them:

```
$ openclaw config unset agents.defaults.models.openai/gpt-5.6-terra
Config path not found: agents.defaults.models["openai/gpt-5"]["6-terra"]. Nothing was changed.
```

The bracket form works:

```
$ openclaw config unset 'agents.defaults.models["openai/gpt-5.6-terra"]'
Removed agents.defaults.models["openai/gpt-5.6-terra"].
```

Since essentially every model id contains a dot, plain dotted paths can never address entries in this map. Worth either documenting the bracket form in `openclaw config --help` or handling the trailing segment as a literal key.

### Workaround applied here

Rebuilt the fallback chain on ids confirmed present in the catalog, deliberately spanning three providers so no single provider outage can exhaust it, and removed the orphaned mapping. Happy to supply sanitized diagnostics or run a specific command if useful.

issues.body:
### Summary

On Windows, OpenClaw's Gateway **silently stops delivering replies** while the host is busy running another memory/CPU-heavy application (in our case, a local GPU render job). It keeps **receiving** inbound channel messages, but every dispatch fails with:

```
prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main
```

No user-visible error is surfaced, inbound messages are dropped, and the Gateway does not recover by itself. To be explicit: **this is not a request for more RAM.** We are reporting that a *mainstream* machine (16–32 GB) can reach a state where the assistant becomes silently unusable, and that this should be survivable/degradable at the program level.

### Why we believe this is a program-level robustness issue, not a hardware ask

- 32 GB — often 16 GB — is a mainstream configuration, and local apps that legitimately consume the whole machine (renders, compiles, games, video editing) are normal. An assistant process should not require the user to keep the machine idle.
- We first hit it on a 32 GB host, then upgraded the host to 64 GB; the *class* of failure (dispatch publication failing under resource pressure, with no self-healing) is only moved to a higher threshold, not fixed by more RAM.
- The damaging part is the **failure mode**, not the slowness: messages are accepted and never answered, with no signal to the user, and recovery is not user-recoverable.

### Observed sequence (2026-09-22, sanitized)

```
13:00:44 [gateway/heartbeat] heartbeat failed: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main
13:01:00 [gateway/admission] admission closed: suspend phase
13:01:00 [channels/<channel>] abort signal received, stopping
13:01:00 [gateway/admission] admission reopened: suspend phase
13:01:00 [channels/<channel>] reconnecting (websocket) ... client started
13:12:37 [channels/<channel>] received message (p2p)
13:12:37 [channels/<channel>] dispatching to agent (session=<redacted>)
13:12:37 [channels/<channel>] failed to dispatch message: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main
13:12:37 [channels/<channel>] inbound debounce flush failed: ... same error
   -> repeats for every inbound message (13:12:38 / :40 / :44 / :52)

13:00:37 [sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold elapsedMs=2905 operation="session branch summaries read"
13:00:37 [gateway/ws] res sessions.branches.list 5241ms
```

Two notes that seem important for triage:

- This window ran on the host's earlier configuration, before the DRAM-speed change described further below (the additional memory modules were installed later that day), so it is **not** attributable to that instability.
- After the failure window the Gateway process is gone (nothing listening on its port) and the Windows Scheduled Task did **not** restart it.

### Recovered evidence from 2026-09-21/22 (captured at the time)

Earlier gateway logs rotate daily, so the operator kept local captures of the relevant windows. Quoting them (sanitized):

**1. The Gateway process was frozen for ~76 s (2026-09-21 16:51 local):**

```
[gateway/health] host timing gap detected: process was frozen ~75834ms; restarting channels when idle and refreshing health
... cpuCoreRatio=0.812 active=0 waiting=0 queued=0
```

Note the counters immediately before it — `active=0 waiting=0 queued=0`: the Gateway had **no work of its own** at that moment; it was starved while the host was busy with something else.

**2. OpenClaw's own memory-pressure diagnostics fired (2026-09-22 17:16 local):**

```
[diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=warning reason=rss_growth rss=1.28 GiB heap=507.1 MiB threshold=512 MiB thresholdRatio=130% rssGrowth=665.8 MiB
```

This is the application's own diagnostic, not our inference: its resident set had grown by ~666 MiB above its configured threshold and the built-in monitor escalated to `warning`. We read this as an internal-footprint signal rather than a host-level one; the host-level picture is in *Validation* below.

**3. 49 occurrences of the dispatch error on 2026-09-22:**

```
{"subsystem":"gateway/heartbeat"} {"error":"prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main"} "heartbeat failed: ..."
```

**4. `openclaw gateway status` output (2026-09-21, 32 GB host):**

```
Command: node.exe --max-old-space-size=8192 ... gateway --port 18789
Gateway heap: service argv: --max-old-space-size=8192; installer recommendation: 8192 MiB old space
  (32606 MiB physical capacity; adaptive cap 8192 MiB; native headroom cap 24454 MiB); runtime V8 ceiling: not measured

The Gateway did not report its own version.
Runtime: running
```

Questions this raises for us: how are the `adaptive cap` / `native headroom cap` values derived, and are they appropriate for a host that is **also** running a large local job? (This host had 32606 MiB physical at the time.) The probe also reported "did not report its own version" — i.e. the Gateway was unresponsive to that probe too.

**5. Windows-side low-memory events: none found.**

We re-ran the correct query (`ProviderName='Microsoft-Windows-Resource-Exhaustion-Detector'`, and also by event id `2004`) across the last 7 days: **no events**. The System log reaches back to 2026-06-05, so this is not a retention artifact. The application-level signal in (2) is therefore our primary memory-pressure evidence.

### Mechanism: why it does not self-heal on Windows (captured 2026-09-21)

From the same-day forensics (operator notes + logs):

- Health checks timed out at the **182 s** budget: `Timed out after 182s waiting for gateway port 18789 to become healthy`, `Gateway process is running but port 18789 is still free (startup hang/crash loop or very slow VM startup)`, `Gateway restart timed out after 182s waiting for health checks`.
- Under that pressure the **SQLite work runs on the main thread**: `slow OpenClaw agent database open ... elapsedMs=8555 (validation 8535ms)`, `slow SQLite transaction hold x14`, `slow SQLite session write x10` (operations include agent.write, session-entry.patch, session.maintenance.plan, state.write, session.lifecycle.mutate, session.transcript.turn).
- The Gateway can then be **alive but not answering** ("half-alive"): `openclaw gateway status` reports *running* and the port accepts connections, while the probe reports `timed out before reaching Gateway` and `The Gateway did not report its own version.`, together with `host thaw channel restart deferred: gateway still has active work` and `cron: GatewayDrainingError: Gateway is draining` / `isolated agent setup timed out before runner start`.
- The decisive one for *self-healing*: after `schtasks /End` the task instance ends but **child processes survive**. This host's gateway is a parent/child tree (`index.js gateway --task-supervisor` → `…service-child-windows-job-anchor.js` → `index.js gateway --task-supervisor-child=…`). The surviving process **holds the `state-lifecycle` lock**, so the next start is refused:

```
Gateway failed to start: another OpenClaw process owns state-lifecycle.
```

The operator had to kill the leftover node processes manually before the Gateway would start again.

Observed cost of this path (same host): using the official restart command (`openclaw gateway restart`, which goes through `schtasks /End` on Windows) **left stale processes and produced ~10 minutes of a dead-but-trying state (2026-09-21 22:02–22:12)** before the process tree was cleaned up and the port was confirmed free.

**Quantified pressure on the same host (operator's capacity ledger, 2026-09-21/22):**

- Transcript reads: **40–86 s per turn**, and **15 freezes in one day**
- `agent` database 407 MB; the DB integrity check alone takes **15.9 s** at that size
- Plugin/tool surface: **33 of 69 plugins enabled**; tool-catalog assembly measured at **~14 s per turn**
- Runtime ceiling hit in practice: `live runtime limit (256) reached`; 28 sessions already stored
- Log volume ~5–13 MB/day (retained 7 days)

**Why this matters for the ask:** on Windows the service wrapper cannot be relied on to end the *process tree* or release the internal state lock — so "self-heal" means OpenClaw must own its process tree / lock lifecycle, not just rely on the wrapper.

### Kept separate: the later crash-loop was a hardware-side finding

A later crash-loop on the same host (same day, evening) was root-caused to **unstable DRAM**: four DIMMs of the same brand/capacity but slightly different part numbers, running XMP at 3200 MT/s. Dropping to JEDEC 2400 MT/s made it stable, and a 3-stage memory stress test (~931 GB written + read back and verified, 0 mismatches) passes at 2400. That is **not** what this issue is about — we mention it only so the two are not conflated. This issue is the software-side behaviour: **under resource pressure the Gateway silently fails to dispatch, and does not recover.**

### Validation (2026-09-23, our host)

**Positive control — host has headroom → survives (PASS)**

- Host: 64 GB, DRAM at JEDEC **2400 MT/s** (XMP off), 4 DIMMs
- Load: local GPU render — host-wide peak working set **43.8 GB**; host free memory dipped to ~18 GB (≈72% used); **pagefile usage peaked at 4.4 GB** (the host *did* page under this load)
- Result: OpenClaw stayed fully responsive for the entire 23-minute render — **0 heartbeat delays, 0 host timing gaps, 0 channel disconnects, 0 dropped dispatches** (gateway log, 21:15–21:45 local)
- Observed OpenClaw footprint: main node process **~1.16 GB RSS**

**Negative case — host has no headroom → silent failure (observed 2026-09-22)**

- The same class of load on a 32 GB host left only **~1.4 GB free**. The channel kept receiving, but every dispatch failed with `prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main`; afterwards the process was gone and the Scheduled Task did not restart it.

**Interpretation**

The difference between the two runs is **how much headroom is left for OpenClaw**, not the software version. Note that OpenClaw's own footprint is small (~1.2 GB here) — so this is not "OpenClaw eats the RAM"; it is "when the host is saturated, OpenClaw cannot keep its dispatch path alive and does not recover". On a mainstream 16–32 GB machine the saturated case is normal, not exotic.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (CLI and service both 2026.9.5)
- Windows 10.0.26100 (x64), Node v24.19.0
- Service: Windows Scheduled Task; argv includes `--max-old-space-size=8192`, loopback bind
- Channel: chat/websocket mode
- Enabled plugins: 33 (many provider plugins that are not in use)
- Memory search: local embeddings (ollama / nomic-embed-text)

### Expected behaviour

We'd accept any explicit behaviour among:

1. **Degrade, don't die** — when memory/CPU is scarce, shed optional work (embeddings/vector search, concurrency) and keep dispatch alive.
2. **Self-heal** — if the process exits unexpectedly it must be restarted by OpenClaw itself. (Your Windows docs already note that Task Scheduler `RestartOnFailure` cannot reliably restart a process that started successfully once, so supervision belongs to the app.)
3. **Surface it** — if dispatch cannot proceed, tell the user (and log loudly) instead of silently dropping messages.
4. **Lower the standing footprint** — 33 resident plugins is a lot of baseline memory; provider plugins look load-on-demand-able.

### Related

- Open PR **#152530** ("restore model and reply availability after plugin reload failure") fixes the *same* error string, via the **plugin reload / activation-failure** path, reproduced with fault injection. Our host runs 33 plugins, so our scenario may belong to the same class.

### Reproductions we can run on request

We are not going to deliberately load the host further without need — but if you want controlled reproductions, we can run any of the following and attach raw logs:

- **A** (already done, see *Validation* above): current stable config + the same heavy local load → survived, zero dropped dispatches.
- **B**: same load with unused plugins disabled → comparison for #152530.
- **C**: **emulate a mainstream 32 GB machine on a 64 GB host** by capping what is available to OpenClaw (heap limit / job object) under the same load.

### Request

Is this a known limitation of 2026.9.5 for runtime-owner publication when the host is under pressure? What is the intended mitigation — a publication/timeout-budget change, plugin-load isolation, in-app supervision, or should the Gateway fail loudly and restart instead of silently dropping dispatches?

issues.body:
### Summary

Move Android chat's **Jump to latest** action from the conversation header to a floating circular button above the composer.

### Problem to solve

When someone scrolls up in a long chat, the current jump action appears in the top header, far from the composer and the reading area. The compact header icon is also harder to hit and distinguish from the other header actions. Returning to the live edge should be easy with one thumb while preserving the reader's intentional scroll position.

### Proposed solution

Take inspiration from the Control UI's floating scroll-to-bottom indicator and use that pattern in Android chat when someone has moved away from the latest message. Tapping the indicator should return to the bottom and resume following.

### Alternatives considered

Keep the header action: it remains distant from the composer's thumb area and competes with the chat title and other header controls.

### Impact

Affected: Android users reading earlier parts of a long conversation.

Severity: Usability improvement; chat remains functional today.

Frequency: Whenever the reader has manually moved away from the live edge.

Consequence: More reach and visual search to return to the newest message, particularly one-handed.

### Evidence/examples

The existing reader-managed scrolling behavior is described in #98255. The Android chat screenshot fixture on an API 36 emulator shows the current header action and the proposed floating position; before/after images and focused layout checks will be included in the implementation PR.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

### Additional information

This changes Android presentation and touch/accessibility behavior only; it does not change the Gateway protocol or chat-following policy.

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.5, the bundled `memory-wiki` plugin's `memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup` service can fail to settle during activation and cleanup. A targeted plugin reload then fails after the 5-second lifecycle deadline. Wiki status and lint calls also stall, leaving the practical choice between an unhealthy Gateway and disabling the plugin.

The wiki files and configuration remain intact. With the plugin disabled, ordinary memory search works, but the compiled-wiki corpus is not registered.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (`ec9c1a1`), npm global install
- Node.js 24.21.0
- Linux 6.14.0-37-generic x86_64
- systemd user Gateway
- Bundled `memory-wiki` plugin 2026.9.5

## Observed production sequence

A deterministic minimal reproduction has not been isolated.

1. Start the Gateway with `memory-wiki` enabled and an existing compiled vault.
2. Under normal session and SQLite activity, the Gateway remains in the phase `sidecars.plugin-services.memory-wiki.memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup` while liveness warnings report event-loop utilization of 1.
3. Request a supported targeted reload of `memory-wiki`.
4. The reload fails with:

```
Plugin operation failed during activate: Plugin candidate cleanup failed |
Plugin candidate cleanup failed; automatic recovery could not safely start |
plugin host cleanup timed out: plugin candidate retirement |
plugin services failed to start |
Unpublished plugin resource cleanup failed |
plugin service startup timed out after 4999ms
(memory-wiki/memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup) |
plugin service replacement cleanup failed |
plugin host cleanup timed out: unpublished plugin resources |
plugin service stop failed
(plugin=memory-wiki, service=memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup):
plugin service startup settlement timed out after 4999ms
Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied.
```

5. `wiki_status` and wiki lint remain stuck for more than a minute.
6. Disabling `memory-wiki` restores normal Gateway use, but `memory_search` reports the wiki corpus as not registered.

During the incident, the Gateway process also showed 90-112% CPU, roughly 2.7 GiB RSS, slow SQLite transactions, and event-loop starvation. These were concurrent observations, not proof that `memory-wiki` alone caused all resource use.

## Expected behavior

The cleanup service should honor cancellation and settle within the plugin lifecycle budget. A failed reload should leave the previous plugin generation usable, or return a recoverable error without making wiki tools hang. Operators should not have to disable the compiled wiki to keep the Gateway responsive.

## Actual behavior

The cleanup service does not settle before the 4,999 ms deadline. Activation and replacement cleanup fail, wiki operations stall, and the compiled-wiki corpus remains unavailable until the plugin can be safely re-enabled.

## Impact

- Compiled wiki search, status, lint, ingest, and repair workflows are unavailable.
- Work that requires before-and-after wiki lint cannot proceed safely.
- The underlying wiki data is preserved, but the compiled knowledge layer is offline.
- Re-enabling without a bounded recovery risks bringing the Gateway stall back.

## Source-level observation

The bundled service's `start()` awaits compiled-cache owner reconciliation and stale-owner deletion. Its `stop()` aborts source sync and waits for imported source syncs to settle. One of those awaited paths appears able to outlive the host's lifecycle deadline under contention. This is an inference from the installed 2026.9.5 bundle and the runtime error, not a proven root cause.

## Related issues

- #154891 contains the same `memory-wiki-compiled-cache-owner-cleanup` timeout as the trigger for a broader failed-reload rollback problem. This report is specifically about the cleanup service and the loss of the wiki corpus.
- #104719 concerns an uncancelled exhaustive wiki-search fallback and is a separate defect.

issues.body:
### Summary

When the linked WhatsApp account is added to a group and the admin chooses to share the group's message history with the new member, WhatsApp delivers those past messages to the account. OpenClaw 2026.9.5 discards all of them before any hook or memory sees them. There is no configuration that changes this. Related: #20887 (closed as stale, same underlying gap).

### Problem to solve

An agent that joins a group cannot answer anything said before it joined, even though the user explicitly shared the history with it. A plugin that records or indexes chats (memory search) cannot backfill either, because the messages never reach `message_received`.

Where they are dropped, in the `whatsapp` extension of 2026.9.5:

- the socket is opened with `syncFullHistory: false`, and nothing in the extension subscribes to Baileys' `messaging-history.set`;
- `handleMessagesUpsert` accepts only `notify` and `append` upserts, and `shouldSkipStaleAppend` drops every `append` message whose timestamp is older than the connection time (60 s grace), which is exactly what shared history looks like.

### Proposed solution

1. Subscribe to `messaging-history.set`, and accept `append` upserts that belong to a shared-history delivery.
2. Emit each historical message through the existing `message_received` plugin hook (behind the existing `channels.whatsapp.pluginHooks.messageReceived` opt-in), marked as historical (for example a `historical: true` field or a `providerUpdate` marker), without dispatching an agent turn and without any reply.
3. Gate the whole behaviour behind a new option, e.g. `channels.whatsapp.history.ingest: true`, default off, to keep today's privacy posture.

### Alternatives considered

- Exporting the chat from WhatsApp and importing the text file into memory by hand. Works, but has to be repeated for every group the account joins, and defeats WhatsApp's own "share history" feature.
- Forking the extension. Not acceptable for a production deployment tracking upstream releases.

### Impact

Every WhatsApp deployment used as a personal or group assistant with a memory plugin: the account can be added to an existing group and be expected to know its context. Today it silently knows nothing before the moment it joined.

### Evidence/examples

Reproduction on 2026.9.5 (Baileys web channel):

1. Pair the account. Enable `channels.whatsapp.pluginHooks.messageReceived: true` and load a plugin that logs `message_received`.
2. From a phone, add the account to an existing group and choose to share the recent history. The phone shows "You sent <name> message history that starts on <date>".
3. Gateway log: no inbound line for any of the historical messages; the plugin's `message_received` is not called for them; `openclaw automations`/sessions show nothing. Live messages sent afterwards arrive normally.

Code references (dist of 2026.9.5, `extensions/whatsapp`): `handleMessagesUpsert` — `if (upsert.type !== "notify" && upsert.type !== "append") return;`; `shouldSkipStaleAppend` — `APPEND_RECENT_GRACE_MS = 6e4`, compares against `connectedAtMs`; socket options — `syncFullHistory: false`; no occurrence of `messaging-history` anywhere in the extension.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No.

issues.body:
## Summary

On a WhatsApp direct chat whose session policy suppresses automatic replies (session.sendPolicy deny), six consecutive inbound messages from one sender were received by the gateway (each logged whole by `gateway/channels/whatsapp/inbound` and by the `web-inbound` module) but none of them was written to the session transcript, because the embedded agent run for each failed with:

```
Embedded agent failed before reply: Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot
```

The transcript for that session (`agent:main:whatsapp:direct:<counterparty number>`) shows nothing between 12:01:57Z and 12:55:09Z, while the gateway log shows inbound messages at 12:01:59Z, 12:04:00Z, 12:05:16Z, 12:05:17Z (two) and 12:05:18Z (2,015 characters). A later inbound at 12:55:09Z, whose run ended with REPLY_SKIP, was persisted normally. So persistence of the inbound message depends on the run succeeding, and a failed run drops the message from the only store an agent reads.

## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (3928bad), Linux x64 container, gateway bound to loopback, one agent (`main`), WhatsApp channel linked as a device on the operator's account, session policy for the chat: automatic replies suppressed, tool `message` allowed. The runs were triggered by inbound messages while other agent runs were active on the same gateway (two long-running CLI agent calls plus an inter-session `sessions_send` from a Telegram session in the same minute: `agents/sessions-send ... "agent tool caller authority is no longer active"`).

## Steps to reproduce (as observed)

1. Keep two long CLI agent runs alive (`openclaw agent --session-key ... --message-file ...`).
2. From another session, send an inter-session message into the WhatsApp chat's session (`sessions_send`).
3. Have the WhatsApp counterparty send several messages within the same minute.
4. Read the session transcript (`transcript_events` for the session) and compare with the gateway log's `web-inbound` records.

## Expected

An inbound message is persisted to the session transcript whether or not the reply run succeeds; a failed run is recorded beside it.

## Actual

The inbound is logged by the gateway but absent from the transcript; the session's status flips to `failed`; agents reading the session (including the operator's own mirror) never see the message.

## Evidence

- Gateway log lines (same file, same minute): `Inbound message <counterparty number> -> <operator number> (direct, 2015 chars)`, then `Embedded agent failed before reply: Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot` (12:05:18.452Z and 12:05:19.156Z).
- Session store: `select count(*) from transcript_events where session_id=<id> and created_at between <12:01:58Z> and <12:55Z>` returns 0 user messages; the six bodies exist only in the log.
- The operator recovered the six messages from the log by hand; the workaround in use is a mirror that merges the gateway log's `web-inbound` records with the transcript.

## Ask

Persist the inbound before running the reply, or write a tombstone with the body when the run fails, so that a suppressed-reply chat cannot lose what arrived.

issues.body: ### Bug type Regression (worked before, now fails) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary First, credit where due: 2026.9's Control UI is a big step toward a real Claude Desktop-style web interface. The points below are interaction/information-architecture friction on top of an otherwise strong redesign, not a complaint about the direction. ## 1. "Home" is not a root "Home" reads as the website/app convention: one root, where the app opens. In the Control UI it's actually the current agent's default session, and it can't be deleted. With multiple agents there are multiple "Home"s, each one changing silently when you switch agent in the picker directly above it — the opposite of what "root" implies. There is a difference between new empty main session and creating a new session. Different capabilities. Unclear why though. Suggestion: rename to "Main session", "Main" or similar. (Loosely related to #150382, where Home also routes wrong after visiting Dashboards — different bug, same underlying fuzziness.) Still the function of Home is quite ambiguous. I think you should seperate new session and configuration into multiple controls. Explicit and unique function in the UI > "Edit sidebar" and "New" ## 2. "Groups" is actually three different mechanisms, none of which agree with each other Sessions and Groups are shown as if Groups nests inside Sessions, when conceptually it's the reverse (a group is a set of sessions, so they should be siblings). Worse by implmentation, "assigning a group" can mean three different things depending on how you do it: - A gateway-wide `session_groups` table (name + cwd), independent of any agent. Why would you create a group on gateway-level?! Just type the group twice or three times. Way too complicated for simple experience. - A per-agent, per-session `category` field, set via right-click → "New group". - `pinned_at` on the session — reached by dragging a row **above** the "SESSIONS" header, which looks like it should mean "ungroup" but is actually an unrelated pin flag. Reproduced live: a group "Appelflap" existed in the gateway table from testing on one agent. Dragging two sessions into "Appelflap" on a *different* agent (Grease-monkey) never touched that table — it wrote `category: "Appelflap"` into Grease-monkey's own per-agent database. Separately, dragging those same two sessions above the "SESSIONS" header set `pinned_at` on them, which made the "Appelflap" group header disappear from the sidebar entirely (not because the group is empty — it has two members — but because both are now rendered in the pinned zone instead). So a group with real members can silently vanish as a side effect of an unrelated pin action, and nothing in the UI names what any of these three stores actually is. I believe assigned groups should stay within the agent always no exlusion and never escape it's (agent) context. It's an ingredient for headache. A group is a container for sessions within the container agent. You could implement Tags which live among agents but that's a whole different direction of classification. ## 3. "Other" and "Group": entries I never created, can't delete or rename After the 2026.9 migration, my sidebar shows groups called "Other" and "Group" that I never made. Neither exists in any agent's `session_nodes.category` values nor in the gateway `session_groups` table, so they're most likely client-side placeholders, not real stored groups — which would explain why there's nothing to rename or delete. If so, the UI shouldn't render them with the same right-click affordances (rename/delete) as real, user-created groups. ## 4. A group's "Delete" option disappears with its last visible row "Delete group" lives only in the right-click menu on the group's own header row. Whether that row renders depends on "Hide empty groups" (`filtering` / `always` / `never`); unless it's `always`, a group with zero *currently displayed* sessions draws no header at all, so its only delete affordance is unreachable. There's no group-management list elsewhere (e.g. Settings) as a fallback. This is exactly how "Other" and "Group" (point 3) and "Appelflap" (point 2) became permanent. ## 5. New session in Agent A assign agent B and workspace C - Users can start a new session in Agent A and able to select agent B for new chat. Why when we have seperate Agents? Quite more disturbing if you ask me when I'm able to select a workspace that actually configured for another agent. Less is more. Keep it simple. ## Ask - Rename "Home" to name what it is (a per-agent default session). Function of 'home' is ambigues though. I truly think you should seperate controls/settings and sessions/chats. A default new session make more sense then home with hidden controls for settings and a special chat state. Seperate into at least 2 controls: "Edit sidebar" and "New"/"New Session". - place jail agent sessions in agent! - Give Sessions and Groups clear hierarchy and simplify group concept. Do we really need a Swiss army knife for group concept? Modify group should also be available for any group. - Don't expose rename/delete on synthetic entries ("Other"/"Group") that have nothing behind them. - Make group management (delete/rename) reachable regardless of whether the group currently has a visible row. ### Steps to reproduce N/A ### Expected behavior N/A ### Actual behavior N/A ### OpenClaw version 2026.9.6 ### Operating system N/A ### Install method N/A ### Model N/A ### Provider / routing chain N/A ### Additional provider/model setup details N/A ### Logs ```shell ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence ### Impact and severity _No response_ ### Additional information _No response_

issues.body:
﻿### Summary

Clarify the acceptance criteria for adding a new third-party web search provider to `extensions/` (bundled external package), so contributors know when a provider is in scope for this repository versus ClawHub-only.

### Problem to solve

I submitted a pull request adding AnySearch as a web search provider (`extensions/anysearch/`, same shape as the existing bundled search providers). Automated review closed it as a scope-fit item, stating:

> "no missing core capability or maintainer sponsorship establishes a reason to maintain it in this repository"

Coordination note: AnySearch (the upstream vendor) replied to my enquiry and asked me to obtain the maintainer's explicit guidance on the intended integration route before they consider any change of approach, so a maintainer answer here directly unblocks the decision.

That leaves an ambiguity I cannot resolve from the docs, because the existing repository state appears to point the other way:

- Eight comparable search providers are maintained in this repo under `extensions/`: `brave`, `exa`, `tavily`, `perplexity`, `firecrawl`, `parallel`, `duckduckgo`, `searxng`.
- All of them are published as official external packages with `bundledDist: false` and `publishToNpm` + `publishToClawHub` — the same distribution shape as this PR.
- Tavily (#49200) was merged from an external fork PR by a maintainer, and is retained in `extensions/tavily/`.
- `docs/plugins/plugin-inventory.md` lists all of them, including AnySearch once registered, under "Official external packages".

So the current signals are: (a) providers of this class live in this repo, and (b) the automated review considers a new one out of scope. I would like the authoritative rule.

### Proposed solution

A maintainer statement of the intended acceptance criteria for new search providers, e.g. one of:

1. **In scope** — new providers that use only existing public contracts, ship with tests/docs, and follow the canonical keyed-remote-provider shape are accepted into `extensions/` like the existing eight; or
2. **ClawHub-only** — new provider integrations should be published as independent plugins, and `extensions/*` search providers are frozen to the existing set (and if so, whether they are being externalized over time).

If the answer is (2), it would help to know whether the existing eight are scheduled for externalization, since that is the relevant precedent for judging contribution shape.

### Alternatives considered

- **Reopen the closed PR and re-request review.** Not possible: GitHub rejects reopening that PR (`PATCH /pulls/155495 {"state":"open"}` → HTTP 422). I opened a fresh PR (#155666) from the same reviewed branch instead, but I do not want to keep resubmitting without knowing the rule.
- **Publish directly to ClawHub without asking.** Possible, but I would rather confirm the route than publish something the maintainers consider misplaced. If ClawHub is the intended path, I will do that.

### Impact

Affected: external contributors adding search/API integrations, and maintainers who must triage them.

- Severity: blocks contribution — the current signals conflict, so contributors cannot self-determine scope.
- Frequency: every new provider PR (there are recent examples of both outcomes).
- Consequence: avoidable PR churn and repeated automated closures for work that is already implemented and tested to this repository's standards.

### Evidence/examples

- Existing bundled search providers on `main`: `extensions/{brave,exa,tavily,perplexity,firecrawl,parallel,duckduckgo,searxng}/`
- Tavily external-fork precedent that was merged: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/49200
- This contribution's PR (implemented, all checks green): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155666
- Prior automated closure of the same branch: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155495
- Provider implementation uses only public contracts: `api.registerWebSearchProvider(...)` + published `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` subpaths; no core tool, no new SDK seam, no loader change.
- Verification on the current head: provider unit tests 18/18; bundled web search provider contract suite 45/45 (includes `anysearch:anysearch`); live end-to-end against `https://api.anysearch.com/v1/search` for anonymous search, shared cache, vertical routing, non-ASCII decoding, validation, and cancellation; `oxlint`/`oxfmt`/`tsgo:extensions`/`config:docs:check`/`plugins:inventory:check`/ratchets/docs checks all pass.
- Operator cost characteristics: keyless by default (anonymous requests send no `Authorization` header); AnySearch's published free tier provides 1,000 requests/day per key, and their Student & Developer program provides 2,000 calls/day.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance

### Additional information

I am not asking for a specific provider to be special-cased — the question is the general rule for this class of integration. I will follow whichever answer applies: keep the PR as-is for (1), or repackage for ClawHub for (2).
