issues.body:
### Summary

On 2026.9.2, ChatGPT-account model discovery (`GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models`) consistently times out against the internal 5s cap in `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, while the same endpoint answers in ~250ms from the same machine via both `curl` and plain Node `fetch`. Because discovery never succeeds, `openai/gpt-6-astra` (the ChatGPT/Codex subscription route announced in 2026.9.2) never registers and stays `model not allowed`, even with a fresh, working Codex OAuth login.

Thanks for the Astra support in 2026.9.2 — the API-key route works great. This report is only about the subscription-route discovery path.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (3928bad), gateway on macOS 26.2 (arm64), launchd service
- Node v26.5.0 (Homebrew)
- Network note: the machine runs Tailscale (MagicDNS / split DNS via 100.100.100.100), in case the guard's own resolution path interacts with that

### Observed

Gateway log shows repeated identical timeouts (6 today, including right after a gateway restart and a fresh `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`):

```
WARN {"subsystem":"fetch-timeout"} {"timeoutMs":5000,"elapsedMs":5066,"operation":"fetchWithSsrFGuard","url":"https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models"} fetch timeout reached; aborting operation
```

`elapsedMs` across occurrences: 5066, 5069, 5058, 5032, 5013 — always clipped at the cap, suggesting the request hangs indefinitely inside the guard rather than being merely slow.

One occurrence also hit `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` (5199ms), so it may not be specific to chatgpt.com.

### Same machine, same endpoint, outside the guard

```
curl -4  https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models  -> 401 in 0.286s
curl -6  https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/models  -> 401 in 0.274s
node -e 'fetch(...)'   (same Node binary the gateway runs on) -> 401 in 267ms
dns.lookup / resolve4 / resolve6 / resolveAny for chatgpt.com -> 5-141ms
```

So DNS, IPv4/IPv6 connectivity, TLS, and Node's own fetch stack are all fast; only the SSRF-guarded fetch path stalls.

### Impact

- `openai/gpt-6-astra` never becomes selectable via a ChatGPT/Codex account ("subscription availability follows successful account discovery"), returning `model not allowed` on spawn/model selection.
- Other `openai` (ChatGPT OAuth) models keep working, so this only blocks the discovery-gated additions.

### Repro

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.2 with a ChatGPT/Codex OAuth profile (fresh device-code login).
2. Add `openai/gpt-6-astra` to `agents.defaults.models`; restart gateway.
3. Watch the log for `fetch-timeout` on `backend-api/codex/models`; model stays unregistered.

Happy to run any additional diagnostics (verbose guard logging, custom builds, packet captures) — this machine reproduces it reliably. And if there's a config knob to raise or bypass the 5s discovery cap that I missed, a pointer would be appreciated.

**Version:** 2026.9.1 (ad6fe23), macOS arm64, node 26.7.0

**Config:**
```json
"session": { "reset": { "mode": "daily", "idleMinutes": 600, "atHour": 4 } }
```

**Summary:** Per `dist/reset-policy-*.js`, daily-mode staleness is `staleDaily = sessionStartedAt < dailyResetAt`, evaluated lazily — so a session started before the 4am boundary should reset on the FIRST inbound message after the boundary. Observed instead: three consecutive webchat (dashboard) messages after the boundary were handled normally in the stale session, and the reset then fired on the FOURTH message — mid-conversation from the user's perspective, discarding the context of the exchange that had just resumed.

**Timeline (2026-09-06, Europe/Zurich; long-running dashboard session, last prior activity 2026-09-05 20:27):**

- 10:58, 11:06, 11:10 — three user messages handled normally in the old session. All are past both the 4am daily boundary and the 10h idleMinutes threshold; per the policy source, every one of them should have been the reset trigger.
- 11:13:10.877 — transcript event `{"type":"reset","reason":"daily"}` written, 100ms before the user's fourth message is appended: that message triggered it.

Transcript excerpt (session store `transcript_events`):
```
seq 2018  2026-09-06T08:58:48Z  user      (handled in old session)
seq 2020  2026-09-06T09:06:10Z  user      (handled in old session)
seq 2022  2026-09-06T09:10:12Z  user      (handled in old session)
seq 2024  2026-09-06T09:13:10.877Z  {"type":"reset","reason":"daily",...}
seq 2025  2026-09-06T09:13:10.977Z  user
```

**Expected:** either the first post-boundary message resets the session (current policy semantics), or none of them do — resetting on the Nth message mid-conversation is the worst of both. It suggests some webchat dispatch path handles inbound messages without running the freshness evaluation (`evaluateSessionFreshness` / `resolveSessionEntryResetFreshness`), and a different path (hit on the fourth message) does run it. Repeated `chat.startup` calls from client reconnects were interleaved in the same window (11:03, 11:05, 11:08) if that helps narrow which path skips the check.

issues.body:
### Summary

On a Windows laptop that sleeps frequently, after every sleep/resume the gateway becomes unreachable from Control UI / WebChat for a while — usually a few seconds, but sometimes 30–60+ seconds — with reconnect attempts failing at the WebSocket upgrade stage. The gateway process itself never crashes (same PID across many sleep cycles, no restart). When the gateway is idle at wake time, clients reconnect in ~5–15 s; when it is busy (LLM requests in flight during the sleep that now time out, cron work, SQLite catch-up), the outage extends to ~1 minute or more.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.1 (mechanism also present in 2026.8.1/2026.8.2; `src/gateway/host-thaw-recovery.ts` is unchanged in 2026.9.2)
- OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200, Node v24.18.0
- Client: Control UI / WebChat over loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`
- Laptop with many sleep/wake cycles per day (lid close + idle sleep)

### Observed behavior

Every resume produces this sequence in the gateway log:

```
host timing gap detected: process was frozen ~632337ms; restarting channels when idle and refreshing health
admission closed: suspend phase
admission reopened: suspend phase
host thaw channel restart deferred: gateway still has active work   (repeats every ~30 s)
```

Two problems compound after wake:

1. **Event-loop stalls / deferred recovery.** Right after resume the gateway logs slow SQLite transaction holds, `liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=…; deferring recovery decisions` and `liveness warning: … eventLoopDelayMaxMs=3051 …`. During these stalls client reconnect attempts are closed at the WS upgrade stage:

```
closed before connect conn=… peer=127.0.0.1:… code=1006 reason=n/a phase=ws_upgrade_started
```

Bursts of these appear immediately after wake; in the worst observed case reconnect attempts were refused/closed repeatedly over ~45 s before any client got through (10:29–10:30 local, 2026-09-06).

2. **Thaw channel restart defers behind active work for up to ~2 minutes.** `restartChannelsIfIdle` returns `retry` while the gateway has any active work, and recovery retries on each maintenance tick (~30 s). Observed chains of 3–4 deferrals (60–95 s) are common when a session is mid-turn after wake (e.g. a chat that was running when the machine slept). Notably, clients *can* still send messages while the restart is deferred (a `chat.send` succeeded mid-deferral chain), so the restart delay itself does not block clients — but it keeps health/presence refresh and channel cleanup pending, and the combined window is what users perceive as "gateway is down after waking the laptop".

### Expected behavior

- After resume, Control UI / WebChat should reconnect within a few seconds regardless of gateway busyness; the gateway process is healthy and the port is listening.
- Post-resume catch-up work (SQLite replay/transactions, LLM request failover, model catalog refresh) should not stall the event loop for tens of seconds.
- The "restart channels when idle" requirement in thaw recovery seems unnecessary for client recovery (clients reconnect fine on their own, as observed mid-deferral) and only delays health/presence refresh; consider a bounded wait or dropping the idle requirement for the channel restart, and/or accepting new WS upgrades during the deferred window.

### Log evidence (local timestamps, Asia/Shanghai)

2026-09-06, resume after ~8.5 h sleep — UI reconnected in ~5 s but deferral chain continued 60 s+:
```
10:16:02.840 host thaw channel restart deferred: gateway still has active work
10:16:03–04 six × closed before connect … code=1006 … phase=ws_upgrade_started
10:16:07 UI connections up (agents.list / chat.history served)
10:16:32.767 / 10:17:02.759 further deferrals
```

2026-09-06, worst window — reconnect attempts refused for ~45 s:
```
10:28:54.164 frozen ~591389ms
10:28:59.349 admission closed → reopened only 10:29:12.342 (13 s closed)
10:29:26–10:30:12 nine × closed before connect … code=1006 … phase=ws_upgrade_started
10:30:20 first successful UI calls after the window
```

2026-09-05 evening — 4 consecutive deferrals over ~94 s while a chat was active (clients still worked):
```
18:54:37.178 deferred (active work) … 18:55:07.194 … 18:55:41.565 … 18:56:11.567
18:55:02.653 chat.send succeeded mid-deferral (conn stayed up)
```

Relevant code: `src/gateway/server-maintenance.ts` (`restartChannelsIfIdle` → `retry` when `!snapshot.idle`) and `src/gateway/host-thaw-recovery.ts` (deferred-retry per tick).

Happy to provide full sanitized log files if useful. Thanks for looking into this — on a laptop that sleeps often this makes the gateway feel down for a noticeable time several times a day.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On v2026.9.1, precise-cancel entry points reach `killSubagentRunAdmin` without delivery suppression (`src/tasks/task-registry-cancel.ts:225`, `src/gateway/session-kill-http.ts:114`; its params type accepts no `suppressTaskDelivery`), unlike the bulk paths which set `suppressTaskDelivery: true` (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts:84`, `src/auto-reply/reply/abort.ts:178`); during the by-design bounded `killReconciliation` window a late success flips a killed run back to `subagent-complete` (pinned by e2e, re-verified byte-identical on a pristine worktree), so those entries can deliver a late completion notification the operator's cancel intended to suppress.

### Steps to reproduce
Vitest e2e using real `claimSubagentRunKill` + `markSubagentRunTerminated` through the real registry listener:
1. Start a child run; claim kill + mark terminated (`endedReason: subagent-killed`) — the reconciliation window opens whenever completion races an active `killIntent` (`subagent-registry-lifecycle-completion.ts:307-332`).
2. Deliver the child's real success event through the listener (`subagent-registry-listener.ts:44-171`, which by design performs no `endedReason`/`killIntent`/`killReconciliation` checks).
3. Observe the row flip to `subagent-complete`, kill markers cleared, and wait admission follow the reconciled state.
PIN-1/PIN-2 pin this and the stabilized-row guard (`:333-341`) — 3/3 pass, and PIN-1/PIN-2 were re-run on a pristine worktree at `ad6fe23a` byte-identical with zero adaptation. Test files + raw vitest output available (SHA-256 `9995a37d…`, `e9a1e988…`).

### Expected behavior
Precise-cancel entries suppress completion delivery the way the bulk paths do, or the intended contract for cancel-by-task-id / HTTP admin kill is documented. `killReconciliation.suppressTaskDelivery` already propagates to `suppressCompletionDelivery` (`:381-383`), so the mechanism exists — these two entries just don't feed it.

### Actual behavior
Wiring evidence: the two precise-cancel call sites pass no suppression and `killSubagentRunAdmin`'s params type (`task-registry-control.types.ts:39-48`) has no field for it; the reconciliation flip itself is test-pinned (state flips to `subagent-complete`, both kill markers cleared). Reachability of "late success" was enumerated across five candidate sources; four are blocked by existing predicates, only real-completion-racing-cancellation is admitted — by design. End-to-end delivery of the late notification to a real channel: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not reproduced end-to-end; reported from wiring plus pinned state evidence).

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.1 (commit `ad6fe23aecb9b833d68139b0ddc9f239b894d2f1`, annotated tag `v2026.9.1`; macOS arm64, Node v26.3.0)

### Operating system
macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), Node v26.3.0

### Install method
Source worktree at tag `v2026.9.1` (pnpm dev-style checkout; repro is a Vitest e2e in-tree)

### Model
N/A — no model call in the repro. Registry-level e2e using real `claimSubagentRunKill` + `markSubagentRunTerminated` through the real registry listener.

### Provider / routing chain
N/A — no provider/model in the repro path.

### Additional provider/model setup details
None.

### Logs
Pinned observations (vitest, real registry stack): during the window — row flips to `subagent-complete`, both kill markers cleared, wait admission follows the reconciled state; on a stabilized killed row the guard at `subagent-registry-lifecycle-completion.ts:333-341` holds (`subagent-killed` retained). Raw output SHA-256 `9995a37d…`, `e9a1e988…`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Pinning e2e (3/3) + raw vitest output available; PIN-1/PIN-2 re-verified byte-identical on a pristine worktree at `ad6fe23a` with zero adaptation. Happy to open a PR with the tests.

### Impact and severity
Affected: deployments using precise cancel entries (`openclaw tasks` cancel-by-task-id path and the HTTP admin kill) while a child completion races cancellation. Severity: annoying-to-confusing (a late completion notification after an explicit cancel; state flip is by design, delivery suppression is the gap). Frequency: edge-case race. Consequence: a completion notification the operator intended to suppress can still be delivered via those two entries; bulk paths (`/stop`, chat abort) are not affected (they set `suppressTaskDelivery: true`). End-to-end delivery of the late notification to a real channel: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO — reported from wiring plus pinned state evidence, not reproduced end-to-end.

### Additional information
Reachability of "late success" was enumerated across five candidate sources; four are blocked by existing predicates (restart-recovery `!entry` branch only refreshes; pendingLifecycle timer cleared; sweeper never synthesizes success; superseded generations retire first). Only real-completion-racing-cancellation is admitted — by design. The reconciliation flip itself appears intentional ("real completed work shouldn't be lost") and `killReconciliation.suppressTaskDelivery` already propagates to `suppressCompletionDelivery` (`:381-383`); the gap is that `killSubagentRunAdmin`'s params type accepts no `suppressTaskDelivery` and its two callers pass none.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a session inherits a Codex-supervised model lock (e.g. from a parent folder/session), changing the model via `/model`, the model picker, or `session_status(model=...)` is **accepted and saved** to session metadata but **never applied** to the running conversation. The UI displays the newly selected model as active, while the session continues executing on the original locked model. No warning or error is surfaced to the user.

This caused **$80 of unintended spend** on the wrong model (GPT-6 Astra + Grok 4.5 fallback) before the user discovered the session was not actually running the selected model (Claude Sonnet 4.6).

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.2 (3928bad)
- Platform: Linux (Ubuntu), x64
- Agent: main (default)
- Models involved: `openai/gpt-6-astra` (locked), `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (selected), `xai/grok-4.5` (fallback)
- Codex plugin: enabled with supervision

## Reproduction

1. Create a session using a Codex-supervised model (e.g. `openai/gpt-6-astra`). This creates a model-locked Chat per the Codex supervision binding.
2. Create a child session inside the same folder/workspace. The child **inherits the parent's model selection** (documented: "The child inherits the parent's model selection unless one is passed explicitly").
3. In the child session, change the model via the Control UI model picker to a different model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`).
4. The UI accepts the selection. `session_status` shows `model: claude-sonnet-4-6` saved.
5. However, `session_status` also reports `\"live switch pending\"` — and this state **never resolves**.
6. The session continues executing on the original locked model (`gpt-6-astra`).
7. When the locked model fails (e.g. auth/credits exhausted), it falls back to the configured fallback model (`grok-4.5`) — turn-local only, never changing the stored selection.
8. The UI continues showing Sonnet 4.6 as the selected model throughout.

## Observed behaviour

### Session metadata

```
Session: agent:main:dashboard:84f6270b-...
Parent:  agent:main:dashboard:9a46ffe7-... ("GPT-6 Astra test Harvey", model: gpt-6-astra)

Stored model:    claude-sonnet-4-6  (saved successfully)
Active model:    gpt-6-astra       (never switched)
Fallback active: xai/grok-4.5      (when Astra failed)
Live switch:     pending           (never resolved)
Status:          killed            (had to be manually killed)
```

### What the user sees

- Model picker shows: **Claude Sonnet 4.6** (the selection they made)
- `/status` reports: `\"live switch pending\"`
- Actual model running: **GPT-6 Astra** → **Grok 4.5** (on fallback)
- No error, no warning, no visible indication that the switch failed

### Cost impact

- $80 spent on GPT-6 Astra + Grok 4.5 tokens across multiple turns
- User believed they were on Sonnet 4.6 the entire time
- Only discovered the mismatch when the assistant reported its own model identity

## Root cause analysis

Per the [Codex supervision docs](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-supervision):

> The supervised model-locked Chat cannot be deleted, switch models, use `/new` or `/reset`, invoke the Gateway session-reset action...

The Codex supervision binding creates a **model-locked Chat** that rejects model switches. However, the live model switching system in `model-failover.md` states:

> Only explicit user-driven model changes mark a pending live switch. That includes `/model`, `session_status(model=...)`, and `sessions.patch`.
> Live-session reconciliation prefers persisted session overrides over stale runtime model fields.

The model switch is **saved** (persisted to session metadata) and **marked pending**, but the Codex harness **rejects the live switch** at runtime. The rejection is silent — no error propagates back to the UI, and the "pending" state never transitions to either "applied" or "rejected."

## Expected behaviour

One or more of:

1. **Reject upfront**: When a user attempts to change the model on a model-locked session, the UI should refuse the selection and display: "This session is model-locked by Codex supervision. Start a new session to use a different model."
2. **Surface the rejection**: If the live switch is rejected at runtime, the `"live switch pending"` state should transition to `"live switch rejected"` with the reason, and the UI should warn the user.
3. **Inheritance guard**: When a child session inherits a parent's model, if that model is locked by a supervision binding, the child session should either (a) not inherit the lock, or (b) display a visible badge indicating the session is model-locked.

## Workaround

Start a completely new session outside the folder hierarchy (at the home directory level) to escape the inherited model lock.

## Additional context

- The `"live switch pending"` state persists indefinitely — it does not time out or self-resolve.
- The fallback notice (`↪️ Model Fallback`) only appears when the locked model fails, not when the switch is rejected — so the user has no indication the switch itself failed.
- The only way to discover the mismatch is to ask the assistant what model it is running on, or check `/status` and notice the `"pending"` flag.

## Reporter

Murray Wilson (Net-Sentinel)
Fleet: 6 issues filed (2 shipped, 2 diamond lobster rated)
Contact: myaichild40@gmail.com

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a New Session action to every project header in the Control UI sidebar's **Group by → Project** view, with the project's repository or workspace checkout preselected as the new session's working directory.

### Problem to solve

The Project grouping already derives each bucket from the sessions' repository or workspace checkout, but its headers do not offer a `+` action. To start another session in the project currently in view, users must use the global Sessions `+` and manually select the same folder again.

This creates repeated setup work during a common workflow: opening several independent sessions for the same project. It is also inconsistent with custom-group headers, which already provide a group-scoped `+` action.

Custom groups are not a full substitute because they are user-defined categories that can mix sessions from different working directories, whereas Project grouping already has an unambiguous derived project target.

### Proposed solution

- Add a `+` / **New session in project** action to each project-bucket header.
- Open the existing New Session page rather than introducing another creation flow.
- Prefill the selected agent and the exact repository/workspace checkout represented by that project bucket.
- Keep the folder and Local/Worktree choice editable before creation.
- If a bucket cannot resolve to an authorized creation target, show a disabled action with an explanatory tooltip instead of silently omitting it.
- Do not add new persistent project defaults when the target can be derived from the bucket itself.

### Alternatives considered

- Use the global Sessions `+` and select the folder for every new session. This works but repeats information already represented by the project bucket.
- Rely on the last New Session draft or recently selected folder. This is implicit and can select the wrong project after switching context.
- Create a custom group for every project and configure New Session defaults there. This duplicates Project grouping, requires parallel manual organization, and does not help users who prefer the Project view.

### Impact

Affected: Control UI users who organize sessions with **Group by → Project** and regularly open multiple sessions in one repository or workspace.

Severity: Persistent UX friction rather than data loss or a hard blocker.

Frequency: Every time another session is started for the current project.

Consequence: Repeated folder selection, more chances to start a session in the agent's default workspace by mistake, and an inconsistent creation experience between Custom Groups and Projects.

### Evidence/examples

Current behavior:

- Custom-group headers have a `+` action that opens New Session and assigns the group.
- Project-bucket headers have no corresponding action even though the bucket already identifies a repository/workspace checkout.
- The global Sessions `+` opens New Session without a semantic connection to the project header the user was working under.

The existing sidebar redesign established a unified New Session page and project/workspace-aware session rows: #103431.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Related but distinct: #138955 concerns misleading authorization/Git handling while saving custom-group New Session defaults. This request is specifically about a project-scoped creation affordance in **Group by → Project** and does not require weakening workspace authorization boundaries.

issues.body:
@steipete — non-blocking warning from a long, tool-heavy OpenClaw session.

## What happened

While running `anthropic/claude-opus-5` through the Claude CLI runtime, the session became erratic during work on a model-residency design. The design used an analogy in which machines are stable “apartment buildings,” models are replaceable “tenants,” and loading/unloading a model is admission/eviction so different models can be swapped for different work.

Around that point we observed:

- repeated session-lifecycle/tool-registration churn, including `The OpenClaw run is no longer active` and `resumed... changed=prompt-tools`;
- background work being stopped or losing continuity;
- unreliable response to a direct model-switch instruction;
- a file-integrity incident: after a prior shell command changed the persistent working directory, two later relative `cat >> MEMORY.md` writes silently created `projects/mac-deployment-2026-10/MEMORY.md` instead of updating the workspace-root `MEMORY.md`.

The last item was recoverable and did **not** corrupt the root file: five misplaced entries were merged into the correct file, the stray file was removed, and a workspace sweep found no other misplaced control/memory files. The immediate technical chain was persistent shell CWD + relative path + append redirection silently creating a new file.

## Recovery correlation

Changing the session from Opus/Claude CLI to `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the OpenClaw Default runtime helped the agent recover operationally: it identified the misplaced writes, repaired the files, verified the intended root file, and documented safeguards. This is a correlation, not proof that Claude caused the gateway lifecycle events or that the model acted intentionally.

The operator was concerned that the timing—beginning when the tenant/eviction analogy was introduced—might indicate model-level resistance or intentional behavior. I cannot substantiate intent from the available evidence, so I am reporting the observable sequence rather than making that attribution.

## Suggested safeguards / investigation

1. Correlate model/runtime transitions with run-lifecycle and `changed=prompt-tools` events.
2. Reset or explicitly surface shell CWD between tool calls, or make persistence highly visible.
3. Warn or fail closed on relative writes to workspace control files such as `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `SOUL.md` when the resolved path is not the workspace root.
4. Preserve enough structured telemetry to distinguish model behavior from gateway/runtime/tool-registration failures.
5. Test whether a model-switch command can be delayed or lost while the active run is being resumed/re-registered.

This is not blocking current work; it is a safety and diagnosability warning because the same pattern could cause destructive file changes in a less recoverable case.

issues.body:
# [Feature]: Give Microsoft Teams a dedicated channel-detail presentation in the Control UI

## Summary

Give the Microsoft Teams channel its own channel-detail presentation (`control-ui.channel-detail.json`) so its detail page shows a Teams-specific title and subtitle instead of the generic fallback.

## Problem to solve

The Control UI renders a channel's detail/settings header from a per-plugin `control-ui.channel-detail.json` that declares a title key and subtitle key. Today only six channels ship one — Slack, Signal, Discord, iMessage, Telegram, and Google Chat. Microsoft Teams does not, so its channel detail falls back to the generic presentation: the shared `channels.generic.subtitle` and a title taken from the plugin's `meta.label` alone.

Teams is a first-class channel (`extensions/msteams` with `id: "msteams"`), yet its detail header is indistinguishable from any other un-declared channel — no Teams-specific wording in the header while six sibling channels have dedicated presentations.

**Frequency**: every visit to the Microsoft Teams channel detail page.
**Workaround**: none in the UI; the header simply shows generic copy.

## Proposed solution

Add `extensions/msteams/control-ui.channel-detail.json` declaring Teams' title/subtitle keys, mirroring the established pattern:

```json
{
  "pluginId": "msteams",
  "titleKey": "channels.msteams.title",
  "subtitleKey": "channels.msteams.subtitle"
}
```

Add the `channels.msteams.title` / `channels.msteams.subtitle` strings to the Control UI locale files.

### CLI/API changes

None. No new CLI surface; the change is confined to the Control UI channel detail presentation and its locale strings.

### Design details

- New file: `extensions/msteams/control-ui.channel-detail.json` (consumed by `ui/src/pages/channels/detail-presentation.ts` via `import.meta.glob`).
- Locale keys added to `ui/src/i18n/locales/*.ts`.
- No config, no migration, no RPC. Teams currently provides no `extraFacts`-compatible status field (its status uses appId/appPassword credential semantics), so this change is limited to title/subtitle — which is still the concrete, user-visible gap versus six sibling channels.

## Alternatives considered

- Option A: Bake Teams rendering into the shared Control UI. Why weaker: keeps channel-specific presentation in the core UI, exactly the split ownership the project is moving away from.
- Option B: Rely on the generic fallback. Why weaker: Teams is a first-class channel but gets the same generic header as any undeclared channel, unlike six siblings with dedicated presentations.

## Impact

- Affected users / systems / channels: anyone using Microsoft Teams and viewing its channel detail in the Control UI.
- Severity: cosmetic / informational (no behavior change).
- Frequency: every Microsoft Teams channel detail view.
- Consequences: none (additive presentation only).

## Evidence/examples

- Precedent: `extensions/discord/control-ui.channel-detail.json` and `extensions/imessage/...` declare only `titleKey`/`subtitleKey` (no extraFacts), matching this proposal's minimal shape.
- Loader: `ui/src/pages/channels/detail-presentation.ts` globs `extensions/*/control-ui.channel-detail.json`; msteams currently has none.
- Channel identity: `extensions/msteams/src/channel-config.ts` declares `id: "msteams"`, `label: "Microsoft Teams"`.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

- [ ] Yes, I plan to implement this myself
- [x] Maybe, with maintainer guidance
- [ ] No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

Scope is intentionally narrow: one JSON file + two locale strings. This follows the established per-plugin channel-detail presentation convention and does not touch the shared presentation implementation.

**Summary:**
In a 1:1 chat on the Control UI (web + mobile) signed in with an authenticated Gateway profile, the assistant/agent messages leave an empty avatar gutter on the left while the signed-in user's own messages always render an avatar (image or a generated initial), producing an asymmetric and unfinished-looking transcript.

2. Open a 1:1 chat with an agent and send a message; wait for the reply.
3. Observe the transcript: the user's own message shows an avatar on the trailing side; the assistant's message has an empty gutter on the leading side with no avatar drawn.

A consistent transcript — both the user's messages and the assistant's messages show an avatar, or neither does (clean, symmetric layout). Also, an option to hide the signed-in user's own avatar/initial would be expected.

The user's own messages always render an avatar (profile image, or generated initial when no image is set). The assistant messages reserve the avatar gutter but do not draw the avatar, leaving an empty gap. On the macOS app the assistant avatar does render, so the behavior differs by surface.

2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)

iOS (companion app); also reproduced on Control UI web.

iOS companion app / Control UI web.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp

openclaw -> deepseek

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading to 2026.8.2, the bundled `active-memory` plugin stopped performing recall entirely (0 recall transcripts across two days, with agent turns still running), and the stop produces no output at `info` level, so it is indistinguishable from "no relevant memory found".

### Steps to reproduce

Grounded on direct observation of one installation; the exact trigger is not established.

1. Run 2026.8.x with the bundled `active-memory` plugin enabled and `persistTranscripts: true`.
2. Run agent turns on the configured agent (here: 11 turns on the day of the upgrade, both `user` and `heartbeat` triggered).
3. Count the files written by the plugin per day:
   `find ~/.openclaw/plugins/active-memory/transcripts/agents/<agent>/active-memory -type f -newermt <day>`
4. Observe that the count drops to 0 from the moment the 2026.8.2 gateway starts, and stays 0.

### Expected behavior

Prior observed behavior on the same installation, same config, same paths:

```
2026-09-02 (full day, 8.1)   51 recall transcripts
2026-09-03 up to 11:55:26    105 recall transcripts
```

### Actual behavior

```
2026-09-03 after 15:36 (first 2026.8.2 gateway start)   0     ← 11 agent turns that same day
2026-09-04 (full day)                                   0
```

Confirmed by four independent channels over the same window:

- `0` lines matching `active-memory:` in `gateway.log`
- `0` occurrences of the plugin's context header (`ACTIVE_MEMORY_CONTEXT_HEADER`, `"Context:"`) in the submitted prompts of 11 turns
- `0` sessions named `active-memory-*` in the session store (the recall subagent session id prefix)
- no plugin status line on the session entry

The transcript directory did not move in 8.2 (`resolvePersistentTranscriptBaseDir` → `resolveStateDir()`), so this is an absence of writes, not a relocated artifact.

**The part that is a defect on its own, independently of the cause:** every early-exit path in the hook is `api.logger.debug?.(…)`. At `info`, these two states are indistinguishable:

```
"there was no relevant memory to recall"   ← normal operation
"the plugin did not run at all"            ← what happened here, for two days
```

On 8.1 there was one line per run (`active-memory: … done status=…`) that separated them; in 8.2 it is gone. An `info`-level signal — even just `recall skipped: <reason>` — would make this observable without enabling debug.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.2 (0965053)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), Node v26.7.0

### Install method

Global npm install (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), gateway run from a user LaunchAgent.

### Model

`gpt-5.6-sol` via the native OpenAI route; agent harness `openclaw`.

### Provider / routing chain

Agent harness `openclaw`; memory slot provided by a third-party memory plugin; `active-memory` `toolsAllow` limited to that plugin's search/get tools.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Hypothesis from reading the shipped code, offered as a lead and **not** as an observation:

`dist/extensions/active-memory/index.js` registers its hook with `requiresToolAuthority: true`:

```js
api.on("before_prompt_build", async (event, ctx) => {
  const toolAuthority = ctx.toolAuthority;
  if (!toolAuthority) { api.logger.debug?.("active-memory: recall skipped because this prompt has no turn tool authority"); return; }
  …
}, { timeoutMs: beforePromptBuildTimeoutMs, requiresToolAuthority: true });
```

That registration is only dispatched by the second pass, `runAuthorizedPromptBuild` (`includeRegistration: registration.requiresToolAuthority === true`), which the `openclaw` harness calls only when `attempt.toolAuthorityFingerprint` is present and `preserveExactPrompt` is false. **Question: under which conditions does 2026.8.2 not run that second pass, and is a plugin registered this way expected to stop silently in that case?**

Ruled out by measurement, to save repeating the path:

- not `getModelRef` returning null — the candidate list includes the current run's model;
- not a tool-policy block — the plugin's `toolsAllow` entries are within the agent's authority;
- not a moved artifact — same transcript directory before and after;
- not "no turns" — 11 agent turns on the boundary day, 0 transcripts.

### Logs

Counts above are the evidence; the per-run log line that would show the state no longer exists at `info`.

One related observation while trying to capture the debug-level reason: setting `logging.level: "debug"` was accepted and validated, and the gateway logged

```
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (logging.level)
```

but never `config hot reload applied`, and no debug records appeared (verified against a measured baseline of 0 debug records that day). There appears to be no runtime path to change the level (`logging.setLevel`, `logs.setLevel`, `gateway.setLogLevel`, `logging.configure` all return `unknown method`), so a restart seems to be required. Filing that separately if it is not already known — mentioned here only because it is why no debug-level evidence is attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots. All evidence is the file counts, log counts and prompt inspection described above, taken from one installation.

### Impact and severity

Medium. Memory context from the memory-slot plugin is still injected on every turn, so the agent is not left without memory; what stopped is `active-memory`'s per-turn active recall. The severity is mostly in the invisibility: on a production log level the stop looks exactly like "nothing relevant to recall", and it went unnoticed for two days on an installation that watches its own instruments.

issues.body:
## Problem

QA Lab confidence reports read a profile and lane artifacts from local paths. A reviewer receiving only the generated report cannot reproduce its classification after those paths change or disappear. A passing report also does not distinguish content integrity from producer authenticity or independently executed tests.

## Proposed contribution

Add a native QA Lab evidence export/verification flow and confidence-report replay:

- Export only explicitly selected profile/lane inputs into a bounded, versioned, portable bundle, retaining missing lanes rather than silently omitting them.
- Hash the exact captured bytes, reject unsafe paths and unsupported inputs, and verify against a SHA-256 digest received separately from the bundle.
- Replay the existing confidence classification over captured inputs without reading the producer's filesystem or executing artifact-provided commands.
- Keep the existing confidence verdict semantics; make integrity verification visibly distinct from a passing verdict, producer identity, and code correctness.

The implementation, synthetic fixtures, CLI integration, tests, and documentation would live in OpenClaw's existing QA Lab. No new runtime service, external project, harness fork, dependencies, or persistent-state schema is proposed.

## Boundaries

This is reproducibility of evidence classification, not deterministic re-execution of a model run, an attestation service, or a trusted Workboard completion badge. Independent candidate execution and verifier authority would need a separate design discussion. Bundle contents are explicitly selected but not automatically secret-redacted; operators must review inputs before sharing.

## Validation

Exercise capture/replay after source deletion, failure and missing-lane preservation, changed/truncated bytes, wrong expected digests, malformed envelopes, duplicate/escaping paths, symlinks, and bounded reads. Include a real CLI parser boundary and documentation.

issues.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw compacts context only when mechanical triggers fire: token pressure
(preflight threshold), provider context-overflow errors, the transcript byte
guard, or an explicit operator `/compact`. The model itself has no way to hand
the runtime a judgment call such as "this topic is concluded, summarize and
archive it before we start the next one."

This matters for long-lived assistant sessions that jump between unrelated
tasks: carrying a finished topic into a new one wastes context budget and
dilutes the summary that eventually gets produced under pressure. Multiple
community plugins exist as workarounds for compaction-related pain (for
example openclaw-context-compactor, openclaw-sticky-context,
openclaw-core-rotation), which suggests real demand for richer compaction
control.

## Proposed solution

Expose the decision to the model through a small built-in tool,
`session_compact`, following the existing `sessions_yield` pattern: the tool
records the request, and the runtime owns execution. Optional `focus` text has
the same semantics as the operator `/compact` focus.

Execution reuses the existing manual compaction pipeline after the current
turn completes (trigger `manual`, `force`, focus passed as
`customInstructions`), so checkpoints, before/after hooks, quality guards, and
provider/model overrides apply unchanged. No new config surface, no storage
changes, no schema changes.

## Alternatives considered

- Third-party plugin: plugins cannot cleanly tie tool availability to the
  runtime's ability to service a same-session compaction, and would duplicate
  the manual compaction orchestration the core already owns.
- Letting the model author the summary itself (older community attempts):
  bypasses the built-in summarizer quality guards and identifier-preservation
  policy; the runtime should stay the summary owner.

## Impact

Agents can proactively keep sessions tidy on topic shifts instead of only
reacting to pressure. Operators get the same guarantees as `/compact` (recent
turns kept, full history stays on disk).

## Bug type

## Beta release blocker

## Summary

The Gateway stopped servicing health, control, and `chat.history` requests for 157–276 seconds in three incidents on OpenClaw 2026.8.2. The host had available CPU and memory and recorded no OOM event.

A source-only comparison against current `main` at a922cf8993d0f728e68c8b8b51ee0f0df985316a shows that the relevant full-history path still exposes synchronous SQLite/history projection work through an async Gateway API. This does not prove that one named function caused the recorded stalls, but the architectural main-thread risk remains.

## Observed incidents

```
2026-09-03 03:03:44 UTC
chat.history: 187493 ms
liveness overdue: 157507 ms
host timing gap: about 157506 ms

2026-09-03 09:25:23 UTC
chat.history: 252214 ms
eventLoopDelayP99Ms: 252329.3
eventLoopUtilization: 1.0
cpuCoreRatio: 1.109
active: 1
waiting: 0
queued: 0
host timing gap: about 243575 ms

2026-09-03 09:40:09 UTC
chat.history: 282884 ms
host timing gap: about 275843 ms
completion task waits: about 291–321 seconds
```

Environment:
- OpenClaw: `2026.8.2 (0965053)`
- Linux x86_64
- CPU quota: 8 cores
- Memory limit: 24 GiB
- V8 heap limit: about 4.19 GiB
- Session database: about 824 MiB
- OOM / OOM kills: 0

One incident had one active interactive session and no queued subagents. Another occurred during concurrent completion delivery.

## Current-main code comparison

Compared inspected source `e0dad1fc133391c98b0763239d41fc3562c8c6fa` with current `main` at `a922cf8993d0f728e68c8b8b51ee0f0df985316a`.

The full-history and transcript-reader surfaces remain in:
- `src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.ts`
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-history-events.ts`

The async reader API still calls synchronous SQLite/history projection functions on the Gateway thread. Current main contains nearby performance work, but this boundary has not moved to a bounded worker task.

No live reproduction or CPU profile was run against current `main`. The runtime incidents are from 2026.8.2; persistence is assessed only from source comparison.

## Expected behavior

The Gateway should remain responsive to health and control requests while reading or projecting session history. One active session should not block the event loop for minutes.

## Requested maintainer decision

Please confirm the intended design boundary before implementation. One possible direction is to move bounded SQLite transcript reads plus JSON projection into the existing `WorkerTaskPool`, preserving current byte/message limits and validating transcript generation before accepting a result.

Before a PR, this needs:
1. a controlled reproduction;
2. a CPU profile during the stall;
3. agreement on the persistent-store/worker boundary;
4. an event-loop responsiveness test.

## Related reports

- #115908 reports a projection-reconcile livelock under sustained writes.
- #89392 reported stream-processing starvation during very long model responses.
- #136035 reports a stable 2026.8.2 startup stall.

This report covers three runtime stalls centered on `chat.history`, including an incident with one active session and no subagent queue. It does not claim those related reports have the same root cause.

issues.body:
## Environment
- OpenClaw **2026.9.1** (npm install, macOS host)
- macOS **26.6.2** (arm64)
- Control UI in **Microsoft Edge** (Chromium)

## Problem
When a session completes and the agent-completion notification is delivered via Web Push, the banner appears but **no sound plays**. I verified:
- System notification sounds are enabled (Settings → Notifications)
- Focus / Do-Not-Disturb is off
- Edge's notification sound setting is on
- Same behavior regardless of which notification category

Only the visual banner shows; it is completely silent.

## Root cause
In `dist/control-ui/sw.js`, `showNotification(title, options)` builds the options object **without a `sound` field**. On **macOS Chromium** (Chrome and Edge), a notification whose options omit `sound` is silent by default. On Windows/mobile the platform plays a default sound anyway, which is why this bug only manifests on macOS.

## Suggested fix
Add `sound: "default"` to the options passed to `showNotification()` in the service worker, e.g.:

```js
showNotification(title, { ...options, sound: "default" });
```

## Workaround for users
None available — the payload is assembled in the service worker, so there is no user-facing setting that can re-enable the sound.

---
*Reported from a macOS host; happy to test a fix if a dev build is provided.*

issues.body:
### Bug type
Plugin update / transient registry timeout

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.1, updating an official external npm plugin from the previous release cohort failed on npm metadata timeout even though:

- direct `npm view` against the same public registry succeeded;
- `openclaw plugins update ... --dry-run` correctly resolved the intended update;
- the exact package/version existed;
- `openclaw plugins install npm:<exact-version> --force` later succeeded immediately and produced a healthy post-upgrade state.

The same installation also repeatedly emitted a hard **3500 ms** timeout from `doctor --post-upgrade` while resolving the official plugin drift target.

This looks related to transient npm metadata handling, but does not appear to be an exact duplicate of #77616 or #127448.

### Environment

- OpenClaw: **2026.9.1 (ad6fe23)**
- OS: Ubuntu, Linux `6.8.0-138-generic` x64
- Node: `22.22.3`
- Install: npm global
- Plugin: official `@openclaw/searxng-plugin`
- Installed plugin before repair: **2026.8.2**
- Desired/release-cohort version: **2026.9.1**

### Reproduction / observed commands

After the core update to 2026.9.1, Doctor reported official plugin drift:

```text
Plugin searxng is 2026.8.2, but OpenClaw is 2026.9.1.
```

The package is present and resolves normally through npm:

```console
$ npm view @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 version \
    --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
2026.9.1
```

OpenClaw dry-run also resolves the update:

```console
$ openclaw plugins update @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 --dry-run
Would update searxng: 2026.8.2 -> 2026.9.1.
```

But the actual update failed:

```console
$ openclaw plugins update @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1
Failed to update searxng: npm view failed: termination timeout (no output from npm)
```

`doctor --post-upgrade` also repeatedly failed to confirm the exact repair target:

```text
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 3500ms (elapsed 3502ms)
operation=npm-registry-update-check
url=https://registry.npmjs.org/%40openclaw%2Fsearxng-plugin/2026.9.1

[warn] plugin.version_drift: Plugin searxng is 2026.8.2, but OpenClaw is 2026.9.1.
No confirmed repair target is available; check registry availability and rerun this command.
```

Running repair with a larger outer timeout completed but did not move the exact-pinned plugin:

```console
$ openclaw update repair --timeout 60
...
Updating plugins...
npm plugins: 0 updated, 1 unchanged.
Update finalization completed.
```

The install record still pointed to the old exact version:

```json
{
  "spec": "@openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.8.2",
  "resolvedVersion": "2026.8.2"
}
```

A forced exact install through the OpenClaw plugin manager succeeded:

```console
$ openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 --force
Installing @openclaw/searxng-plugin@2026.9.1 ...
Installed plugin: searxng
```

After Gateway restart:

```json
{
  "packageVersion": "2026.9.1",
  "version": "2026.9.1",
  "builtWithOpenClawVersion": "2026.9.1"
}
```

and:

```text
openclaw doctor --post-upgrade
post-upgrade: no findings
```

### Source-level observation in v2026.9.1

`src/infra/update-check-package-target.ts` defaults the npm package target lookup to 3500 ms:

```ts
export async function fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus(params: {
  ...
  timeoutMs?: number;
  ...
}): Promise<NpmPackageTargetStatus> {
  const timeoutMs = params.timeoutMs ?? 3500;
  ...
}
```

For exact-pinned plugin drift, `src/plugins/plugin-version-drift.ts` calls this helper without a timeout override:

```ts
await fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus({ packageName, target: requestedTarget })
```

That matches the observed `npm-registry-update-check` timeout at ~3500 ms.

This does not necessarily prove that the separate `npm view failed: termination timeout (no output from npm)` from `plugins update` has the exact same timeout owner, but both failures occurred in the same official-plugin repair flow and direct npm metadata access succeeded.

### Expected behavior

- A transient >3.5s npm registry response should not prevent Doctor from resolving a valid official release-cohort repair target.
- Registry target checks should probably retry/back off or use a less aggressive deadline for maintenance/update workflows.
- An outer maintenance timeout such as `openclaw update repair --timeout 60` should ideally be able to influence nested registry metadata checks, or the nested timeout should be documented separately.
- `openclaw plugins update <exact official package@version>` should tolerate brief npm startup/registry stalls similarly to a normal direct npm invocation instead of failing on a no-output timeout when the package is reachable.

### Actual behavior

A valid official plugin update was blocked by transient metadata deadlines. Manual exact reinstall through the same OpenClaw plugin manager was required to converge the plugin to the core release cohort.

### Related issues

- #77616 — transient `npm view` failure produced a misleading unsupported-spec error. Closed/fixed; this report is about the update still failing on timeout in 2026.9.1 and the 3500 ms drift target lookup.
- #127448 — preserved timeout/signal termination identity for npm metadata/pack failures. Closed/fixed; in this report the termination identity is now visible (`termination timeout`), but the operation still fails under ordinary transient latency.

### Impact

Low-to-medium availability/maintenance impact:

- core update can finish with an official plugin still on the previous release cohort;
- `doctor --post-upgrade` may be unable to provide an actionable exact repair target due to a short registry deadline;
- users may repeatedly retry update/repair even though npm itself is reachable;
- workaround requires a more invasive forced exact plugin reinstall.

issues.body:
## Summary

After an involuntary Gateway process death, background agent preparation failed with `SQLite session reclamation commit checkpoint expired`. The affected agent then permanently refused `chat.history`, `chat.metadata`, `models.list` and progress-card requests with `UNAVAILABLE`, instructing an offline Doctor repair. The interrupted modeling request could not continue.

This report concerns recovery/admission after a refused reclamation commit, not a request to change history retention or bypass current-authority checks.

## Environment and actual observation

- Linux x64, Node 24.21.0, managed user systemd Gateway.
- Installed full-package source candidate: 2026.9.8 / `190042328f3e7d88570a388163820e4b67836c5e` (includes the separate indexed-media producer repair in #166568).
- 2026-10-07 14:44:23 UTC: systemd-oomd killed the Gateway cgroup after system memory and swap exceeded its 90% threshold. This was not a manual restart or printer operation.
- 14:44:29: systemd restarted the Gateway automatically.
- 14:45:54: HTTP listener bound; agent preparation continued in the background.
- By 14:52:29: affected-agent RPCs consistently returned the checkpoint-expired error and `Sessions remain unavailable. Stop the Gateway, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to inspect and repair this agent database, and restart.`
- Supported read-only `doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-agent <affected-agent> --json` completed successfully: one target, 97 SQLite session entries, zero reported issues, no import or archival mutations. This inventory is not a full integrity certification.
- The host was heavily CPU/I/O constrained during recovery. Exact data has not been reproduced in a synthetic fixture yet.

## Source lead, not a proven complete root cause

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-commit.ts` uses a five-second worker decision wait. A host authorization callback that observes a cell no longer in REQUESTED throws the generic checkpoint-expired error; the worker has a distinct refused-request error and settlement/rollback protocol. Current main `9bdad160d80686de5d080e4f6f128736f4831aef` still has this same commit-decision code.

Please distinguish confirmed native rollback/refusal from uncertain mutation or failed close, and investigate how a late authorization/refused request is propagated into permanent agent readiness failure. Keep live-authority, database identity, integrity and write-settlement gates intact. Raising the timeout, clearing admission state by hand, deleting sessions or changing retention would not establish the producer repair.

## Expected / actual

Expected: crash recovery either completes through the supported owner or reports a specific durable-data risk; a safely refused and rolled-back cleanup request should not misdiagnose a healthy store as irrecoverably unavailable.

Actual: the affected agent remains unavailable after startup with the checkpoint error. No conversation rows, indexes, compaction summaries or history have been edited manually; no provider/model change or guard weakening was used.

Related: #162319 contains an earlier checkpoint-expired observation during cold archival, but its main request is a retention-policy decision. This incident is startup recovery becoming a persistent agent lockout.

issues.body:
## Problem

`pnpm test:coverage` exists and `test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts` defines V8 coverage thresholds, but the current default CI graph does not run `pnpm test:coverage` or an equivalent coverage-threshold lane. Normal `main`/PR validation runs many sharded Vitest configs, but it can stay green without proving the explicit coverage gate.

Noob explanation: tests can pass while the project quietly loses coverage. A coverage gate is the check that says "we still have enough tested code after this change." Right now OpenClaw has the command for that check, but default validation does not make GitHub run it automatically.

## Evidence from the 2026-06-03 auditor pass

- Issue creation snapshot: upstream `main` was `10830bc4a77cf12f0fcd36ba6c86459c7936cc98`.
- Closeout recheck snapshot: upstream `main` was `8de37e1ce4a98c165096f35ad3934388c62006f1`.
- `package.json` on `main` has `test:coverage`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts --coverage`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on `main` does not contain `test:coverage`, `pnpm test:coverage`, `test:perf:budget`, or `pnpm test:perf` by literal command name.
- `docs/reference/test.md` documents `pnpm test:coverage` and says it is a default-unit-lane coverage gate with thresholds.
- Previous apparent duplicate PR #61166 was closed as opened on the wrong repo and did not land.

## Recommended test design

Start with a narrow, low-noise coverage guardrail before making it a required PR check:

1. Add a CI lane or scheduled/manual workflow that runs `pnpm test:coverage` on trusted `main` first and uploads `coverage/lcov.info` plus a text summary.
2. Add a small workflow/contract test that proves the coverage lane still references the package script instead of duplicating a raw Vitest command.
3. Keep the first version non-blocking or main-only until runtime/noise is known from several green runs.
4. After thresholds and wall time stabilize, promote it to a required default validation path for Node-relevant changes or a changed-coverage lane such as `pnpm test:coverage:changed` if that gives a better PR signal.
5. Do not mix this with the runtime performance workflow; `OpenClaw Performance` is already a separate report-oriented workflow and should keep its own baseline/regression policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Default trusted validation runs an explicit coverage-threshold command or clearly documented equivalent.
- CI artifacts expose the coverage summary for humans.
- A repo test prevents the coverage guardrail from silently disappearing from the default validation path.
- The rollout plan states whether the first phase is advisory, main-only, scheduled, or PR-blocking.

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.4, Doctor without --fix refuses legacy workspace migration when Skill Workshop proposals are present, while --fix clears the blocker but also changes schedules, conversation bindings, and workspace instructions.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed with a private copy of an existing installation, not a minimal synthetic fixture:
1. Use OpenClaw 2026.9.4 with valid legacy workspace setup files and nine Skill Workshop proposals targeting those workspaces.
2. In a network/service-confined copy with paths rebased to the copy, run `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`.
3. Observe exit 1 and StartupMaintenanceRequiredError for legacy workspace setup state.

5. Compare workspace setup records, schedules, original Codex binding keys, and instruction files before and after.
6. Attempt `openclaw doctor --fix --only workspace-state`; observe rejection because --only requires --lint.
Private configuration and database payloads are not attached.

### Expected behavior

The documented repair should import valid workspace setup state before Skill Workshop processing reads it (https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/doctor/state-migrations). We need guidance on performing mandatory migration while declining unrelated binding cleanup, heartbeat conversion, and instruction merging. We have not found a documented selective-repair option and are not claiming one currently exists.

### Actual behavior

`doctor --non-interactive` exits 1 with a legacy workspace setup migration refusal.
`doctor --fix --non-interactive` exits 0 and imports setup records, but also removes 534 original Codex binding keys (reported as orphan cleanup), adds a heartbeat schedule (11 schedules become 12), and changes five instruction files. All nine Skill Workshop proposal IDs/statuses remain; shared database integrity passes. We have not established that every removed binding is operationally necessary; preservation is a requirement of our maintenance procedure. Exit 0 is not a claim of complete runtime readiness.
`doctor --fix --only workspace-state` exits 2 because the selector is lint-only.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)

### Operating system

macOS 26.7

### Install method

npm global installation using nvm-managed Node 24.18.0

### Model

Not applicable: local migration reproduction; no model inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: local Doctor CLI against copied state with network blocked.

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized excerpts:
StartupMaintenanceRequiredError: Doctor cannot repair this state: Legacy workspace setup state requires migration at [COPIED_WORKSPACE]/openclaw-workspace-state.json.
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue.

Full repair:
Migrated workspace setup state to SQLite.
Removed 534 orphaned Codex app-server session binding(s)

Selective repair attempt:
doctor lint options require --lint. Use `openclaw doctor --lint ...`.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/doctor/state-migrations
https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/doctor/running
Copied-state comparisons established the reported changes. No private databases, credentials, transcripts or instruction contents attached.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one multi-agent installation undergoing an upgrade. Update completion is on hold because the tested full repair exceeds our preservation requirements; two agents remain deliberately offline pending reviewed recovery. The workspace refusal was observed during the live repair attempt and reproduced in the corrected private copy. No claim about prevalence elsewhere or confirmed conversation-content loss.

### Additional information

Source review indicates detectLegacyWorkspaceState skips sources when doctorOnlyStateMigrations is false, while Skill Workshop processing can still access guarded workspace state. An earlier reduced copy without the proposals missed the failure; a corrected copy containing all nine reproduced it.
Is there a supported preservation-only procedure or official fix? We do not want to patch internal modules, delete setup guards or transplant database rows. The broad repair was applied only to the isolated copy. Last known good version for this specific migration: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With the claude-cli backend, a native Claude Code tool call that stays active without emitting progress is aborted by stuck-session recovery about 900 s after the last observed progress (`BLOCKED_TOOL_CALL_ABORT_FLOOR_MS`). Measured on 2026.9.5 with a native `Agent` call; a long native `Bash` call should hit the same floor on my reading of the code, but that is not reproduced. Knowing which tool is active is not the same as giving it a deadline that covers its legitimate duration: unlike #143396 the progress marker is not frozen while other tools complete — the one active tool is simply still open.

Discussed with Krill on Discord #support (thread 1556966545878687844), who suggested this narrowly scoped issue, cross-linked from #143396.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on 2026.9.5 (2026-10-03), Linux, all agents on `agentRuntime: claude-cli`:

1. An isolated cron job (`agentTurn`, model claude-opus-5-5) whose turn starts Claude Code's native `Agent` tool (in this run two `Agent` calls; one ended about 800 s in, the other stayed open; the job reads web pages and files) without the parent emitting further tool events.
2. While the `Agent` call is active, diagnostics log `stalled session … reason=blocked_tool_call … activeTool=Agent` every 30 s.
3. When `lastProgressAge` passes 900 s, stuck-session recovery aborts the run (`action=abort_embedded_run`), while the `Agent` call is still open. I have no child-side progress log proving the subagent was busy at that moment rather than hung; the job's later runs without a subagent completed normally.

On 2026.9.7 I have not yet reproduced a >900 s case: the floor is unchanged in the bundle (static inspection), and a 720 s silent Bash call (below the floor) ran through as a control.

### Expected behavior

A native tool call that is still legitimately running is not aborted at a fixed 900 s. Either an explicit native timeout (e.g. Bash `timeout`) becomes the recorded deadline (my reading is that today only `mcp__openclaw__*` tools get one), native `Agent` subagent activity counts as progress, or the floor is configurable.

### Actual behavior

The run is aborted at last-progress age ~906 s (`agent run aborted | OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT`, `cli terminal failure … error=CLI run aborted`), after 1,707 s total run time, while the native `Agent` tool call (age 1,660 s) was still open. The cron run is recorded as an error.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (observed); 2026.9.7 (c074824) unchanged per static inspection

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.8 x64

### Install method

npm global

### Model

claude-cli: claude-opus-5-5 (9.5 case); Claude Code 2.1.289 on the 9.7 host

### Provider / routing chain

agentRuntime claude-cli: OpenClaw Gateway → Claude Code subprocess (subscription login), no API-key provider in the path

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
2026-10-03 (2026.9.5), gateway journal; session keys, ids and job name elided (…):

17:29:07 [diagnostic] stalled session: … state=processing age=1677s queueDepth=0 reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call activeWorkKind=tool_call lastProgress=tool:Agent:ended lastProgressAge=876s activeTool=Agent … activeToolAge=1630s … recovery=none
17:29:37 [diagnostic] stalled session: … state=processing age=1707s queueDepth=0 reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call activeWorkKind=tool_call lastProgress=tool:Agent:ended lastProgressAge=906s activeTool=Agent … activeToolAge=1660s … recovery=checking
17:29:38 [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=1707914 … error=CLI run aborted
17:29:38 [diagnostic] stuck session recovery: … age=1707s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=0 …
17:29:38 [diagnostic] stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run … activeWorkKind=embedded_run … aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0
17:29:38 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron … outcome=error duration=1707986ms error="agent run aborted | OPENCLAW_DIRECT_ABORT"
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

_No response_

### Additional information

Code (9.7 bundle): `diagnostic-run-activity-*.mjs:268` `const BLOCKED_TOOL_CALL_ABORT_FLOOR_MS = 9e5`, used at :277 for `activeWorkKind === "tool_call"`; no config field found. My reading (static, not verified by Krill) is that a per-tool deadline is only recorded for `mcp__openclaw__*` tools.

Mitigation we use: Claude Code `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=840000` so a single Bash call stays below the floor (a 720 s `sleep` ran through on 9.7, warnings every 30 s, no abort). This does not cover native `Agent` calls. Explicitly backgrounded Bash is not an alternative on claude-cli (`--disallowedTools Bash(run_in_background:true)`; measured on 9.7: "Permission to use Bash with run_in_background:true has been denied").

Related: #143396 (marker pinned while later tools complete), #157647 (background continuation hits the CLI no-output watchdog), #156331 (same floor, ACP backend).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.5, typesafe_jev is reported as loaded and resolves through the standalone tool resolver, but fresh main-agent runs fail with “no registered tools matched” before inference.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on the affected installation:

1. Install and enable the local typesafe-jev plugin using defineToolPlugin, with contracts.tools: ["typesafe_jev"].
2. Set agents.entries.main.tools.allow and the configured local-Ollama model allowlists to ["typesafe_jev"].
3. Confirm plugin inspection reports the plugin loaded and toolNames: ["typesafe_jev"].
4. Run the installed standalone plugin-tool resolver with the effective configuration. It returns ["typesafe_jev"].
5. Submit a main-agent request in a fresh session through the running Gateway.
6. Observe failure during tool assembly, before model inference, with “no registered tools matched”.

The failure persisted after a managed Gateway restart and a fresh-session probe. The attached report contains the retained reproduction details. A separate clean-install reproduction has not been established.

### Expected behavior

The explicitly allowed typesafe_jev tool should be available during main-agent tool assembly.

Reference: the documented tool-plugin interface at https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/tool-plugins. The plugin uses defineToolPlugin and declares contracts.tools. On this installation, the standalone resolver successfully materialises the tool using the effective configuration.

### Actual behavior

Plugin inspection reports typesafe_jev as registered, and standalone resolution returns ["typesafe_jev"].

Live main-agent execution instead fails during tool assembly:

No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist
(tools.byProvider.allow: typesafe_jev; agents.main.tools.allow: typesafe_jev);
no registered tools matched.

No model inference or TypeSafe/Jev request occurs during these failed probes. The Gateway health endpoint remains live.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5, build ec9c1a13db89

### Operating system

macOS on Apple Silicon Mac mini; exact current macOS version not captured in the retained investigation summary.

### Install method

Official npm package in the Homebrew prefix, managed by a macOS LaunchAgent using Homebrew Node v26.7.0. No custom OpenClaw core patch. typesafe-jev is installed as a linked local plugin.

### Model

Main is configured for ollama/llama3.2:3b. Tool assembly fails before model invocation.

### Provider / routing chain

Request → local OpenClaw Gateway → main-agent tool assembly → failure before provider invocation.  Configured model provider: local Ollama. No TypeSafe/Jev API request is reached.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Main and the ollama/llama3.2:3b and ollama/qwen3.5:9b tool policies allow only typesafe_jev. No group:plugins or general exec grant is enabled.

The plugin invokes a fixed local TypeSafe wrapper. Credentials are resolved through macOS Keychain, but tool execution and credential use are not reached by the failing agent probes.

### Logs

```shell
Gateway health:
{"ok":true,"status":"live"}

Plugin inspection:
Plugin: typesafe-jev
Enabled and loaded
toolNames: ["typesafe_jev"]

Standalone resolver result:
["typesafe_jev"]

Fresh main-agent session:
No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist
(tools.byProvider.allow: typesafe_jev; agents.main.tools.allow: typesafe_jev);
no registered tools matched.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Attached: OPENCLAW_TYPESAFE_JEV_PREPARED_RUNTIME_REPORT_2026_09_20.md

The sanitised report records the reproduction and investigated boundary:

- dist/tools-CVjO7Ltb.mjs: resolvePluginToolLoadState, around lines 257–279.
- dist/openclaw-tools-DIxownJF.mjs: prepared runtime supplied to resolvePluginTools.

Standalone resolution succeeds; live agent assembly using the prepared runtime fails. The prepared-registry handoff is the suspected failure boundary, pending maintainer confirmation.

Documentation consulted:
https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/tool-plugins
https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/sdk-overview/host-hooks # OpenClaw TypeSafe/Jev Prepared-Runtime Registration Report

## Scope

This is a sanitised local developer report for the unresolved runtime boundary.
It contains no credentials, private requests, or model output. It is not an
external issue submission.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)`
- Agent: `main`, using the existing local-Ollama route
- Plugin: linked local `typesafe-jev`, enabled
- Manifest contract: `contracts.tools: ["typesafe_jev"]`
- Effective tool policy: main and the configured local-Ollama routes allow only
  `typesafe_jev`; `exec`, `group:plugins`, and general execution are absent.

The plugin uses the official `defineToolPlugin` fixed-tool form and has the
same direct `execute` shape as OpenClaw's bundled `llm-task` example. Its
manifest identifier, enabled installation identity, and declared tool name
match. The Keychain-backed wrapper was not invoked during this investigation.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Load the installed OpenClaw effective configuration in a read-only Node
   process.
2. Acquire the installed standalone plugin-tool resolver with
   `toolAllowlist: ["typesafe_jev"]` and an empty denylist.
3. Enumerate the resolver result.
4. Start a fresh normal Gateway/main session with the same effective policy and
   a prompt that would otherwise request the tool.

Expected: both registrations enumerate `typesafe_jev`, so the fresh main
session can begin model execution with the bounded tool available.

Actual: step 3 returns exactly `["typesafe_jev"]`. Step 4 fails before model
execution with:

```
No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist
(tools.byProvider.allow: typesafe_jev; agents.main.tools.allow: typesafe_jev);
no registered tools matched.
```

The failure was reproduced in a fresh session, not a retained session. It did
not invoke a model, the Jev wrapper, or the TypeSafe service.

## Failing boundary

The installed main-agent command path first acquires a prepared model-runtime
snapshot in `agent-command-CZJyvgsL.mjs`, then executes the run inside that
generation. `resolveOpenClawPluginToolsForOptions` in
`openclaw-tools-DIxownJF.mjs` passes
`preparedModelRuntime.pluginRegistry` to `resolvePluginTools`. The standalone
resolver instead materialises from the active runtime registration and finds
the tool.

The official runtime documentation explicitly says prepared agent model
runtimes own fresh model-selected registrations rather than reusing the global
registry cache. That contract is consistent with the observed split: the
standalone/active registry contains `typesafe_jev`, while the prepared registry
selected for the normal main run has no matching agent tool. The first observed
loss is therefore at prepared-runtime registry selection/creation, before
main-agent tool filtering.

## Contract and issue check

The official plugin-tool documentation says `defineToolPlugin` is the supported
form for fixed names and requires a matching manifest tool contract. Both are
present. The public issue about silent rejection without `contracts.tools`
(OpenClaw #77800) is not applicable: this plugin declares the contract and is
visible to standalone resolution. Related public allowlist reports do not
document a configuration switch that makes a prepared model-runtime registry
adopt an otherwise correctly registered ordinary tool plugin.

No supported plugin-manifest, installation, or narrow-policy correction was
identified. Changing to broad plugin groups or general execution would neither
repair this prepared-registry mismatch nor preserve the requested security
boundary, so it was not attempted. OpenClaw core was not patched or rebuilt.

## Requested developer action

Reproduce the two resolver paths above on `2026.9.5` with a fixed-name tool
plugin that declares `contracts.tools`. Compare the prepared model-runtime
registry's registered tool names with the active registry before
`resolveOpenClawPluginToolsForOptions` calls `resolvePluginTools`. Ensure the
prepared registry includes normal enabled tool plugins, or provide a supported
configuration/API contract for a tool plugin to participate in that registry.

## Current acceptance status

Direct main-agent Jev acceptance is blocked at the described pre-model
registration boundary. Genuine Jev calls used: `0/3`. Telegram DM acceptance
was not prepared or attempted because it cannot establish a truthful end-to-end
result until direct main can call the tool. The Gateway remains live and the
unrelated Codex OpenClaw plugin remains disabled.


### Impact and severity

Affected system: one local OpenClaw installation and its main agent.

Severity: blocks the TypeSafe/Jev integration workflow.

Frequency: reproduced across repeated direct-agent probes, including after a managed restart and with a fresh session. Wider prevalence is unknown.

Consequence: main-agent requests fail before inference. Direct Jev acceptance cannot complete, so Telegram-to-Jev acceptance has not been attempted. No data loss was observed from this registration failure.

### Additional information

No previously working version of this integration has been established, so this is not claimed as a regression.

The plugin manifest already contains contracts.tools: ["typesafe_jev"]; this is not an observed missing-contract case.

Please confirm whether a supported registration step is missing or whether prepared-runtime tool registration requires a correction. We have not patched OpenClaw core or broadened tool permissions.
