prs.title: perf(workspace): persist incremental checkpoint manifests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Managed sandbox command checkpoints capture, transfer, and persist a complete workspace manifest even when only a few files changed. The recurring reconciliation trigger is the command checkpoint, introduced before the investigated revision range (`28d8ee4f096b`, #152641). Reconciliation/comparison/watcher modules are identical between `7e3fdabe` and `c16b5166`; #178233 adds explicit PR preparation, not a new watcher trigger.

## User Impact

**Approved shared-state `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump: 30 → 31. The agent database version stays 31. Run the backed-up Doctor migration before deployment. Rolling back to an older checkpoint writer requires the verified pre-upgrade backup.**

The local workspace owner now persists per-path baselines and directory subtree digests. Checkpoint receipts contain changed records, deletion tombstones, and previous/resulting roots. One acceptance transaction advances nodes, root, and receipt; interrupted work is recovered or rolled back. Existing baselines convert resumably, and pending legacy receipts retain their original bytes until settlement. Archive/publication consumers still receive complete manifests.

Fresh host Git-index admission remains in every operation. Filesystem discovery still enumerates additions/deletions; hashes are reused only when dev/ino/size/mtime/ctime match. Discovery and baseline-row loading remain O(total paths), while hashing, manifest construction/transfer, and persistence become incremental. Watch events do not authorize skipping discovery. Command checkpoint scheduling is unchanged.

## Evidence

Correctness proof covers real edits, deletions, renames, executable-mode changes, symlinks, same-size edits with restored mtime, interrupted reservation/application/acceptance, restart recovery, committed-but-lost replies, legacy pending receipts, schema rollback/retry, and full-manifest publication. The complete-manifest archive regression reproduces omission of an admitted nested `node_modules` input before the materializer retains the stored baseline’s input policy; all 33 projection tests pass afterward (two existing environment skips). A second regression reproduces lost edits after restoring older archives whose admitted build-input names resemble ignored directories; reading exact archived Git paths restores their custody without admitting future directory contents. The same 33-test file passes after this correction. The cancellation regression fails on the previous implementation: an accepted manifest read remains live after its workspace lease is cancelled. Passing the lease signal lets the existing read pool stop that scan.

Focused checks: checkpoint/tree/store 48 passed (2 existing skips); Gateway 65 passed (2 existing skips); schema-consumer follow-through 122 passed (6 existing skips); migration 3 passed; state-port/historical 22 passed; SQL guards 33 passed; wire fixture 8 passed; final workspace-store 11 passed. Export-collision, wrapper closure, test-plan, changed-file lint/format, one core typecheck lane, and canonical PostgreSQL generation/verification passed. Independent isolated reviews found no accepted P0–P2 findings. Eight reviewed patches retained identical stable patch IDs through the final rebase. Exact-head PR CI status: pending final accounting.

Production delta using the requested exclusions is +1,170 lines (+1,675/−505), including generated artifacts. The approved durable tree, receipt, and migration contract accounts for growth; the full-document checkpoint path retires after legacy receipts settle.

## Measurement

Real prepared managed-workspace checkpoints: 20,000 synthetic 128-byte files × {1, 100, 2,000} edits. The committed driver exercises the local checkpoint owner, real Git staging/application, SQLite receipts, canonical byte verification, and cleanup; it does not invoke a model or container. Baseline `540dbe9cbad8111603e6111d917a9beeef9eb09a`. Candidate refresh is pending the end of isolated CI attribution tests. Existing c1/c100 pairs use frozen inventory below; the two archive corrections are outside their timed checkpoint path. PR head is `f27c090192450202fd2f35d9ee5d4d82fae69150`; earlier checkpoint-only pairs use frozen inventory `88ec40c235390d7fbc40907b7bfc720a2e00d0708c8e9fb6e022540bcd05feb3`. Their warm fixtures have no archive snapshot, legacy baseline, or pending receipt, so neither changed archive branch executes. This qualification does not cover restored/archive checkpoint performance.

Concurrent pairs use one exclusive slot, interleaved CPUs, and swapped placement/preparation order. Preparation uses CPUs 0–63 at nice 19, CPUWeight/IOWeight 10, bounded memory. The shared guard pauses/aborts above load 60, Dirty 2 GiB, or production loop maximum 500 ms. Separate allocation-sampling runs from natural-GC/latency runs. Decisions use the mean of paired percentage deltas: reject ≥20% adverse mean or ≥10% adverse in both pairs. p95 needs ≥200 samples/side; p99 needs ≥1,000. Major GC is context below 50 collections/side; total/minor GC and promotion remain gates. Summed isolate pauses are GC work, not elapsed stop time. The supplied rules define v5; no additional v5.2 criteria were supplied.

**Measurement gate pending; do not merge yet.** All pre-cancellation-fix runs are superseded and excluded. The 100-file allocation pair 2 was also excluded after an overlapping post-run production-loop scrape reached 510.1 ms; a fresh swapped pair on the same source passed the guard and replaces it.

| Changed files | Main allocation/checkpoint, pair 1 | Pair 2 | Mean paired change | Workspace-family change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 135.015 → 8.272 MB | 134.871 → 8.197 MB | −93.898% | −94.534% |
| 100 | 139.724 → 11.393 MB | 137.745 → 11.876 MB | −91.612% | −92.016% |

Allocation: n=10 warm samples/side/pair. Natural-GC and eligible p95 results will replace this pending notice after the full matrix completes.

## CI Attribution and Deployment Signal

Pending final exact-head CI accounting. No CI reruns requested to chase green.

Exact production checkpoints/min cannot be recovered from retained telemetry. Completed-exec proxies were 22.7/min in the r178 hour and 35.6/min in the c16 profile window; these are not checkpoint counts. Workload growth is supported, not proven by a checkpoint counter. After deployment, compare workspace-family main allocation normalized by checkpoint/command volume and workspace size; track FSWatcher allocation separately.

## What Problem This Solves

The dependency audit reports five declarations as unused exports even though their implementations still serve live same-file callers or private test-support code. Keeping those declarations externally visible makes internal details look like supported module contracts and keeps the export check red.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. GitHub identity state, agent skill reset patches, publish-candidate changelog validation, native sandbox cases, and chat history anchor sampling continue through the same owners and call paths. Public SDK, CLI, configuration, permission, and test-support contracts remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change removes only unnecessary module visibility. Four declarations become file-private, the obsolete `GitHubIdentity` alias is removed, and its fixture derives the state type from the still-exported factory. ## Evidence

The failing export audit at the qualified base identified these exact five declarations. On the exact candidate tree, changed-file lint passed, all six selected type groups passed, and the 12 directly affected importer/owner files passed 869 tests. The Control UI build prerequisite also emitted a report-only startup-size overage. The actual paired hosted gate passed at 325,095 bytes, with identical candidate/base asset inventories, so this patch did not change shipped Control UI output. The exact UI tests and both independent reviews passed.

prs.title: fix(mcp): name the exact sign-in command and say plugin instead of connector
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a failed MCP browser sign-in tells the operator to "run openclaw mcp login with this connector's name", and runtime OAuth errors say "Run openclaw mcp login <name>" for every server. The CLI refuses while the Gateway runs and cannot sign in to plugin-declared servers at all (the Linear report). OpenClaw's own copy also calls plugins and MCP servers "connectors", a concept OpenClaw does not have.

## User Impact

User impact: when browser sign-in fails for a server under `mcp.servers`, the error now leads with retrying in Settings and spells out the terminal fallback exactly, for example `stop the Gateway with openclaw gateway stop, run openclaw mcp login linear, then start the Gateway again` (with `--profile`/`--container` when applicable). For a plugin-declared server, errors point to **Connect** on the plugin's page instead of a command that would fail. Runtime OAuth errors (missing, expired or unrefreshable credentials) follow the same rule. The composer **+** menu entry formerly labeled **Connectors** now reads **Plugins**, and Gateway errors, Control UI copy and docs say "plugin" or "MCP server" instead of "connector". No config keys, protocol fields, i18n keys or SDK exports change.

## Why This Change Was Made

On `main`, `openclaw mcp login` is offline-only (`offlineMcpAction` refuses while a Gateway owns the state) and resolves names only from `mcp.servers`. The operator OAuth identity now records whether `mcp.servers` defines the server (when the caller has config), and one helper in `mcp-oauth-identity.ts` picks the recovery text for both the browser sign-in handler and runtime OAuth errors: offline CLI steps only for `mcp.servers` entries, the plugin page for plugin-declared servers, the channel connect flow for per-requester credentials. OAuth behavior is unchanged; only messages change.

<details>
<summary>Changed strings</summary>

Gateway `mcp.authLogin` (`<name>` quoted; commands via `formatCliCommand`):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Connector sign-in requires an administrator connection. | Sign-in requires … |
| This connector cannot use operator browser sign-in. … | This MCP server cannot use operator browser sign-in. … |
| Open Settings on this Gateway to sign in, or use openclaw mcp login in its terminal. | `mcp.servers`: Open Settings …, or sign in from its terminal: *(same stop/login steps as below)*. Plugin: Open Settings on this Gateway to sign in. |
| Connector sign-in authority is no longer active. | Sign-in authority … |
| This connector changed. Close this dialog … | This MCP server changed. Close this dialog … |
| Authentication saved, … check the connector before trying again. | … check the MCP server … / … check the plugin … |
| Sign-in did not finish. Check the connector settings and try again, or run openclaw mcp login with this connector's name in this Gateway's terminal. | `mcp.servers`: Sign-in did not finish. Check the MCP server settings and try again, or sign in from this Gateway's terminal: stop the Gateway with openclaw gateway stop, run openclaw mcp login <name>, then start the Gateway again. Plugin: Sign-in did not finish. Check the plugin settings, then select Connect to try again. |

Runtime OAuth errors (`mcp-oauth.ts`, `mcp-oauth-provider.ts`): "… Run openclaw mcp login <name>." → `mcp.servers`: "… Sign in from Settings → MCP, or from the Gateway's terminal: <same steps>."; plugin: "… Select Connect on the plugin's page in Settings to sign in again."; no config at the call site: "… Sign in again from Settings: select Connect on the plugin's page, or Sign in on the MCP page."; per-requester: "… Reconnect from the channel through the MCP connect flow."

Control UI English: composer menu **Connectors** → **Plugins** (`chat.composer.menu.connectors`); `mcpServers.signInFailed`, `mcpServers.requesterSignIn`, `toolAccess.noTools` and `adminBlocked` now say "MCP server(s)" instead of "connector(s)".

Other copy: composer config-write note `composer connectors: add MCP server <name>` → `composer plugins: add MCP server <name>`; generated Slack app manifest description `<name> connector for OpenClaw` → `<name> app for OpenClaw` (free text; new manifests only); private `@openclaw/mcp-relay` package description and README "connector" → "plugin".

Docs follow the same wording; `docs/tools/mcp.md` now shows `openclaw gateway stop` before terminal sign-in and states the CLI covers only `mcp.servers`; `docs/web/control-ui/settings.md` says plugin-declared servers sign in from the plugin page (**Accounts** → **Connect**). The renamed `docs/date-time.md` heading keeps its old anchor.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Intentionally unchanged and follow-ups</summary>

Identifiers and contracts left alone:

- i18n keys (`menu.connectors`, `menu.noConnectors`), composer menu view id `"connectors"`, item values (`open-connectors`, `connector:<name>`, …) and `connectorItems()`.
- Package names, keywords, config keys, wire/protocol names: none renamed.
- Native Apple apps (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit`, `apps/ios`) still say "Connectors"; renaming needs the native string catalog and an Apple build, unavailable on this Linux host.
- Release notes (historical, release-owned).
- Third-party or unrelated meanings: Bot Framework "Bot Connector", OpenAI/Codex and Claude/ChatGPT connectors, `api.connectors.invoke`, Cloudflare tunnel connectors, package names, undici/TLS connectors, `ReplyConnector`, grammatical connectors.

Follow-ups (behavior, out of scope for this copy PR):

- `openclaw mcp login` cannot sign in to plugin-declared servers and refuses while the Gateway runs (CLI change).
- Root cause of the generic failure in the report: the `mcp.authLogin` ownership check compares the whole plugin metadata snapshot, so an unrelated plugin reload aborts sign-in.

</details>

## Evidence

Before:

![Composer + menu before: Connectors entry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e23b37b6-46d8-4cd1-b12c-3cbba821b60f)

![Plugin sign-in failure before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69d0bf3a-4c6e-4f2d-91e8-a2720832811e)

After:

![Composer + menu after: Plugins entry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bb9ed21-34d1-4bc1-87a5-deb2fbe3c9ca)

![Plugin sign-in failure after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25e5450c-e9dd-4c6b-9b50-0714aa61c9da)

Real Control UI, UI E2E harness, mocked Gateway.

- CLI behavior on `main`: `mcp login` is wrapped in `offlineMcpAction` (`onForeignOwner: "refuse"`) and `requireMcpServer` resolves only `mcp.servers`. A throwaway Vitest run of the real `registerMcpCli` with an enabled bundle plugin declaring `linear` printed `No MCP server named "linear" in …/openclaw.json.`
- `src/gateway/server.mcp-auth-login.test.ts` asserts the exact `mcp.servers` failure text (`openclaw gateway stop`, `openclaw mcp login docs`) and the plugin text; `src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts` asserts the runtime error for an `mcp.servers` entry (quoted `'Remote Docs'`) and for a plugin-declared server. All fail on `main`. Gateway 30/30 + OAuth 14/14 in 70s (proxy env unset; host proxy breaks the loopback OAuth fixture independently).
- OAuth consumers (`mcp-oauth-*`, `mcp-transport*`, `mcp-event-request`, `mcp-cli.oauth*`): 81 tests passed, 34s.
- `ui/src/components/mcp-servers-card.test.ts`: passed, 4.3s. `extensions/slack/src/setup-surface.test.ts`: 19/19, 16.9s.
- UI E2E `chat-composer-capability-menu`, `chat-skill-library`, `new-session-page.capability-menu`, `new-session-page.config-startup`: 19/19, 59s.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (1099s on the final tree): format, i18n catalog, docs, ratchets and every typecheck (core, core tests, UI, extensions, extension tests) green. Failures are all outside this diff: `max-lines` lint errors in 16 untouched files, the max-lines suppression ratchet (3 untouched UI files), unused exports in untouched files, and the core test shard root budget (726/749 vs advisory 720).
- Autoreview (Codex, up to P2) on both commits: no findings ("patch is correct", 0.9 / 0.92).

## Contributor credit

Reported and requested by @Patrick-Erichsen.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @Patrick-Erichsen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/253a9c10-5e39-44f7-8aae-b1191f1f07db)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/8b211410-8307-487c-b849-47c7df28fe07)

## Worked on by

- @Patrick-Erichsen

prs.body:
Supersedes #180069.

## What Problem This Solves

The loading-performance fixture starts a CLI process and Gateway connection for every seeded session.

## User Impact

Faster CI setup and waits, with no production or user-visible change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Seed sessions over one abortable, suite-owned setup connection and close it before the unchanged real CLI handoff. The selected-tail, restored Home, shared-avatar, pagination, and timing assertions remain.

This reapplied the same focused change after the disk-emergency interruption. It preserves assertions and timeouts. The original PR remains closed. We are now integrating the sidebar test repair from `origin/main`; full CI on the integrated head is pending.

## Integrated-head acceptance, frozen before the run

The same-workload baseline is completed scheduled main [39712703143](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39712703143), head `72ad5e9dd83ee4d2b7f89b236f7c9256fd579a55`: **Q 58.184406155 s**. The integrated head must finish at or below **52.3659655395 s** (at least 10% lower), retain the same ordered cases and assertions as that main workload, and pass the stricter of the original and current-main per-case caps. No original cap is relaxed. Integrated-head results are pending.

## Evidence

| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Native file metric | Q 92.598228576 s | Q 53.097977835 s | Q 39.916 s |

The historical file acceptance ceiling is **83.338405718399973 s** (10% reduction); every original ordered case must pass below its original 1.2× duration cap. Prior-head owning Test-step observation: **760 → 499 s** (28 → 28 files; same inventory). This is an observed shard comparison, not a causal savings claim.

Main [#180102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180102) (`8ccf0cc900c0177c7d1575a928831a58f016563a`) changed this test’s workload by removing the readiness observer and avatar-format assertions. The historical **Q 92.598228576 → 39.916 s** result and its savings apply only to the prior workload. The integrated head will be compared with a newly frozen current-main baseline using the same workload and the same 10% file-reduction and strict per-case acceptance rules. No speedup credit will be assigned to the other campaign’s deletions; the new baseline is frozen below and the integrated-head result is pending.

On the prior replacement head, local runtime tests/builds were not repeated. Formatting and `pnpm tsgo:ui` passed. The prior candidate and all fifteen determining owner inputs were byte-identical to the original scoped-clean independent review; source review was reused for that mechanical replacement; the replacement completed one full `ci:full` run.

On the prior replacement head, all original target test names, order, case counts and strict per-case duration caps passed, and the target file cleared its original 10% acceptance gate. The focused speed change preserves every target assertion and timeout. That prior CI attempt was not rerun. These results establish prior-head evidence for the previous workload. ## What Problem This Solves

Attachment readers need one reactive readiness model across initial loading, ticket renewal, and errors.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Text, PDF, and SVG attachment readers now use Solid async computations with `Loading` and `Errored` instead of parallel loading, result, and failure signals. ## What Problem This Solves

Plugin configuration and schema loading now use Solid readiness/error boundaries while keeping the existing synchronous config owner and editable forms.

The config owner already publishes a read completion/retirement receipt. This adds the equivalent schema receipt and consumes both in one shared status component used by Advanced settings and the plugin editor. Read failure keeps the existing retry control; write failure remains owned by the write path. The status slot sits beside the forms so suspension or an error cannot replace editable form DOM. Request admission, permission checks, draft writes, and disconnect rejection remain in the plain owner.

| 8 Throw-only context wrappers | 0 | 0 |
| 9 Independent sibling loading regions | 0 | 0; configuration and schema form one status |
| 10 Root/owner APIs | 0 | 0 |

The completion-only memo returns no resource data and has no separate in-flight affordance, so adding `isPending` or `latest` would add a dependency without replacing a visible flag. prs.title: fix(gateway): attribute prepared session-row stalls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prepared session-row reads and agent roster batches can produce `task=unattributed` main-thread stall warnings after their enclosing operation has awaited readiness. Related: #179929 (attribution extracted without its rejected read budget).

## User Impact

Operators can identify the RPC method or scheduled task behind a slow synchronous read. Examples: `gateway:rpc:sessions.list:session-rows:select` and `scheduler:maintenance:session-refresh:agent-roster`. Session selection, queueing, budgets, and response behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing stall owner now carries the code-owned operation name across awaits and times the select, prepare, consume, and roster scopes synchronously. It keeps the phase separate and constructs the combined label only when recording a stall. There is no per-row instrumentation, new queue, configuration, or schema. Runtime code is net +40 lines: carrying task identity across waits and timing the previously unnamed phases requires new diagnostic coverage. Existing timing, queue, and selection owners remain in place.

## Evidence

Independent review through P2 found no actionable issues. All 55 focused tests passed (stall monitor, prepared-row lifecycle, event-loop health, and roster configuration); both new prepared-row regressions failed on the original code with an empty stall report. Changed-file formatting/lint and the native core typecheck passed. The export-name collision guard and both source-closure files passed (22 cases). All three paired measurements pass the acceptance rule below; the result is neutral.

The focused test command took 32.73 seconds including worker preparation; the changed test files themselves took milliseconds. No Testbox lease or production Gateway mutation was used.

Measurement acceptance, recorded before running: two concurrent baseline/candidate pairs with identical synthetic 5,000-session/6,000-run fixtures, CPU placements swapped in pair 2, one shared measurement lock, and the shared production guard. Warm real WebSocket `sessions.list` requests use the same operation count per side. Measure RPC mean/p95/p99, sampled main-isolate allocation per RPC, total GC time per RPC, promotion, and event-loop delay; report sample counts and each side's maximum GC pause.

Decision rules: stop for a mean paired regression of at least 20%, or at least 10% adverse in both pairs. Opposite delta signs or baselines differing by more than 5× are inconclusive; report absolute and relative deltas, run a third pair for a gating metric, and decide on its absolute mean. p95 requires 200 samples per side; p99 requires 1,000; major GC requires 50 collections. Per-collection pause tails are context when collection counts fall at least 20% and total GC does not rise, except a maximum single pause above max(50 ms, twice baseline). Guard-interrupted pairs are discarded. This explicitly requested diagnostic change may land with neutral performance.


## Paired measurements: neutral

Three concurrent baseline/candidate pairs used identical synthetic 5,000-session / 6,000-retained-run fixtures and real WebSocket `sessions.list` calls. Each side completed 240 warmup requests and **2,400 measured requests returning 200 sidebar rows**. The first two pairs changed sign for allocation, promotion, total GC, and minor-GC p95, so they were inconclusive for those metrics under v5.2; the third pair resolves them using the absolute mean. No eligible metric reaches a +20% mean regression or is at least +10% adverse in both initial pairs. Pair 3's RPC p99 is +10.98% on its own; the three-pair absolute mean is −0.295 ms (−1.04% of mean baseline). This is neutral evidence, not a speedup claim.

Mean absolute deltas: **RPC latency −0.054659 ms; sampled allocation +3,941.99 bytes/RPC (+0.153%); total GC +0.000528612 ms/RPC (+0.359%); promotion −2,060.54 bytes/RPC (−2.477%)**. Minor-GC p95 is +0.077333 ms (+3.955%). Event-loop p99, minor-GC p99, and major-GC tails are context-only because their per-side sample counts are below the required thresholds. The candidate's maximum single GC pause is below `max(50 ms, 2 × baseline max)` in every pair.

Method: Linux x64, Node 26.12.1, source Gateways with the three changed owners substituted at their canonical module URLs. Baseline is `34a4e3bf238e1ebcb0c110d6b912f71bbeceed22`; candidate owner hashes match this PR head. The intervening rebase changes were UI-only; the measured owners and lockfile are unchanged. Both variants used the same resolver wrapper and verified source-package routing. Slot A held one exclusive lock per pair; baseline used even CPUs 96–126 in pairs 1/3 and odd CPUs 97–127 in pair 2, with candidate on the other interleaved set. Each side verified 16 available CPUs, `MemoryMax=16G`, `CPUWeight=10`, and `IOWeight=10`. Preparation used CPUs 0–63 with nice 19. The shared guard ran unchanged before and during each pair; no accepted pair had a guard violation. Setup-only failed attempts were excluded before measurement.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-broadcast-measure.ts \
  --entry <canonical-source-overlay-entry> --state-dir <synthetic-fixture> \
  --scenario sessions.list --row-mode sidebar --limit 200 \
  --clients 8 --rpc-concurrency 4 --warmup-operations 240 --operations 2400 \
  --runs 1 --rounds 1 --allocations --diagnostics --trace-gc \
  --capture-responses --heap-sampling-interval 32768 \
  --start-at <shared-epoch-ms> --port <isolated-port> --mock-port <isolated-mock-port>
```

There were no diagnostic drops, collection errors, or lost histogram samples. All **20 captured filter/sort/paging responses matched in each pair**, after canonical `expandSessionRowFacts` expansion and normalization of the documented timestamps, process-local `rowsRevision` UUIDs, and synthetic fixture paths. No row content, ordering, or count was removed.

Each pair cell is **baseline → candidate; absolute delta (relative delta)**. Tail sample counts are baseline/candidate. Means use all three accepted pairs; absolute means retain their sign.

## Live log proof

A separate isolated source Gateway served a real WebSocket `sessions.list` request (200 rows, totalCount 5,000). A task-only overlay injected one 350 ms synchronous pause into `selectRows`, guarded to fire only for `gateway:rpc:sessions.list`; this overlay was never used in the paired measurements. The existing event-loop logger emitted:

```text
2026-10-22T03:33:52.321+00:00 [event-loop] main-thread stall: elapsedMs=391 task="gateway:rpc:sessions.list:session-rows:select" taskMs=355
```

The controller exited 0 and the owned Gateway shut down. The shared guard reported no failure. The committed regression additionally proves background-task attribution after readiness waits (`scheduler:maintenance:session-refresh:session-rows:select`) and nested roster attribution (`...:agent-roster`).

## CI attribution

Exact-head CI run [39715651391](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39715651391) completed with two inherited non-aggregate failures; the aggregate CI gate remains red. No CI rerun was requested.

- `check-test-types-core-3`: `chat-details-output-intent.test.tsx:27,53` still supplies `artifactsLoading` after #180031 replaced that property with `artifactRead`. [Independent job 119618113966](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39715770605/job/119618113966) has the identical TS2353 errors. Both offending file blobs match this head, that job's actual merge checkout `b61ce93b0f6b775060b326d222a48c6bff31eb3a`, and its main parent `4611232730583082f5c49bd79f1f68dfbfbd1b60`.
- `checks-node-changed`: the pinned-Bun `x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts:944` anonymous read returned 503 instead of 200. #177556 diagnoses the existing fixture race: a second completion write can invalidate a public representation after the fixture's controller-settlement checkpoint. [#179939's baseline proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179939) reproduced the identical failure on both unchanged main `399a360fdfbb15546498a97886cef41fd8cac66b` and its candidate on their third focused invocations. The six causal public-cache/response and registry-completion modules are byte-identical here, and the fixture still has the old checkpoint. This fixture never starts the stall monitor, so the added task scopes call through synchronously. Our head and exact-parent focused Bun replays each passed once; those passes are context, not a claim that the race is fixed.

The focused replay used `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/x-publication-owner-composition.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, the supported path for this source-composition fixture. An initial invocation started automatic E2E build preparation and was stopped before running the test to respect the local compute limit. All other non-aggregate CI jobs passed or were intentionally skipped. Independent review remains clean; no review or security requirement is being waived.

prs.body: Closes #168918 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes unnecessary native chat transcript work while replies stream, active-run counters advance, or unchanged history arrives. ## User Impact Live replies update in short batches while token counters, completion and settled narration continue to update. Scrolling no longer competes with a transcript scroll command for every word. ## Why This Change Was Made Keep authoritative stream state current, pace its displayed text in the default run-loop mode, and observe that text inside the live bubble. Separate telemetry from lifecycle observation and ignore unchanged narration reconciliation. Native size-change anchoring follows the growing reply at the live edge. ## Evidence - **353 shared tests in 5 suites passed**, including coalescing, no transcript invalidation for new words, retired callbacks, history duplicate suppression, lifecycle and narration boundaries. - **60 native simulator tests passed** in RootTabsPresentationTests; the simulator app built successfully. - The original telemetry/history regression tests fail on stock code and pass with the observation fixes. - The hosted replay rendering tests settle the paced display before each rendering assertion; all 19 `ChatStreamReplayTests` pass with that settlement. The unused `liveAssistantText` projection is removed, and its comparison tests now call the retained `liveText` comparison. - SwiftFormat, changed-source strict SwiftLint and diff checks pass. ### Native app run The app ran the native UI test `testPerformanceReviewProof` on the iPhone 17 simulator: a 60-row transcript, a streamed reply, token-only updates, identical history refreshes and completion. It passed, with the 19 `ChatStreamReplayTests`, in the same run. [Evidence summary](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/318910fd42a1ab7eda3486c473e2b8312f92ee19/EVIDENCE.md) · [runtime log](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/318910fd42a1ab7eda3486c473e2b8312f92ee19/runtime-perfproof.log) · [recording](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/318910fd42a1ab7eda3486c473e2b8312f92ee19/recording.mov) · [diagnostic harness](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/318910fd42a1ab7eda3486c473e2b8312f92ee19/diagnostic-harness.patch) | Input to the app | Count | View work logged | |---|---|---| | Streamed assistant text events | 128 | 34 paced flushes, 25 transcript body evaluations | | Token-only updates | 12 | 13 token-indicator body evaluations, 1 transcript body evaluation | | History refreshes | 20 | 16 reported unchanged, 4 changed | | Terminal event | 1 | reply settles into history | Paced reply at the live edge, then a reader paused on rows 48 to 51 during streaming, after completion, and the settled transcript: AI-assisted. [Validation output and sanitized work record](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/2938698b8a2462fb1830753c6e558160). ### Existing physical-device recording [Native iPhone working-indicator recording](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/e8c686ac794bad2342dd9c71d9a935ebefaa5b13/phone-token-display.mp4) shows tokens advancing from 1,233 to 2,210 while elapsed time and activity text update. ![Working indicator from native recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/e8c686ac794bad2342dd9c71d9a935ebefaa5b13/phone-token-display.png)

prs.title: fix(config): preserve whitespace in secrets provider file paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw config set … --provider-source file --provider-path` trims the path before writing `secrets.providers.*.path`, so a credential file whose name ends in a space is silently rewritten to a neighboring path (or a missing path). The same trim hits `--provider-command` and `--provider-trusted-dir`, and resolution/exec validation previously re-trimmed via `resolveUserPath`, so a whitespace-bearing trusted directory could authorize the wrong neighbor executable.

## User Impact

User impact: provider builder paths keep their literal whitespace (matching `--batch-file` / `connect --target-file`), so trailing-space filenames no longer retarget the wrong secret file on disk. Whitespace-bearing `trustedDirs` authorize only executables literally inside that directory; the nearest neighbor without the trailing space is rejected before process creation. Ordinary paths without edge whitespace are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildProviderConfig` used `opts.providerPath?.trim()` (and `.trim()` on command / `normalizeStringEntries` on trusted dirs) before persisting into config. File/exec resolution used trimming `resolveUserPath`. Alix’s `#167116` already preserved connect target-file literals via `readNonBlankString`; this applies the same contract to the secrets provider builder and adds `resolveUserPathLiteral` for resolution + `assertSecureExecCommandPath`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/cli/config-cli-input.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.ts` (`resolveUserPathLiteral`), `src/secrets/exec-provider-path-validation.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.ts`; regressions in `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts`, `src/infra/home-dir.test.ts`, `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`
- Packaged CLI on head `bd8f2287fe3`: **shipped file-provider consume** (literal path beats distinguishable neighbor) + **real upgrade from npm `openclaw@2026.10.5`** (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: file+exec providers still load/validate/resolve) + exec allow/deny-before-start (below)
- Dedup: no open PR on provider-path whitespace; distinct from Alix `#167116` (connect only) and `#167118` (UTF-8 config bytes)

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

1. `--provider-path` ending in a space must be stored literally.
2. **Shipped CLI must consume that literal file-provider path** (not a trimmed neighbor): `node openclaw.mjs config set … --dry-run` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readSecureFile(resolveUserPathLiteral(path))`.
3. Existing `secrets.providers` written by published **v2026.10.5** must still load, validate, and resolve after upgrading the same state dir to this PR head.
4. (Already shown) Whitespace-bearing trustedDirs authorize only the literal helper; neighbor rejected before process creation.

### Canonical reachability path (file-provider consume)

Packaged `node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.<alias> --provider-source file --provider-path '<path with trailing space>' --provider-mode json` → persist literal path → `config set channels.discord.token --ref-provider <alias> --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json` → `collectDryRunResolvabilityErrors` → `resolveSecretRefValue` → `readFileProviderPayload` / `resolveUserPathLiteral` → `readSecureFile`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses `readNonBlankString` for builder persistence and `resolveUserPathLiteral` for file (and exec) resolution. No direct library `resolveSecretRefString` call in this proof — only the packaged CLI entrypoint.

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`, OpenClaw 2026.9.9) on head `bd8f2287fe3` with Node v24.16.0; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Paths redacted to `/tmp/oc168261.*/…`.

### Exact steps — shipped file-provider consume + neighbor

```bash
# Node 24.16+ (packaged CLI) on head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"
SECRET_SPACE="$ROOT/secret "          # trailing space
SECRET_NEIGHBOR="$ROOT/secret"        # no trailing space
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"GOOD"}' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' 'NOT_JSON_WRONG' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"   # distinguishable: INVALID JSON
chmod 600 "$SECRET_SPACE" "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"

node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.vault \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$SECRET_SPACE" --provider-mode json

# Shipped consume (resolvability via packaged dry-run — neighbor is invalid JSON)
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json

# Flip: corrupt spaced file; leave neighbor as VALID {"token":"WRONG"}
# Expect dry-run FAIL (still targets literal spaced path; trim would succeed via neighbor)
printf '%s\n' 'CORRUPT_NOT_JSON' > "$SECRET_SPACE"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"WRONG"}' > "$SECRET_NEIGHBOR"
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider vault --ref-source file --ref-id /token --dry-run --json
```

### Evidence after fix — shipped file-provider consume

```text
=== SETUP (file-provider consume) ===
node=v24.16.0
head=bd8f2287fe3
secret_space_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
secret_neighbor_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret'
space_content= {"token":"GOOD"}
neighbor_content= NOT_JSON_WRONG

=== A1) Persist file provider with trailing-space path ===
Updated secrets.providers.vault. No gateway restart needed.
stored_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/secret '
stored_source= file
stored_mode= json

=== A2) Shipped consume: config set --dry-run (neighbor INVALID JSON) ===
{
  "ok": true,
  "checks": { "resolvability": true, "resolvabilityComplete": true },
  "refsChecked": 1,
  "skippedExecRefs": 0
}
consume_dryrun_exit=0
# Success with invalid neighbor ⇒ packaged CLI read the literal spaced file (GOOD).

=== A3) Flip: spaced file CORRUPT; neighbor VALID {"token":"WRONG"} ===
{
  "ok": false,
  "errors": [{
    "kind": "resolvability",
    "message": "Unexpected token 'C', \"CORRUPT_NOT_JSON\\n\" is not valid JSON",
    "ref": "file:vault:/token"
  }]
}
flip_dryrun_exit=1
flip_result=DENIED_AS_EXPECTED (literal spaced path still targeted; neighbor not used)

=== A4) Restore spaced GOOD; consume green again ===
restore_ok= True
restore_dryrun_exit=0
```

### Exact steps — data-model compatibility / existing settings

```bash
# Simulate pre-fix stored settings (stable-style: no edge whitespace on provider path)
STATE2=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-compat.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE2" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE2/openclaw.json"
LEGACY_SECRET="$ROOT/legacy-secret.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"apiKey":"LEGACY_OK"}' > "$LEGACY_SECRET" && chmod 600 "$LEGACY_SECRET"
# write openclaw.json with secrets.providers.legacy.path = $LEGACY_SECRET (no edge whitespace)
# and channels.discord.token SecretRef → legacy:/apiKey

node openclaw.mjs config get secrets.providers.legacy
node openclaw.mjs config validate --json
node openclaw.mjs config set channels.discord.token \
  --ref-provider legacy --ref-source file --ref-id /apiKey --dry-run --json

# Ordinary (no-whitespace) path still works via CLI; legacy provider retained
ORD="$ROOT/ordinary.json"
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"ORDINARY"}' > "$ORD" && chmod 600 "$ORD"
node openclaw.mjs config set secrets.providers.ordinary \
  --provider-source file --provider-path "$ORD" --provider-mode json
```

### Evidence after fix — compatibility / upgrade retention

```text
=== B) COMPAT: legacy provider paths (no edge whitespace) on this head ===
wrote_legacy_config= /tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json
legacy_path_repr= '/tmp/oc168261.*/legacy-secret.json'

--- config get (loads existing stored provider) ---
{ "source": "…", "path": "…", "mode": "…" }   # redacted by CLI; loads OK

--- config validate ---
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/oc168261-compat.*/openclaw.json", ...}
validate_exit=0

--- shipped consume of legacy file provider ---
legacy_consume_ok= True
legacy_resolvability= True
legacy_refsChecked= 1
legacy_consume_exit=0

--- ordinary no-whitespace provider + legacy retained ---
Updated secrets.providers.ordinary. No gateway restart needed.
ordinary_path= /tmp/oc168261.*/ordinary.json
legacy_still_present= True
legacy_path_unchanged= True
ordinary_consume_ok= True
ordinary_consume_exit=0
```


### Exact steps — real upgrade from published v2026.10.5

```bash
# Authentic release binary (npm registry, not a hand-built fake):
#   npm install openclaw@2026.10.5
#   → OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
#   npm pack shasum 158d80b43644e2feba2a50647803562aa394e080
#   tarball sha256 dbb1bdcf2346292e25f672822b6a9928c234909abe6fee0df5fc4556e769d40e
export PATH="/path/to/node-v24.16.0/bin:$PATH"
OC_OLD=…/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs   # 2026.10.5
OC_NEW=…/openclaw.mjs                         # PR head bd8f2287fe3
ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade.XXXXXX)
STATE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc168261-upgrade-state.XXXXXX)
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$STATE" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$STATE/openclaw.json"

# 1) ON v2026.10.5 — create real secrets.providers (file + exec)
printf '%s\n' '{"token":"UPGRADE_OK","apiKey":"LEGACY_KEY"}' > "$ROOT/vault.json" && chmod 600 "$ROOT/vault.json"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/helpers"
# exec helper speaks protocolVersion 1
cat > "$ROOT/helpers/secret-helper.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash

Row changes received during a load are replayed without resurrecting rows invalidated afterward. Newer held metadata and matching observer receipts survive older roster snapshots; foreign global observer receipts are cleared. prs.title: fix(apple): realtime voice replies play too quietly
prs.body:
Related: #163146

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime voice replies that play through the Gateway relay are much quieter than other speech on the device, so the assistant is hard to hear on an iPhone speaker at a normal volume setting.

## User Impact

User impact: realtime voice replies on iPhone and Mac play about 8 dB louder at the same volume setting.

- This applies to every realtime provider that plays through the relay. Only xAI was measured. A provider that already sends louder speech will be held back by the limiter more often.
- iOS WebRTC realtime sessions and ordinary read-aloud use other players and are not changed.
- People who had turned the volume up to compensate will find voice replies louder than before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relay hands the provider's PCM to the player unchanged. Speech from xAI `grok-voice-latest` arrives at about -22 LUFS with peaks near -4.5 dBFS, and the player's mixer volume cannot go above 1.0, so the only way to raise it is to scale the samples.

The player now applies a fixed +9 dB gain to each 20 ms frame, with a peak limiter: when a frame's peak would pass -1 dBFS the gain drops for that whole frame, then recovers by about 1 dB per frame. Recovery is ramped inside the frame so the level does not step upward.

Tradeoffs, stated plainly:

- One fixed gain for all providers. It is one constant; making it per provider is the next step if another provider is found to arrive louder.
- The limiter has no lookahead, so a gain drop lands on a frame boundary as a step. The Evidence section measures how large those steps are on real speech.
- The ceiling is a sample ceiling. A true-peak meter reads above it; numbers below.

## Evidence

**Level, before and after.** 23.6 s of speech recorded from a live relay session with xAI `grok-voice-latest` (24 kHz mono, 1,180 frames), run through the same `RealtimePCMLoudness` code offline and measured with `ffmpeg` (`ebur128=peak=true`, `astats`):

| | Integrated | Loudness range | Sample peak | True peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | -21.9 LUFS | 3.0 LU | -4.5 dBFS | -4.4 dBTP |
| After | -13.6 LUFS | 3.6 LU | -1.0 dBFS | +0.6 dBTP |

The limiter acted in 66 of the 1,180 frames. No output sample exceeds the ceiling.

**Ceiling decision: keep -1 dBFS.** On the measured speech, it produces -13.6 LUFS integrated loudness and +0.6 dBTP on reconstruction between samples. The 0.6 dB intersample overshoot is inaudible in speech; live iPhone speaker checks across all five xAI voices reported no distortion. A -2 dBFS ceiling measures -14.2 LUFS and -0.4 dBTP, giving up 0.6 LU of useful phone-speaker loudness. The chosen ceiling preserves that loudness:

| Ceiling | Integrated | True peak |
|---|---|---|
| -1 dBFS (this PR) | -13.6 LUFS | +0.6 dBTP |
| -2 dBFS | -14.2 LUFS | -0.4 dBTP |
| -3 dBFS | -14.8 LUFS | -1.4 dBTP |

**Steps at frame boundaries.** On the same recording the gain dropped at 42 frame boundaries. The largest step the drop added between two neighboring samples was 5,158 counts. For scale, the 99th percentile of ordinary sample-to-sample steps in the same output is 8,085 counts, and the largest step anywhere (58,390) is in the provider's own signal in the middle of a frame. So on this recording the limiter adds no step larger than ones the speech already contains. This is one recording of one voice; it does not prove the absence of audible artifacts on other material.

**On a device.** An iPhone build with this change was used for live xAI voice calls on the speaker, with all five xAI voices. The listener judged the level sufficient and reported no distortion. This was by ear; there is no recording.

**Tests.** Two new tests in `RealtimePCMStreamingAudioPlayerTests.swift`:

- `quiet speech is lifted and loud frames stay under the ceiling`: gain, limiting, and gradual recovery.
- `one loud sample late in a frame holds the whole frame under the ceiling`: a frame of quiet samples with `Int16.min` at index 400.

`swift test --filter RealtimePCM` on the PR commit: 9 tests in 2 suites pass.

Each test was seen to fail with the fix weakened and the test file unchanged:

- Gain set to 1.0: the first test fails on all four expectations, starting with `Expectation failed: Self.samples(loudness.apply(to: Self.frame(1000))).allSatisfy { $0 == 2820 }`. The second test passes under this change, as it should: it checks the limiter, not the gain.
- Peak detector changed to ignore negative samples (`abs` removed): the run aborts in the second test with `Fatal error: Float value cannot be converted to Int16 because the result would be less than Int16.min`. The loud sample is no longer limited and overflows.

Shared kit suite on the PR commit: 2289 tests in 195 suites passed. SwiftFormat lint and strict SwiftLint are clean on both changed files.

AI-assisted (Claude).

prs.title: feat(plugins): let authenticated commands launch native subagents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin slash commands need a supported way to delegate bounded helper work under the current requester’s authority.

## User Impact

Plugin developers can explicitly opt authenticated commands into native helper sessions; older or undeclared commands keep the capability absent. Command text is committed as user input, `/stop` interrupts in-flight collection, and helpers remain subject to the requester’s tool ceiling. Authorized non-owners can spend helper-model budget when channel policy permits; this is not an owner-only feature. Maintainer acceptance and green upstream CI are required before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose the existing native spawn/collect runtime to explicitly opted-in plugin commands, without a reply-dispatch hook or a separately privileged agent turn.

- Add command registration `runtimeCapabilities: ["subagents"]` and optional `ctx.runtimeContext.subagents`. The managed registrar must receive a matching `contracts.commandRuntimeCapabilities` manifest declaration. The deprecated direct registrar cannot borrow a loaded plugin's declaration.
- Require `requireAuth: true`, actual sender authorization, current operator/plugin/registry authority, an admitted requester, committed user-turn input, and both native tools in the effective tool surface. Quoted/foreign command text and synthetic suggestions cannot obtain the capability. Ineligible/ordinary preparation paths see `undefined`; authority revocation fails closed. Later native spawn denial is explicit, with no administrator fallback.
- Extract the shared requester producer. Ingress owners supply current authorization, tool authority, turn commit/adoption and admission provenance explicitly; the exported per-run eligibility gate does not require a fabricated message context. Live commands use `auto-reply.plugin-command`. This is an extraction seam for later requester-admitted scheduled commands, **not an implementation or proof of scheduling**.
- Commit the real command text as a user turn before exposure, reusing that recorder commitment on `continueAgent: true`. Native children inherit requester lineage and the effective tool ceiling. The facade expires with the invocation; accepted children remain in native custody. Plugins own short bounded collection waits, persisted pending IDs and resume/handoff.
- Add optional host-sourced `selection: { requested, resolved?, observed? }` receipts. Resolution reads the exact child's canonical session controls, including hook-rewritten controls. Unknown facts stay absent; `observed` is not inferred. Later collection uses `requested: {}` when no raw request was durably recorded. Optional metadata failures/cancellation do not hide already-accepted IDs, including joined callers.

No new hook, scheduler, model-catalog capability, Goal admission rule or restart-recovery owner is added. Existing/undeclared commands and older hosts retain optional-capability compatibility.

## Evidence

**Rebased head `8ece1a1a6562f04226d3c0c1c676f1ec234fe87e`** on `main` `d20b7fbc6c72` (includes #180041). The only conflict was in test support. Main's test cleanup moved the sandbox cases into `subagent-spawn.plugin-native.test-support.ts` and added the `nativeRequestSource`/`holdNativeCapacity` helpers; S1's cases now use those helpers. No production file conflicted, and the PR diff is otherwise unchanged. At the rebased head `8ece1a1a`, the same 19-file focused and affected run passed **278 tests across six shards**, exit 0 (477.89 seconds). That includes 67 native production-boundary tests, all 32 command-boundary cases, and both `/stop` timings (2.04 seconds during collection, 2.76 seconds after settlement). Type-aware lint found 0 warnings and 0 errors on the 24 changed TypeScript files plus the routing MJS. Formatting, diff whitespace, line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race and import-cycle checks passed. `tsgo:core` and the five affected test graphs show only the existing baseline diagnostics described below; none involves a changed file.

**Review follow-up `eaf35b24`:** per ClawSweeper's test note, the Goal resume case in `server.chat-goal.test.ts` is restored to main's version. Its added plugin-command isolation assertion could not reach the command in that harness. The file is now byte-identical to `main` and passed 31/31. Formatting, diff whitespace, line-cap and import-cycle checks passed again on the 27-file diff.

At pre-rebase head `8459809`, the focused and affected run passed **272 tests in 19 files across six shards**, exit 0 (429.62 seconds), including all 66 native production-boundary tests. The command-boundary suite passed all 32 cases. A separate focused `/stop` run passed both stop timings; the in-flight case completed in about 1.5 seconds, not at the 30-second collect deadline.

**Per-file cost disclosure (independent final-head measurement):** `commands-plugin.native-subagents.test.ts` passed 32 cases in **58.9 seconds Vitest duration / 100.4 seconds wall time**, above the 30-second explanation threshold. The first case incurs about 20 seconds of cold tool-surface import. The disk-loaded plugin proves manifest admission and managed-versus-deprecated registration ownership; real authenticated ingress, authorization, effective tool-surface preparation and transcript commitment are necessary to catch facade exposure that a direct factory mock or source-text assertion would miss. Reachable `before_tool_call` denial also needs the real native tool layer. The production-boundary delta adds two `/stop` cases costing about **5 seconds total** (2.45 seconds after settlement and 2.82 seconds during collection in the independent run). A shared per-file default fixture is an optional composition follow-up, not a reason to replace these boundary assertions with cheaper non-behavioral tests.

Coverage includes a real disk-loaded declaring plugin and production command selection/execution/authorization/tool preparation/recorder paths; direct-registrar spoof refusal; absent capability for undeclared, quoted, foreign, synthetic and policy-denied input; explicit reachable `before_tool_call` denial; agent/session binding mismatch; blocked-commit fallback; commit-before-handler and recorder reuse; owner/registry revocation; retained-reference expiry; actual native queued child spawn; literal `custom/test-model` resolution; requester lineage/tool ceiling; concurrent replay and optional-metadata cancellation; `/stop` **during a running collection wait** and after settlement; reset/`not_owner`; capability advertisement; direct restart-safe/Goal admission refusal and existing Goal child-authority coverage. A Goal-to-command isolation assertion was removed because its harness could not reach the command (see the review follow-up above); Goal child-authority coverage is unchanged.

The original 13 plain-text cold-recovery scenarios are preserved. A separate 14th plain-text case exercises recovery with a declaring command registered. Another production command test checks the persisted absence of an agent recovery claim while a committed command handler awaits. **This does not simulate a process restart in the middle of a command handler**, and does not claim to.

Final-head type-aware lint passed for all 24 changed TypeScript files (zero warnings/errors), plus the routing MJS lint. Formatting passed for all 28 changed files. Diff whitespace, line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race and runtime import-cycle checks all passed.

## Base-versus-head qualification

Pinned clean base: `e9a671bf2173c7db41dd8567b3482a4a3abe987d`. Candidate: `8459809cb7edc7fa77808320a8becf00e49bdf17`. Both used the same supported global pnpm store and task-private HOME/TMPDIR/state/handoff SQLite paths, with inherited `OPENCLAW_*` removed. No live gateway update/restart/reload, live handoff store, or provider call was used.

| Check | Clean base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core typecheck | exit 2; 1 diagnostic | identical sorted diagnostics |
| agents-other test typegraph | exit 2; 1 | identical |
| messaging test typegraph | exit 2; 1 | identical |
| plugins-platform test typegraph | exit 2; 1 | identical |
| plugin-sdk test typegraph | exit 2; 1 | identical |
| gateway-server test typegraph | exit 2; 172 | identical |
| `pnpm build` | exit 1 at the TypeScript declaration-input boundary | same failure point |
| `pnpm build:runtime` | exit 0; startup JS gzip advisory 321.6/317.5 KiB | exit 0 at final head; identical advisory; built CLI `--version` exit 0 (`8459809`) |

The common diagnostic is `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-websocket.ts(244,11) TS2353`: `headers` is absent from `ResponsesWSClientOptions`. Gateway-server adds 171 existing `ui/src/**` CSS/library diagnostics. All six sorted diagnostic sets were byte-equal between base and candidate; no changed-file diagnostics appeared. The owner originally ran the six-graph comparison and declaration build at `7c8dfc5` and reused unchanged production evidence after the final test-admission wrapper. Independent requalification subsequently reran **all six graphs and both builds at final head `8459809` and the clean base**, confirming the same sorted diagnostics and declaration-build stop point. Runtime build and CLI smoke passed at the final head. Full build refuses the global-store TypeScript package because declaration inputs must be physically inside the checkout. These failures were reproduced on the clean base; neither the guard nor the dependency layout was weakened. The branch does not touch dependency manifests, lockfiles, tsconfigs, the affected AI transport or UI sources.

These base/candidate comparisons predate the rebase. Typecheck and declaration-build gates therefore remain **not green** in this local installation, and upstream CI qualifies the rebased head. The global-store layout is a plausible environmental contributor, not a proven complete diagnosis. Broad CI and live-provider execution remain unrun; a checkout-local/CI run must qualify those gates before upstream merge.

<details>
<summary>Reproducible local commands and compiler isolation</summary>

`RUN` below was `python3 /tmp/openclaw-s1-run.py`. That wrapper removed inherited `OPENCLAW_*` and set `HOME=/tmp/openclaw-s1-validation/home`, `TMPDIR=/tmp/openclaw-s1-validation/tmp`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-s1-validation/state` and `OPENCLAW_MANAGED_UPDATE_HANDOFF_DB=/tmp/openclaw-s1-validation/handoffs.sqlite`. Commands are repository-relative and were repeated in the clean-base checkout where noted.

~~~sh
RUN="python3 /tmp/openclaw-s1-run.py"
BASE=e9a671bf2173c7db41dd8567b3482a4a3abe987d

$RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile \
  --config.store-dir=/Users/jsy/Library/pnpm/store \
  --config.enable-global-virtual-store=true --config.package-import-method=auto

$RUN node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \

  src/plugins/restart-recovery-hook-safety.test.ts \
  src/plugins/manifest-contract-runtime.test.ts \
  src/plugins/manifest-contract-eligibility.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/commands-goal.test.ts src/gateway/server.chat-goal.test.ts \
  src/plugins/capability-summary.test.ts \

$RUN node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json \
  $(git diff --name-only "$BASE" -- '*.ts')
$RUN node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json \
  test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs
$RUN node scripts/run-format.mts --check $(git diff --name-only "$BASE")
git diff --check "$BASE"
$RUN pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base "$BASE"
$RUN pnpm check:assertion-safety
$RUN pnpm check:test-timeout-race-ratchet --base "$BASE"
$RUN pnpm check:import-cycles

# Both base and candidate: task-local compiler exception, not a shared-store edit.
# TSRS_BINARY alone is insufficient: the tsrs package must also be local.
mkdir -p .artifacts/compiler-inputs
compiler_package=$(realpath node_modules/tsrs)
compiler_binary=$(node --input-type=module -e \
  'import getExePath from "./node_modules/tsrs/lib/getExePath.js"; console.log(getExePath())')
cp -cR "$compiler_package" .artifacts/compiler-inputs/tsrs
cp -c "$compiler_binary" .artifacts/compiler-inputs/tsrs-binary
shasum -a 256 "$compiler_binary" .artifacts/compiler-inputs/tsrs-binary

ln -s ../.artifacts/compiler-inputs/tsrs node_modules/tsrs

$RUN env TSRS_BINARY="$PWD/.artifacts/compiler-inputs/tsrs-binary" pnpm tsgo:core
for graph in agents-other messaging plugins-platform gateway-server plugin-sdk; do
  $RUN env TSRS_BINARY="$PWD/.artifacts/compiler-inputs/tsrs-binary" \

The original and cloned pinned TSRS binaries matched SHA-256 `c04e14af7538fd95272c40e4902d6048aa637cecd40cb3429b94f646e20ebceb`. Compiler clones and consumed temporary checkout/build/test artifacts are task-local; no global package contents were changed.

</details>

## Review and risks

Earlier independent passes found no remaining P0–P3 findings in the corrected delta at `7c8dfc5` and the subsequent stop-proof delta at `8459809`; those are historical scoped verdicts, not an unqualified current approval. Current independent final-head requalification found no P0/P1 or new authority/lineage/tool-ceiling regression, but returned **NEEDS-FIXES for P2-N1 (the missing cost disclosure)** plus optional P3 follow-ups. The same reviewer closed P2-N1 after this disclosure was added; the optional P3s below remain open as follow-ups.

That reviewer independently passed 272 tests in 19 files (696.5 seconds wall), another 172 tests in 10 affected files, and temporary clean-merge checks against captured `origin/main` `76707b46ae79` (122 tests in 8 files plus 16 selected production-boundary cases). These are separate runs with overlap, not an additive unique-test total, and the temporary merge is not the frozen branch head.

A temporary Gateway probe traversed real `chat.send` → `executeDispatch` → `handlePluginCommand` → native command preparation. With a profile-authenticated operator it exposed the facade and committed command text before the handler; without recoverable profile authority the facade was absent. **Harness-only workaround:** the reviewer inserted the probe command into the request-scoped registry so it could be selected. This is not proof that the unchanged test registry loader discovers the command normally, nor installed SDK consumption. Spawn reached the native tool but was refused by the harness model catalog; **positive provider inference was not proved**.

The `/stop` mutation test proves that dropping the facade dispatch abort signal permits an unwanted continuation. **Limit:** its fixture connects the dispatch signal to the admitted session-turn owner signal by hand. The existing production `/stop` → controller → reply-dispatch abort link has sibling coverage, but that link is not re-proven end to end by this test.

Optional composition follow-ups (no S1 code/head changes in this draft-only correction): snapshot capability arrays once before validating/storing to harden trusted in-process forged arrays; document exactly supported profile/recorder-backed ingress; clarify the future scheduled-ingress comment and requester type seam; add an unhand-wired abort-link proof; document completed-result delivery after revocation; consider shared default-manifest fixtures. These remain explicit rather than being presented as fixed.

**Maintainer acceptance is required before merge** for this additive public capability/authority surface. No current CODEOWNERS entry covers the changed paths, and the local independent review does not replace upstream review.

Missing provenance on channel messages retains ordinary channel sender authorization, matching the existing reply-dispatch path. An authorized non-owner may spend child-model budget under that requester's tool ceiling; this is an operator-policy tradeoff, not an owner-only guarantee. A native slash surface targeting a different session fails closed. Selection describes host controls, not provider telemetry. Accepted children can outlive their command; retained facade references cannot.

prs.title: fix(ios): restore the last chat, send voice to the chat on screen, keep command drafts
prs.body: Related: #163153 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: on iOS, relaunching the app forgets the chat you were in; Talk, push-to-talk, Watch start and wake word can send to a different chat than the one on screen; child sessions are not nested under their parent in the sidebar; and a failed `/new`, `/reset` or `/compact` deletes the typed command. ## User Impact User impact: users reopen the app in the chat they left (per Gateway and agent), can rely on voice input going to the visible chat, see child sessions under their parents in the sidebar, and keep the typed command when a local command fails. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Last chat:** focus is saved per Gateway through the existing settings owner and restored before the first frame. Changing agent, or a roster refresh that removes the selected agent, clears both active and saved focus through the same selection transition, so a retired agent's chat cannot keep routing chat or Talk. Forgetting a Gateway erases its saved focus with the other per-Gateway preferences, so re-pairing the same Gateway does not reopen the forgotten chat. Reset Onboarding, which forgets every Gateway, erases their saved focus the same way. - **Talk routing:** Talk follows the presentation's current chat; callbacks from a replaced chat model are ignored; launch, enable, foreground, Watch start and wake word synchronize to the visible chat. - **Sidebar:** ancestry is resolved from child metadata before pin/group placement. - **Local commands:** `/new`, `/reset` and `/compact` report whether they ran. The draft is cleared only after the command ran, and only if it is still the draft that was submitted (same composer session, same revision, same text). `main` cleared it before running, so any failure lost the typed command. A stale compaction result is still dropped rather than applied to the chat the user moved to. ### Navigation parity Restore the saved chat on cold launch and prioritize child-side ancestry. This brings iOS into line with the Control UI, which [loads the saved Gateway-scoped chat](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/app/settings.ts#L403-L422) and [uses it for initial navigation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/app/bootstrap.ts#L238-L253). The macOS Dashboard uses the same Control UI with a [persistent per-profile WebKit data store](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardBrowserSessionStore.swift#L113-L130). The web sidebar [places children under their parents](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.ts#L100-L142) and [prioritizes child-side ancestry over parent-owned child lists](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e28a63d8b99e7fc11d6392d8fa3ae475584a5164/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-parent.ts#L18-L80); iOS should preserve that same placement when a parent roster no longer lists the child. ## Evidence - Shared kit suite: 2337 tests in 196 suites passed. - The iOS app builds for the simulator, and the app suites this change touches passed there: 365 tests in 5 suites (`GatewayConnectionControllerTests`, `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`, `RootTabsSidebarRegressionTests`, `TalkVisibleSessionTests`, `ChatLaunchRestoreTests`). - Strict SwiftLint is clean on the changed source files. Red → green: - **Command finishing after a chat switch** (new here, measured on `main` `bbaabd6ced1`): `command finishing after a chat switch consumes the draft it was typed in` fails for all three commands on the first version of this change, where a successful command that finished after the reader switched chats reported "did not run" (the typed command stayed in the old chat's draft; 3 issues), and passes once the result means "the command ran". An independent review of the first carve found this; the same gap was in #163153 as filed. - **Failed commands:** `failed local command keeps its draft` (3 commands) and `failed reset fallback keeps new command draft` fail on `main` (4 issues, measured on `bbaabd6ced1` with only these tests added), which clears the draft before running the command, and pass with the change. - **Talk routing:** 7 functions / 9 cases; 6 failed on the original pre-fix baseline (retired model refocused Talk onto a cron chat; cold launch, Watch start and wake word used stale keys). Measured for #163153. - **Roster removal:** `roster removal of the selected agent forgets its saved chat` fails without the fix (focus, saved focus and relaunch selection all keep `alpha`) and passes with it. Measured for #163153. - **Reset Onboarding:** `onboarding reset forgets saved chat focus for every paired gateway` fails without the fix (the saved chat survives the reset and reconnecting either Gateway reopens it; 4 issues) and passes with it. - **Forget Gateway:** `forget gateway erases only its saved chat focus` fails without the fix and passes with it; another Gateway's saved focus is kept. Measured for #163153. - **Agent switch:** `agent switch forgets the previous agent's saved chat` fails without the fix (2 expectation failures) and passes with it. Measured for #163153. - **Sidebar nesting:** six failing assertions on the original pre-fix baseline, plus a pinned-tree depth check. Measured for #163153. ### Cold launch against a real Gateway (simulator) The app, signed in to a scratch Gateway that holds synthetic chats, opens a non-main chat, is terminated, and is launched again as a new process. Nothing is mocked and no preference is seeded; the same UI test drives `main` `b1f3eac43cf` and this change. | | Before terminate | After relaunch | First `chat.history` request after relaunch | |---|---|---|---| | `main` | | | `agent:main:main` | | This change | | | `agent:main:dashboard:traffic-amber` | The request lines were recorded at the Gateway: [cold-history-requests.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/fd4cd088fe742ea46d117635c9e3b96da87adf11/ios-sessions/cold-launch/cold-history-requests.jsonl). ### Upgrade from the latest stable build (simulator) The latest stable release (v2026.10.1) is installed and paired with a scratch Gateway; the agent picker selects a second agent ("Proof Worker") and a saved chat is opened. The app is then replaced in place by a newer build, with no uninstall, erase, re-pairing or seeded preference, and launched. | Installed over stable | Gateway connects without re-pairing | Selected agent after launch | Saved chat | |---|---|---|---| | Stable again (relaunch) | yes | Proof Worker | listed, opens with its history | | `main` `b1f3eac43cf` | yes | Proof Worker | listed, opens with its history | | This change | yes | Proof Worker | listed, opens with its history | Stable, `main` and this change read the selected agent from the same key in the same defaults suite (`gateway.selectedAgentId.v2.`), and the saved chat focus this change adds is a new key beside it. | Stable, before | Stable relaunched | `main` over stable | This change over stable | Saved chat opened after the upgrade | |---|---|---|---|---| | | | | | | Gateway-side request lines for each case (connect, session list, history of the saved chat): [native-request-receipts.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/1485a517841de5cea29c76b45d318d342b657da4/ios-sessions/upgrade/native-request-receipts.jsonl). Test results: [native-test-results.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/1485a517841de5cea29c76b45d318d342b657da4/ios-sessions/upgrade/native-test-results.txt). ### Talk into a non-main chat after a relaunch (physical iPhone, real Gateway) On an iPhone running a build that carries these changes, a new chat (`agent:main:ios-01b3f936-…`, not the main chat) is opened and the app is force-quit. The recording starts on the phone's Home Screen (its upper half is blurred): the app is opened and comes back in that chat while it is still connecting to the Gateway, Talk is started, and the spoken request and the spoken reply appear in the chat on screen. The Gateway stores both in that chat's transcript. | Relaunch: the chat is back before the Gateway connects | Talk listening in the chat | The spoken turn in the same chat | |---|---|---| | | | | Recording, Home Screen to spoken turn (video only): [voice-relaunch-visible-chat.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0641f6f9200869b295200ddf89188c3e99b7d848/ios-sessions/voice/voice-relaunch-visible-chat.mp4). The composer placeholder names the agent (`main` until the roster loads), not the chat. - Gateway log lines: the app's connections close at 02:07:16Z and a new one opens at 02:07:19Z; `talk.session.create` follows on that connection at 02:07:24Z, and Talk session `092ede0b-…` completes its first turn at 02:07:35Z. [voice-gateway-receipts.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0641f6f9200869b295200ddf89188c3e99b7d848/ios-sessions/voice/voice-gateway-receipts.jsonl) - The chat's transcript as stored by the Gateway: rows 3 and 4 are the spoken request and reply, with `provenance.kind` `realtime_voice` and the ID of that Talk session. [voice-transcript-rows.jsonl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0641f6f9200869b295200ddf89188c3e99b7d848/ios-sessions/voice/voice-transcript-rows.jsonl) ### Sidebar nesting and a failed command (simulator, synthetic fixture that is not part of this PR) Three simulator UI tests on a synthetic chat were run on `main` `c1b9f4ec91e` and on this change (fresh simulator each time, `OpenClawUITests` scheme). The fixtures and tests are local-only evidence code, not in this PR: a parent chat with a child and a grandchild reported child-side, and a fixture whose `/compact` and `/reset` fail. | Test | `main` | this change | |---|---|---| | Sidebar shows the child under its parent and the grandchild under the child | fails (`CHILD_NOT_NESTED`: the child sits at the parent's indent, so the rows are a flat list) | passes | | A failed `/compact` keeps the typed command | fails (`DRAFT_LOST_AFTER_FAILED_COMMAND`: the composer is empty after the error) | passes | | A successful `/compact` clears the draft | passes | passes (consumption is unchanged) | | Sidebar on `main` | Sidebar with this change | |---|---| | | | | Failed `/compact` on `main` | Failed `/compact` with this change | |---|---| | | | The "before" command screenshot also shows a simulator system banner ("Ready for Apple Intelligence") that has nothing to do with the app. Physical iPhone (builds carrying these changes together with the rest of #163153): last-chat restoration was accepted on device. AI-assisted (Claude).

prs.title: fix(cron): optional-silent cron run fails after the agent collects its collector child's result
prs.body:
Closes #164887

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an isolated cron run that is allowed to stay silent fails with `Agent couldn't generate a response` when the agent spawned a collector-mode child, collected its result with `agents_wait`, and then ended with `NO_REPLY`.

## User Impact

User impact: a cron job that collects a collector child's result and then finishes silently now ends as a successful silent run, with no announcement, no incomplete-turn error, and no spawn-only child handoff. A run that still has an uncollected collector, a child that owns a completion message, or a required visible reply keeps its current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

`finalizeCronRun` treats a run as a spawn-only handoff whenever it has any accepted `sessions_spawn` receipt. The receipt records the acceptance only, so it could not tell a collector the parent already collected from one whose result is still outstanding. When this PR was opened, `shouldSkipNonVisibleTurnRetry` made the same check on the optional-silence path. Main's #170534 since made an exact `NO_REPLY` silent without that check, so after the rebase this PR no longer touches `incomplete-turn-recovery.ts`, and only the cron finalize change remains on that side.

The fix records the collection fact on the receipt itself. When `agents_wait` returns a child as `done`, the tool-end handler marks that run's `AcceptedSessionSpawn` as `collected`, and `mergeAcceptedSessionSpawnsForRun` keeps the flag across attempts, so compaction or provider fallback cannot drop it. A new `hasUncollectedSessionSpawn` is true when any accepted child is not collected or owns a completion message. Cron finalize uses it. The retry paths keep `hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, so a side-effecting spawn still blocks a replay, as the issue asks ("do not blindly exempt every accepted spawn"). The collected flag is only added to the receipt the producer stored first, so it keeps main's rule that a later projection cannot erase acceptance or revive a cancelled completion obligation.

A collector can be spawned in one attempt and collected in the next, after compaction or provider fallback replaces the attempt. The new attempt's subscription starts with an empty receipt list, so `agents_wait` also marks the receipt in the run-level map that `sessions_spawn` already fills at spawn time, keyed by the run's `operationalRunInstance`. The backend merge after the attempt then returns the collected receipt.

An earlier draft kept the evidence in tool metadata and changed only the silence check. Review found that cron finalize still counted every accepted spawn and that tool metadata resets on compaction, which is why the flag lives on the receipt.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto upstream/main c234ee3561a. prs.body:
Closes #179994

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes Dreaming settings silently losing typed text and number drafts when unrelated configuration updates arrive.

## User Impact
In-progress edits survive unrelated refreshes; actual committed-value changes still update the fields. Validation, autosave, config ownership, and reset-to-default behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Reuse the existing committed-value binding with a memoized text projection instead of reassigning the native input value whenever its surrounding config object refreshes. No new draft state or parser.

## Evidence

Production tsgo:ui passed (explicit native exit 0); full UI production build passed (exit 0). CI results remain pending.

- Browser suite setup attempts hit config startup stalls and system Chrome persistent-profile launch refusal; no passing layout-suite claim. The full-app Playwright before/after reproduction above did run successfully with fresh ephemeral contexts. No security/profile safeguards were bypassed.
- Actual isolated full Control UI + synthetic mock Gateway: Lookback days draft 14 becomes empty before; remains 14 after the same unrelated config publication. No page errors. The mock's existing config.set response was advertised explicitly in the page fixture.
- Independent Codex gpt-6.1-sol helper review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Reviewed full two-file diff plus existing liveValue implementation; review did not execute code.
- Smallest complete fix: one existing binding replaces unconditional native value writes; production +1 net line, no new state/owners, one regression covering text, numeric, commit, and changed committed values. CI timing pending.
