prs.title: fix: owner corrections queue behind reused child commands
prs.body:
Closes #180225. Related: #177698, #175763, #176245.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authenticated owner's normal WebChat correction queues behind an active child command when the reused session still carries a settled predecessor's recovery claim.

## User Impact

Compatible corrections can steer the original active execution again. Unresolved recovery claims and pending terminal sends keep their existing protection. No configuration, schema, dependency, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Command admission could decline to replace an older delivery claim, return the unchanged entry, and still start the new execution. Steering then rejected that execution as `stale-claim`, reported as `reply-owner-ended`.

Retire only a conclusively terminal predecessor with no outstanding delivery or recovery custody, using the existing cleanup owner. Publish the newly admitted claim only while the exact captured predecessor and session incarnation remain current. Keep the predecessor's terminal tombstone and remove its old request fingerprint. This is a focused follow-up to the merged consolidation, rather than another copy of the earlier steering repairs.

## Evidence

- **Actual built Gateway red/green:** owner parent chat → real `sessions_send` → dashboard child → normal Control UI `queueMode: "steer"` correction → actual read-tool checkpoint. The predecessor state is installed through the canonical writer while the isolated Gateway is stopped. All conversations, files, identities, and inference are synthetic; the HTTP provider is scripted loopback inference.
- **Before:** combined build `0bff6fe211deea8b5f7296a1a784ae4e93665768` has the new lifecycle/writer run but the old terminal delivery/source claim. While the original model response is still held, steering throws `Terminal source-reply delivery is closed (stale-claim)` and logs `reply-owner-ended`. The original child misses the correction and an additional child turn consumes it.
- **After:** exact focused commit `208a8ca6c25499441d57b71e53ef495e5375b9ca`, built on main `80b012dc04ae4c79936956db68a0ead1e3e462e2`, records the new delivery/source claim. The original child's next model request consumes the correction, its actual final completes successfully, and the same incarnation remains. There is no extra child turn or steering fallback. The driver and offline helpers are unchanged between runs; every fixture process is joined.
- **34 focused tests pass**, including a real command-admission regression that fails before the fix, settled-predecessor steering, old request-fingerprint cleanup, unresolved-claim preservation, and a terminal tombstone paired with a still-pending send. Wrapper wall time is 46.82 seconds across two shards; hosted CI timing is not yet available.
- Production and owning test types, scoped typed lint, formatting, whitespace, the canonical runtime build, and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. The review found no actionable defect; it independently inspected source and did not execute the product capture.

The original live incident's complete pre-rejection state was unavailable. This reproduces its rejection class and proves the persisted-state defect; it does not claim that every queued message has this cause. Clean-state ordinary chat, direct agent RPC, and actual parent-tool steering controls also pass.

Local activation: combined commit `9c6771331c57ca795db214954d0c98f6ca087c27` preserves the previous deployment and applies the identical focused patch. The full build passes; native stopped-state backup covers six databases and remains retained. Readiness, authenticated RPC, Node 24.22.1, all 27 plugin registrations, unchanged configuration/private service environment, and local plus tailnet UI assets verify the activation. This is operational verification, not an additional operator-conversation steering capture.

<details>
<summary>Scope and proof accounting</summary>

The change adds 58 production lines and 89 test lines, removing four production lines across four files. It reuses the terminal-delivery disposition and claim-cleanup owners, with no new state manager, schema, queue, authority grant, or test-only production hook. The necessary growth distinguishes settled predecessor retirement from unresolved custody and rechecks the exact captured claim at the existing write boundary.

The first exploratory collector omitted the UI's steering flag and was discarded as causal proof. The corrected clean-state controls and the seeded red/green sequence use the real UI request shape and hold the original execution through a tool checkpoint. No private endpoints, operator transcripts, credentials, or real Records data are included.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

File downloads should express their pending operation through Solid 2 while preserving cancellation, stale-result rejection, and retry behavior.

## User Impact

There is no intended user-visible change: the download button keeps its existing progress labels, duplicate-click prevention, error toast, and retry behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

File downloads manually toggled a rendering signal around their asynchronous read. `FileDownloadButton` now presents the admitted read through a native Solid action and an optimistic busy flag, which returns to idle when the action settles. The plain AbortController still owns admission, duplicate prevention, and cancellation; the original callback and scope checks still own which bytes may be saved and which error may be shown.

The action starts after the download callback’s synchronous selection update and races component retirement, so a callback that ignores abort cannot retain the presentation action. A scope-only replacement keeps the original outstanding read admitted, as before; its late save and error are rejected by the existing scope guard.

prs.title: fix(decisions): allow OpenAI batches up to 400 questions
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/277 (service-side Decisions support)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenAI Decisions batches containing 201–400 questions are rejected locally even though the current API accepts up to 400.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenAI and ClawRouter native Decisions V2 callers can evaluate up to 400 questions without truncation. Legacy V1 remains capped at 256; use `contractVersion: 2` for larger batches. No credential, deployment, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Align the shared OpenAI executor and both capability manifests with the official [Decisions reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/typescript/resources/decisions.md), and raise the shared V2 host ceiling. The 255-choice bound, provider-specific admission, and other resource budgets are unchanged. OpenAI, ClawRouter, and shared-limit docs are updated, including the previously missed ClawRouter 200-question statement.

The single-inline-image/4 MiB and JSON budgets remain integration limits, not full vendor wire-option parity. ClawRouter needs service-side support and an eligible key; this PR does not deploy it.

## Evidence

Published head: `41f478dc6e0dc0a7fa6945d5ceab8e541cbc91ef`; tree: `7f91509a01ffa129ffbc8afd1b6c323702957eaf`; main base: `c234ee3561a2ca46b6b847efbb129ffb1e8d46a9`. The publisher's metadata commit has the identical full tree as tested local head `be2c046bd939f990d7f00e8a6b84c97c39d89081`.

- Clean transplant of the independently reviewed candidate, no conflict or touched-file drift. Both diffs have stable patch ID `261195c475024aa8ab381c345f7ffd5b54a4ebca`.
- RED: production-only reversion on the identical patch produced 7 expected failures / 74 passes. Current local GREEN: **115 tests passed across eight files** (81 focused Decisions + 34 host/legacy/tool/prompt-prefix regressions). Tests cover complete 201/400 requests and answers, 401 rejection before transport/catalog, and manifest projection. Private handoff state verified; no paid live calls.
- Core, both provider packages, core-test other shard, and touched extension-test typechecks passed. Type-aware lint passed seven touched TypeScript files, zero errors/warnings. Format, docs format, whitespace, and both extension import-boundary checks passed. Initial missing generated SDK declarations were prepared by their tooling owner; package checks then passed without source/guard workarounds.
- Canonical affected-subpath API comparison (`decisions`, `decisions-openai-runtime`) against the actual base: **no API changes**, digest `ff7b090f`. Prior export-sync/surface-budget checks passed. Full-repository API comparison previously exceeded its 15-minute budget and was not repeated.
- All twelve touched files and four touched tests audited in full. API-only independent review of the identical patch found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Local suite wall time: 250.40s; host/validation/registry 67.64s, prefix 53.68s, tool 27.18s, OpenAI 44.40s, ClawRouter 37.91s. Real registry/prepared auth/catalog/HTTP/cancellation boundaries justify the integration coverage. Prior cold registry deadline failure remains recorded; passing isolated/current runs are not claimed as a timing repair.

### Exact-head CI and failure attribution

[Initial CI run 39712989203](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39712989203) completed with 36 successful jobs, 28 skipped and two failures (extension-bundle plus aggregate gate). Security/dependency reviews, all six selected Security High checks, and all three selected Critical Quality checks passed.

**Levanto: pre-existing deadline-sensitive fixture behavior, not a 400-question routing regression.** The [failed extension job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39712989203/job/119608820613) had native-usage and prepared-prefix failures at 572/628ms against a 500ms fixture deadline. The initial repository helper classified them unknown; the following investigation supplies baseline evidence:

- Ran the unmodified `extensions/levanto/registration.test.ts` **10 times serially at head and 10 at the exact merge-base**, alternating refs. Used the workflow's `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts`, `bun-all` policy, pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+ef37c31de`, same extension config and worker limits; only the include list was narrowed. Local host was macOS arm64, versus Linux x64 in CI.
- **Each ref had seven passing runs and three failing runs: 273 passing tests / seven failures.** All 14 failures exceeded 500ms and moved among unchanged fixture cases. The exact native-usage assertion failed on base at 530/1142ms and on head at 508ms; successful instances took 235–433ms. Original 13-file shard order also ran: head 246 passes; base 242 passes / two failures, including native usage at 601ms and a prepared-header case at 602ms.
- The prepared-prefix case passed all 20 natural repetitions (141–258ms at head; 122–450ms at base). A separate temporary, clock-controlled diagnostic passed **2/2 cases on each ref**: with 0ms consumed, the real provider sends the exact prefix URL and effective header; consuming 501ms from the original 500ms context returns unavailable/transport, makes no HTTP call, and leaves the recorded URL undefined. This explains the original symptom without pretending that exact CI scheduling stall was instrumented or naturally reproduced locally.
- Source trace: Levanto does consume shared V2 validation, but the only changed validator operation is comparing question count against 256 versus 400. Both failing fixtures have one question and take the same validation path. Levanto does not import the OpenAI executor; its URL/header/deadline/transport owners and provider fixture are byte-identical at base and head.

No production changes, timeout increases, assertion weakening, or retry-based test fixes were made. The temporary diagnostic was removed from both checkouts. These results establish inherited timing sensitivity; they do not repair it or identify the underlying scheduling stall.

**Provider scaffold:** [validation job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39712989184/job/119608444055) passed its generated build/test, then failed OpenClaw npm metadata lookup with HTTP 503 during npm's [Degraded Package Install and Publishing incident](https://stspg.io/fr89w5qkp7j4).

The authorized failed-job retry is pending npm registry recovery. CI is **not yet green**; this PR remains unmerged.

Supersedes #180011 and #179478. The former is blocked by damaged native-review checkout metadata; the latter is pinned to retired workflow `1e48ec3a9e3f`. This PR leaves their state and the shared template untouched.

## Problem and solution

The synchronous shell owner scheduled DOM completion through a detached Solid callback and kept a separate pending token. A renderless keyed branch in the mounted shell now registers `onSettled` for each view snapshot, outside the route-readiness boundary. The owner retains its coalesced completion promise; rendering settles it, and unmount settles outstanding work as false. This keeps focus restoration in the same Solid drain and removes the detached scheduler and token.

The existing regression mounts the real shell and retains its assertions for promise identity, caller disposal, and unmount cancellation. No visible markup, host tag, selector, class, route, lazy boundary, dependency, or domain authority changes.

Head `703dd9087d2659f8f9dc522db72b71072c5edf72` merges main `b98018c4433de6a471c7b9376156193debd91af9`. The sole conflict was the Details E2E fixture: main already fixes the empty-section timeout, so this merge keeps main's complete test and drops the redundant synthetic creator change. Head `5e7b6ed1624ecc680cbb83fe39d567789a0c18b5` adds a committed-route interaction precondition, waits for lazy attachment previews independently of the submit button, and records selection plus resolver/startup requests if agent navigation fails. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native language additions, removals, and primary-language changes waited for another native snapshot before appearing. A rejected native write also silently discarded the requested selection, leaving no visible way to retry.

Language edits now appear immediately while native replies settle. Failed edits remain selected with an inline error and Retry action. Retry resubmits only failed fields. Consecutive gestures compose synchronously, older acknowledgments cannot retire newer intent, and leaving Talk does not wait for an admitted edit.

## Ownership and implementation

The native capability exposes completion of its existing setter and releases waiting presenters when disposed, while suppressing retired callbacks and publications. The Solid presenter admits each edit through that owner before entering its action, presents selection and catalog together with `createOptimistic`, and reconciles through `refresh`.

The existing synchronous intent map still owns same-task gestures and per-field acknowledgment retirement. Its callback retains matching failed intent and the actionable error instead of discarding the error. Only the native owner publishes the authoritative snapshot. Shared optimistic catalog and positional option rendering keep values and labels coherent while older actions settle. The existing repeated-same-value matching contract is retained without additional revision machinery.

This head merges current main to resolve a real Updates conflict. It preserves main's complete Updates command-retirement implementation; the only adaptation there is explicitly discarding the native setter's newly exposed Promise. Other coupled callers and fixtures follow the same return contract. No dependency, setting, route, protocol, permission, or startup import boundary changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider still admits and settles the write; the UI refreshes its projection after that receipt and observes later board changes. prs.body:
Replaces https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/69822 with a maintainer-owned branch. Original feature by @gdibble (Gabriel Dibble), credited as co-author.

Related: #63374

## What Problem This Solves

Session-message subscribers can retain stale session state when a session is reset, replaced with a new session, or deleted while their WebSocket stays connected.

## User Impact

Subscribers can consume `socket.drain` notices for `reset`, `new`, and `delete`, including the session key, reason, timestamp, and resolved agent scope. Delivery remains best effort and subject to current subscription and access checks; existing sharing rules still fail closed when a deleted row no longer establishes access. Clients must reconcile state after reconnects.

No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ordered session-change publisher sends the notice to the union of session-list and matching message subscribers, once per connection, before `sessions.changed`. The broadcaster retains its scope, subscription, and sharing checks, including per-agent global-session routing. The protocol catalog, mobile non-consumption allowlist, and event documentation describe the new event.

This replacement carries only the session lifecycle feature and its review repairs. It excludes 21 database/deployment paths whose changes are already represented on main. It also excludes the later OpenAI-compatible HTTP 503 mapping and admission tests: those were added after the original May feature commit and are a separate concern. No unrelated ancestry is carried forward.

## Evidence

- Real WebSocket coverage exercises reset/new/delete with message-only, list-only, and overlapping subscriptions. Publisher tests cover ordering, union/deduplication, and selected-global routing; transport tests cover wrong-session, revoked-access, and node exclusion.
- The focused four-file run passed 47/49 tests. The existing recovery-state reset test hit its 120-second limit, and the delete socket case hit its event waiter. Exact replays of both passed with unchanged assertions and timeouts: recovery-state reset in 53.4 seconds; delete in 7.6 seconds, with all three notices and a successful RPC around 2.8 seconds after the request. The initial timeouts remain unexplained; the passing replay is not claimed as a fix. Temporary timing diagnostics were removed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, all 11 selected changed-test type graphs, targeted Oxlint, changed-file formatting, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm check:protocol-coverage` passed. Protocol coverage accounts for all 67 events.
- Codex branch autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings.

prs.title: feat(slack): create public channels from message actions
prs.body:
Closes #163782

## What problem this solves

OpenClaw’s Slack message tool cannot create a project channel, forcing operators to leave the workflow or use a separate integration.

## User impact

An operator can explicitly enable Slack channel creation with `channels.slack.actions.channels: true` (or the selected account’s equivalent). The action creates a public channel in the trusted workspace, invites the trusted requester when Slack permits, and returns a reusable workspace-qualified target.

## Design and security boundary

Channel creation is **disabled by default** and is no longer part of the ordinary `messages` action gate. This makes workspace administration an explicit operator choice while preserving existing message permissions.

The generated Slack manifest requests bot-compatible `channels:manage` for creation and `channels:write.invites` for requester invitation. Existing Slack apps must be reauthorized after adopting these scopes.

## Evidence

- Focused Slack channel-create/action-runtime tests passed (47 tests), as did `pnpm config:channels:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, and `git diff --check` on current head `71d77bfe365c18f9b1f0e9cd75e8158ce8f0bcac`.
- Current-head CI is terminal and passing.
- [ClawSweeper’s current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-5961532592) found no actionable code findings and marked proof sufficient.

## Current-head proof

The reauthorized disposable-workspace proof created a public channel, invited the verified non-admin requester, delivered to the returned target, and rejected disabled-account creation before Slack I/O. [Inspectable redacted terminal evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6159613571) records the final API boundary and managed-Gateway health without identifiers or credentials.

[Isolated v2026.10.3-to-candidate compatibility evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6159849038) validates the persisted reauthorized configuration with both runtimes, proves the reauthorized credential with `auth.test`, and shows a matching non-secret settings/data fingerprint without touching the managed Gateway.

[Enterprise adapter-to-client transport evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-6160504251) records allowed create/invite plus missing/conflicting-context rejection before provider I/O and caller closure before invitation.

## Before merge

- [x] **Real behavior proof:** published inspectable, redacted terminal evidence for the allowed create/invite/send path and disabled-account pre-I/O rejection.
- [x] **Data-model compatibility evidence:** published the isolated `v2026.10.3`-to-candidate reauthorization/configuration compatibility record.
- [x] **Enterprise transport trace:** published production-client coverage for allowed and rejected Enterprise workspace contexts; live Grid final-I/O remains unavailable to this contributor.
- [ ] **Upstream OpenClaw maintainer decision required:** an upstream maintainer must accept, reject, or specify the administrative-delegation/default OAuth-grant contract described in the [current ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163783#issuecomment-5961532592). This is not a Dillon approval and is not a contributor-owned repair.

No contributor-owned code repair or Slack-proof setup remains open. The sole merge gate is the upstream maintainer decision.

prs.title: fix: stabilize yielded child abort coverage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a scheduled CI failure in the yielded-parent abort scenario when normal provisional-kill cleanup retires the child row before the test's final read. The old assertion treated that intentional retirement as if a surviving child had lost its terminal outcome. Its publication observer also started after one retirement trigger and included a seeded memory snapshot, so the publication check could pass without observing the lifecycle work under test.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Contributors get reliable coverage of yielded-child abort cleanup without a timing-dependent final-row expectation. The test still preserves the two distinct parent outcomes, queue clearing, child-wake retirement, startup recovery, exact killed/error outcome publication, and final child-row retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lifecycle owner publishes the complete terminal child record and then intentionally retires the confirmed killed row. The scenario now starts its existing publication observer before either pending-wake branch can trigger that work, excludes the observer's seeded snapshot, and joins the existing fixture settlement owner in both cases.

After settlement, the test requires at least one real non-null terminal publication and compares its complete outcome with the killed/error outcome captured before cleanup. At that same final boundary it verifies the distinct parent outcomes and requires the child row to be absent in both cases. No production registry, abort, queue, fixture-support, timeout, schema, configuration, dependency, or API code changes.

## Evidence

The retained scheduled failure reported `undefined` at the old `pending=false` final-row outcome assertion while 840 sibling tests passed. The test and all causal publication, confirmation, retirement, and fixture-settlement inputs are byte-identical between that executed source and this branch's base.

On the corrected exact candidate:

- changed-file formatting and source lint passed;
- the affected `core-test-gateway-methods` type graph passed; and
- `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.abort-yielded.test.ts` passed all 8 tests in 33 seconds through the maintained remote test recipe.

Hosted CI, exact-head automated review, and independent engineering review continue on the published head.

prs.title: fix(ui): plan usage stays stale after chat runs
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the chat composer’s plan-usage popover keeps showing old subscription usage after runs finish.

## User Impact

User impact: subscription users can see updated plan usage after a run without reloading the page. Idle chats do not poll, and refresh failures preserve the last displayed usage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI retained the `models.authStatus` response until the OAuth token approached expiry, so usage did not age out independently. The Gateway also serves usage through a 60-second stale-while-revalidate cache, meaning a refresh request can initially return the previous snapshot.

After each run, the chat requests usage only when its Gateway-provided freshness deadline has elapsed. Ordinary reads stay nonblocking. The existing Gateway usage-cache owner enforces the same lifetime, coalesces provider work, and awaits cold/stale usage for post-run requests without broad auth/catalog refresh or a delayed second read.

`models.usage.cacheTtlMs` configures reuse (default `60000`; `0` disables it). For example, `{ "models": { "usage": { "cacheTtlMs": 120000 } } }` selects two minutes. The setting is documented in one sentence and config-field help; generated config-baseline growth of two paths is intentional for the requested `models.usage` object and `cacheTtlMs` leaf. No migration is required; existing configurations retain the 60-second default.

Codex-backed OpenAI usage first reuses fresh quota notifications from a live shared client with the exact profile/account binding, agent scope, start configuration, and desktop generation. Hits start no child and send no quota RPC. Stale, mismatched, native-home, and setup/runtime-artifact capture contexts retain the existing isolated read. The protocol's sparse-notification contract was checked in sibling Codex `092d3ac`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/account.rs:657`.

There is no idle polling. With stable credentials/config and healthy reads, rapid turns reuse one browser request and Gateway provider fetch per configured interval and scope, instead of forcing a provider fetch per turn. Initial ordinary and post-run modes may each issue one RPC; ordinary reads never wait behind a pending usage fetch. Explicit auth refresh and invalidation may bypass reuse. Provider fallback/auth-refresh paths can add requests. Accepted tradeoff: an inactive Codex notification reused near expiry can be nearly two cache lifetimes old when the Gateway entry expires; this avoids adding another timestamp/persistence contract. Existing credential resolution may still refresh and persist OAuth credentials, but this change adds no persisted state.

Provider errors retain displayed quota; retired connection/session responses are ignored. Provider accounting delays can still leave values unchanged.

## Evidence

### Historical live before/after verification (original v2 implementation)

The screenshots and timings below predate the architectural cleanup. They demonstrate the original bug and v2 fix, not a live test of the new usage-only RPC.

Holger Gruenhagen first reproduced the discrepancy on installed **2026.10.5**: the popover showed **1% / 13%**, while the account showed **18% / 16%**.

He subsequently tested the base UI and the v2 patch on his own Gateway, using main `f481daa` and a real ChatGPT Plus account.

| Observation | Before: base UI | After: v2 patch |
|---|---|---|
| Plan-usage popover | Stayed at **0% / 16%** after three runs | Updated from **18% / 19%** to **23% / 20%** |
| Account usage, checked through CodexBar | **16% / 19%** | **23% / 20%**, matching the popover |
| Gateway activity | No `models.authStatus` read after any run | Forced read immediately after each run, one follow-up read 5.5 seconds later, then no further reads |

**Before — popover at the end (0% / 16%)**

![Before — popover at the end (0% / 16%)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/638a2de5-17fc-4e8e-8464-d8ddc50f48b1)

**Before — CodexBar at the same time (16% / 19%)**

![Before — CodexBar at the same time (16% / 19%)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5eb8ee6e-0c7b-4730-9dd3-7cc398af3692)

**After — popover at start (18% / 19%)**

![After — CodexBar at the same time (23% / 20%)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37aa2940-5669-41f3-a9fa-e1623c0e5e32)

Percentages are **5-hour / weekly** usage. Live request timing is based on Holger’s Gateway-log observations. Redacted screenshots supplied in the work session corroborate the displayed values.

### Current refinement verification

- Gateway pacing regression failed before the change: ten post-run reads caused ten additional provider fetches despite a warm cache. Default/configured TTL now reuse the snapshot; zero disables reuse; expiry fetches again.
- 144 focused Gateway/cache, config-validation/tier, UI-reader, and mounted-popover tests passed. Combined repository-wrapper wall time: **69.93s** across four shards (69 Gateway/cache tests: 34.33s including compilation; 56 config tests: 18.22s; 3 tier tests: 0.93s; 16 UI tests: 7.92s). Invoked through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`, the maintained `pnpm test` owner, to avoid linked-worktree install reconciliation.
- The mounted popover retains usage across rapid runs and refreshes after the returned 120-second deadline, with shared split-pane requests and no idle polling. Browser/Gateway clock skew and nonblocking ordinary reads are covered.
- Codex regression failed before the change: ignored notification quota 25% and returned separately fetched 80%. The final four focused Codex suites passed **209 tests** in **48.94s** repository-wrapper wall time, including compilation. Nine cache/identity scenarios exercise notification reuse, configured lifetime, expiry/disabled reuse, and account/profile/agent/config/retirement misses.
- Core/UI production, Gateway/UI test, and scoped Codex production/test typechecks passed; targeted lint and formatting passed. The Codex scoped checks extend canonical extension configs; direct per-package tsconfig invocation is not a standalone check because of existing cross-root/package-boundary configuration diagnostics. An initial base-tsconfig invocation was likewise replaced by the canonical core lane, not treated as product failure.
- Extracted coherent Codex usage, config-label, and Gateway-test siblings to satisfy the existing line-cap ratchet; full-branch and staged ratchets pass. After extraction, 69 Gateway/cache tests passed (35.09s Vitest; 42.09s wrapper including the config tier shard); the final Gateway test extraction passed all 57 tests again (44.04s Vitest; 56.01s wrapper including compilation).
- Config documentation baseline regenerated and checked; docs MDX and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh staged-candidate AutoReview completed **clean through P2** after the extractions; no accepted/actionable findings. The only subsequent change removes an obsolete max-lines suppression, verified by lint.
- Current-head CI seconds are pending. No live provider/account benchmark or live Gateway mutation was performed; historical screenshots below are not proof of the refined cache path.

### Conflict resolution against current main

- Integrated main `2f17d4d533a8` into previously reviewed head `2858e2cbee16` without rewriting PR history.
- Regenerated the two config baselines from the combined schema (main's 2548 core paths plus the two requested usage paths). Kept main's Codex test cleanup and the usage-cache mock. Production changes merged automatically; reviewed semantics are unchanged.
- All **267 focused tests passed** across Codex request/shared-client, config validation, mounted plan usage, and chat session refresh (**72.70s** repository-wrapper wall time; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`). Targeted typed lint, generated-baseline verification, full-PR line-cap ratchet, and whitespace checks passed.
- Prior P2 review retained for this mechanical reconciliation; hosted CI on the new merge commit remains pending. No PR merge performed.

### Historical automated verification (original v2 implementation)

- **177 focused tests passed across four test files** before the final lint-only correction.
- After that correction, the two affected test files were rerun: **12 tests passed**.
- **Targeted lint passed across all five changed TypeScript files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.**
- The rapid-run regression failed against the previous fix and passes with v2: two runs ten seconds apart update the open popover **1% → 18% → 22%**.
- No additional usage requests occur during two simulated idle minutes.
- Coverage includes shared split-pane requests and skipping the delayed read after requesting owners retire.

### Historical CI follow-up verification (before architectural cleanup)

- Fixed the plan-usage test’s possibly-undefined pane by binding the first mounted pane directly; no production behavior changed.
- [checks-ui (2/3), original head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39669364992/job/119463599789) failed 16 terminal-recovery assertions because the fixture counted the new auth-status read as a history request. Reproduced all 16 locally, then separated auth-status fixture responses while retaining all history ordering/count and transcript assertions. This was a deterministic fixture incompatibility, not evidence of a browser timeout. The workflow uploads its timeout-named diagnostics on any failure.
- After repair: **31 focused tests passed across three files**; targeted lint and formatting passed.
- Ran `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json --noEmit`: all five TS18048 pane diagnostics are gone. The four existing `provider-usage.tsx` diagnostics below remain; this command still exits 2.

The saved base and patched typecheck outputs are identical; these errors also occur on the tested main baseline. Typechecking is not reported as passing.

Reproduced and live-tested by Holger Gruenhagen.

prs.title: test(ui): await web push settle points instead of wall-clock waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `ui/src/app/web-push.test.tsx` > "serializes rapid preference edits without dropping the latest full object" flaking on the Bun UI shard (CI run 39569175257 attempt 1, `checks-ui (3/3)`: `expected undefined to be truthy` after 1003ms; the same test passed in 103ms on Node).

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. This removes a deterministic-tier CI flake from the Control UI Bun shard.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause.** `createWebPushCapability` loads `web-push.runtime.ts` with a lazy `import()`. In a Vitest worker that import is a module fetch from the Vitest main process: forks over IPC on Bun, threads on Node. The rest of initial reconciliation runs on microtasks, with no timers and no pending mocks. So whether `snapshot.preferences` is set depends on how fast the runner answers the fetch and schedules the worker. It does not depend on the code under test. The test wrapped that wait in `vi.waitFor`, whose default 1000ms deadline is much shorter than the 60s test timeout. On the failing shard the 4-vCPU runner had load 5.4, with 3 Bun forks plus Chromium. Sibling tests in the same file were also slow there. For example, the fully event-driven "refreshes routed canonical profile defaults" test took 841ms on Bun and 2ms on Node. A slow import fetch or a stalled worker therefore loses the race against the 1000ms deadline. A longer timeout would only make that race less likely.

**Fix.** Wait for the real settle points:
- the next preferences publication (the existing `nextPreferencesPublication` helper, moved to file scope and shared),
- a deferred that the Gateway mock resolves when it receives the request being waited for (`preferences.set`, `push.web.vapidPublicKey`),
- or the published read receipt.

Each wait is bounded only by the test `signal` through `withinTest`. The same fix applies to the six sibling tests (two of them are the `it.for` Settings cases) whose first wait was gated on the lazy import. - **Reproduced the CI failure deterministically.** I added a scratch Vite plugin (not committed) that delays the main process's answer to the worker's fetch of `web-push.runtime.ts` by 1.1s. I ran the target test alone under the pinned Bun with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE=0`:

  - after: 10/10 passed at about 1.12s
- **Same harness, per test.** Before, 7 more tests failed: "preserves initial reconciliation failures…", "retires pending reconciliation…", "reruns full reconciliation…", "ignores stale reconciliation…", "ignores a stale preference action…", "keeps the current Gateway error…", and both "resets a mismatched browser subscription…" cases. After, every test in the file passed alone, and 5/5 full-file runs passed.
- **Plain Bun.** Before the change, an unloaded Bun run of the target test took about 103ms (two 50ms `waitFor` polls) and never failed locally, even under CPU stress. After the change, 20/20 Bun runs passed and the target test took 1–5ms.

prs.title: test(agents): prove live compaction from the successful direct read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the release-only live test `agent-session.openai-compaction.live.test.ts` > "automatically compacts tool history and resumes from its SQLite checkpoint" failing its seed check when the model's first `read` call passes `offset: 0`, or when the model keeps the file marker out of its context.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change. This removes a flaky failure from the release live lane (Native live agents) without weakening what the lane proves.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause.** The runner leaves `tools.codeMode` at its default `"auto"` tier, and that tier engages Code Mode for `gpt-5.6-luna`. The offline replay below confirms it: the model-visible tools were `exec` and `wait`. The seed transcript therefore holds Code Mode `exec` results, not raw `read` output. In those results the model decides what the script returns. The two recorded failures follow from that:
- The first cell called `read({ offset: 0 })` and was rejected (`offset: must be >= 1; received 0`). The retry cell then read the file, saved the marker with the guest `store()`, and returned only `{"markerStored":true}`. The session store stays outside model context, so no tool result carried the marker, and `expect(suppliedText).toContain(marker)` failed. Line 325 on `release/2026.10.6`.
- A cell can likewise return a slice instead of the full file text, which breaks the tail-marker and length checks.

This test owns compaction of tool history and SQLite replay, not Code Mode orchestration. Its premise is that the file contents reach the model through tool history and then survive compaction.

**Fix.**
- Pin the direct tool surface with `codeModeOverride: false`, as the other runner live tests already do. The `read` result is then the file text in tool history.
- Build the seed precondition only from successful `read` results (`toolName === "read" && !isError`), so a rejected first call such as offset 0 does not count and does not break the check.

Every downstream assertion is unchanged: compaction checkpoint summary contains the marker, no tool results after compaction, the compact and replay replies equal the marker, and the replay stays under budget.

**`read` with offset 0: no product change.** `offset` is documented as a 1-based start line. The model already sees `offset?: number /* integer, >= 1 */` in the Code Mode quick index and the schema `minimum: 1` on the direct tool. The rejection names the field, the received value, and the expected input. In the recorded case the model self-corrected in one turn. Treating 0 as "from start" would add a second spelling for line 1, and it would hide 0-based callers whose `offset: 5` silently reads one line early. The owner contract is coherent as it stands.

## Evidence

- **Offline replay through the real test body.** No `OPENAI_API_KEY` was available locally. I wrote a scratch harness (not committed) that runs this file's actual test body. It sets `OPENCLAW_LIVE_OPENAI_COMPACTION=1` and uses `configureAiTransportHost({ buildModelFetch })` to serve scripted OpenAI Responses SSE, covering the seed, compaction summary, compact, and replay requests.
  - Before (origin/main), with the recorded Code Mode sequence (offset 0 rejected, then a `store()` cell returning `{markerStored:true}`): the test fails at `expect(suppliedText).toContain(marker)` with the same error text as the release run.
  - After, with direct `read` called with `offset: 0`, then `read`, then `STORED`: the whole live test passes. Output: `budget=10420 compactions=1 replayTokens=3037 sqliteReplay=passed toolMarker=preserved`. The request log shows `read` exposed directly (no `exec`).
  - After, negative check with only the rejected offset-0 call and no successful read: the test still fails with `expected '' to contain 'TOOL-MEMORY-…'`, so the contract is not weakened.
- **Live gap.** This has not been rerun against the real OpenAI API. The release live lane (Native live agents) is the remaining proof.
- `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/agent-session.openai-compaction.live.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 1.7s wall time and reports "No test files found": default suites exclude live files, so there is no CI cost outside the live lane. The offline replay ran the test body in about 9.3s.
- `tsgo` (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json`), oxlint, `run-format --check`, and `git diff --check` are all clean. Autoreview (Codex, P2 threshold) came back scoped-clean.
- The commit cherry-picks cleanly onto `origin/release/2026.10.6` (`git merge-tree` exit 0).

prs.body:
Closes #178120.

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can quote the wrong input when an embedded run consumes another message while an earlier answer is buffered. Capture each assistant message’s consumed input synchronously, retain it through buffered delivery and native transcript persistence, and preserve its implicit reply classification through final threading and pending-final recovery.

## User Impact

Answers retain the input they consumed. Implicit targets respect `off` / `first` / `all`; explicit quotes and quote suppression retain precedence. Legacy transcript JSON remains readable. The optional source fact needs no configuration or database migration.

## Evidence

Current head: `09517e7ab48747e2935ffbab41d3c90d2bde4202`. Its actual conflict with main `94dacc48dfb325197481e95cc0fe3fd863eec645` is resolved. The pending-final test retains the entire upstream consolidation plus this contribution’s six regressions. The native database-worker inventory retains both the reply-source case and upstream update-repair cancellation case, once each. Independent review found no actionable resolution defect.

On this exact resulting tree, secretless Linux containers with Node 24.22.0 and dependencies installed from the new frozen lockfile pass:

- **32 focused native cases:** all three subscriber source cases, all 28 pending-final owning-file cases, and the real persisted implicit-source retry case. The other 194 restart-recovery cases are excluded by an explicit name filter, not claimed as executed.
- Production core types and all three affected native test-type graphs: `core-test-agents-root`, `core-test-agents-sessions`, `core-test-messaging`.
- Native type-aware core and test-inventory lint, formatting on all 17 contribution paths, and contribution whitespace checks.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.reply-source.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/pending-final-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Parent `eb3874c1` had separately passed 94 focused cases across capture/persistence, final recovery, payload production, transcript reading and reply threading, with one existing Windows-only case skipped on Linux. The subscriber fixture persists captured assistant messages and reads their actual source IDs through the native database worker.

The shared `autoreview` executable is unavailable and was not run. Native compiler, lint, format and test budgets were not changed.

The complete native published-package `sqlite-volume` survivor recipe **passes** in [run 39504398170](https://github.com/ChuLaiTheGreat/openclaw/actions/runs/39504398170), job `118909878709`, completed 20 October 2026 at 22:49 UTC. prs.title: fix: bump markdown-it to 15.0.3
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

markdown-it 15.0.2 spends quadratic time on one link reference whose label or title is never closed. Chat markdown, public session HTML, Matrix formatting, and oc-path parsing still install that version. 15.0.3 fixes the multiline reference scan.

## Evidence

Production dependencies now pin markdown-it 15.0.3:

- `ui/package.json`
- `packages/markdown-core/package.json`
- `extensions/matrix/package.json`
- `extensions/oc-path/package.json`
- `package.json` (the root entry is under devDependencies; `src/gateway/control-ui-public-session-render.ts` imports `markdown-it` from that package)

`pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `markdown-it@15.0.3` with integrity `sha512-+Az7Ojz3iRGu8KYMvJ6xVhvrxP3eE+vEtJX75Ow88XBpcQNV/0lGX5ZynIIBftREo4DC2jsveAMDaeltmm8QvQ==`. That release requires `argparse` `^3.0.3`, so the lock adds `argparse@3.0.3`. The existing `entities@8.1.0`, `linkify-it@6.1.0`, `mdurl@2.1.0`, `punycode.js@2.3.1`, and `uc.micro@3.0.0` entries still satisfy the other ranges. `markdown-it-anchor` and `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` peer snapshots now point at markdown-it 15.0.3. No other packages were bumped.

`pnpm-workspace.yaml` keeps the 7-day `minimumReleaseAge` gate. It adds reviewed excludes for `markdown-it@15.0.3` (remove after 2026-10-23T01:25:15.267Z) and `argparse@3.0.3` (remove after 2026-10-22T21:58:50.520Z). Install rejected the lock while those two versions were inside the window. The same list already carries dated excludes for other reviewed packages.

Node v24.19.0 rendered one unclosed link-reference label (`[unclosed-label` plus N continuation lines) with default options:

```
lines=2000 bytes=90015 15.0.2=33.89ms 15.0.3=20.61ms
lines=4000 bytes=180015 15.0.2=139.73ms 15.0.3=27.02ms
lines=8000 bytes=360015 15.0.2=467.66ms 15.0.3=33.29ms
lines=16000 bytes=720015 15.0.2=1546.95ms 15.0.3=49.03ms
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** One unclosed link-reference label makes markdown-it 15.0.2 render much more slowly as the input grows. The public session document renderer uses that parser.
- **Real environment tested:** Windows, Node.js v24.19.0, pnpm 12.12.1. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` on this branch resolved markdown-it 15.0.3 from the patched lock. The supply-chain policy check passed.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Called `renderPublicSessionDocument` from `src/gateway/control-ui-public-session-render.ts` with one user message. The message was `[unclosed-label` plus 600 lines of `continuation words without a closing bracket` (27015 characters, under the 32768 character message cap).
- **Evidence after fix:**
```
{
  "markdownIt": "15.0.3",
  "inputChars": 27015,
  "elapsedMs": 14.06,
  "htmlChars": 63344,
  "renderedUnclosedLabel": true
}
```
The same payload shape on standalone markdown-it, outside this renderer, was:
```
lines=2000 bytes=90015 15.0.2=33.89ms 15.0.3=20.61ms
lines=4000 bytes=180015 15.0.2=139.73ms 15.0.3=27.02ms
lines=8000 bytes=360015 15.0.2=467.66ms 15.0.3=33.29ms
lines=16000 bytes=720015 15.0.2=1546.95ms 15.0.3=49.03ms
```
- **Observed result after fix:** The patched OpenClaw public-session renderer returned HTML that contains the continuation text in 14.06 ms. The installed parser was 15.0.3.
- **What was not tested:** the Control UI browser and the Matrix gateway were not started. A 16000-line message is longer than the public session message cap, so that size was timed only on the standalone parser.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): keep source fence deadline relative across thread clock origins
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway SQLite source fence with a 120s deadline could live *longer than 120s* whenever a Bun worker is spawned after the host thread: the host seeded an absolute `deadlineNs` from its own monotonic clock origin, but Bun restarts `process.hrtime` at zero per thread, so the worker's clock reads a different (behind) origin. The worker then compared `now >= deadlineNs` against a deadline inflated by the host's head start, letting the fence outlive its intended bound. This change keeps the deadline *relative* across threads.

- Problem: an absolute monotonic deadline computed on one thread cannot be compared on another thread when each thread has its own `process.hrtime` zero point (Bun).
- Solution: the host factory captures its own absolute deadline for its own in-thread check, and passes a relative `deadlineMs` in the attachment; the worker derives its own absolute deadline from that relative duration on its own clock at receipt.
- What changed: `SqliteSourceFenceGrant.deadlineNs: bigint` → `deadlineMs: number`; `createSqliteSourceFenceAdmission` derives a host-side absolute deadline and forwards the relative duration; `runSqliteSourceFence` derives a worker-side absolute deadline once at receipt; the publication source passes `deadlineMs: 120_000`; tests cover the divergent-clock-origin case.
- What did NOT change: the 120s timeout value, the fence semantics, the admission/settlement contract shape other than the deadline field, and the `sqlite-worker-operation-admission` direction (already fixed upstream).

## Why This Change Was Made

This mirrors the same fix pattern already merged upstream in `c7f00f1` (`fix(sqlite): keep Bun Gateway startup from expiring worker admission instantly (#172756)`), which converted the *worker-operation-admission* direction from an absolute cross-thread deadline to a relative duration. The *source-fence* direction (this bug) was the same class of defect left un-fixed.

**Best fix**: yes — relative deadline across threads is the minimal, canonical way to express "this fence must last this long regardless of which thread's clock observes it."

**Alternative**: passing the host's absolute `deadlineNs` but tolerating clock skew. Rejected — it re-introduces the same origin mismatch on Bun and cannot be bounded without knowing the spawn delay.

**Risk**: `Math.ceil` on the relative duration and clamping at 0 keep the derived deadline from rounding down; a 0ms deadline expires immediately on both sides. The worker derives its deadline once at receipt, so the fence is bounded by the same real duration the host intends.

## User Impact

Operators get a source fence that actually enforces its configured timeout under Bun's per-thread monotonic clocks, instead of a fence that can outlive its deadline by the worker-spawn delay. No behavioral change to the 120s default or to already-committed flows.

## Evidence

**Pre-fix (source reverted to absolute `deadlineNs`, new test kept) — the fence wrongly accepts an expired admission when the worker clock origin lags the host's:**

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-source-fence.test.ts --run -t "worker clock origin is behind"

 FAIL  |infra| src/infra/sqlite-source-fence.test.ts > expires a deadline admission when the worker clock origin is behind the host's
 AssertionError: promise resolved "{ id: 'worker-clock-behind', …(1) }" instead of rejecting
```

The host seeded its deadline from a clock origin 5s ahead of the worker (simulating a worker spawned behind the host). The worker compared against the inflated absolute deadline and **accepted** a 0ms fence that should have expired immediately.

**Post-fix (relative `deadlineMs`, worker derives its own deadline at receipt) — the worker correctly rejects the expired fence:**

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-source-fence.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
```

The added test drives `createSqliteSourceFenceAdmission` with the host factory's first `process.hrtime.bigint()` mocked 5s ahead of the worker's real clock and `deadlineMs: 0`; post-fix the worker derives `workerNow + 0ms` from its own clock and rejects with `SQLite source fence authority expired`.

**Open PR collision check:** searched open PR topics and scanned changed-file lists for `sqlite-source-fence.ts`, `sqlite-source-fence-admission.ts`, `sqlite-source-fence-contract.ts`, and `github-publication-source.ts`; no open PR touches them. The canonical upstream sibling fix `#172756` is already merged and only covered the worker-operation-admission direction.

**What was not tested:** a true multi-threaded Bun process with real per-thread `process.hrtime` zero points (the host node runtime shares one clock across threads, so the divergence is simulated via a mocked host clock). The relative-vs-absolute reasoning is the same one validated upstream in `#172756`.

prs.title: fix(doctor): avoid incorrect warnings for aliased models
prs.body:
Supersedes #178889, thanks @KrasimirKralev.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor treats a primary model alias such as `gem` as `openai/gem`, producing incorrect tool-policy and model-schema warnings and reporting a cron job pinned to the alias target as a different model.

## User Impact

Doctor checks the model selected by the runtime, including agent-specific aliases. Cron overrides using an alias or its concrete target compare equally; genuinely different models still warn. Configured aliases and stored data are unchanged. This is an advisory diagnostic correction, including post-update Doctor runs, with no migration or new options.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove Doctor's separate primary-model parser and use the existing runtime selection owner at all four callers. Resolve both sides of cron comparisons through the shared alias index while retaining the authored provider-namespace counts. Remove the now-unnecessary local cron parser and unsafe agent-model cast.

Production: +46/-56 lines (net -10). Tests: +109/-0. Documentation: +2; assertion baseline shrinks by one entry. Release-note context: fix false Doctor model/tool warnings and cron mismatch warnings for aliased primaries; credits @KrasimirKralev, supersedes #178889.

## Evidence

- Six regression cases fail on base `cce29b29453c35a6bb49d6249005c836506a79e1`: default/agent schema frames, cron alias comparisons in both directions, provider MCP policy, and preview policy warnings.
- All four focused files pass on Node and the pinned Bun fork: 48 tests per runtime. New cases also retain controls for another provider or a genuinely different cron model.
- Node also passes all directly affected suites and immediate consumers: 243 tests across 13 files, including Doctor config flow, cron-owner repair/refusal, native admission, preview scan notes, health contributions, startup maintenance, schema runtime/inspection, and read-only cron state. The four-file command batch took 200.22s wall time; the unchanged cron-owner file accounted for 115.038s across 18 cases (slowest 11.394s), repeatedly creating isolated state and exercising real migration/cleanup workers.
- Focused file wall times: Node command pair 27.13s, preview 19.94s, frames covered in the 27.24s two-file flow batch; Bun command pair 31.15s, preview 41.83s, frames 43.06s. Most wall time outside the preview/migration cases is shared worker compilation.
- Built CLI proof uses an isolated HOME/config/state and a free port. Base `node dist/entry.js doctor --non-interactive` exits 0 but prints both the unavailable-message-tool warning and `Unknown model: openai/gem`. Candidate `pnpm dev doctor --non-interactive` exits 0 and prints neither. The config remains byte-identical (SHA-256 `92fba7aec1df565e50092acea79cc1eb0fe8ad4d638fe945e42b7bc96ce0995b`). No operator Gateway was changed or restarted.
- Core, Doctor-test, and other-core-test typechecks pass. Touched-file oxlint/oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass. Madge: 0 cycles. Assertion-safety ratchet passes (one obsolete entry removed).
- Line-cap ratchet passes. The full max-lines ratchet fails identically on the untouched index/base and candidate for existing suppressions in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`, `ui/src/pages/config/config-page-state.ts`, and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-state.ts`; none of those files or their baseline are changed here.
- Independent isolated Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Full `check:changed`, including SQLite inventory, is deferred to PR CI under the campaign's local gate budget. No package-upgrade or model-inference claim is made by this diagnostic-only proof.

Both runs used this synthetic config:

```json
{

```

```sh
# Baseline, after building unchanged main via pnpm dev:
env HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/alias-doctor/home" OPENCLAW_HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/alias-doctor/home" OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$PWD/.artifacts/alias-doctor/state" OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$PWD/.artifacts/alias-doctor/state/openclaw.json" OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=28891 node dist/entry.js doctor --non-interactive
```

prs.title: fix(plugins): pack plugins with authored manifests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw plugins pack` rejecting valid `definePluginEntry` and `register(api)` plugins with “plugin entry does not expose tool or feature authoring metadata.” Callable registration exports could also be invoked as authoring factories during packing.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can package ordinary native plugins with an authored manifest into a bundled archive. Authors must install `esbuild` in the plugin project and repack/install the artifact; linked installations still need their own bundled build. Existing resource and dynamic-loader restrictions remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Packing now validates the runtime entry selected by the package, including `runtimeExtensions`, through the existing native export resolver. It checks registration and manifest identity without invoking registration. Entries carrying tool/feature metadata still receive generated-metadata and Control UI freshness checks; `plugins build` and `plugins validate` retain their authoring-factory behavior.

The shared entry-loading code has one owner. The documentation explains that TypeScript compilation and `plugins build` do not bundle backend dependencies, and that `plugins pack` produces an archive without rewriting a linked `dist/`.

<details>
<summary>Incident and measured loading bottleneck</summary>

The investigation began with Gateway stalls during concurrent work and a model picker reporting unavailable models after an auth-triggered plugin rebuild timed out. On stock OpenClaw 2026.10.5 with Node 26.12.1 on macOS arm64, profiling identified prolonged synchronous worker-bridge waits during plugin imports.

Valid, compiled plugins retained large TypeBox/Cheerio dependency graphs. Local packaging fixes produced these native plugin-load measurements:

| Measured plugin group | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Three tool plugins combined, median | 49.851 s | 0.669 s |
| One Cheerio-based plugin, median | 8.073 s | 0.303 s |

The Cheerio plugin's graph shrank from 257 JavaScript modules / 901 import edges to 4 modules / 50 edges. Its final five loads were 300.7–309.2 ms; the comparison reuses the earlier five-sample baseline. Profiling also showed that leaving repeated CommonJS builtin resolution in a bundle retained substantial synchronous bridge cost.

These measurements come from the local plugin fixes that motivated this PR. This PR enables the existing packer for ordinary native plugins and improves authoring guidance; it does not change the synchronous Gateway loader or add support for module-relative runtime resources. The first lifecycle exception was not retained, so its exact original exception remains unknown.

</details>

## Evidence

- Regression proof on the base: ordinary entry cases failed at the metadata requirement, and the callable entry was invoked while packing. The new cases pack, extract without the source project or `node_modules`, register, and execute the bundled tool. Rejection cases cover mismatched runtime identity, missing registration, and stale generated metadata.

prs.title: perf(ui): avoid session rereads for speed hint updates
prs.body:
## Problem and change

Provider fulfillment-tier observations caused open chat panes to reread their session descriptors after refreshing speed hints, despite unchanged session-model facts. This is a remaining trigger after #179937.

Carry the Gateway’s existing distinction through the metadata invalidation owner. Catalog-only observations refresh the catalog while preserving settled and in-flight session facts. Configuration, authentication, model-policy, session changes, and direct command revalidation retain their existing refresh/retirement behavior. No new cache, timer, configuration, or protocol is introduced. The runtime UI delta is +19/−7 lines (net +12); this distinction preserves the genuine refresh contract. The other changes extend the existing synthetic benchmark and its documentation.

## Measurement

Three concurrent baseline/candidate pairs, with interleaved CPUs 64,66,…,94 versus 65,67,…,95 and swapped assignments in pair 2. One exclusive slot was retained across the block. The shared guard was used unchanged; no pair was interrupted. Pair 1 had one high-load warning, below the guard’s consecutive-minute abort condition.

Each side uses a real isolated Gateway, built Control UI, 5,000 synthetic sessions, 6,000 retained runs, 200 approvals, 100 cron jobs, and 12 worktrees. Each 60-second warm window completes 24 streaming turns across three sessions and two cron runs. A real `sessions_spawn` child is seeded and reused. Interactive windows additionally perform ten hover/picker/navigation actions. There are three windows per phase per side, all with matching work and controls and no browser, RPC, or cleanup errors. Actual windows were 60.0025–60.0067 seconds; rates below are duration-normalized. CPU is the Gateway main thread’s user+system CPU, not browser CPU.

| Pair / phase | Describe/min B→C | Session models/min B→C | All browser RPC/min B→C | Main CPU ms/min B→C | CPU delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / no interaction | 18.00→0.00 | 18.00→14.00 | 245.98→219.99 | 10709.30→10269.57 | -439.73 (-4.11%) |
| 1 / interactive | 20.00→4.00 | 17.00→17.00 | 260.97→250.98 | 8689.10→8589.21 | -99.89 (-1.15%) |
| 2 / no interaction | 16.00→0.00 | 16.00→16.00 | 239.99→232.99 | 10279.49→10309.48 | +30.00 (+0.29%) |
| 2 / interactive | 20.00→4.00 | 18.00→17.00 | 261.98→252.98 | 8299.46→8419.28 | +119.82 (+1.44%) |
| 3 / no interaction | 16.00→0.00 | 16.00→15.00 | 243.99→230.97 | 9839.44→9868.90 | +29.46 (+0.30%) |
| 3 / interactive | 19.00→5.00 | 17.00→16.00 | 267.98→254.99 | 9509.19→9599.52 | +90.33 (+0.95%) |

| Combined metric | Mean baseline→candidate | Mean absolute delta | Mean paired relative delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Describe/tab-min | 18.165→2.167 | -15.999 | -88.03% |
| Session models/tab-min | 16.999→15.832 | -1.167 | -6.81% |
| All browser RPC/tab-min | 253.482→240.483 | -12.999 | -5.12% |
| Gateway main CPU ms/min | 9554.321→9509.317 | -45.004 | -0.45% |

Decision rule v5.2: a ≥20% adverse paired mean, or ≥10% adverse in both initial pairs, rejects. Opposite signs or >5× baseline differences require absolute deltas, an inconclusive two-pair result, and a third pair for gating metrics. CPU signs differed, so the third pair was run. The final CPU absolute means are −126.76 ms/min without interaction, +36.75 ms/min with interaction, and −45.00 ms/min combined. This is neutral CPU, not a claimed CPU speedup; no adverse gate was reached. All baseline ratios were below 1.15×.

Interactive model rates also had opposite signs: pair 1 +0.000198/min (+0.00117%, equal raw counts with slightly different durations), pair 2 −1.000275/min (−5.55744%), pair 3 −0.999355/min (−5.87906%). The final absolute mean is −0.666477/min. Catalog reads remain legitimate for changed speed hints; the main result is removing the redundant descriptor read. No GC or tail-latency claim is made.

The initial diagnostic reproduced 16 catalog-observation events causing nine session model reads and nine descriptor reads with unchanged session-model revisions. Ordinary warmed turns/cron activity did not produce recurring reads after first-use setup. This establishes a concrete trigger, not attribution of every production request.

Reproduce using the existing `scripts/perf/control-ui-reload-fixture.ts` launcher with `--service-tier-port`, `--service-tier-responses fast,default`, `--stream-delay-ms 75`, and `--subagent-seed`, then `scripts/perf/catalog-polling-measure.ts` with:

```text
--load-runs 1 --load-path /chat/main --expect-session agent:main:main
--activity-session agent:main:main --activity-models openai/gpt-5
--activity-run-mix --activity-cron --duration 60 --interval-ms 6000
--reload-census --min-sidebar-rows 10
```

Supply the owned fixture URL, storage-state file, Gateway PID, common future `--start-at`, and output path; add `--activity-interactions` for the interactive phase. The fixture README documents setup.

## Proof and limits

Both regression boundaries fail before their fixes and pass afterward: the shell-to-pane test sees two redundant settled descriptor reads; the pending-read test sees two reads instead of one. All 54 focused metadata tests pass (3.89 seconds including wrapper; 2.41 seconds in Vitest). The targeted UI typecheck and changed-file format/lint checks pass. Independent P0–P2 review is clean, including full binding/cache/store context for the pending-read correction.

[Exact-head CI 39711071866](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39711071866) passed on `f4f1c446bb7b8ed6f16c7e3f877a514f622ed270`: 46 successful jobs, 24 skipped, no failures. Required CI/security gates are green. The previous head hit an inherited sidebar-order timeout also present in [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39707038848/job/119589613950); no rerun was used to chase green. The substantive pending-read fix triggered the final passing run.

The controlled benchmark uses the same runtime built from baseline `a928225b43b17e78661a3bf9ef3a12d959724387` on both sides, changing only the four reviewed Control UI sources for the candidate. It is not a full runtime build of the later rebased PR head; exact-head CI supplies that broader validation. The pinned baseline includes #179937. The measured startup bundle is 325,831→325,826 compressed bytes; both exceed the unchanged 325,657-byte baseline cap.

The synthetic provider’s observation frequency does not establish production frequency. The browser verifies stable model/speed controls; hint text transitions are covered by the focused regression because the synthetic catalog omits fulfillment-hint fields. No production deployment was performed. The post-deployment signal is that catalog-only observations no longer produce paired descriptor reads.

prs.title: feat(codex): support read-only plugin tools
prs.body:
Closes #180029

## What Problem This Solves

Codex plugin users cannot currently restrict a connected app to read operations when its tools lack destructive annotations.

## User Impact

A plugin can opt into `read_only: true`. Only enabled tools explicitly marked read-only are available; missing classifications, disabled tools, and write tools are denied. The default remains off, and existing `allow_destructive_actions` behavior is preserved. This applies to connected apps, not unrelated native MCP servers or individual actions within a tool.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing app policy now projects read-only eligibility into native tool permissions and retains it through inventory refresh, binding recovery, shared app ownership, and scheduled execution. Explicit revocation prevents an old native tool grant from restoring write access. This reuses the existing policy lifecycle instead of introducing a separate configuration mechanism.

The generated plugin configuration budget increases by one (4782 to 4783) for the requested opt-in `read_only` field; no other configuration surface grows.

## Evidence

The review fixes preserve native name-before-title enablement and approval precedence through persisted binding replay and retain each scheduled creator's read-only restriction even after current plugin settings are relaxed. Missing inventory still fails closed; existing authority records without the new optional field remain readable.

Current focused verification: 20 read-only/scheduled-classification cases, 51 scheduled-authority cases, and 42 binding-store cases pass. Production/test typechecks and focused lint/format pass. Independent review of the final enablement-precedence repair found no P0–P2 issue. The new regression fails before the repair and passes afterward.

Production OpenClaw configuration building, serialized policy restoration and scheduled startup generated the configurations exercised by a local native Codex app-server 0.153.4 fixture with empty MCP annotations:
- Permissive consent: the read executed and the write never reached the backend.
- Title-based prompt: one consent request was declined, with zero backend calls.
- Scheduled replay after disabling current read-only mode: a newly classified read executed; writes, a former read reclassified as a write, and a disabled read never reached the backend.

The earlier 18-tool classification check also allowed 10 enabled reads and blocked 6 writes plus 2 disabled tools; a separate write-enabled positive control reached the backend. These are isolated synthetic-backend checks, not live external-service queries or deployment proof.


[Inspectable generated permissions and native request/response/backend traces](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180030#issuecomment-6330610875) cover the allowed read, forbidden write, declined title consent, canonical-name enablement override, and saved scheduled cap after policy relaxation/read-to-write reclassification. Existing SQLite reopen and legacy authority fixtures also pass. [Package Acceptance run 39708028702](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39708028702) now passes at exact head `d23d8733639dfc2025a9cddddc1b9999ba98f4ea`, including upgrades from published `openclaw@2026.10.5` to the candidate tarball in the `base` and `cron-scheduled-authority` scenarios. Both exercise the normal updater, Doctor/migration, stored-state survival, and Gateway readiness with manual restart. This complements the Codex-specific binding replay/native enforcement proof above; the generic upgrade lane does not claim a live Codex binding migration or external-service query.

Related: #167796, #179526

## What Problem This Solves

Removes the unreachable heartbeat executor, scheduler, response tool, and outcome store after Automations and ordinary session events took over their runtime entry points. Keeping these definitions leaves a second execution model in the codebase even though Gateway and plugin producers no longer use it.

## User Impact

Periodic jobs continue through the session controller's admission and settlement path. Doctor's heartbeat migration and once-only notice remain intact. This completes the executor portion of Peter's October 3/12 design; the breaking SDK retirement is documented in the migration guide and handled by #180106.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is S4c, following S4a #180079 and S4b #180106, in the replacement stack for #179526 and #167796. The earlier slices are S1 #178650, S2 #178764, and S3 #179387 (replacing #178990). S4d follows with the remaining internal turn flags, bootstrap branches, and wake helpers.

Delete the retired runner/scheduler, response-tool plumbing, outcome publication, and their direct tests together. Preserve active coverage at ordinary owners: background exec custody, Cron restart and execution budgets, session-event delivery, and Gateway publication. The shared response/metadata types require a wider mechanical caller update; no compatibility shim or second lifecycle owner is introduced.

## Evidence

The prepared source passed 511 focused tests in 24 files, scoped production/test type graphs, typed lint/format, prompt snapshots, database-worker inventory, and shrink-only baseline generation. Independent Codex review was scoped-clean through P2. Fresh-main integration checks and exact-head CI are recorded before landing; prepared-source proof is reused only for unchanged inputs.

No external-provider live campaign was repeated. The retained live session-event probe now uses ordinary Cron jobs, and local boundary proof exercises the production admission/settlement owners with synthetic I/O.

Fresh integration starts at S4b merge `e897d98dcc2a`. It retains the current-main Codex bridge helper, tool-schema check, inventory cleanup, and ordinary Telegram format test. The sole conflict removed only the obsolete heartbeat-runner test. B's delivery-held and ordinary-exec custody repairs remain intact.

The final slice spans 165 paths: executable source −5,050 lines, tests/support −11,273, and docs/metadata −17. The typed response-option closure accounts for the path count; no compatibility shim or new owner was introduced. The final integrated diff is scoped-clean through P2 review.

Core, agent, messaging, tooling and focused extension type graphs pass. Owner generators and formatting pass. Final Codex review is scoped-clean through P2 across both complete review passes. Typed lint passes for changed core, script, and extension files. Exact-head CI is recorded before landing.

The subsequent main merge retains the new queue-input authority adapter, execution-selection propagation, source-turn context, and shared transcript-target helper. Three generated prompt conflicts were regenerated through `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`. The merge delta passed 114 execution/admission cases, prefix and prompt-snapshot tests, four targeted type graphs, typed lint, formatting, and a scoped-clean P2 Codex review.
