prs.title: perf(gateway): keep publication recovery off the readiness path
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pending GitHub publication recovery can delay Gateway readiness and agent dispatch while local Git commands or GitHub requests wait. Three observed boots reached ready in 21.63, 96.51, and 36.54 seconds; publication recovery accounted for 6.38, 81.38, and 21.17 seconds respectively.

## User Impact

The Gateway can become ready and admit agent dispatch while pending publication recovery continues. Required placement authority recovery and personal-publication confirmation invalidation still finish before dispatch opens. Publication effects retain their existing authority, durable recovery, and shutdown-drain contracts. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Publication retries now run in the existing tracked background reconciliation operation after session retirement, instead of blocking placement-runtime startup. A retirement failure postpones the initial retry to the existing scheduled recovery sweep. Runtime production code has no net line growth (6 added, 6 removed); no cache, owner, or parallel implementation is introduced.

The startup benchmark can seed a real pending publication and delay one read-only local Git command. It records that both builds actually reach and complete this boundary, and retains missing requester authority so the synthetic request cannot publish externally.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the original code because startup remains pending during held publication recovery; it passes with the fix and also verifies that shutdown drains the held recovery. All 191 focused tests pass: 48 across startup, startup cleanup, startup maintenance, recovery events, and publication runtime; 43 startup-benchmark tests; and 100 credential-writer-guard tests. The runtime regression fails on base; the fixture-guard regression also fails before its repair. Changed-file formatting and lint pass. Independent review is clean through P2 on the full final patch. Broad validation belongs to PR CI.

CI caught two fixture writer edges that needed explicit review. The historical fixture is created in a new exclusive root before Gateway launch. The guard now permits only its private helper to insert one shared publication and execute one exact SQL literal removing requester authority from that synthetic request. Other callers, duplicate writes, changed predicates/values, and appended SQL remain rejected. No production authority bypass was introduced.

## Paired measurements

Three concurrent groups, five fresh boots per side per group (15 per build). Group 2 swaps the interleaved CPU placement; group 3 resolves the two mixed-sign metrics under v5.2. Every boot passed ready/RPC, exact plugin inventory, delayed-publication completion, common post-ready completion milestones, and clean shutdown without a forced kill.

Workload: eight agents, 4,096 sessions, 128 MiB inert payload, and 44 loaded plugins (17 bundled plus 27 synthetic). A pending publication waits 10 seconds at a real read-only local Git boundary. Separate network namespaces and missing historical requester authority prevent external publication. Fresh process/state roots use a warm host filesystem cache.

| Group (n=5/side) | Metric | Baseline mean | Candidate mean | Absolute Δ | Relative Δ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Ready | 23.788 s | 13.012 s | -10.776 s | -45.30% |
| 1 | First sessions.list RPC | 23.901 s | 13.102 s | -10.798 s | -45.18% |
| 1 | Sampled process-tree CPU | 37.000 s | 34.400 s | -2.600 s | -7.03% |
| 1 | Peak RSS | 3518.664 MiB | 3545.242 MiB | +26.578 MiB | +0.76% |
| 1 | Common startup work complete | 43.826 s | 33.428 s | -10.398 s | -23.73% |
| 1 | Shutdown | 0.980 s | 1.015 s | +0.036 s | +3.65% |
| 2 | Ready | 24.258 s | 13.511 s | -10.747 s | -44.30% |
| 2 | First sessions.list RPC | 24.353 s | 13.617 s | -10.736 s | -44.09% |
| 2 | Sampled process-tree CPU | 35.600 s | 34.200 s | -1.400 s | -3.93% |
| 2 | Peak RSS | 3531.422 MiB | 3490.075 MiB | -41.347 MiB | -1.17% |
| 2 | Common startup work complete | 42.320 s | 33.397 s | -8.924 s | -21.09% |
| 2 | Shutdown | 0.772 s | 0.662 s | -0.111 s | -14.35% |
| 3 | Ready | 23.005 s | 12.350 s | -10.655 s | -46.31% |
| 3 | First sessions.list RPC | 23.088 s | 12.434 s | -10.654 s | -46.15% |
| 3 | Sampled process-tree CPU | 35.800 s | 32.400 s | -3.400 s | -9.50% |
| 3 | Peak RSS | 3542.532 MiB | 3570.477 MiB | +27.945 MiB | +0.79% |
| 3 | Common startup work complete | 42.060 s | 31.623 s | -10.437 s | -24.81% |
| 3 | Shutdown | 0.852 s | 1.421 s | +0.569 s | +66.81% |

The original swapped groups improve ready by 10.762 seconds (44.80%) and first RPC by 10.767 seconds (44.63%) on the mean paired delta; sampled CPU improves 5.48%. RSS (+26.58, −41.35 MiB) and shutdown (+35.77, −110.81 ms) initially had opposite signs and were treated as inconclusive, not adverse.

After the required third group, the absolute mean across all three groups is:

- Peak RSS: +4.392 MiB (+0.12% of the pooled baseline; 3530.873 → 3535.265 MiB).
- Shutdown: +0.165 s (+18.97% of the pooled baseline; 0.868 → 1.032 s).

Shutdown is the measured tradeoff: the final absolute mean rises 164.65 ms, or 18.97% of the pooled baseline, below the 20% rejection threshold; the original swapped groups were +3.65% and −14.35%, so they also do not meet the both-groups rejection rule. One candidate shutdown took 3.762 seconds versus 0.537 seconds on its paired baseline; its trace attributes 3.316 seconds to plugin-metadata closure. That sample remains included. The v5.2 decision uses the absolute mean rather than the mean of relative deltas.

All gating metrics pass. The third group is decided on absolute means; no metric was rejected on a tiny-baseline relative mean. Completion time is additional context. The rejection rule is a ≥20% adverse paired mean or ≥10% adverse in both swapped groups, with mixed signs or >5× baseline differences requiring the third group.

<details><summary>Latency spread and low-sample tails</summary>

Each cell has n=5. Values are median [minimum, maximum] in seconds. The maximum is also the nearest-rank p95 at n=5; these tails are context only, below the 200-sample p95 gate minimum. No p99 gate is inferred.

| Group | Metric | Baseline median [min, p95/max], n=5 | Candidate median [min, p95/max], n=5 |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | Ready | 23.441 [22.588, 24.868] | 12.829 [11.711, 14.350] |
| 1 | First RPC | 23.561 [22.696, 24.960] | 12.917 [11.811, 14.432] |
| 2 | Ready | 22.975 [21.865, 27.699] | 12.822 [11.364, 15.777] |
| 2 | First RPC | 23.044 [21.939, 27.893] | 12.912 [11.449, 15.933] |
| 3 | Ready | 23.245 [21.730, 24.032] | 12.793 [10.879, 13.329] |
| 3 | First RPC | 23.366 [21.820, 24.122] | 12.887 [10.947, 13.426] |

</details>

The runtime removes the readiness dependency without abandoning work: representative pair 1-7 reduced worker-environment startup from 10.579 seconds to 11.5 ms while publication recovery still took 10.806 seconds and completed after ready. Required placement authority remains ahead of dispatch, and shutdown still joins publication recovery.

Protocol and limits: the shared guard is unchanged (2,500 ms production loop maximum, load 60, dirty pages 2 GiB); all measured pairs use slot B with baseline on even CPUs 64–94 and candidate on odd CPUs 65–95, reversed for group 2. Group 1 acquired the lock per boot; groups 2 and 3 held it across their five boots. No accepted measurement was interrupted by the guard. Preparation and fixtures were sequential under the prescribed low-priority CPU/IO limits.

CPU/RSS cover equal completed work: delayed Git read, initial post-ready database maintenance, and final handler prewarm must all finish before teardown. The initial ready/publication-only window permitted unequal background initialization, so its resource samples were excluded before this campaign. Setup failures (missing fixture identity/launcher, bypassed delay wrapper, and wrong plugin count) and the canceled preliminary run are also excluded. Accepted cohorts are group 1 indices 7–11, and groups 2/3 indices 1–5. Sampled process-tree CPU has whole-second resolution; RSS is sampled every 100 ms. No cold production page-cache experiment, real GitHub latency experiment, or per-collection GC measurement was performed.

The builds compare pinned base `a928225b43b17e78661a3bf9ef3a12d959724387` with this runtime patch. Later rebases and the final current-main check did not change the affected startup/publication owners; current-head CI supplies broad validation. Production behavior awaits the next approved deployment/boot.

Reproduction uses the committed benchmark with fresh roots, identical plugin JSON, a common start epoch, separate baseline/candidate entries and the CPU/guard/lock arrangement above:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-gateway-startup.ts --case teamBoot --fixture-root <fresh-root> --bundled-plugin-fixture <44-plugin-json> --publication-git-delay-ms 10000 --entry <build>/dist/entry.js --runs 1 --warmup 0 --timeout-ms 120000 --start-at <common-epoch-ms>
```

Exact-head CI run [39708232280](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39708232280) passed all 38 executed jobs. Same-second duplicate [39708232491](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39708232491) was canceled immediately. The separate security-review aggregate selects the highest run ID, skipping only wholly skipped runs, and therefore projects that canceled duplicate as a CI failure. The exact publisher source at `5c5be9edb3855812a302c9807b1edfbb4e180154` confirms that selection. Its security workflow succeeded; no CI rerun or branch update was requested to chase this unrelated aggregate status.

Live signal after an approved deployment: readiness should precede completion of `sidecars.worker-environments.publications`; placement authority recovery must still precede dispatch, and agent RPCs should not return the startup-unavailable error after ready. Publication recovery and its warnings may finish later. No production Gateway was changed or restarted.

prs.title: fix(codex): recover requests after reused connections disconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interrupted Codex requests when a reused app-server connection disconnects during a later turn: recovery can inherit an already-ended turn's authority and fail with `This turn has ended`.

## User Impact

Eligible requests can rejoin their original native turn without repeating tool effects. After a Gateway restart, the notice says recovery is being checked rather than claiming the request has already resumed; unknown tool outcomes still receive the existing terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bind the connection-abort callback to its registering attempt's async context. This preserves the existing ownership and authorization checks without replaying prompts or retrying external effects.

This draft targets `kimiyu_openclaw_2026-10-01-beta1-reviewed` at `327b89d9b16d452d5a28f14d02abdf1776d9dfe1`. It changes neither the native version pin nor deployment topology.

## Evidence

- The new async-context regression fails before the fix and passes afterward; the focused recovery suite passes 19/19. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Latest native-runner wall time: 65.93s (Vitest: 62.15s; new regression: 412ms). Hosted CI seconds are not yet measured.
- The focused restart-notice test passes. Formatting, core/extension type checks including test graphs, focused type-aware lint, and dependency/plugin/architecture guards pass.
- The required dead-export scan reports the same unused `notifyCommandRestartRecoveryFailure` on both the exact unchanged base and candidate. No check was disabled or bypassed; the aggregate check is not fully green.
- Isolated real-Gateway tests with published Codex 0.163.0: three trials each at effect-before-response and result-before-callback-ack disconnect barriers. All six original turns completed with one original start, one effect, and one final delivery; the unpatched Gateway interrupted those turns.
- Hard restart and the unchanged 315-second drain deadline preserve a single effect and report truthful failure for uncertain work. A subsequent tool request on the same persisted thread completes without replaying the old effect.

Integration model and Slack endpoints were synthetic. These results establish isolated recovery behavior, not authenticated production recovery. Hosted CI has not yet been verified.

## Real authority-owner integration evidence

A separate isolated run uses the installed Gateway's supported trusted-proxy authentication and canonical profiles, with distinct actor/controller identities (neither is gateway-owner). The actor submits through public `chat.send`; the controller revokes the actual actor profile through public `users.setRole`. Model/Slack endpoints and identities are synthetic. No production identity provider or credentials are involved, and no authorization guard is stubbed or disabled.

The relay holds an actual replacement-connection `thread/read` response. In the negative case the role mutation commits before releasing that response and the already-accepted tool response. This exercises authority changes across the awaited recovery boundary.

| Observation | Authorized principal | Revoked principal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original `turn/start` count | 1 | 1 |
| Recovery `thread/resume` count | 1 | 0 |
| Matching message-write effect count | 1 | 1, before revocation |
| Replacement callback result | `success: true`, parsed `deliveryStatus: sent`, structured message receipt | No recovery admission |
| Successful public final | 1 | 0, also checked via controller `chat.history` |
| Independent authorized principal | Still usable | Fresh request completes |

Sanitized timeline (2026-10-21, UTC):

- 06:50:52.020: warmup completes on native connection 2.
- 06:50:52.618: allowed turn starts on the same connection 2; after disconnection it recovers on connection 3. At 06:50:53.004, the exact replayed call's response reports successful tool delivery; the public final arrives at 06:50:53.148.
- 06:50:54.054: controller commits `users.setRole` for the actual actor profile; effective role is read back as revoked and its socket closes. The held recovery response is then released.
- Through 06:53:18.944: zero additional native tool calls for the revoked original turn and zero requests to the synthetic Slack endpoint. The controller's fresh request completes at 06:50:54.884.

Correlation: allowed native thread/turn `01a15d3a-1ec9-7bc0-8365-69df3624615d` / `01a15d3a-1f4b-7671-b2b6-b64fd664d6a7`; revoked thread/turn `01a15d3a-231f-7330-89f4-88d80d4feee5` / `01a15d3a-23a8-7333-9383-cda34496407f`. Retained raw trace SHA-256: `07643e0cedae7e558d2c97b2738324072da01e861c1592a5ec06fe2797a07da1` (652855 bytes).

Scope: published Codex 0.163.0 with the retained packaged Gateway's compiled callback patch (bundle SHA-256 `ca6c4aa90b1d182e32cde65f8d4436f9d934daa1b8fe26fa470c5db44f20a424`), not a fresh build of this entire PR head. Exact-head source tests are listed above. These observations establish allowed recovery and rejection after actual principal revocation within the observed window. Cancellation could not confirm native termination; this does not prove unloading, complete resource cleanup, universal absence of later I/O, or authenticated deployment recovery.

prs.title: fix: make Daybreak independent of retiring model aliases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Daybreak workflows rely on Blue/Red aliases retiring October 28, 2026, and must retain automatic recovery through authorized Access configuration without changing the selected model or processing speed.

## User Impact

The chat menu uses segmented Access choices matching Speed and shows **Access above Effort above Speed**, but only when the active account/model/runtime explicitly advertises a Daybreak program. Unavailable options are absent; unknown or empty capabilities hide Access entirely. There are no requested/reported status or explanatory paragraphs below Access. **Use model default** clears the session override; Standard is an explicit selection. If account capabilities no longer expose Access, **Clear saved Access** remains available in the model menu. Clearing is explicit; unavailable program choices and explanatory Access paragraphs remain absent.

The advisory Doctor check reports configured retiring aliases without rewriting models or account pins. **Automatic cyber recovery retries the same model once with authorized Blue Access**, without changing the saved session selection. Exact model pins and an empty model-fallback list do not disable this configuration retry. Ordinary configured cross-model fallbacks remain separate. Review saved session overrides and scheduled jobs separately before retirement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the aliases retire. A replay-safe, structured cyber refusal in Standard/default mode can retry the same provider/model/runtime/account with Blue Access. Existing Blue/Red requests are not retried or downgraded, and `cyberFailover.mode=off` remains authoritative. Current account/credential/route grants are required before submission; there is no entitlement inferred from a model name, auth type, or another account. Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove retired `cyberFailover.model` fields through the existing core/plugin migration owners; explicit mode/cooloff settings and ordinary primary/fallback model configuration are preserved. Program selection (`standard`, `daybreak_blue`, `daybreak_red`) remains independent of Fast/Ultrafast. Empty model configuration (`accessPrograms: {}`) leaves selection unspecified; null is invalid.

Authenticated ChatGPT model discovery supplies caller-specific program metadata. The Gateway projects it as optional `availableAccessPrograms.cyber` on each account/model/runtime choice, preserving unknown versus explicitly empty results. The existing account/catalog lifecycle owns invalidation; no new cache or state store is introduced. Saved session overrides are checked again at execution, and native Codex verifies the same client/account model catalog before its turn starts.

This OpenClaw integration supports the native Codex turn-scoped parameter with ChatGPT authentication and rejects explicit programs with native API-key authentication before submission. This is the integration’s current scope, not an upstream limitation: pinned Codex 0.162.1 rejects API-key programs when its separate feature is disabled and forwards them when enabled. **Platform API-key discovery now reads explicit caller-specific program metadata from the official Codex models endpoint, using the same selected key.** Public `/v1/models` remains the model-inventory authority; metadata cannot add an unlisted model. No model-name, plan, or approval-label inference and no billable Responses probe is used. Custom routes and header overrides cannot inherit official grants. The existing selected-account refresh now reaches the HTTP cache and publishes changed outcomes to open UI consumers. Native Codex API-key execution remains unsupported by this integration; official Platform and ChatGPT Responses endpoints remain separate. The 60-second HTTP-cache lifetime is not a polling timer or instantaneous revocation guarantee. Selected profile/key and route isolate observations; project/organization request-header overrides are ineligible for default-route grants. Missing, empty or failed metadata hides Access while ordinary inventory remains usable.

References: [Daybreak](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/daybreak), [Fast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode), [Ultrafast](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode).

## Evidence

### Follow-up CI repairs

Published repair head: **916b9b1dd1a82587227006a34620e80004ecba36**. Exact-head hosted CI is pending; no merge or auto-merge is authorized.

The repair candidate is signed `b51d8456b48ef87a0cf5105ad557255c5b06ea0d`, integrating pinned main `787a4336ec5c3b71136a270a72d0122bd688f5a5`. Its exact tree is `e8e9c7131710276e15e55c4541869c4b163b8d0c`. Focused validation passed: 25 dispatcher cases, seven command-harness cases, one real-browser sidebar case, affected agents/commands typechecks, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks.

- CI [39709987200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39709987200) on ae4781 completed with 102 successful, 20 skipped, and three failed jobs. The commands typecheck exposed a PR-authored test-helper mismatch; the fixture now passes its session key separately and uses the permitted Blue-only run-scoped recovery value. The exact failing compiler lane reproduced red and then passed with the fix; all seven harness cases pass.
- UI shard 6 waited for the removed **Reorder Beta** control. The failed base and PR have identical test and header-renderer blobs; upstream [bc9b820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bc9b82033dd83f298ab8b936faa11044f2b0d175) intentionally removed that control. The local real-browser reproduction failed at the same locator. This integration includes upstream [cadafc0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cadafc0084e25aa63a91506d4378d1f6db7ea7d2), which exercises header dragging and verifies complete persisted section order; the browser test passes after integration.
- The real dispatch-fixture conflict is resolved by keeping upstream's extracted case owner and source-turn authority assertions, moving both Standard/Blue cases into that owner, and retaining Access forwarding assertions. No production fallback, authority, assertion, budget, or dependency-policy weakening.
- The exact-ae4781 ClawSweeper review completed with no code/security findings; its outstanding item was this CI investigation. Earlier review and behavior proof retain their source revisions. New-head hosted checks remain separate.

### Rebase, cleanup, and history-preserving publication

- Local rebase and cleanup were reviewed at signed eeb137b3503e3e35b56877fb9f158ff8f0a302b0, tree 231d3831eebfbb38e2465d401e70e328ab5e6d06. To preserve the existing PR history, signed ca8f0125953547ee179ab697a45141494c94928d integrates main 7df418158195a01ca4e4981cb8ddbb4b826ffe13 into published b7b897786058894e983c166bf9caae00c9514f23 and applies the same reviewed cleanup. Its entire tree exactly matches eeb137; all test, dependency, generated and runtime inputs are byte-identical. Original and rebased histories remain preserved. No published history was rewritten.
- Removed unrelated native credential/dead SQLite method churn, Bifrost discovery test, superseded provider fixture workaround, obsolete overlay type test and historical scrolling workarounds. Current upstream behavior is retained. Omitted tree-identical publication bookkeeping from replay, retaining the original recovery ref.
- Accepted ClawSweeper’s test-cost suggestion: removed three redundant mocked Access cases. They use the same request owner as the retained seven-case production-client writer suite, not a distinct adapter contract. Account/catalog revocation and replacement denial plus subscription lifecycle proof remain.
- Complete snapshot comparison preserved merge-only guards, Gateway proof routing, lazy approval catalog consumers and generated output. Refusal metadata follows the current result type owner; cron parameters follow the current inference-binding owner. No dependency, workflow, assertion or budget weakening.
- Current focused boundary suite passed 142 tests across 16 files/eight routed shards; Cron consumers passed 22 tests/four files; UI consumer tests passed 48 tests/six files. Core/extensions/UI production compilation, scoped typed lint, config/protocol generators, i18n verification, full build and formatting passed. Task-local dependency setup now matches pinned Solid rc.16, without manifest/lockfile changes. Current-base UI performance comparison passes: startup JavaScript 325,056 bytes gzip, below the 325,657-byte enforced limit; chat/new-route budgets also pass. Initial compiler-root and browser startup failures remain recorded with their focused repairs/qualification below.
- Current compiler ownership gate and all four affected leaf typechecks pass. Gateway-root/Gateway-other/infra/state-logging have 719/566/713/716 roots under the unchanged 720 cap. Four unnecessary agent/plugin reallocations remain removed; the necessary Gateway and PostgreSQL ownership moves retain exact-once test coverage.
- Current real built UI/Gateway proof passed the desktop and mobile selection/reload/queue/stale-clear flow. The mobile fixture now focuses the real composer before opening its focus-revealed toolbar; no production behavior or assertion changed. Six capability UI scenarios and the zero-inference Platform discovery case passed in the preceding run and were not repeated. The focused repaired case passes, with its format, UI-E2E typecheck and typed lint; the other case is intentionally excluded by the targeted name filter, not claimed as rerun. Chromium startup initially failed on workspace socket-path length, resolved through the documented matching installed headless shell. External catalog/Responses I/O remains synthetic.
- Whole-candidate P0–P3 autoreview completed all 36 passes. It found a real run-scoped Access omission in the unsupported CLI guard; the guard now uses the effective run-scoped-or-saved selection. The real command-boundary regression was red, then green; CLI siblings and prompt-prefix tests pass (91 tests). Index-only truncation/catalog defects were resolved by staging the already-qualified complete source. Three other findings were declined with owner/source evidence, including a seven-test passing controller proof of fresh roster/default retention. The exact staged repair delta then passed independent P0–P3 review with no actionable findings. Targeted core, agent-test, UI-chat typechecks, typed lint and formatting pass.
- The rewritten-history publication was rejected. A same-base metadata refresh reconciled the PR projection with its existing branch; the recovery uses ordinary fast-forward publication of the history-preserving candidate. The initial history-preserving publication was **ae4781c569435c2dd8287abb8be219e788fdb3d0**, with the identical previously reviewed tree. Its failed hosted checks are attributed above; neither those failures nor historical CI below are relabeled. No merge or auto-merge is authorized.

### Retained behavior proof and limitations

- Earlier red/green implementation proof covers same physical model/provider/runtime/account/effort/speed, one authorized Blue escalation, exact pins, empty ordinary fallback lists, off, missing/revoked grants, route isolation, cancellation and committed-work no-replay. Each receipt retains its original SHA.
- Seven native-config cases use actual runCodexAppServerAttempt, CodexAppServerClient, account/catalog decoding, admission and serialized turn/start. Allowed Blue preserves model/high effort/priority speed; late revocation or replacement prevents a write. External daemon startup/I/O is synthetic, not successful real-account Blue inference.
- Actual built UI/Gateway proof at 23ba3458 covered Standard/Blue/Red, independent Medium/Fast, dismissal/reload, mobile queue, stale-grant clearing, SQLite and same-model Standard→Blue wire recovery. External model/catalog transport was synthetic. No real user state or credential copying.
- Upgrade proof used stable 2026.10.5 with synthetic config and actual Doctor repair: only retired target fields removed, normal model routing/auth/mode/cooloff preserved. Stable’s absent native plugin warning is not native inference proof.
- Earlier explicit live-provider proof cost $0.059019 and was not repeated. Real native account observations were Standard-only; successful native Blue inference is not claimed.

### CI and review provenance

- Historical head 05d7b955d1174528947c60c87a4cf6a503a0c06b: [CI 39557250828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39557250828), 120 successful / 16 skipped / two failed (dashboard fixture and aggregate), positively matched to scheduled-main failure with identical owner/test blobs. [Security Review 39561711319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39561711319) passed. These are not acceptance for the rebased candidate.
- Earlier group-defaults failures were positively inherited. An older touch reversal remained unattributed despite passing focused replays; no touch repair or all-green claim. Full source/job attribution and original errors remain in the work session. No remote rerun or relabeling.
- [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177812#issuecomment-6279630547) reviewed historical c34a80a with no actionable code/security findings. Its redundant-test suggestion is now applied locally. No claim of current-head review and no refresh request before confirmed publication.

### UI evidence

Existing inspected captures are reused from published `0e1f5b107a5da940e2629db3e2ea66e1eeddd9cd` (tested tree `6b80ac3ca80253f8594e86f5bff4a7529b764e1d`), not relabeled as new screenshots. They use the production-built UI and an actual isolated Gateway; external catalog/Responses I/O is synthetic. [Gallery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177812#issuecomment-6290718978) includes mobile and ordinary multilevel effort states.

**Before** — same narrow account catalog, desktop dark 1440×900:

![Before: Access dropdown and full-red Medium minimum](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bdc51e1-0049-4b67-9fba-9a685e6201b6)

**After** — segmented Access, neutral Medium minimum:

![After: segmented Access and neutral Medium minimum](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86a82b0a-bad2-4ae0-9985-bae368d82812)

The full-red minimum predates this PR: the old highest-non-Ultra style also applied at the first stop. The narrow synthetic catalog exposed it; the correction preserves authoritative effort levels and prevents minimum/maximum styling overlap. An ordinary Low/Medium/High/Ultra catalog places Medium at the second of four stops. Earlier built-product/browser evidence remains retained under its original SHAs; it is not relabeled as rebased-head verification. No new visual design change is intended by the rebase or cleanup.

prs.title: fix(browser): avoid repeat DNS checks for unchanged action URLs
prs.body:
Related: #178058

## What Problem This Solves

Browser actions repeat a DNS policy check while preparing the response URL, even when that same address was admitted earlier in the request.

## User Impact

Unchanged-tab actions avoid one redundant lookup and return the same result and URL. This draft addresses the response-only duplicate; it does not claim to eliminate all per-action DNS checks or prove meeting audio recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The action route opts in to reuse its admitted address only for response URL projection, with an exact URL and complete navigation-policy match. Changed URLs, changed policies, missing admission and cancellation retain validation. Execution and navigation guards remain authoritative. There is no cross-request cache, new setting or protocol change.

## Evidence

Actual Browser Bridge HTTP actions against an isolated Chrome 155 tab on macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0, with the default browser policy and real system DNS. Five serial baseline/candidate pairs used fresh processes; all 30 actions per revision returned identical page data and response URLs. All ten `about:blank` controls performed zero hostname lookups.

| Measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DNS lookups per unchanged action | 4 | 3 |
| Warm action median (25 samples) | 270.30 ms | 270.70 ms |
| Warm action p95 | 289.54 ms | 287.59 ms |
| Cold completion median (5 samples) | 4770.63 ms | 4827.54 ms |
| Cold completion p95 | 5633.91 ms | 5371.78 ms |

The committed opt-in workload is rerunnable with:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs extensions/browser/scripts/bench-act-dns.ts --chromium <chromium-executable> --output <result.json>
```

Cold completion includes isolated browser/page/bridge startup and the observer positive control. Action timing excludes observer flushing. Host load and controller CPU/RSS are recorded; aggregate metrics did not regress by 20%. The workload's initial lint overlapped the first two pairs. No delayed DNS or simulated browser/provider results were used; slow-resolver stalls and meeting audio loss were not reproduced.

- New unchanged-URL regression fails on the base because it performs two policy validations rather than one; the other nine cases pass. All ten pass with the fix, including changed URL, in-place policy mutation, missing admission and cancellation controls.
- Three focused owner/action/navigation suites passed all 90 cases (7.07 seconds wrapper wall time). After the final test-only adjustment, the changed 10-case file passed again (19.94 seconds including cold compiler setup); CI case time is pending.
- Browser package production types, targeted test/workload types, typed lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed.
- One independent P0–P2 autoreview completed with no actionable findings.

Full PR CI is currently skipped because this PR is a draft; the local results above are not a full-CI claim.

Production delta: 25 insertions / 3 deletions in two files. The remaining additions are the focused regression coverage and opt-in measurement workload.

Detection, Suggested Profiles, and Installed Agents are adopted; unmerged candidates receive no credit. Cron belongs to the recipes lane. Each PR’s exact paired-build base is reported separately below.

This candidate adopts Provider login/activation and Start Chat: Provider mutation families move from 2 adopted / 5 pending / 1 exception to 4 / 3 / 1. Provider component-lifetime cleanup moves from 2 pending to 0; Installed Agents has already landed. No other checklist count changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Provider sign-in and Start Chat still used imperative pending presentation instead of native scoped Solid 2 saving actions. Their existing request and navigation contracts must survive the migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider login, access, and saved-profile activation now use a generator action with an optimistic saving flag around each admitted wizard RPC. Start Chat uses the same saving presentation while its existing session owner creates the session. Saving stays separate from aggregate view props, preserving the native dialog's settlement, input identity, cancellation, and visible failure recovery.

The plain owners still admit requests synchronously and own config reconciliation, cancellation, result publication, and navigation. Scope replacement retires presentation before publishing new connection or agent facts; the original operation promise remains consumed and returned. The extracted Start Chat owner preserves its existing generation/client success and navigation checks. Connection epoch and agent checks additionally qualify presentation only.

The selected-model and missing-profile calculation moves intact into the existing login-providers module. A shared saving presenter serves the wizard and chat callers. No optimistic credential success, session key, or extra RPC is added. Existing owner reconciliation has no additional consumed refreshable server slot that would justify an invented affects/refresh call. Query and provider selection remain local interaction state. Login and discovery lifetime cleanup now pair with onSettled.

The existing Model Setup completion body moves unchanged into its owner-approved completion helper, keeping the caller under the file-size limit. Model Providers and Model Setup supply the same small connection-epoch and synchronous-presentation-retirement interface. The wizard's optional busy prop is consumed optimistic-first; no markup, selector, route, or lazy boundary changes.

Full CI exposed a wizard presentation regression: a wizard command publishes a starting or input step and then continues waiting for an admitted operation or browser callback. Holding saving until that whole command completed hid the controls needed to cancel or finish sign-in. The shared wizard adapter now reports each starting/step publication, releasing only the temporary saving presentation. The original owner operation continues consuming the callback and retaining cancellation, admission, and credential-completion authority. A held-callback regression verifies that the link, Copy link, and Cancel remain usable with one login admission. Before the runner starts, a presentation-only admissionPending prop derives the Checking dialog from the exact returned state snapshot and existing mutation admission; queued Cancel retires that admission without dispatching activation. No retained copy of a wizard step or remount key is needed.

A further held-read regression covers the interval after the runner publishes a credential step but before RuntimeConfig finishes its admitted configuration refresh. The wizard retains the plain mutation admission busy fact during that interval; its separate optimistic saving presentation may retire at the owner checkpoint. This keeps controls disabled until the owner can accept the next answer without hiding the step.

prs.title: fix(release): show Pacific time in FRV progress
prs.body:
## Summary

- show full UTC and Pacific timestamps on human-facing `frv watch` and `frv continue` progress
- use `America/Los_Angeles` so the Pacific label follows PST/PDT automatically
- show the same dual timestamp for rate-limit retry deadlines

## Why

FRV progress was emitted only in UTC despite the standing Pacific-time convention for release operations. That made live release coordination require manual timezone conversion, especially around retry deadlines and UTC date boundaries.

The existing progress formatter remains the single owner for both commands. The simplification pass removed test-only exports and kept JSON `at` fields and audit records unchanged; no new state or compatibility path was added.

Closes RRI-384.

`pnpm check:changed` passed the touched-file format, lint, ratchet, and test-type lanes after the declaration fix. Its full-tree graph-budget and dead-export scans still report unrelated existing failures on `main`.

Independent review found no P0/P1 issues. The review used the supplied exact diff semantics because the review child did not have filesystem access.

## What Problem This Solves

Camera selection persisted only after Talk accepted the device, while Settings discarded the completion and maintained separate error text. A superseded switch could hold an older presentation, and a failed device discovery left its alert visible during retry.

The selected camera now appears immediately while Talk switches devices. A failed selection returns to the confirmed preference and shows the current error beside the same focused selector. Retrying clears old feedback. Only a confirmed current selection is saved; leaving Appearance does not wait for the hardware response.

## Ownership

The existing media-device owner admits the camera receipt and retains hardware switching, supersession, and confirmed-only persistence. Solid presents the optimistic selection and process state through an action and two projections. Receipt-keyed discovery status clears old feedback without remounting the selector.

Panel and route intent retire presentation synchronously. Navigation can complete while the media owner still records the eventual hardware outcome. The main integration preserves the separately landed Updates presenter in ConfigPage. No setting, dependency, protocol, route, or stored-state shape is added.

prs.title: fix(memory): honor the agent timeout for deep consolidation
prs.body:
Fixes #177068

## What Problem This Solves

Deep consolidation in memory-core dreaming used a hard-coded 60-second completion timeout. Unlike the light/REM/deep narrative phases fixed in #167984, it ignored an explicitly configured `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, so slow local models could never finish the phase and promotions silently degraded to append-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dreaming sweep already resolves the configured agent timeout through the timer-safe `resolveAgentTimeoutMs` resolver for narrative generation. This change forwards that resolved value into the deep-consolidation completion only when `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is explicitly configured. When the setting is absent, scheduled deep consolidation keeps its existing 60-second deadline, preserving the policy retained by #167984.

## User Impact

Operators with slow local models can let deep consolidation finish by configuring the existing `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`; no new config key or migration is required. Users who never set that value keep the existing bounded 60-second consolidation behavior and 48-hour narrative default.

## Evidence

- Explicit `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is resolved once through the existing timer-safe resolver and forwarded to the consolidation completion.
- With the setting absent, no consolidation override is passed, so `consolidateMemory` keeps its 60-second default.
- Added sweep regression coverage for both paths: an explicit 180-second budget reaches consolidation, while an absent setting leaves consolidation at 60 seconds.
- Added direct-caller coverage that `consolidateMemory` retains the 60-second fallback when no timeout is supplied.
- `vitest`: 2 files / 29 tests passed (`dreaming-consolidation.test.ts`, `dreaming-sweep-narrative.test.ts`).
- `vitest`: 3 adjacent memory-core files / 112 tests passed (`short-term-promotion.test.ts`, `short-term-promotion-owner.test.ts`, `dreaming.test.ts`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass on every changed file.
- GitHub CI on the previous revision passed `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, and `check-lint`.

### Real-model end-to-end proof

Verified on head `975597e0f211` with `OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (975597e)`, an isolated
state/workspace, the shipped `openclaw gateway run` entry point, and the managed
dreaming cron job. Model calls were sent unchanged to a real DeepSeek route behind
the local `cc-switch` proxy. To make the timeout boundary deterministic without
spending a large real-model budget, an uncommitted loopback timing proxy added
exactly 65 seconds only to consolidation requests. This is transport delay, not
synthesized model output, and is not presented as a natural slow-model benchmark.

Timeout absent (existing 60-second default):

```text
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=custom-127-0-0-1-15721 api=openai-completions model=deepseek-chat elapsedMs=59870 name=TimeoutError message=The operation was aborted due to timeout
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent durationMs=60088 error="The operation was aborted due to timeout" errorName=TimeoutError
[plugins] memory-core: consolidation failed (The operation was aborted due to timeout); using append-only fallback.
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=1, applied=1, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=1).
```

Explicit `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds: 180` with the same candidate and the same
65-second consolidation delay:

```text
[proof-proxy] POST /v1/chat/completions bytes=1526 consolidation=true delayMs=65000
[proof-proxy] completed status=200 elapsedMs=65858
[proof-proxy] POST /v1/chat/completions bytes=3279 consolidation=false delayMs=0
[proof-proxy] completed status=200 elapsedMs=2297
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=1, applied=1, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=1).
```

The 180-second run had no `TimeoutError` or `consolidation failed` line and published
the consolidated entry to `MEMORY.md`:

```markdown
## Consolidated Memory (2026-10-19)

<!-- openclaw-memory-promotion:memory:memory/2026-10-19.md:2:2:76a2a1ac5bf8 -->
- The proof177246 test profile stores durable notes with the marker NEEDLE-177246 and prefers concise release notes. Source: memory/2026-10-19.md#L2-L2
```

The cron result for the 180-second run reported `durationMs: 72772` and
`completionStatus: "succeeded"`; the 60-second control reported `durationMs: 66123`
and used append-only fallback. Raw evidence is retained under
`contributions/pr-177246-evidence/` in the contributor workspace. A naturally slow
model run remains optional supporting evidence, but the deterministic real-Gateway
control now exercises the changed timeout selection directly.

### Latest-stable upgrade validation

Upgraded an isolated install of npm `openclaw@2026.10.5` (`1b58cb9`) to this
PR head `44c9a5740` (`2026.10.5`) with an existing config and indexed memory
workspace. The captured `openclaw doctor --fix` log ends with `Doctor complete.`
and shows the agent database migration and its pre-migration backups:

```text
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-9e8f4bbf....bak
Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: .../openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-9e8f4bbf....bak

- Upgraded agent database schema in .../openclaw-agent.sqlite: v25 -> v31.
Backup: .../openclaw.json.bak
Doctor complete.
```

The explicitly configured values were byte-for-byte identical before and after
the upgrade (redacted of secrets):

```json
{
  "agents": { "defaults": { "timeoutSeconds": 180, "model": "proof177246/deepseek-chat" } },
  "tools": { "allow": ["memory_get", "memory_search"] },
  "provider": { "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:15721/v1", "api": "openai-completions" }
}
```

Both memory files kept their exact pre-upgrade SHA-256 hashes
(`MEMORY.md` `ef9e53e5...32af6`, `memory/2026-10-20.md` `3512ef8b...02275`),
and the upgraded CLI’s `memory search KEEP-177246 --json` returned both files
with the `KEEP-177246` snippets intact. Focused coverage on the merged head
also passed: 5 files / 141 tests.

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Codex) under the submitting operator's direction. The operator reviewed the issue, diff, and test evidence before submission.

prs.title: fix(doctor): settle missing retained originals onto verified survivors
prs.body:
Closes #179957

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `doctor --session-sqlite recover` defers duplicate-archive settlement forever when the historical original path is already missing, even though a byte-verified surviving archive exists.

## User Impact
Offline recovery can now reconcile historical archive references whose originals vanished, instead of reporting `restored=0 ... reason: doctor recover completed with remaining issues` on every run. In the linked report, 6,420 missing references all had surviving archives matching the receipt size and SHA-256, yet none were settled.

## Why This Change Was Made
The settlement loop asserted that every non-disposed original still exists on disk before recording a replacement, so a retained original whose file had already vanished failed with "artifact is unexpectedly missing" and its references were never repointed. The replacement-retention check likewise required every reference to be disposed before keeping the repoint.

A missing retained original has nothing left to retire: settlement now skips the existence assert and disposal selection for it (the survivor was already byte-verified in the same loop) and still records the replacement, and a replacement survives when every reference is disposed or its original file is absent. The "Archive was recreated after disposal" guard and the identity-mismatch deferral for changed originals are unchanged.

## Evidence
- Regression in `doctor-session-sqlite.duplicate-lookup.test.ts`: two byte-identical retained archives, the original's file removed, settlement now reports `historical_duplicate_settled` (previously `historical_transcript_deferred` with "artifact is unexpectedly missing") and the survivor's bytes stay intact. Red on base, green with this change.
- Neighbors stay green: the remaining 3 settlement cases in `doctor-session-sqlite.duplicate-lookup.test.ts` and all 18 cases in `doctor-session-sqlite.retirement-mutations.test.ts` (node 24.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --run`).
- Not run locally: full commands suite and typecheck (CI covers).

prs.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): honor silent message sends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nextcloud Talk drops OpenClaw’s requested silent-send flag, so messages intended to be quiet can create chat notifications.

## User Impact

Users can request `silent: true` for text and native file shares without changing normal notification behavior or channel configuration. Messages remain visible. Quiet file sends fail before media reads/uploads if the server’s required capability cannot be confirmed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing shared flag and Talk’s native controls, preserving bot-authored text, API-user-authored files, replies, receipts, and text fallbacks. Silent file metadata is supported through `media-caption`, not `silent-send` or `silent-send-state`.

No new configuration, dependencies, shared-core changes, or default-silent policy. Native-voice work remains separate in #178521; this PR does not bundle it or claim runtime voice compatibility.

## Evidence

- [Upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39712317406) passed on the submitted head.
- [Focused source qualification](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/39709430733): 14 quiet-send regressions and 5 prefix-stability cases passed; 54 existing media/core/handoff and 20 automatic-inbound cases retained behind exact production/fixture/docs byte-identity guards following a test-style-only repair. Production/test types, affected lint, docs, canonical formatting and whitespace checks passed. No skipped tests counted as passes.
- The same request-boundary regression fails on original production code: 10 intended failures, 4 normal-send controls passing. Final source review at P0–P2 found no actionable issues. New 14-case suite: 0.202s test time; 51.24s command wall including cold transforms on GitHub.
- [Real-server proof](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/39711691610): exact package installed into an isolated Gateway against disposable Nextcloud 35.0.2 / Talk 25.0.6. All six cases passed. Normal text/file controls produced 1/2 recipient notifications respectively. Quiet text with a server-parsed mention, six-chunk text, captioned file and captionless file reply produced zero notifications. All messages remained visible with their expected silent state and sending identity; recipient file bytes matched.
- Configuration remained unchanged during the sends, no unexpected fixture errors occurred, and Gateway/fixture server/container cleanup passed. No production deployment or restart. This proves actual server notification state, not phone push/audible behavior, native-voice runtime behavior, or a real-model conversation.

<details>
<summary>Exact artifact and proof boundaries</summary>

Source/build commit: `a460fbdd3b6f626e02ad803516b94d46ed8188ca`.
Canonical package SHA-256: `4966a72bd6a30bc4da9c9cb386ece8fefe0ab8b0a22e2c15fc00aff2f4c71ff7` (independently downloaded and hashed).
All six source-file hashes match the qualified input and package identity. The real-server run reuses that exact package from [its successful build](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/39710201330); the first integration attempt stopped before sending on a retired fixture-only heartbeat key. The successful follow-up corrects only that disposable configuration, not product code. QA workflows and proof fixtures are separate from this six-file product patch.

Normal false/omitted sends retain their existing request behavior. Quiet files check `media-caption` using the existing authenticated same-origin client before reading/uploading media and recheck cancellation/custody afterward. Bot text requires no additional API-user credentials. Existing upload cleanup, uncertain-publication reconciliation, and receipts are unchanged.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the session watchdog stops an automation, run history and chat failure alerts lose the reason, sometimes replacing it with a session-cleanup error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing controller's stop reason to Cron through its own abort signal, and preserve that fact on both returned and thrown completion paths. User/restart cancellation, execution authority, tool cleanup and non-provider retry behavior keep their existing owners. No configuration, storage-format or migration change.

This addresses the watchdog attribution path in #138528. Its separate immediate exec-denial classification and historical 150-second approval trigger are outside this change.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

## User Impact

**Do not merge or deploy this draft.** It preserves the attempted receipt design and regression evidence for a maintainer decision. The unfinished-migration recovery and startup-notice implementation is tracked in #163803; this draft does not close the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The draft observes physical SQLite transactions, carries committed observations through worker admission and heartbeat settlement, and stores run ID, migration identity, path, and pre/post content versions in existing `migration_runs.report_json`. Bounded update history holds a private receipt ID. It adds no SQLite tables, columns, dependencies, configuration, or CLI options.

Two blockers remain:

1. **Observation cost versus the 60-second heartbeat lease.** Every observed transaction takes two full-content observations. Each observation includes at least five full database scans, plus copy/WAL work. The heartbeat's first observation occurs before renewal checks expiry. At an effective scan throughput of 32 MiB/s, five scans of a 1 GiB database take approximately 160 seconds before copy overhead, exceeding the existing 60-second lease. This is a source-derived cost illustration, not a benchmark.
2. **Same-run heartbeat commits are classified as foreign.** Transaction A can commit, then heartbeat B from the same update can commit before A completes its post-commit observation and `PRAGMA data_version` check. A is permanently marked unattributed even when B supplies a valid same-run receipt, disabling rollback after the updater's own writes.

Recommended direction for acceptance: keep full fingerprints at admission/settlement and investigate bounded commit evidence owned by one coordinated run-lease writer, including renewal, with continuous same-connection SQLite `data_version` checks. Run/lease identity must bind actual writer custody; it is not authority by itself. `data_version` is connection-local, so simply replacing content fingerprints with its numeric value, ignoring a changed value, or excluding heartbeat writes would not safely resolve the foreign-write guard.

## Evidence

Exploratory proof before this split passed real agent schema 21 → 24 → restored 21, retaining the original conversation rows and covering shared-state lease writes (11.643 seconds of test execution; 48.71 seconds file wall time). The activation authority-refusal service fixture passed in 23.719 seconds. Restoring the pre-fix capture producer failed at the missing restorable receipt.

These small-state results do not resolve either blocker. Full validation is incomplete. The pending P1 review and broader test run were interrupted after the owner audit established the design defects; no clean review or complete suite result is claimed. This commit is preserved as a design artifact under an explicit review waiver, not as a release candidate. Auto-merge remains off.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: named administrators signed in through a trusted proxy cannot report a failed update, even though they can check or retry it.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The RPC and Control UI incorrectly treated the synthetic `gateway-owner` profile as reporting authority. Both now use administrator scope. The server rechecks that scope alongside existing connection/run authority before side effects; reviewed consent, current-attempt/digest checks, and duplicate protection remain enforced. Reporting keeps the resolved named profile unchanged. Check status and Retry already use the same admin scope.

Release-note context: trusted-proxy administrators can report update failures without changing authentication mode or their persistent device grant. This changes reporting authorization only; updater execution, backup, rollback, configuration, and schemas are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: migrate existing state before container readiness
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes container image replacement leaving existing agent databases and legacy workspace state unusable while the Gateway can still announce that it is ready.

Fixes #152935, fixes #152939.

Thanks to @Conan-Scott for the OpenShift/Kubernetes reproduction and to the anonymous Discord reporter for the Unraid/Docker workspace and audit-migration case.

## User Impact

Routine image upgrades migrate existing state before serving requests, without a separate offline `openclaw doctor --fix` step. Startup preserves verified pre-migration SQLite backups alongside the existing config backups and exact-byte workspace archives. Default/system agent refusals keep readiness false and expose the actual admission reason; unsafe migrations exit 78 before a ready announcement. Optional agent isolation and recoverable warnings remain supported.

Release-note context: container upgrades now run Doctor's stopped-writer migrations automatically and cannot report healthy while a core agent database is refused. Rollback requires restoring the matching state backups with the old image. No new schema, dependency, config setting, or CLI option is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup was applying runtime admission to migration inputs before repairs and omitted migrations reserved for stopped writers. It now borrows Doctor's existing exclusive maintenance owner without entering its managed-service stop/restart path, runs the same migration graph, and verifies runtime admission afterward. Readiness and ready logging consume that admission result.

The end-to-end proof also exposed completed SQLite worker cleanup that remained marked pending and an uncached lease inspection that could create a WAL before config refusal. Those paths now use their existing cleanup receipt and private snapshot owners. A preserved plugin-sidecar conflict remains an advisory warning so unrelated repairs can complete safely.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with official `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.9.4` and `:2026.9.5`: schema-19 agents were refused after replacement, `/readyz` returned HTTP 200 with `ready: true`, and default-agent session RPC returned `UNAVAILABLE`. Offline 9.5 Doctor repaired the same input to schema 21.
- Candidate image: startup and offline-Doctor-then-startup twins pass for the published 9.4 state and the combined legacy workspace/audit fixture. Both agents are schema 21 at the first successful readiness response, and default-agent session RPC succeeds. Per fixture, 115 table-count comparisons and 62 user-payload hashes match after identical lifecycle steps; shared schema remains 17.
- Six candidate-created SQLite backups preserve old schemas, payloads, row IDs, and integrity, with runtime lease rows removed. Restoring those backups in an independent copy boots published 9.4 and passes the session RPC. Workspace archives preserve the exact source bytes.
- Inconsistent default-agent schema markers exit 78, never announce ready, and preserve the refused database's data.
- Focused migration, admission, maintenance, worker-cleanup, and Gateway readiness suites pass, including fail-before regressions. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, and final P1 autoreview is scoped-clean. Logs are retained with the local proof artifacts.

The audit fixture is explicitly synthetic historical state applied to a copy of the published 9.4 input: a fresh 9.4 install already creates the current audit shape. Offline Doctor leaves canonical validation queued until Gateway boot; both twins are compared after that same boot/RPC/stop sequence. All table counts are recorded. Shared lifecycle, diagnostic, and paired-device counts are not equality assertions; the only observed count difference after matched boots is `diagnostic_events`.

The image uses the repository Dockerfile on Linux arm64 with the release workflow's selected plugins. Its immutable per-file source manifest binds the tested working-tree bytes; the image's Git metadata records their base commit rather than claiming uncommitted edits were already a commit.

Final image: `openclaw:l844-e24c2e6f010a`, ID `sha256:cec14c3de607df0a319c29596b0dc4580f0da7ef6f779ca1d2d671057978ea7d`. Source manifest: `e24c2e6f010a2517742590c1652b64c24a4ab8658030e2a058355dfcb25a3dca`. All 33 changed/new files matched before and after proof. The local transcript is `.local/l844-proof/proof-candidate-3/transcript.txt`, with schema/count/hash results and rollback/unsafe summaries beside it.

Diff split: production +359/−111; tests and test support +834/−173; docs +22/−1.

prs.body:
## Final temporary docs-proof receipt

The [single Linux job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35677502472/job/106586982565), attempt 1 at carrier `fa567f1e4d19bfbe5ba12bfdd97aa0824fc25139`, ran canonical `pnpm docs:site` against [fs-safe release proposal 588](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/588), exact source `80a34f9800a75c975469d9c41ee56fa45025babb` / tree `042a9bd0b07ba725e5be315ba1e17973b7294404`.

**The canonical docs command passed; the overall temporary job failed.** On Linux x64 / Node 24.21.0 / pnpm 12.4.2, the command returned 0 without signal in 1.715817167 seconds. Its 54 HTML pages and six expected assets passed the output oracle, including the canonical builder's navigation, local-target and cross-page-anchor checks. All 65 authenticated docs/command inputs and the full tracked Git diff were unchanged afterward.

The failure was the extra `test ! -e node_modules` assertion. [pnpm 12.4.2 defaults to installing out-of-sync dependencies before scripts](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/v12.4.2/pnpm/crates/config/src/settings.rs#L1479-L1484). It automatically verified/installed workspace dependencies before running the script: 193 packages across nine workspaces, with the allowed esbuild postinstall. Lockfile resolution was skipped and the input hashes remained unchanged. The builder itself uses only Node builtins and two checked-in modules, but that does **not** mean the canonical pnpm command avoids installation. The earlier no-workspace-install claim, including that text in the retained command receipt's scope label, is incorrect. The measured command span includes installation; it is not a cold docs-only benchmark. The subsequent `git diff --check` line was unrun in this job; release preparation has its separate earlier check.

Authenticated evidence artifact `10673442396`: 10,745 bytes / SHA-256 `c61aabc8386d00bc0336897e73b6f225c99e43fbb6fb0dfb13f0c6835f7a2642`. Before/after input manifest: `6ee246fe1bc84b316e8e0c1f674e2ed7d3c36fe0d92013afd7046d1845522766`; 60-file output inventory: `8aa1f46ec88d6ea1cbc9677e3d169f6dd1699cbabead17778f1bc9c335d0361a`. Independent custody and pnpm-lifecycle review support carrying the actual docs result without rerunning it to remove the mistaken auxiliary guard.

This is static docs-build proof, not exhaustive fragment-only-anchor, browser, external-network, deployment, package/native build or release proof. No fs-safe merge/tag/npm publication, OpenClaw dependency adoption or native finalizer/ARM clearance follows. This temporary PR is to close unmerged with its source, branch and proof retained. The earlier X failure and direct-owner pass below keep their original identities and limits.

---

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149882

## What Problem This Solves

The FreeBSD x64 real-finalizer test rejects an unsafe temporary directory, but the config snapshot and validator boundaries discard the nested filesystem cause needed to choose a repair. This draft supplies a separate sealed diagnostic candidate and one native reproduction case.

## User Impact

**Diagnostic only. Keep this PR draft; never merge its instrumentation or temporary workflow.** There is no shipping fix, permission change, dependency update, or claim that the original failure is resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two temporary blocks observe the existing failure after authority checks: the snapshot records at most eight cause nodes and four known path roles; the validator relays at most one closed-schema reconstructed record. Each record is bounded to 8 KiB without raw messages, stacks, paths, or environment values. Signed Node bigint metadata is preserved. Original validation, refusal, cleanup, SQL, test assertions, and deadlines remain unchanged.

The completed sealed X consumer ran exactly the original positive finalizer case and reproduced the failure, with its original nonzero result preserved. Its native report and closed child relay are recorded below. A parent-only/missing/malformed record is inconclusive, and post-failure metadata is not an atomic throw-time cause.

## Completed owner-only proof

The new temporary successor isolates the independently established fs-safe representation bug. It fetches only two immutable, builtin-only `secure-temp-repair.ts` modules from `openclaw/fs-safe`, checks API path/type/size, Git blob and SHA-256 on the host, then rechecks bytes before direct native TypeScript import in the guest. No OpenClaw package, dependency override, package-manager install, build, or original test rerun is involved.

- Old published 0.18 owner: `3ba5c9504ae5bf89837f491f0f227c68de14778a`, 5,586 bytes, SHA-256 `7271fed7aed56d0d796c6a2da2bb9ad3cd3f1131099a495c8d7ee55a1bb81072`.
- Repaired owner: reviewed `33436f37f3b4060784250eabdbea24ef05dee30f`, 5,860 bytes, SHA-256 `f9f315ce5d5f71e88ddd8743b23a37cc7e71e71bc0e00c25beda2996bf6817ee`. These bytes exactly match the subsequently landed [fs-safe repair](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/586) at `9a0b7258043c599672f364b1f3aaed63db81e1f2`; the already reviewed source pin remains unchanged.

On disposable FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE-p3 x64, the probe records the actual Node 24 patch and requires a real negative device observation. Without one, it exits 78 as inconclusive. The same actual stat goes through old receipt rejection and new raw-identity admission. Four task-owned cases exercise `0777` and `0500` through ordinary repair and finalization, each ending at `0700` with device/inode/owner preserved. The actual default builtin adapter supplies all filesystem authority; open/close wrappers only observe and delegate those calls. Counts and a post-close `EBADF` check verify descriptor closure. Parent/sentinel identity and bytes, source hashes, and removal of the unique task root are checked. Failures and cleanup failures cannot report success.

Signed proof carrier `5a7a6db9644275dcb7e5342b5197a49301aabf4d`, tree `4fd1352f6da5c9987956977e061a07285cb6fe59`, has sole predecessor `956eba7050d9f038fad3c8ea971372a3097e8d1d`; the one draft synchronize admission requires that predecessor and attempt 1. Independent source/custody review and fresh scoped autoreview passed. Three shell blocks and the Python/JavaScript probe parse; native owner execution passed as recorded below. Success would prove this dependency owner on real filesystem facts, not the integrated resolver/finalizer or exact earlier throw site.

## Native owner result

[Run 35675912239, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35675912239/job/106582295931) succeeded at carrier `5a7a6db9644275dcb7e5342b5197a49301aabf4d` on FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE-p3 x64, Node 24.21.0, root. The actual directory reported device `-5291551583207762996`, inode `17`, UID `0`, mode `040700`. The same real stat was rejected by the old published owner and admitted unchanged by the repaired owner, whose bytes exactly match landed fs-safe `9a0b7258043c599672f364b1f3aaed63db81e1f2`.

All four `0777`/`0500` × ordinary/finalize cases ended at `0700`, preserving raw device/inode/owner, parent/root identities and sentinels. Each recorded one actual open, close, access check and repair; closed descriptors returned `EBADF`. Source posthashes passed; the task directory was removed and the command exited zero. The retained native raw receipt is 66,060 bytes/SHA-256 `8554a1ae5918459e9cabeb224b166870b11d0a9d2083992da07868f354bf73f3`. Independent receipt and landed-source verification passed.

This proves the direct fs-safe owner regression and repair on a real negative-device filesystem. It does not prove integrated OpenClaw resolver/finalizer success or uniquely assign the earlier X throw. No package was published or OpenClaw dependency changed.

## Evidence

- Original [x64 native failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35665462384/job/106550117739): exact package/root/AI restoration passed; 62 native cases passed, one failed, one skipped. The positive finalizer failed with `Unsafe fallback OpenClaw temp dir`. Its nested cause remains unproven.
- Diagnostic source `1388021b60cd6b87ec5bb840fdcfbd06e39f3530`, tree `282fcc4a3ee7d7af39c51fb39b97ca3545dff873`, sole parent `10725d8613c64f5efdc8ea58eae70a3b8f4276ac`. Removing the two observation blocks restores both parent modules exactly. The 568 added production lines are temporary observation/schema validation, not a shipping repair.
- Earlier producer attempts stopped at [whole-bundle retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35670060951/job/106564287710) and [unsupported emitted writer syntax](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35671497886/job/106568758126). Neither sealed a candidate or supplied native evidence. Those collector defects were corrected with 58 mechanics cases, including authenticated actual emitted excerpts and negative binding/guard controls; optional raw UTF-8 excerpt caps never gate full proof traversal.
- [Successful producer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35673571733/job/106575212070), attempt 1, carrier `d1bf78d0108c6db492689d929411e9f299ede05a`: canonical build and seal passed. All 8,625 runtime modules were inventoried; all three marked modules were package/build-equal and fully parsed, including the 54,048,916-byte worker. Both observer and relay writers passed their actual builtin/fd2/origin/8 KiB checks, with no collector errors. This is package proof, not unit/native execution.
- Sealed artifact `10671799140`, 245,524,296 bytes, SHA-256 `732e2c45254e4c8e23eabe47845c68f17eb40e93564bf6051a7a695c4dae8655`; manifest `21902bc002cceafc66ce6f3a6da5e95a0872267aa56b8876dca4221bc2fc6cb0`; source archive `3580f587a467a1a9aa6c5b552e1ec67b9398f94d9b16ee5c24467144655bfc1f`. Candidate package is 81,933,646 bytes/SHA-256 `ada48abf6796713285c7ed6d34de4561ac1d3a7bf9a39a42a579b87763ed8379`, version 2026.9.5. API, canonical manifest serialization, and upload receipts agree; consumer verification remains mandatory.
- The consumer's 44 extracted-oracle and shell mechanics cases passed, including zero selection, genuine/generic failure, native test/hook timeouts with the process flag false, malformed/missing diagnostics, relay provenance/privacy, signed metadata, and original-exit precedence. These are synthetic oracle checks, not native candidate execution. Independent custody and oracle reviews passed; fresh scoped autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue and verified the final source snapshot.
- Producer runtime was Linux x64 Node 24.21.0/pnpm 12.4.0/fs-safe 0.18.0. The guest keeps the existing Node 24-major package route and records its actual patch. Patch/environment drift limits comparison; nonreproduction cannot clear the original Node 24.21 failure. Metadata-only dependency inventory follows the test on both outcomes and does not load a native addon or claim cross-stage byte equality.

Completed X consumer `956eba7050d9f038fad3c8ea971372a3097e8d1d` (tree `25d63b462b138c7de95c4599f637638a7e229a1e`) has the sole producer parent `d1bf78d0108c6db492689d929411e9f299ede05a`; only the temporary workflow changed. Its one synchronize admission requires that exact predecessor.

## Native result

[The one FreeBSD x64 consumer run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35674957302/job/106579401592), attempt 1 at consumer `956eba7050d9f038fad3c8ea971372a3097e8d1d`, reproduced the original failure. Actual guest: FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE-p3, Node 24.21.0, root, pnpm 12.4.0. Artifact/manifest/source/package checks, all 28 source pins, and exact restored root/AI graph of 10,822 files passed; no rebuild occurred. Post-test source/package/graph identities remained unchanged.

Exactly the selected case failed after 44,208 ms at its original success assertion; eight cases were filtered. There were no suite errors, unhandled errors, or process timeout; the native report SHA-256 is `e43b9df8574abba37177a6320617d1d6d286353cf8f3e01e58cbb5391c0df221`. The first verification failure was `candidate-config-failed` with the unsafe-fallback error; the subsequent gateway recovery timeout was downstream. Status precedence was preserved: test `1`, report/posthash/dependency/relay `0`.

One validated child-relay record selected `logging-fallback`. The post-failure preferred and fallback logging directories were root-owned, directory/non-symlink, mode `0700`, and passed write/search access. Both reported device `-5291551583207762996`, with positive inodes and complete metadata. The actual fs-safe package remained 0.18.0; its 621-file metadata inventory matched the recorded package inventory. No native-addon probe was performed.

This is a valid reproduction and post-failure observation, not native fix clearance. The graph contains only the outer fallback-admission error, with no nested cause or syscall. Although fs-safe 0.18's receipt predicate rejects the observed negative device representation, its ordinary resolver would preserve that rejection as a nested cause. The missing cause and non-atomic observation therefore prevent assigning the exact historical throw to that predicate. Happy-path ledger/lease assertions after the original success assertion were not reached; no successful lease-absence outcome is claimed.

Retained native raw receipt: 201,544 bytes, SHA-256 `e6c2aa530ffafc55ac3f8acd390bcd708be33632a30240ae3ef63e3dc215069e`. This remains separate from the ARM heartbeat diagnostic and the unchanged original product candidate. The fs-safe source repair has landed but has not been released or integrated into the X package, which still uses 0.18.0. No native fix clearance is claimed.
