prs.title: perf(update): reuse plugin generations during candidate validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Candidate update validation repeatedly acquires the same installed external plugin sources and dependency trees for entry, setup, and Doctor surfaces.

Related: #154381, #154114, #144858. Thanks @ZaneMc-AO and @agebreak0083 for the field reports.

## User Impact

This draft reuses prepared plugin generations within one disposable candidate rehearsal while keeping each executing consumer's files independent. It is held for Peter's decision: historical measurements reduced repeated acquisitions, but increased logical copy output by **24.55%**, and the effect on slow disks and Windows remains unproven.

The scope is generation reuse only. Session-settlement repair is tracked in [#155138](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155138); Doctor lint deferral is isolated in [#155244](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155244). Neither repair remains in this PR’s authored delta.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-generation owner prepares one private source generation and its dependency-inspection facts, publishes it inside the disposable rehearsal, and supplies isolated runtime copies. Worker envelopes preserve that rehearsal identity across nested state scopes. Native links and SDK resolution remain bound to the candidate. Unavailable preparation records a warning and uses independent acquisition.

The installed 2026.9.4 driver still owns its initial snapshot copy and 300-second clamp. Candidate-side reuse cannot remove that already-running driver's work. The remaining change is **16 paths: production +1406/−438, tests +485/−0, docs +7/−0**.

The decision is whether the reduction in repeated source acquisition justifies the extra copying of complete writable views on slow storage. No Windows or slow-disk improvement is claimed; keep this PR draft while that tradeoff is unresolved.

## Evidence

The source split is exact: seven lint/settlement files were returned to main at `8c56f7239e98dbee1369e036d6b594fd560b9d9d`; only their two documentation paragraphs were removed. All 15 retained source/test paths match the previously published producer `4b01224f5fc6dbbb66380abee06c2efaa3ec1213` byte-for-byte, and the seven-line generation paragraph is unchanged. `git diff --check` passes. A fresh generation-only build, test run, and published-driver hop have **not** been claimed.

Historical diagnostics used the published npm `openclaw@2026.9.4` updater with isolated state/free ports, ten v19 agent databases (365.797 MiB total; largest 338.73 MiB), and seven external npm plugins (Codex, WhatsApp, Discord, Slack, DeepSeek, Mistral, and Venice; 477.500 MiB total). The candidate upgraded the databases to v22; all three diagnostic hops passed integrity/foreign-key checks and retained transcript/trajectory hashes. The reporter timeout was not reproduced on the Linux Testbox.

**The following source-acquisition comparison held both the settlement repair and lint deferral constant. It is historical generation-reuse evidence, not a fresh measurement of this generation-only, full-lint PR.**

| Historical variant | Source acquisitions | Source write MiB | View copies | View logical MiB | Source + view logical MiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Control with settlement + lint deferral | 29 | 1472.268 | 0 | 0.000 | 1472.268 |
| Generation reuse with settlement + lint deferral | 7 | 477.272 | 15 | 1356.502 | 1833.774 |
| Generation reuse with settlement + full lint | 7 | 477.272 | 29 | 2379.292 | 2856.564 |

The first two rows grow by **361.506 MiB (+24.55%)**; Codex accounts for 87.94% of that increase. Complete bases replace selective entry acquisitions, and runtime consumers copy complete bases. Reflink was unavailable (`ENOTSUP`), so independent writable views used ordinary copies. These are observed API/logical payload bytes, not physical disk-write counters. The 2856.564 MiB full-lint row still includes settlement repair and is not a new generation-only hop.

Historical uninstrumented runs used three samples per variant. With settlement and lint deferral held constant, generation reuse changed validating-ledger median 64.056→62.713 s, with overlapping ranges (60.674–105.110 versus 57.210–66.566 s); rehearsal median 24.643→25.628 s also had overlapping ranges. Canary startup median changed 10.696→7.558 s. These data do not establish a generation-only end-to-end speedup. The ledger includes npm staging and is not the exact validator interval.

The unchanged generation implementation previously passed package builds and owner/sibling tests within the combined tree. Historical one-worker costs were 6.35 s wall / about 1.8 s tests for the generation-rehearsal file, and 24.50 s wall / about 1.7 s tests for plugin repair. Those runs and the combined-tree full checks are retained evidence, not new proof for this split. Fresh P1 autoreview of the generation-only composition is scoped-clean with no actionable P0/P1 findings. Exact byte/path checks and `git diff --check` passed; no new generation-only runtime proof is claimed.

The diagnostic probe paired all recorded acquisition/copy spans with successful outcomes and observed no measurement/settlement faults. Each hop lacked 26 other process-exit markers (24 threads and two child processes), so whole-log completeness remains unknown. Published-driver copy timing covered seven project copies; per-plugin `copyIn` attribution and physical disk counters were unavailable. These limits remain part of the draft decision.

Current generation-only head: `5dab15e8425d9ddc6d4b1831eda6a89176502a8c`. **DRAFT / HELD for Peter’s decision. No landing or auto-merge.**

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149882, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156547

## What Problem This Solves

The FreeBSD updater authority repair and Doctor refusal diagnostics need one fresh canonical package built from their reviewed composition. This temporary draft produces that package and its immutable source seal. Close it unmerged after the evidence consumers finish; no release or permanent CI change is intended.

## Source and Scope

Signed product commit `dc432efeb910a26f15156fc2961265c75c79ff2c`, tree `726f72214c70e9a5d5829092ae32d044f5a67150`, has exactly two ordered parents:

1. Primary repair: `aca8f05544e2f77f255fb411b1298974c20f60af`, tree `dd92b4bf50f2aa05d44e289bfd4fbed1f7e0ea5e`.
2. Doctor diagnostics: `5dd54332e20fdb92a8621bd88a338470b0ae2e03`, tree `189df58f47aaa0ef6e5ad315b496857942685144`.

Independent recursive comparison confirmed the disjoint 136 + 3 path union against frozen main `c6b21f6f086a8f3c16bbd37eb143906c9035a09e`, with no additional product change. Both genuine component commits are reachable from the product commit.

Signed workflow carrier `c285c9178800e21ea159f6ffe8a365c685688f38`, tree `e0b219a443da4d65dec9a3434c94ceee5fbe39d0`, has ordered parents `ad8038bfdbe0b33705591f55538053d8ef17ab5e` and the product commit. Its only exceptions to the product tree are the three existing temporary workflows. The native and refreshed workflows retain their historical bytes and cannot qualify the new package without separately reviewed consumer pins.

The producer independently binds the still-open source PR heads (`3c8392a78d30825159149b391d5170568cabb9ad` and `7ed02170fc6a2ee025480311a83a88ada625631a`) to the signed, unpublished correction commits through ancestry. It does not pretend those identities are equal.

## Validation and Package Contract

- The primary final tree passed the affected three files: 42 assertions, no skips; all 130 scoped lint inputs; production, seven selected test graphs, root and script types. Source-before, tests-after and source-after match. Earlier receipts cover 30 files / 2,187 assertions and 136 postbuild assertions on the preceding `a9c552f` tree; they remain historical evidence for unchanged owners, not a full-suite result on the final head.
- The exact Doctor tree passed its two focused files: 16 + 11 assertions, no skips, explicit single-worker invocations, scoped lint and types.
- Both focused remote workloads completed successfully and their leases reached authoritative cleanup completion.
- The composite and producer received independent source, ancestry, package-input and custody review. Targeted formatting plus YAML, shell, Python and Node syntax checks passed.
- This producer performs one fresh frozen install and full canonical package build with Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.4.2. It retains original build/capture exits, complete source and tar inventories, emitted finalizer and package-entry bytes, and the canonical seal using the real numeric GitHub run/attempt.
- The candidate source version remains `2026.9.5`. The authenticated published `2026.9.6` inventory is carried with its 39 required paths; the producer checks their packed bytes against emitted output. Presence is not upgrade success.

The workflow refresh is +48/-26 lines. The added checks bind component ancestry, changed install inputs, carried release inventory and immutable installer bytes. No product source is added by this carrier.

## Historical Evidence

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35844436595 remains historical custody only: fixture generation passed; fresh ARM root refused package-path inspection after Doctor; fresh ARM ordinary recorded `doctor-failed` before outer cancellation. Those originals do not establish current-source native success or guest settlement. Earlier package seals are not substituted for this build.

The historical Codex settlement-fixture cleanup stall observed on baseline `8860655` remains a named follow-up. It was not diagnosed as a current-main regression, repaired, or waived by this composition.

## Remaining Validation

Authenticate the new package and seal, then consume those exact bytes in the reviewed native cells and installed published-9.6 updater checks. The positive first-hop fixture deliberately relabels only candidate package/build metadata and its content inventory to `2026.9.99-first-hop.0`, above the published baseline; it is not a release.

The separate installed-driver refusal lane must retain the new fixed Doctor diagnostic in both the actual update result and its exact saved run, reject before package activation, preserve the prior installation and service identities, and complete owned cleanup. An injected worker signal tests propagation only; a missed worker or different refusal is nonqualifying, with no timing retry.

Each source PR still needs its own publication, exact-head CI/review and native landing. No package build, installed update, native success or source-PR merge is inferred from this draft.

prs.title: test(state): capture ARM heartbeat startup evidence
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149882

## What Problem This Solves

This temporary draft collects missing evidence for an emulated FreeBSD ARM heartbeat startup failure. **Do not merge its instrumentation or workflow.** The producer has succeeded; this update replaces it with one ARM-only consumer of that sealed candidate. The completed validator timing job will not repeat.

## User Impact

No shipping change or root-cause claim. Product B4 `10725d8613c64f5efdc8ea58eae70a3b8f4276ac` remains unchanged. Diagnostic source D `cd488985182fbf0a7a43899ac1b84bc1a1a91054` retains the existing 5,000 ms deadline, SQL, lease authority, refusal behavior and cleanup. Its numeric timestamps perturb timing and are not atomic snapshots. Helper intervals cannot distinguish CPU, I/O or descheduling.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original ARM Doctor reached initial renewal but failed startup at 5,040 ms against the unchanged 5,000 ms deadline. D records private bounded numeric observations at existing boundaries, after original failure revocation and after joined worker termination. There is no configuration switch, preload, import probe, retry or product repair.

The consumer authenticates the exact producer run, attempt, head, job, artifact ID/size/digest, canonical manifest, source archive, package inventory and installed bytes before executing the candidate. Only the published 2026.9.4 tarball crosses from the separately authenticated successful C6 Linux artifact. The failed C6 overall run is not described as successful.

The original published 9.4 install and fixture/bootstrap commands precede candidate replacement. Builtin-only content verification follows installation; ordinary Doctor is the first candidate CLI invocation. No rebuild, native test matrix, x64 rerun, first-hop update or installed foreground-update route runs here. The unchanged absent-service inspector guard remains in place; no global service configuration is changed.

After either Doctor outcome, metadata-only dependency identity, installed content verification and closed numeric observation parsing run. The shell preserves an original nonzero Doctor result across subsequent diagnostic or output failures; successful Doctor still requires all postchecks. Direct shell/VM termination or host cancellation remains incomplete execution. No fs-safe/native addon is imported for inventory. Missing observations mean nonreproduction or inconclusive evidence, never readiness proof. The displayed Doctor tail is limited to 64 KiB; the task log and parser input are not described as bounded by that tail limit. Successful Doctor additionally requires bootstrap survival, plugin loadability and equality of all five original plugin source hashes.

## Evidence

- Original ARM failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35657209609/job/106528852379. Later installed-update proof was unrun.
- Successful D producer: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35671000380/job/106567196453, attempt 1, carrier `0dfed319ce8b1b1bada2a62a66f4f889f4810b56`. Source tree `9356615b6e6525373835bda8381565973cbf8022`. Canonical build 8m09s; full emitted observation checks 13s; 36 passing cases across three files with zero skipped/failed, command 51.830s; unchanged Kysely, transaction-boundary and SDK guards passed. Tests/guards step 1m32s; seal 18s.
- Actual package/build-equal parent modules were fully parsed, including a 54,041,594-byte worker bundle and a 12,388-byte shared chunk. Both retained all nine parent observation marks, clock/CAS and executable output; heartbeat worker retained all 21 marks. Optional debug excerpts totaled 5,427 raw UTF-8 bytes. The earlier `.js`-only selector and debug-retention failures were collector defects; neither earlier run sealed a qualified candidate.
- Artifact `10671740772`, 246,651,995 bytes, digest `sha256:295514afd13da81ce53303752a08cbe1734dd7fb8e74febd7a7909ee3d69e653`; manifest `5e5fbfc5b7cb57c0d0cd9ce1b9e47dfbdfb55731c4ebf59aeae5e79b75ca2b5d`; source archive `e928f6d6663ccc164e5326f6f0bf33fa6342ebcb33ba5fce741568244a041794`. Candidate 81,934,928 bytes / `c6089424435c88d9aba3418d2e987e0350501793095e724bacd8df6a65bfba19`, version 2026.9.5. Producer API/upload/manifest receipts agree; the native consumer also authenticated the downloaded bytes before execution.
- Consumer `eff2a8b0405c875b73d1cad162a7ee151288a02e`, tree `5c614fe1b1973429cf2bb1d2a81e59142f962b4d`, sole parent the successful producer carrier. One exact-predecessor synchronize event on this draft admits ARM execution; no ready transition or repeat validator job.
- Independent custody and observation reviews passed. Fresh scoped autoreview completed with no P0–P2 finding. Actual shell failure-path smoke preserved Doctor 7 through failing tail/helper creation, retained those failures after Doctor 0, and preserved success. Exact five-file hash checks passed intact files and rejected changed or missing files. Closed-schema parser smoke rejected invalid/private fields and accepted valid numeric observations.
- Native ARM consumer [run 35672516333, attempt 1, job 106571916418](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672516333/job/106571916418) failed in ordinary Doctor on FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE-p3 / arm64 / Node 24.21.0, under QEMU aarch64 emulation on an amd64 host. Both strict artifact downloads, canonical manifest/member/source checks, published 9.4 SRI, bootstrap, and installed candidate content admission passed. Doctor was the first candidate CLI invocation.
- Two valid numeric records show startup ordinal 1 with the parent coordinator retained. The timer callback occurred at 5,045.193 ms, failure at 5,048.697 ms, and joined worker termination at 5,134.287 ms (stop code 1). Every worker-body/open/renewal marker remained unobserved through the joined snapshot; open and renewal attempts were zero. Node's online event was observed. This run failed before any observed worker body, so it does not locate the original initial-renewal delay or establish historical B4/C6 cause.
- Doctor stopped at media-persistence; later transcript, profile, plugin and orphan repairs were unrun. Success-only bootstrap survival, plugin loadability and five-file source-hash checks were unrun; ARM Vitest was intentionally unrun. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where deterministic installer, update, logging, system-run, and node-daemon tests inherited host-specific macOS path aliases, BSD utility formatting, buffered stderr timing, or the current operating system. Those fixture assumptions caused canonical recovery validation to fail even though the product behavior under test was unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixtures now canonicalize temporary roots before comparing resolved paths, count retry attempts without BSD `wc` padding, write the stderr boundary synchronously, assert system-run operand roles instead of a host-dependent aggregate count, and establish an explicit Linux platform context for systemd-linger cases. Production behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible product change. Maintainers get deterministic platform-focused tests on macOS and Linux, with stronger system-run approval-binding assertions.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix macOS reproduction: `test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts` failed 4 cases (113 passed), showing `/var` versus `/private/var` path mismatches and padded retry attempts such as `attempt        2`.

prs.title: build(deps): bump @openclaw/fs-safe to 0.21.3
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Filesystem watch rescans are the largest allocation feeder in the Team round-25 heap profile (about 570 MB sampled per 30 seconds). OpenClaw still pins fs-safe 0.21.2, which rescans for unrelated native hints.

## User Impact

Memory and skill watchers receive the published watch fixes and allocation reductions. The dependency bump needs no operator configuration or state migration; plugin loading is unaffected. Existing update/install flows resolve the new exact version.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pin `@openclaw/fs-safe` to exactly 0.21.3 in the root and all 12 consuming workspace packages, and regenerate `pnpm-lock.yaml` with pnpm 12.5.1. Move the existing exact-version cooldown exceptions to the reviewed 0.21.3 package and its seven native helpers, with a documented removal date of 2026-10-07T12:47:42.593Z.

The bump exposed a sandbox FIFO test coupled to fs-safe's private Python function name. Its existing one-second watchdog now guards the actual FIFO open without rewriting dependency internals. An inherited SDK failure is also fixed: main's internal `withUserPathBaseDirectory` helper escaped through a deprecated wildcard facade. Explicit exports preserve the eight existing public home-directory helpers; the measured wildcard ratchet shrinks 47 → 46 without widening export budgets.

A later CI run exposed an existing lifecycle test-readiness race. The failed-announcement cleanup waiter now joins its already-retained lifecycle root before checking native SQLite publication. Entry-only and delivered-state waits, state/payload assertions, fake-time limits, and observation lifetime are unchanged; no production code or new permanent cases are involved.

From the [fs-safe 0.21.3 release](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/releases/tag/v0.21.3):

> **Faster watch rescans:** unrelated native hints skip rescans, and relevant hints reconcile affected directories, reducing scan work and allocation.

The release also fixes spurious overflow for excluded/atomic-save temporary files (openclaw/fs-safe#773), Windows nonrecursive removal error classification (openclaw/fs-safe#771), and copy/staging failure handling (openclaw/fs-safe#763).

## Evidence

Upstream openclaw/fs-safe#774 measured a 502-file memory-watch fixture:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Visits per relevant event pass | 513 | 55 |
| Sampled allocation per relevant event pass | 8.16 MB | 1.33 MB |
| Full scans from unrelated detailed hints at two edits/second | 120/min | 0/min |

Periodic and uncertain-event reconciliation remain full. These are upstream fixture measurements; Team's post-deployment allocation result remains unmeasured.

The npm registry and generated lock agree on `sha512-sBm68f4QiZrrqlZxbOlqVIutrmOK/KLZBrwyPIhV7xXJmlPFc6ZET8AggcU3hMDM3dDSUYgA8LUupxwTB2DZsg==`.

All heavy proof used `blacksmith-testbox`, profile `openclaw-check`. All task-owned leases are confirmed stopped.

### Final merged-candidate proof

Lease `tbx_01m3svhh11xxdv2j6hmtzpe89g` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36763690353)) verified source/manifest/lock SHA-256 hashes before execution:

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passed with fs-safe 0.21.3.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/*watch*.test.ts src/skills/runtime/refresh*.test.ts src/infra/fs-safe*.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/fs-safe-compat.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-mutation-helper.test.ts src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-windows-task.test.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts`: **320 passed, 5 Windows-only skips, 32 files; eight shards in 153.88s**.
- `node scripts/generate-npm-package-lock.mjs --all`: **103 npm package locks generated and validated**. Product npm locks are temporary artifacts, so no npm-format product lock is committed.
- Combined remote command: 3m58.4s including sync, install, tests, and lock validation.

The merge resolves a real conflict with main `7ab9b2158982`: the independently landed [#161990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161990) already fixed the Windows interruption failure. Its updater implementation and documentation are retained byte-for-byte; this PR has no updater-code or docs delta against that main revision. The dependency inputs, FIFO repair, and SDK repair remain byte-for-byte identical to the reviewed versions.

### Earlier validation and CI findings

Lease `tbx_01m3spd11y933mmjmk39jv1yz2` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36752973256)) passed the originally requested consumer suites: 256 tests, 5 platform skips, 64.31s. `node scripts/ci-npm-lock-admission.mjs` returned `skip=false`. Full `check-changed` against the recorded branch base `ad8327f586926caf7a6a3e8c2e361ef162c98f84` passed for dependency commit `10eedda18c8a` in **37m15.5s**, including types, lint, dependency guards, 103 npm locks, and runtime cycles. The initial `--base origin/main` comparison saw unrelated newer-main test reductions as reverse growth; the pinned-base check selected the actual change.

[Initial CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36758377865) exposed four failing shards:

- The obsolete FIFO source replacement reproduced on lease `tbx_01m3ssnhz6peje55wzeqgmhqq4` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36759813212)): 27 passed / one failed before repair; 28 passed after repair. Changed-test cost: `pnpm test src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge-mutation-helper.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took **3.14s wall**.
- The same lease passed the SDK suite with main's new helper present: 11 tests in 13.77s. The canonical report retains **4,594 public exports / 2,698 callables**, with 46 wildcards. Targeted lint and line-cap checks passed.
- Windows SIGINT compensation reproduced independently on lease `tbx_01m3st60kzwgpthr2ctmh38h4e` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36760887713)): 19 passed / one failed. A matching repair passed all 25 existing lifecycle/ownership tests, targeted lint, and core types on lease `tbx_01m3ste2vq5z2qfwgev6ebnce0` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36761401606)); it was then superseded by the canonical main fix above.
- Private completion cancellation did not reproduce in its original 13-file Gateway group on lease `tbx_01m3st63pcp9t1xt9sm7s8tktc` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36760894387)): 44 tests passed in 103.69s, including the unchanged case in 3.513s. This is a non-reproduction, not a fix. Both the replay and observed CI runtime used Node 24.19.0; the workflow's requested 24.21.0 variable did not reflect the runtime. The same error predates this bump and is documented in [#161461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161461); the original competing writer remains unidentified.

Initial lock generation used lease `tbx_01m3snz1p8txjdnadamkx5qnwn`: `pnpm install --lockfile-only --no-frozen-lockfile` passed after carrying the approved exact-version cooldown entries through regeneration. A reused native sync omitted the modified tracked/ignored lockfile; its frozen install stopped before tests. A fresh lease with explicit source hashes resolved the tooling issue.

Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. No new tests were added, assertions or deadlines were not weakened, and no speculative Gateway cancellation fix was made. Native Windows and Team after-deployment performance were not exercised in this Linux lane.

### Lifecycle readiness repair

[CI run 36764646421](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36764646421) passed every other selected lane but failed the corrected-final retry-grace case while waiting for `cleanupHandled=false`. Its file duration was 30.96s. An unchanged original-order replay passed 14/14 on lease `tbx_01m3swp94wvmmtm6wwwb66ndbr` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36766041774)); that was recorded as non-reproduction, not a fix.

Controlled proof on `blacksmith-testbox` lease `tbx_01m3sx0rdcez4tweg61y1rkep9` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36766708971)) then held the real finalization commit after the first failed RPC. The old waiter failed with the exact CI message after 40 fake milliseconds. Releasing that same root published the expected pending state and payload with one RPC. The repaired waiter stayed pending through the same held-write window, then succeeded immediately on release. Temporary controls were removed before validation.

- `CI=1 OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14/14, **32.32s wall**, 30.49s Vitest.
- Requester-wake and announce-loop helper consumers: 28/28, 61.20s wall.
- Scoped typed oxlint: zero warnings/errors, 7.5s; formatting and diff checks passed.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. This establishes the missing settlement join without claiming to reconstruct the original CI scheduling delay. Lease stopped.

### Latest CI follow-up

[CI run 36768437726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36768437726), head `c876d483c5e5`, completed with every selected lane green except `checks-node-changed-compact-large-26` and its aggregate CI gate. The same-owner device sign-in case in `src/gateway/setup-inference.first-signin.integration.test.ts` expects `confirm` but receives the ordinary GitHub device-login `note`. The expansion came from main's [#162020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162020), after this branch's integration; this PR does not change that file.

The failure is independently reproduced with **both dependency versions**:

- Exact CI merge `7f1708f8072e86308be5a696cc3ac9e7a66efa8a` (fs-safe 0.21.3), lease `tbx_01m3syv79dbkyhfj7ga9tkzz09` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36770385792)): original nine-file `gateway-database-workers` group with CI's eight workers, normal sequencer, and Node 24.19.0: **68 passed, one failed, one skipped; 102.89s suite / 142.97s wall**.
- Exact CI main parent `ecb897146e5c47a6cde4e0d5552ce7d70c3700c3` (original fs-safe 0.21.2), separate fresh lease `tbx_01m3sz76yemecmyhvxkhngvbwk` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36771130863)): unchanged expanded test fails the same line 420 assertion, **53.30s suite / 90.47s wall**, using matching Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.5.1.

Temporary diagnostics found that the actual Copilot callback receives `credentialOnly=false` and no domain change, but its SDK-bound `ensureAuthProfileStore` sees zero profiles on the third invocation. The core caller passes one saved token-reference profile and core runtime snapshots already contain the materialized credential. Joining the prepared model owner leaves those facts and the failure unchanged. The missing-settlement hypothesis is therefore unsupported; whether the empty SDK view belongs to native test-module wiring or production auth ownership remains unresolved.

Four scoped diagnostic runs preserved the assertion and failed it in 34.45s, 35.52s, 38.00s, and 42.07s suite time. Temporary source instrumentation was restored byte-for-byte; both detached proof worktrees were removed. No speculative auth repair, weakened assertion, CI rerun, or empty push was made. **The PR remains open with this inherited CI failure; auto-merge is enabled by the maintainer watcher, and no manual merge was attempted.**

<details>
<summary>Sign-in reproduction commands</summary>

Original group on the CI merge:

```sh
env CI=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=8 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts src/gateway/github-publication-requester.test.ts src/gateway/gateway-auth-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/github-publication-requester-aliases.test.ts src/gateway/gateway-route-model-reuse.test.ts src/gateway/setup-inference.first-signin.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/models-list.freshness.integration.test.ts test/plugins/codex-model-catalog.gateway.test.ts src/gateway/gateway-cron-process-identity.windows.test.ts src/gateway/gateway-ssh-upload-signal.test.ts
```

Unchanged main control and each temporary diagnostic:

```sh

```

All runs used normal sync and required artifact preparation through the installed Crabbox CLI; no local suites, builds, or typechecking ran.

</details>

prs.title: perf(sessions): avoid recloning registry maintenance reads
prs.body:
> Superseded by #160510, merged as `c23c65947920b7a53d51d39384f3cd1630e3390c` at 2026-09-28 17:33 UTC. The merged owner removes both whole-store clones and retains full-entry deletion CAS and live commit authority, with additional snapshot-race coverage. This PR's final head passed all CI before the overlap was detected. Closing this duplicate keeps one implementation on main; the branch and its remaining validated fixture/routing repairs are retained for follow-up. No merge or production deployment was performed from this lane.

## What Problem This Solves

Session-registry maintenance deep-copies every session entry on the Gateway thread after its worker read. A deployed allocation sample attributed 770 MB in 30 seconds to that callback. Worker transport already provides owned entries, so the second whole-store copy is unnecessary.

## User Impact

Maintenance allocates less memory while preserving preview isolation, pruning, transcript archival, and live commit guards. No configuration, schema, retention, migration, or update behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume the owned worker result directly and share pruning between preview and apply. This removes both whole-store `structuredClone` calls and 15 lines of application code. The generic worker reader already returned its result directly.

CI investigation also produced bounded tooling/fixture repairs: retain Node's existing GC-test ownership for plugin retention tests; keep FaceTime's port claim until helper shutdown; join parent-fork writers before teardown; coordinate fake clocks with real worker I/O; and wait for UI startup before assertions. The CLI broadcast and concurrent native-client stalls remain unexplained; their fixtures gain failure diagnostics without changing deadlines or assertions.

The change reuses existing fixtures and table-driven coverage without adding production test seams, persistent caches, or configuration options.

## Evidence

The allocation fixture used 150 entries with an 8 KiB saved prompt each, 20 warmed calls per mode through `runSessionRegistryMaintenanceForStore`, a 4 KiB sampling interval, and both collected-object flags. Measurements include main-thread worker receipt and maintenance consumption.

| Mode | Before bytes/read | After bytes/read | Reduction | Extra whole-store clones/read |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Preview | 3,024,146 | 1,680,654 | 44.4% | 1 → 0 |
| Apply, no eligible removals | 2,985,677 | 1,659,785 | 44.4% | 1 → 0 |

Profiled time was 5.06 → 4.01 ms/read for preview and 3.17 → 2.13 ms/read for apply. These used separate leases of the same class after a sync failure; timing is indicative. A same-process 500-entry consumer benchmark measured 2,756,118 → 366,678 bytes/read and 7.09 → 0.22 ms/read. Both preview/apply regression cases failed on the original clone and passed after removal.

All heavy execution used **blacksmith-testbox**, profile **openclaw-check**. No local suites, builds, or typechecks, and no production runtime changes/restarts. All thirteen task-owned leases are stopped. Final head `a376cd0172e561526a0f63693368ba9a510a47b5` passed [CI run 36456785996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36456785996): 127 successful jobs, 21 intentional skips, zero failures or pending jobs.

<details>
<summary>Testbox validation and CI repair evidence</summary>

The requester retry-clock repair follows @vincentkoc's #160407 (`88e3331026a1`); its duplicate branch edit and the config-audit watcher edit were removed once byte-identical to main. The changes reuse existing fixtures and table-driven coverage without adding production test seams, persistent caches, or configuration options. The duplicate UI liveness fixture edit was removed after `d6aa710c5091` landed on main with the same canonical seed and an additional deterministic delayed-describe check; the PR no longer changes that file. The recovery-admission fixture likewise follows main's `9fe93a204e3b`, which observes each failed write and bounds fake timer advancement; our duplicate repair was removed after that overlap became a conflict. Main also supplies the synthetic-build artifact model through #160532 (`4902e4ae49a6`) and the stronger delayed-startup/sidebar-peer probe in `6b9da9dc0287`; their equivalent branch edits were removed. Combining our earlier sidebar hydration wait with main's deliberately held startup would otherwise block that fixture. The same cutover applies to main's owner-keyboard probe (`94cbd1335dfb`). The measured source-reader optimization is now provided by #160517 (`abb37032e7f7`) and the related planner improvements in #160531; its duplicate implementation and regression were removed from this PR. Main's `d9569745764f` also supplies the equivalent heartbeat completion-hook repair; its duplicate was removed after source comparison. Main's `e256cbef8ae0` supplies Send readiness for all companion commands and held-module cleanup (113 integrated E2E cases passed); the narrower branch edit was removed. Main's #160410 (`93a13da9a036`) supplies the complete typed sharing-evidence fixture for avatar rendering; the branch's unproven URL-only hypothesis was removed.

During CI repair, the original Git-prefilter reduction was superseded by main's native multi-term reader. The subsequent matching-only repair below has also landed independently on main, so neither duplicate remains here. Profiling the actual CI merge then found 42,519 files parsed, including 40,398 that matched none of the requested terms; parsing consumed 29.2 seconds. Term-scoped reads now discard unmatched rows before import parsing and leave them uncached for later full-graph discovery. Default full reads are unchanged. In the original three-file group on the same Testbox, the previously timed-out planner case improved **81.228 → 41.455 seconds (49.0%)**; all 114 cases passed. The group's overall wall time was dominated by its unrelated process-report sibling and did not improve (149.47 → 153.67 seconds).

- Baseline `tbx_01m3k5zbb5wshpateke7nf5fs5` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36379821141)): allocation fixture passed; both copy regressions failed as intended.
- Candidate `tbx_01m3k6swh76hv0dvrbqt762nn4` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36380831744)): allocation fixture and maintenance tests passed. Accessor, read-only accessor, entry-reader, registry, restart-recovery, and registry-lifecycle proof passed six files across three shards in 50.06 s. `pnpm test src/config/sessions/session-registry-maintenance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: six cases, 24.052 s wall including cold compilation, 3.925 s test bodies. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed guards, formatting, types, and dead exports, then hit the inherited UI line cap already fixed by #160159 and incorporated into the branch.
- Retention/port diagnosis: `tbx_01m3kbxmsfb540e3pawc4dagwf` and `tbx_01m3kdb5g13f6f624cj2b7nf9g`. The original Bun shard and direct-source probes reproduced retention failures despite full GC, producer-local cleanup, and 32 collections. All nine unchanged cases passed Node. Routing regression failed all three policy rows on old code. Temporary probes were removed.
- First CI repair `tbx_01m3kex9r0z619bp1vkwwpsen5` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36392270990)): `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 179 cases / 4.632 s wall. Original group passed all 532 cases as nine Node + 523 Bun. FaceTime's 18 cases passed 20 standalone runs, and its original 31-file shard passed three times (459 passes, 48 existing skips each). Standalone FaceTime wall: 6.029 s cold, approximately 5.1–5.4 s warm. Matching types/lint passed.
- Second-pass diagnosis `tbx_01m3khbvzjnatywk0jk5h2fnnc` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36396356559)): reproduced heartbeat admission and planner ownership mismatches. Mobile-pairing original shard passed 456 cases plus 20 focused repetitions; no timer attribution was established. Preflight shard passed 544 cases; its import timeout did not reproduce. Recovery-admission timeouts were observed and later investigated below.
- Fixture validation `tbx_01m3kpatnkkmta5arfhm3kzmka` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36405252790)): source hashes verified. Focused custody/handoff/update proof passed 51 cases / 22.23 s. Parent-fork's 16 cases passed 20 times (22.254 s first wall, 14–27 s afterward); its original 56-file shard passed three times (657 passes, five existing skips). Original heartbeat and planner shards passed 95 and 131 cases. Five affected typegraphs and scoped lint passed. Single-file `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: heartbeat 40 cases / 75.236 s, update authority 19 / 10.791 s, planner seven / 141.773 s.
- Actual conflict resolution used base `da51d9edccb3`; range-diff proved the performance and first repair commits unchanged. Upstream heartbeat, active-Node, planner expectation, and custody diagnostic fixes were retained. `tbx_01m3ksahndxsnpybxq7dhppfnw` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36410588130)) passed all 22 maintenance/parent-fork cases. Updated custody assertions rejected a proposed early-return guard, which was removed. `tbx_01m3ksv0qfszs0cxxzh9pxtmd6` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36411466468)) then passed all 24 unchanged custody cases and the upstream heartbeat regression, with source hashes verified.
- Planner/config repair `tbx_01m3ktzh0erpmaar5fwx2nbep1` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36413422577)): original config job's three groups passed before the fixture repair; that replay alone is not claimed as a fix. Profiling isolated Git's candidate prefilter, and the paired query comparison above proved identical candidates. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.test.ts test/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` passed 2,100 cases. prs.title: test(update): accept service advisories in no-op upgrade checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Superseded by #157037, merged as `88d8a4c20e1387f08d59e62e2d26513650973868` while this PR was being validated. That change repaired the same false failure in the published-upgrade survivor's already-current check.

## User Impact

The canonical fix is on main. It accepts an empty step list or the fixture's exact non-mutating service-skip advisory and rejects unexpected maintenance. This duplicate PR should not replace that stricter assertion.

## Why This Change Was Made

An already-current update skips package mutation but may still perform managed-service maintenance or record why service management was skipped. The [existing update contract](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/update/how-updates-run#validation-and-activation) already permits policy refresh when core is current, including with `--no-restart`. The reconciliation recorders use zero duration and exit code zero for diagnostic steps; their displayed command is not an execution receipt.

The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched by its candidate. The landed correction changes only the survivor interpretation, retaining shipped driver output and handoff markers. No new configuration or runtime behavior is needed.

## Evidence

- The landed fix's [published-driver qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35967271417) passed on candidate `b986e458`: published 2026.9.4 updated to the candidate, preserved operator state and cron ownership, passed Gateway health, the strict no-op assertion and clean Doctor check, and restored the original backup under the original runtime. The lane took **621 seconds**. This is reused evidence from the landed owner, not this PR's Testbox run.
- This PR's before/after assertion probes passed **9 cases in 359 ms**. The proposed broader assertion is superseded by the exact fixture contract now on main.
- On Blacksmith Testbox (`blacksmith-testbox`, profile `openclaw-check`), lease `tbx_01m39750nfd48rpqd4w30bjq36`, the scoped changed-file gate and probes passed in **119.5 seconds**. Independent review was scoped-clean through P2. The lease is stopped.
- This lane's full survivor attempt never reached the scenario: candidate package compilation stalled in `tsdown-packages`; the memory-bounded retry hit its **900-second** build deadline. It is not a green cell and is not being relabeled as one.
- This PR's [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35976994719) passed all **40 selected jobs**, with no failures. Required security checks also passed.

prs.title: fix(scripts): review-init fails under Octopool string rewrite protection when GH_REPO is unset
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `scripts/pr review-init <PR>` and `scripts/pr merge-run <PR>` fail with `GitHub API failure while reading PR #<PR>: gh pr view exited with status 1 after 3 attempts.` / `error: string rewrite protection blocked unsafe input` when `gh` is the Octopool shim (0.7.0) and no host-qualified `GH_REPO` is exported.

## User Impact

User impact: maintainers can run the native `scripts/pr` review and merge flow from an ordinary openclaw checkout without exporting `GH_REPO`, on any Octopool version. A host-qualified `GH_REPO` (`https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw` or `github.com/openclaw/openclaw`) is still honored first and is now documented in `scripts/AGENTS.md`. No product or CLI change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repository discovery ran `gh browse` with a child-only `GH_BROWSER` launcher that prints the URL instead of opening a browser. Octopool 0.7.0 refuses that singleton command under string rewrite protection, so every metadata read died before the wrapper reached its authoritative REST checks. Octopool 0.7.1 accepts the command again, but the wrapper should not depend on the shim's allowlist for something Git already knows.

Discovery now resolves in this order: a host-qualified `--repo`/`GH_REPO` selection (unchanged); otherwise, with no selection at all, the checkout's `origin` remote read through the wrapper's selected Git (`https`, `ssh://`, and scp-like forms normalized, SSH ports dropped, `GH_HOST` mismatch ignored); only when neither resolves does it fall back to the existing `gh browse` launcher. Unqualified `owner/name` selections still go through `gh browse` because only `gh` owns the configured default-host mapping. The subsequent REST read of the repository remains the authority check exactly as before, so no trust decision moves to the remote URL text.

Trust-anchor note (scripts/AGENTS.md wrapper rules): `scripts/pr-lib/github.mjs` is part of the `scripts/pr` wrapper closure and the `OPENCLAW_PR_GITHUB_SNAPSHOT_ROOT` byte-identical snapshot set. This branch is therefore a wrapper-editing branch: classified `landing` subcommands run only under the canonical/origin-main wrapper, and a worktree carrying this diff loudly substitutes the canonical wrapper until the change lands. No wrapper-component inventory, materialized dependency set, or `.sh` wrapper file changed. Landing must use the canonical wrapper (`GH_REPO=https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw` avoids the pre-fix browse path on Octopool 0.7.0).

## Evidence

- Reproduced against the exact Octopool 0.7.0 binary (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/octopool/0.7.0/bin/octopool` symlinked as `gh`): `node scripts/pr-lib/github.mjs read pr view 155085 --json number,state` fails with `string rewrite protection blocked unsafe input` without `GH_REPO` and succeeds with `GH_REPO=https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw`; the sourced wrapper path (`pr_meta_json 155085 false`) reproduces the reported `GitHub API failure while reading PR` message. After the fix both invocations print `{"number":155085,"state":"MERGED"}` on 0.7.0.
- New `test/scripts/pr-repository-locator.test.ts` (20 cases through the real `github.mjs` CLI with a traced fake `gh`, isolated temp git repos, poisoned PATH Git): https / scp-like / `ssh://` with port / https with port / `GH_HOST` case-insensitive match resolve from `origin` with no `browse` call; host-qualified `GH_REPO` and `--repo` win over a different remote without consulting Git; no remote, non-git cwd, `file://`, local path, `git://`, `GH_HOST` mismatch, and unqualified selections fall back to exactly one `browse` call; `OPENCLAW_PR_GIT`/`GIT_EXEC` are resolved against the child cwd. Nine of these cases fail on the pre-fix file (browse supplied the wrong repository).
- `test/scripts/pr-metadata.test.ts` fixture now runs from a temp git repo with a configurable `originRemote` (default matches the fake), so the real checkout's remote cannot leak into the suite; the protected-writer default-repository case now covers both origin discovery (0 browse calls) and missing-origin fallback (2 browse calls).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/pr-repository-locator.test.ts` 20 passed; `test/scripts/pr-metadata.test.ts` 113 passed; `pr-wrapper-source-closure`, `eager-import-closure`, `plain-gh` 57 passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` exit 0 (testRoot, docs, tooling lanes); `git diff --check` clean.
- Isolated Codex autoreview (P1 threshold): scoped-clean.

Actual base `cadafc0084e25aa63a91506d4378d1f6db7ea7d2` is an ancestor of the candidate; measured runtime head `cb7ddbfbdfc41c09f300e912ef6d093a2c747bd5`, final candidate `835a079995c09976ca96641a42644e2e91d8ca76` (parent cb7ddbf). All 118 base production blobs exactly match qualified d920/e897/891. The two fresh native AST records match exact base/head Memory source hashes and have zero syntax diagnostics. Scope-manifest.json binds every file to Git blob ID, SHA256, family and LOC.

C/E/U/N = eligible candidate / named allowed exception / unresolved / native. Only Memory add-on toggles and engine selection receive proposed C→N credit; all read classifications remain unchanged. **33 candidates remain on this proposed head.** Neither this candidate nor other pending PRs receives merged credit. Items 1, 2, 5–10 count eligible sites rather than raw APIs; named owner/primitive exceptions remain.

| Touched category | Files | Base LOC | Candidate LOC | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| production | 1 | 663 | 697 | +34 |
| testsSupport | 2 | 917 | 1,064 | +147 |

The owner admits and settles each write before its generator action presents a scoped expected value and co-written saving flag. Per-operation retirement releases stale presentation while preserving authoritative write settlement. Expected rejection and committed-write refresh warnings retain their distinct existing visible outcomes; accepted catalog receipts reconcile server state without duplicate requests or artificial affects/refresh calls. Engine-off and curated edits remain synchronous shared autosave-owner draft operations.

Source proof includes the actual ConfigPage beneath RouterOutlet: a held add-on write, usable destination and disconnected old host before completion, and no destination error after late rejection. The census auditor did not execute tests, builds or installs; owner proof results must be reported separately.


## What Problem This Solves

Memory engine and add-on writes started their authoritative work inside a Solid action and manually reset saving afterward. Admit each write through the existing configuration owner first, then present it with connection-scoped optimistic value and saving cells. Connection replacement, admin revocation, read-only catalogs, and page departure retire presentation while the owner finishes the write and reloads the catalog.

A review also exposed a stale-outcome bug: access could return before a retired RPC finished, allowing a replacement action to queue; the old failure then appeared after the replacement succeeded. Error and refresh-warning publication now checks the existing captured retirement promise. This adds no generation counter or parallel state, and preserves committed runtime notices and authoritative settlement.

The accepted catalog receipt already invalidates and reconciles the async memo, so no duplicate RPC or broad affects/refresh call is needed. Separate browser event turns retain independent optimistic completion. Programmatic double-dispatch in one task retains Solid's combined transaction semantics.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression before fix | Both admin-scope and read-only-catalog cases fail on the parent because a retired failure remains rendered after the replacement succeeds. |
| Affected unit file | All 27 Memory mutation tests pass on pinned Bun, one worker, including real RouterOutlet/ConfigPage departure before held RPC release and late-rejection isolation. The two affected retirement cases also pass after replacing a synchronous flush await. |
| UI typecheck | Passed. |
| Scoped typed lint / format / whitespace | Passed with the root UI TypeScript configuration. |
| Production Knip | Passed. |
| Independent P0–P2 review | Fresh current-base source review and independent test-only review found no actionable findings; captured source verified. |
| Gateway retry CI repair | Both 100% and 140% text scale cases pass (2/2). UI tsrs, scoped typed lint, formatter, whitespace, and final production Knip pass. |
| Same-host production build / strict bytes | Exact-base and candidate builds passed; paired strict check has no violations. |
| Visual proof | Three inspected synthetic 1440×1200 states, embedded below: settled, both operations pending, engine complete while add-on stays pending. Existing before/after pairs match byte-for-byte; the new outcome guards do not alter these states. |

Production `memory-page.tsx`: 663 → 697 LOC (+34). Tests/support: 917 → 1,064 (+147): Memory mutation test 759 → 913 and Gateway retry E2E 158 → 151. The incremental review repair adds four production lines and 54 test lines; the complete three-file diff is +227/−46, including the test-only theme snapshot repair. All items 1, 2, 5–10 retain zero eligible sites. The two command groups become native; lower-level owner contracts and named exceptions remain unchanged.

No route, host tag, CSS class, dependency, or configuration contract changes. Simplification uses the already-owned retirement promise, preserves the existing write queue, and removes manual saving cleanup rather than introducing a new owner.

## Paired gzip budget

| Surface | Exact cadafc0 base | Head cb7ddbf | Delta |

| Startup JS | 325,506 B | 325,544 B | +38 B |
| Chat JS | 1,442,004 B | 1,442,058 B | +54 B |
| New Session JS | 1,019,753 B | 1,019,804 B | +51 B |
| Startup CSS | 40,912 B | 40,912 B | 0 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | 0 |

Startup remains over the 325,000 B campaign cap; +38 B is within the standing 64 B allowance. Both sides use identical metadata and the same frozen seven-plugin private-QA inventory, with all 29 generated inputs verified. This is an explicit fixture, not a clean default inventory. The strict paired check reports no violations. Independent qualification passed for both 7,027-file archives, all 3,267 tracked inputs, the 29 preserved generated inputs, runtime maps, toolchain sources and identical metadata. All 21 locale groups pass (maximum delta +3 B). Both sides used Node 24.22.0 and pnpm 12.12.1. The final candidate adds only the Gateway retry E2E repair; it is excluded from both build-input manifests. All 3,274 consumed tracked-input hashes were reverified against the new head, so these measurements retain their actual cb7/cada runtime labels without a duplicate build. Previous-head measurements remain historical.

## CI

Full run [39711963930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39711963930) completed on cb7ddbf. Its sole non-aggregate failed case was `Gateway retry feedback > keeps automatic recovery stable at 100 percent text scale`, comparing two colors at line 132 after dark-to-light emulation. The original case passed on the qualified exact cadafc0 base, so this failure receives no inherited waiver.

The test read spinner and label colors in separate browser calls; a theme change could land between them. Both checkpoints now compare one synchronous browser snapshot. The equality assertions, timeouts, and dark/light coverage remain unchanged; no retry was added. Both text-scale cases pass locally on the repaired head, with UI tsrs, scoped lint/format, production Knip, and a clean isolated review. New-head `ci:full` supplies landing evidence. prs.title: fix(codex): release exact closed thread handoffs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
A Codex thread handoff waits for the retired app-server process to exit. Unrelated sibling leases can keep that process alive after the exact target thread has closed, blocking scheduled or interactive continuation indefinitely.

## User Impact
A successor can continue once the old physical client reports the exact target thread closed, while unrelated sibling sessions keep using that process. Ownership loss without a closure signal still preserves process-exit writer fencing.

## What Changed
- record bounded, physical-client-scoped exact `thread/closed` receipts across same-build module copies
- race retired process exit against the exact target closure and clean listeners on every path
- clear stale receipts only after successful new thread retention
- cover closure before and after listener registration plus the no-closure negative control

## Validation
- [x] focused Codex lifecycle/runtime tests: 33 passed
- [x] extension production and test typechecks
- [x] touched-file typed lint and format
- [x] independent P0-P2 review: no findings

This extracts the exact-thread handoff repair from #174967 while leaving its busy-message behavior decision and security-sensitive changes out. #178764 already covers scheduled session admission; #177351 is Goal/autonomy scope and is intentionally not included.

Limits: synthetic in-process app-server transport; no live Codex binary integration. Exact-head PR CI supplies broad proof.

prs.title: fix(github): open reconnect flow from active sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's managed GitHub OAuth credential expires, `github_identity_status` can diagnose the state but cannot get the operator into the masked reconnect flow from the active session. Long-running release work must stop and wait for the operator to find the agent's Tools settings manually.

## Why This Change

- Adds a capability-negotiated `screen` action, `github_identity_settings`, that routes only the requesting Control UI to the current agent's Tools panel.
- Keeps the OAuth flow entirely inside the existing masked Control UI; no token, code, or callback data enters model context.
- Makes `github_identity_status` direct the model to open that flow and re-check identity health afterward.
- Requires an action-specific client capability in both tool construction and Gateway routing, so older or cross-origin Control UIs fail closed instead of silently ignoring the command.

## User Impact

An active release session can diagnose an expired GitHub identity, open the correct reconnect surface for the requesting operator, and verify recovery without losing the session or exposing credentials.

## Evidence

- 91 targeted tests across Gateway routing, screen/status tools, tool registration, Control UI capability negotiation, and UI navigation.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`
- `pnpm protocol:check`
- Focused `oxlint`
- `pnpm format`
- `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`
- Two independent reviews; the only initial P1 (mixed-version clients silently ignoring the action) was fixed and the re-review found no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings.

## Limits

This opens the existing operator-owned reconnect flow; it does not move OAuth handling into the model or auto-authorize GitHub access.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): split cached chat mount after connect dispatch
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reloading a full-UUID chat deep link waited for `sessions.resolve` before mounting an already cached transcript, leaving a serial blank/skeleton interval. The pane can now mount from an exact, scoped snapshot after the initial connect request is sent. Cached rows hydrate in a separate task after hello; `sessions.resolve` remains authoritative and replaces deleted, moved, or mismatched routes.

The snapshot path requires a full UUID, matching agent, matching account/host snapshot key, and the same connection revision after its asynchronous read. Roster matches keep their existing precedence. Parsed prewarm data stays with the snapshot-store owner and is shared with hydration.

## Write hold scope

Only composer sends and restored queued sends/outboxes wait for route confirmation. Admission already requires an exact full-UUID and agent match on the account/host-scoped snapshot, so a stale mapping means the session was recently deleted or moved. Other mutations retain server-side authorization and target resolution by session key, ID, or view ticket, and fail safely without writing to another session. Task suggestion, question, and board-action affordances come from live data. User-composed messages are the harmful stale-target case, so delivery is held until confirmation. A different confirmed outbox remains independent.

This scope is an explicit maintainer decision. The previous per-call-site holds across goals, history actions, boards, discussion, headers, reactions, menus, sharing, settings, and run lifecycle are removed. No generic mutation gate or new targeting registry is introduced.

Reconnect verification stays at the route loader and is loaded through the existing async boundary. Moving its route-specific parsing out of eager startup code also removes this PR’s startup gzip growth without raising a ceiling.

## Accepted tradeoff

The previously accepted comparison showed hello +14.5 ms paired (11/11 slower), against transcript paint −252 ms, final rows −205 ms, and LoAF blocking −93 ms. The earlier tuned experiment showed hello +13 ms versus transcript −240 ms, final rows −197 ms, and LoAF −29 ms. The hello shift was accepted because it did not cascade into the outcome metrics.

L156/#177153 was reverted in #177760 after an early mount delayed hello and subsequent RPCs. The split schedule preserves the corrected handshake timing and yields cached-row hydration after hello. **Live revert rule: revert if live hello or final rows materially regress after deployment.** This PR does not deploy the service.

## Evidence

Campaign evidence for a signed-in reload of a dashboard deep link recorded 14 visible states and sidebar settlement around 15 seconds. This change targets the cached-chat route-resolution dependency.

The accepted performance comparison is retained below. A subsequent canonical-global reopen repair is described after the tables; it does not execute for these explicit UUID routes.

Same repo Chromium, Team-scale fixture and probes across all variants. Eleven interleaved triplets: baseline / original split / final tuned split. Connect is withheld until 340 ms and then takes 220 ms; resolve/describe take 195 ms. The primary gate is at least 100 ms better transcript paint and at least 9/11 faster pairs; hello follows the explicitly accepted tradeoff. Other secondaries use the campaign IQR/paired regression rule; FCP may rise at most 50 ms.

The final transcript-paint gate passes in 11/11 pairs (paired median −252 ms). Final rows improve 11/11 (−158.9 ms paired), LoAF 10/11 (−38 ms paired), and FCP is flat. Hello-handled shifts +15.6 ms paired (10/11), while response dispatch is flat (−0.2 ms paired); no downstream cascade appears. The warm-roster control has overlapping IQRs and no regression. The off-roster request census is 50 → 51 RPCs: one additional session-scoped `cron.list`; other method counts match.

The first mount task is 78 ms median, ending at 415–422 ms. Final cached-row hydration runs in a separate 151 ms median task, starting 615–628 ms, after hello-handled in all 11 runs. Original split folds that work into the hello task; its LoAF result is worse than the tuned split.

## Prior split-mount validation

Head `974978ffcd7b51361e2cbf940984b57d484f141e`:

- Autoreview clean through P2 for the scoped-send candidate; all patches remained identical through rebase.
- Packaged runtime/plugin build, core/UI/script typechecks, formatting, controller/i18n checks, and touched-file lint pass.
- Focused unit/browser tests: **164/164 pass** across 11 files. Focused native E2E: **33/33 pass**, including warm navigation, deleted/moved/mismatched routes, held composer and restored outboxes, unrelated confirmed outboxes, and reconnect during admission.
- Full UI E2E: **848 passed / 2 failed / 4 skipped files (854)**; **3679 passed / 2 failed / 4 skipped tests**; **5544.11 s**. Both failures have baseline/main evidence below. The changed snapshot-route file passes all 13 cases in the full run, and real-Gateway reconnect continuity passes.

All remote proof used AWS lease `cbx_b98c9da9a02b`, fixed `c7a.4xlarge`. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`. Focused unit tests also prove the new admission/send behavior fails on the old production path.

| Full UI: QA-lab automation management | `Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal.` Same case/error reproduced with the baseline runtime projection (32 s including build); its owner and the entire extensions/src/test/config trees are unchanged. |
| Full UI: header/subagents | Same case and line 122 hidden `.chat-details-session` assertion as [scheduled-main run 39693906280 / job 119546724037](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39693906280/job/119546724037); timeout budgets differ (10 s remote, 30 s CI). |
| Changed checks: max-lines suppressions | Same three unchanged files fail in the baseline projection (5 s): chat-message tests, config-page state, sessions-page state. |
| Changed checks: core graph boundary | Same baseline gateway-root 726 / infra 749 roots exceed 720 (1 s); the entire src/test/config trees are identical. |
| Changed checks: unused exports | Same seven symbol findings reproduce in baseline (100 s); owner/policy files and symbol-reference inventories are identical. Production unused-export scan passes. |

The baseline classification runs retained the candidate UI test files while restoring all changed runtime route/pane/send owners. Source hashes, tree identities and symbol-reference comparisons verify the unchanged inputs to those global guards. They are baseline-runtime projections, not a claim that the whole checkout was main.

The subsequent canonical-global CI failure is resolved by the owner repair below; it is not classified as inherited from a passing replay.

## Canonical global reopen repair

Final head: `5ee2d37fa4293184e0ace4695f9304125fe6be27`; current base: `cadafc0084e25aa63a91506d4378d1f6db7ea7d2`.

[CI run 39696722804, job 119556453178](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39696722804/job/119556453178) exposed a real ordering defect: an implicit canonical-global reopen selected the default agent before the roster arrived, then retained that default because it was valid. A saved selection could consequently reopen `/chat/dummy` instead of `/chat/openclaw`. The resolver now chooses defaults and validates the saved selection after the roster read and existing connection checks. This removes ten runtime lines; explicit agent precedence, removed-agent fallback, and reconnect fences remain intact.

The new deterministic regression fails with the old owner (`/chat/dummy`) and passes after repair (`/chat/openclaw`). The pre-repair head reproduced the identical native-E2E failure in a diagnostic pilot (1/3 head attempts; base 0/3). That small pilot is not a rate comparison. The completed final-head comparison used thirty alternating-order pairs on one AWS `c7a.4xlarge`, pinned to two CPUs with native E2E `--maxWorkers=2` and the same `chat-boot-render-storm` companion. Each invocation used fresh browser state and a separate module cache. Tracked source was verified against the selected revision before each trial.

| Revision | Valid target attempts | Target failures | Setup failures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Final `5ee2d37fa429` | 30 | 0 | 0 |
| Base `cadafc0084e2` | 30 | 0 | 0 |

These counts do not establish that the original failure was inherited or quantify an amplification by the split mount. The matching native failure and red/green deterministic regression establish the repaired ordering defect. No timeouts, retries, weakened assertions, or test-only production hooks were added.

Final focused units: **179/179 pass across 12 files**, including the new saved-agent regression and existing warm-route, connection replacement, snapshot admission, composer, and outbox boundaries. `corepack pnpm test ui/src/app/bootstrap.agent-selection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took **10.895 s** (12 passing tests; new cold module cache).

Final same-toolchain bundle comparison on the updated base: startup gzip **325,800 → 325,703 B (−97 B)**. The base-aware budget check reports no violations or warnings; no ceiling is raised. The unchanged absolute 325,657 B limit remains exceeded by both builds (base +143 B, final +46 B). Chat boot is 1,443,181 → 1,443,906 B, below its unchanged 1,500,000 B ceiling. This replaces the original +170 B startup growth.

Final proof: AWS lease `cbx_28bd62bf493a`, [run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_aa4758e57314428a68b96d939b2138ef). Full UI and changed-file validation are in progress. Exact-head [CI run 39710543926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39710543926) is green, including selected UI E2E shards; the transient dependency-review status completed successfully without a rerun. Full-diff and final-commit autoreview are clean through P2, the latter with the resolver, caller, identity helpers, and test setup supplied as source context.

Per the follow-up instruction, no new 11-triplet performance comparison is required: the explicit full-UUID route returns before the changed implicit-landing block. The accepted performance table above remains tied to its original measured head. The message-delivery hold and UUID admission are unchanged by this repair.

## Code size and ownership

Application runtime: **+158 LOC** (239 additions / 81 deletions), reduced from +272. The requested production filter (`git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- ':!*.test.ts' ':!*test-support*' ':!docs/*'`) is **+172 LOC** (272 / 100), 25 files; that filter also includes bench/test helpers. Necessary growth implements scoped UUID admission, authoritative replacement, split hydration, and message-delivery hold/resume. It removes the obsolete per-action policy and shares the snapshot parse between admission and hydration.

Files are confined to the chat route/snapshot/send/pane owners, app route verification, and the existing bench/fixture/probe owners plus their regression tests. No server schema, durable record, configuration option, or permission model changes.

## Synthetic before / after

The attached 400/800/1100/1500 ms filmstrips use only the synthetic Team-scale fixture. Screenshot capture is illustrative; the untraced measurements above are the performance evidence. No private captures are uploaded.

Refreshing the Agent roster or workspace file inventory copied loading and error presentation beside the synchronous capability. Native async memos now consume the admitted completion beneath `Loading` and `Errored`; `isPending` drives the controls, and `latest` distinguishes an initial unresolved receipt from a retired read. Only the notice is keyed, so the picker, editor, Refresh controls and drafts retain their DOM identity.

A failed forced inventory refresh previously triggered a content reread whose success erased the inventory error. Content refresh now follows only successful inventory results. The failed receipt stays visible beside the cached editor, including first-load failure, until explicit retry or owner retirement. The capability retains synchronous admission, access, cache and retirement authority. Its legacy loading getters derive from the active request, and existing nonthrowing public results remain available to other consumers. The separate file-request map and unused inventory-error copy are removed.

The unchanged default-agent and identity commands now live in `lib/agents/mutations.ts`, imported directly by their two lazy Agents callers. prs.title: fix(gateway): reuse committed Copilot sign-ins on setup retries
prs.body:
This draft is superseded by the equivalent canonical fix already on main: [332e4d3ec02d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/332e4d3ec02df53b18003155fe44a0a102b383e1). It landed during this lane's validation. The comparison confirms the same host-authorized selection and direct SecretRef resolution; the production differences are a private null/undefined sentinel, predicate order, and local destructuring. Closing the duplicate preserves one repair owner. The independent reproduction and stress evidence below belongs to this candidate; fresh confirmation of the landed main revision is complete: **20/20 consecutive Gateway passes and 56/56 provider tests**; details follow.

## Canonical main confirmation

Fresh `blacksmith-testbox` lease `tbx_01m3t4afnsd8av3k6gpg4d93w3` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36781180040)) verified clean main **`0eade92d5a610fc0d1653136cf166632e741e83e`**, including canonical fix **`332e4d3ec02df53b18003155fe44a0a102b383e1`**. The lease is stopped (`completed`).

- `CI=1 pnpm test extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **56/56 passed**, 38.49s Vitest / 40.36s wrapper wall.
- `CI=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/setup-inference.first-signin.integration.test.ts --pool forks`: **20/20 consecutive passes**. Case median **18.948s**, range **15.234–35.878s**. Per-run case seconds: 35.878, 19.447, 19.173, 19.873, 20.234, 18.284, 17.314, 17.278, 19.194, 19.714, 21.469, 18.963, 21.799, 18.934, 18.200, 17.933, 17.252, 15.234, 15.724, 16.874.

The canonical implementation and its regression tests are already on main. This PR's alternative implementation and test-support extraction were not merged. The candidate's three original-group replays below remain candidate evidence; they are not relabeled as executions of the newer main revision. The historical 90-second startup-timeout attribution gap remains.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes GitHub Copilot setup retries starting a fresh device login after setup has already saved a usable sign-in. The provider also ignored the profile selected by `models auth login --profile-id`.

Related: #161496, #161655, #162038. The expanded WebSocket coverage in #162020 exposed the credential disagreement.

## User Impact

Interactive reuse stays bound to the profile supplied by the host. Empty or absent candidates start a fresh login. Existing tenant-switch behavior, credential-only connection flows, protected SecretRefs, and noninteractive onboarding retain their contracts. No configuration, migration, dependency, or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider auth contract already makes `existingProfiles` the authoritative reconnect view. Copilot instead reopened the SDK auth store to choose a profile, then reopened it again to resolve the token. Remove those interactive rereads and resolve the selected credential directly.

The integration fixture made the disagreement deterministic: its Vitest core graph published the fresh shared-store owner as `state-db`, with one committed profile, while the native SDK graph retained `legacy-main`, with zero profiles. Waiting for core publication cannot reconcile that second module's cache. Using the host's prepared view fixes the existing provider contract violation without changing the Gateway fixture, its assertions, timeout, or mocks. The separate noninteractive store reader remains required by unattended onboarding's documented stored-token fallback.

## Evidence

Candidate manual heavy validation used `blacksmith-testbox`, profile `openclaw-check`, lease `tbx_01m3szx3hq2dgw2mep4szt5rwc` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36772552478)). The baseline was current main `3bc0356e6a6af17ba6a993435629900f50f21f36`; source hashes were checked after sync. The lease is confirmed stopped (`completed`).

- Baseline: `CI=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/setup-inference.first-signin.integration.test.ts --pool forks`, ten consecutive invocations: **10/10 failed**, all at `expected 'note' to be 'confirm'`. Case times: 50.517, 22.687, 23.759, 22.340, 18.214, 20.817, 18.742, 17.805, 16.874, 17.921 seconds; median **19.780s**.
- A temporary diagnostic confirmed distinct core/SDK reader identities, `state-db`/one profile versus `legacy-main`/zero profiles. Instrumentation was removed, and the integration file is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Registered-provider regressions on old production code: **4 failed / 53 passed**. They prove selected inline/reference credentials win over another stored profile, and empty/absent host candidates cannot borrow it.
- `CI=1 pnpm test extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **57/57 passed** after the fixture extraction, **33s command wall / 30.71s Vitest**. Vitest attributes 15% of that duration to test execution; transforms/imports dominate. The registered provider boundary protects account selection, SecretRef preservation, and tenant handling. The added cases use the existing fake-time device-flow fixture.
- Same integration command at the fix: **20/20 consecutive passes** with unchanged 90-second timeout. Case median **19.160s**, range **16.263–30.253s**. Every run completed replacement, first inference, and revoked-retry no-effects assertions. This establishes correctness; warmed before/after times do not establish a startup performance improvement.
- Original `agentic-gateway-server-isolated-hosted-1` group, decoded from job `110068947997` in run `36768437726`, replayed through `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with its original 16 files/two configs, `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_GROUPS_GZIP_BASE64`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=8`, and plan concurrency 1: **3/3 passed**, **97 passed / one Windows-only skip each**. Wall times **279s / 302s / 291s**; sign-in case times **37.810s / 28.544s / 39.154s**. Node **24.19.0**, pnpm **12.5.1**.
- `CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 3bc0356e6a6af17ba6a993435629900f50f21f36`: **passed in 460s**, including extension/test types, typed lint, formatting, dead-export scans, plugin guards, and ratchets. The first attempt correctly rejected growth in the existing oversized `index.test.ts`; its existing fake-clock, device-fetch and TTY helpers were extracted unchanged into `device-auth.test-support.ts`, preserving every case and leaving the Gateway integration unchanged. Extension typechecking then required an explicit `return undefined` for the selector's existing fallthrough result; that behavior-neutral correction is included. No ratchet exception was added.
- Final confirmation after the behavior-neutral explicit return: `CI=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts src/gateway/setup-inference.first-signin.integration.test.ts --pool forks --maxWorkers=1`: **58/58 passed across both files**, **96.43s wrapper wall**, including native runtime artifact preparation.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the final diff, including the helper extraction: **scoped-clean through P2**.

The first lease command could not load Vitest because dependencies were absent; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` repaired that prerequisite before baseline execution. Those prerequisite exits are excluded from the ten test results.

Historical 90-second failures are a separate attribution gap: the two earlier timeout runs spent 54.856s and 61.753s reaching Gateway connection, then reached the mocked probe at 87.776s and 88.928s. Neither showed a settlement deadlock. The current baseline reproduced the credential assertion instead; this PR does not claim to repair an independently identified startup stall, and does not extend deadlines or add retries. No live provider credentials or deployment were used.
