## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app embeds Peekaboo 4.6.0 and misses the automation reliability fixes in the 4.7.0 tag.

## User Impact

The next OpenClaw macOS app build includes background window-geometry sequencing fixes across move, resize, set-bounds, and maximize; positional-click value-policy and AXPress click-receipt fixes; batched exact-field Accessibility metadata reads; generation-pinned hotkey targets; Bridge deadlines preserved across transport queueing; and refusal of conflicting explicit Bridge sockets.

No OpenClaw configuration changes are required. The Bridge protocol version remains 1.38 and the client-signing policy is unchanged. Upstream adds an optional inline-pixels capability and observation metadata, so this is not a claim that every Bridge payload is byte-identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pin the embedded PeekabooBridge and PeekabooAutomationKit products to 4.7.0 and regenerate the SwiftPM lockfile. Only the Peekaboo pin changes; AXorcist remains 0.1.11. The upstream Swift Collections pin fixes the standalone CLI's 4.6.0 startup failure and does not change these embedded products.

Upstream: [Peekaboo 4.7.0 release](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/releases/tag/v4.7.0), [tagged source](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo/tree/v4.7.0). The remote tag was verified; GitHub still reported the release entry as a draft during validation, so publication is not claimed here. Related: #158022, the preceding embedded dependency update to 4.6.0.

## Evidence

- `swift package resolve` passed in 224.77 seconds. Peekaboo resolved to `f3c6b1b32528290a959244d1ac12d54af3d42928`; a full pin comparison confirmed every other pin is unchanged. SwiftPM regenerated `originHash`.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw --jobs 4` passed in 314.95 seconds (Swift 6.4, Xcode 27.2). The first attempt stopped after 57.81 seconds because the fresh worktree lacked generated Mermaid resources; the normal CI prerequisite (`node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs`, after its filtered frozen-lockfile install) fixed the environment before the successful build.
- Independent Codex autoreview completed with `scoped-clean`, exit 0, no accepted/actionable findings at the default P0 threshold. The first invocation failed before producing a review; selecting the installed Codex binary explicitly allowed the requested review to complete with isolation preserved.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and `git diff --check` passed.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` found an inherited `file_length` violation in `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardManager.swift:1666`: 1,534 counted lines exceed 1,500. That source and `config/swiftlint.yml` are byte-identical to `origin/main` at `2e1d5069633326a9a405a1bf3e0fa0ed35987fc8`. No unrelated source was changed.
- [Exact-head CI run 36678791268](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36678791268) is attached to `eaac4d8c5c498c45941ad62c90857905b0255b91` and was still in progress at handoff. A subsequent [security review status](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36678791276) reports success (no sensitive product changes); the combined CI gate remains pending. CI is not claimed green.

prs.title: refactor(automation): retire heartbeat into cron and session execution
prs.body:
Related: #134994 — [retire heartbeat into ordinary automations and session execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/134994).

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

This branch is in the main repository and remains editable by maintainers. This is a draft: the explicit remaining decisions and proof gaps below are not waived by publication. No merge or release is requested.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where operators managing monitoring through Automations still encounter a separate heartbeat executor, configuration and reconciliation path, while System busyness shows bare heartbeat events rather than identifiable work and outcomes. Background process, task, hook and restart notices also depend on that special path, even when periodic monitoring is disabled.

The split ownership makes automation edits/deletion unreliable and couples immediate session work to a scheduler that should not own it. This change retires the execution subsystem rather than renaming or hiding its events.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scheduled monitoring becomes ordinary editable `agentTurn` jobs. Immediate completions and notices use normal session admission, follow-up queues and delivery, with exact lifecycle, cancellation, authority and original-route ownership. There is no replacement heartbeat scheduler, special response tool or outcome store.

Doctor converts existing jobs in place, preserving IDs, disabled state, anchors, pending scheduling slots, history and scratch revisions. A provisioning/cutover receipt in existing configuration state prevents restart or repeated Doctor from recreating a deleted job. Migration plans asynchronous work before synchronous SQLite commits, verifies canonical data before removing legacy inputs, and fails visibly on ambiguous/corrupt receipts.

The approved shared-state **15 → 16** fence prevents older gateways from silently ignoring migrated execution/delivery policies. Agent schema stays **19**; `heartbeat_outcomes` remains structurally present but inert after meaningful pending context is migrated once. Deferred physical deletion is tracked in `src/state/README.md`. Gateway protocol stays **4**, with narrow deprecated external adapters backed by canonical cron/session machinery; eventual wire removals are tracked as protocol-v5 TODOs.

Investigation also reproduced and fixed two host-lifecycle leaks: delayed completion inherited a disposed transcript writer, and real predispatch admission inherited an already-released Gateway root. The completion handoff now uses existing independent-root and transcript-detachment owners through actual settlement, including queued execution, with cancellation removing the exact suspended admission waiter. Existing shutdown and target-generation fences remain intact.

## User Impact

Operators can edit monitoring like any other automation. Optional per-job active hours, idle-only execution, owner delivery, direct-message policy and explicit-empty-scratch behavior are available through ordinary authoring surfaces. Scratch CAS and self-scoped result recording belong to the existing `automations` tool; ordinary `NO_REPLY` provides silence. Missing scratch remains distinct from explicitly empty scratch.

Immediate results no longer require periodic monitoring. Busy foreground turns are not interrupted, original delivery routes are retained, and reset/replaced sessions reject stale work. Ordinary run history and System busyness expose job/run identity and actual outcomes. An explicit-empty skip remains `skipped` with failed completion/CLI exit 1, while known non-delivery is recorded as `not-delivered` rather than unknown. Raw protocol-v4 compatibility diagnostics remain available in a separately labeled legacy-inspection section.

**Draft decisions / remaining merge gates:**

- Three legitimate SDK deprecation annotations preserve the approved external contracts but exceed unchanged deprecation budgets: total **1137 / 1134**, and `reply-runtime` **4 / 1**. Public entrypoint/export/callable counts are unchanged at **147 / 4355 / 2593**. No tags were hidden, APIs deleted, counters raised or environment overrides used. Accepting those exact deprecation-budget changes still needs an explicit maintainer decision.
- The former **24-hour suppression of identical alert text across separate heartbeat occurrences** is not reproduced by ordinary same-occurrence cron receipts. Its retirement is a proposed behavior difference, not an approved compatibility decision and not equivalent deduplication. Prompt guidance is not a deterministic substitute. This must be resolved before readiness.
- Native runtime proof remains incomplete: the macOS runtime-test launcher requires disposable credentialless macOS CI, and the iOS build encountered the previously reported WebRTC dependency fingerprint mismatch before compilation. Compilation/schema/format checks are not presented as native runtime proof.

## Evidence

**Owner and integration checks.** Final combined execution/lifecycle/Doctor/SDK/status selection passed **612 tests in 31 files**. The preceding coherent cleanup selection passed **4,226 tests in 135 files**, plus **168 E2E tests**; these selections overlap and are not summed. Full type programs, lint, static/runtime import-cycle checks, protocol/Swift-generation/native-schema guards, SDK public-name parity and the private-QA build passed. Final retention tests, docs MDX/links/glossary checks and build passed after adopting the retained-API portion of [#135322 — retain shipped plugin contracts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/135322). That resolved the five dated SDK expiry failures without deleting APIs or moving dates. The overall changed check is still red on the two deprecation-count overages above.

Representative commands actually executed:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.transcript-scope.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.test.ts src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/sessions/session-lifecycle-admission.test.ts src/sessions/session-lifecycle-admission.pending.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.test.ts src/cron/session-run.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.notify-on-exit-ack.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime-output.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.process.delivery.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript-write-context.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-transcript-lifecycle.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/delivery-queue-runtime.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/webhook-request-guards.test.ts
```

```bash
pnpm tsgo:all
```

```bash
pnpm lint
```

```bash
pnpm check:import-cycles
```

```bash
pnpm check:madge-import-cycles
```

```bash
env OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build
```

**Real execution.** [Live proof run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33572029038) passed both OpenClaw and Codex runtime cells: exec completion with cron disabled, asserted busy overlap without interruption, real child spawn/read/result after the foreground turn ended, exactly one child delivery to the original direct conversation, natural main-session cron delegation and reset fencing. Natural cron deduplication and model-created one-shot/recurring/restart scenarios also passed, with no skipped cells or retried model actions. A separate metadata lane used a mock provider and is labeled as such. One earlier setup-only attempt failed on a stale prepared dependency; a fresh normal frozen-lockfile install repaired preparation before any model action ran.

This live run used the fixed pre-cleanup candidate. Every later live-to-final change was classified during integration; the handoff execution/settlement body retained parity apart from private naming, type-only ownership and formatting, and the root helper differed only in its ownership comment. It is not claimed that the final source fingerprint itself ran the earlier model suite. The observed Codex executable was version 0.151.0; upstream response-model identity was not available. Upstream dynamic-tool and turn-lifecycle contracts were inspected directly, independently of the installed binary identity.

**Actual stable-source migration.** Synthetic data was produced through the actual `v2026.8.1` production owners at shared schema 15 / agent 19, not inserted using current-schema fixture SQL. Built Doctor migrated a writable copy to 16/19, preserving job identity, disabled cadence/anchor, history, sessions and exact scratch bytes/revision. Meaningful pending context migrated once; the inert table remained. Repeated Doctor preserved domain state. Ordinary cadence/scratch edits, stale-CAS rejection and permanent deletion survived further Doctor runs. The actual old reader refused schema 16 without changing either database; the candidate reopened, and a separate restored backup opened through stable owners. All original protected paths retained their hashes, modes, flags and inodes. This is stable-source synthetic-data proof, not an installed-npm or real-user-history claim.

**Independent review.** Fresh complete-target Codex autoreview completed with exit 0, `scoped-clean` at P0, across **36 complete bounded passes with zero findings**; 27 complete owner modules were supplied as additional context. The reviewed final source is byte-identical to the final UI/proof snapshot. This is scoped blocking-issue review, not a claim of a separate P1/P2 pass.

**Visual proof.** The final real-Gateway flow passed: actual canonical diagnostics and job/run/skipped event, UI name/window edits with strict effective-policy readback, exact scratch content at revision 2, and retained Skipped/Not delivered history. Recording caught a real layout bug: inherited `nowrap` clipped the run ID and hid the outcome despite correct DOM text. One event-scoped CSS declaration fixes it; the existing browser test failed on real line geometry at desktop/mobile widths before the change and passed afterward. Nineteen debug-owner tests, scoped checks/types/styles and canonical `pnpm ui:build` also passed. All 10,951 non-UI build entries remained byte-identical to the earlier full build.

The final layout regression and UI build commands were:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/debug-diagnostics.e2e.test.ts
```

```bash
pnpm ui:build
```

Before/after fixture-only images and a cropped editor/scratch/history recording excerpt have been independently inspected for publication. The excerpt omits opening machine diagnostics and a capture-only gray transition; it is not presented as the full continuous recording. Original captures are retained locally. Earlier recorder assumptions about unexported execution fields, explicit `bestEffort:false` default materialization, and a hidden history-filter match were corrected at the observed public/UI contracts, without changing runtime behavior to satisfy the recorder.

**Size.** The 973-path patch is **production +10,854 / −11,474 (net −620)**; **tests/support +12,658 / −24,835 (net −12,177)**. Generated/snapshots net −7, tooling/configuration net −6, docs net +345 and QA scenarios/support net +337 are separate. Same-category moves cancel in net totals. No root changelog, dependency, budget or protocol-version changes are included.

**Current GitHub state.** Head `c0cb2d87eb15cff3325137e319cf5c283cc755b0` is draft and GitHub reports `CONFLICTING` with current `main`. Normal pull-request CI has not attached; successful metadata/triage checks are not runtime CI. A main rebase and exact-head CI are still required before readiness, alongside the explicit decisions and native proof gaps above.

No operator Gateway, live state, credentials or native app Keychain was used for proof. Owned proof Gateways, browsers and Testbox leases are cleaned up; no agent transcripts are attached. The PR remains draft pending the named compatibility decisions, native proof gaps and exact-head CI evidence.

![After: actual job, run, and skipped outcome in System busyness; event-only crop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6970f30-8cc2-4eb3-9171-e4e1d1a93215)

![After: editable delivery, active-hours, idle, and empty-scratch policies](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e507041-51ae-40e6-a734-bcf63927a4fa)

![After: actual skipped and not-delivered history](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d368982c-87f7-4deb-b56a-88c579412c13)

prs.title: fix: task list loses every task when a stale task registry instance restores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the task registry's resident rows could be wiped when a stale task registry module instance ran a readiness check against its own default store while a live instance had already published rows from a different store. In CI this surfaced as `src/gateway/server.tasks-list-performance.test.ts` failing with `expected [] to have a length of 10001` (run 36244868550, job 108412590514) while the backing store still held every mutation.

## User Impact

No user-visible change for a single Gateway process. Task registry rows, store selection, and restore readiness now have one process-wide owner, so a second module instance of the registry (plugin SDK bundles, non-isolated test workers) can no longer replace rows another instance published. The flaky Gateway test is fixed at its owner rather than in the test.

## Why This Change Was Made

`task-registry.process-state.ts` deliberately keeps the resident task rows, revision, and projection dirty flags on a `Symbol.for` global so duplicate module instances share them. The configured store (`configuredTaskRegistryStore`) and the restore status (`taskRegistryRestoreState`) were module-local. A second instance therefore saw "uninitialized" readiness and the default SQLite store, restored an empty snapshot into the shared rows, and cleared the shared dirty flag, so the live instance answered `listTaskRecords()` from a "ready", clean, empty projection.

The gateway-server Vitest project runs with `isolate: false`; the non-isolated runner resets the module graph after every file, but timers and promise chains from an earlier file keep their old module instance alive. A late `ensureTaskRegistryReady()` from that instance is exactly the write the prior instrumentation lane (`.artifacts/l1297`) could not attribute: it comes from a module instance the test file never imported.

This moves the store cell and restore state into the process state next to the rows they govern. `getTaskRegistryStore()`, `configureTaskRegistryRuntime()`, `resetTaskRegistryRuntimeForTests()`, and every restore-state read/write in `task-registry-state.ts` now go through the shared owner; no behavior changes for a single instance. The flow registry keeps rows and restore state together per instance already, so it is unaffected.

## Evidence

- New regression `task registry process state > keeps published rows when a stale module instance restores from its own store` (`src/tasks/task-registry.process-state.test.ts`): a live instance publishes rows from an in-memory store on an open state database, `vi.resetModules()` produces a stale instance, and its `ensureTaskRegistryReady()` must not change either instance's `listTaskRecords()`. Fails on `main` with `expected [] to deeply equal ['task-c','task-b','task-a']`, the CI symptom; passes with this change. Measured cost: 211 ms (`pnpm test src/tasks/task-registry.process-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`).
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server.tasks-list-performance.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2 passed (both cases), 54 s wall locally.
- `pnpm test src/tasks/task-registry-terminal-notification.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry-projection-read.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.restore-admission.test.ts`: 4 files, 104 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: clean. Codex autoreview (P2 threshold): one finding, that a per-instance default store object would not match a shared failed-restore record, addressed by latching the first default into the shared cell; rerun scoped-clean. `oxlint` and `oxfmt` on the changed files: clean.
- The Testbox shard replays from the earlier lane (original 40-file shard with 2 workers, same shard under CPU contention, predecessors + target with 1 and 4 workers) all passed before this change because worker assignment decides which stale instance is alive; the regression above pins the mechanism deterministically instead.

Auto-merge is intentionally off for this PR.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the `checks-node-compact-small-*` shard failed on unrelated changes when `test/scripts/openclaw-e2e-instance.test.ts` › "terminates descendants in the tracked process group" ran on a hosted 4-core runner: the test allowed only two seconds for two Node processes to publish PID files, receive SIGTERM, and exit, and reported "tracked child still alive" or "did not receive SIGTERM" under load.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three poll windows in the embedded bash script grow from 100 to 500 iterations of 20 ms (ten seconds each), and the `runBash` timeout grows to 40 s so it can never cut the windows short. The assertions and the helper under test are unchanged; this only gives a timing-dependent check a tolerance proportionate to slow runners.

## User Impact

None for users. Maintainers stop seeing this shard fail on hosted reruns of unrelated PRs.

## Evidence

- Failing occurrence on a Swift-only PR after a hosted rerun: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33723004348/job/100547029771 (`AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0` at `expectShellSuccess`, shard `core-tooling-isolated`).
- Local: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/openclaw-e2e-instance.test.ts` → 38 tests passed.

prs.title: fix(codex): warn when required apps are unavailable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Embedding runtimes can require a Codex app, but previously had no operational warning when the signed-in account had not installed or authorized it.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now accepts an explicit `requiredAppIds` list in the Codex plugin config. It performs one live `app/installed` check per account and required-app set, logs a targeted warning for each unavailable app, coalesces concurrent checks, and retries only when the inventory check itself fails. The check does not read or change turn configuration.

## User Impact

Operators get a concrete warning when a required app cannot expose tools because the account has not installed or authorized it. Runtimes that do not declare required apps are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/configured-app-availability.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-thread-cleanup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`: 4 files and 163 tests passed.

prs.title: fix(slack): allow standalone workspace sends
prs.body:
Related: #121373

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where standalone `openclaw message send --channel slack --target channel:<id>` commands for normal Slack workspace installs fail with `unsupported_enterprise_slack_delivery` because the command does not start the Slack monitor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Slack monitor is the owner of process-local installation identity, so an absent identity means the monitor did not run; it is not evidence that the account is Enterprise Grid. Bare targets remain rejected when the monitor has positively detected an Enterprise Grid install or has a degraded identity, while workspace installs and standalone commands retain bare-target delivery.

## User Impact

Operators can send Slack messages from the standalone CLI to ordinary workspace channels without first starting the gateway. Detected Enterprise Grid accounts still require workspace-qualified targets.

## Evidence

- The existing Slack channel boundary test covers bare delivery when no monitor-owned identity is present.
- The existing provider identity-recovery test covers rejection while identity is degraded and acceptance after workspace recovery.
- The existing Enterprise delivery tests continue to cover rejection of bare targets for detected org installs.
- `oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/detached-target-admission.ts extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider.auth-test-token.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused runtime tests and CI are pending.

prs.title: fix(ingress): heartbeat deferred queue ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel event can be durably claimed and then deferred while it waits for an existing reply-lane turn. The ingress watchdog was still measuring only elapsed wall time, so valid queue ownership lasting longer than five minutes was dead-lettered as `handler-timeout`. When the reply lane later tried to adopt the event, the claim had already been lost and no reply was delivered.

## Desired Behavior

The watchdog stays armed after deferral. The reply queue sends a lifecycle heartbeat only while that exact deferred lifecycle remains owned by the queue: pending, in flight, or represented in queued summary sources.

This makes the claim renewable, not unbounded:

| State | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Dispatch never hands off | The watchdog dead-letters it as `handler-timeout`. |
| Reply queue owns the deferred lifecycle | The queue heartbeat renews the watchdog deadline. |
| Queue ownership disappears or the heartbeat throws | Heartbeats stop; the watchdog recovers the orphan as `handler-timeout`. |
| The queue adopts, abandons, or completes the lifecycle | The heartbeat timer stops and normal lifecycle settlement continues. |

Slack and Telegram preserve the same lifecycle heartbeat contract.

## Implementation

- keep the adoption-stall watchdog armed for both `dispatching` and `deferred` phases
- rearm it when ingress hands the lifecycle to the reply queue
- expose an optional deferred-heartbeat callback and interval on the shared lifecycle
- start the queue heartbeat only after enqueue succeeds
- renew only while the same lifecycle is still present in queue-owned work
- stop the timer on adoption, abandonment, completion, ownership loss, or heartbeat failure
- derive the heartbeat cadence from one third of the configured adoption-stall timeout

## Evidence

- Regression first: the previous unconditional-watchdog-clear patch failed a new orphaned-ownership test because an abandoned deferred claim never reached `handler-timeout`.
- Shared ingress and reply-queue suites: 4 files, 37 tests passed.
- Slack and Telegram suites: 4 files, 76 tests passed.
- Orphan recovery: removing queue ownership stops heartbeats and dead-letters the claim with `handler-timeout`.
- Long-wait unit coverage: a deferred lifecycle survives a simulated 60-second queue wait behind a 5-second watchdog through queue-owned heartbeats.
- Real two-thread run: a victim message waited behind a real 480-second holder task. Its durable event stayed claimed past the 300-second boundary, completed 443.545 seconds after claim, and produced its exact thread reply 450.811 seconds after send with zero retries and no failure reason.
- Native `linux/arm64` gateway image built successfully from commit `5e7d435fb0494ae46d32fce94c2adc6fd6a6bf67`.
- Production core and extension typechecks passed.
- Exact-head autoreview reported no actionable findings.

The repository-wide test typecheck remains blocked by pre-existing errors in unrelated sandbox path-safety files; this branch does not modify them.

prs.title: fix: Codex apps disappear from scheduled jobs
prs.body:
Related: #113475

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who create isolated scheduled jobs from a Codex-backed agent would lose Codex native tools and connected apps when the job ran.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduled-job creator cap only captured OpenClaw-owned tools, while Codex provides shell/files and connected apps through a separate app-server surface. This change records that native surface as one reserved capability when it was available to the creating turn, then recognizes that capability during the scheduled run.

The finite `toolsAllow` list remains a hard upper bound: explicit narrower lists do not receive the capability, sandbox checks still apply, and Codex continues to emit an exact per-app policy with `_default.enabled=false`. This matches Codex's separation between [app policy](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/7431f10d0d4b4ecf5df08a853b41859013b17e45/codex-rs/connectors/src/app_tool_policy.rs#L33-L100) and [native app enablement](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/7431f10d0d4b4ecf5df08a853b41859013b17e45/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_context.rs#L230-L239).

## User Impact

Default-capped Codex cron jobs can use the same creator-authorized connected apps and native Codex surface as the creating turn. Jobs with an explicit narrow tool list remain restricted.

## Evidence

- Added coverage that captures the reserved capability only when the creator has the Codex native surface.
- Added coverage that recognizes the capability while empty and ordinary finite allowlists remain denied.
- Added a full Codex attempt regression showing a default-capped scheduled run enables its authorized Google Calendar app.
- Current head: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts` passed 60 tests.
- Current head: the exact deadcode export check passed with 0 entries.
- `src/agents/tools/cron-tool-creator-cap.test.ts`: 6 passed on the runtime-change commit.
- Managed integration proof on runtime-change commit `6d93a5f6ffb96679441bf8c2cba935cd1125dfca`: a creator-created isolated job retained the reserved capability, invoked an authorized read-only Codex app successfully, and delivered the exact expected marker. The synthetic job was removed afterward.
- Current head `b3782cd114e3697efc1283a2d4b4a1083a58cce7` adds only a test-local copy of the opaque capability value so the production constant is no longer exported solely for tests; runtime behavior is unchanged.
- `git diff --check`
- Autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

The full `run-attempt.test.ts` file was not a valid local signal: the local Node 25.5.0 runtime links SQLite 3.51.2, which OpenClaw correctly rejects as unsafe before test setup. The focused policy suites and managed integration proof above passed.

AI-assisted change: Codex investigated the regression, authored the patch and tests, and ran structured review. I reviewed the behavior and understand the security boundary described above.

prs.title: feat(agentsapi): transfer attachments and hosted files
prs.body:
## Why

Agents API conversations need admitted attachments in the hosted workspace and completed files returned to the user so hosted work can produce useful deliverables.

## What Problem This Solves

The Agents API harness cannot otherwise place an admitted attachment in its hosted workspace or deliver a completed hosted file through OpenClaw's outbound media path. This change connects those two boundaries while retaining host ownership checks and transfer limits.

## Change

Upload host-admitted file attachments into the hosted Linux workspace, including follow-up uploads to an existing connected environment. Return completed-turn artifacts under `/workspace/outputs` through OpenClaw's managed outbound media. Transfers remain bounded to 5 MiB per file, 10 MiB per direction per turn, and 50 files per direction per turn.

Retain attachment preparation, the staged-input SDK helper and documentation, and the provider-route fixture update from the original combined PR. Native function relay, tool policy, hooks, receipts, and result middleware are already on main through #154208.

This PR now targets main. File-transfer commit `af9a16310d1caad52a87238ab9914ed47edd819b` was rebased onto captured main `dfb6474c538f493a70a4d2c399703966899a9ed0`. Rebase conflicts were resolved by moving file hooks into the current attempt module and using the current official OpenAI SDK for environment uploads, artifacts, and root-turn retrieval. The existing SDK transport, cancellation, session fingerprint, history reconciliation, and terminal usage paths are preserved.

Replaces #151872, which GitHub closed during restacking and previously refused to reopen.

## Scope and deferred work

This PR's initial support scope is an OpenAI-hosted Linux VM, a Linux Gateway using native Linux filesystem storage or a Docker-managed volume, and hosted sessions created with the file-transfer instructions, including subsequent reuse. The recorded live proof uses a Linux ARM64 Gateway and ordinary Slack attachment flows. Running that Linux Gateway in Docker on macOS with a Docker-managed state volume fits this profile; macOS host bind-mounted state does not yet have passing publication evidence.

The hosted VM and the Gateway are separate environments. Hosted Linux execution alone does not establish Windows Gateway compatibility. These are scope decisions for this increment, not claims about every environment supported by the underlying API.

Pre-feature session migration is not applicable to this PR: this Agents API integration has not launched, and there are no real user sessions carrying the earlier instructions that file transfer was unavailable. No migration or automatic session reset is required for this increment.

Deferred TODOs for later work:

- [ ] Normalize and verify workspace-staged inbound paths on a native Windows Gateway.
- [ ] Repair or prove managed-media publication with macOS host bind-mounted Gateway state. The observed failure remains documented below; use native Linux or Docker-managed volume storage for this increment.
- [ ] Add channel-specific live proof beyond Slack, including Telegram, plus browser Control UI and end-user OpenClaw CLI attachment-flow proof. The Gateway API coverage below is already completed; the remaining entry points are unverified by this task, not declared broken.

The two approved in-scope review fixes preserve completed replies when artifact collection fails and bind outbound publication to current attempt authority at the final filesystem effect. Both have passing focused regression proof. New local Docker Gateway and ordinary Slack proof has confirmed CSV, UTF-8, and both generated binary files by actual download and byte comparison. The oversized-output case proved completed-reply retention and non-delivery of the 6 MiB file. Its inaccurate native “Attached” wording and missing Slack failure message are documented MVP limitations. Local testing is complete. ClawSweeper revision 23 reviewed exact head `87070fc9c3bb6e1f9180c53487e12fab301fb767`: no actionable findings, no security findings, and no remaining before-merge items. It accepted the bounded MVP scope and local Slack evidence.

Self-hosted environments, image generation, and image understanding remain outside this file-transfer increment.

## Evidence

Current published head: `87070fc9c3bb6e1f9180c53487e12fab301fb767`, retaining base `0b5cd517978843d37348825fc1f6472fac6ead0b`. The final commit documents the already-approved Linux Gateway storage scope and missing-attachment limitation; production code remains identical to the tested package source `9123c7553138e21d21b5d0b5e9016cf994effd24`. [Current CI run 36196016070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36196016070) passed: 122 successful jobs, 19 skipped, and no failures, including the aggregate gate. Security Review run `36196015860` passed on the same exact head.

On preceding head `d2a5f0138623d286ca40384fd9791fd3acb29195`, CI completed 121 successful jobs, 19 skipped and no failed jobs. Only the `pr-fail-fast` watcher was cancelled when the documentation commit was pushed, so the workflow conclusion is cancelled. Security Review run `36194562992` passed for that preceding head. Its only difference from the built core was two type-correct test assertions.

### Review fixes

Completed assistant text now survives an ordinary artifact listing, download, or publication failure. The completed reply is committed to the transcript and presented while the attempt still records the transfer failure. Successful collection keeps its existing ordering. Cancellation and revoked authority still prevent reply persistence and presentation. Commit: `f52813a0fd5`.

Artifact publication now uses the host reply-media capability, composing the admitted host's authority, the native attempt's current-authority check, and cancellation through the managed-media write boundary. The provider supplies already-admitted bytes rather than a Gateway filesystem path. The artifact-specific buffer route preserves the original file bytes, including arbitrary binary files, without applying workspace-image transformations. Commits: `251911a730e` and `5f9842d1d45`.

### Review-fix validation

Tested source: `9123c7553138e21d21b5d0b5e9016cf994effd24`.

- All **51 focused tests in four files passed**, covering attempt settlement, file custody and publication, host reply-media preparation, and the shared media-store authority lifecycle. The single-worker command completed three routed Vitest shards in 71.35 s, with **71.78 s process wall time**, including compiler preparation.
- The three selected regression cases failed against the original production source `a6fdf67841cc467c3f52e7cc8deae29d592856eb` with the current tests applied, in **19.05 s process wall time**. The completed-reply case returned no assistant text. Native-binding revocation and abort during media-save preparation each left an outbound file. These cases pass with the fixes.
- The attempt regression checks actual persisted transcript content, the returned completed assistant and text, and one presentation callback. Cancellation and revocation cases verify that the reply is not persisted or presented.
- The publication regressions exercise real admitted host authority and the media-save path, revoking authority during save preparation before the filesystem write. They verify that no outbound file remains. The suite also checks that successful publication preserves the downloaded artifact bytes.

Measured command:

```sh
pnpm test extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.test.ts extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-files.test.ts src/agents/harness/host-capability.reply-media.test.ts src/media/store.read-scope.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The Agents API shard passed 27 tests in 24.60 s; the host reply-media shard passed three in 18.53 s; the media-store shard passed 21 in 22.03 s. The previously existing actual-byte transfer-budget case took 10.382 s. These are measured local test costs. The successful current-head CI workflow elapsed 975 s from run start to terminal update, including shared jobs and scheduling; this is not an isolated or marginal cost for these tests.

On `d2a5f0138623d286ca40384fd9791fd3acb29195`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passed in **26.99 s process wall time** and the three attempt regressions passed in **29.62 s Vitest / 33.03 s process wall time**. The preceding `9123c755` CI run failed only the source job `check-test-types` (138.8 s), with these test-owned diagnostics:

```text
extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.test.ts(59,19): error TS2339: Property 'terminal' does not exist on type 'AgentHarnessAttemptResult'.
  Property 'terminal' does not exist on type 'AgentHarnessLegacyAttemptResult'.
extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.test.ts(96,21): error TS2339: Property 'terminal' does not exist on type 'AgentHarnessAttemptResult'.
  Property 'terminal' does not exist on type 'AgentHarnessLegacyAttemptResult'.
```

The correction checks property existence and deep equality without reading a property absent from the legacy union member. It changes no production code. The final storage-scope paragraph passed scoped MDX parsing, formatting and whitespace checks; it changes no runtime or test behavior.

### New local Slack proof

The native Linux ARM64 Docker Gateway uses the complete canonical package built from `9123c7553138e21d21b5d0b5e9016cf994effd24`, plus the complete canonical Slack plugin built from `1db3820f9131c6894a6567b97a333b8b6d4deff8`. The only changes from the core package source to current head `87070fc9c3bb6e1f9180c53487e12fab301fb767` are the two test assertions and the storage-scope documentation paragraph, so the production source is identical. The Slack plugin includes the separately tracked formatter fix; this remains a composed runtime, not a claim that this PR includes that fix. The core package SHA-256 is `02aa818c839a74f5ebe09801630c4bfb2bacf88d448fa8b097301039b85f64b9`.

- An ordinary Slack upload and returned-file download preserved all 123,183 CSV bytes. A 140-byte UTF-8 follow-up was also downloaded and compared byte for byte. The follow-up reused the same hosted session with a distinct turn.
- The two-binary request generated two 1,024-byte files. Both actual Slack downloads exactly matched their respective generated managed-file bytes. Native Slack desktop inspection found both attachment cards and a filename-only inline-code reply without local paths.
- The oversized-output case created a 6,291,456-byte file. The completed final answer was preserved exactly once, no file was delivered, and the terminal record was `run-failed-before-reply`. Slack nevertheless said “Attached” without a file or visible failure. This proves reply retention and non-delivery of the oversized file. The native “Attached” wording and missing user-visible Slack error remain documented MVP limitations; no full failure-presentation pass is claimed. Further handling of this corner case is deferred beyond the initial increment.

### Current evidence limits

The approved local testing is complete: ordinary CSV, UTF-8, and two-binary transfers passed, completed-reply retention was observed on the oversized-file failure, and final-effect publication authority passed the focused regressions. The exact runtime composition is recorded above. Oversized-file success wording and missing Slack error presentation remain documented MVP limitations, with no full failure-presentation pass claimed. ClawSweeper revision 23 reviewed exact head `87070fc9` and accepted the fixes, final-effect authority proof, support guidance, and bounded MVP scope. It reported no actionable findings, no security findings, and no remaining before-merge items. Earlier Slack and Gateway API evidence remains bound to its recorded source and composed image.

The attempt still reports artifact-transfer failure. Existing recovery may continue a settled transcript for a classified transient error; this change does not establish a universal no-retry guarantee or change recovery policy. The demonstrated authority defect was a stale local outbound-file write, not demonstrated unauthorized Slack delivery. Earlier CI failures and the macOS bind-mount limitation retain their previously recorded evidence and uncertainty.

### Earlier evidence

Earlier published head `a6fdf67841cc467c3f52e7cc8deae29d592856eb` was rebased onto main `0b5cd517978843d37348825fc1f6472fac6ead0b` after the upstream Team Reports repair landed. The rebase was conflict-free, all nine commit patches have equal range-diff mappings, and the fresh whitespace check passed. [CI run 36182693597](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36182693597) passed on its first attempt: 124 successful jobs, 19 skipped, and no failures, including the aggregate gate. Security Review passed for the same exact head in run `36182691856`. The type check and both previously failing test lanes pass; the earlier Bun crash remains unexplained and is not claimed repaired. The Slack local-path formatter repair and its regression were moved unchanged to #158276, based directly on current main. This PR no longer changes the Slack formatter. The document-projection test correction remains. Earlier evidence below is bound to its recorded source and image; the running test Gateway has not been altered by this source split.

- Real Slack testing exposed an existing formatter defect: Markdown links to local output paths became invalid Slack links and exposed internal paths. The repair is now in the separate Slack PR referenced above; this file-transfer PR does not include it.
- The extracted formatter regression failed on the original formatter and passed with the fix. Its 38 passing tests and focused checks belong to the separate Slack change, not this PR’s current diff.
- Earlier real Slack transfers delivered a 123,183-byte CSV, a 140-byte UTF-8 follow-up, a generated JSON summary, an exact text copy, and two generated 1,024-byte binary files. Actual Slack downloads matched independent inputs or generated managed-file bytes. Desktop inspection found both binary attachment cards but exposed the invalid local-path links, so that run is not a full user-visible pass.
- The live Slack file-transfer retest used the unchanged verified core build plus the complete canonical Slack package built from `1db3820f9131c6894a6567b97a333b8b6d4deff8`. All 5,714 package files matched the canonical archive; offline full channel registration and plugin Doctor passed. Two newly generated 1,024-byte binary files were uploaded to Slack, downloaded, and compared byte for byte with their generated managed-media sources. Native Slack desktop inspection of the exact test thread verified both attachment cards and the complete filename-only reply without local paths. The final response used inline-code filenames, so this live retest did not exercise conversion of Markdown links containing local paths; the original-input focused regression covered that conversion. This is composed-image evidence, not a newly rebuilt core claim.

### Live entry-point coverage

| Entry point | Result | What was exercised |
|---|---|---|
| Slack | Transfers PASS; oversized-output messaging is an MVP limitation | New composed runtime: CSV, UTF-8, and both generated binaries independently downloaded and byte-compared; both binary cards and clean filenames inspected in native Slack. Oversized output retained the completed text but did not surface transfer failure. Exact source and composition limits are recorded above. |
| Gateway chat and artifact APIs | PASS on source `404910a3502120b99b25f651d34da9460a901845` | A terminal-run Node driver used the packaged `GatewayClient`, submitted files through `chat.send`, waited for completion, listed returned attachments with `artifacts.list`, requested HTTP download tickets with `artifacts.download`, and fetched the actual bytes. |
| Browser Control UI | Not exercised by this file-transfer proof | No browser upload, rendered attachment interaction, or browser download was performed in the Gateway API run. |
| End-user OpenClaw CLI | Not exercised by this file-transfer proof | Running a Node driver from a terminal and making diagnostic `gateway call` requests are not CLI file-transfer tests. |

The Gateway API run uploaded and returned a 147-byte CSV and a 134-byte UTF-8 text file. Both downloaded files matched their independent input bytes and SHA-256 hashes. The follow-up reused the same Gateway and hosted session with a distinct hosted turn. Retained receipt and file readback reconfirm these results; this PR update does not represent a new live run or current-head deployment. The earlier informal description "webchat proof" referred to these Gateway protocol calls, not a browser Control UI test.

- Live file transfer passed through ordinary Gateway `chat.send`, `artifacts.list`, and ticketed HTTP `artifacts.download` on a native Linux ARM64 packaged Gateway. A 147-byte CSV and a 134-byte UTF-8 text file were each uploaded, copied by the hosted shell, returned as attachments, downloaded, and independently compared byte for byte. The second upload reused both the Gateway session and the hosted session, with a distinct hosted turn. No per-test model override was used.
- The serving Gateway build identity matched the tested source commit. The complete canonical package passed archive validation, native filesystem dependency loading, contained dependency-link checks, and plugin doctor. Installed official OpenAI SDK 7.17.0 resolved from the root, Agents API plugin, and OpenAI plugin. Native production dependencies were installed by npm from the canonical package; this is not a frozen pnpm Docker dependency-install claim.
- Final focused local tests passed against that SDK. Transport tests replace guarded fetch; custody/publication tests use real managed/staged files and outbound persistence.

| Scope | Tests | Vitest duration | Process wall time |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SDK uploads, receipts, pagination, bounded downloads and cancellation | 23 passed | 1.14 s | 2.52 s |
| File custody, transfer limits and output publication | 20 passed | 11.29 s | 12.40 s |

- CI on `1db3820` exposed a stale existing expectation that native image projection discards admitted documents. The test now verifies that documents survive projection and reach the harness. All 16 tests in the dispatch suite passed (23.20 s Vitest, 26.29 s process wall, including worker compilation), and all 17 neighboring media-projection tests passed (9.17 s Vitest, 11.33 s process wall). Formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- The earlier broader local run passed 270 tests in 12 files across six shards in 85.18 s, covering Agents API, provider routing, attachment dispatch, media persistence and Gateway attachment ownership. This is earlier-head evidence, before the test fixture import and lint corrections.
- Core and extension production/test type checks passed, including all 25 core test shards. Core and extension lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The changed-check command passed 20 preceding guards, including package exports and plugin boundaries, before the pre-existing root-count limit below. The remaining scoped guards and dead-code checks passed separately.

Live downloaded SHA-256 values matched their independent upload fixtures:

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `returned-first.csv` | 147 | `aa0a90b4333c5def8bb94c7389759a055ba776005d194e89905b8ba43d423ec9` |
| `returned-second.txt` | 134 | `ac7eee5eb02a6cdffd5ee334b97b5697f5d4e8188ae5364fedf7037f24dd3bd5` |

Earlier full core package SHA-256: `479ba30076f1ac9130ebf20735e704b060f67774c692fc4ab674252483c714c0`.

Current canonical Slack package SHA-256: `61769c5251c98b1ad0e4b0ba0cb5e4849245461f739df7eae99344cd023bdcf2`.

## Limitations

The aggregate local changed-check command did not pass. Its failure was:

```text
Core test shard root budget
test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json: agents-root: 721 test roots exceeds the advisory 720 limit; rebalance when convenient
Core test shard root budget exceeded
```

Read-only comparison found the same 721 selected roots on captured main `dfb6474c538f493a70a4d2c399703966899a9ed0`, with identical root membership and unchanged owning configuration/scripts. This PR does not add to that count.

The first live fixture used macOS bind-mounted Gateway state. Upload and hosted download persisted identical bytes, but managed attachment publication failed with `Managed document attachment "returned-first---c0aff79f-838b-4ffe-9abc-8900655697f5.csv" could not be prepared`. An isolated call to the packaged publication owner reproduced `FsSafeError: file identity changed or could not be verified` on the bind mount and passed on container-native storage. The live proof above uses a fresh native Docker volume, the same unmodified image and source, and the ordinary Gateway path.

The native-volume run initially stopped at an incorrect driver filename assumption because managed filenames contain a UUID suffix. The driver was corrected to use OpenClaw's existing filename decoder, then resumed the already accepted first turn without replaying it. Exact-byte checks and the second upload passed. Neither fixture correction changed production code.

The file-custody suite's actual-byte budget case took 10.041 s. Earlier-head [CI run 36162950528](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36162950528) was cancelled after one source job failed: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-12`. The aggregate gate also failed; 23 jobs passed, 19 skipped and 99 were cancelled. The source failure is `TestTeardownError: src/gateway/boot.test.ts: singleton openclaw.stateDatabaseLifecycle failed`, followed by `SqliteWorkerError: Shared-state admission requires the host broker`. All 527 test assertions in that Node subset passed before the suite teardown failure. The owning sources are unchanged from the captured base, but no PR-independent cause is proven. A local group replay did not reproduce that teardown failure; it instead failed `src/gateway/mcp-http.keepalive.test.ts` with `AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality` at line 166. That replay had 526 passing tests, one failed test and one skipped test. Its Bun subset could not start because `spawn bun ENOENT`. No blind CI retry or source refresh was used to obtain green. Security Review passed for the same source head. The file-transfer tests did not produce completed CI timing in this cancelled run.

[CI run 36171273192](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36171273192) on `1db3820` ended cancelled by fail-fast after `checks-node-changed-compact-large-16` failed. The source failure was `AssertionError: expected [ { …(2) } ] to be undefined` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/backend.test.ts:265`; the received value was the admitted document. This was a PR-caused stale assertion, corrected in `c126a1245b87be57cf354c6da888c437d5002b5b` and verified locally as recorded above. The failed source job ran for 167.35 s, with 1,842 assertions passing and one failing. Security Review passed for `1db3820`. [Earlier-head CI run 36174801996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36174801996) was in progress at the last snapshot before the extraction commit. Security Review passed for `c126a1245b87be57cf354c6da888c437d5002b5b`. CI run `36177800488` for extraction head `5ce6b7002b1b4d78d1e84a2beb636ccb855c40c8` was cancelled by fail-fast after `checks-node-changed-compact-large-16` failed. Attempt 1 completed 31 successful jobs, 19 skipped, 91 cancelled and two failed including the aggregate gate. The source job completed the preceding 134-test Gateway group (one skipped) and the two-test Node subset, then the Bun subset exited with `panic: Segmentation fault at address 0x2`, `exited by signal SIGSEGV`, and exit 139 before any completed test case was reported. The tested merge was `913fd41f3d3dcb02c4fff3e5d3612e7d57fa1c06`, merging this head with base `847863aae3b7d92b27f56cc4d565b11f33aa301b`. Bun was the checksum-pinned Linux x64 `1.4.3-canary.1` build `ddfce5d01`. The runtime pin, worker startup, dependency lock and routing sources match that base; this does not establish a PR-independent cause. Main CI passed on both the tested base and the later inspected main, and no relevant upstream repair was identified. A prepared Linux Testbox reproduction could not run because the configured provider has no authenticated organization. Attempt 2 diagnostically replayed that exact failed job without source edits, a runtime change, or a rebase and passed. The retained checkout was the same tested merge and the Bun binary passed the same checksum check. The previously crashing Bun group passed all 55 files (610 tests passed, 19 skipped; 125.82 s). The workflow routed the replay to a GitHub-hosted runner with 4 logical CPUs and approximately 16 GiB RAM, compared with the original runner’s 8 CPUs and approximately 32 GiB, so this is not an identical-host reproduction. The full replayed job passed in 17m 47s; the original crash remains unexplained, and the passing replay is not a claimed fix. The aggregate still failed because 91 other jobs retained fail-fast cancellation. Attempt 3 was requested to complete those missing check results; no source refresh or blind repeat of a failing assertion was used. Security Review passed for `5ce6b700`; no aggregate CI pass is claimed for that head. Attempt 3 then failed `check-test-types` and `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-25` on the same missing Team Reports source barrel: `extensions/team-reports/src/scheduler.test.ts(12,57): error TS2307: Cannot find module './sources/index.js' or its corresponding type declarations.` The type check also reported `extensions/team-reports/src/scheduler.test.ts(846,27): error TS7006: Parameter 'input' implicitly has an 'any' type.` The scheduler source was identical in the tested merge and its base, with no Team Reports changes in this PR. Upstream had deleted the barrel but missed this test caller. [Repair 7c4866c73b31](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7c4866c73b31f9a4e4ee24d2323f179aa7c531ff) replaces that import with the direct Discord and GitHub source owners. The current head includes that landed repair through the rebase recorded above. This rebase is tied to that specific source repair, not to the unexplained Bun crash, and does not add local runtime or test proof.

ClawSweeper identified gaps in completed-reply retention, Windows staged paths, outbound publication authority, and instructions for pre-feature hosted sessions. Completed-reply retention and final-effect authority now have the fixes and regression proof recorded above. New local Slack uploads/downloads and binary rendering passed. The oversized-output case proved completed-reply retention and non-delivery; inaccurate native success wording and missing Slack error presentation remain accepted MVP limitations, with no full failure-presentation pass claimed. Local testing is complete. ClawSweeper revision 23 accepted both fixes, final-effect authority proof, live Slack evidence, and the support documentation on exact head `87070fc9`, with no actionable findings, security findings, or remaining before-merge items. Windows Gateway support remains a deferred TODO. Pre-feature session migration is not applicable because this integration has not launched and has no real user sessions with the earlier instructions. No session has been reset automatically. The separate Slack formatter PR tracks its remaining screenshot evidence. The desktop retest described above included that extracted fix and is retained as historical evidence, not a pass for a newly deployed extraction head.

Image generation remains unsupported by this prototype. Image understanding was excluded from this test scope. Historical tools-parent evidence does not validate this file-transfer head.

## Why

The Agents API harness needs access to OpenClaw Gateway tools so hosted agents can use enabled capabilities and retain actual tool calls and results in conversation history.

## What Problem This Solves

Add Gateway function-tool declarations and result handling to Agents API sessions, reuse shared harness execution and bookkeeping, and project native commands into OpenClaw history. Existing hosted sessions retain their declarations and workspace; an explicit reset adopts current tools.

Preserve accepted steering through terminal tool cleanup. The latest repairs admit ordinary child sessions under the supported tool policy, persist usage for tool-terminated turns, and project the available native history prefix before Gateway tool results. Usage aggregation lives in a separate sibling module to satisfy the line-cap rule.

Rebased onto main at `63d299c31b06150cc5fbff90c3b8123290608e13`. The shared Codex contracts and removed aliases follow the upstream cleanup. Independent rebase review confirmed preservation of the Agents API changes.

## Evidence

Current head: `5289507e3a2751f24b884cda09ce2e043d93b138`. [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36094073514) finished with 128 successful jobs, 18 skipped and two failed, including the aggregate gate. The conflict-free rebase preserved all 32 PR patches and incorporated upstream Kysely annotation repair `af545bf3b6add3f90825e1532bfeac884a4a3c0c` and native loopback/LAN fixture routing repair `63d299c31b06150cc5fbff90c3b8123290608e13`. Their checks now pass. No unrelated repair or check bypass is included in this PR.

The only remaining source failure is [Codex Computer Use setup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36094073514/job/107943446726), in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts`, "releases the install mutation fence before the guarded readiness thread": `AssertionError: expected 8 to be greater than 8`. CI tested merge `d93e618f98a2c93b8b352d47fc79804b0f98dc81`, whose tree equals the source head. The fixture, readiness producer, client, fence, dependencies and routing are unchanged from base, and the PR's changed tool-execution modules do not execute on this path. No PR-specific cause is demonstrated. The fixture uses a 150 ms deadline and polling, but the underlying install rejection is suppressed, so a timer race remains an inference rather than a reproduced cause. No retry or speculative fix has been made.

The preceding configuration-fixture timeout did not recur and its job passed. That passing run alone does not establish the earlier timeout's cause or prove a repair. Merge remains blocked by the current required CI gate.

Local diff checks pass; the unchanged PR code previously passed formatting and line-cap checks. Required CI remains enforced.

[Comprehensive real Docker evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154208#issuecomment-5826043937) records 64 distinct Gateway calls across 31 function names on the earlier tested head, plus native command/search projections, state changes, messaging, continuation, settlement and completed-turn usage. It also records the child-admission, durable-usage and history-order findings that motivated the latest repairs. Tests used ordinary Slack, the configured default model, actual hosted Linux sessions and native arm64 Docker, without mocks, fakes or special input modes.

[Earlier upgrade and reset evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154208#issuecomment-5822250465) covers the explicitly identified earlier source. Neither live report is a fresh Docker pass for the final rebased head. The latest repairs have source review and CI coverage; their fresh live rerun was not performed.

## Limitations

Generated-audio provenance and heartbeat-decision retention remain outside this change. The latest live campaign did not establish the precise accepted-steering/terminal-cancellation race, genuine interrupt recovery, native multi-call batching, reconnect/replay behavior, Tokenjuice transformation or a Codex backend run. Its complete results and evidence boundaries are retained in the linked report.

prs.title: fix(slack): batch Enterprise Grid messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Enterprise Grid users sending rapid consecutive Slack messages would have every message dispatched separately even when inbound debounce was configured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enterprise events now use the existing team-qualified debounce key and temporarily release each durable ingress lane while the message waits in the in-memory batch. A combined lifecycle settles every durable claim together, while durable ingress remains the sole retry owner so failures cannot race a second in-memory retry.

Commands, media messages, relay delivery, and unqualified workspace routing are unchanged.

## User Impact

Rapid text messages from the same sender in the same Enterprise Grid DM or thread can be combined into one agent turn. Messages from different workspaces remain isolated by `teamId`.

## Evidence

- Before the production change, the new regression failed because the first Enterprise durable ingress lifecycle was never deferred into the batch.
- `pnpm test extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler.test.ts --run` — 25 tests passed.
- The regression verifies combined text, distinct workspace keys, preservation of the scoped client, and settlement of every durable ingress claim.
- Existing retry coverage verifies that Enterprise failures remain owned by durable ingress redelivery rather than a competing in-memory retry.

AI-assisted; I reviewed and understand the lifecycle and retry behavior in this change.

prs.body:
Continuation of #156168, preserving @VACInc’s feature without rewriting the contributor branch. The original stays open until this maintainer-owned continuation lands.

## What Problem This Solves

Adding a second shortcut name for a model currently replaces the name users already rely on.

## User Impact

Models can have several case-insensitive aliases while existing `alias` configurations keep working. CLI writes and provider setup preserve existing names, settings, and alias targets. Additional names work in `/model`, shorthand commands, policy validation, and Doctor/runtime routing.

Per-agent overrides retain replacement semantics. Existing single-alias configs need no migration; remove the new `aliases` field before downgrading to a version that does not support it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional `aliases` array shares the existing alias index. Repairs cover additive writes, capitalization, built-in opt-outs, environment references, policy ownership, and route-scoped retirement. OpenAI setup now checks both alias fields before claiming `GPT` and preserves names already configured on its default model.

The generated config inventory adds exactly four schema paths (**2462 → 2466** against base `11867abe45c8`); channel/plugin counts are unchanged. The assertion ledger only shrinks. The native PR wrapper inventory includes the two new alias modules. No public SDK exports, credential handling, model-policy semantics, or CI limits are relaxed.

Original feature and contributor credit: Vito (@VACInc).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7b5079bf-8f1b-4f52-b581-4740112e2505)

## Evidence

**Provider setup and stored-config compatibility:** the actual registered OpenAI API-key method runs through the plugin registry, a source-fenced config write, disk reload, alias resolution, and CLI model selection. The test uses a synthetic existing-profile input; it does not claim live vendor authentication or inference.

| Secondary `gpt` alias | Redirected to the OpenAI default | Original target retained |

Both persistence cases also retain model parameters and the explicit policy. Existing-profile credential conversion is not invoked. The secondary-alias regression failed against the old writer after real setup and reload, not a mocked config write.

- **41 config/persistence/CLI tests passed** after the registered-provider repair; **8 OpenAI default-model tests passed**. The other 375 tests in the earlier 414-test feature/cron batch remain unchanged.
- **Full OpenAI plugin suite:** 1,382 passed, one skipped.
- **Doctor:** 133 tests passed. The old expectation enabled Codex for an alias that the actual runtime already resolved to Anthropic. The unknown-alias fallback remains covered; two new runtime/Doctor agreement cases fail against the old Doctor owner and pass here. No production fallback was added to preserve the obsolete expectation.
- **Wrapper:** 14 extracted-runtime/dependency tests and three source-closure tests passed. The actual missing-module failure was reproduced before adding its two source inventory entries.
- **Placement fixture:** the required empty `policyConfig` is now supplied; its exact Gateway typecheck and all three lifecycle cases pass. Assertions and deadlines are unchanged.
- **Independent P3 AutoReview:** the feature and substantive follow-up repairs are scoped-clean. No hostile behavior identified in the reviewed changes. Core/extension typechecks, graph boundaries, dead-export scans and policy guards passed; the final mechanical callback rename cleared the lint finding, and core/extension lint passed.
- **Test-audit:** retained real owner-boundary checks, strengthened setup/Doctor coverage, and kept the unknown-alias positive control; no test-only production seams or weakened assertions.
- **Deslop:** kept the shared alias owner and existing setup structure. Pure cron and Doctor fixtures were extracted unchanged to satisfy source-size guards; no limits or coverage were removed.

It has not been restarted. ClawSweeper’s current-head review reports no actionable code or security findings and accepts the setup/config-compatibility evidence, but still requires completed Telegram behavior proof. This is not a merge-ready claim. Previous-head failures were the named Doctor expectation and wrapper inventory omission above, not unexplained failures retried for green.

prs.title: feat(agentsapi): configure an independent API key
prs.body:
## Why

Agents API needs an independent API key setting so operators can preserve their Responses API configuration and choose the credential used by the Agents API plugin.

Related: #156287

## Behavior

Configure `plugins.entries.agentsapi.config.apiKey` with a standard SecretInput, such as `${AGENTS_API_KEY}`. When configured, Agents API uses that credential with the official SDK endpoint. An unavailable, empty or unresolved dedicated key fails without falling back to a provider key or auth profile. No URL setting is required. Configurations that omit the setting retain their existing authentication.

The plugin declares the secret through the existing plugin configuration contract. A generic plugin-owned authentication mode keeps host provider credential preparation out of that attempt. This changes authentication ownership; it does not isolate a trusted plugin from the full runtime configuration. Shared compaction preparation now owns this decision for both direct and queued callers, and the existing BTW model preparation was extracted without changing its behavior.

The generated configuration inventory adds four plugin leaves: the API key plus the standard SecretRef `id`, `provider` and `source` fields. Core and channel inventories are unchanged.

## Validation

- Production build passed. The final runtime source is unchanged from the built commit; subsequent changes only regenerate the configuration inventory and improve test typing/assertions.
- 127 tests passed across 13 files, covering the plugin SDK client/session, auth planning, model preparation, compaction, isolated completion and BTW paths. The final fixture changes also passed their two seven-case suites.
- The dedicated-key regression fails against the original harness because it sends the Responses credential, and passes with this change.
- Independent runtime and final test reviews reported no P0/P1 findings.
- The complete changed-file check is running; its final result will be recorded here.

SDK request tests intercept the network and use synthetic credentials. Live Agents API and Gateway behavior have not been tested in this PR. No running Gateway configuration or service was changed by this task.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the approval clock fixture expiring during database-worker initialization, before it can test native SQLite lock contention.

## User Impact

- Independent **P0–P3 review is scoped-clean** for this exact two-line repair. The clock file remains byte-identical to the verified candidate after conflict resolution; its directly used store/worker clock owners are unchanged.

This proves the controlled initialization mechanism, not the exact historical CI scheduling cause. Current-head CI and review remain required. No timeout, retry, assertion, baseline, production permission, or real-clock behavior was weakened.

prs.body:
Related: #155164 (CI investigation only; its branch is unchanged).

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway tests can report an extra active request root after an agent command finishes because legitimate deferred participant-history persistence has not finished yet.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This is test-only: production persistence, root ownership, cancellation, and timeout semantics are unchanged.

**Validation limitation:** the three targeted cases pass, but the original full shard still has six other failures. Two additional chat-case failures remain causally unresolved; this PR does not claim a green full shard or that those failures are unrelated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The trace shows the RPC and agent-execution references being released while participant persistence still holds the last request-root reference. It eventually releases normally, after the original test polling deadline.

Use the existing async-work scope in a test observer to join real participant recording before sampling the unchanged root count. The observer neither fakes writes nor releases roots. It changes the fixture's async-work scope, not Gateway's separate root-admission context; it proves settlement, not successful persistence or shutdown behavior. An existing agent-send assertion block is extracted to respect the chat test's file-growth guard.

Production delta: **0**. Tests/support: **+41 / −15, net +26** across four files. No timeout increase, retries, worker pin, serial configuration, or production test seam.

Requested and co-authored by @jalehman.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/f5b2cc84-4c31-46f1-94db-58500b7178e8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/dcf1bc38-3863-4fa8-9af5-5e9f705bf7d4)

## Evidence

Proof used main base ab4c2cd05829d56822d57828cdbb8a403eb54c8c, Linux, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.0, and Vitest 5.0.0. The committed patch matches the reviewed/tested diff exactly.

- **Before:** all three targeted assertions fail on unmodified main: detached agent and chat/history expect zero roots but see one; auth-refresh expects two but sees three. Focused run: 64.96s wall.
- **After:** all three pass, both focused and within the original ordered two-worker 81-file selection. Focused wrapper: 56.21s; full replay including its 305-case dispatch prefix: 1154.57s. Full Gateway group: **1159 passed / 6 failed**, with all three original cases passing.
- **Negative control:** removing only the production execution-root release makes all three repaired assertions fail again. Mutation restored. This control preceded the final helper extraction/same-turn count-sampling refinement; the final form is covered by full replay and independent review.
- Participant/root/scope siblings: **55 passed**, 8.47s wrapper. Full chat file: **68 passed**, 96.33s wrapper. The two additional chat cases also passed focused; this does not establish unrelatedness.
- Changed checks passed: formatting, core-test typechecks, lint, boundary/ratchet and dead-export checks. Independent P0–P2 review of the final helper/extraction was scoped-clean. The review did not include the later full-shard result or all unchanged shutdown-owner source.

The [original failing CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35734766276/job/106769552912) was independently reproduced on main without the env-default feature. Existing archive-placement repair #155751 is retained, not duplicated; both formerly failing archive-placement cases now pass.

### Remaining shard failures

Four cases match the preserved earlier main replay: first-turn-binding timeout, orphaned recovery remaining pending, and two shared-token CLI abort-authorization failures. Their causes were not repaired here.

Two additional agent.wait cases failed in the final packed replay: stale-snapshot teardown saw one remaining root, and a following lifecycle-event wait timed out. Both pass focused and full-file runs. Similar deferred persistence and fixture interference are plausible, but unproven; no speculative fixes were added.

No repeated flake-qualification matrix, one-worker before/after benchmark, live Gateway proof, or green hosted CI is claimed. Historical host/cache conditions and actual parallel completion order are not identical.
