prs.title: feat(plugins): bind scheduled work to service lifetimes
prs.body:
**Draft held for restructuring. This combined candidate will not be marked ready or merged. It is being split into the SDK/host contract, plugin family migrations, and a separately justified node-host cut. The private scheduler fallback will be removed.**

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin maintenance timers can outlive the service or account that owns their sockets, state, and delivery work during shutdown or replacement.

## User Impact

Bundled plugin scheduling now closes admission, cancels waiting jobs, and joins admitted callbacks before retirement completes. Domain owners still decide reconnect policy, delivery custody, and final flush ordering. Versioned V2 service, account, binding, and node preparation contracts require the generic scheduler; published V1 APIs remain source-compatible through their documented deprecation window.

Update behavior: normal updates run the existing plugin Doctor owners before the candidate runtime starts. Matrix thread-binding JSON and supported Nostr JSON/replay seeds migrate with backup inventory, byte-preserving archives, conflict checks, and retryable refusal. Direct binary replacements must run `openclaw doctor --fix` before restarting those plugins. Existing canonical rows and delivery custody win; schema versions and retention policies do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

One narrow `PluginServiceSchedulerV1` capability wraps `GatewayScheduler.scope()`. Service, account, and node hosts inject it and retain cleanup custody across deadlines and failures. All bundled consumers migrate together so their timer bookkeeping can be removed without introducing competing lifetime owners. Plugin callbacks run without inherited requester authority. Published scheduler-less monitors and binding managers use one deprecated compatibility factory; expired service leases cannot mint another lifetime.

Doctor now owns the legacy readers removed from Matrix and Nostr runtime. Verified release writers fall inside the `v2026.3.1` retention cutoff, so these migrations remain supported. Matrix retains failed final snapshots and exact migration source claims. Nostr completes only new or partial legacy ingress markers and clears a replay seed only after successful processing and an unchanged observed bus row.

Deliberate behavior corrections include joining ordinary account cleanup after a stop timeout, retaining both node preparation and cleanup failures, awaiting WhatsApp's initial one-shot delivery drain, and canceling FaceTime inspection while keeping native call control available for final cleanup. Existing explicit HTTP route-handoff and service deadline authority fences remain intact.

Production: **+3,916 / -2,013 / net +1,903**, across 207 production files under `src/**` and `extensions/**`, excluding tests, test support/harness/helpers/utilities, E2E, and fixtures. This grows because it adds a versioned lifetime boundary, preserves published contracts, and moves durable normalization into Doctor. No reduction is claimed. Count verified against all 501 files from all pages of the GitHub files API (`per_page=100`). The earlier classifier wrongly omitted `src/plugin-sdk/plugin-test-api.ts`. GitHub uses Myers diff accounting; the local default histogram algorithm also shifted five additions and deletions without changing the net. These totals use the complete GitHub file list and the campaign exclusions, including test-harness files.

Significant overlap: the candidate preserves main's service-start authority changes and Workboard callback guard. The HTTP registry helper is separate from the route-owner hunk in #159448; CLI lifetime extraction is separate from #160442's node CLI changes. Any later conflict will be resolved against current main behavior.

## Evidence

Independent review completed through P2 with no actionable findings remaining. Its sole latest observation assumed Matrix retries lacked queue recovery; both base and candidate already use `persistQueue.catch(...)` before chaining the next write, and the candidate includes a failed-persistence replacement regression. Testbox functional/type/lint checks, canonical SDK API and surface accounting, build and entrypoint profiling, the published-driver update cell, and the real multi-plugin Gateway SIGTERM proof remain pending. Final results and measured costs will replace this pending evidence before readiness.

prs.title: refactor: migrate historical compaction state with Doctor
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Moves supported historical compaction state out of runtime cleanup and history readers without losing retained history or token metrics. Releases including `v2026.7.1` and `v2026.9.3` wrote checkpoints that still serve both responsibilities.

## User Impact

Doctor converts checkpoints into canonical retention references and finite metrics on existing compaction events. Runtime consumes those canonical facts. Transcript text, retained-entry boundaries, unrelated fields, and opaque large integers remain intact. Verified backups retain original bookkeeping and unmatched metrics; Doctor never invents a matching compaction event.

The normal update-time Doctor owns conversion. After direct binary replacement, run `openclaw doctor --fix` before starting the Gateway with historical rows. Prior-head source, build, SDK, package, and the hot/cold **2026.9.7 → candidate** cell passed. The separate replay cell exposed a live Doctor file-input defect that the current head fixes. Fresh validation and all three update cells for the current head are pending; this PR is not yet ready to merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Migration now uses Doctor's existing entry rewrite, backup, cold restore, import-spool, and transaction owners. Ordinary edits and rewinds preserve retention; forks and explicit resets retain their release behavior. Cross-store repair refuses concrete history-custody loss while preserving originals. A cold-to-hot restore may precede a later refusal; immutable archives remain available to database backups. No schema-version change is introduced.

The shared backup owner captures current repair inputs instead of reusing a stale schema rollback snapshot. Canonical repair backs up and revalidates pending validity before admission, then rebuilds its decisions. Existing path validation rejects aliases, including external stores. The path-containment correction accepts a legitimate child named `..keep`. Import backs up an existing destination before restoring cold history or changing metrics.

Published 9.7 copies SQLite into its disposable rehearsal but omits cold archive files. Significant overlap: #164512 shares Doctor repair-snapshot and source-path validation owners. Its integration must retain these final main behaviors. Main's formatter-import and preview-readiness corrections are included in the base; this PR does not duplicate them.

**SDK:** public `SessionEntry` is unchanged and ordinary entry projections omit `retainedHistoryReferences`. Existing `session-store-runtime` writer aliases `recordSessionMetaFromInbound` and `updateLastRoute` return an internal entry type, so their reachable return types gain optional `retainedHistoryReferences: { sessionIds: string[]; artifactPaths: string[] }`. The prior `93dc` SDK comparison reports this additive public effect: no entrypoints added/removed and no direct export changes; 182 exports have changed reachable declaration closures, including internal migration/query declarations. The inspected full digest is `c1327cf8305739de6e15dcbf2832659b950d1c390cac5759fe20fc2d08898322`. No compatibility export is retired. `SessionEntry.compactionCheckpoints` was already removed in #154131 and is absent from stable 9.7 public projections.

Scope is `src/**` and `extensions/**`, excluding tests, support/helpers/utils/harnesses, E2E, and fixtures. The installed update proof found a second rehearsal gap: 9.7 copies admitted SQLite but omits legacy session JSON/JSONL. Replay's SQLite input was canonical while its checkpoints lived in `sessions.json`. The early ACP scan normalized every JSON row merely to find ACP metadata, so strict runtime projection refused it before the transcript importer ran. The current head adds one Doctor-only intermediate shape that preserves checkpoint and locator inputs through file/key/ACP repairs; identity/scalar normalization remains shared and the canonical importer stays strict. The two outer migration cases cover canonical and alias keys, both non-ACP and combined ACP/checkpoint rows, durable ACP metadata, and exact locator/transcript preservation.

Prior package run `run_325041de8a6e3a34c03ef74133baa4c2` passed in 655.218 s and SDK surface run `run_6083178d8a5e4c98eef81fe61a06f391` passed in 5.770 s. At `93dc`, update run `run_87a68ef4af312212faaa7de39e8ecc2f` passed the hot/cold cell (published update 318.383 s, repeat Doctor 12.432 s, candidate Gateway history 18.680 s). Its replay update failed live ACP preflight after 236.530 s; changed databases and retained snapshots were preserved. Custody did not run. That run remains failed overall, with its successful cell attributed only to `93dc`.

Original `93dc` regression run `run_5e20579735d53f531bc42dc9e3192d3c` failed both new cases for the intended ACP/orphan-key refusal in 46.790 s. Fixed production head `b06b3259164848c2de358aea8de70890b870a1e8` passed the complete outer migration suite (72.699 s), legacy-file suite (22.825 s), ACP suite (31.213 s), and round-trip suite (24.646 s) in `run_e93d7736704646d5190c36881f6341b1`. The current test-only child asserts the exact preserved locator; no product assertion, timeout, or retry was relaxed. Those first four passing suites retain their original producer; remaining suites, new delta checks, SDK report, package, and all three new update cells are still pending.


Candidate: `e818d504d7beeaf3372dd2f0236586d89a650cd6`; base: `3f6c1d3a23b90c52b3bf317afc5291e7f1125e32`. Independent Codex reviews are clean through P2, including the final mechanical correction. No local builds or tests ran.

Their original negative controls remain failed at their original heads: the `..keep` control (34.310 s), stale-backup control (24.156 s), and three admission/alias cases (31.118 s). prs.title: refactor(infra): share home-relative path resolution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Effective-home and OS-home path resolution duplicate the same trimming, tilde expansion and absolute-path conversion.

## User Impact

No intended path change. OpenClaw paths still honor `OPENCLAW_HOME`; external CLI paths still use the OS-home resolver. Blank inputs remain blank, ordinary paths do not resolve a home, and named-user forms such as `~another` remain literal. Existing fallback/error behavior and literal dollar characters are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the path-processing body while passing the existing required-home resolver without calling it until the tilde branch. Keep the two public wrappers, their structural option types, and the `resolveUserPath` falsy-input guard. Current normalization-core imports/re-exports, home discovery and the unresolved-tilde option remain with their existing owner.

Production: **-11 lines**. Tests: **+21 lines**. This mechanical refactor needs no changelog entry.

## Evidence

- Primary review covered the complete home owner/tests, config/state and CLI-credential callers, relevant SDK/trajectory path callers, sibling tilde behavior, and the previous literal-dollar and public-wrapper changes.
- Four new public cases cover lazy home resolution and literal named-user tilde handling through both wrappers. Existing tests cover effective/OS home separation, fallback/errors, dollar expansion and falsy user-path inputs. The existing CLI credential test keeps Codex, Gemini and MiniMax files anchored to OS home despite an OpenClaw-home override.
- Direct Codex source inspection at `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: `codex-rs/utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs:1–134`, `codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs:4301–4311`, and `codex-rs/login/src/auth/storage.rs:150–246`. Home selection and path-based storage identity remain outside this refactor; no live Codex/auth claim is made.
- Historical whitespace validation is not new-head runtime proof. No tests, builds or checks were run on the local Mac for this refresh.
- One exact-head P2 review at `6b94c7f7783b13178a942e3fc45214ca834a9e40` completed scoped-clean with no findings. It used the diff and supplied current-owner/dependency context; primary review read the complete owners and callers. Tests were not executed.
- Hosted home tests, canonical normalization-core home tests, credential sibling tests, pinned types/lint/format, aggregate CI and native review remain pending. Stale local dependencies were not reconciled.

Named follow-up from source inspection: **Honor the supplied environment for tilde trajectory directory overrides.** `src/trajectory/paths.ts` reads `OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR` from its supplied environment but resolves its tilde without forwarding that environment. This pre-existing caller behavior is unchanged here; no runtime reproduction is claimed.

## Current-Main Refresh

Signed head `209086ec83d114a4687c6b4578e3a85cf2991e9f` is refreshed onto main `63fa1d2dedac5eb6ffa5ec690457d41e8ac22cd0`. Git range-diff is patch-identical to the reviewed candidate; the unrelated redundant-test deletion already on main remains preserved. The two-file PR scope is unchanged.

The previous [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34822438886) failed two inherited fixtures, not the home-path assertions:

- The [QA attribution fixture timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34822438886/job/103908294166) now includes the fixture-owned docs-root mitigation from [147986](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147986). The original slow phase was not conclusively isolated; new CI must establish the result.
- The [Windows lease replacement failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34822438886/job/103908292218) has the supervisor-owned lease retirement fix from [156049](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156049).

Both canonical commits are included in this base. Fresh exact-head hosted CI passed as recorded below; no old failed run is presented as passing evidence.

## Current-Head CI

[CI for `209086ec83d114a4687c6b4578e3a85cf2991e9f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35956015358) completed successfully, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. [ClawSweeper Revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148092#issuecomment-5661355386) completed on 2026-09-24 at 05:01 UTC for this exact head, with no concrete patch finding. Its remaining request is measured one-worker cost for `src/infra/home-dir.test.ts` and CI seconds.

The retained [preflight log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35956015358/job/107494396861) has no expanded group-to-job mapping, and the run retains no test-plan artifact. The exact execution job and file-specific timing therefore could not be recovered; no standalone one-worker result is claimed. Collect only the missing owner-file cost measurement through the approved remote proof route, without rerunning the complete successful CI suite.

Native tooling qualification, review, preparation and squash remain; no merge or local runtime proof is claimed.

prs.title: feat(gateway): enforce scoped guest models and foreground-only work
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156269.

## What Problem This Solves

Shared Gateway operators need to offer guests approved models and bounded conversation work with understandable Stop, cleanup and restart outcomes.

## User Impact

Guest restrictions reuse the existing role `modelPolicy`. Accepted work must satisfy both its immutable original ceiling and current policy. Automatic selection chooses an allowed route for that caller without changing shared staff pins; explicitly forbidden choices and unsupported routes visibly refuse.

Foreground-only guest work preserves conversation history and drafts. Stop holds admission until owned cleanup settles. Restart records a visible stopped notice without automatically replaying work; continuing requires a fresh authenticated request. Uncertain sandbox cleanup prevents reuse.

Catalogs, session metadata and UI choices respect the same restrictions. Narrow session events require current identity and every referenced session’s live sharing fence. Unrestricted staff behavior, defaults and workspace locations remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model authority, foreground admission, native allocation/retirement and session/UI access must agree throughout execution and cleanup. The existing policy owner carries authority through nested work and binds logical selection to the actual provider delegate. This does not certify additional native runtimes or Codex routes.

<details>
<summary>Change scope against the frozen base</summary>

Production/tooling: 334 paths, +13,019/−5,772 lines (net +7,247). Tests/helpers: 151 paths, +21,257/−965 (net +20,292). Production growth implements the four shared authority, foreground, native lifecycle and session-access boundaries above; it does not add a separate policy configuration or database schema.

</details>

Existing JSON records gain `foregroundRun` and `retirementPolicy` metadata. No new `roles.models` configuration, database, table, column or schema-version bump is introduced. **Older-binary rollback of candidate state remains unqualified:** restart, backup and updater evidence do not establish equivalent enforcement after downgrade.

https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/74 remains a separate, unaccepted draft. Source landing does not deploy this feature or change operator access infrastructure.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `addc4ec21a4a7226530e612b8f4881626e0920a1`, tree `8fdca6d8a4bb3749a9de27290f1d2c50cf2672b4`.

- Actual private-QA build passed in 5m52.411s; all four real Linux UI scenarios passed with no skips. Strict same-toolchain startup-budget comparison against frozen base `0c7d77cd` passed.
- Five-pass scoped production review at `d63b7688` was clean. Subsequent diagnostic and transcript-selector changes are test-only and received scoped review.
- Historical native final-effect coverage: Docker7 and Podman6 passed at `36c5fc4862ad09b22bf63edcec9a0da9ccaa0c76`, with no skips. The 444-case composite remains revision-bound: 299 at `eda43e0eacb294d6b4ec8cad0d7720b522503947` and 145 at `ee23da7771abd28bfcd953e2ef918805d38fa4df`; these are not an exact-head aggregate.
- Exact-head GitHub CI remains pending publication and native gate admission.

Restart checks count one transcript notice, excluding its separate accessibility announcement, and verify reload, no replay and a fresh request.

<summary>Real Linux UI: Stop, cleanup uncertainty and restart</summary>

prs.title: improve(runtime): avoid unused flow config preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Async task-flow operations construct a config reader and copy environment state even though they never use that reader.

## User Impact

Flow operations spend less CPU preparing unused configuration state, especially with larger environments. Run visibility and config freshness checks remain unchanged.

This is a scoped tradeoff: the large-environment run-read control used **8.90% more CPU** in the paired median, with roughly **61 MiB higher current RSS** after warm calls and final disposal. These costs are included below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep config-reader capture on run get/list/resolve, before their first await. Flow operations retain their state admission checks without constructing the unused reader. Mutation paths and public APIs stay unchanged.

This avoids reader preparation and environment copying; it does not claim to eliminate config-file reads.

## Evidence

The measurements below remain bound to the original `f0b9eb02b4d551e12d4d078e853c401f753ab1f6` head and its `01457af6876f1c4be61f492d86b0ac7fc596853e` base. Current head `bdd81c5b8db53b15d785a51af9c1ce9593c717d5` retains the identical production/test patch reapplied on main `12fe32ebbb77d90a2dae6c093ecfdbbce851ff81`, incorporating the canonical Knip script-root and SwiftLint fixes. It also repairs the embedded-writer contention test described below. The original performance measurements were not rerun or relabeled for the changed head. Exact-head [hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35859135278) completed successfully for `bdd81c5b8db53b15d785a51af9c1ce9593c717d5`; skipped checks do not supply execution proof.

[Native Linux proof run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35841621557), using Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.0, Vitest 5 and the repository's canonical infra project with its native fork pool. Baseline `01457af6876f1c4be61f492d86b0ac7fc596853e`; candidate source is exactly the two-file change committed as `f0b9eb02b4d551e12d4d078e853c401f753ab1f6`.

- Full `src/infra/sqlite-worker-task-runtime.test.ts`, in original order: candidate **22/22 passed**. Baseline passed 21/22; its sole expected failure is the new capture-count assertion. The Vitest JSON report’s end-minus-start wall span was **26.784 s candidate / 20.749 s baseline**, one complete functional execution per arm. The enclosing native command intervals were **59.516 s candidate / 50.454 s baseline**. These are separate from both the framework file spans and the repeated warm CPU measurements below.
- The existing real-worker parity case still checks all **14 public reads** and now records reader captures falling **14 → 4**. The delegated observer is restored before output/count assertions.
- The bare-owner selector-drift case passes in both arms: a pending read cannot silently switch between two valid config sources. That pending read does not publish replacement config; a subsequent fresh read can adopt it.
- Two untimed count workers and ten uninstrumented timing workers completed. Every flow count phase drops reader captures to zero; run-read capture counts stay unchanged. Output parity is checked before counts or timings are accepted.

Five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs; 25 warmups and 100 awaited calls per warm row. Small environments had 208 keys; large environments added 2,048 keys, for 2,256 total. Values below are **medians of paired percentage changes**, not ratios of separate arm medians.

| Warm operation | Wall time | Process CPU | CPU lower in |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Small flow list | −79.93% | −79.02% | 5/5 pairs |
| Large flow list | −99.45% | −99.26% | 5/5 pairs |
| Small run get, control | −10.30% | −11.82% | 3/5 pairs |
| Large run get, control | +7.70% | +8.90% | 2/5 pairs |

Controls were mixed: large-run warm CPU ranged from −6.87% to +24.13%. Its first-call CPU paired median increased 46.09 ms, its two-call pair CPU increased 4.35 ms, and its timed disposal CPU increased 8.78 ms. The two-call CPU control was worse in all five pairs.

Large-run current RSS paired medians were **+60.57 MiB after warm calls** and **+60.92 MiB after final state disposal**, higher in all five pairs. Whole-worker peak RSS increased **15.06 MiB** in the paired median, higher in four of five pairs. Four ordered cases share a worker and prior outputs, so these process-wide measurements do not establish allocation, leak or GC causality.

“First call” starts after imports and fixture preparation; it is not process startup. The two-call phase uses already-warm handles separated by a microtask. Timed disposal joins plugin retirement, database closure and runtime reset; state cleanup and environment restoration follow and are included in the final RSS observation.

The complete result archive, source/runtime/dependency joins, terminal/control receipts and external provider/process custody were verified. The outer tool truncated console output, so full console-byte retention is not claimed. Scoped independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; formatting and whitespace checks passed.

The later [hosted CI run 35853098853](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35853098853) exposed a fixture failure in the embedded-writer contention case: a Gateway lock inspection could exhaust its 15 ms wall-clock budget before the expected writer-contention error. The saved failure does not distinguish the initial inspection from the catch-time reinspection. The test now supplies one logical clock to those inspections and the existing acquisition clock/sleep hooks, while retaining real lock files, SQLite coordination, the live writer PID, and the exact 15 ms contention assertion. It immediately observes rejection of the first run, restores the clock spy, and always releases and awaits the original run in `finally`.

The exact fixture change committed in `bdd81c5b8db53b15d785a51af9c1ce9593c717d5` passed **129/129 tests** in one complete, original-order `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` execution through the canonical commands project on native Linux x64, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.0, and Vitest 5. The repaired case passed once; there were no skips, todos, suite failures, or unhandled errors. The enclosing test command took **25.571 s**; the framework file span was **1.050 s**. This proves the logical contention contract, not a 15 ms wall-time bound or a performance improvement. The complete 12-member result archive, full console output, unchanged source/dependency endpoints, and final provider/process custody were verified. Fresh scoped review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. No baseline or performance experiment was repeated.

[Hosted CI run 35844478752](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35844478752) had a **20 min 12 s** workflow metadata window (09:42:06–10:02:18 UTC). Its dependency gate failed on two script entrypoints unchanged by this PR; the aggregate gate also failed. Installation and the production dependency scan passed. The elapsed time covers the whole workflow. Hosted file/shard mapping and file-specific timing were not recovered. This is the original-head failure, not a result for the repaired head. The canonical Knip fixes, including [PR #156415](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156415), are now incorporated. Successor exact-head CI passed as linked above; this does not relabel the original failed workflow or rerun the historical performance comparison. Native landing remains outstanding.

This proof does not establish a Gateway-wide or end-to-end application speedup.

prs.title: fix(doctor): preserve current owners during restored-index replay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes newer session ownership and activity being rolled back when `openclaw doctor --fix` sees a restored copy of a previously imported legacy session index.

## User Impact

Repeating recovery preserves the current session owner, lifecycle, and activity. A verified replay may retire redundant recovery files or append a missing transcript tail; ambiguous or reordered history stays available for inspection. There is no configuration or schema-version change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The import owner now recognizes completed recovery receipts from the same producing target and checks the current owner before replay. Already-present events must match in their original order; appending unseen events additionally requires an exact prefix. Source verification and a disk-backed staging pass are reused within each bounded batch.

The legacy import flow is extracted into its own module so receipt fencing, batching, and import accounting have one owner. Production changes add 644 net lines for these ownership and source-verification contracts; regression tests add 1,102 lines.

## Evidence

- The restored-index regression fails against the original production source: one stale entry is imported instead of zero.
- 73 focused cases pass across completed replay, shared recovery owners, the SQLite importer, and mainline retained-plugin conflict recovery.
- The replay regression file passes 18/18 without a wall-clock ordering delay: 58.36s Vitest duration, 63.39s measured wall time; the cross-run receipt case completes in 2.717s.
- Independent extraction review found no changed lifecycle ordering or new import cycle.
- Core types passed at `f5da6c9800cd9262f8d198df9e2f0da54e7c4086`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35821381778
- Affected test types and structural guards passed at `ef972a62a136e47872c2330fcd19b51fdc344c76`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35822246995
- Candidate `9be118123461bab044b024b6fd51489cc99e8dce` passed corrected test lint plus the full build, native-module, runtime-closure, SDK, and UI checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35823205096. A later portal-sync warning occurred after the successful Testbox stopped; the product checks had already passed.
- Exact head `64fa30d55330bb7400755b5b793e278ea11c25aa` differs only by removing the unnecessary 2ms test delay; the focused 18-case replay suite passes as measured above.
- Autoreview's actionable findings were repaired. Two remaining reports were independently adjudicated: complete ordered containment performs no append, and authoritative receipts cannot contain conflicting suffix IDs. Identical repeats are repaired before replay; differing duplicate IDs mark the original import incomplete and therefore cannot authorize a replay.

Related follow-up: intentionally activating a retained inactive transcript prefix through suffix deletion needs projection rebuilding; this repair does not change that behavior.

prs.title: fix(auth): keep sessions pinned when their selected account is unavailable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A session could silently switch accounts after its explicitly selected auth profile was removed.

## User Impact

A compatible user-selected account remains pinned. If its credential is removed, admission reports the unavailable account; restore it or explicitly select another account. Existing credentials can still rotate during temporary cooldown or provider failure. Missing automatic selections can be cleared and reselected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three asynchronous selection paths prepare one scoped provider fact before deciding whether to preserve a missing user pin. Published runtime and persisted owner facts retain precedence over configuration. The existing synchronous SDK/session-writer contract remains synchronous.

The shared preparation owner preserves isolated and personal-account boundaries, raw selected-credential precedence, reader cleanup, and rejection when a session selection changes during an awaited read. Documentation distinguishes removed credentials from temporary failures.

No stored schema, serialization format, migration, or dependency change is introduced by the auth delta. The provider-owner reader projects existing credentials; it adds no storage writer or serialized-field definition.

## Evidence

### Current Head Qualification (2026-09-27)

Current head: `543bc3ca7a92b1f1b10e00752c1345a588517d5f`, with 85 changed paths. It contains 20 commits beyond the previously recorded `1ac16808` candidate, changing 63 paths in that successor delta. **Not ready to merge:** the visible current-head CI gate is pending ("Waiting for CI"); returned exact-head runs are metadata/review workflows, not application CI. The [current ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155849#issuecomment-5781105221) still identifies missing final-effect proof. The results below remain predecessor evidence, not qualification of this successor.

Scoped source review found no introduced defect in the five auth-preparation owners inspected. The early selected-profile check runs before optional catalog discovery, with native-owner revalidation first and a fresh later auth-store read. It does not establish an account-identity fence across every later await. The two extracted Codex startup helpers preserve their prior bodies and timeout behavior. This is not a complete 85-path review or runtime proof.

Against inspected main `b8bf36603553bb2136153c7f46c39784b33018fe`, early profile admission remains absent, so this audit does not establish supersession. Preserve main's newer OAuth-flow policy and canonical late auth planner when integrating. The endpoint-alias test's later planner call does not retain the explicit pin; it does not directly prove pinned endpoint eligibility end to end.

Remaining successor-bound evidence: bounded configured-account removal, distinct-account final transcript effects, no alternate-account provider I/O, an independent account-A control, and deliberate recovery of the original persisted session with the unchanged assertions below. Preserve completed evidence and rerun only proof made necessary by the changed owner boundary. Existing branch/proof ownership is unchanged.

### Retained Predecessor Evidence

Predecessor candidate: signed `1ac168089ddde916f1a9ab931c34bf88de0d9a58`, above frozen integration base `409f0a95993d2255ab5b2514771cc1cc5e910d58`. All 26 changed paths and the final implicit-void Vitest hook correction received source review. **That predecessor's Gateway proof and hosted CI failed; neither result qualifies the successor.**

Predecessor native proof on Darwin/Node 26.7:

| Workload | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Whole Codex app-server fixture file | 23 passed; no failed, pending or todo tests |
| One invocation of all 15 owner/sibling files | 558 passed across all 15 files; no failed, pending or todo tests |
| All three Gateway product cases, including native build prerequisites | 1 passed, 2 failed |

The passing Gateway case repaired mixed legacy auth into SQLite and sent the selected OAuth profile to the app-server fixture. Both removal cases first recorded a uniquely completed pinned-account turn with matching native fixture account evidence. The configured-account removal then failed because the session lifecycle error was `LLM request timed out.` instead of the bounded unavailable-profile error. The distinct-account removal passed the preceding failed-session/bounded-error checks, then failed because no captured `session.message` matched the combined current-run/failed-status predicate. This does not prove that no transcript event existed. These failures are not yet attributed to a verified owner defect.

The later no-alternate-account-I/O assertions, independent-A control and deliberate recovery of the original session were **not reached**. The recovery assertions remain unchanged: original session ID/revision, explicit persisted A/user pin, unique completed A trace, persisted `done` with the new run ID and cleared error, and matching original-key chat-final. No timeout, assertion, worker setting or guard was weakened; no retry was run.

The failed Gateway command returned raw/managed/launcher exit 1 after all owned children joined. All 16 independent source/input afterchecks passed. Complete raw streams, native nested reports and their recorded modes/hashes are retained: 72 files, 11,896,551 bytes. Receipt-read status is separate from workload status; the overall proof remains **FAILED**.

## Observed Predecessor Test Cost

These are timings from the normal proof invocations, not isolated benchmarks or estimates of incremental PR cost.

| Workload | Managed wall time | Native wrapper / Vitest / file timing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Earlier whole resolved-pin file, 23 passed | 22.859 s | wrapper 22.54 s; Vitest 20.85 s; JSON file span 0.2098 s (default report 214 ms) |
| Whole fixture, 23 passed | 9.758 s | wrapper 9.47 s; Vitest 7.76 s; file 1.508 s |
| ONE15, 558 passed | 158.710 s | wrapper 158.45 s; seven native shards plus report merge |
| Gateway, 1 passed / 2 failed | 427.002 s | Vitest 423.70 s; file 105.342 s; includes native build/setup |

Gateway setup separately reported a 290.5 s native build, a 3.1 s fixture build and 15.137 s worker preparation after a cache miss. These components must not be added to the already inclusive command wall time. Its three case durations were 53.972 s, 23.638 s and 27.729 s; the two failures ended before their remaining assertions.

ONE15 native per-file reported durations:

| File | Tests | Duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts` | 138 | 28.724 s |
| `store-owner-publication.test.ts` | 46 | 14.471 s |
| `store.scope.test.ts` | 4 | 0.012 s |
| `usage.inherited-owner.test.ts` | 8 | 2.298 s |

In `gateway-auth-recovery.test.ts`, the rate-limit turn made two HTTP 429 requests; the subsequent auth turn returned an error with zero provider requests. Earlier lifecycle-contention warnings do not establish its actual terminal cause, database operation or lock holder. Diagnosis remains open; this is distinct from the local Gateway failures.
- The same run's routing shard passed, including resolved-pin 23 and model-selection 93. Available shared cost is 705 s for its whole CI job and 39.92 s for the routing shard; neither is isolated or incremental cost for this PR.

[PR #155929](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155929) closed as its duplicate. No additional auth-branch integration or duplicate repair is claimed.

prs.title: fix(update): Gateway stays stopped for minutes while package updates re-hash the install
prs.body:
Related: #160693

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: package updates keep the Gateway stopped for minutes on large installs because publication (`package-swap`, about 164 s on a 4-CPU Docker/OverlayFS host) re-hashes both ~38k-file package generations at every checkpoint.

## User Impact

User impact: shorter Gateway downtime during package updates driven by this version onward, with the same content verification wherever a package generation becomes or stays authoritative. The published 2026.9.6 driver's first hop is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`publish()` calls `inspect()` four times with one launcher, and each call fully hashed two generations: 8 full-tree hashes while the Gateway is down, although the owner itself only renames the roots between checks. The hash walk already records a complete metadata receipt for its own concurrency check. The owner now keeps that receipt (per pass, in memory, keyed by recorded fingerprint and current root identity) and uses a complete metadata sweep at intermediate checkpoints and for backups about to be removed. Every authority boundary still hashes content: first publish check, final live check, preflight, rollback/disarm, and the live package check before retirement. A shared writable mmap can defer timestamp updates, so metadata alone never proves content at those boundaries. Any receipt mismatch falls back to a full hash and strict equality. No journal, schema, fingerprint format or marker change.

Update behavior (published driver x candidate): 9.6's shipped driver runs its own first hop unchanged; publications driven by the fixed version do 3 full hashes instead of 8 (plus 1 instead of 2 for same-owner retirement).

## Evidence

- Regressions: hash-count per publish ([1,2] reads for previous/candidate, fails on main at [4,4]); a false-unchanged receipt at the final live check still refuses byte tampering; existing tamper cases and the concurrent metadata-sweep race keep refusing.
- Focused publication/activation/integrity suites: 200 tests / 10 files pass; tsgo, oxfmt, oxlint clean; Codex autoreview clean at P2 after the mmap finding was addressed.
- Local synthetic publish of 20,001 files per generation: 18.3 s -> 8.9 s.
- Lane timings (4 CPU, running-Gateway `update-restart-auth` and `update-first-hop-compat-2026.9.6`): pending, will be added.

prs.title: perf(tooling): stream native declaration outputs
prs.body:
## Outcome
Closed without landing: the full SDK comparison did not justify this optimization.

Matched ABBA runs on one Linux worker, identical pinned install and 7 GiB kernel scopes: baseline 90.849/101.085 seconds and 6,894,493,696/6,752,440,320 peak bytes; callback emission 107.297/100.952 seconds and 6,784,827,392/6,727,839,744 peak bytes. Average peak fell about 1%; average runtime rose about 8.5%. Every run completed with zero kernel OOM events and 11,165 declaration files.

Byte hashes differed. The reverse pair localized 23 differing files; inspected samples include declarations of the modified tooling itself and property-order changes in inferred types. Full byte parity is not established, so this is not an accepted output-equivalence result. Focused native fixtures passed, but the measured full-workload benefit is too small to justify the extra staging path.

## Proposed change (not landed)
Emit native declarations through the compiler's filesystem callback into the existing private staging directory. Previously `emitToString` retained every output string in Go and returned the whole collection while the semantic program was still alive.

The same Program, diagnostic queries, roots and compiler options remain. Output paths are admitted before staging; callback write failures are latched until RPC completion. The native compiler exits and the existing input seal succeeds before Node materializes the returned text map. Callers retain ownership of final publication.

Pinned TypeScript supports [host callback emission](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/blob/f29aeb9f825d96feea27841f3f7342dbf0df68a8/tsc/internal/api/session.go#L3277); [emitToString collects all output](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/blob/f29aeb9f825d96feea27841f3f7342dbf0df68a8/tsc/internal/api/session.go#L3355).

## Dependency
Stacked on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160152. Land that prerequisite and retarget to main before merging.

## Validation
Candidate: `a155b907e0205936412b278caa6b760ca040f309`.

prs.title: improve(ui): reduce typing latency during streamed replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long streamed replies interrupt typing and scrolling when pane commits force synchronous transcript layout inside animation-frame callbacks.

## User Impact

Pane commits remain batched while input gets its rendering opportunity first. The measured comparison reduces p95 input-to-next-frame latency from 35.05 to 12.35 ms, renderer task time 10.8%, and long tasks 5.6%. Reader position, native footer clamps, prefills, voice controls, and responsive navigation retain their contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Lit scheduling boundary resumes connected pane commits through a MessageChannel task after the input frame. Cancellation closes both ports and releases the owned waiter; retired deliveries cannot release newer work. Initial rendering and visibility catch-up remain immediate. The transcript still observes geometry synchronously around each actual DOM commit, preserving native-clamp versus reader-motion authority.

The affected owners now preserve their asynchronous contracts:

- Captured reader anchors finish measured prepend corrections before another paint; a dependency-free touch-state type keeps this handoff acyclic.
- Route-prefill cleanup waits for the consuming pane's commit and rechecks presentation ownership. Menu insertion updates the native editor immediately so another keystroke cannot overwrite it from stale text.
- A quick voice tap reconciles the actual readonly attribute through Lit's existing live directive, even when the intermediate pressed state never renders.
- Responsive sidebar focus restoration waits for the active, presented pane to create its navigation toggle, then rechecks connection, route, pane and focus ownership.
- Comment deletion and save restore focus after the attachment commit and sibling pin geometry work; retiring a pane or newer user focus cancels the pending restoration. This fixes first-of-two deletion losing focus when an unkeyed list removes the old second-row button.
- Composer submenu focus follows the committed view and the dropdown item’s own update completion. It preserves newer focus intent instead of focusing an outgoing item in the earlier input frame. Native show/hide events always update the owner; stale rendered props cannot discard a close event and reopen the attachment picker.

Paused-clock E2E fixtures explicitly deliver one virtual render frame; the compaction test retains exactly 177 seconds total. Other affected fixtures wait for their visible row, retired marker, or detached rail before taking snapshots. Existing behavioral assertions remain; no production scheduler bypass, real sleep, timeout increase, or new polling was added. The stream-event scheduler remains because it also batches persistence and input-arrival work before Lit invalidation.

## Evidence

Final candidate: `8e704b16db0674b83440a0d0685334561a3f0a0a`, source tree `d6e1026699955830c2290ce79ecc117f897cc46d`. Performance measurements below use scheduling-equivalent parent `389a0f07c186`; the final repairs only change submenu/comment focus and E2E synchronization, with no scheduling changes.

Interleaved A/B/A/B on one Blacksmith Testbox, Chromium 144 at 4× CPU throttle, production bundles, unchanged l72 mock-Gateway harness. The control restores the unbatched pane owner from then-current main `c0e6951d6f02`; all other controls match the candidate. Each trial renders the same 16,201-character reply in 676 chunks while typing.

| Median metric | Unbatched control | Batched owner (`389a0f07c186`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Runtime | 64.36 s | 56.34 s |
| Long tasks | 368.50  | 348.00  |
| Worst task per run | 215.00 ms | 188.50 ms |
| p95 frame gap | 125.00 ms | 133.35 ms |
| p95 input-to-next-frame | 35.05 ms | 12.35 ms |
| Renderer task time | 62,036.84 ms | 55,347.41 ms |
| Style time | 13,639.64 ms | 14,155.55 ms |
| Layout time | 12,928.10 ms | 13,238.03 ms |

Tradeoff: p95 frame gap is 8.35 ms higher in this block. This improves input responsiveness without claiming uniformly smoother animation. The producer is browser-owned and slows under load; this is fixed-reply UI proof, not Gateway capacity. Input latency measures event-to-next-animation-frame delay rather than physical display latency.

A separate interleaved published-parent/`389a0f07c186` comparison confirms the interaction repairs preserve the existing fast-input behavior: `86302ff19d2a` → `389a0f07c186` runtime 51.87 → 50.49 s; long tasks 347.5 → 329.5; worst task 163.5 → 179.5 ms; p95 frame gap 116.70 → 124.95 ms; p95 input 11.15 → 11.25 ms. Absolute timings vary between blocks; use their matched controls. All eight trials delivered 676 chunks and the final sentinel, had no page errors, and finished at zero bottom distance.

Validation on the final source:

- All 220 focused pane/anchor/composer/page/navigation/comment cases passed, 17.56 s wall; browser ownership/annotations 23/23 passed, 9.86 s.
- All 233 targeted mock-Gateway E2E cases across 32 files passed: the previous 80-case set in 129.34 s, the 61-case menu/tool/comment/retirement/selection set in 105.44 s, and the latest 92-case failure cohort in 72.42 s.
- The latest reported regressions reproduced as 18 failures / 92 cases on the published head; the same source with the unbatched pane passed 92/92. Product repairs fix menu event admission and commit-aware focus. Fixture repairs await committed panels, disclosure bodies, selected models, closed dialogs, and keyboard-history updates, while retaining existing value/focus/resource assertions and exact virtual-time budgets.
- The avatar alignment fixture returned `{}` for the required membership response, causing the sharing header to throw before committing the transcript. It now supplies the required membership fields; no production avatar, geometry, or fallback change was added.
- A broader Testbox sweep retained 357 passing files across an interrupted run and a bounded follow-up. Exact-head hosted CI supplies the complete UI E2E inventory check; its discovered failures are included in the targeted cohort above.
- `pnpm check:import-cycles && pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: zero runtime and type cycles, 43.36 s.
- Full-branch changed-lane gate passed in 1,140.55 s with 0 warnings and 0 errors. The final ten-file repair also passed its changed-lane gate against that verified head in 469.07 s, with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- Production UI build/startup budget passed, 0.18 s: startup JS 370,984 B / 371,332 B, 348 B headroom; startup CSS 50,247 B / 51,200 B.
- Deslop clean; independent Codex review of the full candidate and subsequent repairs clean through P2. Existing E2E cases reproduce the product regressions; no new cases or timeout increases were added.

A separate cron fixture typecheck failure reproduced on main and was fixed upstream in `c0e6951d6f02`, which this branch includes. No duplicate cron repair was added. The main-refresh commit published concurrently had exactly the same source tree as the locally tested merge; its work was preserved.

Total PR delta: production +219/−76 (net +143), tests +329/−153 (net +176), including an intact scenario extraction required by the existing file-size cap. Necessary growth owns cancellation and draft/focus authority across deferred commits; superseded microtask cleanup, duplicate lookup logic, and a redundant navigation condition were removed. The assertion ratchet also shrank by one stale zero-count row after the old menu cast was deleted. No Gateway protocol, config options, or database changes.

Remote proof: provider `blacksmith-testbox`; final lease `tbx_01m3g4zves4x6ge7tppm5vk7bw` ([Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36283293762)). Earlier evidence used `tbx_01m3fysyga6305zgkb5etpm9gt`, `tbx_01m3frgf7e6xhc8n6qb869qs4m`, and `tbx_01m3fjgqkmch3mtrkqvhy7sfyq`; replacements followed provider-ended leases. Commands: targeted `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` invocations, both cycle checks, `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, production UI builds, `pnpm ui:check-performance`, and the l72 A/B harness.

<details>
<summary>Inspected synthetic before/after captures</summary>

The capabilities action preserves the unbatched baseline appearance. Crops omit unrelated lower composer controls; the unchanged E2E assertions prove focus, insertion, and every-frame history anchoring. Captured on the initial repair before the behavior-preserving owner extraction.

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse stable tool catalog fingerprints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway repeatedly hashes unchanged tool catalogs while setting up concurrent requests, including freshly rebuilt tool objects with identical definitions.

## User Impact

Less main-thread CPU during tool-catalog registration. Tool selection, execution policy, current executor binding, and per-run catalog lifetimes are preserved. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fingerprint owner retains bounded, detached descriptor snapshots and their existing streaming digests. Every lookup compares current descriptor content with the owned snapshot, so rebuilt objects can reuse a fingerprint while in-place nested schema edits invalidate it. The cache never retains executable tools. Catalog registration, restriction, and refresh all use this owner; the former local fingerprint implementation is removed.

Retention is capped at 256 entries, each admitted under a 64 KiB accounting budget charging UTF-16 strings/keys and per-value overhead, with bounded depth. Proxies, accessors, unsupported objects, cycles, and oversized definitions use the original streaming hash path. Remote/client schemas retain their existing nontraversing replacement-token contract. This preserves the allocation improvement from #158805 while avoiding repeated digests for unchanged definitions.

## Evidence

Five interleaved before/after pairs in one process, after 100 warmup requests per implementation. Each sample registers 1,000 fresh catalog lifetimes with 40 synthetic tools containing 12 schema fields each, through the actual `applyToolCatalogCompaction` entry point:

| Metric | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median main-thread CPU/request | 0.514 ms | 0.348 ms | 32.3% |
| Median wall time/request | 0.532 ms | 0.350 ms | 34.3% |

CPU uses `process.threadCpuUsage()` to separate host scheduling noise. Same-process peak RSS was approximately 555 MiB; this does not isolate cache memory. This is focused catalog-stage proof, not a new swarm run or a claim about Gateway-wide latency.

- The new cross-request reuse regression fails on the original implementation because it computes two descriptor hashes instead of one. The candidate also preserves fresh executor binding and distinct per-run counter scopes.
- Regression coverage includes in-place nested input/output-schema edits, proxy traversal counts, getter reads, oversized-schema fallback, and preservation of the existing error for arrays that lose their iterator. The existing suite covers remote-schema nontraversal, hook binding, duplicate IDs, catalog cleanup, tool restrictions, and dynamic availability.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-search-catalog-fingerprint.test.ts src/agents/agent-tool-availability.test.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: final 170 tests passed, 26.62 seconds wall.
- Standalone changed-file cost: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-search-catalog-fingerprint.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: final 5 tests passed, 58.47 seconds wall (48.76 seconds Vitest duration; 27 ms test execution). Wall time is dominated by compilation/imports; the runtime boundary is needed to prove the current registered executor runs.
- The first changed-lane check caught a test-only TypeScript arity error in direct invocation of the catalog’s union-typed executor. The regression now uses `ToolSearchRuntime.callValue`; the exact affected typecheck passed in 2.50 seconds. Final `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passed in 688.88 seconds wall, including core typechecking, all 25 test typecheck groups, lint, and selected repository guards.
- Deslop: inspected all changed hunks; no unrelated cleanup or compatibility wrappers added.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the final head: scoped clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Production LOC: +159/−44, net +115. Tests: +109/−0. The additional code owns detached snapshot capture/comparison, bounded retention, and safe fallback; it avoids changing plugin schema mutability or executor ownership.
- Full build/swarm and hosted CI completion are outside this component proof. The requested 200-open-PR overlap check found no PR touching the production files.

prs.title: perf(infra): create worker task signals only for host exchanges
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Busy Gateways spend main-thread CPU creating and aborting unused signals for ordinary worker tasks.

## User Impact

**The targeted worker stage improves, but the full Gateway workload regressed in both measured pairs; that regression remains unresolved.** Noninteractive worker tasks allocate less and complete with less host-side bookkeeping. Existing cancellation, caller context, native settlement, and host-exchange signal behavior are preserved. Protocol, configuration, schemas, stored data, and update behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker pool's task-lifetime signal is consumed only by host-exchange callbacks, but every task eagerly created an AbortController and aborted it on completion. The pool now creates that controller immediately before the first actual host callback and reuses it until task completion. Noninteractive tasks keep their existing external cancellation path and no longer create an unused controller or AbortError.

The profile-driven investigation traced the residual main-thread bucket to its nearest synchronous application callers. It contains many small owners plus scheduler time with no recorded application ancestor; it is not one 0.29 ms chunk handler. Worker task completion was the largest actionable individual owner. This is a bounded improvement, not a claim that it eliminates Gateway stalls.

## Evidence

- Focused worker lifecycle tests: 72/72 passed across worker-task-pool.test.ts, worker-task-pool.owned.test.ts, and worker-task-pool.cleanup.test.ts with one worker; final runner wall 100.48 s, predominantly cold fixture compilation. Changed-file cost: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/worker-task-pool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 43/43 in 38.85 s wall. Existing cancellation and settlement cases remain intact. The existing two-exchange case additionally proves one task signal stays live across callbacks and aborts at successful completion, without another worker boot.
- Local interleaved component benchmark: five A/B pairs, 20,000 real noninteractive worker tasks per run after 2,000 warmup tasks, Node 26.9.0. Uninstrumented median main-thread CPU 344.153 -> 254.192 ms (17.208 -> 12.710 us/task, 26.14% lower); median wall 463.73 -> 370.92 ms. Shared-host variation is substantial. Separate counting runs show controller allocations and aborts deterministically 20,000 -> 0 in every pair. Median sampled process RSS in timing runs 90.31 -> 89.27 MiB.
- Production LOC: +5/-4 (net +1), because teardown must skip restoring a caller context when no signal was exposed. Tests: +7/-1 (net +6).
- Deslop: no additional changes needed. Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, zero findings.

- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passed, exit 0, 935.48 s wall on the shared host, including core and all 25 dependent test type graphs, formatting, lint, three export scans, and boundary guards. The first attempt exposed an existing stale install (`@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.18.2 instead of locked 0.20.0); one frozen install corrected it before the passing run. No tracked dependency files changed.


### Same-box Gateway profiles

One four-core Blacksmith Testbox, `tbx_01m3ep9q9zmz7wnr73t10xanxa`, Node 26.9.0/pnpm 12.4.2; [hydration run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36237780511). Baseline `2442c3026935502866361d05dd28cef5cd055137`, candidate `0922d21a5a9bc72fbbec9a74190d0a6aff089302`. Full builds passed in 7:15.01 and 7:24.39. A/B/A/B order, 100 WebSocket clients / 50 active, 120-second load, seed 1, fresh isolated Gateway state each time. All four runs used CPU profiling and no queue-counter probe; builds never overlapped measurements.

| Run | Completed/sent | Main CPU ms/chunk | Worker core ms/chunk | Worker abort ms/chunk | First delta p50/p95, s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | 439/439 | 0.998923 | 0.009432 | 0.00314925 | 4.9584 / 8.4048 |
| B1 | 418/418 | 1.097401 | 0.006602 | 0.00001091 | 6.2002 / 9.5603 |
| A2 | 411/411 | 1.077397 | 0.010097 | 0.00338255 | 5.9067 / 9.6357 |
| B2 | 389/389 | 1.158265 | 0.007665 | 0.00005441 | 6.6373 / 11.8382 |

Median worker-core cost **0.009765 -> 0.007134 ms/chunk (-26.94%)**; its overlapping abort subtree **0.00326590 -> 0.00003266 (-99.00%)**. Main-thread CPU/chunk **1.038160 -> 1.127833 (+8.64%)** and first-delta p50 **5.4325 -> 6.4187 s (+18.15%)**. These results establish the owner-stage saving, not an end-to-end performance improvement or a demo-capacity guarantee.

All runs had zero failed/pending turns, RPC errors, disconnects, active/unattributed executions at close, or integrity errors. Removing each client's first turn still leaves slower candidate latency. Host interval samples showed 61.1–62.2% idle, zero stolen CPU and swap, and maximum I/O wait 0–1%; they do not explain away the regression as contention. Costs increased across multiple stages, especially residual work (+0.02403), persistence (+0.01881), and broadcast (+0.01235 ms/chunk). Fixed run order leaves time/order effects and product causality unseparated; the broader regression needs coordinator assessment. All observations are retained.

### Residual attribution

The original stage rules were reproduced exactly using retained generated-source region maps. Samples from the residual were reassigned to their nearest synchronous application source owner, scaled by measured main-thread CPU and normalized to load-window provider chunks. These amortized figures include per-turn work; they are not direct timings of a chunk callback. GC and missing asynchronous ancestry were not assigned invented owners.

The refreshed baseline residual is **0.250142 ms/chunk**. Top production owners, median A1/A2:

| Owner | CPU ms/chunk |
| --- | ---: |
| Worker task-pool core | 0.009765 |
| CJK token-budget estimation | 0.004695 |
| Provider fetch/SSE normalization | 0.004402 |
| Trajectory runtime | 0.004306 |
| Tool-schema JSON projection | 0.003053 |
| Guarded response-body stream | 0.002873 |

A further 0.055810 ms/chunk has no recorded application ancestor, and 0.003508 is profiler harness work. The rest is distributed among smaller owners. The historical 0.29 ms/chunk bucket used an older base and additional instrumentation; it is not a matched comparison with these fresh profiles.

The open-PR census found no overlap in the two changed production files. Raw profiles, complete source maps, scripts, and measurements are retained in the campaign's l65 evidence directory. Every downloaded archive matched its remote hash. The exact Testbox is stopped and independently verified completed. No landing or release is requested by this PR.

prs.title: perf(agents): prepare workspace snapshots in workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent turn preparation still reads mutable workspace state synchronously on the Gateway main thread, and discovering a workspace alias can synchronously wait for the shared-state writer coordinator.

## User Impact

Workspace snapshot reads and alias registration no longer execute SQLite on the Gateway main thread. Setup completion, disappearance protection, alias repair errors, cold database initialization/migration, and read-only inspection semantics are preserved. There are no Gateway protocol, configuration, schema, retention, or update-behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first preparation snapshot precedes the attestation write; subsequent bootstrap reads protect against setup completed during asynchronous filesystem work. Setup writes already carry their committed result forward, so caching an earlier snapshot would weaken existing foreign-commit and disappearance checks.

Mutable access retains the canonical state owner's admission, reads current facts through the existing read worker, and carries the resolved identity/aliases into the writer only when an alias needs registration. That transaction rereads authoritative state and checks current caller authority at transaction and commit admission. Ordinary admitted snapshots do not acquire writer custody. The former main-thread implementation is removed, and attestation and alias writes share their admission adapter.

Related: #158797. Overlap inspection found only independent shared-dispatcher additions in #158848, #158845, #158768, and #158414; none implements this workspace change. Rebased onto `1011b10bb5b2` without conflicts.

## Evidence

Five interleaved before/after trials per workload, each with 50 `ensureAgentWorkspace` skip-bootstrap preparations, real SQLite workers, and isolated synthetic state. Both sequential and 50-concurrent batches ran in the same process per comparison. Baseline workspace implementation: `2442c3026935`; dependencies restored to the pinned lockfile, including `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.20.0. The shared macOS host was busy.

| Workload | Main-thread exec calls | Main-thread coordinator acquisitions | Main-thread CPU, median | Wall, median | Process RSS, median |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Sequential, canonical path | 100 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 55.101 → 62.073 ms | 131.553 → 127.464 ms | 346.2 → 348.8 MiB |
| Sequential, 50 new aliases | 300 → 0 | 50 → 0 | 93.844 → 90.308 ms | 146.497 → 210.182 ms | 374.9 → 378.6 MiB |
| Concurrent, canonical path | 100 → 0 | 0 → 0 | 37.751 → 49.380 ms | 78.788 → 96.691 ms | 386.4 → 397.1 MiB |
| Concurrent, 50 new aliases | 300 → 0 | 50 → 0 | 62.679 → 76.263 ms | 106.589 → 143.013 ms | 420.3 → 424.6 MiB |

All measured main-thread SQL calls fell to zero (sequential baseline: 550/1,500; concurrent baseline: 452/1,402). This is a main-thread SQL/coordinator isolation improvement, **not a throughput improvement**: the final concurrent batches used more host CPU and wall time. RSS is cumulative in each comparison process, not a memory improvement claim. Worker transport/admission overhead remains a profiling opportunity; dedicated-box swarm capacity is unproven.

The six-file workspace safety run passed **146 tests, one skipped**, in **251.99 s** wall: workspace preparation, state store, worker reads/writes, alias recovery, and setup-only SQLite safety. The strengthened preparation regression failed against the original implementation because main-thread SQLite `prepare` was called, then passed with the candidate.

Standalone costs with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| File | Result | Wrapper wall |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `src/agents/workspace-attestation.worker.test.ts` | 6 passed | 91.31 s |
| `src/agents/workspace-state-read.worker.test.ts` | 12 passed | 48.52 s |
| `src/agents/workspace-state-store.test.ts` | 41 passed | 103.80 s |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-read-worker.test.ts` | 34 passed | 38.16 s |

After restoring the pinned dependency and reusing the admitted read context, the 18 worker tests passed again in **33.61 s** wall. Core typecheck also passed after the stale install was repaired.

These standalone costs include source-worker fixture compilation and runner startup on the saturated host. Worker boundary, cold admission, foreign-commit visibility, and transaction/commit rollback are exercised with real workers; the existing persistence suites retain their isolated store lifetimes. CI per-file timings are pending.

Production LOC: **+154/-74, net +80**. Tests: **+61/-30, net +31**. Docs: **+9**. Production growth is the typed worker transport, retained admission, and transaction/commit authorization needed to remove the synchronous path without creating a cache or weakening safety checks.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed in **772.76 s** wall, including core and all 25 core-test typecheck graphs, lint, dead-export scans, schema/legacy-store guards, and zero runtime import cycles. The initial run caught an over-broad helper return annotation (fixed) and a stale local dependency installation (restored once with the frozen lockfile); no dependency or lockfile changes are included.

Deslop: clean. Fresh Codex autoreview on the final committed branch: **scoped-clean through P2, no accepted/actionable findings**. `git diff --check` passed.

No full build or swarm was run; proof is component-scoped. Setup merge, expiry, and deletion remain separate synchronous migration work outside this unit. This PR is for coordinator review and is not being merged here.

prs.title: perf(sessions): offload large pending input reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large pending-message pages and individual message lookups monopolize the Gateway thread while SQLite materializes and parses accepted input.

## User Impact

Control UI history and pending-message expansion use less Gateway-thread CPU for large reads. Small reads stay inline. Large payload reads take longer in wall time because they cross the worker boundary; this change does not claim faster chat acknowledgements or first tokens.

No protocol, configuration, schema, retention, or update behavior changes. Existing incognito stores remain process-local.

## Why This Change Was Made

Salvages the read-side benefit from closed #158687 without its staging regression. The existing byte-selection query gates payloads above 1 MiB. A bounded version of the existing count query also sends backlogs above 1,024 rows to the existing transcript reader worker. One shared kernel serves both paths and preserves the bounded in-memory sort, byte limit, exact messages, and pagination cursor.

The worker reads one SQLite snapshot and returns parsed messages plus custody identity fields. The host retains the physical database owner through live custody checks and interruption repair, including identity verification immediately before a repair write. All page/input callers await the result. Staging, completion, promotion, and normal custody writes remain with their existing owner.

Receipt lookup remains a bounded metadata query. The earlier “duplicate preparation” benchmark calls staging again, so it is an unchanged control here. `readSessionSubmittedInput` remains synchronous because recovery/admission commit guards consume its fresh comparison; safely offloading that path requires separate preparation and invalidation work.

Related overlap inspected: #158699 changes receipt state, while #158680, #158588, and #158583 extend other history-worker operations. None implements this size gate; their independent operations are preserved.

## Evidence

Interleaved A/B and B/A runs in two persistent, isolated processes on Node 26.9.0 / Apple M3 Ultra, with synthetic SQLite stores and warmed operations. Ten rounds; medians below. CPU is `process.threadCpuUsage()` and excludes worker CPU. Baseline is `ffbff291cf74`; measured production candidate is `3d3a375138f6`; final head `4f693fa26f76` adds the verified caller/test and lint-only follow-up. Shared-host scheduling makes wall times noisy. Unchanged controls are not claimed as improvements.

| Operation | Main-thread CPU before → after (ms) | Wall before → after (ms) |

prs.title: improve(gateway): reduce session update work for concurrent viewers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Frequent session updates repeat row preparation, presentation, and encoding for every connected Control UI viewer, increasing Gateway CPU use during large shared demos.

## User Impact

The Gateway spends less CPU publishing the same session rows to many viewers. Each recipient keeps their current authorization, model visibility, profile envelope, and sequence. Wire fields and configuration remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session presentation owner now retains prepared facts for one synchronous publication and reuses rows with the same actual recipient view. Owner revisions invalidate those facts when a send reenters the Gateway and changes a session, profile, policy, or run. The broadcaster reuses canonical row encodings while preserving native serialization for dynamic payloads. Serialization hooks are checked again for each recipient, including hooks installed by an earlier send.

Based on main after #158408 and #158497. Overlap review found #158581 (event lineage), #158587 (live-text delivery), and #158614 (mention expiry) touch adjacent parts of the projection/broadcaster; none implements recipient row-view reuse. Their ownership remains separate.

## Evidence

A focused publication benchmark uses the real resident projection, connection publication, authorization, presenter, and broadcaster with 100 synthetic admin recipients and 50 tracked runs. Sockets complete immediately. Seven interleaved before/after rounds each publish 50 events; startup is excluded. Baseline is main `76e32e924413` (the measured owner source is identical to `9bb0e452d9bb`).

| Per 100-recipient publication | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median main-thread CPU | 3.028 ms | 2.458 ms |
| Median wall time | 3.043 ms | 2.465 ms |
| Projection `.state` reads | 201 | 1 |
| Row presentations, one view | 100 | 1 |
| Delivered frames | 100 | 100 |
| Bytes in the first measured publication | 277,890 | 277,890 |

CPU falls **18.8%**. This is component proof on a shared host, not an end-to-end prompt-latency claim. The regression also exercises distinct profiles with the same view, per-recipient roles, exact sequences, source hooks, native getter/Proxy behavior, same-generation updates, and run replacement during a send. A separate real-entrypoint probe reproduced accumulating row mutations from a hook installed mid-fanout and matches baseline behavior after the fix.

Focused commands use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| File | Result | Command wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `src/gateway/session-row-presentation.test.ts` | 5 passed | 203.80 s |
| `src/gateway/server-broadcast.session-serialization.test.ts` | 22 passed | 12.33 s |
| `src/gateway/server-broadcast.serialization.test.ts` | 27 passed | 245.58 s |

The original five-file boundary run, including board and scope siblings, passed **84 tests** in **589.49 s** command wall time. The table records post-rebase checks; the final hook change reran the presentation file. The slow wall times include cold worker compilation and shared-host contention. The added cases reuse the existing state/socket fixtures and introduce no timers or Gateway boots. The native state/publication boundary is needed to catch missed invalidation; a mocked cache alone would not prove it. Hosted CI durations are pending.

- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passes, including core types, all 25 test type-check groups, lint, dead exports, and structural guards.
- `git diff --check` and formatting pass.
- Deslop completed; fresh Codex autoreview is **scoped-clean through P2**, with no accepted/actionable findings.

prs.title: perf(gateway): keep progress updates from blocking other chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Progress-card updates synchronously run SQLite on the Gateway thread, delaying other Control UI clients during bursts of updates.

## User Impact

Progress-card persistence leaves the Gateway event loop available while the canonical agent worker completes the write. Revisions, conditional dismissal, reset rollback, authorization, and post-commit broadcasts retain their existing behavior. No protocol, schema, configuration, or update migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The asynchronous admission queue previously called the native card writer on the host. PUT now sends one typed operation to the existing agent executor. It captures payload and routing before waiting, retains the physical database, and checks live authority at transaction entry and commit. Incognito and reset mutations keep their existing transaction owners.

The kernel accepts admitted handles only, removing its unused path-based database opener and test-only transaction convenience. Reads and writes consume the schema owner's current admitted facts instead of probing the catalog or repeating already-satisfied lazy DDL.

Related: #158465, #158559, and #158570 touch the shared executor for metadata patches, archive reads, and WAL maintenance. Their changes were inspected; none implements progress-card mutation, and their operation branches compose independently.

## Evidence

Five interleaved A/B rounds of 50 synthetic registered `progressCard.put` handler updates, comparing the original implementation at `31a5754546a0` with this branch on Node 26.9.0/macOS arm64. Medians on the shared campaign host:

| Measurement per 50 updates | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First event-loop callback delay | 17.27 ms | 0.82 ms |
| Host SQLite calls | 250 | 0 |
| Host progress-table statements, including DDL | 150 | 0 |
| Host thread CPU | 13.55 ms | 73.52 ms |
| Sequential completion time | 17.20 ms | 168.93 ms |

This is an I/O isolation improvement, not a throughput win: broker admission and communication increase CPU and sequential latency. The operation counts establish removal of host SQL independently of host load. This does not claim improved demo-scale WebSocket latency; no swarm rerun was performed.

All 256 tests pass across 11 files. Commands use `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1` on the same Blacksmith Testbox:

| Scope | Tests | Command wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Progress-card worker boundary | 6 | 35.74 s |
| Card kernel | 12 | 3.92 s |
| Reset/card lifetime | 12 | 28.53 s |
| RPC, authorization, refresh and queued refresh | 56 | 41.85 s |
| Session accessor, canonical-key Doctor and migration siblings | 170 | 59.55 s |

The worker regression fails on the original Gateway store for both queued-input mutation and host SQL, then passes on the final implementation. The final worker file spends about 2.4 s in tests; its wall time includes worker compilation. No timers, sleeps, polling, or new worker pinning were added.

Changed checks passed after making the now-unused board database resolver private: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 62637559950b` completed in 1544.63 s, including all 25 test typecheck graphs and all unused-export scans. The preceding full-branch selection supplied the unchanged checks; its unused-export finding was fixed. `pnpm build` passed in 366.48 s on the final production code. Its report includes a non-blocking Control UI startup gzip warning (363.0 KiB versus a 362.6 KiB budget).

Full core lint ran in 371.59 s and reported an unused test-spy binding, now fixed, plus one unrelated failure: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.test.ts` has 1025 counted lines against a 1000-line cap. That file is byte-identical to the base (blob `962499dee34e5bcd8eec3ac781e52488a46d7b44`). The final worker test passes focused lint and all six cases on the final head; script lint passes in 33.64 s. The unrelated replay-test line-cap error remains a validation limitation. Hosted PR CI timing is pending.

Final Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. `git diff --check` passes. Production: **+91 lines** (248 added / 157 removed); tests and test support/routing: **+255** (282 / 27); docs: **+7** (8 / 1). The production growth supplies explicit target/admission handling and the typed executor operation after deleting the unused opener and redundant transaction path.
