prs.title: perf(sessions): offload durable pending-input custody
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent chat sends and reconnects perform durable pending-input writes and potentially large reads on the Gateway main thread, competing with streaming and other browser requests.

## User Impact

Accepted input remains durable before `chat.send` acknowledges it. Staging, promotion, completion, terminal disposition, and stale-input repair use the existing agent executor. Cancellation retains custody and admission until accepted writes settle. Large history/input reads use the existing reader worker; small bounded reads and receipt lookups stay inline.

The worker broker increases warm staging CPU and wall time in the measured burst. This PR removes main-thread durable transactions but does **not** demonstrate faster ACKs, first tokens, or overall burst responsiveness. Large-read main-thread CPU improves substantially.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous Promise-based staging queue still ran synchronous SQLite, while finish bypassed that queue. The cutover preserves the outer FIFO, revalidates live authority at transaction and commit admission, and publishes committed consumption before SessionManager view adoption. Cancellation closes execution immediately, joins accepted completion writes, and settles terminal disposition before releasing registration. A resumed successor also preserves its existing superseded stop reason so provisional cancellation cannot become a generic task failure during cleanup.

Reads inspect stored byte metadata before materializing payloads. Up to 1 MiB stays inline; larger payloads use the existing history reader. Counts probe at most 257 indexed rows before offloading a larger scan. Live duplicate preparation carries compact identity facts and rechecks registered custody after yielding. No new cache is introduced.

The existing synchronous SessionManager SDK and process-held incognito kernels retain their contracts. Schemas, stored bytes, durability, retention, protocol, configuration, and update behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Interleaved main-thread CPU and wall measurements

Synthetic compiled-owner benchmark on Node 26.9.0 / Apple M3 Ultra, comparing the provided built reference (`e952abb4aff8`) with this candidate. Two isolated persistent processes, warmed operations, six samples in alternating before/after order, canonical agent database paths. Values are medians in milliseconds. `process.threadCpuUsage()` excludes worker CPU. The reference is the campaign's supplied build, not an exact build of this branch's merge base.

| Work per sample | Main CPU before | Main CPU after | Wall before | Wall after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 tiny receipt lookups | 5.703 | 7.632 | 5.681 | 7.621 |
| 50 pages of 20 × 1 KiB inputs | 6.999 | 8.142 | 6.990 | 8.153 |
| One 10 MiB page | 45.002 | 2.226 | 63.980 | 69.511 |
| 100 × 1 KiB input lookups | 4.756 | 6.436 | 4.742 | 6.460 |
| One 8 MiB input lookup | 7.048 | 1.542 | 7.100 | 8.894 |
| 50 tiny duplicate preparations | 19.626 | 21.335 | 19.699 | 21.375 |
| 50 preparations with 128 KiB saved metadata | 23.292 | 23.212 | 23.335 | 23.311 |
| One 8 MiB live duplicate preparation | 12.354 | 7.076 | 12.405 | 7.097 |
| Durable staging: 50 distinct sessions × 1 KiB | 25.830 | 88.028 | 26.280 | 173.829 |

The initial all-worker implementation lost on tiny reads; those reads now stay inline. Bounds and authority checks still add some CPU. Large-page CPU drops 95%, large-input CPU 78%, and large duplicate-preparation CPU 43%. Larger count scans also improve main-thread CPU: 20 reads over 4,096 pending rows take 20.995 → 11.997 ms CPU and 24.371 → 50.421 ms wall; 10 reads over 32,768 rows take 99.748 → 7.405 ms CPU and 102.880 → 121.282 ms wall. The count benchmark verifies full totals and 20-item pages.

A separate six-sample interleaved 50-session write run with a 1 ms event-loop-delay monitor measured 31.115 → 114.780 ms main CPU, 49.792 → 604.946 ms wall, and median maximum event-loop delay 7.186 → 19.161 ms under shared host load. It does not establish a responsiveness win. Tests independently assert that the migrated custody operations perform no host writes; bounded reads intentionally remain on the host. Broker coordination/batching and custom-path owner discovery remain follow-ups.

### Validation

Focused proof uses `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`. Local wall times include compilation and contention on the shared campaign host:

- Pending-input and consumed-input suites: 90/91 initially passed (649.65 s); the corrected ownership-error assertion passed on replay (113.62 s). Four settlement/repair regressions passed (347.64 s), and four later retirement/replay cases passed (42.05 s).
- Schema compatibility: 7 passed (599.19 s). Promotion/lifecycle: 31 across three shards passed (502.46 s). Metadata observer/recorder fixtures: 6 passed (447.52 s).
- Transformed-input replay failed before the kernel fix with the expected admission conflict (140.74 s), then passed (324.38 s).
- Bounded reads and acceptance-time projection: 5 passed (323.04 s); pagination/byte bounds: 2 passed (232.12 s).
- Earlier local parent-resume proof timed out in `sessions.resolve` before reaching its target boundary. No timeout was increased; the actual case passes remotely. Doctor test routing and acceptance-time fixtures were corrected after their documented failed runs; passing replays are not claimed to fix the unrelated local timeout.

Blacksmith Testbox proof used one reusable active lease, `tbx_01m3e28sqzpt2htxvw9sdr2afq`, with source-hash verification before each run ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36220294647)):

- Six Gateway files: **93/93 passed, 78.22 s wall**, including durability before ACK, failed-write retry, parent authority, resumed cancellation, shutdown, placement cancellation, and reclaim preparation.
- Final custody/history bundle: **65/66 passed, 86.43 s wall**. The failure was a stale fixture variable introduced while sharing the test fixture; the corrected collected-input case **passed in 17.85 s**. All three repair/lifecycle cases and all six pending-history Gateway cases passed in the full bundle.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` was run remotely and completed through its canonical plan continuations. Earlier production and all 25 test graphs passed; affected graphs were rerun after fixes. Final production typechecking passed in **45.13 s**. Core lint completed all stripes; its only remaining diagnostics were three redundant test type arguments, corrected and revalidated with the canonical type-aware runner (**18.15 s**, no diagnostics). Script lint, schema/storage/boundary guards, import cycles, export scan, format, and ratchets passed. Remaining guard continuation took **140.93 s**. Final affected test graphs passed in **118.33 s wall** (agent/session graph 41.4 s, Gateway-method graph 55.8 s), and the line-cap check passed.

No full build or swarm end-to-end run was selected; compiled worker-owner and real-Gateway test boundaries provide the focused proof. Hosted CI is still authoritative.

Deslop completed on the branch diff. Independent reviews drove fixes for completion/cancellation settlement, registered custody during retirement, replay of admission-transformed messages, and stale repair racing owner publication. The latter regression failed with the expected live-owner interruption error (38.98 s wall), then all three repair/lifecycle cases passed (43.25 s), with the final fixture-import replay also passing (50.36 s); repair now filters candidates under the shared writer FIFO. The final full-branch Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 defects; separate reviews of the subsequent direct-import, redundant-type-argument, and fixture-cleanup corrections were also clean. An earlier fresh-commit callback finding was rejected because the unchanged append kernel deliberately invokes that callback only without accepted pending custody; an apparent early-abort return was also disproved by tracing its fallthrough, which exposed and led to fixing the real early admission-release path.

Production: +2,213 / -843, net **+1,370** lines across 44 files. Tests and test support: +1,023 / -468, net **+555** across 53 files. Documentation: +23 / -6, net **+17**. Growth pays for typed worker commands, split SQL/host ownership, bounded-read routing, asynchronous cancellation settlement, and the complete caller migration. The old durable owner paths are removed; retained synchronous paths have the SDK, incognito, or measured bounded-read contracts described above.

Integration overlap was checked against 200 open PRs before publication. The now-merged pending-page sorting optimization in #158449 must follow the moved reader into `session-accessor.pending-inputs.read.ts`. Shared executor files overlap open #158465, #158570, and #158680; the admission caller overlaps #158586. Reader infrastructure also overlaps open #158583/#158588 and merged #158450/#158530/#158559. This branch retains its original campaign base; integration must preserve those owners’ changes. This PR covers pending-input custody only.

GitHub reports merge conflicts against current `main`. This ready-for-review PR is intentionally unmerged for campaign coordination and integration with the overlapping owners listed above.

prs.title: perf(auth): avoid completion stalls on SQLite contention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent chat completions can block the Gateway event loop while successful auth-profile usage waits for a SQLite writer on the main thread.

## User Impact

Success bookkeeping for agent-local, shared, and personal model accounts executes through the existing database workers. The change improves responsiveness under SQLite contention but adds worker transport latency and memory overhead; it is not a throughput improvement. Stored credentials, schemas, configuration, Gateway protocol, and update behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Success and inline failure share one reducer, worker adapter, and publication owner. A per-state-root async mutation queue preserves ordering with credential resets and other asynchronous auth writes. Preparation captures the original database and environment before waiting, and synchronous worker transactions reread authoritative rows and recheck live authority before writing. First-use creation waits for its queue position.

Known commits remain successful if publication or cleanup fails, with affected snapshots invalidated. Unknown outcomes reject without replay. Confirmed lock refusals retain the existing logged, non-fatal bookkeeping result. Personal accounts remain outside shared credential snapshots. Existing synchronous APIs and conditional rollback retain their native contracts.

## Evidence

Five warmed samples of 50 actual `markAuthProfileSuccess` calls against isolated synthetic state on the shared campaign host; initialization excluded:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread `BEGIN` calls per burst | 50 | 0 |
| Healthy median batch time | 104.19 ms | 1,017.11 ms |
| Healthy median maximum event-loop gap | 40.41 ms | 47.37 ms |
| Healthy worst event-loop gap | 65.32 ms | 56.06 ms |
| Healthy peak sampled RSS | 308.20 MiB | 445.48 MiB |
| Median batch time with a 250 ms SQLite writer | 370.08 ms | 813.48 ms |
| Median maximum gap with that writer | 299.22 ms | 25.72 ms |
| Worst gap with that writer | 308.11 ms | 26.23 ms |
| Peak sampled RSS with that writer | 456.03 MiB | 418.27 MiB |

The contention case demonstrates main-thread isolation. Healthy-path event-loop timing does not show an improvement, and the roughly 10× healthy batch latency is a material tradeoff. Scheduling noise on the saturated host limits extrapolation to a live demo.

Validation uses `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`:

- Success worker and write-admission tests: 32 passed, 232.17 s command wall.
- Profile mutation, inherited-owner, and failure siblings: 66 passed, 130.37 s command wall.
- Local/shared committed-publication failure cases: 2 passed, 52.65 s command wall.
- Final complete success-worker file: 22 passed, 127.70 s command wall (110.41 s Vitest phase, 34% in test bodies). The four lock-outcome cases first produced two expected failures and two passes on the pre-fix code, 145.43 s command wall. The table was subsequently moved to its dedicated outcome file and extended to agent ownership.
- Final outcome table and write-admission siblings: 21 passed, 260.84 s command wall. The additional agent lost-result case failed before correction (205.10 s baseline command wall). Total unique focused coverage across six files is 105 tests.
- Controlled regressions failed before correction for credential-reset overtaking, competing first-use creation, and stale derived snapshots after publication failure. Corrected cases passed without timers, sleeps, polling, or write retries.
- Additional actual-source contract proof: six scenarios passed in 198.92 s, including success/failure ordering, personal ownership, and scoped first use.
- Focused tests exercise actual worker artifacts because reducer-only mocks cannot prove native identity revocation, FIFO admission, or settlement after a committed write loses its reply. Slow local wall times are dominated by artifact compilation and module transforms; only the runner's quiet-output watchdog was extended, not test/hook timeouts. No full release build, live Gateway, or provider calls were run.
- Targeted compiler diagnostics and type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. Final deslop found no further cleanup. Final independent Codex branch review: scoped-clean through P2, no accepted/actionable findings. Earlier ordering, invalidation, and outcome-classification findings were fixed and covered by failing-before/passing-after regressions.

Production: +1,402/−498 (net +904); tests: +756/−107 (net +649). Growth is the typed transport for agent/shared/personal owners, captured lifecycle/identity authority, full asynchronous mutation admission, and shared post-commit publication. The old success persistence path and duplicate failure/publication plumbing were removed; synchronous public APIs keep their existing contracts.

The required remote changed-file gate remains incomplete. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3djaj3xvkenzz533v9vqbby` passed initial guards/core graph and found three type errors that were corrected. Subsequent source-sync attempts hit wrapper/native transfer timeouts; the reused lease expired before the final gate could run. The lease is stopped/completed. Hosted CI is authoritative for the remaining full typecheck/lint/build coverage.

prs.title: perf(sessions): keep durable chat metadata patches off the Gateway thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent chat starts and completions can pause the Gateway while durable session metadata patches execute SQLite on its main thread.

## User Impact

Writer claims, usage accounting, and pending-delivery metadata now use the existing agent database worker, keeping their durable SQL off the Gateway thread. Completion accounting also consumes an applied live-model switch in the same fenced mutation. Stored data, schemas, configuration, and update behavior are unchanged; process-held incognito and maintenance scopes retain their native owner.

This improves responsiveness at a worker transport, memory, and CPU cost. It is not a throughput or CPU-reduction claim. The landing assessment accepts this measured component tradeoff for the requested responsiveness and database-worker ownership change. Representative concurrent completed-turn capacity and tail latency remain unmeasured; no claim is made for those outcomes. Worker writes also invalidate connection-local host inventory caches, so a later full-inventory host read can reparse the store. Native writer-owned caches retain their O(changed keys) path; resident Gateway projections consume keyed events and exact-row fallback. No cross-connection freshness check was relaxed to reuse an unsafe cache.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared patch owner now executes snapshot reads and authoritative compare-and-write in the worker. One physical writer reservation spans preparation, synchronous worker transaction, native settlement, and publication. Live authority is rechecked at transaction and commit admission; committed bookkeeping precedes identity observers even if ordinary result delivery is lost. Native exceptions and replacements share the mutation/publication owners.

Prepared node snapshots compare persisted column values across worker transfer, which normalizes SQLite row prototypes. This preserves the unchanged-row fast path without newly decoding independently mutable participant data; changed rows and live authority still require normal revalidation.

Stopping a preaccept collector now waits for its terminal session publication before deleting the provisional session. This closes a cancellation race exposed by asynchronous patch execution while retaining exact-row deletion and successor guards.

Main was merged without rebasing, preserving archive admission (#158559), committed archive-recovery facts (#158660), incremental projection (#158489), typing (#158552), sandbox facts (#158610), and accessor changes. CI-exposed fixtures now await their actual worker/notification completion owners before resetting state or closing mock transports. The iMessage fixture cutover updates every caller; unchanged chat-database helpers moved into test support to keep the oversized test file within its growth ratchet. Production behavior was not changed by those fixture repairs. The schema warning for `extensions/imessage/src/test-support/chat-db.test-support.ts` is a test-only false positive: it contains the identical synthetic Messages table and helpers extracted from `monitor.last-route.test.ts`, and that test is its only importer. No product table, migration, index, retention rule, or storage format changes. `liveModelSwitchPending` is an existing serialized field; this change clears it in the existing fenced accounting mutation as part of completion accounting.

## Evidence

The original five-sample warmed 50-claim benchmark reported main-thread `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` calls **50 → 0**, median maximum event-loop gap **91.85 → 7.71 ms**, worst sampled gap **161.11 → 98.68 ms**, median batch wall **395.03 → 636.58 ms**, and peak sampled RSS **429.95 → 475.34 MiB**.

Awaiting the canonical async close preserves the complete discovery/reaping assertions. Original CI shard times were 73.79 s and 42.93 s. Other interrupted shards were cancelled; failed jobs were not rerun to obtain green.

[Run 36222848653](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36222848653) exposed memory state removal before retained worker lease cleanup (ENOTEMPTY/retired-owner errors), and iMessage fixtures closing mock watches before flush completion and rotating shared state before agent cleanup. Memory reproduced its original email→gmail failure order; the original iMessage shard reproduced 2 failures / 671 passes. Repairs await the existing cleanup, debounce-completion, and sent-hook owners. Suppressed delivery now also proves the dispatcher actually ran. Original CI shard times were 84.54 s and 139.47 s.

That run also found an unrelated chained type assertion in `server-chat-progress-snapshot.ts` from advancing main in merge ref `aa57b34043827f9f9613929c28e0ba6e366fba37`, whose main parent was `4a2f1239af1094d0b1702795dcc8360957c3363e`. The PR head did not contain that assertion. Main already fixed it in `66b812f26e725cd709e08860d2cb46ba496cd308`; the fixture push refreshes the merge ref with that fix. No passing full-main CI claim is made for the intervening security-only run.

[Run 36225038969](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36225038969) found two further deterministic fixture mismatches and cancelled the remaining jobs. Group session seeds used ambient state while group mutations used an explicit fixture environment; the original shard reproduced 7 failures / 164 passes. Seeds now retain the same environment, with awaited agent cleanup before shared-state teardown. Doctor sandbox migration teardown removed its state before worker cleanup; the original file reproduced 13 failures / 7 passes. Awaiting the existing agent/shared-state closers fixes teardown without changing assertions. The original CI shards took 96.06 s and 213.06 s. No production changes were needed.

[Run 36226232994](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36226232994) found the Activity recap relocation test polling for a cold worker commit within its default window (CI shard 71.98 s). CI and targeted local reproduction observed the third model completion while the new recap was still updating. The test now awaits the existing terminal publication callback before asserting covered messages, text, and the delayed old-owner fence. No production or timeout change was needed.

A local replay of that shard also timed out after 120 s in the unchanged OAuth refresh/cancellation integration case and its cleanup retained an incomplete harness receipt. One isolated unchanged replay passed in 60.172 s test time (166.96 s command wall), with normal cleanup. The original blocked phase remains unknown; host load or non-isolated ordering are plausible but unproven. No fix or passing-replay-as-fix claim is made for that local failure; hosted CI remains a required gate.

[Run 36228571428](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36228571428) exposed standing-intent teardown removing shared state before the retained agent worker lease settled. Standalone baseline reproduced 17 failures / 2 passes. Awaited agent/shared-state closure revealed four intended write-failure cases installing their synthetic trigger before the worker schema admission; the fault helper now admits and holds the worker first, then installs the identical trigger. Original domain-error/rollback assertions and deliberate synchronous admission-fault closes remain intact. Both suites pass; production schema guards are unchanged. Original CI shard: 111.34 s.

[Run 36230549921](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36230549921) passed the prior cron group, then exposed two Doctor-auth preview fixtures synchronously reopening a store while its worker resources were closing. Full-file baseline reproduced 2 failures / 79 passes. Awaited agent closure now precedes the existing native reset and raw invalid-row/tombstone inspection, preserving every migration assertion. The unchanged prompter factory moved to a focused helper to satisfy the oversized-file growth ratchet. Original CI auth shard: 36.01 s.

[Run 36232868074](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36232868074) exposed a production cancellation race: an independent killed-run timing write outlived retirement publication, so provisional deletion captured the row before `endedAt`/`status` committed. Exact-row deletion then returned `session-changed` although session ID, lifecycle revision, and timestamp were unchanged, and cleanup intentionally stopped. Both native admission cases reproduced locally. The existing retirement-publication barrier now retains the timing/attachment tail until settlement; the existing admitted-continuation API preserves suspension/shutdown ownership. A later main merge preserves the upstream removal of unused iMessage fixture helpers and cursor coverage while retaining the completion signal. Invalid bytes, no-unrelated-parse checks, stale-replacement guards, and post-mutation assertions are retained. Two unchanged synthetic record factories moved into a `.test-support.ts` helper to satisfy the existing file-growth ratchet. prs.title: perf(gateway): offload Activity recap source reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Utility-model-enabled Activity recaps query session metadata on every transcript notification before debounce and read recap transcript batches on the Gateway thread.

## User Impact

Recaps reuse committed session facts and read bounded transcript batches through the existing history worker, reducing avoidable Gateway work during concurrent conversations. Gateway protocol, configuration, and SQLite schemas are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-row projection already owns committed generation, entry, and physical-store facts. Consume those facts before coalescing, and retain bounded request intents while that owner prepares topology. The existing history worker handles source admission, cold restoration, cancellation, and snapshot reads; secret redaction stays on the host.

Queued work retains the service's creation context and existing call budgets. Generation and commit-time checks fence stale results. Lifecycle checks cover both physical stores and the configured selectors used by existing callers. Recap metadata and payload selection share one admitted worker snapshot.

## Evidence

Actual source observer benchmark on Node 26.9.0/macOS arm64 with synthetic sessions and a stub utility model held in flight:

| Transcript notifications | Before wall | After wall | Entry SQL before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 5.81 ms | 1.76 ms | 100 → 0 |
| 1,000 | 57.34 ms | 14.41 ms | 1,000 → 0 |
| 10,000 | 412.86 ms | 101.65 ms | 10,000 → 0 |

These are synchronous notification-handling measurements on a busy shared host, not end-to-end Gateway latency predictions.

- Recap lifecycle/retry and active-event/byte-budget suites: **88 passed**, **265.25 s wall** using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ... --maxWorkers=1` (47 recap tests and 41 accessor tests).
- After the final lifecycle-guard correction: **2 passed**, **323.13 s wall**, covering configured-selector and discovered physical-store holds. Cold worker compilation/transform accounted for most of the run. The new physical-store case failed before the correction with `SQLite session state changed before archive materialization`.
- Utility harness recap case: **1 passed**, 3 filtered out, **48.15 s wall**. No unrelated provider behavior is claimed.
- Related history-worker, readonly snapshot, subscription, and resource-policy suites: **143 passed, 1 skipped** in Blacksmith Testbox. That initial Gateway run also exposed three recap fixture assumptions; corrected fixtures use publication/settlement signals and a properly retired/admitted relocated store. The targeted correction replay passed **6 tests in 78.85 s**, followed by the full green recap run above.
- Original observer negative control failed the zero-entry-SQL assertion at the intended entry point. The readonly snapshot table also covers a real external WAL mutation between admission and payload selection.
- Isolated source smokes passed durable creation, cached-text restyling, and topology retry (**111.97 s**), plus physical relocation and stale-owner fencing (**81.18 s**).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed in **2388.24 s**, including production and all 25 test typecheck graphs, lint, and guards. After the last narrow changes, core/Gateway-root typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and the line-cap ratchet passed again; unaffected successful checks were reused.
- Final-head independent Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**. Accepted topology-retention and physical-store lifecycle findings were fixed. No rejected findings remain. Deslop inspected the complete diff.
- Production LOC: **+638 / -309, net +329**. Test/support LOC: **+447 / -147, net +300**. Growth supplies bounded startup/topology readiness, worker adaptation, and cancellation/identity guards. It adds no recap facts cache or worker pool; duplicate state-window updates and fixture construction were consolidated.

Local validation encountered long macOS filesystem rename and compiled-worker preparation stalls; those interrupted attempts are not counted as passing proof. The task-owned Blacksmith lease was stopped. No running Gateway was used, and no full build or full test suite was run.


### Landing CI repair

Exact-head CI run [36218571200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36218571200) found two defects at `631ed3d97fb815325658b21616ebc991108f8eeb`: a type-inclusive import cycle caused by the history contract deriving its result from the Gateway implementation, and a shutdown fixture that omitted the newly required session-row projection. The remaining job cancellations followed fail-fast cancellation. Neither failure was rerun merely to obtain green.

Commit `060cb8ca1e349b5a1cd1055a8be0df57aa2508b0` moves the batch result shape into the existing history contract and gives the shutdown fixture the real projection. The fixture now awaits an explicit model-start signal rather than polling. Local proof: Madge reports zero cycles (29.90 s); production and Gateway test types, scoped lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Subscription/history-worker siblings passed 111 tests, with one skipped benchmark. The corrected shutdown file passed both cases in 90.76 s wall (13.21 s test time; most wall time was worker compilation/transform on the shared host). An initial local edit mistakenly used `it.each` for a test-context callback; switching to the supported `it.for` API fixed that test-only error. Final independent Codex review was scoped-clean through P2. New-head hosted CI remains the landing gate.

The original ClawSweeper logical-session replacement scenario was checked against the actual mutation owner: committed reset/replacement publication clears queued intents and drops old work before transcript callbacks. A subsequent review distinguished replacement of the physical SQLite file at the same path, which does not publish a session-identity mutation. That separate case was reproduced and repaired as described below.

Main advanced during CI and introduced a merge conflict with the shared history-worker dispatcher extraction. Merge commit `df29d13a92533a631d2a0ae23d72ca9577c5e0e5` incorporates main `4ed4df0e9b3f617c51a03c5e81d37534e0c32865` without rebasing. Conflict resolution preserves all artifact/message read variants and routes recaps through the newly extracted dispatcher. The merged candidate passed 71 focused recap/shutdown/history-worker/integration tests, with one skipped benchmark, in 166.04 s wall; production types and the zero-cycle Madge guard passed. Fresh independent review of the full PR delta against merged main was scoped-clean through P2.


### Physical-store replacement follow-up

Commit `4b697d455da6b05a13804ab51fe61dc30b6cd55f` fixes the refined ClawSweeper finding: a pending immediate request could suppress a newer transcript notification while topology recovery adopted a replacement SQLite file at the same path. The queue now retains the newest identity fields while combining immediate urgency; existing generation and lifecycle checks remain authoritative.

A regression through the real recap service, SQLite backup/close/rename/readmission, and real row projection failed before the fix with `stale` instead of `updating` after recovery. With the fix, all 25 retry-suite tests passed in 114.45 s wall; the new case took 2.88 s. The suite covers real persistence, worker admission, provider recovery, and lifecycle settlement; worker compilation/transforms account for most wall time. Production and Gateway test types, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace, and independent Codex review through P2 passed. Hosted exact-head CI remains required.

### Remaining exact-head CI blocker

Exact-head run [36221077441](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36221077441) at `4b697d455da6b05a13804ab51fe61dc30b6cd55f` failed `checks-node-changed-compact-small-19`: `server.app-sdk-composed-resources.test.ts` / `proves event, run, artifact, environment, and schema contracts` received `AgentDatabaseRegistryChangedError: Agent database registry changed during discovery; retry the read.` Other failed-looking shard results were fail-fast cancellations; the gate correctly failed.

These passing replays do not establish a fix. A temporary forwarding diagnostic pass observed disabled utility routing, lifecycle-persistence entry writes rather than recap writes, and a registry registration beginning between artifact list/get requests and finishing after download. That pass also succeeded. All diagnostic edits were removed. Source inspection found registry-generation guards and the bounded discovery refresh contract, but did not establish which invalidation window caused the hosted exception or a safe repair. No retry budget, guard, assertion, or fixture was weakened.

The contemporaneous scheduled main run `36220989893` showed cleanup-service and filesystem-boundary failures, not this SDK failure, so this failure is not classified as already red on main. No GitHub rerun was requested merely to obtain green. Native preparation/merge has not been submitted; exact-head CI remains the landing blocker.

- publish a canonical immutable receipt after a workflow-dispatch CI gate succeeds
- bind the receipt to exact target, workflow, diff-base, diff-head, selected-lane, scope, native-toggle, release-context, Node, and runner contracts

prs.title: refactor: explore removing Tasks and TaskFlow
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Explore removing the generalized Tasks/TaskFlow layer instead of maintaining a second execution and lifecycle ledger alongside Cron, subagents, ACP, media generation, and sessions.

## User Impact

**Large-change review:** @steipete approved the documented review-size exception; `size: accepted-large` is applied and the original draft is reopened. This does not waive the merge blockers below.

**Exploratory draft—not ready to merge.** Removes the Tasks page/rail, CLI, RPC/events, TaskFlow APIs, and TaskFlow-only Webhooks plugin. Cron execution/history, session controls, native subagent delivery/cancellation, media operations, and Workboard session-based planning remain. Removed integrations intentionally break; there is no automatic workflow conversion.

Following the [approved storage-retirement decision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156532#issuecomment-5798987497), **shared schema 19 drops `task_delivery_state`, `task_runs`, and `flow_runs`** after preserving retained Cron history and provably bound released native subagent outcomes. Only Task/flow lifecycle bindings are removed; independent audit facts, Cron bindings, native sessions/results/receipts, recovery archives, and unrelated data remain. History does not become execution authority. Unknown dependencies refuse migration rather than risk unrelated data.

**Upgrade/rollback:** main’s shared schema 18 and agent schema 23 are preserved. Existing old-updater content/publication deferral remains intact. A downgrade after retirement requires a verified pre-migration backup, not lowered schema markers. No live database has been migrated.

**Known merge blocker:** initial native Codex children that have not reached requester completion admission still lack a durable replacement for the removed cold/cross-parent recovery path. Gateway restart or native-parent replacement can lose that completion obligation. Preserved accepted follow-up receipts and admitted completion recovery do not close this gap; this draft does not claim restart-equivalent behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surviving responsibilities stay with their native owners. Cron owns a small history table with its existing identities, details, partitions, and retention; native subagents retain completion/cancellation custody. A fenced atomic migration extracts supported historical outcomes before retiring the generalized tables. Obsolete persistence, repairs, runtime projections, and Tasks-only tests are removed instead of renamed.

Validation also repaired native wait ordering: published facts no longer discard pending read/cleanup custody, and cancellation joins that work before returning. Native admission again preserves persistence-failure context and refuses untracked dispatch. No new lifecycle ledger was introduced.

Published head: `22c5772d632d57a17c5068295a5fcc5b5ea02ae6` (the publisher’s metadata commit has the exact reviewed source tree). The candidate integrates pinned main `264c3355f0d5db50c223f286df21c8f9e437049d`; GitHub still reports conflicts with newer main, which must be resolved before merge. It also repairs retained Cron transcript sizing and keeps main’s attribution, accessible roles, and close-focus behavior. Page-owned styles no longer get absorbed into measured JavaScript boot groups; no styles, size budgets, or baselines were relaxed.

## Evidence

- Schema/history/audit proof: **156 tests / 7 files passed**, including retirement, released-outcome extraction, rollback/refusal, publication deferral, and read-only admission.
- Native recovery/cancellation closure: **228 tests / 5 files passed**, 49.73s wall. Gateway admission/continuation closure: **337 tests / 2 files passed**, 65.31s. These include the real failed wait/publication/abort boundaries, durable replacement rollback, persistence refusal, and the original registry ordering.
- Broader Cron, Gateway, backup/update and native suites were exercised in selected batches, not the full repository suite. Native archive E2E: **25 tests passed**, 33.23s Vitest plus a 363.7s runtime build. Synthetic Codex retry-policy fixture: **19 tests passed**. All cited runtime batches used `--maxWorkers=1`. Integration builds passed; final package/old-updater proof is separate.
- Canonical UI build and performance checks passed. Largest/startup CSS is **51,144 bytes gzip**; all budgets unchanged. The bundle regression fails on the original style owner. **27 focused tests / 2 files passed** (9.74s wall), with production-bundle Chromium smoke for new/chat/plugins.
- Native locale cleanup carried all existing translations through the owning generator: **zero translation/model calls**. Canonical protocol, SDK, database types/inventory, and localization artifacts were regenerated; docs link audit passed.
- Actual-source synthetic UI captures were inspected and delivered in chat: [initial removal comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156532#issuecomment-5795714072) and [retained Cron transcript comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156532#issuecomment-5804126330). Both pairs are embedded in GitHub.

**Published 9.2 acceptance passed:** [Package Acceptance attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35950915786) completed successfully in **36m51s**, with workflow, tooling, frozen admission, and package source all bound to `22c5772d632d57a17c5068295a5fcc5b5ea02ae6`. The actual installed `2026.9.2` updater upgraded to candidate `2026.9.5`/schema 19. The single `legacy-operator-state` lane passed, including the corrected already-current no-op, clean Doctor, formerly-bundled-plugin Doctor, and subsequent completion checks. Nine jobs passed; 15 unselected jobs were skipped and are not coverage.

The inspected [published proof artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35950915786/artifacts/10790140029) records `passed` / `published-updater-import-preserved`: two retained history rows, the import receipt, and unrelated state were preserved; retired Task/Flow tables and indexes were absent; content schema 19 coexisted with published markers 15 while the old updater remained active. The qualifying Doctor already saw migrated content on entry, so this is preservation proof—not a claim that this particular Doctor first migrated it. No-op/Doctor outcomes are backed by executed source assertions, phase receipts, and successful log markers; their raw standalone reports are not separately published. Backup rollback is not applicable to the 9.2 lane.

The [harness-only no-op correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e1540139144e59cd385aae39428c1474fe2cbe4b) fixed the first run’s advisory misclassification without changing runtime code. Its regression failed on the original assertion; **101 tests / 2 files passed** in 10.85s, with type/lint/Docker-boundary checks and scoped P0 review.

**Proof limitations:** the Doctor/Gateway process fixture reached ready, but the parent’s loopback probe received a non-JSON HTTP 502 through this host’s proxy path. Its assertions and timeout remain unchanged; this is not counted as passing startup proof. No live-provider, native-device, or full-repository-suite claim is made. The installed-package private-completion scenario remains unrun locally.

**Final local verification:** production and all affected test/extension/script/root type lanes passed across scoped runs. Typed lint, full UI stylelint, line-cap and assertion-safety guards passed; baseline changes only remove or reduce retired debt. The source and isolated validation checkout match across **48,600 files**. Related: #142863

Stack: follows #155288 (`openclaw/session-groups-active-registration-custody`). The passive migration drafts remain separate and held.

## What Problem This Solves

Group membership discovery is mixed into the catalog writer and reused by authorization and mutations, making the ownership migration harder to review.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The global catalog, member selection, permission checks, defaults, ordering, and registration custody remain unchanged. This does not activate agent-owned groups or change state schema 17.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing metadata-only membership resolver into one reader module and switch all four production consumers together, preserving their six call points. The complete function signature/body is byte-identical, including the environment, physical store agent IDs, iteration order, `projection: "list"`, and `clone: false`. Remove its old export rather than adding a facade. Only the existing resolver test mock changes module ownership.

## Evidence

- Candidate: **50 tests passed across five suites**, covering membership metadata, global catalog/rename/delete behavior, group RPCs, sharing authorization, and registration workers. The earlier 38-case baseline run is separate evidence.
- Core production and canonical selected test-type graphs passed. Formatting/lint, line/suppression/assertion ratchets, whitespace, and production Knip passed; static and runtime import cycles are zero.
- Source/registration/caller/mock parity and all seven final hashes verified. Fresh independent P0–P2 review: scoped-clean.
- Seven files, **+41/−42** against the immediate base; no new tests, schema fields, runtime flags, compatibility layer, or guard exception.

The first candidate invocation executed no tests because source-shaped proof copies were created during compilation. Those copies were changed to text artifacts after the checks stopped; the compiler guard was left intact. A fresh invocation with a frozen topology produced the 50 passing candidate cases above. The failed receipt remains retained.

**Exact-head hosted CI passed.** [Run 35672510491, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672510491) completed successfully on `0a5db52f064b1e9dbdd6992c3baf5bd0fc8d30f9`: 146 successful jobs and 17 skipped, none failed or pending. Skips are not execution proof. The tested merge `c2229aeac659d87d6e00aa1da9fefc660cdcce6e` has the exact declared base/head parents and matching tree `3fec3d9dfc0e4afeb9e75720f26daf4161c9dcdd`.

All 50 named cases matched individual hosted passing log records: [member reader — 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672510491/job/106572128230), [catalog and registration — 26 + 5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672510491/job/106572128151), [group RPCs — 9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672510491/job/106572127891), and [sharing authorization — 7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35672510491/job/106572127917). Production/test types, production/full-tree dead-code checks, runtime/static cycles and relevant source/lint guards passed. The committed-source trace confirms one resolver, four production importers and six call points, with no old export/facade.

Browser/E2E, native, QA/Docker and compatibility jobs among the 17 skips remain unexecuted proof. The build-artifacts job succeeded, but installation/upgrade behavior was not independently qualified. No broader live-Gateway/native/upgrade claim follows; activation and predecessor qualification gaps remain open.

prs.title: feat(talk): preauthorize exact installed-app launches
prs.body:
## Superseded by split draft PRs

This combined proposal is superseded by the following separately scoped **DRAFT** stack:

1. [#159693 — truthful source execution outcomes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159693), head 6ff285da40af30dad5135b0edc6928e5717a742c, targeting main.
2. [#159695 — constrained Linux app discovery and launch with ordinary confirmation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159695), head fc3c91ad930385e0bb182f2b78290421aaf67bd6, based on #159693's branch/head.
3. [#159697 — optional scoped repeat preauthorization](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159697), head 728319629289470659e5a2fffdaf783ba4348068, based on #159695's branch/head.

All three replacements remain drafts. Supersession is not a merge-readiness, full-CI or deployment claim. The original branch openclaw/talk-scoped-preauthorization-153092 and head af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b are preserved.

The original proposal and historical evidence below remain as context; their earlier source/package/live results are not relabeled as proof of the split heads. Each replacement main body records its own executed behavior proof and limits.

---

Related: #153092

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated voice requests to open the same approved desktop app otherwise require another Talk confirmation every time. This change adds an operator-managed, expiring preauthorization for one exact installed-app target without granting general command execution.

It also repairs the failures found while exercising that path: ordinary continuation must not inherit another client's authority; native consultation must retain its admitted Gateway and operational tool-execution record; a spoken one-shot approval must not survive an overlapping policy-authorized launch and later authorize a replay after policy revocation; and Linux Desktop Entry labels and executable strings must be decoded correctly without admitting shell commands or arguments.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Talk confirmation owner reads `talk.realtime.appLaunchPolicies` from committed runtime configuration. Grants bind the agent, paired voice device, target node, installed app, revision and expiry. Each consultation carries its own fresh authenticated ingress authority; call records and persisted diagnostic data cannot restore a grant.

The Gateway rechecks policy, originating-device revocation and node authority after preparation, then issues a short-lived invocation-bound permit. The node independently revalidates execution permission and the current installed-app descriptor immediately before non-shell dispatch. Preparation remains non-consuming; the final app-effect boundary consumes a matching spoken grant even when a reusable policy independently permits the same action. Revocation prevents effects that have not crossed the authoritative dispatch boundary, not an already admitted launch.

The native-consultation repairs bind the existing admitted Gateway resolver and publish canonical operational start/terminal facts independently of optional diagnostics. They do not fabricate a downstream execution record or remove the missing-record guard. Cancellation is forwarded through the existing invocation path. Existing config, diagnostic and node helper owners were extracted coherently; no second execution mechanism was added.

This refresh is the existing reviewed commit `af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b`, tree `036639cb8a35a41999169700fb877021afb7f5d5`. The frozen review/comparison base is `aac3e8a6ed27301bd56cfe4e97dbf96d88bb53f7`. The earlier published candidate `2daadf0d944d0c48c0e5bae54c484621506eacc1` is an ancestor, not a substitute for this head's proof.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into narrowly scoped repeat app launches while ordinary Talk confirmations, pairing, installed-app sharing, explicit node-command allowlisting and independent execution policy remain in force. Absent or empty policy lists preserve ordinary behavior. A signed device identity used with a shared Gateway token is not equivalent to paired-device-token authentication.

**Still DRAFT: no readiness, merge or deployment claim. The UI performance gate requires explicit disposition.**

Boundaries and compatibility:

- Coverage remains top-level Linux XDG Desktop Entries resolving to a native ELF executable with zero arguments. Shell/script launchers, arguments, field codes, custom working directories and other platforms are outside this contract.
- `Name` and the first stage of `Exec` now use strict Desktop Entry string decoding. Valid paired escaping remains supported; malformed escaping is rejected before the existing quoted-executable parser.
- The existing bounded app-ID schema was not broadened. The installation/filesystem remains a trusted installed-software boundary, not a new isolation guarantee against hostile local writers.
- Ordinary continuation from a different or unknown origin still works, but cannot inherit the prior client's reusable grant. Realtime provider/mode normalization preserves policy lists; canonical schema validation rejects malformed policy values.
- No feature-specific SQL migration or new stored-record version was introduced by these follow-ups. Older strict schemas reject the new policy key even when it is `[]`: an authorized downgrade must revoke/apply, drain in-flight launches, and remove that key before using the older schema.

## Evidence

### Exact source, completed review and focused validation

The full requested branch/local review cycle completed; its final branch-wide **R12 review was scoped-clean, with no accepted findings remaining**. Earlier interrupted attempts were not counted as successful verdicts. This is the retained review outcome for the bounded implementation, not a new merge-readiness review or a claim of current full CI.

- **201/201 focused tests across 12 files** passed on recorded code/test tree `1c98f99628f399c249c4e0ebf6fae67d0519e58c`. Its difference from the final tree is only `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`.
- **37/37 additional ingress/revocation/continuation tests across four files** passed on final tree `036639cb8a35a41999169700fb877021afb7f5d5`: **238 focused tests across 16 files** with the stated input provenance.
- Coverage includes six registered app-launch cases, 15 native Codex integration modes, 29 Linux parser cases, both node launch suites, confirmation/store/cancellation lifetimes, and runtime/manifest behavior. The grant/policy overlap regression failed before the repair with two launches where one was expected, then passed with final-boundary consumption and non-consuming preparation. Malformed Exec escaping likewise had a recorded failing-before/passing-after regression.
- All **12 selected validation steps** passed: 11 static steps plus the behavior-suite step. These covered line/max/assertion ratchets, the core import graph, three hard-zero Knip scans, scoped core/Gateway/Talk-node/root-test TypeScript, and whole-change core/root-test lint. Docs formatting and diff checks passed.
- This does **not** claim full repository CI, every type shard, a fresh installed-plugin/provider matrix, or an automatic waiver of the performance result below. Newly triggered CI must be judged on its actual head and result.

Relevant public scenario sources: [registered app-launch boundaries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/src/gateway/talk/app-launch.registered.test.ts), [native consultation integration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/test/plugins/talk-app-launch.codex-native.gateway.test.ts), [authenticated runtime scenario](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/test/talk-app-launch.authenticated.e2e.test.ts), and [Linux parser regressions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/af640b6de9de6894c6f81acc53e35d43b371fe9b/src/infra/installed-apps-linux.test.ts).

### Real Behavior Proof — executed, with separate evidence scopes

The following are sanitized technical records, not raw private logs or transcripts.

**P1 — isolated authenticated runtime / visible native effect**

- **Claim / surface:** the installed-app path can cross the real Gateway → node → OS boundary and produce a visible native application effect.
- **Scenario / environment:** the authenticated scenario linked above used the `af640b6` source Gateway, a freshly built node process, and a native ELF GUI fixture under Xvfb on isolated Linux x64. Only inference was a deterministic loopback fixture.
- **Observed result / reference:** the selected real-runtime test passed; the retained result records one passing scenario and an observed native window. This is the same-source runtime record, separate from the later delivered archive identified in P2.
- **Limits:** not actual user speech, not a live provider call, and not an installed-tarball upgrade matrix. A fixture window is not the operator's desktop.

**P2 — complete candidate npm archive / integrity and delivery**

- **Claim / surface:** the complete package was built from the intended immutable source and survived transfer without changing bytes.
- **Scenario / environment:** one canonical package build on isolated Linux x64 using Node **24.18.1**, pnpm **12.4.0** and npm **11.16.0** after frozen dependency installation. Actual Git HEAD/tree/index were checked before and after packaging.
- **Observed result / artifact reference:** canonical helper exit **0**; tarball inventory/import-graph checks passed; embedded identity and gzip integrity matched; complete transfer/download copies matched the archive's size and SHA-256. The operator independently confirmed the same identity and 12,395 safe tar members with the required CLI and Gateway-SDK entries.
- **Artifact identity:** `openclaw-pr153299-af640b6-private.tgz`; **77,805,135 bytes**; SHA-256 **6a2740bdd9cf080c426d797c56f790589b9fa31d9bf81f980d8a08a93b2af639**; build **2026.9.5-af640b6de9de-2026-09-22T11-18-39.000Z**; commit/tree as stated above. No public artifact URL is supplied here.
- **Limits:** the enclosing execution reported exit **1**, not an all-green run; see P4. No new installed-plugin acceptance/upgrade matrix is claimed for these bytes. Source-equivalent P1 and historical package CI are not relabeled as that matrix.

**P3 — bounded human-operated live smoke on the delivered build, 2026-09-23**

- **Claim / surface:** an actual voice confirmation can launch the installed Linux calculator, and an operator-observed negative confirmation can leave it closed.
- **Scenario / environment:** the isolated Gateway, Linux node, CLI and external client's Gateway SDK were selected from the P2 candidate. The actual client connection reported the matching build and device-token authentication. The node command surface remained `device.apps` and `device.apps.launch`; no app-launch policy was added for this smoke.
- **Observed result / reference:** operator attestation for this dated scenario reports a confirmation request, affirmative response followed by visible app launch, and both conversation bubbles. In the separate negative case, cancellation was acknowledged and the operator explicitly confirmed the app remained closed. The reported final client state was connected and idle, with `active=false` and `requested=false`.
- **Limits:** this is operator-observed no launch, **not an independently captured no-dispatch/no-spawn trace**. It does not claim a complete refreshed replay/expiry/wrong-target matrix or full call trace. In particular, no-policy yes/no interaction is not a fresh live test of overlapping spoken/reusable grants and replay after revocation; the scoped automated regression covers that invariant. External-client presentation work did not change OpenClaw core bytes.

**P4 — helper-0 / enclosing-1 diagnosis, 2026-09-23**

- **Claim / surface:** successful payload completion can be followed by a nonzero runner exit at noninteractive login-shell logout.
- **Scenario / environment:** one corrected harmless native Crabbox 0.63.0 SSH/`--shell` probe preserved the original `set -eu` login-shell conditions with no TTY. The prior `set -u` control was retained, not rerun. The corrected probe did not require an OpenClaw build.
- **Observed result / sanitized trace reference:** payload statuses **0 / 0 / 0**, then requested `exit 0`; `.bash_logout:6` invoked `/usr/bin/clear_console -q`; that cosmetic command returned **1**; active errexit propagated **raw SSH exit 1 → Crabbox exit 1**. An ERR observer only printed the existing status; it changed no shell options and installed no EXIT trap. No logout file was changed or skipped.
- **Disposition / limits:** the failure mechanism is runner-image logout after a successful payload, not evidence that the canonical package helper failed. It explains the retained helper-0/enclosing-1 split under matching strict conditions, but **does not retroactively instrument or relabel the historical failed run**. The earlier native control also omitted the unavailable repository JS launcher and the original errexit option, so it was not full invocation-equivalence proof. The proposed TTY-only, best-effort cosmetic logout cleanup has not been applied by this PR.

### UI performance gate — measured and explained, NOT passed

One baseline-only UI build used the immutable reviewed base **aac3e8a6ed27301bd56cfe4e97dbf96d88bb53f7**, tree **edbb5e6e96d3f016cc4c7b178b5c32d6e544b44d**, with matching external tools: Node 24.18.1, pnpm 12.4.0, npm 11.16.0, Vite 8.3.0 and Pako 3.0.1. Frozen dependencies and generation inputs were checked. Candidate UI build identity was an explicitly logged **measurement-only seed** to hold metadata constant; actual baseline Git provenance remained the base, not the candidate. The standard helper that rebuilds both sides was not run; retained candidate sidecars were reused.

| Seven startup JS assets | Shipped gzip bytes | Over unchanged 364,774 B limit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Frozen reviewed baseline, matched measurement inputs | **364,777** | **3 B** |
| Retained `af640b6` candidate | **364,815** | **41 B** |

The limit is **364,198 B recorded baseline + 512 B growth allowance + 64 B build-variance allowance = 364,774 B**. The measured pair difference is **+38 B**; both raw startup totals are **1,183,608 B**.

The bounded offline artifact comparison found all seven startup payloads identical after accounting for verified generated asset-name hashes; one was already byte-identical. Gzip headers matched. Per-pair gzip deltas were **+15, +20, +1, +1, 0, +1, 0 B**. Referenced targets were followed rather than blindly normalized: there were no conflicting target mappings or missing executable targets, and one deferred target had a genuine **40-byte raw reduction**. That target difference was retained, not treated as equivalent; source-map payload equivalence is not claimed.

Thus the observed +38 B startup gzip difference is compression of changed generated filename strings, **not added authored startup payload in this artifact pair**. This is one controlled pair, not a repeatability study or a license to change application behavior to chase a different hash. The served-byte measurements and failing gate remain real. Packaging intentionally runs the performance checker in report-only mode, which explains why a printed violation can coexist with a successful package helper.

**The UI gate still needs explicit disposition. Neither name normalization nor the baseline's 3 B excess is a passing score or automatic waiver. No source, lockfile, budget threshold or baseline was changed for this investigation. Readiness is not claimed.**

### Historical evidence retained separately

- **`2daadf0`:** repaired missing native tool-execution recording by publishing canonical operational facts independently of optional diagnostics; preserved the guard, approval and permit boundaries. Its focused native integration, earlier review and operator live acceptance remain earlier-source evidence, not `af640b6` coverage. [Selected Package Acceptance run 35645485296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35645485296) passed its 11 executed jobs, including package integrity, npm 12 install.sh acceptance and selected Gateway/config/onboarding lanes. Fifteen unselected jobs were skipped. Its package SHA-256 was `70dfd6c4123d89d910a9586be0aea887411a2122f670704e8399e9f1dc7408b4`, build `2026.9.5-2daadf0d944d-2026-09-21T19-35-15.413Z`. Those are not the P2 archive or a full current-head CI result.
- **`96c28a9` and earlier recorded trees:** retained admitted-Gateway binding, continuation/lifetime, config-normalization and authority-chain evidence remains historical. The controlled authenticated chain covered shared-token/wrong-device denial, intended-device launch/repeat, policy revocation and originating-device-token revocation. Earlier routing/effect-record failures and their repairs are not erased by the new bounded smoke. [Earlier selected package acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35627427760) is likewise not current-head proof.

The native integration's dependency boundary was personally checked at upstream Codex **8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4**: [dynamic call identity emission](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1085-L1114), [response routing](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs#L18-L52), and [dynamic-tool protocol fields](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs#L1652-L1668). Codex transports call identity/arguments and responses; OpenClaw owns the operational mutation classification and retained Gateway authority.

Worked on by: @brokemac79 (issue, requirements, product scope, and operator validation).

prs.title: [openclaw] feat(slack): add channel canvas create and edit actions
prs.body:
Related: #133016

Overlaps with #136794. This candidate is limited to the channel's native canvas (`conversations.canvases.create`) and verifies its current Slack association before mutation; it does not persist bindings for standalone canvases. Maintainer coordination is needed before proceeding with parallel implementations.

## What Problem This Solves

Slack users can keep durable channel plans and decisions in canvases, but the native message tool has no canvas create/edit actions. Ordinary message editing does not edit a canvas.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `canvas-create` and `canvas-edit` to the native Slack plugin using the existing Slack SDK. Scope this first implementation to a channel's own canvas: verify fresh channel/canvas association with the bot identity and enforce the existing channel and cross-context policies before mutation. Canvas actions do not inherit conversation threads or count as chat replies.

Gate both actions behind a new default-off `channels.slack.actions.canvas` switch. This prevents existing installations from advertising actions that need a scope they do not yet have. Discovery and direct dispatch both enforce the gate, and named-account overrides remain account-scoped.

Standalone canvas sharing, access-control changes, canvas deletion, renaming, and section lookup are not included. No new dependencies are added.

## User Impact

Bot accounts can create a channel canvas or append, insert, replace, and delete sections of its existing canvas. Before use, add the optional `canvases:write` bot scope, reauthorize the app, and set `channels.slack.actions.canvas: true` (or the corresponding named-account setting). These actions do not need `canvases:read`.

Existing installations do not advertise or execute Canvas actions by default. Existing message actions and user-identity accounts retain their current behavior.

The Slack guide documents the scope, reauthorization, default-off configuration, examples, supported operations, whole-canvas replacement, and recovery from an ambiguous mutation response. This patch does not change any live app permissions or deploy a runtime.

## Evidence

- 394 targeted tests passed across 10 files, including the new default-off discovery/direct-dispatch regression, root and named-account config parsing, account-scoped discovery, real Slack SDK request serialization with synthetic transport, bot-only identity, fresh canvas association, named channel policy, malformed input, Enterprise workspace routing, failure/no-retry behavior, local/gateway thread handling, and cross-context restrictions.
- Proved the new default-off regression test failed before the production gate and passed after it. Earlier regression proofs also covered the bot-identity/default-DM defect and the thread/policy defects.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed on the final tree, including core, extension, and test typechecks; focused core/plugin lint; formatting on all 22 changed files; import cycles; dead-export scans; and repository guardrails.
- `pnpm check:docs` passed, including docs formatting, Markdown lint, MDX validation, 7,952 internal-link checks, and config-example validation.
- `pnpm build` passed on Node 26.5.1 with pnpm 12.1.0.
- The latest ClawSweeper P1 finding is addressed by the default-off runtime/discovery gate and setup documentation.

Targeted test command:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/slack/src/canvas-actions.test.ts \
  extensions/slack/src/config-schema.test.ts \
  extensions/slack/src/channel-actions-setup-status.contract.test.ts \
  extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts \
  extensions/slack/src/message-tools.test.ts \
  src/channels/plugins/message-actions.security.test.ts \
  src/channels/plugins/message-action-dispatch.registry.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-spec.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/outbound-policy.test.ts
```

API contract references:

- [Create channel canvases](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.canvases.create/)
- [Edit canvases](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/canvases.edit/)

Outstanding proof before merge:

- A fresh local autoreview was attempted on commit `92831e06` and stopped before sending a review bundle because the required TruffleHog scanner is unavailable in this environment. Automated review remains under the requester's existing explicit waiver; no clean autoreview result is claimed.
- Live Slack create/edit/readback: not run; no authorized test channel with the new bot scope is available to this run. Synthetic SDK-boundary tests are not live proof.
- Follow-up: apply the existing outbound text hygiene policy to plugin-owned document fields if canvas content should strip internal citation/tool-control markers like ordinary message text. This patch currently preserves authored Markdown.

Production growth is 317 lines for the new capability, default-off gate, configuration metadata, and identity/policy boundaries; tests grow by 666 lines, docs by 107. No existing delivery path was removed.

prs.title: feat(ui): recover saved attempts without replacing the draft
prs.body:
Related: #156625. Third focused replacement, stacked on #160792. **Draft only; landing remains paused.**

## What Problem This Solves

Adds explicit recovery of saved attempts without replacing the current draft, replaying old runs, or creating a second queue.

## User Impact

**Send** refreshes the exact saved input and submits complete plain user text as a new message from the current user. It follows ordinary idle, queue, Steer, or interrupt behavior and preserves the composer draft, attachments, and reply. **Discard** hides the saved presentation in this browser; it does not delete Gateway data or abort a run. Incognito decisions stay in memory.

Send intentionally rejects commands, system/forwarded content, incomplete reads, and messages requiring attachment, reply, mention, or work-context metadata. Those retain inspection/copy or native outbox Retry rather than losing information in a partial resend.

**Limit:** persisted retirement follows a qualified ACK from the initial delivery only. If the replacement waits in the queue or needs a later retry, the original saved source can still appear after reload or in another tab, even after eventual delivery. There is no cross-tab exactly-once guarantee or automatic replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing saved-input reader supplies current source and viewer facts; recovery uses the ordinary outbox and send path. Same-client guards prevent duplicate admission, while only explicit accepted ACKs—not local admission, malformed replies, or receipt-free preregistration—persist retirement. Native Retry keeps ownership of its complete payload, including across run-ID rotation. Saved-source ownership is scoped to the current physical session without deleting older outbox payloads.

## Evidence

- Actual failing-before/passing-after cases cover malformed ACK retirement, unchanged-source refresh during Send and ACK settlement, native Retry rotation/removal, and a physical reset retaining an older outbox entry with the same run ID.
- **1,062 unit/consumer tests across 20 files pass**, covering real admission, FIFO, ordinary send modes, current-user attribution, draft/media/reply preservation, native recovery, settings, and scoped races. Submit and ACK normalization are not mocked.
- A real Chromium regression removes the first clicked row, verifies another row moves under the same pointer coordinates, and proves click two cannot Send or Discard that different input. Both cases fail before the click guard; the existing copy interaction remains covered.
- Full-source-app Chromium proof with a synthetic Gateway verifies refreshed complete text on the wire, local-only Discard, the unchanged draft, and ordinary queued follow-ups. This is not live-provider/channel proof.
- Production UI and relevant test types, lint, styles, i18n, line/assertion ratchets, production UI build, and independent P1 review pass. Docs MDX/formatting pass; standalone local markdownlint was unavailable. No dependency, timeout, serial-test configuration, scheduler, or hard-budget change was used.

<details>
<summary>Measured focused test cost</summary>

One-worker wall seconds: payload 2.50; ACK 3.09; races 3.16; recovery preferences 2.10; mounted preferences 1.80. Integration: 4.51 seconds (17 cases); browser controls: 8.80 seconds (three cases, including actual row removal and hit-target verification). The combined 20-file unit/consumer run took 14.10 seconds. CI timing is not yet available.

</details>

### Before

![Saved attempts can only be inspected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61ba5db2-3667-4377-aae1-fb34e06d3844)

### After

![Explicit Send and Discard preserve the separate draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/984931dc-6f3c-425a-bb70-8f5128bbd331)

<details>
<summary>Ordinary queue behavior remains separate</summary>

![An ordinary follow-up remains queued behind the active run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1543455d-9244-4b8d-9b88-ce14d5f30a7b)

</details>

Requested by and co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/9fd56994-d68d-4025-b2ef-f288603a3785)

prs.body:
Related: #160066, #160159, #160177

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Control UI builds failing on main because the same clipboard-image helper was exported twice.

## User Impact

Developers can build the Control UI and unblock PR validation again. Existing image paste, attachment admission, and resize behavior are unchanged. No deployment or Gateway change is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove only the second, byte-identical `dataImageClipboardFile` definition from `chat-attachment-image.ts`. Keep the original helper and the existing caller import. The resulting module exactly matches the original extraction in 2e95cdba84c2.

The root red-main workflow required a direct repair, but GitHub refused the push with `GH013: Changes must be made through a pull request.` This PR is the enforced fallback, not an attempted bypass.

## Evidence

- Current-head CI [36386148574](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36386148574) failed in [control-ui-performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36386148574/job/108812294897): the repaired merge candidate built successfully (15.47 s), then the comparator rebuilt base `3b8ed47b09e61e165ac7ac95e1a03a379d791609` and hit the original duplicate-export parse error after 4.21 s, before comparing metrics. The [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36386148574/job/108812983612) consequently failed. Final run accounting: 2 failed jobs (comparator and aggregate), 24 cancelled, 20 skipped, and 4 successful; cancelled lanes are not passing coverage. This is a broken-base comparison, not a size-budget failure; no rerun, baseline change, or bypass was requested. ClawSweeper review is still in progress.
- Reproduced the exact failure on main baseline `a62d769b3cef9178acc9573f230446828ccc24e4`: `pnpm ui:build` failed with `PARSE_ERROR Duplicated export dataImageClipboardFile` (4.80 s wall).
- After the repair, `pnpm ui:build` passed, including verification of 1,060 finalized Control UI sidecars (14.40 s wall). Its existing advisory report still lists startup JS gzip 48 bytes above its enforcement threshold; no size baseline was changed.
- All 34 existing tests passed across `chat-attachments.test.ts`, `chat-view.attachment-paste.test.ts`, and `composer-attachments.test.ts` (13.45 s wall). Repeated after incorporating the new main test-runner changes: 34 passed (4.03 s wall). No tests were added or changed.
- Focused oxfmt, oxlint, UI typecheck, and `git diff --check` passed (combined 19.59 s wall).
- Independent autoreview completed scoped-clean through P2. The patch is one file with 27 duplicate lines removed.
- Main was rechecked at `3b8ed47b09e61e165ac7ac95e1a03a379d791609`; it still contained both definitions. The repair was rebased patch-identically onto that main. UI/build inputs were unchanged, and affected tests were rerun.

prs.title: fix: stop GitHub links opening in the read-only reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub links open in a separate, incomplete read-only reader instead of following the existing Browser panel route.

## User Impact

GitHub links now behave like other external links: native Mac tabs in the macOS app, or real Agent browser tabs when **Open links in Control UI browser** is enabled. Otherwise they retain normal external navigation. The Browser panel displays the actual GitHub website.

The bundled `github` preview/reader plugin is removed, not disabled. Existing `github` plugin configuration produces retirement warnings rather than blocking startup; `openclaw doctor --fix` removes stale references. GitHub credentials, managed identities, publishing, repository access, and session PR status remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the plugin registration, reader/preview/image RPC implementations, caches, GitHub-only hover enrichment, and obsolete tests/docs. The surviving GitHub transport moves to its core consumers without changing credential selection or network policy. No new preview implementation or routing-priority workaround is introduced.

The shipped generic third-party link-reader SDK remains supported. The old `controlUi.githubPreview` method retains only a nonretryable removed-feature response to preserve its frozen protocol position; it performs no credential lookup or network request. Most of this diff deletes the retired feature and its tests.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway captures click https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155192 from the same synthetic chat at 1600 × 1000, with the same Browser preference and `plugins.allow: ["github", "browser"]` configuration. Before uses base `c6b21f6f086a8f3c16bbd37eb143906c9035a09e`; after uses the candidate build. No mock Gateway, fake native bridge, or composed HTML is used.

Before: the click invokes `github.preview`, `github.detail`, and `github.image` and opens the API reader.

After: the click invokes `browser.request` (`/tabs/open`, `/screencast`, `/act`) and shows the actual GitHub website; no retired reader RPC is requested.

The attached after image is a real, inspected Gateway screencast captured by the diagnostic screenshot after a harness readiness assertion incorrectly queried across a shadow root and timed out. The image shows the settled GitHub page, and the request log confirms the real Browser route. That harness assertion was corrected. A later attempt independently hit a 20-second Browser screenshot timeout; this remains an observed limitation, not a claimed fix. Linux Agent browser routing is proven; live macOS native tabs were not exercised.

After

![After: actual GitHub website in the Browser panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54e60554-8b08-4730-9289-d3ea96c0405f)

Full lint and the remaining checks completed separately on a fresh, equivalently bound Testbox; the interrupted aggregate is not reported as green.
