prs.title: feat(a2a): implement the A2A protocol v1.0 specification
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades the `extensions/a2a` channel plugin from partial 0.3-era support to a **conformance-validated implementation of the A2A protocol v1.0 specification**, tested against the official [a2a-tck](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-tck) conformance suite (remaining failures are limited to scripted-reference-SUT-only scenarios — see Evidence). All configuration remains backward compatible with the original plugin.

## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/a2a` plugin currently implements only a partial, 0.3-era subset of the A2A protocol. A2A has since shipped **v1.0** with breaking changes and new requirements:

- **New method surface**: `SendMessage`/`GetTask`/`ListTasks`/`CancelTask`/`SendStreamingMessage`/`SubscribeToTask` replace the 0.3 dotted methods, plus push notification config CRUD and `GetExtendedAgentCard` — v1.0 clients calling a 0.3-era server get `Method not found`
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` (spec §5.4) with gRPC-transcoding-style path bindings — required for REST-native clients, previously absent
- **Revised error model**: codes `-32001..-32009` with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details, and new HTTP status mappings (`TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502) — the old mappings no longer conform
- **Capability, media-type, and required-extension validation** (spec §3.3.4, §3.1.1, §4.6) — previously not enforced
- **Agent Card caching** (ETag/304, §8.6.1) and the **Extended Agent Card** — previously absent
- **Push notification webhooks** with idempotent delete (§3.1.10) and SSRF protection — previously absent

In short: without this change, the plugin cannot interoperate with A2A v1.0 clients and fails the official conformance suite. With it, it passes (see Evidence below) while every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default.

## Evidence

### a2a-tck conformance suite (official, black-box against a live instance)

Latest completed round (round 5 of 6, after fixes):

- **Overall: 72.5% / MUST requirements: 73.9% passing** (up from a baseline where P0/P1-critical scenarios failed)
- Per-transport: `agent_card` **10/10**; `jsonrpc` 74 passed / 5 failed; `http_json` 63 passed / 6 failed
- Every remaining failure is either (a) `DM-ART-001`/`DM-MSG-001`, which **by design require a scripted reference SUT** echoing `tck-artifact-*` prefixes in artifacts/messages — not satisfiable by an LLM-backed gateway and not applicable to a real deployment, or (b) already fixed and re-verified in round 6 (in progress), e.g. the REST push-config path-binding issue (`PUSH-CREATE-001`) and the jsonrpc snake_case params bug in the TCK client itself
- Round-6 confirmation so far: **all P0 and P1 findings now pass** (verified live against the running instance)

### Unit tests and typecheck (this repo)

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/a2a
Test Files  12 passed (12)
     Tests  131 passed (131)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test   # typecheck: green
```

Coverage highlights among the 131 tests: method aliases, trailing-slash normalization, extended-card error codes (`-32007`), media-type rejection (`-32005` with ErrorInfo metadata), card cache headers + `If-None-Match` → 304, REST status mapping (409/415), push-config path-wins regression (`taskId: "wrong-task-from-body"`), and idempotent push-config delete.

### Config compatibility

- All pre-existing config keys verified unchanged (name/semantics/default) — existing deployments upgrade without touching config
- New keys are opt-in; `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` and the metadata sync check passes

## What's implemented

### Core protocol (§3)
- All **11 JSON-RPC methods** defined in v1.0: `SendMessage`, `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `SubscribeToTask`, the four push notification config CRUD methods (`SetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `GetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `ListTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig`), and `GetExtendedAgentCard`
- Backward-compatible **0.3-era dotted method aliases** (`message/send`, `message/stream`, `tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/subscribe`, ...) so existing clients keep working
- **Agent Card** served at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` with ETag / Last-Modified / Cache-Control caching and `If-None-Match` → 304 handling (§8.6.1)
- **Extended Agent Card** served behind the `extendedAgentCard` capability

### Transports
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` per §5.4, with gRPC-transcoding-style URL path bindings (path parameters take precedence over body fields)
- **SSE streaming** with resumable task updates
- **gRPC-style HTTP status mappings** per §5.4: `TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502

### Error model
- Full v1.0 error codes **-32001..-32009** with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details (reason / domain / metadata); JSON-RPC reserved codes (-32700..-32603) carry no ErrorInfo, as required

### Push notifications (§3.1.10)
- Full config CRUD with **idempotent delete** (repeated deletes succeed silently, per spec)
- Webhook delivery with **SSRF protection** (private-network targets blocked unless explicitly allowed)
- Configurable authentication schemes (bearer, basic, apikey)

### Validation
- **Capability validation** (§3.3.4): calling a method whose capability is disabled returns `-32004` `UnsupportedOperation`; enabling `extendedAgentCard` without configuring it returns `-32007`
- **Media-type validation** (§3.1.1): raw/url part media types checked against `inputModes` (with `type/*` and `*/*` wildcard support) before text-part checks, returning `-32005` with ErrorInfo metadata
- **Required extensions** (§4.6): extensions declared with `required: true` that are not activated via the `A2A-Extensions` header return `-32008`

### Outbound agent-to-agent client
- Full `Message | Task` oneof parsing with ErrorInfo reason surfacing in thrown errors

## Configuration compatibility

- **No breaking changes**: every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default
- New v1.0 features are **opt-in** via new keys: `capabilities.*` (skill discovery, extensions, push), `pushNotifications.*` (auth, webhook options), `rest.enabled`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`
- `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` so core startup validation accepts the new keys
- Config-surface budget: this consciously raises the `channel` baseline by **+30 entries** (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`, channel 3975 → 4005) — exactly the new opt-in A2A v1.0 keys (`capabilities.*`, `pushNotifications.*`, `rest.*`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`, and peers/auth knobs); no existing keys changed

## Notes

- Rebased onto latest `main` (`65fc2f00d`); the diff is limited to `extensions/a2a/` + the regenerated config metadata file, and upstream's `wait()`/`buildContext` refactors from #178508 are integrated
- Happy to split into smaller commits or adjust scope per maintainer feedback

## What Problem This Solves

Adopts worker-local inference in the TUI and Control UI on top of merged #165960.

- Shows worker inference as a placement capability, not as a second source of configuration truth.
- Preserves explicit model/runtime validation and existing Gateway permission checks.
- Uses worker-owned credentials only for the selected direct worker profile.

prs.title: refactor(sessions): unify in-memory turn, queue, and stop ownership
prs.body:
Related: #160737

## What Problem This Solves

Session turns, queued inputs, cancellation and mutations rely on overlapping owners, making it difficult to keep stale callbacks and unfinished cleanup from interfering with the next turn.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is consistent ordering and cancellation across channel, Gateway, native and scheduled work, with successors and mutations waiting for the correct outstanding work to settle.

**Draft for design/code review, not merge-ready.** Full latest-source reply E2E and some isolated integration proof remain incomplete. This is a broad in-memory ownership cutover, not a claim of measured performance or maintenance-time improvement.

**No SQLite schema change:** no tables/columns, schema-version bump or migration; no durable mailbox is introduced. Existing persisted write/delete formats remain, but their admission and cleanup ordering change, including session deletion, maintenance preservation, startup orphan checks and delivery enqueue admission.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing reply-operation owner into a physical-session controller rather than add another scheduler:

- One mailbox/selector for queued inputs and native work; adapters retain authorization, routing, batching and delivery policy.
- Exact store/incarnation, operation, source and backend-attempt identities for late callbacks, steering and cancellation.
- Shared Stop and mutation coordination; an abort or terminal outcome is not proof of raw writer/source settlement.
- Controller-owned progress/watchdog state; global capacity and database write fences remain separate owners.

The goal is correctness and maintainability, not a net line reduction. The implementation is larger and still uses imperative mailbox/lifecycle/Stop modules around a narrower pure phase/outcome reducer.

### Umbrella issue coverage

“Addressed” below means implementation is present in this draft, not that each issue's full acceptance criteria are complete. No issue is auto-closed.

| Issue | Coverage in this draft | Remaining qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Related: #160738 — statechart, invariants and model tests | **Partial:** controller documentation, pure phase/outcome reducer and seeded models driving real boundaries | Not the proposed complete pure controller transition/effect model; full shared acceptance and cost accounting remain open |
| Related: #160739 — busy state and run ownership | Canonical controller ownership and attached native attempts replace independent turn ownership | Distinct busy/admissible/injectable/settled projections remain intentional; cross-surface acceptance pending |
| Related: #160740 — queueing and steering | Canonical mailbox, interrupt priority, collect/source custody and shared admission; old queue/adoption owners retired | Full current reply/channel E2E pending; guarded steering during compaction preserves supported runtime behavior rather than blanket rejection |
| Related: #160741 — Gateway chat.send and agent RPC | Shared input/turn admission; RPC source correlation replaces Gateway-owned queue/abort decisions | Complete mixed-surface, UI and restart acceptance not claimed |
| Related: #160742 — Stop entry points | Common captured-target cancellation with retained cleanup and source-specific scope | Preserve legitimate source-specific effects/hooks; complete entry-point QA pending |
| Related: #160743 — mutations and per-session lanes | Reset/delete/compaction coordination through controller; per-session turn lanes retired | Global capacity, persisted fences and subordinate physical-effect custody remain; isolated integration proof pending |
| Related: #160744 — watchdog | Operation-owned progress/deadlines/recovery, without session-lane reset as recovery | Cancellation timeout cannot declare abort-insensitive work settled; complete issue-level acceptance remains open |

**Not addressed:** #160745, the separately reviewed durable mailbox / restart-persistence stage. No SQLite schema work is included.

## Evidence

Current focused evidence after pre-publication review corrections:

- Required independent review completed all **11 passes**. Its **7 findings were reproduced in 12 failing boundary cases**, then corrected; this is a reconciled review, not a claim of a clean pre-fix verdict.
- **92 passing cases across 9 complete owning test files**, combining applicable receipts without double-counting. Coverage includes exact-input admission, physical-store dedupe, incarnation-scoped mutation, retry custody, deadlines, RPC execution projection, bounded lifecycle responses and seeded models.
- Representative measured runner durations: archive lifecycle **18 cases / 20.59 s**; queue dedupe **16 / 3.15 s**; native lane controller **7 / 3.80 s**. The final lifecycle-only rerun was **11 / 42.45 s**, with 97% attributed to cold worker transformation, not sleeps; these tests exercise the real ownership boundary with deferred work/fake clocks.
- Production core types and all **26 affected canonical test graphs passed**; final local context-reuse cleanup received another core/owner-graph refresh. Scoped production/test lint, formatting, source line caps, assertion safety, import cycles, whitespace and all three native Knip scans passed (zero Knip entries).
- Earlier broad-candidate proof included a normal full package build (**318.67 s**) and **35 type execution graphs (322.41 s)**. That build preceded the final review corrections; it is not presented as a rebuilt final-head artifact.

**Known gaps / failures:**

- Full latest-source **222-case reply E2E is not complete**. The last completed full run on an older candidate was **210 passed / 12 failed**; later focused repairs are not a new full-suite pass.
- Telegram loopback remains unresolved after question registration; two auxiliary root integration files still need genuinely isolated runtime proof.
- Compound max-lines remains red on the inherited **environment budget 477 > 476** at the pinned base; not waived and not raised.
- Full changed-test cost accounting and current-head hosted CI remain pending. No CI reruns or workflow dispatches were used as proof.

<details>
<summary>Review navigation and size context</summary>

Start with `docs/concepts/session-controller.md`, then the controller state/mailbox, lifecycle/Stop and native attachment boundaries. The diff mixes ownership changes, caller migration and fixture changes; it is not 925 independent features.

Pre-publication path inventory (rename sides counted separately): **925 paths**, including **96 untracked replacement files**; **+40,696 / -32,903**, net **+7,793**. Filename-classified runtime: **+18,923 / -15,203**, net **+3,720**; tests/fixtures: **+21,498 / -17,683**, net **+3,815**. These are not GitHub's rename-aware display counts or a complexity/correctness score. The original estimate used a different baseline.

</details>

prs.body:
> **Superseded by [#150493](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150493).** The complete runtime-diagnostics branch is retained in the consolidated PR; this source PR is closed unmerged.

Closes #150323

## What Problem This Solves

Native runtime selection refusals share one public error, so diagnostics cannot distinguish missing prepared ownership, auth and resolution failures, runtime ineligibility, or a revoked commit guard.

## User Impact

No user-visible selection or error-message change. Trusted diagnostic consumers can inspect closed, content-free preparation and validation decisions without changing native auth, ownership, or persistence guards. No migration or configuration change is required.

**SDK rebuild compatibility:** `DiagnosticEventPayload` gains the `model.runtime_choice` variant. TypeScript consumers that exhaustively switch on `event.type` may need an explicit case when rebuilding against this SDK, including an intentional no-op for consumers that do not handle runtime-choice diagnostics. This source-compatibility implication is separate from installed configuration and selection behavior: no configuration migration is required, and the existing auth, ownership, and persistence decisions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The decision owner now emits versioned `model.runtime_choice` facts through the existing trusted diagnostic subscription. Every check explicitly records its reached result or `not-reached`. Delivery is asynchronous and excludes synchronous exporter preparation so observers cannot reenter the final guard.

Diagnostics remain best-effort and are not authorization or persistence receipts. Missing events, unknown fields, disabled diagnostics, and dropped events remain indeterminate. Consumers must isolate their observation window and project only closed allowlisted fields; dispatcher trace metadata is not report-safe.

## Evidence

### Coordinated conflict repair — September 27, 2026

Current source: `36b401427e3de34fb8ee5c9394235fbba11c04c3`. Coordinated with #150493; neither PR has been merged. The branches share one reviewed diagnostic envelope/RPC, dispatch-policy and recorder-policy preparation, rather than competing extractions. Both feature deltas compose without conflicts and preserve the current-main authority, suspension, queued-phase and privacy boundaries. Source cutoff: `bf636cc1bcdd59e65d5074a1bc309d903bf18e65`; later main `0d02ab7aaf657c1872a5dac32369e88504e3bd5c` also merges cleanly in the source-only preview.

- **Focused proof:** 48 focused diagnostic/selection/export cases passed across scoped runs; another 44 Codex-history cases, 30 test-planner cases, and the standalone wrapper-inventory check passed. The changed auth-fixture file passed `pnpm test src/agents/model-runtime-choice.runtime-diagnostics.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` in **16.60 s wall** (12 cases). Its current CI seconds remain pending.
- **Combined proof:** 69 cases across 8 files passed in **129.38 s**; normal `pnpm build` passed in **10m 33.3s**, including package declarations, runtime/plugin checks and shipped UI budgets. The existing CSS advisory remains; no budget was changed. The tested product tree was `0ffa12de9994feecdb751a462e7d9fcc63e9d60b`; subsequent changes only reorder type declarations, remove an obsolete lint exception and its exact baseline entry, and register the canonical Knip entry. Executable recorder statements are unchanged; targeted lint and growth-ratchet checks pass.
- **Types and review:** each branch's production core types passed; composed production, all 25 core-test graphs, plugin/plugin-test and root-test types passed. Fresh independent Astra/high **P0–P2** review of the combined source found no actionable findings. This is source review, not hosted CI evidence.
- **Test audit / deslop:** retained actual ordering, privacy and live-authority boundary tests; replaced the removed auth-fixture setter with its canonical binding API. Removed duplicate declarations from conflict composition and kept one owner per policy. No assertions, timeouts, ignores or limits were weakened; no retry-only changes.
- **Baseline failure:** the broader check exposed [#159888](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/159888), independently reproduced with baseline scanner/config sources. The existing prior-CI verifier was missing from Knip's executable roots. Registering that real consumer preserves the hard-zero policy; the same script scan and 37 checker tests now pass, with a separate clean P0–P2 review. Current main already contains the canonical fix in [0d02ab7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0d02ab7aaf657c1872a5dac32369e88504e3bd5c); these updates use that exact registration. Earlier failed runs remain failed evidence, not relabeled successes.
- **Still pending:** remaining selected local static gates, new exact-head hosted CI, and refreshed ClawSweeper review. **Not declared ready.** Existing SDK/published-plugin compatibility caveats remain unchanged; no merge or deployment is authorized by this update.

All earlier dated qualification below is historical and is not current-head CI proof.


### September 23 conflict integration and explicit prerequisite

Current candidate: `385929812ad2334f9680ce1c23b648355a746d08`, with frozen feature base `d17bc2129b609ae1d60b1242ac40bff5f202835f`. An exact composition preview found three real conflicts in the SDK documentation, diagnostic dispatcher, and stability recorder. The resolved feature tree preserves both queued-phase and runtime-choice trace-preparation guards, current commentary/run types and recorder behavior, the query helper owner, and runtime-choice non-export/non-retention. It does not refresh merely for moving main.

- **Feature qualification:** 88 selected cases passed: 81 dispatcher/exporter/recorder cases, six diagnostic selection/persistence cases, and one compiler-root ownership case. The queued-phase regression fails under the incorrect left-only conflict resolution and passes with both guards. A stale diagnostic fixture import failed before reaching its guard; it now calls the existing `applySessionModelSelectionInternal` owner, matching main's sibling tests, without restoring a production alias or bypassing authority checks. A complete-candidate Astra/high P0–P2 review found no actionable findings. The added queued-phase case executed in 2.33 ms; the 81-case canonical group took 43.55 seconds including setup, the six-case fixture took 19.15 seconds, and the root check took 7.06 seconds.
- **Retained failed gate:** the canonical changed check initially failed only at core lint on the unchanged main `src/cron/service/timer.test.ts`: 1,022 counted lines against 1,000. Its other preceding stages passed, including all production/test typechecks and dead-export scans; all eleven initially unreached checks subsequently passed separately. That original aggregate remains failed, not relabeled green.
- **Independently owned dependency:** [#156569](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156569), exact head `850f3c813ea35ce40dc82f3c9a3fa0dcefd9b246`, owns the timer repair. The dedicated dependency commit `385929812ad2334f9680ce1c23b648355a746d08` carries only the exact two-file implementation from `35ca31b86cfb46462319bac35930d3603a805ad7`. - Paired regression: the previous producer fails three real published-owner → native picker → SQLite → SDK collector assertions due to absent decision events; the candidate passes.
- Six native-entry/collector cases cover acceptance with both validations, refusal, commit-time revocation and nonmutation, throwing observers, synchronous exporter isolation, trust filtering, and closed projection rejecting incomplete facts.

At that OTel-correction boundary, native producer, selection, diagnostic contract, and SDK paths were unchanged. This is bounded behavior/source transport, not whole-package byte equivalence; no package or completed native baseline was rebuilt. The complete scoped two-file changed gate passed, including extension production/test types and architecture checks. **Historical qualification: required hosted CI failed on `5f7ccad039e3`; that head was not fully qualified or merge-ready.** [CI run 35168314141, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35168314141) completed all 157 jobs. prs.title: feat(ui): post human discussion without waiting for the agent
prs.body:
Related: #156797

## What Problem This Solves

Human discussion needs an explicit audience choice without competing send buttons or losing the selected-recipient context.

## User Impact

The ordinary send arrow stays in place. A labeled **Run agent** checkbox sits on the right of the existing **Will notify** strip: checked allows agent work; unchecked posts discussion only. A human reply without selected mentions exposes the same control in its reply row, without claiming anyone will be notified. Selecting a person still defaults to agent participation; a human reply defaults to discussion and permits an explicit checked override.

The choice belongs to the current draft, not a session setting. Clearing/submitting the draft, changing the conversation or incarnation, removing its context, navigating input history, or entering queue editing resets the local override. Failed drafts keep their selection; accepted outbox items keep their recorded audience across retries. Discussion remains text-only in an existing signed-in conversation. No deployment, configuration, protocol, or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This revises the original draft’s **Ask agent / Post to people** buttons following UX review. The **Will notify** renderer was not removed: both its owner and registered call were unchanged in the original stack. The earlier screenshots typed an @name without selecting a person, so they omitted the relevant notification-strip state. The new proof selects real recipients through the registered picker and verifies their outgoing annotations.

The checkbox changes intent only; it never sends. Mouse and native keyboard Space toggle the checkbox; Enter and the ordinary send arrow both submit the selected audience. Recipient avatars, removal, overflow summaries, and notifications retain their existing owners. The people picker also remains available while agent participation is unchecked. New layout rules are scoped to this audience row, not shared reply or command-palette mention strips.

**Review order: 2 of 3; depends on #156820.** Context follow-up: #156839. All three remain drafts; review and land the coordinated contract together, in order, only after normal maintainer gates.

## Evidence

- **277 focused UI tests passed** across composer actions, mention selection/cache, participation, and submit siblings (5.12s Vitest). The changed composer suite has **85 passing tests**, measured separately at **3.63s wall / 2.14s Vitest**, including no-send-on-toggle, Enter/click parity, selected recipients, reply override, draft/history/session/connection resets, and unsupported attachments.
- Actual Chromium + production Lit/Vite UI with a **deterministic mock Gateway** verified real picker annotations, label-click focus and native Space toggling without sending, human-reply Enter with explicit agent participation, 390px long recipients with an intact remove action and 44px checkbox target, and unchecked posting that preserves an existing active stream without an abort or run-policy request. This is not live-provider proof.
- Fresh independent AutoReview of the substantive correction: **scoped-clean at P0/P1**, terminal exit 0. Subsequent repairs were type annotations/test-fixture typing and braces, plus an unsupported-input regression—not a different design.
- Production UI types, the initially failing Gateway-root test graph, and UI-chat test types passed after repairing the Lit sentinel return annotation and an optional test callback. Changed-file lint, new stylesheet lint, i18n verification, source-size/assertion guards, and all three unused-export scans passed. The initial combined changed-check stopped on that type error; it is not claimed as one green full run.
- UI build completed. Startup JS: **371254 B gzip**, below the **371332 B** enforcement limit. Startup CSS remains **51144 B**, below **51200 B**, but above its advisory target. The previously reported isolated Mermaid violation remains **1555.8 KiB vs 960.0 KiB**; no fully green performance-gate or hosted-CI claim.
- Existing Gateway no-run and durable-retry proof is unchanged. Older-persisted-transcript upgrade, native app compilation, live provider, and native warm-thread coverage remain explicit series-level pre-merge gaps.

### Selected mention — central composer change

Both captures use the actual people picker, the same draft, and surrounding chat. The [early implementation checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156838#issuecomment-5805223206) was published before final validation.

**Before** — original draft with a selected recipient and an alternate send button.

![Before: selected recipient and original alternate send button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdd5e016-6699-4a9e-8f7a-4c921b8d1f76)

**After** — notification context preserved; Run agent chooses audience beside it, without a second send button.

![After: selected recipient and right-aligned Run agent checkbox](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a08ae04-39a1-4c11-b204-a75266505bd5)

<details>
<summary>Context gallery: human reply, narrow viewport, normal composer, and active work</summary>

**Human reply without a selected mention:** no Will notify claim. Discussion is the default.

![Human reply without selected mentions, Run agent unchecked](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2eaf41b7-a16c-4939-82bf-4011d57b6290)

**Explicit agent override:** checking Run agent retains the reply context; Enter sends agent participation.

![Human reply with explicit checked agent override](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e31aafd7-2af5-4b41-a0dd-1d89ad0402f4)

**390px viewport:** recipient names move to their own line with the existing overflow summary; checkbox label and remove action remain visible and separate.

![Narrow composer with multiple long selected recipients](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2d91d08-050c-4769-9768-9981da898d72)

**Normal composer:** ordinary send and no unnecessary participation row.

![Normal composer without participation controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12b43023-93f7-4383-b4d9-dc04d964227a)

**Active work, before posting:** Run agent is unchecked while an existing response continues.

![Existing active work with unchecked discussion draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87d271cf-0617-4591-819e-7c2915376bab)

**After posting:** the discussion is visible and the same active stream remains; no abort request or agent-run acknowledgment was created.

![Discussion posted while existing work continues](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e58dfdaf-cef4-426c-bcfc-8ff9b53c0c27)

</details>

## Contributor credit

Requested and co-authored by @vincentkoc.

UX correction requested and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.body:
Closes #159820

## What Problem This Solves

The Lobsterdex needs downloadable coloring sheets and matching full-color guides without changing its cards. A guide must be the **identical coloring sheet filled with color**, not a differently outlined version of the animated pet.

## User Impact

A discreet top-right download icon, opposite the existing link icon, offers **Coloring sheet (PDF)** or **Color guide (PDF)**. It appears on hover/keyboard focus and stays visible on mobile/touch layouts. Bulk downloads provide a ZIP of either format, including undiscovered catalog entries without changing discovery history.

The original card dimensions, padding, layout, artwork, names, lore, dates, and shiny marker are unchanged. Every export is a one-page A4 PDF generated locally; nothing is uploaded by this feature.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both modes now use **one print-art generator**. It owns the same geometry, pruning, unfilled regions, opaque pure-black strokes, widths, caps, and joins. Only the opaque fill colors differ. This fixes missing/thin/colored outlines on details such as Squeaky's antennae, claws, highlights, eyes, connectors, and string.

The separate color renderer and its size-based contour heuristic were removed. Palette fills are resolved in an isolated static light document, with fill alpha flattened onto paper-white so a colored area cannot reveal extra rear outlines or fade the black edges. The PDF layout/ZIP workflow and quiet download menus remain shared and unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Current feature head:** 0ab1d7de6081502eebac5034f5861416eb5c3e2d.
- **All 45 pairs checked:** replacing only the guide's filled colors with white produces an SVG identical to its blank counterpart for every catalog entry, including the three character-draft additions. Geometry, visibility, linework, and viewBox are the same. All five paired-catalog contact sheets below were inspected.
- **Existing blank sheets preserved:** all 45 new blank PDFs are pixel-identical to the previously delivered pack under independent PDFium rendering at 600 px width. Both native ZIPs contain 45 valid one-page A4 PDFs (90 documents parsed).

All 3 artwork tests pass over the main catalog: 1.079 s test time / 4.20 s command wall; the new linework comparison takes 310 ms. The owned lease stopped successfully. A portal-sync warning occurred after successful proof and cleanup.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint (0 warnings/errors), formatting, whitespace checks, and a fresh independent P0–P2 review passed. This generator repair removes **76 production lines net** and adds **71 test lines net**.

## What Problem This Solves

Shared-session history can lose the distinction between human discussion and an agent assignment, and a reply to another human can be mislabeled with the current sender's name.

## User Impact

Later context retains the explicitly selected discussion audience and the referenced message's recorded author and role. Compaction and native quoted-history adapters do not turn human discussion into an assignment. Unattributed older messages stay unattributed rather than borrowing the current connection's identity.

This does not change transport ChatType, access control, agent-run admission, or existing stored message bytes. It adds no classifier, configuration, schema version, or dependency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core draft already carries audience through the embedded model boundary. This final slice keeps that fact in the compaction formatter and Codex quoted-history adapter, and resolves bounded reply context from the actual stored target. Untrusted names and reply bodies remain per-turn user context, not stable system instructions. The existing metadata string sanitizer is extracted unchanged to respect the source-size limit.

prs.title: feat(chat): record human discussion without activating the agent
prs.body:
Related: #156797

## What Problem This Solves

A message intended for another human in a shared Control UI conversation currently enters the agent-send lifecycle.

## User Impact

Signed-in Control UI clients can explicitly record human discussion without starting, queueing, steering, interrupting, or recovering agent work. Ordinary requests and follow-ups retain their existing behavior; mentioning a human does not automatically suppress a request to the agent.

This first contract is deliberately **text-only in an existing session**. Attachments, new-session creation, goals, and outbound delivery overrides are not supported in discussion mode. No protocol/database version bump, configuration change, or deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing chat owner branches on explicit `participation: "humans"` before agent admission. It reuses authenticated authorship, durable input custody, transcript publication, and committed mention delivery, and acknowledges a committed message with `status: "posted"` instead of pretending a run started. An immutable authenticated fingerprint prevents a consumed message ID from accepting different discussion text.

**Review order: 1 of 3.** The dependent UI draft is #156838; the remaining reply/compaction/native quoted-context draft is #156839. prs.title: fix(agents): preserve restart ownership and explain runtime refusals
prs.body:
Closes #150323
Fixes #159918

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channel-plugin tasks stalling during Gateway restart when the raw inbound runner lacks an explicit reply dispatcher, and makes native runtime-selection refusals distinguishable without changing selection or authorization decisions.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish native runtime refusal reasons through trusted diagnostics; the public refusal message and selection behavior are unchanged.

Pending replies from that entry point retain their owning Gateway and participate in its restart cancellation and recovery. The additional diagnostic observations make restart ownership and admission testable without treating a terminated CLI as proof of success. They do not grant authority or change admission, target checks, signal delivery, or RPC results.

**Compatibility scope:** routed plans without an explicit dispatcher deliberately select their owning Gateway rather than ambient state. Third-party plugins depending on ambient selection have not been validated. Explicit dispatchers, prepared turns, and standalone use remain covered. Maintainer acceptance of this documented compatibility risk remains required before merge; it is not assumed.

The optional `gateway call --traceparent` carries only existing diagnostic envelope context. Core owner/admission events stay internal; raw owner objects, session identities, and private trace associations are not published by the harness.

**Runtime-diagnostics SDK compatibility:** `DiagnosticEventPayload` gains the `model.runtime_choice` variant. Exhaustive TypeScript consumers may need an explicit case when rebuilding, including an intentional no-op. This does not change installed configuration, auth, ownership, selection or persistence behavior. The existing SDK/security-owner compatibility decision remains separate before landing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw-event path now uses the existing instance-bound reply dispatcher. The deprecated inbound/turn alias continues to share that owner-bound runner.

For the missing evidence, core observes the actual admitted owner immediately before each tool-hook handler. A separate native event records the actual restart-admission result. Fresh diagnostic spans associate those facts across the CLI process boundary; no RPC-time async-local-owner inference remains. Observations never invoke authority assertions or replace authorization.

The conflict-driven main refresh preserves upstream Cron requester issuance, composed revocation checks, device-token storage fences and caller-lifetime cleanup alongside the existing observation contract. Main still needs the raw-dispatcher fix; no retired path was restored.

Runtime-selection diagnostics record versioned, content-free preparation and validation facts through the trusted diagnostic stream. Delivery remains asynchronous, cannot reenter the final commit guard through trace preparation, and stays outside OTel export and support-bundle retention. Shared event, delivery and recorder policy owners now serve both changes.

## Evidence

### Consolidated implementation — September 27, 2026

**One canonical PR, superseding #150324.** Current head: `b62a43be2adba7d0149a3aea4a76e66d5dd791de`. Both complete original branches remain ancestors: runtime diagnostics 36b401427e3de34fb8ee5c9394235fbba11c04c3 and restart ownership edb58e9e76138206e8c26081b584c27f7228e234. #150324 is closed **unmerged**; no changes have landed on main. The original source cutoff is bf636cc1bcdd59e65d5074a1bc309d903bf18e65. The consolidation commit94971d8c4577 matched the reviewed combined tree d2daf2df1da0732240cb5ae3d8393d9015c10e10; the later617 commit adds the explicit retirement fence described below.

- **Runtime-parent CI (61779353df3) — green; new tooling-head CI pending:** [run36356040484](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36356040484) completed with **159 successful and20 skipped jobs, zero failures**. The exact-head openclaw/ci-gate check succeeded at22:56:35UTC; the final rollup was SUCCESS with zero pending checks. No failed historical run is relabeled as a pass. Fresh exact-head CI for b62a43be2ad is required and pending; the parent pass is not called a new-head result.
- **Real transport proof — pass, retained across tooling-only conflict repair:** [sanitized ledger, executable hashes and complete reproducer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150493#issuecomment-5860771904). The proof executed at61779353df3. The only617→b62 changes are scripts/pr and its wrapper test; exact Git object equality verifies unchanged src, packages, extensions, docs, config, package/lock files, native launcher, E2E provider fixtures and build entrypoint. The actual built native CLI Gateway and loaded fixture channel used the normal agent/OpenAI HTTP pipeline and a separate-process HTTP delivery receiver. A raw resolveTurn callback was held across the public authenticated planned-restart RPC. Replacement generation2 was already live and delivered a second real reply before the old generation1 callback was released. That callback returned its plan, then failed with the canonical Gateway lifetime error: **zero old-owner transport attempts and zero receiver requests**. Native PID59 was retained: this is planned **in-process** replacement, not a cold-process restart. No module mocks, replacement reply resolver, patched dispatcher, or seeded delivery result. This is real local TCP with synthetic provider/channel services, not third-party-account or published-plugin upgrade proof. The fresh rootless, network-none namespace used no host credentials or operator state. CLI build:48.82s; successful runtime proof:31.898s; orderly child joins, container exit0 and owned-container removal verified. Earlier bootstrap/oracle failures remain documented in the receipt.
- **Retirement fence / local verification:** the seven-line owner repair composes existing runtime, Gateway and caller cancellation, checks it after lazy import and before dispatch, and carries it into the existing reply pipeline. Fixes channel-plugin tasks stalling during a Gateway restart when they enter through the injected raw inbound runner without an explicit reply dispatcher.

Direct push to `main` was attempted as required and rejected by the repository ruleset, so this PR is the fallback path.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking **Dismiss progress card** does nothing for unfinished or note-only progress cards, despite the UI offering the action.

## User Impact

User impact: users can clear the displayed progress card in every supported state without stopping the active agent or deleting the conversation. An old click still cannot clear newer progress. No schema change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI and documented contract already allow dismissing every card state, but storage retained a completed-checklist-only restriction. Remove that obsolete restriction at the storage owner while preserving the expected-revision check and revision tombstones.

## Evidence

This patch moves pending forwarded updates into arrival order; it is not a fix limited to already-consumed messages. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes older messages forwarded from another agent session appearing pinned below newer replies while they wait to be consumed.

## User Impact

Forwarded agent updates now stay in conversation order instead of following every new response to the bottom. Normal human sends, the queue dock, and execution scheduling are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript treated every unconsumed input as a ceiling for the active response. The existing forwarded-message classification is shared with turn grouping, including cron forwards.

- Both new forwarding regressions failed on the unchanged base and pass with the fix.

prs.title: fix: private project sessions ignore the selected GitHub identity
prs.body:
Related: #147459

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: starting a Gateway session on a private GitHub project can use the discovery/service credential instead of the selected agent’s authorized GitHub account, even when that agent can access the repository.

## User Impact

User impact: New Session and visible `sessions_spawn` project cloning and refresh use the effective managed agent identity, including an inherited system identity. An unavailable or changed selected credential stops preparation instead of silently trying another account.

No configuration, protocol, permission, sandbox, or setup-script authority changes. Agent-independent `projects.add` and discovery retain their existing service-credential contract; sessions without a managed identity retain the documented service/environment/anonymous path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both creation paths already converge on the same workspace preparation owner. This change uses the existing GitHub read-identity owner there and carries its live credential/run checks through Git attempts, retries, and clone registration. Deferred refresh uses the same selection. It does not add a credential resolver or change protected credential storage. The retained no-managed-identity behavior follows the [existing Gateway-source contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2214920d0da40517aaf39a471f832fdbbbc41b4c/docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md); `projects.add` remains agent-independent under its [existing request schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2214920d0da40517aaf39a471f832fdbbbc41b4c/packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/projects.ts#L110-L113). Cloud repository restoration retains its separate pinned-checkpoint/worker-binding contract.

## Evidence

- **Red/green through real creation owners:** on base `2214920d0da40517aaf39a471f832fdbbbc41b4c`, both New Session and the real visible-spawn tool sent the synthetic service credential rather than the selected agent credential. Both pass with this fix, along with inherited-system identity, missing/removed credentials, deferred retry, and refresh-revocation cases. These tests use real local Git repositories, managed profile fixtures, SQLite registration, and worktrees; GitHub verification and the network endpoint are stubbed.
- **Separate authenticated transport proof:** the actual clone transport successfully cloned an authorized private GitHub repository into an isolated task-owned checkout using the existing per-agent managed launch credential. No TLS relaxation, credential-file copying, live Gateway change, or repository edits were used.
- **Focused validation:** 103 passed; two existing error-wording assertions failed in `server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn.test.ts`. Both failures were independently reproduced on untouched base `2214920d0da40517aaf39a471f832fdbbbc41b4c`; neither assertion was changed. The nine new identity cases all pass. Sibling coverage retains sandbox containment, raw-cwd restrictions, setup-script authority, cancellation, and pinned-base retry behavior.
- **Publication recheck:** all **44** identity and project-registry tests passed on the final commit. **Changed checks:** passed (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <six changed paths>`), including core and core-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, dead exports, import cycles, and applicable guards. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Subsequent lint edits only add required braces.

**Gaps:** the authenticated check covers Git transport, not a full deployed New Session/private-GitHub end-to-end run. The original production `clone_failed` response discarded detailed Git output, so this PR does not claim to establish its exact low-level cause or to fix the separate `projects.add` failure. No UI presentation changed. Full repository build/test suites were not run.

Requested by VACInc; commit includes the requested co-author credit.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a session in a new browser tab briefly labels it “Disconnected” during a healthy initial connection.

## User Impact

New tabs keep their normal title while loading. Actual connection failures and reconnects still show “Disconnected,” and the marker clears after recovery. No change to caching, loading speed, authentication, or connection behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cached shell renders before the Gateway handshake completes. Its title treated every non-connected phase as a disconnect. The title now distinguishes normal startup from failed or lost connections using the existing Gateway snapshot, without new state or timers. Pending approval counts remain hidden until connected because a stale queue is not actionable.

## Evidence

- Three startup regressions failed against the original title logic and pass with the repair. Coverage includes slow initial loading, actual first-connect errors, reconnect/offline/reload-required states, and recovery.
- 102 focused navigation/title tests passed. The changed suite alone: `pnpm test ui/src/app/app-host.document-title.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 21 tests, 3.490 seconds wall time. CI seconds are not yet measured; no new CI lane or fixture boot was added.

- UI and affected test typechecks, formatting, typed lint, stylelint, repository guards, and all three unused-export scans passed. The original aggregate check exhausted its 240-second budget during unused-export scanning; that scan was completed separately with a sufficient budget.

The test now targets Escape at the already-actionable job link, establishing keyboard focus inside the menu rather than leaving it on the titled CI trigger. The same active-tooltip replay passes with the focus correction. prs.title: refactor: unify filesystem observation for reloads and refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Consolidates the separate Config, development supervisor, Skills, and Memory observation engines so recovery and shutdown use one guarded filesystem contract instead of parallel Chokidar/native implementations.

## User Impact

Each workflow retains its validation, settling, source-selection, and cache/index policy. Notifications remain advisory: they never authorize reads or silently admit a replacement Root. Shutdown joins owned work and preserves genuine teardown errors without stranding independent resources.

**Dependent implementation draft—not ready to merge or install from the declared registry pins.** This needs [fs-safe #666](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/666) and a legitimate published version exposing /watch. Registry version 0.19.0 does not contain this feature; manifests deliberately do not pretend otherwise.

Native observation is limited to actual Node.js/Linux with trusted procfs. macOS, Windows, Bun, and other unsupported runtimes explicitly select polling by default. CHOKIDAR_USEPOLLING=false, 0, and empty values remain native-only and may leave observation unavailable on unsupported hosts. Package-owner acceptance of this platform/resource tradeoff remains a before-merge decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

fs-safe owns guarded observation, reconciliation, and physical retirement. Consumers retain accepted/rejected Config include policy, development-source filtering and trusted links, Skills discovery versus supporting-resource invalidation, and Memory dirty→settled→index ordering and host placement.

This removes direct Chokidar dependencies and superseded transports. Admission is bounded: Config four native workers, development four lifetime-pinned Roots, and Memory/Skills sixteen native workers each per process. Starting, retiring, and failed-close workers retain their budget. These are ceilings, not a performance-win claim.

## Evidence

Local qualification uses the immutable unpublished candidate 39c949e88e4de3381db008e8ab18e27faf0bce8d from [artifact 10863096644](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/36132581730/artifacts/10863096644). Both tarballs were integrity-checked; all 608 installed root-package files and two native-package files match. Installation used a temporary package-manager hook—not library patches, vendoring, or type shims. No hook or local artifact dependency is committed.

- Real Config registration ENOENT → joined close → retry → later native edit; genuine worker-termination failure prevents rearming. Canonical include-boundary retargeting cannot silently expand a cached admission. Real guarded-snapshot → source → automatic-poll cases cover both existing and missing files beneath a pinned directory alias, after the initial source read at readiness has completed.
- Real development-source link retargeting and later edits in native and autonomous polling modes.
- Skills entry→directory and directory/missing→symlink startup races: trusted targets are observed before availability, then later native edits reach the cached loader. Supporting create/atomic-replace/delete reaches sandbox copies without discovery invalidation; settling distinguishes observation loss from genuine cleanup failure.
- Memory committed-index replacement/removal/nested edits in native and autonomous polling modes without search/manual reconciliation hiding missed notifications; alias retargeting, dangling targets, and held selected-file settling.
- Real manager shutdown: independent cleanup after observation failure, provider retries, accepted sync work, retained database leases, and held remote transport retirement.

The canonical include handoff’s missing-file case takes ~0.5s; its first existing-file case included ~19s shared worker compilation (~21s total). Measured other local case costs: Skills native admission ~0.7s, supporting resources ~0.9s, Memory alias flow ~0.5s, manager cleanup ~0.05–1s, and committed-index filesystem cases ~8–10s each. Cold worker compilation is separate (~18s). Sixteen Linux subscriptions added ~269 MiB RSS and 112 active descriptors; joined close returned descriptors to baseline.

Whole-candidate AutoReview completed; actionable consumer findings were repaired. Independent scoped reviews found no new P0–P2 issues in the final Config alias and bootstrap corrections. Main integration exposed an extra initial Config invalidation that could supersede restart work: bootstrap reconciliation now retains the former ignore-initial behavior, while detailed startup activity, overflow, and later unknown invalidations remain actionable. The known dependency-release gate remains open.

Earlier focused qualification passed 88 Skills cases. After integrating main and resolving the overlap, 757 Gateway cases, 42 Config cases, 39 affected Skills cases, and all 128 CI routing/Windows inventory cases passed. Gateway wall time was 41.64s; Config was 10.51s. Production and changed-test lint passed. The original five-job/time bounds are unchanged, with all newly added main Windows cases retained; three additional OS-neutral helper/lifecycle files stay in Linux/macOS rather than the Windows list. Portable polling, path-policy, and Windows behavior coverage remains enrolled.

The held-scan/backpressure continuation reproduced both remote workers returning with accepted stdout writes still blocked. One bounded notifier now joins output independently from physical cleanup, preserves final availability ordering, stops admission on output failure, and handles reentrant shutdown. Native Config stop/replacement, native Skills/development shutdown, and real Memory polling scans held across stdout backpressure, EOF, and output failure now have direct proofs. The final affected run passed **73 tests across 11 files in 83.30s**; held-scan bodies take tens to hundreds of milliseconds. Independent continuation AutoReview found no actionable P0–P2 issues.

**Source-bound local qualification:** code commit `c20b18568c81310af75ab3e6a7c58e6a09e42f26` passed full core and extension production/test typing, SDK export/surface checks, scoped lint, and the documented checkout-local full build (**6m 59.6s**) against the exact candidate artifact. The earlier service-identity refusal was not bypassed: this build used its ordinary checkout-local owner without changing Gateway identity or credentials. Installed artifact bytes were reverified (608 root-package files and two native-package files). This is artifact-bound proof, not a clean registry install. Integration is pinned to main `e124d77e00fadc6108ed5bfc0e57101a40151197`, not a moving target. Memory queue/provider ownership and guarded no-follow sampling are preserved; 23 Memory integration tests passed (45.12s), with Memory typing/lint passing. Earlier worker cases passed 4/4 and Gateway fixture typing/lint passed. The RPC runtime launch was refused by installed-service publication admission; no identity or service was changed.

**Remaining qualification:** clean installation from the declared registry pins and actual consumer macOS/Windows/Bun execution. The declared dependency does not export /watch; a compatible legitimate release must be pinned before that clean-install proof. This host is Linux without Bun or a desktop runtime. [Blacksmith run 36140098730](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36140098730) previously lacked authentication to download the exact artifact; its lease was stopped and the unchanged attempt was not repeated. Platform proof needs an approved matching runtime/runner and supported artifact transfer or the released dependency. The package-owner platform/resource decision remains open.

## Contributor

@vincentkoc requested and directed this migration.

## What Problem This Solves

**Superseded:** this repair was independently landed on main in [3928d51bf8e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3928d51bf8eeca51e409ab2bfd31928cbbfcd539). This PR was closed without merging to avoid duplicating it. The remaining independent pasted-text repair is [#157375](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157375). Evidence below describes this retained proposal, not a claim that it was merged.

Four release-manifest contract tests fail before writing their manifests because their fixtures omit the sealed-artifact and registry inputs required by the current workflow writer.

## User Impact

Hermetic CI fixtures: no real GitHub credentials, registry access, or publishing actions are needed. Production release policy, workflow coverage, timeouts, and retries are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(exec): avoid approval prompts for read-only audit suppression searches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Read-only searches mentioning `security.audit.suppressions` were receiving the extra approval intended for suppression edits. Related: #82728.

## User Impact

Trusted, completely analyzed file inspections can avoid that extra prompt, while ordinary exec/node approval rules still apply. Writes, mixed commands, redirections, executable-bearing options, uncertain analysis, dispatch wrappers, and startup-bearing shells remain gated. The shipped direct config get/schema/validate exception and existing full/off behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared policy consumes the existing authorization plan, executable resolution, root-option parser, and shell-startup owner. Both lexical and canonical executable paths must be trusted. It distinguishes new file inspections from legacy direct config reads so hosts can preserve the inspected command through final execution.

Gateway inspections use the existing pinned renderer without loading saved shell aliases/functions. The actual implicit shell must also be an absolute, trusted, startup-free POSIX transport; unsupported envelopes retain approval. Nodes use the existing planned-argv and identity checks through final dispatch, including the companion request. This prevents a checked reader from being replaced by a snapshot function, dispatch wrapper, or intervening PATH change.

Duplicated option parsing and repeated policy-drift fixtures were consolidated without removing assertions. The full diff against pinned main `202336dcd5f7032bc53b23069220a2c51da44749` is **+1,001/−543, net +458 across 19 files**. It is not net-negative: closing the demonstrated final-execution gaps adds binding logic and real regressions. Upstream deletions are not credited to this cleanup. Main was integrated only for the actual Gateway fixture conflict.

## Evidence

Latest tested source: `45a3c775d4f885a91945f2706f6a80d69b885c56`.

- **217 passed / 2 platform skips across six suites** on the dispatch correction: node system.run (97), Gateway approvals (50), suppression policy (44), real Gateway execution (14 + 1 skip), SDK review input (6), and node allowlist (6 + 1 skip). The implicit-shell qualification then passed the Gateway/integration suites and three new envelope cases. Final focused validation passed **79 tests**: ordinary policy (70), SDK (6), and shell envelopes (3). These overlapping scoped runs are not added into a misleading single total.
- Core production types and affected test graphs passed. Scoped lint reported **0 warnings/errors**; formatting, diff checks, current-base line-cap checks, and runtime cycle checks passed.
- Real `createExecTool` proof first reproduced a saved `grep` function mutating the synthetic audit file under full/on-miss. Direct and pipeline inspections now read the unchanged fixture without starting the snapshot; full/off still executes the writer control. The same test supplies an inherited writer-bearing `BASH_ENV` and proves the actual environment owner removes it.
- Real node execution first reproduced a reader inserted earlier in PATH during policy commit. Direct/payload drift now fails before runner invocation or I/O; transport drift uses the pinned original shell. Workspace reader/dispatcher, nested wrapper, symlink, and startup negatives remain, with full/off writer controls.
- Independent reviews completed and findings were checked against the actual owners. The snapshot finding is repaired. The conditional `BASH_ENV` concern is rejected with producer source plus real Gateway and node proof. The final transport review identified an unconditional Windows qualification; that branch now conservatively returns false, leaving legacy direct reads unaffected.

### Compatibility and limits

The helper shipped through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime` in v2026.9.6. Its boolean API and legacy `{command, segments}` direct-read exemption remain, with or without raw segment text. Legacy source is independently reanalyzed and must match one complete segment and argv. Failed analysis, writes, mixed commands, forged argv, and generic readers without authorization plans remain gated. Three legacy read regressions failed before the compatibility repair and passed afterward.

Current real execution proof is Linux Bash/sh/grep. Windows analysis is exercised in policy/Gateway/SDK tests; native Windows/macOS execution is not claimed. The implicit zsh/tcsh/PATH-shell tests prove rejection at the envelope boundary, not native shell execution. Prior real zsh/fish proof is retained only for the unchanged explicit-node startup classifier. No live profiles, configuration, or deployment were changed.

Landing is paused for a scope decision about the shared startup classifier: non-login zsh/fish commands unrelated to suppressions can also lose auto-review eligibility, affecting headless workflows. The requester has been asked whether to retain that broader protection or narrow this PR. Exact-head CI remains pending; no merge has been submitted.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI prompts can stay queued while the agent is idle when reconnect overtakes an in-progress send preparation, until the page is refreshed.

## User Impact

Eligible queued prompts resume automatically after reconnect instead of needing a page refresh. Existing delivery checks, queue order, edit holds, and server-requested retry delays remain enforced. No configuration or storage migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The outbox scheduler records a new wakeup while an older asynchronous preparation is pending. The older attempt must not erase that wakeup when it returns pending. The scheduler remains the single owner of the next pass and rechecks the existing retry owner before continuing.

Reported by Vito.

## Evidence

- **227/227 focused tests pass on the final candidate** across send, submit, outbox-loading, abort, and queue-reordering suites. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Both reconnect regressions failed before repair because no `chat.send` was issued. An additional retry-order regression failed on the first repair and now passes: a previous wake cannot bypass a newer server-requested retry delay.

prs.body:
Related: #156340

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes main-agent narration disappearing into a clipped status line during a run, and agent avatars dropping toward the bottom of tall replies.

## User Impact

Narration stays inline, in order, with normal Markdown formatting and tool activity. After a dashboard turn finishes, its work collapses under **Worked for …**, leaving the final answer visible. Expanding that heading restores the sequence. Agent avatars stay aligned with the top of the turn.

Tool-call grouping, its wording/counts, scrolling, and subagent rows are unchanged. Failed, blocked, unknown, and skipped outcomes remain visible. **Keep commentary** still controls settled history, not whether the active run's narration survives a refresh. No configuration, storage, provider, or harness changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the latest-commentary relocation path and reuse the existing transcript renderer, completed-work disclosure, duration formatter, and outcome summaries. Both harnesses use this shared Control UI path. Commentary still appears when a segment completes; this does not introduce token-by-token commentary streaming or new grouping state. Active commentary retention shares the existing progress owner’s explicit or inferred run identity; the avatar repair changes one shared alignment declaration.

**Maintainer decision:** @vyctorbrzezowski requested this presentation and the avatar follow-up; existing tool-call grouping and subagent rows remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- The inline-narration regressions fail before the repair and pass afterward. The completed-heading regression run likewise changed from **11 failures / 5 passes** to all passing.
- **460 local tests passed for the original narration/heading candidate**, covering narration/history reconciliation, retention, completed-run timing and ownership, outcome visibility, disclosure behavior, and transcript rendering. The 21 focused cases take 3.36 s through the wrapper; the 394 chat/transcript sibling cases take 17.34 s; the 45 isolated rendering cases take 5.41 s in Vitest.
- Six production-build Chromium narration scenarios already passed: live/reconnected commentary, evicted replay, cursor recovery, pre-steer reload ordering, split-history continuation, and growing-frame scroll following. [Narration browser execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35928760963).
- Completed-run browser proof passes: the heading uses only the matching run’s 13-second duration, survives reload, and expands to the existing tool presentation. The visualization/row-layout sibling also passes. The final focused browser invocation takes 17.05 s; [Testbox execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35933584463) uses `blacksmith-testbox`, lease `tbx_01m389ehtf2h2xgje0denrk4f2`, with wrapper exit 0. An initially incorrect test selector expected a group around a lone tool; inspecting the rendered DOM confirmed the existing single-tool presentation, and the corrected assertion passes.
- Core-test and UI typechecks, changed-file lint/style/format checks, i18n, dead-export scans, and repository guards pass. A lint-only shadowed variable was renamed and rechecked.
- Follow-up validation: **297 chat/progress tests pass** (9.15 s wrapper / 5.47 s Vitest), including three inferred-run cases that fail before the fix: segment identity, tool identity, and cached identity, each with a future queued run present. Retention still removes settled commentary. The earlier review’s inferred-run P2 is repaired by sharing the existing lazy progress result, not adding another identity resolver.
- **Six Chromium avatar layout cases pass** (11.69 s wrapper / 6.32 s Vitest; 100 ms test execution). The desktop avatar assertion failed by 33.59 px before the shared CSS repair. Changed-file static gates pass for all four follow-up files.
- Actual-UI avatar proof on the updated head: the default avatar’s top offset is **69.5 px before / 0 px after**, and remains 0 px with work expanded. Uploaded-image avatars stay at 0 px. Mouse expansion, keyboard collapse, and both avatar variants pass with zero page errors. An initially incomplete sharing response in the capture fixture was corrected; production disclosure code was unchanged.
- Independent review found no further P0–P2 defects in the repaired working tree; the reported index-only copy of the recovered-run bug was resolved by staging the reviewed repair. Browser evidence uses the actual Control UI with a mock Gateway, not live provider execution.

### Inline narration — before

Related: #155314, #155317

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic Decision experiments need one explicit, persisted opt-in that future consumer PRs can share without treating model selection as consent.

## User Impact

Settings → Labs gains a default-off Decision assistance switch. **Foundation only: no automatic consumers are connected, and enabling it starts no inference.** Saved opt-in remains visible without a model; each participating agent still needs an effective Decision model. Unreadable or stale configuration is shown as unknown, not disabled.

The explicit `decision_evaluate` tool is exempt and unchanged. Shared Decision execution, provider registration, credentials, downloads, consumer modes, and action authority are unchanged. This does not complete or close the broader integration issues.

## Why This Change Was Made

- UI and manual config share the optional Boolean `agents.defaults.experimental.decisionAssistance`. Only explicit `true` opts in. Off/reset preserves sibling settings and model selections.
- Core-only `isDecisionAssistanceEligible(config, agentId)` requires strict opt-in AND an effective model from `resolveDecisionModelSetting`, preserving inherited defaults and explicit empty agent overrides. It consumes prepared config and a trusted owning agent ID without provider probes, secret resolution, polling, or inference.
- Existing Labs patch/revision/refresh and save-generation handling remain the owners. No plugin SDK expansion or new Decision registry.
- The authorized Boolean intentionally raises the generated core config-field budget from 2454 to 2455.
- The consumer-free core module has a narrow Knip source entry. Remove this entry when the first automatic consumer imports the helper; no fake production invocation was added to satisfy unused-export checks.

## Evidence

Verification for source commit `dfba736e220f81992bc9e4281c35230c39c1a871` is reused, without rebasing or feature expansion.

| `src/agents/decision-assistance.test.ts` | 16 passed | 1.70 s |

Tests cover the four opt-in/model combinations, omitted/false and options-only configuration, inheritance, empty overrides, pending/failure/reconnect behavior, unknown configuration, persistence and reset. Real Control UI with a **synthetic Gateway** verified canonical revision-aware patches, schema acceptance, no-model opt-in, reload persistence, and sibling preservation.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes CI preflight failing to find its manifest script when the checkout and workflow use the same revision, plus the lint and coercion-owner guard failures introduced when that script was extracted.

## User Impact

Pull requests can reach their planned checks again. No product behavior changes. Different-revision runs still require the trusted workflow harness and fail if it is missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the manifest entrypoint by checkout/workflow revision identity, preserving the target working directory and dispatch-only TypeScript loader. Resolve the script's lint errors without changing CI routing or weakening rules. Move its exact boolean grammar to the existing dependency-free argument owner, with duplicate declarations still forbidden. Remove an obsolete successful-fallback summary whose producer now rejects missing bounded plans.

## Evidence

- Actual workflow-shell/Node entrypoint: four same-revision failures reproduced before the fix; all 12 same/different/missing-harness cases pass afterward, plus four existing import/loader checks (4.27s).
- Final helper correction: exact `pnpm check:coercion-helpers` fails before and passes after (14.80s). Focused proof passes 136 cases (25.60s), including the 12 entrypoint cases, real boolean-routing, frozen sparse imports and dependency-free closure. The strengthened duplicate-owner guard passes all 11 cases (5.13s).
- Type-aware scripts/test lint, formatting and diff checks pass on the final candidate. Prior candidate planning proof passed all 507 cases; unchanged entrypoint workflow lint passed. No blanket exemptions or changed baselines.
- Fresh full-candidate independent autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2.
- The broader prior-candidate guard run had 156 passes and one unrelated failure: the unchanged Mantis Slack IP-discovery fixture received a real check-IP response rather than fake curl output. A focused local replay failed identically; the same unchanged case passed in the independent Testbox baseline (25ms at `a3bc205d7f42`). The local interception cause remains unresolved. Combined planning/guard wall time was 216.39s. This is not a claim that every guard or full CI passed.
- Hosted workflows were not dispatched or rerun for this repair. The ongoing main baseline is separate prior-head evidence.

## Worked on by

@steipete requested and authorized this CI repair.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/bca94781-5883-4623-b4db-b67759e38d78)

prs.title: fix(test): scope desktop retry requests to the explicit target
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Superseded:** this repair was independently landed on main in [dbd7453fd2f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/dbd7453fd2ff2db7192fdbef4515404d80be7cc2). This PR was closed without merging to avoid duplicating it. The remaining independent pasted-text repair is [#157375](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157375). Evidence below describes this retained proposal, not a claim that it was merged.

The desktop failure/retry E2E test can count automatic chat discovery as an extra explicit-target retry, failing with three status RPCs where it expects two.

## User Impact

Test-only repair in one file. Production desktop behavior, target authority, timeout settings, retries, and CI coverage are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A chat can already be discovering its assigned worker when a user opens another desktop explicitly. That read-only discovery is not a retry or fallback by the explicit presenter.

The fixture holds real background discovery across the manual open/retry and checks each owner: exactly one failed initial direct-target request, exactly two direct-target reads overall, one correctly targeted observation and one connection. It accounts for the **complete parameterized status journal**, so unexpected targets or a third direct-target read still fail. The original no-observation/error, no-picker/fallback, and exact retry ordering assertions remain. Successful status responses are restricted to the requested target.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/89b333b5-710d-4f77-9a50-98477d15cf1f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a6a286d2-db40-45b2-93f6-8fd4c516c20c)

## Evidence

- Original required failure: [CI 36013302644, E2E job 107680345538](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36013302644/job/107680345538), expected total status count **2**, received **3**.
- First replay used the original **79 executed files / 370 tests**, three workers, Node **24.19.0**, and Chromium **153.0.8010.12 / v1243** on the configured Blacksmith Testbox. All passed. This ordinary non-reproduction is **not claimed as fix evidence**.
- Controlled real-browser ordering held actual discovery while the explicit target failed and retried. With the original global assertion intact, it failed with the same 3-versus-2 result. Captured RPC parameters were **other-worker → worker-desktop-1 → worker-desktop-1**.
- Under that same ordering, the repaired case passed in **1.4 s**. Complete desktop file: **22/22 passed**, **47.39 s Vitest wall** (**104.997 s provider command including source/dependency preparation**).
- Repaired original executed cohort: **79/79 files, 370/370 tests passed**, no skips; **501.83 s Vitest wall**, **549.034 s provider command**. Full source-capsule/tree bindings were checked before each invocation. The task-owned Testbox was stopped and its completed state verified.
- Qualification preceded extraction from the combined repair branch. This one-file PR retains byte-identical desktop, production UI, and E2E inputs; unrelated release and pasted-text test-fixture edits are separate. Fresh exact-head CI remains required.
- Fresh independent P2 review found no actionable issues. All selected repository type, lint, formatting, ratchet and dead-export checks passed for these exact bytes.

Hosted failure telemetry did not retain RPC parameters, so its precise third caller remains unknown. The controlled experiment demonstrates the fixture’s global-count defect, not an unrelated production defect. The original compressed pre-shard inventory was damaged in the supplied log; the replay reconstructed all 79 executed paths without missing mappings rather than claiming identical original shard packing.

Local loopback proxy policy and remote source-privacy exclusions were preserved. Remote proof resumed only after incorporating the independently landed tracked-scratch cleanup in #157308. Provider portal-sync warnings did not alter recorded command/test exit status.
