prs.title: feat(workers): run native inference on dedicated workers
prs.body:
Closes #154388

## What Problem This Solves

Operators need native model inference and coding-tool execution in a dedicated worker environment without placing its provider credentials on the Gateway.

## User Impact

**Windows worker-local inference is deferred.** Existing Windows Gateway/proxied-worker and CLI secret-input behavior is unchanged. The new native-inference configuration is rejected explicitly on Windows; the shared secret-input helper and its tests are byte-identical to the PR base.

An explicitly configured paired-device profile can run the native agent loop, model requests, and authorized shell/file tools together on the worker. Set `settings.inference: "worker"` to opt in. Omission or `"gateway"` keeps Gateway inference; existing embedded agents and Gateway-proxied worker inference remain the defaults. The UI labels the routes **Through Gateway** and **Direct from worker**.

Configured-default New Session creation and active worker-session follow-up messages no longer require an unused Gateway provider credential. This exception applies only to the selected published worker profile or an authoritative active worker placement. Ordinary cloud/device placements, explicit model/runtime selection, model existence, authorization, and runtime/profile compatibility checks remain enforced. Raw profile settings and credentials are not exposed.

The old device-profile spelling `runtime-local` and existing stored snapshots remain compatible; `openclaw doctor --fix` normalizes authored profile config to `worker`. The internal worker launch value remains `runtime-local`, so this naming/UI update does not change that wire contract. No database-schema, dependency, or default-mode changes. Startup credentials now travel over a private one-shot pipe rather than the initial worker environment; use compatible node-host and worker builds together.

After a worker-inference turn has been admitted, losing the Gateway connection ends that turn; reconnecting does not resume its model request. A fresh turn requires fresh admission.

The feature is opt-in, but rollout still requires compatible Gateway, node-host, and worker builds. Older nodes do not understand `nodeHost.workerRuns.nativeInferenceConfig`; retire worker-inference placements and remove native profiles/config before downgrading. The new mode is not an OS sandbox. Interactive worker exec approvals, worker LLM-review transport, automatic compaction/retry, arbitrary provider-plugin loading, and an additional OpenClaw-managed nested container remain unsupported. Approval-required execution is denied rather than approved or rerouted. Worker inference currently requires the built-in `device` provider.

**Remaining integration limit:** worker-held credentials do not make explicit model/runtime selection available in the Gateway catalog. Use the configured-default UI or CLI/API flow; explicit selection still requires Gateway-published availability. This is not a global auth bypass.



**Mandatory dedicated default (optional):** set `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile` to the native worker profile ID. Control UI removes the placement/workspace chooser and uses the agent’s configured default model. The Gateway automatically prepares and dispatches ordinary sessions under their existing create/run permissions; manual profile dispatch remains admin-only. API and channel turns enforce the same policy. An unavailable required worker blocks the turn rather than running it locally. The existing initial-message Retry/Stop and uncertain-delivery flow remains the owner.

Enabling this policy does not silently move an existing bound workspace. Existing local-folder sessions without a managed workspace need an operator-led transition or a new session. Sessionless model helpers and standalone local CLI runs are intentionally unavailable under the policy. Leave `requiredProfile` unset for existing optional placement behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse existing placement, admission, process supervision, coding tools, transcript commits, and live events instead of introducing another execution protocol. The node captures trusted model metadata and credentials at startup and projects the authorized grant to each worker. The Gateway retains session and policy authority; worker inference cannot silently fall back to Gateway inference.

The UI reads an optional, validated placement fact from the recorded profile snapshot. Only an active exact worker-turn binding publishes worker session metadata. Missing metadata means Gateway behavior. Setup, compatibility, and limits are documented in `docs/gateway/cloud-workers/native-inference.md`.

## Evidence

### Worker label — current copy update

Commit `4197fab8e3e03846f3eee3c8f3288fdf1e56f0a8` replaces the deployment-specific label with **OpenClaw worker**; the generic fallback is **Worker**. Copy only: placement, provisioning and permission behavior are unchanged.

Validation: 11 focused UI tests (5.15s wrapper wall), UI types, scoped lint and i18n checks passed. Both built-UI mocked-Gateway scenarios passed with capture enabled (17.32s Vitest); no real worker-node provisioning is claimed. The temporary Testbox was stopped and independently confirmed completed.

**Before**

![Before: Dedicated OpenClaw label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f42220a0-2378-4a16-8be7-82deffe99d36)

**After**

![After: OpenClaw worker label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37eda5e5-0bd2-46a7-99e6-dd2a2480b9e0)

### Mandatory dedicated default — current update

Commit `63681e2c7bc9d88ee21245c809d06a6440eba005`. The server policy is optional and additive; no database schema, shared Windows pipe mode, or protected baseline was changed.

- 354 existing routing/admission/recovery/protocol checks passed, plus the new required-policy/configuration checks. Real handler and channel-initialization composition uses actual SQLite and managed worktrees; only worker dispatch is a boundary fixture.
- Required and optional UI flows pass in the built Control UI against a controlled Gateway, including creation, first message, and follow-up. Required mode uses ordinary write scopes and does not advertise or call manual dispatch. [Before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154390#issuecomment-5841740169).
- Core/UI production and ten affected test type graphs passed. Documentation link/config-example and i18n validation passed. Fresh review: two independent P0–P2 review passes; canonical-agent and shared-physical-owner findings were repaired and reproduced red/green. Incognito source selection was also repaired through the existing exact-entry reader.
- Browser proof: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3dgwg777qfhmbksjhn8zwmw`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36203957267); 2 tests, 18.57s lane wall / 3.84s test time. Lease stopped and verified completed. Local browser preflight was blocked by the host loopback policy; it was not bypassed. This is not a live platform/provider deployment test.

**Landing remains held:** the protected configuration baseline now reports **2465 > 2463**, plus hash drift (the native-inference key and required-profile key). Those files were not changed without approval. Existing Windows native-inference deferral remains in force.


**Required-profile CI follow-up:** The failed type stripe in run [36207005670](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36207005670/job/108305778634) found two stale async task-projection calls inherited from main, in a file unchanged by this PR. The exact upstream repair already exists in [#158520](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158520); no competing patch was created. Cancelled CI jobs are not passes, and the protected config-baseline gate remains separate.

<details>
<summary>Review repairs, change size, and measured test cost</summary>

Mandatory placement now receives the canonical run target before model preparation. The target resolver itself is read-only: ordinary RPC/channel admission creates real sessions; sessionless helpers are not given fabricated sessions. Exact-entry preparation retains the canonical physical database owner independently of the logical session agent, including private and shared stores. The full seven-case handler/channel/SQLite/worktree composition and nine target-owner sibling cases passed after the source-owner repair.

Production delta: +1186/-85 (net +1101); tests +1223/-157; docs +83. Growth provides server-owned automatic placement across existing entry points and the locked UI, with explicit source/operation lifetime. It reuses the existing dispatch coordinator and workspace lifecycle; no new runtime state store or parallel execution protocol was introduced.

Measured local whole-file wrapper wall times, serial --maxWorkers=1:

| Test file | Wall |
| --- | ---: |
| `src/gateway/server.required-worker-profile.test.ts` | 34.98s |
| `src/gateway/worker-environments/required-profile.test.ts` | 8.62s |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run-orchestrator.required-profile.test.ts` | 15.34s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/required-placement.test.ts` | 3.37s |
| `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-placement-required.test.ts` | 3.41s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-place-browser.test.ts` | 2.89s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/palette-session-draft.warm-roster.test.ts` | 3.32s |
| `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-submission-flow.test.ts` | 3.77s |
| `src/agents/session-placement-required-profile.test.ts` | 4.63s Vitest (single-file lane) |
| `src/config/zod-schema.cloud-workers.test.ts` | 1.42s Vitest (single-file lane) |
| `ui/src/e2e/worker-inference.e2e.test.ts` | 18.57s Vitest on Testbox |

The 34.98s composed Gateway test includes cold handler/worker-runtime preparation, real SQLite ownership, and real managed-worktree creation. Pure dispatch mocks would miss canonical-agent, incognito, and shared-store regressions. No per-test Gateway process or new serial test configuration was added. Exact-head hosted test cost remains pending CI.

Scoped lint has no remaining non-size diagnostics. Seven touched modules exceed the local 700-line limit; the repository’s canonical CI limit policy reports these as advisory. No rule override or baseline exception was applied.

No live platform deployment or real Windows native-inference execution was claimed.

</details>

### Earlier native-inference proof — conflict refresh and startup custody (September 25)

Head `d4de9f8ffbdc8e0e10c2f2db0d42cfd43d48fa67`, tested tree `1035e260eb272334e916d86f859816b678f076d0`. Rebased with merge topology preserved onto main `e74db47ae34c31afb78bb85faeaacd449b4cc1bc`. Original contributor commits through `844c0e90eb94f688de595d7b218c4bd01aee8a7b` remain ancestors. Previous merge-owned security repairs and both follow-up corrections are retained; the final tree exactly matches an independently composed pre-rebase head plus current main with the conflict resolved. The newly overlapping worker-runtime declaration now uses main’s shared `WorkerTranscriptClient` / `WorkerLiveClient` types while retaining `nativeInference`. Its type-erased executable JavaScript is identical to the pre-rebase module. The Windows deferral remains intact, and both shared secret-input files still have zero diff from the new base.

**Earlier conflict resolutions are preserved.** The composition retains main’s role/model restrictions, catalog freshness, selected-agent defaults, async inference admission, original-session-store authority, preparation summaries, and runner inventory. Worker-only credential handling now uses those current owners rather than restoring older parallel checks. Taking main’s UI side without that adaptation reproduced four failures; the owner-level repair and relevant UI siblings pass. Five native-proxy denial assertions now await the updated async API.

#### Review findings addressed

- **P1 — initial-environment credential exposure:** independent AutoReview found that deleting the startup variable after exec does not erase Linux `/proc/<pid>/environ`. A real permitted worker `exec` tool reproduced the exposure using synthetic credentials on the pre-fix composed tree: ordinary environment checks were false, but `initialCarrierHasCredentials` was true. The identical security observation is false after the repair. Startup JSON now uses the existing one-shot `SpawnSecretInput` pipe; the environment carries only fd `3`. Both producer and reader enforce a 2 MiB bound; the reader drains and closes the descriptor before tools, and delivery buffers are cleared. No credential file, new protocol variant, or environment fallback.
- **P2 — Windows reader/handle mismatch:** The earlier global standard-pipe change is removed. It affected existing Windows secret-input callers rather than only the new opt-in, so this PR now restores the shared implementation and tests exactly to main at its merge base. Only explicit `nodeHost.workerRuns.nativeInferenceConfig` is rejected on Windows, before registry/credential reads. Undefined configuration remains a no-op; POSIX private-pipe delivery is retained. **Follow-up: Windows worker-inference transport** must use an opt-in-compatible solution and prove native Windows large-payload delivery, closure/cancellation and unchanged existing callers before enablement.
- **Cancellation proof follows main’s intentional contract:** #156452 stops new transcript submissions after cancellation. The native process test now requires unchanged committed history, no additional transcript submission, an aborted finishing event, and its durable ACK. Provider HTTP still must close. Replacement proof checks no readmission, no duplicate provider call, and no stale output rather than a timing-dependent final stderr string.
- Corrected the E2E fixture’s runtime typing, a shadowed Doctor variable, and a projection test’s duplicated expected-value construction.

The first automated review reported the P1; it was not a clean verdict. Follow-up inspection found the Windows P2; Windows native inference is now explicitly deferred instead of changing shared transport defaults. These dispositions and observed regressions are the basis for the repair—not a claim that a subsequent full automated review returned clean. This closes the identified carrier exposure, **not** the broader same-UID host-isolation boundary; the worker mode is still not an OS sandbox.

- **CI follow-up:** [the exact-head dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36140524578/job/108089539033) found three unused internal exports. Commit `79ab28029e7d437526b921e2437d6c0741316bc7` removes the unused schema/type exports and moves test imports to the canonical config-schema owner. Both phases of `pnpm deadcode:full` now pass locally, plus 23 native-runtime/startup cases and their production/test types. The native-runtime file measured 2.902s command wall with one worker. Runtime bodies are unchanged. The same CI run’s docs failure is the known protected config budget/hash gate, which was not altered.

#### Verification

- **Fresh rebase verification:** 201 focused worker/Gateway/protocol cases, all 10 compiled native-process cases, and 47 UI cases passed. prs.title: fix(ui): keep mobile approval decisions visible
prs.body:
Closes #131165

## What Problem This Solves

On mobile, opening a long pending approval queue could let the queue become the modal's outer scroll owner. Scrolling to later requests moved every decision action above the viewport, leaving operators unable to approve or deny without finding their way back to the top.

The defect reproduces at 390×667 with 23 pending approvals. Against production files byte-equal to current `origin/main`, scrolling the queue moved the Deny action from `y=582.3` to `y=-376.7`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval card now owns one bounded modal layout:

- approval details and pending requests share one scrollable review region;
- the decision group is a non-scrolling footer;
- selecting another pending approval resets the review region to its beginning;
- inline chat approvals and the generic modal adapter are unchanged.

Queue rendering moves into the approval-card owner so content and actions cannot acquire competing viewport budgets. The obsolete outer `exec-approval-modal-stack` scroll owner is removed instead of adding another nested scroll path.

Production delta: **+33 lines** across the approval component and stylesheet. Test delta: **+104 lines**. The production growth establishes the single scroll-owner boundary, a closed modal-vs-inline prop shape, 44px mobile targets, and selection reset; no fallback, configuration, protocol, or alternate approval flow is added.

### ClawSweeper review resolution

- **Production delta (+33): accepted.** The added structure establishes the approval card as the single owner of queued review content and decisions, replaces the competing outer scroll owner, encodes modal-vs-inline requirements in a closed prop shape, and guarantees 44px mobile actions. ClawSweeper and fresh autoreview found no smaller absorbing refactor; no fallback or alternate approval flow was added.
- **Prior Rank-up moves checked.** The full PR comment history contains the pickup acknowledgement and the current substantive review only. There is no earlier substantive ClawSweeper review or prior Rank-up list to carry forward.

## User Impact

The approval workflow remains the same. Approvals stay passive until opened, the full queue still uses the existing modal, and dismissing it records no decision. On mobile, operators can scroll long details and queued requests while every available decision remains visible and reachable in a footer with at least 44px touch targets.

### Desktop impact (verified at 1200×800)

Desktop interaction is unchanged: the queue still opens in the same modal, the same decision buttons and keyboard shortcuts are available, dismissing records no decision, and the existing approval callback remains authoritative.

The multi-request desktop layout is **not pixel-identical**. On current `main`, the approval card is approximately 540×360px with its decisions inside it, followed by a separate 540×131px pending-requests panel. On this PR, the pending queue is enclosed inside one approximately 540×492px approval card and the decisions appear below the queue. Single-request desktop approvals retain the same content and interaction but also use the new review/footer ownership boundary.

Matched Chromium captures at 1200×800 with the same route, dark theme, three approvals, command, and framing:

| Desktop before — current `main` | Desktop after — this PR |
| --- | --- |
| ![Desktop before: decisions are inside the approval card and pending requests are in a separate panel below](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52260d3e-4c20-4eee-9d15-4782fdbb88cf) | ![Desktop after: pending requests and decisions are enclosed in one approval card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5345f4a-0f79-4211-9ee7-d7f56bd287ac) |

This is a consequence of moving queue rendering into the approval-card owner for all modal widths. If preserving the current desktop panel hierarchy is required, the implementation must be narrowed before merge rather than describing desktop as unchanged.

## Evidence

Matched Chromium captures at 390×667 after scrolling the same long pending queue:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: pending approval rows fill the viewport and no decisions are visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eccb6ef1-cb70-40bb-b632-62f79116cdf9) | ![After: later pending rows remain visible while Allow once and Deny stay on-screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5326af9f-4760-4b86-bd5e-db83f90195b2) |

The images are the original matched repro captures. The same real-browser mocked-Gateway regression was rerun after rebasing onto current `origin/main`; the pre-fix run failed for the intended off-screen-action reason, and the repaired run passed.

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/exec-approval-card.test.ts ui/src/components/exec-approval.test.ts ui/src/e2e/approval-flow.e2e.test.ts` — 35 passed (30 component, 5 browser E2E).
- Current-`origin/main` pre-fix browser regression — failed as intended after scroll (`Deny: y=582.3 → -376.7`).
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- ui/src/components/exec-approval-card.test.ts ui/src/components/exec-approval-card.ts ui/src/components/exec-approval.test.ts ui/src/components/exec-approval.ts ui/src/e2e/approval-flow.e2e.test.ts ui/src/styles/components.css` — formatting, repository ratchets, dead-code scans, UI i18n, core/UI typechecks, oxlint, and stylelint passed after the required dependency refresh.
- `pnpm build` — passed, including plugin control-plane probes and the production Control UI bundle. The first sandboxed attempt failed only because its native Node probe was denied (`spawnSync /usr/bin/node EPERM`); the host-permitted rerun passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` — clean; no accepted/actionable findings, correctness 0.99.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.

Known proof boundary: the browser evidence uses the repository's real Chromium + mocked-Gateway E2E flow rather than a credentialed operator Gateway. The changed behavior is entirely local Control UI layout, and the test exercises the production modal and Gateway approval-event path.

## Worked on by

- @Takhoffman

prs.title: fix(agents): expose session Stop without browser login
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents asked to stop another session have no general Stop tool and send users to a browser login or a manual Stop click instead.

## User Impact

Users can ask an authorized Gateway agent to stop work in another session without resetting, archiving, or deleting the conversation. Session-wide Stop clears queued follow-ups by default; `clearQueued: false` preserves them, and an optional run ID narrows cancellation.

The coding and messaging profiles expose the tool to non-owner callers, while existing tool policy, sandbox visibility, agent-to-agent policy, and Gateway sharing/role checks still apply. Native subagents retain their controlled-tree cancellation; standalone embedded mode and the separate cloud-worker session-tool RPC surface are not expanded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `sessions_stop` rather than exposing the owner-only `sessions` management tool. Cancellation stays with the existing Gateway abort owner. A live admitted agent can stop browser-owned work only for the exact agent/key/session generation admitted by the router, without acquiring admin scopes or browser identity. Ordinary external-client ownership checks remain unchanged. Missing caller authority or an in-process Gateway fails before target lookup, with no credential-based transport fallback.

## Evidence

- 225 focused tests passed across tool registration/policy, stop targeting, Gateway cancellation authorization, queue ownership, yielded sessions, and descendant cancellation.
- The real in-process tool-to-Gateway regression proves an identified non-admin agent can stop authorized browser-owned work, preserves a stale incarnation, rejects unrelated/private targets, and rejects a caller revoked after router admission. The same external write-only caller remains denied.
- Core and extension production/test type checks passed; formatting and type-aware lint passed.
- Independent review completed with no remaining P0/P1 findings after fixing the missing-admission guard.
- Proof uses isolated state and the real in-process router, not the live Team Gateway. No deployment or full CI run was performed for this draft.

<details>
<summary>Measured local test cost</summary>

Each file was run with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Wall times include runner/setup overhead; the first stop-tool run spent 95% of its Vitest time in cold shared compilation, not assertions. CI timings are not available yet.

| Test file | Tests | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/tools/sessions-stop-tool.test.ts` | 22 | 44.70 s |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-stop-tool.test.ts` | 3 | 13.40 s |
| `src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.test.ts` | 57 | 27.98 s |
| `src/agents/tool-catalog.test.ts` | 12 | 1.48 s |
| `src/agents/agent-tools.policy.test.ts` | 39 | 9.33 s |
| `src/security/audit-cross-agent-session-access.test.ts` | 26 | 8.02 s |

The other 66 tests cover existing cancellation/queue/yield/cascade contracts. No test timers or Gateway server boots were added.

</details>

prs.title: improve(ui): prototype smaller translation-memory checkouts
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162699

## What Problem This Solves

Investigates reducing the 87.30 MB of Control UI translation memory in developer checkouts without dropping locales or changing translation bytes.

**Draft experiment, not recommended for adoption:** the checkout reduction comes with a substantial Git-history penalty. Human review is required; do not auto-merge.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change, npm-package reduction, or browser-payload reduction. Source checkout memory files shrink to 30.02 MB, saving 57.28 MB (65.6%). GitHub shows binary locale changes; maintainers would use the new offline decoded-diff/recovery CLI. Git cannot efficiently delta the compressed content in the measured small-edit case.

## Why This Change Was Made

This prototype measures the complete storage change rather than gzip size alone. All 20 files are converted byte-for-byte, paired with their host-tool reader/writer, verifier, Vite watcher, locale-refresh workflow and strict CI routing. Node's built-in gzip is host-only; no browser decoder, dependency, Git filter, or automatic merge driver is added. Recovery documentation preserves translations added after migration.

The result favors retaining raw JSONL: one French translation-row edit added **177 bytes** to the raw two-version Git pack versus **1,474,943 bytes** for gzip. This is a controlled sample, not a prediction for an entire repository's history. The single read/decode/parse probe also used **28.9% more CPU**; it is exploratory, not a production speed or memory claim.

## Evidence

- Frozen source: `55bbbf9ddcad46c7746ef8c66c73c5c71197406f`. Remote Linux, Node 24.19.0, Git 2.53.0, gzip level 6.
- All 20 original files decompress to identical bytes; repeated encoding matched on the same Node/zlib runtime. Cross-version gzip byte stability is not promised; unchanged translation text is not recompressed by the writer.
- Raw/gzip totals: 87,299,708 / 30,024,556 bytes.
- Git pack settings: window 10, depth 50, one thread, compression 6; identical object ordering/path hints. Disposable object stores only, no real repository repacking.
- Read/parse probe: 180,740 admitted entries in both forms; raw 443 ms, gzip 609 ms. One sample, buffer-based microbenchmark, not cold-I/O or end-to-end build performance.
- 173 focused tests passed across six files: memory CLI, translation tooling, sync plan, verifier, CI policy and Vite locale handling. The initial CLI lint finding was repaired with `toSorted()`; CLI lint, its four tests and formatting then passed on the final source.
- Format, workflow validation, root-test lint, UI lint, scripts types and UI types passed remotely. Two independent source reviews found no actionable P0-P2 issue.
- The real offline CLI reported no decoded diff across all 20 migrated files. Same-locale nonoverlapping merge, visible conflicting edits, and rollback preserving later translations passed in disposable Git/file fixtures.
- UI builds succeeded in both forms. **Exact build-byte parity did not pass:** both emitted 2,052 files; candidate total output was 300 bytes larger, with 861 added/changed and 859 removed paths, mostly hashed assets. The cause is not established; no browser regression or speedup is claimed from these observations.
- **Aggregate changed check did not pass:** its line-count ratchet stopped with `spawnSync git ENOBUFS` while comparing the source capsule against its older `origin/main` baseline. Scoped checks above do not replace that gate. A correctly scoped aggregate run and exact build parity remain prerequisites for any adoption.
- Authenticated locale-refresh and producer no-op proof were not run. No provider calls or regenerated translations were made.

Adoption remains blocked on human judgment about the measured history/review costs. The prototype does not authorize optional/minimal-library work or a broader format redesign.

prs.title: fix(gateway): queued plugin reload with --wait leaves model runtimes stale while it waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: while `openclaw plugins reload <id> --wait` sits queued behind in-flight plugin work, the Gateway serves stale or retired model runtimes for the whole wait, which in a live incident lasted 45 minutes.

## User Impact

A queued `--wait` reload leaves agents' prepared model runtimes current and serving until the plugin work it waits on has finished. Cancelling a queued reload leaves nothing to roll back. `--wait` still waits without a deadline.

A related limitation remains and is out of scope here. While the reload is queued, the replacement reservation on the reloading plugin refuses new agent runs whose plugin set includes it (`Plugin <id> replacement is in progress`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`reloadGatewayPlugins` called `prepareConfigEffects` before `drainRetainedWork`. `prepareConfigEffects` marks every prepared model runtime stale with `waitForReplacement`. That releases idle prepared plugin publications, which disposes private per-workspace plugin registries, and makes model-runtime readers wait for a replacement that only arrives when the reload commits. With `--wait` the retained-work wait has no deadline, so those effects lasted as long as the reload stayed queued.

The reload now reserves the handoff instances, waits for retained work, revalidates, and only then calls `prepareConfigEffects`. The reservation (`PluginInstance.reserveReplacement`) still rejects new `retainWork()` and new retained consumers on the handoff instances while the reload waits. That keeps the protection against drain starvation that the earlier ordering provided. A wait that is cancelled or fails now ends in phase `prepare`, so the reload reports `unchanged` and runs no rollback.

## Evidence

- Regression: `explicit drain wait preserves retained work beyond 60s and can complete` and `... can cancel` in `server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts` assert that `prepareConfigEffects` is not called while the reload is queued, is called once after the work releases, and that a cancelled queued wait calls no rollback. Running them against the `main` version of `server-plugin-reload.ts` fails 3 tests (`expected "prepareConfigEffects" to be called 0 times, but got 1`); with this change all pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-plugin-reload*.test.ts`: 5 files, 120 tests pass.
- Test cost: the change adds assertions to existing tests in `server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts`; that file runs in 22.65s wall with `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugin-reload.recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. No new test files.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: production typecheck, lint, and gateway test typecheck pass. The core-test graph stops on an inherited `main` error in the unchanged `ui/src/components/session-group-defaults-dialog.ts` (`readMissingScopeError` is not imported).
- Autoreview (Codex) reported no findings.

prs.title: fix(codex): prevent stale native sessions from mutating successors
prs.body:
Related: #156938

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale native Codex sessions that could write or retain a successor's thread subscription after session authority changed. A peer's live process could incorrectly satisfy the stale initiator's retention check.

## User Impact

Current admitted native work can finish, while stale initiating sources cannot retain a reusable thread using another source's process. Peer work keeps its physical listener until its own process settles; exact old cleanup cannot evict a newer claim. Native steering rejected before enqueue remains available after cancellation instead of being reported as delivered.

No new operator configuration, stored binding format, schema version, retention policy, or permission is introduced. The complete merge-base diff against `1b31d2443e51dccc595b3e7208b8b696df26e222` has no package, lockfile, plugin manifest or SQL schema delta. `session-binding-codec.ts` preserves the relocated normalization/encoding bytes after whitespace normalization, the stored version-1 envelope, and legacy schema-1/2 importer; `migration/session-binding-sidecars.ts` and `session-binding-orphans.ts` still consume that version-1 envelope. These source checks establish compatibility disposition, not full installer/updater or stable-tag upgrade execution; those were not run. Existing binding codec normalization is relocated unchanged; current worker facts add the already-stored predecessor field and compose existing source restrictions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native process owner decides initiating-source custody. The existing physical subscription token/protection owner holds only required cleanup while peer work remains, and publishes no warm claim for the rejected initiator. Session row authority reaches the canonical worker transaction/commit grant and physical request writer; lease and mutation constraints both survive when they originate from distinct session rows. Definitive native ingress rejection clears the steering owner's exact dispatch receipt before retry backoff.

Published candidate: `2099e55d534a8ddba3fa58c5f415418388b049f2`. Rejected or failed upload admission releases only its own reservation, so a corrected request can reuse its key. No new configuration, stored format, schema migration, or operator action is required.

The existing sharing owner consumes exact worker-prepared rows and membership under the retained physical storage owner. prs.title: fix: stabilize source watcher event assertions
prs.body:
Closes #165566.

## What Problem This Solves

The source-watcher CI fixture can receive a second `package.json` callback while it expects the newly created `src/new.ts`. The test waits for fs-safe's metadata reconciliation, but the source observer's separate asynchronous content scan can still be reading the package when the fixture rewrites it. That overlap makes the exact filename assertion fail intermittently.

## User Impact

This makes the existing developer-source observation test coordinate its file edits with the content reads it exercises. Production watcher behavior, restart timing, file filtering, and callback semantics are unchanged. The assertions still require no callback for unchanged content and one callback with the exact expected filename for each subsequent change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture now uses its existing real-file-open spy to hold two package reads. Reaching the second read proves that the serialized source owner has finished the unchanged pass, so the test can assert silence there. It then completes the package rewrite before releasing the next open. Both gates are released in `finally`.

The redundant rewrite of the original `{}` bytes is removed because it could itself truncate the file during an earlier queued scan. The explicit overflow still forces a real unchanged-content scan. No production completion API, sleep, debounce adjustment, or broader callback matcher is introduced.

## Evidence

The original [release-validation failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37292384100/job/111705937774) reports expected `src/new.ts`, received `package.json`, with one callback. A controlled baseline run reproduced that exact failure by holding the real package descriptor across the fixture's rewrite, then allowing the unchanged hashing and notification code to continue. The correction passed the same strict callback checks.

On Linux x64 with Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.5.1, Vitest 5.0.1, and fs-safe 0.23.0:

- `pnpm test src/infra/watch-node-observation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 9/9 passed, 2.51 seconds wall time.
- `pnpm test src/infra/watch-node.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 30/30 passed, 30.85 seconds including worker preparation.
- The controlled baseline reproduction failed at the intended assertion in 2.39 seconds; a pristine baseline observation passed 9/9, consistent with the original intermittent scheduling defect.
- The selected affected baseline passed 197 assertions in 15 files across the boundary, infra, and runtime-config lanes. Test execution took 76.93 seconds; selection plus execution took 95.12 seconds.
- The selected infra test type graph passed. The static gate accounts for 42 passing check families and four reproduced baseline failures in dead-code/import-cycle checks, whose relevant inputs are unchanged by this fixture correction. Production dependency audit and the exact-base private-key scan passed.

Final verification completed on the unchanged patch:

- 20 standalone full-file runs passed all nine cases on Linux with Node 24.19.0 and fs-safe 0.23.0.
- Three complete runs of the original 64-input shard plan passed. The Linux run executed 43 files with 599 passes and three platform skips in 99.24 seconds. Two macOS arm64 runs with Node 24.21.0 executed the same 43 files, each with 603 passes and two platform skips, in 78.75 and 63.60 seconds. The count difference comes from existing platform-specific cases. Two historical heartbeat suites had already been consolidated into the retained owner suite before this patch.
- With fs-safe 0.23.1, the [published-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37315517199/job/111781562041) passed all nine observation cases on the actual merged target using Linux and Node 24.19.0. The changed case took 118 ms, the file took 1.74 seconds, and its native runner took 3.04 seconds.
- The 30 caller tests also passed on target `60c24e3be3f4` with this patch and fs-safe 0.23.1, using macOS arm64 and Node 24.21.0: 15.32 seconds in Vitest, 17.73 seconds including preparation and cleanup.
- Published-head CI and its required gate passed. Every counted remote run reached process exit 0 after final worker-generation verification.

The failure card offers **Don't ask again for this run in this browser**. The choice is scoped to the Gateway, profile, and update run in this browser; another run can prompt again. Manual Ask OpenClaw and failed-update history remain available.

This is not a cross-device preference or cancellation of an already-dispatched investigation. Closing a card, acknowledging it, or choosing Review update does not opt out.

**Design decision:** Use a bounded, browser-local opt-out for the newest 32 Gateway/profile/run identities. If saved history cannot be read, pause automatic investigation rather than risk ignoring a saved choice; keep failure guidance and manual Ask available. Failed saves retain the decline in this tab with a visible retry. This implements the persistent opt-out requested in #143900 without server-state or permission changes. The earlier product-decision wait is resolved.

**Draft:** Current-main integration, exact-head required CI, and native landing gates remain outstanding. This design decision is not a claim that those gates passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing bounded update-run receipt owner for explicit opt-out intent, separate from session-scoped investigation receipts. Fresh checks at presentation and final automatic-send admission prevent a queued or lazy-loaded prompt from bypassing a saved choice.

If saving fails, this tab retains the declined run across Gateway/profile switches and shows a retry notice without claiming persistence. Unreadable browser history blocks automatic admission with visible guidance; manual Ask remains usable. The existing 32-entry bound and unrelated alert behavior are preserved.

No server, config, schema, default timeout, or retention-policy change. This addresses the explicit per-run opt-out, not every possible repeated-prompt cause.

Release-note context: Control UI adds an explicit per-run, per-browser choice to stop repeated update-failure investigation prompts.

## Evidence

Exact signed head: `b9ad909d45f954d5e3344e72eec06117733de5ed`.

- Independent native P3 review: scoped-clean; accepted actionable findings addressed.
- 46 focused owner/runtime unit tests passed, including failed-save scope switches, stale callbacks, bounded history, new-run rearming, presentation races, and manual Ask.
- Two real-browser desktop/mobile cases passed against the bundled UI, covering storage failure/retry, saved opt-out, reload, and manual Ask.
- Scoped formatting, lint, and applicable i18n checks passed.
- Static types passed: `pnpm tsgo:ui` and canonical test stripes `15/18` (ui-pages), `16/18` (ui-e2e), and `17/18` (ui-other). These are selected UI projects, not a repository-wide typecheck.
- True baseline captures at `5f14ada90ce5f70897f358ce21b72d21560afcbc`: two passed. Signed-candidate captures: two passed, two baseline rows unselected. Desktop 1400x1000 and mobile 390x1000 used the same capture bytes, synthetic failed npm update, and Access question; no update replay or message-bearing chat request. Chromium 153.0.8010.12.
- One earlier capture invocation accidentally selected the baseline rows on the candidate through a shared suite-title match. The corrected candidate-only filter passed without code or assertion changes.

Proof ran on a trusted macOS normal checkout using the approved local fallback after the remote source-verification route failed. Hosted CI and Linux execution are not claimed by this evidence.

**Screenshot delivery verified:** [Desktop and mobile before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148018#issuecomment-5660314448) is embedded in the PR conversation. An independent anonymous Chromium check verified HTTP 200, exact PNG byte counts and SHA-256 hashes, correct natural dimensions, and visible complete decoding for all four images. The initial unauthenticated fetch returned HTTP 404; its cause is not established. These synthetic mock-Gateway captures do not claim live-update execution.

Scope: production +108/-8, tests +657/-5, documentation +11. The production growth owns explicit intent, bounded browser persistence, visible failure handling, and the presentation/send fences together; no detached helper API or new storage service.

Related: #153401

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `update repair` reporting successful finalization without explaining that an already stopped managed Gateway was not started. It also dropped maintenance-restoration warnings from the terminal JSON outcome.

## User Impact

Standalone repair now reports that it did not start the previously stopped Gateway and names `openclaw gateway start`. The terminal result carries this warning, including readiness warnings from restoration. A Gateway explicitly stopped outside update custody is not started by guessing earlier operator intent.

This applies to standalone repair across dev, beta, stable, and package/Git installs; it does not change the installed old updater's preflight. Existing custody still restores services stopped by this repair, and parent-owned activation remains with the update parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintenance already knows whether it stopped the service and owns restoration. Its warning list now records the intentional non-start outcome and reaches finalization's existing Doctor warnings, so the final message agrees with the service action.

## Evidence

- 43 tests pass across `doctor-maintenance.settlement.test.ts` and `update-command-lifecycle.test.ts`, covering no unexpected restart, warning propagation, parent-owned activation, and cleanup/restoration boundaries.

The built candidate CLI ran `openclaw --profile <isolated> update repair --json --yes --timeout 120`: exit 0, terminal status `warning`, `restart: false`, and the profile-specific start guidance in `postUpdate.doctor.warnings`. The native service remained unloaded before/after; task profile and plist were removed. prs.title: fix: session status badge unreachable by keyboard and unnamed for screen readers
prs.body:
Closes #180196

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: keyboard users cannot reach the per-session status badge on the Control UI Sessions page, so its "Status: <label>" tooltip is unreachable and screen readers announce only the bare status word.

## User Impact

User impact: keyboard and screen-reader users can now reach the session status badge in the Sessions table and hear the full "Status: <label>" description, matching the goal badge in the same row.

## Why This Change Was Made

`renderSessionStatusBadge()` rendered the status element with no focusable trigger, so nothing could receive focus for it. The goal badge beside it in the same row already wraps a focusable element that carries an `aria-label`, and the tooltip component only attaches its trigger listener to a focusable slotted element, so the sibling's existing contract is the right one to reuse rather than inventing a new pattern.

The badge now uses that same wrapper: the trigger is focusable and its accessible name is the full "Status: <label>" string the tooltip shows. No new i18n key was needed; it composes the existing `sessionsView.status` label.

## Evidence

**Before**: focus stays on "Skip to main content" after walking the page; the status badge has no focus ring and no tooltip. The E2E walk records `tab-trace reached status badge: false`.

**After**: the same walk reaches the badge: focus ring on the status pill, and the E2E assertion passes with `tab-trace reached status badge: true`.

Screenshots are attached in the follow-up comment below.

Checks run on `9ab47386778` with Node 24.16.0:

- `ui/src/pages/sessions/view.test.ts` — 60/60 passed, including the updated run-state badge assertions that now check each wrapper is a focusable span named `Status: <label>`.
- New `ui/src/e2e/sessions-status-tooltip.e2e.test.ts` — passes on the fixed tree; on the unfixed tree it fails because the Tab walk never reaches the trigger. Verified both directions by stashing the source fix and re-running.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json` — exit 0.
- `oxlint` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

Screenshots are Chromium 152 at 1440x900 over the repository's mock-Gateway E2E harness. Not tested: Firefox/Safari tab order, screen-reader announcements, and physical mobile. The tooltip popup itself is an animated Web Awesome surface that the screenshot helper freezes, so the "after" frame shows the focused trigger rather than the open popup; the open state is asserted separately in the E2E test. `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` could not run in this worktree because `@openclaw/ai` is not built there; the change adds no new catalog key.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): recover settings-held messages after a reconnect interrupts Send
prs.body:
Related: #175271

The requester has explicitly lifted the draft pause and authorized ready-for-review status and a new ClawSweeper re-review. Requester setup testing remains unconfirmed. The exact cleanup and its prior head received independent P0–P3 Codex AutoReview with no actionable findings, as recorded in the linked requester handoff.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a queued message remaining on “Applying chat settings” when the Gateway connection closes between Send admission and the browser-input handoff while a settings change is pending.

## User Impact

Interrupted input returns to the composer when it is still empty, or remains as a failed queued item if a newer draft exists. Text and attachment bytes are preserved. Existing retry/removal controls remain available; reconnect does not automatically resend the interrupted input.

## Why This Change Was Made

The settings RPC already rejects on socket closure. The Send handoff could nevertheless return early after its MessageChannel yield, before entering the existing settings-settlement owner. That left a live waiting-model projection after the settings promise had settled and disappeared.

Skip only that redundant input yield when settings are pending. The existing asynchronous settings wait still yields to the browser and owns settlement. No timeout, retention policy, server-queue inference, or delivery retry is added.

Reported by @ikun676767.

## Evidence

### Re-review handoff — current head 2d007a6

The previous ClawSweeper verdict reviewed b0b4453629b5fc93fa45835e85b00c35d4d983d5. Please assess the current head **2d007a6f9b4bfb0bdab07d7f4c4146459c928cf8**, including the intervening test-quality follow-up and reviewed cleanup:

- **What changed:** strengthened exact-payload and newer-draft recovery assertions, added explicit manual-resend verification, and removed investigation-only logging. The final cleanup removes six explanatory comment blocks and an unrealistic response injected after a closed mock socket (17 deletions). The production condition is unchanged from the prior reviewed fix.
- **Review focus:** confirm all eight unit scenarios still exercise the production settings/reconciliation and recovery owners; unsent text/attachment bytes and newer drafts survive; Remove prevents late delivery; reconnect sends nothing automatically; an explicit browser resend submits exactly once. No timeout, retry policy, or inference of nonacceptance from an empty server queue was added.
- **Current-head verification:** 29 focused Node tests and 3 Chromium scenarios passed, as did both scoped TypeScript graphs, targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks. The requester-supplied independent P0–P3 AutoReview covered the prior head and exact cleanup with no actionable findings. Detailed revision-specific evidence follows.
- **Status correction:** the requester explicitly lifted the draft pause, and the PR is now ready for review. Requester-environment testing remains unconfirmed; the synthetic-Gateway browser proof is not a claim of live-model or requester-setup testing. The broader issue remains only partially addressed.

### Cleanup verification — 2d007a6f9b4bfb0bdab07d7f4c4146459c928cf8

- Applied the [reviewed cleanup handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179799#issuecomment-6331138623) exactly against dc7c78170b56f6ca446804ef475c7f0f6a5718f7: **17 deletions in three files**. All three resulting Git blob IDs match the patch. The production condition remains `options.yieldToInput && !options.pendingSettings`.
- **29 focused Node tests passed** across chat-settings-disconnect, chat-send-settings, and chat-submit-handoff. All eight disconnect scenarios remain: three settings/reconciliation interruption points, Remove with late settlement, and four text/attachment × empty/newer-draft cases. Payload preservation, recovery, removal, and zero automatic sends remain asserted.
- **3 Chromium scenarios passed** across chat-settings-disconnect.e2e and chat-flow.pending-settings.e2e. Recovery restores the exact prompt, removes stale queue rows, enables Send, and sends exactly once only after an explicit manual click. Node 24.20.0; Chromium 156.0.8078.4 / Playwright 1.64.0. Focused browser command exited 0 in 38.52 s (Vitest 32.99 s).
- Both scoped TypeScript graphs (ui-chat and ui-e2e-chat), targeted oxlint (**0 warnings / 0 errors**), formatting, and git diff --check passed. The focused browser harness generated only its isolated UI fixture bundle; **no full repository build, full test suite, dependency install, installed-app change, or shared Gateway change** was performed.
- Independent P0–P3 AutoReview and the comment audit are the completed review evidence supplied in the handoff for the prior head and this exact cleanup; they were not rerun here. No additional bot review was requested during the cleanup; the requester subsequently authorized a new ClawSweeper re-review.
- **Still pending:** requester setup testing. The explicit draft pause has been lifted by the requester; this does not assert that setup testing is complete. This browser proof uses a controlled synthetic Gateway, not a live-model or requester-environment run. Earlier red/green and screenshot evidence below remains tied to its original revisions; no new baseline-red run is claimed for this comment/test-only cleanup.

### Earlier proof (revision-specific)


- Reproduction baseline: cffdc96369474e6f2c28f0a3273abba2e16bc50b (package version 2026.10.5). Publication base was reconciled to main at 2fe1956ea1a69b77b79e94de51519a72c2309067; only the four intended chat/test files differ.
- Original red/green proof used the real browser/protocol client and session/settings/outbox owners, controlled socket close and native MessageChannel under both Node 24.20.0 and repository-pinned Bun 1.4.4. The later Node quality pass independently covers all four text/attachment × empty/newer-draft recovery variants; all four fail with the original unconditional handoff and pass with the repair.
- Eight focused scenarios pass: patch interruption; queued reconciliation interruption; in-flight reconciliation interruption; explicit removal with later settings completion; and four independent text/attachment × empty/newer-draft recovery variants. Retained attachment bytes are checked through the actual payload owner. No premature chat.send occurs.
- On the refreshed publication candidate: all 385 queue/settings/reconnect/transport tests across 12 files passed. The strengthened settings/Remove event-backed path also passed its 27-test Node run. Production UI and both test typecheck graphs plus the production UI build passed again after base reconciliation.
- UI production, chat-test and chat-E2E-test typechecks pass; targeted oxlint, formatting and git diff --check pass. Production UI build succeeds.
- Focused Node test execution: approximately 57 ms test time, 1.50 s Vitest duration, 4.39 s command wall time. CI timing is not yet available.

### Browser disconnect/reconnect proof

The committed browser scenario now runs against the bundled Control UI in **Chromium 156.0.8078.4 / Playwright 1.64.0**, using the existing synthetic Gateway fixture. The before/after screenshots below were captured at published head **b0b4453629b5fc93fa45835e85b00c35d4d983d5**. The later quality-pass head changes only the two test files; production behavior and those screenshots are unchanged.

- **Before:** temporarily restoring only the original unconditional handoff yield makes the browser regression fail at the intended assertion: after reconnect, “Applying chat settings” still has count **1**, expected **0**. The client is connected and the prompt remains in the queue.
- **After:** the committed fix passes. The screenshot shows the exact unsent prompt restored to the composer and Send available. The test asserts no automatic chat.send before or after reconnect.
- Both selected browser files report passing results: the disconnect/reconnect scenario plus the two existing reasoning/speed and unrelated-roster-refresh scenarios. Final runner file durations: **4.24 s** and **3.43 s**. The original standalone fixed run also exited successfully. One intermediate capture invocation was interrupted after Vitest reported a pass; its process exit is not counted as a completed command. The final runner results were recovered from Vitest's persisted results after the reporting store exceeded its size limit.
- Before entry asset: index-B3yChhUD.js, SHA-256 adf6e1a383a773edb47b29ad30714908f54a4eb18c10134251c721b0ff2dbf02. After entry asset: index-CfNQKNfj.js, SHA-256 551a0c40022e78a523078d622720616b53fd6fd2a29e6fa094df7937e8d655cd.
- The prior missing-library blocker was resolved with checksum-verified Debian libraries and font configuration under the isolated workspace, not a shared-system install. No shared Gateway or live configuration was changed.

**Before** — connected again, but the original handoff leaves the prompt stuck.

![Before: original handoff leaves Applying chat settings after reconnect](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e294d60-7379-4ca0-9d7c-50e5fad0e216)

**After** — the fix restores the complete synthetic prompt to the composer without sending it.

![After: prompt restored to composer and Send available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cefcfc7e-c9e5-46fa-86d7-d1bd530dd514)

**Remaining limits:** this is a real Chromium/bundled-UI flow with a controlled mock Gateway, not a Windows/Doubao or live-model run. Local independent Auto Review previously could not execute because its configured authentication profile was unavailable. The subsequent requester-supplied independent review is recorded above; no local reviewer execution is claimed. ClawSweeper's prior review at b0b4453629b5fc93fa45835e85b00c35d4d983d5 reported no actionable code findings. Requester setup testing has not yet been confirmed complete.

This proves one concrete stale waiting-model path, not every reported send blockage or the reporter’s original lost-ACK theory. v2026.10.4 source contains the same unconditional handoff/early-return pattern; that release was inspected, not executed.

### Test-quality follow-up — dc7c78170b56f6ca446804ef475c7f0f6a5718f7

- Strengthened browser assertions: exact prompt restored to the composer, no stale queue rows, Send enabled, zero automatic sends, then one explicit click produces exactly one correctly addressed chat.send and clears the composer.
- Independent text/attachment × empty/newer-draft coverage checks that retained attachment bytes survive without mixing into a newer draft. Removed investigation-only asset download and hash logging from routine browser tests.
- Verified locally: **29 focused Node tests** and **3 bundled Chromium scenarios** passed. All four payload/draft regressions and the browser stuck-label assertion fail with the original production handoff; the repair was restored afterward. Both changed test typecheck graphs, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Production source is unchanged from the previously reviewed head. Only the two test files changed in this follow-up (+45/-31 lines).
- Test cost: Node three-file command 10.77 s wall; changed disconnect cases approximately 71 ms test time. Browser regression 4.10 s; two browser files 39.06 s wall including fresh UI build. Current-head CI results are separate from these local results.
- Local Auto Review preparation succeeded after preserving a task-generated Chromium crash-settings artifact outside the source diff, but reviewer execution failed because its configured authentication profile was unavailable/rate-limited. The requester subsequently supplied the completed independent P0–P3 review and exact cleanup linked above.

prs.title: refactor(ui): pair page resources with Solid lifetimes
prs.body:
## Solid 2 checklist

Native TypeScript AST census on exact base `97d54bbd14bb` and signed head `ba4eb582332c`; 16 logical production modules, **5,878 → 5,899 LOC (+21)**. Counts describe these touched modules; the named owners retain the remaining work.

| Item | Before → after and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Native handlers | Conditional intrinsic bindings **0 → 0**; separate handler changes are in #179118. |
| Lifecycle | `onCleanup` **14 → 2**, so **12 removed**; `onSettled` **12 → 20**. Setup returns paired teardown. |
| Async reads | Existing Debug section-state map **1 → 1** here; #179755 owns its native async migration. Archive's native reads remain intact; synchronous owners retain authority, cancellation, polling, and URL-driven retirement. |
| Mutations | `action` **1 → 1**, `createOptimistic` **3 → 3**; existing mutation authority remains. |
| Code splitting | `lazy` **1 → 1**; existing deferred page/overlay boundaries remain. |
| State shape | `createSignal` **25 → 23**, `createStore` **2 → 4**; local Debug history and Meetings drafts use store mutations; RPC snapshots remain request-owned. |
| JSX | Manual `createComponent` **4 → 0**; Activity, its route adapter, and Debug use JSX. |
| Context | Throw-only wrappers **0 → 0**. |
| Sibling loading | `Loading` **2 → 2**, `Errored` **2 → 2**, `Reveal` **0 → 0**; existing boundaries remain. |
| Owner APIs | `createRoot`, `getOwner`, `runWithOwner` each **0 → 0**. |

`createEffect` remains **4**, `createMemo` remains **21**; render effects, `untrack`, and `flush` remain **0**. The two retained cleanup calls belong to the Meetings request primitive and PluginPage's synchronous authorization owner.


## What Problem This Solves

Several page resources split setup from teardown, while Activity and Debug construct Solid content manually. Debug history and Meetings input drafts copy local collections for each update.

## User Impact

Page listeners, timers, subscriptions, and native element registrations release with the lifetime that acquired them. Activity keeps its host tag, selectors, route owner, and lazy boundary. Debug keeps event-log updates, timestamp deduplication, its 90-sample history cap, and its lazy overlay boundary. Meetings retains unrelated drafts and URL-equal clears.

## Why This Change Was Made

Component setup returns its cleanup through Solid 2 `onSettled`. Synchronous request primitives and PluginPage's authorization owner retain their existing cleanup. Activity and Debug use JSX; Activity's existing state and live route effect stay in `activity-page.tsx`, while `activity-route.tsx` receives router props and owns shell layout behind the existing lazy route. The plain host type lives in the central JSX declarations. Git recognizes the page rename, so the existing effect allowance carries without adding an allowance. Debug history and Meetings drafts use store mutations; RPC snapshots remain owned by their request owner.

## Evidence

Current signed head `23cd0dd0d82ddc628ea1649af6dc74dae9a55362` adds only failure diagnostics to the existing HTML publication test on top of `ba4eb582332c`. Its production, configuration, build inputs, and all other tests are byte-identical to that revision. The production metrics, census, and captures below retain their exact original source attribution. The pre-click snapshot starts without awaiting it; only a failing original click/poll assertion awaits and publishes its scalar facts.

Signed head `ba4eb582332cc9b37d13e4e7de6e96bf6bb1d8c1` merges official main `97d54bbd14bb20748d850eb7de8c185ea56c5181` after GitHub reported an actual conflict. The three conflicting validation files take exact main blobs: hourly planning [#180088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180088), integration/source-owner budgets [#180097](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180097), and optional Subagents metadata attachment [#179958](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179958). Those supersede this branch's corresponding earlier repairs. All retained authored blobs match the independently reviewed `6601f5ef7a48` revision, and the integration received source review.

The retained unit/test-support repair checks the executor's effective child resource environment instead of a retired mixed-membership serial heuristic. It preserves independent selected-file, configuration, ownership, timing-key, and wide-row worker-budget assertions. Only include-file transport is omitted from resource comparison. Main's integration/source-owner repair does not update these unit cases.

[Archive #179912](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179912) retains authority over native archive reads and immediate request cancellation; this PR supplies the local draft store and paired component lifecycle. Official [#179775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179775) owns profile registration, [#179885](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179885) owns worker-budget behavior, and [#179879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179879) owns obsolete Activity route metadata removal.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Current UI types | Exact `ba4eb582` `pnpm tsgo:ui` passes (6.018 s). Frozen installs pass on both compared checkouts. |
| Production dead-code check | Exact `ba4eb582` `pnpm deadcode:knip` passes (197.470 s); no ignores added. |
| Production pair | startup: 325,389 → 325,370 B (-19 B); chat: 1,442,960 → 1,442,934 B (-26 B); new: 1,020,426 → 1,020,402 B (-24 B). Build0/0; strict base/head/pair 0/0/0; requests unchanged True; CSS unchanged True. Same machine, Node 26.12.0/pnpm 12.12.1, timestamp, branch, and build options; actual commit/build ID retained per head. Base/head build time 31.609/35.541 s. |
| Directly affected planner unit cases | Exact `ba4eb582`: 4/4 selected cases pass in one pinned-Bun invocation (92.30 s Vitest / 97.973 s total): precise ownership/timing for Blacksmith, GitHub, and hybrid, plus the >96-test E2E/plugin worker-budget case. Existing caps and timeouts are unchanged. Material imported inventory changes were audited; no dependency-equality reuse is claimed. |
| HTML diagnostic checks | UI types pass; focused typed lint passes after correcting a local-name collision; format and diff checks pass. Independent diagnostic P0–P2 review is scoped-clean; final timing and early recorder corrections received separate source review. One prior lint invocation stopped in unrelated package declaration preparation before reaching lint; its existing timeout remains unchanged. |
| Independent review | Six complete independent P0–P2 partitions and final source verification are scoped-clean. The later one-line hourly fixture repair also received a complete scoped-clean review before main superseded it. Retained authored blobs are unchanged; exact-main conflict resolutions were separately inspected. |
| Reused owner proof | Meetings and summaries 36/36 (57.96 s Vitest / 82.372 s total), including drafts, pagination, permission retirement, cancellation, and summary lifecycle. Unchanged Activity 11/11 at `05465955` and profile 15/15 at `7deadab7` retain original-head attribution. |
| Current CI | Exact signed `23cd0dd0d82ddc628ea1649af6dc74dae9a55362` [39714034729](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39714034729), attempt 1, completed successfully at 2026-10-22 03:13:50 UTC: 63 passed, 23 skipped, no failed or cancelled jobs. Every UI shard and both real-Gateway jobs passed with `ci:full` present. This passing run does not establish the cause of the earlier HTML counter failure. |
| Previous-head CI | Exact `ba4eb582` [39706837688](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39706837688) completed with 60 successful jobs and two failing names: the HTML publication counter remained 0 after Count, and sidebar reorder timed out focusing Reorder Beta. HTML passed on completed scheduled main 39707038848, so no inherited exception was claimed. The current head passes both cases. |
| Prior CI, not waived | `c6fee165` [39701616890](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39701616890) completed with 60 successful jobs and two failing names: hourly main cap and sidebar reorder. Main now owns the hourly correction. Sidebar correction landed separately as #180167 (superseding #180108). Neither old failure is a waiver for this head. |
| Visual evidence | Exact base/head captures pass (7.42 s baseline / 7.71 s head), zero page errors. All four full frames inspected and synthetic-only. Activity PNGs are byte-identical; expanded Debug has the same visible geometry and content apart from the canonical footer commit label. Node is used only for Playwright; unit tests use pinned Bun. |

The HTML failure investigation retains two exact `97d54bbd14bb` baseline attempts. The first stopped during cold-worker setup at the existing no-output watchdog; after canonical worker preflight, the second reached Gateway setup but timed out at the existing 60-second readiness limit. Neither reached a browser assertion, so neither proves inheritance. The uploaded CI artifact contains only public app/frame-depth diagnostics; no click trace or screenshot was uploaded. A focused test-only diagnostic follow-up records scalar document identity, handler, counter, and geometry facts around the unchanged Count action, only when it fails. It does not claim a fix or change any assertion, timeout, cap, or product behavior.

The net contribution is **25 files, +237/−149** against actual base `97d54bbd14bb`. The production increase pairs setup and teardown, expresses the route adapter in JSX, and replaces local collection copies with draft mutations. No dependency, planner policy, cap, timeout, ignore, or runtime owner is added.

<details>
<summary>Prior-head CI and production evidence</summary>

At `7deadab7b44f`, [CI 39689422469](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39689422469), attempt 1, finished with 57 passing jobs, 4 failures, and 23 skips. Primary failures were the hybrid precise-owner assertion, hourly 80/79 cap, and optional Subagents metadata visibility wait. The hourly error reproduced on exact old base `40a236fe` under CI runtime policy; the hybrid baseline timed out and one unchanged Subagents replay passed. Those results do not establish inherited-failure exceptions for the replacement head. Initial repair tests exposed an include-file comparison defect, which was corrected before this revision. Some wide/source-owner local cases timed out and an attempted UI replay stopped during artifact setup; neither supplies an assertion verdict. No timeout, guard, or cap was changed.

At `96928a67676b`, [CI 39668063809](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39668063809), attempt 1, completed with 59 successful jobs and 23 skipped. All UI units, both real-Gateway jobs, security-fast, lint, production/test types, and ratchets passed. The planner shard passed 77/77 file tests and 81/81 shard tests. Its earlier planner expectation correction is now superseded by official main #179885.

The sole failed nonaggregate job was the mixed-attachment gap assertion at `chat-responsive.e2e.test.ts:462:25`, expected −875.6875 px to be greater than 4 px. The case, error, and frame matched completed [main 39671240295 / job 119469897530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39671240295/job/119469897530); test, renderer, and stylesheet blobs matched the actual tested PR merge `6f31d9f0f9a4056913fbc1278d6552e2d08155d8`. This is prior-head evidence, not current-head CI. The newer completed main run 39679539559 passes the attachment case, so its earlier exception is retired.

The `be3bdd50e999` / `96928a67676b` production pair had gzip deltas of startup +10 B, chat −41 B, new −25 B; both builds, both strict checks, and paired strict check exited 0. Request counts and CSS metrics were unchanged. This remains historical comparison evidence.

A reporter verified the Vitest controller runtime and pinned Bun executable, not each test worker. prs.title: fix(ui): restore short-route typechecking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes core test typechecking failing after short-session routes began carrying resolution ownership, which blocks otherwise unrelated pull requests.

## User Impact

Developers can validate changes again without weakening stale-route protection. No intended change to session navigation or its public API.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give locally resolved and revalidated results the loader's existing freshness callback. Keep the asynchronous resolver's own callback, so every successful resolution carries the correctly owned callable before the final handoff.

This is a separate repair from the hashing optimization in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152355; it does not change that optimization.

## Evidence

- All five core test typecheck jobs in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35827111960 reported the same `TS2322` at the final route handoff.
- Fresh P0-P2 review found no actionable correctness, security, or ownership regression.
- The focused Testbox attempt at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35830841048 stopped during source sync with exit 124; no tests or changed gates ran. Its lease was closed. Hosted CI on this repair must pass before landing; this is not a test waiver.

prs.title: fix(ui): unblock architecture checks for chat attachments
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161173

## Outcome

Superseded by Peter Steinberger's independently landed fix in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/77cbd9513ea8b608faff40767ed77abe357f88d7 while this draft was validating. The landed source removes the same backward import and keeps the same three optional fields inline. Closing this duplicate without merging it.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the architecture gate fails after the chat-page refactor, blocking unrelated pull requests such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161175.

The reader imported the controls props type while those controls already imported the reader lifecycle. The static import graph therefore contained a two-module cycle.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore the reader's independent three-field options type, using the same optional property types as before. Keep the controls-to-reader dependency in one direction and document why the small structural contract is intentional.

No checks, baselines, runtime code, configuration, or attachment behavior are changed.

## User Impact

Restores an acyclic attachment type graph so developers can pass the architecture gate. There is no visual or runtime change.

## Evidence

- [Failing hosted architecture check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36565853846/job/109397963270), independently reproduced locally before the fix: one cycle between `chat-attachment-controls.types.ts` and `chat-attachment-reads.ts`.
- Independent P2 review found no actionable findings.
- Before/after esbuild TypeScript transpilation produces byte-identical JavaScript.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Post-fix `check-madge-import-cycles.ts` passed with zero cycles, down from the reproduced single cycle.
- Selected UI/core checks were stopped after the equivalent fix landed. This draft does not claim a completed changed-check run or green hosted CI and will not be merged.
- No new implementation-shaped test is needed: the existing static import-cycle gate reproduces the defect directly. No screenshot or live attachment-flow claim; the diff changes only types.

prs.title: fix(test): avoid coauthor cleanup failures in fast CI workers
prs.body:
Related: [canonical CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36124483652/job/108041446946)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes co-author fixture cleanup failing in thread-based CI and leaving its state-directory selector active for later tests.

## User Impact

Internal test routing only; production attribution, workspace resolution and database behavior are unchanged. The fixture now runs with the host-owned database broker required by its cleanup fallback. Existing cleanup custody and all assertions remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

All nine attribution assertions passed in the failed run, but cleanup of an exited native worker reached a host-only broker path from a reused Vitest thread. The rejected cleanup left the fixture environment selected; a later workspace-default test then observed that same fixture root.

Register this stateful consumer with the existing parallel infra fork owner and preserve its former unit-fast watch admission. Extend existing registry, explicit/watch routing and compact-planner checks so the file has exactly one appropriate owner. No new worker configuration, serial pin, retry, timeout, cleanup suppression or environment-reset shortcut.

The initiating reason native cleanup became unsettled is still unknown. This repairs the demonstrated host-capability mismatch, not every possible native cleanup failure.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/89b333b5-710d-4f77-9a50-98477d15cf1f)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0d269c5d-9227-44e0-8dc2-a1a4b228e3fc)
- [Independent review, integration and publication](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/a6a286d2-db40-45b2-93f6-8fd4c516c20c)

## Evidence

- Controlled termination of the real native reclamation worker after test work reproduced the actual fallback: all nine attribution assertions pass, thread-based cleanup refuses host-broker admission, and the following workspace assertion observes the retained selector. The identical controlled boundary in a reused fork completes fallback cleanup, restores the environment, and passes all 11 assertions. This is fault-injection proof of the cleanup boundary, not a claimed reproduction of its original initiating cause.
- Seven routing assertions fail without registration. With the repair, 738 selected registry/planner checks passed in 37.41 s wrapper wall; 1,155 unrelated cases were filtered, not counted as passes.
- Uninstrumented registered-owner proof passed 21 cases: coauthor 9, workspace 2, prompt sibling 10. Combined wrapper wall 36.11 s including 17.77 s worker preparation; coauthor test-body time approximately 1.7 s. All production and fixture/test assertion source is unchanged.
- Full changed-file gates passed in 173.12 s, including root-test typechecking, formatting/lint, dead-export scans and selected guards. Fresh independent review through P2 found no actionable findings (13.51 s). [Hosted fixture job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36132619608/job/108066975566) passed all nine coauthor cases in the intended infra fork config. Its owning group passed 634 tests with 10 skips; the fixture appears in exactly one decoded group and is excluded from all three unit-fast groups.
- **Current merge blocker:** [ready CI 36132619608](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36132619608) failed model-list inventory assertions and then cancelled remaining jobs. The discovery-lifecycle case returned no learned rows, and three freshness variants lost expected published rows. Source analysis identified the missing legacy-success discovery facts addressed by the existing [#158113](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158113). That owning repair still needs its own CI/review corrections and landing; no duplicate patch is being added here. Independent base-versus-PR execution attribution remains unproven, and passing fixture qualification is not a green CI claim. Completed exact-head ClawSweeper review found no code/security findings.
- The affected routing/test owners are unchanged on inspected main `d43208fc`; adjacent native-cleanup PRs do not supply this host routing change. No full-main recovery claim.

---
[View the OpenClaw team session](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0d269c5d-9227-44e0-8dc2-a1a4b228e3fc)
