prs.title: fix(state): break deferred migration read cycle
prs.body:
## Problem

Landed #165498 made `deferred-plugin-migrations.ts` consume the admitted state read stack while `openclaw-state-read-operation-registry.ts` still imported that high-level migration owner to register `plugins.deferredMigrations.read`. Madge now reports a runtime cycle from deferred migrations through startup/state reads and back through the operation registry.

This inherited failure is visible in #165554's `check-guards` job; that PR does not touch any state path. The full-main guard passed before #165498.

## Solution

- Extract the deferred-migration schema, row readers, and worker read operation into a leaf store module.
- Keep the high-level migration owner consuming that leaf.
- Register the worker read operation from the leaf instead of importing the high-level owner back into the state read stack.

No behavior, schema, or stored-data contract changes.

## Evidence

- Original failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37307076693/job/111754067905
- Prior full-main guard before #165498: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37305235308/job/111747358131
- `git diff --check` passed.
- No local preflight or test suite was run at the release lead's direction; required CI is the proof path.

prs.title: fix(swarm): wait for child cleanup before reporting cancellation complete
prs.body:
Related: #130741

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: stopping a Swarm can report a child as cancelled while its preparation, final result save, or runtime cleanup is still pending.

## User Impact

User impact: Stop waits for the selected children's owned cleanup, preserves an already accepted cancellation when the caller loses access, and reports cleanup failures instead of treating them as success. Children cancelled before starting retain their terminal session identity without acquiring a start time or invented execution history.

The 500 ms responsiveness target remains unproven by this PR's validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep each queued child's preparation attached to its existing scheduler reservation, and keep the exact running child registered until its final result save and runtime disposal finish. Cancellation checks current ownership before new effects, preserves the outcome of an accepted Stop, and continues settling captured descendants when another child's cleanup fails. Cleanup that cancels its own session waits for its terminal write without waiting on itself.

## Evidence

Validated commit `eb8f26e19f2b06b1418ad5597da03c86e2df2e7b`:

- 214 tests passed across 11 files, covering queued preparation, FIFO reservations, cancellation during access revocation, replacement runs, terminal saves, runtime disposal, and descendant cleanup. The five-file regression group took 278.654 seconds; six sibling-control files took 234.199 seconds.
- All 32 canonical changed-file gates passed, including core types, all 25 test type graphs, dead exports, lint, and storage/import guards (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged --timed`, 1299.545 seconds).
- `pnpm build` completed successfully in 1878.942 seconds, including runtime, SDK, and UI output. Build checks verified 158 public SDK subpaths, loaded 53 built modules, and verified 1024 UI sidecars.
- Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the scoped change.

The build exited successfully but still reported inherited UI budget failures: startup JavaScript was 371731 / 371332 bytes gzip, and Mermaid was 1593188 / 983040 bytes gzip. The tested base predates the separate repair in #157161; these results do not establish an asset-budget pass. No new real-provider latency measurement or exact-head CI result is included in this local proof.

<details>
<summary>Changed-test command costs</summary>

Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24, pnpm 12.4.2). Command wall includes the canonical runner and compiler/cache overhead. These seven files ran once each, serially; no retries. Accepted-stop costs are reused historical measurements with identical test and kill-runtime bytes, not fresh timings of this standalone commit. CI seconds are pending.

| Test file | Cases | Command wall |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.context-resources.test.ts` | 21 | 45.687 s |
| `src/agents/subagents/swarm/swarm-scheduler.test.ts` | 26 | 3.143 s |
| `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.owner.test.ts` | 22 | 13.648 s |
| `src/gateway/chat-abort-lifecycle-internal.test.ts` | 21 | 12.025 s |
| `src/gateway/session-utils.queued-collector-revocation.test.ts` | 11 | 37.028 s |
| `src/gateway/session-utils.queued-collector-settlement.test.ts` | 23 | 67.467 s |
| `src/gateway/session-utils.queued-collector.test.ts` | 34 | 72.672 s |
| `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.accepted-stop.test.ts` | 4 | 54.179 s (original correction); 105.144 s (combined candidate) |

The preparation run included a compiler-cache miss; later runs retained the existing cache. The two reused accepted-stop measurements have the same test and kill-runtime bytes as this commit but different surrounding checkouts. They are reported separately rather than presented as this commit's timing.

The settlement and queued-collector files exceed 30 seconds of test time. They exercise the real cancellation and session handlers, scheduler reservations, persisted session identity, and cleanup ordering together. A scheduler-only test cannot establish that Stop waits for the captured runtime and terminal save, preserves replacement sessions, or publishes the correct never-started history; the smaller scheduler and lifecycle tests cover their individual contracts separately. The queued-collector file's existing integration coverage is retained; this change adds one terminal-identity assertion.

</details>

prs.title: fix: state migration leases target a retired database
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: state migrations lose their lease when a retired database's filesystem identity is reused by another database while its lazy worker is still retained.

## User Impact

Database operations stop reusing invalidated workers, and a lazy worker refuses a removed or replaced original database instead of recreating it. No schema, configuration, or public API changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The database lifecycle already invalidated the old admission, but shared-worker selection checked only the physical file key. Record that canonical lifecycle admission once at worker entry creation, then retire and join the exact stale actor before reuse. Keep it separate from the caller's short-lived schema admission so successive valid schema scopes can share the same worker.

The existing-only backend also checks its captured identity at the first native open. Aliases retain their existing sharing behavior; there is no automatic alias retargeting or fallback.

Known boundary: external same-path, same-inode replacement without canonical lifecycle invalidation remains a separate follow-up. Raw birth timestamps cannot safely establish a universal file generation.

## Evidence

- Exact signed source: `5f623a384410d1f8a00a28413b54ac8655df5354`; tree `f94140e32e968917dc57a0fcb65b685ea6d0b984`.
- Linux Blacksmith proof: [native Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36328022430), one worker per file. Node 24.19.0: 129 passed. Maintained Bun 1.4.3, revision `a70be26b47560ede9b7646451e66e3f735195672`: 127 passed and two pre-existing Node-only topology skips.
- The unchanged original migration file passed all 23 cases in declaration order on each runtime. Focused coverage includes retained-worker retirement and join, zero/changing file metadata, sequential schema scopes, unexpected-error propagation, lazy missing/replaced locators, aliases, and asynchronous lifecycle behavior.
- Actual Vitest reporter/fork executable hashes and native worker manifests were verified, including the patched backend input digest `58eb3fb2eddda3435942b05bd4d4fa716459fbd348d602ffa00f38db1ce2a8c3`.
- All six-path changed-file gates passed (1,280.162s), including formatting, core typecheck, all 25 test type graphs, lint (zero warnings/errors), and schema/lifecycle guards. The remote command exited 0; local wrapper cleanup exited 2 after a disk-full receipt write failure. The Testbox was stopped; its local capsule is retained by the native admitted-state guard. This is passing remote proof, not a successful local artifact or cleanup receipt.
- Independent owner review and installed source review found no remaining actionable finding. Production: +49 net lines for lifecycle ownership and the lazy-open invariant; tests: +220 net lines.

The two Bun skips assume four shared carriers, which does not match Bun's existing dedicated-worker topology; no new skip was added. Dedicated-slot saturation coverage is a separate follow-up. The maintained Bun run's known directory-FD warning is repaired separately in [openclaw/bun#16](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/pull/16); it did not fail these tests.

<details>
<summary>Proof cost</summary>

One Testbox lease, observed queued at 15:01:43 UTC and stopped at 15:36:32 UTC on 2026-09-27. The passing native command took 28m2.580s; focused file wrappers totaled 5m54.345s and changed gates took 21m20.162s. An earlier pre-test observer assertion incorrectly compared the transport parent to the source branch parent; it failed before tests, was corrected to the receiver-installed transport base, and reused the same immutable source and lease.

</details>

prs.title: fix(startup): avoid full copies for closed WAL header checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Header-only schema preflight copies an entire closed WAL-mode agent database when no integrity receipt is available. Large databases can spend substantial startup time copying data that the header check does not need.

## User Impact

Doctor and startup header checks can read a consolidated agent database directly when exclusive source admission is available. This requires no migration or configuration change. Full integrity and readiness checks, retention, and the existing fallback remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing immutable source reader to header-only requests. Its owner still excludes managed source handles, rejects WAL/SHM/journal sidecars, checks file identity before and after reading, and retains custody through native close. Startup still repeats admission under its lease.

## Evidence

- Both new regressions failed on the original code and passed with identical fixtures after the repair. The real preflight now completes one schema inspection with zero agent snapshots.
- **27 tests passed across three owning and integrity test files**, including source preservation, sidecar and held-owner refusal, full-check fallback, corruption handling, cancellation, and clean native child closure.
- Core production types, the owning state/logging test type graph, full-rule lint, formatting, pinned-base line/assertion guards, and documentation sanity passed.
- Fresh independent P2 review of the four-file change, with nine unchanged owners and callers supplied as context, found no actionable issue.

The normal production build, current-head CI, and live startup/Swarm latency remain pending. These tests do not establish a 500 ms performance pass.

<details>
<summary>Measured changed-test costs</summary>

Measured once per file using Node 24.21 and `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`. Command wall time includes canonical test-worker preparation; other task validation was running concurrently.

| Test file | Passed tests | Command wall | New regression body |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `src/state/openclaw-agent-schema-inspection-worker.test.ts` | 8 | 40.30 s | 451 ms |
| `src/state/openclaw-database-preflight.schema-only.test.ts` | 11 | 104.88 s | 3.24 s |

The native matrix reuses one child. The preflight suite exercises real SQLite/WAL ownership and cleanup; the new case must cross the actual preflight boundary to detect the unnecessary-copy fallback. Hosted CI cost will be recorded when available.

</details>

prs.title: fix(channels): delegated workers take over chat conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: delegating work can redirect later chat messages to a subagent instead of the agent the user was talking to.

## User Impact

User impact: delegation no longer changes who receives the next message in a chat channel. Native subagents and agent-spawned ACP workers cannot own a DM, group, thread, or topic. This deliberately removes automatic and manual native-subagent channel binding, including `/subagents spawn --thread`.

**Chat channels only.** Independent Team/Web UI sessions, WebChat/TUI/internal coordination, ordinary channel threads, normal agent routing, and explicit user-created ACP sessions remain supported. Visible app sessions retain their persistent follow-up guidance.

Existing worker bindings are ignored at runtime rather than deleted by a startup migration. Safety does not depend on retained job records, idle expiry, or a background sweep finishing after startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared binding owner rejects delegated targets before effects and applies the same rule to channel routing and bound delivery. Durable session provenance covers old aliases and visible child sessions even after their original job record expires. Asynchronous reads revalidate binding identity before admitting their results.

Telegram native/plugin commands, Slack external events and interactions, and Discord command/reply paths use policy-bearing admission instead of treating synchronous binding projections as permission to execute. The incomplete takeover sweep and unused spawn-binding helpers are removed. Explicit `/acp` sessions remain a separate user-controlled feature.

## Evidence

**Fresh stable-to-candidate upgrade: passed (2026-09-26).** [Update Migration run 36235766906](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36235766906) passed on its first attempt, using published `openclaw@2026.9.6` and the exact `7add7a5fd422da70838e2d2a748eb75615c72521` candidate package. The released updater ran first, followed by real Gateway stop/start on the same persisted state. The selected legacy-operator-state scenario verified configuration, approvals, agents, native cron histories and ownership, authored workspace data, a candidate turn, clean follow-up Doctor, already-current second update, and backup restoration. Runtime lane: 1,001 seconds. Gateway, updater, npm and persistence were real; model responses were mocked.

**Same-chat continuity: passed in a separate isolated installed-package proof.** A real published-Gateway `chat.send` created the session; no session/transcript rows were seeded. After its installed updater completed (79.9 seconds, exit 0), candidate `chat.history` returned the original two messages byte-equal, including metadata, with the same canonical key and session ID. A candidate turn continued that session to four messages while preserving the original prefix; another cold restart retained all four byte-equal. The candidate model request contained the original user/assistant turns. Workspace-file bytes were unchanged. Three distinct Gateway host processes have source/build/start identities and normal joined exit-0 receipts; owned processes and ports were cleaned up. The Team service and operator state were untouched.

The broader stable-to-candidate update successfully applied the existing core state-schema 18→19 migration (agent schema remained 23). **This PR adds no binding-deletion or schema migration.** These upgrade tests do not substitute for the still-failing regular CI gate below or prove live delegated-channel routing.

<details>
<summary>Upgrade identity and proof boundaries</summary>

- Published baseline source: `eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b`; tarball SHA-256: `1a7355691bc0e605222ba818f1f72c1787253c78dfeb0df6be2086ec73b71e63`.
- Candidate tarball SHA-256: `f4acdedc35cbcc51e37bc0a7fc9cdf7974ea4a5fe32013910ba8a9aa19a475e8`. Both packages label themselves 2026.9.6; full build/source identities, not the version label, establish the upgrade.
- Hosted workflow/harness: `e7a71e9078224ca68212a3c990074ba46b41706d`. The credential-free Update Migration wrapper selected only `legacy-operator-state` with explicit baseline 2026.9.6. Runtime artifact: `docker-e2e-update-migration` (10904801724).
- The general hosted scenario uses separate baseline/candidate chat IDs. The supplemental public-API test above closes that continuity gap and supplies the distinct-process receipts absent from the hosted artifact. Both exercise manual cold lifecycle with `--no-restart`, not service-manager restart.
- The local fixture's ancillary memory indexing received two 401 responses with a synthetic placeholder credential. Chat generation and history assertions passed with the local mock; embedding success, real-model quality and network-offline execution are not claimed.
- Hosted first-hop exit-snapshot diagnostics were unavailable and some published log excerpts were capped. Successful update/build-transition and completed runtime assertions are independent receipts, not inferred from that missing diagnostic.

</details>

- Before the current-main refresh, **713 focused regression and sibling-contract cases passed** across native spawning, channel binding/routing, Discord, Telegram, Slack, Matrix, Feishu, account isolation, and UI-session preservation. These include registered handlers and real isolated persistent stores, with transport boundaries mocked.
- Pre-refresh validation included full core/extension production typechecks, all core-test compiler shards, extension-test typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, docs, generated metadata, import-boundary, database/schema, and unused-export checks. Findings were repaired without weakening limits or assertions.
- Pre-refresh `pnpm build` passed, including packaged runtime/SDK declarations, Control UI output, and UI size budgets. A subsequent app-only persistence-note preservation change passed focused tests and a separate source review; it does not change channel binding or package boundaries.
- Mandatory independent P0–P2 review completed clean after the accepted findings were addressed. A separate final scope review confirmed that app persistence remains separate from channel ownership and that the removed helpers had no remaining production callers.

**Current-main refresh:** merged `5dc4df504e6` while retaining contributor history and the existing Discord/Slack refactors. A follow-up to `b458b9f1c6b` resolved only a generated configuration-baseline conflict; the reviewed channel-routing implementation stayed byte-identical. All 140 Discord and 241 Slack cases in the overlapping regression suites passed; the extracted binding-fixture consumers also passed. Core/extension production types, extension-test types, scoped type-aware lint, and growth/assertion guards passed. Configuration and prompt artifacts were regenerated from the combined source. Fresh review found no actionable defect: its lone missing-callback report is contradicted by the existing `assertActive?: () => void` declaration and successful compiler checks. Hosted CI for the refreshed commit is tracked separately; the earlier build is not presented as a new-head CI result.

**Hosted CI is blocked.** [Current-head run 36221373044](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36221373044) ended cancelled after the [originating cleanup test failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36221373044/job/108347673976): cleanup-service.applied-summary.test.ts reports “Agent database resources are closing” after reopening. The test, cleanup-service.ts, and database-resource owner are unchanged from base b458b9f1c6b. Causality/pre-existence is not established; this is not claimed to be a harmless flake. No cleanup/database-lifecycle or filesystem changes have been folded into the channel-only patch, and no additional unchanged-head retries are planned.

The CI-discovered Discord autocomplete and iMessage fixture defects have been repaired without changing production policy. The iMessage repair preserves stable binding identity, verifies both admission reads, declares explicit agent ownership, and awaits real reaction completion with cleanup instead of a one-second poll. All 23 focused iMessage cases pass; types, lint, growth/assertion checks, and repair-only review passed. Current head: 7add7a5fd42; hosted validation remains incomplete because of the blocker above.

<details>
<summary>CI attempt history and bounded repairs</summary>

**CI follow-up:** [run 36218081412](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36218081412) found two autocomplete assertions failing because a test fixture omitted the configured binding’s required stateful target. Commit e6f88041619 completes and type-constrains that fixture and strengthens its context assertion; it does not change production policy. All five autocomplete tests passed in 41.17 seconds, with extension-test typechecking, scoped lint, growth/assertion checks, and a fresh repair-only review passing. A new exact-head CI run is required; the cancelled predecessor is not green evidence.

On e6f880, [attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36218953977/attempts/1) hit an ENOENT while scanning an rsync temporary manifest. The workspace-sync test and quota implementation are byte-identical to the base; no filesystem code was changed here, and the failure is not claimed to be a proven pre-existing flake. One documented failed-job retry was used.

[Attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36218953977/attempts/2) exposed seven iMessage fixture assertions/errors, repaired in 7add7a5fd42. That attempt cancelled the earlier workspace-sync job, so it did not establish that the filesystem case passed. There are no skipped-check waivers or further unchanged-head retries planned.

</details>

**Live-channel upgrade proof remains incomplete:** instrumented Telegram readiness confirmed that the configured Convex CI environment pair works: the test credential was acquired, TDLib readiness succeeded, and the lease was released. The subsequent bot-identity request to the skill’s loopback Telegram Test API proxy received HTTP 502, text/plain, “Secret egress proxy refused the request.” The local proxy’s upstream-to-Telegram callback was never reached. This is a host secret-egress refusal, not missing Convex credentials; its exact internal refusal reason still needs diagnosis. No alternate identity or transport was used. The existing Telegram upgrade script also expects continued child routing and must be adapted before it can judge this new parent-routing policy. Neither passing upgrade test above exercises old native/agent-ACP channel bindings, explicit user ACP preservation, or live channel input. Existing focused channel tests remain separate evidence. No new live Telegram/Discord/Matrix proof is claimed; the author’s earlier evidence is not proof of this revised implementation.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and repaired fixture details</summary>

The final Telegram/Slack follow-through group passed in 120.01 seconds wall. The Discord binding-contract group passed 85 cases in 106 seconds. Representative serial sibling runs: Telegram binding lifecycle 27 cases in 28.86 seconds; account-scoped binding storage 13 cases in 79.56 seconds (including cold compilation); Slack binding compatibility 2 cases in 19.40 seconds. Shared contracts/remaining command-resolution helpers passed in 69.80 seconds. The final app-persistence and Slack interaction group passed in 40.94 seconds. Timings include harness startup/compilation; they are not live-channel latency. CI timing for the pushed head is pending.

Old positive fixtures that incidentally created subagent bindings now use ordinary or explicitly user-owned sessions. Authority, FIFO, persistence, expiry, account-isolation, and unbind assertions remain. Tests waiting for database work now wait for actual queue admission rather than assuming one microtask is sufficient. Historical/private-manager worker fixtures remain where they test legacy storage behavior.

</details>

## Contributor credit

Original PR and implementation by @obviyus. Follow-through preserves the original commit, with co-author credit to @obviyus and @joshavant.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/4168b516-fed4-4828-aa60-385f30036fb4)
- [Delegated binding-policy implementation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b53ff30c-0012-4323-96de-f1e1d6c4f2f7)
- [Slack external-event implementation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/92a099b1-04fd-4207-bf36-e7b585d1c666)

Submission and native-terminal actions are adopted on main through #179833; this candidate moves New Session to 4 adopted / 2 pending mutation families and 0 pending / 2 allowed cleanup sites.

The TypeScript owner retains selection, queued intent, write success, retry, and close/reopen behavior. `affects` and `refresh` reconcile the visible failure derivation; the owner's synchronous selection supplies the expected checkbox value. Settings remain editable while the footer exposes saving through `aria-busy`.

Presentation retires synchronously on settings/palette close, authenticated binding replacement, and Gateway invalidation. This fixes the observed reconnect deadlock without cancelling the already admitted write. Background autosave, bootstrap migration, and accepted one-use cleanup retain their existing owner contracts and have no separate explicit saving affordance.

Title preparation is now plain TypeScript with explicit disposal, paired with page setup through `onSettled`. The two retained `onCleanup` sites have concrete contracts: subscriptions and reconciliation bind before the first child read and must cover pre-settle disposal; each conditional settings control owns its focus registration even when removed before the panel settles. Host tags, classes, selectors, routes and lazy boundaries remain unchanged.

prs.body:
Related: #166718

## What Problem This Solves

`config patch --dry-run` can report success when a large provider-catalog reduction will be rejected by the real write's size-drop guard, misleading deployment preflights.

## User Impact

Structured config previews now fail early with a `write-safety` error and the same size-drop reason as the writer, plus its existing recovery guidance. The preview leaves config bytes unchanged and creates no backup or rejected-payload file. If persistence preparation refuses the change, JSON output retains the assignments, input modes, completed checks, and counters; plain-text output retains the original refusal. Existing write protection remains enabled; this does not add a public size-drop override or change value-mode's documented limited validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and commit share preparation of the authored, metadata-stamped payload and its canonical size baseline. Include-only mutations retain their existing write route instead of applying the root-file guard to an expanded config. The writer continues to own runtime activation, rejection artifacts, auditing, publication, and rollback.

The related roster-retention preview work in #153069 does not evaluate the serialized-byte guard. The public override requested in #166718 remains a separate product decision, so this PR does not close the entire issue.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the registered-CLI regression fails because the large-shrink preview succeeds; moderate-shrink and include-owned controls pass.
- Real CLI proof uses the normal `pnpm openclaw config patch --file <patch> --replace-path models.providers.bounty.models` entry point in isolated task-owned home/config/state, with 409 synthetic provider models and no provider calls or credentials. The original live failure was reproduced at `2b988ee83444` (the affected owner code is unchanged at this PR's base `80322af5c7e5`).
- Committed candidate `9982d96b8c1d` results: 409→32 root preview and actual write both reject with `size-drop`; the preview preserves original bytes and creates no artifact. 409→300 root and 409→32 include-owned changes pass preview and persist the exact requested model count. Include-owned writes preserve the root file. A real provider-builder shrink also rejects in both preview and commit; its preview has `checks.schema:false` and still returns `write-safety`, directly proving the review correction.
- `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 99 passed; 51.68 s runner wall time. The materially changed integration file has 34 tests and takes 29.83 s Vitest wall time; the cases reuse its existing real config-command fixture.
- Unchanged writer/reference coverage, run at `9982d96b8c1d`: `pnpm test src/config/io.write-config.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 130 passed; 62.96 s total. Covers existing canonical-format/BOM sizing, references, include ownership, refusal, and rollback contracts.
- The supported CLI wrapper completed the production build for live proof. Core and core-test typechecks and changed-file lint passed. The aggregate changed check stopped at the unrelated existing `observePlacementAuthority` unused export in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-authority.ts`; this file and its references are unchanged by the patch. The subsequent ready-for-review CI result and current follow-up are documented below.
- Follow-up `9b8e17b2b06`: parser-validated builder/batch inputs and thrown persistence refusals have registered-command regressions that failed before their corrections. For the empty-roster refusal, the old JSON path returned `operations:0`, empty `inputModes`, and false checks; its text-output control already passed. The corrected real CLI returns `operations:1`, `inputModes:["json"]`, all completed checks true, preserved counters, and the original schema refusal. It exits 1, leaves config bytes unchanged, and creates no backup/rejected file. The matching non-JSON regression preserves the exact original diagnostic.




### CI and conflict follow-up (2026-10-10)

Integrated main `0c94b6966078` to resolve the real `src/config/io.write.ts` import conflict. Both intents are retained: upstream `composeConfigWriteAssertions` and this PR's shared payload preparation. The PR delta against the new base remains the same nine files; no Doctor test, timeout, assertion, or CI workflow was changed.

The previous CI run [37805483456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37805483456/job/113409493434) failed on `runs legacy state migrations in yes mode without prompting` at 30.228 s (30 s limit), causing the aggregate gate to fail. Diagnosis did not reproduce that failure:

- Exact old PR source `9b8e17b2b064`: original seven-file shard order, separate file processes, macOS arm64 / Node 26.4.0: all 87 tests passed; the named test took 10.582 s. A standalone diagnostic retained all assertions and the deadline, observed maintenance admission in 65 ms and overall completion in 12.939 s, and was removed afterward.
- Same old source in a credential-free Linux arm64 container, Node 24.19.0, 2 CPUs / 8 GiB: all five Doctor-file tests passed; the named test took 18.558 s. This matches the CI Node version and resource limits but not its Linux x64 hardware. The container was removed after diagnosis.
- Conflict-resolved candidate: original seven-file shard, all 87 tests passed; the named test took 12.338 s. Config CLI and writer suites passed 202 tests (34 integration, 65 CLI, 103 writer), 67.86 s combined runner wall time; integration file 27.12 s Vitest wall time.

The original CI timeout remains unattributed. These passing replays are not presented as a timeout fix; no retry logic, longer deadlines, weakened assertions, or speculative production changes were added. The subsequent CI run [38082056748](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38082056748) passed all 86 jobs on `64e6949e85a3`; this is prior-head evidence.

Final local validation on `64e6949e85a3`: types, targeted lint, formatting, and all remaining selected guards pass. The aggregate check stops at 17 Knip findings; the same canonical scan on a separately installed, clean `0c94b6966078` worktree reproduces the identical set (15 authentication/runtime exports, one Solid lint export, one UI test-helper export). They are inherited rather than introduced by this PR.



### Review guidance and async conflict follow-up

Commit `3687439fae0` reuses `createConfigWriteSafetyRejectionError` for actionable recovery guidance in both JSON and text previews, retaining the size-drop reason. The existing registered-command case failed before the message repair and now verifies both output formats and unchanged config/files. No new test fixture or production abstraction was added.

Integrated main `c6d71fae0ed` to resolve the writer conflict from #168481: topology preparation is now asynchronous, so the preview and writer await it and the shared payload type consumes its resolved value.

Validation: 202 tests passed across config CLI integration (34), CLI (65), and writer (103); 101.20 s runner wall time. Integration-file Vitest wall time: 46.38 s. No hosted CI timing for this new head yet.

Final local checks: production types, all core-test type groups, scoped lint, formatting, and the selected ratchets passed. The aggregate changed check stops at four Knip unused exports outside the PR diff: `stripClaudeCliGeneratedUserPrefixes`, `createChannelApprovalHandlerAsync`, `GitHubConnectionsContent`, and `reconnectGateway`. Their defining files match the integrated base; no clean-base Knip replay was run for this head. These findings remain recorded, not suppressed.



### Conflict refresh (2026-10-11)

Integrated main `0ff0202128f` for the new writer conflict. Preserved upstream's agent-deletion authority check before publication and awaited metadata recording. Applied upstream's payload cleanup in the extracted shared preparation function; audit metadata remains computed by the writer. No new behavior, tests, or dependencies were introduced by this conflict repair. The prior head `3687439fae09` had a successful [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38109291576); that remains prior-head evidence.

## Summary
- expose an optional, source-compatible `enqueueRun` capability on the service-owned cron facade
- define its contract as durable queue acceptance, not automation payload completion

Workboard captures its lifecycle service across Gateway hook turns. Service-owned queue admission keeps authorization valid without making agent-end cleanup wait for the automation payload. Older hosts may omit the optional capability; Workboard logs the failed nudge without blocking lifecycle synchronization.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve agent ownership in custom session stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Non-default agents using `global` or `unknown` keys with a custom session store could fail baseline validation, persist state in the wrong agent, or silently discard a final reply during durable queue admission.

## User Impact

Creation, subsequent turns, command finalization, CLI continuity, and final delivery retain the selected agent. Another agent's session stays untouched. No configuration or database-schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A session key and store locator do not always identify the logical agent. Carry the resolver's selected identity through baseline reads and writes, command admission and persistence, and CLI binding and compaction. Physical database selection and lifecycle validation remain with the existing storage owners.

The final-delivery correction carries that identity through all three marker producers, completion metadata, durable queue settlement, recovery claims, cleanup, and wakeup. New private calls require an owner. Older persisted queue completions without an owner retain their historical locator semantics; an explicit owner never falls back or scans other agents. Existing writer and lifecycle authority checks remain enforced.

Supporting helper extractions keep the edited entry points within their size limits.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the earlier compiled reply failure and both command failures. Real finalization regressions verify durable agent isolation, cleanup, and a second turn; 200 focused storage, delivery, compaction, and CLI cases passed.
- Passed the complete changed-file gate against pinned base `55995369eca3`, including all 25 test-type graphs. The main carry passed four affected Gateway/worktree and BOOT membership cases and their owning checks while preserving the 20 qualified production postimages.
- Reproduced five model-switch fixture failures on the unchanged head, repaired the required resolver identity and exact delivery expectation, and passed all 138 cases, owning checks, and independent P2 review. CI run `35737199515` passed on that correction.
- The later delivery review finding reproduced as two real marker-to-queue failures for `ops/global` and `ops/unknown`, plus two recovery-controller failures. The correction passed 81 focused cases, including actual queue delivery, legacy serialized recovery, conflicting authority, explicit-owner no-fallback behavior, shared physical SQLite ownership, and neighbor preservation.
- Passed 33 existing producer cases, the normal full build, and the full changed-file gate pinned to `e18b90de5832`. The final private-owner type tightening and fixture fields passed 26 affected cases, core and owning-test types, lint, and fresh independent P2 review. Those 26 cases overlap the focused suite; they are not an additional unique total.

Earlier CI and intermediate fixture failures remain recorded. An earlier size check used a stale tracking ref; final checks use pinned bases. The prior archive-lifecycle failure remains with its existing lifecycle owner in #155701. Existing synchronous recovery reads remain separate async-storage work; this PR corrects their owner scope and does not claim that reply recovery is fully asynchronous.

Related: #154864. Auth-profile pin isolation landed separately in #155717.

## Measured Test Cost

Single-worker measurements use the normal test wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`; wall time includes its preparation and cleanup. These are observations on the same local host, not a performance improvement claim.

| Scope | Cases | Wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full outbound completion integration file, before correction (`e18b90de5832`) | 2 | 34.26 s |
| Same full file after correction (`31619fa6600f`) | 8 | 29.55 s |
| Six focused pending-final/recovery files | 81 | 266.92 s |
| Existing pending-final producer selection | 33 | 1079.83 s, including 808.1 s normal build; Vitest 222.50 s |
| Final private-owner fixture selection | 26 | 105.71 s |

The outbound file exercises actual SQLite storage, queue admission, completion settlement, and serialized recovery with a synthetic transport; a pure argument test would miss the demonstrated dropped-delivery defect. Before/after timings include different cache/preparation costs and are not directly comparable as a speedup. The previously run full model-switch suite took 104.09 s for 138 cases with the normal worker policy.

Current CI run `35744775396` reported an encrypted-tool continuation timeout in job `106803912989`: 135.08 s test-step wall time, including its existing 90-second test limit. It was the sole failure; all other checks passed. The unchanged test passed locally on both the PR head (37.139 s) and the exact CI merge `cc2e9b75c9ed` (20.252 s). One isolated [Testbox reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35748341827) on that merge with Linux/Node 24.19, two workers, two-CPU affinity, and the unchanged 90-second limit also passed (36.964 s test, 70.25 s wrapper). Remote-only failure-phase observations changed no assertions and emitted no failure report. The lease had 16.56 GB RAM versus CI's 8.22 GB and was stopped after the command exited 0. These passes do not establish the historical timeout's cause; no CI rerun or speculative fixture fix is claimed. The earlier `e18b90de5832` run remains historical green evidence only.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes redundant security-review enforcement and pending status resets when a PR author edits only the title or body.

## User Impact

Internal CI change; no product runtime change. Positively identified title/body-only edits no longer make GitHub API calls or enqueue security enforcement from the event resolver. The lightweight event workflow still runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Title and body are outside the existing approval snapshot. The resolver now recognizes only nonempty title/body change records whose descriptors contain exactly a string-valued `from`, after validating repository and PR identity. Base retargets, unknown or mixed edits, malformed payloads, head changes, approval-comment edits/revocations, and CI completion retain their existing live review paths. No guard, permission, workflow trigger, or approval policy changes.

The payload shape follows the [official edited-event schema](https://github.com/octokit/webhooks/blob/main/payload-schemas/api.github.com/pull_request/edited.schema.json). A combined-entrypoint regression also verifies that title/body changes remain outside approval authority, so a future authority expansion cannot silently invalidate this optimization.

## Evidence

- Before: the actual resolver CLI on base `f17f50ac9fba54e449640db387960d8f7e692b9a` made two reads and published a pending status for a body-only edit.
- After: 28 direct resolver CLI/API-trace controls passed in 1.905 seconds, covering accepted text edits, conservative ambiguous cases, identity rejection, approval revocation, duplicate-head recovery, and CI completion. These execute the real entrypoint with intercepted API responses; they are not a recorded production webhook run.
- Node syntax, exact-version oxfmt 0.67.0, staged privacy inspection, and `git diff --check` passed. The managed checkout is code-only; no dependency installation or shared-install reconciliation was performed.
- Native whole-PR P2 passed with no findings on `d15d2fcf33171475831361a1dfef8927932f5cf5` against the frozen base; final source verification passed.
- Canonical hosted tests passed in [CI 35578579611/1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35578579611), testing merge `2c8f0e5b78899426dafd81761feac7febcd46449` (`d15d2fc` into `fd578cb`). The [event test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35578579611/job/106266249098) passed 74/74 event cases; its observed group interval was 4.607 seconds (08:36:54.9864303–08:36:59.5936670 UTC). The [combined-guard test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35578579611/job/106266248938) passed 56/56 combined-entrypoint cases; its observed group interval was 6.751 seconds (08:36:48.1629209–08:36:54.9141531 UTC), including the new authority-coupling case in 64 ms. These are observed CI group intervals, not isolated benchmarks or measured savings; the second job also ran a separate test-projects group.
- The exact-head ClawSweeper review found no code or security defect and accepted the owner-level fix. Its canonical-test timing request is satisfied above. Its independent SecOps approval request remains open: the requested team has not approved, and ruleset `23692106` enforces code-owner review for this resolver even on maintainer-authored PRs. Administrative task authorization does not waive that enforced review. Remaining full-CI/status checks and the required approval must clear before landing. No additional rating-only re-review was requested.

Tooling: +29/-0 lines; tests: +110/-0; product runtime: unchanged. The small production increase owns conservative event classification at the existing resolver; no second review policy or cache was introduced.

Named follow-up: preserve underlying API errors in security-review diagnostics. That separate diagnostic change is not included here.

prs.title: refactor: retain session ownership during post-commit work
prs.body:
Related: #142863

## What Problem This Solves

Session writes currently release their physical writer before an awaited follow-up can finish, allowing later lifecycle work to overtake that follow-up. This is the storage foundation for the agent-owned group stack split from #142863.

## User Impact

No group behavior or database schema changes in this PR. Existing callers keep their current behavior. Later stack layers will use this bounded continuation to prevent delayed category registration from reviving deleted groups.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an optional `afterCommitted` continuation to creation, lifecycle mutation, and canonical replacement. It runs after successful SQL commit/publication but before the existing physical writer is released. Its context retains the original revocable native owner and captured environment; close revokes authority and joins completion. Post-commit failure does not mean the durable write rolled back.

**Scope:** seven storage files only. No Gateway/UI/native-client activation, schema migration, or upgrade-driver changes. Most added lines are regression coverage.

prs.title: fix(update): complete native restarts after executor delegation
prs.body:
Related: #159385

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native restart finalization failing with “The update process is still running” after an otherwise successful update on the 2026.9.7 candidate.

## User Impact

Legacy finalizers can complete the real native restart and publish their terminal result. Current authority, receiver binding, child extinction, deadlines, snapshots, and rollback attempted-start protections remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a two-file incremental correction stacked on integration head 3c5ec84cd7bb5edd07580960879e97aa1dd7b5cf, not a duplicate of its backports. Backport c3c20e0241b placed the parent mutation-fence assertion inside the delegated child callback. The child owner deliberately suspends that fence until its process joins, so the assertion rejects before native activation. Check the parent immediately before delegation instead; the child owner still revalidates current authority before running and binding its receiver.

Current main 168ebc5b67080909f825858d16308a94278c5342 does not contain the erroneous inner assertion. This is release-only.

## Evidence

- Isolated exact-base reproduction: both grantless-scratch-owned-parent-pnpm-root-move and grantless-scratch-owned-parent-git-root-switch failed with executor-settlement errors and no result.json. Both pass with the ordering correction (2/2; 25.24 seconds including native worker preparation).
- Existing real native custody scenarios now assert that the parent mutation fence remains suspended when the attempted-start callback fires, and that the callback is observed once before successful activation. No new process fixtures or timeout changes.
- All four related files passed: 65/65 tests across native custody (19), legacy finalization (27), service command (9), and source replacement (10). Total wrapper wall time 143.80 seconds. Existing custody file: 59.63 seconds including worker preparation; the patch adds assertions only, no new native processes. Full wrong-handoff/run/root/version/scratch/parent and revoked/retargeted refusals remain green.
- Standalone P0–P2 autoreview produced no report after 10 minutes and was stopped at the explicitly requested bound. Review is incomplete, not clean; this causally proven patch is published for actual hosted review/CI rather than prolonging the stalled reviewer.
- Both exact legacy cases also pass with pinned Vitest 5.0.0 using a read-only diagnostic resolver (2/2; 28.34 seconds wrapper wall time); no shared package files were edited.
- Scoped formatting and type-aware lint passed (0 warnings/errors); git diff --check passed. Full core typecheck could not start because the borrowed installed tree lacks the target typescript-native/package.json alias; this is an unrun gate, not a passing typecheck.
- Local diagnostic runtime is Node 26.8.2 / Vitest 5.0.1, using the pinned TypeScript 6.0.3 read-only diagnostic resolver and repository test wrappers. A Node 24.19.0 checksum download was refused with HTTP 403; no proxy or supply-chain controls were bypassed. Hosted Node 24 / Vitest 5.0.0 proof, Claw review, and full release validation remain required before the parent lands this change.

Parent owns landing and full release/installed-upgrade validation. No live service or release publication action is part of this patch.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the retained Telegram delivery-trace test sending its synthetic final edit before the scripted server flood wait expires. This is a maintainer-requested 2026.9.7 release repair following the concrete diagnostic from #159385. Related: #157349.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The release test again protects finalizing the existing preview only after Telegram's retry-after deadline, without sending an extra answer or weakening backoff. All five golden files and their full assertions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release backport f488a8cdfd6 moved flood-wait ownership from the draft stream to the per-token account limiter. Production bot-core installs that limiter on the grammY API. The older trace fixture supplied a hand-made API object and bypassed the new owner entirely.

Use a real grammY API with a recording synthetic fetch and the existing account flood transformer. Only ordinary scheduler pacing uses the existing test injection seam; the real flood gate and final retry policy execute. Reset token-scoped state per scenario and continue rejecting unexpected transport methods. No golden refresh, assertion relaxation, dependency edit, or timeout change.

This is release-only: main intentionally removed this trace fixture and its goldens in de5e31b8958 (#155040). Do not restore retired main coverage or alter production backoff to accommodate an obsolete fixture boundary.

## Evidence

- Diagnosed on c6770887, then rebased the identical one-file patch onto release base 7044fb5 so the PR does not include the parent dependency repair.
- Original exact c6770887 diagnostic: 4/5 trace tests pass; rate-limit case fails because the final edit occurs at 1700 ms rather than 2400 ms after a 1400 ms response with retry_after=1.
- Repaired same-runtime trace: 5/5 pass against unchanged goldens, retaining idle at 1700 ms and final edit at 2400 ms. Trace test time 163 ms; Vitest duration 19.34 s; wrapper wall 21.31 s including worker preparation and verified cleanup.
- Trace plus account-throttler siblings: 22/22 pass, including token-wide backoff, skipped previews, final recovery, cancellation, and overlapping deadlines. Wrapper wall 22.56 s.
- Exact mapped changed-extensions-config-105 selection (10 files): 125/125 pass after repair, versus the original diagnostic 124 passed / 1 failed. Wrapper wall 59.81 s. This remains the diagnostic runtime, not a claim that the entire hosted bundle is repaired.
- Independent standalone autoreview was attempted with the scoped patch and causal context; the reviewer timed out after 600 seconds (engine exit 124) without a verdict. This is not a clean review. No Claude fallback CLI is installed. Current-head hosted ClawSweeper review remains mandatory.
- Formatting and git diff --check pass. Focused lint wrapper is blocked before lint by unavailable typescript-native/package.json in the borrowed diagnostic dependency set.
- Local evidence uses Node 26.8.2 / Vitest 5.0.1 and a process-local cached TypeScript 6 resolver with read-only borrowed dependencies. The installed grammY 1.46.0 and transformer-throttler 1.2.1 match the candidate package pins. It is **not** target Node 24 / Vitest 5.0.0 parity, hosted CI proof, or live Telegram proof. No network requests or real channel messages were sent.

Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review remain required before landing. Parent maintainer owns shepherding and landing; this PR does not resolve the other unexplained release runtime failures.

Related: #157709. Thanks to @vyctorbrzezowski for the concurrent diagnosis and repair in #157848; this version keeps the contracts in existing modules rather than introducing new modules or moving runtime functions.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes architecture checks failing on unrelated PRs because profile and Gateway startup contracts introduced two static import cycles.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Release Checks lanes fail on main and in 2026.9.7 Full Release Validation (independent run 36475789054; main's own 36475640978) because tests drifted from recent product changes.

## User Impact

User impact: no runtime change. QA Lab parity/runtime-pair, restored-requester settle e2e, native live agent/gateway suites, Docker live Codex harness, and the Telegram group-policy hot-reload scenario stop failing on stale assumptions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- #158642 (d919bfbb) changed the subagent settle wake to "Every subagent in this batch has now settled". The qa-lab mock-openai matchers still looked for "spawned from this session", so handoffs stalled at 45000ms even though the child reported `delivery: delivered`.

- `telegram-group-policy-hot-reload` nulls the root and account `groupAllowFrom` arrays, but config.patch refuses array removal unless those paths are in `replacePaths`.

## Evidence

- QA mock-openai suites 180/180 pass. The restored-settle e2e passes 4/4. The QA parity scenario fails on main and passes with this change.

Provider API-key saves/removals, default-model changes, and confirmed logout currently expose the plain owners' busy facts directly. Connection, agent, route, and disposal changes retire only the old presentation; they do not cancel an admitted write. Config operations move intact into a focused module to keep the controller within its size limit.

prs.title: test: steering compaction test fails when the checkout path is short
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the steering test "keeps source validation until foreground delivery after pre-prompt compaction" fails deterministically when the checkout lives at a short absolute path (found by the local full-suite run of release/2026.9.7 on a Linux Crabbox box, checkout `~/oc`).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The release candidate's unit suite no longer depends on where the checkout lives.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test used the session's default system prompt, which embeds absolute checkout paths. With the test's 4k context window, a short path left a small positive headroom, so compaction preparation was rejected and the only provider request was foreground inference (`compacting: false`). Longer paths (macOS, GitHub runners) made headroom negative, which falls back to the retained-history budget, so the test passed there. Pinning a short base system prompt through the supported session API makes the test exercise compaction on every host.

## Evidence

- Linux Crabbox (AWS c7a.8xlarge, Ubuntu 26.04, Node 24.19 and 24.21), release SHA 56fb8872ed775: failed 5/5 before, passed 2/2 after (`pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-submit.steering.test.ts`, 4/4 tests).
- macOS: passes before and after.
- Test cost: unchanged (same four tests, one extra setter call).
- Autoreview (Codex): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

Lands on release/2026.9.7 first, then comes back to main.

prs.title: fix(qa): keep repeated Telegram RTT on the selected scenario route
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated Telegram RTT checks used the hard-coded logical conversation `telegram-rtt-room/group` even after the selected `channel-canary` scenario had already passed on its declared `qa-routing-primary/group` route. In the 2026.8.33 frozen-candidate release checks, the canary reply passed but every follow-on RTT sample missed its reply (0/20) across three attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The npm Telegram release runner now resolves the repeated probe's logical conversation from the selected catalog scenario when it declares `execution.config.conversationId` plus a supported direct/group transport policy. Valid canonical scenarios without route metadata preserve the existing generic RTT conversation. Partial, conflicting, and unsupported route declarations fail immediately.

This keeps route policy with the release runner that consumes it, adds no scenario-ID special cases or new environment/config surface, and preserves the documented explicit RTT selector contract. Root regression tests read real catalog scenarios through QA Lab's public `test-api` barrel; they do not load private plugin source.

The branch also includes one behavior-neutral current-`main` gate repair: omitted-media status rendering moved from the 708-line attachment renderer into the existing attachment-status module. This is a pure move (24 additions / 24 deletions) and restores the 700-line lint cap.

## User Impact

Telegram package release validation now matches repeated replies in the same logical conversation used by the selected scenario. Mention-gated group scenarios and DM-only scenarios retain their declared routes; unannotated explicit RTT selections keep the historical generic route.

No OpenClaw candidate, runtime package, release branch, tag, native Telegram destination, authorization policy, config, or stored-data contract changes.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix live release evidence: candidate Release Checks [36349516587](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36349516587), attempts 1–3. Each installed and started candidate `f773aa06a1a9`, passed the package Telegram canary with `QA-CHANNEL-CANARY-OK`, then recorded 0/20 repeated RTT samples.
- Root cause: `scripts/e2e/npm-telegram-live-runner.ts` constructed the follow-on probe on `telegram-rtt-room/group` instead of the selected scenario's declared conversation.
- Catalog/probe tests: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-round-trip.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog-channels.test.ts test/scripts/npm-telegram-live.test.ts` — 3 files, 83/83 passed.
- Boundary regression: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` — 20/20 passed; root tests load catalog proof through `extensions/qa-lab/test-api.js` only.
- Compatibility regression: catalog-backed `telegram-status-command` coverage proves a valid unannotated explicit RTT selection retains `telegram-rtt-room/group`.
- UI gate repair: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-attachments.test.ts` — 28/28 passed; `pnpm tsgo:ui` and targeted oxlint passed.
- Complete changed-surface gate at exact head `5a240c38273`: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — green, including formatting, all `tsgo` projects, dead-code scans, broad lint, and import-cycle checks.
- Test audit: coverage protects scenario-route ownership and the existing explicit-selector compatibility contract at the catalog-to-probe boundary; no test-only production seam.
- Fresh independent Sol/high AutoReview at exact head `5a240c38273`: scoped-clean through P1, no accepted/actionable findings.

Production/tooling LOC: +39/-2 (net +37), establishing selected-scenario route resolution in the release runner. Tests: +72/-8 (net +64). Docs: +3/-1. UI gate repair: +24/-24 pure move. Scenario fixture: +3/-2.

## ClawSweeper finding resolution

- **Preserve documented explicit RTT scenario selection (P1): applied.** Entirely unannotated valid scenarios retain the generic RTT conversation. Partial declarations remain invalid.
- **Catalog-backed coverage / Rank-up move: applied.** `telegram-status-command`, `channel-canary`, and `telegram-reply-chain-exact-marker` are loaded through the public QA Lab test barrel and asserted through probe construction.
- **Public-boundary correction: applied.** The root test no longer runtime-imports private extension source; `test/extension-test-boundary.test.ts` is green on the exact head.
- **Live proof gap:** the frozen-candidate failure is the pre-fix live reproduction. Post-fix live package proof will run through canonical Full Release Validation after merge so it uses trusted merged tooling without changing candidate bytes.

prs.title: fix(e2e): restart upgrade survivor after migration convergence
prs.body:
Related: #119051

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where manual Docker upgrade-survivor candidate starts could receive the explicit migration-convergence refusal and the harness would fail immediately instead of restarting against the converged state.

## Why This Change Was Made

This branch's upgrade-survivor launch path retries exactly once, and only when the first candidate gateway exits with status 1 and emits the exact migration-convergence refusal. The retry preserves state, config, port, environment, and arguments. It now covers both the manual survivor start and the pre-update candidate-auth start used by update-restart-auth; package self-update remains excluded.

## User Impact

QA and release validation become reliable when a candidate needs one restart after migration convergence. Product runtime impact: 0.

## Evidence

Retained historical branch proof:
- 191 focused helper and harness tests passed on `895d15ff782299d27e5ad6b0bb66cd4ebeba372f`.
- The exact-refusal matrix covers near matches, unrelated status 1, non-1 exits, a second refusal and stale logs. Bash syntax, formatting and diff checks passed at that historical revision.
- This is not current-main integration or exact-current-head qualification.

Current-main re-audit, September 26:
- [Package Acceptance completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36258167554) using tooling `8977ea332fbf9ba0a8ddc6c75af4ad7f27cee82e` and the published `openclaw@2026.9.2` package, source `3928bad9badfcb6c7d140530435e806fb8092190`.
- The sole selected Docker lane, `upgrade-survivor`, passed the real package update, Doctor, config/state assertions and foreground candidate start without this PR's retry. One lane attempt, 215 seconds; startup 9 seconds; status 2 seconds; cleanup joined. Package integrity and npm installer companion checks also passed.
- Package SHA-256: `3431f4cd2d8dbd6b936def2694ac27e19fa0256295cf4ada0f652ecf1c9ee520`.
- [#134002](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134002) and [#134410](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/134410) replaced the old pre-update foreground/PID-adoption setup with Doctor and a managed service. Its manager owns descendant drainage and preserves exit-78 refusal; the removed foreground mechanism is not a reason to restore this helper.

Published-upgrade compatibility result, September 26:
- [Package Acceptance run 36259445828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36259445828) failed the single published `2026.9.1` to `2026.9.2`, `base/manual` cell on the same frozen tooling. One 231-second attempt; no timeout; cleanup joined.
- The baseline's exact convergence refusal was recovered by the existing [#151607](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151607) helper, and baseline readiness passed.
- The failure is at `update-candidate`, before the candidate Gateway start. Package installation, the swap and the updater's internal Doctor each returned 0, but the update returned `post-update-plugins` / `post-plugin-doctor-invalid-config`: `plugins.load.paths` still referenced the fixture's deliberately removed `survivor-unavailable-path`. The outer update success/recoverability assertion rejected that result.
- Frozen `missing-load-path.sh` intentionally runs this fixture for base/manual. This is a historical package/fixture compatibility blocker, not proof of the original post-Doctor candidate-start refusal. The published trajectory remains unqualified; neither this failure nor the passing manual cell establishes whole-PR supersession.
- Retained outcome artifact: `10911534530`, SHA-256 `d3849b76cbb98bef20a889d626d482d424ffaef6790302083b52655e99e5e1d6`. Existing artifact omissions remain explicit; no unavailable inner diagnostics are claimed.

Current-source published-upgrade result, September 26:
- [Package Acceptance run 36261184406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36261184406), attempt 1, built source `5a27fda95008f6926b0c75d7a560524615694267` as version `2026.9.6`, with frozen tooling `8977ea332fbf9ba0a8ddc6c75af4ad7f27cee82e`. Package SHA-256: `07995e95dc505d00548e7469ca5493cb68e6d370e260f6d0560d90f8ba1ede16`.
- The only selected Docker cell was published `2026.9.1` to that source-built package, `base/manual`; no omitted lanes. One 586-second attempt, no outer timeout, cleanup joined. The owned temporary proof ref was removed and absence verified after completion.
- Baseline convergence, update, candidate/installed package identity, the unchanged missing-path preservation and warning assertions, Doctor, and config/state survival passed. This clears the earlier historical-package fixture blocker for this current-source candidate; it does not turn the historical run green.
- The cell then FAILED at `gateway-start`: strict readiness polling exhausted while the candidate was still alive. It reached HTTP listening and sidecar startup, but the required ready marker did not appear. No candidate retry was attempted, and this did not reproduce the old exact exit-1 migration-convergence refusal.
- The last completed startup trace was `sidecars.model-auth`; the encompassing `sidecars.model-runtime` completion was absent. Source places configured model-runtime snapshot publication at that boundary. This narrows investigation, not root-cause attribution.
- Source exposes a 120-second foreground model-preparation budget before degraded startup; the harness requires a 90-second startup budget and uses 360 strict readiness polls. This failure does not establish a deadlock or that the product's degradation fallback failed. Neither budget was changed. The retained diagnostics contain no `modelRuntime.stage`, `pendingAgents` or `degraded` status. Capture that existing status at the unresolved boundary in a justified diagnostic continuation before choosing a source repair; do not infer which inner await blocked from the last completed trace.
- [Lane evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36261184406/artifacts/10912773847) and [source admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36261184406/artifacts/10912956542) were independently inspected. The nested Gateway capture is capped at 16 KiB and the nested package-integrity diagnostic was omitted for size. The separate package-integrity and npm installer CI jobs passed; candidate readiness and later RPC assertions remain unqualified.
- A source-only comparison at current-main checkpoint `d0931ccefcc25dae4853cc4ac1921c2ff5f58e51` preserves the inspected convergence/refusal and upgrade-harness owners. New capture-lifetime, source-identity and retained-dependency changes are not a proven readiness fix or execution proof at that newer SHA.

Diagnostic harness continuation, September 26:
- Diagnostic-only tooling candidate `4a7031afaf039df4584bac37ce44c3d1edca6df6`, tree `39509daf83bc2fe3f418e08e6f3b8475d5a81e96`, adds one bounded direct-local `/readyz` and `/startupz` observation before cleanup. It preserves the original readiness exit status, startup budgets and strict assertions. No application runtime change or retry was added.
- [Causal harness proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36270998916) at `816174f20ba1` produced two intended baseline failures at the missing-capture assertion and five candidate passes, with three filtered baseline cases. Sixteen changed-check stages passed, including root-test typechecking and scripts lint. The aggregate failed only on the new test helper's Promise rejection lint rule; that failed receipt remains preserved.
- The one-line Error-with-cause correction passed independent review. [Exact final-tree follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36271408668) passed all five selected cases, root-test lint, formatting, Bash syntax and diff checks. All 211 source/dependency pins match. Remote fixtures were removed, transport source stayed unchanged, leases completed, and the final wrapper exited 0. Actions cancellation during one-shot cleanup is not an application failure. Earlier stages are retained with their original SHA, not relabeled as a fresh full final-head run.
- The [first fixture-setup failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36270690784) is also retained and is not causal regression proof.
- [Package Acceptance continuation 36271589195](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36271589195) completed with FAILURE on the single published `2026.9.1` to the same candidate, `base/manual` cell. Exact source and downstream admission passed; package integrity and npm installer checks passed. The unchanged product/package was reused from immutable artifact `10912776972`, producer run `36261184406`, attempt 1. One 659-second lane attempt, no outer timeout, no container OOM, joined cleanup. No product rebuild, retry or timeout increase.
- The new bounded capture reports both `/readyz` and `/startupz` unavailable because each request timed out. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In message-tool-only chats with a live progress card, the model sends a separate "I'm checking X…" message on top of the card's preamble. Users see the same acknowledgment twice (reported with a Codex-harness gist; reproduced on the OpenClaw harness with `gpt-6-astra`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The `message` tool's `final` description told the model to "set false for progress", which competes with commentary. Codex's own mid-turn message tool says the opposite: use it for things that need the user's attention, and put routine progress in commentary.

The `final` description now follows that framing, in the one place both harnesses read. The duplicate "Set `final=false` for progress" sentence is removed from the OpenClaw-harness messaging prompt.

## User Impact

The model's preamble stays in the progress card; it no longer sends its own separate acknowledgment. Blockers, task-changing findings, and answers to status questions still go out mid-turn.

Not fixed here: OpenClaw's own fixed "I'm continuing this work…" message after `sessions_yield`. That is tracked in #160990.

## Evidence

Live Telegram Test Server runs, real `gpt-6-astra`, OpenClaw harness, `visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, progress card with commentary:

| Arm | Runs | Model's own separate acknowledgment |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 3 | 3/3 |
| this change | 3 | 0/3 (preamble shown as a card row) |

- No-card control (streaming off): the model still communicates normally; the final answer arrives.
- Real-progress control (a two-stage task asking for a mid-way update): both stage updates are still sent.
- Focused prompt/message-tool tests pass; prompt snapshots regenerated with `scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts`.

prs.title: fix(plugins): share unchanged captured plugin code across inventories
prs.body:
Refs #160959

## Problem

A Gateway with a large installed plugin blocks its event loop for tens of seconds whenever that plugin is captured. `capturePluginGenerationArtifact` copies the plugin package and its declared dependency tree synchronously. The same **unchanged** plugin is also captured again every time another registry loads it:

- **Startup:** the Gateway registry captures the plugin. The prepared model runtime (`loadAgentRuntimePluginRegistryHandle`, `src/agents/runtime-plugins.ts`) then loads its own registry and captures the same plugin a second time.
- **Every prepared-runtime republish** (for example an `agents.defaults.model` patch, auth/model reloads, #160120-style refresh loops) loads plugins in a **new `PluginCache` inventory** and captures again.

The first revision of this PR (bfacdaa) shared captures per inventory. That fixed nothing in the live Gateway because each republish uses a fresh inventory. This revision shares them process-wide.

## Fix

Captured code for an unchanged installed plugin is shared by every instance that binds it, across inventories.

- **Key:** origin, real root, entry, standalone flag, dev source root and SDK resolution. `expectedSourceDigest` must match. `isSourceUnchanged()` must pass: it checks every captured input's stat identity (dev/ino/mode/size/mtime/ctime) and directory listing, plus every selected native namespace. It does not reread file bytes.
- **Custody:** the capture directory, loader hooks and TypeScript builds are released when the last holder's module disposal runs. A retiring instance's own value views are still revoked (`reloaded or disabled`).
- **Native custody:** every inventory that holds a capture borrows the capture's native admission state (`borrowPluginNativeAdmissions`). Native namespace roots are released only after the last holding inventory retires. This also covers a native namespace admitted lazily after another inventory started sharing the capture.
- **Missing modules:** once a capture observes a module it cannot resolve, it is not reused. Installing that dependency later therefore gets a fresh capture.
- **Recovery binds** (`nativeRecovery`, `recoverySourceMap`) are never shared.

### Behavior change (@steipete, owner decision needed: this relaxes a #144252 invariant)

Removed invariant: **a new inventory implies fresh module identity for unchanged source.** Unchanged installed plugins now share module identity and module results across live instances and inventories, including Gateway and prepared-runtime registries. Bundled plugins already work this way. `register()` still runs per instance with that instance's API. Registered callbacks, runtime-store slots, lifecycle and cleanup stay per instance. Module-scope state in plugin code is shared.

What stays isolated:
- Edited source, a changed native namespace, or a module missing at capture time gets a fresh capture and fresh module evaluation. The old holder keeps its old bytes.
- A retired instance's views are revoked.
- Capture bytes and native roots are not deleted while any holder or holding inventory remains.

Lazy module work runs inside the holder that currently has an active call, or else inside the newest accepting holder. For shared code, a retired instance can no longer be told apart from a live one as the origin of that work. This follows from sharing module identity and is part of the same decision.

`docs/plugins/architecture.md` ("Runtime instance and source lifetime") is updated.

## Evidence

Like-for-like live runs on this Mac: an isolated Gateway (own state dir and port), the **same** synthetic 878 MB plugin (`plugins.load.paths`, 20,403 files, 200 dependency packages), and the same script: startup, 5 forced republishes via `config.patch agents.defaults.model`, `plugins.reload` of the unchanged plugin, then an edit and another reload. Event-loop stalls come from a 50 ms-tick preload that logs gaps over 500 ms.

| | main 4d4d99d | this PR c9325fb |
|---|---|---|
| Startup captures | 2 | **1** |
| Startup event-loop stalls | 51.3 s + 48.3 s | **20.2 s** |
| First `/healthz` answer | 67.6 s | **26.6 s** |
| Republishes 1–5: new captures | 5 (one per republish) | **0** |
| Republishes 1–5: `config.patch` round trip | 39.7–98.5 s | **1.2–2.2 s** |
| Republishes 1–5: max event-loop stall | 37.1–96.0 s each | **0.7 s** |
| Capture dir set across republishes | changes every republish, 2–3 dirs | **constant (1 dir)** |
| Capture disk across republishes | 1.7–2.6 GB | **877 MB constant** |
| `forced retirement` warnings | on every republish | none |
| `plugins.reload`, unchanged source | 2 new captures; stalls 16.5 + 26.9 + 24.9 s | 1 new capture, old released; stalls 11.5 + 17.3 s |
| `plugins.reload` after editing one file | 2 fresh captures (2 dirs, 1.7 GB) | 1 fresh capture; old released after drain (1 dir, 877 MB) |

`plugins.reload` of unchanged source still recaptures once. Reload deliberately disposes the old registration before it activates the replacement (`server-plugin-reload.ts`: drain → dispose → activate), so no holder carries the capture across. The prepared runtime is also marked stale before that drain. This PR does not change that ordering.

Tests:
- `shares one unchanged capture across live instances and recaptures edited source` binds through a fresh inventory each time. It **fails on main 4d4d99d** (different captured file) and passes here. About 80 ms.
- `recaptures unchanged source after a missing dependency is installed` fails if the missing-module reuse block is removed. About 40 ms.
- `keeps lazily admitted native bytes while another inventory holds the shared capture` fails with `ENOENT` on the captured `.so` if the native custody borrow is removed. About 60 ms.
- Three existing tests (`reclaims only the retired … generation's Node cache records`, `shares the native %s host owner across plugin generations and recovered workers`, `keeps declared source package imports and self exports in one emitted graph`) expected fresh module identity for unchanged source. They now edit the source before the next load, which keeps their fresh-generation assertions.
- Focused suites pass: 365 tests across 16 files (plugin module generation incl. interop/sdk/disposal/update/sibling-assets/native-layout, generation artifact incl. admission/ownership/streaming, loader recovery, capture recovery/directory, conditions, provider-discovery capture lifetime, doctor lint plugin captures/native admission, startup source captures, run-main cleanup, prepared catalog worker custody/captures), plus 7 adjacent loader-consumer files (116 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.

Not in this PR: the cost of the **first** capture (about 20–50 s for this plugin, depending on page cache). That work is O(files) and synchronous (`copyFile` + FICLONE, pinned lstat traversal, rehash). It remains a follow-up on #160959.

Also note: the `thinkingDefault` → prepared-runtime refresh → restart seen in #160959 is already fixed on main by #160274 (cb3755a).
