**Superseded by [25f07e880f5d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/25f07e880f5d4e05375d14f07bfb6cc416295aeb) on main; this PR was not merged.** The landed fixture observes the browser’s actual config.changed event before the existing replacement-row assertion and read-failure injection, and releases its observer in finally. It preserves the same row-retention, recovery and agent-switch coverage. The browser event path clears the old catalog before notifying the observer; the subsequent DOM assertion supplies the replacement-row barrier, so this PR’s additional request-ID fence does not establish a remaining uncovered contract.

The landed commit records native controlled reproduction, 20 full-file passes and three cohort runs with an explicitly unrelated failure in one cohort. Those are the landing owner’s recorded results, not a new replay here. Main containment was independently verified; no whole-main recovery is claimed. Our exact-head CI and durable review also passed, but a green superseded branch is not a reason to rebase a duplicate fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the real-Gateway palette test can lose its accepted model row when a late config event overlaps the simulated failed read.

## User Impact

Test-only repair; no user-visible behavior or cache policy change. Config and agent changes still retire old display facts. Existing row-count, failure-retention, recovery, navigation and agent-switch assertions remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

A CLI config write can publish replacement rows before its later config.changed event. Seeing the first row was therefore not enough to start rejecting browser replies: the late event could correctly retire the row while every replenishing read was rejected.

The fixture now waits for that event and a successful native main-agent read issued afterward containing the target model. It retains the existing visible-row assertion before injecting failure. No retries, sleeps, deadline increases or product changes.

Contributor credit: requested by and co-authored with @vincentkoc.

prs.title: fix(ci): recognize recorded mirror generations after inode reuse
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160010

Source-mirror recovery treated a directory inode as a generation ID. If the filesystem reused that inode after disposal, a valid successor was mistaken for the old slot and recovery refused to retire the old disposal record.

Under the existing allocation lock, recovery now validates the recorded generation first. A valid successor preserves its slot, contents and lock while only the exact old disposal record is removed. Same-generation disposal still requires the original identity; unknown replacements retain the existing refusals. Production +7/-9; tests +62/-0.

Validation at `080d21c85a1f6e3ac5fd7ce5d77404e537e2d1cc`: deterministic real-filesystem regression failed all four receipt/lock combinations against the original source and passed with this change. All 13 relevant recovery/replacement tests passed (22.61 s wrapper); scripts typechecking, production typed lint, formatting and whitespace passed. Complete bounded Testbox comparison took 58.64 s. A fresh P0–P2 review found no actionable defect.

The fixture retains and reallocates the actual empty inode; the production allocator generates the new ID and receipt. It also holds a real SQLite slot lock during successor recovery. No production receipt, success response, or filesystem identity is mocked.

prs.title: fix(matrix): bind E2EE readiness to client generations
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119920

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes four Matrix E2EE lifecycle races in the split from #119920:

- readiness probes could outlive terminal sync/generation changes, lose a wake, or hang past timeout;
- Rust crypto could finish initializing after terminal stop and leave its newly assigned backend running;
- QA image timeout cancellation did not reach matrix-js-sdk's active upload;
- shutdown could return at its deadline while IndexedDB persistence later committed a snapshot.

This remains limited to Matrix generation/readiness, upload cancellation, persistence shutdown, and the QA E2EE lifecycle that owns those operations. It does not add scenario configuration, room setup, CLI/gateway, Docker, recording, release, or live evidence changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical owners now enforce the lifecycle:

- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/client-base.ts:381-432` races each async readiness probe against sync/error/abort changes and rechecks captured generation ownership before accepting success.
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/client-base.ts:680-718` re-stops matrix-js-sdk if delayed Rust crypto initialization settles after the OpenClaw generation stopped.
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/client-core.ts:445-457` passes the QA operation's `AbortController` into matrix-js-sdk's upload contract; `extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/matrix/substrate/e2ee-client.ts:491-522` keeps readiness, encryption, upload, and dispatch in one tracked operation. Cancellation can abort an active upload; once message dispatch starts, its send promise remains authoritative and timeout reports unknown completion rather than a false aborted-send result.
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/client-base.ts:577-612` propagates one absolute shutdown deadline and abort signal to persistence; `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/idb-persistence.ts:305-344` checks cancellation again immediately before the snapshot write, preventing a late commit after shutdown returns.

The repair also removes duplicate lifecycle policy: failed shared generations are deleted at the startup producer, QA uses the plugin SDK timeout primitive, and one generation-aware readiness loop owns both startup and encrypted-room readiness.

## Direct Dependency Evidence

Personally inspected installed matrix-js-sdk 41.9.0 source and declarations:

- `matrix-js-sdk/src/sync.ts:80-97,821-855,887-929`: `ERROR` may recover, cached `PREPARED` is marked `fromCache`, live sync emits readiness after processing, and sync persistence occurs before/after those transitions.
- `matrix-js-sdk/src/client.ts:1470-1542,1564-1576`: startup is async; `stopClient()` stops the current crypto backend and is idempotent once client polling is stopped.
- `matrix-js-sdk/src/client.ts:1993-2048`: Rust crypto assigns `cryptoBackend` only after asynchronous import/initialization, so an earlier stop cannot clean the late backend.
- `matrix-js-sdk/src/http-api/interface.ts:192-215`, `src/http-api/index.ts:55-165`, `src/http-api/fetch.ts:257-305`: upload cancellation is owned by `UploadOpts.abortController`, which drives both XHR and fetch cancellation.
- `matrix-js-sdk/lib/client.d.ts:949-958,1160-1176,2763-2769`: declarations confirm async start/init, synchronous stop, and the upload options contract.

## Provenance

- Reviewed head `95bac4d76966d78e92711336c68ab761593db1b7` introduced the readiness wait, generation checks, QA operation cancellation, and shutdown deadline paths where findings 1, 3, and 4 manifested.
- The upload gap combined that head's QA abort signal with the older wrapper from `5402ef192d5`, which did not expose matrix-js-sdk's upload controller.
- Delayed crypto cleanup is the interaction between the async init path from `5402ef192d5`, shared generation retirement from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119570 (`a3419d4a4b4c894b47a9273181735d091f4d502f`), and the new generation checks at `95bac4d`.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep collector spawn requests in submission order
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent `collect` subagent spawn requests in the same swarm group could launch out of submission order. The collector admits children FIFO, so the first-submitted request should reserve and launch first; instead, whichever request finished an earlier async step first won. This surfaced as an intermittent CI failure in `src/gateway/session-utils.queued-collector.test.ts` (shard `agentic-gateway-server-isolated-hosted-19`), hitting two unrelated PRs (#159173, #159185) on the same day with `expected [ <run A> ] to deeply equal [ <run B> ]`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSubagentSpawnRequest` (`src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-request.ts`) awaited the requester session lookup (capturing the requester window so a reset cannot redirect child results) **before** reserving the request's FIFO slot. Under load a later request's lookup could resolve first, so it reserved and launched first. The test was asserting a real ordering guarantee; the product violated it.

The group key (`[requesterAgentId, requesterInternalKey, swarmGroupId]`) is now derived synchronously, and for collector requests the whole resolution, requester capture through FIFO reservation, runs in a per-group `KeyedAsyncQueue` (the same helper ACP and meeting-bot already use in core). Submission order is therefore reservation order within a group. Non-collector requests bypass the queue, other groups stay concurrent, and child preparation and execution remain outside the critical section. The queue isolates rejections and drops a key once its tail settles.

## User Impact

Collected (swarm) subagents launch in the order they were requested, and the recurring `queued-collector` CI failure goes away.

## Evidence

- Deterministic regression (reordered requester lookup) in `session-utils.queued-collector.test.ts`: fails on `main` (1 failed, 33 passed) with the observed run-id mismatch; passes with the fix.
- On Blacksmith Testboxes via Crabbox: the file 30/30 runs (1,020 tests), 173 owner/sibling tests, and three replays of the original CI shard (396 tests each) passed; `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean ("patch is correct", 0.86); queue cleanup and rejection isolation verified against `src/plugin-sdk/keyed-async-queue.ts`.

Production LOC: +196 / −186 (net +10; whitespace-insensitive: +23 / −15 — the body moved into a closure). Tests: +18 / −1.

prs.title: fix: stop heap-profile tests rejecting small live allocations
prs.body:
**Superseded by [b2dfd4e9dc58](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b2dfd4e9dc58c95ad3d87cd161ce5f2f94503e97).** That main change primes the fixture before sampling and preserves the original exact-zero assertion. Its 21-case heap-profile owner suite passed on Node 24.21.0 in 21.39 seconds; native controls returned zero with collection history disabled, 209,718,400 bytes when enabled, and rejected a deliberately retained 1,048,592-byte row. This PR's additional sample-selection predicate is no longer needed for the reported failure.

## What Problem This Solves

The native heap-profile test can fail after its temporary arrays have been collected because it requires every sampled allocation attributed to the workload function to disappear. Scheduled CI reported 65,728 bytes on that frame with collected-object retention disabled, failing the exact-zero assertion.

Fixes #165559.

## User Impact

This corrects an internal CI assertion. Heap profiling behavior, collection flags, defaults, privacy, output bounds, sampling interval, and timeouts remain unchanged. The test still rejects surviving workload-sized allocations with collection disabled and still requires the expected allocation history when collection is enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

V8 attributes allocations to a JavaScript stack and reports weighted sizes. A function's total can include smaller live runtime allocations as well as the arrays intentionally created by the test. The fixture allocates MiB-sized backing stores, so its collected-allocation check now selects those samples by workload node and allocation size. It retains exact zero for the disabled case and the existing greater-than-190-MiB positive control. Total frame bytes remain in the diagnostic output.

The existing asynchronous major-GC boundaries remain intact. No additional GC loop, sleep, warmup, production seam, or tolerance for surviving workload bytes is introduced.

## Evidence

The [original scheduled failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37297696800/job/111722985146) ran Node 24.19.0 at `5b618f2d8cb8`; the affected test, helper, and profile owners are unchanged through this branch's baseline `0be92a681d99`. The earlier asynchronous-GC correction in #160414 is present. The exact residual object's type is unknown, and the intermittent 65,728-byte result was not reproduced in the focused replays.

A bounded Linux Node 24.19.0 / V8 13.6.233.17-node.51 probe measured 200 workload samples of 1,048,592 bytes, totaling 209,718,400 bytes. A deliberately retained row produced one such sample and failed the exact-zero check. Disabling collection retention failed the positive threshold. All eight ordinary disabled captures returned zero. Because [V8's frame total sums nonnegative allocation terms](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.19.0/deps/v8/src/inspector/v8-heap-profiler-agent-impl.cc#L529-L585), the original 65,728-byte total cannot contain one of those MiB backing-store samples. The probe took 1.06 seconds and reported 147,796 KiB maximum RSS.

On the Cloud Mac with Node 24.21.0 and pnpm 12.5.1, the original and candidate owner file each passed all 21 tests. The candidate retained 8 samples / 8,388,736 bytes, returned zero dropped-workload bytes with collection disabled, and returned 209,718,400 bytes with collection enabled. Existing privacy, byte-cap, inspector-listener, overlap, cancellation, and cleanup assertions passed.

`pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-heap-profile.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 6.73 seconds for the candidate, including preparation; the native case took 121 milliseconds. The original took 19.91 seconds with cold worker preparation. These timings do not establish a performance improvement. Independent engineering review has no remaining finding, and the separate P0 autoreview is scoped-clean.

The applicable remote baseline also completed the selected type graph, 209 tests across 15 affected/boundary files, generated-contract and boundary checks, the production high-severity dependency audit, and the trusted-base private-key scan. The affected batch took 83.58 seconds; the type helper took 70.72 seconds. The exact-head [hosted CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37313613241) passed. Its changed-test job took 166 seconds and the boundary job took 176 seconds, including runner setup. On Linux Node 24.19.0, the full heap-profile file passed all 21 cases against the candidate combined with main `2fec39f57319`; Vitest reported 3.92 seconds, and the native case took 224 milliseconds.

Four inherited static failures remain recorded against the older base: unused X/wizard exports (removed on main by [3ce21a465526](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3ce21a465526e038dc328c74afdf66b5b9ee2f0e)), the existing deferred-migration static import component (repaired by [21901766c534](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/21901766c53433f1f269e996055ffc617a1766e7)), and the full-tree unused-file report for the worker benchmark and its worker. The benchmark failure reproduced on the untouched baseline; this patch changes no import, export, entrypoint, or scanner setting. The checks remain enabled, and these failures are qualified separately from the heap change.

Final confidence coverage passed on the same candidate tree with Cloud Mac Node 24.21.0: 20 independent standalone file invocations (420 passing cases), followed by three native replays of the recorded `core-runtime-infra-process-hosted-2` shard. Each replay selected the original 125-file cohort, preserved the logging/process config order and two-worker limit, and passed 1,439 cases; 54 existing platform-specific cases remained skipped. The shard runs took 137.48, 98.22, and 133.16 seconds, with native completion confirming all work joined. This supplements the matching Linux Node 24.19.0 hosted owner proof. Exact-head hosted CI passed, and the completed ClawSweeper review rated the patch Platinum with no code finding.

prs.title: improve(sessions): avoid unrelated store discovery for raw history reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Raw session-history requests discover unrelated agents' stores before entering the history worker, so their preparation cost grows with configured agent topology.

## User Impact

Raw history reads now skip unused auxiliary discovery while retaining selected-database identity, cancellation, restoration, and worker-lifecycle checks. No configuration, schema, or public API change is required.

The measured benefit is topology-dependent: the 64-agent fixture improved substantially; the one-agent and display controls do not establish a general latency or zero-overhead claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing asynchronous source preparer now captures and retains the selected physical database before choosing whether auxiliary discovery is needed. Ten selected-transcript request kinds use that path; the display readers (`rpc`, `http`, and `delta`) retain full discovery and lineage validation. This adapts the original draft to the current asynchronous admission owner instead of dropping its physical-identity fence.

Production changes are +30/-12 lines (net +18), preserving that ownership boundary without a new cache or preparation flow. Tests are +502/-125 (net +377). Release-note context: raw session-history reads avoid discovering unrelated agent stores.

## Evidence

- Baseline mechanism control: all ten selected-only cases fail the new no-discovery assertion; all three display controls pass. Candidate tests cover all 13 request kinds, seeded outputs, actual worker inputs, cancellation/revocation, and file, alias, and missing-parent replacement across awaits.
- Seven focused files passed: 150 tests, with one existing optional measurement test skipped. After the erased optional-signal annotation correction, the prior 54-test lifecycle layout passed again. The new shared-fixture lifecycle order described below awaits fresh CI.
- Canonical core/coreTests checks passed across the recorded runs: core types, all 25 test-type graphs, scoped type-aware lint, format, and required guards. The original failed type check and its passing correction remain distinct; this is not a fabricated single-run check result.
- Measured test cost: the seven-file command took 90.072 s including preparation. Reporter intervals for the changed lifecycle/runtime/source suites were 44.427 s, 0.857 s, and 1.918 s. The prior 54-test lifecycle run reported 41.662 s of test assertions and 62.309 s for the whole command, including startup/teardown. These historical timings do not measure the new shared-fixture layout or isolate its incremental cost.
- CI exposed four broadcast tests that still assumed auxiliary registry discovery. The test-only follow-up replaces that barrier with the real selected-source preparation: 12 cases cover by-id/count publication, zero registry reads, unrelated churn, state/selected-store retirement, physical replacement, and preparation-error propagation. At `95fa3d69`, all 12 cases passed in the [43-file, 860-test Node sibling shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36323915670/job/108633559283) (60.99 s reported), and required CI, owning test types, lint, and guards passed. The earlier production, functional, and benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
- Claw's lifecycle-cost finding is addressed by sharing one real seeded state per cancellation/revocation scenario: 20 full fixture setups become 2, with all ten raw request kinds and every dispatch, settlement, handle-close/reopen, and worker-exit assertion retained. Each iteration clears its observer and joins its close before the next kind. The separate exhaustive 13-kind output/work-count matrix stays unchanged. These real worker/database fences need integration coverage; mocking them would not prove resource settlement. No sub-30-second or causal runtime improvement is claimed before measuring the new order.
- Normal signed-commit hooks, targeted `oxfmt`, independent lifecycle-plan review, and fresh structured delta review passed for the shared-fixture follow-up. Exact-head runtime/type/lint validation of its new sequential execution order is pending CI.

Five alternating baseline/candidate pairs used ten independent Node 24.19.0 Linux processes on a 4-vCPU AMD EPYC Testbox. Each process measured 100 invalidated real `sessions.get` requests and 25 display reads with a small seeded transcript, at 1 and 64 configured agents. Count spies and assertions were outside timing; callback/result capture and existing RPC fixture mocks remained. Full responses matched within each process; cross-process message DTOs matched after normalizing only their validated per-fixture physical-source namespace.

| Fixture | Raw wall change, paired median (range) | Raw process CPU change, paired median (range) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 agent | -2.07% (-15.64% to +10.69%) | -1.79% (-16.14% to +37.25%) |
| 64 agents | -90.54% (-90.95% to -86.14%) | -87.53% (-87.91% to -81.24%) |

At 64 agents, median raw wall time per request was 25.944 ms before and 2.454 ms after. In the separate five-request count prepass, raw inventory/registry calls changed from 5/5 to 0/0 at both sizes; display remained 5/5.

Display controls had paired-median wall/CPU increases of 11.59%/17.09% at 1 agent (about 0.086/0.145 ms per request) and 2.58%/5.01% at 64 agents (about 0.573/1.127 ms per request). Their cause is not established by this finite fixture; display overhead attribution remains a follow-up, not a proven regression or a non-regression claim. Process CPU includes Worker threads and excludes the external broker. Whole-command RSS ranges overlapped, all samples had zero swaps, and no memory or reader-fairness improvement is claimed.

The broader distinct-key/coalescing fairness experiment from the earlier review is deferred to the separate history-fairness follow-up. This change does not alter queue admission, worker counts, or coalescing ownership; the existing lifecycle/coalescing coverage passed, and no fairness benefit is claimed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an already-running Full Release Validation parent ends in `orchestration_error` when `main` deletes a workflow path that its pinned tooling still enumerates.

## User Impact

User impact: release operators can retire an unused workflow without corrupting Diagnostic Drain for parents that were already dispatched with an older Tooling SHA. There is no product runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pinned tooling `3dd99d187a21` queries successful runs through the exact default-branch path `full-release-flake-classification.yml`. Removing that path in #163412 changed the expected empty run list into a GitHub API 404 during parent run 36993276463.

This restores only an inert compatibility tombstone at that path. It has no `workflow_dispatch`, token permissions, checkout, artifact upload, or receipt writer; its sole `workflow_call` job exits with an error. Historical revisions also cannot issue receipts when selected by ref: the retired job and recorder both required `refs/heads/main` and the exact main workflow SHA, while `main` now resolves this tombstone.

The release-CI lifecycle contract now requires this tombstone pattern until no older pinned parent remains active or rerunnable, and requires verifying that historical non-default refs cannot invoke the retired writer.

## Evidence

- [Failed Diagnostic Drain](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36993276463) records the exact 404 and sealed `orchestration_error` at Tooling SHA `3dd99d187a2120f4032c0766159800d5c8e3df8e`.

prs.title: fix(models): Gateway start acquires provider catalogs with no catalog reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Gateway start spins up the prepared model-catalog worker and a full plugin generation to discover provider catalogs, even when no one ever opens a model list. That raised headless Gateway memory by roughly 260–350 MB and failed the Kova release performance gate (gateway-tree peak RSS over 1,200 MB).

## User Impact

Headless and CLI-only Gateways no longer pay for provider-catalog discovery at startup. Account models still appear after sign-in and credential changes, as #145190 intended. After a Gateway restart, discovery starts in the background on the first catalog read: opening Models, connecting the Control UI or a native app, or a channel model picker. Starter models are served immediately in the meantime.

UI-connected Gateways do not get a reduction from this PR. The same acquisition cost is deferred to the first connect-time catalog read (numbers below). The real reduction for them is the follow-up: a catalog-only worker load instead of a full plugin-generation isolate.

## Why This Change Was Made

#145190 (thanks @obviyus for the account-discovery work) added `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs` to every configured-runtime publication commit. The acquired provider inventory lives only in process memory, so at startup every credentialed provider counts as changed. Each start therefore acquired catalogs in the retained catalog worker.

This PR:
- Removes the acquisition from the publication commit. It stays for a credential change adopted by that commit, so sign-in during a config replacement still discovers.
- Moves startup discovery to the existing non-blocking catalog read hook (`refreshExpiredModelCatalog`). The first read of each configured owner runs one latched `changedOnly` acquisition, which returns without touching the worker when nothing changed, then falls through to expiry renewal.
- The first-read acquisition waits for the Gateway's existing post-ready work barrier. Providers are marked pending immediately, and retirement cancels the wait. A Control UI that connects right after startup therefore does not stack catalog discovery on top of startup allocations. The barrier clears itself once settled and on runtime close.
- Keeps standalone CLI reads passive. A failed initial discovery waits for Retry/Refresh instead of retrying on every read.

Production LOC is net −6 (+96/−102). Nearby cleanup in the same prepared-model runtime files funds the fix: duplicate provider predicates, a redundant replace-mode branch, redundant credential-presence checks, and a single-use store factory.

Follow-ups:
- Catalog-only worker load: #160501.
- Persisting accepted provider inventory, so restarts with unchanged credentials skip discovery entirely. This is a storage change that needs its own review.

## Evidence

- Bisect (Kova mock-provider, same harness): Gateway RSS was 664 MB at #145190's parent 58253d15 and 1,019 MB at 3d7d2116 (+355 MB). Neighbors confirm: 21d76606 671, 69cbf9f8 680, 6526b90c 1,016.
- Strict release-profile Kova, repeat 3, main vs main minus the publication-commit acquisition:

  | Lane | main | without the acquisition |
  |---|---|---|
  | fresh-install | 1,005 MB | 879 MB |
  | onboarded | 1,062 MB | 846 MB |
  | bundled-plugin-startup | 1,083 MB | 802 MB |
  | gateway-performance | 1,146 MB | 878 MB |

  The gateway-tree >1,200 MB failures are gone. Cold agent turn is unchanged (6.5 vs 6.9 s).
- Local isolated Gateway, 14 bundled plugins, synthetic credentials, sampled every 500 ms:
  - Headless, ready + 120 s: peak 896 → 767 MiB, steady 715 → 585 MiB.
  - Connected client reading `models.list` right after ready, measured after discovery settled + 60 s (medians of 3 runs; shared-host run-to-run spread is about ±30 MiB):

    | Build | Peak MiB | Steady MiB |
    |---|---:|---:|
    | main | 924.7 | 885.9 |
    | first-read acquisition without the post-ready wait | 956.4 | 871.3 |
    | first-read acquisition waiting for post-ready work, prototype | 927.8 | 856.9 |
    | this PR (simplified barrier) | 938.1 | 906.6 |

    UI-connected Gateways stay at main's level within noise. The acquisition cost is deferred to the first catalog read, not reduced.
- Tests: 91 tests across 15 files pass, with new regressions for:
  - no acquisition at publication;
  - one latched first-read acquisition;
  - adopted-auth overlap;
  - a native-only empty inventory;
  - partial inventory retained across a reload.

  Negative controls fail on the old code. Typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Kova dispatch on this PR head: pending (linked in a comment when complete).
- Codex autoreview (gpt-6-astra, P0–P2) on the rebased branch: scoped-clean.

prs.title: fix(cli): route daemon entry lazy forwarders through named loaders
prs.body:
Fixes red main.

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

`check-export-name-collisions` (CI `check-source-contracts`, `pnpm lint:tmp:export-name-collisions`) fails on clean `main`. The stable daemon CLI entry defines lazy wrappers with the same names as their owners, written in a form the guard does not recognize as a lazy facade. This keeps the lazy wrappers and their exported names, and moves each `import()` into a named zero-argument loader. The guard recognizes that shape as forwarding, not a second implementation.

### Root Cause

- `5de949fc462` ("perf(cli): defer service imports from the update recovery entry") replaced the `src/cli/daemon-cli.ts` re-exports with `export async function` wrappers. Each wrapper runs `const runtime = await import("./daemon-cli/…js"); return runtime.<sameName>(…)`. The goal is to keep installed update drivers from loading the service/plugin graph before the ledger settles.
- `scripts/check-export-name-collisions.mts` does not count same-name forwarders as definitions (`isForwardingOnlyFunction`), but only when the module object comes from an **awaited zero-argument call** (`isAwaitedZeroArgumentCall`). `await import("x")` passes one argument, so all nine wrappers counted as definitions and collided with their owners.
- Failing job: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36449947535/job/109022525871. Reproduced locally on clean `origin/main` (`202336dcd5f`):

```
- {"name":"assertForegroundUpdateOrigin","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts"]}
- {"name":"isManagedUpdateRequesterOwner","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle-context.ts"]}
- {"name":"runDaemonInstall","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/install.ts"]}
- {"name":"runDaemonRestart","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts"]}
- {"name":"runDaemonStart","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts"]}
- {"name":"runDaemonStatus","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/status.ts"]}
- {"name":"runDaemonStop","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts"]}
- {"name":"runDaemonUninstall","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts"]}
- {"name":"waitForGatewayUpdateRecovery","files":["src/cli/daemon-cli.ts","src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle-context.ts"]}
Give each behavior one exported spelling.
[check-export-name-collisions] FAILED (exit 1)
```

### Exact change

`src/cli/daemon-cli.ts` only. It adds five module-local loaders (`loadInstallRuntime`, `loadLifecycleRuntime`, `loadStatusRuntime`, `loadLifecycleContextRuntime`, `loadManagedServiceHandoffRuntime`), each `() => import("…")`. The nine wrappers now call `await loadXRuntime()` instead of `await import("…")`.

### Scope boundary

- The exported names, signatures, and laziness stay the same. Installed update drivers import these names from this entry, so they stay.
- Each call still runs a plain dynamic `import()` with no extra caching layer. It does not use `createLazyRuntimeMethod`, which would cache rejected imports and change recovery behavior after a runtime swap.
- No guard allowlist or baseline change. No change to the guard script.

## Verification

- `pnpm lint:tmp:export-name-collisions` → `export name collision guard passed.` (failed with the list above before the change)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` → exit 0
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/daemon-cli.update-run.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-foreground.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-triage.test.ts` → 2 shards passed (these tests import the touched entry)
- `oxlint src/cli/daemon-cli.ts`, `oxfmt`, `git diff --check` → clean

### Real behavior proof

The behavior being fixed is the CI guard failure. The same command CI runs (`pnpm run lint:tmp:export-name-collisions`) failed on clean `main` and passes on this head. Runtime behavior is unchanged: each wrapper still loads the same module lazily when called.

The obsolete implementation, landing and runner work is retired. The old-fixture comparison and the former #158299 qualification wait are **not conditions for closing this superseded PR**. No current duplicate-copy regression has been established, and no new runtime pass, CI pass, installed-update acceptance or native no-loss result is claimed. Historical failed CI and review findings remain historical evidence, not waived checks or reasons to revive the retired startup path.

The still-relevant acceptance criterion transfers to the existing original recovery/startup and installed-update outcomes, including independently owned #144005/#145169 work: preserve current startup and explicit Doctor freshness, ownership, integrity and no-loss guarantees while avoiding a redundant full-family copy of an unchanged eligible agent family within one owning invocation. Required rereads after lease acquisition, recovery, repair or state-root relocation must remain fresh; deliberate readiness rereads are not themselves duplicate-copy defects. Criterion-specific acceptance or disposition by those existing owners remains pending, separate from this PR closure. Genuine current-original native and no-loss checks remain required in their owning outcomes.

Public head is unchanged at `1c9303cea9e9014034b073aa86aebbeee9b96df8`. Closure is without merge, branch deletion or linked-issue closure. Compact unpublished source and original contributor attribution remain retained until criterion-specific custody is accepted or explicitly disposed of. The obsolete task environments have been removed. No implementation, tests, installs or live-service changes are part of this closeout.

The material below is preserved historical candidate evidence and attribution; this section supersedes its older open-disposition and qualification statements. Closing this PR does not close #149984 or complete the independently owned original recovery outcomes.
<!-- atomic-update-original-tracking:end -->

---

Related: #149984. Current-main disposition remains open.

## Historical candidate problem

Before the upstream startup cutover, Gateway startup could copy unchanged agent databases again when Doctor repeated admission under its migration lease. The following describes the original candidate and its historical evidence, not current-main behavior.

## Intended impact of the original candidate

Unchanged, positively owned, sidecarless WAL agent databases avoid the second Doctor copy. Changed sources and ownership, config, registry, checkpoint and readiness decisions still receive fresh inspection. No operator action, schema/configuration change, or relaxed integrity policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry complete schema facts within one Doctor invocation, publish only after admission and snapshot cleanup succeed, and discard them after refresh, failure, cancellation or termination. Other startup reuse already landed in #151805 and #153130 is not reimplemented.

The original seven-file commit was stacked on #144005 at immutable `4146d06f8a3208222189d14af897325d4daa4fb3`; its separately published shared-preflight cleanup fix is a prerequisite, not part of this diff. Preserve that branch's existing authorship and @steipete's startup work. Thanks to @vyctorbrzezowski for the report.

## Evidence

On the exact public composition (immutable base plus only seven paths):

- All **48 tests passed**: 30 Doctor regressions (115.8 s wall), plus 18 affected startup-prepared, Doctor startup/database and shared-cleanup tests (59.4 s wall). Independent API-key production/whole-test review is clean; both initial P2 findings are resolved.
- Focused types, lint, formatting and whitespace pass (two existing max-lines warnings, unsuppressed).
- The complete native Doctor file costs **115.8 s command wall / 108.3 s Vitest duration**, below the approximately120 s job budget. Real worker/SQLite coverage is needed for WAL-only writes, symlink/source replacement, actual migration-lease admission, cleanup ordering and child-process settlement; pure fact-container tests cannot prove those boundaries. Existing worker scopes reuse native imports without sharing case state. CI timing will be recorded once available.
- Independent review found a compiled-helper resolver mismatch and unnecessary native imports in the original tests. The revised preload redirects and verifies the actual emitted helper graph before execution; all30 distinct regressions remain, with no weaker assertions or larger budgets. The initial interrupted run and failed-closed first repair are not claimed as passing.

Commands: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.facts.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`; affected startup-prepared, Doctor startup/database and schema-cleanup suites run with an explicitly verified task-private handoff resolver. No live service or handoff store is used.

The same five production postimages were previously exercised in a supported isolated Gateway run: two initial agent copies, zero lease-refresh copies, 1,310,720 bytes avoided, two fresh readiness inspections, HTTP 200, all observed processes exited and staging empty. That composed fixture retained a CPU-degraded readiness flag, and background verification did not finish before teardown. This is supporting component evidence, not a claim of public-head Gateway, latency, installed-update or native no-loss proof.

Whole-file audit covers every test/preload line, fixtures, native helper resolver readbacks, process joins and teardown. No skips, weakened assertions, retry/timeout increases or removed regressions. prs.body:
## Summary

Repair the session and SQLite ownership boundaries used by **OpenClaw Code Mode** continuation and ordinary admitted input persistence. Retained execution must keep the original authority, commit at most once, and refuse stale or foreign ownership without changing durable rows. This is correctness work, not a Code Mode efficiency or Beta claim.

Current signed head: `8837ca59748e195b0517b791c576924a089d9f3b`; tree: `ec53c8d3ccf154183088fdbd53df59c5a3dbb7e2`. Its ancestry preserves merge `d272c07aedfba39cf7cea56f3a938741a8cbe0a7`, frozen main `ab1b93295ad0f0c093563585bbc76f2e6ce39686`, and prior candidate `9b8401c7cb4f4e6b5984f349798c6e8f302b0af5`. This is not a claim to track later moving main. The PR remains draft; protected build/check/selected-test proof, attached CI and exact-head review are pending.

## Root Cause And Canonical Repair

Asynchronous preparation, native worker execution, and synchronous SDK publication must share one captured database/session owner. Reconstructing authority after an await, treating a received result as joined cleanup, or publishing against a changed transcript identity can admit stale work, duplicate a durable result, or release custody too early.

- Bind ordinary and nested workers to canonical maintenance/schema authority, including the original command assertion at request and commit boundaries. Authority/protocol failures fence successful wire results; failed cleanup retains UNKNOWN custody.
- Share the canonical transaction journal, transcript snapshot and SessionManager view owners. Preserve committed identity, rollback ordering, synchronous SDK coexistence and one-shot publication.
- Acquire sharing readers before awaits; carry full database identity, including replacement identity, through worker reads and volatile publication.
- Preserve main's accepted-device, upload/Goal, follow-up completion and lifecycle owners. Await input settlement before releasing execution ownership. Do not restore retired Tasks/TaskFlow or coordinator paths.
- Declare the isolated child-test fixture through a literal `new URL(..., import.meta.url)` dependency, so the trusted test planner selects its runnable parent rather than a `test-support` helper. The strict gate validator is unchanged.
- Use literal source URLs as actual canonical worker-descriptor inputs, including the verifier helper. This closes the same missing-edge class for production workers without importing executable children, adding dead markers or weakening the trusted selector. All 59 registry descriptors and the verifier descriptor remain equal to their prior values.
- Repair three consumers of relocated canonical exports. No compatibility re-export, retry, timeout increase, rule relaxation, schema bump or protocol bump is introduced by these integration repairs.
- Preserve honest module boundaries: a real lazy read-only title operation for worker dispatch, canonical post-COMMIT ACP publication, compiler-entry byte capture rather than treating workers as generator-executed imports, and complete native archive inputs.
- Consolidate shared query/transaction ownership, preserve the first authoritative rollback failure, and join cleanup without losing independent failures or UNKNOWN custody. Test fixtures retain actual scheduler, authority, memory-scope and lease-identity contracts.
- Extract the complete retained chat work lifetime owner. Private issuance, captured admission/controller/generation, reference counts and joined release remain unchanged; consumers no longer load unrelated Goal/session lookup policy. The original runtime cycle guard reports zero SCCs.

The projection-file extraction first adapted from [PR 161124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161124) is already in the frozen main integration; its canonical implementation and contributor credit are retained.

## Current Evidence

| Proof | Exact source | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |

Failures span three maintainer fixture files byte-identical to frozen `ab1`; the remaining unit-src run was canceled through the native supervisor and joined. No full-suite pass. |

The protected publisher must evaluate its exact plan before owner/config/capacity/budget admission. Coverage is selected tests plus attached CI, **not full `pnpm test` equivalence**. |

prs.title: ci: bound serial test critical paths
prs.body:
## Summary

- supersede closed PR #150746 with a runner-neutral replacement
- cap changed-extension fallback bundles at four serial config groups, independent of runner backend and timing estimates
- split current macOS Swift validation into independent `kit-tests` and `app-tests` phases
- keep historical targets on the existing single `tests` phase and preserve one lint/cache owner
- skip Node/Apple-asset setup and the macOS app build cache in the package-only kit phase

## Why

PR #150729 exposed two unrelated serial critical paths:

- `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-8` ran 11 independent extension config groups serially. Its 240-second estimate became 19m58s of test execution.
- `macos-swift (tests)` ran the Talk-trait build, OpenClawKit tests, Swabble tests, and app tests serially. Those test steps accumulated 16m+ after setup, producing a 22-minute job.

The extension planner still emits 41 fallback jobs after the group cap, so this bounds stale-timing damage without increasing the matrix. The Swift split follows package ownership: kit/trait/Swabble work no longer waits on the app test suite, and the kit phase avoids app-only setup.

The prior revision's Blacksmith-only named-owner singleton rule has been removed entirely. PR #150742 was separate stale-workflow evidence: its branch predated #150137 and still demoted planner-requested 32-vCPU jobs to 16-vCPU, forcing the runtime to serialize their groups. Current `main` already removed that demotion.

## Expected critical path

- extension fallback: at most 4 serial config groups per bundle instead of 11
- macOS Swift: approximately 13–14 minutes for `app-tests` and 9–10 minutes for `kit-tests`, instead of 22 minutes serially

## Validation

- planner suites: 297 passed
- focused post-rebase extension fallback regression: 1 passed
- focused post-rebase macOS workflow contracts: 15 passed
- `check:changed`: all gates through script typechecking passed; test-root typechecking is currently blocked by existing ACpx errors reproduced unchanged on `origin/main`

prs.title: fix(update): npm-global updates reject their activation receipt
prs.body:
Related: #164528

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: npm-global updates abort at `package-swap` after retained-runtime construction hard-links the updater's completed activation receipt.

## User Impact

User impact: once a release containing this backport is installed, later `openclaw update` runs no longer reject the updater's own `operation.sqlite` receipt as a foreign hard link. Hosts already running 2026.9.7 or 2026.9.8 still need the documented one-time manual package-manager hop because those shipped updater drivers fail before they can activate the fixed candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained runtime can adopt the enclosing global `node_modules` owner when OpenClaw resolves a hoisted dependency. The shipped 2026.9.7/2026.9.8 inventory then treated `.openclaw.package-activation-*.control/operation.sqlite` as runtime code and hard-linked it, raising `nlink` from 1 to 2. The package-activation integrity owner correctly rejected that mutation.

This release backport preserves the strict integrity check. It excludes exact activation-control directories from retained-runtime inventory and rejects explicit runtime links into recovery state. The production repair is the focused activation-control portion already merged to `main` in #160663; this PR adds a true npm-global regression that forces hoisted-owner adoption and failed on the release branch before the repair.

Production delta: +39/-4 lines. The positive delta establishes the recovery-authority boundary already canonical on `main`; weakening the link-count guard, copying mutable control state, or changing global dependency-owner discovery would be broader or unsafe. Test delta: +38/-5 lines.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-retained-runtime.test.ts` failed with `operation.sqlite` `nlink=2` (`1 failed, 27 passed`).
- Fixed retained-runtime boundary: the same command passed (`28/28`).

- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` passed all shards.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): avoid usage polling with setup tokens
prs.body:
Replaces #155805 (maintainer edits disabled); credit @saariuslystoned and @RamiNoodle733. Their original commits are preserved without rewriting.

## Follow-up to #146726

Closes #143419 and carries the compatibility repair from #146726 onto a branch writable by this account.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Anthropic setup-token profiles poll `/api/oauth/usage`, which those tokens cannot authorize, and then surface a misleading quota error.

## User Impact

User impact: a stored Anthropic setup-token profile no longer makes the unsupported OAuth usage request. If a claude.ai web session is configured, quota loads from that fallback; if that fallback fails, status shows `Claude web usage unavailable`. Existing OAuth and API-key profiles keep their previous usage paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classification uses the stored auth-profile type. Anthropic setup-token onboarding persists `type: "token"`; OAuth login persists `type: "oauth"` even when the access token uses the `sk-ant-oat01-` shape; API keys persist `type: "api_key"`. Token prefix alone must not suppress usage.

## Compatibility decision

**Maintainer decision — 2026-09-23:** Ayaan accepted this compatibility tradeoff: “go for it, claude's setup-token is inference only”. Stored Anthropic `type: "token"` profiles skip OAuth usage polling, including manually pasted bearer credentials that might otherwise have usage scope.

Evidence that this is the stored-profile contract, not an over-broad skip:

- Anthropic's only writers of `type: "token"` are setup-token auth and `models auth paste-token`, both validated by `validateAnthropicSetupToken`.
- OAuth login writes `type: "oauth"`. API-key auth writes `type: "api_key"`.
- Profile order already prefers OAuth (`typeScore` 0) over token (1) over API key (2).
- A static/env `sk-ant-oat01-` credential with no stored token profile still uses the OAuth usage path.
- Runtime proof did not find a working stored OAuth or API-key profile that loses quota access under this classification.

No code change in this follow-up. If later evidence shows a supported Anthropic writer storing a working OAuth usage token as `type: "token"`, narrow then.

## Evidence

Exact head: `c119d0e89f4673d1750cdccd5000b5bd6b5bfba8`

Isolated disposable store only. Temporary `HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, loopback HTTP fixtures, synthetic sentinels. No live user Gateway, no inference/chat, no real provider request.

After-fix request counters and usage snapshots from the PR-head Anthropic usage owner plus official auth-profile upsert:

| Case | OAuth `/api/oauth/usage` | Other requests | Resulting snapshot |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Fresh setup-token profile (`type: "token"`) | 0 | none | auth `{ handled: true }`, provider omitted |
| Existing stored `type: "token"` profile | 0 | none | same skip |
| Configured claude.ai web-session success | 0 | `claude.ai` orgs=1, usage=1 | `5h` window at 17% |
| Web-session fallback failure | 0 | `claude.ai` orgs=1 | `error: "Claude web usage unavailable"` |
| Existing stored API-key profile | 0 | none | `{ handled: true }` (unchanged; not setup-token) |
| Static oat01 credential, no stored token profile | 1 | none | `5h` window at 23% |

prs.title: fix(telegram): unblock model switches during active turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram model selections can wait behind an active turn or pending inbound work instead of acknowledging promptly.

## User Impact

User impact: authorized standalone `/model` selections and configured model shortcuts can acknowledge while another turn is active, without cancelling or replaying that turn. Mixed task text, media-bearing directives, unauthorized commands, and plugin/skill command collisions keep ordinary ordering.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram transport now classifies standalone model selections before both durable and live lane scheduling, using the current runtime configuration. Literal selections and unambiguous configured aliases use a dedicated model lane; aliases owned by plugins or session skills stay on the ordinary chat/topic lane. Restart replay is deliberately conservative because command ownership can change while a row is queued, and only authorized collisions may drain pending fragments across senders.

Core active-session admission reuses the same standalone model parser, while retaining ordinary admission and foreground delivery fencing for media, mixed prose, unauthorized commands, and executable command owners.

## Evidence

- Real grammY handler coverage holds an ordinary turn while literal/native model selection and configured shortcuts dispatch, with cross-topic `/stop` still reachable.
- Cross-sender regression coverage proves a skill-owned alias stays behind pending fragments; an unauthorized alias cannot flush another sender's fragment.
- Durable transport coverage proves a freshly verified alias keeps its model lane from admission through claim and real grammY dispatch while ordinary work is held; restart recovery remains conservative and stale model lanes demote safely.
- Media regressions keep captioned model directives behind buffered text in both Telegram scheduling and core active-run admission.
- Foreground-delivery coverage proves an owner-free alias releases its provisional fence after collision resolution while executable owners retain ordinary ordering.
- The public channel-runtime reference documents the optional worker-backed session reader's inputs, missing-entry and error behavior, and conservative older-host fallback.
- Focused behavior proof: 412 distinct passing cases across command classification/admission, foreground delivery, grammY concurrency, bot construction, sequential keys, durable ingress, ingress-factory handoff, and the real durable monitor → grammY path.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passed, including formatting, line caps, Plugin SDK surface/boundaries, core and extension typechecks, lint, dead exports, and import cycles.
- `pnpm build`: passed in 4m 21.9s. The unrelated Control UI startup gzip diagnostic remains (370960 B vs 370876 B); this PR changes no UI files.
- P3 autoreview: scoped-clean after resolving all verified findings. No hostile behavior was identified in the reviewed changes.

Test discipline receipts:

- Test audit: every changed test protects a distinct observable boundary; no test-only production seam or near-duplicate was retained. Fragment ordering, fresh admission-to-claim scheduling, restart replay, absent-capability fallback, collision admission, and delivery-fence regressions were demonstrated failing at their owner boundaries and passing after repair.
- Deslop: final diff reviewed for narration, speculative guards, type laundering, duplicate helpers, and style drift; no actionable cleanup remained.
- Flake triage: one unrelated stale-forwarded-claim timing assertion missed its bound after back-to-back E2E builds; the unchanged full 12-case file passed on the diagnostic rerun, and no assertion or timeout was weakened. Deterministic fixture, type, deprecated-import, and dead-export failures were repaired at their owning boundaries.
- Measured costs: the prior 388-case grouped behavior run completed in 110.91s; foreground delivery added 10 distinct cases in the 34-case delivery/admission shard; the final changed Telegram shards passed 50 cases in 25.36s and the 12-case durable E2E file in 26.56s. New timer-sensitive tests use observed barriers rather than sleeps or polling. Exact-head CI passed in 22m 34s wall time across the initial run and one failed-job retry; the unrelated Crabbox macOS signing-fixture shard passed on retry in 4m 35s.

### Known limitation

No production Telegram Test Server or end-to-end provider switch was run. User-visible behavior is verified through the real grammY middleware, core dispatch, and durable SQLite ingress boundaries with controlled held work.

prs.title: fix(agents): require human approval for actual permission changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Full Access delegated setup can change the rules governing agents and Gateway clients without an explicit human decision. At the same time, a path-only approval floor unnecessarily interrupts harmless edits merely because they sit beside permission settings.

Split out of #158120 so the setup-usability changes and this approval boundary can be reviewed independently. This refinement keeps the user in control without treating every nearby config write as self-escalation.

## User Impact

Full Access applies ordinary delegated changes automatically. Approval depends on the actual validated before/after authority change, not just the config path:

- **Automatic:** writing the same policy value; replacing a parent while preserving policy; changing operational exec timeouts, background/cleanup timing, highlighting, or notifications; unrelated model, memory/search, logging, and outgoing credential edits.
- **Human decision:** actual tool/exec, sandbox/filesystem, channel conversation/sender admission and tool policy, owner/sender allowlist, approval, security, Workshop approval, or Gateway authorization changes (including browser origins, Host-header fallback and embed trust). This includes tightening and removals that change inherited policy, not only expansion. Inbound Gateway credentials and their configured reference dependencies affect who can authenticate and remain protected.
- **Invalid input:** normal config validation errors, without creating an unnecessary approval request.

The existing approval card or `/approve` flow remains available. An authorized human can approve the less restrictive choice and it is applied; this is not a blanket refusal. Restricted sessions retain their existing approval behavior. The existing authorized-human contract is intentional: owners may designate channel approvers, including nonowners, and authorized approval clients retain their scoped/device-bound access. This introduces neither an owner-only restriction nor a broader reviewer set.

No new config option, config schema, or wire-protocol change. The boundary concerns delegated config operations; it is not a sandbox for an otherwise unrestricted host process.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical config-set runner now exposes a host-only admission callback over validated before/after values. Proposal inspection uses that same parser, roster mapping, environment/topology preparation, and validator without committing a write. The permission comparison resolves known exec inheritance and sandbox/filesystem defaults while preserving meaningful explicit policy layers. Unresolved host exec defaults are not assumed to mean Full Access; this is not a universal privilege-ranking algorithm.

An automatically admitted operation carries the comparison into the actual write snapshot as well. A concurrent policy tightening cannot turn an earlier no-op decision into automatic restoration of old authority. Existing snapshot-conflict, live-run, cancellation, and human-approval checks remain in place.

Contributor: @obviyus. Follow-up commits preserve the verified co-author credits.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @obviyus](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/2c767100-72fb-4796-a84a-1ef6b8013323)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/subagent/5064dc14-ace4-4821-b29a-5ef3421b2c14)

The original discussion session also contains the follow-up implementation and verification.

## Evidence

### Follow-up candidate `9f8790c53c6b78bf4afb513ed9f22215ed0495d4`

The revision-3 review accepted the real reviewer-to-writer proof, but identified missing sender-admission and embed-trust settings. This follow-up repairs those comparisons rather than adding a blanket channel/config approval rule:

- Channel policies and account overrides, explicit empty allowlists, conversation membership, supported user/role/bot admission, and canonical nested DM/group-DM settings are included. The comparison preserves the actual wildcard inheritance difference between Slack, Telegram, Discord and Matrix; ordinary prompt edits stay automatic when they preserve authority.
- Browser embed sandbox/external-URL trust comes from the canonical UI bootstrap resolver. Explicit safe defaults, model-routing metadata and token-only setup remain automatic.
- A real human approval still applies the requested trusted-embed or sender-allowlist change. No owner-only restriction, new credential approval, permission default change or new configuration flag was added.

The original omission was reproduced with ten failing real config-evaluation cases. Additional review findings were checked against actual owners and repaired with regression cases, including Matrix's admitted conflicting legacy/canonical fields and its shipped room alias. An unsupported Telegram `topics.*.tools` hypothesis was rejected by the strict schema and the real evaluator; no unsupported policy surface was invented.

Final frozen-candidate verification: **160 tests passed in 89.43s wrapper wall time** across policy comparison (32), real canonical config evaluation/writing (69), and registered Gateway approval integration (59). The Gateway file took 67.90s. Core production and affected services/Gateway-method test type graphs passed, as did changed-file lint, formatting, assertion/line-cap/max-lines ratchets, runtime cycles and all 14,620 internal doc links. The completed independent staged-source review found no actionable P0/P1 defect. Commit creation preserved the exact validated tree. Earlier whole-core/extension checks below remain tied to their earlier revision; no fresh full repository suite or live/socket replay is claimed.

The existing Full Access default and unattended wait/expiry behavior are unchanged from the proposal. Maintainer acceptance of that release/upgrade tradeoff remains explicit; this code update does **not** fabricate that decision. The [author's published direction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158120#issuecomment-5835404111) remains trusting owners with keys and a separately reviewed small floor.

### Earlier candidate and authority proof at `8fb5a6ac26821fe501cfc8470a928079239b1ef8`

The comparison now covers validated channel group/direct/channel/room/guild/team tool policies and account overrides, meaningful empty overrides and Telegram direct-entry shadowing, subagent tool restrictions, and effective Control UI allowed origins (including `gateway.publicOrigin` inheritance) plus Host-header fallback. Ordinary prompts/display settings and policy-preserving writes remain automatic. Unsupported Telegram topic `tools` paths are rejected by the strict schema, not invented as a new policy surface.

The final composed-tree run passed **114 tests in 137.92s**: permission comparison 20, canonical config validation 41, and registered Gateway approval integration 53. The Gateway file used 81.78s wall / 73.90s summed test time; its existing fixture is reused, without per-case Gateway process boots. The extension test facade exposes the real Telegram approval capability for the boundary proof.

### Actual reviewer-to-config effects

The fixture uses production `openclaw.chat` and `approval.resolve` handlers, real Telegram authorization/custody resolution, the real approval manager and SQLite decision owner, and the canonical config writer. Inference and client identities are synthetic; this is in-process production-boundary proof, not live Telegram or socket-Gateway proof.

| Case | Durable approval | Final config effect |
|---|---|---|
| Explicitly configured nonowner delegate | Allowed | Requested less restrictive Host-header-origin setting is saved |
| Unconfigured reviewer | Remains pending | Original config bytes unchanged |
| Delegate revoked after custody preparation, before decision consumption | Remains pending | Original config bytes unchanged |
| Revoked requesting run | Cannot apply | Original config bytes unchanged |
| No reachable approver, then cancellation | Settles without approval | Original config bytes unchanged |

A valid consumed approval is distinct from an attempt made after reviewer revocation; this proof does not invent retroactive revocation semantics. Current requester liveness and write-time effect guards remain in force. Existing saved Full Access modes need no schema migration. An unattended protected proposal waits or expires/cancels rather than silently writing or granting itself authority.

### Reviewer-authority disposition

Configured approval delegation is existing documented behavior, not a new privilege grant: `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` defines `operator.approvals` as deliberately granted remote-execution-grade authority and explicitly permits configured channel approvers who are not command owners. `extensions/telegram/src/exec-approvals.ts` resolves explicit approvers before the owner fallback. `approval-channel-custody.ts` and `approval.ts` recheck current actor/account custody and decision authority. The title/docs therefore say **authorized human**, not owner-only. The positive delegate and negative unauthorized/revoked cases prove that boundary without taking authority away from user-configured delegates.

Fresh staged-tree automated review completed; one reported group-wildcard finding was independently disproven against the registered production resolver. Telegram groups resolve through `resolveTelegramGroupToolPolicy` → `resolveScopeToolsPolicy`, which retains wildcard tools for a prompt-only exact entry. Actual resolver execution returned identical `deny: [exec]` policy before/after and `requiresApproval: false`. Telegram direct-entry selection differs and is separately protected. Adding the proposed group restriction would unnecessarily gate an operational edit.

The current-main conflict was resolved by merging pinned `c817021248a9` without rewriting published ancestry. Core production, all 25 core test type graphs, extension production/test types, changed core/extension lint, formatting, docs links/baseline, doctor-contract guards, dead exports, import cycles and remaining selected guards passed. Broader checks found fixture-only type/import/manager-constructor issues and an unbound spy assertion; these were fixed against the real contracts without suppressions or weaker assertions. The Gateway file was replayed after the constructor fix (53 passed, 80.81s wrapper), and the five reviewer cases were replayed after the spy-handle fix (5 passed, 48 deliberately filtered, 21.53s wrapper), with affected type graphs rechecked. Successful earlier stages were retained; failed aggregate commands are not presented as green full-wrapper runs. The only changes after independent semantic review were those fixture-contract corrections. The committed tree was verified equal to the validated staged tree.

### Socket-QA limitation

An isolated QA Gateway started, but its synthetic local QA-bus poll received a non-JSON host-proxy response, and mock-provider calls saw connection resets. Proxy controls were not bypassed; task-owned processes and temporary Gateway state were cleaned up. The expanded socket scenario is present but has **no passing socket-QA receipt**. The production-boundary matrix above is completed substitute evidence; no full repository test run or live channel replay is claimed.

### Original-revision channel evidence

The following Telegram Test Server evidence belongs to the initial `23e0666d1165` revision (Convex-leased userbot, isolated Gateway, QA mock provider, Full Access owner). The live channel scenario has not been rerun for the effect-based refinement.

This remains a draft. Earlier screenshots are historical evidence, not a claim of current-head live-channel execution.

prs.title: fix(ui): mark help and documentation links that leave the app
prs.body:
Closes #150454 ## What Problem This Solves Help and documentation links such as Learn more and Docs looked like internal views even when they opened outside the app. A small arrow identifies selected help destinations. Text-link arrows inherit the link color, including hover, and ordinary text can wrap naturally; only the final word and arrow stay together. ## User Impact Selected help and documentation links visibly identify destinations outside the app while preserving text wrapping, inherited link colors, and integrated-browser behavior. ## Why This Change Was Made One shared label renderer follows the existing navigation owner instead of adding indicators to every external URL or changing link actions. Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/e71a7faa-5bbd-4458-b3c8-ac69bf2fe64f) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/41623014-e36b-4d93-83b4-1cc3cce69e7c) ## September 21 final-review preparation **Still draft and unmerged; no landing or deployment requested.** Current head: `daedb2336469069ab045d2f38323ee48f2955a33`. Production UI is byte-identical to the captured/tested `fb27f9c9414e11e0da31c284b7b9009265c9394e`; the final commit repairs only three browser-test accessible-name expectations. Refreshed with main `03b6338390f16fe6b343508fbf0641ed2b257462` only because four real merge conflicts existed. The refresh preserves the current link-reader escape hatch, lifecycle cleanup, and lazy pairing copy. - Focused routing/shared-component tests: **34 passed**. - Production UI build: **passed**. The complete changed gate passed (native exit 0; 1,247.962 s), including core-test/UI typechecking, dead exports, lint, styles, formatting and source i18n verification. The shallow remote checkout skipped its base-relative environment-variable comparison, so that particular comparison remains a gap. - Startup performance: **passed**, JavaScript **365,269 B / 365,488 B** and CSS **51,111 B / 51,200 B**. The limits and baseline are inherited unchanged from main; this PR does not relax them. CSS remains above the advisory target, with 89 B hard-ceiling headroom. - Independent scoped review: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the substantive diff pass; the inventory-only pass could not assess behavior. - Exact-target product CI: [run 35549715919](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35549715919), dispatched for `fb27f9c9414e11e0da31c284b7b9009265c9394e` because draft-event product jobs skip. **Not green**: manual-dispatch strict generated-locale checking fails on catalog fallback baseline drift (source verification passes); Windows scheduled-task probing timed out at its unchanged 5,000 ms deadline; QA profiles 2/6 and 3/6 failed their subagent completion scenarios at 60 seconds. The Windows/QA owners are unchanged by this UI-only diff. Other failures include iOS tests and Gateway tasks-list performance. The three UI E2E failures caused by the changed accessible names were repaired without weakening exact matching, including the internal MCP-link exclusion; **all 17 tests in those three files and formatter check pass** in [final repair validation 35551441178](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35551441178), with fresh independent P0–P2 review clean. No blind reruns or weakened limits. A complete green CI result for the final head remains unestablished; this is not declared final-review ready. - Bundled real-browser regressions: **3 passed**. [Fresh inspected Before/After mobile screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150528#issuecomment-5754212465) are embedded in the PR comment; both images decode at 780×1688. Structured delivery in the final-review chat is blocked because this session exposes no message attachment tool. The current proof set published here is one mobile/light pair (2 images). Desktop captures still showed a loading sidebar and were rejected for final delivery; broader settled desktop/dark evidence remains incomplete. Historical screenshots and metrics that follow describe the older `ab9996f54e60dae71f13c3828840f6001f54b2fe` head, not this refreshed candidate. Two sampled historical GitHub image URLs returned HTTP 404 on this review host. ## Decision rule Keep the cue only on selected **text links to external help or documentation**: settings Learn more, Apps Docs, Help menus, Pairing help and a few contextual help links. The audit retains **56 items** and excludes **86** from the original 142-item inventory. Product navigation, verb-led action buttons, GitHub cards/chips, visible URLs, brand pills and logos, author handles, About, system/error content and chat/Markdown receive no added marker. Within Apps cards, only the selected Docs or Setup guide link receives the cue; the card, platform brand and adjacent actions do not. A Help menu label such as Get help or View changelog identifies a help destination; Download and Create PR execute actions. Context decides, rather than the presence of an external URL alone. The approved Help submenu treatment also includes Discord community for consistency: its text names Discord, but its leading icon is a generic community icon, not the Discord logo. Text-link arrows are small and trailing, use currentColor, and stay with the final word without turning the entire label into an unbreakable box. Header cues use the existing space after the prose so adding the arrow preserves the original text lines. Only the Help submenu variant is muted and right-aligned. Apps documentation links use narrower horizontal padding to keep Setup guide alongside the store action without changing its parent layout. Pairing help and plugin Documentation already had external indicators at the merge-base; this change normalizes those existing indicators rather than introducing their first cue. Help menus align them in the right column. One shared label renderer supplies the cue and one translated new-tab announcement; the existing navigation owner suppresses it when the destination opens in the integrated browser. Existing destinations, actions and functional icons are preserved. ## Risk and coverage - All 142 original items were inspected individually. The tables below group the 56 retained help/documentation links by surface and state the exclusion rule for each removed group. - **Fresh KEEP proof (56 items, 224 pairs):** Before is merge-base [`c5cff2f122e2c4a02a844f6b111d7643865273e8`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c5cff2f122e2c4a02a844f6b111d7643865273e8); After is the committed repair [`ab9996f54e60dae71f13c3828840f6001f54b2fe`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ab9996f54e60dae71f13c3828840f6001f54b2fe). All four cells were captured for each retained help link in this regression round. - **Measured layout and color:** the first and last label words retain their merge-base y in all 224 comparisons, both normal and hover. The 34 measured header/help cases (136 cells) retain preceding prose and line counts; first-word x is identical and final-word x differs by at most 1/64 px from text shaping. Text-link SVG colors match their links. The eight Help-menu items intentionally keep muted, right-column cues. - **Excluded items:** the Removed section lists all 86 exclusions and their reasons. Their original destinations and actions are preserved. - Both sides use the actual Control UI built by its Vite source server with the same synthetic Gateway fixtures, Chromium channel `chromium`, DPR 2, product fonts, `--font-render-hinting=none` and `--force-color-profile=srgb`. The fresh evidence has **224 pairs**, light/dark at **1440×1000** and **390×844**, with **376 PNGs** covered by visual inspection. Byte-identical recaptures reuse the original inspection only after SHA-256 verification. The visible tables show desktop/light pairs; click any screenshot to open its full-size image. - Native-host fixtures exercise WebUI presentation, not native apps. Dreaming's existing decorative mascot can vary between loads. Existing cropped fixtures retain the same framing on both sides. - Coverage includes retained help links, excluded actions/content, one accessible announcement, internal links, integrated-browser routing, menu geometry and copied message text. Current performance and review results are recorded below. ## Evidence Validation completed on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m2qwgjzpxmmt61d6p9kt66kx`, [workflow 35234224835](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35234224835). The final native changed gate, build, i18n verification, and browser regressions passed. The standalone startup performance check remains red. | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Focused shared-component and routing tests | 34 passed | | Full Control UI suite | 1,249 files; 21,545 passed; 4 existing skips | | Final browser regressions | 3 passed in development mode and 3 passed against the bundled app | | Final changed gate | Exit 0; types, declarations, dead exports, lint, Stylelint, formatting, and other selected guards passed | | Final build | Exit 0 | | Final i18n verification | Passed within the native changed gate | | Fresh scoped review | No actionable P0–P3 findings | | Standalone startup performance | Exit 1; JavaScript exceeds the unchanged absolute ceiling | The browser tests cover both words of “Learn more” against an undecorated prose baseline across narrow widths, inherited arrow color including hover, the mobile permissions link, neutral Help menu alignment, and the Chrome Web Store / Setup guide row. The original `4081245` failed all three regression cases: text moved to another line and arrow color differed from link text. Full-suite and focused results were retained from the unchanged shared-helper snapshot; the final CSS, Apps row, and strengthened assertions were revalidated through the browser tests and complete changed gate. | Run | Native result | Reported command duration | Reported total duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Original `4081245` regression | Exit 1; intended layout and color failures | 135.195 s | 137.741 s | | Intermediate shared-helper validation | Focused, full UI, browser, build, and i18n passed; performance failed. Changed gate interrupted after dead-export scans; no terminal native exit | Not reported; local observer exited 143 | Not reported | | Final six-file validation | Changed gate 0; browser 0; build 0; performance 1; overall exit 1 | 745.415 s | 745.719 s | The final command also retained a remote receipt recording the validation payload duration as 670 s. Provider command timing includes source preparation. The native exits above are authoritative; stopping the completed lease can make its hosting workflow appear canceled. Startup JavaScript is **363,018 B gzip**, **430 B above** the unchanged **362,588 B** enforcement ceiling. It is 280 B above the measured base (362,738 B) and 26 B below the previous `4081245` build (363,044 B). Startup CSS uses one request and 48,488 B gzip, below the 51,200 B hard ceiling. No performance baseline, ceiling, or exception was changed. | Diff against `c5cff2f` | Files | Added lines | Removed lines | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Production | 19 | 243 | 49 | | Tests | 5 | 403 | 0 | ## KEEP — help and documentation links | Surface | Items | Decision | |---|---:|---| | Settings headers and contextual help | 34 | Learn more and contextual help are separate text links without a destination cue. | | Help and permission menus | 9 | Help-menu cues stay muted in the right column; Permission-menu Learn more uses an inline currentColor cue. | | Apps documentation | 9 | Docs and Setup guide identify help, while a platform logo does not identify the documentation origin. | | Pairing help | 2 | Normalize the existing external-link icon and new-tab announcement beside internal device navigation. | | Plugin documentation | 1 | Normalize the existing Documentation arrow through the shared help-link renderer. | | Channel dialog help | 1 | Plain Docs in the dialog header can look like an internal view. | ### Settings headers and contextual help Learn more and contextual help are separate text links without a destination cue. | Item / owner | Reason | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | 25. settings/general — Learn more (web)
