prs.title: feat(ios): show remote run progress in Live Activities
prs.body:
**Superseded by the narrow published stack indexed at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147272. This aggregate remains CLOSED without merging; its branch, signed checkpoint, recovery refs and historical evidence are preserved.**

October 1 decomposition: the publication, store, Gateway and native endpoints remain https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147297, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147303, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147319 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147325, now each ending a smaller sub-stack. All 11 replacement slices are drafts and below 3,000 changed lines. Their cumulative endpoint trees exactly preserve the prior reviewed checkpoints; no parent/main ref was rewritten.

Relay contracts: https://github.com/openclaw/clawpushrelay/pull/5; relay service: https://github.com/openclaw/clawpushrelay/pull/4. Current evidence and blockers belong to each slice and the root index, not the historical record below. Inherited dependency audit, eventual landing-base qualification, mixed-host compatibility, native final-I/O/key-loss recovery and signed-device/widget/live-service proof are not waived. User retains final merge; no merge, auto-merge, deployment or provisioning occurred.

<details>
<summary>Preserved aggregate checkpoint and historical evidence</summary>

**Historical status at the September 11 checkpoint:** the reviewed 29-commit checkpoint was published, but its parent had moved and the branch conflicted. Prior-checkpoint CI failed; it did not qualify that head. The following record is historical, not the replacement stack's current status.

Published checkpoint: `762d629f8fea0ef6b34837bdd3ef4abf5d37d032`, tree `05396ce0292a6e96ed4996317053c9949ba35646`; 29 signed commits above prior pinned parent `5e226bdc97ea39e7687ce75fc4b467fe98f20973` in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143631. The complete private source/index proof tree matches this committed tree. A normal fast-forward advanced the prior published `65713a6da68cd64c996826a77217215c1481ae77` by four reviewed test/test-support commits. September 11, 2026 publication readbacks confirm the parent branch, parent PR head and app base at `41fc160aeb25f78a0805a423da852174d6a5ae27`, with the app CONFLICTING/DIRTY. The checkpoint was constructed and proved against `5e226bd`, not this new stack. A stable parent handoff and deliberate integration remain necessary. No new CI was dispatched for this publication, and no further parent integration was performed.

Prior-checkpoint CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34585354606 is terminal and failed. It used the canonical full `ci.yml` route for exact `65713a6`, not `762d629` or its integration with base `41fc160a`. Both core-lint failures were the same subscription-test line cap; the fixture dedup passed its focused gates. iOS failed test-module compilation at the transport fixture's actor boundary; the repair has compiler-reduction proof, not full iOS qualification. Android third-party reconnect-header failure remains unresolved; the change adds bounded post-failure diagnostics only. The macOS native approval-allowed assertion failed; a controlled witness proves and repairs the runner's response-observation race, not the sanitized historical count or full native outcome. Full Swift exhausted its 30-minute job budget: runtime began 25m40s into the job after Kit and Mac builds, with test progress until five seconds before cancellation and a restored cache. No specific stuck case or deadlock was established.

Two previously failing lanes passed on exact `65713a6`: [core-fast-isolated](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34585354606/job/103218484489) recorded 129 passing files, one skipped file, 1,872 passing tests and 25 skips, including all nine real PowerShell readiness/visibility cases; [tooling-15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34585354606/job/103218481108) recorded 59 passing files, 2,403 passing tests and seven skips. These results supersede those lanes' older failures for `65713a6`; they do not explain the historical causes or qualify `762d629`.

## What Problem This Solves

iOS operators should be able to start a run, lock or suspend the app, and see truthful progress and its eventual outcome without keeping a foreground connection alive. Local-only Live Activity updates do not provide that workflow.

Remote updates must stay attached to the exact authenticated run. Reconnects, delayed callbacks, token rotation, and pending terminal writes must not switch owners, invent completion, or let an obsolete response retire the current activity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The backend reuses canonical admission, committed session facts, and authenticated ownership to register, recover, rotate, revoke, and dispatch bounded activity updates. Terminal facts absorb progress; exact settlement fences reject stale responses without a second run ledger.

Composer, native-send, and outbox acknowledgments carry the captured run/Gateway/profile binding into the existing Live Activity and App Attest owners. Per-activity tokens remain separate from ordinary-push credentials. Suspend/resume/retire/forget use those owners rather than an unbound fallback.

The integration with prior pinned parent `5e226bd` preserves its derived protocol registry and native ownership changes, regenerates owned Swift/Kotlin/inventory/workboard outputs canonically, and retains all feature methods and strict native assertions. Six Swift fixture sites now use the actual failable-identity/public-thinking contracts. Proxy additions record bounded, redacted connection phases for diagnosis; they are not a claimed fix for the parent's unproven connection failure.

## User Impact

- Remote run activities require a supported official relay-backed device build, compatible relay/Gateway, existing disclosure and notification enrollment, and iOS Live Activity permission. Local/direct-push and simulator builds do not start them; ineligible sends do not perform the optional activity owner lookup.
- Activities start only after an accepted send and exact run preparation, including bounded session-ID resolution for first-send/outbox cases. Queued, rejected, or uncertain sends do not create one. An unavailable activity does not resend an accepted message.
- Generic status and factual times cover running, tool use, approval needed, completed, failed, cancelled, and timed out. Prompts, tool names, session labels, and error details are excluded. Local attention, tool, voice, and connection presentation remains separate and higher priority.
- Backgrounding or disconnecting suspends enrollment work without cancelling the run or manufacturing a terminal result. Staleness means updates are delayed. Forget removes the registry entry, stops the fleet, and finishes synchronous local credential/cache cleanup before awaiting remote retirement under the same-Gateway cleanup barrier.
- Forget ends matching local activities, including completed or cold-start tiles, without cancelling the run. **Cold local removal does not confirm remote revocation:** saved selectors cannot reconstruct authenticated ownership; unavailable remote cleanup remains explicit.
- Storage is bounded to 8 sendable activities per device, 256 per Gateway, 4,096 retained rows, a fixed 8-hour lease, 2,048-byte snapshots, at least 5 seconds between progress deliveries, terminal retries bounded by five minutes and the lease, and 24-hour credential-free tombstones. The approved lazy table retains inherited schema version 17. Retries preserve reserved payload bytes/timestamps; ordering waits for real wall-clock time rather than inventing future timestamps.

No operator configuration, environment variables, dependencies, or protocol-version bump are added. No deployment or provisioning was performed.

## Evidence

**External qualification still required:** canonical Convex generation against an authorized existing deployment, including `convex/_generated/api.d.ts` for the activity modules; real indexes, transactions, and routing; initial real Apple App Attest enrollment; and signed physical-device APNs proof while locked/suspended. Device proof must cover progress/terminal display, rotation, recovery, retirement, and ordinary-notification coexistence. Mock services, local signatures, paired-Gateway witnesses, and APNs acceptance alone do not establish those results.

**Companion relay:** https://github.com/openclaw/clawpushrelay/pull/4 remains draft at unchanged head `0bf5e9574db6cdaa2ee9f7281e67e61b64d7a316`; exact-head `validate` is green: https://github.com/openclaw/clawpushrelay/actions/runs/34434936868. This does not close the external-service/device gates.

Local checks ran in retained private copies whose source bytes, Git file modes, and indexes matched the recorded trees, not committed-head checkout runs. Carrier commits were kept separate from evidence identities. Toolchain: Node 26.7.0, pnpm 12.3.4, patched Vitest 5.0.0, TypeScript 6.0.3, and oxfmt 0.65.0.

| Current integration proof | Recorded input and command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backend owner and real Gateway | Tree `499314650e070f825163485644b7ba98f2988beb`, committed as `602169e5268a5d3c07788dd384fc639c55eebd9f`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` for method list, status/read visibility, profile authorization, activity store, terminal handoff, and `chat.live-activity-live-proof.test.ts` | 145 passing cases, including an authenticated accepted send and canonical first running fact before controlled-provider output. |
| Same-database older reader | Candidate tree `49931465`, exact parent reader `5e226bdc97ea39e7687ce75fc4b467fe98f20973` / tree `f50c04ad783fb719efe8401f51ef2502cf935e51` | All four phases passed: lazy absence; candidate registration/observation; older ordinary APNs use preserving rows; candidate reopen with fresh claim/authorization and terminal credential/snapshot/claim clearing. Both schema markers stayed 17; schema digests and SQLite checks passed. |
| Protocol and production types | Tree `49931465`; `pnpm run protocol:check` with explicit parent base; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` | Registry/schema/Swift/Kotlin/since/generated-diff aggregate and core production types passed. Canonical generator repeats were stable. |
| Native launcher and proxy diagnostics | Before the approval-response synchronization repair; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/macos-native-test-launch.test.ts` and `test/scripts/qa-gateway-rpc-proxy.test.ts` | 85 launcher and four real-loopback proxy cases passed. Exact forwarding/reconnect, withheld upgrade cancellation, HTTP 403 auto-close, invalid upgrade failure, bounded metadata, and joined cleanup covered. Scoped format/lint, scripts types, and root/tooling test types passed. No native app/device execution is claimed. |
| APNs ownership consolidation | Prior-checkpoint tree `d3f5f6644997dd936b9d14a177307e39735ea921`; original dispatch + cancellation files, then combined `src/infra/push-apns-dispatch.test.ts`, through `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` | 17/17 before and after, exact expanded inventory and table order. Existing case bodies/assertions/deadlines/finally blocks stayed byte-identical; private cancellation fixtures moved inside their sibling describe. Format/lint passed. |
| Selected core test types | Prior-checkpoint tree `d3f5f664`; `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json <complete changed-path list>` | Ownership preflight and all 17 selected graphs passed. Consolidation restores 720 infra roots without changing caps, config, runtime, or coverage. |
| Subscription fixture dedup | Commit `593b49f2b72d64b65aab5c2690a7a31ef9d8f247`, tree `0e83134f2c643e460c9df5348cadb6525c815198`; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.test.ts` | 26/26 passed. Pinned format/lint and the changed-path-selected gateway-root type graph passed. Only seven identical cron defaults were shared; assertions, order, persistence wiring and test-root count stayed unchanged. |
| Transport fixture isolation | Commit `81baeebc5d57b1c23a7759e6cf5fa1f5ee3dbd54`; one caller-inherited `isolated (any Actor)? = #isolation` parameter | Swift 6.3.3 object-compilation reduction with complete concurrency reproduced the sending diagnostic before the parameter and passed after it. Zero runtime tests; not full iOS test-module proof. SwiftFormat 0.63.0 passed. |
| Android reconnect observation | Commit `ea9dda6`; original display assertion retained, with bounded post-failure state/semantics observation | Diagnostic-only, non-atomic observation; original assertion remains the cause. No retries, state forcing, raw descriptions or identifiers. Source/style/privacy review passed; local Android compilation, runtime and pinned ktlint were not run because the required local SDK/tooling was unavailable. |
| Approval response synchronization | Commit `762d629f8fea0ef6b34837bdd3ef4abf5d37d032`; runner SHA256 `b40c752702e954f0809f3810f2695f2c5cdc14869a4378489088393193bcaabf`; matching private source/index tree `05396ce0` | Real loopback proxy plus actual extracted runner cases and existing `waitFor`: controlled RED at 0 versus 1 and 1 versus 2 responses; both repaired handlers stay pending until upstream reply release, then pass. Four extra-count/false-response scenarios retain strict rejection. Existing assertions and retirement/pending checks are unchanged. All owned sockets/listeners joined; format, scoped lint, scripts types and root-test types passed. This is mechanism proof, not a native app/Gateway authorization run or a claim about sanitized CI counts. |

The 21-commit parent replay preserved authors, dates, messages, and trailers; all 21 replayed commits were signed anew. Seventeen patches were equal and four had reviewed parent-integration adaptations. Three scoped fixture/proxy commits and the APNs consolidation produced `65713a6`; four further test/test-support commits produce the published `762d629` checkpoint. The four repair paths, separate two-path consolidation, latest three-file repair, and final runner repair each received test-audit/deslop and fresh scoped Sol-high P0 autoreview: no findings, confidence 0.99. Integration adaptations also received direct independent source review and canonical generation/range/blob proof. Earlier full-branch review is historical, not a newly claimed whole-PR review.

**Privacy and automated-review limits:** the outgoing full capture at tree `194cfea98a5a679c51f3047182ecb216a127abf8` was scanned offline with verified TruffleHog 3.97.4, verification disabled, all result classes included, and fail-on-scan-errors enabled. Exit **183** retained four reports for the same manually verified synthetic negative-userinfo URI across parent/candidate and decoders; this is not zero findings. No scan error was reported. Subsequent canonical-deferred/APNs-test-move deltas were reviewed separately. The final four-file delta, four commit messages and both body previews passed manual review and the scoped ordinary-personal-data/credential-shape preflight; this was not a fresh full scan of head `762d629`. The latest ClawSweeper comment, verified September 11 at 10:30:39 UTC before publication, was updated that day at 09:50:37 UTC and links https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/34586069095: input-safety blocked, no model verdict or Rank-up moves. The comment exposes no detected value or path; no finding attribution is inferred from the prior synthetic-fixture classification. This is not a verdict on `762d629`, and no unchanged-input retry was requested. A historical sanitized artifact exposed only one of two findings; the second remains unattributed, and the fixture anonymization is not asserted to explain it.

**One-shot private tooling diagnostic:** Darwin arm64/Node 26.7 ran the original 59-file selection once against private source/index tree `d3f5f664`. It finished with a summary and exit 1: 56 files passed, three failed; 1,821 tests passed, four failed, eight skipped. Two Android workflow shell cases reported an unbound array variable, the release-matrix shell case rejected lowercase parameter expansion, and the survivor shell case failed to create a `tsx` IPC listener (`EINVAL`). No stall was reproduced. The retained collection markers confirm the first 28-file order matched the historical prefix; the two reported hashes use JSON-array versus newline-terminated serialization of that same ordered array. Platform, outcomes and diagnostic instrumentation still limit comparison. Phase markers used stderr and could affect the no-output watchdog; there was no periodic output. No 200-second pending snapshot was created, and missing throw/per-reset markers limit localization. The original runner was restored byte-for-byte and all owned processes joined. This is not a qualification pass or an explanation of the prior Linux wait. The separate private PowerShell diagnostic made zero attempts because `pwsh` was unavailable; no install or retry was used.

<details>
<summary>Historical proof and unresolved failure leads</summary>

- **Older local proof:** candidate `4a1a8b6d34b991bf265b534964fa40964cbf0f73` / tree `f58c863f30ac8f01f5007ffc2f12816c887784e4` retained 195 runtime passes, ten static passes, and a four-phase schema-17 roundtrip. Tree `d923136de95830f17748cf5a45e1ef137559c38e` retained 77 unchanged event cases and 17 core plus four other type gates. Tree `9ebb5786b2ea520cc0701b61c2d34e374730cfb3` retained 58 launcher and 15 selected workflow-guard passes. The cron anonymization at tree `ee229018c2a60dde38862e8c96557ce884c90cc9` retained two passing cron cases. None is relabeled as current-head execution.
- **Native compiler/host witnesses:** real Foundation/Testing object compilation reproduced the sending/self failure before the explicit Sendable capture and passed afterward, with zero runtime tests. The actual runner/proxy/ws 8.21.3 witness proved correct frontend host on primary/approval initial connections and reconnects, unchanged custom headers/connect bytes, and closed resources. These scoped repairs do not convert earlier hosted failures into passes. The latest six Swift fixture fixes still require exact-head iOS compilation.
- **PowerShell readiness/visibility:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34489462331/job/102912376336 recorded five readiness and four case-timeout failures, teardown SIGTERM/null outcomes, then a real summary: nine failed, 1,861 passed, 25 skipped. Exact `65713a6` passed all nine cases; the historical cause remains unestablished.
- **Tooling-15:** prior Linux runs repeatedly reached 1,586 passing cases, four skips and 28/59 files, then exited 143 after the 300,000 ms no-output watchdog without a summary. Exact `65713a6` completed all 59 files successfully. Neither that pass nor the separate private diagnostic establishes the historical cause.
- **Uncorrelated heartbeat in reset/yield fixture:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34483325937/job/102891581468 recorded one failure and 5,335 passes. An unmarked heartbeat request preceded the marked flow; strict later cancellation assertions were not reached. The parent contained the same recorded scenario, but wake origin and integration timing contribution remain unknown. No heartbeat suppression or rerun cleared it.
- **Coordinate worker retirement in concurrent state-schema probes:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34472053034/job/102854681138 retains the inherited teardown race. Intentional zero-wait retirement refusal has sibling coverage; a finally error can mask the body error, so fresh-open success/failure remains unestablished.
- **Native hosted history:** ba954 built the iOS app but failed test-module compilation and a macOS surface-port assertion, without final native receipts. Its full Swift job passed. Parent 5e's macOS native proof passed, while its iOS runtime attempt timed out before an upstream connection was observed; cause remains unproven. No fresh full-native/device pass is inferred from those results.

</details>

Reviewed checkpoint `762d629` accounting against prior pinned parent `5e226bdc97ea39e7687ce75fc4b467fe98f20973`, not the current GitHub base `41fc160a`:

| Classification | Files | Added | Removed | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

Stack base: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158091

## What Problem This Solves

Installed-skill retrieval changes need a reproducible relevance baseline, separate from benchmarks that measure task completion with curated skills.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Developers can compare retrieval revisions through the real `skills_search` tool using fixed synthetic queries and catalog sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an offline evaluator, labeled fixtures, and metric tests. The report separates top-1 hits, recall at the result limit, complete multi-skill recall, reciprocal rank, no-match false positives, cold/warm latency, and RSS observations. A fixture digest and per-query results make comparisons auditable.

The default corpus has 17 queries, including body-only terms, related skills, paraphrases, a multilingual request, and two no-match requests. Additional inventory entries measure catalog growth, not semantic hard-negative quality. This is not a SkillsBench task-completion score and makes no embedding or model-quality claim.

prs.title: feat(claws): adopt existing workspaces with recoverable ownership
prs.body:
Supersedes #115670. Closes #126785. Related: #115662; #125345 remains the configured-agent follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves

`claws add` rejects existing workspace directories even when their declared files already match the Claw.

## User Impact

Users can explicitly opt into adopting an existing workspace with `--adopt-existing-workspace`, without rewriting matching files or deleting the adopted directory during removal. Conflicting content, unsafe paths, and overlapping agent workspaces remain blocked. No schema-version migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adoption records consent and file ownership, preserves recovery across interrupted installation, and binds bootstrap publication/removal to the actual owned file rather than matching bytes alone. Configuration admission rechecks the workspace after package installation. Shared bootstrap publication retains main’s private `0600` default.

This maintainer-owned replacement preserves the reviewed work and original commit authorship from #115670, whose history was previously consolidated during conflict resolution. Credit: @sasan1200 and @giodl73, with maintainer integration and repairs by @jalehman. The original PR retains detailed implementation and prior validation history.

## Accepted downgrade contract

Maintainer acceptance: older readers may fail closed on the adoption ownership marker. Downgrades are unsupported; no downgrade compatibility layer is required for this change. Return to a compatible build to manage or remove the installation. Do not delete the marker to bypass this protection.

## Evidence

prs.title: design: should agent skill allowlists hide the agent's own Workshop skills?
prs.body:
## Design question: should an agent's skill allowlist hide its own Skill Workshop skills?

No code in this PR. It records a maintainer decision that our setup surfaced; an implementation exists locally and is held until this is decided.

### What happens today

An agent with a non-empty `agents.entries.<id>.skills` (or inherited `agents.defaults.skills`) allowlist runs Skill Workshop as usual. Workshop creates, revises, and in the weekly collection review consolidates, renames, or retires skills under `<state-dir>/agents/<id>/agent/workshop-skills`. The allowlist is matched by name, and Workshop never consults it. So:

- a newly learned Workshop skill is invisible to the agent that learned it until an operator adds its name;
- a consolidation that renames an allowlisted skill silently drops it, and the old name is left stale in the list;
- the agent still spends review turns maintaining skills it can never load.

On our setup, 25 of 26 Workshop skills were "Excluded by agent allowlist", and 4 allowlist names no longer existed. Most of the 25 were never listed, not renamed. (A separate PR makes `skills_read` say "not available to this agent" in this case instead of the false "Unknown installed skill".)

### The two contracts

- **#59992** (inherited agent skill allowlists): "`agents.list[].skills` … non-empty list => final skill set for that agent", "`[]` => no skills", and one skill-visibility contract across prompts, snapshots, slash commands, and sandbox sync. Docs: "Use allowlists to restrict which skills an agent sees, regardless of where they are loaded from."
- **#135528** (per-agent Skill Workshop, `feat(skills)!`): "Workshop skills are agent-owned"; docs list the Workshop tier as visible to "Only that agent" and say "Workshop skills learned by one agent are not shared with another agent." This PR also parametrized `src/skills/discovery/chat-commands.discovery.test.ts` "reports allowlist-hidden %s skills without loading another agent's skills" over `["workspace", "workshop"]`. That test asserts an alpha Workshop skill outside alpha's allowlist is hidden, and that `$hidden` errors with "Update the skill allowlist…". The PR body and docs don't discuss allowlists. The test's headline invariant is cross-agent isolation, but it does pin "allowlist hides Workshop skills".

### Options

1. **Keep today's contract** (allowlist is final for every source). Operators with allowlists must add each Workshop skill by name and fix renames by hand. Workshop is effectively manual-approval-only for these agents.
2. **The agent-level allowlist admits the agent's own Workshop skills** (the held implementation):
   - Applies only to `agents.defaults.skills` / `agents.entries.<id>.skills`. A non-empty list keeps naming the final set of *shared* skills.
   - `[]` still means no skills, Workshop included.
   - Channel/group `skills` scopes still narrow Workshop skills, and naming a Workshop skill there keeps it.
   - `skills.entries.<name>.enabled: false`, session `/skills` overrides, and the apply-time scanner still govern Workshop skills.
   - Ownership is proven by Gateway discovery (`openclaw-workshop` source on a Gateway-hosted root), never by a workspace host's label.
   - Provenance is carried through the existing name-list filter as an internal `workshop:*` / `workshop:<name>` entry, so channel narrowing stays exact.
   - Flips the `workshop` variant of the #135528 test. Docs and config help gain one sentence.
3. **Workshop writes allowlist entries** when it creates or renames a skill. Runtime config writes, and free-form renames during the weekly review can't be detected. Not recommended.

### Trade-off

Option 2 reconciles the two contracts and doesn't retire #59992. The allowlist stays the final word on everything shared across agents and on `[]`. Workshop skills are already scoped to one agent by location, so an allowlist that hides them only turns off the agent's own learning. The cost: an operator who uses a non-empty allowlist *specifically* to suppress Workshop output would need `skills.entries.<name>.enabled: false` or `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "off"` instead. The allowlist is documented as a visibility filter, not a security boundary.

### Decision needed

Keep (1) or adopt (2)? Stale allowlist names would no longer matter for Workshop under (2). Doctor does not warn about them today, and this proposal adds no warning.

prs.title: fix(agents): deliver final answers that end a response before more same-input work
prs.body:
> Draft for discussion, stacked on #164774. Not for landing. The commit is a minimal sketch so the trade-off can be read against real code; it needs a maintainer decision before any review or CI work.

## Question

When one model response ends in a completed `final_answer` and the model then keeps working on the same input (async tool results arrive, it calls more tools, and it writes a new answer), should OpenClaw deliver the earlier answer as well?

- **Today (and #164774):** no. A later answer supersedes it. #164774 keeps the earlier answer only when the follow-up adds nothing (`NO_REPLY` or empty).
- **This draft:** yes, the way Codex shows each completed non-commentary item: the earlier answer is delivered once, in order, before the later one.

## Two real occurrences (our setup, `openai/gpt-6-astra` over `openai-responses`, Telegram)

1. **Follow-up is `NO_REPLY`.** One response: async `web_search`, commentary + `sessions_yield`, async `web_fetch`, then `final_answer` with the full answer. The follow-up after the async results was `NO_REPLY`. On main the answer is lost and the user gets "⚠️ Agent couldn't generate a response". **#164774 fixes this one.**
2. **Follow-up does more work and answers again.** One response: async `view_image`, async `process`, then `final_answer` with the main answer and a link to an official document. The follow-up response polled again, read an image (async), and produced an empty `final_answer` tail. The next response wrote a short new answer that reads as if the first had been seen ("Here's the official close-up…"). Only the second answer reached the user; the link was lost. **#164774 does not change this; it is listed there under "Not changed".**

Both have the same transcript shape: a call-free tail fragment of a split async response whose text is `phase: final_answer`.

## Why the current behavior exists (#141444)

> Fixes an issue where users received a burst of obsolete intermediate answers at the end of a tool-using conversation when a `before_agent_finalize` hook deferred delivery. Earlier answers could still be sent after a newer accepted answer or terminal `NO_REPLY`.

> It records which message blocks belong to tool continuations, including normal-stop tails of async responses, and supersedes only their older text.

`docs/concepts/streaming.md` (from #141444): "A later answer supersedes deferred text from earlier tool turns, including when the final answer is `NO_REPLY`." Related: #149925 ("Final answers still replace progress within one input; silent answers do not leak progress"), #150539, and #152786 (text written beside the last tool call is not promoted; recovery uses the tool-free finalizer).

## The trade-off

| | Supersede (today) | Deliver sealed answers (this draft) |
|---|---|---|
| Model corrects itself after the async results | User sees only the correction. | User sees the first answer, then the correction as a second message. |
| Model builds on its earlier answer (occurrence 2) | User loses context the model believes they saw. Later replies refer to things the user never got. | User gets both, in order. This matches what the model wrote. |
| Exact repeat | Once. | Once (the earlier seal is dropped and the repeat is delivered at its later position). |
| `NO_REPLY` follow-up (occurrence 1) | Fixed by #164774. | Same outcome without the payload special case: the sealed answer is delivered and `NO_REPLY` adds nothing. |

Codex (`../codex` `c248f6d48b`) does the second. A non-commentary message item is finalized and shown when it completes (`codex-rs/core/src/stream_events_utils.rs:383-397`). Any tool call still sets `needs_follow_up` and the turn samples again (`:356`; `session/turn.rs:2780`, `:566`, `:653`), so nothing the model said is retracted. Codex's next-turn deferral (`stream_events_utils.rs:122-135`, `session/input_queue.rs:275-296`) applies only to inter-agent mailbox mail, not to tool results.

## #141444's scenarios under this draft

- **Answers written beside an async call** (`text` + `toolCall` in one message, with stop `toolUse` or `stop`), followed by a terminal answer or `NO_REPLY`: **unchanged, still superseded.** Only a call-free `phase: final_answer` message with `stopReason: stop` is sealed. Text in a message that carries a call is progress.
- **Completed answers to earlier user inputs:** unchanged (user-boundary segments).
- **Deferred media with an obsolete caption** (a call-free `final_answer` with media, then commentary, then the final answer): **intended change** for real async tails. After #164774 that message has `stopReason: stop`, so its caption is a completed answer and is delivered with the media. The model wrote it as the answer. #141444's fixture uses `stopReason: toolUse`, which is not sealed.
- **Deferred prefix extended by the final text:** unchanged (the prefix message is `toolUse` and has no phase).
- Commentary before a call: unchanged, never delivered.

## Sketch (this commit)

- At the next assistant `message_start`, a previous message that is `stop`, `phase: final_answer`, call-free, with visible non-silent text is pushed as a #149925 answer segment marked `continued` (no new state store). An exact repeat at a later `message_end` pops the seal.
- `payloads.ts` keeps one rule: segments are answers. `continued` segments do not get `precedingInputAnswer`, so voice consult and transcript-truncation recovery treat them as the current input's answer. #164774's `inputAnswer`/`answerStands` special case goes away.
- `settled-turn-finalization.ts` keeps the current input's delivery floor at the last user-boundary segment.
- Deferred release (`reply-delivery.ts`) is unchanged: segment boundaries already protect sealed answers from supersession.

Sketch-level evidence only. Through the real Responses → `runAgentLoop` → subscriber → block pipeline → payload path, both occurrence shapes deliver both answers once, an exact repeat is delivered once, commentary or text beside a call is not delivered, and #141444's beside-a-call cases are still superseded. A live Telegram Test Server run with real `gpt-6-astra` for occurrence 2's shape (fetch, answer without waiting, then fetch again and write a new message) showed a progress draft, then the first answer, then the second answer, with the draft deleted and no warning.

## Decision needed

Should a completed `final_answer` that ended its model response be delivered when the model keeps working on the same input? If yes, this replaces #164774's payload special case and partly reverses #141444 for call-free async tails. If no, close this draft and keep #164774 as is.

prs.title: feat: show built-in Docker and clawctl supervisor guidance
prs.body:
Related: #157668. RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/75

## What Problem This Solves

Externally supervised Gateway refusals do not tell Docker Compose or clawctl operators which command to run on the host.

## User Impact

Set `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=docker` or `clawctl` for external supervision with built-in host instructions in lifecycle, Doctor, onboarding, and supported CLI/Control UI update refusals. Existing `external` keeps generic copy. All three values enforce the same ownership restrictions and preserve the restart handoff; commands are displayed, never executed. Unknown/unset modes retain their existing behavior.

Docker instructions assume the `openclaw-gateway` Compose service and a published image. The update command neither advances pinned tags nor rebuilds local images; customized/local-build deployments should use `external`. clawctl supplies only its known start/stop/restart commands; unsupported actions remain generic. Current Windows packaging pins `external` and therefore keeps generic copy; selecting the new preset requires adoption by a launcher with an upgraded payload. Changing the host shell variable does not override the current packaged launcher.

Older releases recognize only `external`: upgrade every Gateway/CLI writer before selecting the new values, and restore `external` before downgrading. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core owns two fixed presets selected by the existing mode variable. No new environment variable, plugin, SDK extension, configuration key, or CI exemption is needed; the variable count stays 486/486. Update responses carry transient display guidance, never stored in update history. The UI clears it on access loss, reconnect, and status errors. Update watcher code and labels load with the existing lazy update flow to preserve the startup budget.

This is a separate main-based alternative to #157679, which remains untouched. The requested design for this PR is fixed core presets selected by the existing mode value; the plugin alternative is not a prerequisite. No persistent schema or data-model semantics change in this PR.

## Evidence

- Mode-only core/CLI/Doctor: 56 tests; Gateway: 75 tests; real shared-state worker boundary: 45 tests. All passed.
- UI: 184 unit tests and 13 production-build browser scenarios passed, including copying commands, retained update results, and stale-guidance retirement.
- Core/UI/test type checks, architecture checks, focused lint, i18n verification, docs MDX checks, and formatting passed. Independent review findings resolved.
- Full build, tarball integrity, and final UI performance check passed on `5b93d99777c2` (startup gzip 371,270 B / 371,332 B). The published updater installed the exact candidate; installed Docker/clawctl/external refusals, Docker update copy, and unset/unknown config validation passed. Rollback to 2026.9.6 passed using `external` and the verified pre-upgrade database backup (the older release cannot read schema 19). Config bytes were preserved.
- Rebased onto main `47a9e77007f`, including `a99102804eb`, which fixes the inherited QA catalog reference. The unrelated shared Swift Periphery failure (`GatewayExternalAuthorizationError` redundant public accessibility) remains unchanged on that main revision. Current-head CI also reports an unrelated chained assertion in `src/gateway/server-chat-progress-snapshot.ts:36`, identical on current main `4a2f1239`; [failing boundary job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36222565960/job/108350569410). Remaining checks are running.

![Generic external-supervisor refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84fc3cea-9cde-4368-a066-75a067265d0d)

Docker mode selected, with host command copied:

![Docker supervisor guidance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e547e46f-2165-409f-a67c-9ca6aaeb4538)


Review cleanup: Docker guidance now states the deployment project directory and existing Compose file set/order. Docs explain default discovery, `COMPOSE_FILE`, and when to retain `external`. Existing supervision tests passed (28 tests; 1.01 s Vitest / 2.34 s runner wall), and the existing three browser scenarios passed in 20.74 s with the longer context and command copy verified. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`AGENTS.md` asks agents to get approval before intentional schema changes and to read the storage checkpoint, but it sets no default. An agent can treat a schema-version bump as a normal option, even when a same-version additive change would work. A bump that ships without matching older-updater support blocks installs from updating, and bumps are the main reason downgrades are unsupported.

## User Impact

User impact: fewer schema-version bumps, so fewer updates blocked by missing updater support and fewer installs that cannot downgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

One line in the runtime safeguards, next to the existing schema-check rule:

- Avoid schema changes.
- When one is needed, prefer a same-version additive change (a new table, or a bare nullable column), as the [versioning contract](docs/reference/database-schemas/versioning.md) already allows.
- A schema-version bump needs maintainer discussion before implementation and matching older-updater support.

The versioning contract and storage review checkpoint are unchanged; this only sets the default an agent reaches for.

## Evidence

Docs-only change to `AGENTS.md`. The linked `docs/reference/database-schemas/versioning.md` exists on `main` and defines which changes may stay at the same schema version.

## What Problem This Solves

Disabling the composer also disabled its plus menu, preventing read-only users from inspecting session Skills and Connectors.

## Evidence

- All 71 focused UI tests and 15 browser scenarios passed on the current-main candidate. They cover the rendered composer, read-only navigation and selected revisions, writable flows, and denied mutations.
- Fresh independent correctness, maintainability, and test-structure reviews found no actionable issues on current main.
- Inspected Playwright screenshots use an isolated mock Gateway. The read-only flow recorded no `chat.send` or `sessions.patch` requests. The same evidence is attached in the originating chat.

Measured with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` (wall time includes the UI build and browser startup):

| Browser suite | Tests passed | Local wall time | CI file execution |

| `chat-composer-capability-menu.e2e.test.ts` | 13 | 48.62 s | 24.070 s |
| `chat-skill-library.e2e.test.ts` | 2 | 33.34 s | 6.443 s |

The five-file UI run took 21.08 s wall. UI/E2E type checks, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. ClawSweeper also reviewed head `080452508968` with no actionable findings.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Read-only menu unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe5b87c4-008b-472f-9ad3-a7b904276f86) | ![Skills and Connectors available while attachments remain disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7953e7e4-2733-44e1-85a9-bade4f025d6e) |

## CI status

The changed browser suites passed on `080452508968375be7d8ece0d16268066250866a`, but the required gate is blocked by an unrelated [initial-connect loading-skeleton failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36600704177/job/109517800964):

prs.title: fix(agents): keep collector launches in submission order
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent collector spawns can launch out of submission order when the later request's asynchronous requester-session lookup finishes first.

## User Impact

Collector launches retain the documented FIFO order under the group's concurrency limit. Failed or cancelled requester lookups release their reserved position so later collectors can proceed. Ordinary child cancellation, requester identity, and private completion behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requester-worker change in #159135 placed an await ahead of the existing collector FIFO reservation. The scripts sweep in #159199 exposed the race through the Gateway queued-collector suite on its CI merge tree.

Collectors now reserve their position before their first await and capture the requester after the executor holds that reservation. The existing executor cleanup withdraws and releases the reservation on lookup failure or cancellation. Ordinary spawns keep their previous capture and admission order. Both paths use one requester-read helper, retain worker-backed SQLite access and authority checks, and preserve the established error result for already-cancelled calls. There is no additional queue, configuration, schema, or protocol.

## Evidence

Independent Codex review of the complete candidate is scoped-clean through P2. Validation ran on [Blacksmith Testbox run 36276852584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36276852584), lease `tbx_01m3fxtnhhmxefc0rman8xk4fb`, with Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 12.4.2. The lease is stopped. It verifies all changed source hashes after synchronization against base `547bb312f4098cd0f28f71cc45a7e351e944b1ff`.

- Deterministic regression gates the first requester lookup until the second spawn is accepted, then checks actual dispatch order. With original production code, the second collector launches first and the assertion fails. The corrected owner passes.
- The full requester-incarnation file passes all 12 tests, covering FIFO, failed and cancelled lookup cleanup, already-cancelled no-effect behavior, ordinary cancellation, dirty-sibling validation, and native/visible/ACP requester identity. Measured command: `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.requester-incarnation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 28.347s wall (includes worker preparation).
- Authority/preparation, scheduler, Gateway queued-collector and fs-safe/import-boundary siblings pass (118.466s). The original 18-file CI group passes with the repair (144.025s).
- Twenty repetitions of the four deterministic cases pass: 80 test executions, 20.156–26.073s per command, 458.855s total. A subsequent mechanical grouping of two existing context captures satisfies the unchanged 700-line cap; the complete requester suite and fresh independent review pass afterward.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 547bb312f4098cd0f28f71cc45a7e351e944b1ff --timed` passes in 468.380s, including all 25 core-test type graphs, lint, dead exports, cycles, and storage/security guards. `pnpm build` passes in 406.349s. The final wrapper returns `exitCode: 0` / `runStatus: succeeded`.

The original CI failure was in `session-utils.queued-collector.test-support.ts:222` on merge tree `b014d5fc4348a0ccc7b4c5d9b0694ab93c82fc00`. A replay of the exact 18-file group on that unmodified tree passed, demonstrating why a passing retry is not a fix. The new controlled lookup inversion supplies the original-red/candidate-green proof without sleeps, retries, weaker assertions, or serialized spawn submissions.

The entry-point composition is necessary: the scheduler’s existing FIFO unit coverage passes while the original requester lookup can reorder calls before they reach it. These tests use explicit promise gates and the existing isolated state fixture, with no model or network calls.

**Superseded by main:** `5cf18de3d103a6bea797cbfe52fa8f51dce8c596` independently landed the FIFO repair while this PR was completing CI. The landed owner retains the exact reservation hold through requester acquisition and transfers it into execution, with requester-incarnation and failed-read coverage. Fresh Blacksmith Testbox verification of the landed `src/gateway/session-utils.queued-collector.test.ts` passes all 35 cases in 62.905s on the main-containing scripts candidate `ecd179ea0355eabe424743c38497acb13d7bbcab`. Closing this duplicate unmerged so there is one canonical implementation. The earlier independent proof and successful CI remain recorded above.

prs.title: test(sessions): await database retirement before cleanup reopen
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the session-cleanup test intermittently reopening its database while asynchronous resources are still closing.

## User Impact

This is a test-fixture repair. Production cleanup and resource-admission behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The applied-summary suite called the synchronous test reset before reopening. That reset begins asynchronous resource retirement without joining it; a subsequent cleanup can reach the admission guard while the retiring owner still holds custody and fail with `Agent database resources are closing`.

The fixture now awaits the existing asynchronous close owner before its root-scoped reset/reopen and during teardown. The synchronous reset still clears validation and terminal caches. All archival, history, preview, and repeat-cleanup assertions remain intact.

Found while validating #158638. **Closed externally as already applied on main:** #158688 supplies the scoped reopen plus a retirement assertion, and `6c7544adc9826fa637425a2fa967389e0507a800` supplies the awaited teardown. The plugin cleanup has been rebased and retargeted to main. This PR was not merged or reopened.

## Evidence

Independent Codex review is clean at P0–P2.

Linux Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3e7g69mr3795gxdhcvqa2mh` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36224816492)), Node 24.19.0:

- Original captured 93-file runtime-config selection: 1,366 tests passed on this replay. This does not prove the intermittent failure resolved.
- Candidate complete suite: 21 consecutive runs passed, 9 tests each (189 test executions). `pnpm test src/config/sessions/cleanup-service.applied-summary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took 30s including cold worker preparation; additional runs took 26–30s.
- Corrected captured selection: three complete passes, each with 93 files and 1,366 tests, taking 167s, 181s, and 167s. The additional two ran at exact fixture head `b54f803ea2844878e2cfaa88fdab36a213aa4427` on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3ea9hahc43v8w8gqdwcw210` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36227290367)), using `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with the captured group. The recorded two-worker configuration and ordered include selection were retained; scheduling remains nondeterministic.
- Resource-owner suite: 37 tests passed, 17s, preserving rejection during closing custody.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passed, 256s.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36225538924): passed on `b54f803ea2844878e2cfaa88fdab36a213aa4427`. In [checks-node-changed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36225538924/job/108359286293), this was the sole file: 9 tests passed, Vitest duration 40.66s, supported-runner wall 42.31s, complete test-step wall 43.85s.

CI attributes 66% of Vitest duration to transformation and 29% to tests. The existing archive/history/reopen integration suite exercises real SQLite custody; this repair adds no test or process fixture and keeps all assertions.

The patch reached ready-to-land proof before another maintainer applied the repair and closed this duplicate. Both fixture-proof leases are stopped.

Original failure: CI run `36223265090`, job `108353051732`, `cleanup-service.applied-summary.test.ts` age/reopen case. The fixture and resource owners were unchanged by the originating plugin cleanup. The source race is the unjoined asynchronous close at the fixture's reopen boundary; no production admission barrier was relaxed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Blob/File attachment failures in `pnpm test:ui` when pnpm installs separate Vitest instances for the repository root and UI package. Found while validating #158198; the original package-worker Blob failure was reproduced on clean main.

## User Impact

Developers can run UI package tests with the existing JSDOM adapter applied. Product UI, Gateway, configuration, storage, and dependencies are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preload imported root Vitest while the package launcher started UI Vitest. Each installation owns its own environment object. Native module resolution now searches the executing worker's package first, retaining the preload's dependency scope for plain/eval children that inherit `execArgv` outside the workspace. Native ESM loading preserves the original module semantics.

The regression starts root and UI-package Vitest from the UI directory and reuses the existing Blob-byte/revocation and FileReader assertions. Existing database-verifier tests independently cover inherited child preloads and remain unchanged.

## Evidence

**BLOCKED on hosted CI; not ready to land.** The repair's selected remote checks pass, but the latest CI session-cleanup failure was not reproduced on clean base, and its existing owner repair is still open. The maintainer recovery rule requires stopping here instead of retrying CI or rebasing merely to obtain green.

Head: `b5016e8935a994b47e7b7d892250f0326449a63e`; verified source tree: `e95c798acbe2a946d42ab263dd34592d53ec198e`. One clean rebase onto `fac60421d4549764e4cacf3836b7217905273098` incorporated main's filesystem-boundary fix `9d5ab59b5af`. Both commits were patch-identical: all hunks retained, none dropped.

Fresh proof on Blacksmith Testbox with Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.2, frozen dependencies and verified source:

- `pnpm test test/scripts/run-node-package-bin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **16 passed**, 2.88s Vitest / 3.65s reported test-runner wall. Test execution was 1.838s; the new cases took 0.599s and 0.575s. Per-file hosted timing remains unavailable from the cancelled CI runs.
- Existing JSDOM/custom-element, database-verifier, and filesystem-boundary suites: **60 passed** across three Vitest shards. The unchanged verifier contributes 27 cases and the boundary suite 23. An inherited eval preload probe also passed before the patch-identical rebase.
- Bun 1.4.2 package-worker tests: **16 passed**; the UI's configured Bun fork pool: **nine attachment paste/read cases passed**, 4.49s Vitest.
- Full `pnpm test:ui`: **1,524 files / 25,598 tests passed, four existing skips**, 457.07s Vitest / 463s command wall.
- Complete `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- test/vitest/vitest.jsdom-preload.mts test/scripts/run-node-package-bin.test.ts`: **passed**, 254s, including root test types, dead-export scans, formatting, lint, and guards.
- Original-source negative control at clean main `4f62a433acb72506d050a0fa3faa5d0a977896bf`: the new UI-package worker case fails on the actual Blob `_buffer` error while root Vitest passes from the same UI working directory.
- Independent Codex review through P2: no accepted/actionable findings on the complete corrected patch. Current-head ClawSweeper revision 2, reviewed at 06:08 UTC, also reports no actionable code/security findings. This does not override failed CI.

### Hosted CI disposition

The [latest exact-head run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36222370882) failed and cancelled remaining jobs. Its tested merge was `d0db601813b13f704be33a2e87e5d06711f1a470`, with clean main parent `bed7385166380136b880e21f58232416d5375ebf`.

1. `lint:no-chained-type-assertions` reports `src/gateway/server-chat-progress-snapshot.ts:36`. The same focused canonical rule fails on both the CI merge and clean parent, with identical source/config blobs. Main already contains owner fix `66b812f26e7`, which removes the assertion chain through typed native coercion.
2. `cleanup-service.applied-summary.test.ts` fails the age-pressure reopen case with `Agent database resources are closing`. Replaying the original four CI groups with the original two-worker settings passed the relevant **93 files / 1,366 cases on both parent and merge**, including both age/count reopen cases. Thus the CI failure remains unreproduced; a passing replay is not a fix. The broader replay failed 15 service-path fixture cases on both sides because the temporary checkouts were under `/tmp`, producing `temporary-program` diagnostics. Those group runs are not claimed as passing CI replicas. Parent/merge wall times were 351s / 348s; Testbox used Node 24.19.0 while hosted CI used 24.21.0.

Source inspection identifies an unjoined synchronous-close/reopen boundary in the failing fixture. Existing **open** owner repair [#156419](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156419), head `f7f7505a89a21eda2dafa70cf6d58177c2b77e20`, adds `await closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesAsync()` at the exact reopen and teardown points. It has not merged. No further CI retry, rebase, or merge request was submitted after this stop condition was established.

Earlier CI exposed four inherited-child failures in the initial resolver; the corrected preload restores those unchanged verifier cases. A separate main-side ACPX filesystem import failure was reproduced on its exact CI merge and clean parent, then resolved by the one rebase incorporating `9d5ab59b5af`. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion, dependency, or baseline policy was weakened.

### Remote receipts and limitations

All commands used `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs` with provider `blacksmith-testbox`, explicit lease reuse, and source verification. All owned leases are stopped.

| Lease | Work and result |
| --- | --- |

## What Problem This Solves

The opt-in Crabline Gateway proofs either stop at an unrelated prepared-flow guard or treat a redacted diagnostic path as an executable filename.

Only two existing fixtures and their shared test helper change. No production seam, dependency upgrade, new test case, timeout, retry or skip is added. The retained Crabline 0.1.28 candidate stays isolated from the repository dependency.

## Fixes Found Along the Way

prs.title: test(agents): settle requester retry before advancing time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The requester-wake regression suite can time out real worker I/O while its fake clock jumps across a retry window, failing CI under runner load.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The fixture lets the admitted retry finish before advancing past its worker deadline, while retaining the original 151-second window and exact no-duplicate-continuation assertions.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single 151-second timer advance starts the 30-second requester retry and can also expire its newly created 60-second state-worker task before real I/O completes. The no-next-child case now advances to the persisted retry time, joins the retry's owned work, then advances the remainder of the original window. Native retry timers still execute; no timeout, retry count, assertion, or skip is weakened.

This was found while validating #160038 and is kept separate from the provider refactor.

## Evidence

- [CI 36410960587, job 108891389343](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36410960587/job/108891389343) failed `preserves serial continuation without replaying an accepted wave (cli, next child accepted=false, requester final=false)` with completed cleanup but delivery error `worker task timed out`.
- Managed Codex review: scoped-clean through P2.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3kw5zqt1eqbp5w6tcsp20mj` verified commit `19759973fb6bb3e98badc36595d69459c7b66863`, tree `e7a45c9b7416fff1d417b29ace656cc659afea96`. **20 complete file runs passed (360 cases); three original eight-target job runs passed (24 target invocations); full selected changed checks passed.** The command exited 0, and the lease was stopped.
- The unmodified eight-target baseline passed this replay. The recorded CI failure remains the observed intermittent reproduction; the passing replay is not claimed as a fix.
- Cost: `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` took **46.94s median wall** across 20 runs (range 35.99–69.79s). This existing 18-case E2E suite owns durable settlement and no-replay behavior through real worker I/O plus CLI/native composition; no tests or process boots were added.
- Prior-head `19759973fb6bb3e98badc36595d69459c7b66863` [CI 36419185500](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36419185500) passed. Its file invocation took **74.27s**, with Vitest reporting 72.44s total and approximately 27.5s in tests; transforms dominate the remaining time.

<details>
<summary>Remote commands and original job selection</summary>

All commands ran serially through `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox --id tbx_01m3kw5zqt1eqbp5w6tcsp20mj --timing-json -- OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 OPENCLAW_TESTBOX_REMOTE_RUN=1 ...`, after frozen install and source verification.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main --head HEAD --timed -- src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts
```

The file command ran 20 times without retrying failures. The shard runner used the captured original `OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_TARGETS_JSON`, two inner workers, and one admitted plan to preserve the original job order:

```text
extensions/diagnostics-prometheus/src/install-runtime.e2e.test.ts
extensions/ollama/src/node-inference.paired-node.e2e.test.ts
src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts
src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts
src/channels/plugins/contracts/mattermost-read-authority.contract.test.ts
src/channels/plugins/contracts/session-binding.registry-backed.contract.test.ts
src/commands/onboard-guided.inference.e2e.test.ts
src/plugin-sdk/facade-runtime.test.ts
```

</details>

## Final disposition

Closed as superseded by #160407, merged as `88e3331026a1daf43b093fbfa6a27c7494b72b86`. A fresh main fetch confirmed the same retry-before-clock-advance repair at the fixture owner. This PR was not merged.

The final local follow-up also bounds the recorded retry by the original 151-second horizon. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3m0yhnp5ydfaaavdqvar80d` passed all 18 cases and selected changed checks for final fixture blob `bedd093b4cee162ce17ca28e662d12b0be4490a7` (head `f2d8a8ede1accf04afdfd4e24b03aa9b8719d0c9`). An adverse control changing the native retry delay from 30 seconds to 180 seconds failed specifically at the bound assertion; production bytes were restored before checks. This proves the added assertion, not exact-head CI for the follow-up or a claim that main contains that extra assertion. The original 20-file-run and three-job-run evidence above remains the repeatability evidence for the shared scheduling mechanism.

prs.title: fix: Claude CLI handoffs are recorded as user interruptions
prs.body:
Closes #179486

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a successful `sessions_yield` records that the user interrupted Claude, both in imported history and in the native context used to continue after child completion.

## User Impact

Delegated results resume the same saved Claude conversation with the original request and tool receipts. This prevents new false interruption records; existing saved history is preserved.

A yield now closes the subprocess, so its continuation pays process startup time. Ordinary compatible turns still reuse their warm process.

## Why This Change Was Made

After the existing host confirms consumption of the successful yield result, finish that admitted handoff and join the existing process cleanup owner. Resume the same native session on the next turn. Remove the unused native interrupt request/acknowledgement mechanism and abort-result normalization. Native output remains the session-ID authority, including on a fork's first turn. Genuine cancellation retains its error path.

Related work: #180182 changes imported-history classification. This patch prevents the false interruption from being written into the native conversation and reaching its resumed model input; it does not filter history markers.

## Evidence

Built Gateway, installed Claude CLI, native MCP `sessions_spawn` / `sessions_yield`, child completion, history import, native model request capture and operator `chat.abort`. The native-fork control uses `sessions.create(fork: true, parentSessionKey)` and checks that structured source history survives. Sanitized terminal output:

```json
{
  "before": {
    "importedUserInterruptRows": 1,
    "resumedModelSeesUserInterrupt": true,
    "genuineUserAbort": true,
    "genuineUserRequestClosed": true
  },
  "after": {
    "childCompletionReceived": true,
    "visibleFinals": 1,
    "sameNativeSession": true,
    "resumedHistoryHasOriginalUser": true,
    "resumedHistoryHasYieldResult": true,
    "importedUserInterruptRows": 0,
    "resumedModelSeesUserInterrupt": false,
    "genuineUserAbort": true,
    "genuineUserRequestClosed": true
  },
  "nativeFork": {
    "forkSeedHistoryRetained": true,
    "forkAdoptedNewNativeSession": true,
    "sameNativeSession": true,
    "importedUserInterruptRows": 0,
    "resumedModelSeesUserInterrupt": false,
    "visibleFinals": 1,
    "genuineUserAbort": true,
    "genuineUserRequestClosed": true
  }
}
```

- The causal subprocess regression fails on the clean base at the false user-interruption record; the genuine-cancellation control passes. Final fresh/fork cases verify the old process exits before resuming retained native history. A review-found synthetic fork-ID overwrite also fails on the prior candidate and passes after removing that unsupported field.
- `pnpm test:extension anthropic`: 433 passed, 1 existing Linux-only OOM-score skip across 37 files. Final focused cases and 35 native-ID/core-yield consumers pass. Related imported-history, output-stream and prompt-prefix consumers: 88 passed across 3 files on the earlier candidate; those owners are unchanged by the fork-ID correction.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the complete diff and owning context found no actionable findings after the fork-ID correction. The reviewer used supplied source and proof; it did not rerun the project.
- Canonical plugin-boundary and final test types, type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Final normal `pnpm build` passes in 173.8 seconds, including 157 public SDK subpaths; private-QA runtime build passes. UI startup gzip 318.1 KiB >318.0 KiB remains a nonfatal build advisory.

Actual host: macOS 27.0.1, Claude 2.1.281. External model responses come from controlled local TLS services; native CLI, Gateway, tools and persistence are real. No live Anthropic API or unconstrained-model behavior is claimed. The reporter's Linux/Claude 2.1.294 environment was not run. Task processes, isolated state and local services were cleaned up.

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

Installed-agent toggles now show their expected checked value through Solid's optimistic presentation. The plain owner still admits writes synchronously, verifies the selected agent and connection, and ends disable saving at the config acknowledgement. Rejected writes reconcile with current config and retain the existing visible error.

Consent start and answer operations each get a bounded saving action. The existing admitted enablement state retains the row's enabled intent through human-input checkpoints; each action settles before the next human decision so the native modal can open through its own onSettled lifecycle. A small optional wizard `busy` prop keeps the optimistic flag outside aggregate view props and preserves Cancel behavior and input identity.

The previous map no longer owns both admission and expected values: a plain Set keeps admission, while row-scoped optimistic signals own display. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes detached channel-origin subagents and collector tasks remaining interrupted after a Gateway restart. Follow-up to #180090.

## User Impact

Eligible children resume in their original session and retain their normal parent-completion or collector-result delivery. Session-scoped operators can resume their own child work. Explicit cancellation, replaced sessions, and revoked authority remain terminal.

This does not reconstruct deleted sessions or expired registry records. Previously settled work may need a fresh request in its retained parent or child session after checking for an existing follow-up. Collector retention is unchanged; no configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery required an operator snapshot even for channel-origin children, and collector registration skipped capturing that snapshot entirely. The registry now restores channel requester identity from the child's existing exact-session private claim and captures the existing operator source for collectors. Recovery uses fresh admission with the host-owned exact-session binding, preserving the original result owner.

Startup timing counters sum overlapping requester groups; they can exceed activation wall time. This correctness fix makes no benchmark or startup-speed claim.

## Evidence

The detached restart integration regression fails on the previous code: valid channel children and collectors never dispatch, and recovered operator requests lack the host session binding. It exercises persisted interruption, Gateway replacement, resumed registry custody, and late completion or collector settlement. Channel network delivery and a production deployment are outside this proof.

Validation: all 10 detached restart regression cases pass; changed-file formatting/lint and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass. The isolated independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Five focused neighboring files pass all 206 cases: `subagent-registry.completion-authority.test.ts`, `subagent-registry-restart-recovery.test.ts`, `server.sessions.recover-in-place.test.ts`, `chat-send-subagent-custody.test.ts`, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`. Broad validation is delegated to PR CI; no benchmark was needed.

Production delta: +162 lines; test delta: +151 lines. The added code restores the existing channel requester contract with current parent/Gateway lifetime checks. It does not add a new recovery owner, persisted format, cache, or configuration option; collector launch now shares the existing source capture.

prs.title: fix(telegram): retain peer progress and visible requester follow-up
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can lose its progress card and final follow-up after an agent delegates work to a peer. A new message from the same owner can also suppress an already accepted result. Retained cards can freeze the original checklist and accumulate obsolete running rows when the requester resumes and delegates again.

## User Impact

Pending peer work keeps one automatic card through requester processing and receives a visible final reply in the original conversation. The card follows the requester's updated plan, including checklist removal. Closed follow-up owners remove their own rows; explicit failures remain visible. Meaningful acknowledgments and Telegram streaming preferences are preserved. Private child and peer plans remain excluded.

A new channel message retires the old turn's automation entitlement without cancelling a still-valid original result. The return remains bound to its original caller, conversation and session incarnation; it never borrows the new turn's owner privileges. Private completions remain private. Stop/reset and revoked completion-source authority still prevent delivery.

```text
delegate → retain card → receive peer result → requester processes → final reply
new user message → retire old automation authority; retain valid pending result
stop/reset → close that requester's follow-up
```

Progress remains process-local and is not restored after a Gateway restart. Stop/reset retires the requester's follow-up without cancelling unrelated peer work. This PR does not close the broader durable completion contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing completion owner, requester authority, native delivery and confirmed draft handoff. Ordinary and queued requester turns share that owner. Telegram waits for the first card receipt before adoption and uses its existing compositor queue for plan updates. The new-message repair separates retired automation scope from still-current completion custody, following the distinction already used by native requester continuations. No new job store, polling loop, configuration or permission model is introduced.

The compatible public contract follows the [review recommendation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173026#issuecomment-6190834951): existing `adoptProgressDraft` keeps waiting-only replacement semantics; separate `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` opts adapters into retaining a card alongside an ordinary reply. Telegram and Discord implement both. Old adapters continue normal meaningful-reply delivery. Retained drafts may implement optional `updatePlan`; Telegram does so.

**Human decisions remain:** the channel SDK area owner must accept these additive contracts, and an eligible maintainer must approve security-sensitive changes on the resulting head. Automated proof/review acceptance is not either approval. No human reviewer is assigned.

## Evidence

**Current conflict repair, `e6b45f59ec843bcefba47831be71d9bbf20d18fa`:** integrated pinned main `b9d5ac5f7f56e99e3256982963b701584950e7c4` after a real merge conflict. The manual production resolution removes two obsolete imports from `sessions-send-tool.ts`: the existing prompt helper owns restart wording, and main's shared admission helper owns lane selection. The documentation keeps the Telegram status/final-reply contract together with main's new-turn wording. Main's separated peer admission, native-child completion ownership, source-reply reconciliation and authority cleanup remain intact.

**Scope and regression checks:** 35 authored files without upstream overlap remain byte-identical to `2558d59fcf4e56a05cecf73b6bf5c4935e7d658b`. One additional existing peer fixture now explicitly supplies main's required `claimRequesterTurnCompletion: false`, matching its prior non-child, non-claiming setup. The agent-tool type check first caught the missing field with TS2741 and passes after this one-line adaptation. No assertion was weakened and no new runtime behavior was introduced by the conflict repair. Prior behavioral review is reused for this mechanical integration; no additional review request was made.

**Current local proof:** all 155 targeted cases pass across session-send admission/follow-up (25), requester authority/direct announcement (81), ordinary/queued waiting and automation delivery (47), and real channel/Gateway peer-return/reset flow (2). The initial invocation took 135.50 seconds across four shards including cold compilation. After adapting the fixture, all 12 tests in its file pass again (11.42 seconds). Production `tsconfig.core.json`, agent-tool test types, scoped lint with the canonical core configuration, formatting and authored diff checks pass. An initial lint invocation expanded into plugin-boundary artifact preparation; it was stopped and replaced with the supported core-only lint configuration, not a relaxed rule set.

**Local environment gap reconciled by hosted proof:** the local Gateway-server test type graph remains recorded as failed: ten diagnostics in eight UI files identical to pinned main, with installed Solid `2.0.0-rc.14` versus required `2.0.0-rc.16`. [Hosted core test-types stripe 5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39713110580/job/119610435722) explicitly ran `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json` and passed in 17.7 seconds with exit code 0. prs.title: fix: workspace downloads fail when rsync renames temporary files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes workspace reconciliation failing with “directory not found” when rsync renames a temporary download file while the Gateway checks transfer quotas.

## User Impact

SSH-backed cloud workspace downloads can finish through normal rsync temporary-file renames. Byte and entry limits, directory identity checks, transfer cancellation, and final verification still apply. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared directory walker closes its iterator when metadata lookup encounters a vanished leaf. Retrying or skipping the directory would miss later siblings. The inbound-transfer owner now streams that directory with fs-safe root admission and exact directory identity checks, continuing the same iterator only for a direct missing-leaf lookup. Every enumerated name consumes the entry budget, regular files consume the byte budget, and symlink targets are not traversed. A real scan failure still cancels and joins the writer before returning.

## Evidence

The deterministic disappearance regression failed in all three cases before the production change: an in-quota download was rejected, and byte/entry violations reported the missing leaf instead of evaluating later siblings. The repaired quota tests and real-rsync workspace test pass: 19 tests across two files. Coverage includes replaced root/nested directories, symlink traversal, genuine directory read denial, writer settlement, and final quotas after transfer completion. The changed quota test file takes approximately 0.2 seconds of test execution; the real-rsync sibling takes 12.4 seconds locally.

Focused tests, targeted lint, formatting, production typechecking, and the Gateway test type graphs passed. Independent review found no actionable issues through P2. The broader local changed check stops on the inherited UI E2E type import error fixed on main by da8149b8; this PR does not modify that unrelated test. Exact-head [CI run 36227644256](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36227644256) passed on 497680a395f7fd964daaf490e3d4616267afdf47. The native watcher reports green, and native hosted preparation passed without changing that head.
