prs.title: refactor(process): deslop process
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Process and session runners repeat lifecycle, output, and admission logic, making the same invariants harder to maintain consistently.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Existing cancellation boundaries, output limits and decoding, process cleanup, public exports, and Gateway admission rules are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Share session command startup, cancellation, deadlines, and retained cleanup between extension exec and local Bash. Their output/error adapters retain the existing behavior, including exec cancellation ending at exit while Bash cancellation continues through cleanup.
- Use one path for stdout/stderr capture and decoder flushing, and one predicate for command output termination options.
- Reuse the existing Gateway admission predicates and independent-root admission operation. Remove queue/admission forwarding functions and duplicate normalization after queue-entry construction.
- Delegate PTY termination to the terminal handle, and process-group disappearance checks to their existing owner.
- Retain the supervisor completion promise directly instead of wrapping and unpacking a single-result array.
- Normalize numeric exec options once, share command-failure typing, simplify npm environment defaults, and remove identical Execa encoding branches.
- Delete the Bash test-only global registration and forwarding module; tests import the existing timeout owner directly. Shrink its assertion baseline from 2 to 1 using the canonical counter.

The Execa transport remains: native descriptors, file output, and independently launched applications still require their existing contracts.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passed on Blacksmith Testbox, including core typing, all 25 core-test typecheck shards, root-test typing, lint, format, ratchets, boundaries, and import-cycle checks.
- `pnpm build`: passed, including verification of all 158 public plugin-SDK subpaths.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over the process/session owner suites and real cross-shard callers: all 10 selected Vitest shards passed in 148.33 seconds. Coverage includes broker startup, byte/character caps and decoding, input admission, process-tree extinction, queue deadlines/admission, PTYs, Bash, Git, sandbox transport, update descendants, Gateway restart, and a public-SDK command consumer.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Rebased onto current main with an identical patch (`git range-diff` reports `=`).

[Isolated validation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35824138679), Testbox `tbx_01m36d2x0ennen57za1s379dkr`: the composite command exited 0. The lease was stopped after verification; the wrapper's command result is the proof outcome even if lease cleanup marks the enclosing workflow cancelled.

### Real command behavior observed

The isolated run exercised native processes, not only mocked helpers. `exec.real.test.ts` launched a parent and SIGTERM-resistant descendant, observed `killed: true` on timeout, and verified both PIDs became dead. The real Bash output fixtures exercised output completion with working and failing spill writes. These after-change results came from the same validated patch (`git range-diff` confirmed the publication rebase was patch-identical):

```text
PASS src/agents/sessions/exec.real.test.ts
  does not resolve a timeout while a SIGTERM-resistant descendant is alive — 6031 ms
PASS src/agents/sessions/tools/bash.test.ts
  settles real Bash output for fault-large — 603 ms
  settles real Bash output for writable-large — 524 ms
  settles real Bash output for fault-small — 541 ms
  surfaces a configured shell launch error — 7 ms
  ignores output callbacks after execution settles — 24 ms
PASS src/agents/sessions/tools/bash-termination.test.ts
  does not report a timeout until forced tree cleanup settles — 163 ms
All 10 selected Vitest shards passed in 148.33 seconds.
```

The last termination case is a deterministic deferred-cleanup boundary test; it complements the native-process cases above. This is runtime behavior evidence, not a not-applicable proof assessment.

The first local run hit three 20-second timeouts in the owned-worker relay suite while the 16-CPU host had a load average near 89 (later 164); its other cases took 14–19 seconds. The unchanged suite passed in the isolated Linux run. No timeout or assertion was weakened, and this is not claimed as a fix for the local contention. Initial static failures were corrected with the exact Bash assertion-baseline shrink and two type-only declarations in the shared helper.

Changed-test cost on that contended host: `pnpm test src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 19 tests in 78.15 seconds wall; `pnpm test src/process/supervisor/adapters/pty.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 17 tests in 74.45 seconds wall. The new cancellation cases use fake timers. Bash's test change only replaces its deleted forwarding import; its existing real-output cases passed in the isolated suite.

The requested production-filter shortstat is `18 files changed, 362 insertions(+), 614 deletions(-)` (**252 net lines removed**). That filter includes 15 lines of deleted test infrastructure; **production-only removal is 237 lines**. This remains below the requested reduction target.

### CI follow-up

The initial exact-head CI run has 165 passing checks but is blocked by [checks-node-compact-small-43](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35830311139/job/107081505324). Its tooling group passed 1,084 tests and failed `managed-child-process > joins nested preparation cleanup (resistant=true, abort=true)`: the post-cleanup assertion observed one remaining non-zombie PID.

That fixture executes the separate, unchanged scripts-side managed-process runner and TSX shim. Its inspected implementation dependency graph does not overlap this PR's changed implementation files. The CI log does not identify the surviving PID's fixture role or start identity, so the cause is not established. The original-order Linux/Node 24.19.0 replay with the same 41 files and two workers passed all 1,085 tests, including the failing case (5,218 ms), on Testbox `tbx_01m36m1kadyh9hd3ekxfa5a85j` ([replay run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35834051420)). A passing replay is not claimed as a fix. No assertion, timeout, or CI result has been weakened or rerun for a green result; the original CI failure remains unresolved.

prs.title: fix: read merge state as the publishing GitHub account
prs.body:
Related: #154652

## What Problem This Solves

Native landing can reject a fully green PR when the shared GitHub reader reports review requirements that do not apply to the publishing account.

## User Impact

Maintainers can land eligible PRs using their actual GitHub permissions. Required CI, review, identity, pinned-head checks, and retained merge outcomes remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read merge observations and squash previews through the existing protected JSON-stdin CLI route. The new reader accepts only fixed observe/preview operations, preserves enterprise hostname ports, and retains primary-quota fallback without classifying mutations as reads. Ordinary cached metadata reads keep their existing owner.

The real failure was verified with identical query variables, main commit, and PR head: the relay returned `MERGEABLE/BLOCKED`, while the publishing account returned `MERGEABLE/CLEAN`. The repaired helper returns the publishing account's result through its actual read-only entrypoint.

## Evidence

- A native regression failed at the original BLOCKED admission and passes with the repair, including exactly one recorded merge dispatch.
- Focused publisher, observation/preview quota-fallback, and mutation non-replay checks passed: four tests in 26.75 seconds. New CLI contract cases preserve enterprise ports and reject mutation mode before invoking GitHub (136 ms, 138 ms, and 66 ms).
- The broader native suite passed 149 of 150 cases in 544.47 seconds. One existing same-workflow REST fixture exceeded its 20-second child deadline; that exact case passed serially in 13.913 seconds. The original failure is retained as an unexplained timing failure; no deadline, retry, or assertion was weakened.
- Scoped formatting, typecheck, lint, import/dead-export, and policy guards passed. Independent P0/P1 review is clean.

No merge permissions or repository rules are changed. This is the bounded tooling repair needed to finish the already-reviewed dependency update.

The initial implementation head passed every hosted test job. The new native publishing-account regression took 3.660 seconds; the three CLI contract cases took 89, 69, and 37 ms (195 ms total). These are reported case durations, not file wall times.

CI's full unused-file scan identified the shell-launched reader as a missing entrypoint. It is now declared beside the existing REST CLI in the established Knip entry list; no ignore or baseline exception was added. The exact production/full-tree unused-file gate passes with zero entries, and fresh independent P1 review is clean.

Follow-up CI exposed two fake GitHub clients that parsed read queries only from command-line arguments, plus assertions that identified mutations or snapshots from that transport shape. The fixtures now decode JSON input and record the operation while preserving exact-head, single-dispatch, freshness, writer identity, and admin-revocation assertions. The original supervised-merge failure reproduced before repair; all seven affected ordinary, pending-auto, and authorization cases pass in 52.07 seconds across three files. The completed prior-head CI reported no other failures.

The final fixture repair passes local changed checks (types, policy/dependency guards, dead exports, and lint) and fresh independent P1 review. It changes only three test files, with 37 insertions and 38 deletions; no assertions, deadlines, production guards, or repository permissions are weakened.

prs.title: improve(test): bound full-suite infrastructure process groups
prs.body:
Related: #139428

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary full-suite runs currently place the entire infrastructure test selection in one long-lived process group.

## User Impact

No product-facing change. Supported full-suite runs can execute infrastructure tests in bounded whole-file groups under the existing worker ceiling. Explicit selections and unsupported platforms keep their existing behavior. This remains a draft pending real-workload performance evidence; no speedup is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Vitest’s native file collection to preserve the configured selection, then assign exact include files to groups of at most 150 files. Preparation, reporting and scheduling consume the resulting groups. Retain include files when process completion is uncertain, and preserve signal cleanup. The tests preserve upstream fixture-lifetime repairs and exercise Windows fallback without pretending that Windows provides verified POSIX process groups.

## Evidence

- Current complete admission file: 142 passed; all 127 original cases retained plus 15 regression cases. Four complete runner/report/cleanup/process siblings: 235 passed on the preceding base, with relevant owner inputs unchanged.
- Current native inventory: 1490 unique infrastructure files. Positive regression verifies native collection and native acceptance of each exact chunk. Fault cases cover uncertain completion, malformed inventory, missing files, watchdogs and cleanup signals.
- Full changed-file gate passed; independent review is clean through P2. Initial typechecks exposed an unchanged-main import error, resolved by adopting upstream #157659 rather than adding a duplicate fix.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/test-projects-build-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21.01s command wall, 20.12s Vitest, approximately 699MB maximum RSS on macOS/Node 24.19. Original file cost 13.88s before the 15 added cases. This is test cost, not workload performance evidence.
- [Native Windows replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36076285424) at this exact commit passed: 100 cases passed and 42 existing POSIX-only cases skipped, including all 15 new cases passing. Native win32/x64, Node 24.19, one worker; 6.60s Vitest and 7.45s wrapper. Source/dependency bindings and project order matched. Actions owns final runner teardown; descendant settlement is not independently attested.
- Full selected-workload performance comparison remains pending.

prs.title: test(codex): show native output-fidelity failure context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

[Full release validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35562648356/job/106218529079) can fail the native Codex output-fidelity fixture with `Expected native command execution` without showing the native tool response or the events that arrived.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. The next fixture failure will include enough synthetic context to distinguish a command rejection from a missing or late completion event. The underlying failure remains unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing failure label now includes the first 2,000 response characters and event method, item type, ID, and status. The fixture uses an isolated native home and environment, fixed synthetic file contents, and an anonymous loopback provider; request bodies, environment values, and full notification payloads are not captured. Execution, ordering, timeouts, and assertion outcomes are unchanged.

## Evidence

On base `a9b3c3a151cdaed1045f66cbc7605cbe4ed1a7c4`, the two native cases and 11 output-fidelity unit cases passed on macOS. The combined single-worker command took 196.72 seconds; the native file reported 64.75 seconds in Vitest, primarily source transformation. The full selected changed gate and independent P2 review passed.

Both actual native cases also passed in the [Linux CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35612418856/job/106374911545) for this exact head. Its group passed 335 tests across 12 files without skips, taking 141.69 seconds in Vitest and 144.24 seconds in the wrapper, on Ubuntu 24.04.3 x64 / Node 24.19.0. The diagnostic did not fire, so this pass does not identify the original failure's cause. An earlier Testbox attempt stopped during source sync and supplies no test proof.

The overall CI run is red on a separate question-refresh callback assertion. [The fixture-clock repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154968) reproduces the missing callback under controlled preparation-budget exhaustion and preserves the original assertions; historical Linux timing attribution remains unconfirmed. This PR does not claim a green overall workflow or an event-order fix.

prs.title: fix(plugins): preserve Git staging under group-writable umasks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Git plugin installation under a group-writable umask creates a staging parent that the workspace safety check rejects, losing the intended same-filesystem staging path.

## User Impact

New Git plugin staging parents remain admissible under umask 0002. Existing directory permissions and stricter operator umasks are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Request mode 0755 when creating the staging parent, matching normal umask 0022 behavior while preventing group/world write bits. Keep the real workspace admission checks, pre-clone fallback, and no-retry-after-callback behavior unchanged. Extend the existing filesystem placement test to inspect the resulting permission bits.

## Evidence

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3166bxexfvgnc9r5m2bcy28`, Linux with umask 0002, [proof run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35563872939). A real filesystem probe confirmed the original 0775 parent was refused and the 0755 parent admitted. The original owner produced two failures with the strengthened assertion; the final 30-case owner file passed in 12.666s, and all 114 sibling cases passed.

Full build, selected changed checks, and independent P2 review passed. This fixes a production creator defect exposed by testing; failed baseline runtime is not a speedup claim. Hosted CI is required before landing.

prs.title: perf(sqlite): avoid loading unrelated memory helpers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SQLite snapshot and backup paths import the broad memory-engine storage barrel to access one SQLite extension loader. Loading the unrelated helpers adds startup work to these paths and their tests.

## User Impact

Snapshot and backup callers load less unrelated code while preserving their SQLite behavior. The focused snapshot command saves a conservative 1.9–2.6 seconds against the warmed baseline. No schema, durability, recovery, updater, or public SDK contract changes. There is no memory-saving claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Import the existing `host/sqlite-vec` loader directly in three core callers and the Git-backup fixture. The loader implementation, health checks, closed-handle guard, and extension-loading cleanup are unchanged. Existing tests continue to exercise real SQLite and vector setup; no assertions or cases are removed.

## Evidence

Crabbox / Blacksmith Testbox proof against base `c79a03cd8a36` and candidate `c481f1d60ab4` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35590735497)) preserved all 41 snapshot case statuses: 39 passes and two existing platform skips in each natural ABBA arm. The canonical `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-snapshot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` command, with JSON/verbose reporting, took A1 **27.651s**, B1 **16.144s**, B2 **15.448s**, A2 **18.068s**. A1 was colder; comparison with warm A2 gives the conservative **1.9–2.6s** saving. Test-body times stayed around 1.1–1.2s, locating the gain in import/startup work. Mean peak RSS increased 1.92%.

All 191 sibling cases passed with five existing skips. Single-file command walls using the same runner and `--maxWorkers=1` were 27.837s for backup verification, 29.182s for backup SQLite, 26.149s for the local repository, 19.985s for repository directory identity, 39.304s for Git backup, 17.485s for Git-backup failures, and 1.870s for the loader. Full build passed in 490.153s and selected changed checks in 2054.836s. Source hashes match the candidate, and the unchanged four-import patch has a clean independent review.

Current [CI run 35602185438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35602185438), attempt 1, passed the aggregate gate for this head. It tested merge `90e7d0c1e3a2926579b877466b59b2b9e79a8f27` on main parent `cc69fd0745d8ecb9072cb49c59b000e5d81ebcaf`. Actual passing-case duration sums from its logs are below. These exclude imports/setup and are not whole-file or command walls.

| File | CI test-body seconds | Passed / existing skips |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/infra/sqlite-snapshot.test.ts` | 1.128 | 39 / 2 |
| `src/snapshot/git-backup.test.ts` | 15.161 | 28 / 1 |
| `src/commands/backup-verify.test.ts` | 0.460 | 72 / 1 |
| `src/snapshot/local-repository.test.ts` | 1.794 | 63 / 3 |
| `src/snapshot/git-backup-failure.test.ts` | 0.512 | 3 / 0 |

The historical [release-check timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35560058268/job/106211261835) matches the prepared-tarball inspection hang repaired in [#154567](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154567). That owner reproduced a blocked npm inventory subprocess, removed it by collecting entry names and size during existing strict tar extraction, and added a regression rejecting the old subprocess path. The historical run captured no blocked-phase trace, so attribution of that precise incident remains inferred; no specific userspace GC stack was captured. The green CI merge contains this owning fix, with byte-identical release-check implementation and test, so its success is validation of fixed source.

Qualification reuses the owner's reported 20 standalone runs and 115 sibling cases, plus [three complete original-order Crabbox replays](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35698720454) newly completed on the fixed CI merge: **32 files, 658 passes, zero failures, and one existing skip each**, in **218.557s / 175.795s / 213.749s**. All 45 source hashes were verified before and after the runs. The sole omitted historical file was retired upstream in #154215. The extra passing case relative to the earlier 657-pass report comes from an unchanged ownership table expanding a newly added registry entry from #153216; no case was removed. These replays used Node 24.19.0, two-CPU affinity, and 16.56 GB RAM versus the original runner's 8.22 GB. Matching-resource reproduction belongs to the owner's evidence. The owner's differently selected paired runs and this campaign's earlier pre-fix replay receive no credit as these three fixed-source original-order runs.

A source audit against main `b85727e388e0` confirms all four old imports remain and the same loader is still reexported by the barrel. The four substitutions merge cleanly while retaining the later concurrent-recovery fix in #155075. The recorded green CI predates that later main change; native preparation and live merge gates still own admission against the current base.

prs.title: improve(gateway): avoid repeated placement reads during session refresh
prs.body:
Related: #150270

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing many changed session rows repeatedly queries and decodes the same worker-placement facts on the Gateway thread.

## User Impact

Session refreshes share placement, move, and workspace-result facts within each bounded synchronous slice. List, description, and archived-session fields keep their existing behavior. No configuration or schema migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing placement store supplies one batch to the resident session owner, and reconciliation reuses the decoded placements. Exact requested session IDs remain the result keys, including IDs whose database lookup is normalized. Publication epochs invalidate prepared facts before they can be committed, and cold or previously unprepared rows retain exact reads.

The obsolete independent projection getters are removed with their callers. This is a prerequisite optimization for the broader worker-offload work in #150270; that work still needs to integrate with the current resident owner.

## Evidence

- 62 focused cases passed, including actual kernel startup, dirty-row query bounds, archived pages during catalog renewal, workspace-result state, and exact requested-ID behavior.
- Four ordinary/locked, prepared/exact requested-ID regressions failed before the normalization correction and passed afterward.
- Relevant type, formatting, lint, and changed-file checks passed. Independent review through P2 has no actionable findings.

Matched CPU and callback-gap measurements remain a pre-merge check. An earlier macOS experiment used a different request path and had mixed or worse whole-burst results; it is not performance acceptance for this candidate. The new comparison includes normal background scheduling and accounts separately for the response and completed deferred work. No production-wide saving is claimed.

prs.title: fix: diagnose gateway startup heap exhaustion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where operators cannot identify which gateway startup action exhausts the JavaScript heap because existing startup traces are emitted only after an action finishes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add temporary, bounded startup diagnostics immediately before and after startup actions, unusually broad SQLite reads, and task maintenance. SQLite diagnostics include only allowlisted table and column names, query shape, row counts, call sites, and memory usage; SQL text, bound values, session identifiers, and message contents are excluded. There are no schema changes or changes to returned query results.

This is a diagnostic-only candidate for reproducing a startup crash. It should not be merged as the permanent fix before identifying the operation responsible.

## User Impact

Operators can identify the precise startup action and query shape preceding a gateway heap crash. There is no intended behavior change for end users.

## Evidence

- 54 focused gateway, SQLite, and task-maintenance tests pass.
- Added regression coverage proves private session identifiers and message contents never appear in emitted query diagnostics.
- Changed-file formatting and lint checks pass.
- Independent structured review found no accepted or actionable findings; the changed-content secret scan passed.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve SQLite reads when cwd becomes unavailable
prs.body:
## Superseded

Superseded by canonical commit [8e303782bb567](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8e303782bb5677edbb27c77c222b568fb692dbbf), which chooses a valid temporary child working directory when the host cwd pathname is unavailable.

The bounded caller review confirmed that the relevant database and staging paths, worker entry point, and preload are absolute. Canonical auth separately checks live owner authority and physical database identity before and after the read; cwd is execution context, not that authority. The existing staging and session owners can therefore keep a concrete launch cwd. No remaining requirement justifies this PR's unknown-cwd types, disabled reuse, or per-preparation staging runtime.

A focused independent P0–P2 comparison found that this alternative's strict canonical-auth cwd check could reject an otherwise valid read. That finding is accepted, and this alternative will not land. The unchanged original unavailable-cwd updater regression also passed on clean main commit `25eb94b22ac699f7878f2889160a9d24264c1522`, which includes the canonical fix: one passed, 36 skipped, 19.40 seconds in Vitest. The canonical commit separately records its [Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36743809113).

The earlier 117-test and [Package Acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36736504189) results remain historical evidence for the alternative candidate, not a reason to retain its extra implementation. No physical cwd-removal experiment was performed. The accepted auto-merge request was confirmed cancelled; no merge request from the later recovery attempts was dispatched.

<details>
<summary>Historical proposal and validation</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an update can fail during read-only SQLite inspection after package replacement makes the original working-directory pathname unavailable.

## User Impact

User impact: updates continue reading their already selected state paths and retain normal snapshot cleanup instead of failing on a fresh working-directory lookup. Canonical auth reads still require a captured working directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native snapshot children can inherit cwd when its pathname is unavailable. Such preparations require absolute inputs and own separate staging sessions through retirement; unknown cwd never qualifies session reuse. The existing generation, native-child, source-identity, and cleanup owners remain responsible for the operation. No configuration, schema, persistence, or permission change is introduced.

## Evidence

The existing unavailable-cwd updater regression failed on the original source and passes with this repair. The regression simulates the failed cwd lookup; it does not remove or replace a live source directory. The final focused worker run passed 116 tests across seven files (58.96 seconds in Vitest), including native cleanup, snapshot staging, source isolation, auth broker behavior, and relative-path rejection. The updater regression passed separately (20.40 seconds in Vitest). Core production and all core-test typecheck shards passed. Selected changed-file guards, formatting, and lint passed after correcting a union construction and parameter reassignment caught during validation. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects.

Changed-file test-body timings from the existing final verbose run (sum of every reported case duration; excludes import/setup):

| Changed test file | Cases | Reported test time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `sqlite-readonly-native-resource.test.ts` | 17 | 34.383 s |
| `sqlite-readonly-worker.test.ts` | 45 | 14.303 s |
| `sqlite-readonly-worker.auth.test.ts` | 22 | 22.876 s |
| `sqlite-snapshot-staging-runtime.test.ts` | 8 | 0.186 s |

The native-resource file includes real child/process cleanup and snapshot-custody cases; its three new path-rejection cases exercise the RPC boundary before the copy or staging command is dispatched. These timings reuse the completed run rather than claiming separate per-file wall-clock measurements. The ordinary published 2026.9.5 → exact `aae754c87d3b` candidate upgrade cell passed in [Package Acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36736504189). The installed updater, candidate identity, automatic migration, Doctor, state survival, dependency cleanup, and Gateway health/readiness/status passed (1,010 seconds). The lane used manual restart; its first-hop post-core snapshot was unavailable. It does not exercise physical cwd removal.

Maintainer-requested repair following the candidate-update receipt migration in #161813.

Maintainer review resolution: [ClawSweeper’s completed review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161916#issuecomment-5913396645) found no code or security defect. Its timing request is addressed above. The physical-directory experiment remains outside this repair’s explicit scope; the maintained ordinary published-updater compatibility cell passed. Missing-cwd behavior is covered by the failing-getcwd regression and real native child/IPC and cleanup coverage, without claiming that the installed lane physically removes cwd.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36728884843) failed one pre-existing catalog source-ABA assertion and its aggregate. That assertion always expects foreground rejection, although the unchanged Gateway API may return retained catalog data after five seconds. The unmodified exact baseline file passed 12/12 locally. A baseline-only scheduling probe then held its existing provider barrier for 5.5 seconds, preserving production code and original assertions: the same assertion failed while the other 11 cases passed. This is a controlled scheduling variant, not a claim that the unmodified baseline failed or that CI’s exact timer settlement was instrumented. Background publication, owner and credential fences remain required. The failure was independently attributed and reviewed; any landing uses the authorized pre-existing-CI exception while preserving the failed CI status and enforcing security and required reviews.

The regression runs two ordered files in a real fork and checks the durable policy value; existing cleanup-failure and retained-custody assertions remain intact.

The nested fixture now uses the maintained Vitest runner and compiled-subprocess plugin. This prepares its real SQLite worker during collection and preserves the supplied worker-cache policy without inheriting the parent run's descriptor or cache slot. The original five-second action deadline remains.

## Evidence

A controlled run on Linux/Node 24.19.0 restored the old mapping and reproduced `Shared-state worker opening path changed` through the real policy writer in 278 ms. ## What Problem This Solves

Plugin migration can lose its lifecycle lease when a cached database worker still points at a retired path after the database moves.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Matching physical file identity does not renew a worker's original path admission. The existing owner now checks that admission, joins retirement of an invalid idle actor, and opens under the unchanged current caller. Cleanup failures still propagate. Expired schema scopes retain their existing error behavior, including the registry readers that must reject an expired scope.

## Evidence

On Linux/Node 24.19.0, three real relocation regressions fail on the original owner and pass after the repair: two writes recreate the retired path, and a write during an active callback is incorrectly accepted. The added cases take about 2.46 seconds; the focused command takes 24.16 seconds.

The 97-case owner/schema/registry proof passes in 53.78 seconds, including unchanged expired-scope assertions. The current version of the failing CI group passes 436 tests with two skips in 165.53 seconds; four retired Task paths are absent from current main. Production and touched test types, scoped lint, guards, deslop, and independent review through P2 passed.

The earlier broad changed check encountered an unrelated media-test type error fixed by #159836. Main also already contains async migration-fixture cleanup from #159733; this change preserves that owner and adds the full refusal receipt to assertion failures. prs.title: fix: keep Gateway rollback-compatible after additive SQLite columns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where rolling a Gateway back to an older build at the same SQLite schema version could refuse startup after a newer build added a backward-compatible nullable column. This occurred when `73bdb4b924f` added `worktrees.run_end_cleanup_json TEXT` at state schema v6 and the older `e4309e0c` verifier treated that safe extra column as drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical SQLite verifier now has an owner-controlled forward-compatibility mode for unknown bare nullable `STRICT` datatype columns on stable tables. Global and per-agent database owners enable it; known-column drift, optional-table drift, defaults, constraints, unique indexes, triggers, virtual schemas, and table options remain exact and fail closed.

This is the smallest owner-boundary repair and does not change either SQLite schema version. The database policy and public schema reference now document the compatible no-version-bump column shape.

## User Impact

Operators can roll back across compatible same-version additive column changes without the Gateway being bricked by a benign schema mismatch. Incompatible or ambiguous schema changes continue to require a version bump and are still refused.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kzjpq4ssk1x44v7xm8gws91g`: [combined proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/31301195404)
  - `src/infra/sqlite-schema-contract.test.ts`: 33 passed
  - `src/state/openclaw-database-maintenance.test.ts`: 16 passed
  - exact older-to-newer `run_end_cleanup_json` repair regression: 1 passed
  - `pnpm check:changed`: core, coreTests, and docs lanes passed, including typechecks, lint, max-lines, dead-code, database-first, import-cycle, and schema-version guards
  - docs index and formatting checks passed
- Autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, high): clean, no accepted/actionable findings (confidence 0.99)
- Production LOC: +29/-8 (net +21); tests: +129/-0; policy/docs: +3/-1. The production growth establishes the shared schema-compatibility ownership boundary for both database families.

prs.title: fix(auth): restore the previous connection after failed sign-in activation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The original defect has been fixed independently on `main` by [cd75f44](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cd75f44f9cd3fb2476beb313f87d8b8acd50f2f5), which restores credentials before recovery auth reads and consumes the successful rollback receipt. This draft is superseded; it retains the independent reproduction and validation below and does not request landing. The read-only comparison used `main` at `2d85731967cbcc6acf3c6913436af9e0f93701ea`.

## User Impact

The intended behavior is that the replacement reports its activation error while the previous connection remains usable without restarting the Gateway. The isolated public Gateway proof below observed that behavior on this draft’s exact commit. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery published the restored configuration before rolling back its credential. A reload could capture auth readers between those operations, then correctly reject them as stale when rollback changed the auth revision. Restore the credential in the existing recovery preparation hook, before readers start, and share its completion result with post-write recovery. A refused rollback retains its original error and is never retried; config and credential ownership checks remain intact.

Upstream implements the same preparation ordering. This draft additionally retains a rejected rollback result, whereas upstream may invoke a refused rollback again after config undo. Direct inspection of the real owners found no material remaining defect: each call retains compare-and-swap ownership checks, newer values remain protected, and failed recovery still reports failure. The synthetic throwing-rollback test establishes call count and error-object retention, not a further user-visible regression on upstream. No duplicate production change is proposed.

Historical draft production delta: +10/-1, net +9 lines, including the ordering comments. The shared completion result covers both callback orders and both success and failure without adding another recovery path. Tests: +163/-10, net +153 lines.

## Evidence

- Before: unchanged production base `3420ad17`, with a scheduling barrier around real readers and rollback, reproduces the hosted `AuthProfileRuntimeReadStaleError`: one failure/three passes alone, and one failure/121 passes in the original nine-file batch. It controls a legal race schedule and preserves the actual auth guards and recovery owners.
- After: Exact `b046c09bff3e797f78ce69f950475225b04e798d` passed 20 standalone runs (4 cases each) and three original nine-file runs (122 cases each): 446 case executions, with unchanged source and empty owned process groups. The original-group runs took 44.31/45.30/45.32 seconds. Six coordinator cases cover both callback orders, no-write, unclaimed and inline recovery, and original rollback failure. The 53 related wizard, credential lifetime and concurrent-owner tests passed.
- Changed-file cost through the supported worktree test wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`: `config-reload.activation.integration.test.ts` median 16.18 seconds across 20 runs (16.15–17.20); the new six-case `setup-inference-transition.test.ts` took 29.85 seconds, including 19.69 seconds of cold worker compilation (40 ms of cases). These are local wall times; hosted costs are not yet available.
- Canonical runtime preparation passed in 41.28 seconds and stamped the exact commit. A strict artifact fence verified physical separation from both installed Gateways; no native profile was changed.
- **Public Gateway supplement passed on exact `b046c09`** through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/setup-inference.first-signin.integration.test.ts`: exit 0, 34.96 seconds. It exercised first sign-in, actual `openclaw.setup.activate.start` / `wizard.next` replacement activation, one injected post-promotion preparation failure and one real credential rollback. It verified the ordinary activation error, restoration of the agents/models/gateway/plugins/auth sections, the previous credential and model route, the saved replacement remaining inactive, and no recovery restart. Final `openclaw.setup.verify` succeeded with the previous synthetic credential after the real reload-settlement predicate became true and one explicit retry. The first verification after recovery returned the documented readiness-unavailable result despite completing its working-credential probe; that observation is retained.
- This is one after-only public RPC composition with controlled provider transport, supplementing the paired real-reloader regression. It is not browser, live-provider, native-profile, repeated-public-run, or current-main execution proof. Four earlier incomplete attempts remain retained: three stopped at initial verification; one diagnostic reached rollback but used an invalid temporary auth-read barrier. All temporary fixture bytes were restored; permanent source/build identities stayed unchanged; owned process groups and observed native temporary state settled.
- Full changed checks passed, including production types, all 27 test type graphs, lint, format, dead exports and guards. Independent source review found no actionable P0-P2 issues; the required automated review also passed at its default P0 scope.

This pre-existing failure surfaced in [the updater repair CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36622847591). [That PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161338) remains separate. The conflict is confined to the production transition and its existing integration regression, both changed by the upstream fix; the added coordinator test merges cleanly. Metadata workflows passed, but no normal CI proof is claimed for this conflicting draft. Native deployment remains separate and unverified by this PR. prs.title: fix(ui): resolve a bare filename link to its nested workspace file
prs.body:
Fixes #173975

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI turns an inline-code filename in an assistant message into a file link.
The link asked the Gateway for that bare name, which resolves against the workspace
root, so a file that lives in a nested workspace directory answered
`session file not found` while an explicit full-path link to the same file opened
fine. The preview then showed the generic missing-file message even though the file
was present and readable.

## User Impact

A basename link now opens the file it names when the session workspace holds exactly
one file with that name. The reported case - `ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md` inside
`labs/file-organizer/output/sorted-copy-001/` - opens instead of failing.

References that cannot be resolved honestly keep the existing failure and never open
a different file: several files share the name, the workspace search was truncated,
the only match sits outside the workspace root, the match is a directory, or the
reference already carries a path (`labs/output/REPORT.md`). Absolute and
`../`-bearing references are never searched.

Nothing else changes: authorization still runs on `sessions.files.get`, the
`session_file_too_large` metadata fallback and the existing `resolveError` copy are
untouched, and no configuration or migration is involved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat reference carries only the displayed name, so the client is the only layer
that knows a basename was intended and can offer a second look before reporting it
missing. The lookup reuses the existing workspace search the Files browser already
uses (`sessions.files.list` with `search`), and retries the normal read with the
resolved path, so every existing path check and admission step still applies.

A single exact match is required. Ambiguity or a truncated listing keeps the original
failure rather than silently picking whichever entry the search returned first -
the same guard the reporter validated in their local workaround.

## Evidence

New owner test `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace-reference.test.ts`
(6 cases) drives the shipped entry point `openSessionWorkspaceFile` with the existing
session-capability fixture: one nested match resolves and re-reads by the resolved
path; four negative cases (ambiguous, truncated, escaping, directory) keep the
missing-file failure; a path-bearing reference never searches.

- Red before the source change: `5 failed | 1 passed (6)` - the resolution case and
  all four guards fail with `session file not found`.
- Green after: `6 passed (6)`.
- The pre-existing owner suite `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.test.ts`
  still passes, as do the sibling `chat-session-workspace-{artifacts,loading,rail}`
  suites (27 passed).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` pass on both changed files.

The first red/green pair ran on the `2026-10-15` main tree; after rebasing onto
`main@32748bce75c` (which merged the Files download work in `#172042`) the red/green
pair was re-run on the same source and reproduced exactly: `5 failed | 1 passed`
before, `6 passed` after.

## Not verified

- `tsgo` was not run over the full UI graph locally; the day-old worktree used for the
  local runs predates the Files download merge, so the later rebase is verified by the
  focused suites above rather than a whole-graph type check.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace.ts` is also touched by the open
  `#162552` (binary/PDF file links); this change is additive to the loader wrapper and
  the bare-name guard, so it should rebase, but the overlap is worth a reviewer's eye.

## AI Assistance

AI (Codex) drafted the analysis, the code change, and the tests, and ran the local
verification above. A human reviewed the diff before submission.

## Latest CI repair (2b790dcff5)

- Fixed `check-test-types-core-3` by typing the `setFile` mocks against `SessionWorkspaceHost["sessions"]["setFile"]`, returning the complete session-file shape, and narrowing the Markdown preview before asserting its fields.
- Focused owner suite: `1 passed (9 tests)`.

## Latest repair and real Gateway/browser proof (82b3d9769)

- `82b3d9769` separates VCS metadata (`.git`, `.hg`) from content directories that make a search incomplete (`dist`, `node_modules`, and similar build/cache roots). Without this, every normal Git checkout returned `truncated: true` merely because `.git` existed, so the bare-name fallback could never resolve an otherwise unique file. Regression coverage now proves both sides of that split.
- Validation on this head: `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-files.test.ts` passed `44/44`; `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` passed on both changed files; `pnpm build:runtime` completed.
- Real environment: built this head, launched a Gateway on loopback with Control UI and a synthetic OpenAI Responses fixture, then clicked the inline-code `ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md` link in the served browser UI.
- The observed Gateway RPC sequence was:

  ```text
  sessions.files.get  {"path":"ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md"}
    -> session_file_not_found
  sessions.files.list {"search":"ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md"}
    -> exactly one nested match, no truncated flag
  sessions.files.get  {"path":"<workspace>/labs/file-organizer/output/sorted-copy-001/ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md"}
    -> success
  sessions.files.set  {"path":"<same nested path>"}
    -> success (saved sha256 fd14ff0861a48056821b55d61508994e4cff54c665961cdd156ac5294a29bf54)
  ```

- The browser opened the nested file, showed `NESTED-MARKER-174009`, and the edit/save round-trip reached disk.
- After adding `dist/ORGANIZATION_REPORT.md`, the same search returned the nested match with `truncated: true`; the UI did not retry the read and showed `session file not found`, so it refused to choose an arbitrary duplicate.
- Real local artifacts from this run: `resolved.png` (sha256 `e5c3faddf86a7c23408c1135d26b0c364ea8009e468c7b142f031a2d8480121c`), `saved.png` (`42351dfcc611f8d10f0553b374afe897f299a6cdfa85f1382a3920dac1967486`), `ambiguous-guard.png` (`399f3e2dd228a07462c16238f39ea6f93c80208428fe1b87747f06dd1798a53e`), and the full RPC trace `proof.json` (`48601c0867d87ce0fbb7e3eecce7558c6ebfa53593bb9f64f34a0b56775eab17`).

prs.title: refactor(sessions): move persisted member writes off the Gateway thread
prs.body:
Builds on the agent database execution foundation in #153150 and test isolation in #153286, both landed on `main`. This PR targets `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Adding or removing a persisted session member executes ordinary SQLite writes on the Gateway thread.

## User Impact

Membership row mutations now run through the existing agent database worker. Authorization, responses, events, private database permissions, duplicate adds, and absent removals keep their existing behavior. Incognito membership retains its process-held native owner. No schema, retention, RPC, SDK, or migration contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Finite membership commands use the canonical agent executor and synchronous connection-bound kernels. Transaction and commit admission revalidate live manager authority, and the transaction checks the exact session instance and removal compare-and-swap conditions. Callers await durable completion.

The current-main integration preserves retained sharing facts: acknowledged writes update the existing projection before row observers run, while uncertain outcomes invalidate it. The retained-authorization regression fails with raw publication and passes for both durable and incognito stores after this integration. Existing evidence codecs moved to their sharing-identity owner without changing values or policy.

## Evidence

Local validation below is bound to `054198a9a5394b5c8ab8c452479897ffb341b09f`, based on main `7fb336731e19227871609972fb6f6c7cb071b6c0`. Hosted checks and review must bind the new published head.

- All 141 focused cases across 11 files passed, including registered Gateway mutations, recovery and GitHub publication callers, retained authorization, exact-instance/removal checks, events, permission repair, physical ownership, and worker cleanup.
- All 247 routing controls, the complete normal selected checks, and `pnpm build` passed on the frozen current-main candidate. Fresh source and proof-harness review through P2 found no actionable findings.
- Actual signed loopback Gateway proof passed 19 RPCs/nine mutations across cold, warm, and reopen flows, six durable readbacks, and two private-permission drift checks. It exited naturally with code 0 and no cleanup errors. Source, build artifacts, installation topology, runtime bytes, and the mapped SQLite provider stayed bound through final postflight.
- Each RPC recorded zero host `session_members` DML. The full protected interval through reopen, cleanup, and exit also added no membership DML. All eight native methods plus construction were calibrated before product imports, with no reset. Late-write and unknown-database controls fail final acceptance.

The 11-file behavior wrapper took 664.11 seconds, including imports and transforms. The native worker/lifecycle and registered authorization boundaries require these real flows; helper-only tests would not exercise commit admission, physical store custody, or publication before observers.

This is the membership mutation cutover, not complete Gateway SQLite offload. The raw capture contains 5,488 native calls during RPCs and 17,477 overall, including calibration, fixture/bootstrap, authority/projection reads, and other native work. The only three membership-DML counter hits were intentional positive calibration. This compiled proof covers Node 24 on macOS, with its actual SQLite 3.53.4 provider; it makes no Bun claim.

Related: #150153. The macOS prerequisite #151432 is merged; this focused Windows slice targets main.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Gateway inspection can read a guessed launcher instead of the task's registered action, and service refresh can replace native Task Scheduler settings that belong to the operator.

## User Impact

Inspection follows the registered task action, and refresh preserves the existing principal, triggers, and settings. The reader supports the asynchronous VBS form shipped in 2026.8.2, the synchronous form in 2026.9.2/2026.9.3, and the current launcher.

Registration or runtime inspection timeouts retry the complete strict inspection once with the update's existing timeout budget. A retry retains registered-launcher inspection; persistent failure reports its diagnostic without granting service-control authority. Existing best-effort warnings and ownership refusals remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep task identity and service mutation with the native definition owner and remove duplicate task-name normalization. Preserve the native probe's bounded diagnostic and timeout metadata through strict command inspection so the existing update recovery policy can act on it. This slice adds 289 production lines; the full replacement series must finish with a net reduction.

## Evidence

Four original inspection/preservation regressions fail before repair. The published 9.2/9.3 launcher case also fails against the old combined PR and passes with this fix. Nine focused local test files, full changed checks, production/test types, lint and independent P0–P2 autoreview passed on the earlier inspection candidate.

The timeout follow-up at `2b4a1b0caea08e4a7d28089479ed280930c7ef3f` reproduces six failures through the real strict command reader, service-state orchestration, and update-maintenance entry. The fixture supplies loaded-state facts and mutation spies and simulates Windows transport/path reads. All six regressions pass after repair; the focused group passes 270 tests with one existing skip. Full changed checks and fresh P0–P2 autoreview pass. Registration, revalidation, repeated timeout, mixed command/runtime timeout, and silent native failure cases retain the strict flags and caller budget.

Retained Windows Server 2022 / Node 24.19.0 proof passed three native cases at head `2a79add0c3de44185512ff0ec09e579cc17a2979`: task presence, current disabled nested-task preservation, and published synchronous-launcher preservation of principal, triggers and ACL. Test tasks were removed and the VM was independently verified released with no host. The harness could not confirm descendant cleanup; VM destruction supplied final settlement. An earlier source-transfer timeout ran no tests and is retained separately.

The retained native cases do not establish full fresh installation, actual interactive-task activation, or a published-updater transition. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35338946311) passed. Dedicated Windows CLI proof at the frozen current head completed with failures and remains a landing blocker. The fresh-install cell reached the managed Gateway and passed its functional assertions, but its process observer did not complete, so that run failed cleanup verification. Separate upgrades driven by the published 2026.9.3 and 2026.9.4 CLIs both exited 1; their failed results and independently settled cell cleanup are retained. Related: #162288

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes cloud worker dispatches failing before enrollment because a package-shipped prepare script imports a source-only Kysely generator.

## User Impact

Cloud workers can package the Gateway runtime again while source installs continue generating Kysely declarations. Published installs retain their existing lifecycle behavior. No configuration, schema, protocol, or SDK changes are required; operators need a build containing this fix to replace the affected runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The static package validator correctly rejected a literal import even though a source-schema guard made it unreachable in published installs. Source preparation now lives in an unshipped entry point, and the existing package-manifest owner selects the self-contained hooks command when preparing a package. The hooks script remains shipped for its cross-platform install contract (introduced in d21abb88e43c).

A cheap PR test reads the actual package allowlist and uses the same import-closure validator as node bootstrap and release packaging. It covers shipped source scripts and launchers without a build; built dist edges remain covered by the full package check. Existing CI policy watches select the test for manifest, launcher, and script changes. Docker dependency-stage copies and install-cache fingerprints follow the new preparation entry point.

## Evidence

The reported live evidence was three dispatches on main, through GCP, Hetzner, and AWS, each failing about five seconds after the request:

```text
Node distribution openclaw has an incomplete built import closure; rebuild and restart the Gateway: scripts/prepare-git-hooks.mjs imports missing scripts/generate-kysely-types.mts
```

Locally, the new regression failed on base 34a0d304a8dc with that exact missing-import diagnostic, then passed after the fix. The validator was not weakened, and no computed import specifiers were added.

- Focused lifecycle, codegen, validator, cache, workflow, and node-bootstrap tests: 100 passed across eight files, including all 33 node-bootstrap artifact cases.
- Final pack/cache/workflow followup: 22 passed; 25 unrelated prepack cases excluded by the explicit test filter. The real pnpm pack fixture verifies source preparation executes, the source-only entry is absent from the tarball, and the source manifest is restored. pnpm 12 strips publish lifecycle scripts from its final manifest; the separate prepared-manifest test exercises the hooks-only command.
- New closure test, standalone with `pnpm test test/scripts/package-source-import-closure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 1 passed, 64 ms test time, 2.02 s Vitest wall, 5.97 s runner wall. CI timing is pending.
- Other changed-test costs with one worker: prepare lifecycle 1.383 s (3 cases), workflow cost 0.073 s (20 cases), dependency fingerprint 8.885 s (1 existing case), selected real pack case 21.346 s. The pack test needs an actual package-manager lifecycle to prove command ordering and manifest restoration.
- Scoped changed checks passed scripts tsgo and all four root-test tsgo shards, script lint, dead-export scans, and repository guards. Changed-test lint initially found existing missing braces; targeted oxlint passed after repair. Explicit fingerprint lint also passed after equivalent whitespace-parser style fixes.
- Changed-file oxfmt, pinned actionlint on all three touched workflows, zizmor with the repository's configured thresholds, and `git diff --check` passed. Default-threshold zizmor also reported six existing low-severity local-action syntax suggestions, outside the configured gate.
- P2 autoreview: local and committed-branch review scoped-clean.

The pack fixture initially exposed a missing copied source entry and an incorrect expectation about pnpm's manifest stripping; both were corrected. One later attempt was interrupted by a concurrent lint temporary-file mutation invalidating the compiler snapshot; the final checks ran sequentially and passed. No product failure was hidden by retries.

No full build or test suite was run under the loaded-host constraint. This proves the shipped source import closure directly and the bootstrap artifact behavior with its existing fixtures; it does not claim a fresh live cloud dispatch. No Gateway was started, stopped, or restarted.

```sh
/usr/bin/time -v env CI=1 corepack pnpm test test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.test.ts
```

All four runs passed the same **325 cases in identical order**.

| Arm | Command wall | User + system CPU | Peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | 402.28 s | 451.26 s | 1158.9 MiB |

prs.title: fix: prevent Codex settlement cleanup from hanging
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex settlement tests hanging during cleanup when a contended SQLite coordinator wait outlives the simulated turn clock.

## User Impact

There is no intended user-visible behavior change. This removes a shared source of CI stalls without changing execution budgets, SQLite admission, cancellation, or test assertions. No migration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Coordinator acquisition measured its deadline with the native monotonic clock but scheduled its abortable backoff through global timers. A settlement test could finish its assertions and restore real timers while history maintenance was waiting on a simulated 25 ms backoff. The discarded wakeup left maintenance holding the archive queue, and session-owner cleanup could never finish.

Use Node's native abortable timer for both coordinator acquisition paths, matching the existing acquisition helper's default clock. The retry interval, deadline, authority checks, abort reason, and process-lifetime behavior stay intact. The focused acquisition unit test explicitly simulates this native sleeper alongside its simulated monotonic clock; the Codex settlement tests remain unchanged.

## Evidence

The failure was observed on the merge refs for #156764 and #156758; this is not a claim that their branch changes introduced it or that a `main` CI run was red. All affected owner files and the failing tests remained identical on main at `2512775add63106306e7ee5ad40324143f5abe86`.

- Original [bundle-8 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35929054433/job/107411333991) failed after 55 minutes, including the runner's inherited automatic retry. No manual rerun was used. The corresponding #156758 job had the same first-attempt failure before an inherited replay passed.
- The original protocol-validation → settlement order reproduced the 180-second cleanup hook failure locally. Trace evidence isolated the stranded 25 ms coordinator backoff and the archive queue it retained.
- With the repair, those unchanged tests pass: 23 tests, 47.96 seconds including cold compilation. The full 12-file group also passes: 107 tests, 133.73 seconds of Vitest time; that run used local timing-cache ordering.
- Acquisition retry, deadline, cancellation, and live-authority tests plus the native SQLite worker-preparation sibling pass: 18 tests, 15.66 seconds total. The modified unit file's test cases take approximately 64 ms; the native worker sibling protects FIFO, cancellation, refusal recovery, and cleanup custody.
- On fresh main plus this repair, the exact original hosted 12-file execution order passes: 107 tests, 172.92 seconds including cold compilation. An external proof sequencer enforced the original order while retaining the repository configuration, isolation, setup files, and timeouts.
- Local proof used pnpm 12.4.2, Vitest 5.0.1, and Node 26.7.0. The failing hosted job used the same Vitest version on Node 24.19.0; the new PR keeps the normal hosted CI gate.
- Independent managed review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. Selected preflights, compiler graph boundary, production core typechecking, and five core-test graphs passed. A subsequent shard was canceled when concurrent host workloads exhausted memory; the remaining 20 canonical graphs are running, and selected lint/guards remain pending. This draft does not claim the complete static gate.
- The current #156758 [bundle-18 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35935503860/job/107431815160) independently repeats the same settlement cleanup failure: the 60,000 ms and maximum-budget cases and the held assistant-start case each reach the unchanged 180-second hook timeout. This is streamed job evidence while that run remains active, not a completed job result.

prs.body:
Related: #144592

Depends on #148213. This PR targets `codex/mcp-oauth-read-worker`; retarget to `main` only after that predecessor has landed.

## What Problem This Solves

Onboarding recommendation reads and checkpoints perform SQLite work on the calling thread.

## User Impact

Users retain the same selection, retry, and completion behavior for valid stored recommendations while persistence runs through worker threads. Recommendation reads now reject malformed header metadata (inventory hash and offer, acceptance, or update timestamps) instead of trusting it; extra top-level record fields remain intact and match normalization is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery uses the existing independent read-only owner, and five mutations use the shared-state actor. CLI actions and wizard callbacks await durable selection, skill-install checkpoints, and deferred completion after plugin configuration is saved. Workspace keys, compare-and-update checks, accepted-offer retention, and the SQLite schema stay intact.

The connection-level machine-state reader returns unknown JSON, and the onboarding owner decodes its record. Existing generic machine-state APIs retain their caller-owned shape contract. This removes the extra lint suppression exposed by CI without changing its allowlist.

This candidate retains MCP/Fleet parent `7cf7fa52d2a7`, its reader tags, backup outcome dispatch, and cleanup ancestry.

## Evidence

- The repair at `4920b61ad786` passed 155 owner, CLI, wizard, decoder, readonly-lifetime, and unchanged suppression-guard cases. Twelve pure decoder controls cover valid headers, top-level passthrough, prior match normalization, and malformed headers without injecting invalid data into SQLite.
- Final scoped core/test types, typed lint, guards, all three export scans, and fresh P2 review passed. The normal `pnpm build` passed at `4920b61ad786`.
- On Node 24.21.0 and Bun 1.4.2, the unchanged fully compiled driver exercised storage/CAS, registered CLI actions, synthetic wizard checkpoints, reopen, and cleanup with all seven parent-thread SQLite counters at zero and 14 successful reader tasks per runtime. Source, commit/tree, and full build hashes were verified before and after each run.

The preceding `e6b89770` qualification remains pinned to that revision: 265 store, wizard, CLI, reader-lifetime, runtime-scope, and routing cases plus one ordinary backup outcome/reopen case; build and compiled zero-call proof. Its CI run failed only the extra-suppression workload and the aggregate gate; the repair fixes the actual helper type rather than altering the guard.

The historical `6e898ee6` → `8c0637e4` comparison remains attributed to those exact revisions: 9,443 → 0 instrumented parent SQLite method calls on both runtimes. The current `4920b61ad786` proof independently confirms zero; it is not a new baseline comparison. Measurements exclude canonical SQLite capability/prototype calibration and use prepared synthetic config; they do not claim a speedup or whole-Gateway performance result.

prs.title: fix(tasks): preserve selected work through cancellation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A delayed Lobster result could cancel a newer approval checkpoint. Cancellation could also acknowledge a persisted transition before its projections were readable, or transfer an earlier request to newly arrived work. Synchronous control reads could block or fail while a cancellation worker held the database lifecycle.

## User Impact

Managed Lobster run/resume cancellation now awaits worker-backed flow state, including childless workflows. Task cancellation retains the selected task, flow, run, backing instance, and caller authority across asynchronous work. Gateway cancellation uses prepared session/profile facts and preserves permission revocation during those waits. An already settled cancellation retains its result when the caller later retires.

This cut covers flow state, task-projection settlement, and file-backed Gateway access. Native ACP/subagent database control, process-held incognito access, and their remaining lifecycle tails stay with their existing owners as explicit follow-ups. Schema, stored formats, retention, and update behavior are unchanged.

## Ownership and Compatibility

One flow cancellation implementation records intent before child dispatch, joins task publication under native cancellation holds, and rereads children before finalization. Lobster supplies its original flow record so a delayed outcome cannot cancel a newer checkpoint. The legacy public cancellation facade keeps its name and lazy import boundary and delegates to this implementation. Capture-only cancellation context reads share the existing global holder without initializing storage. Core cancellation retains its task-store and bound-producer authority across an admitting-registry handoff; registered external runtimes retain their exact live instance guard.

A newer committed projection can supersede a worker readback. Cancellation awaits the existing canonical async reader to settle that projection and rechecks authority; actual publication errors still refuse success. Writes are not replayed, and the existing flow retry/settlement owner is preserved. Existing external task runtimes can still own unmirrored records, while an initially absent core selection cannot acquire a later core task through delegation or fallback.

Maintainer compatibility decision: this newer bundled Lobster requires the optional async cancellation capability for managed run/resume. The shipped v2026.9.6 host lacks that method despite satisfying the manifest floor. Update the host together with the plugin to enable managed mode. Refusal occurs before flow creation or runner execution; ordinary workflows on the same older-host fixture remain usable. A legacy synchronous fallback would restore the selected-flow and worker-boundary defect, so it is intentionally excluded. This capability cutoff introduces no protocol/version bump or stored-data migration. Existing public legacy APIs remain available under their named compatibility contracts.

Related: #158235 and #159064.

## Evidence

Registered managed run/resume observed 1,497 and 1,475 host data-SQL API calls before this change and zero afterward, with durable cancelled-state checks. That original counter excluded only the canonical coordinator database. These whole windows include the registered factory, managed workflow, and async persisted readback after warmup. After integration with canonical main `77847b56720394e530edc77181171f68699edbe7`, the same registered run/resume and Gateway assertions also pass under the current observer, which counts host SQL prepare/exec and statement execution APIs with no coordinator exemption. They measure API invocations across the workflow; cancellation-only counts, distinct SQL statements, and latency were not measured.

Real-worker proof covers childless flows, delayed checkpoint replacement, child completion during cancellation, caller retirement, failed flow/child publication, unrelated flow-store failure, and newly arrived task delegation. Gateway cases include nonadmin cancellation with zero host data SQL from backing preparation through response, plus membership, role, alias, requester, and request-lifetime revocation. Native concurrency/publication cases preserve completion precedence, exact generations, accepted stops, and held settlement.

The import-boundary repair passed all 86 unchanged legacy dispatch, owner, cancellation, and run-owner tests. The full build passed on the import-boundary candidate, including CLI bootstrap imports, Plugin SDK exports, plugin loading, and UI bundle checks. The final publication repair passed all 35 focused public-flow, real-worker, and registered Lobster cases, including three causal refusal regressions and the unchanged failed-readback negative. Production/test type graphs, typed lint, source/SDK/schema/import/authorization guards, formatting, and dead-export checks have been exercised throughout the cut. The final core ownership repair also passed all 66 unchanged SDK command, cancellation-worker, task-owner, and Gateway cases; its baseline reproduced eight command-cancellation failures. Fresh independent review is clean. Final-head CI remains the merge gate; no baseline or counter allowance was added.


The final review repair preserves the original absent selection when an external cancellation callback fails: `found` remains false, the failure reason is retained, and no later core work is acquired. The existing external-only table reproduced the defect before the fix and passed all 13 cases afterward. The independent worker-routing expectation now includes the extracted Gateway cancellation file; all 452 routing checks pass.

### Test cost

Measured serially with the repository test runner and `--maxWorkers=1`, using Node 24.21.0 on Darwin arm64. Candidate measurements use `afa3b904254ba83c009d9ed0a7017603a1845ae6`; the original Gateway file uses `81915ffe8df206ecc28f74da49b57fe21cdb1366` in the same checkout and dependency installation. Package, lock, workspace, and workspace package manifests match. Case time is the sum of verbose case durations; Vitest and process elapsed time also include collection, imports, and wrapper overhead.

| Test file | Cases | Case time | Vitest elapsed | Process elapsed | Compiler cache |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `src/tasks/task-cancellation.worker.test.ts` | 13 | 14.366 s | 19.78 s | 71.17 s | Miss |
| `src/tasks/task-flow-cancellation.worker.test.ts` | 5 | 13.811 s | 23.01 s | 41.06 s | Hit |
| `extensions/lobster/src/lobster-tool.cancellation.test.ts` | 4 | 4.097 s | 25.29 s | 30.29 s | Hit |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.cancel.test.ts` | 14 | 28.895 s | 45.91 s | 51.70 s | Hit |
| `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control.publication.test.ts` | 13 | 18.583 s | 35.44 s | 39.90 s | Hit |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` (candidate remainder) | 29 | 30.353 s | 48.63 s | 53.30 s | Hit |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` (original) | 37 | 43.658 s | 84.65 s | 90.99 s | Miss |

These are cost measurements, not a latency-improvement claim: the candidate has 43 Gateway cases across two files versus 37 originally, and cold/warm compiler state differs. Real persistence, worker admission, publication, and authorization races justify the worker and Gateway costs; mocks would miss the defects they protect. The remaining Gateway file retains actual persistence and authorization coverage. Per-file CI timing was not available in the saved CI output; whole-shard timing is not substituted for it. Final-head CI remains required.


### Cron completion handoff

Exact-head CI on `afa3b904254ba83c009d9ed0a7017603a1845ae6` exposed two existing real `onTimer` cancellation regressions. Aborting a cron handle released its timer outcome before asynchronous task cancellation finished; that outcome could record the task as failed first. Both failures reproduced locally with the terminal-outcome refusal reason.

The cron owner now carries its accepted operator-cancellation reason into the first task terminal write. Cron history and public events retain their existing error vocabulary, and a payload completed before cancellation retains its completion outcome. No failed row is retroactively promoted to cancelled. Existing synchronous cron producer/history persistence remains a named follow-up; these cases do not extend the native subagent host-SQL claims to real cron timers.

The two original regressions pass. A focused extracted table also checks an abort-ignoring runner, immediate settlement on abort, and a payload completed before cancellation while webhook delivery remains pending. All 79 focused and sibling cases pass, including timeout precedence, task history, receipt finalization, command interruption, and delivery completion. Core/cron test types, focused typed lint, file-size guards, and fresh independent review pass.

The new `src/cron/service/timer.cancellation.test.ts` has 3 cases: 5.295 s summed case time, 65.70 s Vitest elapsed, and 76.30 s process elapsed on a compiler-cache miss using the same one-worker command/environment above. The extracted remainder `timer.regression.test.ts` has 47 cases and 33.715 s summed case time; it passed with 29 unchanged sibling cases in an 83.27 s process. That combined process time is not a per-file measurement. Its real timer, persistence, timeout, and receipt boundaries justify retaining the slower coverage. Per-file CI timing for the repaired candidate is still pending.


CI on `72722312a49af59591606967f67314e2cc2e228f` passed the cancellation assertions but exposed a fixture teardown race: the script case reset its registry synchronously while native database cleanup remained active, and the immediately following case encountered the same borrower. The fixture now awaits the existing canonical asynchronous database close after its original execution joins and before registry reset. No production guard, assertion, timeout, or retry was weakened. The exact outstanding reader was not identified from the CI stack, and the local pre-fix ordered pair passed; this is an explicit lifecycle-order repair, not a claim of deterministic local reproduction. Both complete timer/cancellation files pass (50 cases), with owning types, lint, line-cap checks, and fresh independent review clean.


The retained Linux CI log for `f4d319821b92bfe82fb5e56e2fcf63761b0d8770` confirms all 47 `timer.regression.test.ts` cases passed, including that script/restart pair, followed by SQLite owner retirement. Summed case time was 7.478 s; this is not per-file elapsed time or a cross-platform performance comparison. The containing job was subsequently cancelled by fail-fast after the separate native Codex rotated-parent history-preparation failure. The overall CI run is not reported as green.


### Canonical recovery integration

The separate rotated-parent defect is now fixed by merged #159735 (`77847b56720394e530edc77181171f68699edbe7`). The composed cancellation candidate passes all 16 rotated-parent cases, including the exact `finishes-after-registration` case that failed its prior CI. The integration also passes 468 routing cases, 14 Gateway cancellation cases, 44 task/flow cases, and 4 registered Lobster cases: 546 total across five runner shards (966.61 seconds combined runner time, not per-file latency).
