prs.title: chore(ci): reduce Blacksmith load with guarded hosted checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hybrid CI spends Blacksmith capacity on independent checks with enough measured slack to tolerate standard hosted runners.

## User Impact

Reduces CI runner cost without changing test coverage, worker limits, timeouts, critical-path runner labels, or the configured backend. This is a routing trial; no user-visible runtime change. A prospective health snapshot cannot rescue jobs already queued or guarantee against a later hosted assignment wave.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move five 16-class checks to `ubuntu-24.04` only on canonical main pushes and trusted automatic hybrid PRs selecting the two fixed Windows lanes: dependencies, core test-types 1 and 2, extension package boundaries, and runtime topology architecture. Every sample satisfies `1.4 × duration + 180 seconds <= slack`. The existing UI/security offload decision keeps priority; these five consume only remaining capacity within the unchanged 45-row hosted limit.

Keep compact Node jobs, extension test envelopes, UI E2E, preflight, builds, lint, central test types, QA, Android, and Windows on their current routes. The lighter 8-class compact bins remain excluded even when they have slack. Docs, i18n, security reevaluation, and admitted security-fast already use hosted runners, so there is no additional saving to claim there.

Preflight samples recent canonical main CI attempts using read-only Actions access. Assignment wait excludes the preflight dependency. Any observed wait of at least 180 seconds, missing fresh assigned evidence, malformed data, or an API error retains the new five rows on Blacksmith for this run and records a warning/summary. At most four requests share a ten-second deadline. There is no service, new repository variable, variable mutation, retry policy, or new job. Existing retry/fallback routing stays intact. Documentation covers the existing operator backend switch for sustained incidents and the inability to migrate already queued jobs.

## Evidence

Baseline: six successful main runs on September 20, `35518231054`, `35518255065`, `35518791853`, `35518915535`, `35520028134`, `35520044205`; all pages reconciled to `total_count`. Exclude skipped pseudojobs: including them produced the original 37/14/6/5/25.5 class summary and distorted runtime medians (some skipped durations are negative).

| Executed class | Jobs/run before → predicted after (median) | Duration median | Slack median | Hosted prediction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Blacksmith 32 Linux | 36 → 36 | 7.17 min | 8.17 min | 19.35 min (×2.7; retained) |
| Blacksmith 16 Linux | 10 → 5 | 4.61 min | 10.86 min | 6.45 min (×1.4) |
| Blacksmith 8 Linux | 4 → 4 | 3.75 min | 9.29 min | 5.25 min (×1.4; retained) |
| Blacksmith 4 Linux | 5 → 5 | 5.72 min | 9.00 min | 8.00 min (×1.4; retained) |
| Blacksmith Windows | 0 → 0 (range 0–2) | 12.28 min | 3.27 min | unchanged |
| Hosted Ubuntu | 18 → 23 | 2.15 min | 12.77 min | unchanged |
| macOS | no executed samples | — | — | unchanged |

| New hosted row | Duration median | Slack median | Hosted prediction | Worst residual after prediction +3 min |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dependencies | 3.66 min | 11.80 min | 5.12 min | 178 sec |
| core test-types 1 | 4.51 min | 10.97 min | 6.31 min | 47 sec |
| core test-types 2 | 4.10 min | 11.45 min | 5.74 min | 112 sec |
| extension package boundary | 3.21 min | 12.22 min | 4.49 min | 214 sec |
| runtime topology architecture | 2.16 min | 13.15 min | 3.02 min | 378 sec |

The modeled job-envelope wall remains **16m18s median, 15m32s–16m54s range** in all six samples. Definition: first job creation through aggregate-gate completion; the captures contain jobs, not workflow lifecycle timestamps. This prediction excludes the new health-read overhead. The PR run must measure that overhead, hosted cache/setup cost, actual waits, and overall completion. A broad PR selects more test jobs than these main runs, so its wall is observational rather than a controlled same-workload comparison. Executed hosted jobs in the baseline waited 5.5 seconds median / 99 seconds maximum from job creation to start (the earlier 2-second median included skipped entries).

Blacksmith Linux minutes: median **371.37 → 353.22**. List-rate estimate: **$19.609 → $19.045/main run**; median paired saving **17.64 minutes/$0.565**. Medians do not subtract linearly. Rates per minute: 4/8/16/32-class = $0.008/$0.016/$0.032/$0.064 (now verified against the provider pricing page); This paragraph reports Linux only; all-platform figures below include Windows. Billing rounding is excluded. Rounded-per-job saving would be approximately $0.672, not verified invoicing. Public-repository hosted Linux minutes are free. An eligible Windows-selected PR has the same modeled saving; other PRs retain these checks on Blacksmith because precise Node plans do not establish enough critical-path slack. There is no separate measured PR baseline in this sample and scoped PR savings depend on selected rows.

Local proof: 41 focused routing/health guard cases passed; 332 planner cases passed (330 initially, with both new-file inventory cases passing after staging); `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, workflow lint/security checks, type-aware oxlint, formatting, docs listing/MDX checks, and `git diff --check` passed. The lint canary correctly rejected an unknown-valued template expression. Codex local review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Candidate head: `33becc81fde48807835ebd59f62f94a79f200c81`.

The initial PR CI run `35526323851` failed before fanout because the sparse `.ci-harness` export did not contain the new helper. The correction reads the current checkout on automatic current-revision jobs; an executable workflow-step regression reproduced `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before the fix and passes afterward. The correction passed changed checks and fresh P0–P2 review. Workflow validation reused the installed hook at its exact configured revision when a repeated Python virtualenv bootstrap stalled.

The full local workflow guard invocation was interrupted after an existing cache fixture stalled for over five minutes in native pnpm initialization on macOS. Its failing bootstrap was sampled, and the later routing-specific run passed. The PR CI run supplies the complete Linux guard proof. Exact-head branch review and native CI measurements will be appended before handoff. Not for landing as part of this task.

### Native offload trial

[Run 35527301597](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35527301597), head `6c875c5fece748aabc5953de60629f67e3d4d625`, admitted all five rows to `ubuntu-24.04`. Preflight sampled seven fresh hosted jobs, maximum assignment wait 3 seconds; its health step took 5 seconds. The manifest recorded 19 base / 29 total hosted rows, below the unchanged 45-row cap.

| Moved check | Hosted prediction | Measured | Wait | Remaining slack |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dependencies | 5.12 min | 6m36s | 5s | 8m13s |
| core test-types 1 | 6.31 min | 7m46s | 3s | 7m05s |
| core test-types 2 | 5.74 min | 8m16s | 5s | 6m33s |
| extension package boundary | 4.49 min | 5m56s | 3s | 8m55s |
| runtime topology architecture | 3.02 min | 3m23s | 3s | 11m28s |

All five passed. Hosted durations exceeded the CPU-only prediction, but none became critical. This evidence prompted the final cohort guard: short or unknown PR plans retain Blacksmith placement and do not run the health probe. Main and the fixed Windows workload are the measured headroom cohorts; fast Node-only scopes also skip the probe.

The run executed 66 jobs: 1 Linux 32-class, 21 16-class, 1 8-class, 12 4-class, 2 Windows 8-class, and 29 hosted Ubuntu. Under the prior routing, this same selection would have 26 16-class and 24 hosted rows; the other counts stay unchanged. Hosted waits were 3s median / 5s maximum, versus 5.5s / 99s in the executed-job baseline. The job-envelope wall was **16m01s**, compared with **16m18s median** in the six-main cohort; Windows part 2 was the tail. This is an observational comparison across different workloads, not a paired speedup claim. The 5-second guard cost is visible and no zero-overhead guarantee is claimed.

Using [current list rates](https://www.blacksmith.sh/pricing), including Windows 8-class at $0.032/min, the six-run main model is **371.37 → 353.30 Blacksmith minutes** and **$19.68 → $19.10** (medians, including a 5-second probe allowance). Median paired saving is about **17.56 minutes/$0.56**. The trial measured **175.68 minutes/$5.41** across Linux and Windows. Applying the main sample's old-route check durations to this PR selection estimates **193.24 minutes/$5.97 before**; this counterfactual is not a measured matched PR baseline. Hosted Linux minutes are free for this public repository; invoice rounding/discounts are not modeled.

The only job failure was `control-ui-performance`, with startup JS **364,920 B > 364,806 B**, plus the aggregate gate reflecting that failure. R1 modifies no UI runtime source or performance baseline and retains that job's existing hosted route. No baseline was raised. The final cohort refinement passed 41 focused guard cases, including before/after regressions for non-main pushes and PRs without Windows. Workflow, docs, formatting, and type-aware lint checks passed; its P0–P2 review is scoped-clean. Final exact-head whole-branch review is scoped-clean through P2. CI results are recorded below.

### Final-head guard and CI status

Head `33becc81fde48807835ebd59f62f94a79f200c81`, [run 35529486045](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35529486045): preflight reported `no-fresh-hosted-evidence` (zero usable samples), retained the five checks on Blacksmith, and emitted 19 base / 24 total hosted rows. This is live proof of conservative fallback; the preceding native trial above supplies the admitted-row timing evidence. Unit fixtures cover the explicit three-minute assignment-stall boundary.

The run has an unrelated type-check blocker at `src/infra/update-triage-resolution.ts:92`: TS2345, because an `env?: ProcessEnv` formatter is passed directly as an `Array.map` callback, whose second argument is a number. The same diagnostic appears in retained hosted production types and Blacksmith core test types. This branch changes no `src/` files. R1 does not alter that code or weaken its checks.

The completed final-head run executed 66 jobs. Its job-envelope wall was **19m35s** versus the six-main median **16m18s**. Workload jobs finished at **16m37s**; the unchanged always-hosted aggregate gate then waited **174 seconds** for a runner (3 seconds of execution). Hosted waits were **2s median / 174s maximum**. This existing gate remains outside the new offload safeguard; a flat whole-run wall is not established under hosted assignment delays.

| Blacksmith Linux 32 | 1 | 1 |
| Blacksmith Linux 16 | 21 | 26 |
| Blacksmith Linux 8 | 1 | 1 |
| Blacksmith Linux 4 | 12 | 12 |
| Blacksmith Windows 8 | 2 | 2 |
| Hosted Ubuntu | 29 | 24 |

The fallback run used **185.15 Blacksmith minutes / approximately $5.68** at list rates including Windows; it moved zero rows. Failed compiler checks ended early, so this is a billed-work estimate, not a steady-state comparison to the healthy offload trial. The run failed six check jobs plus the aggregate gate. All remaining jobs passed, including `control-ui-performance`; the earlier UI size failure is therefore historical trial evidence, not the final blocker.

Final head `33becc81fde48807835ebd59f62f94a79f200c81` is pushed; whole-branch Codex review is **scoped-clean through P2**. The local worktree is clean. The PR is open and **not merged**. The separate update-triage type error blocks green CI; no source repair, baseline expansion, backend-variable change, or critical-path runner-label change was made outside R1.

prs.title: fix(ci): reduce PR lint and planner overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR static checks widen source changes to whole-package lint, enumerate every compiler graph before selecting all of them, and serialize independent checks behind that planner. The first version of this PR still measured a 640-second zero-test floor.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Eligible PRs lint changed files plus transitive import consumers with the same rules and compiler configurations. Hourly main and full release validation retain full lint. Changes to lint/configuration owners, deleted or ambient inputs, and oversized consumer sets retain full lint conservatively.

Auto-merge is off for coordinator integration. The requested broad ≤300s and narrow ≤180s targets remain unproven; native warm compiled-cache proof requires a successful trusted main publisher after integration. This PR itself changes the lint runner and therefore correctly keeps full lint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing import-graph owner now supplies complete transitive consumers, including type-only edges and aliases. Preflight/row commands carry those prepared file selections; each row receives only its files. Seeded native-rule proof catches a changed-file violation and an unchanged aliased consumer after an exported type changes to a Promise.

Guaranteed-full compiler plans return the canonical graph inventory without running all 57 discovery queries first. Compiler-boundary validation remains required in independent additional checks; when that job is not selected, including data-only and release-fast paths, the planner retains it. Source-only narrowing still performs native compiler discovery. Additional checks start directly after preflight, and guards-selected plans remove the duplicate coercion check.

The observer adopts CP10's existing final-workload retirement implementation; the final gate still joins and validates that workload. GH2 owns the remaining gate runner placement. The extension-boundary job restores compiled receipts when available and publishes them only after successful trusted-main validation. PRs remain restore-only. The SDK warmer stays a fallback. Cache validators and canaries are unchanged.

Coordination: CP10 (#158708) owns row packing, Node admission and observer policy; GH2 (#158257) owns runner routing; RV4 owns test tiers. Preserve GH2's `dependency_stripe` and `compactCoreLint` additions during integration. No runner classes, permissions, dependencies or paid services added.

## Evidence

### Controlled Linux measurements

| Measurement | Before | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exact prior PR planner input, complete wall | 60.85s | 23.12s |
| Guaranteed-full type selection | native graph discovery | 0.0s logged selection |
| Extension compiler cache archive round trip | 392.73s; 125 compiled | 12.17s; 0 compiled, 125 validated |

Planner timings are separate Testbox sessions and are not a same-host paired speed claim. The earlier paired compiler-concurrency change measured 68.26→60.85s with byte-identical output. The current planner preserves compiler graph coverage while changing lint selection to four script files plus twelve root test files for that recorded input.

With `GOMAXPROCS=2` and one lint thread, a single core file took 19.07s, a script file 5.65s, UI file 7.56s, and full core stripe 4 took 57.90s. A separate debug capture reported 18.7s elapsed with only 3.218ms summed rule execution (2.980ms type-aware, 0.238ms native). Program construction and other startup dominate; the residual is not an independently instrumented program-build timer.

The compiled-cache transport qualification archived 13,835,113 bytes. SDK preparation was 125.980→3.408s and compiler work 266.422→8.409s. Canaries ran both times (1.112/1.213s); all 17 invalidation/canary tests passed. This is same-backend archive qualification, not a native Actions warm-hit measurement.

### Validation

All 22 importing test files for the changed import-graph helper were exercised under their routed Linux CI configurations, together with six owner/workflow files (4,657 cases). Five stale workflow expectations were corrected and the complete affected workflow file passed. The later manifest-fixture change was verified through all three importers: 478 cases passed in 107.89s command wall. Existing assertions and test cases remain; native seeded lint coverage proves both changed and dependent violations.

Fresh P2 Codex autoreview completed with no actionable findings. Script and root-test typechecks, workflow lint, dead-export scan, scoped lint including boundary guards, Docker/raw-HTTP guards, formatting, and Knip passed. Knip used the repository's pinned `deadcode:knip` entry (29.48s); an earlier direct `pnpm exec knip` invocation failed because Knip is intentionally not an installed workspace binary. Two mechanical test lint issues were corrected. Final Linux single-file walls: changed lint 14 cases in 4.57s; changed compiler graphs 16 cases in 1.56s. All eight changed test/support files pass type-aware lint (10.96s). No full suites ran on the Mac.

Testbox provider: Blacksmith Testbox; primary lease `tbx_01m3hp7kpbb4mpgbpbd7n4waav`, [hydration run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36328102846). Source SHA256 maps were verified before each command. The original PR's 823-case proof remains valid for its unchanged compiler-concurrency work; continuation proof above covers the new helper and planner paths.

### Native before and after

Continuation implementation `e8e7e11386d3` initially exceeded GitHub's documented 500 KiB workflow-file limit (513,658 bytes versus 511,632 previously). Both push run 36333478852 and exact-head dispatch 36333703605 stopped before creating jobs. Comment-only repair `899449e6a55233476071de4e3c7d4c85ccd571e7` reduces the file to 511,511 bytes; parsed YAML is deeply identical, syntax validation passes, and fresh P2 review is clean. [PR CI 36334312859](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36334312859) now runs on that exact head. That run exposed a deterministic standalone-lint fixture failure: graph expansion in the shard executor pulled a planner-only helper into its standalone bundle. The continuation repair moves expansion to the existing changed-check planner while preserving canonical file validation in the executor. All 11 files from the failing tooling shard pass on Testbox (1,115 cases, four existing platform skips, 165.12s), including all 40 unchanged process-boundary cases; planner/lint owner proof adds 21 passing cases in 4.88s. Fresh P2 review is clean.

The canceled run's gate endpoint was 584s; this is censored evidence, not a successful whole-run measurement. Completed components remain useful: planner endpoint 295→130s, materialization 144→1s, and core-lint endpoint 585→442s. Full-lint execution 262→267s confirms unchanged coverage rather than a full-lint speedup. Extension validation finished at 433s (SDK 45.145s + 125-plugin compilation 267.126s); compiled cache missed and the SDK fallback hit. Channel contracts finished at 483s. The observer took the failure/cancellation path, so this run does not qualify normal-tail retirement. Repair head `d42b0d93150e4e72939223834ee2a2ddeef88e6c` is under [exact-head PR CI 36336098116](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36336098116). Both script/root typechecks, lint including boundary guards, dead exports and Knip passed after the repair. Native complete wall is pending.

### Baseline critical paths

Seconds below come from completed successful first-attempt PR runs. Broad means a selected workload of 83 Node rows, not an unrestricted fallback. “Zero-test” is a counterfactual subtracting named test steps while preserving measured launches, setup, static work and observer/gate lag; no correctness checks were disabled to measure it.

| Run | Actual gate wall | Zero-test projection |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Broad selected workload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36318963445) | 813s (13:33) | 739s (12:19) |
| [Latest one-test PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36319301593) | 593s (9:53) | 593s (9:53) |

| Broad critical job | Queue | Checkout | Node/cache/install | Build/restore | Work | Other | Tail |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| preflight | 7 | 27 | 2 | 0 | 52 | 2 | 4 |

prs.title: ci: bound Node row work and trim PR control latency
prs.body:
Broad PR CI underestimated expensive Node families and packed oversized groups into long rows. Stale family weights, mismatched runner/worker identities, and a lost whole-owner timing fallback after file splitting caused the underprediction. Native Blacksmith measurements are no longer discounted as hosted estimates. The changes preserve the selected inventory while pricing exact config/file/worker identities, splitting oversized families, applying measured runner costs, and bounding predicted Node test work at **300 seconds**. Runtime preparation is charged separately.

Landed directly on main under the updated CI spend policy: timing sampler [`ef681882ffe9`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ef681882ffe9781c814dc5b374dc10ddfe414e37), packing/weights/workers [`b3f4c0aa540b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b3f4c0aa540be135b722bec27922f105611b598d), and control jobs/completion [`1ea24b2dc36f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1ea24b2dc36f809ff2113965ef4ca6ba6c1387f9). This PR is closed as the evidence record; no PR merge or auto-merge was used.

Gateway methods use four workers only with at least eight available CPUs and 28 GiB memory, retaining the two-worker fallback. The final controls preserve main's parallel Node/ratchet admission from [`e337075dd7c0`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e337075dd7c0b60e164e78cbad75ac722dc5fbd9); the earlier unlanded inline-ratchet proposal was removed. Eligible hybrid ratchets and check planning use existing Blacksmith capacity, and the failure monitor may retire with one workload left while the aggregate still waits for and checks it. Check-plan's cache input is separate from the plain setup anchor. Current-main tests and assertions, permissions, dependencies, and deadlines are preserved.

## Result and limits

**An actual complete PR wall below ten minutes remains unproven.** The last complete green PR run [36335233081](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36335233081) took **650 seconds (10m50s)** from creation to terminal metadata, with 111 successful Node rows and 11,601.80 whole-run Blacksmith class-vCPU-minutes. Its creation-to-last-job wall was 649s and job span was 645s.

The normalized frozen-inventory model below projects a conditional **595-second terminal scenario** and **at least 3.15% lower modeled changed-surface compute**. It is not a measured speedup: 50 candidate rows lack complete prior-envelope observations. The final controls retain the model's higher 30.47-vCPU-minute control reserve even though their documented standalone-ratchet plus check-plan bound is 20.00; no extra saving is credited for dropping the inline-ratchet proposal. Incoming main changes were preserved without refreshing proof merely because main advanced.

The latest native PR attempt [36358815890](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36358815890) was cancelled by fail-fast after **361 seconds**, following the cache-consumer guard failure. That exposed the shared-anchor integration bug, now fixed at the workflow owner with the existing assertion unchanged. The manual run [36358837201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36358837201) was stopped after the CI-spend instruction; its **1,353-second** terminal wall is censored and is not PR-equivalent. It had 130 successful, four failed, and twelve cancelled Node jobs. Cached failures include UI locale fallback drift, missing native zh-CN translations, and a pnpm download connection reset before cron tests; other manual Node failures were not fully triaged after the spend-policy change. Neither cancelled run qualifies wall or cost. No replacement dispatch, rerun, or proof push was made.

## Proof

- Linux Testbox: fresh full core planner **213/213** in 95.168s and selection/integration/command/helper/plugin inventory **314/314** in 247.046s. Both importers of the shared planner helper ran completely.
- Linux workflow owners: **846 passing cases** plus the reproduced cache-consumer failure, 171.897s; workflow validation passed in 25.055s. The corrected existing cache regression passed locally in **4.461s**. The final parallel-admission reconciliation passed seven focused routing/cache/PR-graph cases and all **24 hosted-budget cases** (11.590s), with current-main parallel-admission assertions retained.
- Final scoped checks passed: workflow validation 16.424s, script/test lint, root-test types 22.258s, documentation links 17.468s, formatting and diff checks. Completed prior 33-file changed gates, boundary lint, types, and three Knip scans are reused for unchanged owners; the interrupted later static scan is not reported as a pass.
- Three Gateway four-worker shard replays and three CLI two-worker fallback replays passed. Gateway sampling observed summed readable `/proc` RSS at most 8.98 GiB and available memory at least 6.71 GiB, without OOM. These one-second samples are not cgroup/process-tree peaks, and PSI was unavailable. Policy/config proof is reused; this is not a claim that every subsequently changed test file was replayed three times.
- Fresh Codex P2 reviews are clean for the landed units, including the final main-conflict reconciliation. The Testbox is stopped. Main pushes followed the authorized direct-landing route; no additional CI was triggered for proof.

The separate preview-fixture repair [`b2452cb21199`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b2452cb2119924a1459efc2ff665d2c5dc225681) retained every assertion and passed its full 17-case file and original 54-file/266-case UI selection. The survivor initialization and wrapper argument repairs were already on main.

## Frozen same-inventory model

The final ordinary broad PR model preserves identical coverage and passes the 300-second Node prediction cap and +10% compute guard. It compares main `b2452cb2119924a1459efc2ff665d2c5dc225681` with committed candidate `5e956c56214c140110b59c61f9a22c4d298b3b29` (tree `2ef26c34f16fb3100eadb1642165c57f6f268149`) using the same 33-path scope, tracked inventory and hybrid options. The stack is sampler `4924f245bc6e85750f836eaa66b393debe463a98`, packing `da93944bf65e495f0441d3f48e3100dccdc540fa`, and controls `5e956c56214c140110b59c61f9a22c4d298b3b29`.

| Same-inventory measure | Main policy | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Core Node / plugin rows | 68 / 46 | 71 / 45 |
| Total Node rows / cap | 114 / 130 | 116 / 130 |
| Core / plugin file-config tokens | 11,849 / 3,166 | 11,849 / 3,166 |
| Largest emitted Node test prediction | 669s | 300s |
| Largest Node test wall under common current prices | 609.84s | 300.00s |
| Modeled changed-surface class-vCPU-min, 50s setup/tail | 11,551.69 | 11,187.83 |
| Modeled cost change | — | -3.15% |
| New comparable native actual wall | Unmeasured | Unmeasured |

Cost includes all Node jobs, the two core dist jobs and conservative allowances for changed controls/boundary routing; unchanged non-Node work is omitted on both sides. These are changed-surface model totals, not complete-run billing. The guard uses the higher of direct candidate predictions and conserved common-price allocation. No worker-speedup credit is assumed. Core group/file allocations are inferred; each plugin envelope is repriced by the current estimator.

| Setup + teardown per row | Main placement | Candidate guard | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 41s | 11,232.49 | 10,866.23 | -3.26% |
| 50s | 11,551.69 | 11,187.83 | -3.15% |
| 60s | 11,906.36 | 11,545.16 | -3.03% |
| 90s | 12,970.36 | 12,617.16 | -2.72% |

The last complete green PR actual remains run **36335233081**: **650s (10m50s)** workflow-created-to-terminal-metadata wall; **649s** creation-to-last-job and **645s** first-job-to-last-job, with **4s** initial admission, **111/111 Node rows passed**, **11,601.80** whole-run class-vCPU-min. Its inventory differs from this candidate. Using that run's latest Node runner admission of 151s and 50s setup/teardown gives predicted Node completion at **501s**. Matched prior child-envelope timings yield a known-subset Node completion of **565.49s**. If prior UI completion (576s) and terminal tail (18s) repeat, the raw conditional creation-to-last-job scenario is **594.00s**, measured from workflow creation and already including the reference run’s 4s initial admission. Adding the observed 1s metadata finalization gives **595.00s** on the conservative workflow-created-to-terminal-metadata clock. A future strict wall claim must use that terminal clock and include the new run’s actual initial queue and finalization. This is not a complete forecast or a sub-ten-minute result: **50/116 candidate rows contain unobserved envelopes**. Group evidence comprises 225 exact matches, 100 inferred uniform file allocations and 86 unobserved descriptors; only 36 rows are entirely exact matches on the same class. Split allocations assume no additional process-start cost. Exact envelope matching binds file/config/worker descriptors, not all underlying test/product bytes after incoming main changes.

All before/after rows are below, including emitted/common predictions, preparation and classified prior-envelope scenarios; new complete comparable actuals are explicitly unmeasured. `publication-provenance.json` binds source/tree/inventory/workflow/timing hashes and the generated outputs. Timing schema and reader key-count guards passed before each plan was generated.


All rows use the same current inventory and task scope. New native actuals are unmeasured. Prior-envelope scenarios reuse descriptor-matched observations or explicit file allocations; they are not new row measurements.

prs.title: ci: move PR verification to hosted runners
prs.body:
PR verification now uses GitHub-hosted Linux and Windows capacity while keeping the existing job inventory. The expanded matrix in this PR branch was withdrawn; the smaller final implementation landed directly on main in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ab416e262cb97e8ca49505d903ec57c566c09bb1 under the maintainer's CI-spend policy. This PR is closed without merging its branch.

The final workflow places the waiting `pr-fail-fast` monitor, preflight and control jobs, static checks, Node rows, builds, and UI verification on `ubuntu-24.04`, and PR Windows tests on `windows-2025`. It preserves current-main cancellation grace, originating-failure reporting and `ci-gate-red`, every selected test/check, worker limits, cache trust, and main/manual/release routing. The integration retains main’s independently landed known-main-failure classification and read-only fork monitoring. Hosted placement uses the hosted cache path even when the logical check profile remains Blacksmith. No backend variable was changed (`OPENCLAW_CI_RUNNER_BACKEND` remains `hybrid`).

Hosted setup honors the repository's existing same-major Node pin in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/84bf30fecf13c1c288fdb7d005152095c7230e88. The repository pin had already advanced to 24.21.0; this change did not bump it. Historical Blacksmith toolcache reuse explained the observed 24.19.0 versus hosted 24.21.0 difference. Raw HTTP/TCP probes passed on both versions, so a Node patch-version transport regression was not established. The proxy fixture's asynchronous persistence/response-close/drain repair was already upstream in #158848.

The broad inventory comparison against main `056e84786a06` has 115 Node rows before and after: 70 compact Node rows plus 45 supplemental rows. Total compact rows, including two dist rows, remain 72. Windows remains five rows covering 149 files. Main independently packed extension lint from six to three jobs during landing; the final routing preserves that reduction, with 23 static rows before and after this patch. All 12,430 canonical inventory entries are identical (SHA-256 `5de58df91586938149c449ce6c43adbd3da535821f2772620aa09c35c1677b4e`). Compact/total/active Node caps remain 90/130/96, and all 37 job names and strategy objects are preserved. Android retains its existing Blacksmith 8-class if selected. QA, Docker seed, and real-Gateway proof retain their separate policies and are normally omitted from PRs. No Blacksmith Node exceptions remain in the covered PR families.

Validation used focused Linux Testbox proof and independent Codex review at P2. The original placement patch passed 780 focused routing cases. Current-main integration passed 321 corrected workflow guards in 64.936 seconds; 450 planning and 12 PR-control cases from the preceding integration were reused because their tested contracts were unchanged. The changed-file gate passed in 255.294 seconds, including types, lint/guards, formatting and zero-unused Knip checks; explicit boundary lint and the complete inventory comparison also passed. After integrating main `056e84786a06`, all 46 affected routing/census/PR-control cases passed, followed by a refreshed inventory comparison, boundary lint, workflow lint, formatting, final source verification, and a clean P2 review of the integration delta. Subsequent conflict-free landing rebases retained the identical reviewed patch (stable patch ID `90062e070e9a25059961eef1216cda3596314df5`). No shared test helper changed. Earlier source-bound suite and shard proof was reused; no `ci.yml` proof run was dispatched or rerun to qualify this final layout.

The measured baseline broad run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36166233840 finished in 18m43s with 134 Blacksmith jobs and 14,987.40 requested-label vCPU-minutes. Family costs were monitor 69.33, preflight 12.27, types 455.47, lint 149.87, dependencies 81.60, topology 88.00, extension boundaries 73.87, Windows 488.53, compact Node 11,846.93, supplemental Node 1,646.67, build 74.40, and gate 0.47 vCPU-minutes. The covered families now select hosted runners, so their expected Blacksmith allocation is zero; this is routing evidence, not a measured final-run saving.

Baseline hosted queue waits were p50/p95/max 2/3/22 seconds and peak occupancy was 23. The withdrawn expanded experiment reached 256 hosted jobs with waits 4/210/330 seconds; two aligned peaks would demand 512 slots against the approximately 500 shared org slots. Its failed/cancelled run does not qualify the final layout. Final wall time, per-row latency, queues, peak occupancy, and sustainable concurrent broad-PR count remain unmeasured. The final 96-active-Node cap is unchanged. Observe ordinary CI rather than spending another proof run; the earlier 8/10/18-minute targets are not claimed as proven.

Related fixture repairs landed separately: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/66898a633464e85e4aea8fd5a0fd2043c88025af (CLI diagnostic), https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e36b63c106a6df8e173cb091dbef8158a96e20a0 (Windows launcher provenance), https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b3b78c42caba45c6b78b44e16bf606db795af8c9 (restart recovery fixture), and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b9a42793fc4d8df1a8e9a4df1541ad80d9b31439 (update-lease fixture isolation). Existing upstream board, upgrade, native admission and UI virtualizer repairs were reused. Two historical native failures remain unreproduced: cron wake-now passed original and pressured shard replays, and Gateway title passed its original 99-file/1,153-case shard. Passing replays are not claimed as fixes.

prs.title: test(ui): await canonical roster before involvement assertions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the intermittent initial row-visibility failure in the source-mode session involvement e2e test. Maintainer-requested follow-up to the pre-existing failure on #154380: run `35591173211`, job `106306075661`, `checks-ui-e2e (8/13)`. That PR has merged as `d229666927c` and did not introduce this race.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. The test keeps its original visibility assertions, source server, concurrency policy, and timeout budgets.

## Why This Change Was Made

`page.goto()` only waits for document load. Foreground chat startup intentionally holds background roster hydration until the selected transcript is authoritative. The initial foreign-owned row comes from the canonical `sessions.list` snapshot; the test has not selected “Involving me” yet.

A captured Linux failure starts the visibility assertion at trace time 3.621s. Foreground history becomes ready at 8.356s, `sessions.list` starts at 8.357s, and canonical revision 1 publishes both rows at 8.451s. The assertion fails at 8.641s; the failure screenshot already contains the row. A second trace reaches the assertion deadline while the source-mode chat module graph is still loading, before `chat.startup` or `sessions.list` is sent.

The session-management fixture now waits on the existing session-owner subscription for a noncached canonical roster before starting the unchanged row assertion. It does not wait for the target row, sleep, retry, raise a timeout, or change foreground-first product admission.

## Evidence

- Linux Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m320qwmt0yc7c63a1350177j`, [lease run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35602679261), pinned source `05117d9db7bf8211ac1d5fe6b3a3da6232eedb25`. The unchanged lockfile was reused after hydration.
- Standalone source-mode file, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=8` with the config's serial source-server policy: **before 2/20 failed; after 0/20 failed**. Both baseline failures are the original initial visibility assertion; failure traces are retained. Earlier Linux Testbox sampling independently measured 2/20 on main and 0/20 on the then-PR head.
- Current CI config/shard `8/12`, including this file: **3/3 passed, 53 files and 205 tests each** (481 s, 515 s, 427 s wall). An initial environment preflight of shard 8 found missing Playwright ffmpeg; the browser prerequisite was installed before counted shard proof.
- Foreground admission / roster owner tests: **44/44 passed**; owner-first / startup-priority e2e siblings: **16/16 passed**.
- Static proof: **focused UI e2e tsgo graph, type-aware oxlint on both files, floating-Promise canary, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed**. `check-changed` passed its common guards/catalog checks; its broad 25-graph core test type pass was stopped in favor of the maintainer-authorized type-aware lint substitute and focused compiler graph.
- Measured changed-file cost (`pnpm test ui/src/e2e/session-mention-involvement.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`): **20.20 s wall / 17.524 s test time**. No new test cases or process boots.
- Independent review through P2: pre-commit and committed branch reviews both **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings.

Shard command (three planned runs, with the CI config retaining its own worker policy):

```sh
CI=true OPENCLAW_UI_E2E_SKIP_REAL_GATEWAY=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=8 \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner --shard 8/12
```

## Hosted CI

[Run 35610842110](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35610842110) tested this head. [Shard 8, job 106369786740](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35610842110/job/106369786740) passed all 53 files and 205 tests; the involvement file passed all three cases in **9.624 s**.

Two other isolated UI shards failed:

- [Shard 1, job 106369786396](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35610842110/job/106369786396): `chat-mobile-bubble-margin.e2e.test.ts`, final `system-notice` case, exceeded the unchanged 120000 ms test limit after the preceding 27 cases passed. Diagnostics were collected after teardown had closed the page, so the stalled operation is unknown.
- [Shard 11, job 106369786910](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35610842110/job/106369786910): `chat-position-rail.e2e.test.ts`, light-mode native Tab reentry, focused `position-rail-226` after sampling current marker `position-rail-230`. The renderer remained responsive; the evidence does not distinguish a position change between sampling and Tab from an incorrect keyboard entry point.

Neither failing test imports or invokes the changed readiness helper; This PR changes no production code. Log, source, caller, and recent-history inspection found no safe fix for either separate sighting. Existing earlier rail repairs are already present and cannot be claimed to resolve this failure. No CI rerun was requested. Further reproduction needs a separate Linux capture of the original case/order; these failures remain unresolved.

At handoff, `checks-node-compact-large-14` (job `106369788625`) is still running. The overall run remains in progress and cannot pass with the two UI failures above.

prs.title: chore(deps): update OpenAI SDK to 7.23.0
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updates every OpenClaw owner of the OpenAI Node SDK from 7.20.0 to 7.23.0 on the current root-lock baseline.

## User Impact

No intended user-facing behavior change. OpenAI Responses, Chat Completions, Agents API sessions/events, and memory embeddings retain their existing OpenClaw-owned request, authority, streaming, error, abort, and storage contracts.

## Scope

- Pins `openai` 7.23.0 in the root package, `packages/ai`, `extensions/agentsapi`, and `extensions/memory-lancedb`.
- Regenerates only the corresponding `pnpm-lock.yaml` records.
- Preserves the original contributor commit as the first parent and integrates current `main` as the second parent.
- Final main-relative diff: five dependency files, 15 additions and 15 deletions, with no production or test source changes.

## Upstream Contract Review

Directly compared `openai-node` v7.20.0 (`1672b1c0befbae5b87b6b57e5b3eef5b600f3b5d`) through v7.23.0 (`b073a4ddadb121d2bd17ce23e235ff969192f0e0`), including source, generated types, package metadata, README, API docs, and changelog.

- `src/client.ts:921-971` retains URL/query construction while bounding retry normalization and sanitizing logged values.
- `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:95-180` retains explicit request-option authority, including headers, retries, timeout, signal, stream, fetch, and security options.
- `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:30-105` applies the same request-option resolution without changing OpenClaw's body or stream contract.
- `src/resources/beta/agents/sessions/sessions.ts:151-180` retains managed session creation and event streaming.
- `src/resources/beta/agents/sessions/events.ts:18-92` retains message/cancellation/tool-result submission, idempotency headers, bearer security, event streaming, and abort-capable request options.
- `src/resources/embeddings.ts:15-38` retains the embedding request and response shape; this source is unchanged between the inspected tags.
- Package metadata retains Node `>=22.0.0`, the same optional peer ranges, and no install lifecycle scripts. The registry SHA-512 for 7.23.0 matches the lockfile.

## Codex Hard Gate

Personally inspected sibling Codex at exact SHA `bb1af235ea2822d7a40f75ef52e4d6a2cde84da2`.

- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/common.rs:251-329` defines the Responses request and HTTP-to-WebSocket field mapping; `:353-359` emits tagged `response.create`.
- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses.rs:60-97` and `:128-162` own HTTP `POST /responses` streaming.
- `codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs:228-332` and `:367-405` own WebSocket request/terminal-error lifecycle and the `/responses` connection.
- `codex-rs/core/src/client.rs:838-924` constructs model input, tools, reasoning, storage, stream, cache, text, and metadata fields; `:1142-1170` owns request-scoped headers and transport options.
- `codex-rs/core/src/stream_events_utils.rs:287-325` routes completed response items into cancellable tool execution.
- `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs:1656-1690`, `protocol/v2/turn.rs:387-410`, and `protocol/v2/item.rs:1233-1243,1307-1317` define thread, turn, item, raw response, and terminal notifications.
- `codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_state.rs:107-142,154-178` owns listener replacement, cancellation, active-turn projection, and terminal tracking.

Codex therefore owns its Responses wire/runtime and app-server terminal behavior independently of OpenClaw's Node SDK pin.

## memory-lancedb Persistent-Data Disposition

ClawSweeper's manifest-path persistent-data warning is not applicable to this update:

- `extensions/memory-lancedb/embeddings.ts:83-152` fingerprints provider/model/key/base URL/dimensions, submits the existing generic `/embeddings` request, and normalizes vectors locally.
- `extensions/memory-lancedb/config.ts:30-55,92-101` remains the model and dimensions owner.
- `extensions/memory-lancedb/lancedb-store.ts:24-100` retains the stored schema and fixed-size vector contract.
- `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts:101-107,147-181` retains model/dimensions startup identity while allowing only auth/base URL rotation.

The bump changes no schema, configured model or dimensions, vector normalization, database path, row format, migration, retention, or re-embedding contract.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `pnpm build`
- `packages/ai` OpenAI provider/transport focus: 13 files, 293 tests passed
- Agents API: 9 files, 150 tests passed
- memory-lancedb: 19 files, 176 tests passed
- Gateway OpenAI/OpenResponses and agent transport focus: 4 files, 221 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`
- dependency pin, patch, root-ownership, ownership-surface, install-ownership, and 104 npm lock guards passed
- `git diff --check`
- exact-head AutoReview at P1: scoped clean, no findings

`pnpm build` completed successfully. It reported the existing non-fatal Control UI startup-JS measurement at 373,672 bytes versus the 373,454-byte enforcement reference; this dependency-only diff does not touch UI source or build policy.

No changelog entry is required: this is dependency-only maintenance with no intended user-facing behavior change, schema change, or migration.

## 2026.10.10-beta.3

### Highlights

- Windows reliability: restore fresh state initialization and Gateway startup, hide SQLite helper windows during app updates, and make forced Gateway reinstalls tolerate launcher timestamp settling. (#176194, #174969, #176174, #176945; related #176111, #174906, #176163, and #176872) Thanks @skyzhao1223, @RomneyDa, @easyteacher, @throwingbones, @tjarrau-dev, and @cnnceart.
- Upgrade recovery: converge app-owned plugins to the upgraded core version, restore affected agent stores including held system agents after schema-changing updates, and scope migration rollback backups to the versioned tables being changed. (#174257, #175007, #176783, #172671; related #174120 and #176669) Thanks @RomneyDa, @kazuyuki-eguchi, and @PennyVibe.

### Changes

### Fixes

- Agent state: concurrent initialization can no longer let two agents claim ownership of the same agent database. (#174251)
- Codex and native apps: previews no longer block replies after a context refresh, session replies resume after native child recovery, bound Codex history survives app-server restarts, and native app messages send again after reconnecting. (#177716, #177564, #172705, #171528) Thanks @jjjhenriksen and @RomneyDa.
- Background tasks: completions are no longer dropped when the config changes mid-turn. (#169529; related #169054) Thanks @wangmiao0668000666, @RomneyDa, and @Oldrich333.
- Discord: restore native slash commands in channels and threads. Thanks @montrellcruse and @RomneyDa.
- Agents: keep the prompt cache when a rate-limited run retries, and preserve steering messages that arrive without an explicit target. Thanks @montrellcruse, @RomneyDa, and @obviyus.
- Cron/CLI continuity: preserve CLI chat sessions across cron announce wakes instead of resetting their provider session. (#176218; related #176208) Thanks @eliavb43 and @RomneyDa.
- CLI tools: invalidate reused CLI sessions when the available tool catalog changes, restoring tools such as `exec` after Gateway restarts and preventing stale catalogs from reaching spawned agents. (#176577; related #175670) Thanks @RomneyDa, @jackylecalvez2, and @vincentkoc.
- GMI: omit unsupported `reasoning_effort` values on GPT-5.6 tool turns so the provider no longer rejects them with HTTP 400. (#176709) Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Windows updates: recognize Scheduled Task permission denials in every Windows display language, keep Windows plugin dependency links across Doctor phases, and clean up backup scratch directories without EPERM failures. (#178624, #178219, #169672, #176836; related #176743) Thanks @RomneyDa, @n572770, @xutongxue233, and @WG-Mojo.
- Update and Doctor: update finalization honors `TMPDIR` for disposable copies, Doctor suggests a retry instead of a restore after snapshot contention, and repeated Docker container restarts no longer take a full Doctor pre-repair capture each time. (#178009, #176779, #173711; related #176750 and #173564) Thanks @RomneyDa, @WG-Mojo, and @8bitsforge.
- Memory: cold Gateway starts no longer open every memory index (restoring 2026.10.4 startup memory), memory files keep indexing after plugin reloads, and plugin reloads no longer time out during slow dreaming cleanup. (#174718, #167756, #169945) Thanks @RomneyDa and @Stronggenetics.
- Nodes: synchronous node exec output is no longer repeated as a separate `Exec finished` wake after the waiting caller already received it. (#164511) Thanks @holgergruenhagen and @obviyus.
- macOS: long exec commands through the macOS app node no longer fail after 20 seconds. (#172117; related #139706) Thanks @holgergruenhagen, @RomneyDa, @ylcn91, and @Colton-Harris.
- Control UI: offer desktop setup instead of Retry when Host Desktop is off, model pickers refresh when the catalog changes mid-read, and locale refresh works again after adding a source-only locale. (#177888, #174812, #172689; related #174368) Thanks @etzelm, @RomneyDa, and @hannesrudolph.

issues.title: webui: "Context compacted" divider never says why — background idle compaction looks identical to context-window pressure
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Every compaction in the WebUI transcript renders the same two-line divider: `Compressing context…` → `Context compacted`. It carries no information about *why* compaction ran: `ContextCompactionEvent` only has `compaction_id` + `phase` (`nanobot/events.py:37-42`), and the WebUI wire payload forwards exactly those two fields (`nanobot/webui/outbound_wire.py:101-105`).

That matters because two very different mechanisms produce that divider:

1. **Context-window pressure** inside a turn — the request no longer fits the model budget.
2. **Background idle compaction** — `idleCompactAfterMinutes` (default 15) — which rewrites the transcript into a summary checkpoint purely because the session sat idle, with no relation to the model's context window (`nanobot/agent/autocompact.py` → `Consolidator.compact_idle_session`).

On my install the second case dominates: 15 `context_compaction` records in `~/.nanobot/webui/websocket_*.jsonl`, **13 of them without a `turn_id`** (background idle path), only 2 emitted inside a turn. So the transcript keeps announcing "context compacted" on sessions that were nowhere near the 200k budget, which reads as "your model's context is exhausted" — confusing for users on large-window models.

The idle trigger is also undiscoverable from the UI: `idleCompactAfterMinutes` is config-file only (`grep -r idleCompact webui/src` → 0 hits), so there is no in-app way to learn that idleness, not window pressure, caused it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. nanobot 0.3.5, WebUI over local WebSocket; provider `opencode_go`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, preset `contextWindowTokens: 200000`.
2. Leave `idleCompactAfterMinutes` at its default (15).
3. Open a topic, send one short message, leave it idle for more than 15 minutes, come back.
4. The transcript shows `Context compacted` — indistinguishable from a real window-pressure compaction.
5. Confirm which path ran:
   ```
   grep -h context_compaction ~/.nanobot/webui/websocket_*.jsonl | grep -vc turn_id   # 13
   grep -h context_compaction ~/.nanobot/webui/websocket_*.jsonl | wc -l              # 15
   ```

### Expected Behavior

The divider should state the trigger and, ideally, the reclaim:

- `Idle compaction after 15 min idle · 12k → 3k tokens`
- `Context limit reached (182k / 200k) · summarized 140 messages`
- `Manual /compact`

and link (or at least hint) at how to turn the idle scan off, since it is not exposed in WebUI settings.

Minimally: do not render background idle compaction as a full transcript divider, or mark it explicitly as a background/maintenance compaction.

Note the inconsistency with the earlier "silent compaction" work: #5780 / #6029 made background compaction quiet on chat channels (`notify=False`), but the WebUI still renders a full divider for it, so the user-facing result of "quiet" is not visible in the WebUI.

{"event": "context_compaction", "chat_id": "301140c1-…", "compaction_id": "a86a35b533404b65b30f74a131f17b8a", "phase": "succeeded", "created_at_ms": 1792574155881}

WebSocket (WebUI)

prs.title: feat(attachments): support local files and video attachments
prs.body:
## Why

WebUI rejects videos before they reach the existing upload backend, and native TUI path pastes remain plain text. Add video attachment entry points and let both clients reference files the gateway can already read, without uploading or copying their contents.

Related to [NAN-284](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-284).

## What changed

- Share lightweight `attachment.inspect` checks and send-time workspace/readability/format/size validation in the gateway. Mixed messages use local paths or existing HTTP upload tokens and retain the current limits: one MP4/WebM/MOV video up to 20 MiB, plus four non-video attachments up to 6 MiB each / 24 MiB total.
- Add WebUI video picker/drop support and standalone-path conversion in WebUI/TUI, with removable attachments and retained text/drafts on failure. Preserve browser `File` and clipboard-image uploads, including first-message rejection/retry.
- Serve borrowed local references in place through session-scoped signed media URLs; recheck permissions, support byte ranges, reflect source changes, and keep borrowed originals out of upload/temporary-chat cleanup. Persist attachment origin so immutable uploads retain their original signed URLs and private immutable HTTP cache policy, including after canonical history replay.
- Start uploaded-video playback from the durable URL returned by `message_accepted` and preserve that player/source through canonical history hydration. Pending user bubbles do not retain the encoded video body; fresh history/reloads use the same signed URL. Local path references keep reading their original file.
- Skip upload-store inspection/pruning for text-only and local-only sends. Remove the redundant preliminary upload resolution while retaining batch validation before commit; uploaded sends return from three staging scans to the original two.
- Resolve the previously failing verification: make Windows fixtures independent of symlink privileges, copied Scoop shims, and optional username environment variables; include the process-naming type dependency in the dev environment; fix stale typed WebUI fixtures/mocks and load Vite declarations in the full-project typecheck. Make the stream idle-renewal test independent of host scheduling while retaining real timeout/cleanup checks. No tests or type checks are disabled.

## Scope

WebUI, native TUI, and their shared gateway attachment ingress/media replay are covered. The frontend and gateway ship together and use the matching release's attachment contract; no independent-upgrade compatibility layer is added. Other channels' receive/download/storage behavior is unchanged. Videos still enter the agent context as `[Attachment: path]`; native provider video input, transcoding, frame extraction, and transcription belong to NAN-190.

## Tradeoffs

Borrowed references intentionally follow the current original file rather than a snapshot. Removing a draft, discarding uploads, or deleting a session must not delete that file. Only borrowed references use `Cache-Control: no-store` to reflect changes and current permissions; managed uploads retain `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Assistant outbound staging remains unchanged. Browser files still use the existing upload pipeline, but an uploaded video no longer pins an encoded preview in its message/player state.

## Blast Radius

The shared upload batch policy, WebSocket message admission, user-media signing/replay, and both composers are affected. Signed borrowed-media URLs recheck the session workspace instead of staging a copy; managed-upload signing keeps its original ownership and cache behavior. Test/config-only follow-up commits repair the existing full-project verification failures separately from the attachment behavior changes.

## Performance follow-up

Five alternating same-machine runs compare `4e908b1` with the performance candidate `f38412977`; the original feature base (`909b277`) is also included in the send-path comparison. These measurements were not repeated after the rebase or test-only CI repair. Workloads and failures are preserved in the local evidence bundle.

| Measurement | Before → after |
| --- | --- |
| Staging scans per text / uploaded send | 1 / 3 → 0 / 2 (original base: 0 / 2) |
| 20 MiB video, settled CDP backing-storage delta after GC, median | 28,637,774 → 674,746 bytes (26.67 MiB less; not browser RSS) |
| 49,701-byte upload, second normal HTTP fetch | 50,001 → 0 transferred bytes, with identical decoded body |

The real WebSocket test completes 300 accepted/answered turns per source (50 measured + 10 warmups per run). Admission p50/p95/p99 medians are 9.13/16.04/18.97 → 9.56/15.37/17.52 ms; the original base is 9.41/14.12/17.68 ms. Completion p95/p99 medians are 128.40/173.09 → 129.42/180.89 ms, with overlapping run ranges. These results establish removal of the extra scans and the measured cache/encoded-storage costs, not blanket latency or total-memory parity. JS used-heap delta medians are 5,815,068 → 6,044,652 bytes; concurrency and other machines are not covered.

## Verification

Current source: `1cfbf6b7356fa4c38e99171f62dc4d2395a92cfe`. The latest follow-up changes only `tests/providers/test_internal_streaming.py`; production timeouts, CI commands and coverage thresholds are unchanged. All 12 renewal cases pass with a controlled 350 ms scheduling pause and fail as expected under an injected incorrect whole-call deadline. Earlier failed attempts remain archived.

| --- | --- |
| Full local Python, parallel suite + serial CLI, with coverage | PASS at `1cfbf6b73`: 10,152 passed, 131 skipped; 86.19% coverage against the unchanged 75% gate |
| Python full `basedpyright --outputjson` | PASS at `1cfbf6b73`: 411 files, 0 errors / warnings |

| Touched Python `ruff check`; full PR `git diff --check` | PASS at `1cfbf6b73` |

prs.title: fix(cron): prevent overlapping executions of the same job
prs.body:
## Problem

`CronService.run_job()` can enter the callback for a job that is already suspended in another manual run or in the scheduler. The WebUI's Run action creates a new `run_job()` task on each request, and a manual run can also overlap a due timer. Both invocations execute the agent callback and append a successful run record. This can duplicate model/tool work for one automation.

This was found by source inspection and reproduced offline on `main` at `fbb61a373f47769734a0d47d8f61935ffca84b84`; it is not a claimed production incident.

## Change

- Claim the job ID before awaiting its callback, shared by manual and timer entry points; release it in `finally`, including cancellation.
- Return `False` from an overlapping manual run, including `force=True`. Other jobs remain concurrent, and a later intentional run of the same job still works.
- Add event-coordinated regressions for manual/manual, timer/manual, manual/timer, cancellation, and persisted run history.

The guard is local to one `CronService` instance. It does not provide distributed locking or crash-safe exactly-once execution. Related #3245 proposes a persisted cross-instance claim; this patch does not implement that. Historical #961 was closed by its author in February; the current manual-run paths still reproduce the problem.

## Verification

- New regression file against unchanged main: **3 failed, 1 passed**. All three overlapping cases execute the callback twice; the cancellation control already passes.
- `python -m pytest tests/cron -q`: **181 passed** after the fix.
- `ruff check nanobot/cron/service.py tests/cron/test_cron_single_flight.py`: passed.
- `basedpyright nanobot/cron/service.py`: **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes**.
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: passed (13 rules, 216 files).
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed.

Tests ran on Windows with Python 3.12.14 and workspace-local temporary directories. The restricted sandbox initially blocked Windows asyncio's local socketpair during event-loop creation; rerunning the offline checks with local socket access allowed produced the results above. No real model/provider requests, channel delivery, full-repository suite, or browser end-to-end run were performed.

## AI assistance and review status

Codex inspected the source and related contributions, wrote and ran the before/after tests, implemented the fix, and reviewed the complete diff under LJK-ikun's direction. This PR is a draft for human review. The account owner has not yet confirmed reading and understanding every line; no human-review attestation is being made on their behalf.

prs.title: fix(exec): yield long-running commands by default (NAN-328)
prs.body:
## Why

An `exec` call that omitted `yield_time_ms` waited for process exit, potentially keeping the agent blocked for the entire configured runtime. A command can already have printed an error while leaked browser resources keep its process alive. The agent needs to regain control to inspect output and decide what to do next.

Tracks [NAN-328](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-328), including the agreed design and acceptance criteria.

## What changed

- Default model-facing `exec` observation to 1000 ms. If the command is still running, return its session ID, current output and runtime facts; continue through `exec_session` without launching it again.
- Preserve implicit closed stdin, explicit interactive stdin, independent hard/inactivity budgets and cancellation ownership. Clarify that `exec_session(until_exit=true)` is still bounded by its observation timeout.
- Preserve completed results for trusted direct `!command` through an explicit internal completion method; update output-focused tests to request or observe completion rather than assume every default call has finished.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Agent calls exec] --> B[Start managed execution]
    B --> C[Observe for at most 1000 ms by default]
    C --> D{Execution finished?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Return output and exit status]
    D -->|No| F[Return running and session ID]
    F --> G[Agent regains control]
    G -->|Observe again| H[Bounded exec_session wait]
    H --> D
    G -->|Investigate| I[Inspect logs or process state]
    G -->|Stop| J[Terminate and reap execution tree]
```

## Scope

No new scheduler, automatic stall verdict, command replay, UI changes, completion push, production configuration changes or shared-runtime restart. The temporary browser script that exposed the issue is outside this product change.

## Tradeoffs

A long command can require another tool call to observe completion. This intentionally favors returning control over holding the agent inside a tool call. Trusted direct `!` commands have no agent observer, so their existing complete-result behavior remains explicit and separate.

## Blast Radius

The shared shell execution path also serves `rg`; its schema and default observation follow the same contract. Existing runtime limits, process-tree cleanup and tool activity projection are unchanged. Consumers must treat a running result as a handle to the existing execution, not a reason to rerun it.

## Verification

- Regression-first: both real-process default-observation cases failed on the base behavior and pass with the fix, including error output followed by a still-live process, implicit stdin EOF, later output and nonzero exit.
- Full tool suite plus trusted user-shell and runtime-maintenance tests: **1268 passed, 69 skipped** (`pytest tests/tools tests/command/test_user_shell_command.py tests/agent/test_runtime_maintenance.py -q --tb=short -n 2 --dist=worksteal`).
- Ruff on all changed Python files, import boundaries and `git diff --check`: passed.
- BasedPyright on the three affected production files: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- Full-project BasedPyright did **not** complete within a 180-second command budget; no full-project typecheck success is claimed.

Local verification used the installed real ripgrep binary first on the test process PATH. With the default Scoop shim first, an unchanged test that copies `rg.exe` alone fails because its adjacent shim metadata is missing; the same failure was reproduced on the exact base, and the exact-base test passes with the real binary. No product config, test assertion or skip was changed to work around that environment issue.

prs.title: fix(webui): save settings when editing completes (NAN-323)
prs.body:
## Why

Settings currently treats a 600 ms typing pause as the end of an edit. That can save intermediate context-window values and lets an older response replace a newer draft. Save at explicit editing boundaries instead.

Refs https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-323

## What changed

- Replace the shared debounce with completion-driven, revision-deduplicated saves: blur/close/navigation complete text and numeric edits; discrete controls still save immediately.
- Serialize saves per draft owner and capture their target, preserve edits made during requests and native automatic restart, and retain failed/invalid drafts for retry instead of closing the editor.
- Apply the boundary across model presets, capabilities, network safety, channel setup and Linear. Keep empty numeric input as an invalid draft rather than silently converting it to zero.

## Scope

No backend runtime changes, dependency changes, configuration migration or larger debounce. Existing explicit creation/credential workflows remain explicit. Application UI close waits for saving; browser/process shutdown cannot guarantee asynchronous persistence.

## Blast Radius

Shared settings forms and their dialog/navigation lifecycle. Main risks are duplicate saves, wrong-target writes, newer-draft loss and failure handling; regression coverage exercises those paths.

## Verification

At `171eb6b2ce2363a55762cbe09e10a69d4b181553`:

- PASS: full-project `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run build`.
- PASS: six settings/Linear test files, **198 tests**. Includes controlled pending responses, edits during saves, renames, target switching, invalid input, failed close/retry and unmount. Native restart draft-loss regression was observed red, then green after the fix.
- PASS: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/webui/test_settings_edit_admission.py -q`, **1 test**. Controlled save/admission interleavings cover pre-commit, committed-but-response-pending, post-refresh, explicit presets and already-admitted turns.
- PASS: real Chromium + isolated gateway/provider. An intermediate `5` and final `500k` each remained focused for 1200 ms without modifying disk; closing the editor saved **500000**. A new topic received the actual `NAN323_OK` model reply, and its persisted completion recorded **context_window_tokens = 500000**.
- **FAIL: full WebUI unit suite, 3191 passed / 7 failed** (file preview, temporary-chat navigation, one Markdown-math timeout). A targeted repeat had 139 passed / 2 failed; both failures also reproduced at exact base `130f4edef` with identical dependencies. A full base run had 2689 passed / 261 failed / 234 skipped, including six hook-timeout suites, so it does not establish complete attribution for the remaining candidate failures. No timeouts/assertions were weakened and unrelated tests were not repaired.

Draft pending broad-test/CI confirmation. The isolated verification processes are stopped; production config, sessions and runtime were not changed.

## Summary

Day-0 support for `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (now live on MiniMax pay-as-you-go and Token Plan).

With the remap, nanobot sends `reasoning_effort: "low"` + `reasoning_split: true` instead.

**Behavior note:** the remap is provider-wide, so `none`/`minimal` on older MiniMax models (e.g. M2.7) now also sends `low` + `reasoning_split: true` instead of `reasoning_split: false`. I verified that M2.7 and M3 both accept this (HTTP 200). The existing M2.7 `minimal` test was updated accordingly, and a test pins the M2.7/M3 effort menu to its `main` values. Happy to scope this per-model instead if you prefer.

- `pytest tests/providers`: all pass (1420 + new cases). `test_internal_streaming.py` fails to import (`No module named 'agent'`) on `main` as well.
- Full suite (`--ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py`, as in CI): the same 17 webui/channel tests fail with and without this change (environment-related: SSH/remote/scheduling). No new failures.
- `ruff check` on the changed files: clean.

prs.title: feat(network): centralize proxy settings and add MCP routing (NAN-315)
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements [NAN-315](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-315).

- Configure one ordinary, visible shared proxy address in **Settings → Advanced**, with **Use proxy** switches for supported providers, Web access, Telegram/Discord/Slack/Matrix/WhatsApp, and HTTP/SSE MCP connections. Includes all ten locales.
- Select the route before the first MCP OAuth attempt. Discovery, registration, token exchange/refresh, transport, tool calls, reconnect, and selective hot reload share the same instance-scoped route. Explicit proxy failures do not fall back to direct connections; target and redirect SSRF checks remain enforced.
- Migrate legacy single-address file/environment settings after source merging; preserve saved opt-outs and unresolved credential references. Existing two-argument channel plugins retain their construction API through explicit shared-proxy opt-in.
- Follow-up review repairs register the public MCP proxy mutation, retire consumed proxy drafts without overriding later saved opt-outs, preserve OAuth-provider false flags across saves, handle combined-userinfo/Discord scheme environment templates correctly, and keep proxy credentials out of connection traceback diagnostics while retaining useful error details.
- Update usage and upgrade documentation. MCP error classification/copy remains in [NAN-316](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-316).

## Upgrade notes

`network.proxy` replaces per-feature addresses; features store `useProxy` flags. One old address is promoted automatically on load and written on the next normal save. Different old addresses require explicitly choosing one shared address; no multi-proxy compatibility is retained.

For an old Discord configuration using an entire URL environment reference plus separate credentials, first combine them into one full-URL environment variable and set `network.proxy` to it. Literal URLs and scheme templates with credential references migrate without writing resolved secrets.

## Verification

Tested source: `7aa0515c1a92b2f8e65756cf5ebc328b507eab20`; frozen comparison base: `b32b1327ceb0e7fb9ecbb3ad9f0e7bf04fccb8a6`. Tracked dependencies and lockfiles are unchanged. Three independent first-pass review areas and a fresh repair cross-boundary review were completed; source review is separate from runtime evidence below.

| Check | Actual result |

| Config + Docker configuration + complete settings routes | 237 passed, 1 existing platform skip |
| Full Python, `pytest tests nanobot/channels -n 3 --dist loadfile -q --tb=short` | **FAIL:** 10,278 passed, 130 skipped, 4 failed. The same four signatures reproduce in the exact frozen-base attribution subset: configured ripgrep shim, Windows symlink privilege, and two remote-discovery username/environment cases |
| Full Vitest, `bun run test --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` | 3,045 passed across 172 files |
| Complete local Playwright suite, one worker, zero retries | 176 passed; own Chrome contexts |
| Full BasedPyright | **FAIL:** the same two unresolved/unknown `setproctitle` diagnostics as the exact frozen base |
| Ruff, Python/client import boundaries, WebUI typecheck/lint, production build, diff check | Passed; build retains the existing chunk-size advisory |
| Isolated built gateway + real Chrome, desktop/narrow | Visible-address save/refresh/clear, first-OAuth proxy setup, missing-address refusal, unavailable-proxy failure, public WebSocket proxy mutation, and saved disabled state after refresh passed |
| Real recording proxy + MCP SDK | Discovery, registration, token exchange/refresh, activation, tool calls, and terminated-session recovery use the selected route |
| Diagnostic safety regressions | Real HTTPX constructor and setup/cleanup chain/group failures retain useful type/stack/stage text without raw or decoded selected-proxy credentials; short credentials do not corrupt diagnostic words |

The new worktree initially lacked the ignored environment `uv.lock`, causing one additional benchmark prerequisite failure. Copying the unchanged provisioned lock after verifying identical pyproject bytes fixed that setup; the benchmark and full Python rerun above include it, with no dependency sync or test weakening.

## Figma authorization limitation

The shared proxy reaches the real Figma MCP 401 challenge and OAuth discovery metadata 200. The actual first-authorization attempt then receives **403 Forbidden during client registration** at `https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/mcp/register`. User-Agent, minimal-metadata, and callback-host controls did not change that refusal.

[Figma's official remote-server instructions](https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/) require approved MCP clients and direct new clients to request access. This is a service-side prerequisite consistent with the observed registration refusal; full Figma account authorization remains blocked, not passed. No client-name impersonation or speculative transport workaround was added.

Production configuration and shared gateways were not changed. The user's earlier preview is preserved, and the repaired preview uses separate synthetic data. Final-head CI is reported separately from local verification.

At the bounded final-head status check, [CI run 39588557900](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39588557900) was still running. Python 3.11, Windows process compatibility, and Docker had passed; remaining jobs were pending/in progress. No continuous CI monitoring was started.

prs.title: fix(agent): finalize stopped turns without checkpoints (NAN-211)
prs.body:
## Why

Stopping a request before its first runtime checkpoint leaves `pending_user_turn` persisted. `/stop` reports success, but the next gateway startup treats that marker as an interrupted request and shows an unnecessary recovery decision.

Linear: [NAN-211](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-211)

## What changed

- Materialize any available checkpoint, then finalize the cancelled turn through the existing session owner's `finish_turn()` operation regardless of whether a checkpoint exists.
- Preserve completed tool results and the existing shutdown/discard guards.
- Add a persisted 2×2 regression covering explicit stop versus gateway shutdown, both before a model response and after completed tools. Update the existing checkpoint-preservation test to observe the owner operation used for finalization.

## Scope

This fixes newly stopped turns. It does not migrate or clear pre-existing recovery metadata, change the frontend, alter recovery classification, or change storage schemas. Gateway shutdown continues to preserve interrupted work for confirmation.

## Blast Radius

The change is confined to the AgentLoop cancellation finalizer and its tests. Explicit stop must clear pending state without losing completed work; lifecycle shutdown must still retain recovery state. Both contracts are covered by the regression and real-process checks.

## Verification

- Regression first: **1 failed / 3 passed** on the unmodified base; the failure was the stopped request without a checkpoint. All four cases pass after the fix.
- `uv run --no-sync python -B -m pytest tests/agent tests/session tests/command -q -n 3 --dist loadfile`: **2284 passed, 4 skipped**.
- CI's repository-wide `ruff check` scope: **passed**.
- `uv run --no-sync python -B -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: **passed** (13 rules, 216 files).
- Real gateway processes and WebSockets with an isolated loopback OpenAI-compatible SSE fixture: reproduced the erroneous recovery on the base; verified stop-before-response and stop-after-tools remain recovery-free after graceful process shutdown/restart, completed tool results remain saved, and genuine gateway shutdown still requires recovery confirmation. Restart did not issue another model request. All owned processes, listeners and temporary runtime data were cleaned up.
- Full-project BasedPyright: **FAIL**, with two Windows `setproctitle` import/type diagnostics in `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py`. The frozen base, checked with the same interpreter/dependencies, produces the identical two diagnostics. No type-check success is claimed.

The provider fixture is local and deterministic; live-provider and browser visual acceptance were not performed. There are no frontend changes.
