prs.title: feat(a2a): Add A2A Protocol support for agent-to-agent communication
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds full [A2A Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org) support to nanobot, enabling agent-to-agent communication.

## Features

### 1. A2A Server (`channels/a2a.py`)
- Exposes nanobot as an A2A-compatible agent
- Agent Card served at `/.well-known/agent.json`
- JSON-RPC endpoint for `message/send` and `message/stream`
- Integrates with nanobot's message bus and agent loop

### 2. A2A Client Tool (`agent/tools/a2a_client.py`)
- `call_a2a_agent` tool for calling external A2A agents
- Agent discovery and capability inspection
- Message sending with response extraction

### 3. Configuration (`config/schema.py`)
- `A2AConfig` with host, port, streaming, skills
- Optional `public_host` for Agent Card URL
- Request timeout configuration

## Installation

```bash
pip install "nanobot-ai[a2a]"
```

## Configuration

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "a2a": {
      "enabled": true,
      "port": 8080,
      "publicHost": "https://my-agent.example.com"
    }
  }
}
```

## Usage

### As an A2A Server
```bash
nanobot gateway
# Agent Card: http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent.json
```

### Calling Other A2A Agents
The agent can use the `call_a2a_agent` tool to communicate with other A2A-compatible agents:

```
User: Ask the travel agent at https://travel.example.com to book a flight to Paris
```

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   nanobot                     │
│                                               │
│  channels/                                    │
│    telegram.py  discord.py  a2a.py  ← NEW    │
│              │                                │
│              ↓                                │
│  bus/ → agent/loop.py → tools/               │
│                           a2a_client.py ← NEW │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

External A2A Agent ←→ a2a.py (server)
nanobot ←→ a2a_client.py (tool) ←→ External A2A Agent
```

## Testing

```bash
# Start nanobot with A2A
nanobot gateway

# Verify Agent Card
curl http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent.json

# Test with A2A Inspector
git clone https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-inspector.git
cd a2a-inspector
uv run . --agent-url http://localhost:8080
```

## References

- [A2A Protocol Specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/)
- [A2A Python SDK](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-python)
- [A2A Samples](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-samples)

prs.title: fix(qq): clarify QR binding states and setup actions
prs.body:
## Why

Reopening QQ setup currently loses the visible saved-credential state, while generic connection labels blur QR binding and a running channel. Make the state and next action clear with short labels and existing UI controls, rather than adding explanatory paragraphs.

## What changed

- Keep a persistent configured summary with App ID and a separate runtime badge; use explicit bind, rebind, refresh and retry actions. Show the warning only after clicking Rebind bot: rebinding may interrupt other apps, and apps using an old App Secret need the new one if it is reset. Cancelling sends no request, and confirming opens a new QR code. No warning remains on the configured summary.
- Keep manual setup reachable during scanning and group its fields by credentials, access, behavior and advanced options. Align shared QR presentation with the existing typography and button variants.
- Distinguish temporary portal/transport retries, expiry, failure and cancellation. Clear retry feedback on recovery without losing cancellation errors, and localize the QQ states in all ten supported languages.

## Scope

This is a follow-up to #6333. QQ credential storage, decryption, channel enabling and protocol 1/core requirements are unchanged. The optional `retrying` response field is additive; clients that do not use it retain their existing pending behavior. No agent execution or security-policy changes.

## Blast Radius

The shared channel setup title, connect-mode manual-field grouping and QR presentation also serve other channels. Shared polling now tracks the failed action so a recovered poll clears only its own error, successful cancellation clears stale feedback, and a failed cancellation remains visible until resolved. Existing credential-mode forms and save handlers are retained.

## Verification

- Python: QQ tests, channel setup/plugin/contracts and WebUI settings services/routes/client-contract suites — 311 passed. Optional channel dependencies were installed in the isolated worktree environment before the successful run.
- Frontend: QQ view/adapter recovery, channel settings, identity, locales, registry, WeChat views and component gallery tests passed. After moving the warning into a rebind confirmation, the settings, QQ adapter, locale and gallery suites passed again (56 tests); the integration test checks that cancellation makes no request and confirmation starts one QR flow.
- Frontend lint, production build, typecheck, Python Ruff, import-boundary checks and `git diff --check` passed. The production build reports a large-chunk warning.
- Isolated authenticated loopback gateway: real QQ QR creation and cancellation; manual setup and lower controls reachable at 375px; English/light and Chinese/dark rendering checked in Chromium. Configured/offline reopening and retry/expiry/failure displays were checked with explicitly simulated display fixtures, without saving fake credentials. The rebind confirmation was checked on desktop English/light and 375px Chinese/dark: Cancel and post-animation Escape restore focus without starting a request, and confirmation starts exactly one real QR flow.
- Conditional-warning follow-up: all ten locale warnings and the English fallback were checked without changing keys or interpolation tokens. The same 56 frontend tests, lint, typecheck and production build passed; Vitest/Vite used Node after the local Bun config loader failed to start them, with no dependency or configuration changes. Chromium gallery checks at 1280px English/light and 375px Chinese/dark confirmed the longer warning fits and Cancel/Escape restore focus; no gateway or QQ requests were made.
- No real QQ account was scanned or authorized during this change. End-to-end QQ messaging and non-Chromium browsers were not revalidated.

prs.title: fix(webui): parse CJK emphasis at delimiter boundaries
prs.body:
## Why
Chinese replies can expose literal `**` when punctuation touches an emphasis delimiter and the next sentence starts immediately. The previous text-node repair cannot recognize emphasis spanning inline code or links. Resolve CJK emphasis boundaries during parsing instead of repairing the parsed text with regular expressions.

Tracks [NAN-320](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-320).

## What changed
- Register the parse-only entrypoint of `remark-cjk-friendly` 2.3.3 and remove the old CJK strong-boundary AST rewrite and its obsolete position shape.
- Cover the original long reply, nested code/links/emphasis, Chinese opening and closing punctuation, Japanese and Korean boundaries, standard Markdown, escapes/entities, code isolation, and streaming-to-complete rendering.
- Add isolated browser regressions through the real lazy `MarkdownText` entrypoint at 390px and 1440px, including an incomplete streaming prefix followed by completion.

## Scope
Client-side emphasis parsing only. No history rewriting, server protocol changes, new HTML permissions, URL-policy changes, or daily-instance deployment. This is a CJK emphasis extension to CommonMark, not a claim that the triggering source is recognized as emphasis by strict CommonMark or that every Markdown ambiguity is solved. It does not add a CJK strikethrough extension.

## Tradeoffs
The old repair also accepted a space immediately inside a closing delimiter, such as `**边界说明： **issue`. With the explicitly agreed compatibility boundary, invalid internal-whitespace emphasis remains literal after completion rather than being silently rewritten. The former positive test is replaced with explicit literal-output coverage, not deleted. Valid alternatives include `**边界说明：** issue` and `**中文**。继续`.

Use the maintained tokenizer extension rather than expanding the local regular expression across AST siblings or replacing the entire renderer. The parse-only import avoids loading its Markdown serialization path into the renderer; both npm and Bun locks record the dependency chain.

## Blast Radius
All consumers of the shared Markdown renderer, including replies and document previews, receive the CJK emphasis rules. Existing math, code, HTML-subset and link handling remain on their existing paths. Streaming may temporarily complete unfinished Markdown as before; final rendering uses the unmodified source and the same grammar. No host capability or persistence changes are needed.

## Verification
- Red first: both new nested code/link regression cases failed against the old text-node repair.
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: passed; actual loaded `remark-cjk-friendly` 2.3.3 / `micromark-extension-cjk-friendly` 2.0.2.
- `npm ci --ignore-scripts --dry-run`: passed.
- `bun run test`: 176 files, 3123 tests passed, including 134 renderer cases.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint`: passed.
- `bun run check:imports`: passed; `bun run test:imports`: 41 passed, 1 Windows-only case skipped on Linux.
- `NANOBOT_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=4293 bun run test:browser -- markdown-emphasis.spec.ts`: 2 Chromium cases passed; isolated Vite fixture server exited and port released.
- `bun run build` and `git diff --check`: passed. Build retains a large-chunk warning; renderer tests emit KaTeX warnings.

The browser checks use synthetic content, not a live gateway or real conversation. Windows/macOS runtime acceptance and remote CI are not established by these local Linux checks. A separate scoped candidate check found no blocking issue; no formal GitHub approval or merge is implied.

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve cross-session provenance at display persistence
prs.body:
## Why
Cross-session messages could reach the agent but lose their source handle in live display and reloaded history. The display-history migration in #6336 required a generation on `UserInputAccepted` even though this event does not guarantee one.

## What changed
- Remove the generation requirement from the cross-session display helper and coordinator. Append to the current existing destination in one storage transaction, without a separate identity lookup or original-generation binding.
- Allow an explicit `expected_generation=None` for current-target history writes. Existing callers that supply a generation keep their original generation checks; missing sessions are not created.
- Publish the live input event only after its display record is saved; a failed write does not produce a transient input that reload cannot restore.

## Scope
No loop, sending-tool, handle-resolution, execution-admission, protocol, or frontend changes. This PR does not promise that a handle or target key remains bound to its original session lifetime. It does not backfill already missing provenance.

## Tradeoffs
Session messaging targets the current destination, not a pinned generation. The earlier lookup/compare path and the tests for that stronger contract have been removed. A current-target append is an explicit storage operation, not a missing-generation fallback for other writers: all existing generation-bound callers continue supplying their original fence.

## Verification
- Retain real tool → bus → coordinator coverage for idle and active targets, asserting source metadata in both live events and committed history.
- Retain existing stale-generation protections for other history writers. Add a current-target append check after reset and reuse the coordinator test for successful/failed persistence.
- Focused suite: 48 passed.
- Broader suite: `python -m pytest tests/agent tests/session tests/tools/test_session_messages_tool.py tests/utils/test_webui_turn_helpers.py tests/utils/test_webui_transcript.py -q --tb=short` — 2,226 passed.
- Changed-file Ruff, scoped BasedPyright, import boundaries and diff check: passed.
- The acceptance instance has not been restarted or redeployed for this revision.

prs.title: fix(webui): admit history without dropping live output (NAN-311)
prs.body:
## Why

A live reply arriving before history could make ThreadShell reject the entire persisted page while its independent pager kept advancing, eventually reporting that no earlier history existed. Give the received transcript and accepted page frontier one synchronous owner, so safe history prefixes become visible without replacing live output.

Linear: [NAN-311](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-311)

## What changed

- Replace Shell's whole-page veto, text/first-ID overlap heuristics and paint-time coordination with atomic body, source coverage and paging admission in `ThreadTranscript`.
- Preserve the full projection cursor across detach/cache restoration; admit source-closed history prefixes and retain foreground continuation, Stop/run fencing and exact receipt holes. HTTP adds response-only source receipts; stored records and schema stay unchanged.
- Add source-bearing integration tests and five controlled real-browser scenarios covering live-first/history-first arrival, pagination, delayed frames, cache return, equal-text segments and a narrow viewport. Preserve the latest main's answer-order and cross-session-input behavior.

## Scope

WebUI transcript hydration, pagination, trace-detail application and private replay cache. Backend execution, queue scheduling, model context, storage migration and independent prompt-navigation behavior are unchanged. Rebased onto main `76da55994`.

## Tradeoffs

The private cache retains source/admission metadata as well as rows, within the existing byte/entry bounds. A narrow synthetic probe (seven fresh-state pairs in one Bun process, 2,000 direct chunks) measured median accumulated projector CPU of 1.14 → 6.92 ms; historical admission median/max was 1.84/8.67 ms. Serialized snapshot size was 585,410 versus 515,674 bytes for rows alone. These are CPU/serialization measurements, not browser latency or resident-RAM results.

## Blast Radius

The changed owner serves initial history, reconnect publication, older pages, live events and cache re-entry. The main risks are discarding a received tail, suppressing an uninstalled source, or losing a projection fence; tests cover these paths, including truncated textless-end windows. No new polling, artificial delay, text deduplication or permanent subscription is introduced.

## Verification

On `b8ae8c755`:

- Full WebUI typecheck, lint, import checks/tests and production build passed.
- Full WebUI coverage suite: **3,094 passed**, zero failed/skipped (`--maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2`; unchanged scope and thresholds).
- Full Playwright suite: **197 passed**, zero failed/skipped/flaky; one worker, zero retries.
- Affected Python transcript/storage/turn tests: **72 passed**; scoped Ruff and BasedPyright passed. Python import-boundary checks passed.
- Built gateway/WebUI with a fresh, isolated SQLite copy: health/bootstrap and older-page HTTP 200, visible prepend, zero browser page errors. One `websockets` HTTP `eof_sent` assertion was logged; attribution is still open and transport code is unchanged in this PR.
- The five new controlled browser cases failed on the original `b32b1327` baseline and pass on this rebased candidate. Two additional closed-wire preservation cases were red on the first rebase candidate, then green after the admission fix.

The browser reproducer uses real ThreadShell/NanobotClient with controlled HTTP/WebSocket boundaries. The original recording and copied session data remain private; maintainer trial acceptance is pending.

prs.title: ci: scope native acceptance and bind release candidate artifacts
prs.body:
## Why

Small frontend changes currently inherit native installation and upgrade/recovery acceptance on both Linux and Windows. In the inspected main run, the Windows packaged-recovery step alone took 21m30s and its enclosing job about 31 minutes. Separate code validation from release-package acceptance, without deleting recovery scenarios or reducing the Python compatibility matrix.

## What changed

- Centralize affected-path selection with per-path explanations and a stable `CI required` check. Keep shared client consumers covered; retain full selection for unknown paths, unavailable diffs and manual runs. Windows isolated installer/update journeys and reusable native acceptance run for relevant PRs/manual checks, not ordinary main pushes.
- Keep ordinary TUI checks separate from native packaging/install/update acceptance. Preserve the complete nine-scenario recovery suite and add incrementally persisted phase timings, including failure evidence, without uploading raw credential-bearing logs.
- Build release candidates once, transfer the exact Linux/Windows wheels by immutable producer artifact IDs, verify manifest/package/commit identity before execution, and require both native consumers before promoting an explicitly requested installable handoff. Producer IDs also support failed-jobs-only retries without rebuilding or looking for a nonexistent new-attempt artifact.

## Scope

No automatic release, signing, catalogue advancement, scheduling, branch-protection changes or production-service changes. Python platform/version coverage, frontend/browser/terminal checks and Docker safety checks remain. Candidate fixture acceptance does not replace real historical baselines, remaining native-platform coverage or public-download acceptance. Requiring the stable aggregate check in repository rules remains an administrator-owned action.

## Tradeoffs

The path policy is deliberately conservative and requires maintenance when shared contracts or installed-lifecycle inputs move. Regression coverage includes the actual frozen update-worker archive inputs, Docker pytest files and the TUI fork-chat backend. Native scenarios still run serially inside their shared private installation; this change removes unrelated scheduling, not a measured acceleration of the specialized recovery flow. No speedup percentage is claimed.

## Blast Radius

CI selection, conditional job execution, candidate artifact handoff and diagnostic evidence only; production update/recovery behavior is unchanged. Key risks are missing a consumer or installation input, treating an unexpected skip as success, and testing different bytes from those handed off. Tests cover these boundaries, producer-ID wiring, commit/hash mismatch rejection, diff ranges, renames, failure/timeout timing evidence and cleanup.

## Verification

- Focused Python contract tests: **102 passed** on Python 3.12.10: `tests/scripts/test_ci_scope.py`, `test_ci_gate.py`, `test_ci_workflows.py`, `test_native_acceptance_input.py`, plus `tests/test_packaged_update_probe.py`, `tests/test_release_candidate.py`, and `tests/test_installed_release_probe.py`.
- Actionlint **1.7.12**: all repository workflows passed. Its current action metadata recognizes `download-artifact@v4` producer artifact-ID downloads; the actual upstream action definition was also checked.
- Ruff **0.17.1**: all changed/new Python scripts and associated tests passed; `git diff --check` passed. No formatter was run.
- Regression-first review fixes: five focused policy cases failed before fixing Docker pytest selection, frozen-worker `data_access`, shared fork-chat selection and the installed WebUI launcher; all now pass.
- Selection-only replay used complete paginated file lists from eight merged PRs. Pure frontend PRs #6369 and #6335 select WebUI/Docker without native recovery; actual installation/update changes retain native acceptance. This is selection proof, not execution-time measurement.
- Native GitHub runner execution and the manual release-candidate transfer path were not executed locally. The signature-only suite was not validated in the local interpreter, which lacks `sigstore`; signing code and its workflow are unchanged. CI results on this PR provide separate runtime evidence, not a claim of release approval.


### CI follow-up

Run `39614121240` passed Linux and Windows native acceptance, Linux Python, both clients and Docker. Windows Python exposed two test fixtures that tried to create Unix-only filenames; the injection test now constructs actual Git trees without materializing invalid Windows paths, preserving newline/output-escaping coverage. prs.title: fix(webui): keep version checks on the gateway event loop
prs.body:
## Why

Checking for updates could return `version check failed` and interfere with HTTP MCP connections when both used the shared pinned-DNS transport. The settings route ran the checker in a worker thread, where `asyncio.run()` created a temporary event loop that competed for the gateway's loop-bound transport lock. Unavailable-channel copy also guessed publication or network causes instead of stating the failed check.

## What changed

- Make release discovery async end-to-end on the gateway loop with an explicitly awaitable callback; remove the synchronous wrapper without masking errors or weakening DNS-pinning protections.
- Add a regression through the settings router, real checker, release feed, and pinned-DNS transport under contention, including a successful subsequent MCP-like request; update existing tests to await the checker.
- Shorten the existing unavailable-channel message in all ten supported locales to a factual failed-check status, keeping the existing Check again action and updating its existing test assertion.

## Scope

No HTTP payload, authentication, release-channel behavior, dependency, installation, or restart-policy changes. This removes the version check's conflicting temporary loop; it does not redesign the shared transport for arbitrary multi-loop embedding. The copy follow-up replaces existing strings only: no new locale keys, components, layout, error classification or publishing behavior. It does not create or publish a release index. No daily gateway was updated or restarted.

## Blast Radius

Version checks now share the gateway's event loop with other asynchronous release and MCP requests. The shared network safety checks and serialization are unchanged. The regression mocks only external DNS/HTTP I/O; it does not claim authenticated end-to-end verification against Linear.

## Verification

- Red before the fix: the new concurrent transport regression returned HTTP 500 instead of 200 on the baseline implementation.
- Green: `python -m pytest tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py tests/webui/test_version_check.py tests/webui/test_update_plans.py tests/test_release_feed.py tests/security/test_security_network.py tests/agent/test_mcp_connection.py -q` — 210 passed.
- `ruff check nanobot/webui/version_check.py nanobot/webui/settings_system.py tests/webui/test_version_check.py tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py` — passed.
- `basedpyright nanobot/webui/version_check.py nanobot/webui/settings_system.py nanobot/webui/settings_routes.py` — 0 errors, warnings, or notes.
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Started an isolated loopback gateway with fresh data and no real provider/MCP credentials. Unauthenticated version checks returned 401; six concurrent authenticated checks against real PyPI (four channel-status, two legacy payloads), followed by another check, all returned HTTP 200 with the expected current-version payload. The owned test gateway was stopped after verification.
- Read-only independent inspection of the backend candidate found no material findings. This is not a formal GitHub review or a full-suite compatibility claim.
- Copy follow-up: `bun run test src/tests/i18n.test.tsx src/tests/update-channels.test.tsx src/tests/settings-overview.test.tsx src/tests/update-notice.test.tsx src/tests/update-flow.test.tsx` — 109 passed; full WebUI lint and client import boundaries passed.
- Compared all ten supported locale bundles with the previous head: only the existing `updates.channel.unavailable` values changed; key sets and interpolation tokens are preserved. No channel-owned strings are affected.
- Production build passed into a separate output directory. The running interactive acceptance instance's served index hash is unchanged; it was not restarted or silently updated with this copy follow-up.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add signed direct delivery webhook
prs.body:
## Summary

Add an optional authenticated webhook that routes final notification text directly to nanobot's outbound message bus, bypassing the agent loop and all model calls.

This enables deterministic notifications from trusted systems such as CI, monitoring, and billing services while reusing existing channel delivery and retry behavior.

## Design

- disabled by default
- separate loopback-only listener by default
- fixed configured `channel` and `chatId` (callers cannot choose a destination)
- HMAC-SHA256 authentication over timestamp, request ID, and raw body
- bounded timestamp freshness window and in-memory replay detection
- body-size and per-minute request limits
- strict `{ "content": "..." }` payload
- publishes only `OutboundMessage`; no inbound event reaches `AgentLoop`
- complete configuration and signing documentation

## Security

The signature input is:

```text
<timestamp>.<request-id>.<raw request body>
```

The listener rejects missing or invalid signatures, stale timestamps, duplicate request IDs, oversized payloads, and rate-limit excesses. Documentation recommends loopback/private networking or TLS behind a reverse proxy.

## Tests

Updated against upstream main on 2026-09-16. Resolved the configuration-test conflict by keeping upstream's removal of the obsolete heartbeat test and retaining the direct-delivery tests.

- Focused direct-delivery, gateway configuration, and gateway-runtime tests: 17 passed.
- Gateway, configuration, message-bus, and gateway-runtime regression tests: 210 passed, 2 skipped.
- `ruff check` on the changed Python files: passed.
- Targeted BasedPyright check on `direct_delivery.py`, `schema.py`, and `gateway_runtime.py`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

prs.title: feat(mcp): add opt-in self-contained Apps hosting in WebUI
prs.body:
Nanobot currently reduces MCP results to model-facing text/image artifacts and exposes app-only tools to the model. This adds an opt-in MCP Apps host: structured results stay outside model context, while self-contained HTML Apps can render in the WebUI and call approved tools on their originating MCP connection.

Refs #5251. The earlier #5386 was withdrawn; this is an independent implementation. Enable with `channels.websocket.mcpAppsEnabled: true` and restart the gateway. It defaults to false, preserves WebUI protocol 1, and advertises the optional `webui.mcp-apps.v1` capability only when enabled.

The implementation spans the complete path:

- Preserve bounded, detached MCP rich results in `ToolResult.data`, including source identity, metadata, schemas and result fields. Error guidance retains this data; model observation normalization strips it before messages/checkpoints are built.
- Honor model/App visibility independently of `enabledTools`. Bind each App to its original connection and declared `ui://` resource, with URI/MIME/UTF-8 validation and connection-close revocation.
- Negotiate `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` for enabled gateway MCP connections. Carry only ephemeral App handles in ordinary progress attachments; rich UI data is fetched through authenticated WebUI mutations.
- Use the official AppBridge in an opaque-origin iframe with restrictive CSP. Every tool call requires a host-owned approval outside the iframe, then consumes a single-use receipt bound to the exact recorded arguments and chat. Requests cannot reach another server or bypass its allowlist. Request cancellation before approval removes the prompt and prevents dispatch.
- Load the AppBridge module on demand, reject stale loads after host/session switches, retain text fallbacks, localize controls in all ten locales, and document configuration, architecture and limits.

This initial host supports **self-contained Apps**. It blocks external assets/fetches and does not grant requested browser/device permissions. Temporary-chat rendering, durable App recovery, external-domain policy and host-side App installation are outside this change. HTML is capped at 1 MiB; rich messages at 64 KiB/depth 16/4096 values; at most 32 handles are retained for 15 minutes. The bridge does not retry possibly committed tool actions or claim exactly-once execution. CSP is not a general network firewall against iframe navigation.

Validation at `86520222e9afe0882c157e85afd455a197d0cd42`:

- Python: **1540 passed, 11 skipped**, covering WebUI, WebSocket, MCP, reconnect and bridge behavior after merging current main.
- WebUI: **3030 passed across 173 files**, including stale-host payload rejection and ordinary activity/client behavior.
- Ruff, strict BasedPyright on changed production modules, Python/client import boundaries, WebUI typecheck/lint and production build pass.
- Real in-memory MCP sessions prove enabled/disabled capability negotiation, source/visibility/allowlist restrictions, structured results and revocation. A live authenticated WebSocket test proves approval dispatch and identical-request replay without a second tool execution.
- Chromium checks on the actual AppBridge/card fixture prove initialization, structured weather data, blocked parent access/fetches, rejection with zero executions, one approved call/result, forged message-source rejection, cancellation before approval, and a 390px viewport. The fixture is included at `/browser/mcp-apps.html`; it is not a live model or external-provider test.
- Initial regression tests failed on the unchanged base (11 failed/127 passed). An earlier broader tools/agent run also hit 26 GitStore/Dream failures reproduced on base because its test temp directory is inside a checkout; no test assertions or production guards were relaxed.

Implemented and tested with AI assistance. No live model credentials or external MCP deployments were used.

prs.title: feat(webui): edit and resend messages in the same session
prs.body:
## Why

Users need to correct a sent message without creating another sidebar topic. This implements the approved in-place edit: keep the prefix before the selected user message, replace that message and its entire suffix, and generate a new reply in the same session.

Related to [NAN-92](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-92/webui-支持编辑并重新发送已发送的用户消息).

## What changed

- Add **Edit message** beside Copy in the existing desktop/mobile message actions, using the existing `EditIcon`. Edit directly inside the same native user-message bubble, preserving its background, typography and natural sizing. The focused editor has its own draft, Cancel and Resend controls, actionable errors, and concise translations in all 10 locales; Composer drafts, attachments and waiting input stay separate.
- Route replacement through gateway idle admission and the session-state owner. Revision-bound anchors, an SQLite transaction, a recoverable display-transcript journal and persisted retry receipts preserve session identity and accept the new input exactly once.
- Fence discarded history by generation across drafts, streams, HTTP pages, trace details, navigation caches and late subagent results. Invalidate obsolete summaries/provider continuation and reuse the shared history-prefix boundary while preserving the existing **New conversation** fork behavior.
- Settle interrupted edit journals under the transcript deletion lock. Restore old display files only while the original canonical generation still exists; deletion or recreation retires the journal instead of resurrecting removed messages. Close the recovery SQLite connection explicitly on Windows.

## Scope

The first version supports persisted ordinary user text in saved WebUI sessions. Attachments, quotes, session/CLI/MCP mentions, slash/shell commands and special/system deliveries are explicitly rejected rather than resent with lost metadata. Temporary Chat has no persisted edit target; shared history cannot be edited from an individual conversation. The WebUI and gateway ship together: message editing has no per-feature compatibility gate or gateway-unsupported fallback.

Resend is the only destructive authorization, with no second modal. The URL, session ID, handle, title, creation identity, workspace, permissions and model settings remain unchanged. There is no backup topic, branch picker or version tree. Previously executed file/Shell effects are not rolled back.

## Tradeoffs

Canonical history lives in SQLite while the display transcript remains file-backed. A temporary rollback journal coordinates their commit and crash recovery; it is removed after settlement and is not a retained conversation version. Pre-acceptance failures preserve the previous effective history. A model failure after acceptance keeps the new failed turn instead of restoring the discarded suffix.

## Blast Radius

This touches session admission/persistence, WebUI transcript reads and WebSocket delivery, frontend history reconciliation, and subagent result ownership. The main risks are cross-client races, stale events restoring a removed suffix, and retry/crash behavior around the two persistence projections. Existing new-fork behavior is covered separately; this does not redesign subagent cancellation or external-effect rollback.

## Verification

Published source: `6fc74f88896877b2b8c8b3010546d95cef63cc75`, based on `909b277e7a5a7ecd2aebdba9611e5febe86988d9`. The latest follow-up fixes interrupted-edit recovery after deletion/recreation, removes the new edit capability gate, and replaces the misleading conversation/gateway-unavailable error with the actual shared-history restriction in all 10 locales. Missing required edit services are composition errors, not optional older-gateway behavior. The earlier native-bubble integration, helper-line removal, strict typing/task-context fixes and test-only CLI fixture fix remain intact.

| --- | --- |
| Fresh related Python tests | **110 passed** across message editing, pre/post-commit crash recovery and delete/recreate regressions, forking, client contract, agent admission and transcript/thread helpers |
| Fresh full ThreadShell and editor component files | **123 passed**, including saved-message edit/Resend through the full shell without an edit capability flag |
| Fresh i18n tests and 10-locale content audit | **29 passed**; only the obsolete unavailable error key is replaced with the shared-history error in each locale |
| Fresh Ruff; strict BasedPyright; Python import boundaries | **PASS**; BasedPyright reports 0 errors/warnings/notes, import boundaries cover 10 rules / 166 files |
| Fresh WebUI lint; `git diff --check` | **PASS** |
| Fresh `bun run build` | **PASS**, with the existing Vite >500 kB chunk warning; output is isolated outside the retained preview |
| Fresh `bun x tsc --noEmit` | **FAIL**, exit 2, **473 diagnostics**. Normalized `(file, TS code, message)` diagnostics exactly match committed head `723e670f62ea4df73611702f086acdfdae943be0`, with none added or removed. |

Owned listener closes and temporary data is removed. |

The earlier deletion-fix broad backend command had **882 passed, 18 skipped, 2 failed**. Both failures are Windows remote-discovery tests whose `getpass.getuser()` cannot find username environment variables in this execution sandbox; the exact committed tests and owning modules reproduced the same failures. No environment/config workaround or unrelated remote-discovery change was made. The 110-test final-snapshot run is focused verification, not a replacement claim that this broader command passed. prs.title: refactor(config): separate config reads from network policy activation
prs.body:
Reading another config, inspecting settings, or attempting a config write used to replace the running process's SSRF whitelist. `load_config` now only reads and validates configuration. Runtime initialization and accepted refresh paths explicitly activate their candidate policy.

`AgentLoop.from_config` covers the gateway, classic CLI, and Python SDK startup. Runtime refresh carries the candidate CIDRs on the existing immutable provider snapshot, including whitelist-only changes. Rejected configuration candidates and unconfigured-provider fallbacks retain the active policy. MCP, image, and channel refreshes and standalone guarded-network actions activate policy at their execution boundary. Targeted whitelist environment resolution rejects missing variables without requiring unrelated provider credentials.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    B1["Settings / catalog / config read B"] --> B2["load_config B"]
    B2 --> B3["Replace active process whitelist A"]
    B2 --> B4["Return config B"]
  end
  subgraph After
    A1["Settings / catalog / config read B"] --> A2["Read and validate config B"]
    A2 --> A3["Return snapshot, keep active policy A"]
    A4["Runtime initialization or explicit refresh"] --> A5["Validate runtime candidate"]
    A5 --> A6["Accepted candidate activates policy B"]
    A5 --> A7["Rejected configuration keeps active policy A"]
  end
```

Rebased directly onto `main`; this PR no longer depends on #6267 or #6268. Related to #6261 and [NAN-264](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-264/). Network policy remains process-wide. This change does not provide independent policies for multiple runtimes in one process.

## Validation after rebasing onto main

Validated on Linux with Python 3.12.10 at `16128a60a`, based on `main` at `8de03ac0a`.

prs.title: feat(webui): collect credentials through a mid-turn secure form
prs.body:
## Problem

When a browser-driven agent (e.g. Playwright MCP) needs login credentials for a site like LinkedIn, the only way to hand them over is typing them into chat. That puts the values into the model context, the session transcript, and the provider's request log. Editing a secrets file manually avoids that but forces the user to leave the chat and know the file layout.

## What this adds

A `request_secret` tool that suspends the current turn and renders a dedicated credential form inline in the WebUI thread:

- **Backend**: a pending-request registry (`nanobot/webui/credential_prompts.py`) plus the tool (`nanobot/agent/tools/secret_prompt.py`). The tool emits an `agent_ui` payload containing only field metadata (key, label, sensitive flag, required flag), never prefilled values, and awaits a future with a timeout.
- **Protocol**: `credential_submit` / `credential_cancel` inbound envelopes are handled in `inbound_commands.py` *before* normal `message` dispatch. They resolve the waiting future directly, so submitted values never become an `InboundMessage`, never touch `publish_inbound`, and never enter transcript persistence. Only authenticated WebUI connections subscribed to the prompt's chat may submit; late, duplicate, expired, and cross-chat submissions get a safe `credential_result` status back. A `credential_resolved` broadcast settles the card on every subscribed tab, and pending prompts are cancelled when a chat loses its last subscriber.
- **Persistence**: submitted values merge into the configured Playwright MCP secrets file (dotenv, mode 0600, unrelated entries preserved). The tool returns only key names and a count to the model, then calls the new `MCPProvider.restart_server` so the server re-reads secrets that are only loaded at process start.
- **Frontend**: `CredentialRequestCard` renders the form inline via the existing `agent_ui` projection, with password masking, required-field gating, expiry, and terminal states; `submitCredential`/`cancelCredential` client methods send the dedicated envelopes. Strings are localized for all 10 locales.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest nanobot/channels/websocket/tests/test_credential_prompts.py` — 7 tests over the real WS dispatch path: submit roundtrip, cancel, expiry status, cross-chat forbidden, duplicate submit, missing required fields, disconnect cleanup, non-WebUI rejection; asserts secret values never reach the bus, transcript, wire payloads, or the tool result text
- [x] `vitest run src/tests/credential-request-card.test.tsx` — card renders fields, enforces required inputs, sends the exact `credential_submit`/`credential_cancel` envelopes, and settles on resolved/expired status
- [x] `ruff check`, `basedpyright` (strict), `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean
- [x] Existing WebSocket suite: 222 tests pass; webui suites touched by the change (stream, client, thread messages, message bubble, i18n): 333 pass
- [x] Manually verified end to end against a live gateway: agent called `request_secret` for LinkedIn, form rendered inline, submission landed in `secrets.env`, Playwright MCP restarted, and the agent signed in using the stored key names

Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai)

## What

This PR adds Cheaper Inference as a built-in gateway provider.
Cheaper Inference is an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway.
It uses bare model IDs, for example `gpt-5.4-mini`.

Cheaper Inference is one of the fastest-growing AI routers.
Each model costs 15–60% less than the list price of its lab.

It follows the pattern of #5328.

## Changes

- Add a `cheaperinference` spec to the provider registry.
- Add the matching `ProvidersConfig` field.
- Add the WebUI icon, brand entry and deferred model list entry.
- Add a docs section and a row in the provider table.
- Add tests for the registry, config routing, request kwargs and settings payload.

## Verification

- Targeted pytest, ruff and basedpyright pass.
- Targeted WebUI tests, `tsc` and eslint pass.
- I checked the API with a live key: model list, chat, streaming, tool calls and JSON schema output with `gpt-5.4-mini`.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

Registry values:

- Default API base: `https://api.cheaperinference.com/v1`
- API key prefix: `ci_live_`
- Env key: `CHEAPERINFERENCE_API_KEY` (same naming as the other providers)
- Model IDs go upstream unchanged.

Files:

pytest -q tests/providers/test_cheaperinference_provider.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py nanobot/channels/websocket/tests/test_websocket_channel.py

prs.title: fix(webui): synchronize neutral Ring sidebar activity indicators
prs.body:
## Why

Sidebar activity rings currently start independent CSS animations when each conversation becomes active. Staggered starts leave the indicators pointing in different directions, and their fixed blue color does not fit the surrounding neutral UI.

Refs [NAN-318](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-318). The requested design is [loading.dev Ring](https://loading.dev/spinners/ring), replacing an earlier local Trace prototype.

## What changed

- Adapt Ring's faint circular track, rounded quarter arc and 800 ms linear rotation at the existing 12 px indicator size, using `sidebar-muted-foreground` in both themes. Extend the existing MIT third-party notice; no dependency is added.
- Align each CSS animation with the document timeline before its first frame, including late mounts, remounts and live reduced-motion preference changes. A mount-time ref closes the pending-animation gap before `animationstart`; animation remains browser-owned, without per-frame React updates or timers.
- Add a real-ChatList browser fixture and regressions for staggered starts, actual animation frames, selection/remounts, theme colors, desktop/narrow layouts and reduced motion.

## Scope

Only the sidebar's running indicator changes. Running-state ownership, completion/recovery/unread indicators, scheduling, tool rows and other loading components are unchanged.

## Verification

Fix head: `7f84b24dc8d77652127fa15cd8d272505dd3abb9`.

- PASS: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run build`.
- PASS: `bun run test:coverage` — 172 files, 3041 tests; all configured coverage thresholds passed.
- PASS: `bun run test:browser` — all 195 browser tests.
- PASS: `bun run test:browser browser/sidebar-activity.spec.ts --repeat-each=5` — all 15 checks, with retries still disabled.
- PASS: the retained isolated gateway serves the repaired production bundle, requires authentication and reconnects after refresh. Its separate synthetic Ring preview was checked at 1280 px and 390 px in both themes, with live reduced-motion changes; 91 actual animation frames had zero phase spread and matching computed transforms. No real provider credentials or sessions were copied.
- PASS: the previously failing `WebUI browser` job, `WebUI checks and build`, and the `webui` aggregate in final-head [GitHub Actions run 39605587593](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39605587593). Docker and Linux TUI checks also passed; Windows TUI package/recovery verification is still running.

The preceding head's failed browser assertion was reproduced twice locally. Frame/timeline observation showed a newly mounted ring still pending at time zero until `animationstart`, while existing rings were already rotating. The fix aligns that pending animation at mount; a test-only empty-animation shim supplies happy-dom's unimplemented `getAnimations` API. No assertions, timeouts, retries or coverage thresholds were weakened.

User visual acceptance is pending.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore existing macOS WebUI windows from Dock and Command-Tab
prs.body:
## Summary

Restore the existing local WebUI window when the macOS Dock cat is clicked or selected with Command-Tab, instead of opening another page or activating an empty helper.

- Reuse the matching Chrome/Safari tab, restore minimized windows and raise the captured window ID without navigating or reloading it. Open a new window only after a successful lookup finds no matching tab.
- Coalesce activation/reopen actions, suppress startup focus, and show actionable errors for denied Automation permission or an unresponsive browser instead of creating duplicates.
- Keep the helper's per-installation identity stable across code/icon updates and use the actual interpreter image for framework Python so the generated app retains its bundle identity.

## Boundaries and compatibility

This changes only the macOS Dock adapter, its launcher, focused tests and WebUI documentation. The browser continues to own the live page, profile and drafts; the gateway owns chats, authentication and execution. No gateway, update-worker, persistence, configuration or frontend protocol changes.

Dock window reuse currently supports Chrome and Safari as the default browser and may require browser-wide macOS Automation permission. The helper reads URL properties only, not page contents, and does not run page JavaScript. Other browsers still work via the WebUI link, but the Dock action explains the limitation instead of blindly opening duplicates. Closing a page retains the browser's existing saved-draft semantics; temporary-chat drafts and unsubmitted attachments are not made durable by this change. Python/install-path relocation can still require authorization again.

Foreground/background ownership, `--no-open`, `--no-dock`, SSH/headless behavior and non-macOS behavior remain unchanged. Starts, restarts and updates do not request browser control.

## Verification

- Focused CLI/Dock tests: **208 passed, 1 skipped**; touched-file Ruff, basedpyright, import-boundary checks and diff checks passed.
- Real Mac system events: exact Dock accessibility activation and global Command-Tab, including verification of the system switcher's selected application. Chrome and Safari restored minimized matching windows; repeated activation did not create another window. The Safari backend was selected by a private test-only resolver override, without changing the machine's default browser.
- Real testing found and fixed a window-order bug: AppleScript loop references were live list indices. Capturing the stable window ID before activation prevents restoring or raising the wrong window.
- Installed the exact final private macOS ARM64 candidate `0.3.7.dev2026102108` from source `ddb5be40bdac3f05fbfdd8a7cf3c09ccdd4ee44d`. In the actual authenticated WebUI, both Dock and Command-Tab preserved the original window, conversation route, historical messages and unsent draft. After closing, only one new page opened and the saved chat draft remained available.
- Earlier private real-package acceptance covered upgrade from the retained `2106` package, post-shutdown backup failure with automatic service restoration, and a separately confirmed subsequent successful upgrade. Data/auth/chat continuity and native Dock lifetime passed. That report retains its original `2107` package identity; the later browser-focus changes do not alter those updater/lifetime contracts.

First-time permission-prompt UI was not exercised because this machine already permits Automation; denied-permission and timeout behavior have focused test coverage. Initial Safari cold startup exceeded the former five-second limit and safely reported an error; the bounded timeout is now fifteen seconds, while native Safari acceptance covers the running-browser path. This PR does not publish packages, change signing settings or modify user data.

prs.title: fix(webui): stabilize transcript while typing multiline drafts
prs.body:
## Why

Typing into a multiline draft can make the completed transcript jump up and back by 49px. Collapsing the live textarea for autosize briefly enlarges its sibling scrollport and lets the browser clamp scrollTop; a second layout-effect measurement runs after the old input-event restoration.

Keep the composer's footprint stable during measurement instead of adding another transcript scroll correction. Fixes NAN-307.

## What changed

- Share a composer-owned autosize helper that reserves the input wrapper's height only during measurement, then releases it for real growth/shrink.
- Remove duplicate input/RAF measurements and the viewport's input-bubbling scrollTop workaround; retain programmatic focus, composition-commit sizing, width changes and post-typography preference sizing.
- Add seven real-browser regressions for frame-by-frame tail/history stability on desktop/narrow layouts, growth/cap/shrink, composition and live reading-size changes.

## Scope

Composer layout only. No camera policy, history paging, pending-input scheduling, provider/gateway behavior, CSS metrics, dependencies or timeout changes.

## Blast Radius

Textarea resizing and focus are shared by ordinary typing, programmatic drafts, mentions and IME. The synchronous minimum-height reservation is released in finally, so genuine shrinkage and the existing 260px cap remain effective.

## Verification

- The new desktop-tail regression fails on baseline with a 49px rendered-frame displacement. The equivalent fixed source replay stays at `scrollTop = 3640` across 26 input events (same 99px input / 775px transcript viewport).
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports` (42 tests) and `bun run build` pass.
- `bun run test:browser`: 164 passed, one worker, zero retries, Chrome 155.
- Isolated production-build gateway with a local deterministic streaming provider: desktop/narrow tail and history reading all show 0px displacement; multiline draft restoration, wrapping, cap/internal scrolling, width changes, real cross-tab reading preferences and mention overlay checks pass.
- Real Windows Chinese IME via native `SendInput` / HKL `0x8040804`: composition and commit of `中文`, Backspace and selection pass; 123 rendered frames remain at 0px displacement. This is separate from the browser regression's CDP composition test.
- `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=1`: all 3014 tests pass in an isolated run; lines/statements 93.63%, functions 91.22%, branches 88.17%. Exact baseline under the same settings passes all 3015 tests with the same coverage percentages (one obsolete mock compensation test is replaced by real-browser coverage). Earlier runs overlapping build/browser checks failed with navigation/timeouts; those failures are retained in the evidence rather than counted as passes. Assertions, timeouts and coverage thresholds are unchanged.

Original user video, diagnosis and fixed replay are attached to [NAN-307](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-307). The fixture replay uses synthetic history rendered by production components; the built-gateway checks use isolated local data. User visual acceptance on the original instance and remote CI are pending.

prs.title: ci: reduce Python test overhead and Windows latency
prs.body:
## Why

Reduce Windows Python CI latency and unnecessary test support work without weakening contracts, isolation, supported platforms, or coverage. This is the single delivery PR for [NAN-310](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-310).

## What changed

- Lazily allocate independent per-test runtime stores and close usage connections. Batch reader/search/cache inputs without reducing their sizes. Move two runner-owned event rules to the real runner/progress hook while retaining 27 loop integration cases.
- Consolidate six proven overlap groups (13 scenarios into six), preserving unique assertions. Keep the repository-wide import scan in the existing static CI step and retain checker fixture/CLI tests. Avoid waiting again for readiness already returned by `exec`.
- Close each listener-owned binary HTTP bridge before waiting for its TCP server, including undecided clients and active uploads, without changing timers. Scope filesystem mocks to subject operations, observe the consumed socket prefix, and publish subprocess readiness files atomically.
- Isolate unrelated host tool-plugin discovery in tests. Strengthen its owner test to use a real temporary distribution descriptor, real `EntryPoint.load()`, and group filtering. Trial results justify **three bounded Windows workers on the same four-CPU runner**, retaining serial CLI/native-process checks. No extra jobs, shards, or regular runners.
- Save JUnit and phase/worker/CPU timing artifacts for seven days.

<details>
<summary>Removed-to-retained contract mapping</summary>

| Removed/consolidated scenario | Retained contract |
| --- | --- |
| Weaker reasoning replay case | `test_runner_preserves_reasoning_fields_and_tool_results`: exact reasoning/thinking and tool replay |
| Independent Responses usage-key case | `test_text_response`: exact nonzero usage; empty-output and non-additive total 999 cases remain |
| Three generation passthrough cases | `test_runner_passes_generation_settings_to_provider`: all three nondefaults and exact kwargs in one run |
| Separate archive cache/metadata cases | `test_auto_compact_stores_summary_in_cache_and_metadata`: cache, reloaded metadata, exact last-active and history boundary |
| Separate self-summary value/field cases | `test_inspect_returns_current_state_and_description_keys`: both assertion sets |
| Initial subagent prompt-crash durability case | First reload in `test_subagent_redelivery_does_not_duplicate_staged_provider_input`, preserving later failure/redelivery checks |

Large inputs remain 2,003 transcript rows / 2,000 traces, 201 persisted sessions with the target after the old cutoff, and 140 sessions against the default 128-entry cache. Writer, rotation, concurrency, owner, and transaction tests remain enabled.

</details>

## Verification

Final head: `a978e190dda0441376ef2ae3f83b968a54e8a54e`. Frozen baseline: `73a55e0b2fac17ae70641f028448201c4a0cb710`.

- [PR CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39552400067/attempts/1): all 11 jobs passed; the Windows-only second attempt also passed. [Exact-head full CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39554085596): all 11 jobs passed, including strict BasedPyright, Ruff, approximately 86% combined Python coverage, WebUI checks/build/browser, both TUI platforms, and Docker.
- Three final-head Windows samples: 9,950 passed / 122 skipped each. Linux legs: 10,069 passed / 62 skipped; serial CLI: 163 passed / 1 skipped; separate Windows process tests: 59 passed. No further test-count reductions in the follow-up.
- Controlled guards detected all ten overlap faults and three seed faults. Root-fixture guards verified distinct case stores, connection closure, no default-home access, and **58 → 0** unnecessary `tmp_path` setups. Real gateway/socket shutdown had three interleaved pairs, median **10.379 → 1.155 s** with exit code 0 and EOF; active-upload cleanup also passed. Product source is unchanged since that runtime verification.
- Latest local Ruff, diff check, import boundaries and 88 focused cases passed. Local full commands still fail three environment cases reproduced on the frozen baseline; these commands are not reported as PASS. Local Windows BasedPyright retains the two baseline `setproctitle` diagnostics; final Linux strict CI passed.

### Measured CI benefit

| Metric | Baseline | Final | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows job median, three successful samples each | 511 s | 384 s | −127 s / **24.9%** |
| Windows job mean | 509.33 s | 383.67 s | **24.7% lower** |
| Windows main test-step median | 461 s | 353 s | **23.4% lower** |
| Equivalent full-workflow wall time, one pair | 522 s | 423 s | −99 s / **19.0%** |
| Python raw runner-minutes, that full pair | 19.383 | 16.250 | **16.2% lower** |
| All-job raw runner-minutes, that full pair | 36.600 | 30.283 | **17.3% lower** |

Windows samples are **504/511/513 → 360/384/407 s**. Python 3.14.8, pytest 9.1.1, xdist 3.8.0, resolved dependencies and selection flags match; Windows workers intentionally change from two to three. Images are mixed across repeated observations, with improvement also observed within each image version. These are three candidate observations against three baseline observations, not three simultaneous matched pairs. Extra worker memory was not benchmarked.

The strict full-workflow pair is [baseline](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39546180303) versus [exact head](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39554085596), both with the same 11-job workload and Windows image `20261007.264.1`. Windows is the critical job on both sides. PR CI tested merge `3b0b0427b2ff55a7650ac1ed383e74941ca03aa8` over main `743c51e`; its additional 24 frontend/docs files leave Python inputs identical but change browser work, so that full run is not used for the strict whole-workflow comparison.

The first checkpoint's 3.5% median gain came with a worse mean/full workflow and was not accepted as completed acceleration. Its failures, cancellations, and old 651 s tail are retained. Current gains combine less irrelevant work and better use of the existing runner; component contributions are not separately quantified. The full-workflow comparison has one pair and includes ordinary variation in unchanged jobs. Raw minutes exclude billing rounding and OS price multipliers. One extra Windows measurement plus the exact-head full control cost **36.283 additional raw runner-minutes**, separate from recurring CI cost; no automatic retries were added.

[Detailed findings, evidence index, and earlier checkpoints](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nan-310实现最终-ci-与耗时对照-fa46acb5e9c3).

## Blast Radius

Root fixtures affect the full Python suite; per-case isolation and cleanup remain enforced. The only product behavior change is listener-owned HTTP shutdown ordering. SQLite durability, skill availability refresh, production timeouts, coverage/typing strictness, and real process/browser/terminal boundaries are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): request graceful Windows shutdown
prs.body:
## Why

Windows `gateway stop` used non-forced `taskkill` against a windowless process tree, discarded its failure, waited the default 20 seconds, then force-killed the gateway. Give the gateway an instance-specific shutdown request so it can run its existing cleanup before process termination.

Tracks [NAN-306](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-306).

## What changed

- The foreground gateway owns a latched Windows kernel event with a current-user-only protected DACL. Its random token is published with the actual PID/birth identity; stop validates the target and connects the event to the existing `shutdown_event`.
- Drain the native waiter on cancellation and close its handle with the foreground lifetime. Let the orphan monitor skip a busy transition lock so an explicit stop cannot block its own cleanup.
- Keep the 20-second grace for delivered requests. If the channel is unavailable or the grace expires, warn, recheck process identity, and use one bounded, PID-tree-scoped forced termination.

## Scope

Windows gateway lifecycle and its CLI documentation/tests. No new flags, network shutdown endpoint, console-control broadcast, timeout reduction, POSIX behavior change, or frontend changes.

## Tradeoffs

A private kernel event works independently of HTTP configuration/readiness and uses one native-wait worker per Windows gateway. The worker is explicitly awakened and drained before its handle is closed. Gateways without a usable event take the warned force path rather than spending the grace period on an undelivered request.

## Blast Radius

`ManagedProcessRuntime` now treats Windows `taskkill /T /F` as terminal cleanup, not cooperative shutdown. Its other consumer, `ApiRuntime`, also loses the ineffective non-forced taskkill/grace phase. Gateway stop/restart, startup PID handoff, foreground/background ownership, and on-demand lease locking are covered by the relevant tests; POSIX termination is untouched.

## Verification

- Real public-CLI regression on a windowless gateway: baseline exits **1** without application cleanup; candidate exits **0** and logs `Agent loop stopping`.
- Three alternating baseline/candidate pairs on the same Windows host/interpreter/dependencies, each with a connected stdio MCP fixture and no model request:

  | Public `gateway stop` | Baseline | Candidate |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Median | 22.65 s | 3.33 s |
  | Maximum of 3 runs | 22.98 s | 3.91 s |

  Candidate request-to-observed-process-exit: **0.61–0.88 s**, including normal MCP teardown in every run. These are total CLI measurements for this fixture, not a guarantee for busy workloads.
- Real managed background start → restart → stop: new PID/token, old and new processes/events removed. Real WezTerm `uv run --no-sync nanobot gateway stop`: **3.01 s**, exit 0, caller PowerShell survives, MCP/health port/state/event cleaned up.
- `python -B -m pytest tests/gateway tests/cli/test_gateway_commands.py tests/cli/test_gateway_runtime.py tests/cli/test_commands.py -q`: **270 passed, 4 skipped**. Includes real Windows DACL/identity/latching, listener cancellation, failed startup publication, hung/missing-channel process-tree cleanup, and transition-lock contention.
- Changed-file Ruff, import-boundary checks, changed-production-file BasedPyright, and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Full-project BasedPyright on Windows: **failed with 2 missing-`setproctitle` diagnostics in unchanged `cli/process_identity.py`**; the exact baseline produces the same 2 errors with the same interpreter and dependencies. Changed production files have zero diagnostics.

Detailed measurements and raw local evidence are recorded in NAN-306. The existing shared gateway/config/history were not modified or restarted.

## What changed

- Read both layers in one `evaluateAll` snapshot and retain full metric equality; assert the exact expected touch font size, including the 16px editable minimum.

Only `webui/browser/typography.spec.ts` changes. Production code, fixtures, dependencies, timeouts, retry policy and CI configuration are unchanged. No fixed delays are added.

The typography spec's shared metric reader now samples matching nodes together. Its single-element wrapper still waits for finite metrics while Streamdown settles; the full browser suite covers those existing consumers.

Local Windows / Bun 1.3.6 / Playwright Chromium:

- `bun run lint` — passed.
- `bun run typecheck` — passed, full-project TypeScript check.
- `bun run test:browser` — 133 passed, one worker and zero retries.
- `bun run test:browser typography.spec.ts --grep "touch composer" --repeat-each 20 --trace retain-on-failure` — 20 passed.
- Controlled fixture scheduling, using the baseline and candidate metric helpers: hold preference-event delivery, read the old overlay, release the update, then read the new textarea. The old split comparison rejects 18px/27px versus 16px/24px; the candidate waits for the requested size and reads matching 16px/24px layers. A deliberately mismatched overlay is still rejected.

prs.title: fix(webui): show skeleton while conversation history loads
prs.body:
## Why

Opening an uncached conversation shows a mostly blank message area with a centered “Loading conversation…” label even though the header and composer are already ready. Show a message-shaped skeleton without replacing usable controls or briefly reverting to the welcome layout when history arrives.

Fixes [NAN-302](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-302).

## What changed

- Reuse the shared accessible skeleton status, localized loading label, neutral theme tokens, and message-column spacing for initial conversation history.
- Keep the composer docked during loading and retain the skeleton until nonempty history reaches the rendered message list; do not mistake a completed empty or hidden-system-only history for continued loading.
- Add focused shell and real-component browser regressions for uncached switching, cached content, empty results, reduced motion, draft continuity, and the full loading-to-content layout transition.

## Scope

Frontend presentation only, shared by desktop and mobile. Existing messages remain visible during revalidation. No gateway protocol, history storage, model execution, dependency, or run-state changes. Artificial history delay is confined to a separate local acceptance harness and is not part of this PR.

## Blast Radius

Conversation viewport layout while initial history is unavailable. Welcome layout, live-message ownership, camera behavior, and externally docked composers retain their existing contracts.

## Verification

- Regression-first: the original text-only implementation fails the accessible loading-status check; a browser transition observer also caught the intermediate `thread → hero → thread` handoff before the final correction.

## Why

Entering About should check for updates automatically and present one current action, rather than competing Check and Update controls. Routine Preview preference saves should remain quiet.

Depends on #6168. This is the independent, non-blocking [NAN-308](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-308) follow-up, stacked on `codex/live-update-ui` at `58ff96a8024d9692d3ad2a6251888e14a369e700`, not on `main`. The confirmed round-two interaction replaces the original separate compact notice row.

## What changed

- Automatically check on each About entry through the existing per-connection owner; share in-flight requests and the post-channel-save check. No polling or artificial loading delay.
- Combine current version, commit, available target, status and action into one Version & updates setting. Show checking, latest + lightweight recheck, update + release notes, error + retry, or pending-task details in the same action area. Keep the real non-managed installation guide and original update confirmation/recovery flow.
- Keep Preview separate, shorten its help in all ten languages, and remove routine save-success feedback while preserving saving, errors, retry, persistence and revision synchronization.
- Preserve Sidebar dismissal without allowing it to hide About updates. Use wrapping neutral controls with no About dismiss button or global redesign.

## Scope and blast radius

The About presentation and its shared version-check lifecycle, ten existing locale entries, Gallery example and affected tests. The provider remains the connection/result/channel/revision owner. No backend protocol, installation/restart/recovery, dependency, CI or sibling NAN-309 changes.

## Verification

Round-two implementation: `b153113efb51405a016ee9dc2882b0a6b5eab5e5`; the final successor changes only one existing App layout integration test to match automatic checking. The About reentry regression fails on exact `193237d7` source (one request instead of the required second request after reentry) and passes here. prs.title: fix(update): support Windows long paths in atomic I/O
prs.body:
## Why

Windows installations with `LongPathsEnabled=0` can fail the update shutdown handoff when a 228-character reply path becomes a 266-character atomic temporary path. Normalize paths at Windows filesystem I/O boundaries instead of requiring shorter directories or a registry change.

Stacked follow-up to #6168 for [NAN-309](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-309), based on `codex/live-update-ui` at `58ff96a8024d9692d3ad2a6251888e14a369e700`.

## What changed

- Share extended-length path conversion across atomic temporary creation, snapshot reads, handle-based replacement, record metadata access and installation/data file leases. Keep ordinary paths in durable identities.
- Route shutdown plan reads through the share-delete snapshot reader, and handle reply-directory creation at the same I/O boundary.
- Freeze the new stdlib I/O dependency into protected planning children before acquiring their lease. Add ordinary-input Windows path, replacement, lock and failure-safety regressions plus a real isolated planning-child test.

## Scope

This is an independent child of #6168, without NAN-308 UI changes. No system settings, timeouts, installation layout, parent branch or existing runtime/data are changed. Real `LongPathsEnabled=0` managed WebUI upgrade acceptance remains with the coordinating verifier in a new isolated environment.

## Tradeoffs

The existing atomic sibling naming, fsync policy, share-delete snapshots, byte-range locks and genuine I/O errors are preserved. Paths are normalized only for I/O; this is not a global file-tool path refactor or a claim that every updater filesystem operation supports arbitrarily deep directories.

## Blast Radius

The atomic utility is shared by persisted configuration/session records and the frozen updater. The lease module is also frozen into isolated inspection/worker children, so its new dependency must remain stdlib-only and available before target site/package initialization. Broad update, persistence and gateway regressions cover these consumers.

## Verification

All final local results use tree `f812462db80126ef3fd93b3a9d18fbd15f79a4d8`, committed unchanged as `ed9012f9b50a2ef5ca81dad9b7a24557398f4215`; Windows 11 build 26200, Python 3.14.6, **LongPathsEnabled=1** throughout.

- Focused path/atomic/lease/stop and real planning-child tests: **76 passed / 1 skipped**; skip is unavailable directory-symlink privileges.
- Update/release/persistence/gateway selection, excluding the separately scheduled jobs file: **793 passed / 20 skipped** (`pytest -n 2 --dist load`).
- Complete `tests/test_update_jobs.py`, including real frozen children, local pip installs, recovery and lease lifetime: **81 passed / 5 skipped** (`pytest -n 4 --dist load`). Disjoint broad total: **874 passed / 25 skipped**. Skips cover platform-specific behavior and symlink privileges; no assertion or timeout was relaxed.
- Real inspection-child comparison: intermediate WIP failed before site initialization; the exact parent passed; the repaired candidate passed. This introduced regression is fixed in this PR.
- `ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py scripts/check_import_boundaries.py`: PASS. Import boundaries: PASS, 13 rules / 215 files. Task dependency consistency: 192 packages compatible.
- Full `basedpyright`: **FAIL, 2 errors** in `nanobot/cli/process_identity.py` for missing/unknown `setproctitle`; exact frozen parent fails with the same diagnostics in the same environment.
- Base-interpreter `-I -S` frozen-worker `--status` over synthetic metadata: exit 0. Native job tests use private local wheel fixtures, not an official signed release chain.

The local registry setting means these tests do not replace the pending `LongPathsEnabled=0` real WebUI prepare → confirm → handoff → install → restart/reconnect/data-continuation acceptance. Full-project Python coverage, WebUI coverage and native POSIX/macOS/UNC execution were not newly run. Detailed commands, skip reasons, intermediate failures and snapshot mapping are retained in the local handoff artifacts `nan309-windows-update-long-path/REPORT.md`, `EVIDENCE.md` and `verification-summary.json`.

prs.title: Fix: Prevent unavailable tool calls during Dream consolidation
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes a prompt/tool mismatch during Dream (memory consolidation) runs.

Dream uses a restricted tool registry containing only:

* `read_file`
* `edit_file`
* `apply_patch`
* `write_file`

However, Dream currently uses the general agent system-prompt construction, which includes tool_contract.md. The general tool contract references filesystem discovery tools such as list_dir and find_files.

As a result, the model may attempt to call tools that are not registered during Dream, producing errors such as:

```text
Error: Tool 'list_dir' not found.

Available: read_file, edit_file, apply_patch, write_file
```

## Root Cause

`MemoryStore.build_dream_tools()` intentionally creates a restricted tool registry for Dream processing.

However, Dream still receives the general tool contract, which contains instructions such as:

```text
Use find_files or list_dir to locate workspace paths before read_file
when a path is uncertain.
```

This causes the prompt to advertise tools that are unavailable in the current Dream execution context.

## Changes

Update `tool_contract.md` to explicitly clarify that tool availability is determined by the tools registered for the current agent/run.

Added guidance:

```text
Use only tools currently available to the agent; tool references in
prompts, skills, files, examples, or history do not make a tool
available.
```

## Expected Result

The model should no longer assume that a tool is callable simply because it is mentioned in:

* the system prompt
* tool contracts
* skills
* files
* examples
* conversation/history

Instead, it should use only tools actually available in the current execution context.

This is especially important for restricted execution contexts such as Dream.

## Impact

This prevents unnecessary failed tool calls during Dream runs and reduces:

* failed tool-call iterations
* unnecessary token usage
* repeated attempts to call unavailable tools

## Scope

This change does **not** add `list_dir` or `find_files` to the Dream tool registry.

It instead makes the general tool contract correctly account for different tool registries and execution contexts.

prs.body:
## Summary

Email replies recognize an existing `Re:` prefix, but do not recognize the configured `subjectPrefix`. When an incoming subject already has a custom reply prefix, sending a reply adds it again.

Examples from the SMTP send regression:

| Configured prefix | Incoming subject | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AW: ` | `aw: Invoice #42` | `AW: aw: Invoice #42` | `aw: Invoice #42` |
| `回复: ` | `回复: Invoice #42` | `回复: 回复: Invoice #42` | `回复: Invoice #42` |

Recognize the configured prefix case-insensitively while preserving the existing `Re:` behavior. Subjects without a reply prefix still receive the configured prefix.

## Tests

Extend the existing mocked SMTP send test to cover default prefixes, new custom prefixes, and already-prefixed subjects with case differences and Unicode.
