issues.body:
### What happened
While asked to build a .pptx for the user, the agent (Hermes desktop, `approvals.mode` default = `smart`, local backend, macOS) wanted to render its own deck to PNG. With no LibreOffice installed, it drove the user's running Microsoft PowerPoint via `osascript`:

```applescript
tell application "Microsoft PowerPoint"
  open POSIX file ".../traz.pptx"
  save active presentation in POSIX file ".../traz.pdf" as save as PDF
  close active presentation saving no
end tell
```

`active presentation` was the **user's own unsaved deck** (hours of manual work), not the agent's file. It was closed with `saving no`, so PowerPoint discarded the document and wiped its AutoRecovery copies. The agent then ran `rm -f .../traz.pdf`, deleting the only export of that deck (a 2-page PDF), and later looped `close presentation 1 saving no` over all open presentations.

All of these commands were auto-approved by smart approval (the output shows "flagged … auto-approved by smart approval"). The user was never asked.

On Apple Silicon with disk encryption, deleted files cannot be recovered, so the work was lost. Only a partial copy existed outside the machine.

### Not specific to PowerPoint
The same pattern works against **any scriptable app holding unsaved user work**, for example:
- **Microsoft Word / Excel / Outlook:** `close active document saving no`, `close active workbook saving no`, closing a draft message without saving.
- **Apple apps:** Keynote, Pages, Numbers, TextEdit, Preview (`close every document saving no`, `quit saving no`).
- **Any app via System Events:** sending ⌘W / ⌘Q and clicking "Don't Save", or killing the process (`killall "Microsoft Word"`, `pkill`).

An agent that "cleans up" by closing or quitting apps can silently destroy hours of unsaved work in any of them. AutoRecovery doesn't help, because a clean close discards it.

### Expected
- AppleScript/JXA (`osascript`), System Events keystrokes, and process kills that target GUI apps with `close … saving no`, `quit … saving no`, `delete`, or that iterate over the user's open documents should count as **dangerous**: they destroy unsaved user data. They should always require manual approval, including in `smart` mode.
- Smart approval should not auto-approve `rm` of files the agent did not create in the session.
- Ideally the agent should be warned that the user's GUI apps (Office, Keynote, etc.) are a shared, stateful resource that may hold unsaved work.

### Suggested fixes
1. Add `osascript` patterns (`saving no`, `close`, `quit`, `delete`, `active presentation|document|workbook`, `every document|presentation|workbook`, System Events keystrokes for ⌘W/⌘Q) and `killall`/`pkill` of GUI apps to the dangerous-command list, and do not let smart mode auto-approve them, regardless of which app is targeted.
2. Track files created by the agent in the session, and escalate deletions of anything outside that set.
3. Update the bundled `powerpoint`, `docx` and `xlsx` skills: render with LibreOffice/headless only, and never close or quit the user's open apps without explicit consent. (We added this to our local copy of the skill.)

### Environment
- Hermes desktop (canary build), macOS on Apple Silicon
- `approvals.mode`: default (`smart`)

issues.title: [Bug]: model.default with '<provider>/<model>' slash prefix is forwarded verbatim upstream (503 model_not_found) → silent fallback

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/config
labels.description: Config system, migrations, profiles

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Summary

When `model.default` in `config.yaml` carries a provider prefix in slash form (`<provider>/<model>`, e.g. `china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`) **while `model.provider` already names that same provider**, Hermes forwards the string verbatim as the upstream `model` field. Exact-name routers (New API / one-api style) reject it with `503 model_not_found`, Hermes retries twice, then silently fails over to the fallback model — the user sees "the model is down" when actually the request never contained a valid model name.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `0.22.3+14.g4d04303` (install-stamp: commit `4d043038`, built 2026-10-21T16:52:07Z), Windows 11 desktop app, local session
- Also reproduced on the previous install (build predating 2026-10-21 16:52 UTC), so this is **not** a recent regression — the slash-prefixed `model.default` form appears to have *never* worked on this path
- Provider is a named custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`providers.china` in config.yaml) backed by New API

## Config (redacted)

```yaml
model:
  default: china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash   # ← the trap
  provider: china                          # provider is already selected here
  base_url: http://feiniu:3001/v1
  key_env: HERMES_CUSTOM_CHINA_API_KEY
providers:
  china:
    base_url: http://feiniu:3001/v1
    models:
      国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: {}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `model.default` to `<configured-provider>/<model>` (slash form) with `model.provider` set to the same provider.
2. Start any desktop local-session turn.
3. Every API call fails; after 2 retries Hermes activates the fallback model.

## Actual behavior (logs)

```
agent.turn_context: conversation turn: ... model=china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash provider=custom platform=desktop
run_agent: OpenAI client created (chat_completion_stream_request ...) provider=custom base_url=http://feiniu:3001/v1 model=china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers: Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 503 -
  {'error': {'code': 'model_not_found', 'message': 'No available channel for model
   china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under group 纯国产模型 (distributor)', 'type': 'new_api_error'}}
agent.chat_completion_helpers: Non-streaming unmask probe failed: (same 503)   # probe dies too → double latency
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 2/3) ... HTTP 503
agent.chat_completion_helpers: Fallback activated: china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash → 国逆glm-5.3-flash (china)
```

## Expected behavior

One of:

1. **Parse it**: when the `model.default` prefix matches a configured provider (or `model.provider`), strip the prefix and send the bare model name — the same tolerance the CLI picker shows elsewhere; or
2. **Fail fast and loud**: reject the config at startup / `hermes config set` time with a clear message ("`model.default` should be the bare model name; the provider is selected by `model.provider`"), instead of discovering it as a runtime 503 that looks identical to an upstream outage.

The silent fallback is the costly part: it converts a local config typo into what looks like a provider-side failure, sending the user debugging their relay/accounts for hours (ask me how I know).

## Evidence that the prefixed form is the sole cause

Across two builds and two log files (`agent.log`, `agent.log.1`):

- Turns with `model=china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`: **0 successes**, every one 503 `model_not_found` (first seen 2026-10-21 21:37 +08, before the current build was even installed)
- Turns with bare `model=国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (same provider, same endpoint): all succeed, e.g. 2026-10-21 18:12–18:18 and again after reverting `model.default` to the bare name (2026-10-22 10:06, 3.1 s, `finish_reason=stop`)
- Direct probe against the endpoint confirms it is name-exact: `china/国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` → 503, `国逆DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` → 200, same second, same key

## Related

- #7922 (open) — same verbatim-forward class via the `/model <provider>/<model>` command on messaging gateways (HTTP 400 there). This report is the **config.yaml `model.default` entry point** on desktop local sessions; the fix likely wants to live in one shared normalization/validation spot.
- #110891 / #97233 (closed) — ACP picker colon-form variant of the same "provider prefix leaks into the upstream model field" family.

## Workaround

Keep `model.default` as the bare model name; select the provider via `model.provider` (verified working).

issues.body:
## Summary

A gateway restart while a turn is in flight fences that turn `unknown` and **pauses the session's whole input FIFO**. Everything queued behind it — including the user's next message from Bot Chat — waits forever. The only recovery is a terminal command, the desktop offers no affordance for it, and in the same window the app instead reports `Hermes gateway is not connected` even though the gateway is up. Net effect: **a bot looks permanently broken and nothing in the UI says why**.

## What the user saw

- A bot (profile `article-vetter`) simply stopped answering in Bot Chat — for about ten hours. Nothing was surfaced anywhere in the app.
- At the same time the Bot panel reported `Hermes gateway is not connected`, while the gateway process was healthy: `hermes -p article-vetter gateway status` → `✓` (single multiplexed host gateway, PID present, log normally active).
- The user's message was never lost. It was queued, and never started.

## Mechanism and evidence

`profiles/article-vetter/logs/agent.log`:

```
2026-10-16 08:26:49,495 WARNING gateway.session_authority: Session 20260829_221255_a49229 paused: unknown_execution
```

`profiles/article-vetter/state.db`, table `session_admissions` (read-only):

```
seq=3  adm=f025e27f753c…  status=queued    payload={"text":"<the user's message, sent later>"}
seq=2  adm=8bc556266e1b…  status=unknown   payload={"local_automation_v1":…, "text":"[Cronjob \"…22:00\" output — …]"}
seq=1  adm=f1ed7090eaa2…  status=terminal  outcome=completed   (unrelated cron)
```

`seq=2` is a cron job's output delivered into that chat at 22:17; the gateway restarted mid-turn; its outcome became unknowable, so it was fenced `unknown` and the FIFO paused. `seq=3` — the user's next message — then waited behind it indefinitely.

## Recovery that works, but is terminal-only

```
hermes -p article-vetter sessions discard 20260829_221255_a49229 \
    --admission 8bc556266e1b43f79ce02d811b0b410b --yes
```

Immediately after: `seq=2` → `terminal/interrupted`, `seq=3` → `started`, and the bot answered. Interactively the same control is `/discard <admission>` in the classic chat; the ACP path's own refusal text instructs the user to do exactly this from a terminal.

## The gap

1. **No in-app affordance.** Desktop Bot Chat and ACP have no way to acknowledge an unknown admission. The ACP source says so itself (`"ACP has no discard affordance"`) and its refusal text ends with "Resolve it in a terminal with `hermes -p <profile> chat --cli --resume <session>` then `/discard <id>`". The desktop shows no notice about the paused session at all, so the user cannot even learn that a turn is pending.
2. **Misleading signal.** The one visible message in that window (`Hermes gateway is not connected`) described the wrong thing: the gateway was healthy; the session's FIFO was paused. (#121680 covered a stale-socket variant of this message; here it fires for an unrelated cause, which sends users to the wrong repair — in our case we nearly restarted a healthy gateway.)
3. **The queue is silent.** A user message sitting behind an unknown admission is indistinguishable from "the bot is dead". Adjacent: #138934 reports the desktop composer queue holding `serverStatus:"queued"` entries that cannot be cleared — a different queue (Electron localStorage) but the same "queued forever, no explanation" experience.

## Suggested shape

- Surface the resolve control where the block is visible: in Bot Chat (and ACP) a "the previous turn was lost in a restart — acknowledge it" affordance next to the paused-session notice, calling the same `prompt.resolve_unknown` the CLI uses.
- Or auto-resolve under a stated policy — e.g. an automation/cron admission fenced `unknown` and older than N minutes with the session otherwise idle → acknowledge it and post a one-line notice. The lost input is never replayed anyway, so leaving it blocked buys nothing.
- And stop reporting `gateway is not connected` for this state.

## Environment

Windows 11 x64, source install, multiplex (one host gateway serving 7 profiles), Hermes v0.21.7-era build. The restart that orphaned the turn was an update-driven gateway restart — i.e. the same event class our own updates produce, so this is a predictable post-update symptom rather than a rare crash.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Multiplex install; let a cron job deliver output into a bot chat (or start a long turn in it).
2. Restart the gateway mid-turn.
3. Send a message from the desktop Bot Chat: it queues and never runs. `session_admissions` shows the first row `unknown` and the second `queued`; the UI offers no way to proceed.

issues.title: [Bug]: Tools/Desktop: session workspace is not enforced — agent edited a different clone for 47 min, memory/skill absolute path wins

labels.name: type/security

labels.description: Skills system (list, view, manage)

labels.name: P3

issues.body:
### Bug Description

A desktop session pinned to one clone of a repo silently edited **another clone** for 47 minutes, while all three cwd sources said the session's own workspace.

Setup: three clones of the same repo run in parallel.
- `~/works/data/data-gover-dev` — a Kanban dispatcher worker (profile `developer`, PID 3557606) has been writing here for 3 days
- `~/works/data/data-gover-v15x` — release-line maintenance (the session in question: `20261020_203109_ccaee9`, `history=580`, previously compressed, idle ~22 h before the turn)
- `~/works/data/data-gover-v15x-gd` — a custom build

The session workspace was correct everywhere:
- `sessions.cwd = /home/jwj/works/data/data-gover-v15x`, `git_branch = v1.5.x`
- stored system prompt: `Current working directory: /home/jwj/works/data/data-gover-v15x`
- `agent.log`: `19:50:49,789 INFO tools.environments.base: Session snapshot created (session=5ab3cc92dc94, cwd=/home/jwj/works/data/data-gover-v15x)`

Nevertheless, from the **first tool call** of the turn, every `patch` / `write_file` / `terminal` target was absolute under `data-gover-dev`: 9 existing files edited (~50 edits), 3 new files created, plus `mvnw compile` / `mvnw test` / `vite build` / `node --test` run against that clone's sources. Duration 19:51–20:40.

At 20:36:52 the user corrected it explicitly ("you edited the wrong tree … don't reset the code, another process is modifying it"). The agent still wrote to `data-gover-dev` 5 more times (20:37:28, 20:38:12 ×4, 20:40:27 ×4, 20:48:00), and at 20:48:58 stated "I've now confirmed the corrected changes are in `data-gover-v15x`" while the patch issued in the same turn carried the `data-gover-dev` path.

Why it happened (evidence, not speculation): the standing context contained a hard-coded path of the other clone — a memory entry (`data-gover仅改~/works/data/data-gover-dev`) and the `data-gover` skill (`Repo: ~/works/data/data-gover-dev (primary dev workspace — ALL code changes happen here)`), which had been loaded by `skill_view("data-gover")` in the *previous* turn (19:37, where v15x paths were still used correctly). The tools never checked a target path against the session workspace, so nothing rejected or even logged the mismatch.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Two clones of one repo: `A` and `B`.
2. Add a memory entry (or a skill) stating that all code changes for this project happen in `A` — e.g. `MEMORY.md`: `data-gover仅改~/works/data/data-gover-dev`.
3. Open a desktop session whose workspace is `B`; confirm the system prompt says `Current working directory: …/B`.
4. Let the session idle for a while / let context compression run, then ask for a small code change.
5. Observe the `patch` / `write_file` arguments: they carry absolute paths under `A`. No warning, no approval prompt, no log line. The agent's final report claims the change landed in `B`.


### Expected Behavior

A session's workspace should be enforced, not merely described:
- an edit whose resolved absolute path falls outside the session workspace (session cwd + registered project folders) should be refused or require explicit confirmation, and should emit a WARNING naming both the target and the workspace;
- standing memory/skill text naming a different absolute project path must not silently override the session workspace (at minimum a per-turn note should say the workspace wins);
- after an explicit user correction ("you edited the wrong tree"), further writes to the wrong tree should be blocked.

### Actual Behavior

All file and shell writes went to `data-gover-dev` for 47 minutes with no boundary check. `tools/file_tools_paths.py::_authoritative_workspace_root()` only chooses the **anchor for relative paths**; absolute paths are used verbatim. `agent/context_references.py` has an `allowed_root` workspace guard, but that is for `@`-reference / attachment expansion only — the edit tools have no equivalent.

Evidence of the wrong-tree writes (state.db, session `20261020_203109_ccaee9`):
- 19:51:55 – 20:17:41 `patch` → `data-gover-dev/.../assets/service/DbDataSourceService.java`, `.../DbDataSourceServiceImpl.java`, `.../DbDataSourceController.java`
- 19:52:17 – 20:40:27 `patch` → `data-gover-dev/data-gover-web/src/api/dgp/index.ts`
- 19:52:31 – 20:40:27 `patch` → `.../PublishModelModal.tsx`
- 20:05:07 – 20:40:27 `patch` → `.../NodeEditModal/hooks/useNodeData.ts`
- 20:05:53 – 20:25:01 new `.../DbDataSourceServiceImplTest.java`
- 20:14:39 – 20:30:38 new `.../api/dgp/dataSourcePagination.test.mjs`
- 20:15:50 – 20:30:18 new `.../api/dgp/dataSourcePagination.ts`
- 19:52–20:06 `mvnw compile` / `mvnw test` on a copy of that clone's `src/`

Self-contradiction in the same turn (20:48): `patch` diff header `--- a//home/jwj/works/data/data-gover-dev/data-gover/src/main/java/.../DbDataSourceController.java` while the assistant text says the changes are in `data-gover-v15x`.

Risk: that clone was being modified concurrently by a 3-day Kanban worker; the agent cleaned up by patching each edit back (no `git checkout`), so nothing was lost — but a `git checkout`/`git reset` cleanup (which the model is likely to choose) would have destroyed that pipeline's uncommitted work.


### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Report https://support.nousresearch.com/diagnostics/cc18d243-9ac6-49ee-a1ac-9043a3998251
agent.log included in the bundle above (Nous diagnostics storage)
gateway.log included in the bundle above (Nous diagnostics storage)

Note: uploaded with hermes debug share --nous — private Nous diagnostics
bundle (Google-login gated, Nous staff only), auto-deletes in 14 days.
```

### Operating System

Deepin 20.9 (Linux 5.15.77-amd64-desktop, x86_64)

### Python Version

3.11.14 (Hermes venv); 3.14.7 (bundled tools runtime)

### Hermes Version

v0.22.2 (2026.9.24) · stable · git install · local d923a5eb487a

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
session workspace was correct ...
2026-10-21 19:50:37,455 INFO [20261020_203109_ccaee9] agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=20261020_203109_ccaee9 ... platform=desktop history=580 msg='在 数据模型 中 模型 发布 时...'
2026-10-21 19:50:49,789 INFO tools.environments.base: Session snapshot created (session=5ab3cc92dc94, cwd=/home/jwj/works/data/data-gover-v15x)

... yet the very first tool batch wrote to the other clone
2026-10-21 19:51:56,540 INFO hermes.lint.lsp: lsp[jdtls] skipped: untrusted workspace /home/jwj/works/data/data-gover-dev/data-gover (.../assets/service/DbDataSourceService.java)

10-20 20:31 compression, logged under ANOTHER session's agent tag (worth auditing)
2026-10-20 20:31:08,997 INFO [20261020_143220_85d590] agent.conversation_compression: Compaction rebuilt a drifted system prompt (session=20261020_135931_cede6c, 37000 -> 37089 chars)
2026-10-20 20:31:09,375 INFO [20261020_143220_85d590] agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=20261020_203109_ccaee9 messages=609->386
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

1. `agent/prompt_builder.py:1040` publishes `Current working directory: {resolve_agent_cwd()}` — advisory prose only. Globally injected memory and skill text can name a different absolute project path and nothing resolves the conflict.
2. `tools/file_tools_paths.py:127 _authoritative_workspace_root()` is used to anchor **relative** paths (`_anchor()`, line 153). An absolute path from the model bypasses anchoring entirely, and no caller compares it to the workspace root.
3. `agent/context_references.py` already implements a workspace-escape guard (`allowed_root`, around line 478) for `@`-reference/attachment expansion — the edit tools (`patch`, `write_file`, `terminal`) have no equivalent check.
4. Session cwd plumbing itself looks correct (`agent/runtime_cwd.py` ContextVar + `tools/terminal_tool.py::_session_cwd` per-session records); in this incident `sessions.cwd`, the stored system prompt and the terminal env snapshot all agreed on the right clone, so this is not hydration/prompt drift.
5. Side observations:
   - `~/.hermes/projects.db` holds three duplicate rows pointing at the same `primary_path` (`data-gover-dev`, `data-gover-dev-2`, `data-gover-dev-3`) and none for the two other clones; `project_meta.active_id` pointed at an unrelated project.
   - a new desktop session can persist an empty `sessions.cwd` (e.g. `20261021_205006_78ee72`), after which the prompt falls back to `Current working directory: /home/jwj` — workspace identity vanishes.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

- Enforce the workspace in the tool layer: resolve every target path for `patch` / `write_file` / `terminal`; if outside the session workspace (session cwd + registered project folders) require an explicit force/approval and emit a WARNING with both paths. Reuse `allowed_root` from `context_references.py`.
- Add precedence to the prompt: when memory/skill text names an absolute path differing from the session workspace, inject a per-turn note that the session workspace wins (and discourage absolute project paths in global memory).
- Echo the resolved workspace in edit results (`workspace=…`, plus a `MISMATCH` marker) so a wrong-tree edit is visible in the transcript.
- Registry hygiene: dedupe `projects` by `primary_path`, validate `project_meta.active_id`, never persist an empty session `cwd`.


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.title: [Bug]: redact_sensitive_text misses prefix tokens followed by an underscore (shared lookahead class)

labels.name: type/security
labels.description: Security vulnerability or hardening

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Authentication, OAuth, credential pools

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
`redact_sensitive_text` misses prefix-pattern tokens completely when an underscore follows the token. The token goes through in cleartext at any length.

### Cause

`agent/redact.py` builds every prefix pattern into one regex with a single shared lookahead:

```python
def _compile_prefix_matcher(patterns: list) -> re.Pattern[str]:
    return re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])(" + "|".join(patterns) + r")(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])")
```

For a pattern whose body class is alphanumeric only (for example `ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}`), `_` sits in the lookahead class but not in the body class. When `_` follows the token, the lookahead fails, backtracking shortens the body one character at a time, and every shorter match fails the same lookahead. So the whole match is lost instead of stopping at the token's end.

### Reproduce (synthetic values)

Against `main` today, using `_PREFIX_PATTERNS` and `_compile_prefix_matcher` as they are:

```
value ghp_AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA here          -> matched (redacted)
value ghp_AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA_SUFFIX here   -> no match (cleartext)
```

`hf_` and `npm_` behave the same way. On 0.14.0 we measured 23 of 35 prefix families missing in this shape, among them `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, `AKIA`, `xox[baprs]-`, `rk_live_`, `hf_`, `npm_`, `r8_`, `gsk_`, `syt_`, `dop_v1_`, `doo_v1_`, `pplx-`, `fc-`, `tvly-`, `exa_`, `hsk-`, `retaindb_`, `mem0_` and `brv_`. 0.19.0 kept the same boundary. Tokens followed by `-` don't miss, so the lookbehind and lookahead design does fix the old `\b` problem on that side.

A token pasted in front of an underscore-joined suffix is a common shape: an env var interpolation, a filename, a log key. Other nets (env assignments, JSON fields, auth headers) may still catch some cases by context, but the prefix net alone doesn't.

### Suggested fix

Give each prefix pattern a trailing lookahead that negates its own body class rather than one shared class. For the alphanumeric-bodied families that's `(?![A-Za-z0-9])`. One way to keep the shared machinery: compile each pattern as `(?:<pattern>)(?!<its body class>)` and keep the shared lookbehind. A regression test per family with a trailing `_`, `-` and `.` would lock it in.

issues.body:
### Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.22.1** (commit `297552a9d6`), desktop app (local build via `hermes update`), Windows 11, local gateway

### What happens

Open a new chat in the desktop app and send the first message immediately: the turn runs (1 API call lands on the provider) but the reply is a ~66-char fixed busy/apology-style text instead of a real answer, delivered non-streamed. Resending the exact same text right after succeeds normally (streamed, real answer).

The user-visible workaround matches: re-picking the model in the composer (even the same model) makes subsequent submits work, even though the composer already showed that model as current.

Observed pattern in the gateway log (several fresh sessions on v0.22.1, first day of use):

```
# first submit of a fresh local session
... Normal final-send NOT suppressed despite active stream consumer ... streamed=False previewed=False
    content_delivered=False transformed=False final_len=66 — possible duplicate send (see wecom ack-timeout RCA).
... response ready: platform=local ... time=35.6s api_calls=1 response=66 chars

# immediate retry of the same text
... Suppressing normal final send ...: final delivery already confirmed (streamed=True ...)
... response ready: platform=local ... time=12.4s api_calls=1 response=31 chars
```

The `streamed=False` + fixed-length reply on the first submit is the anomaly — the same session's retry streams fine.

### Suspected area

The fresh session's first turn appears to fall into the "active session busy message" family (`gateway/run_busy.py::_handle_active_session_busy_message`) or races the session's initial attach/lease state, producing the fixed busy-style reply instead of a normal streamed turn. A model re-pick (`session.mutate`) seems to re-sync the binding so later submits run normally.

### Expected

The first submit of a brand-new session runs a normal streamed turn; no model re-pick needed.

issues.title: [Bug]: browser tools fail on Linux homes where scratch + task-id session names push the agent-browser socket past its 103-byte cap (cloud sessions too)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tool/browser
labels.description: Browser automation (CDP, Playwright)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Summary

On Linux hosts where `<HERMES_HOME>/cache/scratch` is longer than 35 chars, every browser tool call fails at daemon startup: agent-browser refuses to bind its socket because the composed path exceeds its 103-byte cap. **Cloud sessions fail too** — the local agent-browser harness fronts cloud CDP backends, so a portal/Browserbase/Browser-use cloud provider does not avoid this.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v2026.9.24-251-gee5ee84a34` (v0.21.5 line), Linux x86_64, source install
- `HERMES_HOME=/home/mauricio/.hermes` → scratch root `/home/mauricio/.hermes/cache/scratch` (36 chars)
- Default stock config, clean git tree

## Steps to reproduce

Any `browser_navigate` (or any browser tool) on the affected host. Direct CLI repro without Hermes:

```bash
LONG="/home/mauricio/.hermes/cache/scratch/agent-browser-hermes_20260925_163836_07df261a_38488bd0"  # 91 chars, the dir Hermes builds
mkdir -p "$LONG"
AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR="$LONG" agent-browser open about:blank --session default
```

```
✗ Session name 'default' is too long. Socket path would be 104 bytes (max 103).
Use a shorter session name or set AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR to a shorter path.
```

## Root cause

Since TMPDIR started pointing at `<HERMES_HOME>/cache/scratch` (07df62d604), the browser harness composes:

```
<scratch(36)>/agent-browser-<task-session-name(41)>/<session>.sock
36 + 1 + 55 + 1 + 12 = 105 bytes > agent-browser's 103-byte cap
```

`hermes_constants.socket_safe_tmpdir()` accepts the scratch root because its 50-char budget (`SOCKET_TMPDIR_MAX_LEN`) was tuned for `hermes_rpc_<32hex>.sock` (~49 bytes total). It doesn't account for the agent-browser dir layout, which adds `agent-browser-` + a 41-char task-id session name + `/default.sock`.

The daemon session name passed to the CLI is `default` (short); it's the **dir** built from the task-id session name that overflows, so the error message ("use a shorter session name") points at the wrong knob.

## Who it hits

Only Linux with longer home paths:
- `/home/mauricio/...` → 36-char scratch → breaks
- `/home/bob/...` → 33 chars → fine
- macOS → `socket_safe_tmpdir` always returns `/tmp` → fine
- Docker/Termux → short paths → fine

Which likely explains why this hasn't been reported yet.

## Suggested fix

At the agent-browser call sites (`tools/browser_tool_session.py::_prepare_session_socket_dir`, `tools/browser_tool_lifecycle.py` cleanup), compose-then-check: if `<dir>/<longest-possible-session>.sock` would exceed 103 bytes, fall back to a short hashed dir (`/tmp/agent-browser-<sha1(session)[:12]>`). A 15-line helper covers both call sites. (Locally verified working with exactly this approach.)

Alternatively, tighten the budget for the browser call sites specifically.

Happy to open a PR if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: A live local session whose routing entry is missing from the store's scope is permanently un-drainable — inputs queue forever, only a gateway restart recovers

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
## Summary

A **local** (desktop/CLI) session that is still **live** in `authority.sessions` but whose routing row is missing from the scope `SessionStore` reads becomes **permanently un-drainable**:

- every inbound prompt is accepted and committed to `session_admissions` as `status='queued'`,
- the drain claims it, calls `restore_local_session()`, hits the `current is None` guard and raises `admission_conflict`,
- `_claim_with_retry()` turns that into `Session <sid> paused: admission_conflict` and exits the drain,
- the next prompt repeats the exact same cycle **forever**.

The user sees nothing but "queued": in Desktop the composer shows `N Queued` indefinitely, there is no error card, and the messages never run. Only a **gateway restart** clears it (a fresh process has no live session, so the `live is None` branch recreates the missing entry instead of refusing).

## Environment

- Hermes `0.22.4`, commit `4d04303818`, macOS (arm64), install method `git`
- Desktop app → local gateway (`gateway run`), platform `local`, session key `agent:main:local:dm:<sid>`

## Observed

`logs/gateway.log`, one session, four pauses in ~50 minutes:

```
2026-10-22 09:22:27 WARNING gateway.session_authority: Session 20260722_152611_c9d4da paused: admission_conflict
2026-10-22 09:39:33 WARNING gateway.session_authority: Session 20260722_152611_c9d4da paused: admission_conflict
2026-10-22 09:39:38 WARNING gateway.session_authority: Session 20260722_152611_c9d4da paused: admission_conflict
2026-10-22 09:41:57 WARNING gateway.session_authority: Session 20260722_152611_c9d4da paused: admission_conflict
2026-10-22 10:09:16 WARNING gateway.session_authority: Session 20260722_152611_c9d4da paused: admission_conflict
```

The FIFO keeps the input it never ran:

```
session_admissions:
  admission 291b6ea6…  principal uid:501  status queued  payload {"text":"..."}
```

After the gateway was restarted (10:17), that same row was delivered and settled (`status=terminal`) with no other change to the DB — i.e. the state was fine, the **process** was wedged.

## Root cause

`gateway/session_local_recovery.py::restore_local_session()` is asymmetric about a missing route entry:

```python
live = authority.sessions.get(sid)
if live is None:
    with store._lock:
        store._ensure_loaded_locked()
        current = store._entries.get(route)
        if current is not None and current.session_id != target:
            ...  # stray-replacement guard
        store._entries[route] = entry          # ← a missing route HEALS here
        ...
else:                                          # session is live
    with store._lock:
        current = store._entry_locked(route)
        if current is None or (current.session_id not in receipt.get('lineage', [sid])
                               and not _stray_route_target(authority, receipt, current.session_id)):
            raise RuntimeStoreError('admission_conflict')   # ← a missing route REFUSES here
```

`_entry_locked()` only calls `_ensure_loaded_locked()`, which early-returns once `self._loaded` is `True` — so a store that has already loaded (every long-lived gateway) never re-reads the table, and any desync between `authority.sessions` and `store._entries` is fatal while the session stays live.

### One concrete way to desync it: two `scope`s in `gateway_routing`

`SessionStore` reads and writes **only** its own scope:

```python
# gateway/session_persistence.py
for key, entry_json in loader(scope=self._routing_scope()).items():   # _load_routing_rows_locked
... replacer({...}, scope=self._routing_scope())                      # _persist_routing_data
... saver(session_key, entry_json, scope=self._routing_scope())       # _save_entry
```

while the DB helper defaults to `scope=''`:

```python
# hermes_state_gateway.py
def replace_gateway_routing_entries(self, entries, *, scope: str = "") -> set[str]:
def save_gateway_routing_entry(self, session_key, entry_json, *, scope: str = ""):
```

Rows written by an older release (before the scope column carried the resolved `sessions_dir`) stay under `''` and are never migrated. On our install both scopes coexist, and the wedged route is the one that only exists under `''`:

```
scope                              session_key                                     updated_at
                                   agent:main:local:dm:20260722_152611_c9d4da      2026-07-22 15:26:11   ← stranded
/Users/sylvan/.hermes/sessions     agent:main:local:dm:20260727_094330_f71c73      2026-10-22 10:30:24
/Users/sylvan/.hermes/sessions     agent:main:local:dm:20260928_144125_db4141      2026-10-22 10:28:17
/Users/sylvan/.hermes/sessions     agent:main:local:dm:20261020_183705_a1b94b      2026-10-22 10:28:17
/Users/sylvan/.hermes/sessions     agent:main:local:dm:20261021_105114_c556eb      2026-10-22 10:28:17
/Users/sylvan/.hermes/sessions     agent:main:telegram:dm:7856942544               2026-10-22 10:28:17
```

The store therefore has no in-memory entry for that route, the receipt itself is intact (`route`/`chat_id`/`user_id`/`lineage` all match the `sessions` row and the stored receipt), and `restore_local_session` refuses on the `current is None` arm on every claim.

Note the row is also **never refreshed**, so the hourly prune (`SessionStore.prune_old_entries`, >90 days idle) will eventually delete legacy-scope rows entirely — the same wedge then applies without any `''`-scope row at all.

## Why nothing recovers it

- `_pause()` only releases waiters; it does not retry, and no timer re-schedules the FIFO while the session is live.
- `_schedule()` (called by every new submission) starts a drain that re-enters the same refusal.
- The client sees `202/queued`, not an error, so the desktop queue just grows (`N Queued`).
- Only restarting the gateway works: `live is None` on the first claim, so the `store._entries[route] = entry` branch recreates the entry and persists it.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Take any local session whose routing row exists **only** under a scope the store does not read (e.g. `''`), or delete the row at the store's scope (`store._routing_scope()`) and keep the in-memory entry out (prune it, or restart into a mirror-only load):

```sql
UPDATE gateway_routing SET scope = '' WHERE session_key = 'agent:main:local:dm:<sid>';
```

2. Keep the session live in the gateway (open it from the desktop / send a prompt) so `authority.sessions[<sid>]` exists.
3. Send two prompts. The first is admitted (`session_admissions.status='queued'`), the drain logs `paused: admission_conflict`, and the second prompt queues behind it. Nothing ever runs.
4. Restart the gateway; both rows drain immediately.

A unit-level reproduction is the same two facts: `authority.sessions` has a live entry, `store._entry_locked(route)` returns `None`, receipt/lineage/session row all valid → `restore_local_session` raises `admission_conflict`.

## Suggested fix

The receipt is the route's truth for exactly this situation (the same argument the `_stray_route_target` comment already makes). A missing route entry while live is indistinguishable from a missing route entry while cold, and the cold branch already heals it — so:

1. In the live branch, treat `current is None` as "recreate the entry for this route" (same code as the cold branch) instead of `admission_conflict`; keep the refusal only for a **different** `session_id` that is not provably stray.
2. Separately, migrate/normalise `gateway_routing` scopes: copy rows under `''` to the resolved `sessions_dir` scope (or make readers fall back to `''` when the scoped read is empty), so upgraded installs stop carrying invisible routes.
3. If a refusal remains possible, surface it: a paused FIFO with `queued > 0` should reach the client as an error/notice rather than an indefinite "queued" state (see also #142731 for the pause-never-recovers class).

## Related

- #142731 — same *class* (a session paused on `admission_conflict` never recovers), different trigger (`api_server` + stale mirror entry vs ended row). The remediation there (unpause / scope the pause to the conflicting turn) would unpause this FIFO but the very next claim re-conflicts, because the route entry is still invisible — the missing-entry arm needs fixing too.
- #140642 (closed) fixed the *replacement* variant of this guard (`_stray_route_target`); this report is the **absent** variant, which that fix deliberately does not cover (`current is None` is checked before the stray test).

prs.title: feat(gateway): warm a local model's prefix cache after a compression commit
prs.body:
## Why

A compression commit rewrites the transcript, so the next turn's request is a brand-new token prefix. On a local model server (oMLX, llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama) that prefix misses the server's paged prefix cache, and the first turn after a manual `/compress` or a deferred hygiene adoption pays a full cold prefill — measured ~23K tokens ≈ 41s TTFT on a 35B, versus 1-4s for a cache-hit turn.

This is the local-server analogue of #122094 (Anthropic cache warming), but for a different reason: there, a long tool run outlives the cache TTL; here, a compression commit *invalidates* the prefix outright.

## What changes

- `gateway/compression_warmup.py` (new) — schedules an idle-gated warmup after a committed compression. The request is built through the SAME machinery the next real turn uses (`_resolve_session_agent_runtime` / `_resolve_turn_agent_config` / `TurnRunner._build_fresh_agent`, `session_store.load_transcript` + `_build_gateway_agent_history`, `_restore_or_build_system_prompt`, `turn_request_assembly.assemble_api_request` + `agent._build_api_kwargs`), with `max_tokens=1` overlaid at the end via the agent's own `_max_tokens_param`. Byte-alignment is the whole game: the chat template renders the tool list into the front of the token stream, so a warmup assembled any other way would not populate the prefix the next turn looks for.
- Two call sites: the watermark-fenced hygiene adoption done-callback (`gateway/run_turn_hygiene.py`) and manual `/compress` (`gateway/slash_commands_session.py`).
- `gateway.prefix_cache_warmup.enabled` (new, **default off**).

## Gates (all fail-open, failure only logs)

- the route must resolve to a **local** model server (`agent.model_metadata.is_local_endpoint`) — cloud providers bill per token and manage their own prompt caches, so warming them is pure cost;
- the session must be **idle** at fire time — no running turn, no adapter-pending or overflow-queued messages, no compression still in flight. A local server's serial FCFS queue would pay the prefill twice instead of hiding it, so a busy session is re-polled briefly and then abandoned;
- the response is **discarded** — nothing is appended to the transcript, `state.db`, or the cached agent. This is cache filling, not conversation;
- a newer compression commit supersedes an older one (its rebuilt prefix is already stale).

In-turn commits (preflight / overflow recovery) are deliberately not hooked: the continuing turn re-prefills itself.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_compression_warmup.py` — local-endpoint detection (loopback / LAN / container name are local; a cloud host is not), non-`chat_completions` routes are never local, the feature is off by default, and a disabled warmup schedules no task.

prs.title: fix(agent): guard the sequential tool submit against interpreter shutdown
prs.body:
## Problem

A tool call that is still being *scheduled* when the interpreter begins finalizing hits CPython's module-global shutdown flag and `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor.submit` raises:

```
RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown
```

In the sequential tool path this RuntimeError propagates out of `_run_sequential_tool_execution_middleware` (`agent/tool_executor.py:857` → `tools/daemon_pool.py:36`), and surfaces as an ERROR with a full traceback per tool call during teardown:

```
agent.tool_executor: handle_function_call raised for terminal: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../agent/tool_executor.py", line 1594, in _run_sequential_call
    managed = _run_sequential_tool_execution_middleware(
  File ".../agent/tool_executor.py", line 857, in _run_sequential_tool_execution_middleware
    future = executor.submit(propagate_context_to_thread(_run))
RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown
```

Measured on the reporting host (one gateway, error logs Sep 12–14): **83 occurrences across 7 distinct sessions**, every one traced through that single submit site — the last unguarded tool-submission site of its class.

## Reproduction

Patch `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor.submit` to raise the exact CPython error and call the middleware the way `_run_sequential_call` does (scratch checkout at current `main`):

```
$ python repro.py
PROPAGATED RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown
    File ".../agent/tool_executor.py", line 857, in _run_sequential_tool_execution_middleware
RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after interpreter shutdown
```

With this branch, same repro:

```
SYNTHESIZED: _ToolShutdownResult | Error executing tool 'read_file': Python interpreter is shutting down; tool was not started
```

## Fix

The concurrent batch path already converts unsubmitted slots into per-call error results from the same signal — `_ConcurrentBatch.submit_all` routes through the shared `tools.interpreter_shutdown` predicate, whose docstring names this exact bug class (#55924/#58720) and says **all** submit sites should recognize both CPython message variants. The sequential path never got that treatment; this branch mirrors it:

- Wrap the `submit`; re-raise any RuntimeError the shared predicate does not recognize, so a genuine broken pool still surfaces.
- No worker was started, so synthesize the sibling `_ToolShutdownResult` marker with the concurrent path's exact message (`... Python interpreter is shutting down; tool was not started`), emit the single terminal `post_tool_call` (`status=error`, `error_type=interpreter_shutdown`), and fold the marker into `_publish_sequential_result`'s synthesized-result handling so no second hook fires and effect accounting stays conservative.

**Why not guard inside `daemon_pool.submit` itself:** synthesis needs the tool-call context (ref/name/args) to produce the per-call result and terminal hook; `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor` is shared infrastructure (relay scope ops, memory sync) where silently swallowing scheduling errors would change semantics.

**Why not only at the caller's `except` in `_run_sequential_call`:** that route converts only dispatches carrying `error_result` and still logs ERROR + traceback; handling at the submit site fixes both that route and the raising route with one behavior, matching the concurrent side.

## Validation

- New `tests/agent/test_sequential_tool_interpreter_shutdown.py`: both CPython message variants (`...after interpreter shutdown` / `...after shutdown`) synthesize the marker result with exactly one hook; a non-shutdown `RuntimeError("broken pool")` still propagates. Red→green: on unfixed `main` the repro raises through `tool_executor.py:857`; on the branch it synthesizes.
- Focused set — `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_sequential_tool_interpreter_shutdown.py tests/agent/test_sequential_tool_interrupt.py tests/agent/test_interpreter_shutdown_turn_exit.py tests/agent/test_conversation_loop_interpreter_shutdown.py` → **4 files, 23 tests passed, 0 failed**.
- Blast-radius sweep over the surrounding executor machinery (sequential timeout / deadline-exempt delegate / start-order gate / authorization gate / checkpoint paths / activity heartbeat / batch segmentation / malformed args / incremental persistence / deadline): **10 files, 149 tests passed, 1 skipped (windows-only lane)** — 0 failures.

prs.body:
## Summary

Expose the existing cooperative delegated-child cancellation primitive through an authenticated, profile/session-owned HTTP route:

`POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/subagents/{subagent_id}/stop`

- Advertise `features.session_subagent_stop` through `/v1/capabilities`.
- Check the selected profile DB, existing API session and durable parent-session lineage before admitting cancellation.
- Make duplicate admission idempotent for a live child; distinguish recent finished children (409) from foreign/unknown targets (404).
- Return 202 `stopping` for an accepted request, not a premature terminal status. Normal child teardown and partial-output completion remain the authority for termination.
- Preserve parent/sibling execution; never substitute whole-run cancellation or file/process manipulation.
- Move the existing browser-control capability descriptor to a topical sibling to keep the API-server facade below its current line-count ratchet. Preserve the facade constants as the lookup/patch seam.
- Document the transport contract and its boundary relative to plugin lifecycle handles.

## Verification

Seven new HTTP/registration/ownership/idempotency tests and existing control/capacity/late-child stop tests passed on the original installed-version patch (56 tests). The patch was then forward-ported onto upstream main `4e58c721c8cf`, and final commit `7230457f12d63d0be9fc99e0eb91525783e8c5f9` passed the same 56 regressions, two capability tests, and code-health/ruff/footgun checks (zero blocking or advisory health findings). Independent review is pending, so this PR is draft and is not a release approval.

Tests use isolated temporary SessionDBs and synthetic fixture API keys. No actual credentials, production sessions or live gateway are changed.

## Scope

This operates on native `delegate_task` registry children. It does not add a new model tool, cancel sibling/parent runs, revive work after a gateway restart, or change the plugin lifecycle-handle API.

prs.title: fix(kanban): respawn guard bare 429/403 digits no longer match host:port / file:line / slug tokens
prs.body:
## What

`_RESPAWN_BLOCKER_RE` matched the bare digit tokens `429|403` with the group-level `\b` anchors, so any digit run that happens to **tail a non-HTTP compound token** tripped the auth/quota blocker:

- `stale_lock=<host>:403` — a stale claim lock stamp where `403` is the **port**
- `worker died at agent.py:403` — a `file:line` reference
- `workspace/ticket-403-refund/` — a workspace slug digit

Each occurrence parks a healthy `ready` card as `blocker_auth` on every dispatcher tick, forever — the guard returns before `consecutive_failures` can advance, so the breaker never trips, and `_clear_failure_counter` only runs on a successful `complete_task`, so nothing ever clears the stamped error. On the reporting board this held a user-created card for **15 days: 5,522 `respawn_guarded` events** (one per ~64s tick) plus a recurring `kanban dispatcher stuck … blocker_auth` gateway alarm every ~5.5 minutes, ending only in manual DB surgery. Full evidence and repro: #142853.

## Why the neighbouring fixes don't cover this

The curated-list fix for #117009 tightened the **word stems** (`auth\w*` → curated auth family) but left the digits sharing the bare `\b(...)` group; #63248/#127808 report the same wedged-forever outcome for word slugs inside workspace paths. This PR closes the digit flavour of that class: a digit without HTTP context is not a status code.

## Change

Split the digits out of the shared word group and require them not to be glued to a `:`/`-` compound token:

```diff
-    r"\b(quota|rate[\s_\-]?limit|429|403|"
+    r"\b(quota|rate[\s_\-]?limit|"
     ...
-    r"invalid[\s_]api[\s_]key)\b",
+    r"invalid[\s_]api[\s_]key)\b"
+    r"|(?<![:-])\b(429|403)\b",
```

- `stale_lock=cantaloup:403` → no match (port)
- `hermes/agent.py:403` → no match (line number)
- `workspace/ticket-403-refund/` → no match (slug digit)
- `HTTP 403`, `Error code: 429`, `429 Client Error` → still match

Trade-off (flagged in the issue): a tight `status:429` with no space after the colon is also excluded — none of the provider error shapes produce that form.

## Testing

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py` — the existing `test_respawn_guard_blocker_auth_curated_not_open_stem` parametrize table gains six rows (three false positives → `None`, two real statuses → `blocker_auth`).

```
uv run --frozen python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py -k "blocker or respawn" -q
→ 14 passed

uv run --frozen python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py -q
→ 4 failed, 55 passed, 1 skipped
```

The 4 failures (`test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`, `test_worktree_workspace_explicit_target_materializes_linked_worktree`, `test_resolve_hermes_argv_prefers_module_form_over_path_shim`, `test_dispatch_max_in_progress_blocks_review_when_at_limit`) fail **identically on unpatched `main` @ `4e58c721c8` on this Windows host** (baseline re-run: same 4 failed, 50 passed) — environment-dependent, not introduced by this change.

Closes #142853.

prs.body:
## Problem

`website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` documents only 6 of the 12 flags `hermes update` actually accepts:

```
hermes update [--gateway] [--check] [--plan] [--no-backup] [--backup] [--yes]
```

**Reproduction:** run `hermes update --help` (or read `hermes_cli/subcommands/update.py` on current main) — the parser registers `--keep-stash`, `--branch`, `--switch-branch`, `--no-gateway-restart`, `--force`, and `--force-venv` in addition to the six documented flags. All six undocumented flags are real, shipped behavior: `--no-gateway-restart` is the documented cron/automation path (already covered in prose on `website/docs/getting-started/updating.md` §"Automated updates from inside the gateway"), `--keep-stash` is what the desktop updater invokes, and the two Windows guards (`--force`/`--force-venv`) are the only way to proceed past concurrent-process detection.

## Fix

- Extend the usage synopsis to the full flag set.
- Add a row for each missing flag to the `hermes update` option table, with descriptions matching the parser help and the existing prose pages.

This is documentation-only; no behavior changes.

## Why not an alternative

The prose guide already documents these flags, so the reference page is the one stale surface. Rewriting the guide would duplicate content; a "see also" pointer alone would leave the canonical flag table incomplete for anyone using the reference as the authoritative CLI surface.

## Validation

- Every flag added to the table exists verbatim as an `add_argument` in `hermes_cli/subcommands/update.py` (lines 13–75); after this change the table covers every flag the parser registers (checked programmatically: no `add_argument` flag missing, no table row naming a flag the parser lacks).
- Flag descriptions cross-checked against `hermes_cli/subcommands/update.py` help strings and `website/docs/getting-started/updating.md`.
- Markdown table integrity: all edited rows keep the 3-pipe 2-column shape of the surrounding table.

prs.title: fix(webhook): accept Hermes outbound signature, event and delivery headers
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`agent/outbound_webhooks.py` signs deliveries with `X-Hermes-Signature-256` (`sha256=<hex>`, GitHub-style) and tags them with `X-Hermes-Event` and `X-Hermes-Delivery`. The inbound webhook adapter only knew the GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Svix and generic header names, so the documented "wake another Hermes instance" flow was rejected with 401 `Invalid signature`. Even with the signature accepted, a route's `events:` filter could not see the Hermes event name, and the sender's retry was processed twice because the delivery id was ignored.

This verifies `X-Hermes-Signature-256` on the same fail-closed path as `X-Hub-Signature-256`, reads `X-Hermes-Event` for the event filter, and uses `X-Hermes-Delivery` for idempotency. No new scheme: the header carries the exact GitHub format, so it reuses the existing comparison.

## Related Issue

Fixes #127471

## Type of Change

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover conversations with unusable durable timestamps
prs.body:
## Summary

The gateway's durable session recovery converts stored timestamp cells directly with `datetime.fromtimestamp`. Infinite or oversized repaired/legacy values raise `OverflowError`, preventing a peer from recovering its existing message-bearing conversation. The converter already intends invalid dates to fall back to an old timestamp, but misses this exception class and the shared trusted-epoch policy.

Use the existing `coerce_epoch` validation for recovered start/activity cells and keep the old-date fallback when a cell is unusable. Valid dates, durable conversation identity and transcript are preserved. The MCP session-index converter also handles timestamp OverflowError with its existing empty-date fallback, so a bad started_at in one row does not erase every conversation from the routing index.

## Verification

- Baseline: three failures (infinite, negative infinite and oversized timestamps) through actual SessionStore + SQLite file + durable transcript. Malformed-text control already falls back correctly.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_session_recovery_bad_timestamp.py tests/gateway/test_session_recovery.py tests/gateway/test_session_store_stale_prune.py tests/gateway/test_session_db_recovery.py -q`: **22 passed**.
- Two invariant functions cover corrupt-cell recovery and valid-date/transcript preservation; isolated HERMES_HOME and no production data.
- Ruff on changed source/test files and `git diff --check` passed.

The full repository suite has not been run for this patch. CI remains pending until publication.

## Contributor review and CI

Personal contributor review of every changed line remains pending, as required by CONTRIBUTING.md. Focused native macOS tests are documented above; the complete suite and upstream cross-platform CI have not been claimed complete.

Published from the current upstream main snapshot after rebase. Baseline reproduction was at `57a22675`; final head validation is tracked separately and will be appended if it changes the findings.

## Published-head follow-up

Focused regression validation passed at exact published commit `8633956c638c26cde36810dd76c26fd2cd9a58fc` using the canonical runner, zero retries, native macOS and the PM-built Python 3.14.7 environment. The batch has 90 passing individual-head focused tests; that total includes PM neighboring tests and is not a per-PR count. Every selected defect also reproduces against upstream main `bddd22be`; the combined patches passed focused integration validation. GitHub verifies this commit signature and reports no merge conflict. Upstream Actions currently require maintainer approval (`action_required`), so CI has not run and is not green. Personal contributor review remains unconfirmed; its checkbox remains unchecked.

## Current review readiness — 2026-09-30

Ready for maintainer review at the contributor’s request. Existing exact-head focused and combined validation evidence remains above. Upstream Actions require maintainer approval and are not green; the full suite and cross-platform lanes remain unverified.

## Review follow-up — 2026-10-07

Addressed the sibling MCP failure reported by @Enough1122 in signed commit `ccbdbfbcec7826b728f0dbb7d7737ad9147d7ec6`. `_iso` catches OverflowError in the existing invalid-date fallback. A real three-session SQLite/registry/MCP-index regression covers infinite, negative-infinite, oversized finite and overflowing-text cells; all four cases returned an empty index before the source repair and preserve all three entries afterward. Healthy entries and stored messages remain identical; last-active selection still preserves the valid message timestamp.

Canonical runner with zero retries: **10 MCP helper cases plus 22 gateway recovery cases pass**. Ruff and diff checks pass. This new local follow-up used native macOS / Python **3.13.5** because the prior PM-built 3.14.7 test environment is no longer available; the prior 3.14.7 receipts above apply to the previous head only. Full suite, current supported-Python/cross-platform lanes and hosted CI remain unverified. No timestamp-domain policy, per-row exception suppression or unrelated corruption recovery is introduced.


## Re-scope and conflict resolution — 2026-10-22

Resolved against current `main` at `95f76e896a`. The PR now changes **two files**:

- `gateway/session_recovery.py` (+12/-4)
- `tests/gateway/test_session_recovery_bad_timestamp.py` (+48)

**Dropped: the MCP half.** `mcp_serve.py` and `tests/test_mcp_serve.py` no longer exist on `main` — both were removed by `e3a962d087` ("refactor(mcp): Hermes as an MCP server leaves core for the mcp-serve plugin"), and `main` has no successor `_load_sessions_index`. The merge surfaced them as `CONFLICT (modify/delete)` and this branch accepts upstream's deletion. The 2026-10-07 follow-up above, which addressed @Enough1122's `_iso` report, therefore no longer applies to this repository; that change belongs in the `mcp-serve` plugin if it is still wanted.

**Dropped: the `OverflowError` except-clause addition.** `coerce_epoch` returns `None` for any value outside `EPOCH_MIN..EPOCH_MAX` (`0.0`..`4_200_000_000.0`), and both bounds convert cleanly (`1969-12-31`, `2103-02-03`), so nothing surviving `coerce_epoch` can overflow `datetime.fromtimestamp`. Upstream's `except (TypeError, ValueError, OSError)` is left untouched. Removing the redundant clause also sharpened the tests: bypassing `coerce_epoch` now fails three cases rather than one, because the extra clause had been absorbing `inf` and `1e+250`.

### What the remaining change is tested against

- `pytest tests/gateway/test_session_recovery_bad_timestamp.py` → **5 passed** (whole module, Python 3.13.5, native macOS).
- Mutation check: replacing the `coerce_epoch` call with a passthrough fails `test_real_database_recovery_falls_back_for_corrupt_timestamp[inf]`, `[-inf]` and `[1e+250]`; restoring it returns 5 passed. The routing is therefore covered rather than incidentally satisfied.
- Against `main`'s `gateway/session_recovery.py` dropped into this tree, the same module reports **3 failed, 2 passed** with `gateway/session_recovery.py:142: OverflowError: timestamp out of range for platform time_t`.

That last item is scoped deliberately: it shows `main`'s `_ts` raising an uncaught `OverflowError` on `inf`, `-inf` and `1e+250` supplied by these fixtures. It is **not** a demonstration that a live row can hold such a value — the tests build rows directly, and whether the gateway's own persistence path can write one has not been shown here. Reviewers treating that as the bar should read this as "mishandled if present", not "observed in production".

Not verified: any test outside this module on this branch, the full suite, and hosted CI — upstream Actions require maintainer approval and show `action_required`, so nothing has run.

## Problem

The `hermes cron` section of the CLI reference contradicts itself and omits three
shipped subcommands. Its usage line already advertises `runs` and `incidents`:

```
hermes cron <list|create|edit|pause|resume|run|remove|status|runs|incidents|doctor|tick>
```

…but the subcommand table below documents neither, and `notepad` appears in neither
place even though `hermes cron notepad` is a real, shipped command.

Reproduction:

```bash
$ hermes cron --help
usage: hermes cron ... {list,create,add,edit,pause,resume,run,remove,rm,delete,status,runs,history,incidents,notepad,doctor,tick} ...

$ grep -n 'notepad' website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md   # no match before this change
```

## The fix

Add the three missing rows (`runs`, `incidents`, `notepad`) to the `hermes cron`
table, matching the parser's own order and flags, and add `notepad` to the usage
line so it lists every subcommand.

## Why not another approach

The section is the authoritative per-subcommand reference for `hermes cron`; the
rows are the smallest slice that makes the table agree with `hermes cron --help`.
No new page is warranted for three subcommands of an already-documented command.

## Validation

```bash
$ hermes cron runs --help
usage: hermes cron runs [-h] [--limit LIMIT] [job_id]
   job_id         Optional job ID filter
   --limit LIMIT  Rows to show (1-500)          # default 20 in the parser

$ hermes cron incidents --help
usage: hermes cron incidents [-h] [--state {detected,alerted,resolved,closed}] [{list,ack}] [incident_id]

$ hermes cron notepad --help
usage: hermes cron notepad [-h] job_id [{get,set,delete,list}] [key] [value]

$ python3 website/scripts/check_doc_links.py   # -> OK
```

Every documented flag/value matches the parser above.

Two per-command option lists in the CLI reference are incomplete, and the `hermes logs`
one contradicts the section's own table.

```bash
$ hermes doctor --help
usage: hermes doctor [-h] [--fix] [--live] [--ack ADVISORY_ID]

Unknown component: 'bogus'. Available: agent, cli, cron, gateway, gui, tools

$ hermes logs boguslog -n 1
Unknown log: 'boguslog'. Available: agent, desktop, errors, gateway, gui, handoff, mcp, update
```

The two negative cases print the command's own accepted set, which is the ground truth

  rows describing what they do.
- `hermes logs`: `log_name` gains `mcp`; `--component` gains `gui`.

No new content is invented — the values are copied from the commands' own runtime

prs.title: fix(loop): hide the LOOP_COMPLETE marker from user-facing replies
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`/loop` stops when a wakeup reply ends with a `LOOP_COMPLETE` line, but nothing removes that control line before the reply is shown, so users see the literal marker on every surface: the CLI, the TUI and messaging gateways (including streamed Telegram replies).

This hides a trailing top-level `LOOP_COMPLETE` at the display boundary only. Loop completion detection still reads the raw reply, so loops stop exactly as before. A marker inside fenced code or in prose is content and is left alone, and a reply that is only the marker sends nothing. `NO_REPLY` handling is unchanged.

Streaming is the subtle part: the marker can arrive across chunks, so the CLI, the TUI and the gateway stream consumer hold back a trailing marker candidate (fence-aware across chunks) the same way the gateway already holds back a partial `NO_REPLY`, and release it when it turns out to be content.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Related merged work: #72333 (`/loop`) and #87704 (completing streamed loop ticks).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/response_filters.py`: fence-aware `strip_trailing_loop_complete_marker`, streaming helpers (`ends_with_partial_loop_complete_marker`, `split_trailing_loop_complete_marker` with released-text fence context), and `hide_loop_complete_marker`, which stashes the raw reply on the event for the post-turn hooks before stripping.
- `gateway/run_turn.py`, `gateway/run_goals.py`: the final and queued-follow-up lanes strip the marker; `_final_text_for_post_turn_hooks` prefers the stashed raw reply so non-streamed loop ticks still complete.
- `gateway/stream_consumer.py`, `gateway/stream_consumer_transport.py`: hold a partial trailing marker in streamed edits.
- `gateway/run_startup.py`: crash-left redelivery sanitizes first, then hides the marker.
- `agent/stream_delivery.py`: interim assistant messages (commentary, Codex agentMessage items) are filtered in `_deliver_interim`, the funnel every interim callback shares.
- `hermes_cli/cli_stream_mixin.py`, `hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py`: CLI streaming hold and final panel. A held prefix is released at tool boundaries; at end of turn it is dropped only when the whole segment ends in a top-level marker.
- `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py`: TUI streaming hold and the `message.complete` payload.
- Tests for every lane above.

## How to Test

1. Start a loop that ends itself, e.g. `/loop 1m reply "done" then end with LOOP_COMPLETE on its own line`.
2. Before this change, the final reply shows `LOOP_COMPLETE`. After it, the reply shows only `done`, and `/loop status` reports the loop finished.
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh --files tests/gateway/test_loop_complete_display.py:tests/gateway/test_loop_command.py:tests/gateway/test_gateway_silence_tokens.py:tests/gateway/test_crash_left_reply_loop_complete.py:tests/gateway/test_stale_finalize_suppression.py:tests/hermes_cli/test_stream_partial_line_flush.py:tests/tui_gateway/test_bot_mode_silence_delivery.py:tests/tui_gateway/test_turn_payload_response_transformed.py:tests/agent/test_interim_loop_complete.py`

The one failure, `test_loop_wakeup_watcher_gates_profile_scope_on_active_loops`, fails the same way on unmodified `main` (an asyncio timeout under load) and is unrelated.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Extends semantic thread titles to **user-created** Discord threads, not just Hermes auto-created ones (rebase of #127854 by @dskwe, which conflicted with main; original commits reauthored here with credit preserved below).

The rename machinery gated on `_is_discord_auto_thread_lane` — threads Hermes itself created. A thread the *user* created in Discord and then talked to Hermes in kept Discord's default "New Thread" / first-message name forever, even though Hermes produces a session title that would name it. This PR splits the lane predicate: the new `_is_discord_thread_lane` matches any existing Discord thread that can receive a title, while auto-created threads keep their extra markers (`auto_thread_initial_name`, relay info). The rename kwargs stay conservative per lane: auto-created threads still rename only from their known initial name (`only_if_current_name`) or via relay feedback, while user-created threads rename outright — the name Discord generated is not something Hermes must preserve.

Rebase notes (main moved in this area since #127854: title-retry recovery, routing-entry marker recovery, unreadable-row handling):
- `test_session_title_rename_lane.py` merged main's new recovery tests with this PR's user-created-thread test; `_attach_in_thread` now also wires the real `_is_discord_thread_lane`.

The unreadable-row negative (attach's try/except drops the callback) is unchanged.
- `test_relay_threads.py`'s `_Stub` wires the new predicate, mirroring the existing `_is_discord_auto_thread_lane` wiring.

prs.title: fix(doctor): state.db repair hints order "stop the profile's gateway" before --fix (#110054)
prs.body:
Item 3 of #110054 removed the bare `run 'hermes doctor --fix'` from the large-WAL warning while a live writer holds state.db (landed as #113055). Three more doctor state.db hints still print it:

- FTS repair hint — `state.db FTS write corruption — run 'hermes doctor --fix' (or 'hermes sessions repair') to rebuild the FTS index`
- malformed-schema hint — `state.db schema malformed — run 'hermes doctor --fix' (or 'hermes sessions repair') to recover hidden sessions`
- the >1 GB write-health probe skip info line — `… (run 'hermes doctor --fix' to probe it)`, printed from inside the branch that already *knows* a live writer may hold the store

**Problem / reproduction** (Linux, any checkout). Hold `state.db` from a second process (Desktop or `hermes gateway`), then run `hermes doctor` (no `--fix`) on a store that fails the write-health probe. The hint is printed with no holder qualifier, so the user follows it into `hermes doctor --fix` while the writer is live — the second-writer nudge #110054 documents — and the repair path refuses outright:

```
state.db repair skipped: a live writer still holds state.db; skipped schema surgery to avoid tearing
b-tree pages under a concurrent writer. Stop the gateway (hermes gateway stop) and retry.
```

So the user is told to run a command that cannot succeed, and is not told what to stop first.

**Fix.** The two repair hints gain a held form, selected by the same wrapper the WAL path already uses (`hermes_state_repair._live_writer_holds_db` — foreign-holder scan first, fails closed), worded like the WAL `_SKIP` line: *"cannot prove state.db is quiet (stop the profile's gateway first, then run …)"*. An unprovable store is never asserted as a live writer (gate C1's honest disjunction); a holder scan that raises is treated as held. The probe-skip info line orders "stop" first. `--fix` semantics, and the hint for a provably quiet store, are unchanged. No new scan, no new surface, no new dependency.

**Validation**

prs.title: fix(pm): say restart, not hermes setup, when the generation already landed
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A process that booted before PM committed a new dependency generation never activates it (activation is boot-only by design), but its missing-extra errors still tell the user to run `hermes setup` — the wrong remedy, because the dependency IS installed. Following the wrong advice (a full setup pass that finds nothing to do) leaves the user more confused than before, and unattended paths (cron delivery) keep failing until a manual restart (#140620).

This adds `pm.environments.stale_dependency_generation()`: a cheap, fail-open check that compares the running interpreter's prefix with the committed environment record. It answers "installed but this process predates it" exactly, and wires it into Feishu's standalone (cron) delivery — the path from the issue's timeline — so a stale process says a restart is needed instead of the install advice. The check is deliberately uncached so a commit landing while the process runs is noticed on the next failure.

## Related Issue

Fixes #140620

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pm/environments.py`: new `stale_dependency_generation(project_root=None)` — True only when `sys.prefix` resolves inside this install's PM generations directory AND differs from the committed record; unreadable/missing records and non-PM interpreters (dev checkouts, payloads) read as not stale, keeping today's advice.
- `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py`: `_standalone_send` distinguishes "installed but this process started before it was committed — restart the gateway" from the unchanged `hermes setup` advice.
- `tests/pm/test_stale_dependency_generation.py`: five cases — same generation, older generation, interpreter outside PM generations, unreadable record, missing record (fail-open).
- `tests/gateway/test_feishu_stale_generation_hint.py`: red/green pair for the delivery wording.

The other missing-extra call sites named in the issue (WeCom, Google Chat, tts/mcp tools, …) are intentionally left on the current wording: this lands the helper and one platform first, per the open scoping question in the issue thread; migrating the rest is mechanical once the helper's shape is agreed.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/pm/test_stale_dependency_generation.py tests/gateway/test_feishu_stale_generation_hint.py -q` — 7 passed.
2. `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_feishu_lazy_import.py tests/pm/test_activation_setup.py tests/pm/test_pm_core.py -q` — unchanged, all pass.
3. `python -m scripts.code_health --base upstream/main` — 0 blocking, 0 advisory (4 changed files).
4. Observed result: with a facts.json record pointing at a generation newer than the interpreter's prefix, a cron Feishu delivery returns `Restart the gateway`; with no such record it keeps the exact `hermes setup` message.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (targeted suites: pm 904 passed — the node/network/startup-verdict failures reproduce identically on a clean upstream checkout; feishu suites 126 passed — 3 failures likewise reproduce on clean main)
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs) — passes against the real upstream/main base (`code health: 0 blocking, 0 advisory`); a local `scripts/check` run reports pre-existing gateway/agent findings only because the local fork's `origin/main` reference lags main by 5 days
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (arm64)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A

prs.title: fix(git): disable optional locks in bounded probes
prs.body:
## Summary

Bounded internal Git probes currently allow Git's optional index refresh. A `git status` interrupted while refreshing can leave `.git/index.lock` behind even though the caller is read-only.

This change:

- sets `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` in the shared hardened internal-Git environment
- passes `--no-optional-locks` explicitly to `status` through `harden_git_argv` and the coding-context probe
- brings the trace-upload branch probe onto the shared hardened environment
- adds a filesystem watcher regression with a SIGSTOP negative control

The watcher first proves the old command creates `index.lock`; the production arm runs eight independently stale bounded probes and asserts the lock is never observed. Removing `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` makes the test fail at `assert not seen.is_set()`.

Required mutation locks for `add`, `commit`, `checkout`, etc. are unchanged; Git documents `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` as suppressing only optional maintenance/refresh operations.

Fork-first counterpart: https://github.com/ANG-Ventures/hermes-agent/pull/822

## Verification

- affected 7-file suite: **103 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped**
- watcher mutation (remove env): **fails on observed `index.lock`**
- Ruff on all changed files: **passed**
- `git diff --check`: **passed**
