prs.title: fix(teams): answer 400, not 500, to a body that is valid JSON but not an object
prs.body:
## What

`_AiohttpBridgeAdapter._aiohttp_handler` refuses a body that cannot be parsed, but it never checked what the parsed document *is*. A body that is valid JSON whose top-level value is not an object — an array, a bare string, a number, `true`/`false`, `null` — passes that guard and is handed to the SDK as the activity. `HttpServer.handle_request` then calls `body.get("type")` on it:

```
ERROR microsoft_teams.apps.http.http_server: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
"POST /api/messages HTTP/1.1" 500 197
```

The SDK's own catch-all logs it with `logger.exception` (an ERROR row plus traceback) and answers HTTP 500. That is the observed production incident behind this PR: a client posted `[]` to a live bridge and got a 500 and a traceback instead of a refusal.

## The change

One check, right after the existing parse guard and before the handler call:

```python
if not isinstance(body, dict):
    logger.warning(
        "[teams] refused a request body that is not a JSON object: %s %s from %s "
        "(%s bytes): top-level %s",
        request.method, request.path, request.remote,
        request.content_length if request.content_length is not None else "unknown",
        _body_json_type_name(body),
    )
    return web.Response(status=400, body=json.dumps({"error": "invalid JSON body"}),
                        content_type="application/json")
```

- The answer is the same short generic JSON body the unparsable shapes already get, so the two refusals cannot drift apart; it echoes nothing of the request.
- The WARNING names the method, the path, the remote address, the content length and the top-level JSON type (`array`, `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`). `_body_json_type_name` reads only the type, never the value, so no body byte can reach the log.
- The SDK handler is not called for that request, so the SDK only ever receives a mapping.

Unchanged: an unparsable body keeps its 400 and its decode-reason WARNING wording; a JSON object without `Authorization` still gets the SDK's 401; a signed Bot Framework activity is still answered 200 and processed; any other exception inside the handler still reaches aiohttp's error log with its traceback. This is a body-shape check, not suppression — no `AttributeError` arm, no catch-all.

## Commits

1. `fix(teams): answer 400, not 500, to a request body that is not valid JSON` — the parse guard (rebased from the closed PR below).
2. `fix(teams): answer 400, not 500, to a body that is valid JSON but not an object` — this change.

## Supersedes #139951

#139951 carried only commit 1, was closed on 2026-10-21 without merging, and its head branch went with the deleted fork, so this branch re-lands that commit on today's `main` and adds the non-object check on top.

## Tests

Upstream has no test surface for this handler: `_aiohttp_handler` appears nowhere but `plugins/platforms/teams/adapter.py` itself (`grep -rn "_aiohttp_handler" plugins tests` → the definition and its `router.add_route` line).

The same change is covered in The ValueExchange's image-time port of this adapter (`services/hermes-barney/patches/patch_teams_json_body_guard.py` in `vx_meetings_ai_content`), where the patch is applied to a byte-for-byte copy of this file and driven over a real aiohttp server with the real `microsoft-teams-apps` `App` behind the bridge: 42 tests, including a JSON array and each bare scalar getting 400 with one WARNING and the SDK never being called, a marker string that must appear in no log record, an unsigned JSON object still getting the SDK's 401, and a RED proof that the unpatched adapter answers 500 to the same array with the SDK's `no attribute 'get'` ERROR.

## Divergence from the port (pre-existing, not introduced here)

The port's parse clause names `(ValueError, LookupError, RecursionError)` — a client-declared charset that does not exist raises `LookupError`, and a body nested past the interpreter's recursion limit raises `RecursionError`, and neither is a `ValueError`. This PR keeps upstream's `except ValueError` exactly as commit 1 wrote it and adds only the non-object check. The two are one class apart and the port records it; say the word and I will widen the clause here too so the two are identical.

## Problem

`display.compact: true` in config.yaml had no effect on the interactive CLI: the full welcome panel (caduceus art, tools, MCP servers, skills) still drew. `HermesCLI.__init__` and `cli.main` defaulted `compact` to `False`, and `cmd_chat` passed `getattr(args, "compact", False)`, so the `compact if compact is not None else display.get("compact")` fallback in `cli_init_mixin.py` never reached the config.

There was also no way to drop the intro or the idle `/ commands · @ files · ! shell` footer hints.

## Change

- `compact` defaults to `None` in `HermesCLI`, `cli.main` and `cmd_chat`, so `display.compact` applies when no flag is passed.
- `display.banner` (default `true`): `false` skips the startup intro (banner, welcome line, tip) on launch and on `/clear`. Warnings and advisories still print.
- `display.composer_hints` (default `true`): `false` hides the idle footer hints. Busy-state hints (`enter interrupt · tab queue · ctrl+c stop`) are kept.
- Both keys are documented in `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Salvages #47091 by @Randool: adds a Bark skill for push notifications to iOS devices,
as an **optional** skill (`optional-skills/productivity/bark/`).

The original commit is cherry-picked unchanged so authorship is preserved; follow-up
commits move it and address the review on #47091.

## Why optional-skills

Bark is iOS-only. Per CONTRIBUTING (bundled skills should be broadly useful) and
`skills/AGENTS.md` (niche skills go to `optional-skills/`), it is installable via
`hermes skills install official/productivity/bark` instead of loading for everyone.

## Changes vs #47091

- Removed the end-to-end encryption claim (no tested path existed).
- Added `scripts/bark_push.py` (stdlib only): JSON POST, correct UTF-8 handling,
  `--dry-run`, non-zero exit on rejected pushes, device key never printed.
- `BARK_TOKEN` is the only env var (secret) and is read from the environment only —
  there is no command-line flag for it, so the key cannot land in shell history, a
  process list or a tool transcript.
- The server URL is skill config (`metadata.hermes.config` → `skills.config.bark.server`),
  not an env var; `BARK_SERVER` is not read anywhere.
- Withdrawal (`--id <id> --delete`) sends only `id` and `delete`, as Bark's parameter
  documentation requires; it no longer demands a body.
- Read timeouts, `OSError` and `http.client.HTTPException` are reported as a redacted
  `BarkError` instead of a traceback.
- Added `tests/skills/test_bark_skill.py` (31 hermetic tests, no network), including
  coverage that the device key never reaches stdout or stderr on any error path.
- Generated docs entries required by the skill docs contract.
- Mapped the original commit's author email in `contributors/emails/` so the
  attribution check passes for the cherry-picked commit.

## How to test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_bark_skill.py -q
  → 1 file, 31 tests passed, 0 failed

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_skill_docs_contract.py tests/skills/test_authoring_standards.py -q
  → 2 files, 1492 tests passed, 0 failed

scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills -q
  → 34 files, 1782 tests passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (windows-only lane)

python scripts/check
  → scripts/check: 12 checks, ok

python website/scripts/check_doc_links.py
  → OK: no route-style links in hand-authored docs.

python3 optional-skills/productivity/bark/scripts/bark_push.py \
  --title "Hermes" --body "报告完成：3 个测试失败 & 2 个跳过/共 5 个" --dry-run
  → {"title": "Hermes", "body": "报告完成：3 个测试失败 & 2 个跳过/共 5 个"}

python3 optional-skills/productivity/bark/scripts/bark_push.py \
  --id build-42 --delete --dry-run
  → {"id": "build-42", "delete": "1"}
```

Manually verified delivery and withdrawal on a physical iPhone: a push returned
`{"code":200,"message":"success"}` and appeared on the device; sending the same `id`
with `--delete` returned 200 and removed the notification (Bark delivers the deletion
as a silent push, so Background App Refresh must be enabled).

Supersedes #47091.

prs.title: - Title: docs(gateway): correct lid-closed guidance for macOS gateway hosts
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The "Keeping the host awake" section of the multi-profile gateways guide ends with a warning that `caffeinate` can't override lid-close sleep. It sends MacBook users to their Energy Saver / Battery preferences instead. Both halves are backwards:

- **On AC power, `caffeinate -s` keeps a lid-closed MacBook awake.** The section's own `caffeinate -dis` examples already include it. I tested it: lid closed for 3 minutes on AC with `caffeinate -s`, no sleep, and the gateway kept answering throughout.
- **Idle-sleep settings don't.** With only `caffeinate -i`, `pmset sleep 0` and a keep-awake app's idle session active, closing the lid logged `Clamshell Sleep … Using AC` within about 5 seconds, and the gateway went offline. This is the symptom in #21697. Apple's IOKit documentation says the same for the assertion `caffeinate -d` creates: the system may still sleep on lid close.

This PR rewrites the warning to cover:
- what does block lid-close sleep: `caffeinate -s` on AC, `pmset -a disablesleep` on battery too, and closed-display mode;
- the trade-offs of each;
- how to check the current state.

## Related Issue

Refs #21697. This is docs only; it doesn't change gateway behavior.

## Type of Change

- [x] 📝 Documentation update

## Changes Made

prs.title: feat(desktop): show fallback route health status

## Product value
Fallback status is most valuable during an incident, not after it. This change publishes sanitized route-health transitions as they happen—primary to fallback, fallback switching, cooldown/exhaustion, and recovery—so operators can diagnose degraded connectivity without guessing or exposing secrets. It reduces time spent correlating logs with UI state while preserving multi-session safety and existing gateway semantics.

## Summary
- Expose the active fallback route in sanitized gateway runtime status.
- Publish route-health transitions through an optional, nonblocking callback with duplicate coalescing.
- Show the ordered primary/fallback chain, active route, cooldown retry time, and failure reason in the Desktop gateway panel.
- Preserve `fallback_status`, `multiplex_standalone_reason`, exit reasons, stopped-gateway semantics, and cross-platform behavior.
- Omit ambiguous route state when multiple sessions are active because the gateway menu has no session selector.

## Safety and limits
- No credentials, API keys, headers, base URLs, or raw exception payloads are included in the status projection.
- Callback failures do not block completion or bring down the agent.
- This improves diagnosis of route state; it does not change provider selection policy.

## Test plan

- Broader focused suite: 157 passed; 1 unrelated Windows POSIX `ps` fallback test failed because the environment is Windows.
- Python compilation, diff check, conflict scan, and targeted secret scan passed.
- Desktop tests were not run because `apps/desktop/node_modules` is absent; no packages were installed.

prs.title: fix(cli): honor no-restore-cwd during session resume
prs.body:
## Summary

Honor `--no-restore-cwd` throughout classic CLI session resume, including
both early history preload and late history loading before agent initialization.

## Reproduction

Create a session whose recorded working directory is A, then resume it
with `--resume <session_id> --in B --no-restore-cwd`.

Before this fix, Hermes entered B during argument handling, but early or
late session-history loading called `_restore_session_cwd()` and moved the
process cwd—and `TERMINAL_CWD`—back to A. The root cause was that the
launch option was not propagated to the classic CLI's session restorer.

## Fix

Pass `no_restore_cwd` through `cmd_chat`, `cli.main`, and `HermesCLI`, and
check it where session cwd restoration is decided. With the option set,
neither the process cwd nor `TERMINAL_CWD` is restored from the session.
Without it, recorded-cwd restoration remains enabled; a stale
`TERMINAL_CWD` is synchronized when the process is already in that cwd.

## Tests

Regression tests use a real temporary SQLite session with cwd A and
verify both early and late loading from B. They also cover option
propagation and the inverse behavior without the option.

79 relevant Hermes tests pass; `git diff --check` passes. No model call
is required.

prs.title: feat: usage-window plan support
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds client support for subscriptions whose included usage is tracked as allowances (for example today, this week, this month, and a separate allowance for large models) instead of a credit balance. Hermes only displays what the server sends: allowance names, percent used, reset times and model labels all come from the server, so Hermes contains no plan logic. Accounts on any other plan, and any other provider, see no change.

## What changes for usage-window plans

**Usage**
- `/usage` (CLI, TUI and messaging) shows one bar per allowance with percent used and time to reset.
- Desktop Settings → Billing shows the same allowances as gauges, plus a "Keep going on credits" setting that controls whether top-up credits are used once an allowance runs out.
- Notices warn when an allowance is close to its limit and when it has run out.

**Model pickers (CLI, TUI, Desktop and messaging platforms)**
- Recommended models for the plan are listed first.
- Models are tagged **Large** (uses more of the allowance per message) or **Free**.
- When an allowance is used up, the picker says so once and shows when it resets. Models it blocks are dimmed where the platform supports it.
- Choosing a Large model shows a one-time notice that it uses more of the plan's usage.

**At a limit**
- The refusal message says which allowance ran out, when it resets, and what can still be used.
- Hermes never switches models on its own. The fallback chain is not used for a usage-window limit; the user picks a model or waits for the reset.
- Platforms that already have buttons offer a one-tap switch to an available model.
- Messaging platforms point to the Portal instead of `/topup`.
- With a credential pool, only the refused model is benched until the reset, not the whole credential.

## Compatibility

- Without a window plan, every code path is the same as before.
- Usage-window response headers and refusal codes are honoured only on Nous routes, so another upstream can't trigger this UI.
- Additive only: no existing config, API or CLI behaviour is removed.

## Tests

New and updated tests cover header parsing, notice policy, the error classifier and recovery path, credential pool benching, picker ordering and labels, `/usage` rendering, gateway limit offers, TUI usage and limit lines, and the Desktop billing view.

prs.title: fix(approval): pass request_id to pre_approval_request on the gateway path
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On the gateway approval path, `pre_approval_request` observers receive the prompt payload but not the `request_id` that the gateway notification carries. `_ApprovalEntry.__init__` always sets `data["request_id"]` (`tools/approval_gateway_wait.py`), and `notify_cb(dict(entry.data))` sends it to the client. The hook gets `**payload`, which is built separately and has no id. A plugin observing approvals therefore can't correlate the hook with the card the client shows, and can't answer it through `approval.respond`, which takes the request id.

This passes `request_id=entry.data["request_id"]` to `pre_approval_request` on the direct path, and the leader's id on the coalesced-follower path (`coalesced=True`), so followers can be correlated with the prompt they're waiting on. `payload` has fixed keys and never contains `request_id`, so there's no duplicate-keyword risk.

The classic-CLI path answers inline and has no request id. The CLI/gateway parity test (#131876) now drops `request_id` in `_capture_hooks`, the same way it already drops `turn_id`, `tool_call_id` and `session_id`.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. I searched open and merged PRs and issues for `pre_approval_request request_id` and found nothing.

## Type of Change

## Changes Made

- `tools/approval_gateway_wait.py`: pass `request_id` to `pre_approval_request` in `_await_gateway_decision`, and the leader's id in `_await_coalesced_leader`.

prs.title: fix(picker): fold ollama's :cloud tag so a pinned pick can't twin its catalog row
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Ollama lists model ids **bare** in `/v1/models`, but accepts the same model's **`:cloud` tag form** interchangeably on completions — one upstream model, two spellings.

A pick pinned to the `:cloud` spelling therefore matched no catalog row. The picker rendered that model **twice**: once as the discovered bare entry, and once as a synthetic twin of the pick injected by the backend. The twin carried the current-model checkmark, so the user saw the same model listed twice with the marker on the copy that was not really in the catalog.

This PR folds the two spellings onto one model, so the picker lists it **once** — and still marks it as the current model.

## Related Issue

No issue. The duplicate row was reported on the model picker for an Ollama Cloud (`ollama-cloud`) provider, whose `https://ollama.com/v1/models` endpoint lists ids bare while the configured pick used the `:cloud` tag form.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/model_switch_providers.py` — `same_ollama_model()` decides when two ids name the same ollama model, and `_finalize_picker_rows()` no longer injects the `:cloud` pick into a row that already lists the bare equivalent.
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-options.ts` — new `currentCatalogId()` (which catalog id does this pick name?) and `sameSessionModel()` (does the live session still name the row's model?), both provider-scoped to the ollama slugs.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.tsx` — the visible checkmark, the keyboard highlight, and the always-include-the-active-model pin all resolve the current row through `currentCatalogId()`.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/use-model-menu-controller.ts` — the live-session guard that decides whether an effort edit still targets the running model folds the same way.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_picker_ollama_cloud_tag.py`, `apps/desktop/src/lib/model-options.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.test.tsx` — regression coverage.

### Why one helper

The desktop had three separate answers to "which row is the current model?", and the fix for the duplicate row had reached only the one that built the rows. The other two still compared ids exactly, so folding the tag there was what actually restores the checkmark. Routing all of them through one helper keeps them from diverging again.

### Semantics

- **Provider-scoped.** Only the `ollama` and `ollama-cloud` slugs fold. OpenRouter-style `:suffix` ids name distinct models and never fold, and neither does Ollama's real hyphenated `-cloud` tag (`qwen3-coder:480b-cloud`) — only a trailing `:cloud` folds.
- **Exact match wins.** An exact catalog id always wins over a folded one.
- **The fold bridges an omission.** The fold applies only when the pick's *own* spelling is absent from the catalog, so a catalog that lists both spellings marks only the row the pick names literally.
- **Canonical ids are preserved.** The result is always the catalog's own id, so visibility and favorite keys keep addressing the model they always did, and the pick itself is never rewritten.
- **Absent ids are not a model.** Two empty ids do not name the same model, so an empty pick matches nothing.

## How to Test

1. Pin an Ollama Cloud model using its `:cloud` tag form (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud`); the catalog lists it bare (`deepseek-v4.1-flash`).
2. Open the model picker: the model is listed **once**, and that row carries the current-model checkmark.
3. The row shows the live effort/fast/tier of the running model, and editing effort on it reaches the session.

Automated:

- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_picker_ollama_cloud_tag.py tests/hermes_cli/test_list_picker_providers.py -q` — 14 passed.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/model-options.test.ts src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.test.tsx --project ui` — 70 passed.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `python scripts/check --commit HEAD` — 12 checks, ok.

The desktop regression test renders the picker with a `:cloud` pick over a bare catalog row and asserts exactly one row renders, that it carries the checkmark, and that a row the pick does not name carries none.

## Checklist

## Related work

Two open PRs touch the same area from the other direction — #52613 (`fix(ollama): preserve cloud model suffixes in picker`) and #59819 (`fix(ollama-cloud): preserve :cloud tags for local-daemon proxy in model catalog`). Both change `hermes_cli/models.py` (the catalog-merge seam). prs.title: fix(feishu): fall back to plain text when a post send is rejected with 99992402
prs.body:
## What

Extends `_POST_CONTENT_INVALID_RE` in `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py` to also
match Feishu's generic param-invalid code `99992402`, so a `post` message rejected with
`[99992402] field validation failed` degrades to the existing plain-text fallback
instead of exhausting the retry budget and dropping the message.

## Why

Feishu returns `99992402` for post payloads that fail server-side validation (e.g.
empty content rows, malformed post JSON) — not only for the literal "content format of
the post type is incorrect" wording the regex currently matches. Today those sends
retry 4× with exponential backoff, then fail permanently and the response is lost.
Treating the code like any other post-format rejection lets the plain-text fallback
engage and the message is delivered without formatting.

Only the numeric code is matched, not the "field validation failed" text, to keep the
fallback trigger precise.

This complements the routing-level fixes discussed in the linked issues (topic-group
reply routing, stale `thread_id` stripping): for routing-caused `99992402` the text
fallback fails identically and the error still surfaces — just without the wasted
retry loop.

## How to test

    scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_feishu_post_fallback.py -v

New regression tests cover: response-rejected post → text fallback; exception-raising
post → text fallback; `edit_message` update rejected → text fallback; both attempts
failing → original error preserved.

Manual: configure a Feishu gateway and force a post rejection (e.g. a `no_agent` cron
delivery whose content produces an invalid post payload); before the patch the send
fails after retries, after the patch it arrives as plain text.

## Platforms tested

macOS (arm64), Python 3.14.7 — targeted tests via `scripts/run_tests.sh`;
`python scripts/check` (12 checks) green. Note:
`test_feishu.py::test_download_remote_document_blocks_connect_time_rebind` fails in
this environment on unmodified `main` as well (pre-existing, unrelated to this change).

## Related issues

Related to #81398, #35576, #54498 — all `99992402` symptoms; this addresses the
post-payload rejection class only.

prs.title: fix(desktop): never badge the default branch with a PR whose head is the trunk
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Sessions on the default branch were badged with any own-repo PR whose head is the trunk. In my case a long-closed `main -> pre-v5-baseline` PR showed as `#2` on every `main` session and linked a dead PR.

The PR lookup now also asks GitHub for the repository's default branch, in the same GraphQL query (no extra round trip). Any PR whose `headRefName` equals the default branch is dropped, whether it was found by branch or recovered by number. A PR from the trunk is never "the session's PR": it would badge every trunk session, open or closed. PRs on every other branch resolve exactly as before, and the existing cross-repository guard stays.

## Related Issue

Fixes #142826

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.ts`: `prQueryFor` requests `defaultBranchRef { name }`. Response parsing moved into a new `prsFromRepository()`, which applies the existing fork guard plus the new trunk filter. Moving it out also keeps `reviewPrList` under the code-health cyclomatic-complexity target.
- `hermes_cli/web_git.py`: the same change in `_pr_query` and `review_pr_list`.
- `apps/desktop/electron/git-review-ops.test.ts`: new test, `reviewPrList never badges the default branch with a PR whose head is the trunk`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_git_trunk_pr_badge.py`: new test covering `review_pr_list` the same way.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/git-review-ops.test.ts -t "never badges"`: the test passes. With the `git-review-ops.ts` change stashed, it fails, because the closed trunk PR is returned for `main` both by branch and by number.
2. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_web_git_trunk_pr_badge.py`: the test passes. With the `web_git.py` change stashed, it fails the same way.
3. Manual: open a session on `main` in a repo that has a closed PR from `main`. The badge no longer appears; sessions on feature branches with PRs are still badged.

Full run with `scripts/run_tests.sh` on this branch (macOS 27.0.1, Python 3.14.7, 12 workers): 64,970 passed, 202 failed, 1,853 skipped. None of the failing files is touched by this PR. Rerunning the 70 failing files on unmodified `main` at `8f555f4f92` reproduces them (state.db repair tests colliding with my running gateway, worktree, update routing, local toolchain); the few that differed were flaky on isolated rerun, and the two `test_update_finish.py` real-compiler tests fail identically in this checkout with the change reverted. The new tests pass (`tests/hermes_cli/test_web_git_trunk_pr_badge.py`; `git-review-ops.test.ts` 17/17) and fail without the fix.

prs.title: test(desktop): pin the cross-backend stored-transcript probe contract
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`fetchStoredTranscriptAcrossBackends` (`#94724` no-owner recovery) had no test coverage at all — nothing pinned the behaviour the no-owner path depends on: that a miss on the ambient store is **not** proof of absence, and that the search keeps walking the registered backends.

This adds the symmetric control requested in the review of the closed #118304, plus the surrounding contract:

- an ambient hit wins and no registered backend is probed;
- an ambient 404 still probes the registered backends by id — **the routing signal survives the first probe**;
- the ambient connection id and `local` are never probed a second time;
- a backend that cannot be reached (ECONNREFUSED) does not stop the walk;
- every backend missing — or every backend unreachable — lands on the documented aggregate `null`, never on a throw;
- no connection registry installed → `null` after the single ambient read.

## Related Issue

Refs #94724 (no-owner recovery), #88540 (a 404 is only proof of deletion from the owning backend), closed #118304.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/api/sessions.test.ts`: new `fetchStoredTranscriptAcrossBackends (#94724 no-owner recovery)` describe with six cases; the shared `./client` mock now also stubs `connectionScoped` and `ambientOwnerConnectionId`, which `getLatestSessionMessages` reads before it dials.

No production code changes: the contract already holds on the current head — this PR locks it in, which is what the closed PR's review asked for ("that test should be red on this exact head and green only when the routing signal survives the first probe").

## How to Test

```sh
cd apps/desktop
npx vitest run src/api/sessions.test.ts --project ui
```

Verified locally: 19 passed (6 new). `npx eslint src/api/sessions.test.ts` clean.

prs.title: fix(gateway): label configured vs active runtime model on fallback
prs.body:
## Summary
Gateway `/status` and `/model` could report different models after fallback activation, while `/model` labeled the configured value as **Current model**. Both values are internally defensible, but the UI did not explain that they represent different layers of state. Aligns messaging surfaces with the runtime-identity direction from #54509.

## Change
- `gateway/slash_commands.py`:
  - New shared helper `_resolve_active_runtime_route(session_key)` → `(model, provider, fallback_active)` via live agent → cache → empty (same resolver for `/status` and `/model`).
  - `/model` (no-args): captures raw configured values before the override overlay; with fallback active shows `Configured primary:`, `Session override:` (if any) and `Active route (fallback):` — never calls the configured value "Current" in that state. Without fallback: behavior unchanged.
  - `/status`: detects `agent._fallback_activated` (live agent/cache) and the persisted `gateway_runtime.fallback_active` in the session DB (idle case); with fallback active shows `**Model (fallback active):**` + `**Configured primary:**`. Without fallback: unchanged.
- `tests/gateway/test_model_command_fallback_labels.py` (new, 7 tests): fallback active → distinct labels + active fallback shown; no fallback → unchanged; override present; idle-session fallback via session DB.

## Verification
- `tests/gateway/test_model_command_fallback_labels.py`: **7 passed**.

Closes #83910

prs.title: fix(gateway): persist @image: refs for unified-runtime inbound image turns
prs.body:
…on prose

Symptom: since the unified gateway runtime, image turns submitted from the Desktop app persist the vision-enrichment prose as the user row. The desktop renderer rebuilds attachment thumbnails from @image:<path> directive lines only, so after the turn is persisted (or on reload / restart) the user bubble shows the model-only description prose and the image is gone (#142500).

Root cause: _enrich_inbound_images replaces message_text with the enrichment prose before the turn runs, and _hmwa_apply_message_timestamp (building the durable user row) cleans that already-replaced text — the enrichment rides straight into the store. The tui_gateway submit path keeps the two forms apart (persist_user_message = caption + @image refs via _build_persist_message_with_image_refs); the unified inbound path lost that split.

Change: the split is restored where the enrichment happens. A text-mode image turn buffers (caption, image_paths) beside the existing native_image_paths buffer — same lifecycle: set in _enrich_inbound_images, cleared at the next inbound prepare, consumed one-shot at the persist seam. _hmwa_apply_message_timestamp consumes it and persists caption + @image:<path> directives (after the same timestamp/note cleaning the plain path applies); the queued follow-up path in run_turn.py goes through the same swap via _durable_turn_persist_text, keeping that file under its FILE_LINES ratchet. The enrichment keeps riding the model-facing text. Also fixes a latent missing import this exposed: tui_gateway/session_history.py used Path in two module-level builders without importing it — _build_persist_message_with_image_refs NameError'd in any process that called it directly, silently swallowed by the timestamp path's broad except.

Measurements: three new contract tests — an enriched turn persists caption + @image refs while the model text keeps the prose; a plain turn's persist is unchanged; a stale buffer is cleared by the next inbound prepare so a dead turn cannot leak its caption into the next turn's row. All three red on main (no buffer machinery). Six-file seam surface (the new tests, the discord-note contract, session-history canonical, local session recovery, two tui lease/heartbeat suites): 22 passed, 0 failed. python scripts/check --base upstream/main: 12 checks ok.

Fixes #142500

## What does this PR do?

Restores the persist split the tui_gateway submit path always had: unified-runtime inbound
image turns now persist `<caption> + @image:<path>` refs (what the Desktop renders back as
thumbnails) instead of the vision-enrichment prose.

Implementation, tests, and verification by @potoior on their fork branch — a handoff from
#142500, since their account is at the repo's open-PR ceiling. Root-cause analysis and the
regression window are documented in the issue.

## Related Issue

Fixes #142500

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_inbound.py` — `_enrich_inbound_images` buffers `(caption, image_paths)` beside the existing `native_image_paths` buffer (set at enrichment, cleared at the next inbound prepare, consumed one-shot at the persist seam)
- `gateway/run_turn_prepare.py` — `_hmwa_apply_message_timestamp` consumes the buffer and persists `caption + @image:<path>` directives after the same timestamp/Discord-note cleaning the plain path applies
- `gateway/run_turn.py` — queued follow-up path swaps via `_durable_turn_persist_text` (keeps the file under its FILE_LINES ratchet)
- `tui_gateway/session_history.py` — adds a missing `Path` import (latent NameError in `_build_persist_message_with_image_refs`, silently swallowed by the timestamp path's broad `except`)
- `tests/gateway/test_vision_enrichment_persist.py` — 3 new contract tests (all red on `main`)

## How to Test

1. Run the Desktop app with a model whose image input routing resolves to text mode, paste a screenshot, add a caption, send.
2. Reload the session / restart the app: the user bubble renders the thumbnail; the persisted row in the message store is `caption` + trailing `@image:<path>` directive lines (not the enrichment prose).
3. `pytest tests/gateway/test_vision_enrichment_persist.py` — 3 passed (red on `main` without this change).

prs.title: fix(sessions): heal bare custom provider before persisting the route
prs.body:
## Problem

`custom` is the billing class every named custom endpoint reports, not a routable identity. Once a session row stores it, the next turn/resume calls `resolve_runtime_provider("custom")`, finds no endpoint or API key, and fails:

```
provider 'custom' resolved without credentials (no endpoint or API key configured)
```

Reproducible whenever two or more `custom_providers` entries share one `base_url` (a relay serving several model families under one endpoint). Three gaps made it durable:

1. `canonical_custom_identity` matched the endpoint first and returned the first configured entry, so a session on the second entry healed to the wrong sibling (or not at all).
2. `SessionDB.update_session_model` persisted whatever provider it was handed.
3. The gateway's model-switch writer passed `result.target_provider` through untouched, while the CLI path already healed it (`_heal_bare_custom_provider`).

## Fix

- `runtime_provider_custom`: add `find_custom_provider_identity_for(base_url, model)` and prefer it in `canonical_custom_identity` when a model is known; endpoint-only matching remains the fallback.
- `hermes_state_sessions.update_session_model`: refuse to persist a bare `custom`; when no name can be recovered the stored route is kept untouched.
- `gateway/slash_commands_model._record_model_switch`: heal the name from `(base_url, new_model)` before writing the route.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_bare_custom_provider_route.py`: 6 cases covering endpoint ambiguity, model disambiguation, canonical preferring the pair, the state-layer refusal, and recovered-name persistence.

The local install has no pytest, so the assertions were exercised with an equivalent monkeypatch shim (6/6 pass) rather than pytest itself.

prs.title: MCP tools with a root union input schema load and show their arguments
prs.body:
MCP tools whose input schema is a root-level union now load and show the model their real arguments, instead of failing the whole server or showing an empty argument list.

## What was broken

Servers that build a tool schema from a zod `z.union` / `z.discriminatedUnion` (or hand-written `anyOf` roots) put every argument inside root `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf` branches. Two failures, depending on whether the server also wrote `"type": "object"`:

| Server sends | `origin/main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `{"anyOf": [...]}` (no `type`) | MCP SDK rejects the **whole** `tools/list` page → `registered 0 tool(s) from 0 server(s) (1 failed: records (1 validation error for ListToolsResult …))`. Every tool on that server is gone. | Page re-read below the SDK's result validation, `"type": "object"` filled in → `registered 1 tool(s) from 1 server(s)` |
| `{"type": "object", "anyOf": [...]}` | Loads, but the strip of root combinators (strict backends reject them) leaves `properties: {}`. The model's first call is `{}` and fails. | Branch arguments lifted into one flat list; `action` becomes an enum; first call correct |

## Changes

- `tools/mcp_tool_schema.py::list_tools_repairing_schemas(session)` wraps `session.list_tools`: on a pydantic `ValidationError` it re-reads the page through the session's dispatcher (`send_request` validates every `tools/list` result against the protocol surface before returning), fills a missing/`null` `type` on `inputSchema`/`outputSchema`, validates, and applies the SDK's `_absorb_tool_listing` so output-schema bookkeeping stays intact. `functools.wraps` keeps the SDK signature visible to the pagination calling-convention probe. Used by initial discovery, `list_changed` refresh, and the `list_tools` keepalive (so a server like this does not flap on keepalive either). mcp is pinned at 2.3.0; if the private hooks are absent the original error stands.
- `tools/schema_sanitizer.py::lift_root_union_properties` runs before the existing root-combinator strip, for every tool (MCP and plugin): branch properties join the root; differing schemas for one name become an `anyOf` (same-typed consts collapse to an `enum`); a name is required only if every `anyOf`/`oneOf` branch requires it, or any `allOf` branch does; constraint-only branches (`{"required": [...]}` with no properties) are left alone. When union branches need different argument sets, one line is appended to the description: `Argument sets (provide one): action="get", id | action="search", query`.
- `unrename_tool_args` lifts the registry schema the same way, so a sanitized key inside a branch (`"a b"` → `a_b`) still maps back at dispatch.
- Docs: new "Tools with union input schemas" section in the MCP guide.

## Validation

**Live repro (real `hermes chat -q`, xAI `grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning`, real stdio MCP server with a zod-style discriminated union, `state.db` read back):**

| Leg | Tools registered | Server-side call log | Final answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, bare union | 0 (ListToolsResult validation error) | no calls | "The owner of record R-42 could not be found." |
| PR, bare union | 1 (`filled the missing "type": "object" on records.inputSchema`) | `{"action":"get","id":"R-42"}` ok | `ops` |
| main, typed union | 1 | `{}` → error, then `{"action":"get","id":"R-42"}` | `ops` (after a failed call) |
| PR, typed union | 1 | `{"action":"get","id":"R-42"}` ok, first try | `ops` |

`tool_describe` output read back from each session's `state.db`:
- main: `"parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}, "required": []}`
- PR: `"properties": {"action": {"type": "string", "enum": ["get", "search"]}, "id": …, "query": …, "limit": …}, "required": ["action"]` plus the argument-sets line

**Tests:** `tests/tools/test_mcp_root_union_schema.py`, two invariants, both red on `origin/main`:
1. A real stdio server (spawned subprocess, real `ClientSession`) with a bare root union lists every tool, and the model-visible schema has the lifted arguments, enum discriminator, intersection-required and the description line.
2. `allOf` required-union, `oneOf` required-intersection, constraint-only branches untouched, and dispatch-time key unrenaming through a lifted branch.

All 111 `tests/tools/test_mcp*` / schema test files: 1013 passed, 0 failed (includes `test_mcp_list_pagination.py`, whose 1.x `cursor=` convention case drove the `functools.wraps` design).

## Scope notes

- Open Bedrock PRs (#139090, #139101, #19739) strip root combinators on the Converse path; they are about a provider wire, not about losing the arguments, and are not touched here.
- Scouted port: a competitor's changelog shipped "MCP tools with union inputs now work instead of failing" this week; this is the hermes equivalent, covering both the load failure and the empty-arguments failure.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf5865/O0OGIcN9nTsWVb7n2lHeO_nZjzojyC.png)

prs.title: feat(local-models): local engine registry — pick, add, edit and test engine binaries
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a **Local engine registry** to Settings → Providers → Local Models.

Today the local runtime can only use the pm-provided, "managed" llama.cpp build. Users who run their own llama.cpp (a HIP/Vulkan build that pm does not ship, a pinned newer `bXXXX`, a distro package) have no supported way to point Hermes at it. This PR adds:

1. A native combobox (`Select`, `role="combobox"`) under **"Local engine"** that lists every registered engine and switches the active one.
2. Full **CRUD for custom engines**: add, edit, remove — with binary path selection, launch **args** and **env** per engine.
3. A **probe** endpoint that runs `<binary> --version` so a binary can be validated *before* it is registered (accepts a raw path or a stored engine id), and surfaces the version string in the UI.

The built-in `managed` entry stays the non-editable fallback (backend refuses mutations on it), so a broken custom engine can never leave a user without a working local runtime path. Mutations take the existing config mutation lock and bounce the local runtime cleanly; `bootstrap`/`supervisor` resolve the active engine through the registry, and the existing `local_runtime.backend` choice (auto/cpu/cuda/…) flows from the selected engine.

## Related Issue

No existing issue for this; closest related pain points: #123795 (runtime ignores `local_runtime.backend`), #123677 (managed HIP build silently CPU) — both stem from having no way to manage engine binaries. Duplicate-checked against open and merged PRs.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/local_runtime/engines.py` (new) — config-backed engine registry: list/add/update/delete/select/probe, validation (unique name, absolute existing path, `KEY=value` env lines), built-in `managed` entry, active-engine resolution.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/local_models.py` — `GET/POST /api/local-models/engines`, `PUT/DELETE /api/local-models/engines/{id}`, `POST .../engines/select`, `POST .../engines/probe` (raw `path` or `engine_id`; never registers implicitly).
- `hermes_cli/local_runtime/bootstrap.py`, `supervisor.py` — resolve the active engine, pass its args/env to the spawned server.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/local-models-engine-section.tsx` (new) — engine combobox + management list (add/edit/remove/test), missing-binary warning, extracted `EngineForm` component; i18n keys for all shipped languages (engine strings also translated in ja/zh; remaining gaps recorded via the standard `overlay-gaps.json` ratchet). The `localModels` i18n type lives in a topical sibling `types_local_models.ts`.
- `apps/desktop/src/api/local-models.ts`, `src/types/hermes.ts` — client functions and `LocalEngine` type.
- Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_local_models_routes.py` (CRUD, builtin protection, select + bounce, probe incl. an unsaved path, status surfacing), `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/local-models-engine-section.test.tsx` (new).

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_local_models_routes.py -q` → 33 passed.
2. `cd apps/desktop && vitest run src/app/settings` → all pass, and `vitest run src/i18n` (completeness ratchets) → all pass.
3. Launch the desktop app → Settings → Providers → Local Models: the "Local engine" combobox lists the managed engine; **Add engine** → pick any llama.cpp binary → **Test** shows its `--version` → save → it becomes selectable, launch args/env apply on runtime restart; managed engine shows no edit/delete.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this feature
- [x] Targeted pytest suites pass (`test_local_models_routes.py` 35/35). Full `pytest tests/ -q` on Windows 11 has pre-existing environment failures (`import pwd`, Linux-only tests, symlink privileges) that reproduce identically on the pristine base commit — unrelated to this change.
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (26300)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] N/A — feature is documented in-UI; `docs/` does not cover `local_runtime` internals
- [x] N/A — `cli-config.yaml.example` does not carry `local_runtime` keys (pm-managed section)
- [x] N/A — no architecture/workflow change

### Live backend status after engine edits (added commit)

The desktop's bottom-left backend indicator (and every other readiness
surface) repaints only when a `setup.ready` event lands. Engine edits used
to bounce the local runtime silently, so an open client kept painting the
previous engine's verdict until the next ambient tick. `_restart_for_engines()`
now re-broadcasts `setup.ready` with `{reason: "engine_mutation",
runtime_restarted: bool}` — same event the readiness refresh already
consumes, no new protocol — and two tests pin the contract, including the
failed-bounce case surfacing as `runtime_restarted: false` instead of a
stale green dot.

prs.title: fix(memory): keep built-in memory store alive under --ignore-rules
prs.body:
## Summary

Hardening PR: `--ignore-rules` (and `--safe-mode`, which sets `HERMES_IGNORE_RULES=1`) must not disable the **built-in memory store** (MEMORY.md / USER.md). Durable user memory is *state*, not an injected rule — only context rule files (AGENTS.md / SOUL.md / .cursorrules) are the "rules" that `--ignore-rules` is documented to skip.

## Root Cause

`hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py` passed `skip_memory=self.ignore_rules` to `AIAgent(...)`:

```python
skip_context_files=self.ignore_rules,
skip_memory=self.ignore_rules,
```

In `agent/agent_init.py` the built-in store creation is gated by `if not skip_memory or _memory_toolset_requested:` and the external provider block by `if not skip_memory:`. So with `--ignore-rules` / `--safe-mode` active, the user's durable MEMORY.md / USER.md state was silently dropped from the session — while the external memory provider (when configured) keeps operating, contradicting the documented "additive, never replacing" memory contract.

Commit `596dda907` (#65429) already established the intended semantics: *"skip_memory=True was meant to skip the external memory *provider* for flush/background agents, but it also suppressed creation of the built-in file-backed MemoryStore."* The CLI binding to `ignore_rules` regressed that intent for interactive chat.

## Change

- `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py`: keep `skip_memory=False` under `--ignore-rules` — memory is never skipped by the rules-isolation flag. `skip_context_files=self.ignore_rules` still skips AGENTS.md / SOUL.md / .cursorrules.
- `cli.py`: updated the `ignore_rules` doc comment to match the new behavior.
- `tests/agent/test_skip_memory_store_65429.py`: regression coverage —
  - `--ignore-rules` combo (`skip_context_files=True` + `skip_memory=False`) with `memory_enabled=True`/`user_profile_enabled=True` → built-in store **created**;
  - same combo with memory disabled in config → store stays `None` (behavior preserved; `--ignore-rules` must not *enable* memory the user disabled).

## Verification

- `pytest tests/agent/test_skip_memory_store_65429.py -q` → **4 passed** (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_ignore_user_config_flags.py tests/hermes_cli/test_safe_mode.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_startup_model_cost_guard.py -q` → **17 passed**
- `ruff check hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py cli.py tests/agent/test_skip_memory_store_65429.py` → clean
- `git diff --check` → clean

## Note

This is a **separate hardening fix**, discovered during investigation of #85622 — it is **not** the root cause of that issue (the reporter confirmed a clean environment), so this PR does **not** close #85622; that investigation continues with the reporter.

Related open work: #72075 / #51797 / #73005 / #59402 thread `--ignore-rules` into the one-shot path with `skip_memory=True`; those PRs treat persistent memory as an injected rule, which this hardening PR argues against. If merged, the one-shot path should follow the same memory-is-state principle.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Updated `--ignore-rules` behavior so it skips only context rule files.
  * Persistent memory, including built-in memory, remains available when rules are ignored.
  * Memory operations now work consistently while external memory providers remain appropriately skipped.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified that `--ignore-rules` does not disable persistent memory.

prs.title: fix(agent): end the turn when a model keeps sending non-object tool arguments
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Caps how long a turn can spend on a model that keeps sending tool arguments that aren't a JSON object. Today there are two unbounded loops:

1. **Valid JSON that isn't an object** (`[1, 2]`, `42`, `"x"`) passes `validate_tool_calls`. The executor answers `{"error": "Invalid tool arguments"}` (the message in the issue), and the loop re-requests with no limit.
2. **Closed but undecodable JSON** (`{'q': 'x'}`, `{"q": "x",}`) goes through 3 silent retries, then error results, then `_invalid_json_retries = 0`, and repeats. Args that *don't* end in `}`/`]` (the issue's literal `"{not json"`) already stop on the first call via truncation detection.

Changes:

- `agent/turn_tool_validation.py`: non-object JSON now takes the same retry-then-error-results path as undecodable JSON. The "truncated" check still keys only on real decode errors. A per-turn `_malformed_args_recoveries` counter caps recovery rounds at **2** (9 model responses in total, versus about 500 today); the next failure ends the turn via `_partial_exit(..., "malformed_tool_call", retryable=False)`. Any round whose arguments all validate resets the counter.
- `agent/turn_failure_copy.py`: adds the `malformed_tool_call` site code and chat copy (names the model, points to `/model`).
- `agent/error_surface.py`: provider layer (switching model is the fix), non-retryable.
- `agent/turn_context.py`: adds the counter to the per-turn reset.

## How this differs from #125389

That PR counts rounds in `turn_tool_round` *after* validation. Undecodable-but-closed arguments return `"continue"` from `validate_tool_calls` before that code runs, so they're never counted. Probe against its head, with 60 bad responses mocked:

| arguments | #125389 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `{'query': 'x'}` | 61 calls, no stop (`failure_reason=unknown`) | 9 calls, `malformed_tool_call` |
| `{"query": "x",}` | 61 calls, no stop | 9 calls, `malformed_tool_call` |
| `[1, 2]` / `42` | 3 calls, `malformed_tool_call` | 9 calls, `malformed_tool_call` |

Also, `site_copy("malformed_tool_call")` there is called without fields, and `site_copy` defaults missing fields to `""`, so its `{model}` / `{attempts}` placeholders render blank (" tried to call a tool  times in a row"). This PR passes `model=agent.model`.

## Related Issue

Fixes #125368

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/agent/test_run_agent.py -k "malformed_tool_arguments or valid_tool_round_resets"`: 7 pass. On `main`, the 5 parametrized "ends the turn" cases loop until the mocked responses run out, and the 2 recovery/reset cases pass both ways, so normal recovery is unchanged.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent tests/cron/test_cron_failure_notice_copy.py tests/gateway/test_api_server.py`: 10043 passed, 3 failed. The 3 (`test_compaction_prompt_rebuild.py::TestWorkspaceSnapshotPinnedAcrossCompaction`) fail identically on unmodified `main` on macOS.
3. The existing site-code tests (`test_site_failure_codes_never_collapse_to_unknown`, copy/table consistency) cover the new code.

## Checklist

- [x] Read CONTRIBUTING; Conventional Commits; only related changes; tests added
- [x] Searched existing PRs: #125389 targets the same issue; see the comparison above
- [x] Tested on macOS (Darwin 25.5)
- [x] Cross-platform: N/A (pure loop logic)
- [x] Docs/config/schemas: N/A (no new config key; the cap is a constant like the existing 3-strike invalid-name exit)

prs.title: fix(state): store identical reasoning/reasoning_content once
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Reasoning-content providers (DeepSeek, Kimi, …) return the same chain-of-thought as both `reasoning` and `reasoning_content`, and `_message_row_params` wrote it into both columns, so every reasoning token was stored twice. The issue measured ~283 MB on a 2.35 GB profile.

`reasoning` is built from `reasoning_content` in `extract_reasoning`, so when the two are byte-identical this stores the text once: `reasoning` is written as a short NUL-prefixed marker (`_SHARED_REASONING`), and both read paths (`_rows_to_conversation` and `_row_to_message_dict`) swap it back for `reasoning_content`. A NULL couldn't mark this, since turns that carry `reasoning_content` alone also store NULL. Callers get exactly the same message dicts as before.

Two cases are deliberately excluded:
- **Blank pads.** The thinking-mode tool-call pad writes `reasoning_content=" "` with no `reasoning`. Only non-blank text is deduplicated, so a pad never gains a `reasoning` field on read and `apply_reasoning_content_policy` behaves as before.
- **Differing text.** For example `reasoning` also includes a `reasoning_details` summary. Both columns are kept as-is.

Existing rows are left alone. They still hold both copies and read back the same. This PR stops the growth but doesn't reclaim space already used. A backfill (`UPDATE … SET reasoning = <marker> WHERE reasoning = reasoning_content AND TRIM(reasoning_content) <> ''` followed by VACUUM) seemed better as a separate maintenance change if you want one.

## Related Issue

Fixes #125273

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_state_messages.py`: added `_SHARED_REASONING`, `_reasoning_is_shared`, and `_restore_shared_reasoning`; the write side replaces the duplicate with the marker and both read paths restore it.
- `tests/hermes_state/test_reasoning_roundtrip.py`: added `TestSharedReasoningStoredOnce`, covering storage, both read paths, differing text, reasoning-only, reasoning_content-only, the blank pad, rows written before this change, and fork.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state/test_reasoning_roundtrip.py`: 14 pass. Without the source change, `test_identical_text_is_stored_once` and `test_fork_keeps_one_copy` fail and the round-trip tests pass either way, which shows the change only affects what's on disk.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state` plus every test file under `tests/agent`, `tests/gateway`, `tests/hermes_cli`, `tests/tui_gateway`, `tests/acp_adapter` that mentions reasoning: 1331 passed. The 62 failures (repair / auto-vacuum / FTS rebuild / cross-VM mount detection) fail identically on unmodified `main` on macOS; I diffed the failure lists and they're the same.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] Conventional Commits

- [x] Only changes related to this fix
- [ ] `pytest tests/ -q` all pass: see note above; the relevant suites pass, and the remaining failures are pre-existing on macOS
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Tested on macOS (Darwin 25.5, Python via `uv sync --group dev`)

prs.title: feat(photon): per-platform stateless inbound + session wipe CLI
prs.body:
## Why Photon inbound from one chat key shares a single **persistent** session (`agent:main:photon:dm:`). Every new inbound reloads the full conversation history. On the amper deployment that history (50+ turns of "we built one-off PDFs by querying the warehouse") fights a strict `SOUL.md` shell-router contract: the agent pattern-matches a fresh inbound as a continuation of prior turns and skips the mandated `terminal(...)` router call. The gateway log showed the smoking gun — the same session key reused for every inbound: ``` chat=any;-;+177****2727 ``` ## What Add an **opt-in, per-platform** `stateless_inbound` option (default `false`). When set, the gateway forces a **fresh session for every inbound** — no prior history is loaded. A fresh session is a brand-new conversation, so it's inherently prompt-cache-safe: nothing is rebuilt mid-session and message alternation always starts clean. Every other platform / deployment is unaffected (default off). Enable per profile: ```yaml # config.yaml platforms: photon: stateless_inbound: true ``` ### Changes - **`gateway/config.py`** — bridge `stateless_inbound` from a platform's config section into `PlatformConfig.extra` via the existing shared-key loop (same path as `require_mention`), so `platforms.photon.stateless_inbound: true` (or a top-level `photon:` block) lands in `extra`. - **`gateway/run.py`** — `GatewayRunner._inbound_is_stateless()` reads the option; `_handle_message_with_agent` passes `force_new=` to `get_or_create_session()` and logs when it forces a fresh session. This is the single canonical inbound agent-invocation path where history loads. - **`plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`** — read the option for operator visibility and log it at startup (enforcement stays in the gateway, same config source — one source of truth). - **`hermes_cli/main.py`** — add `hermes session wipe --platform

--chat ` (plus a `session` alias for the `sessions` group) to clear ONE contaminated session: deletes its messages + row and drops it from the gateway session index so the next inbound starts fresh. Other sessions are untouched. - **docs** — `stateless_inbound` + enable/wipe commands in the photon README. ## Before / after gateway log **Before** — same session reused, history dragged in: ``` inbound message: platform=photon user=+17725212727 chat=any;-;+17725212727 msg='build the PBI deck' ... -> get_or_create_session reuses agent:main:photon:dm:any;-;+17725212727 -> session 20260620_095816_3a16a651 (load_transcript: 50 prior turns) inbound message: platform=photon user=+17725212727 chat=any;-;+17725212727 msg='now the other PBI' ... -> reuses SAME session 20260620_095816_3a16a651 (load_transcript: 52 prior turns) # contaminated ``` **After** (`stateless_inbound: true`) — fresh session per inbound: ``` inbound message: platform=photon user=+17725212727 chat=any;-;+17725212727 msg='build the PBI deck' ... stateless inbound: forcing fresh session (platform=photon chat=any;-;+17725212727) -> session 20260620_120001_aaaa1111 (load_transcript: 0 turns) inbound message: platform=photon user=+17725212727 chat=any;-;+17725212727 msg='now the other PBI' ... stateless inbound: forcing fresh session (platform=photon chat=any;-;+17725212727) -> session 20260620_120145_bbbb2222 (load_transcript: 0 turns) # no visibility of message 1 ``` ## Tests `tests/gateway/test_photon_stateless_inbound.py` (11 tests, all green): - **Config bridge** — `platforms.photon.stateless_inbound` and the top-level `photon:` form both reach `extra`; absent ⇒ off. - **The gate** — `_inbound_is_stateless` is true when configured, false by default, false for unconfigured platforms, and does **not** leak across platforms (photon-on does not make telegram stateless). - **End-to-end** — the same chat sends two PBI messages: they land in two different sessions and the second loads an **empty** transcript (zero visibility of the first). A **control** test pins the legacy persistent behavior (second message *does* see turn 1) — i.e. the exact contamination this flag removes. - A source-level guard pins that the inbound handler actually consults the gate, so the wiring can't silently regress. Existing `tests/gateway/test_config.py` + session auto-reset suite still pass (71 tests). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: test: make interrupted-update regression suite runnable on Windows
prs.body:
Three cases in `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_interrupted_pull.py` cannot run on Windows today, although they cover exactly the failure mode this suite exists for. The causes are in the test harness, not in the product logic they assert:

| case | Windows failure | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_killed_pull_is_restored_on_next_launch_and_update_reruns` | `error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: other.py` → `SystemExit: 1`. Windows git defaults to `core.autocrlf=true`, so fixtures written with `newline=""` are reported as local modifications and `merge --ff-only` refuses to run. | pass `-c core.autocrlf=false -c core.filemode=false` to the clone **and** persist them with `git config`, because the later `git status` / `git merge` calls in the same repo reread the repo config. |
| `test_restore_runs_the_installers_store_git_when_path_has_none` | `[WinError 193]` / `[WinError 216]` — the case writes a `#!/bin/sh` script and executes it as git; Windows `CreateProcess` will not run a file without an image header. | write an empty placeholder file and monkeypatch `update_custody.run_git`, recording calls that go to the store path and forwarding them to the real git. The assertion that the store's git is the one invoked is preserved. |
| `test_an_empty_head_answer_keeps_the_marker` | same `WinError 193` — the empty file used as a git stub cannot be executed. | patch `_custody_git` directly: the case is about git answering an empty `rev-parse HEAD`, not about spawning a binary. |

Non-Windows runs keep the original POSIX shell stubs unchanged.

### Verification

Windows 11, git 2.55.0.windows.3, Python 3.14:

```
env -u HERMES_HOME uv run --no-project --with pytest \
  pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_interrupted_pull.py -q

26 passed, 14 skipped in 92.32s
```

`HERMES_HOME` has to be unset, otherwise `tests/home_io_guard.py` aborts every test that touches a real install (10 errors, independent of this change). The 14 skips are the pre-existing platform markers (Linux inotify / `/proc` holder scan / POSIX shell stubs / symlink creation).

Targeted rerun of the three repaired cases: `3 passed, 37 deselected in 11.12s`.

prs.title: fix(tui,gateway): refresh session.info when a fallback switch or primary restore changes the route
prs.body:
## What does this PR do

Fixes part 1 of #78613. When a provider fallback activates mid-turn, the status bar keeps naming the failed primary until the turn ends. With this change it names the new model as soon as the switch happens, and it names the primary again as soon as `restore_primary_runtime` puts it back.

Seen in practice: two TUI sessions attached to the local gateway hit the Anthropic subscription limit mid-turn and fell back to Bedrock (`Fallback activated: claude-opus-5-5 → global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 (bedrock)`). Their turns ran on Bedrock for another 7 and 27 minutes, and the status bar showed `claude-opus-5-5` the whole time. The label comes from `session.info`, and the gateway sends that at turn end (`publish_settled_info`) but not when the route changes during a turn.

## Design

- `agent/route_binding.py` (+14): `notify_route_change(agent)` calls `agent.route_change_callback` if one is set. It catches and debug-logs anything the callback raises, then returns True so the caller's success result is unchanged.
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` (net 0): `try_activate_fallback` returns `notify_route_change(agent)` on its success path, after the model and provider swap.
- `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` (net 0): `restore_primary_runtime` does the same after `reinstall_primary_runtime`.
- `agent/agent_init.py` (net 0): `route_change_callback` defaults to None. Hosts install it.
- `gateway/local_viewer_events.py` (+3): `wire` installs the callback for a local-viewer turn, and `restore` puts the previous value back (it is listed in `_TURN_ATTRS`). Messaging turns never call `wire`, so they are unchanged.
- `gateway/session_local_inventory.py` (+15): `publish_route_info` publishes `session.info` through `turn._publish_execution` (generation-fenced). It builds the payload with the same helper as `publish_settled_info`, which now shares it, and it skips the one-turn `model_override` eviction because a route change is not a one-turn admission.
- `tui_gateway/agent_factory.py` (+2): `_make_agent` installs a callback that emits `session.info` for the session. The in-process path is still live (`tui_gateway/owner_forward.py` runs turns in process unless the gateway ledger holds work, and the dashboard hosts `tui_gateway.server`).

Neither of the two facade files grows, and `scripts.code_health` reports 0 findings.

Out of scope: provider qualification in the status bar (#78613 part 2), any frontend change, the compute-host bridge, and any change to fallback decisions, cooldowns or notices.

## Related

- #78613: this PR covers part 1 only.
- #78666 (closed): an earlier attempt at both parts. This PR is smaller, covers the gateway local-viewer path that attached TUI and Desktop sessions now use, and adds the restore direction.
- #73772: notifying the user when a fallback happens. This PR changes only the model label and adds no notice.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

New tests: `tests/agent/test_fallback_route_change_callback.py`, `tests/gateway/test_local_viewer_route_change.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/test_make_agent_route_change.py`.

```
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/agent/test_fallback_route_change_callback.py tests/gateway/test_local_viewer_route_change.py tests/tui_gateway/test_make_agent_route_change.py tests/gateway/test_local_viewer_events_turn.py
=== Summary: 4 files, 38 tests passed, 0 failed ===
```

The new tests fail on the base commit (55ee4acd) and pass with the change. They check the following:
- A successful switch or restore calls the callback once, and the new model is already in place when it runs.
- A failed, exhausted or deferred switch does not call it, and neither does a restore blocked by the rate-limit cooldown.
- A callback that raises leaves the switch or restore in place and its True result unchanged.
- A local-viewer turn publishes exactly one `session.info` on the new route, and `restore` puts the attribute back afterwards.
- A messaging turn installs no callback and publishes nothing.
- The in-process TUI gateway emits `session.info` for the session's sid.

For each of these checks, a copy of the code with that guard removed makes the matching test fail. Of 25 such copies, 24 were caught. The one not caught changes only the debug log level.

Existing tests: `tests/gateway/test_local_viewer_*.py`, `tests/agent/test_fallback_*.py`, `tests/agent/test_conversation_fallback_state.py`, the files that reference `restore_primary_runtime`, `try_activate_fallback` or `_TURN_ATTRS`, and the `tests/tui_gateway/` files that touch `session.info`. They give the same set of failing test IDs on main and on this branch. Two of them fail on main already: `test_run_agent.py::TestExecuteToolCalls::test_sequential_tool_calls_run_without_delay` and `tui_gateway/test_protocol.py::test_approval_for_a_ws_client_that_never_advertised_settles_the_queue_entry`.

`ruff check --config ./ruff.pre-commit.toml` passes on all 10 files, and `git diff --check` is clean.

prs.title: fix(pm): treat ffmpeg as a host gap on Windows Server 2016 (#130064)
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On Windows Server 2016 (build 14393) the pinned BtbN win32-x64 ffmpeg cannot start: it imports `SetThreadDescription` from KERNEL32, which this OS only exposes through KernelBase. Every invocation, including the install's `-version` smoke probe, dies with `0xC0000139` (STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND), so `hermes pm install` and every `hermes update` fail at the dependency step. Users end up patching `pm/lock.json` locally, and that patch then breaks the updater's checkout or gets parked by `--keep-stash`.

This PR makes `Ffmpeg.missing_reason` report a host gap when all of these are true:
- the host is Windows and the target is the host's own target,
- the lock's ffmpeg artifact for that target is a BtbN build,
- KERNEL32 does not export `SetThreadDescription` (checked with `GetProcAddress`).

With the gap reported, `tool_roots`/`source_install_packages` leave ffmpeg out of the required-tool closure, and the sync and update complete. The gap clears itself when the Windows pin is not a BtbN build. It fails open (no gap) if the lock or the probe can't be read, and it does nothing on other targets or non-Windows hosts.

## Related Issue

Fixes #130064

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pm/packages.py`: `_kernel32_missing_exports()` (GetProcAddress probe), `_win_ffmpeg_host_gap()`, and `Ffmpeg.missing_reason` override.
- `tests/pm/test_ffmpeg_windows_host_gap.py`: gap reported and closure trimmed when the export is missing; no gap when it is present; non-BtbN pin skips the probe entirely; other targets and non-Windows hosts untouched; probe failure fails open.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/pm/test_ffmpeg_windows_host_gap.py tests/pm/test_ffmpeg_resolution.py -q` (17 passed)
2. On a real Windows Server 2016 host (`Windows-2016Server-10.0.14393-SP0`) with the upstream lock:
   ```
   _kernel32_missing_exports(('SetThreadDescription',)) -> ['SetThreadDescription']
   Ffmpeg().missing_reason('win32-x64') -> "this Windows host's KERNEL32 does not export SetThreadDescription (Windows Server 2016 / build 14393); the pinned BtbN build cannot start here"
   ```
   On that host the staged BtbN `ffmpeg.exe -version` exits `3221225785` (0xC0000139).
3. `python scripts/check` passes.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (#130073 only decodes NTSTATUS in the probe error; it does not unblock the update)
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: ran `tests/pm` filtered to related areas; the only failures (`test_recovery.py::test_startup_validation_checks_real_ruamel_dependency`, `test_worker_registry.py::test_definition_import_failures_are_package_errors`) fail identically on unmodified `main` in this environment
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes

prs.title: fix(codex): collapse same-id empty-tool-call twins on streamed and non-streamed paths
prs.body:
## Observed symptom (why this exists)

A scheduled cron job (`gpt-5.6-luna` over the copilot Responses route) began failing delivery. The run would stall re-reading the same file, then stop itself with `I stopped retrying because I kept running read_file 5 times without making progress...`.

Inspecting the stored assistant `tool_calls` for that session revealed the root shape directly: **one batch carried two `tool_calls` entries with the *same call_id*** — one with the real JSON arguments, one with empty `{}`:

```
call_1Cl2K... : read_file  arguments='{"path":"memories/MEMORY.md"}'
call_1Cl2K... : read_file  arguments='{}'
```

Both were executed: the populated twin returned the file contents, the empty twin returned `Cannot read '<workdir>': not a regular file (directory, FIFO, socket, or device)` (and `terminal` → `Invalid command: expected string, got NoneType`). The empty-argument call is what the LLM kept retrying.

## Problem (root cause)

The Codex/Responses routing in Hermes has **two** independent normalization paths that turn Response output into chat-style `tool_calls`:

1. **Streamed** — `agent/codex_runtime.py::_CodexResponseAssembler` consumes SSE events and assembles `output`.
2. **Non-streamed** — `agent/codex_responses_adapter.py::_normalize_codex_response` → `_OutputScan.scan` turns `response.output` items directly into `tool_calls`.

Some Codex backends (observed at ~100% on `gpt-5.6-luna` / `gpt-5.6-sol` over the copilot Responses route; ~0% on other models/routes) emit a single logical `function_call` as **two same-id items**: one with real `arguments`, one with empty/`{}` arguments (e.g. a bare `output_item.added` before the completed `output_item.done`, or repeated `output_item.done` for one id).

Neither path collapsed those: each same-id item became its own `tool_calls` entry, so the empty twin reached the tool executor with no arguments.

The existing dedup cannot catch it: `run_agent._deduplicate_tool_calls` groups by `(tool_name, arguments)` and `{"command": …}` vs `{}` have *different* keys, so the pair survives; `uniquify_tool_call_ids` only renames duplicate ids and the SDK objects rejected the in-place edit (`Could not uniquify duplicate tool call id ...`). The empty copy was executed, not just shown.

## Fix

Deduplicate same-id `function_call` tool_calls on **both** normalization paths, preferring the one with real (non-empty, non-`{}`) arguments:

- `agent/codex_runtime.py` — added `_dedupe_output_items`, run in `result()` **after** settlement (covers the done-only and the pending-settle streams).
- `agent/codex_responses_adapter.py` — added `_dedupe_same_id_tool_calls`, applied right after `_OutputScan.scan` (covers the non-streamed `response.output` route the cron job actually uses).

`message`/`reasoning` items and genuinely-distinct call ids are untouched.

## Tests

New `tests/agent/test_codex_runtime_same_id_tool_call.py` (fails before, passes after) covers both paths:

- streamed: bare-add + done → one call with args; two same-id done frames → one call with args; distinct ids preserved; all-empty duplicates keep the first; message items untouched.
- non-streamed `_normalize_codex_response`: empty-then-full same id → one call with args; full-then-empty → same; distinct ids preserved.

All existing settle/`codex_app_server`-related suites pass. The cron job re-run after deploying the fix produced **zero** same-id empty twins across 146 tool calls (was dozens before); the only remaining "repeated id" instances across messages carry identical real arguments (not an empty twin) and are normal provider id reuse. The only unrelated failure in the agent batch is `test_auxiliary_client.py::…anthropic…` — a pre-existing dependency-gated failure (missing `anthropic` package), reproducible on `main` without this change.

releases.body:
# Hermes Agent v0.22.4

**Release Date:** October 21, 2026

> Patch release. Desktop stops showing suggestion pills above the composer, plus small plugin and dashboard fixes, for the CLI and installer, the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## Fixes

- **Desktop no longer shows suggestion pills above the composer.** The pills appeared for no clear reason, mostly nudging you to set up MCP servers. They and the helpers that only they used are gone. ([#142559](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142559))
- **Plugins that install nothing skip the dependency consent step.** A plugin that declares no dependencies, or whose `pyproject.toml` installs nothing, now enables without an empty consent prompt. ([#142569](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142569))
- **Dashboard: WhatsApp can be safely re-paired after logging out.** ([#142439](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142439))
- **Desktop plugin review:** the surface lint no longer flags prototype writes; reviewers check them by hand. ([#142586](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142586))
- **Desktop: the approval-mode chip follows the active profile's mode.** ([#142565](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142565))
- **Release builds:** the desktop bundle's pre-build check gets enough time to verify archived build inputs when storage is slow. ([#142623](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/142623))

Also new in the plugin catalog: bubblewrap (bwrap terminal backend on Linux), Singularity/Apptainer, mcp-serve (Hermes as an MCP server), agent-importers (`hermes import-agent`, now with Cursor), inbox and workflow-record from Hermes Labs. Telegram Business moves to the Hermes Labs community tier.

## About this release

Measured at commit `4d04303818b`, the window since v0.22.3 contains **14 non-merge commits** across **82 changed files** (+1,475 / −3,022) and **13 merged PRs**.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.
- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: [v0.22.3...v0.22.4](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v0.22.3...v0.22.4)
