issues.title: update-nanoclaw skill refresh: local adapters fail validation or get overwritten, no opt-out

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## What happens

The update's skill refresh thinks every channel import in
`src/channels/index.ts` came from a skill. That is not always true. Two
things break:

**Case 1: my own adapter blocks the update.**

- I have an adapter that lives in my tree. I wrote it. There is no
  `.claude/skills/add-<name>/SKILL.md` for it.
- The refresh fails with `Missing .claude/skills/add-<name>/SKILL.md`.
- One failed skill blocks the whole `validate` phase. The update stops.

**Case 2: my replacement adapter gets silently swapped back.**

- I replaced `src/channels/matrix.ts` with a native adapter (the direction
  PR #2844 explored before it was closed).
- The refresh overwrote it with the `@beeper/chat-adapter-matrix` bridge
  copy from the `channels` branch. It also re-added that dependency and its
  pnpm patch to `package.json`.
- Then `validate` committed all of it. No warning.
- Same problem for small local patches on skill-installed adapters (in my
  install, the WhatsApp voice note flag). But the silent adapter swap is
  the sharp end.

## Why it happens

At `ad8837c8`:

- `detectInstalledSkills` reads the barrel imports. Every import becomes
  `add-<name>` (`scripts/update-skills.ts:93-95`).
- No `SKILL.md` = hard error (`scripts/update-skills.ts:159`).
- A `SKILL.md` with zero directives = also a hard error
  (`scripts/update-skills.ts:163`).
- `validateUpdate` runs the refresh, throws if any skill failed, then
  commits everything the refresh wrote
  (`scripts/update/transaction.ts:308-310`).

Nothing in this chain can say "this adapter is mine, leave it alone". Copy
directives always overwrite. So a deliberate replacement looks the same as
stale skill output.

## How to see it

**Case 1:**

1. Create `src/channels/foo.ts` that self-registers.
2. Append `import './foo.js';` to `src/channels/index.ts`. Commit.
3. Run the update. `validate` fails:
   `Missing .claude/skills/add-foo/SKILL.md`.

**Case 2:**

1. Replace `src/channels/matrix.ts` with your own code. Commit.
2. Run `validate` on an install that has `add-matrix`.
3. Your file comes back as the registry copy, inside the
   `chore: refresh installed skill payloads` commit.

## Suggested fix

Give forks a supported opt-out. Two ideas:

- A frontmatter flag in `SKILL.md` (for example `refresh: local`). The
  refresher reports the skill as refreshed and touches nothing.
- For case 1: treat an import with no matching skill as "local, skipped"
  plus a warning, instead of failing.

My current workaround: a marker `SKILL.md` per local adapter, with one
idempotent `nc:append` directive (the barrel import line, already present).
It passes the checks and the refresh becomes a no-op. It works. But it is a
trick, not a contract. And the zero-directive error message ("cannot be
refreshed headlessly") reads like the goal was completeness, not banning
local adapters.

## Related, but not blocking

- #3451 fixes companion-import attribution. It keeps the missing-skill
  failure for unclaimed imports on purpose, so it does not cover case 1.
- #2844 (closed) is why a fork may carry a replaced Matrix adapter at all.

Assisted by Claude; reviewed and verified by a human before submission.

issues.title: Claude agents can't read PDFs: agent image has no pdftoppm (poppler-utils)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

main `a62a8d2f` (local image build). Earlier mains are the same: the Dockerfile has never installed poppler-utils.

### Host platform

Linux

### What happened?

A user sent a Claude agent a 60-page PDF and asked about page 47. Claude's Read tool returned an error instead of the page:

```
pdftoppm is not installed. Install poppler-utils (e.g. `brew install poppler` or `apt-get install poppler-utils`) to enable PDF page rendering.
```

(Same text when reproduced with Claude Code 2.1.296 inside a fresh main image.)

The agent then looked for `python3`, `mutool`, `gs` and `qpdf`, found none, and replied that it could not read the page. It happened in both runs:

- Run 1: "I can't read page 47 yet. This environment has no PDF renderer: `pdftoppm` is missing, and so are Python, `mutool` and `gs`…"
- Run 2: "I can't read page 47 yet. The PDF page renderer (`poppler-utils`) isn't installed…"

In the same runs Claude read every JPEG and PNG. OpenCode, on the same VM with the same PDF, answered correctly.

### What did you expect?

Claude reads the PDF and answers the question.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. Build the agent image from main: `./container/build.sh`
2. `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh nanoclaw-agent-v2-<slug>:latest -c 'command -v pdftoppm || echo missing'` prints `missing`.
3. Send a Claude agent a PDF longer than 10 pages and ask about one page.

### Cause

Claude Code's Read tool turns PDF pages into images with `pdftoppm`, from poppler-utils. `container/Dockerfile` does not install poppler-utils.

### Fix

#4174 adds `poppler-utils` to the agent image (+6.4 MB).

### NanoCo's own images

The hardened image is built by Echo, not from `container/Dockerfile`, so it may lack `pdftoppm` too. Check an image with `docker run --rm --entrypoint sh <image> -c 'command -v pdftoppm || echo missing'`. If it prints `missing`, Echo needs to add poppler-utils.

### Channel or interface

CLI / terminal

### Agent provider

Claude

issues.title: [capability] Let an agent reset its own session and resume from a handover
issues.body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Long research-style runs fill an agent's context window. Once it is full, the SDK auto-compacts, and details are lost in a way nobody controls. An agent can already watch its own context size and write a handover file before the limit, but it has no clean way to start fresh by itself:

- `/clear` only works as an inbound message from a human (`isClearCommand` in `poll-loop.ts`). The agent's own output is not treated as a command, and after `/clear` the agent stays idle until the next message.
- `ncl groups restart` needs admin approval each time and restarts the whole container.
- Transcript rotation (`maybeRotateContinuation`) runs only at a cold start and only by size or age, not on demand.

### What should be possible?

An agent can end its **own** session at a point it chooses, e.g. right after writing a handover file. The runner then starts a fresh session that automatically begins with a resume prompt ("Read HANDOVER.md and continue"), in the same conversation/thread. No human action, no approval, only the calling session is affected, and a running turn is never cut off.

### What kind of skill is this?

Container skill

### Who benefits?

Anyone running agents on long, multi-step work (research, coding, data studies) who would rather hand over deliberately than rely on auto-compaction.

### What have you tried?

A semi-manual workaround: the agent asks, a human types `/clear`, then "continue". Deleting `continuation:claude` from `outbound.db` by hand only takes effect at the next cold start, because the poll loop keeps the continuation in memory.

### What would this change?

A working implementation (with tests) is on my fork, branch [`feat/agent-session-reset`](https://github.com/carstenf/nanoclaw/tree/feat/agent-session-reset), based on current `main`. It is in core today because it needs the poll loop; happy to repackage it as a skill if you prefer that shape.

- New MCP tool `reset_session({ handover_path, reason, resume_prompt? })` (`mcp-tools/session.ts` + `session.instructions.md`). It only validates and records `pending_reset` in session_state.
- `poll-loop.ts`: ends the query (`end()`, not `abort()`) at a turn boundary once nothing is answering, queued or being pushed, then clears the continuation (same as `/clear`), archives the old transcript into `conversations/`, posts a one-line notice to the origin thread, writes `last_reset`, and starts a fresh query with the resume prompt as a system-origin message on the same reply route. A reset still pending at container start runs before resuming.
- New optional provider hook `archiveContinuation` (Claude implementation reuses `archiveClaudeTranscript`). Providers without a continuation get "not supported".
- Guardrails: handover must exist, be non-empty and at most 30 min old; at least 15 min between resets; at most 6 per 24 h; refused in task runs. Overridable via `NANOCLAW_RESET_*` env vars.

Removal: delete the tool module and its import, `session-reset.ts`, and the poll-loop/provider hunks.

One finding from live testing that may matter beyond this feature: when a follow-up is pushed into a running turn, the Claude SDK can absorb it into that turn and emit a **single** result. The poll loop then keeps a phantom entry in `queuedTurns` and stays `answering`. The implementation works around this for the reset (it also treats ~10 s of silence after a result as idle; `end()` still lets any real in-flight turn finish), but the same desync could affect other turn-boundary logic.

### How could we test it?

- `bun test --isolate src/session-reset.test.ts` (8 tests): guardrail refusals; reset only after `result`; continuation cleared and new query started without resume; notice in the same thread; transcript archived; carry-over across a container restart; phantom queued turn.
- Full agent-runner suite passes, typecheck clean.
- Live: ask the agent to write a handover and call `reset_session`. It ends its turn, the notice appears, and it answers again in the same thread from a fresh context, continuing from the handover.

### Can you help maintain it?

- [x] I can help maintain this skill.

issues.title: chat-sdk-bridge: redundant Button 'value' param corrupts Discord approval custom_id, causing silent-reject + duplicate resend

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
**Severity:** high — approval/ask_question cards on Discord are unusable; every click resolves to the wrong option.

## Summary

In \`createChatSdkBridge\`'s \`ask_question\` card builder (\`src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts\`), each option button was created with **both** \`id\` and \`value\` set to the same index:

\`\`\`ts
Button({ id: \`ncq:${questionId}:${idx}\`, label: opt.label, value: String(idx), style: opt.style })
\`\`\`

The Discord Chat SDK adapter concatenates \`id\` and \`value\` with a newline when both are set on the same button. The resulting \`custom_id\` comes back corrupted, e.g. \`"ncq:<questionId>:0\n0"\` instead of \`"ncq:<questionId>:0"\`.

\`resolveSelectedOption()\` (same file) then fails to cleanly parse the index out of the corrupted tail, so a click on **Approve** does not resolve to \`render.options[0].value\` ("approve") — it falls through to returning the raw (corrupted) candidate string. Downstream, \`resolveOneCLIApproval()\` treats anything that isn't literally \`'approve'\` as a deny, so **every approval click is silently treated as a rejection**, and depending on the response-handler's retry/resend path this can also cause the same approval card to be resent multiple times.

## Repro

1. Trigger any \`ask_question\`/approval card on a Discord-wired agent (e.g. an OneCLI credential approval).
2. Click "Approve".
3. Observe in logs (with the diagnostic warning from the linked PR, or by inspecting the raw event) that the resolved \`customId\` tail is \`"0\n0"\` rather than \`"0"\`.
4. The approval resolves as rejected; the card may resend.

## Root cause

\`Button()\`'s \`id\` alone already carries full routing info (\`questionId\` + option index — see the comment directly above the call site explaining why the index, not the full value, is encoded). The extra \`value: String(idx)\` is redundant and is what the Discord adapter concatenates onto \`id\`.

## Fix

PR: (opening — see below) removes the redundant \`value\` param, and adds two diagnostic \`log.warn\` calls (in \`chat-sdk-bridge.ts\` and \`onecli-approvals.ts\`) so a similar render-metadata mismatch shows up in logs instead of looking identical to an intentional decline.

Verified live on a real Discord-wired install: before the fix, clicking Approve produced \`customId\` \`"ncq:...:0\n0"\`; after, \`"ncq:...:0"\`, and the approval resolved correctly on the first click.

prs.title: fix(container-runner): pre-create session mount points as the host user
prs.body:
Fixes #3951.

## Problem

The session directory is bind-mounted at `/workspace`, and other mounts are nested inside it (`/workspace/agent`, `/workspace/global`, provider state volumes, allowlisted extras at `/workspace/extra/<name>`). When a nested target is missing on the host, rootful Docker creates it there **as root**.

`deleteTaskCommand` destroys the task session's mailbox, then `rmSync`s the session directory, then deletes the central `sessions` row and the run log. The `rmSync` throws `EACCES` on the root-owned stubs, so the last two steps never run. The session stays `active` with no `inbound.db`, and `collectTasks` warns about it every minute from then on.

## Change

`buildMounts` now ends with `ensureSessionMountPoints(mounts, sessDir)`. It creates every mount target whose nearest enclosing mount is `/workspace` itself inside `sessDir` before the container starts: a directory, or an empty file when the mount source is a file. That keeps the whole session tree owned by the host user. It skips:

- targets nested under another mount (e.g. `/workspace/agent/CLAUDE.md`, which lives in the group folder)
- targets outside `/workspace`
- targets that already exist
- any path that resolves outside `sessDir`

A creation failure is logged as a warning and doesn't block the spawn; Docker still creates the target as before.

## Not included

- Existing installs keep their current root-owned stubs; the host can't `chown` them itself. A one-time fix through a root container works, e.g. `find <sessions> -mindepth 3 -maxdepth 4 -user root -type d -exec chown <uid>:<gid> {} +`. That's probably a release-note item.
- Optional follow-up: have `deleteTaskCommand` delete the `sessions` row even when the directory removal fails.

## Testing

- New `src/container-runner.mount-points.test.ts`, 4 cases: directory and file targets are created; nested and non-`/workspace` targets are skipped; existing targets are left untouched; paths that escape `sessDir` are ignored.
- `pnpm run build` and the full `pnpm test` pass (2977 passed).
- On a live Linux install, 176 of 179 session directories had root-owned stubs. After a one-time `chown` they are owned by the host user, and with this patch deployed new spawns create the targets as the host user. (That install's orphaned session from the original failed delete had to be removed by hand; this patch prevents new ones, it doesn't repair old ones.)

## Summary

The agent is told when one of its messages permanently fails to deliver, instead of believing it was sent.

- **Problem**: after `MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS` the delivery loop only marks the outbound row failed in the session DB. Nothing reaches the agent, so it reports the message as sent ("sent — check the DM") while the user never sees it. Seen with a file Slack rejected with `missing_scope`.

prs.title: fix(telegram): give the getUpdates long poll a client-side deadline
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Telegram inbound no longer stalls for ~15 minutes after a network change.

- **Problem**: `@chat-adapter/telegram` long-polls `getUpdates` with no client-side timeout. On a black-holed connection (no RST, e.g. after a Wi-Fi/NAT change) the request hangs until the kernel gives up on retransmits. No inbound message arrives meanwhile, while outbound keeps working on fresh sockets.
- **Fix**: `installPollDeadline` wraps the adapter instance's `telegramFetch`: `getUpdates` is aborted after its long-poll `timeout` + 30 s and fails with a plain error, so the poll loop backs off and retries. Every other Bot API method is untouched.
- **Scope guard**: an abort the adapter itself requests (polling stopped) still surfaces as `AbortError`. If a future adapter drops `telegramFetch`, the bridge logs a warning and polls as before.

## Related work

No issue; seen on a live install on 2026-10-03 (inbound dead for ~20 min, `ss` showed the getUpdates socket stuck with unacked data). Carried as a local patch since.

## Change kind

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops Telegram dropping any reply that contains a link with `_` in its URL. That covers email addresses like `first_last@example.com` and web URLs like `...?agent_name=x`.

- **Problem**: the adapter's GFM parser autolinks bare emails and URLs as `[text](url)` and does not escape `_` inside the URL. Telegram rejects the whole MarkdownV2 message ("Can't find end of Italic entity" / "Can't find end of a URL"), and delivery is dropped after retries. We first hit it with email addresses. It then showed up with a gateway connect link (`...&agent_name=olivia`): every reply carrying that link was dropped, so the agent looked silent to the user.
- **Fix**: before rendering, any link whose URL contains `_` is replaced by plain text. Autolinks and `mailto:` links become their text. A labelled link keeps its label and shows the URL after it in parentheses. The text is escaped normally (`first\_last@example\.com`), and Telegram clients still linkify it.
- **Scope**: only links with `_` in the URL change. All other links render as before.

## Related work

No issue. The fix is small and confined to the Telegram adapter, and regression tests cover it.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`ncl groups restart --id <other group>` from an agent now restarts the target group instead of the caller.

- **Problem**: the agent branch of the restart handler ignored `--id`. It killed the caller's session and wrote the `--message` on-wake row to `<target group>/<caller session>`, a folder no session row points at. A global-scope agent got `{ restarted: 1 }` while the target never restarted (#3911).
- **Fix**: take the calling-session branch only when `--id` is the caller's own group. A foreign id goes through `restartAgentGroupContainers(id, …)`, the same path a host call uses, which already handles `--message`.
- **Out of scope**: who may target another group. Group-scope agents are still denied a foreign `--id` by `src/cli/guard.ts`, and the command stays approval-gated.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): keep every pending question answerable in a chat
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Keeps every pending `ask_question` card in a WhatsApp chat answerable, not only the newest.

- **Problem**: `pendingQuestions` held one entry per chat, so a second card overwrote the first. The earlier card stayed on screen, its slash commands matched nothing (forwarded to the agent as text) or hit the newer card, and its `pending_approvals` row never cleared.
- **Fix**: a list per chat. `matchPendingQuestion` scans newest first and returns the index, so only the card that was answered is dropped.
- **Ambiguity**: two cards can both offer `/approve`, and a WhatsApp reply carries nothing tying it to a card. Newest wins — it is the card the user was just shown. Each entry keeps the card's title and a one-line detail, and the confirmation names what was answered and lists what is still open, so a second bare `/approve` landing on the next card is visible.
- **Bound**: `PENDING_QUESTIONS_PER_CHAT_MAX` (16) caps the list per chat; dropping the oldest logs a warning. `PENDING_QUESTIONS_MAX` still bounds how many chats hold a question — it never bounded cards within one.
- **Out of scope**: `src/channels/imessage.ts` has the same one-entry shape and likely the same bug. Separate PR.

<details>
<summary>Observed, and what the confirmation looks like</summary>

Three cards sent to one DM; only the last could be answered. The other two stayed on screen with unresponsive commands and their rows stayed pending.

After the fix, answering with `/approve`:

```
✅ Approved by Jason: Install Packages Request (Agent "main" is attempting to install a package + rebuild container: apt: imagemagick)
1 more waiting in this chat:
• Install Packages Request (Agent "main" is attempting to install a package + rebuild container: apt: ffmpeg)
```

The detail is the whole question flattened to one line (cut at 120 chars), not the first line: `install_packages` puts the package on line 2, so two installs would otherwise read identically. Up to 3 open cards are listed, then `…and N more`.

</details>

## Related work

No issue. Safe to review directly: the change is local to `src/channels/whatsapp.ts`, and the three new helpers (`matchPendingQuestion`, `questionDetail`, `formatAnswerConfirmation`) are pure and unit-tested.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`

## Validation

- `pnpm test` → 4202 pass vs 4188 on channels (the 14 new tests are the only difference); tsc --noEmit clean.

prs.title: fix(setup): wait for docker before starting the systemd unit
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the generated systemd unit wait for Docker before starting the host.

- **Problem**: the unit only had `After=network.target`. On a Pi reboot the host started before dockerd was ready and hit `FATAL: Container runtime failed to start`. `Restart=always` recovered from that one, but it adds a crash-loop to every boot. Adding `After=docker.service` alone doesn't help the default install, which is a user unit: a user unit can't order itself against system units.
- **Fix**: an `ExecStartPre` loops on `docker info` every 2s, capped by `TimeoutStartSec=300`. It also adds `After=network-online.target docker.service` + `Wants=network-online.target`, which take effect for root/system installs.
- **Out of scope**: rewriting units that are already installed. Existing installs pick this up the next time setup's service step runs.

## Related work

No issue. The change is confined to the `renderSystemdUnit` template, plus a test.

prs.title: fix(signal): use a monotonic clock for the daemon startup wait
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops a boot-time clock step from failing the Signal adapter's startup.

- **Problem**: `waitForDaemon` timed its 30s budget with `Date.now()`. A Raspberry Pi has no RTC, so it boots on the last saved timestamp and NTP then steps the clock forward. In the observed case the step was 43 minutes, landing about 20s into the wait. The loop exited at once, `setup()` threw "Signal daemon failed to start", and the host ran for two days with no Signal adapter. Every outbound reply failed with `MissingChannelAdapterError`.
- **Fix**: measure the wait with `performance.now()`, which is monotonic.
- **Out of scope**: retrying an adapter whose `setup()` fails. Today that failure leaves the channel down until a restart.

## Related work

No issue. It's a two-line change confined to `waitForDaemon`.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm run build` → clean
- Manual: diagnosed from host logs on a Pi. `systemd-timesyncd` logged "Initial clock synchronization to 14:35:38" and the adapter error followed 1.5s later, while host logs showed startup at 13:52:10. With the fix deployed, the service restarts and Signal connects normally.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

No new test. A real clock step can't be simulated without mocking `performance.now()` alongside `Date.now()`, and that would only assert the implementation.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now accepts the Anthropic Console's newer API key types instead of refusing them at the "Paste your API key" prompt.

- **Problem**: the Console now issues user (`sk-ant-usr…`) and service-account (`sk-ant-svc…`) keys. Both gateway skills' prompts (`add-onecli`, `add-iron-proxy`) accepted only `sk-ant-api…`, so setup refused a working key.
- **Fix**: one shared check in `setup/lib/anthropic-credential.ts`, used by both prompts. Any `sk-ant-<type>` counts as an API key except an OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat`), a refresh token (`sk-ant-ort`) or an Admin key (`sk-ant-admin`). Refresh tokens and Admin keys are refused. An OAuth token pasted at the API-key prompt is stored as an OAuth token, because the prompt can't go back to the menu. The OAuth prompt still takes only `sk-ant-oat`. The API-key prompt asks for a single-workspace key, because NanoClaw sends no `anthropic-workspace-id` header and a multi-workspace key gets HTTP 400.
- **Release**: this should go in 2026.10.1 if it merges in time (#4158).

## Related work

No issue. Found in the OneCLI 1.45 e2e matrix for #4094 (row P1). The bug was already on main before #4094.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The `channels` side of #4168: text-command answers and the web chat wait for the host too.

- **Problem**: WhatsApp (Baileys), iMessage and the local web chat answered a pending question themselves before the host decided. They closed the question and posted "✅ Approved by <name>" even when the host refused, so the approver could no longer answer.
- **Fix**: they wait for the host's outcome. Accepted: confirmed, question closed. Refused: question stays open, nothing posted (no private reply on these channels; the web chat shows the refusal only to the person who clicked). Closed: "No longer available". WhatsApp answers to one question are queued: a later answer waits for the earlier one and counts if the question is still open (so an approver's answer after a refused one isn't lost). The web chat draws the resolution the server returns, and none for a card the host updates itself (a gateway approval). WhatsApp Cloud names the card a button reply quotes (`cardMessageIdOf`), so the host's card check covers it.
- **Any core**: the updater copies these adapters from `channels` onto cores with and without click outcomes. On an older core `onAction` returns nothing, which counts as answered as before (confirmed and closed); WhatsApp Cloud's `cardMessageIdOf` goes in through a spread, so an older core still builds. Checked by type-checking the adapters against `main`, `v2026.10.1-rc.1` and `v2026.10.0`. iMessage needs no answer queue: it handles messages one at a time. A refused answer on WhatsApp and iMessage posts nothing, by design: neither has a private reply.
- **Copies**: #4168's commits, with the shared click files byte-identical. `permissions/index.ts` keeps `channels`' name-prompt code until main's #4148 arrives with the next sync.

**How to review**: review #4168 first. This PR's own change is the adapter files (`whatsapp.ts`, `imessage.ts`, `local-web.ts`, `local-web-page.js`, `whatsapp-cloud.ts`, about +100/-40 lines); everything else is #4168 copied over, byte-identical. Squash on merge.

prs.title: fix(approvals): resolve a clicked card only after the host accepts the click
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A clicked approval card now changes only after the host accepts the click.

- **Problem**: the channel edited the card (buttons removed, "✅ Approved by <name>") before the host checked who clicked. When the host refused the click, the request stayed pending, but the card showed it as decided and had no buttons left.
- **Fix**: response handlers return what a click did (`accepted`, `refused`, `closed` or `ignored`), and `onAction` passes it back. Both click transports (Chat SDK and Discord's forwarded gateway events) run one pipeline: decode the option, hand it to the host, then show only what the host did. A refused click keeps the card and its buttons; the clicker gets a private note where the channel has one (Slack, Google Chat, Teams, Discord flags 64). `closed` (the request's session, event or target is gone) shows "No longer available". Discord acks at once (type 6) and removes the buttons only after acceptance. Clicks on one card run one at a time, display included; a click that stalls past 10 s lets the next go ahead but can't draw over it.
- **Host-owned card check**: channel registration moves its question to a second card with new options (the agent choice). The host now counts only a click from the card the question lives on (migration 029: nullable `card_message_id`, no backfill; NULL = unchecked, as before), so an old card or a copy can't resolve against the new options. A failed agent-choice delivery puts the question back on the first card. An unknown-sender approval claims its row and adds the member in one transaction, so two racing responses decide once.
- **Each decision once, reported early**: question answers, channel connect and Reject, and unknown-sender approvals claim their row first (with their writes in one transaction where they share the central DB), so two racing clicks decide once. Every deciding path reports acceptance right after its claim, before the agent is woken or a message replayed; a question answer that can't be written closes the question (logged) rather than reviving it for a second answer. A plain Reject on a card whose admin chose "Reject with reason…" is ignored, so the reason isn't lost; "Reject with reason…" arms capture before its prompt is sent and is reported only once armed; if the prompt can't be sent, the request is rejected without a reason. A name reply for a new agent and a Connect or Reject click on the same registration take turns, so the channel is wired once; once it is decided, its name prompt is dropped and the replayed message reaches the agent. An accepted click stays with its handler even if that handler's later work throws. A decision that outlasts the 10 s hold still draws over a card that shows none.
- **Skill seam**: a render may add `afterClick({ outcome, selectedOption, userId, actorName, messageId, platformId, threadId })`, returning a card to draw (drawn as returned, whatever the outcome) and a private note, or nothing for the default. A skill decides in a prepended response handler and draws through its render resolver, without decoding options or dispatching. Clicks carry the card's thread; a Discord click's channel is the encoded one (a thread by its parent). A handler that still returns `true` compiles and owns the click, but shows nothing and logs a warning (such handlers returned `true` for refused clicks).
- **Out of scope**: the native WhatsApp, iMessage and local-web text-command paths on `channels` (their own PR, which also sets WhatsApp Cloud's `cardMessageIdOf` to the card a reply quotes). Non-deciding actions (`registerQuestionActionHandler`) on Discord's forwarded path: a modal can't open after the type-6 ack.

## Related work

Stacked on #4147 (base `fix/approval-card-full-action` @1e2a2291); merge after it. The bug is older than #4147 and affects every channel. No public issue.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 3927 pass; 3 fail the same way without this change (`setup/gateways/selection` expects a pnpm WARN this machine doesn't print; `scripts/update` e2e timeouts under load, pass alone).
- Tests: a refused click leaves the row pending, the buttons in place and no "Approved by" text; an approver's click still resolves the card; a second click waits for the first; afterClick card/note on both transports; `closed` shows "No longer available"; after the agent choice an old card or a copy is ignored while the new card works; racing clicks decide once (unknown sender, question answer, channel connect and Reject); a plain Reject while a reason is awaited is ignored and the reason still reaches the agent; a reason prompt that can't be sent rejects plainly; a name reply racing a Connect click never leaves an agent unconnected, and the replayed message reaches the agent; acceptance is reported before a wake that hangs; gateway approvals still fail closed.
- `chat-sdk-bridge-late-click.test.ts` (end to end through the real approvals handler, Chat SDK and Discord paths): an approval still being applied, then a late Deny on the same card and on a copy: one edit only, the action runs once.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` -> clean. Codex adversarial review on each set of changes; real findings fixed (the last commit fixes the last round's two findings and was not reviewed again). Left: a host restart while the agent-choice card is being delivered leaves the registration waiting (safe, no stale click counts); a stranded registration's way out is its own follow-up. `ncl groups delete` and `ncl messaging-groups delete` remove a pending registration outside its turn: if its approver was asked for a new agent's name, their next DM is dropped once.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Approval cards change only after the host accepts the click; a click from someone who can't answer the card leaves its buttons in place.
Discord: clicks on approval cards from a durable approval gateway are now recorded (they were ignored).
```

## Security and trust boundaries

prs.title: fix(update-skills): attribute a barrel import to the skill that appends it
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

**What** — `detectInstalledSkills` attributes a channel-barrel import to the skill that actually appends it, instead of assuming every import has its own `add-<name>` skill.

**Why** — `/add-slack` appends two imports to `src/channels/index.ts`: `slack.js` and its `slack-a2a-guard.js` companion. Detection maps each one to `add-<name>`, so the refresh looks for a skill that does not exist and fails:

```
Missing .claude/skills/add-slack-a2a-guard/SKILL.md
```

`refreshInstalledSkills` treats that as a failed skill, which blocks `/update-nanoclaw` validation on any install with Slack. I hit this on a routine update.

**How it works** — ownership is read from the skills' own `nc:append to:src/channels/index.ts` directives: an import a skill declares belongs to that skill, and a skill owning several imports is refreshed once under its own name. An unclaimed import still maps to `add-<name>`, so a channel installed without a skill is still reported — the missing-skill check keeps its point. A `SKILL.md` that fails to parse simply claims nothing; refresh reports the parse failure itself with a better message than detection could.

**How it was tested** — two cases added to `scripts/update-skills.test.ts`: the companion case (asserts one entry, not two) and an unclaimed import (asserts `add-<name>` attribution still happens). I verified the companion test fails on `main` and passes with the fix. Full file green (6/6), `tsc --noEmit` clean, and the real update that surfaced this now validates end to end.



Refs #3529

```release-note
`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops at validate on installs with Slack. The skill refresh now credits each channel import to the skill that adds it, so it stops looking for `add-slack-a2a-guard` and `add-slack-a2a` skills that don't exist.
```

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Ports `/add-dial-tool` to OneCLI agent grants so Dial keeps working after the 1.45 pin move in https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094. Merge right after it.

- **Problem**: on 1.44+ the project policy API and secret lists the skill used answer `410`, so it stops at its 1.42 gate and `/add-dial`'s tool offer aborts setup. The gateway's upgrade also deletes `Dial: blocked agents` and gives Dial to every agent, so the upgrade guide now deletes the key first and the re-run recreates it.
- **Fix**: `dial-secret.ts` updates the Dial key in place (its id and grants stay), then the skill detaches it from this install's unchosen groups and attaches it to the chosen ones, which also re-narrows an upgraded install. It gates on 1.45.x, no agent still in `all` mode, and a CLI with `agents grants`. `dial-policy.ts` is gone.
- **Behavior change**: new groups never get Dial until the skill runs again. With no agents yet, `/add-dial` installs the tool with nobody holding the key.

## Related work

Stacked on https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094 (base is its branch; retarget to `main` after it merges, which also starts CI). Replaces the policy path from https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4052 (and #4036's guard). prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves NanoClaw to OneCLI gateway 1.45.0 and CLI 2.11.0, the required stop before 2.x, and decides what a new agent group may use now that 1.44+ starts every agent with no grants. Supersedes #4082 and keeps chiptoe-svg's commits.

- **Problem**: on 1.44+ a new group's OneCLI agent holds nothing, so it cannot reach its model. Working out a group's secrets from other agents' grants widens or narrows access depending on history nobody can see.
- **Fix**: NanoClaw records the id of each model credential its provider logins save, per install, and on every spawn attaches the ones for the provider the group runs (an older install with nothing recorded is matched once by the names NanoClaw writes, and duplicate names are refused). Tool secrets and app connections are opt-in: `/add-vercel` now asks which groups and picks its token by host, and Tavily's paid-key upgrade attaches its key to the group. A new `pre-upgrade-check.sh` runs before the pin is saved and stops on anything the conversion deletes or changes.
- **Out of scope**: `/add-dial-tool` (stacked PR on `feat/dial-tool-grants`, merges in the same sitting), per-group model keys (#3205), docs portal pages.

## Related work

Supersedes https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4082. Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3532, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3205, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4052, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4036.

## Validation

- add-onecli payload suite applied per `nc:copy` (SDK 2.2.1), plus `tsc` over the applied files: 156/156. Full vitest and `tsc` pass.
- Tests cover each rule (model credential only, the spawn path passing the provider, repair on the next spawn, provider switch, late login, one-time name match only when nothing is recorded, duplicate names refused, `/add-vercel` token choice, the record lock, 1.42 no-op, every upgrade-check exit) and failed when the rule was broken on purpose.
- VM end to end, all pass: fresh 1.45 install, 1.42 to 1.45 upgrade (check stops before the pin is saved, 0 failed conversions), restore rollback, `/add-codex` after groups exist plus a provider switch.

- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [x] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
[BREAKING] The OneCLI gateway pin moves to 1.45.0 (CLI 2.11.0). Detect: `docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' onecli` shows an older tag. Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs. Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential. On a 1.42 gateway, new groups still get every key until the gateway is upgraded. prs.title: fix(gchat): tell the agent when a file arrives from Google Drive
```
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Tells the agent why a file shared from Google Drive never arrived, so it asks for an upload instead of guessing.

- **Problem**: Google Chat sends a file shared from Drive as a Drive id only (`source: DRIVE_FILE`, `driveDataRef.driveFileId`, no `attachmentDataRef`). Chat's [media download](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/api/reference/rest/v1/media/download) refuses Drive files, and the app's service account can't open the sender's Drive. The agent sees only `[image: name]`.
- **Fix**: `gchat.ts` passes `extractRawText: gchatDriveFileNote` to the bridge. For each Drive attachment it adds one line to the message: the file was not downloaded, so ask the sender to paste or drag it into the chat. Uploaded files are unchanged. Core is unchanged too: this uses the existing `extractRawText` hook (v2026.10.0+).
- **Out of scope**: downloading Drive files as the sender. That needs add-on `oauthScopes` with the restricted `drive.readonly` scope and per-user consent.

## Related work

No issue. Found during the live test for https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/issues/3206, a separate bug. vercel/chat has no Drive issue or PR. The change is two functions and one config line in `gchat.ts`, plus tests, so it carries over when `gchat.ts` moves to `add-gchat/payload/` in the channels move.

They cover the note, quiet output for uploaded/empty/malformed payloads, several files, the Pub/Sub shape, append order, factory wiring, and a hostile name (`"`, `]`, newline, U+2028, U+202E). A guard pins that adapter 4.41.1 gives Drive files no `fetchData`, so a bump that adds Drive downloads fails it.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels`: 643 passed, 19 skipped. `tsc --noEmit`, eslint and prettier are clean. Codex adversarial review: no defects.
- Live (2026-10-21 19:20Z), on an exe.dev test install with a real Workspace add-on Chat app and adapter 4.41.1: an image sent through the Drive button reached the agent as `[Google Drive file "Screenshot 2026-10-21 at 15.47.39.png" was not downloaded: …]`. <!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Hands the photos and PDFs a user sends to the provider as structured attachments, so a vision model sees the file instead of a line saying it exists.

- **Problem**: core puts attachments in the prompt text only. The `/add-opencode` payload (https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3733) already turns structured attachments into file parts, but core never sends any, and the payload would throw on this PR's original shape (no `sourceMessageId`).
- **Fix**: `extractAttachments` builds `PromptAttachment[]` (source message id, name, mime, staged path; string fields only) for each file the host staged, and the poll loop passes it to `query()` and to follow-up `push()`. The text line stays, so a provider that ignores the field is unchanged. The payload forwards only JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP and PDF, identified by their first bytes, and keeps everything else (including incomplete entries) as prompt text. If OpenCode still refuses a file part, the turn is retried once from the prompt text.
- **Out of scope**: remote URLs (never fetched, still prompt text). https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/2618's content blocks can build on this type.

## Related work

Related: https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/2618, https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/1683 (host-side staging, does not touch this seam). No issue: the payload's file-part path has been unreachable since #3733 merged.

## Summary

Makes the Resend (email) channel send again: agent replies and the "Connect yourself" hello.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops attachments being dropped when a channel's message id contains `/`.

- **Problem**: attachments are staged under `inbox/<message id>/`, and `extractAttachmentFiles` refused any id that is not a plain file name. prs.title: Sanitize path-separator message IDs for attachment staging (#3206)
prs.body:
## Problem

`extractAttachmentFiles` in `src/session-manager.ts` gates inbound attachment
staging on `isSafeAttachmentName(messageId)`, which rejects any value
containing `/` or `\`. Google Chat message IDs are resource paths
(`spaces/<space>/messages/<id>`), so every one of them fails this check and
the function returns before writing anything — inbound attachments on
Google Chat are silently dropped. The agent still receives the attachment
metadata/filename in the message text, so it reports a file that was never
actually staged.

Slack/Discord/WhatsApp message IDs are opaque single-component tokens, so
they pass the check today and are unaffected.

## Fix

Added `safeAttachmentDirName(id)` to `src/attachment-safety.ts`:
- returns the id unchanged when it already satisfies `isSafeAttachmentName`
  (Slack/Discord/WhatsApp staging paths are byte-identical to before)
- otherwise derives a single-component slug (unsafe chars, including `/`,
  `\`, `..`, collapsed to `-`) with a short SHA-256 suffix of the original id
  appended, so two ids that differ only in stripped characters can't collide
  onto the same inbox directory

`extractAttachmentFiles` in `src/session-manager.ts` now sanitizes
`messageId` into `inboxMessageId` via this helper *before* it's used as the
inbox directory name / `localPath`, instead of rejecting the whole message.

### What did NOT change (security guarantee preserved)

This is a path-traversal guard, so I was deliberately conservative:

- `isSafeAttachmentName` itself is untouched — it still rejects any `/`,
  `\`, `..`, `.`, NUL, or non-basename value. Nothing was "relaxed".
- Containment does not come from `isSafeAttachmentName` rejecting the raw
  messageId — it comes from `safeAttachmentDirName`'s output always being a
  single, safe path component *by construction*, plus the unchanged
  defense-in-depth already in place:
  - `ensureContainedInboxDir` (symlink lstat + realpath containment check
    against the inbox root)
  - the `wx` exclusive-create flag on the actual `writeFileSync`
- The outbound side (`readOutboxFiles`, `clearOutbox`) and the A2A forwarding
  path (`agent-route.ts`) are untouched — those message IDs are host/container
  generated (`msg-<ts>-<rand>`, `a2a-<ts>-<rand>`), never externally supplied,
  and were already always safe.

## Tests

- `src/attachment-safety.test.ts` (new): unit coverage for
  `safeAttachmentDirName` — passes safe ids through unchanged, derives a safe
  component for a Google Chat-style resource path and for a traversal-shaped
  id, is deterministic, and does not collide two different unsafe ids that
  sanitize to the same slug.
- `src/host-core.test.ts`: replaced `should reject inbound attachments when
  messageId is unsafe` (which asserted the old drop-the-message behaviour)
  with two tests — one confirming a traversal-shaped id (`../../escape`) now
  lands in exactly one sanitized subdir of the inbox with nothing written
  outside the session's inbox root, and one confirming a Google Chat-style
  `spaces/<space>/messages/<id>` messageId now successfully stages its
  attachment.
- Existing regression tests for malicious *filenames* (as opposed to message
  ids) — pre-placed symlinks, `../../../tmp/pwned`-style filenames — are
  unchanged and still pass, since `isSafeAttachmentName` on `filename` was
  not touched.

Ran narrowly: `npx vitest run src/attachment-safety.test.ts
src/host-core.test.ts src/session-manager.attachments.test.ts
src/modules/agent-to-agent/agent-route.test.ts` — 69/69 passing. Also ran
`npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) and `npx eslint` on the changed files (0 errors,
only pre-existing unrelated `no-catch-all` warnings in code I didn't touch).

## Note (from the issue)

Fixing this alone isn't sufficient for Google Chat attachments end-to-end —
per the issue, `@chat-adapter/gchat` also omits `alt=media` on the Chat media
endpoint, causing `fetchData()` to 400 before bytes ever reach this code.
That's a separate bug being fixed upstream in `vercel/chat`, not addressed
here.

Closes #3206

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Gateway approval cards always show the full action.

- **Problem**: on cards with details the action was only the title, and card text could be cut with no sign.
- **Fix**: the card text starts with the full action; a long action or title moves there under a short fixed title. No fixed cut: values that must still be shortened end with "… (N more characters not shown)", and left-out details are counted.
- **Overflow**: a channel can declare which cards it shows whole (`cardFits`). A card that doesn't fit posts its full text in up to 5 labelled parts, then a short card with the buttons; if it can't, nothing posts and the request is refused (a gateway approval is denied). A partial post leaves a short note, and a retry resumes. A resolved card keeps at least the decision and who made it.
- **Clicks**: clicked cards resolve the same way everywhere, Discord included: the buttons go first, then the decision, then an escaped update within the channel's limits. A late or repeated click leaves a resolved card as it is.

## Related work

Follows #4135 and builds on #4117 (carstenf), which fixes Discord's option decoding; lands together with #4156 (channels), which declares `cardFits` per channel. Merging this first is safe: no channel on `main` declares `cardFits` or `maxCardTextLength`, so nothing overflows until #4156 lands. No issue: found internally. prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-copilot GitHub Copilot SDK provider
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an upstream-ready `/add-copilot` provider skill that installs GitHub Copilot as a NanoClaw runtime while keeping the device-login token in the credential gateway.
- **Problem**: Prior Copilot-provider approaches passed the token through environment or container state, which widened the credential boundary.
- **Fix**: The provider sends only a non-secret SDK placeholder; the gateway injects the real token for the licensed Copilot API host (through the gateway-neutral credential store) and for `/copilot_internal/*` on `api.github.com`.
- **Out of scope**: Glob path scoping in the gateway-neutral credential store; the helper keeps a OneCLI call for the one credential that needs it (see Notes).

## Related work

No issue closes. This overlaps with nanocoai/nanoclaw#399, nanocoai/nanoclaw#1351, and nanocoai/nanoclaw#1704: those older approaches passed the token via env/container surfaces, while this provider keeps it in the gateway.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-copilot/SKILL.md` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts --testNamePattern 'add-copilot|provider skill descriptors'` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts --all add-copilot` -> passed; applied in a disposable checkout, installed `@github/copilot-sdk@1.0.14`, ran provider-contract verification and installed payload tests, and built the local image.
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> passed.
- `pnpm run lint` -> passed with existing warnings only.
- `pnpm run format:check` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run setup/providers/skill-descriptor.test.ts` -> passed.
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> passed.
- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test` -> passed: 513 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail.
- Live, on a real install (OneCLI gateway, business Copilot plan): a CLI-channel message got a streamed reply; the agent ran a shell tool and the `send_message` MCP tool, and resumed the session on the next message. The container's env, every `/proc/*/environ`, and the Copilot state dir held no real token, only the placeholder.
- `pnpm test` -> failed in unrelated timeout/git-fixture tests; clean `upstream/main` (`c2663b17`) fails the same command in the same environment with unrelated timeouts and `safe.bareRepository` fixture failure.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Adds `/add-copilot`, a GitHub Copilot SDK provider skill that authenticates through the credential gateway instead of container-readable tokens.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- The Copilot device-login token never enters the container; the SDK receives a non-secret placeholder and ambient GitHub token env vars are stripped.
- `api.github.com` is not in `modelDomains`; the OneCLI grant for that host is path-scoped to `/copilot_internal/*`.
- The helper is OneCLI-only and macOS-keychain-only, and fails clearly elsewhere.
- The licensed Copilot API credential goes through `getCredentialStore().connection()` (#4106's seam): host-wide, `Authorization: Bearer {value}`, `proxyValue` = the container's placeholder (`payload/scripts/copilot-login.ts` `copilotApiTarget`, kept in sync with the container by a test).
- Two pieces stay OneCLI-specific because the seam cannot express them. The `api.github.com` secret must cover every path under `/copilot_internal/`: the Copilot CLI calls several undocumented paths there (token exchange, user, entitlement checks), and the set changes between CLI versions. The seam limits a credential to one exact path, so a list of exact paths would break silently on the next CLI bump, and a host-wide grant would expose the token's repo scopes to all of `api.github.com`. The individual-endpoint block rule has no neutral form yet.

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-repo-self-edit — admin-approved edits to NanoClaw's own source
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-repo-self-edit`, a skill that lets chosen agents propose edits to NanoClaw's own source as a git patch. Every edit is admin-approved with the full diff on the card, and it is reverted automatically if it breaks the build or the restart.

- **Problem**: CLAUDE.md lists "direct source-level self-edits" as a planned second self-modification tier. Today an agent that finds a bug in NanoClaw can only describe the fix. The operator has to apply it by hand.
- **Fix**: a new `propose_repo_edit` MCP tool writes a `repo_self_edit` system action. The host module registers it through the existing seams: `registerDeliveryAction` with a guard spec, `registerApprovalHandler` → `reenterGuardedDeliveryAction`, and one `onHostStart` callback. Held proposals get the same treatment as `install_packages` / `add_mcp_server`.
- **Approval gate**: from the container path the guard always holds for the group's admin chain. Groups not listed in `REPO_SELF_EDIT_AGENT_GROUPS` are denied before any card is sent. The card shows the whole patch through core's `fenceForCard` (`src/card-text.ts`), with no length cap. A patch too long for one card is refused by `requestApproval`'s card-length check, which tells the agent to shorten it; nothing is truncated. The precheck runs again on the approved replay against the current tree.
- **Editable paths**: `src/`, `container/agent-runner/src/`, `container/skills/`, `docs/`.
- **Never editable**: `.env*`; any git-ignored path (`data/`, `logs/`, group state); anything outside the editable paths (`package.json`, lockfiles, Dockerfile). Also refused: the files that make approval meaningful (guard, approvals, permissions, mount security, gateway providers and coordinator, `env.ts`, `upgrade-state.ts`, delivery, and this skill's own files), plus renames, symlinks, mode changes and binary patches.
- **Commit hygiene**: only the patch's own files are staged and committed (`git commit -- <files>`). Other staged or unstaged work in the checkout stays untouched. Every commit and every revert re-stamps the upgrade marker, so the startup tripwire accepts it.
- **Rollback**: a `container/` edit is typechecked first. On failure it is reverted; on success the group's containers restart. A `src/` edit goes to a detached `scripts/repo-self-edit-watchdog.sh`. The watchdog builds, restarts via `setup/lib/restart.sh`, and requires the same host instance after a settle window. On a failed build, a failed start or a crash loop it commits the reverse of the edit's files, rebuilds and restarts. The host reports the verdict to the agent. A rollback is always a new commit. It never uses `reset --hard`, and never plain `git revert`, which refuses while other work is staged.
- **Agent never holds write access**: the agent reads source through a read-only mount. SKILL.md says to mount `src/` and warns never to mount the project root. The host applies the change.
- **Out of scope / follow-ups**: editing `package.json`/Dockerfile (would need an image rebuild on apply and on revert). Multi-card patches for larger changes. A dry-run mode where the agent asks the host to run tests on a proposal before carding. The watchdog has not been exercised under systemd.

<details>
<summary>Apply footprint</summary>

- Copies `src/modules/repo-self-edit/*` (module, guard, policy, git primitives, checks, state, 2 tests), `container/agent-runner/src/mcp-tools/repo-self-edit.{ts,test.ts,instructions.md}`, and `scripts/repo-self-edit-watchdog.sh`.
- Two barrel lines: `import './repo-self-edit/index.js';` after `self-mod` in `src/modules/index.ts`, and `import './repo-self-edit.js';` after `self-mod` in the MCP-tools barrel. The host line sits before `community-portal` because `community-portal/registration.test.ts` takes the last `onHostStart` callback.
- One `.env` line: `REPO_SELF_EDIT_AGENT_GROUPS`. It is read on every proposal, so changes need no restart.
- REMOVE.md reverses all of it.

</details>

## Related work

No issue. Searched open and closed PRs and issues for "self-edit", "self modification", "draft activate" and "self-mod source". #2635 (`patch_bridge`, closed by its author as opened against the wrong repo) patched a separate bridge service, not this checkout. #3783 (code mode) gives agents sandboxed coding workspaces and does not edit the install itself. Safe to review directly: nothing reaches trunk code until the skill is applied, and applying it changes only the two barrels.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

All commands were run with the skill applied per SKILL.md in a clean worktree on `upstream/main`. The applied copies were then removed per REMOVE.md.

- `pnpm run typecheck` -> clean
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> clean
- `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors (the 188 warnings are the existing set; `eslint src/modules/repo-self-edit` -> 0 problems)
- `pnpm run format:check` -> clean
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/modules/repo-self-edit/ src/guard/ src/modules/community-portal/` -> 43 passed
- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test src/mcp-tools/repo-self-edit.test.ts` -> 3 passed
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-repo-self-edit/SKILL.md` -> no problems; `vitest run scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts scripts/skill-directives.test.ts scripts/skill-policy.test.ts scripts/test-registry-skills.test.ts` -> 293 passed
- `shellcheck scripts/repo-self-edit-watchdog.sh` -> clean
- `pnpm test` (full) -> 2949 passed. One failure was ours: `community-portal/registration.test.ts` depends on barrel order, fixed by placing the barrel line as above. The other 7 failures are all in `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts`, which is untouched: 5 s timeouts on a loaded machine, and they still time out when that file runs alone. The same flake is noted in #3783.
- Coverage, by integration point:
  - Host `repo-self-edit.test.ts` imports the real modules barrel. It asserts the delivery action, the approval continuation and the `repo_self_edit.apply` guard entry are registered. It asserts guard decisions: hold, deny when not listed, deny for non-agents, and a grant cannot bring back a delisted group.
  - The same test drives dispatch → card → approval handler → guarded replay into a throwaway git repo: commit of only the patch's file while staged and untracked work survives, revert on a typecheck failure, watchdog hand-off and verdict report, a docs-only edit, a re-check on replay, and 11 refusal cases.
  - `watchdog.test.ts` runs the real script with a stubbed build and restart: kept when healthy, reverted on a build failure (other staged work survives), reverted on a crash loop.
  - Container `repo-self-edit.test.ts` asserts the barrel import and drives the tool through a real MCP client.
- Manual path CI cannot cover: a live host restart through launchd/systemd. The watchdog's `systemd-run --user` path is untested.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-repo-self-edit skill: chosen agents can propose admin-approved patches to NanoClaw's own source, with automatic revert if the build or restart fails.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **New capability**: agent-authored code runs on the host after approval. The admin approval is the trust boundary. Everything else is defense in depth: the per-group opt-in, path policy, protected files, git-ignore check, clean-apply check and re-validation on replay.
- **Untrusted input**: the patch and reason come from the container. They are rendered on the card with core's `escapeInvisibles` and `fenceForCard` (invisibles and backticks escaped, fenced), so they cannot spoof card fields or break out of the fence. They reach git only via `execFileSync` argv or stdin, never a shell. Paths are parsed with a whitespace-free pattern and checked for `..`, absolute paths, backslashes and NUL.
- **Credentials**: `.env*` and every git-ignored path are refused. The credential gateway and env reader are protected. SKILL.md forbids mounting the project root into the container. Commits skip git hooks (`--no-verify`) so repo hooks never run inside the host process; the typecheck/build gates replace them.
- **Host processes**: the watchdog runs detached from the service (a transient `systemd-run --user` unit where available) and calls only `pnpm run build`, `setup/lib/restart.sh` and `setup/lib/host-status.mjs`.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

- [x] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: fix(discord): strip newline suffix from custom_id before parsing Gateway interactions
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes every Discord DM approval-card button tap routing to **reject**, regardless of which button was pressed.

## Root cause

`@chat-adapter/discord` encodes button `custom_id` as `<actionId>
<value>` (newline delimiter). The Gateway interaction handler in `handleForwardedEvent` parsed `custom_id` directly without stripping the `
<value>` suffix, so `tail` ended up as `"0
0"` instead of `"0"`. This failed the `/^\d+$/` check in `resolveSelectedOption`, returned the raw string, and the approval handler's `if (selectedOption !== 'approve')` fast-path rejected everything — including taps on the Approve button. The "0 0" display visible in the edited embed was the raw `"0
0"` fallback label rendered by Discord.

## Fix

Extract the `actionId` by slicing at the first `'
'` before parsing the colon-delimited segments. This mirrors what `decodeDiscordCustomId` already does on the webhook path.

## Changes

- `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` — one-line fix in `handleForwardedEvent`
- `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge-gateway.test.ts` — regression test: fires a real `GATEWAY_INTERACTION_CREATE` event at the bridge's local HTTP server with a `
`-encoded `custom_id` and asserts `onAction` receives a clean index string (`"0"`) with no newline

prs.title: fix(chat-sdk-bridge): redundant Button value param corrupts Discord custom_id
prs.body:
Fixes #3456

## Summary

- Approval-card buttons were created with both \`id\` and \`value\` set to the same option index. The Discord Chat SDK adapter concatenates \`id\` and \`value\` with a newline when both are set, producing a corrupted \`custom_id\` like \`"ncq:<questionId>:0\n0"\` instead of \`"ncq:<questionId>:0"\`.
- \`resolveSelectedOption()\` then can't cleanly resolve the corrupted tail back to the real option value, so clicking **Approve** gets treated as a deny (\`resolveOneCLIApproval()\` maps anything other than literally \`'approve'\` to \`'deny'\`) — approvals silently reject, and the card can resend.
- Fix: drop the redundant \`value\` param. \`id\` alone already carries the full routing info (questionId + option index) — see the comment directly above the call site.
- Also adds two diagnostic \`log.warn\` calls (\`chat-sdk-bridge.ts\`, \`onecli-approvals.ts\`) so a similar render-metadata mismatch is visible in logs instead of looking identical to an intentional decline.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified live on a Discord-wired install: before the fix, clicking Approve produced \`customId\` \`"ncq:...:0\n0"\`; after, \`"ncq:...:0"\`, resolving correctly on the first click.
- [x] \`pnpm vitest run src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts src/modules/approvals/\` — 52/52 pass

## Related

- #3455 / #3454 — a separate bug found and fixed during the same troubleshooting session (poll-loop heartbeat gap). Unrelated code path, listed here only because both surfaced while debugging the same install.
- #3457 — message-dedup fix, also unrelated code path, same session.

prs.title: feat(skills): add /contribute-upstream operational skill for giving fork features back
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/contribute-upstream`, an operational skill that helps any customized NanoClaw fork give its local features back upstream safely, as seams and skills instead of long-lived edits.

- **Problem**: forks that edit upstream files directly pay for it on every `/update-nanoclaw`: each edit is a potential conflict. Giving features back by hand is slow and easy to get wrong (wrong route, leaked internal names, work identity on commits).
- **What it does**: four modes. `map` inventories local-only files vs files owned by installed skills (registry branches and gateway payloads filtered out) and upstream files edited by churn, classifies each feature as `bugfix` / `seam` / `skill` / `docs` / `local-only`, and records decisions in a numbered ledger. `contribute <slug>` builds one approved feature in its own worktree off `upstream/main` (or off a dependency's `contrib/<dep>` branch), verifies, scrubs, and opens the PR. `status` writes a numbered report per PR (links, review state, new feedback, conflicts; several PRs per feature supported). `reconcile` runs after `/update-nanoclaw` to move local code onto merged seams.
- **Why seams**: `references/seam-patterns.md` describes how to split a feature into a behavior-neutral upstream base plus a local override that registers into it, so the fork's upstream-file edits shrink to one line.
- **Safety**: two operator gates per feature through `AskUserQuestion` (may it be contributed; may this exact diff and body be pushed). A blocking scrub check (`scripts/scrub-check.ts`) scans the branch diff, commit messages, branch name, and PR body for private IPs, home paths, emails, internal hosts, credential shapes, and a per-install denylist. Commit authors are checked too: only the operator's personal email passed via `--allow-identity` is allowed. Internal systems of the operator's employer or organization are classified `local-only` and never contributed.
- **Configurable**: fork owner (`--owner` / `CONTRIB_FORK_OWNER` / `gh api user`), contribution remote (default `contrib`, created with `gh repo fork` when `origin` is private or not a fork), and ledger, status, denylist, and optional divergences paths (defaults under `.nanoclaw-contrib/`, chosen so they don't collide with `.nanoclaw-migrations/` used by `/migrate-nanoclaw`).
- **Footprint**: skill-owned files only. The skill edits no core file and no other skill. At runtime it writes only under `.nanoclaw-contrib/` in the operator's checkout.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Documents a folder convention that keeps a fork's in-tree code from conflicting on upgrade.

- **Problem**: the docs say "every change is a skill", but they don't say where a fork's own code should sit in the tree before it becomes a skill, or where a skill's copied-in files should go. Edits inside upstream files are what make upgrades expensive.
- **Evidence**: in one real fork upgrade across ~420 upstream commits, 124 fork-only new files produced 0 conflicts. 208 edits inside upstream files produced 91 conflicted files (~200 hunks).
- **Convention**: fork-only code goes in one folder that mirrors the upstream layout (`src/local/`, `container/agent-runner/src/local/`). It is wired in with one barrel line per upstream file, each guarded by a registration test. Upstream behavior is extended by wrapping (a decorator), and upstream helpers are imported, never copied. When a fork needs an upstream decision to change, it proposes a behavior-neutral seam upstream.
- **Where**: a fuller section in `docs/customizing.md`, plus a short section (under 12 lines) in `CLAUDE.md` that links to it. The Docs Index entry for `customizing.md` is updated to match.
- **Out of scope**: no code, no new doc file. The registration-test details are left to `skill-guidelines.md`, which the new section links to.

## Related work

No issue. Docs-only and additive: it adds to the skills model in `docs/skills-model.md` and changes nothing it already says.

prs.title: fix(discord): Approve clicks recorded as reject (custom_id value suffix not stripped)
prs.body:
## Problem

On Discord, every **Approve** click on an approval card is recorded as a **reject**. The card footer shows `0\n0 by <user>` instead of `✅ Approved by <user>`.

## Cause

`@chat-adapter/discord` encodes a button's `custom_id` as `<actionId>\n<value>` (`encodeDiscordCustomId`). The approval card's Approve button (`id: ncq:<approvalId>:0`, `value: '0'`) therefore arrives as `ncq:<approvalId>:0\n0`.

The raw `GATEWAY_INTERACTION_CREATE` handler in `handleForwardedEvent` takes everything after `ncq:<id>:` as the option index, gets `'0\n0'`, which fails the `/^\d+$/` check in `resolveSelectedOption`, and is passed on unchanged. `handleRegisteredApproval` treats any value other than `'approve'` as a rejection.

## Fix

Strip the adapter's `\n<value>` suffix before resolving the index (one line). Legacy custom_ids without the suffix (e.g. `ncq:q-1:approve`) are unaffected.

## Tests

- New regression test in `chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` posts a Gateway click with `custom_id: 'ncq:q-index:0\n0'` and asserts `onAction(..., 'approve', ...)`.
- It fails without the fix and passes with it; the full file passes (38/38), `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Verified on a live install: Approve on an `install_packages` card now approves and rebuilds the container.

prs.title: refactor(agent-runner): turn-lifecycle hook registry for the poll loop
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds a turn-lifecycle hook registry so installs can attach per-turn behavior without editing `poll-loop.ts`. Nothing changes unless a hook is registered.

- **Problem**: anything that has to act on a turn has to be written into the loop body itself. That includes enriching inbound rows before formatting, picking a model per batch, observing provider events for progress or tracing, and reacting to a failed query. Every such edit conflicts with upstream changes to the poll loop.
- **Fix**: new `container/agent-runner/src/turn-hooks.ts` with `registerTurnHook({ name, beforeTurn?, prepareQuery?, onProviderEvent?, onError? })`. It follows the same pattern as `registerProvider` / `registerTools`: register at module scope, get loaded through the `modules/index.ts` barrel.
- **Hook points**:
  - `beforeTurn(ctx)`: runs after pre-task scripts and before formatting, for the opening batch and for follow-ups (`ctx.followUp`). Rows in `ctx.messages` may be rewritten in place.
  - `prepareQuery(input, ctx)`: opening batch only, just before `provider.query()`. It may return a replacement `QueryInput`.
  - `onProviderEvent(event, routing)`: runs on every event after `handleEvent`. It is fire-and-forget and never awaited, so it cannot stall the stream.
  - `onError(err, ctx)`: runs when the query throws, before continuation recovery.
- **Isolation**: hooks run in registration order. A hook that throws or rejects is logged as `[turn-hooks] <name>.<point> failed` and skipped. It never breaks the turn or the hooks after it.
- **Behavior-neutral**: with no hooks registered, `beforeTurn` and `onError` do nothing and `prepareQuery` returns the same input object. The only structural edit is that `processQuery` now gets `input.prompt` / `input.continuation`, which are the same values when no hook runs.
- **Out of scope**: runner commands, result-text transforms and delivery changes. Those are separate seams.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3921, #3925, #3932, #3939 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

No issue. This is a small, inert seam, so it is safe to review directly. #2842 proposes a much broader set of extension points, including poll-loop hooks. This PR is the single poll-loop piece, kept minimal on purpose.

**How this differs from `onExchangeComplete` (#4105).** That callback belongs to the provider: `createProvider` attaches it (`container/agent-runner/src/providers/factory.ts:36`), it fires once after each finished exchange to archive the transcript, and an install cannot register its own. The hooks here are registered by installs and run at points `onExchangeComplete` does not cover: `beforeTurn` and `prepareQuery` before the query starts, `onProviderEvent` for each event in flight, and `onError` when the query throws.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [x] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bun test src/turn-hooks.test.ts` -> 7 pass. Covers:
  - registration order at every point
  - isolation of throwing and rejecting hooks
  - `prepareQuery` chaining, and pass-through when no hooks are registered
  - duplicate-name rejection and unregister
  - an end-to-end `runPollLoop` run in which hooks rewrite opening and follow-up rows, adjust the query input, observe events, and get `onError`
- `bun test src/turn-hooks.test.ts src/poll-loop*` -> 137 pass, 0 fail. The existing poll-loop suites are unchanged.
- `bun test` (container/agent-runner) -> 487 pass, 0 fail.
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> clean.
- `pnpm run typecheck` -> clean. `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors, with warnings already present on the base. `pnpm run format:check` -> clean.
- `pnpm test` -> host suite. The files that timed out under parallel machine load all pass when rerun alone, except `src/templates/create-agent.test.ts`, which collides on a fixed `/tmp` path with another concurrent run. The diff touches only `container/agent-runner/`, which vitest excludes.

prs.title: fix(add-codex): keep the turn open on an error Codex will retry
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A transient stream error that Codex retries on its own no longer fails the NanoClaw turn.

- **Problem**: before each automatic retry, Codex sends `error` with `willRetry: true` ([`bespoke_event_handling.rs:1055-1071`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1055-L1071)). Its protocol says such an error does not interrupt the turn. `runOneTurn` ended the turn on every `error`. A network blip therefore failed the turn with "Reconnecting... 1/5" while Codex kept going, and the real reply was dropped.
- **Fix**: an error with `willRetry: true` now yields a `progress` event and leaves the turn open. Any other error still ends the turn. When retries run out, Codex sends a final error with `willRetry: false` ([`core/src/session/turn.rs:817-831`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn.rs#L817-L831)), so the turn still ends then.
- **Behaviour change**: Codex 0.162.1 retries a lost connection without limit by default. A long outage now fails at the existing 10-minute turn timeout ("Turn timed out after 600000ms"), not at the first retry.

## Related work

Stacked on #4165, which changes the same handler, so review that first. When #4165 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to main.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Codex agents that start sub-agents keep their own turn: a sub-agent's events no longer end, fill or redirect it.

- **Problem**: Codex 0.162.1 streams every sub-agent thread it spawns on the same app-server connection ([`app-server/src/lib.rs:1291-1309`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/app-server/src/lib.rs#L1291-L1309)). Sub-agents are on by default (`multi_agent` is Stable). `runOneTurn` ignored `threadId`. As a result, a child's `turn/completed` or `error` ended the parent turn early. A child's `turn/started` moved the turn id that steer and interrupt target. The child's message text could also become the parent's reply.
- **Fix**: events from another thread now only yield `activity`. A parent waiting on a sub-agent stays alive for host-sweep, but child events no longer change the parent turn.
- **Out of scope**: an `error` that Codex will retry still ends the turn. The stacked follow-up PR fixes that.

## Related work

No issue: this bug turned up while working on the Codex image-generation fix. The change is safe to review directly because it touches only the add-codex provider payload.

Draft #4164 (image generation) changes the same handler, so expect a small context conflict next to the new guard. With this guard, a sub-agent's `imageGeneration` item is dropped before #4164's branch runs. If child images should be sent, that branch moves above the guard.

- add-codex container suites with the payload applied: 183 pass, `tsc -p container/agent-runner` clean. The only 2 failures are the `cli-tools.json` entry tests: the quick harness does not merge that file, and main fails the same 2.
- New tests in `codex.turns.test.ts`, all 3 failing on main:
  - a child `error` or `turn/completed` leaves the parent turn running;
  - child text never becomes the result;
  - abort interrupts the parent turn, not the child's.
- Not run live: a real sub-agent run needs a ChatGPT-paired VM.
