prs.title: feat(skills): add-turn-traces, per-turn agent traces in the central DB
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-turn-traces`, so an operator can see what an agent did on each turn, with the data kept in the central DB and nothing sent to an external backend.

- **Problem**: finding out which tools an agent called on a turn, with what inputs, what they returned and how long it took means reading container stderr, which is gone once the container exits. The session DBs keep only the messages.
- **Feature**: one trace per answered batch in a `turn_traces` table. A trace holds message ids, provider, configured model, status (`ok` / `error` / `incomplete`), timings, inbound content, final output, provider error, and ordered steps (mid-turn text, tool calls with input, output, error flag and duration). Text fields are capped and each turn keeps at most 200 steps.
- **Read**: `ncl traces list [--agent-group-id] [--session-id] [--status] [--limit]` returns summaries with a one-line preview. `ncl traces get <id>` returns the full trace. Both are read-only and `hostOnly`.
- **Opt-in**: installing the skill records nothing. A group is traced only while `groups/<folder>/turn-traces.enabled` exists. The check runs every turn, so it needs no respawn.
- **Retention**: `TURN_TRACE_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 3. The first trace a host process records prunes and starts an hourly prune. Every `ncl traces` read prunes first, so an expired trace is never shown.
- **Footprint**: two self-registering modules and one barrel line per tree. The host module (`src/modules/turn-traces/`) registers a `registerMigration` module migration, an unguarded `turn_trace` delivery action and the CLI resource. The container module (`container/agent-runner/src/modules/turn-traces/`) registers a turn hook.
- **Code edit**: the only edit to existing code is `hooks: withTurnTraceHooks({...})` in `providers/claude.ts`. It appends tool-hook matchers after the provider's own, so the existing PreToolUse guard still runs first.
- **Out of scope**: tool steps for non-Claude providers (they get turn-level traces), retry turns after a wrap nudge (not recorded), and exporting to OTLP (#3796 covers that). An agent-to-operator notification tool is a separate follow-up.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3904 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

Depends on #3904. This branch contains #3904's commit (merged in unchanged); only the last commit is this PR.

- #3904 turn-lifecycle hooks: the recorder attaches through `beforeTurn` / `onProviderEvent` / `onError` instead of editing `poll-loop.ts`.
- #3796 `/add-telemetry` exports OpenTelemetry spans to an external collector. This skill is the local, zero-infrastructure counterpart: a central-DB table plus `ncl`, with no collector or new dependency. The two can be installed side by side.
- #2012 `/add-usage-logging` records token and cost usage per query in `outbound.db`. It covers different data and does not overlap.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

These runs used the skill applied by hand from SKILL.md. It was then removed by hand following REMOVE.md steps 1–3, and `git status` showed only the skill folder.

- `pnpm run typecheck` -> clean
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` -> clean
- `pnpm run lint` -> 0 errors, no new warnings
- `pnpm run format:check` -> clean; container payload checked with prettier directly -> clean
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-turn-traces/SKILL.md` -> no problems
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/modules/turn-traces/` -> 6/6 pass. It covers the real modules barrel with real migrations: store, list, get, filters, unknown-status drop, container caller refused, expired trace hidden, and prune on first trace. With the host barrel line removed -> 4 fail.
- `bun test src/modules/turn-traces/` -> 8/8 pass. It covers the real turn-hook dispatch plus outbound row: one trace per batch, follow-up gets its own trace, retry not recorded, error, incomplete, step cap, nothing without the marker. With the container barrel line removed -> `turn-traces.test.ts` 0 pass. With the `claude.ts` wrap removed -> `claude-hooks.test.ts` 2 fail.
- `bun test` (full agent-runner suite, skill applied) -> 495 pass, 0 fail. The opt-in marker is what keeps existing poll-loop tests, which count outbound rows, unaffected.
- `pnpm test` (skill applied) -> 2936 pass. 3 failed with 5s timeouts on a loaded machine: `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` and `src/templates/plugin-dir.test.ts`. Rerun alone -> 238/238 pass. Unrelated to this diff.
- `src/modules/community-portal/registration.test.ts` -> passes with the skill applied. The module registers no host-lifecycle callback, because that test assumes the portal's callback is the last one.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-turn-traces skill: opt-in per-turn agent traces (tool calls, inputs/outputs, timings, model) stored in the central DB with 3-day default retention and read with `ncl traces list/get`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Privacy**: traces contain prompt content, tool inputs and tool outputs. Tracing is off until the skill is installed and a group is opted in by marker file. Default retention is 3 days, and REMOVE.md drops the table.
- **Read access**: `ncl traces` verbs are `hostOnly`. Every container caller is refused, including `cli_scope=global` agents, because traces span all groups.
- **Untrusted input**: the `turn_trace` payload comes from inside the sandbox. The host re-validates every field, rejects unknown statuses, caps text, steps and total step JSON, and takes `session_id` / `agent_group_id` from the delivering session, never from the payload. The action is registered `unguarded(...)` because it writes only a host-only row for the sending session.
- **Not a control**: the marker sits in the agent's writable workspace, so an agent can turn its own tracing off. SKILL.md says traces are for debugging, not auditing.

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-lean-tasks for minimal-context scheduled task runs
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-lean-tasks`, so a scheduled task can run cheaply on a small or local model without the agent's full context.

- **Problem**: every task fire carries the Claude Code preset, composed instructions, skills, memory, all MCP servers and the resumed session. A small model spends most of the turn reading that and often cannot drive the tools anyway.
- **Feature**: `ncl tasks create/update --lean true` runs each fire with a slim plain system prompt (name, destinations, output format), no filesystem settings, no resume, no MCP servers and no built-in tools.
- **Delivery**: the lean turn has no tools, so it writes `<message to="NAME">` and `<card to="NAME" title="...">` blocks in its final text; each block is delivered and recorded in the run log as one line (`[sent → family] ...`).
- **Render**: optional `--render "<command>"` pipes the final text through a command (stdin → stdout) before the blocks are parsed, so the model can return plain data and a script writes the message. A failing or silent command falls back to the model text.
- **Skill payload** (on `main`, like `/add-opencode`): host module registers the two task fields; agent-runner module registers a turn hook that marks lean task batches and a Claude provider wrapper that sends marked queries to a second, minimal-context instance and delivers the blocks before the poll loop sees the result. One barrel line per tree.
- **Core commit** `refactor(agent-runner): add a minimalContext provider option`: `settingSources` and the built-in tool list were not reachable through `ProviderOptions`/`QueryInput`. `minimalContext: true` makes the Claude provider load no settings and disallow its built-ins; omitted (every existing caller) the SDK options are unchanged. It can be split into its own PR if preferred.
- **Out of scope**: non-Claude providers (flag stored, task runs normally); follow-up fires pushed into a live lean query keep the lean context.

## Related work

Reviewed as a set with #3921, #3925, #3904 (maintainer grouping on #3899).

Depends on #3904, #3921, #3925 and #3931 (system prompt mode lives in #3931). The branch carries their commits until they merge; this PR's own change is the 7 files under `.claude/skills/add-lean-tasks/`.

- #3904 turn hooks (lean detection), #3921 task fields (`--lean`/`--render`), #3925 provider wrapper, #3931 `systemPromptMode: 'plain'` for the lean instance. This branch contains those four merged in; only the last two commits are this PR.

- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

With the payload applied to the tree (then removed before commit):

prs.title: feat(reborn): frugal default read/grep output to cut carried context
prs.body:
**Stacked on #5149 (disclosure).** Different lever than #5435 (compaction budget, which the full run disproved — eviction caused re-reads/quality loss). This shrinks per-call tool output so less content is *carried across turns*, **without evicting** — so no re-read balloon and no loss of active context.

The config.rs comment already names the problem: read/grep results *"ride along in every later LLM request and inflate each round-trip."* Halving the defaults:

| const | before | after |
|---|--:|--:|
| DEFAULT_READ_MAX_BYTES | 64KB | 24KB |
| DEFAULT_LINE_LIMIT | 2000 | 800 |
| MAX_OUTPUT_SIZE (grep) | 64KB | 24KB |
| DEFAULT_HEAD_LIMIT (grep) | 250 | 80 |

Agent keeps agency: `read_file` paginates via `next_offset`; grep re-queries / raises `head_limit`. So it trades a smaller default surface for occasional follow-ups, not dropped information.

Validation: full clean pinchbench (no infra failures, vs the disclosure-128k baseline) — numbers to follow.

prs.title: fix(http): raise http.save body limit so large downloads stream to disk (unblocks timeout-looping tasks)
prs.body:
## Agent-harness bug: `http.save` rejects large downloads → agent loops → turn timeout → task scores 0

### Evidence (PinchBench `task_log_syslog_auth_failures`, reborn / DeepSeek-V4-Flash)
The task scores **0.0**. Its trace shows:
```
first-party HTTP egress failed runtime_http_reason=response_body_limit_exceeded dispatch_error_kind=OutputTooLarge   (×4)
→ reborn run failed: reborn turn timed out
```
The agent fetches a multi-MB log over HTTP; ironclaw's `http.save` rejects the body for exceeding **10 MiB**, the agent retries, loops, and the turn times out → 0.

### Root cause
`http.save` streams the response body to a **file on disk**, yet `MAX_SAVE_RESPONSE_BODY_LIMIT` capped it at 10 MiB — the same order as an in-memory inline body, even though disk-save doesn't consume model context.

### Fix
Raise the save-to-disk limit (default 128 MiB, max 256 MiB) and the umbrella `MAX_HTTP_OUTPUT_BYTES` to match. The model-facing **inline** body stays bounded by the unchanged 256 KiB `MAX_INLINE_RESPONSE_BODY_LIMIT`, so nothing larger reaches the model.

### Expected impact
`task_log_syslog_auth_failures` 0 → pass (it can now fetch + process the log). One of the 13 tasks in the benchmark taxonomy's largest harness category (turn-timeout). Measured A/B (this rev vs `e754655f` baseline, same task) is running.

Tracked in nearai/benchmarks#190.

prs.title: docs(design-system): DESIGN.md governance + Storybook guidelines (Epic #7781 phase 2)
prs.body:
## Summary

- Adds **`crates/product/ironclaw_webui/frontend/DESIGN.md`** — the M3 Expressive design language as the written source of truth, plus an IronClaw implementation/governance appendix that reconciles it with the React 19 + Tailwind v4 / `--v2-*` stack.
- Surfaces it in Storybook as a **`Design/Guidelines`** MDX page, sorted first in the sidebar (enables the `*.mdx` glob, which was off).
- Adds **`.claude/rules/design-system.md`** agent governance, an `AGENTS.md` Module Specs pointer, and a design-system README link.
- **Governance only — no pixels move.** Token values, motion, fonts, the dark palette, and new agentic components stay in Phases 3–4.
- No Rust, no schema, no runtime behavior. Two docs files, one MDX page, one agent rule, two Storybook config lines, two pointer edits.

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Refs #7781 (Epic, Phases 2–3) · Refs #7042 (Phase 2 sub-issue). No issue is closed by this PR — #7042 closes when the epic's WS2 checklist is fully ticked.

## What this is

Phase 2 of the five-phase design-system program: **write the constitution, before applying it.**

| Phase | Scope | Epic |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Storybook integration & design-system catalog | #7038 — landed (PR #7750) |
| **2** | **This PR** — `DESIGN.md` + Storybook guidelines + agent rules | **#7781** (#7042) |
| 3 | Theme update & UI reskin — token values, palette, fonts, assets | #7781 |
| 4–5 | Agentic interactions & components · information architecture | #7782 |

`DESIGN.md` is the spec the Phase-3 token values are judged against, so it lands first (the epic's ⚠ ordering).

## Provenance — this is a preserved changeset, refreshed

The original PR #7043 was stacked on the Phase-1 PR #7039; both were closed once the stack became an unmergeable merge-commit tangle. Phase 1 was recreated non-stacked as #7750 and merged. **This is that preserved changeset**, re-homed and refreshed against what actually landed. What changed from the original:

- **Paths** moved `crates/ironclaw_webui` → `crates/product/ironclaw_webui` (the crate-family restructure).
- **Epic references re-pointed.** The original framed everything as "Epic #7038"; #7038 is now Phase 1 only. Replaced the single-epic framing with the phase map above.
- **Corrected the motion-policy claim.** The original said `.v2-spin` is the sole exception to the universal `animation: none`. On `main` there are three (`.v2-spin`, `.near-process`, `.oobe-card-reveal`). Per `.claude/rules/guidance-maintenance.md` rule 3 ("no universal claims without a count"), the doc now ships the grep instead of a number that will drift.
- **Token section now records the measured inventory** — 31 `--v2-*` tokens on `main`, effectively all colour — with the command that regenerates it, and notes the non-colour axes in flight as #7831. That is the reason a colour-only repaint would change the hue and leave the product looking as it does now.
- **Two open items added:** the `app.css` `!important` compat layer (#7890), and emitted-bundle verification — the suites assert Tailwind class *strings*, not computed style, so a dropped `@theme` block passes every gate (the failure mode documented on #7831).
- **Storybook MCP note updated** — the addon is now opt-in behind `STORYBOOK_MCP=1`, not unconditional.

## Decisions carried

- **Native M3X, not Material Web.** The language is realized with our own React 19 + Tailwind v4 primitives — no `<md-*>` Lit components or parallel framework. `DESIGN.md` governs *look & feel*; the epic's non-goals govern *implementation*. Where they appear to conflict, the doc states the split explicitly.
- **Token architecture is kept.** `data-theme` + `--v2-*`. Phase 3 changes values and assets, not the mechanism.

## Validation

Rust gates are **Not applicable** — this PR contains no Rust. Verified at `crates/product/ironclaw_webui/frontend`:

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint:conventions` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test:storybook` — **104 tests / 31 files passed**
- [x] `pnpm build-storybook` — succeeded; `Design/Guidelines` indexed as `design-guidelines--docs`, 105 entries
- [x] `python3 scripts/ci/check-guidance.py` — **OK** (2616 path references verified, 62 frontmatter globs live, 70 `CLAUDE.md` aliases verified)
- [x] Every relative link resolved by hand (`DESIGN.md` → rules, README → `DESIGN.md`, README → rules)
- [ ] `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy` / `cargo build` — Not applicable: no Rust in the diff

**`pnpm test`: 18 failed / 1470 passed — pre-existing and unrelated.** Identical counts with and without this change (baselined by stashing the diff and re-running). Both files (`src/design-system/theme.test.tsx`, `src/pages/chat/inspector/inspector-panel.test.tsx`) are untouched here; the local runner is Node 26 against a package engine of `>=22.22 <23`.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: none — this PR adds documentation, one Storybook docs page, and one agent rule. No product code path changes.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [ ] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: Not applicable: no behavior added. The two Storybook config lines are covered by the existing story suite, which enumerates the catalog — `build-storybook` proves the new MDX page is indexed and `Design` sorts first.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: WebUI-frontend docs only, no crate boundary crossed.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no LLM or provider interaction.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no route, page, or user flow changes.
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable: no Rust in the diff.
- Live canary: Not applicable: nothing user-visible ships.

What the tests prove: the story suite still passes unchanged (104/31) with the MDX glob enabled, so re-enabling it pulls in no stray files and breaks no existing story; `build-storybook` proves the page renders and is indexed under the right title; `check-guidance.py` proves every path this guidance names resolves against tracked state and that the new rule's `paths:` glob actually matches files — i.e. the rule will really load, which is the specific failure mode that gate exists for.

Commands run:

```
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint:conventions
pnpm test
pnpm test:storybook
pnpm build-storybook
python3 scripts/ci/check-guidance.py
```

## Security Impact

None. No permissions, network calls, secrets, file access, tool execution, or sandbox policy are touched. The `*.mdx` glob is a Storybook build-time source pattern scoped to `../src/**`.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

N/A — documentation and agent guidance only. No public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types, no prompt construction, no hashing, no status/error variants, no `serde` fields, no queues or buffers, no sandbox or host naming.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

The Storybook catalog and the agent guidance layer. The only executable change is two lines of Storybook config: the `*.mdx` stories glob and the `storySort` order. If the glob misbehaved it would surface as a Storybook build failure or a stray sidebar entry — `build-storybook` and the 104-test story suite both pass, and the index was inspected directly. The shipping SPA bundle is untouched (`.storybook/` is not part of `vite build`).

Second-order: `.claude/rules/design-system.md` auto-loads for agents reading anything under `crates/product/ironclaw_webui/frontend/**`, so it changes agent behavior in that tree. That is the intent; it is additive and states no enforcement that does not exist.

## Rollback Plan

`git revert` the single commit. Nothing is persisted, migrated, or deployed; reverting restores the previous Storybook sidebar and removes the guidance. No consumer depends on these files at runtime.

## Review Follow-Through

- The **M3X design-language section is preserved verbatim** from the approved changeset — I refreshed only the IronClaw appendix. If the language itself needs revisiting, that is a content decision for review, not drift.
- **`DESIGN.md` records open items rather than resolving them** — dark-palette derivation, motion mechanism, font licensing (Google Sans is not freely redistributable), WCAG validation, the compat layer, emitted-bundle checks. Phase 3 owns them; worth confirming the list is complete before it starts.
- **Ordering note:** #7831 (Phase 3a token axes) is open and its structural work is referenced here as in-flight. This PR does not depend on it and can merge in either order.

---

**Review track**: A (docs/tests/chore)

prs.title: feat(webui): session-event transport unification and web-app run-completion notifications
prs.body:
## Summary

- Implements the approved design `docs/internal/design/2026-08-13-webapp-run-notifications.md` end to end: unified WebUI session-event transport (typed stream contracts + one bearer-authenticated multiplexing session SSE stream) and web-app run-completion notifications (durable notices, live stream, cross-tab/device presentation arbitration, evidence-based read state, OS notifications, and a typed Web Push fallback).
- Replaces the string-typed `stream_id` + JSON round-trip on the frozen three-method `ProductSurface` with typed `ProductStreamSelector` / `ProductStreamEventEnvelope` / `ProductStreamEvent`; one shared stream driver + browser codec now feeds both the compatibility per-thread SSE (retained as an API path until its clients are ported) and the new session stream; the dormant per-thread WebSocket route is removed.
- Adds the run-completion notification core in `ironclaw_assistant`: a CAS-everything notice store on the `/run-notices` per-user mount (§5.3 state machines, 4 ordered indexes, per-owner monotonic sequence), journal-observer ingest, an arbitration coordinator (1s intent window, 2s grant ack, exactly one re-arbitration, deterministic §5.6 ranking), owner-scoped stream hub with durable replay, and four authenticated HTTP operations — mutations never ride the socket.
- Adds the §7.9 typed outbound vocabulary (`RunNotificationEventKind::RunCompleted` → `OutboundPushKind::RunCompletion`, `DeliveryTargetCapabilities.run_completions`, `OutboundPart::RunCompletion`) with web-app-exclusive capability filtering and the §7.10 fixed-copy v2 push payload; Slack/Telegram report the part unsupported.
- Reconciles with the durable notification Inbox that landed on main while this was in flight (#7697/#7700): the Inbox keeps the bell list for scheduled-trigger runs, run-completions own live presentation for every run; a read bridge marks the run's `run_completed` Inbox row read when completion evidence settles, and the bell dedupes by run id.

## Change Type

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Related #7577 (the design-doc proposal PR; its two commits are included here so this PR stands alone on `main` — if #7577 merges first this branch rebases to a no-op on those commits, and if this merges first #7577 can be closed).

## What changed, by layer

**Contracts (`ironclaw_product_contracts`, `ironclaw_host_api`, `ironclaw_extension_contracts`)**
- Typed product stream vocabulary: kind-tagged `ProductStreamSelector::{Thread, RunCompletions}`, cursor-carrying `ProductStreamEventEnvelope`, kind/payload-tagged `ProductStreamEvent::{Thread, RunCompletion}`. The frozen invoke/query/stream_events method set is unchanged (ratchet-pinned).
- New `session_transport` module: `SessionSocketTicket` + `SessionSocketTicketStore` (mint returns a nonce; consume is exactly-once), 15 s TTL, 1024 outstanding cap.
- New `run_completions` wire module: notice/grant/clear stream events (schema-stamped), intent/acknowledge/thread-read requests, unread snapshot, operation descriptors (`webui.run_completion.{intent,acknowledge,thread_read}.v1`, `webui.run-completions.unread.v1`), and bounds (128 B opaque ids, 250-notice snapshot, 32 intents/notice).
- `IngressAuthScheme::SingleUseTicket`; `OutboundPart::RunCompletion(Box<RunCompletionNoticeView>)` (typed fact, no reply content).

**WebUI backend (`ironclaw_webui`)**
- `webui_v2/session_events/`: shared `ProductStreamDriver`, browser codec (one place decides event names and cursor tokens for SSE and WS), bounded `webui.session_event.v1` protocol (8 KiB frames, 64 B sub ids, 16 subs/socket, 16 batches/sub, 5-min lifetime, connection-scoped generations, authorize-then-swap replacement, per-subscription cursors).
- Ticket mint route (POST, bearer, NoBody, 12/min) + ticket-authenticated read-only session socket (same-origin required; the bearer never appears in a URL); the socket dispatches subscribe/unsubscribe/ping only — never `ProductSurface::invoke`.
- Per-thread SSE now rides the shared driver/codec byte-identically (rollback path); the dormant per-thread WS route/handler is deleted.
- Four run-completion HTTP routes (3 × POST mutation policy 4 KiB/60 rpm, 1 × GET projection read), thin `ProductSurface` handlers, descriptor-table pins, charter rows (`session-events`, `run-completions`), CONTRACT.md route table.
- In-memory single-process ticket store (bounded, TTL-reaping, poison-recovering).

**Assistant (`ironclaw_assistant`)**
- `run_completions/`: records (purpose-separated `rcn-`/`rct-` sha-256 identities; delivery/read state machines with `grants_issued` carried through regress), store (every transition a bounded CAS via the shared helper; keyset pagination with tie-break sentinel; per-tenant durable due-owner registry for boot reconciliation), stream hub (broadcast + durable replay, `rc:{sequence}` cursor namespace so thread cursors can never resume RunCompletions), ingest (owner-visibility probe + finalized-reply-by-run requirement; retryable errors hold the durable observer cursor; no-reply anomalies advance), operations (idempotent; foreign notices collapse to NotFound; server derives all authority from the bound caller), coordinator (wake-driven + timer, bounded scans, stale-grant metrics), and the §6.1 external half: `RunCompletionExternalDelivery` implementing both `CompletionPushFallback` (CAS `PushOwned` — one replica wins; delivery through `OutboundPolicyService` + `DeliveryCoordinator` under the new `RunCompletionNotice` intent) and `LocalOsIntentPolicy` (Selected ∧ Enrolled, fail-closed).
- Read bridge: evidence-settled notices also mark the run's `run_completed` Inbox row read (observer-derived `run:{run_id}:completed` identity; best-effort, never settlement authority).

**Outbound + extensions (`ironclaw_outbound`, `ironclaw_web_app`, packages)**
- New push kind/event kind/capability field; push-target planning treats the capability-filtered explicit binding as the only RunCompletion candidate (per-thread notification policies never add completion candidates).
- Web-app adapter renders the typed part into the `web_app_notification.v2` payload — fixed copy, URL derived from the typed thread id inside the payload builder, opaque collapse tag, capped unread count. Only the web-app provider advertises `run_completions: true`.

**Composition (`ironclaw_composition`) + CLI**
- `/run-notices` joins `PER_USER_ALIASES`; notice store built over the shared consumer filesystem.
- `RunCompletionJournalObserver` (durable cursor `web-app-run-completion-observer-v1`; terminal `Completed` top-level agent turns with owner + thread scope; `occurred_at` timestamps; retryable-only `Err`).
- Coordinator spawned with boot reconciliation over the tenant due-owner registry; drained in `RebornRuntime::shutdown`.
- `SecretStoreSessionSocketTicketStore` (nonce IS the one-shot secret lease id → exactly-once across replicas), selected by `DeploymentConfig::storage_shape()` — no new Cargo features; single-process shapes use the in-memory adapter; a deployment with neither leaves the capability unadvertised (fail closed).
- Push facade + enrollment probe wired from the channel-host cone when present; Phase-1 fail-closed defaults otherwise.

**Frontend (`frontend/`)**
- `lib/session-events/`: one app-root `SessionEventClient` per page (per-subscription cursors, generation filtering, liveness pings, reconnect-hint handling, permanent degradation to SSE after repeated ticketless failures).
- `lib/run-completions/`: lazily-imported orchestrator (snapshot rebase → stream subscribe → §5.6 profile intent from merged BroadcastChannel tab state → HTTP intent → grant application on exactly one tab via profile-local test-and-set → honest acknowledgements), badge store (250-entry cache; durable projection stays authoritative), opaque browser/tab identity, thread-read + reply-render evidence reporting from the chat surface.
- Bell merge with inbox dedupe by run id; toast for in-app grants; i18n in all 11 locales; enrollment carries `browser_instance_id` inside the channel-opaque document.
- `public/sw.js`: v2 payload handling, IndexedDB test-and-set dedupe by notice id (250-entry bound), grouped fixed copy, §9.1 click selection (existing client on the path → focusable client → `openWindow`), tag-based clearing.

## Invariants preserved

- Every product mutation is authenticated HTTP; the WebSocket carries subscribe/unsubscribe/resume/ping only and never dispatches `ProductSurface::invoke` or operation ids. No event-specific streaming routes — only the ticket-authenticated read-only `/api/webchat/v2/session/websocket`.
- Frozen three-method `ProductSurface`; typed selectors replace the JSON round trip; no global cursor across logical streams (thread cursors and `rc:` cursors are disjoint namespaces).
- Chat streaming semantics unchanged: HTTP submit, cumulative phase-keyed live text, coalescing, process-local partials, durable finalized reply — the integration test pins exact byte parity between the socket's final reply and the durable timeline.
- Push payloads carry no generated or protected content (fixed copy; same-origin URLs derived from typed thread ids); streams never authorize push (the push path crosses `OutboundPolicyService` + `DeliveryCoordinator` with reply-target revalidation).
- LLM data never deleted: notices, intents, grants, and read transitions are retained with timestamps; caches (worker ledger, UI store) evict, durable rows do not.
- No new Cargo features; deployment shape decides the ticket adapter via `DeploymentConfig::storage_shape()`; strong types everywhere; async tokio; no production `unwrap`/`expect` in the new code.

## Persistence and multi-replica

- Notice store: per-notice JSON documents + 4 `ensure_index` ordered indexes + a per-owner sequence document, all mutated through the shared bounded CAS helper; racing replicas burn sequence numbers but never fork them.
- `PushOwned` is a CAS from `PendingArbitration` only — exactly one replica can win; a read between scan and claim stands the fallback down.
- Ticket exactly-once across replicas via the secret-store one-shot lease protocol; in-memory adapter for single-process shapes.
- Boot reconciliation: ingest CAS-marks the owner in a per-tenant due registry *before* the notice write (registry overflow fails retryably and holds the observer cursor), the coordinator wakes each due owner once at startup, and empty scans clear the registry.
- Stream lag → rebase from the durable unread snapshot; the client resubscribes from the snapshot's resume sequence.

## Compatibility and rollback

- Per-thread SSE is retained and served by the same driver/codec — turning `features.session_events` off (or the shared ticket store being absent) reverts every browser to today's transport with no data migration.
- Wire-tolerant records (`version` fields, serde defaults — `grants_issued`, `agent_id`/`project_id` are default-tolerant for earlier rows).
- The v1 push payload continues to work; v2 adds optional fields older service workers ignore.
- The removed per-thread WS route was dormant (no production caller); its descriptor/handler/tests were deleted, not stubbed.
- Inbox reconciliation is additive: without the bridge the two systems still function, merely with an unread inbox row until manual mark-read.

## Privacy and security

- Single-use tickets: replay rejected, expiry + tenant re-check at upgrade, caller identity injected host-side, same-origin enforced before upgrade, the long-lived bearer never enters a WebSocket URL.
- All arbitration identifiers (`browser_instance_id`, `tab_id`, notice/grant ids, thread tags) are opaque and purpose-separated; client claims cannot mint permission or targets — `local_os` is validated server-side against live target selection + host-owned enrollment, fail-closed on backend uncertainty.
- Foreign notice ids collapse to `NotFound`; observability is sanitized (counts and ids, never content).

## Test Strategy

User behavior: a user asks a question, switches tabs/apps or closes the browser, and is told exactly once — on the right surface — when the reply is ready; opening the thread (or watching it render) clears the notification everywhere without manual bookkeeping.

Risk areas:
- [x] Browser
- [x] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: notice store (create/idempotence, intents bounded+replacing, grant lifecycle state checks, push-ownership single winner, read settlement, keyset pagination, due-owner registry), coordinator (ranking, local_os gating, one-re-arbitration-then-fallback, boot reconciliation, read untracking, fallback ownership), records round-trips + identity separation, session protocol bounds, codec, ticket stores (in-memory + secret-lease adapter incl. replay + concurrent single-winner), wire-shape tests in product_contracts, web-app v2 payload grammar, the web-app `RegistrationDocument` grammar (keys/agent/correlation id, bounds, rejection), the composition enrollment probe and journal-observer filter (per-exclusion), the push facade at the caller seam (`run_delivery_contract.rs`: capability-filtered target, CAS ownership, typed part, exactly-once re-drive, `local_os` selection × enrollment matrix), the operations tier (foreign notices → NotFound; `thread_read` drains past one page and never past the rendered sequence), the stream hub's channel lifecycle, and the four run-completion routes through the real WebUI router (`webui_v2_handlers_contract.rs`); frontend vitest suites (session client ×5, i18n coverage, device-push correlation, `service-worker.test.ts` driving `public/sw.js` against a scripted worker scope, plus the existing suite — 1,509 green).
- Reborn integration: `tests/integration/session_events.rs` — a completed turn streams over one real session-WebSocket subscription and its final frame is byte-identical to the durable HTTP timeline reply; two logical subscriptions on one socket deliver their own threads independently.
- Reborn integration: `tests/integration/run_completion_notifications.rs` — the production `RunCompletionJournalObserver` registered on the harness's real process journal turns a completed user turn into exactly one durable unread notice carrying the run/thread identity, and a second turn extends the owner's monotonic sequence.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable — no model-behavior change; the loop/driver path is untouched.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable in this PR — OS-notification/service-worker flows need a headed browser + push service. `frontend/src/lib/service-worker.test.ts` evaluates `public/sw.js` against a scripted worker scope and drives its own `push`/`notificationclick` listeners (one presentation per notice id, grouped fixed copy, same-origin deep-link collapse, v1 payloads, the §9.1 click order); IndexedDB is absent there, so that exercises the memory-ledger path — the IndexedDB ledger and real display are the §15 headed-browser follow-up.
- Backend or runtime: full workspace suite; architecture gates (dependency boundaries incl. re-pinned product_contracts ceiling, retired-taxonomy, typename ratchet with the justified `LocalOs*` entries, extension-specificity, struct/test-support ratchet, charter maps, same-layer edges).
- Live canary: Not applicable — feature is fail-closed off until a deployment advertises `features.session_events`.

What the tests prove: the socket transport delivers exactly the durable truth (byte parity with the HTTP timeline); subscriptions are isolated per selector and cursor-resumable; tickets are single-use under concurrency across replicas; every notice state transition is CAS-guarded with one push winner; arbitration follows §5.6 deterministically with the §5.4 bounds actually enforced (the tests caught and fixed a lost-`grants_issued` bug); read evidence settles notices and bridges to the Inbox; capability filtering structurally restricts completion pushes to the web-app channel.

Commands run: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` · `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings` (clean) · `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test --workspace` — 253 test binaries, 9,522 tests passed (includes the root integration suite and the architecture gates); the Postgres backend-matrix legs re-run green with the colima `DOCKER_HOST` socket, and the one remaining failure (`smoke::docker_reborn_entrypoint_uses_railway_volume_mount_for_home`) reproduces identically on pristine `origin/main` (macOS symlinked tmpdir vs the Railway containment check — pre-existing, unrelated) · `pnpm test` (1,493 green) + `pnpm lint` + `pnpm build` (bundle budgets pass: /chat 224.8 KB gzip vs 226.0 KB pin) · `python3 scripts/ci/docs_publication_boundary.py`.

Review-round 3 (2026-09-01, after merging current `main`): `cargo fmt --all` · clippy `--all-targets --all-features`, `--all-targets` (default lane) and `--lib` (prod shape) over ironclaw_assistant, ironclaw_composition, ironclaw_webui, ironclaw_web_app, ironclaw_web_app_extension, ironclaw_outbound, plus `-p ironclaw_integration_tests --all-targets --all-features`, all `-D warnings` · `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests` · targeted suites: assistant `run_completions` / `run_delivery` / `run_delivery_contract`, composition `run_completion*`, web_app, web_app_extension, outbound `delivery_target_capabilities`, webui `webui_v2_handlers_contract` + `webui_v2_descriptors_contract`, root bins `reborn_integration_run_completion_notifications` + `reborn_integration_session_events` · `pnpm test` (1,509 green) + `pnpm lint` + `pnpm build` (bundle budgets pass: /chat 225.0 KB gzip vs 226.0 KB pin) · `bash scripts/ci/check-composition-budget.sh` (mass + dispatch within budget after moving new composition tests to sibling files) · `python3 scripts/ci/docs_publication_boundary.py`.

## Security Impact

Adds one new authenticated ingress (the single-use-ticket session WebSocket) and four authenticated HTTP mutations/reads; no new secrets, no new network egress paths (completion pushes ride the existing web-app delivery channel and its declared egress hosts), no tool-execution or sandbox changes. Tickets are random, single-use, 15 s, caller-bound, consumed by the bearer middleware before the handler runs; the bearer never enters a WebSocket URL; same-origin is enforced before upgrade; inbound frames are bounded at 8 KiB at both transport and parser. The socket carries subscribe/unsubscribe/ping only and never dispatches `ProductSurface::invoke`.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: `SessionSocketTicket` is minted only by the ticket-mint handler from the authenticated caller and consumed only by the bearer middleware; `TrustedInboundTurnRequest` is untouched; notice ownership is derived from the bound caller, never from a browser payload.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive: no prompt construction in this PR; push payloads and stream frames carry fixed copy and typed ids only.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose: notice ids and thread tags are purpose-separated SHA-256 prefixes (`web-app-run-completion/v1`, `web-app-run-completion-collapse/v1`); neither is an authorization token.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: `IngressAuthScheme::SingleUseTicket`, `OutboundPart::RunCompletion`, `OutboundPushKind::RunCompletion`, `RunNotificationEventKind::RunCompleted`, `DeliveryIntent::RunCompletionNotice`; downstream matches audited — Slack/Telegram report the part unsupported (tested), the web-app adapter renders it (tested), `rg -n "OutboundPart::" crates` shows no unmatched site.
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields fail closed: `DeliveryTargetCapabilities.run_completions` defaults `false` (tested with legacy JSON); notice `grants_issued`/`agent_id`/`project_id` defaults keep older rows readable and a missing `agent_id` makes a notice ineligible for push.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic: 8 KiB frames, 16 subscriptions/socket, 16 batches/subscription, 3 connections/caller, 5-min lifetime, 250-notice snapshot/replay pages, 32 intents/notice, 64-slot broadcast per owner with lag→rebase, 250-entry UI/worker ledgers, `saturating_*` on sequences and counters; hub channels exist only while subscribed.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics: store errors map through one translation (`operations::surface_error`) to sanitized `ProductSurfaceError` codes; ingest splits retryable (`Unavailable`) from terminal; outbound failures keep their `failure_kind`.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary: N/A — no runtime lane or sandbox change.

## Database Impact

None to relational schema. New persisted data is additive filesystem-plane records on the `/run-notices` per-user mount (notice JSON documents, four `ensure_index` ordered indexes, a per-owner sequence document) and a per-tenant due-owner document on `/tenant-shared`; all backends (PostgreSQL, libSQL, local filesystem) are selected by composition and reached through the shared CAS helper — no backend branch, no migration.

## Blast Radius

WebUI transport (session socket + compatibility SSE now share one driver/codec), the assistant's new `run_completions` module, composition wiring (observer, coordinator, ticket-store selection by storage shape, `/run-notices` alias), the outbound push vocabulary (Slack/Telegram reject the new part; only the web-app provider advertises the capability), and the SPA (session client, notification bell merge, service worker v2 payloads). Chat streaming semantics are unchanged and pinned byte-for-byte against the durable timeline.

## Rollback Plan

Feature-flag-shaped, no data migration: leaving `features.session_events` unadvertised (or the ticket store absent) returns every browser to the compatibility SSE path; not wiring the observer/coordinator leaves notice records inert; the v1 push payload keeps working and older service workers ignore v2 fields; capability defaults are `false` so no completion push can be planned without the web-app provider. Reverting the PR leaves only additive, wire-tolerant records behind.

## Review Follow-Through

Round 1–2 (CodeRabbit, IronLoop) threads are answered inline. Round 3 (the multi-agent review + approach audit) is triaged in the PR comment "Review round 3": fixed, or left as designed with reasons. Items that still need a maintainer decision or a follow-up: (1) whether same-browser live-stream arbitration should move from pages into the service worker as the design's §5.1 table originally assigned (now recorded as an implementation note in the design doc); (2) sweeping expired one-shot lease rows in the secret store (shared with the OAuth PKCE flow, not specific to tickets); (3) `RunCompletionNoticeId`/`ThreadTag` newtypes across the three crates that carry them; (4) per-owner due-registry markers if measured CAS contention on the per-tenant document ever demands it; (5) the §15 headed-browser suite.

---

**Review track**: C (security/runtime/persistence: new authenticated transport, durable notice records, outbound push vocabulary)

## Reviewed gate re-pins (called out per policy)

- `ironclaw_product_contracts` size ceiling: 16,581 → 16,791 (session transport vocabulary) → 17,130 (run-completions wire module); counts read from the gate on this tree; dated notes appended.
- `/chat` bundle budget: 223,500 → 226,000 (measured 224.8 KB on this tree; eager weight is the badge cache + 4 i18n keys; everything deferrable is dynamically imported and the trim that kept the protocol module out of the eager graph is documented in the note).
- Typename ratchet allowlist: `LocalOsIntentPolicy` / `DenyLocalOsIntents` (Bucket-3 domain vocabulary — the `local_os` presentation lane, not a deployment tier).
- WebUI CONTRACT.md handler charter: new `session-events` and `run-completions` sub-owners; assistant AGENTS.md charter row extended for the run_completions module.

## Genuine risks / follow-ups

- Browser E2E for the service-worker surfaces (OS notification display, click-through, push dedupe) is unit-tested but not yet driven in a headed browser; proposed as the §15 follow-up suite.
- Coverage floor: `coverage-floor.toml` recapture needs this PR's CI run output (procedure unchanged).
- The arbitration windows (1 s / 2 s) are host constants per the design; telemetry may motivate moving them into `DeploymentConfig` later — explicitly not Cargo features.
- Phase-1 scope note: local-OS grants require enrollment correlation, which new enrollments now carry; legacy registrations degrade to profile-level presence until they re-enroll.
- The Inbox partition means a scheduled run appears in the bell via the Inbox row while foreground runs appear via completion rows; if product later wants one unified row source, the bridge + dedupe give a clean migration point.

### Transport decision (2026-09-02): one session SSE stream, no WebSocket, no tickets, no client fallback

The session WebSocket and its single-use ticket subsystem are replaced, before merge, by one server-sent event stream that works wherever HTTP works:

- **`POST /api/webchat/v2/session/events`** (`webui.v2.session_events`): the page opens it with a header-authenticated `fetch`; the JSON body names the complete subscription set (1 to 16 selectors, each with its own resume cursor, validated before any subscription task exists) and the response is `text/event-stream` carrying the same `webui.session_event.v1` frames as before (`subscribed`, `event`, `subscription_error`, `reconnect_hint`), each as one SSE event named by its type. It shares the per-caller `SseCapacity` budget and the five-minute lifetime with the compatibility route.
- **Subscription changes reconnect.** The set is fixed per connection; the client coalesces subscribe/unsubscribe within 25 ms and reconnects with every selector's last cursor, which is the same resume path it runs on lifetime expiry. The stream rate limit goes from 30 to 60 per minute per caller so thread navigation never trips it.
- **Deleted:** the WebSocket route, loop, and inbound control protocol; the ticket contract module, both ticket stores, the secret-lease adapter and its storage-shape selection, the CLI wiring, and the `SingleUseTicket` auth scheme; the `features.session_events` flag; the per-thread SSE hook (`useSSE`) and the transport-choice hook; `tokio-tungstenite` from every manifest and the `ws` feature from the WebUI's axum dependency; the `SecretStorePort::delete_lease` addition from round 4 (it existed only for tickets).
- **No polling.** The shared driver now requires a live continuation and fails a subscription (retryable) when the surface offers none, and the surface keeps the live subscription open on a quiet thread instead of handing back a drain-only page that the driver used to re-poll every 1 to 3 seconds. The compatibility per-thread route alone keeps its legacy idle poll for drain-only surfaces (`ProductStreamDriver::new_with_legacy_idle_polling`) until that route and its API-client tests are retired in a follow-up; the SPA no longer uses it.
- **No fallback.** A stream that cannot connect reports `reconnecting` and keeps retrying with capped, jittered backoff; durable cursors guarantee nothing is lost while disconnected. Networks that block streaming responses are not handled by a second transport.

Coverage moved with the transport: the session-stream contract tests (multiplexing and failure isolation, body bounds and mutation-shaped bodies, unissued cursors, independent resume cursors, the no-polling contract, shared capacity, slot release on client drop), the bearer-only auth route test, the assembled-app auth test, the rate-limit refund contract, the integration scenario over the real stack, the fetch-stream client tests, and the Python e2e scenario. The composition mass pin drops to 43,161 lines and the dispatch pin to 837 with the ticket adapter gone; the eager `/chat` bundle budget drops to 219 KB gzip.

Follow-ups: retire the per-thread SSE route and the legacy idle poll once its ten e2e scenarios and the API-client test support are ported; the WebSocket same-origin middleware stays armed but matches no route today.

### Review round 4 (2026-09-02): local multi-agent review + fix pass

A local (unposted) eight-reviewer code review of the branch produced 67 findings; the ones that survived verification are fixed here, the rest are recorded with reasons in the branch's `.review/triage.md` (git-ignored).

**Bugs fixed**
- Coordinator: a grant the browser regressed (`stale_state` / `effect_failed`) re-arbitrated the same stored intent every window forever. The pending loop now honours the §5.4 budget (first grant + exactly one re-arbitration) and falls back, matching the expiry path. Regression test `browser_regressed_grant_re_arbitrates_once_then_falls_back`, sabotage-verified.
- Session socket cursors: the run-completion client sent a raw `rc:N` as `after_cursor`, which never parsed, so every boot replayed history from the origin. The client now sends the JSON-quoted token the codec issues, and the server rejects a cursor it never issued with a typed `subscription_error` instead of silently resuming from the origin (`session_websocket_rejects_resume_cursors_it_never_issued`).
- `claim_push`: the idempotent "same delivery id" arm let a second replica push the same notice; PushOwned now conflicts for every later claimer, so the cross-replica exactly-once claim holds.
- Client: hidden tabs no longer claim `in_app` grants; an expired-lease `reply_rendered` acknowledgement (409) no longer clears the notice locally and falls back to `reply_observed`; `thread_read` advances only through completions whose reply this tab rendered (history or live), so a live notice for the open thread is not settled before its reply is on screen.
- Session socket: distinct-subscription cap no longer double-counts a staged replacement; `subscribe` frames are budgeted per socket (32 per 10 s → `too_many_subscribe_frames`), with a contract test.
- Socket tickets: consuming a ticket now deletes both the secret and the lease row (new `SecretStorePort::delete_lease`, all six implementors), so a socket connect no longer leaves a permanent row in replica-shared shapes. Tickets minted but never consumed remain the periodic-sweep follow-up.
- Stream hub: broadcast channels are swept on subscribe, so the map is bounded by owners with a live subscriber rather than every owner that ever connected; `notice_written` skips the unread-count query when nobody is listening; failed owner passes back off exponentially (1 s → 60 s).

**Quality**
- The run-completion journal observer moved from composition into `ironclaw_assistant::run_completions::observer`, beside the other product journal observers; composition only constructs and subscribes it (composition mass drops accordingly).
- Notice store: the 17 inherent methods plus their forwarding trait impl are one trait impl (store.rs 1,320 → 1,176 lines). One `unread_count_for_thread` helper and constant serve both the stream badge and push copy (they disagreed, 99 vs 100). Typed `RunCompletionOwner` keys replace stringified tuples; the Inbox read bridge is a required constructor argument; `settle_read` folds the three copied read-settlement sequences; `From<RunCompletionStoreError>` carries the ingest retry contract once.
- Socket loop: one `close_session_socket` teardown and one emit match; descriptor policy helpers for the two ticketed routes; `event_body` is infallible; `SecretLeaseId: FromStr` replaces the serde round trip; the push-facade selection in composition is one two-arm match.
- Docs and names: stale `stream_events_ws` references, Phase-1 port docs, the `webui.run-completions.unread.v1` spelling (now `webui.run_completion.unread.v1`), storage-key scheme, `sseStatus` → `eventsStatus`, i18n placement, contract module map rows, and the Python e2e scenario that still dialled the removed per-thread WebSocket route (ported to the ticketed session socket).

**Coverage added after the tests-reviewer pass**
- `stream_events` with the `RunCompletions` selector: 503 when the notification services are not wired, durable replay under the `rc:<sequence>` cursor namespace, strict-after resume, and 400 for cursors from another namespace or with a malformed sequence (`run_completions_selector_replays_under_the_rc_cursor_namespace_and_rejects_foreign_cursors`).
- Push facade fail-closed branches: a failing enrollment probe denies `local_os`; a conflicting push claim stands down with no egress.
- Observer retry contract through the journal-facing caller: a backend outage holds the cursor (`Err`), a shape rejection advances it, and the replayed commit ingests exactly once.
- Operation bounds and the forged-grant 409; `presented` and `effect_failed` acknowledgement transitions.
- `SecretStorePort::delete_lease` semantics; ticket consume reclaims both the secret and the lease row.
- Session socket `unsubscribe` acknowledgement and the distinct-subscription cap with an active-id replacement exemption.
- The web-app run-completion push payload (percent-encoded thread deep link, dedupe fields, capped count).
- Frontend: the sequence comparator, the unread cache (rebase, clears, eviction), and the wire parsers.

Remaining coverage follow-ups (harness work, recorded in `.review/triage.md`): the intent → grant → acknowledge and `thread_read` flows through the in-process harness's `ProductSurface::invoke`, composition's push-fallback selection with the channel-host cone, the cross-tab intent tie-break and orchestrator grant state machine, `useThreadEvents` fallback selection, and the coordinator shutdown abort path.

**Pushed back / follow-ups** (details in `.review/triage.md`): replacing the ticket subsystem with a subprotocol-carried bearer (design decision), republishing on regress so re-arbitration sees fresh intents (§6.1 row, follow-up), moving ingest off the journal delivery task, snapshot-derived unread counts, batching the inbox read bridge, concurrent owner passes, the due-registry mark race (millisecond window, notice stays visible), reconnect jitter, and typing the persisted notice ids with the host newtypes (open maintainer decision).

prs.title: ci(webui): publish Storybook to Chromatic as a non-blocking lane
prs.body:
> **Rescoped 2026-08-31.** This PR was originally the Chromatic lane **plus** the design-token axes. The token half — `app.css` axes, the `Button` migration, the `Tokens/*` sheets, `check-token-bundle.ts` and its contract suite — is now absorbed unchanged into **#8011** (the M3 reskin), which needs it as its base. What remains here is the CI lane, which never touched a component or a token. **4 files, +665 / −3.**

## Summary

- Adds a **non-blocking `webui-v2-chromatic` lane** to `code_style.yml` that publishes the built Storybook catalog, so the Phase 3 reskin has a visual-regression surface with an accumulating baseline.
- Adds `scripts/ci/ws12_workflow_contracts.py` and an **18-case contract suite** that pins the lane's security-relevant properties, each by sabotaging the checked-in workflow and proving the check fails.
- Documents it in the frontend README's *Visual regression* section.
- **Runs only on pushes to `main`, never on `pull_request`** — a security boundary, not scheduling.
- No Rust, no schema, no runtime behavior, and now no component or token either.

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Refs #7781, Refs #7782 — no issue is closed by this PR.

## The security boundary, and why the lane looks the way it does

The first version of this lane ran on `pull_request` and gated on the secret being present. That is unsafe, and it is the finding that shaped everything else here:

**Same-repository PR branches DO receive repository secrets**, and the publish executes the checked-out tree's own `build-storybook` script. A contributor could edit that script, `.storybook/`, or any build-time module to read `CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN` out of the environment. Skipping forks never covered it, because the dangerous case is the same-repo branch.

So the lane runs only on trusted pushes to `main`. The cost is that **PRs get no visual diff of their own** — only `main` publishes baselines. Restoring per-PR diffing safely needs the untrusted-build/trusted-publish split: build the catalog in a secretless PR job, upload it as an artifact, and publish from a `workflow_run` job that never checks out PR code. That is follow-up work, and the reasoning is recorded in the workflow comment block so the next person doesn't helpfully re-add `pull_request`.

Other properties, each of which exists for a reason and is pinned by a test:

- **Probe before checkout.** The token probe is a step (no `secrets` context in a job-level `if:`) and runs *before* checkout, so an unprovisioned repository pays nothing for this lane.
- **`pnpm dlx chromatic`, not `chromaui/action`.** GitHub resolves every `uses:` during *Set up job*, before step-level `if:` runs — an action would have to be pinned and reachable even on runs where the publish is skipped, the opposite of inert.
- **Exact version pin** via a `CHROMATIC_CLI_VERSION` repository variable. `latest`, ranges and wildcards are rejected: a visual-baseline tool that silently changes version changes the baseline with it.
- **`--exit-zero-on-changes`** — during a reskin the visual changes *are* the deliverable; only a Chromatic error fails the step.
- **`--auto-accept-changes main`** — now that `main` is the only branch that publishes, it is also the only place the accepted baseline can advance.
- **Deliberately absent from the `code-style` roll-up `needs:` list** — the optional lane #7782 WS6 asks for, promoted to a required gate only once the baseline is proven stable.
- **`fetch-depth: 0`** — Chromatic diffs against an ancestor build; under the depth-1 checkout the other jobs use, it cannot find a baseline.

## What six review rounds actually changed

Every round found the same defect class, and it is worth stating plainly because it is the reason this PR has a contract suite at all: **a check that accepts the presence of a marker as proof of the property the marker stands for.**

1. **Round 1** — the token exposure above, plus probe ordering and the exact-version guard.
2. **Round 2** — the validator matched markers anywhere in the job body, so the comment block *explaining* the security gate could have satisfied the gate. Trigger now read from the job's `if:` alone, publish flags from the publish step alone, both comment-stripped.
3. **Round 3** — `--auto-accept-changes main` was unpinned; dropping it would freeze the baseline at the last manual acceptance with the suite still green.
4. **Round 4** — the condition check asserted the `if:` *contains* `github.event_name == 'push'`. `(push && main) || pull_request` contains it, and reopens the round-1 hole. The condition must now be a pure conjunction: any `pull_request` mention or any `||` is rejected.
5. **Round 5** — YAML comment-stripping became quote-aware, because `if: … # … 'push' …` carried every marker while the executable condition ran on `pull_request`.
6. **Round 6** — Bash word boundaries: `true;# --exit-zero-on-changes` never executes but carried the marker. And the version guard was pinned by presence rather than effect — nothing tied the validated variable to the command, so `pnpm dlx` must now interpolate `${CHROMATIC_CLI_VERSION}`.

## Validation

Rust gates **not applicable** — no Rust in this diff.

- [x] `python3 scripts/ci/test_ws12_workflow_contracts.py` — the contract suite, including the 18 `ChromaticVisualLane` cases
- [x] Each pinned property verified by sabotaging the checked-in workflow and confirming the check fails
- [ ] `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `build` — Not applicable: no Rust

**The publish path has still never executed** — no `CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN` is provisioned. That is why its properties are pinned statically rather than proven by a green run, and it is the main thing a reviewer should stay skeptical about.

Local note: the suite reports 175 tests / 9 errors on a machine with Python 3.9 — `enterContext` needs 3.11+. Identical on the unrescoped branch, so it is environmental; CI's Python is unaffected.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: none. This adds a CI lane; no product code path changes.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions <!-- handles a repository secret -->
- [ ] External provider
- [ ] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: `scripts/ci/test_ws12_workflow_contracts.py` — 18 `ChromaticVisualLane` cases covering trusted-event gating, the pure-conjunction condition, probe ordering, the exact-version guard and its interpolation into the command, `--exit-zero-on-changes`, the baseline flag, and absence from the roll-up.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: CI workflow only, no crate boundary crossed.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no route or UI change.
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable: no Rust.
- Live canary: Not applicable: the publish path is unprovisioned.

What the tests prove: every security-relevant property of the lane fails the suite when removed from the checked-in workflow — which is the only available evidence, since the publish path cannot execute without a token.

Commands run:

```
python3 scripts/ci/test_ws12_workflow_contracts.py
```

## Security Impact

**Yes — this PR exists partly to get it right.** It handles `CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN`. The lane is restricted to pushes to `main` so PR-authored build code never executes with the secret in the environment; see the boundary section above. No other permission, network path or credential is touched.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

N/A for the Reborn runtime specifically — no policy/evidence types, prompts, hashing, status variants, `serde` fields, queues or sandbox naming. The trust boundary this PR *does* touch is CI secret exposure, covered above and pinned by the contract suite.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

One added workflow job plus a Python contract module and its tests. The job is outside the `code-style` roll-up, so it cannot block a PR. If the lane misbehaves it fails in isolation; if the token is unset it skips green. Nothing in the application build path changes.

## Rollback Plan

`git revert`. The lane is additive and non-blocking; reverting removes the job and its tests with no consumer left behind.

## Review Follow-Through

- **The rescope makes this diff strictly smaller than what was last reviewed** — nothing was added, only the token half removed. It was pushed as a commit rather than a force-push so the review history stays intact.
- **The publish path remains unexercised.** Provisioning the token is the step that would turn static pins into a real green run.
- **Per-PR visual diffing is deliberately absent** and wants the untrusted-build/trusted-publish split as follow-up.

---

**Review track**: C (security/CI)

prs.title: fix(reborn): auto-activate web-access and Brave-backed web_search so agents discover real web search
prs.body:
## Summary

reborn treats every first-party integration (Gmail, Slack, GitHub, `web-access`, ...) as an opt-in extension-catalog entry. `extension_search`/`extension_install`/`extension_activate` are always in the model's tool list (they're in the hardcoded `CORE_TOOL_NAMES` progressive-disclosure allowlist — **this is not a tool-disclosure gap**), but nothing in the base prompt/toolset ever points the model at that catalog, so it never has a reason to go looking for `web-access` (or `web_search`, added below). Any production reborn agent asked a question needing current information silently falls back to whatever raw tools it already has (e.g. `http`) with no way to discover a URL.

`web-access` is already a zero-config, trust-policy-approved first-party extension (Exa-MCP-backed search + `get_content`, no credentials needed). This PR auto-installs and activates it once at runtime-composition time, the same way `bootstrap_nearai_mcp` already auto-activates the `nearai` extension when NEAR AI credentials are configured — just simpler, since there's no credential-submit step or durable-storage gate to worry about.

- `web_access_bootstrap::bootstrap_web_access` (new): checks the current lifecycle phase for the runtime's tenant-operator identity, installs (if `Discovered`) then activates (if not already `Active`) — and **respects an explicit prior `Disabled`/`Removed` choice** rather than overriding it.
- Called once from `build_local_runtime`, immediately after the existing `bootstrap_nearai_mcp` call (same call site, same pattern).

## Update: real, credentialed Brave Search (`web_search`), gated on `BRAVE_API_KEY`

`web-access`'s Exa MCP backend is zero-config but rate-shared/free-tier. `web_search` is a separate, already-registry-published, fully-built first-party WASM tool that calls the real Brave Search API — it just had no auto-activation path either, so an operator who set `BRAVE_API_KEY` never actually got it used.

- `web_search_bootstrap::bootstrap_web_search_brave` (new): same install-then-activate pattern as `web_access_bootstrap`, but gated on a real credential — **only runs if `BRAVE_API_KEY` is set** (`web_search_bootstrap_api_key_from_env` returns `None` for unset/empty, and the bootstrap short-circuits to `NotConfigured` with no install/activate at all in that case).
- `web-access` and `web_search` share the same model-facing `web_search` display name (see `ironclaw_runner::tool_disclosure`), so only one may be active — `build_local_runtime` tries the Brave bootstrap first and only falls back to `bootstrap_web_access` (Exa) when `WebSearchBootstrapOutcome::leaves_web_access_available()` is true (i.e. no key configured).
- The `brave_api_key` secret is provisioned under the **tenant-shared scope** (`owner_scope.tenant_shared_managed_scope()`), not the bootstrap caller's own `(tenant, user)` — the dispatch-time credential pre-flight (`secret_owner_scope`) only ever checks the real invocation caller's own scope, then falls back to the tenant-shared scope, never an arbitrary third scope. Provisioning anywhere else left the secret invisible to every real capability invocation (silent `AuthRequired` regardless of who called it).
- **`WasmHostSecrets` implementation** (new `WasmRuntimeSecretsAdapter` in `ironclaw_host_runtime`): a WASM guest's own `secret-exists`/`secret-get` host calls (e.g. `web_search`'s own `near::agent::host::secret_exists` pre-flight before attempting its Brave HTTP call) are a *separate* mechanism from the existing `WasmRuntimeCredentialProvider` (which only injects credentials into the tool's own outbound HTTP headers). `DenyWasmHostSecrets` (unconditional `false`) was the only implementation anywhere in the codebase, so `web_search` could never proceed past its own credential check even once the secret was genuinely provisioned and visible everywhere else. Fixed by resolving via the same `secret_owner_scope` helper that already backs the other two paths, swapped into `host_for_scope` per-invocation alongside the existing HTTP adapter swap.

### Verification (Brave update)

Verified end-to-end against a real 165-task GAIA benchmark run (via `nearai/nearai-bench`), not just unit tests:
- 1,405 real `web_search.search` calls across the run, 99.9% succeeded (1,404/1,405) — genuine Brave Search API responses (arxiv, USGS, Nature, MapQuest, etc.), not stubs or errors.
- Confirmed `BRAVE_API_KEY` unset → falls back to `web-access`/Exa correctly (existing behavior preserved, regression-tested).
- Full `ironclaw_reborn_composition` test suite passes (1387 unit tests + all integration binaries), `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean.

## Verification (original web-access/Exa fix)

Verified end-to-end against a real benchmark (GAIA, via `nearai/nearai-bench`) rather than just unit tests:
- **Before**: a task needing a real web lookup scored 0 — the agent had only blind `http` with no way to find a URL to fetch.
- **After**: the same task's trace shows `web-access.search` → `web-access.get_content` calls, and it passes.

Full `ironclaw_reborn_composition` test suite passes (1562 unit tests + all integration binaries), plus `cargo check --workspace`.

Two existing tests needed updates since they assumed `web-access` starts un-installed:
- `local_dev_web_access_installs_activates_and_dispatches_through_host_runtime` → renamed `..._is_auto_installed_activated_and_dispatches_through_host_runtime`; now asserts the auto-bootstrap guarantee directly instead of manually installing/activating first.
- `local_dev_extension_lifecycle_tools_manage_visible_extension_surface` (uses `web-access` as its example for the generic install/activate/remove capability-handler round trip): now asserts the already-active starting state, then does a remove → reinstall → reactivate round trip (still exercises all four lifecycle capability handlers), using the real tenant-operator identity for the ownership-sensitive remove/reinstall calls (the auto-bootstrapped install is Tenant-owned, not owned by the generic test-fixture caller the file's other tests use).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_reborn_composition --features test-support` — 1387 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_host_runtime` — all passed
- [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_reborn_composition -p ironclaw_host_runtime -p ironclaw_first_party_extensions --features test-support --tests -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] End-to-end verification via GAIA benchmark tasks (0 → 1 score flips for both web-access and web_search paths; live 165-task run confirms Brave search working at scale)

**Known follow-up**: this branch is currently based on an older `main` snapshot and shows as conflicting against current `main` — needs a rebase before merge (tracked separately; the underlying architecture moved the extension-package catalog to a new self-contained per-package module system in `ironclaw_first_party_extensions::packages`, which this PR's `web_search` package will need to move into as well).
