prs.title: feat(webui): operator surface for the IronHub agent link
prs.body:
## Summary

- An operator can only obtain the IronHub register URL and install the hub-minted shared key through the CLI today, so a deployment cannot complete an agent link from the WebUI at all. This adds that surface to the Extensions page.
- The panel shows the register URL to paste into IronHub, reports whether a key is stored and whether the register gateway is actually running on one, accepts a key, and removes a stored key.
- `IronhubLinkAdminService` is declared in `ironclaw_product_contracts` and implemented in `ironclaw_extension_manager::ironhub`, next to `RebornIronhubLinkService` and `IronhubSharedKey`. No new dependency edges: that crate already depends on `ironclaw_secrets` and `ironclaw_product_contracts`, and already stores operator-set deployment credentials through the same substrate in `admin_configuration.rs`.
- The key is written to the encrypted standalone secret store under a fixed handle, never to plaintext state. `IRONHUB_AGENT_SHARED_KEY` keeps its existing precedence, so nothing about the current env-based deployment path changes.
- One ratchet raise: `ironclaw_product_contracts` 15909 to 15970, for the port and its wire DTOs. Declaration only. `scripts/ci/composition-budget.toml` is unchanged.

## Change Type

- [x] New feature
- [x] Security

## Linked Issue

Related #5409. That PR carried the deep-link gateway and its WebUI half onto Reborn and was closed unmerged; the backend landed separately afterwards, the operator-facing half did not.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings` (CI, both matrix lanes)
- [x] `cargo build` (CI)
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `ironclaw_product_contracts`, `ironclaw_extension_manager`, `ironclaw_composition`, `ironclaw_assistant`, `ironclaw_webui`, `ironclaw`, `ironclaw_architecture_tests` (124 suites, 3714 tests), plus the frontend suite (141 files, 1254 tests)
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` if database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed
- [ ] Manual testing
- [ ] `review-pr` / `pr-shepherd --fix`

All eight CI lanes are green on `c1c7d0510`: Code Style, Tests (Reborn), Reborn E2E, Platform & Compat, Regression Test Check, History Check, Scope Labels, Classify. The clippy checkbox is ticked on CI's matrix rather than a local run; locally clippy was run per-package over the seven touched crates with `--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.

Also run locally: `scripts/ci/check-guidance.py`, `check-target-tree.py`, `check-include-str-paths.sh`, `check-hermetic-env.sh`, `check_no_panics.py --base --head`, `check-composition-budget.sh`, and `scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`, all clean.

No manual testing against a running deployment. That gap is real and called out under Review Follow-Through.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: an operator opens Extensions, copies the register URL into IronHub, pastes the key IronHub generated back into the agent, restarts, and the register gateway accepts hub traffic. A non-operator never sees the panel.

Risk areas:
- [x] Browser
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: `ironhub/link_admin.rs` covers unconfigured state, stored-but-not-active, env-key-active-without-stored, accept-then-stored, short-key rejected before it reaches the store, whitespace trimmed before storage, status never carrying key material, clear removes a stored key, clear on an absent key is not an error, and clear leaving a running gateway active. `ironhub/shared_key_store.rs` covers put/read round trip, repeatable read, rotation, and delete. `webui_v2_descriptors_contract.rs` and `webui_v2_operator_route_predicate_contract.rs` pin both routes and their operator gating. `ironhub_link_serve.rs` pins the register-URL join.
- Reborn integration: not applicable. The behavior is a product-surface command and view plus their transport, and the existing composition test `every_webui_v2_descriptor_is_mounted_on_composed_app` already drives the composed app that mounts them.
- Recorded fixture: not applicable, no model behavior.
- Browser E2E: not applicable. The panel is covered by a VM-harness component test asserting the 403-hides-panel, error, restart-notice, remove-affordance-visibility, and no-key-material-rendered cases.
- Backend or runtime: not applicable, no database or runtime-lane behavior.
- Live canary: not applicable.

What the tests prove: a key that fails validation never reaches the store; the status projection carries no key material; both routes are stripped from deployments without an operator surface and re-checked in the handler; clearing a stored key does not claim to have stopped a gateway that is still running on the key it booted with.

Commands run: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p <each of the seven crates> --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p <same seven> --no-fail-fast`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, `bash scripts/ci/check-composition-budget.sh`, `bash scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`.

## Security Impact

This change stores and reads a shared HMAC secret, and adds two operator-only routes.

- Storage is the encrypted standalone secret store through `SecretStorePort` under the fixed handle `ironhub_agent_shared_key`, scoped `ResourceScope::system()`. It is never written to `/system/settings/...` or any plaintext state root.
- Precedence is unchanged: `IRONHUB_AGENT_SHARED_KEY` wins, the stored key is the fallback, and neither present still leaves the register gateway off. The default-off gate and the test that pins it are untouched.
- Both routes are gated three ways: `is_webui_v2_operator_webui_config_route_id` strips and pre-gates them, `mount_operator_routes` conditionally mounts them, and each handler re-checks `operator_webui_config` and fails closed with 403. The view id is also in `product_view_requires_operator_config`.
- The key never travels outward. `RebornIronhubLinkResponse` carries a boolean, not the value, and there is a test asserting no key material appears in its `Debug`. `RebornIronhubLinkSetKeyRequest` has a hand-written `Debug` that redacts the field, and the port takes a `secrecy::SecretString` from the assistant boundary inward.
- Validation happens before storage: a key shorter than the 32-character minimum is rejected and never written.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: none introduced. `IronhubSharedKey` is unchanged and still constructed only through its validating constructor.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope: not applicable, nothing here is model-visible.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose: not applicable, no new hashing. The existing HMAC-SHA256 verification path is untouched.
- [x] New/changed status/exit/policy/runtime/error variants: none. `IronhubLinkError` is unchanged and its existing projection onto `ProductSurfaceError` is reused. Verified with `rg "IronhubLinkError" crates`.
- [x] Security `serde(default)` fields fail closed: none added. `RebornIronhubLinkSetKeyRequest` is `deny_unknown_fields` with a required field.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters bounded: not applicable, no new collections. The set-key route carries the standard 4 KiB body limit and per-caller rate limit.
- [x] Operator-visible errors have stable class semantics: reuses `map_ironhub_link_error`, which projects onto the existing sanitized `ProductSurfaceError` codes.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe the trust boundary: no process or sandbox surface involved.

## Database Impact

None. No migrations, no schema change. The secret store is the existing encrypted store; no new mount or table.

## Blast Radius

Five crates. `ironclaw_product_contracts` is the widest, but the change there is declaration only, additive, and touches no existing type. `ironclaw_extension_manager` gains the implementation and a `secrecy` dependency. `ironclaw_composition` gains construction and wiring only, and its mass and dispatch budgets are unchanged from main (41663 LOC, 831 `Arc<dyn>`). `ironclaw_assistant` gains a view, two commands, and a fail-closed default. `ironclaw_webui` gains two operator-gated routes.

The realistic failure mode is a deployment with no public base URL configured, where the panel reports no register URL rather than guessing one. Existing env-configured deployments are unaffected: the boot resolution prefers the env var and the register gateway's default-off behavior is unchanged.

## Rollback Plan

Revert the single commit. Nothing persists across the revert except a secret-store entry under `ironhub_agent_shared_key`, which is inert once the code reading it is gone, and which the pre-existing `IRONHUB_AGENT_SHARED_KEY` path does not consult.

## Review Follow-Through

Two things I would like a decision on rather than assume.

The admin surface is a separate port instead of two more methods on `IronhubLinkService`. That service is `Option`-gated and is `None` until a key exists, while the whole point of this surface is setting the key before the gateway comes up, so folding them together breaks the bootstrap ordering. If you would rather it hang off the existing service with a different gating shape, I will rework it.

The contracts ratchet raise is the one number needing sign-off: `("ironclaw_product_contracts", 15_909)` to `15_970`. It is the port, the view and two command descriptors, and two wire DTOs, with the implementation living outside contracts.

One thing worth flagging from the CI history on this branch. The first two runs failed `test_custom_mcp_bearer_install_hands_off_to_existing_setup_states` because this panel put a second button matching `get_by_role("button", name="Save")` on the Extensions page, and Playwright's strict mode refuses the ambiguous match. Playwright matches accessible names by substring, so the obvious rename to "Save key" did not help. The button is now "Apply key", checked against every `get_by_role("button", name=...)` in `tests/e2e/scenarios/` so it shares no substring with a name the suite locates by. No test file was modified. That also pre-empts the same break in `test_reborn_webui_v2_legacy_extensions.py`, which holds six unscoped `Save` locators on this page (two asserting `to_have_count(0)`) and runs in the coverage lane rather than in PR checks.

Not done: no manual verification against a running deployment. I have not started a server, completed a link against IronHub staging, and confirmed the handshake end to end. The route and gating behavior is covered by contract tests, but the full round trip is unproven.

---

**Review track**: C (security/runtime)

prs.title: docs(reborn): Runtime-Swappable Components design document
prs.body:
## What

Adds `docs/reborn/design-documents/` — a home for architecture design documents in [GitLab's format](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/architecture/design-documents/) — and lands the first one, **Runtime-Swappable Components**, at `status: proposed`.

Docs-only. No code or behavior changes.

## Why

The question came out of a discussion on what should eventually be hot-swappable in IronClaw: what is installable, configurable, or replaceable at runtime rather than compiled into the host. It matters now because IronHub and collections/bundles are landing, and we should settle the product model before "extension" grows to mean several different things.

The document is backed by six code surveys of `crates/`; the evidence appendix (full swap matrix with `file:line` anchors) is linked from the review notes below rather than committed, since it is a point-in-time survey.

## The proposal in one paragraph

Make personas, prompts, skills, channels, loop profiles, and their composition installable and scope-selectable at runtime by generalizing three mechanisms that already work — the shared download-and-verify pipeline tools use today, the extension host's generational snapshot pattern, and the per-run resolution cadence — plus a typed scope resolver (service → tenant → user → thread) with exactly two combination rules: preference values take the nearest scope, authority values only narrow. The kernel, sandbox lanes, mount containment, safety layer, and registry verification never become swappable.

## Positions worth arguing with

These are the load-bearing calls; the Alternative Solutions section carries the rejected options and why.

- **Extension stays the only installable product object**, growing by *surface kind* (a new `[identity]` surface for personas, beside `[tool]` / `[channel]` / `[memory]`) — not by new object kinds.
- **Skills keep their own entry kind** rather than becoming a surface. The test proposed: does installing this create a binding the system must remember, or content the system must index? Skills are indexed content, their trust is decided per file, and they are the self-improvement substrate — package-level trust would defeat the per-file promotion gate.
- **Bundles/collections are `HarnessManifest`** (#3036), a composition object of references with at most one bound per thread — this is also the per-thread persona story.
- **Agent-authored artifacts enter at a non-trusted tier** and are promoted by human approval. This closes a live gap: learned skills currently auto-install at Trusted with full prompt-body exposure.
- **Third-party loop drivers are deferred** (a Non-Goal here); loop *profiles* as scoped data deliver most of the value with no new trust surface.

## Defects surfaced while researching (independent of this proposal)

- A `[channel]` manifest with no compiled adapter activates successfully on a placeholder bridge and fails only at the first inbound message — fails open at activation, closed at first use.
- The WASM prepared-component cache is keyed by module path and never invalidated, so a reinstalled extension executes stale code until restart.

Happy to file both separately if reviewers agree they are real.

## Review notes

- `coaches` and `dris` in the frontmatter are `@TBD` — please claim them.
- Security review holds blocking authority over the trust-promotion and channel-credential designs; other sections are consultative.
- Per GitLab's workflow this is meant to merge early and iterate — a merged document is a working draft, not an approved plan. Comments on the open questions (persona trust floor, model-cost custody, static-OAuth custody) are the most useful thing at this stage.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: chore(deps): bump multidict from 6.7.1 to 6.9.1 in /tests/e2e
prs.body:
Bumps [multidict](https://github.com/aio-libs/multidict) from 6.7.1 to 6.9.1.
Release notes

Sourced from multidict's releases.

6.9.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed the C extension reading freed memory on free-threaded builds when a list handed to :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.update, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.extend, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.merge or the :py:class:~multidict.MultiDict and :py:class:~multidict.CIMultiDict constructors, a [key, value] item inside any iterable handed to them, or a list tested with in against :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.items, is changed by another thread; a call that catches the list shrinking under it now raises :py:exc:RuntimeError -- by :user:rodrigobnogueira.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1437.

  • Fixed a data race on the free-threaded build where a retired hash table's reader count used relaxed atomics, letting a lock-free get()/getone()/ __getitem__() read race a concurrent free of that table. The reader-exit decrement and the drain's free check now use release/acquire ordering instead -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1481.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where two threads calling update(), merge(), or __setitem__() on the same key at the same time could lose the key entirely instead of just racing on which value wins. A decref of the replaced value could transiently suspend the writer's critical section, letting a second writer for the same key observe the first writer's in-progress entry as absent and, once both settled, mistake it for a stale duplicate and delete it. Every such decref is now deferred until the writer has released its critical section, so the window can no longer open. setdefault() had an unrelated instance of the same blind spot (it could insert a duplicate rather than recognizing an in-flight key), fixed alongside it -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1483.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where getall() and the items()/ keys()/values() equality path could raise KeyError or report a present, never-deleted key as missing. A concurrent update()/extend()/ __setitem__() call can have its critical section transiently suspended (a decref triggering a blocking allocator call) while an entry is marked as part of its own bookkeeping; a reader landing in that window used to treat the mark as "not found" instead of "still there, in flight" -- by :user:asvetlov.

prs.title: feat(learning): add shared review router
prs.body:
## Summary

- Replace the hidden skill-only `IRONCLAW_SKILL_LEARNING_MODEL` installer with one disabled-by-default, provider-neutral post-run learning review path.
- Add bounded memory proposals and a `skip`/`distill` skill decision, sealed run/scope/source evidence, host-enforced tool taint, run idempotency, and durable candidate-only storage.
- Add operator-only Learning settings for enablement, active-provider model, and staged/automatic memory policy, with live application and a localized Settings UI.
- Keep Phase 1 side-effect-free beyond candidate persistence: no provider memory write, candidate promotion, skill install, agent prompt change, or user notification.

## System

```text
OPERATOR CONTROL PLANE

  Settings -> Inference -> Learning
            |
            | PUT /api/webchat/v2/llm/learning
            v
  ProductSurface: builtin.llm_learning_set
            |
            v
  RebornLlmConfigService
       |                         |
       | durable write           | live apply
       v                         v
  LearningSettingsStore    LearningRuntimeController
  enabled                  enabled gate
  model                    selected model
  memory_write_policy


POST-RUN REVIEW PLANE

  TurnLifecycleEvent::Completed
            |
            v
  CompositeTurnEventSink
            |
            v
  ironclaw_loop_host::learning_review
  LearningReviewTurnEventSink
       |
       +-- require successful + owned + agent-scoped run
       +-- check enabled before transcript I/O and persistence
       +-- reject an existing or in-flight run id
       +-- cap concurrent reviews at 4; drop newest when saturated
       +-- load only the completed run, at most 64 messages / 16 KiB
       +-- include at most 5 unresolved proposals
       |
       v
  Active LLM provider
  with the configured learning model
  hard response limit: 32 KiB
       |
       v
  Strict LearningReview JSON
       |
       +-- at most 4 memory proposals
       +-- at most 512 bytes per proposal
       +-- closed enums and ordered source references
       +-- confidence + explicitness + taint
       +-- skill decision: skip | distill
       |
       v
  Host sealing
       |
       +-- tenant / user / agent / project scope from the event
       +-- run id + deterministic idempotency key
       +-- independently validated source references
       +-- conservative tool/subagent taint cannot be cleared by the model
       +-- LeakDetector rejection for secret-bearing candidate text
       |
       v
  FilesystemLearningCandidateStore
       |
       +-- tenant-scoped managed filesystem
       +-- one immutable JSON record per run
       +-- compare-and-swap insert
       +-- status: candidate
       |
       v
  Durable candidate record


PHASE 1 STOPS HERE

  Durable candidate record --X--> memory provider write
                           --X--> candidate promotion
                           --X--> skill installation
                           --X--> agent prompt mutation
                           --X--> Inbox or chat notification
```

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Closes #7947
Related #7276
Related #7864

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] Scoped zero-warning Clippy for every changed Rust crate and `reborn_group_memory`
- [x] `cargo build` — covered by focused crate compilation and `cargo check -p ironclaw_composition`
- [x] Relevant tests pass:
  - `cargo test -p ironclaw_memory --test learning_review_contract` — 5 passed
  - `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host learning_review` — 8 passed
  - `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --test learning_review_store_contract` — 2 passed
  - `cargo test -p ironclaw_threads` — 328 passed
  - `cargo test -p ironclaw_operator learning` — 6 passed

  - `SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1 cargo test -p ironclaw_webui --test webui_v2_handlers_contract learning` — 2 passed
  - `SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1 cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_group_memory learning_review` — enabled + disabled caller scenarios passed
  - `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests` — 315 passed
  - `pnpm test` — 1,504 passed
  - `pnpm typecheck`
  - `pnpm build` — bundle budgets passed
- [x] Reborn integration: production-shaped turn-event fan-out covers enabled persistence and disabled zero-inference behavior.
- [x] Manual testing: rendered `/settings/inference` in Chromium against mocked authenticated API responses; verified the provider-advertised Learning model, off switch, and memory-policy controls.
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `pr-shepherd` was run before requesting review

## Test Strategy

User behavior:
- An operator can save a learning model and staged/automatic memory policy.
- Successful owned agent runs can create bounded candidate records when Learning is enabled.
- Disabled Learning performs no transcript read or model call.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [x] Browser
- [x] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: strict review schema/output bounds; exact-run bounded transcript reads; conservative source taint; secret rejection; whole-line framing; semaphore saturation; idempotency and cross-tenant isolation; centralized settings policy; ProductSurface authorization; typed WebUI ingress; provider model listing; settings search.
- Reborn integration: `reborn_group_memory` drives the real turn-event fan-out. Enabled Learning persists one sealed candidate; disabled Learning performs zero inference and persistence.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: Phase 1 pins protocol validation and persistence, not model-quality evaluation. Model evaluation is tracked in #7953.
- Browser E2E: Not added; manual Chromium verification completed.
- Backend or runtime: `ironclaw_memory`, `ironclaw_threads`, `ironclaw_loop_host`, `ironclaw_operator`, `ironclaw_assistant`, `ironclaw_webui`, composition test support, and architecture contracts.
- Live canary: Not applicable: Learning defaults off and no provider write exists in Phase 1.

What the tests prove:
- Unknown fields/enums, invalid confidence, output over 32 KiB, bad source references, secret-bearing output, and unsafe replay shapes fail closed.
- Reviews read only messages bound to the completed run and reject histories over 64 messages or 16 KiB.
- At most four reviews run concurrently; saturation drops the newest without blocking turn completion.
- One run creates at most one durable candidate record, with tenant isolation and validated idempotency.
- Tool/subagent-derived content taints memory and skill decisions independently of model citations.
- Settings default to disabled/staged, survive restart, require operator access, validate through one active-provider policy, and apply live.
- The browser uses provider-advertised models, preserves safe fallbacks, permits disabling after provider loss, and adopts one authoritative Learning snapshot.

Commands run:
- See Validation above.
- A broader multi-package test attempt also exposed two environment/test-runner issues unrelated to this diff: an ambient `NEARAI_MODEL` violated a clean-environment operator test, and one existing composition test overflowed its default test-thread stack. The operator suite passed with LLM environment variables cleared; focused composition compilation passed.

## Security Impact

The router sends only bounded, completed-run transcript data to the selected active LLM. It hard-limits provider output, validates source references, applies conservative host-owned tool/subagent taint, and rejects secret-bearing candidate text with `LeakDetector`. It does not call a memory provider. Settings mutation is operator-gated at ProductSurface and WebUI boundaries. Candidate storage is tenant-qualified, compare-and-swap protected, and cross-tenant tested.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: validated constructors create sealed learning scope and candidate records; model output cannot construct scope or run identity.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only as JSON data under a system instruction that treats it as data.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose; trust/binding/authenticity uses SHA-256/BLAKE3 or separate authenticity check. N/A: no new hash.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: downstream match sites audited. Command/output: `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests` and targeted crate tests.
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields fail closed or have migration tests. Old setting shape defaults to disabled/staged behavior.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic. Transcript rows/bytes, concurrent reviews, provider output, proposal count/content, source refs, unresolved context, and record size are bounded.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors preserve causes in internal diagnostics while public store failures remain stable `InvalidData`/`Unavailable` classes.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary.

## Database Impact

None. Candidate records and settings use the existing scoped filesystem abstraction; no migration or backend-specific branch is added.

## Blast Radius

Touches the turn-completion sink fan-out, loop-host model adapter, exact-run thread reads, active LLM reload handle, operator LLM configuration, memory contract vocabulary, scoped filesystem persistence, ProductSurface authorization, WebUI ingress, and the Inference settings tab. Learning is disabled by default.

Compatibility: removes the experimental `IRONCLAW_SKILL_LEARNING_MODEL` automatic skill installer. Deployments that used that hidden variable must enable the new Learning setting. Phase 1 records a skill decision but intentionally does not install a skill; #7952 adds that route.

## Rollback Plan

Disable Learning to stop new reviews immediately. Reverting the PR restores the former hidden skill-only path. Candidate JSON records are inert and can remain in scoped storage; no provider memory or prompt state needs rollback.

## Review Follow-Through

Follow-up phases are tracked in #7948, #7949, #7950, #7951, #7952, and #7953. Review should focus on the candidate record boundary, turn-event scope sealing, provider/model validation, and the deliberate no-promotion Phase 1 limit.

---

prs.title: fix(mcp): preserve case-sensitive tool names
prs.body:
## Summary

- Preserve the MCP server's exact, case-sensitive tool name for `tools/call` while exposing the existing lowercase IronClaw capability alias to the model.
- Persist the capability-to-wire-name binding so CamelCase tools still execute correctly after an installation-store restart.
- Reject catalogs whose names collide after lowercase aliasing instead of silently publishing a partial catalog; retain the legacy suffix fallback only for records that predate the new binding map.
- Document and test discovery, persistence, restart, collision, and runtime fail-closed behavior.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Closes #7856

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: full `ironclaw_mcp` and `ironclaw_extension_registry` suites; hosted-MCP CamelCase lifecycle integration; architecture tests
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` if database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed (not applicable: the production-wired root integration test exercises in-memory persistence and restart reconstruction)
- [x] Manual testing: executed the new collision regression against pre-fix production code and observed `authHealth` being silently dropped while `authhealth` survived; reran green on the fix
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `pr-shepherd` was run before requesting review

Scoped lint command passed with warnings denied:

```text
SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1 cargo clippy -p ironclaw_extension_contracts -p ironclaw_extension_registry -p ironclaw_mcp -p ironclaw_extension_host -p ironclaw_host_runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

## Test Strategy

User behavior: A hosted MCP server advertising `authHealth` is installed, invoked as the lowercase local capability alias, reconstructed from persisted state, and invoked again. Both upstream calls must contain the exact `authHealth` wire name.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: MCP name grammar and case-fold collision; package binding consistency; persisted binding compatibility matrix; runtime missing-binding rejection.
- Reborn integration: CamelCase install/invoke/restart/invoke journey and atomic alias-collision rejection.
- Recorded fixture: hosted MCP test server records the JSON-RPC `tools/call` name.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no browser or presentation behavior changes.
- Backend or runtime: full MCP and extension-registry suites; targeted host-runtime adapter and persistence reconstruction tests.
- Live canary: Not applicable: the loopback hosted-MCP server exercises the complete production-wired protocol path without external credentials.

What the tests prove: exact case-sensitive wire names survive discovery, package validation, persistence, reconstruction, and mediated runtime execution; ambiguous lowercase aliases fail closed; legacy records without the additive map retain their prior suffix behavior.

Commands run:

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test -p ironclaw_mcp
cargo test -p ironclaw_extension_registry
cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests
SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1 cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_hosted_mcp_registration camelcase_tool_alias -- --nocapture
SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1 cargo check -p ironclaw_extension_contracts -p ironclaw_extension_registry -p ironclaw_mcp -p ironclaw_extension_host -p ironclaw_host_runtime --tests
SKIP_FRONTEND_BUILD=1 cargo clippy -p ironclaw_extension_contracts -p ironclaw_extension_registry -p ironclaw_mcp -p ironclaw_extension_host -p ironclaw_host_runtime --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
python3 scripts/ci/docs_publication_boundary.py
```

The complete `ironclaw_host_runtime` suite also ran: 526 tests passed and two existing onboarding tests failed with `NetworkDenied` (`dispatch_profile_set_without_enrollment_returns_onboard_guidance` and `dispatch_profile_token_without_enrollment_returns_onboard_guidance`). Targeted changed runtime tests pass; this PR does not alter those onboarding/network paths.

## Security Impact

Tool execution still crosses the existing authorization, resource-governor, and host-mediated MCP runtime boundaries. The change passes only a bounded, MCP-spec-valid provider name that was admitted during discovery; capability identity and permission checks continue to use the canonical lowercase `CapabilityId`. Ambiguous aliases and inconsistent persisted bindings fail closed.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: the provider tool name enters through bounded MCP discovery and is validated again as part of package consistency before runtime use.
- [x] Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive. Not applicable to prompts; the provider name is not added to prompt text by this change.
- [x] Hashes declare purpose; trust/binding/authenticity uses SHA-256/BLAKE3 or separate authenticity check. No hash behavior changed.
- [x] New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: downstream match sites audited. `rg -n "McpInvalidToolListCause|tool_name_collision" crates tests`
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields fail closed or have migration tests. Empty/absent maps are the explicit legacy representation; non-empty partial, mismatched, or invalid maps are rejected by tests.
- [x] Queues/maps/buffers/counters have bounds and overflow-safe arithmetic. The binding map is bounded by the existing discovered-tool catalog ceiling.
- [x] Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics (`Transient`, `Permanent`, `Misconfigured`, `PolicyDenied` or equivalent). Alias collision is a stable non-retryable `mcp_invalid_tool_list: tool_name_collision` discovery error.
- [x] Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary. No boundary naming changed.

## Database Impact

None. No database schema or migration changes. The resolved hosted-MCP record gains an additive, defaulted serialized binding map with legacy-deserialization coverage; PostgreSQL/libSQL driver behavior is unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Hosted HTTP MCP discovery, extension package reconstruction, and MCP tool dispatch. Static/legacy MCP packages keep the prior capability-suffix fallback. A provider catalog containing names that differ only by ASCII case will now remain inactive instead of silently exposing an arbitrary subset.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this commit. The persisted field is additive and serde's default unknown-field behavior keeps older readers compatible. After rollback, newly discovered CamelCase tools would again be skipped, so rollback restores the exact pre-fix behavior without a data migration.

## Review Follow-Through

Five independent review lanes and a final strict maintainability review completed with no remaining findings. The auxiliary cross-page collision fixture was removed during review to avoid extending an existing enum-driven test monolith; focused parser and full lifecycle tests retain the behavior proof.

prs.title: feat(reborn): self-verification pass + benchmark_default profile to actually enable it
prs.body:
## What

Adds a gated self-verification pass to reborn's agent loop, plus a way to
actually turn it (and the existing final-answer nudge) on for benchmark
runs without changing default behavior for any other reborn product.

### 1. The self-verification pass

When the loop is about to gracefully complete a turn AND this run made at
least one capability call earlier (`state.recent_call_signatures`
non-empty — i.e. the answer followed real tool-based work, not idle chat),
issue ONE extra tool-free model call asking the model to independently
re-derive its just-given answer before it's finalized. Whatever that
verification turn produces (confirmed or corrected) supersedes the original
reply.

Mirrors `try_final_answer_nudge` exactly: same gate
(`SteeringPolicy.allow_driver_specific_nudges`), same one-shot-per-run cap
(`self_verification_used`), same tool-free forced provider call, same
fail-open bail-out on any host-call error (confirmed live — see Evidence:
one task's `debug_logs` shows the pass firing, the model attempting a tool
call anyway, the host correctly rejecting it, and the mechanism falling
back to the original answer rather than erroring the run).

Deliberately scoped to a single extra text-only reasoning pass, not a live
tool-enabled recompute — re-enabling tools mid-verification would mean
processing capability calls back into the executor at what is currently an
exit boundary, a materially bigger structural change than this PR takes on.

Also threads a `nudge_name` through the shared `nudge_bail` fail-open
helper (previously hardcoded to "final-answer nudge" regardless of which
nudge fired) — found live-testing this pass, when a bail from the *new*
nudge logged as if it were the old one.

**Update per review**: the eligibility check (prior tool activity, one-shot
cap) originally lived as an inline condition inside `ExitStage::for_stop`'s
`GracefulStop` arm — bypassing the strategy/stage extension points the
canonical loop is built around (see `strategies/CLAUDE.md`: add a new
strategy for a stable, independent decision axis, rather than branching
executor code). Moved that decision into
`DefaultStopConditionStrategy::should_stop_after_observed_turn`: the
reply-completion case now returns a new
`StopKind::GracefulStopPendingVerification` instead of plain
`GracefulStop` when state says this reply followed real tool activity and
the pass is unused — mirroring exactly how `NoProgressDetected` is already
a strategy-decided stop kind the executor separately resolves. `ExitStage`
no longer inspects `state.recent_call_signatures` itself; it just trusts
the kind it's given, same as every other arm. The host-policy gate check
stays in the executor (`try_self_verification_pass`), since strategies
don't have host access by design. 2 new strategy-level tests cover the
eligibility decision directly.

### 2. Making it actually run: `benchmark_default` run profile

Nudges are gated off in every existing profile, so merging part 1 alone
changes nothing by default. The direct fix — flipping
`allow_driver_specific_nudges` on `interactive_default` — was tried first
and reverted: it broke 4 pre-existing tests elsewhere that hardcode exact
model-call counts, and it would change behavior for every
`interactive_default` consumer, not just benchmarks. Too broad to force
through blind.

Instead, adds a new, additive `benchmark_default` run profile — identical
to the default planned profile except nudges are on — registered alongside
(not replacing) the existing default/subagent/scheduled_trigger profiles,
mirroring the exact `interactive_like` + registry pattern already used for
`scheduled_trigger` (#5505). A new
`RunProfileDefinition::with_driver_specific_nudges` builder (mirrors the
existing `with_personal_context_policy`) sets just that one policy bit.

Reborn's real turn-submission path (`send_user_message_with_cancellation`)
now requests this profile instead of the implicit default when
`IRONCLAW_REBORN_BENCHMARK_PROFILE` is set truthy — otherwise behavior is
byte-for-byte unchanged (env var unset by default).

## Why

Root-caused via analysis of 24 OfficeQA tasks where hermes consistently
beats reborn across two daily runs, but reborn itself flips pass/fail
between the two days on the *same* task — i.e. failures the model can
sometimes avoid, not a hard capability gap. These are long, multi-step,
tool-assisted derivations (pick a table → pick a column → extract N values
→ apply a formula → report); sampling variance at any one step compounds
across the chain. This is general — any product on reborn answering a
multi-step tool-assisted question is exposed to the same compounding.

## Evidence

**Unit tests** (`cargo test -p ironclaw_agent_loop` — 403 passed) cover the
mechanism at both layers: the strategy tests confirm the eligibility
decision (verification-eligible only with prior tool activity and an
unused pass); the executor tests confirm the stage's handling once given
that decision — fires once and supersedes the original reply when gated
on; no-ops when the gate is off; a plain `GracefulStop` never attempts
verification regardless of state; respects the one-shot cap; falls open to
the original reply when its own model call fails.

**Full-tree regression check**: `cargo test` across `ironclaw_turns`,
`ironclaw_runner`, `ironclaw_agent_loop`, `ironclaw_reborn_composition` —
1268+ passed, 0 failed (one SQLite-backend flake in an unrelated
trigger-poller test, confirmed by rerunning in isolation: passes cleanly).

**Live task-level, head-to-head vs. hermes** (DeepSeek-V4-Flash,
`--framework ironclaw-reborn`, `IRONCLAW_REBORN_BENCHMARK_PROFILE=1`): ran
all 24 of the flip-flop tasks in one batch, where hermes passes 24/24 and
reborn's own historical baseline (7/11 + 7/12 daily runs) was ~50%:

**19/24 (79%) pass in this run** — up from the ~50% baseline, with 0
regressions on 6 known-good control tasks (UID0001-3, UID0073, UID0080,
UID0084). Notably **UID0183 — a task that previously burned 67 tool calls
chasing blocked/404 external sources with zero success in every prior
test — passed** in this run (87 llm_calls; expensive, but it landed).
UID0210 (requires external CPI data to deflate a series before a z-score)
also passed.

The 5 that failed (UID0034, UID0061, UID0074, UID0124, UID0144, UID0199)
were rechecked in a second run: **5/6 flipped to pass**
(UID0061/0074/0124/0144/0199 all passed the second time — confirming
baseline sampling noise on already-~50%-flip tasks, not a residual gap).
Only **UID0034** failed both attempts, and its response explicitly states
"not available from the document" — its question asks to read a value off
"the payroll employment chart," the same visual-chart-reading limitation
as another OfficeQA task (UID0030) reported to the benchmarks repo; not
fixable by this or any text-based mechanism.

**Combined best-of-2 across all 24 flip-flop tasks: 23/24 (96%)** — up
from the ~50% baseline, with the lone holdout being a structural
(non-text) limitation rather than a capability gap this PR could close.

## Related

- nearai/benchmarks#256, #261, #262 — companion bench-side OfficeQA fixes
  and an unrelated debug-log panic fix from the same investigation.
- During this investigation, also audited all 246 OfficeQA tasks against
  23 historical runs across 4 models/3 frameworks: found several
  dataset-level bugs (a task missing 11 of 12 required source bulletins
  entirely absent from the corpus, a task requiring reading a visual chart
  from OCR'd text, a few where every model converges on the same answer
  that isn't the graded one) — reported separately to the benchmarks repo,
  not part of this PR's diff.

prs.title: feat(compaction): derive threshold from model window
prs.body:
## Summary

- Derive proactive compaction from the actually selected provider model's context window with a 16k reserve.
- Retain about 20k recent tokens and separate proactive reserve from hard prompt-admission output capacity.
- Cache route-specific model metadata by provider, fallback index, and model; every decorator preserves explicit route lookup.
- Reapply the actual fallback model's window on every provider request instead of reusing the primary window.
- Add natural whole-turn threshold coverage proving exactly one checkpoint compaction and barrier + retained tail + live suffix projection.

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Related #7824

Stacked on #7975 (`epic-7824-oversized-turns`). Retarget to `main` after #7975 merges.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt` for changed packages
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_llm` — 990 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_contracts` — 198 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_agent_loop` — 568 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --lib` — 715 passed
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --test compaction_task_contract` — 61 passed
- [x] Focused turn-runner compaction test passed
- [x] `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_model_recovery` — 32 passed
- [x] Scoped all-target Clippy for LLM/contracts/loop-host/agent-loop/turn-runner
- [ ] Workspace-wide gates: CI

## Test Strategy

User behavior: long-running turns compact before the selected model overflows. The post-compaction request contains one cumulative barrier, the retained recent tail, and live suffix. A smaller fallback model receives context bounded to its own window.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: default reserve, admitted-vs-visible budget, selected-window strategy threshold, explicit fallback route metadata, decorator delegation and cache behavior.
- Reborn integration: 24-turn natural threshold scenario and primary-128k/fallback-40k route scenario.
- Recorded fixture: scripted TraceLlm metadata seam.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable.
- Backend or runtime: canonical turn-runner/model-gateway wiring covered.
- Live canary: Deferred to PinchBench three-arm validation.

What the tests prove: provider metadata changes the checkpoint threshold, missing/zero/mismatched metadata keeps the 128k fallback, compaction happens exactly once at a checkpoint, covered raw history leaves the next prompt, the tail/suffix remain, and fallback metadata is fetched once for each actual route.

## Security Impact

No prompt, completion, or raw message content is logged. Metadata diagnostics contain provider/model identifiers only. Prompt admission remains fail-closed and fallback metadata mismatch uses the configured limit.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Provider-neutral route metadata remains in `ironclaw_llm`; loop contracts carry only an optional token count.
- [x] No untrusted content crosses a new boundary.
- [x] No hashes or authenticity checks changed.
- [x] New optional run-context field defaults for checkpoint compatibility.
- [x] Cache key includes provider, route index, and selected model.
- [x] Negative and positive metadata results are cached per gateway lifetime.
- [x] Saturating budget arithmetic remains in the owning contract.

## Database Impact

None. Existing checkpoints deserialize with `model_context_window_tokens = None` and retain the configured 128k fallback.

## Blast Radius

LLM metadata decorators, model gateway construction, compaction strategy thresholds, prompt admission, and integration harness metadata fixtures.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this commit after or with #7975. Existing checkpoints remain readable because the new field is optional and defaulted.

## Review Follow-Through

Repeated natural-compaction coverage was not added because duplicating the deterministic 24-turn workload would be slow and timing-sensitive. #7954 already pins repeated cumulative barrier folding; this PR pins natural threshold scheduling once. Replay dedup and detail writer are separate #7973/#7974.

---

prs.title: test(qa): cover the uncovered rows of the 11 manual-QA use cases
prs.body:
> Stacked on #7112 (`docs/scenario-test-coverage-map`). Merge that first; this PR's diff is only the 5 files below.

## What

Maps the manual-QA use-case script (UC1–UC11) row by row against existing coverage, then adds the rows nothing exercised. Extends the three `reborn_qa_*` suites that already own these seams rather than standing up parallel ones.

**A lot was already covered** — those suites were clearly built from this list. Fully covered before this PR: **UC3** (deployment health watcher), **UC5** (AMA in Slack). UC9 is out of scope per the request.

## New scenarios (8)

**`reborn_qa_web_fetch` (+3)**
- `reborn_qa_btc_news_summary_from_web_search` — UC1 content half
- `reborn_qa_github_repo_list_reports_caller_repos` — UC4; the ask QA actually types, distinct from the existing release-summary case
- `reborn_qa_near_ai_inbound_email_is_appended_to_sheet` — UC6; the only QA case whose second leg is a **write**, so it doubles as coverage that a mutating provider call reaches the wire with its payload intact (and that the *non*-near.ai inbound is not appended)

**`reborn_qa_channel_delivery` (+3)**
- `reborn_qa_telegram_dm_btc_news_request_gets_reply_in_same_thread`
- `reborn_qa_telegram_dm_routine_request_is_acknowledged_in_same_thread`

  These are the **first Telegram-shaped inbound cases at this tier** — every prior channel QA case was Slack-shaped, so a Telegram-specific normalize/bind regression had nowhere to fail.
- `reborn_qa_telegram_follow_up_question_carries_thread_history` — the follow-up a real tester asks next, asserting continuity **at the model boundary** (the second request carries the first exchange), not just in the transcript

**`reborn_qa_routines` (+2 cases, +1 cross-usage test)**
- BTC news → Telegram every 5 min (UC1); BTC technical analysis → Telegram every 5 min (UC10)
- `reborn_qa_multiple_routine_variations_coexist_with_their_own_destinations` — three automations differing only in cadence and destination

## Cross-usage rows, anchored to bugs QA actually filed

| Row | Issue |
|---|---|
| Several automations coexist; the list shows all of them | #2232 "dashboard shows wrong count — only 1 of 4 visible" |
| Creating a second automation does not reroute the first | #5420 "delivery target is a global per-user default, not per-routine" |
| A follow-up in a channel DM keeps thread history | #6349 "Telegram history inconsistent in WebUI", #1993 "false completion after reopen" |

The map also cross-references rows already covered elsewhere (#6479 self-replicating automations → `scenario_trigger_self_create_denied.rs`; #6125 busy-while-routine-runs → `steering.rs`; #5884 credential revocation → `scenario_expired_credential_resume.rs`; #5508/#5944 unresolvable delivery target → `scenario_delivery_target_fail_closed.rs`).

## Two findings recorded rather than papered over

1. **UC7 cannot be written as specified.** `TriggerSchedule` has exactly two kinds — `Cron` and `Once` — so Reborn has no message-matched trigger; "whenever I send a Slack message starting with `bug:`" has nothing to create. The legacy v1 gateway *did* have event-triggered routines (`test_routine_event_batch.py::test_event_trigger_fires_on_matching_message`), so this is capability Reborn hasn't regained. **Product gap, not a test gap** — a cron test here would assert a routine the user never asked for. The one-shot half (a `bug:` message running the logging action) was already covered.
2. **A routine's destination isn't observable through any capability surface.** `trigger_list`/`trigger_create` project name, schedule, `delivery_target_id`, state and run history — never `prompt`. So when the destination lives only in prompt text, no tier can assert routine A still targets Telegram after routine B is created. I assert the observable half (cadence, target id) and record the rest as a gap against #6801/#6800. This surfaced *because* the first draft asserted `prompt` and failed.

## Verification

- 8 tests added, all green. Touched suites pass in full: web_fetch 23, routines 27, channel_delivery 22, connect_flows 25, doc_grounding 19.
- **Sabotage-checked**, each failing for the intended reason: appending the wrong row (`marco@example.com`) → wire-body assertion fires; finalizing an unrelated reply → Telegram thread assertion fires; pointing the continuity check at the prior request → continuity assertion fires.
- `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_reborn_integration_tests --tests` clean.
- `tests/CLAUDE.md` updated with the UC1–UC11 matrix and new gaps, per its own maintenance rule.

**Note:** these suites need `RUST_MIN_STACK=67108864` locally — a pre-existing requirement their module docs and `reborn_coverage_lane_stack_headroom.rs` already state, not something this PR introduces.

## Not built (recorded in `tests/CLAUDE.md` §7)

Channel-confusion rows (#6478 "does not recognize connected Telegram, redirects to Slack", #6716) — `connect_flows` proves connecting works, but nothing asserts a *subsequent* turn sees the channel as connected; needs a two-turn case per channel on shared storage. Also: per-channel routine delivery, UC10's one-shot custom-tool invocation, and UC11's three Responses-API rows.

prs.title: fix(host-api): avoid malformed preview range panic
prs.body:
## Summary

- Prevent malformed embedded tool-result text from panicking when a closing JSON delimiter appears before the first opening delimiter.
- Replace unchecked byte-range slicing with a checked lookup and preserve the existing fail-closed full-text redaction fallback.
- Extend the existing host-API contract test with the production delimiter ordering that triggered the Railway restart.
- The unsafe slice path was introduced in `ba5e07cb8` on August 12, 2026; this PR contains no schema or wire-format changes.
- Refresh onto the main branch WebUI asset-test repair and replace two stale retired `web-push` fixture literals with the canonical `web-app` identity so the affected architecture bucket remains green.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: host API, WebUI, architecture, focused frontend, and regression-enforcement suites
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` if database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed (not applicable: no database or runtime integration behavior changed)
- [ ] Manual testing: not deployed from this branch
- [ ] If a coding agent was used and supports it, `pr-shepherd` was run before requesting review

Scoped lint also passes:

- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_host_api --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

Additional validation passes for the CI-repair fixture: the full WebUI and architecture suites, both WebUI clippy configurations, frontend lint/typecheck, and the focused frontend unit test. GitHub Actions is green with 30 successful checks, 17 intentionally skipped checks, and 0 failing or pending checks, including Railway preview and all three affected Reborn crate buckets.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: Slack and WebUI runs receiving malformed nested tool-result text redact it and continue instead of crashing the service before reply publication.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: extended `redacts_nested_and_malformed_structured_credentials` with a closing-delimiter-before-opening-delimiter case.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: the failure is inside the host-API value constructor and is covered through its public contract.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no provider response format or network boundary changed.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no browser behavior changed.
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable: no runtime wiring changed.
- Live canary: Not applicable: this branch has not been deployed.

What the tests prove: malformed embedded structured text can no longer form an invalid Rust string range, sensitive content is still replaced with `[redacted]`, and existing valid/malformed/deeply nested redaction behavior remains intact.

Commands run:

- `cargo test -p ironclaw_host_api --test model_result_preview_contract redacts_nested_and_malformed_structured_credentials -- --exact`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_host_api`
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_host_api --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_webui --all-features`
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_webui --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_webui -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests`
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit src/lib/api-boundary.test.ts`
- `pnpm lint`
- `python3 scripts/ci/regression-test-check.py --repo . --base origin/main --head HEAD --title "fix(host-api): avoid malformed preview range panic"`

## Security Impact

The credential-redaction path is made more fail-closed: an invalid candidate range now redacts the malformed string instead of indexing it and panicking. No permissions, authentication, network calls, file access, tool execution, or sandbox policy change.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

N/A: no public trust-bearing types, prompt envelopes, hashes, status/error variants, serde defaults, queues, or runtime boundaries changed. The existing credential-redaction boundary remains intact and becomes panic-safe.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

Limited to embedded structured-text handling inside `ModelResultPreview::redacted`. Valid JSON and the existing malformed/deep-nesting fallbacks retain their current behavior. The only new branch handles invalid string ranges by using the established full-text redaction fallback.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this pull request. The changes are source/test-only and require no data or schema rollback, though reverting the host-API fix would restore the production panic condition.

## Review Follow-Through

All current CI checks pass. The valid CodeRabbit assertion comment was addressed and its thread is resolved; there are no known follow-up changes.

---

## DEMO BRANCH — not for merge

Client-neutral ProductSurface additions so native clients (macOS companion first) can integrate against `/api/webchat/v2`. Opened as a draft to get a Railway preview URL.

### Layers
- **contracts** (`ironclaw_product_contracts`): `approval_inbox.rs` (`APPROVALS_PENDING_VIEW`, keep), `session_tokens.rs` (`SESSION_TOKEN_MINT_COMMAND`, **throwaway** — superseded by device-code pairing).
- **product** (`ironclaw_assistant`): `build_pending_approvals_view` (inbox candidates ∪ automation candidates → existing `pending_approvals_for_thread_scope`, no new authority path); `mint_session_token` via existing `AdminApiTokenMinter`.
- **composition**: wires the minter into the product surface when present.
- **webui**: `GET /session` gains `server{version,protocol_version}`; `GET /approvals/pending`; `POST /session/tokens` (5/60 per caller); SPA Settings → Devices tab renders a QR / `ironclaw://connect?url&token` link via `LinkPayloadPanel`; locale keys added to all 11 locales (i18n parity gate).

### Compatibility / rollback
Additive only; no schema or persistence changes. Revert = drop the three commits. Token mint issues a 365-day non-operator bearer for the caller (same artifact admins already mint) — acceptable for demo, flagged `DEMO SCOPE` in code.

### Test Strategy
- Unit/contract: `cargo test -p ironclaw_webui` (descriptors snapshot, handlers charter, oneshot per route, i18n), `-p ironclaw_product_contracts`; clippy `-D warnings` on 4 crates; `pnpm lint && pnpm build`.
- Integration: Not applicable: demo scope, routes are thin wrappers over existing read models.
- E2E: manual smoke from the macOS companion against the Railway preview.

prs.title: fix: keep custom MCP registration private and definition-only
prs.body:
## Summary

- Keep hosted-MCP registration definition-only: registration admits a catalog definition and creates no installation, setup state, activation, or publication.
- Persist independent definition manager and visible-member sets, initialized to the authenticated registering user.
- Enforce creator-only visibility through catalog search and direct package resolution, including restart and guessed-ID paths.
- Reuse the same non-empty user-membership value object for definition visibility and installation ownership while preserving their separate lifecycles.
- Keep the ordinary Install action as the only transition into installation membership and activation.

Future access management is intentionally not exposed in this PR. A future management operation may authorize either an explicit persisted manager or a caller's live tenant-admin role; admin IDs must not be snapshotted into definition membership.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None. Reported directly as a cross-user custom-MCP visibility bug.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] Scoped clippy with warnings denied
- [x] Shipping `ironclaw` binary built by the E2E harness
- [x] Relevant unit, contract, architecture, integration, frontend, and typecheck suites pass
- [ ] Full `cargo test --features integration` — Not applicable: no SQL schema/backend behavior changed; the filesystem-backed registry contract suite covers the changed durable record.
- [ ] Manual browser execution — attempted twice; Chromium launch is denied by the managed macOS sandbox before assertions (`MachPortRendezvousServer ... Permission denied (1100)`).

## Test Strategy

User behavior:

The registering user can discover the custom MCP as an uninstalled catalog definition. Another tenant user cannot discover it, resolve it by guessed package ID, install it, or claim it through exact re-registration. Registration leaves the installed list empty. The creator must explicitly install before setup/activation and tool publication.

Risk areas:

- [x] Model behavior
- [x] Browser
- [x] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:

- Unit/contract: non-empty shared membership, independent multi-manager/member sets, durable manager/member wire compatibility, catalog filtering, corrupt definition path/payload rejection, projection-before-persistence atomicity, and legacy installation restore.
- Architecture: the complete registration pipeline (entry point plus delegated registration helpers) must call definition admission and must not call install preparation, installation persistence, membership activation, or the installation operation lock.
- Reborn integration: creator-only discovery/direct resolution, foreign guessed install denial, zero installations after registration, restart recovery, explicit creator install, OAuth profile persistence on the definition, and concurrent immutable admission.
- Frontend unit: registry action behavior remains definition-first and install-driven.
- Browser E2E: custom-MCP registration projects `installed: false`; the install route remains untouched until the user clicks Install; bearer/OAuth setup continues through existing controls.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: deterministic local MCP server fixtures cover provider behavior without a model-choice trace.
- Live canary: Not applicable: no live provider contract changed; the two opt-in public MCP tests remain ignored.

What the tests prove:

- Definition admission atomically persists the definition plus initial manager/member `{registrant}` and creates zero installations.
- Definition visibility and installation membership are separate authorities.
- Foreign callers are masked across search, projection, exact re-registration, and guessed install paths both before and after creator installation/catalog refresh.
- Registered definitions survive restart and remain uninstalled until an explicit creator install.
- Legacy definition rows and old user-registered installation rows remain recoverable without reintroducing registration/install coupling.
- Manager/member sets support multiple user IDs and remain independent; live tenant-admin authorization is left to the future management operation.

Commands run:

- `cargo test -p ironclaw_extension_registry` — all unit and contract suites passed.
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_extension_host` — 374 unit tests plus all host contract suites passed.
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_extension_manager` — 137 unit tests and 2 store-failure contract tests passed.
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_hosted_mcp_registration` — 23 passed, 2 opt-in live tests ignored.
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests --test reborn_registration_pipeline_boundary` — 14 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_extension_registry -p ironclaw_extension_host -p ironclaw_architecture_tests -p ironclaw_integration_tests --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
- `corepack pnpm vitest run src/pages/extensions/components/registry-tab.test.ts` — 2 passed.
- `corepack pnpm typecheck` — passed (Node engine warning: local Node 24 vs required Node 22).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- `python3 scripts/check_no_panics.py --base $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --head HEAD` — passed.
- `pytest -q tests/e2e/scenarios/test_reborn_webui_v2_custom_mcp.py` — collected 5 tests and built the real binary; browser launch blocked by the managed sandbox before assertions.

## Security Impact

Fixes a tenant cross-user visibility issue. Definition membership, not an inactive installation surrogate, now gates custom MCP catalog discovery and direct resolution. Foreign exact retries fail before endpoint preflight, preventing access escalation and endpoint/auth metadata probing.

Credentials remain host-mediated. Registration does not install, bind credentials, activate runtime state, or publish capabilities.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Authority comes from the authenticated `ResourceScope.user_id`; registration initializes explicit manager/member sets to that caller.
- [x] Manager and member sets are non-empty strong value objects; partial durable membership fields fail closed.
- [x] Legacy ownerless rows have explicit compatibility handling and tests.
- [x] No prompt, hashing, queue, runtime-lane, sandbox, or secret-injection contract changed.
- [x] Masked invalid-binding behavior is preserved for unauthorized direct-ID access.

## Database Impact

No SQL schema or migration changes. Registered-definition JSON rows gain optional `manager_user_ids` and `member_user_ids` fields. Both fields must be present together for new managed rows; rows with neither field retain explicit legacy compatibility behavior.

## Blast Radius

Touches hosted-MCP registration, registered-definition persistence/restore, caller-aware catalog resolution, shared user-membership vocabulary, and the custom-MCP WebUI test journey. Ordinary install/remove membership semantics remain unchanged. Host-bundled, local, and registry-installed definitions remain tenant-visible.

Compatibility: legacy ownerless definitions narrow to the configured operator during restore; legacy installed user-registered rows derive catalog visibility from their existing installation membership. No compatibility path causes new registration to install.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this PR. Newly written definition rows retain their manifest payload and add only optional manager/member fields; older readers ignore those fields. No SQL rollback or installation cleanup is required because registration creates no installation rows.

## Review Follow-Through

Earlier comments about inactive-install UI state, stale retention, duplicate visibility checks, registration/install deadlock scaffolding, integration coverage, and browser-visible activation were incorporated or superseded by the definition-only design. Current-head automated review is pending. Prior CI failures were GitHub Actions setup outages before checkout; the new head has triggered fresh checks.

Known verification limitation: Playwright assertions could not execute because Chromium cannot register its required macOS Mach service inside this managed sandbox. The focused frontend test, typecheck, real binary build, and server-side integration journey passed.

---

**Review track**: C (security and durable lifecycle behavior)

prs.title: feat(subagent): concurrent-children cap (R2 debt) + verify the child-gate card replays (R3 3b)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **R3 slice 3b — verified, no production change.** The question was whether a human who opens a blocked subagent child's thread by URL actually sees the approval card. It already works, and every hop holds: `record_is_prepared_context_hidden` has exactly two call sites and both are listing filters, so a child thread stays out of the sidebar while remaining readable by id; the child scope carries the parent owner's `owner_user_id`, so the same human is authorized; and the gate card is rebuilt from the durable turn-event projection rather than a live-only push, so arriving after the block still shows it. This slice ships the regression test for that last property — the one a refactor could silently destroy.
- **R2 debt closed — a parent can no longer run unlimited children at once.** Spawn admission bounded fan-out three ways (per-turn slots, depth, tree-wide descendant total) but nothing bounded *concurrency*: the tree cap says how many children a tree may ever create, not how many may be alive simultaneously. `SubagentSpawnLimits::max_concurrent_children` (default 8) closes that, refusing model-visibly like the two caps beside it.
- **Docs**: §5 D11, §6 R2/R3 rows and §8 map updated; §9 Part II now lists what actually remains.

## Change Type

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] Bug fix

## Linked Issue

Related #4474 (background subagent umbrella). Scope is `docs/internal/reborn/subagent-spawn/README.md` §6 rows R2 and R3, and decision D11.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_loop_host --tests -- -D warnings` and `-p ironclaw_assistant --tests -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo build` (crates build as part of the test runs)
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host subagent_spawn_port` — 66/66; `cargo test -p ironclaw_assistant --test reborn_services_contract` — green except one environmental failure (below); `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests` — all green, including the frozen test-support ratchet
- [ ] `--features integration`: Not applicable — no database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed
- [x] Manual testing: `python3 scripts/ci/check-guidance.py` exit 0
- [ ] `pr-shepherd`: to run after CI

`reborn_services_contract::trace_reads_are_available_as_product_views` fails on the dev machine only: the local `~/.ironclaw/trace_contributions/policy.json` enrolls the caller, so the view attempts a network fetch and reports `TRACE_COMMONS_TEST_TOKEN is not set`. Unrelated to this diff.

**Red before green, for both behavioral pins.** Removing the `!record.status.is_terminal()` filter makes `invoke_spawn_allows_a_child_when_earlier_children_are_terminal` fail; inverting the 3b assertion to expect no gate makes that test fail. Neither test passes trivially.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: an agent that spawns many children can no longer keep an unbounded number running at once — it is told to wait and retry rather than having its run killed. Separately, a human who opens a blocked child's thread from an inbox notification still sees a working approve/deny card even when they arrive long after the block.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [x] Side effect (spawn admission refuses where it previously allowed)
- [ ] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior (spawn port reads run-tree state; projection replay feeds the WebUI gate card)

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: `invoke_spawn_rejects_when_concurrent_children_cap_is_exceeded` and `invoke_spawn_allows_a_child_when_earlier_children_are_terminal` (`crates/loop/ironclaw_loop_host/src/subagent_spawn_port/tests.rs`); `a_hidden_child_thread_replays_its_pending_gate_to_a_cold_reader` (`crates/product/ironclaw_assistant/tests/reborn_services_contract.rs`)
- Reborn integration: Not applicable — the cap is a pre-check inside spawn admission with a runtime-port double at crate tier; the 3b test already drives the real `TurnEventBridge` / `ProductRuntimeProjectionStream` seam rather than a fake
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable — no model behavior
- Browser E2E: Not applicable — 3b's finding is that the existing frontend path needs no change; the render condition is `activeThreadId && pendingGate`, with no dependency a child thread lacks
- Backend or runtime: Not applicable
- Live canary: Not applicable

What the tests prove: the cap refuses a spawn without submitting a child once the parent's non-terminal children reach the limit, and terminal children do not count toward it — so nobody can "fix" the cap by counting every child ever created. For 3b: a gate event recorded before any subscriber exists is replayed to a cold reader with the same run id and gate ref, so the notification's link keeps working for a human who arrives after the fact.

Commands run: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host subagent_spawn_port`; `… cargo test -p ironclaw_assistant --test reborn_services_contract`; `… cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests`; `… cargo clippy -p ironclaw_loop_host --tests -- -D warnings`; `… cargo clippy -p ironclaw_assistant --tests -- -D warnings`; `cargo fmt --check`; `python3 scripts/ci/check-guidance.py`.

## Security Impact

The cap narrows what a model may do — it refuses spawns that were previously admitted — so it cannot widen authority. It reads the caller's own run-tree state through the port the spawn path already holds; no new data crosses a boundary. The 3b change is test-only. No new ingress, credential, or approval path.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: none added.
- [x] Untrusted content into prompts: none — no prompt or content path touched.
- [x] Hashes: none added.
- [x] New/changed variants: none. `max_concurrent_children` is a new field on `SubagentSpawnLimits` with a default; the only construction sites are its own `Default` impl, composition's `::default()` call, and test-module literals (all updated and compiling).
- [x] `serde(default)` fields: none added.
- [x] Bounds: this change *is* a bound. Its own ceiling — a read-then-decide check can briefly overshoot under parallel spawns in one turn — is marked with a `ponytail:` naming the atomic-reservation upgrade path, and the overshoot stays bounded by the per-turn fanout cap and the durable tree cap.
- [x] Error classes: unchanged. The new refusal is a model-visible `spawn_rejected(...)`, matching the fanout and depth caps; the runtime-port error keeps its existing `map_turn_error` mapping.
- [x] Names: unchanged trust boundary.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

`crates/loop/ironclaw_loop_host/src/subagent_spawn_port.rs` (one pre-check plus a limits field), its test module, one new test in `ironclaw_assistant`'s contract suite, and the design doc. Every spawn now performs one additional `children_of` read before creating a child. The capability remains deny-filtered in production until R9, so no production run reaches this path yet.

## Rollback Plan

Revert the branch. The cap is a pre-check with no durable state, so nothing persists to unwind; reverting restores the previous admission behavior exactly.

## Review Follow-Through

- Remaining R2 debt: the `ThreadBusy` immediate re-enqueue in `activate_parked_parent` (the sweep-based heal already ships; the debt is enqueueing into a now-live parent right away).
- Newly identified, recorded in §9 and worth its own slice: the tree-wide descendant cap surfaces as a **run-ending host error** rather than a model-visible refusal, unlike the fanout, depth and new concurrency caps. `ProcessTreeCapacityExceeded` maps through `TurnErrorCategory::CapacityExceeded` → `AgentLoopHostErrorKind::BudgetExceeded` in `map_turn_error` and propagates as `Err`, which `.claude/rules/tool-evidence.md` says a correctable failure should not do. Not fixed here because converting kernel capacity errors into refusals needs care not to mask genuine infra failures.
- Then R4: counters, `ironclaw subagent edges`, un-ignoring the five e2e tests via harness-side enablement, boot-recovery fairness.

---

**Review track**: B
