prs.title: fix(channels): hand chat users the web app address when a setup ceremony can't run in chat
prs.body:
Chat users blocked on a setup ceremony were told where to go and given nothing to click. This hands them the address, and fixes the defects found while proving it.

## The original defect — two CX cells, one shape

| State × Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Not paired yet** × chat | *"Connect this account … from the extension in IronClaw"* — nowhere to click | `…/extensions?configure=<id>&setup=workspace_bot` |
| **Link owed** × chat | *"Open the Ironclaw web app to link the account"* — nowhere to click | `…/extensions` |

Both ship link-free when no public origin is configured, exactly as before.

**Not what the issue proposed.** #7887 asked for per-caller device-link state on `builtin.extension_search`. Investigating the journey showed that was the wrong layer: the state is already resolved correctly on three of the four surfaces (web app, Extensions page, CLI — all verified in the CX matrix). Only the chat surface fails, and it fails on *delivering a URL*. Enriching search would have fixed one of the two cells, for 1 of the 11 extensions that declare a per-user ceremony. Everything here branches on `ChannelConnectionStrategy` / `AuthPromptChallengeKind`, **never a vendor name**.

## What else is in this diff

Each of these came from review or from live QA against the Railway preview, not from scope creep — but they are real additions and the diff should say so.

**Pairing-arm reachability.** The first fix put the link append inside the manifest branch of `connection_notices`, which is unreachable for any extension with a pairing service — i.e. every production `WebGeneratedCode` channel, including the reported one. The append now happens after either branch produces a policy. Found in review; reproduced live before fixing.

**Ceremony in the deep link.** `?configure=<id>` alone opens the connection-*choice* screen, so a workspace-bot pairing notice could offer personal-account setup — the wrong ceremony, which is the confusion this PR exists to remove. Each strategy now names its own path.

**Origin validation.** The origin behind every link was only trimmed and checked non-empty, so `IRONCLAW_REBORN_WEBUI_BASE_URL=app.example.com` rendered a *relative* link into a customer conversation. `validated_connect_link_origin` in `ironclaw_extension_contracts` is now the single owner, replacing three near-duplicate copies that had already drifted.

**Device-link config gap.** A deployment missing `telegram_api_id`/`telegram_api_hash` failed through `DeviceLinkError::Internal`, which the card renders as *"This Telegram account cannot be linked."* — a terminal claim about a perfectly healthy account. New `NotConfigured` code (none of the eleven existing ones meant "the deployment hasn't finished setting this up"; the nearest, `AccountUnavailable`, **is** the false claim), mapped to `MalformedConfig` rather than `BackendUnavailable`, with copy that names the remedy. Same defect class as the headline bug, one surface over.

**Test-isolation fix.** The integration test set a process-global env var and serialized only *writers*, while `start_channel_host` reads it twice and five of six assembly call sites were unguarded — a flake source in a shared binary. All call sites now route through one locked choke point.

## Reviewer attention

**A pinned assertion changed.** `connect_notice_appends_the_link_only_for_oauth_with_a_base_url` looped all three non-OAuth strategies asserting verbatim copy, justified by "a non-OAuth strategy carries its own deep link". That doesn't hold for this notice: `deep_link_template` interpolates a `{code}` the sender hasn't been issued. Two strategies moved to a new test; **the invariant it protects is unchanged and still asserted** — the auto-starting `/chat?connect=` route never ships to a room that cannot deliver privately.

**An architecture ratchet moved.** Contracts size ceiling 10,841 → 11,092, in `d7562e4d5` on its own so it's visible rather than buried. It buys the deletion of three duplicate origin implementations.

**A latent bug fixed in passing.** A blank origin would have rendered `Or connect directly: /chat?connect=slack` — the relative path the doc comment says must never ship.

## Test Strategy

- **Unit/contract:** extended existing suites rather than adding parallel ones. Regression tests for the pairing arm, the ceremony distinction (asserted as a *difference*, so it pins the invariant not today's strings), and the config-gap classification — each verified red first.
- **Integration:** `slack_unserviceable_auth_gate_*` drive a real Slack turn through `start_channel_host_assembly_for_test` — production wiring, real env read — asserting on the actual `chat.postMessage` body. Verified red before green.
- **Frontend:** the terminal-failure panel test asserts a config gap renders `setupIncomplete` and **not** `cannotRetry`; 1470 tests green.
- **Architecture:** full suite green, including the re-pinned ceiling.

**Not covered, stated rather than implied:** the triggered/proactive delivery path (`channel_workflow.rs:200` → `triggered.rs:1157`). Reaching it needs a background run parked on `BlockedAuth`, and no harness seam exists. The two consumption sites were collapsed into one method so the triggered path *cannot diverge* from the live one where the message is built; what remains untested is the forwarding — two adjacent literals reading the same field.

## Live QA

Verified on the Railway preview with a real Telegram bot and real turns. **Link owed passed** on the intended contract (the model called a linked-account tool and the auth gate fired — not the `extension_search` improvisation path). **Not paired yet failed** and drove the pairing-arm fix. **Already linked was blocked** — unreachable without `telegram_api_id`; that whole CX row remains untested on all four surfaces and is the direction where a linked user could be told to link again.

## Compatibility and rollback

No persistence, schema, auth, secret, or network change. `DeviceLinkErrorCode::NotConfigured` is an added enum variant; all consumers match exhaustively and are updated in this diff. Rollback is a plain revert.

Closes #7887

prs.body:
## What

Adds calling guidance to `builtin.shell`'s model-facing description. Description string only — no handler, schema, or validation change.

```diff
-"Execute shell commands with copied v1 validation and saved-file references for large local output"
+"Execute shell commands with copied v1 validation and saved-file references for large local
+ output. One call runs a full shell command line, so related steps belong in a single call
+ (`a && b`, a `for` loop over ids, a heredoc script) rather than one call per step. Pass
+ `workdir` instead of a leading `cd` — the working directory is per-call and does not carry
+ over between calls."
```

## Why

While benchmarking reborn against openclaw and hermes on a 45-task corpus (same model, `deepseek-v4-flash` via OpenRouter, `--parallelism 1`), reborn issued **~2.2× the tool calls for indistinguishable scores**:

| | reborn | openclaw | hermes |
|---|---|---|---|
| tool calls (45 tasks) | **957** | 426 | 639 |
| mean score | 0.915 | 0.915 | 0.947 |

Per-task, on the worst offenders: 102 calls vs 21, 90 vs 8, 67 vs 18. 83–92% of every harness's calls are shell/terminal, so this is almost entirely shell granularity.

Same model in every case, so the difference comes from the tool surface. hermes's `terminal` description carries ~700 characters of calling guidance; `builtin.shell`'s carries none — it describes what the tool *is* and never says how to call it. The observed behaviour matches: reborn does one `ls`, one `cat`, one `grep` per call and pays a round trip each time.

## Both added claims verified against the handler

- **`command` is a full command line.** `a && b`, `for` loops, and heredocs all pass `validate_command` / `detect_command_injection` — those reject specific exfil and escalation shapes (`| sh`, `base64 -d |`, netcat piping, `eval `), not composition.
- **`workdir` is per-call** (`parse_shell_request`, `shell_core.rs`), so a leading `cd` is wasted.

I deliberately did **not** copy hermes's "filesystem and environment persist between calls" framing. reborn's shell does not work that way — `workdir` being a per-call parameter is the evidence — and an agent acting on a false persistence claim would break. Empirically reborn uses `export` in 0% of 2306 shell calls vs hermes's 8%, consistent with that.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p ironclaw_host_runtime` — 875 tests pass, no failures.
- `cargo check -p ironclaw_host_runtime` clean.
- No test or doc referenced the old string (single occurrence in the tree).

**Not measured end-to-end.** I could not A/B this from the benchmark harness: nearai-bench consumes ironclaw as a git dependency, whose crates resolve to several different revisions, so a single-revision path patch won't build. The behavioural claim above is observational (reborn vs two harnesses whose descriptions carry guidance), not a controlled before/after on this diff. If there's a cheap way to run reborn against a branch build I'm happy to produce the paired numbers on the four worst tasks — the effect size should be obvious.

## Risk

Low. Worst case the model reads the hint and batches commands that were always legal.

prs.title: fix(reborn): load the operator .env, and stop reporting session faults as a bad API key
prs.body:
## Summary

Stacked on #7359 (`fix/credential-owner-scoping`), which owns the reason-kind vocabulary the third commit uses.

A real `serve` run failed with *"model credentials or provider configuration are invalid. Check the selected provider's API key and base URL"*. The key was valid the whole time — a live check against `cloud-api.near.ai` returned HTTP 200, and the configured model was in the response. Three separate defects sat between that healthy key and that message:

- **The key was never read.** `dotenvy::dotenv()` searches upward from the working directory only, so a host started anywhere but a checkout carrying a `.env` boots with none of its bootstrap variables — even though its own Reborn home holds them, beside the `config.toml` that names them. `api_key_env = "NEARAI_API_KEY"` resolved to no credential, so `uses_api_key()` was false and the nearai provider took the session-token branch instead of the Bearer-key one.
- **The dead end was retried.** Nothing calls `attach_renewer`, so every `serve` boot gets `NoopSessionRenewer`. It reported "renewal is unavailable in this build" as `SessionRenewalFailed`, which `is_retryable` treats as retryable — correctly for that variant, since a renewal *attempt* can fail transiently. "No renewal path exists here" is settled before the first attempt, so each failing run burned three attempts and ~7s of backoff before failing anyway.
- **The advice named the wrong thing.** Session faults carried no reason kind, so they inherited the bad-key sentence and sent the operator to inspect a value that had no part in the failure.

`credential_unavailable_faults_carry_distinct_reason_kinds` (added in #7359) predicted the third exactly: *"adding a fourth producer that forgets its reason kind silently rejoins the bad-key bucket."* These were that producer.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Linked Issue

None — found while diagnosing a live `serve` failure.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings` (exit 0)
- [x] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `ironclaw_llm` 922, `ironclaw_loop_host` 633, `ironclaw_turn_runner` 242, `ironclaw_assistant` 405, `ironclaw` smoke 149, `ironclaw_architecture_tests` all green
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` — Not applicable: no database-backed or runtime-integration behavior changed
- [x] Manual testing: reproduced the original failure from the live host's logs; confirmed the stored key returns HTTP 200 from `cloud-api.near.ai` and that the configured model is in its model list, establishing that the credential was healthy and only invisible to the process (`ps eww` on the running `serve` showed 39 env vars, none of them `NEARAI_*`)

One flake, unrelated to this change: `onboard_login_link_then_bearer_authorizes_a_protected_request` failed once in a full smoke run and passed on re-run and in isolation. It spawns a real `serve` and binds a port chosen by `unused_local_port()`, a TOCTOU race that is live on a machine already running `ironclaw serve`. This change is inert there — those temp homes contain no `.env`, and a missing file is ignored.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: an operator whose credentials live in the Reborn home gets a working host instead of a run that fails naming a key it never read; when a session genuinely cannot be established, the run fails on the first attempt and the message says to sign in again rather than to check an API key.

Risk areas:
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior
- [ ] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [ ] Persistence
- [ ] Security or permissions

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: `model_gateway.rs::session_faults_are_not_reported_as_invalid_credentials` (all three session variants); `session.rs::ensure_authenticated_without_a_renewer_fails_permanently`; `retry.rs::unavailable_session_renewal_is_not_retried`; classifier assertions in `retry.rs` and `circuit_breaker.rs`
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: the `.env` seam is process bootstrap, reachable only by spawning the real binary (covered at the CLI tier below); the error-classification changes are pure mappings whose callers are covered at crate tier
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no model request/response shape changed
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: no user-visible WebUI flow changed
- Backend or runtime: `smoke.rs` — three tests driving the real `ironclaw` binary for `.env` precedence
- Live canary: Not applicable

What the tests prove: the Reborn-home `.env` reaches the process environment, and precedence holds in both directions (an exported variable outranks the file; a working-directory file outranks the home one) — so `dotenvy` cannot be switched to override mode without a failure. A renewal that cannot happen is attempted exactly once, asserted as an attempt count through `RetryProvider` rather than on the classifier alone, because that is the only place the regression is observable. Every session fault names its own cause instead of the bad-key sentence.

Each of the three was watched failing for the right reason before its fix.

Commands run:

```
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test -p ironclaw_llm --lib
cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --lib
cargo test -p ironclaw_turn_runner --lib
cargo test -p ironclaw_assistant --lib
cargo test -p ironclaw --test smoke
cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests
bash scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh
```

## Security Impact

No change to permissions, secret storage, redaction, or network reach. One deliberate non-change: `~/.ironclaw/.env` (the v1 state root) is **not** a fallback. `home.rs` actively refuses that directory as a Reborn home, and reborn writes nothing there any more, so reading it back would resurrect a fenced-off path. Operators carrying a v1 file move it to `$IRONCLAW_REBORN_HOME/.env`; `.env.example` documents the load order. Secret *values* are never logged — the new warning lines name a path and an error, never a variable's contents.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: none added. `SessionRenewalUnavailable` is a plain error variant with no authority.
- Untrusted content enters prompts only through an envelope/escaping primitive: N/A — no prompt path touched.
- Hashes declare purpose: N/A — no hashing.
- New/changed status, exit, policy, runtime, or error variants: **yes** — `LlmError::SessionRenewalUnavailable`. `LlmError` is matched exhaustively with no `_` arms, so the compiler enumerated the call sites; `cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets` surfaced the one outside the crates I had already edited (`tools/ironclaw_stress/src/user_turn.rs`, now handled). Command: `cargo check --workspace --all-features --all-targets`.
- Security/durability `serde(default)` fields: N/A — no serialized shape changed. `LlmError` is not persisted or sent over the wire.
- Queues/maps/buffers/counters: N/A.
- Driver/operator-visible errors have stable class semantics: **this is the point of the change.** The new variant is permanent where its sibling is transient, and it is non-retryable for `RetryProvider` and non-tripping for the circuit breaker, because a local configuration gap must not blame a healthy backend and take every other caller of that provider down with it. `ironclaw_llm/CONTRACT.md` enumerates both classification lists explicitly and is updated in the same commit.
- Sandbox/native/host names accurately describe trust boundary: N/A.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

- `ironclaw_cli` bootstrap: every command now sees the Reborn-home `.env`. Because `dotenvy` never overwrites a set variable, a host that already exported its variables is bit-for-bit unaffected; the only behavior change is for variables that were previously invisible.
- `ironclaw_llm`: one new `LlmError` variant, produced today only by `NoopSessionRenewer`. Callers that grouped it with its sibling still group it (`ironclaw_stress` buckets both as `model_provider_auth`).
- `ironclaw_loop_host`: session faults keep `CredentialUnavailable`, so retry/fail-fast behavior at the loop tier is unchanged; only the reason kind and the safe summary differ, which changes the sentence the operator reads.

The plausible surprise is an operator who had a stale `$IRONCLAW_REBORN_HOME/.env` that was silently ignored and is now honored — but it still loses to anything exported, and honoring the file beside `config.toml` is the intended contract.

## Rollback Plan

Three independent commits, each revertable alone:

- `cff1acd` CLI `.env` loading — revert restores cwd-only loading.
- `847cf53` `SessionRenewalUnavailable` — revert restores the single variant and its retryable classification.
- `ff38a1a` session reason kind — revert restores the shared bad-key sentence.

No migration, no persisted state, no wire format, so revert is immediate and needs no data fix-up.

## Review Follow-Through

Two judgement calls worth a reviewer's eye:

1. **No v1 `.env` fallback** (see Security Impact). If we would rather read `~/.ironclaw/.env` with a deprecation warning for existing installs, that is a small addition — but it points reborn at the state root `home.rs` refuses, so I left it out deliberately rather than by omission.
2. **`SessionExpired` keeps tripping the circuit breaker** (`is_transient` returns true for it, unchanged). That predates this PR and is arguably the same category error as the retry bug fixed here, but changing it is a behavior change with its own blast radius and did not belong in the same diff.

Still not fixed, and out of scope: `serve` has no way to *recover* from a genuine session expiry, because there is no interactive terminal and no renewer is wired. The message now tells the operator to sign in again; making the run actually offer that through the existing auth-card surface is a feature, not a bug fix.

---

**Review track**: C (runtime + operator-visible error semantics)

prs.body:
## Summary

- Make the neutral `IRONCLAW_*` environment variables and configuration names canonical.
- Use `~/.ironclaw` as the default product home.
- Keep existing `IRONCLAW_REBORN_*` variables, service identities, paths, and Docker placeholders as compatibility aliases.
- Prevent installation of a canonical service alongside an existing legacy service.
- Ensure canonical and legacy inputs converge on the same validated configuration paths.
- Canonicalize Docker default-config paths before enforcing the `/opt/ironclaw/` boundary.
- Optimize startup environment alias projection from O(N²) to O(N).
- Update Docker, service-management, configuration documentation, and contract tests for the new defaults.

## Change Type

- [x] Feature
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor

- `cargo test --test dockerfile_runtime_home`: 22 tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `scripts/ci/check-hermetic-env.sh`: passed.
- `scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`: passed.
- `sh -n docker/reborn/entrypoint.sh`: passed.
- ShellCheck: Not run locally because `shellcheck` was unavailable.

## Test Strategy

- Unit: canonical defaults, environment parsing, legacy aliases, and service identity compatibility.
- Integration: Docker runtime-home, canonicalized config paths, and configuration contracts.
- Compatibility: legacy environment variables, service identities, paths, and Docker command placeholders remain covered.
- Security: Docker config paths are resolved through `realpath` before enforcing the `/opt/ironclaw/` boundary.
- Browser: Not applicable; configuration resolution is tested below the browser layer.
- Live canary: Not applicable; no external provider contract changes.

## Security Impact

Canonical and legacy configuration inputs use the same fail-closed validation paths. Docker default-config paths are canonicalized before boundary validation, preventing symlink-based escapes from `/opt/ironclaw/`. Secret mediation, authentication, and authorization behavior are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Bootstrap configuration, startup environment aliases, service installation and management, Docker defaults and explicit command compatibility, runtime-home selection, and related documentation.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this PR. Existing legacy aliases allow deployments to roll back without immediately rewriting their configuration. Operators who have migrated to the canonical service identity may need to reinstall or restart the legacy service after rollback.

prs.title: feat(reborn): env-overridable compaction context budget (cut multi-turn re-send cost)
prs.body:
**Stacked on #5149 (progressive tool disclosure).** Disclosure cuts the tool-*schema* cost; this cuts the tool-*result/history* cost.

## Problem
reborn's compaction lets the visible transcript grow to **~108k tokens** (`context_limit 128k − reserve 20k`) before compacting. On long, tool-heavy tasks the agent re-sends a near-full context window **every turn** → the dominant token cost. On pinchbench log-analysis tasks this produced **1–5.6M cumulative input tokens** per task.

## Change
Make the compaction budget env-overridable: `IRONCLAW_PROMPT_CONTEXT_LIMIT_TOKENS` / `IRONCLAW_PROMPT_CONTEXT_RESERVE_TOKENS`. **Unset ⇒ the compiled 128k/20k defaults**, so it's a pure no-op for existing deployments. reborn flows through `PromptContextTokenBudget::default()`, so the override takes effect there; an operator (or nearai-bench) can tighten it to compact sooner.

## Measured A/B (deepseek-v4-flash, disclosure on, 64k vs 128k)
5 cost-dominant pinchbench tasks:

| task | 128k | 64k | Δ | score |
|---|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| task_events | 1.33M | 0.66M | −50% | 0.74→0.73 |
| log_apache_timeline | 3.71M | 1.61M | −57% | 1.0→1.0 |
| log_ssh_brute_force | 1.30M | 1.00M | −24% | 1.0→1.0 |
| log_syslog_auth_failures | 1.57M | 1.30M | −18% | 0.925→0.925 |
| log_apache_client_issues | 0.89M | 0.87M | −2% | 1.0→1.0 |
| **total** | **8.81M** | **5.43M** | **−38%** | all held |

Full-suite clean pinchbench validation (no infra failures, vs the disclosure baseline) is running; numbers to follow.

## Summary

- Replace the former standalone staging-sync workflow with a combined `Main CI Checks` workflow.
- Keep Slack alerts for failed push-to-main CI workflows via `MAIN_CI_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URLS`.
- Fast-forward `staging-release` to a green `main` commit after required push-to-main CI workflows pass for that SHA.
- Preserve fast-forward-only behavior: the workflow skips when `staging-release` already contains the SHA and fails rather than overwriting staging-release-only commits.

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [x] CI/Infrastructure
- [ ] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None.

## Validation

- [x] Created `origin/staging-release` from current `origin/main` with a normal push.
- [x] Parsed `.github/workflows/main-ci-checks.yml` as YAML locally.
- [x] Checked embedded shell snippets with `bash -n`.
- [x] Ran `git diff --check` for the workflow changes.
- [ ] `actionlint` was not available locally.

## Security Impact

This workflow uses the dedicated `MAIN_CI_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URLS` secret for Slack alert delivery and does not print webhook values. The staging-release promotion job grants `contents: write` only to the job that updates `refs/heads/staging-release`, and it performs a normal non-force push. It does not run untrusted PR code; it reacts to completed push-to-main workflow runs.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

N/A: GitHub Actions automation only; no Reborn runtime, trust-bearing type, prompt ingress, policy, sandbox, DB, or host-boundary behavior is changed.

## Database Impact

None.

## Blast Radius

Touches GitHub Actions automation for main CI alerting and branch promotion from `main` to `staging-release`. Possible breakage is limited to Slack alert delivery and the workflow's ability to fast-forward the staging-release ref.

## Rollback Plan

Revert this PR to restore the Slack-only main CI alert workflow and remove automatic staging-release promotion. If promotion must be paused without reverting, protect `staging-release` against direct pushes or disable the `Main CI Checks` workflow.

## Review Follow-Through

Reviewer should confirm the required workflow list and whether `staging-release` should stay fast-forward-only from `main`.

---

**Review track**: C (CI)



Note: This workflow targets `staging-release` (not `staging`) for automated main→staging release fast-forwarding.

prs.title: feat(tool-search): make deferred-tool retrieval a swappable provider
prs.body:
## Reborn: make deferred-tool retrieval a swappable provider

Follows the seam [#6345](https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/pull/6345) established for memory: the host depends on a **port**, the host-bundled implementation becomes one *binding* of it, and nothing below `app` names a concrete provider. This does the same for the ranker behind `tool_search`.

Today `AuthorizedToolSearchIndex` is a concrete `pub(crate)` type constructed inline in `tool_disclosure_port.rs`. It is a good ranker — bounded BM25F, field-weighted, IDF, length-normalized — but it is the *only* ranker reachable, and swapping it means editing the loop host. A deployment that wants a dense retriever, a hosted ranking service, or a domain-tuned index has no seam to bind one through.

### The port

`ironclaw_loop_contracts::tool_retrieval` — declarations only, no ranking logic:

- `ToolRetrievalProvider::fit(&[ProviderToolDefinition]) -> Arc<dyn ToolRetrievalIndex>`
- `ToolRetrievalIndex::search(&str, limit) -> ToolSearchOutcome`
- `ToolSearchOutcome` / `ToolSearchQueryClass` (moved from `tool_search.rs`, which now aliases them so the module and its tests keep their local vocabulary)

**Why two traits rather than one `rank(query, corpus)` call.** Ranking is fitted, not stateless. The host already rebuilds the corpus only on a genuine surface change (turn boundary, surface version, or definition fingerprint) and then serves many `tool_search` calls against that one fitted corpus. Splitting fit from search keeps that amortization in the port, instead of forcing every provider to re-derive per-call state or hide a cache behind interior mutability.

The module docs carry the three contracts an implementation must hold, each of which the current ranker already satisfies and a careless replacement would not:

- **Authorization** — `fit` is only ever handed the effective authorized definitions; a provider must not widen that set, and denied schemas must not reach corpus statistics, ordering, or counts.
- **Determinism** — one fitted index must rank a given `(query, limit)` identically every time, tie-breaks included. The host records search rank into turn state, so a nondeterministic ranker makes disclosure order irreproducible.
- **Confidentiality** — no logging of raw queries or schema text. This is why the host emits only query *class*, count, and latency.

### Wiring

- `NativeBm25fToolRetrieval` in `ironclaw_loop_host::tool_search` implements the port over the existing index. The ranker's code is untouched — it moved behind a trait, it did not change.
- `ToolDisclosureCapabilityDecorator::new` binds it by default, so **behavior is identical unless a deployment opts out**. `with_retrieval_provider(...)` is the opt-out.
- `ToolDisclosureTurnState::search_index` is now `Arc<dyn ToolRetrievalIndex>`; the host holds the port type only.

### One real behavior change: the fingerprint covers the ranker

`definitions_fingerprint` hashed the `RANKER_VERSION` *constant*. With a bindable provider that is a latent bug — rebinding retrieval would leave the cached fitted index in place until the surface happened to change, silently serving the previous ranker's results. It now takes the bound provider's `ranker_version()`. Covered by `fingerprint_separates_rankers_over_an_identical_corpus`.

The rebuild log line gained a `ranker_version` field so a trace can be attributed to the ranker that produced it.

### Tests

- `tool_search_ranks_with_the_bound_retrieval_provider_not_the_native_one` — the swap test. Same corpus and query through both bindings; asserts the native ranking, asserts the bound provider's ranking is what `tool_search` actually returns, asserts the two differ (so the test cannot pass vacuously), and asserts the provider was fitted exactly once over the whole authorized corpus.
- `fingerprint_separates_rankers_over_an_identical_corpus`, `native_provider_reports_the_ranker_version_it_fingerprints_with`.
- All 922 existing `ironclaw_loop_host` tests pass unchanged — including `committed_corpus_quality_gate_and_benchmark_report`, the retrieval-quality gate, which is the load-bearing evidence that the default binding did not shift ranking.

### Architecture ratchet raised

`reborn_contracts_crates_carry_a_checked_size_ceiling`: `ironclaw_loop_contracts` 13_107 → 13_246 (+139). `main` sits exactly at its ceiling, so this is an explicit raise, per the gate's own instruction to record the reason here.

The growth is the port traits, two DTOs, and the contract doc comments above — no ranking logic crossed the tier. The BM25F implementation stays whole in `ironclaw_loop_host::tool_search`, still the only crate in the workspace that names it. I first cut ~35 lines of speculative surface from this module (an `Empty*` no-op provider pair with no caller in this PR) rather than ratchet for API nothing uses; `ToolSearchOutcome::no_match()` survived because the native ranker now uses it for its two early returns.

**No provider-neutrality dependency gate yet, deliberately.** The memory analogue (`only_the_sanctioned_residue_names_a_memory_provider`) polices crate *edges*, and exists because the memory providers are separate packages. This PR adds no second provider crate, so that gate would have nothing to measure. It belongs with the first alternate provider, which is where the `[tool_retrieval]` binding config also belongs — a binding policy selecting between one option is dead config.

### Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p ironclaw_loop_contracts -p ironclaw_loop_host --all-targets -- -D warnings` — zero warnings
- `cargo check --workspace --tests` — clean
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host` — 922 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests` — green with the ratchet above

prs.title: feat(reborn): enable final-answer nudge for interactive runs
prs.body:
## What

Enable the existing **final-answer nudge** for the interactive run profile (the profile `ironclaw-reborn` resolves to), so a turn that would otherwise end **empty** instead synthesizes a closing answer.

## Why

`loop_exit::try_final_answer_nudge` already exists: when the loop would fail closed with no real assistant reply — model-call budget exhausted (`budget.rs:48`) or no-progress detected (`loop_exit.rs:201`) — it issues **one tool-free** model call to synthesize a closing answer from the work already done, routed through the normal reply-admission gate. It's the reborn equivalent of the legacy loop's force-text-recovery.

It was gated off for every profile via `SteeringPolicy.allow_driver_specific_nudges = false`, so in practice a budget/no-progress-exhausted interactive turn finalizes an **empty/failed** turn. On the PinchBench benchmark this shows up as tasks that do real work but return an empty response (scored 0.0).

## Change

One line in `run_profile/resolver.rs`: set `allow_driver_specific_nudges: true` in `interactive_profile()`. The mission profile is left unchanged. Behavior is strictly additive — the nudge only fires on a path that would otherwise produce no answer, is capped at one nudge per run, and a still-empty/declined nudge falls back to the existing typed failure.

## Test

`cargo check -p ironclaw_turns` passes. Existing loop-exit / budget tests unchanged (they construct their own policies).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Failure-mode evidence (why this matters)

Scanning the 2026-06-23 reborn / DeepSeek-V4-Flash baselines, this exact fail-closed-empty path (real work done, then the loop ends with an empty response, `error: null`) accounts for tasks on **both** suites measured:

- **PinchBench:** `csv_gdp_regions`, `earnings_analysis` — 46 and 16 tool calls, then empty (scored 0.0).
- **OfficeQA:** 10 tasks (`UID0031/0037/0110/0219/0114/0165/0244/0175/0150/0208`) — 36–90 tool calls navigating the source document, then empty (scored 0.0).

All show the budget/iteration-exhaustion signal in their debug logs — precisely where `try_final_answer_nudge` fires. So this is 12 candidate recoveries across two suites from a one-line gate flip, not a single-task fix.

**Note on measuring it:** the nudge-eligible condition (clean budget exhaustion) doesn't reproduce on a slow local box — there the turn trips reborn's internal 180s poll-timeout first, a different exit the nudge doesn't cover. Confirming the score impact needs a CI run (the harness's full-suite reborn run currently exceeds the 90-min CI cap, so a small subset suite of the tasks above is the fastest way to verify).

prs.title: docs(design): Telegram linked-device — proposal, plan, checklist, ADR
prs.body:
**Design only. No production code, no behavior change.** Opened as a draft for
review; sign-off is explicitly withheld (see Status below).

## What this is

The engineering spec for letting a user link their **personal Telegram account**
as a real MTProto linked device — what Telegram Desktop is, visible and revocable
in Telegram's Settings → Devices — so the agent can read their conversations and
act as them through the standard messaging operations.

Five documents under `docs/internal/design/telegram-linked-device/`:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | Overview, system architecture, footprint, explicit non-goals |
| `PROPOSAL.md` | Decisions with rationale, per-crate change inventory, review log |
| `PLAN.md` | 8 PRs with dependency edges and per-PR watch-lists |
| `CHECKLIST.md` | Definition of done — each box names something to run or read |
| `ADR-device-link-auth-hook.md` | The auth-hook decision and what it costs |

Also included: `2026-08-07-linked-accounts-design.md`, the network-generic study
this narrowed from (still the reference for WhatsApp/Signal and the deferred
inbound/mirror work).

## The load-bearing decisions

- **Reads are live; no message content is persisted.** Telegram is a cloud
  messenger, so history and search are server-side. That removes the mirror
  crate, the FTS plane, the retention policy, and — because no update stream is
  consumed — the session-sourced ingress ADR from v1.
- **Device-link is an auth method with a narrow adapter hook.** MTProto login is
  a protocol handshake no descriptor can express. This takes the
  extension-runtime spec's own revisit trigger ("a vendor defeats the
  descriptor"). It revokes a stated security invariant; the ADR records the real
  compensation set and the in-process-vs-sidecar trade rather than burying it.
- **Custody extends `ironclaw_auth`** — a linked account *is* a
  `CredentialAccount`. The only genuinely new persistence surface is a
  compare-and-swap write path for a mutable binary secret.
- **Sessions live in the existing telegram package** behind a
  contracts-declared port. **No new crates, no new runtime lane.**

## Why the footprint is what it is

17 crates, mostly small additive arms; the real work is one package and one
frontend card. The count moved five times (9 → 12 → 16 → 18 → 17) — every
correction came from an audit that actually ran the greps rather than from
re-reading the document.

## Verification

Vendor claims were read out of the `grammers` 0.10.0 sources and the reference QR
implementations rather than assumed (§14.1). Several turned out to matter:

- Pull-only operation is safe, and QR **polling** is correct and officially
  precedented — an earlier revision had switched to update-driven on reasonable
  but mistaken review pressure.
- There is **no connector injection point**; `Session::dc_option` is the only
  seam — and it is airtight only because 0.10.0 never persists server-pushed
  addresses. **This makes the `=0.10.0` pin a security control**, not hygiene.
- A retry policy cannot see whether a request is a write, so `NoRetries` plus an
  explicit wrapper is the only way to keep the agent from double-sending as the
  user.

The whole document was then re-verified against `origin/main` after upstream
#7377/#7397 landed (§14.4). Those removed owner-vs-actor and made every run act
as its invoker — which **structurally retired this design's worst finding** and
let the loop-tier enforcement it required leave the footprint.

## Status: sign-off withheld

Two adversarial security passes; the second still withheld sign-off. The
remaining conditions are in the review log (§14.2–14.4). Known open items:

- Supply-chain controls must ship **with** the grammers dependency, not in a
  later hardening pass.
- `sent_unverified` requires a schema **`.v2` graduation** — the standard's
  immutability rule forbids the in-place `.v1` edit an earlier revision proposed.
- Read content is attacker-controlled (a personal account can be DM'd by anyone);
  §6.4 sets the obligation, and upstream #7397 now supplies the pattern to reuse.
- grammers is unaudited and runs in-process. Recorded as an accepted risk with a
  revisit trigger at **N = 2 linked accounts**, not GA.

**Not approved for implementation.** Review the decisions and the withheld
sign-off first.

## Test Strategy

Not applicable: documentation only. The docs publication-boundary gate
(`python3 scripts/ci/docs_publication_boundary.py`) passes; all pages are fenced
under `docs/internal/`.

prs.title: PREVIEW ONLY — Epic #7781 phases 2–3 integrated (do not merge)
prs.body:
> ## ⚠ Integration branch — **preview only, do not merge**
> This exists so Epic #7781 phases 2–3 can be evaluated **as one running app** before any of it merges.
> It is a pure merge of three PRs and carries **no unique commits**. The PRs below stay the merge units.

## What's in here

| PR | Phase | Contributes |
|---|---|---|
| **#7831** | 3a CI | The Chromatic visual-regression lane (rescoped — its token half moved into #8011) |
| **#8011** | 3 | The M3 reskin: palette, type ramp + density, fonts, shim retirement, `tonal` variant |

#8011 is based on `main` and self-contained, so this branch is `#8011 ⊕ #7994`. Merged clean — no conflicts. #7831 is **not** included: it is CI-only now and changes nothing a preview can show.

**160 files, +3088 / −1103** against `main`.

## 🔗 Preview — `https://ironclaw-ironclaw-pr-8005.up.railway.app`

Deployed and verified. Tokens read back from the running page via `getComputedStyle`, both themes:

| | dark | light |
|---|---|---|
| `--v2-canvas` | `#0f0f0f` | `#fcfcfc` |
| `--v2-surface` | `#1f1f1f` | `#fff` |
| `--v2-surface-muted` | `#232425` | `#f2f0f0` |
| `--v2-accent` | `#203b9c` | `#9dd2ff` |
| `--v2-accent-on` | `#fff` | `#041e49` |
| `--v2-text-faint` | `#898b8e` | `#6c6e6d` |
| `--v2-radius-control` | `9999px` | `9999px` |
| `--v2-elevation-1` | `0 1px 3px #00000080` | — |
| `--v2-accent-gradient` | `#203b9c` (flat) | — |

The last row is the by-reference change working: the gradient token resolves through `--v2-accent` rather than carrying its own literal.

**You will need to sign in to see past the login page.** Unauthenticated, the preview shows the login screen only — which does exercise the palette, the pill controls and the 12px field, but has no primary-accent button on it (both CTAs are Button's `secondary` variant, a pre-existing choice). The accent container is best judged in Storybook or in the [review page](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/aa758335-4bd1-4f67-87fc-b28ed5dfde49) until you're logged in.

## How to evaluate

The Railway preview on this PR serves the **whole app** with all three landed together — which is the thing none of the individual PRs can show you:

- **#7831 alone** changes nothing visually (that's its acceptance criterion).
- **#8011 alone** is the reskin, and previews fine on its own — but not alongside the governance page it is judged against.
- **#7994 alone** is documentation.

Worth looking at in both themes (the theme toggle is in the app):

1. **Light mode primary buttons.** On `main` these are white on `#2e9de2` — 2.98:1, failing AA. Here they are a dark label on the `#9dd2ff` tonal container.
2. **Control shape.** Buttons, chips and nav rows are pills now; fields 12px, cards 16px, dialogs 28px.
3. **Surface ladder.** Dark moves from blue-tinted greys to Gemini's neutral near-black (`#0f0f0f` → `#171717` → `#1f1f1f` → `#232425`). Light inverts to white panels on an off-white `#fcfcfc` canvas.
4. **Depth.** Tonal rather than shadowed — the resting elevation step is a 1px contact shadow, not a 30px ambient one.

Design rationale and a live proposed/current compare: **[the reskin review page](https://claude.ai/code/artifact/aa758335-4bd1-4f67-87fc-b28ed5dfde49)**.

## What this preview will NOT show

Setting expectations, because the gap is deliberate:

- **App pages outside the design system keep their old shape.** They pick up the new *palette* through the `app.css` compat shim, so they stay coherent — but their radii, spacing and elevation are untouched until WS3b (#7890 retires the shim; 682 call sites across 72 files, only 6 with a story).
- **No fonts.** Roboto Flex / Roboto Mono vendoring is still open in WS3.
- **No new components or motion.** Those are Phase 4 (#7782).
- **`DESIGN.md` is up to date** as of the latest push to #7994: its token-mapping table carries the shipped values per theme, and "open items" became "what Phase 3 resolved". The two genuinely open items — the motion mechanism and the unconsumed expressive accents — are marked as such.

## Validation

Run on this merged branch, at `crates/product/ironclaw_webui/frontend` unless noted:

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint:conventions` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test:storybook` — 105 tests / 32 files passed
- [x] `pnpm build` — bundle budgets + the design-token bundle contract (40 properties, 4 utilities in `dist/assets`)
- [x] `python3 scripts/ci/check-guidance.py` — OK (2618 path references, 62 frontmatter globs live)

`pnpm test`: the two pre-existing files (`theme.test.tsx`, `inspector-panel.test.tsx`) fail identically on `main` under Node 26 — unrelated to any of this work.

## Keeping it in sync

This branch is disposable. When any constituent PR moves, recreate rather than patch:

```bash
git fetch origin && git checkout -B webui/design-system-phases-2-3 origin/webui/gemini-theme-tokens && git merge --no-ff origin/docs/webui-design-system-governance
```

Two things, both docs/tooling only (no product code changes):

1. **An interactive architecture explorer** for the target Reborn architecture described in `docs/reborn/2026-07-17-architecture-simplification-dto-dyn-local.md` (#6175/#6208).
2. **A reusable `architecture-diagram` skill** that extracts the process used to build it, so the same explorer can be regenerated for any codebase / design doc.

## `docs/reborn/2026-07-17-architecture-simplification-explorer.html`

A single self-contained file (no CDN/fonts/network, theme-aware, opens offline):

- **Clickable stack diagram** — products / interfaces / kernel / runtime lanes / substrates. Clicking a node drives an inspector with its role, interface signature, types, "changes when", and refactor status.
- **Capability as first-class citizen** — the self-extension / multi-tenancy / consistency binding, and the 7-step lifecycle (Declare → Register → Grant → Authorize → Lease → Dispatch → Isolate).
- **Refactor progress** — status dots on every node + a per-slice progress section, mapped to merged/open PRs and the frozen §10 ratchet counts (Slice A stores, Slice B `Local*`, Slice C DTO/`dyn`, §5.8 products-out-of-composition). Vocabulary landed in `host_api` is marked done; the `authorize()` fold wiring is marked in-flight.
- **Scope of cleaning** — a demolition ledger: what gets deleted, staged, with magnitudes measured from the tree (e.g. the 4,258-LOC `InMemoryTurnStateStore`, ~123K LOC of product code in the composition god-crate) and the `build → migrate → delete` ordering.

> Status overlay is a point-in-time snapshot (stamped **2026-07-18** in the page). Pips are indicative groupings; the authoritative remaining-debt numbers are the ratchet allowlist counts.

## `.claude/skills/architecture-diagram/`

- **`SKILL.md`** — recipe-driven procedure in three composable modes: code → diagram; + design doc → current→target transition/ledger; + PRs → progress. Uses grep/`gh`/`wc` recipes that re-derive facts (no hardcoded file maps), verifies "done" against HEAD, and labels relocated-vs-deleted honestly.
- **`references/explorer-template.html`** — a **data-driven** scaffold: the engine renders the stack, inspector, dots, progress cards, and ledger from JS data objects, so the author edits only data (no HTML hand-authoring, no tag-balance risk). Emptying an array hides its section.

## Verification

- `node --check` on the script blocks (both files) — JS parses.
- HTML tag balance — clean.
- Template example ids (`LAYERS`/`STATUS`) all resolve to `DATA` entries (the skill's Step-6 check).
- Authored per `ironclaw-reborn-skill-maintainer`: frontmatter description is triggers-only; recipes over maps; v1 legacy enclave excluded from the Reborn model; dated worked-example provenance.

## Notes

- Not run: the maintainer's fresh-subagent RED-GREEN trap test (rule 9) — happy to run it if you want it recorded before merge.
- The explorer `.html` is a build artifact, not regenerated by CI; it carries an `as-of` date and will drift as the refactor lands. It's meant as a snapshot companion to the design note.

prs.title: fix(compaction): harden oversized turn cuts
prs.body:
## Summary

- Cut compaction at an explicit retained user/assistant boundary and reject retained suffixes beginning with tool results.
- Support oversized single turns by preserving assistant tool calls with their following results while summarizing the preceding prefix.
- Scan complete durable bodies before applying UTF-8-safe, summarizer-input-only head/tail truncation.
- Emit typed truncation counts and omitted-byte evidence without logging or deleting content.
- Surface prompt-budget truncation watermarks through the existing canonical compaction path.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

Related #7824

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`
- [x] `cargo test -p ironclaw_loop_host --test compaction_task_contract` — 61 passed
- [x] Focused `ironclaw_agent_loop` compaction strategy tests — 22 passed
- [x] Assistant/tool-result split caller test passed
- [x] Compaction wire compatibility test passed
- [x] `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p ironclaw_integration_tests --test reborn_integration_model_recovery` — 30 passed
- [ ] Full workspace gates: CI

One unrelated existing `ironclaw_turn_runner::trace_capture` test failed in a broader package run; the changed turn-runner compaction test passed separately.

## Test Strategy

User behavior: a history containing one oversized turn still compacts. The next prompt retains the assistant tool call and all following results together, while the summarizer receives a bounded representation and durable history remains complete.

Risk areas:
- [x] Model behavior
- [ ] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [ ] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: cut selection, first-retained validation, complete-body scanning, UTF-8 truncation, typed response/wire compatibility.
- Reborn integration: overflow recovery drives oversized durable content through real compaction, asserts typed milestone evidence, and reads original history back.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable.
- Backend or runtime: focused turn-runner compaction wiring test.
- Live canary: Not applicable.

What the tests prove: no retained suffix starts at a tool result, assistant call/results remain together, injection in the omitted middle is rejected before truncation, only summarizer input is shortened, and truncation telemetry contains counts only.

## Security Impact

Complete raw bodies are injection/leak scanned before truncation. Single-message validation scans without a full-body copy; multi-message cross-boundary validation uses one fallibly reserved raw buffer rather than XML-expanding the full input. No content, marker range, or secret enters telemetry.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Additive typed compaction request/response fields own the boundary.
- [x] Untrusted content is scanned before omission and XML-framed only after bounding.
- [x] No hashes or authenticity checks changed.
- [x] New serde fields default and omit when absent for old checkpoint compatibility.
- [x] Counts use checked/saturating arithmetic and fallible allocation.
- [x] Durable transcript rows remain unchanged.
- [x] No runtime lane or sandbox boundary changed.

## Database Impact

None. Original transcript and summary artifacts remain append-only. Truncation is system-inference-input-only.

## Blast Radius

Compaction request/response/progress vocabulary, turn-cut strategy, loop-host prompt budget projection, and focused test fixtures.

## Rollback Plan

Revert the commit. Additive fields default for older wire/checkpoint shapes; no stored data rewrite is required.

## Review Follow-Through

Retained-tail/model-window values and replay deduplication are deliberately unchanged. Budget retuning and natural threshold benchmarking remain follow-up #7824 slices.

prs.title: feat(reborn): admin UI for tenant-shared tool credentials (#5459 part 1b)
prs.body:
Sibling to #5499. Addresses the same credential dimension of https://github.com/nearai/ironclaw/issues/5459 but via the WebUI rather than environment variables.

## What this does

For tools that require a **shared API key** (one key for the whole tenant — e.g. an org-wide market-data subscription), an admin can now set that key through the Extensions UI at runtime, without touching the server environment.

### Configure button on extension cards

Tools that declare a shared credential in their manifest get a **Configure** primary action button on their extension card. Previously this was buried in the 3-dot overflow as "Reconfigure". The button is prominent before the key is set; once configured, the card reflects the new state.

### Shared-credential form

The Configure modal shows a single value field (the handle is displayed as a read-only label — it is not something the user names, it comes from the manifest). Submitting stores the value at the **tenant-shared scope** under that handle.

### Operator endpoint

`POST /api/webchat/v2/operator/shared-credentials` — accepts `{ handle, value }`, writes to the tenant-shared secret scope. Admin-only. New DTOs: `LifecycleSharedCredential`, `RebornSharedCredential`.

## How it relates to #5499

Both PRs use the same underlying mechanism:

- **Storage**: tenant-shared scope (`__ironclaw_tenant_shared_admin__` sentinel user)
- **Resolution**: `secret_owner_scope` — checks caller's own scope first, falls back to tenant-shared, returns `AuthRequired` if absent
- **Injection**: host-mediated — the WASM never sees the secret value; it is injected as an HTTP header at egress per the manifest declaration

The difference is the write path:
- **#5499** (env-seed): operator sets `IRONCLAW_REBORN_DEV_SECRET__<handle>=<value>` at serve startup — good for dev/CI
- **This PR** (admin UI): admin sets the value through the WebUI at runtime — good for production

## What is NOT in this PR

- **Per-user credentials** — each user setting their own key (e.g. a personal GitHub PAT) is a follow-up; the resolver already has a caller-first lookup so it composes automatically
- **Per-user install scoping** — installs remain tenant-wide; that is the next part of #5459, built on top of #5499

prs.title: fix(auth): own credentials at tenant+user, and stop reporting causes we haven't established
prs.body:
## Summary

Two independent fixes from one debugging session, one commit each. Both are the same shape: a layer asserting something it had not established.

- **`fix(auth)`** — a credential authorized through the chat auth gate was invisible to the extensions registry and the runtime, which reported "Finish setup" forever while valid tokens sat on disk. Re-authorizing could not fix it. Accounts were addressed by `agent × project × surface × session`; the reader brute-force scanned two of those axes and did not compensate for the other two at all, so the axes that could silently mismatch were exactly the ones with no recovery. Accounts now live at **one address per credential owner** (tenant+user, optionally narrowed to a project), with a copy-forward migration so nobody re-authorizes.
- **`fix(failures)`** — the blocked-auth OAuth card rendered a live "Open *provider* authorization" button even with no authorization URL, so the only possible outcome was a post-click "Service unavailable". Separately, `model_credentials_unavailable` was one sentence ("check the API key and base URL") for three faults with three different fixes, two of which have no key to check.
- The ownership rule existed in **three independent copies**; that is why the storage layer could find a credential while the layer above rejected it. They are now one rule.
- `account.scope` is **provenance, not identity** — it locates the account's secret material. Identity comes from which root a record sits in, so records migrate verbatim and no secret-store change or token migration is needed.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/Infrastructure
- [x] Security
- [ ] Dependencies

## Linked Issue

None — found by direct debugging of a live local instance.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` on all nine touched crates
- [x] `cargo build`
- [x] Relevant tests pass: `ironclaw_auth` (290), `ironclaw_webui` (244), `ironclaw_turn_runner` (222), `ironclaw_composition --test runtime` (13), `ironclaw_architecture_tests` (41), `ironclaw_host_api` failure suite, `ironclaw_assistant`, `ironclaw_extension_host`, `ironclaw_extension_manager`; frontend `vitest run` (1105 across 126 files), `tsc --noEmit`, source-conventions lint
- [ ] `cargo test -p <owning-crate> --features integration` — not applicable: no DB-backed feature lane covers product-auth account storage; the durable service is exercised through its filesystem-backed suite
- [x] Manual testing: root-caused against a live instance — the stranded credential, its on-disk layout, and the three disagreeing read paths were read directly out of the running deployment's libSQL store
- [ ] `review-pr` / `pr-shepherd --fix` not run

**Honest caveat:** the full multi-crate sweep never completed in a single invocation — the machine repeatedly hit `No space left on device`. Every crate passed individually or in small batches, but there is no single clean full-workspace run behind this.

## Test Strategy

**User behavior:** a user authorizes an integration once and it is connected everywhere — chat, the extensions registry, and model tool calls — regardless of which surface they authorized from or which agent was running. Upgrading keeps existing credentials.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [x] Browser
- [ ] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions
- [x] External provider
- [x] Cross-component behavior

Tests added or updated:
- **Unit or contract:** `credential_is_owned_by_the_user_not_the_agent_that_minted_it`; `project_scoped_caller_inherits_the_user_level_credential`; `legacy_accounts_from_every_layout_survive_the_migration`; `binding_crosses_surface_and_session_but_never_the_owner`; `binding_crosses_surface_and_session_for_the_same_owner`; `filesystem_complete_manual_token_crosses_surface_and_session_for_same_owner`; `every_model_stage_reason_kind_routes_to_its_own_category`; `provider_session_storage_faults_are_not_reported_as_invalid_credentials`; `credential_unavailable_faults_carry_distinct_reason_kinds`; `credential_failure_categories_do_not_share_one_misleading_sentence`
- **Reborn integration:** not applicable — the change is inside the auth domain's durable service and its callers; the durable filesystem-backed suite is the seam that owns it
- **Recorded fixture:** not applicable — no model behavior changed
- **Browser E2E:** not applicable — the OAuth card is covered by its existing vm-rendered unit suite, which inspects the rendered node tree
- **Backend or runtime:** `ironclaw_composition --test runtime` (stub-gateway failure category)
- **Live canary:** not applicable

**What the tests prove:** that a credential minted under any pre-migration shape resolves for the callers that need it; that project scope inherits downward and never leaks upward; that migration is idempotent and preserves provenance verbatim (so tokens are not orphaned); that the owner boundary still rejects a different user; and that three formerly-conflated failure causes now render three different sentences, none of which blames an API key that is not the problem.

**Commands run:** `cargo fmt`; `cargo clippy -p … --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p ironclaw_auth --no-fail-fast`; `cargo test -p ironclaw_webui`; `cargo test -p ironclaw_turn_runner`; `cargo test -p ironclaw_composition --test runtime`; `cargo test -p ironclaw_architecture_tests`; `vitest run`; `tsc --noEmit`; `scripts/pre-commit-safety.sh`

## Security Impact

Changes where credential **account records** are addressed, and relaxes the ownership comparison.

- The security boundary is unchanged: tenant and user. Both are still hard-required by `CredentialAccountOwnerScope::matches`, and both come from the per-user filesystem mount, so one user's credentials remain unreachable from another's.
- What was removed — `agent_id`, `surface`, `session_id` — were never security boundaries. They partitioned one user's credentials from themselves.
- Project narrows **downward only**: a project caller inherits user-level credentials; a user-level caller never sees a project's sub-credential.
- Every cross-user, cross-tenant, and foreign-owner test passes untouched. The one test whose *name* suggests otherwise (`extension_oauth_start_handler_does_not_bind_across_owner_boundary`) previously seeded a different **agent** and called that a different owner; it now seeds a different **user**, which strengthens it.
- Raw secret material is not moved, read, or re-encrypted by this change.

## Reborn Trust-Boundary Checklist

- [x] Public policy/evidence/trust-bearing types: none added. `CredentialAccountOwnerScope` is unchanged in shape; only its comparison narrowed.
- [x] Untrusted content in prompts: N/A.
- [x] Hashes: N/A — no hashing added or changed.
- [x] New/changed status/exit/policy/error variants: two `AgentLoopHostErrorReasonKind` variants added. Downstream match sites audited — the routing match in `host_stage_failure_category` is exhaustive by construction, and `sanitized_driver_failure`'s allowlist was updated (it silently collapsed them to `driver_failed`, which the composition runtime test caught). Command: `rg -n "AgentLoopHostErrorReasonKind" crates/`
- [x] Security/durability `serde(default)` fields: none added. Migration reads legacy records with the unchanged `CredentialAccount` shape and has an explicit test.
- [x] Bounds: the migration's legacy walk is bounded per level (`MAX_LEGACY_OWNER_DIRS_PER_LEVEL`, `MAX_OWNER_RECORDS_PER_ROOT`) and fails closed on overflow.
- [x] Error class semantics: the split preserves the fail-fast `CredentialUnavailable` kind; only the user-facing category differs. None of the new categories is auto-retriable, asserted in test.
- [x] Names describe the boundary: `credential_owner_root` and the provenance-vs-identity split are documented at both sites.

## Database Impact

Changes the durable path for product-auth **credential account** records under the `RootFilesystem` mount catalog. No SQL migration and no schema change — this is a path-layout change within the existing filesystem-backed store, so it affects PostgreSQL and libSQL identically.

Migration is lazy, copy-forward, once per owner behind a durable marker, and never deletes. Legacy records remain readable in place if this is reverted.

## Blast Radius

`ironclaw_auth` (account storage, ownership, binding), `ironclaw_webui` (product-auth routes, chat OAuth card, i18n), `ironclaw_host_api` / `ironclaw_loop_contracts` / `ironclaw_loop_host` / `ironclaw_turn_runner` (failure categories), `ironclaw_composition` and `ironclaw_architecture_tests` (test expectations, size ceiling).

What could break: a deployment relying on per-agent or per-project credential isolation *within a single user* would now share one credential. That isolation was accidental rather than designed, but it is the behavior change to be aware of.

## Rollback Plan

Revert both commits. Legacy account records were copied, never moved, so a rollback finds them exactly where the old code looks. Accounts written *after* this lands would live only at the new path and would need re-authorizing after a revert — the only non-idempotent direction.

## Review Follow-Through

- **Project-scoped writes are not wired.** The read path and inheritance exist; nothing elects project scope at write time yet, deliberately, since there is no affordance to drive it.
- **`CredentialAccountOwnerScope` now carries fields its comparison ignores** (`agent_id`, `mission_id`, `thread_id`, `session_id`). They are still read by the migration's legacy walk, so removing them is a follow-up, not dead code today.
- **Legacy records are left in place.** Garbage-collecting them is deliberate follow-up work rather than something to do on a read path.
- **The `ironclaw_host_api` ceiling** moved 18_570 → 18_630, the measured count. Reviewer judgement welcome on whether the inline test justifying the split should instead live in `tests/` so it does not spend contracts budget.

---

- Adds the Expo/React Native mobile companion app under `app/`.

## Test Strategy

User behavior:
Native app users can authenticate, connect to hosted or dedicated IronClaw WebChat v2 backends, read cached conversation state, chat, manage automations, and configure tool approvals. Release operators can build/update through EAS profiles.

Risk areas:
- [ ] Model behavior
- [x] Browser
- [x] Side effect
- [x] Persistence
- [x] Security or permissions

Tests added or updated:
- Unit or contract: App Vitest coverage for API URL handling, hosted deployment handling, hosted login-ticket exchange, and deployment URL normalization; WebUI route tests updated for exact-origin CORS behavior.
- Reborn integration: Not applicable: this change does not alter the Reborn runner or whole-turn execution path.
- Recorded fixture: Not applicable: no model prompt, provider, or request-shape behavior changed.
- Browser E2E: Not applicable: this PR adds a native app and does not include browser automation coverage.
- Backend or runtime: App TypeScript check, Expo export, Expo doctor, native iOS prebuild, iOS simulator Xcode build, WebUI crate tests, and the focused Reborn composition CORS test were run locally.
- Live canary: Not applicable: no live provider or production hosted deployment canary was run in this session.

What the tests prove:
The app TypeScript surface typechecks, unit-covered URL and hosted-connection logic behaves as expected, the Expo project passes doctor checks, the web export bundles successfully, and the generated native iOS project compiles for the simulator. The simulator app launch still needs a rerun with Simulator.app already open because Expo timed out waiting for the simulator app to open after a successful build.

Touches native OAuth/session handling, encrypted local storage, bearer-token pairing flows, and WebUI OAuth/local development route behavior. Secrets remain client-side through SecureStore-backed handling and backend access remains mediated through existing WebChat v2 APIs.

Mobile app package/config/runtime behavior, EAS build/update profiles, hosted mobile OAuth connection flow, WebUI OAuth pending route support, and local WebUI development CORS behavior.

Revert the branch to remove the `app/` companion app additions, docs, dependency lock changes, and WebUI support changes. Existing desktop/WebUI behavior should return to the previous `main` state.

Draft PR opened for maintainer review. Native device/TestFlight validation and any required approved feature issue linkage remain reviewer/project-owner follow-up.

issues.title: [Feature] 增加“退出前不再确认”设置项，跳过 Cmd+Q 退出二次确认
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

每次通过 Cmd+Q、应用菜单、Dock 或托盘退出 LobsterAI 时，都会弹出原生“确认退出”对话框，且没有任何设置项可以关闭。对于把客户端当作常驻工具的 user，一天多次启停时这是纯摩擦。

代码位置：`dist-electron/main/libs/appQuitConfirmation.js`。`before-quit` 对所有用户发起的退出统一调用 `showAppQuitConfirmation`，只有更新安装、应用重启、系统关机/注销会走 bypass。

## Proposed Solution

在「设置」中增加一个开关，例如“退出前需要确认”，默认开启：

1. 开启时保持现有行为，弹原生确认框。
2. 关闭后，用户发起的退出直接执行现有清理流程 `runAppCleanupAndExit`，不再弹框。
3. 安全兜底：仍存在未保存的 Markdown / Office 编辑时，无论开关状态都保留确认或提示保存，避免数据丢失。
4. 该设置持久化到本地 store，与 `auto_launch_enabled`、`prevent_sleep_enabled` 等现有应用设置一致。

## Alternatives Considered

1. 用 `kill -TERM` 退出：可绕过弹窗且会走清理，但普通用户不友好，也容易误伤正在运行的任务。
2. 本地修改 `app.asar`：会破坏 ASAR 完整性校验和代码签名，且每次更新失效，不可持续。

## Additional Context

- 客户端版本：2026.10.16（macOS arm64）
- 场景：常驻使用，频繁启停客户端
- 建议保留“有未保存编辑时强制确认”的兜底逻辑

prs.body:
## Summary

修复 browser 在 Windows 进程检查短暂超时后持续不可用、页面挂起图片阻塞导航，以及 web_fetch 未落实全局代理偏好的问题。工具结束事件同时区分 HTTP 状态、浏览器连接、参数、引用和策略错误，避免外站正文或恢复建议被误判为产品认证、额度或网关故障。

## Related Issue

Related to #2866（用量埋点整合的后续修复）。

## Changes Made

- 保留待核验的 Chrome MCP transport，后续调用重新验证进程身份并清理；保留 PID 复用保护和原有时间预算。
- 新主文档提交并触发 dom-ready 后允许页面操作，保留主文档加载错误和超时处理。

prs.body:
## Summary

Fix image/video confirmation and progress feedback following #2872. Video confirmation now shows a credit estimate when the model catalogue supports one, long requests keep the input accessible, and submitted tasks show progress without a cancellation button that usually fails after dispatch.

## Related Issue

Follow-up to #2872.

## Changes Made

- Estimate video credits from catalogue pricing and the actual request parameters; keep an explicit unknown-cost fallback for ambiguous tiers or unmeasured inputs.
- Keep cancellation before submission and remove post-submission cancellation from both current and legacy task views. Label queued tasks as submitted.
- Use a short confirmation heading and a bounded, scrollable request body while keeping the cost and input visible. Preserve the original question as the plugin answer key.
- Remove duplicate image/video tool-step timers and distinguish preparation from generation. Prefer the persisted client submission time for task elapsed time so server clock skew cannot start a new card at an inflated duration.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests

prs.body:
## Summary

全局默认模型为“快速”或“旗舰”时，悬浮球快捷问答将 `yd-fast` / `yd-ultra` 直接发送给推理接口，导致服务端拒绝。现在先通过已有模型预设 resolve 接口取得具体模型，再按返回的协议请求回答，覆盖总结、解释、润色和翻译追问。

## Changes

- 复用现有认证、账号范围检查和 `/api/models/{preset}/resolve` 客户端；具体模型与自定义供应商保持原路径。
- 解析和推理共用取消信号与超时。关闭、取消、请求替换或切换账号后，丢弃迟到结果，不继续发送失效请求。
- 快捷问答继续使用临时请求，不创建 Cowork 会话。解析失败不回退发送虚拟模型；异常模型结果复用已有本地化提示。
- 为两个预设、协议切换、失败、取消、超时和账号切换补充单元测试。

## Validation

- 相关 Vitest：34 个测试文件，482 项通过，1 项跳过。

- 实机验收窗口离屏，不抢占键鼠。划词使用合成选区进入真实组件及 IPC；翻译追问通过真实卡片输入。未覆盖原生划词和窗口合成。模型和翻译服务响应未替换。

实机脚本、截图、运行日志和登录数据均不入库。本 PR 不修改 renderer/preload 契约、数据库或 OpenClaw runtime。

## Summary

客户端启动期间，悬浮球可能在 OpenClaw gateway 仍为 `starting` 时显示，导致用户提交 chat 后立即被端侧拒绝。改为 gateway 进入 `running` 后再显示悬浮球和任务面板，并补齐任务受理失败的分类与关联日志。

埋点背景：#2866。

## Changes

- 主进程按实际 gateway 状态控制入口显示；提前触发的面板打开请求延后处理。gateway 重启期间隐藏入口，保留草稿，并防止迟到的回调重新显示窗口。
- 复用已有 `failureCode`、`failureStage`、`blockedReason`、`callId`、`taskId`、`turnId` 等字段，区分前置检查、模型配置、会话启动、文件准备和追问失败。没有新增 Hive 字段；新增分类值经白名单过滤，不上报输入正文、路径或原始错误。
- 保持每次提交只记录一个结果，失败请求保留自身的任务关联。补充对应单元测试。

## Validation

prs.title: fix(openclaw): apply IM configuration without restarting the gateway
prs.body:
## Summary

Saving IM configuration currently can force a whole gateway restart, interrupting
unrelated work and racing the configuration file watcher. A successful write RPC
also does not prove that the runtime has applied the edit.

This PR applies eligible configuration changes through the live gateway and
reports the exact mutation's application status. Necessary process replacements
wait for an atomic runtime idle lease and the old process to exit. It also fixes
connection races during that lifecycle while preserving IM history recovery.

## Related Issue

No linked issue. This is one coordinated desktop and pinned-runtime change.

## Changes Made

- Generate live candidates in memory, including enterprise overrides, and make
  the runtime the sole writer of its watched configuration file. IM/binding edits
  and legacy IM restart hints use live synchronization.
- Add a version-scoped OpenClaw patch for opt-in mutation receipts, idempotent
  mutation IDs, exact revision attestation, restart refusal before persistence,
  and idle restart leases. Compare authored/resolved environment placeholders
  correctly so an unchanged authentication token does not trigger a restart.
- Keep write acknowledgement, persistence, and application distinct. Reconcile
  uncertain writes with bounded reads; never infer a restart or duplicate write
  from a timeout. Preserve pending/rejected/applied status through IM IPC and
  Settings, and advance the synchronized fingerprint only after application.
- Join pending handshakes, ignore stale client/process events, prevent reconnect
  from spawning during restart preparation, and cancel late work on shutdown.
  Explicit reconnection still restores IM session discovery/history polling.
- Document the protocol, runtime compatibility boundary, and validation in
  `docs/openclaw-config-delivery.md`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Code refactoring
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

- [x] GitHub Linux full suite at `0d9e5ed9`: **497 test files / 5,135 tests
  passed**, 11 files / 121 tests skipped. All applicable PR checks pass, including
  CodeQL, lint, main/renderer builds, Electron Verify and security scans.
- [x] The reviewed patch inventory includes the added runtime patch. Restart leases
  use an opaque random UUID rather than a hash derived from configuration secrets.
- Local Windows full-suite execution also encountered platform-specific filename,
  symlink and native-install fixture failures; the full-suite result above is from
  the successful GitHub Linux run.

- [x] Tested locally with the upstream dependency set (Node 24.18.0, npm 11.17.0,
  desktop Vitest 4.1.11).
- [x] Added new tests and updated existing handshake fixtures.
- [x] Desktop targeted regression: **15 files, 557 passed, 3 skipped**. Covers
  delivery/diagnostics, impact classification, receipt generation, offline receipt
  attestation, idle stop, IM IPC/UI results, engine restart ownership, connection
  races, existing adapter/history behavior, configuration generation, and
  enterprise merging.
- [x] Pinned runtime unit suites: **53 passed** across gateway Vitest projects
  (three source test files; project executions are counted separately).
- [x] Real gateway end-to-end suite: **10 passed**, exercising actual RPCs and the
  watcher, hot apply, token placeholders, restart refusal before persistence,
  duplicate IDs, invalid writes, saved-candidate attestation, lease expiry and
  commit/admission fencing.
- [x] All **49 runtime patches** apply to pinned OpenClaw
  `ea806575e6450e4d1efdfc72c19f04be982a1b9b`; repeating the upstream patch script
  succeeds.
- [x] Changed-file ESLint with zero warnings, `npx tsc --noEmit`,
  `npm run compile:electron`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [ ] Manual signed-in IM account / installed Electron release acceptance.

The production build retains existing third-party eval/chunk-size warnings;
Vitest prints the existing Vite CommonJS config-loader advisory.

## Checklist

- [x] Followed project conventions and reviewed the complete diff.
- [x] Added comments for lifecycle ownership and uncertain outcomes.
- [x] Updated documentation and added behavioral regression coverage.
- [x] New and relevant existing tests pass locally.

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Main process
- [x] IPC result contract and renderer Settings status

## Additional Notes

Rebuild the bundled runtime with the included v2026.8.1 patch. An older runtime
without `configMutationReceipts: 1` leaves live edits pending; it is not treated as
evidence that an edit was applied or that the gateway must restart. Legacy runtime
RPC clients retain their non-managed configuration behavior.

This does not promise that every IM transport stays connected after its own
credentials change. Channel plugins may reconnect their own transport. Inherited
secret/proxy changes, plugin installation changes, and runtime-classified
restart-required changes still use a coordinated process replacement.

- Restore account identity before loading models, quota, and profile information; retain the existing data refresh for healthy sessions.

prs.title: feat(browser): default to the in-app browser
prs.body:
## Summary

Make the LobsterAI in-app browser the default so Agent web browsing/search stays inside the app instead of launching a separate Chrome window, and fix issues that surface once it is used for runs without a visible browser panel.

### Default + migration
- `defaultBrowserWebAccessConfig.displayMode` → `in-app`.
- Existing installs: the renderer persists the normalized browser config on every launch, so older installs carry an explicit `external` value that a new default cannot change. `migrateBrowserDisplayModeToInApp` switches them **once** in the main process, before the first OpenClaw config sync (window not created yet → no write race with the renderer, no gateway restart after load).
- The applied version is stored as top-level `app_config.browserDisplayModeMigrationVersion`; the renderer's default config records it so fresh installs are never migrated and a later explicit "external" choice is kept.

### In-app browser fixes
- **Zero-size viewport when the panel is hidden** (IM channels, scheduled tasks, another session, minimized window): new `WebContentsView`s were only sized when attached. Verified with Electron 43.5.0: a never-attached view has `innerWidth 0`, and `Page.captureScreenshot` never returns. New pages and the credential-login view now start at the last panel size, or 1280×800.
- Agent `take_screenshot` now has the same 10s timeout as the clipboard capture path (shared `capturePageScreenshot`).
- The agent browser session presents the plain Chrome user agent (drops the app and `Electron/x` tokens that e.g. Google sign-in rejects).
- Non-URL address-bar text searches Baidu (zh) / Bing (en) instead of Google, which is unreachable without a proxy in mainland China (in-app browser and artifact preview address bar).

## Electron-specific behavior changes
- **Storage**: one-time `app_config` write at startup (`browserWebAccess.displayMode`, `browserDisplayModeMigrationVersion`).
- **OpenClaw config**: migrated installs render the `lobster-in-app` browser profile (existing-session driver over the MCP bridge) and the saved-credential MCP server instead of the managed Chrome profile.
- Logins made in the previous OpenClaw-managed Chrome profile are not carried over to the in-app partition.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 7733 passed (new tests for the migration, detached viewport, screenshot timeout, user agent and search URL).
- ESLint (CI rules) clean on all touched files; `tsc` and `npm run compile:electron` pass.
- Manual `npm run electron:dev` validation **not done yet** — suggested checks:
  1. Start with an `external` config → log shows `[Browser] switched the browser display mode to in-app`; settings show the in-app browser. Switch back to external and restart → stays external.
  2. With the browser panel closed / another session open / window minimized, ask the Agent to search and take a screenshot → returns instead of hanging.
  3. IM-triggered task that browses the web.

prs.title: fix(tls): update certificate verifier and roots for CA distrust
prs.body:
## Summary
- Fix the coverage-discovered browser profile lock race: own the lock with a guard that explicitly unlocks on drop, while retaining the guard when container cleanup is unconfirmed. Three deterministic duplicated-descriptor regressions cover release, next-owner exclusion, and quarantine.
- Update both main and desktop lockfiles to `rustls-webpki 0.103.16` and `webpki-roots` / `webpki-root-certs 1.0.10` for the CA distrust incident tracked by Go as CVE-2026-111943. Includes the required main-workspace AWS-LC dependency update.
- Compile the same offline regression against both lockfiles. Reissue all eight upstream public keys under an ephemeral trusted CA, reject them, and accept a benign P-384 key. Fixtures contain only public keys, with upstream provenance, license, and Go SPKI hash checks.
- Document the need to rebuild binaries and update OS/container trust stores. Legacy `rustls-webpki 0.102.8` (Discord/APNs) and native/OpenSSL verification remain separate coverage work tracked in Beads `moltis-p73`; the legacy `webpki-roots 0.26.11` shim now re-exports 1.0.10. This PR does not claim every TLS backend has the eight-key blocklist.

Upstream: [verifier fix](https://github.com/rustls/webpki/releases/tag/v/0.103.16), [root-store fix](https://github.com/rustls/webpki-roots/releases/tag/v/1.0.10). Beads: `moltis-5j4`.
