prs.title: feat(runtime): add capability-taking constructors for turn entry points
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Turn entry points take the capabilities they build from: `run_with_capabilities`, `process_message_with_capabilities`, `Agent::from_config_with_capabilities`, owned SOP steps, delegates, spawned subagents, peer turns and manual `cron_run` jobs. The old signatures stay as adapters over the config-backed set, so configured setups build exactly what they build today.
  - A supplied tool registry is now complete. `ToolSource::native_recipe` defaults to `Ok(None)`, and then the supplied vector is the whole registry: no native factory, skills, MCP servers, peripherals, pipeline, `tool_search` or post-turn skill work. The config-backed source opts into the native recipe explicitly. In that mode native names win over same-name source tools: native factory tools, peripheral and skill tools, MCP tools and MCP capability tools, and `execute_pipeline` and `tool_search` when the runtime builds them. Admitted source tools reach bounded delegates. In both modes a source vector that repeats a name keeps its first tool.
  - Bounded delegation keeps memory writes on the caller's policy. Every ancestor's policy is checked in order on Store, Forget and Purge, the target's tracker is charged once, and background and parallel workers carry the same chain. The background worker is still narrowed by the caller's tool-name filter (#11797). The delegate's inherited tools get the same memory/delivery context filter as the outer registry.
  - Merges current master. Effort-aware routing (#11516) now asks the capability source for its provider, with the route-scoped config, at every site where it chooses one.
  - A native recipe takes a `#[non_exhaustive]` `NativeRecipeInputs` struct with named fields, so the runtime can add inputs without breaking embedder recipes.
  - The interactive CLI now takes its session channel from the capability source's `cli` alias. The config-backed source maps it to the registered CLI channel factory as before; a supplied source with no `cli` channel makes the interactive CLI fail with "This agent has no channel for the CLI session" instead of falling back to the global factory.
  - Adds an external consumer crate (`tests/fixtures/runtime-composition-consumer`) that depends only on the public runtime contract and checks, from outside the crate, that a supplied-only turn constructs nothing native and that an external recipe can select native compatibility. It came from #11526.
- **Scope boundary:** No application wiring: `DefaultCapabilities`, the daemon heartbeat, the cron scheduler and the gateway are not moved here (#11187). No new capability kind, config key, CLI flag or tool grant. The ADR-016 exception row for the widened paths is a separate docs PR for Core review.
- **Blast radius:** Turn construction at every entry point listed above; tool registry assembly in `tools/scoped.rs` (construction mode, name precedence); bounded and independent delegation; vision and effort routing provider construction; `docs/book/src/architecture/runtime-composition.md`. Existing configs keep the native recipe through the config-backed adapters. One visible difference on that path: a child turn (delegate, subagent, peer) started from an adapter-built parent now reuses the parent's observer instead of creating its own.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10993, Related #7432. Contract lineage #11090. Supersedes #11526.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's runtime has always built its own providers, memory and tools from config. This PR lets an embedder hand the runtime those pieces instead, and makes sure the runtime then uses only what it was given. If an application supplies three tools, the agent gets those three tools and nothing else: no built-in tools, no MCP servers started, no skills loaded or written. Before, the runtime quietly added its native set on top.

Running ZeroClaw from config is unchanged: the built-in config-backed source asks for the native set, and every existing entry point uses it.

Two smaller fixes come with it. A delegated agent can no longer write memory beyond what its caller's policy allows, even when the delegation runs in the background. And a supplied tool can no longer take the name of an MCP tool, the pipeline tool or `tool_search` and shadow it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The change is an embedder API with no user-visible surface for configured setups; the named tests below drive the real entry points.

### How I tested

The local runs below are on tree `3318bec49e` (1f7c1745c5). This head adds one clean master merge on top (tree `7c259995fb`), which touches none of this PR's files and on which fmt and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` also pass. The runs used a Linux build with Rust 1.98, `--locked`, an isolated target directory and `umask 022`.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, `Lint` (clippy, `-D warnings`), `Check` (no default features, and default features with all targets) and `Test` (`cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`). `Test` runs the new tests that build without plugin features: the construction traps (`composition::supplied_only_traps`), the native-name precedence tests in `tools::scoped`, the skill-gating pair in `agent::loop_`, and the consumer crate. nextest runs each test in its own process, so the process-wide peripheral trap cannot leak between tests. `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` runs the `tools::r5_namespace_tests::late_tool_search_*` proofs against `tools/scoped.rs`. `Docs Style` covers `runtime-composition.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded as usual. The construction-trap module is Unix-only, because its MCP trap is a shell-script stdio server, so the Windows jobs do not run it. CI tests the consumer crate inside the workspace run, where features are unified with the root package; I ran it on its own as well (below), which shows it builds against the public API alone. A CI step for that is a possible follow-up; this PR does not change workflows.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check
    clean on this head; the last master merge brings #11838's fix for
    tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus -- --exact --test-threads=1 <77 named tests: capability construction, supplied-only traps, native-name precedence, delegation memory policy, model switches, skill gating>
test result: ok. 77 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5894 filtered out
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus
test result: FAILED. 5939 passed; 23 failed; 9 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
    the 23 are tools::r5_namespace_tests::late_tool_search_*, which need the fixture
    components and receipt that the plugins cranelift runtime CI job builds
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus -- tools::r5_namespace_tests::late_tool_search
    with both tool-fixture components built for wasm32-wasip2 and a fixture receipt written the way the CI job writes it
test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5948 filtered out
    each of the 23 wrote a passing case receipt bound to that fixture receipt
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus --no-fail-fast --test '*' --examples
    15 integration-test files and one example: 52 passed; 0 failed
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus --doc
test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p runtime-composition-consumer
test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
cargo +1.98.0 check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features plugins-wasm-cranelift,schema-export,observability-prometheus -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh; bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh   (runtime-composition.md)
    Summary: 0 error(s); Checked 3 local docs link target(s).
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Revert checks: each guard this PR adds was removed one at a time, and the tests named for it had to fail. All 23 did, and the source was restored exactly after each: peripheral, skill, MCP and repeated-name precedence; the `tool_search` claim and the pipeline reservation; the supplied-only parent filter; the skill creation and review gates; the forced native recipe at each of the five entry points; the same-hop, ancestor and hop-two memory policy carry; the SOP memory routes; the #11797 caller-name filter. Commits 8–11 each build on their own: `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p runtime-composition-consumer --all-targets` with the three plugin features above passes on each commit's tree; commit 12 is the tree tested above.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** tree `3318bec49e` (1f7c1745c5) for the runs above; the head 4920032710 (tree `7c259995fb`) adds only a clean master merge, with fmt and the workspace check run on it.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded from check and clippy because the build machine lacks `glib-2.0` 2.70 or newer.

### Follow-ups

- Bounded delegation refusals log one generic cause; logging a non-secret cause class (selection refused, missing runtime or memory, target memory failed) would make them easier to diagnose.
- Effort-aware routing through a supplied provider source has no direct test yet: a recording source at the CLI start, the per-turn re-route and `process_message`, and a config-backed case whose route excludes the agent's own alias.
- Principal memory routing does not reach source-built tools (documented). Before RPC sessions run on supplied sources (#11187), either the source gets the session's principal scope at construction or routing is refused for supplied-only registries unless the source opts in.
- Native tool calls are recorded in history in a shape the skill creator's extractor does not read, so native-tool-call turns never auto-create skills. This is not new here.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. A supplied-only build constructs less than before; a source cannot widen what the policy allows.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for configs, the CLI and existing entry points. No for two embedder APIs that have no in-tree users outside this PR: a custom `ToolSource` now gets a supplied-only registry by default, and code outside the crate that builds `AllToolsResult` with a struct literal must use `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: a custom `ToolSource` that relied on native tools being added must implement `native_recipe` and return `Ok(Some(&defaults::native_compat_registry))`, or wrap `defaults::NoSuppliedTools`. Replace `AllToolsResult { .. }` literals with `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools(tools)` and set the public fields after.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an embedder's agent missing native tools it expected (source needs `native_recipe`); bounded delegations refusing with "Tools could not be prepared safely" when a supplied-only owner inherits native memory tools; provider construction errors on effort-routed turns that name the route's provider.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #11526 by @JordanTheJet
- Scope materially carried forward: the supplied-only registry boundary (reimplemented here as `native_recipe` instead of `uses_native_registry`) and the external consumer with its dependency ratchet (ported to the new selector). #11526's daemon lifecycle tests and the heartbeat MCP gate move to #11187.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why: same author.

The design of this boundary owes a lot to review. Thanks to @tidux, @IftekharUddin and @Audacity88 for the findings on #11174, #11187 and #11526: the `cron_run` escape, pipeline and MCP shadowing, missing supplied tools in bounded delegates, post-turn skill work and heartbeat MCP outside the supplied registry, and the case for an external consumer.

prs.title: fix(config): remove unused pairing-dashboard settings at schema version 4
prs.body:
> Proposes removing unused pairing-dashboard settings. Maintainer approval of this removal is pending; this PR must not merge until that decision is made.
>
> Depends on #11218, which introduces schema version 4; review only the final commit for this removal. This PR's base is `master`, so its diff includes #11218 until that merges.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, stacked on #11218 (head 71967ff972), which introduces schema version 4.
- **What changed and why:**
  - `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]` is removed at schema version 4 through one `Retirement::Remove` entry in `RETIRED_KEYS`. The table goes, with its four settings: `code_ttl_secs`, `max_pending_codes`, `max_failed_attempts` and `lockout_secs`.
  - The `PairingDashboardConfig` struct, the `GatewayConfig::pairing_dashboard` field and their defaults are removed.
  - Pairing never read any of these settings, and two of the documented defaults are wrong:
    - The limits are fixed in the pairing guard: 5 failed attempts, a 300 s lockout and a 10-minute code lifetime.
    - The table documented a 3600 s code lifetime, and suggested that attempts and lockout could be configured.
    - `[gateway.pairing_code]` already sets the code length and character set.
- **No operational readers, checked first:** on master (83f0ff3805) and on #11218's head (71967ff972), the table, the struct and the four setting names appear only in:
  - the schema (declaration, defaults, tests)
  - the schema version 2 → 3 normalizer that retires `code_length`
  - the fixtures and migration tests

  No operational reader in `crates/`, `src/`, `apps/`, `web/`, `tests/` or `docs/` uses these settings to control pairing. Tests, fixtures, defaults and the legacy normalizer do use the names. The same holds on every open head that a separate schema review pinned.
- **Ordering:** the existing schema version 3 entry for `gateway.pairing_dashboard.code_length` stays, and the new version 4 entry follows it. A version 3 or 4 file that still has `code_length` receives the leaf-removal notice first, then the whole-section removal notice. For version 1 or 2 files, the inherited normalizer removes and logs `code_length` earlier; the structured migration report contains only the whole-section removal notice.
- **Operator-visible effects:**
  - A config that still has the table loads with one `Removed` notice naming `gateway.pairing_dashboard` and the reason. `zeroclaw config migrate`, and every full or incremental save, remove the table from disk. For the version 3/4 document-cleanup path, this section removal and any required version-line update preserve the rest of the file byte for byte. Version 1/2 files also undergo inherited structural migrations; full saves retain their normal serialization and default-pruning behavior.
  - A `ZEROCLAW_gateway__pairing_dashboard__*` environment variable is ignored with an `IgnoredEnvOverride` notice, as #11218 does for every retired key. Startup does not fail, and nothing is written.
  - `zeroclaw config get` and `config set` on `gateway.pairing_dashboard.*` now report an unknown property.
  - The dashboard's config forms and the book's config reference are generated from the schema, so the section disappears from both on its own. No checked-in page names it.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No pairing rename: the proposal to move pairing to `[pairing]` is withdrawn.
  - No change to pairing behaviour, `[gateway.pairing_code]`, the migration mechanism or any other key.
  - `fixtures/v1.toml` keeps the table as legacy input. `fixtures/v4.toml` is the schema version 1 → 4 migration chain's output and loses it.
- **Blast radius:** edits are confined to `zeroclaw-config`, whose API is consumed by other crates.
  - The public `PairingDashboardConfig` struct and `GatewayConfig::pairing_dashboard` field are removed. Downstream Rust consumers must drop references to that type and field.
  - The search above found no use of the removed type or field outside the crate in this repository. The reported checks compiled the root crate, gateway and runtime with every target.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #7432. Depends on #11218.
- **Labels:** `release:v0.9.0`

### What this does, simply

The config file has a `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]` section whose settings ZeroClaw never actually used, and two of its documented values were wrong. This proposes removing the section, subject to maintainer approval. A config that still has it loads with a removal notice. Migration and saves remove it; version 3/4 document cleanup preserves unrelated text, while older configs can also need structural migration. Version 3/4 files that retain the legacy `code_length` receive an additional leaf-removal notice.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: covered by unit and migration tests.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the `zeroclaw-config` tests:
  - the migration, load, document-cleanup, save and environment tests below
  - the schema version 1 → 4 fixture round-trip, which compares the generated config byte for byte
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI cannot run v0.8.5 against the result, so I did that by hand (below). CI associated with head `6438988edb66435f81b1280d97f7df808654a381` reports `CI Required Gate`, `Test` and `Lint` successful. Three Docker jobs remain failed. Read-only log and source/history triage attributes them to two problems outside this removal:
  - The [default amd64 Compose smoke job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36806798081/job/110192863314) and [Alpine amd64 Compose smoke job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36806798081/job/110192863356) built their images successfully, then failed with `locked /zeroclaw-data/data, loaded /zeroclaw-data/.zeroclaw/data`. The startup guard introduced on master by [#10621](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10621) makes a pre-existing disagreement between the pre-lock resolver and config loader fatal. These jobs tested synthetic merge `21a0bb644342cd496d8f85a4f667918cfbc061b6`, which includes that guard from master; the guard is absent from #11344's standalone head. This attribution comes from the merge-job logs and source/history comparison; no separate Docker failure on bare master was observed.
  - The [Alpine arm64 source-build job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36806798081/job/110192863391) was killed during release compilation/linking with `(signal: 9, SIGKILL: kill)`, followed by `ResourceExhausted` and `cannot allocate memory`. Runtime smoke steps never ran. The same memory-exhaustion failure appears on [unrelated dependency PR #11210](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36700856642/job/109839769797) and an [earlier #11218 run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36614711595/job/109591028734). The logs establish memory exhaustion, without proving a minimum runner size or that reduced build parallelism alone fixes it.
  - Neither failure is caused by the pairing-dashboard removal. Separate startup/config-resolution and Docker build-capacity fixes remain necessary; these failed jobs are not successful validation evidence.
- **Commands run and tail output** (macOS, Rust 1.96.1, at reported head `6438988edb66435f81b1280d97f7df808654a381`):
  ```
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1813 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out   # lib
test result: ok. 106 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out    # tests/migration.rs
(every other zeroclaw-config target: ok, 0 failed)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings           # exit 0
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p zeroclaw-config --no-deps                # exit 0
cargo check -p zeroclaw --all-targets                                            # exit 0
cargo check -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets                # exit 0
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                       # exit 0
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                               # passed
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **New and updated tests:**
    - A schema version 3 or 4 file holding the table without `code_length` migrates with exactly one `Removed` notice. `config migrate`, load and on-disk document cleanup preserve unrelated text byte for byte, apart from the required version-line update.
    - A version 3 or 4 file that still holds `code_length` gets both notices, in leaf-then-section order. Version 1/2 normalization removes that leaf before structured notices are collected, so those reports contain only whole-section removal.
    - The table is gone after a full save (even from a config read without migrating) and after an incremental save, at schema versions 3 and 4. The reload has no notices.
    - An environment variable on a retired setting is ignored with a notice and writes nothing.
    - Generating the current version no longer emits the table.
  - **Rollback with the real v0.8.5 binary,** in a throwaway home directory:
    1. v0.8.5 reads a schema version 3 file with `code_ttl_secs = 900`, and returns 900.
    2. This branch's migration changes only the version line and removes the table.
    3. With the result relabelled `schema_version = 3`, v0.8.5 reads the dashboard settings as its defaults (3600 and 300).

    v0.8.5 declares the field `#[serde(default)]`, so an absent table means defaults. Pairing policy did not use the removed values, so this does not change operational pairing behavior. This rollback check requires the explicit relabeling above or a restored pre-upgrade backup within #11218's rollback envelope; it does not show that v0.8.5 accepts an unchanged version 4 label or newer active settings.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for config-file loading; no for Rust consumers of the removed public type or field. A config with the table loads, with a notice, and is cleaned on save. Scripts that `config get` or `config set` the four `gateway.pairing_dashboard.*` paths now get an unknown-property error. Those settings never had an effect.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: the four properties and their environment variables are retired (removed with a notice, ignored with a notice).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: allow config migration or save to remove `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]`; remove overrides and scripts using its retired properties. Continue using `[gateway.pairing_code]` for code length and character set. Rust consumers must remove `PairingDashboardConfig` and `GatewayConfig::pairing_dashboard` references.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. For v0.8.5, restore the pre-upgrade config backup or explicitly relabel schema version 4 to 3 within #11218's rollback envelope. The verified v0.8.5 check then reads the absent dashboard table as defaults; this is not a promise that arbitrary older binaries accept a version 4 config or newer active settings.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None for this removal.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** callers of the retired `gateway.pairing_dashboard.*` get/set paths receive unknown-property errors; Rust consumers referencing the removed public type or field fail to compile.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(config): migrate retired keys at schema version 4 and warn on a missing schema_version
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **Credit:** this builds on @singlerider's #8754, opened 2026-07-06, which first identified these inert keys and proposed the move to schema version 4. Its still-valid retirements, its version 3 layout pin for the filesystem relocation, and its version 4 fixture and tests are carried forward here, with a `Co-authored-by` trailer on the retirement commits. This PR also folds #11217, which reads an unversioned config in the version 3 format as version 3, and takes from @NiuBlibing's #9809 the shape of retiring a channel together with every reference to it.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11082 retired `[security.nevis]` but left `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` at 3, so no migration ran. The table was discarded at load with a warning hidden unless `-v` was passed, and it stayed on disk with any plaintext `client_secret`. This PR bumps the schema to version 4 and adds a version 3 → version 4 step driven by a new `RETIRED_KEYS` table.
  - Each table entry names a key path, the version that retires it, whether it is removed or renamed, and the reason shown to the operator. A path segment `ANY_KEY` (`"*"`) matches every key at its level, so one entry retires a key in every `[agents.<alias>]` block or every runtime profile. Each concrete match is reported under its real path. A rename never overwrites an existing replacement, and a blocked rename creates no tables.
  - Retired keys are applied during migration and again on every load of a current-version config. A retired key that reappears in a version 4 file is dropped with a notice, not silently ignored by serde.
  - The same table also drives incremental saves. #11191 made `save_dirty` remove `[security.nevis]` from the on-disk document, since an incremental save rewrites only dirty paths and would otherwise carry a retired table and its secret forward. This PR replaces that Nevis-only helper with `apply_retired_keys_to_doc`, so `save_dirty` and migration share one retirement policy. Wildcard entries work there too, so the eight agent-inline tunables are removed from disk as well. The edit touches only retired keys, keeps comments and unrelated ciphertext byte for byte, and logs each removal only after the atomic write succeeds. #11191's tests are kept against the table-driven cleanup. A save first reads the version of the file on disk. A version 1 or version 2 file is not edited as it stands, because keys retired at version 3 (`[identity]`, an agent's `max_tool_iterations`) are still live inputs to its version 2 → version 3 step. An incremental save first carries the file on disk through the typed migration chain, then applies the dirty paths to the result, so those inputs are converted and keys another handle saved after this config loaded survive. A file whose version cannot be determined (an unversioned file of ambiguous shape) or is newer than this binary is refused by both save paths, so a load that fell back to defaults cannot relabel it and write over it.
  - Containers a retirement leaves empty follow one rule on both paths. A literal container such as `[security]` or `context_compression` is dropped. A table matched by a wildcard is an operator-named alias such as `[agents.coder]` and is always kept, so a reference to it never dangles. `toml_edit` writes nothing for an empty implicit or dotted table, so an alias that existed only as a prefix of retired dotted keys (`runtime_profiles.slow.context_compression.summary_model = …`) is written back as its own `[runtime_profiles.slow]` header, or as `slow = {}` inside an inline table.
  - `zeroclaw config migrate` edits a file at version 3 or later in place: from version 3, reaching version 4 only retires keys and re-stamps `schema_version`, so quoting, number spelling and comments on untouched lines keep their exact bytes. Older files still take the structural rebuild.
  - A `ZEROCLAW_*` environment override naming a retired key is ignored with a notice instead of failing startup as an unknown property.
  - Every change is a `MigrationNotice` carrying key paths and reasons only, never values. Notices print on stderr after every config load, with a line saying `zeroclaw config migrate` writes them. `config migrate` prints them itself and returns them in `--json`.
  - A config with no `schema_version` whose sections are plainly in the version 3 shape is read as version 3 (folded from #11217). That shape means at least one alias-keyed `providers.models.<family>` or `channels.<type>` section, none holding fields directly (the version 2 shape), and no version 1-only top-level key. The version is fixed at 3, not the current version, so the file still runs the version 3 → version 4 step; it reports an `InferredV3` notice telling the operator to run `zeroclaw config migrate`. The version 2 → version 3 filesystem relocation no longer runs for such a file. A version 2 entry whose only content is map-valued fields has the same shape: `[providers.models.openai.extra_headers]` is either the version 2 profile's headers or a version 3 alias named `extra_headers`. Each child table is checked against the real schema by reading the section as one entry and serializing it back; when a child also reads as a field, the file is refused with an error naming the section and asking for `schema_version = 2` or `3`, rather than choosing a reading that loses data. A version 2-only setting in a file otherwise in the version 3 format (a value directly under `[providers]`, or a key the version 2 → version 3 step moves off an agent, such as `provider` or `allowed_tools`) and an empty map-valued field make the shape ambiguous the same way. Any other unversioned config is still read as version 1, and that assumption now prints a warning instead of failing quietly. The version 1 migration reshapes sections written for a newer version. It folds hand-written channel aliases into `default`, the most likely cause of the "half my config is ignored" reports. Testing a real modern config with only its version line removed showed it also nests `[providers.models.<family>.<alias>]` one level too deep, stranding the model and URI. The warning names both effects.
  - Retired at version 4:
    - `[security.nevis]`, which was added in #3651 and never implemented. Its schema field, load shim and validation warning are deleted.
    - Eight agent-inline runtime tunables in every `[agents.<alias>]` (`compact_context`, `max_tool_iterations`, `max_history_messages`, `max_context_tokens`, `memory_recall_limit`, `parallel_tools`, `tool_dispatcher`, `strict_tool_parsing`). No agent field exists for them, so they were silently ignored; the runtime-profile copies are the live ones and are kept.
    - `runtime_profiles.*.context_compression.summary_model`. Only config diagnostics read it; its field and the two diagnostics about it are deleted.
    - `[node_transport]` (with its `shared_secret`) and the WATI sections `channels.wati` and `channels_config.wati` (with their `api_token`). These were retired earlier by code outside the table: the migration chain stripped `node_transport` silently between steps, and load only warned about WATI, so an incremental save wrote them and their secrets back. They are now table entries, and the bespoke detection, its load-only `Config` fields, load warnings, CLI prints and Fluent strings are removed; the table's notices report the same facts.
    - Top-level `[twitter]` and `[reddit]`, and `[channels.notion]`. No schema field reads any of them: Twitter and Reddit stay channels (`[channels.twitter.<alias>]`, `[channels.reddit.<alias>]`) and Notion stays the top-level `[notion]` tool section. `[channels.notion]` uses a new `RemoveChannel` retirement, which handles the references to the channel the way the `alias_refs` cascade does: matched after trimming, entries dropped from `[agents.<alias>] channels` and `[escalation] alert_channels`, and a `[peer_groups.<name>]` bound to it kept and reported, because the cascade treats that binding as hard and never deletes the group. Agent bindings are kept and reported too when dropping them would leave no binding anywhere, which would route every channel to the fallback agent. A test pins the reference sites and their strength to the cascade's, and `config migrate` does not rewrite a file for kept references alone. It runs wherever the table runs, including version 3 files migrated in place, current files on load, incremental saves and full saves (`save()` now applies the table to its output before the atomic replace, since a reference held in the typed config would otherwise be written back), so a later channel retirement gets the pruning with one table entry. A test asserts that no retirement names a current top-level section or a live channel type.
    - Keys the version 2 → version 3 step already drops but no current field reads, which a version 3 or later file could still hold: `gateway.pairing_dashboard.code_length`, `[swarms]`, `reliability.fallback_providers`, `reliability.model_fallbacks`, `tts.default_provider`, `transcription.default_provider`, `transcription.default_model_provider`, `transcription.default_transcription_provider` and a top-level `[identity]`. They are retired at version 3, so they apply only after the version 2 → version 3 step, which still moves `[identity]` into the agents first.
  - The one-time version 2 → version 3 filesystem relocation is pinned to the version 3 layout version. Without the pin, bumping to version 4 would re-run it on every version 3 install and move that install's workspace under a synthesized `default` alias.
  - A version 4 acceptance fixture, `fixtures/v4.toml`, is regenerated from this chain, and the round-trip test compares the generated text byte for byte.
- **Known limits:** `save_dirty` returns early when nothing is dirty, so a config nobody edits keeps its retired keys on disk until a full save or `zeroclaw config migrate`. Every load still drops them from the running config and prints the warning. Separately, `save_dirty` still runs the pre-existing `ensure_blank_line_before_sections` pass over the whole file; it is not TOML-aware, so it can add a blank line inside a multiline string that contains a line starting with `[`. That predates this PR and is not changed here.
- **Scope boundary:** This establishes the mechanism. The inert-key audit found 259 runtime-inert leaf patterns; the rest are not retired here, and `RETIRED_KEYS` is the vehicle for them, one entry each. Not ported from #8754, because master still reads them: `skills.prompt_injection_mode`, which is the fallback for each agent's effective skills mode, `runtime_profiles.*.prompt_injection_mode`, the twelve top-level tool sections (`composio`, `microsoft365`, `project_intel`, `google_workspace`, `linkedin`, `jira`, `notion`, `claude_code`, `claude_code_runner`, `codex_cli`, `gemini_cli`, `opencode_cli`) and the twitter and reddit channels. Their features stay on master. They can be retired in version 4 as `RETIRED_KEYS` entries in the change that removes their code, before this release ships, and `RemoveChannel` covers the two channels. ADR-017 still mentions Nevis users in an acceptance gate and is unchanged. This supersedes the version 4 step in #8754 and the version 3 → version 4 and version 4 → version 5 steps in #9809, whose multi-model shape is additive and needs no step. The schema stays at version 4. This PR also generalizes #11191's incremental-save cleanup, on which it is rebased.
- **Blast radius:** Every existing install. Version 3 configs migrate to version 4 in memory on load, silently unless a retired key is present. `config set`, `config init`, `config patch` and `models set` refuse until `zeroclaw config migrate` has run once, as with every earlier schema bump. Fixtures, dev templates, `demo/config.toml`, the k8s sample and the `Containerfile` default config move to `schema_version = 4`, and so do the `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.debian` default configs, `demo/zeroclaw.toml.example` and the Nix module template (from #11217, which declared them at 3).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11082. Builds on #11191. Related #8754. Folds #11217. Related #9809. Related #3651. Related #6877.
- **Labels:** to be snapshotted after the path and size labelers run. Config is a `risk:high` surface.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's config file carries a version number, so that when a setting is removed an upgrade can rewrite old files and say what it changed. Several settings had been removed without that happening, so they were quietly ignored. Some had been ignored from the start, like tuning knobs written under an agent instead of under its runtime profile. This PR adds a list of retired settings. The upgrade removes each one it finds and prints a plain warning saying why and what to use instead. One entry can cover a setting under every agent or every profile. The first entries are the removed Nevis login block, eight agent knobs that never did anything, and an old summary-model setting. A config file with no version number is no longer read as the oldest version when it is plainly written in the current shape, which used to silently merge your named channels into one called `default`. It warns either way.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions:** An empty temp directory used as `HOME` and `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Write a `schema_version = 4` config with `[agents.coder]` holding `runtime_profile = "fast"` and `max_tool_iterations = 40`, `[runtime_profiles.fast]` holding `max_tool_iterations = 12`, and `[runtime_profiles.fast.context_compression]` holding `summary_model = "haiku"`.
  2. Run `zeroclaw config get runtime_profiles.fast.max_tool_iterations` without `-v`.
  3. Run `zeroclaw config migrate --json`, inspect `config.toml`, then repeat step 2.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 2 prints `12` and warns that `agents.coder.max_tool_iterations` and `runtime_profiles.fast.context_compression.summary_model` were dropped, with reasons. Step 3 lists both notices, removes both keys from the file, and the repeat is silent.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 2 prints `12` and nothing else. Step 3 reports nothing to migrate, and both dead keys stay.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Lint` (clippy `-D warnings`) and `Test`, which runs the config crate's unit and migration suites, the i18n tests and the component tests whose fixtures moved to version 4.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on head `3f047c33d5`, on master `e3775540d1` (merges cleanly with `e16fd898ba`):

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(exit 0)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 1810 passed; 0 failed
test result: ok. 106 passed; 0 failed      (migration integration, incl. the V4 fixture and real-config tests)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
(exit 0)

$ RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p zeroclaw-config --no-deps
(exit 0)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- i18n
test result: ok. 44 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo check -p zeroclaw --bins
(exit 0)

$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
No blocking markdown issues on changed lines.
```

  Also at this head: `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean, the gateway migrate tests, the i18n tests (44 passed) and `cargo check -p zeroclaw --bins`. The earlier run on `b81f88df11` also covered `zeroclaw-macros` tests and clippy for the gateway, channels, plugins and `zeroclaw` crates with Rust 1.98; this revision changes none of those crates except `src/main.rs`, which was checked above.

- **Incremental-save tests:** `save_dirty_removes_retired_nevis_table_from_disk` (the plaintext secret does not survive), `save_dirty_removes_retired_agent_tunables_from_disk` (wildcard entries, alias and live keys kept), `save_dirty_nevis_success_is_logged_only_after_atomic_replace`, `save_removes_retired_nevis_table_from_disk` and `retired_key_doc_cleanup_handles_every_nevis_spelling`. With the `save_dirty` hook disabled, the first three fail.
- **Review regression tests:** `doc_cleanup_keeps_aliases_in_every_toml_spelling`, `config_migrate_keeps_aliases_in_every_toml_spelling`, `structural_migration_keeps_an_emptied_dotted_alias_rendered` and `save_dirty_keeps_an_alias_emptied_through_dotted_keys` (aliases survive dotted, dotted-inline, inline and header-dotted spellings, and reload); `node_transport_and_wati_are_retired_on_every_path` and `save_dirty_removes_sections_retired_outside_v4_with_their_secrets` (no path or secret sentinel survives load, migrate or an unrelated incremental save at version 3 and version 4); `v3_migration_changes_only_the_version_line` and `retirement_migration_keeps_untouched_bytes` (byte-exact output with single quotes, `42_617`, `1e1`, `0x50` and trailing comments). Each fails with its fix reverted.
- **Catalog-completeness tests:** `retired_dashboard_code_length_is_removed_on_every_path`, `keys_dropped_by_the_v3_step_are_retired_on_every_path`, `save_dirty_removes_retired_dashboard_code_length` and `save_dirty_removes_keys_the_v3_step_retired` (migrate, load, document cleanup and an unrelated incremental save at version 3 and version 4, keeping the live sibling settings), and `a_v2_config_still_lifts_its_identity_into_agents`.
- **Real-config tests:** the migration integration suite runs the checked-in dev template three ways. Unchanged, it is not rewritten. With one retired key of each shape added, only those keys are removed and reported, comments survive, and a second migration is a no-op. With its `schema_version` line removed, it is read as version 3 with the inferred-version notice rather than as version 1, and the resilient load resets no section.
- **Unversioned-file and channel-retirement tests:** `a_plainly_v3_file_without_the_key_is_read_as_v3`, `an_inferred_v3_file_is_migrated_to_v4_and_keeps_every_channel_alias` (aliases kept on load, `config migrate` and the resilient load), `an_inferred_v3_file_still_loses_its_retired_keys`, `an_explicit_version_is_never_reported_as_inferred`, the version 1-reading cases (version 2 shape, version 1-only key, no alias-keyed section, the bundled version 1 fixture) and `v1_keys_still_current_are_exactly_the_current_top_level_sections`. `v3_to_v4_retires_top_level_twitter_and_reddit_but_not_the_channels` and `v3_to_v4_retires_the_notion_channel_with_every_reference_to_it` run a version 3 fixture through both the value chain and the in-place migration, checking the pruned agent channel lists, the dropped peer group, the kept telegram references and the comment on an untouched section. `notion_references_are_pruned_from_a_current_file_in_every_spelling` covers a version 4 file with dotted and inline tables. `a_retirement_never_names_a_key_the_schema_still_reads` guards the table. `a_map_only_v2_provider_profile_requires_an_explicit_version` (with version 2 and version 3 stated, each keeping its data), `a_map_only_v2_channel_requires_an_explicit_version`, `an_ordinary_v2_profile_with_a_map_field_keeps_the_v1_reading`, `a_v3_alias_named_like_a_field_is_ambiguous_only_if_it_fits_the_field` and `a_schema_version_beyond_u32_is_refused_not_wrapped` cover the inference edges. `save_removes_retired_channel_references_from_a_new_file`, `save_removes_retired_channel_references_from_an_existing_file` and `save_dirty_on_a_missing_file_removes_retired_channel_references` check the written file and its reload, with the live telegram references kept. With the probe, the full-save pass or the checked cast removed, these seven fail and the ordinary version 2 and clearly version 3 controls pass.
- **Cross-review regression tests:** `save_dirty_over_a_v2_file_migrates_it_before_editing` (identity and the agent's iteration limit survive, as does a key another handle saved after load; version 2 original kept), `saves_refuse_a_file_of_unknown_or_newer_version`, `the_first_save_over_a_v3_file_keeps_it`, `config_migrate_keeps_the_pre_upgrade_original`, `an_env_override_for_a_retired_key_is_ignored_not_fatal`, `retiring_a_channel_keeps_the_last_agent_binding`, `channel_reference_sites_match_the_alias_cascade`, `a_v2_only_setting_beside_v3_sections_requires_an_explicit_version`, `an_empty_map_field_still_makes_the_shape_ambiguous`, `v2_only_agent_keys_are_not_v3_agent_fields` and the gateway's `migration_reports_its_notices`. With each fix removed, the eight tests guarding them fail.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Against a debug build with an isolated temp `HOME`: the three steps above; a version 3 config with `[security.nevis]` and a `client_secret` (the secret is gone from `config.toml` and kept only in the backups); a version 4 config that still holds `[security.nevis]`; and a config with no `schema_version`. Every warning appeared without `-v`, and every second load was silent.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Exact plain-text output`
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `zeroclaw` CLI stderr, locale `en`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

```text
$ zeroclaw config get runtime_profiles.fast.max_tool_iterations
12
warning: dropped retired config key `agents.coder.max_tool_iterations` from <tmp>/cfg/config.toml: agent-inline runtime tunables were never read; runtime profiles are authoritative, so set this key on the agent's `[runtime_profiles.<profile>]` instead
warning: dropped retired config key `runtime_profiles.fast.context_compression.summary_model` from <tmp>/cfg/config.toml: the deprecated bare model id had no provider identity and was never read; `summary_provider` replaced it (context compression itself is not currently implemented in the runtime)
warning: these changes apply to this run only. Run `zeroclaw config migrate` to write them to <tmp>/cfg/config.toml.
```

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** As above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Clippy for `zeroclaw-runtime` ran on `--lib` only; its `--all-targets` run stops on a pre-existing unused-import lint in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs` (macOS test build, from #10931). This PR touches only that crate's Fluent files.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `zeroclaw config migrate` now removes `[security.nevis]` from disk, including any plaintext `client_secret`; before, it stayed indefinitely. The backups still hold it: `config.toml.backup`, and the pre-upgrade copy `config.toml.v3.backup` described under Rollback. The migration guide tells operators to delete the backup; it should now name both copies. Notices carry key paths and reasons only, never values; a unit test asserts this. The pinned filesystem relocation removes a risk this bump would otherwise have introduced: re-running the version 2 → version 3 workspace move on version 3 installs.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:
  - After upgrading, run `zeroclaw config migrate` once. Until then configs load normally, migrated in memory, but `config set`, `config init`, `config patch` and `models set` refuse, as with every earlier schema bump.
  - `[security.nevis]`, the eight agent-inline tunables and `summary_model` are no longer config keys. Set tunables on the agent's `[runtime_profiles.<profile>]`; configure `[oidc.<alias>]` with `[users]` and `[permission_profiles]` in place of Nevis.
  - A config with no `schema_version` prints a warning on every command until it has one. One plainly in the version 3 shape is read as version 3 rather than version 1, so its channel aliases and provider entries are no longer reshaped.
  - Top-level `[twitter]` and `[reddit]` and `[channels.notion]` are dropped, as are agent channel and escalation entries naming a `notion` channel. A peer group bound to one is kept with a notice, as is an agent's last channel binding; `Config::validate` reports both as dangling until the operator fixes them.
  - A save over a config whose version cannot be determined, or that is newer than this binary, now fails instead of writing over it. A `ZEROCLAW_*` variable naming a retired key is ignored with a notice.
  - An unversioned config whose shape reads both as version 2 and as version 3 is refused until `schema_version` is added. A `schema_version` past the `u32` range is refused as newer than the binary instead of being narrowed.
  - `zeroclaw config migrate --json` gains a `notices` array.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commits. #11191's Nevis-only save cleanup then returns with it. A config already migrated to `schema_version = 4` is then newer than the binary supports. A version 4 body is a subset of version 3, so setting it back to `schema_version = 3` by hand works; to restore the file as it was, use `config.toml.v3.backup` (or `.v1`/`.v2`). This binary writes that copy the first time it rewrites a file of that version, through `config migrate`, the dashboard's migrate, or a save, and never replaces it. `config.toml.backup` is not a reliable rollback copy: each `config migrate` replaces it, including a later retirement-only one of a version 4 file. The dashboard migrate's `config.toml.bak` is replaced by the next save.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** An unexpected `dropped retired config key` or `moved retired config key` line on stderr for a key that is still in use. `config migrate --json` shows the same entries under `notices`.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #8754 by @singlerider (its version 4 step and its still-valid retirements); #9809 by @NiuBlibing (its version 3 → version 4 and version 4 → version 5 steps only; the multi-model provider change stays in #9809); #11217 by @JordanTheJet (folded here).
- Scope materially carried forward: the inert agent-tunable and `summary_model` retirements, the version 3 layout pin for the filesystem relocation, and the version 4 acceptance fixture and its tests.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? Yes

prs.title: fix(plugins): create the package lock and transaction leases owner-only
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Package install, update and remove coordinate through `.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1` in the plugins directory, and every package transaction holds a `lease` file. Both were created with no explicit mode, so they took the process umask (typically `0644`). Taking the OS lock needs only read access, so any local account that could read the plugins directory could hold the package lock: install and remove then waited 60 seconds and failed, and `plugin remove` could report recovery ownership as unavailable.
  - Following the maintainer decision on #11360 (the default plugins directory is one account's state), both files are now created `0600` on Unix. A small `owner_only` helper in `crates/zeroclaw-plugins/src/host/recovery.rs` sets cap-std's `OpenOptionsExt::mode(0o600)` and is used at the two create sites, the package lock in `Root::lock_within` and the lease in `Root::transaction`. Other platforms keep their current behaviour.
  - When opening the package lock fails, the error now names the lock file: `cannot open the package lock <plugins>/.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1: Permission denied (os error 13)`. This covers all three attempts in `lock_within` (create, read+write reopen, read-only fallback). The error is still `PluginError::Io`; its kind is unchanged and the OS error is kept on its `source()`. No caller reads the OS error from these errors. Only the open is wrapped, not the `lock()` call whose error kinds decide the "no file locking" refusal. The 60-second timeout already names the file. This matters more now, because a lock another account created can no longer be opened at all.
  - Reopening an existing lock or lease is unchanged, so it never widens a mode.
  - `docs/book/src/developing/plugin-protocol.md` states the per-user ownership next to its existing note that any account that can read the lock can hold it, and says what to do about a lock another account created.
- **Scope boundary:** The reopen paths, including the read-only fallback for a lock this user cannot write, open the same files as before. Nothing changes the mode of a lock file that already exists. The `deleting` mark, transaction directories, the 60-second wait and Windows behaviour are untouched. A group-shared plugins directory (`0660`) is not supported here; it would be its own policy.
- **Blast radius:** Package install, update and remove, and their recovery, on Unix. These are the only callers of the package lock (`install_admitted`, `remove_with_report`, `update_admitted`, update recovery, and `displaced_packages`, which lists what an interrupted update left behind). `plugin list` and discovery do not take it. A lock created by a different account, for example root after `sudo zeroclaw plugin install` into this user's plugins directory, is now `0600` and owned by that account. The owner's later install and remove fail at once and name that file, where before they could open it read-only. The issue lists this as the accepted cost of the owner-only policy. The remedy is to remove that lock file while nothing is installing; the next operation recreates it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Partially addresses #11360. It stays open for a lock that v0.8.6 created, which keeps its wider mode after the upgrade (see Compatibility).
- **Release note:** On Unix, the plugin package lock and transaction leases are now created owner-only (`0600`). A package lock that v0.8.6 created keeps its earlier mode, so another local account that can read the plugins directory can still hold it. Run `chmod 600 <plugins_dir>/.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1`, or delete that file while no install, update or remove is running.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw keeps a small lock file in the plugins directory so that two installs or removes never run at the same time, and one more file per operation in progress. Until now those files could be read by other people on the same machine, and reading was enough to grab the lock, so another account could make your plugin installs hang for a minute and then fail. Now only your own account can open them. If the lock was left by another account, for example by a `sudo` install, the error now says which file is in the way. Nothing else about installing or removing plugins changes, and Windows is unaffected.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new unit tests check the modes under two umasks and the error for a lock this account cannot open. The cross-account case needs a second local account.

### How I tested

Two new tests in `host::recovery::owner_only_tests`:

- `package_lock_and_lease_are_created_owner_only`. The umask is process-wide, so for each of `002` and `022` it re-runs the test binary under `sh -c 'umask …'`. It runs the ignored helper `create_lock_and_lease_child` with `--ignored` and checks that the helper really ran (`1 passed`). The child creates the package lock and a transaction lease, then reopens both through a second root. The parent reads the modes; it finds the transaction directory by its lease file. The directory's own mode (`775`, `755`) shows that the child ran under the intended umask.
- `a_lock_this_account_cannot_open_fails_at_once_and_is_named`. It creates the lock through one root, sets it to `000`, then calls `lock()` through a second root. The call must fail at once, the message must contain the lock path, the error must have kind `PermissionDenied`, and the source must carry the same OS error as a plain open of the file. It returns early when running as root, which opens the file regardless. This goes through the same AlreadyExists → read+write → read-only path as a lock another account created. It then checks that creating the lock in a directory this account cannot write (`0500`) names the lock file too.

On `master` with only the first test added (RED):

```text
assertion `left == right` failed: [umask, transaction directory, lock, lease]
  left: [["002", "775", "664", "664"], ["022", "755", "644", "644"]]
 right: [["002", "775", "600", "600"], ["022", "755", "600", "600"]]
```

With only the `owner_only` change and without the naming, the second test fails (RED):

```text
test host::recovery::owner_only_tests::a_lock_this_account_cannot_open_fails_at_once_and_is_named ... FAILED
IO error: Permission denied (os error 13)
```

With the whole change both pass. Removing only the `mode(0o600)` line makes the first test fail again with the same values. Removing only the naming on the read-only fallback, or only the naming on the create, makes the second test fail again. Both pass once the file is restored.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (plugins cranelift backend)` runs the plugins lib unit tests on Linux, which include both new tests. `Lint` and `Test` cover formatting and the rest.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** macOS. The `Scheduled Platform Tests` workflow runs the full workspace on `macos-15`, which includes these tests, but it runs nightly on `master` or by manual dispatch, not on this PR. A maintainer can dispatch it against this branch. Windows has no change; the helper is a no-op there and the test module is Unix-only.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (Linux x86_64. The `--bin zeroclaw` run used umask `022`, as CI does. Under umask `002`, one unrelated root-crate test, `alias_cli::tests::agent_mutation_fails_closed_when_owner_has_no_rpc_endpoint`, refuses its group-writable temp data directory; it does not touch plugin code.)

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                                  exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets -- -D warnings                      exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets --features plugins-wasm-cranelift -- -D warnings   exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift -- -D warnings   exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --no-default-features --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib
  test result: ok. 417 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --lib
  test result: ok. 278 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift
  lib 417 passed, 1 ignored; channel_plugin_e2e 23; egress_plugin_e2e 9; legacy_plugin_migrate 11; reference_plugin 9;
  reference_plugin_e2e 3 passed, 1 ignored; sequential_egress_e2e 4; socket_plugin_e2e 7;
  tool_plugin_e2e 2; tool_plugin_timeout_e2e 5; websocket_plugin_e2e 5; sign_manifest 3; all 0 failed
cargo test --locked --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --bin zeroclaw   (umask 022)
  test result: ok. 759 passed; 0 failed
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/developing/plugin-protocol.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The lock and lease modes under umask `002` and `022`; that reopening either one leaves the mode as created; and the named error for a lock this account cannot open. I did not reproduce the cross-account case, because it needs a second local account.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `master` at `4e82ce46e9` plus this diff, Linux x86_64.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No local macOS or Windows run; see the coverage gap above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. Files are created with narrower permissions than before.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for a plugins directory one account owns. An existing lock file keeps the mode it was created with, and new leases are `0600`. v0.8.5 has no such lock, but v0.8.6 creates it (it arrived with #11236, b3c615644b, which the v0.8.6 tag contains). So a plugins directory used by v0.8.6, or by a `master` build since #11236, keeps a `0644` or `0664` lock after the upgrade, and another local account that can read the plugins directory can still hold it. To tighten it, run `chmod 600` on it, or delete it while nothing is installing. #11360 stays open for documenting that step for v0.8.6 users.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: from v0.8.6, run `chmod 600 <plugins_dir>/.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1`, or delete it while nothing is installing. A plugins directory shared between accounts was never a supported layout. An operator who ran an install as another account (for example with `sudo`) removes that account's `.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1` while nothing is installing.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. Files created while this was in place stay `0600`, which earlier builds open normally as the same account.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Package install, update or remove failing at once with `cannot open the package lock <plugins>/.zeroclaw-package-lock-v1: Permission denied (os error 13)` when the plugins directory holds a lock file another account created.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add persistent session prompt attachments
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an opt-in SQLite collection of four bounded prompts owned by one durable Chat session. Restart preserves them; whole-session reset, deletion and TTL cleanup remove them transactionally with their owner. Legacy prompt binding schema and ownership reconciliation migrate in one immediate transaction, including rollback on failure.
  - Adds current-session `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete`. Mutations require exact one-time approval by default. Global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval = "disabled"` is an explicit operator choice. The tools are direct-only, not skill aliases, pipeline children or inherited auxiliary capabilities.
  - Injects a deterministic next-primary-turn section after immutable host context. Provider context, explicit list and dedicated approval previews retain content; ordinary events, progress and retained/export history mask it without rewriting provider working history. Modifying LLM hooks are skipped for private requests rather than receiving a masked mutable copy. Independent child transcripts do not inherit attachment-bearing parent prompt scope; same-agent SOP continuation retains its existing primary transcript without prompt-tool capability. Unsupported prompt-tool calls are rejected before approval, and their arguments/results are excluded from SOP step audit capture.
  - Binds primary work to the admitted durable incarnation. Chat deletion now coordinates RPC and gateway work: cancel the captured generation, serialize deletion, commit durable alias removal atomically in SQLite, and invalidate the gateway generation only after commit. SQLite rollback preserves the durable owner and leaves an idle WebSocket usable; already-cancelled work cannot be restored. Non-transactional backends delete aliases sequentially and can partially delete them before reporting an error. Gateway cancellation binds the exact admitted queue key and generation, preventing deletion of an underscore session from cancelling a distinct dotted WebSocket session.

### What this does, simply

A chat can keep a small reminder attached to itself rather than relying on remaining conversation history. A later primary turn receives it after restart, but another session and auxiliary workers do not. Successful whole-session reset starts without the attachments. The feature is off by default.

Operators normally approve the exact proposed mutation once. Unsupported confirmation surfaces refuse it; ordinary approvals still work. Prompt text grants no permissions and cannot override immutable safety/host instructions. If the complete collection and required tool-protocol framing cannot fit, provider dispatch fails instead of silently dropping content.

There are at most four attachments, each at most 2 KiB and 8 KiB collectively. Symbolic IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`. Changes take effect on the next top-level turn, not during the already-running turn.

The deletion fix prevents an open WebSocket from recreating a session that RPC just deleted. A same-ID successor is a new owner, not permission for the old connection or queued work to continue. Deleting `team_alpha` does not cancel an unrelated active `team.alpha` WebSocket queue; HTTP/SSE still uses its actual normalized queue and raw abort ID.

Strict approval has one-time allow/reject, no Always, and rejection changes nothing. After committed deletion the old WebSocket reports `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; it cannot recreate or adopt the successor. Durable deletion failure is reported without claiming success and preserves the durable state.

- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**

Hooks cannot read sensitive bodies/results. Content hashes can permit low-entropy guessing; masking is not secrecy.
